Headline_English: Shah Rukh, Rani to receive National Film Award for the first time
Content_Enlish:
After ruling Bollywood for more than three decades, Shah Rukh Khan is finally going to receive his first National Film Award. He has been recognized as ‘Best Actor’ for his performance in the 2023 blockbuster ‘Jawan’. On the other hand, Rani Mukerji has also won the Best Actress award along with Shah Rukh Khan for her emotional performance in the film ‘Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway’. She is also receiving this award for the first time. Indian Express reports. 
This is a special achievement for Shah Rukh, because earlier he had been nominated for 30 Filmfare Awards and won 14 times, out of which 8 times for the Best Actor award—the highest win in this category jointly with Dilip Kumar. In addition, the French government has awarded him awards like ‘Ordre des Arts et des Lettres’ and ‘Legion of Honour’, which is a shining example of his acceptance worldwide. 

Shah Rukh Khan made his Bollywood debut in 1992 with the film ‘Deewana’. In the next three decades, he gave a series of popular films - 'Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge', 'Kavi Khushi Kavi Gam', 'Chennai Express', 'My Name Is Khan' and many other superhit films. 

Meanwhile, 'Twelve Fail' actor Vikrant Massey won the Best Actor award along with Shahrukh at the National Film Awards. This is also Vikrant's first National Film Award. 

On the other hand, Shahrukh Khan's long-time co-star Rani Mukerji also won the Best Actress award for the first time at the National Film Awards. She won the Best Actress award for her emotional and realistic performance in the film 'Mrs. Chatterjee vs. Norway'. Rani, who started her film career with the Bengali film 'Beer Phool' in 1996, made her Bollywood debut with 'Raja Ki Aayegi Baaraat' the same year. 

The songs in the film 'Jawan' also saw success - Shilpa Rao won the Best Female Playback Singer award. On the other hand, Sudipta Sen received the Best Director award for the film 'The Kerala Story'.

Headline_English: Shah Rukh injured in shooting, goes to US for treatment
Content_Enlish: Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan has been injured in an accident while shooting for the movie 'King'. It is learnt that the incident took place while shooting an action scene at Mumbai's Golden Tobacco Studios. Later, he was rushed to the US for treatment. Times of India reported. A source said that Shah Rukh Khan did not suffer any major injury. However, he has pulled a muscle. Earlier, he had injured various muscles of his body while doing various stunts. He is currently resting on the advice of doctors. He will return to shooting for the next schedule of 'King' by September or October. The source further said that Shah Rukh is taking a break from all work for a month. Once he recovers, he will return to shooting with full enthusiasm. Shah Rukh Khan's fans are wishing him a speedy recovery.

Headline_English: Item girl Shefali Zariwala, famous for 'Kanta Laga', passes away
Content_Enlish:
Shefali Jariwala, a popular Bollywood actress and item girl known as the 'Kanta Laga' girl, has passed away at the age of 42. She died of a heart attack on Friday (June 27) night. The actress, who gained immense popularity through Bigg Boss 13, was rushed to Bellevue Multispecialty Hospital in Mumbai by her husband and actor Parag Tyagi and three others. Later, after tests, the doctors declared Shefali dead. The sudden death of Shefali Jariwala has cast a shadow of grief in the entertainment world as well as her fans. Actors have already posted about her untimely demise on social media. 
In 2002, the Hindi pop album 'DJ Doll' was released. Shefali Jariwala gained popularity overnight with the remix video of the song 'Kanta Laga' in it. She was also seen in a cameo role in the film 'Mujhse Shaadi Karoge' starring Salman Khan and Akshay Kumar. In total, he has worked in more than 35 music videos.

Headline_English: Salman Khan's 'Sikander' leaked on 600 websites before release
Content_Enlish:
The wait is finally over. Salman Khan's film 'Sikander' was released worldwide on Sunday (March 30) on the occasion of the upcoming Eid-ul-Fitr. Everyone from the director to the producer is eagerly waiting for the film. But unfortunately, the film was leaked online before it was released on the big screen. According to Indian media reports, the film was leaked online late on Saturday (March 29). However, the film was leaked on not one or two websites, but a total of 600 websites. After the news spread, there was concern among the fans. Film trade analyst Komal Nahta was seen expressing anger over this issue. In a tweet on Sunday morning, Komal said, this incident is like a nightmare for any producer. The film was leaked online before its release. We have heard many such incidents before. Unfortunately, the same thing happened to Sikandar this time too. Nahta also said that the film's producer, Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment, has called for strict action on the whole matter. Not only that, the film has already been removed from 600 websites. But that is only a small part of the damage. The number of websites is increasing and is increasing gradually. This is really a very condemnable act. It can affect the box office. 

Meanwhile, it is not yet known how the film was leaked or from which agency it was leaked. However, the makers have appealed to the police to investigate the entire incident.

Headline_English: Sushant Singh Rajput committed suicide, CBI ends investigation into death
Content_Enlish:
Murder or suicide? After 5 years of the death of popular Bollywood actor Sushant Singh Rajput, the CBI has finally concluded its investigation. On Saturday (March 22), local time, the CBI submitted the final report of the case to the Mumbai court. It has been informed that Sushant Singh Rajput committed suicide. No other aspect has come up in the investigation. 
A CBI official said that the CBI has submitted the final report of the case in the Bandra court. No other information has come up in the investigation except suicide. The CBI has recorded all the information and names of the witnesses in the final report. If everything is fine, the next hearing of the case will be held on April 8.

Headline_English: Parimoni's ex-husband Sourav arrested
Content_Enlish: The DB police have arrested Ferdous Kabir Sourav (29), the ex-husband of actress Parimoni. He was arrested from the Bashundhara Residential area of ​​the capital on Thursday (March 6). It is learnt that the arrested Sourav is an associate of Awami League leader of Keshabpur Municipality in Jessore, Mayor Rafiqul Islam. He was a member of former MP Shahin Chakladar's group. Sourav married Parimoni on April 28, 2012. The dowry was one lakh taka. However, a distance developed between them two years after the marriage. Sourav is the son of Shahana Kabir Fatema, a former female councilor of Keshabpur Municipality.

Headline_English: Actress Anjana passes away
Content_Enlish:
National Film Award-winning actress Anjana has died. She died while undergoing treatment at Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) on Friday (January 3) night (Inna lillahi wa inna ilaihi rajiun). The news of Anjana's death was confirmed to the media by Misha Sawdagar, president of the Film Artists' Association. 

Anjana had been on life support at the capital's PG Hospital for the past three days. It is learned that Anjana's namaz-e-janaza will be held at the FDC on Saturday at 11 am. 

On December 24, heroine Anjana was admitted to a private hospital in the capital. She had a fever at the time. Later, doctors said that her blood infection had spread throughout her body. As a result, she had problems with her heart and kidneys. There was fluid in her lungs. She also had a stroke once. 

Anjana is both an actress and a dancer. Although she does not work in films, she is regularly found at various film events. She has won the National Film Award twice.

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia passed away at a time of great hardship - Jaya Ahsan
Content_Enlish:
The death of BNP Chairperson and three-time former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia has brought an atmosphere of mourning to social media. Facebook has become a book of condolence messages. People from all walks of life and entertainment stars are also remembering the country's first female Prime Minister in emotional messages. 

Actress Jaya Ahsan has mentioned Khaleda Zia's departure in her Facebook status as a loss at a difficult time for the country. She wrote, "Begum Khaleda Zia passed away at a very difficult time. People are waiting for elections and democracy ahead. The value of her presence was immense." 

Recalling the role of Begum Khaleda Zia in the country's political history, Jaya Ahsan further wrote, "Begum Zia was a major character in the movement against military rule and for the establishment of democracy - brilliant in courage and leadership." She added, "A chapter in the country's long political movement has ended with her. May her soul rest in eternal peace." 

It is worth noting that Begum Khaleda Zia had been suffering from various physical complications for a long time. After her release from prison, she was taken to London for advanced treatment on January 7 this year. Although her health improved somewhat with treatment, she repeatedly fell ill due to age-related weakness and complications of multiple diseases and had to be admitted to the hospital. The demise of this influential leader, born in 1945, marked the end of a long and important chapter in the country's politics.

Headline_English: Karan Johar and his 'Homebound' in legal trouble over story plagiarism allegations
Content_Enlish:
'Homebound' became an Indian film that made it to the Oscar shortlist. However, the film has been caught in a major legal dilemma as it has not been able to enjoy the fruits of its success. Popular Bollywood producer Karan Johar's production company Dharma Productions and OTT platform Netflix have been accused of direct story plagiarism. 

Journalist and writer Pooja Changoiwala has launched a legal battle against the film, directed by Neeraj Ghawan. She claims that the story, characters and setting of the film have been taken from her much-discussed novel 'Homebound', published in 2021, without any permission or acknowledgement. 

Pooja Changoiwala said that she had written the novel focusing on the inhumane life, struggle and painful reality of migrant workers in India during the 2020 Corona pandemic. After watching the film, she was surprised to notice that the film had a surprising similarity with the main story, character development and setting of her book. She claimed that the similarity between the second half of the film and the novel is 'unusually close'. 

Based on this allegation, the writer sent a legal notice to Dharma Productions and Netflix Entertainment Services India on October 15. The notice clearly states that her creative work has been used without permission, which is a direct violation of intellectual property laws. 

On the other hand, no official statement has been received from Karan Johar's production company regarding such a serious allegation. However, after receiving the legal notice, discussions are underway with lawyers on the matter and the production company is preparing to deal with the complaint through legal means.

Headline_English: 'Cultural Evening' at Shilpakala on the occasion of Christmas
Content_Enlish:
In the continuation of cultural events focusing on various religious and social festivals with the aim of building an inclusive Bangladesh, a special 'Cultural Evening' has been organized on the occasion of Christmas. The event will be held at Nandanmancha on the Shilpakala Academy premises in the capital on Wednesday (December 25) at 6 pm under the initiative of the Ministry of Cultural Affairs and under the management of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy. 

This cultural evening, organized with the peace, harmony and human values ​​of Christmas in mind, will include musical performances, carol singing and kirtan. Members of various artists and cultural organizations will participate in this festive event. 

Incidentally, various cultural events have been organized around various religious and national festivals throughout the year under the initiative of the Ministry of Cultural Affairs and Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy. Among them, the Moonlight Festival was held at Nandanmancha on March 30 on the occasion of Eid-ul-Fitr. Cultural festivals were organized in six districts of the country, including Nandanmancha, on May 10 on the occasion of Buddhist Purnima. 

Apart from this, on the occasion of Eid-ul-Azha, a joyous festival was organized at Nandan Mancha on June 6, and on the occasion of Sharidya Durga Puja, a two-day Sharidya Cultural Festival was organized at Suhrawardy Udyan on September 30 and at Nandan Mancha on October 1.

Headline_English: Nabila to appear as 'Banalata Sen' on Eid-ul-Fitr
Content_Enlish:
Since the release of her first movie 'Ainabaji', actress and model Masuma Rahman Nabila has been the subject of separate discussions among the audience and critics. After that, she worked in several movies and dramas, but her movie 'Tufan' with Dhallywood superstar Shakib Khan was released on Eid-ul-Fitr last year. When the movie received a good response from the audience, Nabila came into the discussion again. This time, her new movie 'Banolata Sen' is going to be released ahead of the upcoming Eid. 

The actress is very optimistic about the movie. Nabila said, it feels good to think that a movie in which I have acted is being released after a long break. I am really hopeful that 'Banolata Sen' will be able to fulfill the expectations of the audience. I believe that the story, production and acting will be a different experience. 

There are rumors of a bunch of movies being released on Eid-ul-Fitr. In the meantime, the names of several other movies including 'Prince', 'Dum', 'Rakshas', 'Banalata Express', and 'Pink' have been made public. 'Banalata Sen' has been newly added to that list. Producer Masud Hasan Ujjwal had prepared to release the movie in 2024. However, considering the overall situation in the country, the release was postponed. Finally, it has been learned that the movie will be released in front of the audience in the new year. 

This movie is based on Banalata Sen, a fictional character of the powerful poet of Bengali literature Jibanananda Das. Masuma Rahman Nabila has played the title role in the film, made with government funding. Khairul Basar will be seen in the role of poet Jibanananda Das in the movie. Sohel Mondal, Naziba Bashar, Priyanti Urbi, Rupanti Akid, Sharif Siraj, and Sumaiya Khushi have also acted in the film. 'Banalata Sen' receives government funding in the 2021-22 fiscal year. 

Producer Masud Hasan Ujjwal said that he did not compromise in making the film. Even though it took a long time, he completed the work with care. He said that working with Jibanananda Das means extra responsibility. Research, preparation, selection of suitable actors – everything was difficult and time-consuming. Rehearsals were held for a long time and special attention was also paid to production design. 

Regarding the release of the film, the producer said that the release of 'Banalata Sen' is planned to be ahead of Eid-ul-Fitr 2026. The promotion will start soon with an official announcement.

Headline_English: Arifin Shuvo in Bollywood, surprises in teaser
Content_Enlish:
The news of a Bangladeshi actor working in a Bollywood movie or series always creates a special excitement among the Dhaka audience. And if that work is in the main character of the entire story, then the joy undoubtedly increases. This is exactly the case with 'Jazz City'. Dhaka hero Arifin Shuvo has played the central character in this Bollywood series. 

Yesterday, Sony Liv officially released the teaser of 'Jazz City'. In the teaser, Arifin Shuvo is seen in the character of Jimmy Roy, the character around whom the story of the entire series revolves. It can be said that Jimmy is the soul of this series. 

In the teaser, Shuvo is seen in multiple different looks. Somewhere elegant and mysterious in a gray slim cut suit, somewhere else he is dancing in a sparkling white suit. Each look has a retro touch - the atmosphere of the 1970s is clearly reflected in the hair style, clothes and body language. 

Arifin Shuvo said about the character of Jimmy Roy, "This is a multi-dimensional story, where not only dialogues but also music tells the story. Many feelings and situations are expressed through music, silence and moments beyond dialogue. A deep atmosphere of jazz music can be felt throughout the entire series." 

Shuvo has acted in four languages ​​in his first Bollywood project - Bengali, Hindi, Urdu and English, which has given this series a different dimension. 

The teaser reveals that 'Jazz City' is set against the backdrop of the Liberation War of Bangladesh and the seventies. The socio-political reality of that time, the story of human tension and change will emerge in the series. An attempt has been made to bring history and atmosphere to life as much as possible in the production style - so that the audience can really go back to that time. 

The series is produced by Soumik Sen, who has previously garnered praise in Bollywood as the co-director of the discussed 'Jubilee' series. In addition to directing, he also wrote the story and screenplay for 'Jazz City'. Popular Tollywood actress Souraseni Mitra has acted opposite Arifin Shuvo. Apart from this, there are a few other familiar faces from Bollywood and Tollywood. 

Sony Liv has announced that ‘Jazz City’ will be released in Hindi, Bengali and English on February 6, 2026. After the release of the teaser, many viewers have expressed their expectations about the series.

Headline_English: Subhashree responds to controversy over photo with Messi
Content_Enlish:
As part of his India tour, football star Lionel Messi attended an event in Kolkata on Saturday. There, Tollywood actress Subhashree Ganguly took a picture with Messi and shared it on social media. After that, trolls started surrounding him. First, on Facebook, then on the police station, Subhashree's husband, director Raj Chakraborty, filed a complaint about the matter. Now Subhashree herself has opened up about the whole matter. 

Subhashree said that she received an invitation to meet Messi. Accordingly, she reached a specific hotel on Saturday morning. That is where she met Messi for the first time and took pictures. 

According to Subhashree, 'I reached the hotel around 8:30. I met Messi from 10:00 to 10:15 in the morning. Pictures were taken. When I was leaving, Messi's public relations team requested me to go to Yuva Bharati Krirangan. They said that there are various arrangements around Messi. If I go there, they will benefit. 

In response to the question of why only she was invited from the Bengali film industry and did she get this special privilege because she is the wife of a ruling party MLA, Subhashree said, "Their PR team can answer this question well." 

The actress said that she herself saw the situation on the field heating up. She claims that the responsibility for the entire incident lies with the organizers. She also said that she left the place after the situation became chaotic. 

Subhashree raised the question and said, "I myself was sitting in the tent next to the field and could not see Messi. So how will you see it? But was I on the field? Was I standing between you? The way I am being mocked, it seems that I was standing next to Messi on the field. Where is my fault? Is it a crime to go to the hotel and take pictures? It may be my fault that the picture was posted at the wrong time due to technical reasons. 

Expressing her anger, she further said, "I am a woman, am I being attacked because I am an actress in Bengali films? Kareena Kapoor also went to Bollywood. Didn't Shah Rukh Khan go to take pictures? So what is my fault? I am also being ridiculed as someone's ex-girlfriend. The year 2026 is coming. Even as women, women are being addressed like this. Do you think it is right for yourselves?

Headline_English: Multiple defects on ships bound for St. Martin
Content_Enlish:
There are multiple safety flaws in ships plying the Cox's Bazar-St. Martin's sea route. Among these flaws, tourists are traveling to St. Martin's Island at the risk of their lives. On Tuesday, various flaws were identified in the ships in a joint operation by the Coast Guard, BIWTA and the relevant administration to ensure passenger safety. 

Abdul Wakil, BIWTA River Port Officer in Cox's Bazar, said, "During the inspection, we noticed a common and serious flaw in almost all the ships. According to the ship's certificate, there should be a qualified first-class master, but many ships could not find him. Rather, it was seen that the ships have been operated by a second-class master or assistant master for a long time. This situation has been going on since December 1." 

He also said, the ship owner had assured us that a qualified main master would be provided soon. However, in reality, that promise was not implemented. Another important flaw related to the engine room was found during the inspection. Although the maintenance logbook was supposed to be maintained by checking the pressure and performance of the engine every day, this logbook was not maintained properly in most of the ships. 

Abdul Wakil said that several serious defects were found on the ship named Bay Cruise International One. The master in charge there was an assistant master. He could not give a clear idea about the location of the ship's fire extinguishers and other emergency equipment, which is very worrying. 

Coast Guard officer leading the operation, Lt. Commander Salahuddin Rashid Tanvir, said that a joint operation was conducted on tourist ships at the Nuniarachara BIWTA jetty in Cox's Bazar from 3:30 am to 6:00 am on Tuesday. The operation verified the ship's registration, fitness, route permit, firefighting system, first aid equipment and crew proficiency certificates. 

The operation closely monitored the passenger list, compliance with the designated capacity, adequate life-saving equipment and crew responsibility. The defects found during the inspection will be discussed with the concerned authorities and sent in the form of an investigation report and legal action will be taken as necessary.

Headline_English: Khaled Saifullah resigns from NCP
Content_Enlish:
Khaled Saifullah, the joint convener of the National Citizens Party (NCP), has resigned from the party. He has submitted his resignation letter to convener Nahid Islam, seeking his release from all party posts. 

\On Wednesday night, NCP Joint Member Secretary and Media Cell Editor Mushfiqur Us Salehin confirmed the matter to Samakal. He said that he submitted his resignation letter to the party's WhatsApp group around 9:30 pm. 

In the one-sentence resignation letter, Khaled Saifullah wrote, 'I am resigning from all posts of the National Citizens Party.' A copy of the resignation has been sent to the NCP's member secretary, office cell and all central members. 

Khaled Saifullah is the husband of former senior joint member secretary of the NCP, Dr. Tasnim Zara. Earlier, Tasnim Zara resigned from the NCP on December 27. 

The next day, on December 28, the party's joint convener, Tajnubha Zabin, resigned from the NCP. He even announced that he would not participate in the election. He was supposed to contest from Dhaka-17 constituency on behalf of the NCP. He made this announcement in a long post on his verified Facebook on Sunday morning. In the post, Tajnuva Jabin wrote, "Many of you are thinking that maybe I object to the alliance with Jamaat due to historical reasons or women's issues. The more frightening reason is the process in which this has happened. It is being given the level of political strategy, electoral alliance, etc. I would say it is planned. It has been brought to this point by arranging it." 

On December 30, two more leaders resigned from the NCP. They are Asif Mustafa Jamal (Nehal), a member of the party's central committee, and Azad Khan Bhasani, the chief coordinator of the farmers' wing. Mustafa Jamal announced his resignation in a post on his verified Facebook account on Monday night. Apart from being a member of the NCP's central committee, he was also a member of the publicity, publication and environment cell and the secretary of the social media subcommittee of the party's election management committee. 

Jamal officially announced his resignation from all responsibilities and posts of the NCP in a Facebook post. He said, "The NCP has unfortunately completely failed to keep the promise it made to build a new Bangladesh, a new political settlement and a new state structure on the blood of nearly 1,400 martyrs." Jamal alleged that instead of breaking the old state structure and the same state arrangements, the NCP has gradually adapted itself to that system. He wrote, "Keeping in mind my responsibility and respect for the country and its people, I do not want to remain responsible for all the failures of this organization for a moment." 

On Sunday night, Azad Khan Bhashani, the chief coordinator of the party's farmers' wing, announced his resignation from the NCP. In a post on his Facebook account, he announced his decision to "formally sever ties" with the NCP. Azad Khan is the grandson of oppressed public leader Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani. On September 6, he was given the responsibility of the chief coordinator of the NCP's farmers' wing. 

In a Facebook post, Azad Khan said, "I first joined the National Citizen Committee and later the National Citizen Party out of the dream of the people-oriented, anti-imperialist and anti-discrimination politics shown by the oppressed public leader Maulana Bhasani. In that political continuity, I took on the responsibility of the chief coordinator of the party's farmers' wing. But I have to say with great sadness that in real experience, I have felt a clear lack of the historical responsibility of building a new Bangladesh, compassion for the people and the depth of sacrifice that is needed here. The expected success has not been seen in building a new political settlement either."

Headline_English: The shadow war between India and Pakistan is fueled by assassinations
Content_Enlish:
India is carrying out a series of deadly assassinations in neighboring Pakistan. On Tuesday, the US media outlet Washington Post published a report on these assassinations. It mentions several individuals who were involved in attacks on India or its agents at various times. New Delhi is now trying to kill them through Pakistani and Afghan agents, which began in 2021 under the current Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 

A man named Aamir Sarfaraz beat an Indian spy to death in a Lahore jail in 2011. At that time, he was sentenced to death. But he was released after the murder. India believes that their spy was killed in a planned manner by Pakistan's intelligence agency. India killed Sarfaraz by hired killers to avenge that incident. However, some sources claim that Sarfaraz is alive. Following this incident, Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that there have been some recent murders with direct Indian involvement. 

The report said that since 2021, India's intelligence agency 'RAW' has tried to kill at least half a dozen people in Pakistan. Not only that, they have also tried to kill pro-Khalistan Sikh leaders in the US and Canada. India has conducted experiments in Pakistan to see if the assassination is successful. After that, they have planned to kill Sikh leaders in Western countries. 

A Pakistani official said that the details of the assassinations carried out by India in their country have not been disclosed in this way before. Because it would raise questions about their intelligence capabilities. But many do not want to keep the matter quiet anymore. Because under Modi, India is now becoming a superpower. They feel that the assassinations carried out by India should be exposed. 

Before the issue of India's assassination attempts in the US and Canada came to light, Pakistan's spy chief Nadeem Anjum had informed US spy chief William J. Burns about this in 2022. 
The Indian Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the allegations, according to the Washington Post. However, when Indian officials were questioned about these matters earlier, they neither denied nor admitted it. They said that assassinations are not part of their policy. An official said that Pakistan and Western countries did not hand over the militants despite India providing sufficient evidence. He said that the United States has killed many terrorists in Pakistan through drone strikes. 

India passed a strict anti-terrorism law in 2019. Since then, it has started publishing lists of suspected militants or terrorists. The Washington Post reported that 11 of the 58 people currently on the list have been killed or attacked. In addition, the Washington Post has learned about 10 people whom India had labeled as terrorists and who were later killed. All of them were shot dead at close range by unknown gunmen. 

In another report, the Washington Post reported that the opposition party in the Maldives planned to oust the current President of Maldives, Mohamed Mujibur Rahman, through impeachment. For this, they sought $6 million in assistance from India. The money was allegedly given as bribes to 40 MPs from Muizzu's own party, high-ranking police and army officials, and powerful terrorist groups. However, the matter did not go further. The opposition tried to ally with New Delhi after the withdrawal of Indian troops from the Maldives, the media reported.

Headline_English: World's fastest train launches in China
Content_Enlish:
China has unveiled its own new train. The passenger train can travel at a speed of 400 kilometers per hour. The speed of the CR450 model train increased to 450 kilometers during test runs, according to the Chinese Ministry of Transport. 

After its official launch, it will be the world's fastest train. This will surpass China's current 350-kilometer-per-hour CR400 train. This model of train began passenger transportation in 2017. 

The new train was jointly built by Chengchun Railway Vehicles and Sifang Company Limited. They praised the train, saying that its speed, energy efficiency, noise control and braking system are quite good. 

The state-run China Daily reported that the train has undergone 3,000 simulations and more than 2,000 platform tests. However, it needs more line tests and other refinements before it can carry passengers. 

China has been ahead of everyone in terms of rail services in the past decade. The country has built thousands of kilometers of new railway lines. This has brought trains to every part of the country. China currently has 160,000 kilometers of railway lines. Of which 46,000 kilometers are high-speed lines. 

Since the 1980s, hundreds of billions of dollars have been spent in Asia and Europe to build high-speed trains and improve services. Japan's Shinkansen and France's TGV introduced the world's first high-speed trains, which later became popular as an alternative to air travel.

Headline_English: S Alam Group to reopen 9 closed factories
Content_Enlish:
S Alam authorities have decided to reopen 9 closed factories. The business organization has announced that these factories will be reopened from Wednesday, the first day of the year. 
On Tuesday evening, a notice signed by S Alam Group's Human Resources and Administration Department Head Mohammad Borhan Uddin said that the management authority's decision to close the factory issued on December 24 has been withdrawn. This order will be effective from January 1. 

However, S Alam authorities did not clarify the reason for the simultaneous closure and reopening of 9 factories. When contacted with the company's top two officials on Tuesday night, they refused to make an official comment. 

DGM Engineer Rafiqul Islam of the closed S Alam Refined Sugar Industries Limited told Samakal, "I have received a notice to reopen the factory. The factory will be opened from tomorrow (Wednesday). 

It is worth noting that on December 24, the sudden closure of 9 factories was announced through two separate notices signed by S Alam Group's Human Resources and Administration Head Mohammad Borhan Uddin. Factory workers immediately protested this announcement and made 10-point demands.

Headline_English: Thousands of conspiracies are underway against the country: Jamaat Ameer
Content_Enlish:
Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has commented that thousands of conspiracies are underway against the country, saying that there are minorities and majority. He said, a group of conspirators want to divide the country into two parts. There is no such nation in the world that has been able to gain dignity by dividing. Thousands of conspiracies are being hatched against us, against the country. This conspiracy will stop 360 million hands of 180 million people with strong hands. We need national unity now. 

He said these things while speaking as the chief guest at a road meeting at Birganj Government College in Dinajpur on Sunday. 

Dr. Shafiqur Rahman said, our country is a country with immense potential. Why is the situation of a country rich in green and lush natural resources like this? The reason for this is because of those who have run the country before. They have stolen, robbed, and sent the wealth of the people of this country abroad. In the last 15 years, 26 lakh crore taka has been smuggled out. First they sent the money, then they themselves fled. Those who have love for the country can never flee the country. 

He also said that the previous government killed 11 top leaders of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami one by one. They killed them in the name of judicial courts. Yet no one from Jamaat escaped. 

The Jamaat Ameer said that after August 5, everyone can speak freely. Earlier, people were in a culture of fear. After August 5, not only Jamaat-e-Islami but the entire people of Bangladesh achieved freedom with the liberation. 

Under the chairmanship of District Ameer Principal Anisur Rahman, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Rafiqul Islam, District Secretary General Dr. Muhaddis Enamul Haque, Birganj Upazila Ameer Azizur Rahman and others were present.

Headline_English: Each cigarette reduces life expectancy by 20 minutes: Research
Content_Enlish:
Each cigarette takes 20 minutes of life away from a person. Accordingly, a pack of cigarettes takes an average of seven hours away from a person's life. Such information has emerged in a recent University College London (UCL) study. 

Researchers have urged smokers to quit the habit in the new year after this new study on the harm of cigarettes. They say that smoking reduces life expectancy much faster than doctors have thought for a long time. 

According to this new analysis, if a smoker reduces his smoking to 10 cigarettes a day from January 1, then his life can increase by one day by January 8, one week by February 5 and a whole month by August 5. And if he maintains this habit for the whole year, his life can increase by 50 days by the end of the year. That is, he can avoid dying at least 50 days earlier. 

UCL Principal Research Fellow Dr. Sarah Jackson said that people do not know how harmful smoking is. A regular smoker loses about a decade of his life to smoking. 

A 2000 BMJ study found that a cigarette shortens life by an average of 11 minutes. However, a more recent analysis published in the Journal of Addiction found that this figure had almost doubled to 17 minutes for men and 22 minutes for women.

Headline_English: Government to prepare July coup declaration
Content_Enlish:
The interim government has taken an initiative to prepare a declaration of the July Revolution based on national consensus. The declaration will be adopted to consolidate the unity of the people, anti-fascist consciousness and desire for state reform that was developed through the July Revolution. 

The Chief Advisor's Press Secretary Shafiqul Alam gave this information at an emergency press conference in front of the State Guest House Jamuna on Monday night. 

Earlier, the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement announced on Facebook on Saturday that the 'July Revolution Declaration' would be released at the Central Shaheed Minar in the capital on December 31 (today). After this, Press Secretary Shafiqul Alam said on Sunday that the interim government has no involvement in the declaration of the July Revolution that will be announced by the students. The government wants to see it as a private initiative. 

Amidst various discussions and tensions across the country surrounding Tuesday's announcement, the interim government announced its initiative to prepare a declaration of the July Revolution last night. In a written statement at the press conference, Shafiqul Alam said, "The declaration will be prepared based on the opinions of all participating students, political parties and factions, including the anti-discrimination student movement that led the mass uprising. It will express the perspective of the July mass uprising, the basis of unity and the intentions of the people. We hope that through everyone's participation, this declaration will be prepared unanimously within a few days and presented to the nation."

Headline_English: The enthusiasm of youth will be awakened through songs: James
Content_Enlish:
The 'BPL T20 Music Fest 2025' was organized on Monday with the renowned singer of the subcontinent, Rahat Fateh Ali Khan, as the show stopper. After the capital Dhaka, the second part of this concert is going to be held in Sylhet today. Where the country's top band star James will perform as the show stopper. He will grace the stage today with the band Nagar Baul. 

James's comment on the 'BPL T20 Music Fest 2025' concert, BCB's organization with this conviction to build a youth festival in Bangladesh is certainly praiseworthy. Therefore, today the enthusiasm of the youth will be awakened through songs. 

Along with this top rock star of the country, there will also be performances by popular singer Asif Akbar and his band The A Team and three popular artists of this time, Tosiba Begum, Muja and Sanjay. The concert has been organized by Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) to make the upcoming edition of the country's popular franchise cricket league BPL more colorful. 

The organizers said that they have taken several initiatives to make this edition of the BPL more colorful. Today's music festival, organized with the slogan 'Come and change the country, change the world', is a part of it. The first phase of the 'BPL T20 Music Fest 2025' was organized at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur in the capital on Monday. Its second phase is going to be held today. After that, the third phase of the concert will be held in Chittagong. The first phase of this BPL music festival has received a great response from cricket and music fans. They are also hoping that today will be no exception in Sylhet. 

BCB President Farooq Ahmed said that this colorful music festival is being organized to spread the message of the upcoming BPLA to all levels. BCB is making every effort to make this year's BPL more lively through three colorful concerts courtesy of Madhumoti Bank. 

The organizers also said that the concert will start at 5:30 pm today at the Sylhet District Stadium. It will continue until night. Before that, the stadium gates will be opened for the audience at 2:30 pm. The gates will close at 5 pm. The audience can enjoy this event by purchasing tickets at a fixed price. 

Artist Asif Akbar said, 'I formed a connection with cricket in my youth. So like music, cricket has also influenced my life in many ways. These two things have been my path together. So it is a different feeling to be able to perform at the BPL concert. I believe that this event of BCB with the slogan 'Come and change the country, change the world' will be successful. At the same time, this colorful event and this year's edition of BPL will be memorable. 

Young artist Tosibar said, "Sylhet is my hometown. The thought of singing on the same stage with famous artists in that city fills my heart with a different feeling. So, I will try to make the event lively by playing the favorite songs of the audience."

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia to visit London in first half of January
Content_Enlish:
Finally, the date of BNP Chairperson Begum Khaleda Zia's foreign trip for better treatment is about to be fixed. If everything goes well, the former prime minister will go to London in the first half of January. 

On Wednesday afternoon, BNP Chairperson's personal physician and party standing committee member Dr. AZM Zahid Hossain gave this information. He said, 'Begum Khaleda Zia will go to London for treatment in the first half of January. The final date has not been decided yet.' 

Khaleda Zia was supposed to participate in the freedom fighter rally on December 21. However, the rally was postponed due to physical illness. 

BNP party sources say that Begum Khaleda Zia will be accompanied by a 15-member delegation including seven doctors. Among them are Syeda Sharmila Rahman, wife of Khaleda Zia's late younger son Arafat Rahman Koko, BNP Chairperson's personal physician Dr. AZM Zahid Hossain, Dr. Md. Enamul Haque Chowdhury, Tabith Mohammad Awal, Fakhruddin Mohammad Siddique, Md. Shahabuddin Talukder, Nuruddin Ahmad, Md. Zakir Iqbal, Mohammad Al Mamun, Sharifa Karim Swarna, Chairperson's personal officer ABM Abdus Sattar, Md. Masudur Rahman, SM Parvez, Fatema Begum and Rupa Sikder. 

Earlier, on October 29, Dr. Zahid Hossain had said that Khaleda Zia would first be taken to London in a 'Long Distance Specialized Air Ambulance' for advanced treatment. From there, she would be taken to a multidisciplinary medical center in a third country.

Headline_English: The number of dengue cases in the country has crossed one lakh.
Content_Enlish:
In the past 12 hours, 141 more people have been hospitalized due to dengue. This brings the number of patients admitted this year to 1029. As a result, the number of patients admitted to hospitals for dengue in Bangladesh has crossed 100,000 for the third time. 

Earlier, in 2023, a maximum of 321,179 people were hospitalized due to dengue and 101,354 patients were hospitalized in 2019. 

The Directorate General of Health Services has been keeping information on hospitalizations and deaths due to dengue since 2000. Of these, 321,179 people were hospitalized due to the disease in 2023. The highest number of deaths due to dengue was 1,705 that year. 

The number of dengue patients has been increasing since August this year. On August 20, the number of patients admitted to hospitals crossed 10,000. On September 24, the number of patients admitted to hospitals crossed 25,000. About a month later, on October 21, the number of patients admitted to hospitals crossed 50,000. The next 50,000 patients were hospitalized in the last two months. This number is increasing gradually.

Headline_English: Extortion has not stopped, only the extortionists have changed: Hasnat Abdullah
Content_Enlish:
Hasnat Abdullah, convener of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement, said that it is the responsibility of scholars and ulama to speak out on the overall issues of society. You should speak out against corruption and extortion in mosques. Extortion has not stopped in the country yet, only the extortionists have changed. Occupancy has not ended, only the occupants have changed. There is propaganda being spread that Hindus are being attacked in Bangladesh. The scholar community should be aware of this so that no one can incite conflict by inciting communal hatred. 

The Anti-Discrimination Student Movement organized this meeting at the Upazila Parishad Hallroom on Saturday afternoon. An exchange of views was held with scholars and ulama from Debidwar, Comilla. At this time, Hasnat Abdullah said that Bangladesh is traditionally a country of communal harmony. Those who are minorities are the safest in this country and we are the ones who can keep them the safest. 

Under the chairmanship of Upazila Executive Officer Nigar Sultana and moderated by Mufti Abdul Ahad, special guests included Debidwar Islamia Fazil Madrasa Principal Maulana Alauddin, Islamic Foundation Field Supervisor Tofazzal Hossain, Anti-Discrimination Student Movement Advisor Nazmul Hasan Nahid, Coordinator Muhtadir Zarif Sikta, Siam Ahmed, and others. 

In addition, Hasnat Abdullah held a series of meetings with student movement representatives from 15 unions and one municipality of the upazila at the same place. During this time, he discussed the urgent needs for corruption in various union councils, irregularities in the education and medical sectors, and construction and renovation of roads, bridges, and culverts.

Headline_English: Elon Musk supports Germany's far-right
Content_Enlish:
Elon Musk, the billionaire who is set to join US President-elect Donald Trump's administration, joined the German election campaign on Friday. He described the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party as the country's "savior." 

The European powerhouse will vote on February 23 after the fall of Chancellor Olaf Scholz's center-left coalition government. 

The AfD is in second place in opinion polls. But it could thwart a center-right or center-left majority. Germany's mainstream centrist parties have pledged not to support the AfD at the national level. "Only the AfD can save Germany," Musk wrote in a post on his social media platform, Platform X.

Headline_English: Holding early elections will benefit everyone: Rumin Farhana
Content_Enlish:
BNP's Joint International Affairs Secretary Barrister Rumin Farhana said, since August 5, various quarters have been busy conspiring. They are not willing to give this government a chance to run the country peacefully even for a day. From that point of view, we believe that no other government can deal with such instability or problems as easily as an elected government can. Therefore, a quick election will be beneficial for everyone. 

He said these things in an exchange of views with journalists at the Brahmanbaria Press Club on Tuesday. Rumin Farhana said, through the statement of the chief advisor, we initially got an idea of ​​when the election will be held. This is good news. However, we would have been more happy and assured if the roadmap had been made a little clearer. 

Commenting on the economic stagnation prevailing in the country, he said, domestic and foreign investment is not happening in that way. Because a stable environment is needed for investment. If you think about it from that perspective, there is no alternative to an elected government. 

Regarding the case trading, the BNP leader said, "Many people are being framed in cases due to previous enmity. I would like to request the administration, even if you take a case, do not rush to make arrests. Do some research, investigate. Then, if you find the truth, make arrests. 

At that time, party leaders and activists including various media workers working in the district, former district BNP president Hafizur Rahman Molla Kochi, former general secretary Zahirul Haque Khokon, former joint general secretary ABM Mominul Haque were present.

Headline_English: I want to see murderer Hasina on the gallows: Sarjis Alam
Content_Enlish:
Sarjis Alam, one of the coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, has commented that he wants to see the murderer Hasina hanged on the gallows in the country. He said, Victory Day, independence, constitution and the state can never be one person, it can never be one family. The murderer Hasina turned the state into an individual and a family. Because of this, she has had a farewell that no head of state in the world has had. It is doubtful whether any head of state will have one in the future. 

He said these things in his speech as the chief guest at the painting, writing and poetry recitation, exchange of views and award distribution ceremony organized on the occasion of the great Victory Day and the July-August mass uprising at the Five Star Field in Nilphamari on Tuesday afternoon. 

Sarjis Alam said, if votes can still be taken by putting a few hundred or a few thousand taka in one's pocket on the night before the election in this country, then nothing good can be expected from that state. If the people still decide to vote in exchange for money, then whoever the MP-minister is, they will exploit the people of the country. 

Addressing India, Sarjis Alam said, the relationship will be country to country. Not individual to individual or party to party. The people of Bangladesh are not anti-India, the people of Bangladesh are not anti-Indian. But the people of Bangladesh are anti-communal Modi. The extremist communal Modi has come to power in India on the blood of Muslims. If any party or any person dares to question the sovereignty of the state of Bangladesh at all, then we will resist him even at the cost of our lives. 

Stating that the fight is not over yet, he further said, if there is political division, everyone must unite for the sake of the country and the people of the country. No one should sell their conscience to a party or group. If any leader expects me to be a blind follower of Sheikh Hasina, then two things will happen, one, that leader's intentions are not good, two, that leader is shooting himself in the foot. 

At the end of his speech, he assured to take initiatives regarding the declaration of Syedpur as a full-fledged district. 

Student representative Javed Attari presided over the exchange of views. During this time, central co-coordinator Redwan Islam, Upazila Executive Officer Nur-e Alam Siddiqui, Upazila Assistant Commissioner (Land) Aminul Islam, Saidpur organizational district BNP president Abdul Gafur Sarkar, city Jamaat Amir Sharfuddin Khan, Shaheed Sajjad Hossain's father Alamgir Hossain spoke. The program was hosted by student representative Shakib Khan. Finally, the crest and certificate were handed over to the winner on July 36.

Headline_English: Debapriya becomes member of UN CDP for the third time
Content_Enlish:
Dr. Debapriya Bhattacharya has been appointed as a member of the UN Committee for Development Policy (CDP) for another three years. This marks his third consecutive term as a member of the UN CDP. Dr. Debapriya Bhattacharya is an Honorary Fellow of the Center for Policy Dialogue (CPD) and the Convener of the Citizens' Platform for SDC Implementation, Bangladesh. He is the Head of the White Paper Preparation Committee on the Economy of the Interim Government. 
This information was given in a press release by the Center for Policy Dialogue on Tuesday. It said that Dr. Debapriya Bhattacharya will serve as a member of the UN CDP for the third time from January 1 next year. The UN Secretary-General has nominated Debapriya Bhattacharya for reappointment to this position. Dr. Debapriya Bhattacharya has been serving as a member of the UN CDP since 2018. 
The CDP reviews the list of least developed countries (LDCs) once every three years. The committee makes recommendations to ECOSOC and the UN General Assembly on inclusion and graduation based on set criteria. The new CDP committee will, among other things, review Bangladesh's graduation from LDC status in December 2026.

Headline_English: Imran Khan's interim bail extended
Content_Enlish:
The interim bail of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibri in multiple cases has been extended until January 7. An Islamabad court gave the verdict after hearing one case of Bushra and six of Imran on Tuesday. However, Imran is not being released from prison immediately as he has more cases against him. 

Imran Khan's party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, had held a long march in the capital Islamabad last November demanding his release. On November 26, the workers and supporters reached D-Chowk, the most important place in Islamabad, but the party abruptly suspended the program that night due to a raid by law enforcement agencies. Later, PTI said that direct fire was fired at their workers. At least 12 people were killed in this. However, they are planning to hold a new program again. 

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister and one of the most influential PTI leaders, Ali Amin Gandapur, said yesterday that they will start a non-cooperation movement if Imran Khan gives the order. 

He told reporters in Peshawar that they are ready to implement the new program. The program will start as soon as the party chief gives instructions. 

Gandapur also said that he went to Adiala Jail to meet Imran Khan. But he was not allowed to enter there and did not meet him. 

Imran Khan lost the prime ministership in 2022 after losing the confidence vote in the National Assembly. After that, one case after another was filed against him. On May 9, 2023, he was arrested in the Al Qadir Trust corruption case. He has been living in prison since that day. 
On the other hand, his wife Bushra Bibi was arrested but has been released on bail. She led the PTI's Islamabad long march last month. Bushra had said that she would return home only after Imran was released from prison. But after the party abruptly withdrew the program, she also left.

Headline_English: What Aamir Khan said about quitting acting
Content_Enlish:
After four decades in Bollywood, Bollywood superstar Aamir Khan decided to quit acting during the Corona pandemic. However, his family, including his two children, finally convinced him not to retire from acting. 

Regarding retirement, Aamir Khan said, "I have it in my head that I have retired but I have not retired. So I still have to continue acting." 

France24.com has published a news report quoting the news agency London AFP. There, Aamir Khan said, "In the midst of Corona, I was thinking a lot. Then suddenly I felt that I had spent half of my life in this magical world of films. I felt that I had lost all my time working in this world. I could not accept this thought. I was going through a sense of guilt. Then I felt that enough was enough, I will not act anymore." 

Aamir turned 60 in March this year. He is currently based in Mumbai, India. He has decided to continue acting and producing for some time. 

He is working with his company Aamir Khan Productions. That is why Aamir said that he will work with Salman and Shah Rukh Khan in a movie together this month. 

Mr. Perfectionist said that he had discussed the new film with Salman and Shah Rukh. I met Salman and Shah Rukh six months ago. Then we discussed this. We really need to do a film together. We are in discussions. Let's see how far it goes! 

His film career started in 1970 as a child actor. After that, he won the hearts of fans one after another with his acting skills.

Headline_English: Badshah opens up about being fined Tk 15,000
Content_Enlish:
Bollywood's popular rapper Badshah has been in trouble one after another for the past few years. A few days ago, he got into legal trouble over his music video 'Baola'. This time, the singer has been fined for violating traffic laws. However, Badshah has denied the matter. He claims that he has not been fined. 

The allegation against Badshah is that on Sunday night, he was driving a Mahindra Thar to attend a concert by singer Karan Aujla in Gurugram. To save time, Badshah started driving in the opposite direction. At that time, the traffic stopped him and fined him Rs 15,500. There were 3 other cars with Badshah's car. They also had to pay a fine. 

A video has gone viral on social media. After that, there was a storm of criticism against the singer. 

The rapper has completely denied the traffic violation allegations against Badshah and the fine. He has also issued a statement in this regard. 

His statement is, 'I do not own a Thar car. Besides, I was in a white car that day. I don't drive myself, but I drive carefully. Be it video games or the road, I am always aware.' Source: Hindustan Times.

Headline_English: US welcomes interim government's plan for elections
Content_Enlish:
The United States has welcomed the various steps taken by the interim government in Bangladesh around the upcoming parliamentary elections. The US State Department's Principal Deputy Spokesperson Vedant Patel said this at a regular press briefing on Wednesday local time. 

The question of imposing US sanctions on former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina for her involvement in various crimes including disappearances was also raised in today's briefing. The US has supported the investigation into Hasina's involvement in disappearances. 

Washington has also expressed its reaction on the security issue of minorities in Bangladesh. 

At today's briefing, a journalist wanted to know the US position on the recent announcement of the possible date of the national elections in Bangladesh. He said that the Bangladesh government has announced that they will probably organize the elections in late 2025 or early 2026. What is the US position on this? 

In response, US State Department Principal Deputy Spokesperson Vedant Patel said that we welcome the steps taken by the interim government of Bangladesh to prepare for the elections, which will ultimately give the Bangladeshi people the opportunity to choose their own leadership. 

He further said, the timing of the elections is an issue that we will continue to monitor. Of course, we encourage the implementation of the rule of law, as well as democratic principles, throughout this entire process. And as we want the whole world - our position is in favor of holding free and fair elections in a peaceful manner. 

In another question, the journalist questioned the involvement of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in the disappearance and the imposition of sanctions against her. He said, the New York Times has published a report on the disappearance citing the report of the Commission of Inquiry in Bangladesh. The Commission of Inquiry has found evidence of the involvement of the former Prime Minister in the disappearance. The United States has previously imposed sanctions against those involved in the disappearance in Bangladesh. What is your comment on this? 

In response, Vedant Patel said, we are deeply concerned about reports that hundreds of Bangladeshis have been forcibly disappeared in the last two decades. Enforced disappearance is a serious human rights violation that causes trauma or mental anguish to the victims, such as being detained or disappeared for an indefinite period of time. It creates a trauma of uncertainty on their families. We welcome the efforts of the interim government to investigate this crime and encourage a fair and transparent process to ensure justice for the victims and their family members. 

Later, a questioner asked about the alleged persecution of minorities in Bangladesh and their protests. In response, Vedant Patel said, of course this is an issue that is important to us. Wherever we are in the country, we want to ensure that the protests are peaceful, that the fundamental human rights and human dignity of all people are respected. This is an issue that we attach importance to with all countries and governments and partners around the world. In the case of Bangladesh, we certainly feel the same with the interim government. 

The questioner also wanted to know what was discussed in the last meeting between Indian Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar and US Secretary of State Antony Blinken at the G-7 summit last November and whether there was any discussion there about the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh. 

In response, the Principal Deputy Spokesperson of the US State Department said, we certainly had discussions on a wide range of issues. We have a close partnership with our counterparts in India. Of course, there are security issues, trade issues, and of course there are consular issues, including visas. We have already reported on that meeting with Jaishankar in the readout.

Headline_English: Political parties trying to prove interim government a failure: Nahid
Content_Enlish:
Information and Broadcasting Advisor Md. Nahid Islam said that political parties want reforms to be implemented under them. Therefore, they are trying to prove the interim government a failure. The parties are giving more priority to elections instead of reforms. 

A press release from the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology on Wednesday said that the advisor made these remarks during a meeting with a delegation from the British Global Partners Governance (GPG) at the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday. Nahid Islam made these remarks when former Chilean Social Development Minister Jorge Jackson, a member of the delegation, asked about reforms and elections. 

When Foreign Commonwealth and Development Officer Matt Charter expressed his interest in cooperation, Nahid Islam said that experience and advice were needed on the post-coup democratic process and genocide trials. 

When asked about the challenges of the interim government by former Scottish Parliament member Lord Jeremy Purvis, the advisor said that the main challenge of the government is to advance the law and order situation, economic problems, and reform activities based on compromise with political parties and to establish global communication. 

Nahid Islam said that various propaganda is being spread internationally. Many people are not able to properly explain the mass uprising. People are not able to understand how such a big dictator fell in such a short time. As a result, various conspiracies are being carried out inside and outside the country. Propaganda is also being spread about the oppression of minorities. Many are trying to deny that this movement is a democratic uprising. 

He also said that there has been a human rights crisis in Bangladesh for a long time. People could not vote, thousands of people have been disappeared. People were in a suffocating situation. Therefore, protecting human rights is one of the main goals of the interim government.

Headline_English: Committee to review dearness allowance for government employees
Content_Enlish:
A committee has been formed to review the issue of providing 'Dearness Allowance' to the officers and employees covered by the National Pay Scale 2015. The government has formed a 7-member committee with the Principal Secretary to the Chief Advisor as the convener. 

On Thursday, an office order was issued by the Finance Department, Regulations Sub-Division, Regulations-3 Branch, to form a committee in this regard. This committee has been formed to review the issue of providing 'Dearness Allowance' in favor of the officers and employees covered by the National Pay Scale, 2015, employed by the Bangladesh Government. This information was mentioned in the order signed by Deputy Secretary Syed Ali Bin Hasan. 

The Principal Secretary to the Chief Advisor has been made the convener of the committee. The members are - Senior Secretary of the Ministry of Public Administration, Auditor General and Controller, Secretary of the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance, Secretary of the Office of the Chief Advisor, Secretary of the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division and the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs and Additional Secretary of the Regulations Division of the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance. 

The terms of reference of the committee state that the committee will review the applicability and availability of dearness allowance and submit necessary recommendations. The committee can co-opt one or more officers if necessary.

Headline_English: ISIS claims responsibility for killing Taliban minister Haqqani
Content_Enlish:
The Islamic State group (IS) has claimed responsibility for the assassination of Haji Khalilur Rahman Haqqani, the Afghan Taliban government's refugee minister. The incident took place inside the interior ministry on Wednesday. 

Afghanistan's Amu TV reported this information in a report on Thursday. 

The report said that this is the first time that a top-level leader has been killed since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021. 

The Interior Ministry said that the attack was carried out shortly before Haqqani left his office. Six others were killed in the incident. 

A CNN report said that a ministry spokesman said that the attacker entered the refugee ministry premises posing as a guest. The attacker detonated the bomb while Khalil Haqqani was signing official documents. 

After the US completely withdrew its troops in 2021, the Taliban took complete control of Afghanistan. Since then, security has improved under the Taliban government, which previously saw dozens of bombings and suicide attacks every year.

Headline_English: Discussions underway to return Bangladeshi fishermen detained in India: Foreign Secretary
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh government has started discussions to bring back 79 Bangladeshi fishermen and sailors detained in Paradip, Odisha state, India. They can be brought back soon through discussions. 

Foreign Secretary Md. Jasim Uddin said these things at a press conference at the ministry today, Thursday. He spoke to reporters at a briefing on the upcoming visit of East Timor President Jose Ramos Horta at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs this evening. He is coming to Dhaka after a decade on December 15. 

In response to a question, the Foreign Secretary told Samakal that Bangladesh has contacted India regarding this. Discussions are underway to bring back the Bangladeshis who are detained. He hopes that they can be brought back soon through discussions. 

Meanwhile, a statement from the Indian Coast Guard said that the fishermen along with the FV Laila-2 and FV Meghna-5 trawlers were detained from IMBL last Wednesday during the Coast Guard's regular surveillance. After bringing them to Paradip in Odisha, they were interrogated separately by the Indian Coast Guard, the Crime Branch and the Intelligence Branch of the police. 

A detained Bangladeshi fisherman told reporters in Odisha, "We had mistakenly entered Indian waters." There are 100 tons of fish in the two ships. It is worth one crore taka. Another Bangladeshi fisherman said, "Food, drinks and accommodation have been arranged here." 

On Monday afternoon, the Indian Coast Guard seized two fishing vessels named FV Meghna-5 and FV Laila-2 along with 78 sailors from Indian waters near Hiran Point in Khulna. The two vessels were engaged in deep-sea fishing. There were 37 fishermen and sailors in Meghna and 41 in Laila.

Headline_English: Stock market falls for six consecutive days
Content_Enlish:
The share price of listed Orion Infusion Company has increased significantly in the last two days after imposing a large fine on the family members of the entrepreneurs and directors for stock price manipulation. The price increased by 10 percent in two days as per the closing price. However, considering the lowest price on Wednesday, it has increased by more than 20 percent. 
The share price increased from only 80 to 987 taka between June 21 and October 12, 2022. Based on the investigation conducted in the case of abnormal price increase, the regulatory body BSEC decided to fine Beacon Pharma MD Ebadul Karim Tk 13.15 crore and 9 individuals and institutions including his family members Tk 60.21 crore on Tuesday. 
The review showed that the share was traded at a minimum of Tk 265 on Wednesday after the fine was imposed. However, the price suddenly increased during the transaction on that day and the highest was traded at Tk 300. Trading started at Tk 320 yesterday. However, due to the pressure of selling shares, some shares were traded below Tk 300 in the first half hour. However, due to the pressure of buying again, they rose to the highest price of the day. Even in the last three hours of the four and a half hour trading, there was no seller. Someone has aggressively bought shares and increased the price - this is the impression from the officials of some brokerage houses. 
Although the overall trading in the Dhaka stock market has decreased for a few days, the trading has increased by Tk 47 crore to Tk 351 crore 59 lakh compared to Wednesday. In this case too, the trading of Orion Infusion had the greatest impact. A total of Tk 83 crore 64 lakh shares of this company were traded yesterday, which is about 24 percent of the total trading. Of this, Tk 16 crore 89 lakh shares were traded in the main or public market and Tk 66 crore 76 lakh shares were traded in the block market. 
Apart from Orion Infusion, shares of three other companies were traded at the highest price set by the circuit breaker of the day yesterday - Associated Oxygen, Emerald Oil and Metro Spinning. The prices of these shares increased by 9.5 to almost 10 percent. 
Although the share prices of a few companies increased significantly, most of the companies lost their share prices for the sixth consecutive day. Out of the 397 shares and mutual funds listed on the DSE today, 391 were traded more or less. Of these, 102 increased their prices, 196 decreased their prices and 91 remained unchanged. 
As the share prices of most companies decreased, the main price index DSEX lost 19 points to 5105 points. The index has lost about 133 points in the last six days.

Headline_English: Fireworks and lanterns banned on 31st night: DMP
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has said that flawless security measures will be taken around Christmas, the biggest religious festival of Christians. In addition, bursting of fireworks and crackers in open places and flying lanterns will be completely prohibited on the 31st Night. 

This decision was announced at the DMP's security, law and order and traffic management coordination meeting on the occasion of Christmas and the 31st Night celebrations held at the DMP headquarters today, Thursday. 

At the beginning of the meeting, chaired by DMP Commissioner Sheikh Md. Sajjat ​​Ali, DMP Joint Commissioner (Operations) Mohammad Shahidullah presented the security plan taken on the occasion of Christmas and the 31st Night celebrations through a power point presentation. 

On the occasion of Christmas, an adequate number of police personnel in uniform and plain clothes will be deployed in each church. Visitors will have to enter each church through an archway, and will also be searched manually with metal detectors. The venue will be swept by a dog squad. In addition, there will be fire service and ambulance security. There will be uninterrupted power supply in the church area. No floating shops or hawkers will be allowed to sit in the church area and no bags will be allowed to enter the church. 

Regular patrols and check posts will be increased on the occasion of the Thirty-First Night celebration. In addition, police activity will be increased. Fireworks, crackers and lanterns will be completely prohibited in any open place. No one will be allowed to enter the Dhaka University area without an identity card and traffic will be controlled. Integrated traffic arrangements will be taken in the Gulshan and Hatirjheel areas. In addition, intelligence surveillance will be increased on the occasion of the two festivals. DMP will strengthen cyber patrolling and monitor social media to prevent rumors and propaganda. 

Representatives from various intelligence agencies, armed forces, Dhaka University administration, Dhaka North and South City Corporations, Dhaka WASA, DPDC, Fire Service and various government service organizations presented their opinions and suggestions in the meeting. The DMP Commissioner sought the full cooperation of the city residents to complete the Christmas and Thirty First Night celebrations peacefully.

Headline_English: Former South Korean defense minister arrested
Content_Enlish:
South Korea's former defense minister Kim Yong-hoon has been arrested. President Yun Suk-yul imposed martial law on Tuesday, prompting prosecutors to arrest Kim on suspicion of involvement in the move. 

President Yun's martial law lasted only a few hours. A day later, Kim announced his resignation under pressure. On Saturday, an attempt was made to impeach Yun in parliament. However, the attempt failed when no members of his party, the People's Party, voted to impeach him. 

Even if he survives impeachment, many analysts believe Yun will not be able to stay in power for long. The Guardian.

Headline_English: The next election will be the most difficult and competitive: Tarique Rahman
Content_Enlish:
BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman has said that the next election will be the most difficult and competitive for the nation. He said, ‘During the tenure of the fallen government, the people could not exercise their right to vote. After a long time, they will get the opportunity to exercise their right to vote again.’ 

He said these things while addressing the chief guest while joining the video conference at the BNP’s 31-point day-long departmental workshop organized at the Rangpur District Shilpakala Academy auditorium on Sunday afternoon. 

Tarique Rahman said, ‘The autocrat has been in power in various ways for the past 15 years, trying to build many things by looting people’s money and resources. People have hated them and returned them. We have to remember this. As a political party worker, the biggest capital is the trust, faith and love of the people. Those who remained in power forcibly for 15 years are no more. The reason is that they have lost the trust, faith and love of the people. That is why they have been forced to flee the country. 

Stating that the nation must unite regardless of party affiliation to build the country, he said, "If everyone forms the government together, everyone will be able to speak for everyone's rights. Democracy will be stronger. The trust that the people have in BNP must be maintained. Everyone must be vigilant in this regard. They cannot get involved in conflicts among themselves in any way. For this, leaders and activists of BNP at all levels must remain united and stand by the people like in the past. They must be aware and diligent in ensuring that the trust of the people is not damaged." 

The acting chairman of BNP further said, "The anti-dictatorship movement did not succeed with the BNP's single movement. The movement was successful because people from different political parties and all classes came forward. If the country is to be rebuilt, the nation must be united regardless of party affiliation." 

Addressing the leaders and activists of his party, he said, "We want to rebuild the country in the light of the 31-point plan. The people of the country have trust in BNP. We must maintain that trust. I can't do it alone. Party leaders and activists have to listen to the grassroots level people. Everyone has to maintain the trust of the people from their own position. The party's 31 points have to be delivered to every house. These 31 points are not only of BNP, but many democratic political parties have opinions on them. We have fought against dictatorship for 15 years. The source of all power is the people. So stay with the people, keep the people with you. It is not possible to come to power without the people in any way.' 

BNP's Rangpur Divisional Organizing Secretary Principal Asadul Habib Dulu presided over the workshop, and BNP Media Cell Head Professor Dr. Moudud Hossain Alamgir Pavel provided training on the 31 points. BNP Publicity Secretary Sultan Salauddin Tuku, Rangpur Divisional Co-Organizing Secretary Abdul Khalek, BNP Media Cell member Farzana Sharmin Putul, among others, spoke at the workshop.

Headline_English: Dhaka-Delhi Foreign Secretary-level meeting today
Content_Enlish:
The Foreign Secretary-level meeting of Foreign Office Consultation (FOC) between Bangladesh and India will be held in Dhaka today, Monday. Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Mishri is coming to Bangladesh on a short visit with a delegation to attend it. 

The Bangladesh delegation at the FOC will be led by Foreign Secretary Jasim Uddin. While the Indian delegation will be led by Vikram Mishri. Vikram Mishri is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka around 9 am today, Monday. The meeting will be held around 11 am. 

After the meeting, the Bangladesh Foreign Ministry has organized a lunch in honor of the Indian Foreign Secretary. Then, at around 3:30 pm, Vikram will meet with Foreign Affairs Advisor Md. Towhid Hossain. Later, after a courtesy call on Principal Advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus, he will leave Dhaka. 

The FOC is usually held once a year. One year, it is held in Dhaka, the next year, it is held in New Delhi. However, last year it was held twice. The first time was held in Dhaka on February 15. Later, on November 24 of the same year, the FOC was held in New Delhi. It was held twice, mainly considering the general elections in Bangladesh and India in 2024. 

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that the meeting is likely to discuss issues such as trade, borders, connectivity, water sharing, as well as recent issues. In addition, regional, sub-regional and global issues will be discussed. There will be a message from Dhaka to normalize relations and move forward. Bangladesh is expecting a similar message from India.

Headline_English: Trump announces end to birthright citizenship in the United States
Content_Enlish:
The country's newly elected President Donald Trump has announced the abolition of the law that granted citizenship to those born in the United States. The British media outlet BBC reported this information in a report on Monday. 

In an interview with NBC, Trump said that he plans to abolish the so-called birthright citizenship provision through an executive order. He also said that on his first day in office, he would look into pardoning those involved in the Capitol Hill riots in 2021. 

In response to a question about whether he would want to pardon the hundreds of people convicted of involvement in that riot, Trump said, "These people are going through hell. We will look at the cases. Yes, I am going to take action very quickly. And that on the first day." 

Meanwhile, under the citizenship policy, anyone born in the United States receives a US passport and citizenship even if their parents were born in another country. The provision of birthright citizenship is guaranteed in the 14th Amendment to the US Constitution. 

The amendment states that “all persons born in the United States are citizens of the United States.” Trump says, “This rule must be changed.” However, US immigration lawyers say that Trump’s move would be against the US Constitution and, if it is really implemented after taking office, it will lead to serious violations of the Constitution. 

Although he has promised to end the process of obtaining citizenship for those born in the United States, he has expressed his willingness to work with Democrats to help some undocumented immigrants who were brought to the United States as children. 

In this extensive recorded interview, Trump also said that after taking office as president on January 20, he has promised to issue “many” executive orders, including on immigration, energy and the economy. 

This is the first interview with a broadcast network by the former Republican president since winning the election last November.
