Headline_English: People of the country must remain united to stop Awami fascism: Dulu
Content_Enlish:

Murderer Hasina and her party Awami League carried out the killings in Peelkhana in the name of BDR rebellion, massacred the Hefajat mass gathering at Shapla Chattar, and brutally killed about two thousand people by shooting indiscriminately at students and the public during the July Revolution.

Headline_English: 50 cricketers declare rebellion against the board!
Content_Enlish:
Fifty English cricketers have threatened to boycott the 2025 ‘The Hundred’ tournament in protest against the England and Wales Cricket Board’s (ECB) new no-objection certificate (AOC) policy, the Telegraph reports. 

According to the England Cricket Board’s (ECB) rules, if a county team has a contract to play red-ball cricket, they will not be given permission to play in foreign T20 leagues. That is, if there is a T20 league in another country during county cricket (first-class domestic cricket in England), then English cricketers will have to play red-ball cricket. Also, if there is a league in another country during the Hundred, even if there is a league in another country, no permission will be given. Those cricketers who have a contract to play only white-ball with their county team will be exempted. 

If the ECB follows this rule, English cricketers will not be allowed to play in many foreign leagues. Leagues like Major Cricket League, Canada's Global T20 League, Sri Lanka Premier League, Caribbean Premier League can be county time. However, this rule has been relaxed for IPL, which has created anger among cricketers. That is, if you want to play IPL without playing county, the ECB will give permission. 

British media 'The Telegraph' reported that 50 top English cricketers are thinking of boycotting the upcoming Hundred tournament. Which is being called - a rebellion against the ECB's decision not to issue NOC or no objection certificate to go to foreign franchise tournaments. However, the Telegraph did not reveal who the 50 cricketers are. It is also not known whether any cricketer who has played Tests for England is among these 50. 

If the cricketers take such a decision, the ECB will be in trouble. Because changes are expected to be made to next year's Hundred. The board wanted to sell shares of eight teams. It was heard that IPL teams may also show interest there. The board will be in trouble if it doesn't have 50 cricketers.

Headline_English: Protest at DU against attack on Assistant High Commission in Agartala

We want to make it clear that we will play with India on an equal footing. There will be no king-subject relationship. We will not accept India's dominance as long as we have a drop of blood in our bodies." 

Torch procession by the Student Rights Council 

The Student Rights Council held a torch procession in the same incident. The procession started in front of the university's Madhur Canteen on Monday night and ended at Raju Bhaskar.

Student Rights Council President Bin Yamin Mollah said, India had sided with Awami League before the elections. Now they have given place to their allies including Sheikh Hasina. He said, we now have to fight on two fronts. On one hand, against Awami League's allies and on the other hand, against India's extremist Hindutvaists. We have repeatedly said, ban Awami League. But the government has not done so. 

Addressing Mamata Banerjee, he said, "You are putting oil in your own wheel. Minorities are being tortured in your country. Ensure their security. Don't meddle in Bangladesh's internal affairs. I also want to ask whether you are ethnically united or not." 

Addressing the government, Bin Yamin Mollah said, "We wanted a revolutionary government, so how was such a government formed? We can see that those who have become leaders from the front lines of the movement and the advisors are not in agreement."

Headline_English: Martial law declared in South Korea
Content_Enlish:
South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol has declared a state of emergency and imposed martial law. This is the first time martial law has been imposed in South Korea since 1980.

He made the announcement in a speech to the nation broadcast on state television channel YTN late on Tuesday. According to BBC and Reuters.

In the televised speech, he said, "We will rebuild a liberal and democratic South Korea to eliminate the threat of North Korea's communist forces and anti-state elements. This is an inevitable step to ensure the freedom and security of the people and maintain the stability of the state."

President Yoon said that the opposition party, without caring about the people's lives and livelihoods, has crippled the governance system just to protect their leader from impeachment, special investigations and trial.

Yoon said, "Our parliament has now become a haven for criminals. It has become a law-making autocratic center that is trying to overturn our liberal democratic order. The country has been turned into a drug haven and a state of public insecurity by cutting budgets for key sectors such as combating drug crimes and maintaining public safety.

President Yoon accused opposition lawmakers of cutting budgets essential to the state's main activities. He said, "I will eliminate anti-state forces as soon as possible and return the country to normal."

Meanwhile, Yonhap News Agency quoted the country's military as saying that the activities of parliament and political parties in South Korea will be banned, and the media and publishers will be under the control of martial law commands.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on South Korea's martial law, according to the British news agency Reuters.

Incidentally, Yoon has been at odds with the opposition-controlled parliament since taking office as president in 2022. The ongoing stalemate over next year's budget bill between the opposition Democratic Party and the ruling People Power Party has further heightened tensions.

Headline_English: India's ruling class and Hindutva forces do not want harmony: Nahid Islam
Content_Enlish:

These democracy-loving people of India are our friends. However, the ruling class and Hindutva forces in India do not want such democratic relations and harmony. They see the uprising in Bangladesh and the political awakening of its students as a threat. As a result, they are harboring hatred against Bangladesh. 

On Tuesday, he posted a related post on his verified page on social media X. There, he mentioned that Bangladesh has historical and cultural relations with West Bengal, Tripura and Assam. However, by using the term 'minority oppression', Delhi is trying to rehabilitate the fascist Awami League and disrupt the democratic and nation-building process of Bangladesh. 

The information advisor further said, ‘From the beginning, we have been insisting that the Indian government should stop looking at Bangladesh through the eyes of the Awami League and establish a new relationship based on justice, fairness and mutual respect. The Bangladesh government is committed to ensuring full citizenship rights, dignity and security for all minority communities, including Hindus. Even during the Awami League’s tenure, minorities faced the highest level of oppression, yet Delhi unconditionally supported the Awami League. Although India has failed to ensure the rights of minorities in its own country. It has given shelter and support to the Awami League, a party that oppresses minorities in Bangladesh. 



He further said that by continuing to shelter and provide continuous support to the fugitive Sheikh Hasina, who is responsible for genocide and child murder, the Indian government is at risk of undermining democratic values. It should not be forgotten that the stability and integrity of India is inextricably linked to the stability and integrity of Bangladesh. 

Information Advisor Nahid said, "The ruling BJP is trying to make Bangladesh an internal political issue in India. If this happens, it will be harmful for India's internal politics. Anti-Bangladesh and anti-Muslim politics will not work in India's national interest. Therefore, we call on India to stop spreading lies and propaganda against Bangladesh and maintain harmony and respect for democracy."

Headline_English: Former Chhatra League secretary seeks justice from interim government
Content_Enlish:
Former Chhatra League general secretary and DUCSU GS Golam Rabbani has demanded justice from the interim government. In a post on his verified Facebook ID at 10:30 pm on Friday (November 29), the former Chhatra League general secretary demanded a fair investigation into various types of activities and corruption allegations against him. 

Golam Rabbani wrote, 'Since the beginning of my political journey, I have supported any just demand, regardless of party affiliation, and protested against corruption and irregularities to the best of my ability. I have tried to increase the reputation and public support of the party through my actions and conduct.' 

Stating that I have not received justice from my own party either, he said, 'The party for which I have wasted the best part of my life and youth, for the cherished ideals, and taken hundreds of risks, is the source of extreme injustice from that party, the frustration and suffering of not getting the justice I deserve despite repeatedly crying out, only the victim of injustice can understand!' 

Regarding former VC Farzana of JA, Rabbani wrote, 'To hide the corruption and irregularities of myself and my family, I have made unsubstantiated accusations against former VC Farzana Madam, a proven corruptor of Jahangirnagar University. In a media trial planned by fabricated verbal allegations and a conspiracy of some self-interested people, without getting the 'minimum opportunity to defend oneself' against the allegations brought, I had to resign from my post before the stipulated time. That resignation letter was also fabricated using your name under the guise of deceit!' 

He further said, 'Now the Awami League is not in power. Therefore, I strongly demand our acquittal and bringing the corrupt Farzana to justice through an influence-free and fair investigation. Against whom, the administration of Jahangirnagar University, including students and teachers, has hundreds of thousands of evidence of irregularities and corruption, including audit objections of 66 crore taka, taking commission of 29 crore taka in development work. 

In the post, Golam Rabbani challenged the government and wrote, "In the adverse situation that has arisen, there is full opportunity for impartial verification of the current responsible persons, so I am unequivocally challenging you - in the long time the party has been in power, I have not made any tender for any work or financial benefits from any ministry, government or private office in Bangladesh till today. No former or current MP, minister, bureaucrat or anyone else can say that Golam Rabbani has ever taken any work or financial benefits from them!" 

He wrote, "While leading the Chhatra League, I did not even drink 1 cup of tea from anyone in exchange for a position in the central committee or any organizational unit committee, God willing. Despite receiving many lucrative offers from MPs, ministers, leaders, and businessmen for various committees and positions, I have humbly turned them down. I do not have any property, plot, or flat of my own. Despite having the opportunity, I have never even applied for a government plot or flat by following others. Having no alternative means of earning, I have been working in a private sector job (salary stopped since last July) despite being at the top of the Chhatra League and working for helpless people regardless of party affiliation with my own halal earnings, and even being unable to financially organize my own wedding ceremony. I have had to get the label of 'corrupt' in the false conspiracy of the 'corrupt' members of my own party, Alas Selucas!'' 

He said, 'As an aggrieved victim with good reason, I want justice and redress for the injustice done to me, subject to a fair investigation.''

Headline_English: Former minister Asaduzzaman Noor attacked in hospital
Content_Enlish:
Former Cultural Affairs Minister Asaduzzaman Noor was attacked. He was taken to Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) Hospital for treatment on Saturday afternoon when he was attacked. 

Eyewitnesses said that some people injured in the anti-discrimination movement attacked him when he was taken to the hospital for treatment. 

After the fall of the Awami League government, police arrested former Cultural Affairs Minister Asaduzzaman Noor from Nauratan Colony on Bailey Road on September 16. He has been in jail since then. 

Noor has been an Awami League MP in parliament since 2001. In the last 12th national election, he was elected as a member of parliament from Nilphamari-2 constituency. 

He served as the Minister of Culture from January 13, 2014 to January 7, 2019.

Headline_English: This time, Pagla Mosque received a record amount of 8 crore 21 lakh taka.
Content_Enlish:
The traditional Pagla Mosque in Kishoreganj city has received 8 crore 21 lakh 34 thousand 304 taka this time. This is the highest amount of money counted as donations in the mosque so far. 

Administrative officer of Pagla Mosque Shawkat Uddin Bhuiyan informed this information. Earlier, 7 crore 22 lakh 13 thousand 46 taka was received on August 17. 

The counting started at 7 taka this Saturday morning and ended at 6 pm. This time, 11 donation boxes were opened and 29 bags of taka were found. Foreign currencies, gold and silver ornaments, and several letters and coins were also found in the donation boxes. 

This morning, the donation boxes were opened in the presence of the president of the mosque committee, Deputy Commissioner Fauzia Khan, Superintendent of Police Md. Hasan Chowdhury and other officials. Then the money was filled in synthetic bags and poured on the second floor of the mosque and the counting started under the supervision of the mosque committee and administration. The donation boxes are opened every three months. However, this time it was opened after three months and 13 days. 

128 students of Nurul Quran Hafiziya Madasa, 35 teachers and staff of Pagla Mosque Complex, 150 students of Al Jamiatul Imdadia, 75 staff of Rupali Bank participated in the money counting. The young and old students enjoyed counting such a huge amount of money. Sometimes they expressed their joy by throwing the money into the void. One student showed that someone had given a bundle of 500 taka notes pinned to the bank (50 thousand taka). 

Along with the local currency, several foreign currencies and gold and silver ornaments were also found. Some also donated bundles of 500 taka notes (50 thousand taka). Many letters and notes expressing the desire to fulfill their wishes were also found. 9 officials of the administration cadre, 10 army members, 16 police members and 9 Ansar members are in charge of overall supervision and security. Between the counting, the money was sent to Rupali Bank with the permission of the administration.

Headline_English: Foreign students ordered to return before Trump's inauguration
Content_Enlish:
Newly elected US President Donald Trump will be sworn in on January 20. Before that, the country's universities have instructed their foreign students to return to campus. Because the Trump administration may issue new instructions on higher education and immigration policies. This may put students and workers outside the United States in danger. News from NDTV 

Trump has already announced that he will issue several executive orders on economic and immigration issues once in power. Earlier, Trump took a tough stance on immigration policy for the first time in power. Even a travel ban was issued in the country. 

According to the US Department of State, Educational and Cultural Bureau and the Institute of International Education, 54 percent of the total foreign students in the United States are from India and China. In the 2023-24 session, there are 3 lakh 31 thousand 602 Indian students in the United States. And there are 2 lakh 77 thousand 398 Chinese students. 

David Elwell, director of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Office of International Students, expressed concern on social media that the Trump administration's policy could affect the travel and visa processes of foreign students. Therefore, students who are outside the United States during winter break should return to campus quickly. Because the new policy may delay the visa process. The Office of Global Affairs at the University of Massachusetts has also given the same advice. They said that it would be safest for students to be present in the United States before Trump's inauguration. 

Former US President Donald Trump gave a message to tighten immigration policies during the election campaign. He hinted at imposing restrictions on the border. If immigration policies are tightened, people from many countries, including Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan, could face problems. During the campaign, Trump said that he would use the military to catch immigrants who do not have legal documents. If this happens, it would be clearly unprecedented.

Headline_English: No need to intervene to ban ISKCON
Content_Enlish:
The High Court has expressed satisfaction with the activities of the law enforcement agencies in the murder of lawyer Saiful Islam Alif in Chittagong, focusing on the arrest and presentation to the court of Sammilit Sanatani Jagran Jote spokesperson Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari. In this context, the High Court said, we are assured that the state is giving utmost importance to this. This is their responsibility. We hope that everyone will be assured after hearing this. We want that there should be no harm to the lives and property of the country. Since the government is giving utmost importance to this, it was said, the court does not see the need to intervene in the issue of banning ISKCON at this time. We think that the people of our country are cordial. People of all religions in this country love to live in a friendly manner. That love will never be broken. We also have friendly relations with neighboring countries. 

The High Court bench comprising Justice Farah Mahbub and Justice Debashish Roy Chowdhury made these comments on Thursday after hearing the arguments of the state on the issue of banning the Hindu community organization International Sri Krishna Bhavanamrit Sangh (ISKCON). Earlier, Additional Attorney General Anik R. Haque and Deputy Attorney General Asad Uddin, representing the state, presented the progress of the government's steps in the murder of the lawyer to the court. They told the court that the government is giving utmost importance to the incident. So far, three cases have been filed. In one, 13 people, in one, 14 people and in the other, 44 people have been charged. 33 people have been arrested. Six people involved in the murder have been identified through CCTV footage. 
Earlier on Wednesday, lawyer Monir Uddin filed a petition in the High Court seeking a ban on ISKCON in the Alif murder case. The petition also requested that the murder be investigated with utmost importance and the culprits brought to justice. 

Meanwhile, the Supreme Court Bar Association has demanded a ban on ISKCON during this hearing in the High Court. At a press conference at the Supreme Court Bar Auditorium yesterday, the association's acting secretary Mahfuzur Rahman Milon said that the murder of Alif has caused bleeding in the hearts of 180 million people, including lawyers across the country. Those who believe in fascist ideology are involved in an anti-national conspiracy with domestic and foreign allies. In continuation of that, members of the terrorist organization ISKCON brutally killed Saiful Islam Alif. 

Attempts to unfairly blame the lawyer for the murder 
On the same day, ISKCON Bangladesh held a press conference on the arrest of Chinmoy Krishna Das, violence and the murder of the lawyer. In a press conference organized at the organization's Swamibag Ashram, the leaders of the organization claimed that attempts are being made to unfairly blame ISKCON for the murder of lawyer Saiful. They say that ISKCON Bangladesh has never been involved in any communal or conflictual activities and will not be an exception in the future. 

In a written statement, ISKCON Bangladesh General Secretary Charu Chandra Das Brahmachari said, "Recently, there has been a continuous attempt to spread false, fabricated and purposeful propaganda about ISKCON Bangladesh, focusing on the movement of the Bangladesh Sammilit Sanatani Jagran Jote. Since the change of government through the mass uprising on August 5, some quarters have been trying to create instability by making misleading statements and baseless allegations to discredit our organization. This attempt has reached its peak after the tragic death of lawyer Saiful Islam. There is an attempt to unfairly blame ISKCON Bangladesh for the undesirable incident that took place in front of the Chittagong Court building." 

Charu Chandra Das also said, "We want to clearly state that ISKCON Bangladesh has no involvement in such a shameful incident and the ongoing movement. This falsehood has now reached such a level that even issues like road accidents are being continued as if they were ISKCON's plot. A few months ago, the principal of the promoter Sri Krishna Temple, Leelaraj Gaur Das, member Swatwara Gauranga Das, and the principal of Chittagong's Pundarika Dham, Chinmoy Krishna Das, were relieved of all organizational positions and activities of ISKCON for violating organizational discipline. The activities carried out by them are not the activities of ISKCON. In addition, on October 3, it was announced through an official statement that Chinmoy Krishna Das (Chandan Kumar Dhar) is not the spokesperson of ISKCON Bangladesh. Therefore, his statements are completely his personal. 

ISKCON leaders made four calls to the government. These are - To investigate the false and misleading propaganda against ISKCON Bangladesh and take appropriate action by revealing the real truth. To take effective action against those who are purposefully tarnishing the reputation of ISKCON. To maintain religious tolerance and to refrain from any kind of provocative activities to maintain peace and order. Everyone should work together to maintain peace, harmony and stability in the society. 
ISKCON expressed deep sorrow over the murder of Saiful Islam. ISKCON Bangladesh Treasurer Jyotishwar Gaur Das Brahmachari, Central Member Bimala Prasad Das, Chinmoy Gadadhar Das Brahmachari, Rishikesh Gaurang Das, among others, were also present at the press conference.

Headline_English: Students lock office demanding VC's resignation
Content_Enlish:
Barisal University Vice Chancellor Professor Dr. Suchita Sharmin's office has been locked by students demanding her resignation. At that time, they removed the nameplate. The incident took place at around 1:30 pm on Thursday. A section of students and teachers and staff started the movement since Wednesday demanding the resignation of the Vice Chancellor. They gave the Vice Chancellor an ultimatum until 12 noon on Thursday. It is reported that the Vice Chancellor is currently absent from the campus. 

According to campus sources, before the Vice Chancellor's office was locked, a memorial meeting was held on the campus to commemorate the martyrs of the mass uprising. The Vice Chancellor was the pre-announced chief guest. However, yesterday, his name was omitted and Deputy Vice Chancellor Dr. Golam Rabbani was made the chief guest. The Vice Chancellor's name was covered on the banner. 

Nameplate removed 
Nameplate removed 

Agitating students demand – Vice Chancellor Shuchita is an ally of fascism National Election Monitoring Council (JANIP) Dr. Nazmul Ahsan Kalimullah's associate. After he joined the post of Vice Chancellor on September 23, Dr. Kalimullah was included in the university academic council, examination committee and previous job calculation committee. Since then, he has been facing a lot of criticism from students. Dr. Kalimullah was dismissed on November 19 in the face of their demands. 

It is known that when retired Colonel Abu Hena Mustafa Kamal was appointed as the treasurer of Barisal University, the Vice Chancellor faced a new round of criticism. Mustafa Kamal was the registrar of Dr. Kalimullah Begum Rokeya University when he was the Vice Chancellor. 

One of the leaders of the movement, university student Sujoy Shuvo Biswas, said that his office will remain locked until the Vice Chancellor resigns. Hafiz Ashraful Haque, chairman of the Coastal Studies and Disaster Management Department, said that 53 teachers and many officials and employees have expressed solidarity with the students' movement. 

After the government fell in the mass uprising on August 5, the then Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Badruzzaman Bhuiyan resigned on August 20. Then on September 23, Dr. Shuchita joined as the Vice-Chancellor.

Headline_English: Putin calls Trump 'smart'
Content_Enlish:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has called US President-elect Donald Trump an “intelligent person,” saying he has the ability to solve problems. 

The Russian president made the remarks on Thursday during a visit to Kazakhstan. Putin’s comments come as Moscow’s tensions with the West rise ahead of the Republican president’s inauguration. 

“As far as I can tell, the re-elected President Trump is a really intelligent person. He has already had a lot of experience. I think he will find a way to solve the problem,” Putin said. 

He did not specify what kind of solution he would like to find.

Headline_English: Former MP Rashiduzzaman remanded for 4 days
Content_Enlish:
The court has granted a 4-day remand to former MP from Khulna-6 (Paikgachha-Koira) constituency Md. Rashiduzzaman Morol in two cases of explosives and assault and battery. 

On Thursday afternoon, Judge Anarul Islam of the Paikgachha Senior Judicial Magistrate Court granted his remand. 

According to police sources, Md. Rashiduzzaman was produced before the court under tight security on Thursday. The investigation officers of the two cases had requested a 7-day remand for a total of 14 days. The court granted a 2-day remand in each case after hearing the lawyers of both sides. 

After the fall of the Awami League government, on August 21, Ishita Enam Ritu, a leader of the anti-discrimination student movement in the municipality, and on August 26, BNP activist Rubel Sardar of Chandkhali filed two separate cases against former MP Rashiduzzaman. Remand has been granted in both cases. 

Former MP and former member secretary of Paikgachha Upazila Awami League Rashiduzzaman was arrested by RAB members from a hotel room in Kuakata area of ​​Patuakhali in the early hours of October 16. He is a resident of Maltha village in Paikgachha Upazila. 

Paikgachha Police Station OC Md. Sabzel Hossain said that after the remand was granted, he was brought to the police station and being interrogated. 

Meanwhile, Koyra Upazila Awami League Organizing Secretary and Koyra Sadar UP Chairman SM Baharul Islam was produced before the same court at noon. He was arrested in a case of assault and battery filed by BNP leader Fasiar Rahman at Paikgachha Police Station. He was sent to jail after the court did not grant his bail application. Law enforcement agencies arrested him from the Dhaka International Airport area last Wednesday.

Headline_English: 8 new cases filed against Imran Khan and his wife
Content_Enlish:
Eight new cases have been filed against former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi and party activists. 

The case was filed on behalf of the Islamabad police on Wednesday in connection with the violence surrounding the 'final protest' program called by the former Pakistani Prime Minister. 

The police took action in the case hours after Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif called for tough decisions to free the country from the politics of movement and ensure stability. 

According to a GeoNews report, the cases have been registered in various police stations including Shahzad Town, Sihala, Khanna, Shams Colony, Noon, Nilor, Tarnal, Banigala in Islamabad. The names of Imran Khan, his wife Bushra Bibi and the central leadership of the PTI are in these cases. 

In addition, there are also Ali Amin Gandapur, Salman Akram Raza and Sheikh Waqas Akram. The case names thousands of people in addition to the local leadership of the party. The cases include allegations of terrorism, assault on police, violation of Section 144, kidnapping, and interference in government affairs.

Headline_English: Bangladesh start Asia Cup with victory
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh U-19 team started their Asia Cup journey by defeating Afghanistan by 45 runs. Batting first, Bangladesh set Afghanistan a target of 229 runs. In reply, Afghanistan was all out for 183 runs. 

Chasing the target, the two Afghan openers Mahbub Khan and Uzair Khan were playing carefully at the beginning. But neither of them could extend the innings. When Uzair was out for 8 runs, Mahbub joined him for 16 runs. Faisal Khan took the team's lead with Nasir Khan for the third wicket. After completing his fifty, Faisal could not stay on the pitch for long. He scored 58 runs. Then Nasir followed his teammate's path by scoring 34 runs off 60 balls. Nazifullah Amiri could not extend the innings today either. After the batsman was dismissed for 17 runs off 19 balls, Barakatullah Ibrahimzai (19), Hamza Khan (5), Khatir Stanikzai (3) and Abdul Aziz (5) started the wicket procession. 

Afghanistan were bowled out for 179 runs for 9 wickets. In the 48th over, Allah Ghazanfar was run out and Afghanistan were bowled out for 183 runs. Bangladesh won by 45 runs. Al Fahad and Iqbal Hossain took 3 wickets each for Bangladesh. In addition, Maruf Mridha took two wickets and Rafi took one wicket. 

Earlier on Friday (November 29), Bangladesh lost the toss and opted to bat early. Opener Jawad Abrar returned to the dressing room before opening the scorebook. Then Azizul Tamim put on a 142-run partnership with another opener Kalam Siddique. However, Bangladesh quickly lost a couple of wickets after that. Kalam was dismissed for 66 off 110 balls and Debashish Deba for 1 off 6 balls. Shihab was dismissed for 10 off 15 balls for the team's 182. 

Bangladesh then lost 3 more wickets to add 15 runs. However, Azizul Tamim scored a century with one end in hand. He was dismissed for 103 off 133 balls for the team's 204 runs. In the end, Bangladesh scored 228 runs for the loss of 9 wickets in the stipulated 50 overs. For Afghanistan, Abdul Aziz, Nuristani Omarzai and Khatir Stanikzai took 2 wickets each. Captain Azizul Hakim Tamim was named the Man of the Match for his century.

Headline_English: Electricity and gas crisis wreaks havoc on industrial sector
Content_Enlish:
The power and gas crisis has caused a disaster in the industrial sector. Hundreds of factories have closed in the last few months. Export earnings have decreased. Investment has stalled. Employment is not increasing. These are the comments of businessmen. They also say that if the industrial sector does not survive, economic growth will stop. Therefore, strong initiatives must be taken to meet the gas and electricity needs of the industry. The speakers made these remarks at a seminar organized at a hotel in Gulshan, the capital, on Saturday. 

However, the government says that it has given special emphasis to addressing the energy crisis in the industry. Gas supply has been increased in industrial areas. Emphasis has been placed on exploring ways to increase domestic gas production. 

The seminar titled 'Ways to solve the energy crisis in the country's industrial sector' was organized by the Bangladesh Chamber of Industries (BCI). Advisor to the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Fawzul Kabir Khan was the chief guest and Commerce Advisor Sheikh Bashiruddin was the special guest. In addition, top business leaders and owners of institutions from various industrial sectors were present. 

Professor Dr. Ijaz Hossain. He said, due to the power and energy crisis, production in the garment sector has decreased by 30-35 percent. Production in steel factories has decreased by 25-30 percent. Production in ceramic factories has halved. Costs have increased due to the use of diesel and additional work of workers. Small industries under rural electricity are being affected the most. It is not possible to run their diesel generators. As a result, about 40 percent of small industries are on the verge of closing. He said, the demand for gas in the industrial sector is about 1 billion cubic feet. But now 500 million cubic feet is being provided. The demand for energy in the industrial sector has not increased in the last two years. 

Professor Ijaz said, the demand for gas will stand at 4.3 billion cubic feet by 2030. To meet this demand, we will have to rely more on imported LNG. He said, the price of energy and electricity should be reduced for the good of the industrial sector. 

Advisor Fawzul Kabir Khan said, Tk 370 crore has been saved in the energy sector in the three months after the interim government took power. The government is giving importance to renewable energy. Because, considering the environment and other issues, we have to move in that direction. Tenders for 40 renewable energy projects will be given this week. He said, there is a lack of competition in the public sector. To survive, we have to get out of the bribery trade. Government procurement must be brought into competition. 

Fawzul Kabir said, in the last 15 years, agreements in the power and energy sector have been made with ministers of the previous government and certain business groups with ties to the government. This has disrupted healthy business competition in this sector. It has damaged the country's economy. That situation will change. 

He said, there will be no more business with the government. Good businessmen will get the opportunity to work in this sector based on their qualifications and skills. This will create business competition in the power and energy sector and the country's economy will also grow. From now on, no agreements will be made in the power and energy sector based on political considerations or party relations. He said, since there is no pipeline, that gas cannot be brought to Dhaka or industrial areas. If this gas is brought to Dhaka in CNG format, the crisis in the industry will be reduced to some extent. 

Depicting the endless suffering in connection with gas in factories during the Awami League regime, Commerce Advisor Sheikh Bashiruddin said, "After investing in industrial factories, I had to install a 40-kilometer pipeline with my own money to get gas. I paid Tk 20 crore just for cutting the road for this pipeline. Apart from that, I had to pay a lot of extra money." 

He said, I had to stand in the rain in front of the house of the former State Minister for Energy (Nasrul Hamid) for gas. I had to listen to many lectures from him. I did not even get minimum respect. Even then, I had to say, 'Yes sir, yes sir.' I want to see some people's brains by doing a CT scan. How can people be so criminal? 

The Commerce Advisor said, now businessmen do not have to pay any bribes or bribes. By utilizing this opportunity, there is a great possibility for honest entrepreneurs to contribute to the development of the country's economy. 

Former FBCCI president, former MP and managing director of Ha-Meem Group A. K. Azad said, ‘A few days ago, a businessman came to me. He had partially closed his textile factory. He was on my right side during Maghrib prayers. He was in prostration and crying. He was actually not getting gas pressure. The factory is almost closed. He is not able to pay the bank. Many factories in the Narsingdi area are suffering due to the fuel crisis.’ 

He said, many of us are not able to run factories. Because the workers of the factories that have been closed are coming and vandalizing, demanding jobs. How can we give them jobs, we ourselves are not able to run factories. 

A. K. Azad said, I went to the energy advisor a few days ago. He understands the matter, he spoke to the chairman of Petrobangla. Now, in a better situation, if we get gas like this, we will be able to continue production, but we will not be able to survive. Production costs are increasing. Fuel prices are increasing, workers have to be paid more, US importers are not increasing the prices of products. Because Pakistan is able to provide goods at low prices. Where our exports are negative, Pakistan's growth is good. Six Indian provinces subsidize the wages of workers to investors. Land is free, electricity and fuel are also subsidized. As a result, investors are rushing there. We are unable to sustain business. You provide gas, I will give you foreign exchange. 

He said, I returned from the Cotton Summit in the United States. There, an economist showed that the way taxes are being imposed on China, importers are coming to countries like Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Vietnam. But we are not able to take orders that way. Because we are not able to deliver orders on time. It is not possible to continue production with diesel. If the government increases gas supply to industrial areas, employment will increase, revenue will increase. If necessary, we will cook one meal a day and heat it for three meals. What is the benefit of burning gas in cars? 

Former FBCCI president and BNP leader Abdul Awal Mintu said, at least 1.5-1.5 million people enter the job market every year. In addition, a large number of workers are becoming unemployed due to the loss of jobs from agriculture. Because the use of technology in agriculture is increasing. If these two are combined, at least 2.5 million people are entering the job market every year. Industrialization is needed to provide employment to these people. And for this, electricity and gas are needed the most. If there is a problem in these two, there will be no employment. Inflation will increase. 

Former FBCCI President Mir Nasir Hossain said that uninterrupted gas must be provided to industrial areas, especially Gazipur, Narayanganj and Mymensingh. Special attention needs to be paid to this to sustain the country's economy. 

BCI President Anwar-ul-Alam Chowdhury said at the event that growth in the industrial sector is decreasing day by day. In the 2020-21 fiscal year, the growth in this sector was 10.29 percent, which decreased to 6.66 percent in the last fiscal year. Growth from April to June last year was only 3.98 percent. Due to the energy crisis, 200 industrial factories have closed between March and September this year, and another 300 factories are at risk. 

He said, due to the power and energy crisis, private sector growth fell by 9.85 percent in August and September. Foreign investment fell by 15 percent from July to September. Export earnings fell by about $2.5 billion from the fiscal year 2022-23 to 2023-24. On the contrary, gas prices have increased by 286 percent in the last 5 years. The amount of LCs opened for the import of equipment has decreased by 41 percent, and raw materials have decreased by 9.81 percent. 

Petrobangla Chairman Janendra Nath Sarkar said, earlier, the government was asked to provide more gas for electricity by depriving the industrial sector. Now the situation has changed. We have increased gas supply to the industry. A tender to bring gas from Bhola will be called by next December. In addition, an offshore bidding tender will be opened on December 9. We hope to sign an agreement with a renowned energy company for offshore gas early next year. 

He said, there is a huge potential for gas in various areas of the country, including the hilly areas. Preparations are underway to open offshore bidding for gas exploration in these areas. Hopefully, offshore bidding will be possible by next March.

Headline_English: No matter how much pressure BNP puts, elections will be based on reforms: Nahid
Content_Enlish:
Nahid Islam, advisor to the Information and Broadcasting Ministry of the interim government, said that the government is not accountable to any party, but to the aspirations of the people. Therefore, no matter how much pressure BNP puts for early elections, the government will move towards the elections based on the work of the Reform Commission. He said this in an interview with private television channel 24. 

Awami League will have to apologize, not just face trial: There have been demands from various quarters to ban former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her party Awami League, which were criticized for the July-August massacre. What is the government thinking about this? Asked about this, Nahid Islam said that the Awami League has lost its moral right to engage in politics by killing people indiscriminately during the student and public movements. They will not only have to face trial, but also apologize to the people. 

There may be a conspiracy behind the demands: The interim government is having to deal with a series of demands after the mass uprising. When asked about this, Nahid Islam said that some of the demands are fair, but not all of them. They believe that there may be a conspiracy behind these demands. 

Nahid Islam said that the laws that are obstacles to media freedom will be reviewed. We will try to outline an outline by discussing and reviewing economic-political security and other related issues, so that people in this country can freely practice media in this country without any hindrance.

Headline_English: Unstoppable missile 10 times faster than sound ready: Putin
Content_Enlish:
A day after a new ballistic missile attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro, Russian President Vladimir Putin said the country has a new type of powerful missile stockpile ready for use. 

In an unscheduled televised address on Friday, he said the Oreshnik missile cannot be stopped. The hypersonic missile can travel 10 times faster than the speed of sound. It has been ordered to be produced. 

Putin had previously said such missiles would be used in response to the missile attack in Ukraine. 

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called on world leaders to give Putin a “befitting response.” He has requested that the West provide Ukraine with air defense systems. 

The Interfax-Ukraine news agency reported that Kiev has asked for the US Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) or has offered to upgrade the Patriot anti-ballistic missile defense system. 

The attack on Dnipro on Thursday was described by witnesses as unusual and the resulting explosion lasted for three hours. 

Ukraine launched a missile attack into Russia this week, supplied by the US and the UK. In response, the Russian military fired a new generation of hypersonic ballistic missiles, the Oreshnik, at a military installation in the Dnipro region of Ukraine. 

Russian President Vladimir Putin said in response that the missile could carry nuclear weapons similar to intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs). 

Justin Crump, founder and CEO of risk advisory company Sibyline, told the BBC that Moscow may have carried out the attack as a warning. He said the missile was so fast and sophisticated that it could seriously challenge Ukraine's air defences. 

Several world leaders have warned of the tense situation between Russia and Ukraine this week.

Headline_English: Dhaka University lifts ban on ties with Pakistan
Content_Enlish:
In 2015, the Dhaka University authorities severed all ties with Pakistan by calling an emergency syndicate meeting. The ban was lifted in the university's regular syndicate meeting held recently on November 13. 

As a result, Pakistani students will also be able to study at Dhaka University. Dhaka University students will also be able to go to Pakistan for higher education. Dhaka University will be able to exchange with Pakistan on various issues including education and culture. 

The matter came to light on Monday. Several syndicate members confirmed this information to Samakal. 

When asked about this, Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Administration) Saima Haque Bidisha told Samakal that relations with them were severed at one time. Since it is an academic institution, many people want to go there for scholarships or to attend conferences. Considering that point of view, we decided to discuss the meeting and normalize relations. 

After the decision of the emergency syndicate on December 14, 2015, the then Vice Chancellor Professor AAMS Arefin Siddique said that Pakistan has denied committing genocide in this country, especially in Dhaka University, for a long period of 9 months starting from the night of March 25, 1971. Dhaka University cannot have any kind of relationship with such a lying state. Until they admit to genocide, murder and torture, this institution will not have any kind of relationship with them. 

‘None of our students will go to Pakistan for higher education again. Similarly, we will not accept any of their students,’ he said. 

Recently, a decision was taken to normalize relations at a syndicate meeting chaired by Vice Chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Chowdhury. 

Earlier, on September 5, Pakistan's High Commissioner to Bangladesh Syed Ahmed Maruf, who was posted in Bangladesh, met Vice Chancellor Professor Dr. Niaz Ahmed Khan in his office after almost a decade. 
Pro-Vice Chancellor (Administration) Professor Saima Haque Bidisha, Pro-Vice Chancellor (Education) Professor Mamun Ahmed and other members of the Syndicate were present at the Syndicate meeting.

Headline_English: Order to complete investigation against Sheikh Hasina within a month
Content_Enlish:
The International Crimes Tribunal has ordered the completion of the investigation into the July-August genocide case against former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina within a month. 

On Monday, a three-member tribunal led by the tribunal's chairman, Justice Md. Golam Mortuza Majumdar, gave the order. It has been asked to submit a progress report on the investigation by December 17. 

On the same day, at around 10 am, 13 people, including former ministers and state ministers, who were arrested on charges of involvement in the July-August genocide and crimes against humanity, were presented before the tribunal. 

Later, the hearing of the charges against them began at around 11 am. At the hearing, Chief Prosecutor Advocate Tajul Islam said that in the last 15 years of her rule, there has been no such crime against humanity that Sheikh Hasina has not committed. And these accused present have cooperated in organizing these crimes. 

It is learned that Sheikh Hasina is the only accused in a case of the July-August genocide and crimes against humanity. In another case, there are a total of 45 accused, including Obaidul Quader. On October 17, the International Crimes Tribunal's judicial proceedings began with the issuance of arrest warrants against 46 people, including Sheikh Hasina, on charges of crimes against humanity.

Headline_English: Attempted murder case filed against 187 people including Sheikh Hasina in Chittagong
Content_Enlish:
Another murder attempt case has been filed in Chittagong against former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and 187 others, including her cabinet members, police, businessmen, and lawyers. Kafil Uddin, who was injured in the attack during the anti-discrimination student movement, filed the case in the Chittagong Metropolitan Magistrate's Court on Monday. After the hearing, the court of Chittagong Metropolitan Magistrate Abu Bakkar Siddique ordered the PBI to investigate the case and submit a report. 

Apart from Sheikh Hasina, the list of accused includes former Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader, former Education Minister Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury Nowfel, former Banshkhali MP Mojibur Rahman, former Satkania MP Motaleb Chowdhury, former IGP Chowdhury Abdullah Al Mamun, PBI chief Banaj Kumar Majumder, former Chittagong City Corporation councilors Shoibal Das Sumon, Zahur Lal Hazari, Wasim Uddin, Hossain Hiron, JMS Group MD Mustafa Mahmud, Jatiya Party's Chittagong Metropolitan Convener Solaiman Alam Seth and OCs of various police stations in the city. Apart from this, former general secretary of the city Chhatra League Nurul Azim Roni and leaders and activists of Awami League, Chhatra League and Jubo League have also been made accused. 

Kafil Uddin alleged in the case that while participating in the movement, other accused attacked him and injured others on the orders of Sheikh Hasina and other top leaders of the Awami League. Kafil was injured and undergoing treatment at various hospitals in the city. Now that he has recovered, he has filed a case.

Headline_English: History will recognize those who initiated the AL rehabilitation as enemies of the people
Content_Enlish:
Hasnat Abdullah, convener of the anti-discrimination student movement, has said that history will mark those who take initiatives to rehabilitate the Awami League as public enemies. 

He made these remarks in a post on the social media Facebook on Tuesday afternoon. 

In that Facebook post, Hasnat Abdullah said, ‘The desire to step on the blood of the boys and make Delhi the Qibla and go to the seat of power is a betrayal of the people’s intention of liberation. History will mark those who take initiatives to rehabilitate the Awami League as public enemies.’ 

‘Those who hold the spirit of the July Uprising, who want to reflect the hopes and aspirations of the people, cannot make any other statement about the Awami League in the political arena other than demanding that the Awami League be tried in Bangladesh after 24 years.’

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia invited to Armed Forces Day
Content_Enlish:
The Armed Forces Division of the Office of the Chief Adviser has invited BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia to attend a reception at Senakunj on November 21, marking Armed Forces Day. 

On Tuesday night, Chief of General Staff (CGS) of the Army Lt. Gen. Mizanur Rahman Shamim and Principal Staff Officer (PSO) of the Armed Forces Division Lt. Gen. ASM Kamrul Ahsan delivered the invitation to the BNP Chairperson. 

When asked about this, BNP Standing Committee member and Khaleda Zia's personal physician Professor AZM Zahid Hossain said, "His wife came to the house and met former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia and gave her an invitation." 

BNP Media Cell Member Shairul Kabir Khan said that earlier around noon, army officials handed over invitation cards in the names of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman, party Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and 26 senior leaders to the Chairperson's Private Secretary Abdus Sattar at the Chairperson's office in Gulshan. 

Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus will be present as the chief guest at the reception at the Army Pavilion.

Headline_English: Road blockade in Cox's Bazar demanding lifting of travel ban on St. Martin
Content_Enlish:
A group of people have protested by blocking a road in Cox's Bazar for 2 hours, demanding the lifting of restrictions on tourist travel to St. Martin's Island and permission to spend the night. During this time, tourists in the area had to face extreme suffering. They blocked a road at the Dolphin intersection in Kalatoli, Cox's Bazar town, from 12 noon to 2 pm on Tuesday. 

Although the protesters claimed to be residents of St. Martin's Island, Cox's Bazar environmentalists claim that most of the protesters who occupied the road and protested were not residents of St. Martin's Island, but were brought in on hire from different areas of Cox's Bazar town. Later, after a meeting between the Deputy Commissioner and the protesters' delegation, the protesters withdrew their blockade. 

In this regard, Cox's Bazar Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) Md. Yamin Hossain told Samakal that the Deputy Commissioner had met with the protesters' delegation. They were assured that their demands would be conveyed to the advisor. Immediately after the meeting, the protesters lifted the road blockade. 

In this regard, Mufizur Rahman, chief advisor of the Cox's Bazar Tour Operators Association, said, "We want a review of the restrictions on tourist travel to St. Martin's Island. However, we do not support any movement that creates suffering for tourists by blocking roads like this." 

Bangladesh Environment Movement (BAPA) Cox's Bazar General Secretary Kalim Ullah said, "A movement against the government's decision by bringing hired people from different areas of Cox's Bazar city and blocking roads by pretending to be residents of St. Martin's cannot be accepted in any way." Basically, some hotel owners are instigating this movement. Their provocative planned movement against the government is questioning the image of Cox's Bazar. Not only that, but it is also reducing the number of tourists in Cox's Bazar.

Headline_English: 'Pushpa 2' with a budget of Rs 500 crore is not being released in Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
South Indian icon star Allu Arjun's 'Pushpa: The Rise' movie was a blockbuster. Allu Arjun's craze has reached the sky due to the film. As a result, the audience was eager to watch the second installment of the movie. According to sources, 'Pushpa 2' was made on a budget of Rs 500 crore. Even before it was released, this movie has already collected double the money from the production company. 

'Pushpa 2: The Rule' will be released on December 5. Director Sukumar is coming with the second installment after a gap of three years. 

However, this much-discussed movie is not being released in Bangladesh. Since the Bangladeshi company Action Cut Entertainment announced the release of 'Pushpa 2 - The Rule' in Bangladesh a few months ago, the audience was eager to watch it. 

However, now Action Cut Entertainment's head Anon Mamun says that his company is not importing the movie for now as he is busy with the movie 'Dard'. He does not think that anyone else will import it. 

Bangladesh's Jazz Multimedia also imports Indian movies. However, they will not bring 'Pushpa 2 - The Rule', confirmed the head of the company Abdul Aziz. 

Two weeks ago, the Abhishek Kathachitra released Bollywood's 'Stree 2' in Bangladesh. The head of this company, Zahid Hasan Abhishek, also said that he has not taken any decision on importing 'Pushpa 2 - The Rule'. Earlier, Abhishek could not release 'Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3' in the country despite importing it. Because it has not yet received the censor clearance. As a result, it is no longer waiting to be said that 'Pushpa 2 - The Rule' is not being released in Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Awami League has not given any concessions to JPA in this election: GM Quader
Content_Enlish:
Jatiya Party Chairman and Rangpur-3 constituency candidate Golam Mohammad Quader said, there was no sharing in 26 seats, these are propaganda. We wanted a neutral role of the administration everywhere. Another thing we wanted was to keep the election away from the influence of arms, muscle and money. Then we will hold elections. There, Awami League has picked boat candidates of its own accord. But at the same time, it has fielded strong independent candidates in these seats. They are not rebel candidates, they are independent candidates. Awami League is working directly for those independent candidates. It is not working for our candidate. Awami League has not given any concessions to Jatiya Party in this election. Rather, except for 2/1 of the 26 seats where it has picked boats, there are independent candidates of Awami League. They are working for them. GM Quader said, candidates must have political will to remain in the competition by enduring injustice and oppression. If they withdraw from the election, it will be a big disgrace in the political life of the candidates. In this, people think that either he has sided with the opponent and stepped aside in exchange for something or he has left the election field out of fear. This is not auspicious for politics. Later, he sought votes in the plough by making mass contact with lawyers and common people. 

At that time, he was accompanied by Co-Chairman Rangpur City Mayor Mostafizar Rahman Mostafa, Central Vice Chairman SM Yasir, Cultural Secretary Ajmal Hossain Lebu, Organizing Secretary Abdur Razzak, Co-Organizing Secretary Shafiul Islam Shafi, Central Executive Members Lokman Hossain, Zahidul Islam and Hasanuzzaman Nazim and many others.

Headline_English: Russia will not give up its just demands: Putin

Headline_English: Death toll in Pakistan communal violence rises to 130
Content_Enlish:

CNN reported this information in a report on Sunday (December 1). 

Kurram, a district in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. On November 21, gunmen ambushed a convoy in Kurram district, killing 52 people. Most of them were Shia Muslims. Riots broke out after the attack. 

Since no one claimed responsibility for the attack, rival groups have carried out retaliatory attacks and set fires in several areas. 

Government officials brokered a seven-day ceasefire on November 24, but it did not hold. As a result, 14 people were killed and 27 others were injured in the region in the past 24 hours. 

Kurram is a tribal region of Pakistan bordering Afghanistan. Shia Muslims are a majority in some parts of Kurram district, although they are a minority in other parts of the country. Shia Muslims dominate Kurram district, although they are smaller in number. 

Shia Muslims in the region generally live peacefully with Pakistan's Sunni Muslim majority. However, since last July, a land dispute in Kurram district has turned into communal riots, with many people killed on both sides. 

"Ceasefire talks are underway with tribal leaders and security forces have been deployed to maintain peace," said Javed Ullah Mehsud, deputy commissioner of Kurram district. 

Mehsud added that "authorities have restored internet and mobile services in the area." 

However, the main highway connecting the provincial capital Peshawar with the city of Parachinar has been closed to all traffic, causing shortages of food, fuel and medicine. 

Trade and movement along the Kharlachi border with Afghanistan have also been disrupted.

Headline_English: Cyclone and cold wave threat in December

The regular meeting of the committee was held at the Dhaka Storm Warning Center of the Meteorological Department and through video conference under the leadership of Md. Mominul Islam, Director (Current Responsibilities) of the department and Chairman of the expert committee. 

The December forecast says that the day and night temperatures may gradually decrease in the current month. However, the day and night temperatures may remain normal throughout the month. In addition, there is a possibility of normal rainfall in the country overall. 

The agency also said that in December, moderate to dense fog may fall in the country's river basins from midnight to morning and light to moderate fog elsewhere. Normal flow may prevail in the country's major rivers throughout the month. 

The agricultural weather forecast said that the average daily evaporation in the country this month may be 2.50 to 4.50 millimeters and the average bright sunshine duration may be 6.50 to 8.50 hours.

Headline_English: Biden unlikely to succeed in last attempt
Content_Enlish:
US President Joe Biden's administration may make one last attempt to stop the wars in Palestine and Lebanon. Reuters reports.

Top US officials have made several trips to the Middle East in the past few months to try to broker a ceasefire. However, they may now face negotiations and disagreements, and the parties may decide to wait until Trump takes office in January, according to relevant sources and independent analysts. 

Trump promised to restore peace to the Middle East during his election campaign, but he did not say anything about what the strategy would be. In light of his first-term experience, analysts believe that Trump may take a stronger stance on Israel and provide more support than Biden. 

As Trump begins his second term, US State Department spokesman Matthew Miller said on Thursday, “We will continue to work to end the war in Gaza and Lebanon and increase humanitarian assistance. We have a responsibility to implement these policies by January 20.” 

But as the Biden administration nears its end, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arab leaders are unlikely to pay much attention to Biden. Instead, they will wait for the Republican successor to take action. Trump’s first term has further destabilized the Middle East. 

“They (the Biden administration) no longer have that significant influence. People may still answer their phones, but they will all be waiting for the new administration,” said Brian Finucane, senior adviser to the International Crisis Group’s US program. 

After Trump’s victory in Tuesday’s election over Vice President Kamala Harris, Arab and Israeli officials are now thinking about mitigating potential future damage. 

Egyptian mediators are working with US and Qatari negotiators on a Gaza ceasefire proposal, Egyptian intelligence sources said. They are waiting to see what Trump’s possible policy on the Palestinians would be under him. 

Trump’s victory in the US election is believed to have coincided with Netanyahu’s preference. Netanyahu called Trump’s victory “historic” and, by firing Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, created a situation where the Biden administration would lose a preferred ally.
