May those injured in the mass movement receive lifelong healthcare. May the dreams of the agitators come true. If the youth are given an opportunity, they will introduce Bangladesh to the world in a new way.’ 

Professor KM Aminul Haque, Principal of the Government Science College, said, ‘There is no alternative to science in building a country. In this case, the youth must take responsibility. This college is running on the infrastructure of 1954, which is risky. I seek the advisor’s cooperation in constructing a multi-storey building very quickly.’ 

It is worth noting that Advisor Md. Nahid Islam is an alumnus of Government Science College. Tanzina Ferdous, vice-principal of Government Science College, Sarwar Tushar, member of the Citizens' Committee, Tariqul Islam, a former student of Government Science College, one of the coordinators of the July Revolution, and a large number of students were present at the event.

Headline_English: Trump suggests attacking Iran's nuclear facilities
Content_Enlish:
Israel should attack Iran's nuclear facilities in response to the missile attack. Former US President and Republican candidate Donald Trump made this comment on Friday (October 4). AFP reports. 

gnews Follow Google News to get the latest news from Daily Ittefaq 
In response to a question during the election campaign in North Carolina, Trump said, "They (journalists) asked him (Biden) what he thought about Iran, do you want to attack Iran (nuclear facilities)? And he said, as long as (Israel's) nuclear facilities (Iran) are not attacked. That means you (Biden) want to attack, doesn't it?" 

The former US president also said that when they asked him (Biden) this question, the answer should have been that the nuclear facilities would be attacked first, and the rest can be thought about later. 

However, while Biden has not endorsed an attack on Iran's nuclear facilities, the US president has said that discussions are underway about a possible Israeli attack on Iranian oil facilities. 

Meanwhile, on Friday (October 4), a top US State Department official told CNN that they have not given the Biden administration any assurances that Israel will not attack Iran's nuclear facilities. 

The official said that it would be difficult to say for sure if Israel retaliates on the anniversary of the Hamas attack on October 7. CNN asked the official if Israel had assured the US that it had left the issue of attacking Iran's nuclear facilities out of the discussion. 

In response, the official said, "We hope and expect to see some wisdom as well as strength, but you know there are no guarantees." 

Last Tuesday, Iran launched 180 missiles at Israel. The country claims that 80 percent of its missiles hit Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu then said they would respond strongly.

Headline_English: We are in the field, you can go to the puja mandap without fear: Army Chief
Content_Enlish:
Army has been deployed across the country ahead of Durga Puja. Army Chief General Waqar-uz-Zaman has urged everyone to go to the puja mandap without fear. 
The Army Chief made this appeal while talking to reporters after visiting the Dhakeshwari National Temple on Saturday (October 5) afternoon. 

Waqar-uz-Zaman said, “We are in the field. You will go to the puja mandap without fear. We want a beautiful environment where you can all celebrate the puja.” 

He also said, “Everyone has equal rights in this country. Everyone will follow their own religion. Whatever is needed for this will be done.”

Headline_English: Despite instability in the garment industry, exports increased by 16.27 percent
Content_Enlish:
Despite the political turmoil in the country, exports of goods increased by 16.27 percent in September. This figure for exports of goods has been obtained from the National Board of Revenue (NBR). 

According to the organization, goods worth $3.86 billion were exported in September last year. Exports in September last year were $3.32 billion. Accordingly, exports increased by $540 million last month compared to September last year. 

Although the export figures also include hidden exports from Export Processing Zones (EPZs) and sample exports. This amount is, however, very low. 

According to NBR data, goods worth $382 million were exported in July and $4.07 billion in August last year. At that time, the growth in exports was 3 and 5 percent respectively. In total, goods worth $1,175 billion were exported in the first three months (July-September) of the current 2024-25 fiscal year. This export is 7.89 percent more than the same period last year. 

According to Bangladesh Bank data, actual goods exports worth $3.48 billion were recorded in July. In contrast, the NBR reported goods exports worth $3.82 billion in that month. The agency's calculations also include hidden and sample exports. The central bank basically calculates the actual export figures by excluding them. 

According to the bank's calculations, the amount of goods exports in the 2023-24 fiscal year was $40.81 billion or $4,810 million. This export is 5.89 percent less than the previous year. Goods worth $4,336.4 million were exported in the 2022-23 fiscal year.

Headline_English: President seeks Malaysia's cooperation to send more manpower from Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
President Md. Shahabuddin has sought the cooperation of the Malaysian government in facilitating the movement of more manpower from Bangladesh to Malaysia. The President also requested the Malaysian government to cooperate in the current interim government's 'economic reform' program. 
The President's cooperation was sought during a courtesy call on Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim at Bangabhaban on Friday (October 4). 

The President's Press Secretary Md. Joynal Abedin told reporters that during the meeting, they exchanged views on various issues of bilateral interest, especially trade, investment, economic, technical cooperation, the Rohingya issue and the labor market. 

The President said that Malaysia is the second largest destination for Bangladesh's manpower exports. Bangladesh's manpower is playing an important role in the economic development of Malaysia and Bangladesh. 

The Head of State said that cooperation and partnership between Bangladesh and Malaysia have been increasing in various sectors including trade, investment, agriculture, human resource communication, culture, tourism and education in the past 53 years. 

Congratulating Malaysia on assuming the chairmanship of ASEAN in the upcoming 2025, the President expressed hope that ASEAN, under Malaysia's capable leadership, will make a significant contribution to regional peace, security, and regional trade and investment. He called for support for Bangladesh's candidacy as ASEAN's 'Sectoral Dialogue Partner'. 

Stating that the visit of the Malaysian Prime Minister to Bangladesh will be a milestone in the development of relations between the two countries, the President said that this visit will take the bilateral relations of the two countries to a new height. The relations between Bangladesh and Malaysia are very deep. The Malaysian people love Bangladeshis very much as they have played an important role in Malaysia's economic development. 

President Sahabuddin stressed the importance of making the areas of migration of this labor force to Malaysia transparent and easy. The Malaysian Prime Minister assured technical assistance in implementing various reform programs of the interim government. 

Four cabinet members of Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, concerned secretaries and the Malaysian High Commissioner to Bangladesh were present at the meeting. Bangladesh was represented by Foreign Affairs Advisor Md. Touhid Hossain, Advisor to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Professor Dr. Asif Nazrul and the concerned secretaries were present. 

Earlier, when the Malaysian Prime Minister arrived at Bangabhaban at 4:40 pm, President Shahabuddin presented her with a bouquet of flowers and greeted her. Later, after the meeting in the credentials hall of Bangabhaban, he signed a visitor's book.

Headline_English: Two top coordinators of student movement demand removal of President
Content_Enlish:
New tension has arisen in the political arena of Bangladesh over the demand for the resignation of President Md. Sahabuddin. This time, Sarjis Alam, one of the coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, demanded the removal of the president. Earlier, on the same afternoon, another top coordinator of the student movement, Hasnat Abdullah, also demanded the resignation of the president. 

Sarjis posted a post on the social media platform Facebook at 9 pm on Thursday (October 3). 

He wrote in the post, ‘Ensure justice for the Awami League, form a new constitution, change corrupt Awami bureaucrats, cancel all illegal agreements made during Hasina’s tenure and Chuppu ((President Sahabuddin)) must be removed from the post of president immediately.’ 


Earlier, Hasnat Abdullah wrote in a Facebook post, ‘Ensure justice for the Awami League, form a new constitution, change corrupt Awami bureaucrats, cancel all illegal agreements made during Hasina’s tenure and Chuppu must be removed from the post of president immediately.’

Headline_English: Nepal's electricity will come via India, tripartite agreement signed
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh has signed a tripartite agreement to import 40 megawatts of hydropower from Nepal through India. According to the agreement, Nepal will export this power to Bangladesh through India's internal transmission line for five months from June 15 to November 15 every year. 
Representatives of Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) and India's NTPC Vidyut Bhatra Nigam Limited (NVVN) signed the agreement in Kathmandu on Thursday. 

Advisor to the Ministry of Environment, Forests, Climate Change and Water Resources of Bangladesh Syeda Rizwana Hasan, Nepal's Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Deepak Khadka, State Minister for Energy Purna Bahadur Tamang, Chairman of Bangladesh Power Development Board Md. Rezaul Karim, Executive Director of Nepal Electricity Authority Kulman Ghising and CEO of National Thermal Power Corporation of India Dino Naran were present at the agreement signing ceremony. 

Bangladesh's Water Resources Secretary Nazmul Ahsan and Nepal's Ambassador to Bangladesh Ghanshyam Bhandari were also present. 

According to the agreement, India will supply electricity to Nepal through the 400 kV Dhalkebar-Muzaffarpur cross-border transmission line and India will send it to Bangladesh through the existing line. 

The price of electricity per unit has been fixed at 6.4 cents (100 cents to 1 dollar). In Bangladeshi currency, which is about seven and a half taka. 

Regarding the agreement, Syeda Rizwana Hasan said, 'This agreement is an important step in expanding regional energy trade. It is not only a matter of meeting the immediate electricity demand, but also a process of ensuring long-term and environmentally friendly energy security of our countries.' 

The Environment Advisor is in Nepal on a two-day visit to witness the signing of this historic electricity agreement. Before the agreement, Environment Advisor Syeda Rizwana Hasan met Nepalese Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli at Singha Darbar. They discussed issues of bilateral interest.

Headline_English: Israel declares UN Secretary-General persona non grata
Content_Enlish:
Israel has declared UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres persona non grata. The country's Foreign Minister Israel Katz announced on Wednesday (October 2) that Guterres has been declared persona non grata because he did not condemn Iran's missile attack. BBC News. 
Israel Katz said that the UN Secretary-General has been declared 'persona non grata' and will not be able to enter Israel. 

Katz also accused the UN Secretary-General of being anti-Israel and a supporter of terrorists, rapists and murderers. 

He said that Guterres will be considered a black chapter in the history of the UN for future generations. 

However, the UN Secretary-General immediately condemned Iran's attack on Israel on Tuesday night. He also reiterated his demand for a ceasefire. 

Meanwhile, Iran launched 181 ballistic missiles targeting Israel on Tuesday night. The attack targeted Israeli military infrastructure. 

The US media outlet CNN confirmed that Iran had launched an attack on Israel's Nevatim air base. At least a dozen missiles were seen landing at the base. 

Another US media outlet Axios reported that Israel was preparing to respond to the Iranian attack. An official from the occupation told the media that they would target Iran's oil production facilities and other important infrastructure.

Headline_English: Mizanur Rahman Azhari returns home
Content_Enlish:
Popular Islamic commentator Maulana Mizanur Rahman Azhari of Bangladesh has returned home from Malaysia. He himself gave this information through a post on his verified Facebook page. 

On Wednesday (October 2), Azhari wrote at around 6:30 pm, ‘Alhamdulillah, I have arrived in my beloved homeland in peace. May the Most Gracious bless this return. Prayers.’ 


Earlier, on July 6, he said on Facebook Live, many people have messaged me and called me personally to ask when I will return home. I want to tell them that I will return home soon. I am also looking forward to meeting you. I want to meet you soon in Bangladesh, a free and independent country of equality and humanity. 

In that long video message, he said, I respectfully remember the martyrs who made the movement successful with fresh blood and pray for the forgiveness of their souls. I wish the injured a speedy recovery. I congratulate those who are leading the anti-discrimination movement and are still struggling. 

He called on everyone to be aware of the situation that has arisen in the country after the success of the movement. He said that the victory will be celebrated properly only if they behave responsibly. 

He also called on not to do injustice to minorities. He said that currently many will take the opportunity to attack minorities in their schools and establishments and try to blame Islamists and madrassa students. Therefore, everyone must be vigilant to foil the conspiracies of those who are not happy with this victory. 

He especially told madrassa students that you should ensure the safety of minorities. Be vigilant and aware that no one can attack them. If we make a mistake in these matters, Islam in Bangladesh will lag far behind. 

Bringing up the incident of the fall of the recently resigned authoritarian government, he said that in the pride of power, we forget our real situation and treat people as they are. But recent events have shown us that no oppression is permanent, so we must learn from these incidents. He said that those who will come to the new government system must also remember this issue and learn from it. They too must adopt the path of avoiding oppression.

Headline_English: IMF praises Bangladesh's efforts to address economic challenges
Content_Enlish:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has commended the interim government of Bangladesh for its efforts to overcome the economic challenges posed by the recent instability and major floods in various parts of the country. 

Chris Papageorgiou, IMF Mission Chief for Bangladesh, told BSS, “The authorities’ efforts to begin a sensible adjustment of continued fiscal austerity and non-core capital expenditure in response to the challenging situation are commendable.” 

The IMF mission team led by Papageorgiou visited Dhaka from September 24-30 to discuss recent developments in Bangladesh and the authorities’ reform priorities. 
The IMF mission chief said the timely formation of an interim government has helped the economy gradually return to normal and the political and security situation to be stabilized. 

Papageorgiou added that economic activity is still moving at a somewhat slower pace. However, inflation remains in double digits despite the recent instability and floods. The deterioration in the balance of payments has put additional pressure on foreign exchange reserves. This reflects the outflow of trade debt. 

However, he noted that the steps taken by the government on economic issues are indeed commendable. 

Responding to a question about the fiscal targets of the previous government, Papageorgiou said that the budget was considered an ambitious budget with optimistic tax revenue and ambitious capital expenditure projections. 

He added that historically, weak revenue collection has forced the government to cut both recurrent expenditure and large investments. 

The IMF mission chief said that this (revenue collection) is important to keep the budget deficit within their target. 

“In this context, we support the interim government’s efforts to rationalize capital expenditure by considering effective capacity in the face of persistently high inflation and external pressures and by scaling back non-priority projects,” he said. 

He said the IMF supports the authorities’ goal of setting ambitious revenue targets. These targets must be supported by robust revenue-generating measures. 

Papageorgiou said Bangladesh’s tax-to-GDP ratio has improved marginally in recent years. 

He said a multi-pronged approach is needed to achieve sustainable revenue collection, which includes both tax policy and revenue administration. 

He said key areas for reform in tax policy include reducing large-scale tax exemptions as part of a strategy to shift the tax burden from trade to income tax and VAT, simplifying the value-added tax (VAT) system, and broadening the tax base. 

He said priority reforms to improve tax administration include digitalization of tax collection processes and better tax compliance risk management.

Headline_English: Support for Palestine will continue: Dr. Yunus
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh will continue to support the Palestinian people's struggle for independence, said Principal Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus. 
The Head of the Interim Government told Palestinian Ambassador Yousef Ramadan this on Tuesday (October 1) when he paid a courtesy call on him at the Principal Advisor's residence in Jamuna. 

During the meeting, Palestinian Ambassador Yousef Ramadan praised Principal Advisor Muhammad Yunus's speech at the UN General Assembly. During the meeting, he discussed various issues of mutual interest, including global support for the Palestinian state, the massacre in Gaza and tensions in the Middle East. 

Palestinian Ambassador Yousef Ramadan praised the Principal Advisor's speech at the UN, saying, "It is timely and sheds light on much-needed issues on the Palestinian issue." 

The Palestinian ambassador also said that Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus made a clear statement on the Palestinian issue in his speech. At that time, Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus expressed Bangladesh's continued support for the Palestinian state and its people. 

Expressing the hope that the Palestinians will get the status of an independent state they desire, the Chief Advisor said, "We will continue to support the Palestinian people." 

The Palestinian ambassador said that at least 60 Palestinians have completed their medical studies in Bangladesh and are now serving patients in Gaza as doctors. He also said that more than two hundred Palestinian students are waiting to receive higher education in Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Netanyahu's 'provocative message' to the Iranian people
Content_Enlish:
Amid the unrest over the Israeli attack on Lebanon, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has issued a provocative video message to the Iranian people. The Times of Israel reports. 

In the video message, Netanyahu said, "I talk a lot about the leaders of Iran. But at this crucial moment, I want to say something to the Iranian people. I want to say it directly, without any filter or middleman." 

Addressing the Iranian people, he said, "Every day you see a regime that has subordinated you. They give inflammatory speeches to protect Lebanon and Gaza. Yet that regime is taking our region deeper into war every day." 

Netanyahu said, "Israel has the ability to attack anywhere in the Middle East. We will go wherever we need to go to protect our country and people. Every moment, this regime is taking the great people of Persia to the depths of hell." 

Netanyahu said, most people in Iran know that this regime does not care about them at all. If they really cared about you, they would not spend billions of dollars to keep the Middle East at war. Instead, they would try to improve your quality of life. 

He also said, when Iran is truly free, that time will come much sooner than people think. Nothing will be the same again. Our ancient Jewish and Persian people will finally find peace. Our two countries, Iran and Israel, will find peace. 

Netanyahu said, when that day comes, these rulers will be bankrupt, they will be shattered. Iran will develop like never before. It is through the talent that exists in Iranian society today that global investment, massive tourism development, technological innovation will occur. 

Netanyahu said, I know you do not support the murderers of Hamas and Hezbollah. But your leaders do. You deserve better. The people of Iran should know that Israel is on your side. That future will be one of prosperity and peace.

Headline_English: The US has failed to resolve the Middle East crisis, and Israel is not paying attention either
Content_Enlish:
The United States has repeatedly warned that if Israel increases its bombing or ground operations in Lebanon, the conflict could spread throughout the region. Even a larger war could begin. But Israel, ignoring US calls, has instead increased its attacks. 
Israel has been carrying out intense bombing since September 23 and has also carried out limited ground operations on Monday. As a result, more than 1,000 people have been killed in Lebanon. Among the dead are Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah, several Lebanese and Palestinian leaders, and a top general in Iran's Revolutionary Guard. 

The question is, why has the United States failed to deter Israel from this conflict? A bigger question may be: Can the United States deter Israel from anything at all? 

Israel is not just escalating the conflict. It is also waging a conflict on multiple fronts. Israeli illegal settlers have also carried out about 1,300 attacks in the occupied West Bank. There they have destroyed Palestinian homes, crops and property. But they have not been held accountable. 

Gaza and the West Bank are both recognized as part of a future Palestinian state. This has been accepted by 147 of the 193 UN member states. But Israel has rejected the creation of a Palestinian state, a clear challenge to US policy. 

Even when the US imposes sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements, Israel does not budge. When President Joe Biden proposes a ceasefire for Gaza, Israel does not respond. Even when the US strongly warns against taking unilateral action in Lebanon, Israel does not pay attention. 

Israel is taking action as it pleases. And the responsibility for finding a solution to this crisis falls on the US State Department. Meanwhile, their vague and often contradictory statements are being criticized on social media. 

At a press conference on Monday, US State Department spokesman Matthew Miller said, “We have never sought a diplomatic solution with Hamas.” When a reporter asked, “What about a ceasefire?” Miller replied, “I want Hamas to come to the negotiating table.” 

Miller’s comments contradict previous US policy and statements by officials. In June of this year, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu directly rejected a US-backed ceasefire proposal. He said, “It will be on our terms, and our terms are not to end the war.” 

The US is now in an uncomfortable position due to the escalating tensions between Israel and Hezbollah. They are trying hard to avoid a larger conflict. But their diplomatic efforts have also failed. The question is, how can the US deter Israel, or at all? 

It is clear that Israel is steadfast in its policies and is not paying much attention to US advice. This situation is only deepening the crisis in the Middle East.

Headline_English: Iran fires missiles at Israel
Content_Enlish:
The Israeli military has claimed that Iran has launched a missile attack on Israel. 

Reuters reported this information on Tuesday night, citing an Israeli military spokesman. 

The spokesman said that the Iranian missile attack could be "extensive". 

Israeli Defense Forces spokesman Rear Admiral Daniel Hagari urged citizens to take refuge in safe rooms. 

Earlier, the United States had informed about a possible Iranian attack on Israel. 

Later, Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant discussed a possible Iranian attack and self-defense with US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin.

Headline_English: Elon Musk's 'X' is reopening in Brazil
Content_Enlish:
The Supreme Court has allowed X to resume operations in Brazil. Elon Musk's company is complying with the court's order. 

Supreme Court Justice Alexandra Moraes said that X will be able to resume its services. The judge has allowed X to resume operations because X has now complied with the Supreme Court's order. Musk had previously said that they would not be able to comply with the Supreme Court's conditions. 

The judge said in her ruling that the social media platform can immediately resume operations in Brazil. 
A post from X's global government account said that the biggest thing for them was to ensure that billions of people in Brazil receive their services. It was said that the company would work for the right to freedom of expression within the law. 

Supreme Court order 

Last August, Justice Moraes announced that X's services would be suspended in Brazil until it complied with the Supreme Court's order. 

The Supreme Court ordered that X must have a legal representative in Brazil and that they would have to pay a fine of about $3.28 million. 

Brazil also ordered the freezing of assets belonging to X and Musk’s satellite internet operator Starlink. 

Musk initially said X would not comply with the court order. In late September, the company announced that Rachel Conceicao would act as its legal representative. 

According to Brazilian law, internet companies in the country are required to have a legal representative, so that they can be notified of any legal action or legal issues that may arise against the company. 

The Supreme Court had ordered X to take action against hate speech. But Musk said at the time that it was censorship and that he would not comply with the order.

Headline_English: Cyber ​​Security Act must be repealed: TIB
Content_Enlish:
The Cyber ​​Security Act is not amendable, it is repealable. This act must be repealed. Those in power have used this act as their own tool. 
Speakers made these remarks at a roundtable discussion titled ‘Repeatable Cyber ​​Security Act: People’s Expectations’ organized by Digital Rights and Citizens at the Tafazzal Hossain Manik Mia Hall of the National Press Club on Tuesday (October 8). 

At the roundtable discussion, Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) Executive Director Dr. Iftekharuzzaman said, I will immediately call for repealing this act. If the government has the will, it should not be delayed. 

Demanding compensation for those affected by the Cyber ​​Security Act, Dr. Iftekharuzzaman said, those who have been affected by this act must be compensated. Those who misuse this act must be held accountable. Those who have used the act as a tool of authoritarianism must be held accountable. 

Stating that the law has not changed despite the change in power, Iftekharuzzaman said, there is still a lot of concern. Only the person has changed, not the law. We can still see an example of the practice of establishing intelligence agencies in the name of national security. We have to strongly intervene to prevent this from happening. The interim government has the responsibility to create their legal and institutional infrastructure. They have to intervene there. 

Iftekharuzzaman also said that insecurity has been created in the name of security through the Cyber ​​Security Act or Digital Security Act. This issue is essential when making new laws so that insecurity is not created in the name of law. 

At the meeting, Barrister Jyotirmoy Barua said that the chief advisor of the interim government said to criticize openly. However, cases were filed even during Hasina's time, now cases are being filed. This may be what he (Dr. Yunus) said. 

Sheikh Manzoor-e-Alam, Regional Director for South Asia at Article Nineteen, said, "The mentality of the rulers is to harass. Cyber ​​security has not been ensured in this law. In making a new law, it must be ensured that no one is harassed by that law." 

Miraj Ahmed Chowdhury, Head of Program and Communications at MRDI, said, "If we cannot separate the discussion of national security from the discussion of cyber security, then our much bigger rights will be violated." 

Photographer and human rights activist Shahidul Alam, Chief Coordinator of the State Reform Movement Hasnat Qayyum and many others were also present at the roundtable meeting.

Headline_English: US spends record $17.9 billion on Israel in one year
Content_Enlish:
The United States has spent a record $17.9 billion in military aid to Israel since the war in Gaza began on Oct. 7, according to a report by Brown University's Cost of War Project. The conflict is escalating across the Middle East. 
The Gaza-based independence group Hamas invaded Israel a year ago, killing more than 1,200 people. Many were taken hostage. Israel's subsequent invasion of Gaza has killed nearly 42,000 people. Israel also attacked Lebanon in late September of this year. At least 1,400 people, including Hezbollah fighters and civilians, have been killed in the country since the massive escalation. 

The Cost of War Project report said that since its founding in 1948, Israel, a US protectorate, has been the largest recipient of US military aid in history. Since 1959, it has received a total of $251.2 billion. And the $17.9 billion in aid since October 7, 2023, is the largest single year in military aid to Israel. 

The United States pledged billions in military aid to both countries each year since the signing of a U.S.-brokered peace treaty between Israel and Egypt in 1979. The Obama administration has set annual spending for Israel at $3.8 billion through 2028. 

Since the Gaza war began, U.S. aid has included military financing, arms sales, and transfers of at least $4.4 billion in weapons and equipment from U.S. stockpiles. The bulk of the U.S. weapons delivered this year have been warheads, from artillery shells to 2,000-pound bunker-busters and precision-guided bombs. The report says $4 billion has been spent on Israel’s Iron Dome and David’s Sling missile defense systems, as well as rifles and jet fuel.

Headline_English: 1 arrested with 'whale vomit' worth Tk 21 crore in Teknaf
Content_Enlish:
8 kg 398 grams of ambergris (whale vomit) worth Tk 21 crore has been recovered in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar. At that time, BGB members arrested a smuggler named Shamsul Alam (35). 

Confirming the matter on Monday (October 7), Teknaf Battalion (2 BGB) Commander Lt. Col. Md. Mohiuddin Ahmed said, there was a tip-off that smuggled goods could be smuggled through Shahparidwip Bazarpara area, approximately 700 yards west of BRM-3, which is the responsibility of Shahparidwip BOP, on Sunday (October 6). Based on this, two patrol teams from Teknaf Battalion Sadar and Shahparidwip BOP quickly took up positions in Shahparidwip Bazarpara area. 

In the evening of that day, a BGB patrol team saw a suspicious person coming towards Shahparidwip Bazarpara with a sack. Later, he was able to recover 8 kg 398 grams of ambergris (whale vomit) from a bucket inside a plastic bag in his hand, which was banned for sale. The estimated value of which is 21 crore taka. 

Later, the recovered ambergris (whale vomit) was tested at the Bangladesh Oceanographic Research Institute, Cox's Bazar, and the characteristics and identification of the ambergris were completed. 

He further said that the recovered ambergris was deposited at the Cox's Bazar Deputy Commissioner's Office (Treasury Branch) and handed over to Teknaf Model Police Station through a regular case against the arrested person.

Headline_English: Honors in AI and Data Science launched for the first time in the country
Content_Enlish:
The race for technology is increasing, and its scope in higher education is also increasing. Currently, the situation is becoming such that from shoe stitching to Chandipath - artificial intelligence is taking over everywhere. Realizing this, Green University of Bangladesh is going to launch a graduate course in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science for the first time in Bangladesh. At the same time, the university has launched a software engineering department. 

This information was given at a press conference organized at the permanent campus of the university on Monday (October 7). 

The press conference was attended by the university's Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Mohammad Sharif Uddin, Deputy Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Khawaja Iftekhar Uddin Ahmed, Dean of the Faculty of Science and Engineering Professor Dr. Saiful Azad, Registrar Captain (Navy) Sheikh Mohammad Salahuddin, LPR and Chairperson of the AI ​​and Data Science Department Dr. Muhammad Abul Hasan. 

The speakers at the meeting said that although artificial intelligence is a new subject, its bright future prospects have already emerged. The way it has been growing in popularity over the past two-three years, experts say that this is the future. Not only that, the situation has reached such a stage that people are now forgetting Google and leaning towards artificial intelligence. Basic courses are also being offered from international IT platforms like Amazon; so that they can present themselves in the competitive market in the future. 

At the press conference, Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Mohammad Sharif Uddin said that through AI, human knowledge is being transplanted into machines. As a result, technology has improved, and human productivity has increased. We all use Pathao-Uber, but we do not know how these apps work. AI graduates will work on these subjects. They will enter deeper and deeper levels of computer science. 

Deputy Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Khawaja Iftekhar Uddin Ahmed said that the question may arise, if computer science is already running at Green University, then why AI? Its purpose is to reduce the gap between universities and industry in other areas, including jobs. At the same time, enrich the technology market by creating skilled manpower. 

Dean of the Faculty of Science and Engineering, Professor Dr. Saiful Azad, highlighted the progress and future statistics of the global market due to AI, data science and software engineering. He said that 36 percent of the job market in the world has improved due to AI alone. 

In his speech, he highlighted the goals and objectives of Green University and various initiatives to ensure quality education. 

Registrar Captain (Navy) Sheikh Mohammad Salahuddin said that the use of AI has already started on a wide scale in Bangladesh. It is diagnosing our diseases, organizing treatment and even recently controlling traffic. 

At the beginning of the meeting, Chairperson of the Department of AI and Data Science, Dr. Muhammad Abul Hasan, highlighted the issues of launching undergraduate courses on AI and AI. He said, it is assumed that if the challenges of the fourth industrial revolution and the fifth industrial revolution are to be faced in the future, then AI is inevitable for science and engineering students.

Headline_English: K-pop star ends marriage
Content_Enlish:
K-pop singer Geon has ended her two-year marriage to baseball player Hwang Jae-gyeong. The couple removed photos of each other from Instagram after announcing their separation. 
The girl group T-ara singer's lawyer, Choi Yoo-na, said that Geon has filed for divorce. 

The lawyer said, "The two have decided to divorce due to differences of opinion. After filing for divorce, the two will live separately." 

The BBC reported that they have filed a petition for a settlement at the South Seoul Family Court. Neither will file any charges or lawsuits against the other. 

The couple went public with their relationship in February 2022. The couple got married in December of that year. 

In June of this year, news of the strained relationship between the two came to light. Then the announcement of the separation came. 

Geon debuted as a member of T-ara in 2009.

Headline_English: 7-day ultimatum to ban Chhatra League
Content_Enlish:
The editor of the daily Amar Desh newspaper, Dr. Mahmudur Rahman, has given a seven-day ultimatum to ban the student wing of Bangladesh Awami League, Chhatra League, as a terrorist organization. 
He made this demand at a meeting at the National Press Club on Sunday (October 6). 

Dr. Mahmudur Rahman said that all statues of Sheikh Mujib should be removed. Initiatives should be taken to cancel the nomination of Saima Wazed Putul from the World Health Organization. All agreements made with India should be published. 

He also said that the judiciary was under Awami control. Justice Nizamul Haque Nasim should have been arrested for the Skype scandal. The media in Bangladesh is still under the control of Indian hegemony. The media in Bangladesh has used the narrative of fundamentalism and Islamic militancy to ferry people. 

Dr. Mahmudur Rahman said that the Jamuna Bridge should be named Shaheed Abu Said Bridge and Bangabandhu Avenue should be named Shaheed Abra.

Headline_English: All objectives of attack on Iran achieved: Netanyahu
Content_Enlish:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that all the objectives of the attack on Iran have been achieved. He said that the Israeli airstrike was ‘perfect and powerful’. 

Netanyahu said, ‘We promised to respond to the Iranian attack and we attacked on Saturday... The attack was perfect and powerful. All the objectives have been achieved.’ 

Netanyahu said these in a speech today, Sunday. Hamas attacked Israel on October 7 last year. According to the Hebrew calendar, today is the anniversary of that attack. He gave this speech on the occasion. 

Earlier, on October 1, Iran launched about 200 missiles at Israel. Israel claims to have shot down most of these missiles before they hit their targets. 

Regarding those attacks, Netanyahu said that Iran attacked Israel with several hundred ballistic missiles. But they failed. He also said, ‘We have kept our promise. Our air force attacked Iran, hitting its defense capabilities and missile production facilities. 

Tehran said the attack on Israel on October 1 was in response to the assassination of Iran-backed Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh, Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah and a commander of its own Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). 

On the other hand, Israel said that it attacked Iran last Saturday in response to attacks by Iran and its backed armed groups since the start of the Gaza war. However, Israel has not admitted to any other attacks on Iran before this attack. 

Meanwhile, Iran has admitted that Israel attacked military installations in the capital Tehran and a couple of other provinces yesterday. Tehran said that four soldiers were killed and "limited damage" was caused in these attacks.

Headline_English: Cases filed against 11 leaders of banned Chhatra League under anti-terrorism law
Content_Enlish:
A case has been filed against 11 leaders of the banned Chhatra League on charges of spreading propaganda and conspiring against the interim government. 

A police officer from the capital's Dhanmondi police station filed the case under the Anti-Terrorism Act last Thursday. Police have arrested former Chhatra League leader Ismail Hossain (22) in this case. The Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) court has granted Ismail a two-day remand for questioning. The police report mentions Ismail as the former deputy secretary for human rights of the central committee. 

Chhatra League Publicity Secretary Tariqul Islam, Organizing Secretary Sajibur Rahman, Chhatra League Vice President Mizanur Rahman, Waliul Khalifa, Deputy Mass Education Secretary Mostakim Hossain, Science Secretary Zahidul Islam, Deputy Education and Curriculum Secretary Riazul Islam, Deputy Human Rights Secretary Selim Reza, Agriculture Secretary Mohammad Hossain, Dhaka University Chhatra League Vice President Tamjid Bhuiyan and Organizing Secretary of Surya Sen Hall of Dhaka University Md. Shafiq have been accused in this case. 

Dhanmondi Police Station Sub-Inspector (SI) Monirul Islam alleged that on October 24, at around 2:25 am, he received information that these 11 Chhatra League leaders and 15 to 20 unidentified leaders and activists were holding a procession in front of No. 32, Dhanmondi to spread propaganda against the interim government. Later, at around 2:45 am, he arrived at the scene and saw that the banned organization Chhatra League was holding a procession. At that time, 25 to 30 people ran away after sensing the presence of the police. 

The case file alleged that the 11 accused in the complaint of Chhatra League and others held a procession to ban Chhatra League. They chanted slogans against the interim government and the state for the purpose of conspiring to harm the state. The case alleged that the accused committed a crime under the Anti-Terrorism Act by demanding the withdrawal of the ban.

Headline_English: Former Republican congressional candidate arrested on ballot theft charges
Content_Enlish:
A former Republican candidate for the lower house of Congress in Madison County, Indiana, has been arrested on charges of ballot theft, state police said Tuesday. The suspect has been identified as Larry Savage, 51. 

Indiana police said that on October 3, four voting machines were being tested when two ballots went missing from a ballot box containing 136 ballots. 

Police said surveillance video showed Savage folding two ballots and putting them in his pants pocket after receiving instructions about the validity of the ballot test. 

A search warrant was later issued for Savage and his building was searched. Police officials said the missing ballots were recovered from Larry's car. 

Griffin Reed, the public relations director for the Indiana Republican Party, said in a statement, “We unequivocally condemn any form of criminal interference in the election. We applaud the efforts of law enforcement agencies to ensure justice is served.” 

According to documents found online, Larry has been charged with ballot tampering and destruction. No lawyer has been listed for him. He was released on bond after his arrest. 

Larry had pleaded not guilty before being taken into custody yesterday. 

Voting fraud is rare in the United States. Donald Trump and his Republican party leaders have accused Democrats of voter fraud in the 2020 presidential election. Several of their lawsuits on the grounds of voter fraud have been dismissed in various courts. 

Read more 
Biden votes in the presidential election 
October 30, 2024 
Biden votes in the presidential election 
The US presidential election will be held on November 5. The Democratic Party candidate Kamala Harris and the Republican Party candidate Donald Trump are competing in the election. 

Donald Trump has been falsely claiming for the past four years that the 2020 election was rigged. Most Republicans in Congress have been supporting his claim. Because of their claim, extra caution is being taken in various states and counties this time.

Headline_English: Board not involved in Shakib's inability to return home: BCB president
Content_Enlish:
Shakib Al Hasan wanted to retire from this edition by playing the Mirpur Test against South Africa. But he could not return to the country due to security concerns. Many see this as a failure of the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB). However, BCB President Farooq Ahmed does not see it that way. 

Responding to questions from reporters before the board meeting at the Sher-e-Bangla Stadium in Mirpur today, Farooq Ahmed said, 'What you said about (not being able to return) to play the last Test... we are absolutely not involved in this matter. This is a matter for the law enforcement agencies, the government and Shakib Al Hasan (their matter)... We were supposed to play a completely auxiliary part here.' 

The board president said that he personally made every effort to give Shakib the opportunity to retire in the country, 'Whatever I personally say in front of you, I have tried my best so that Shakib Al Hasan can retire from the country. I tried my best. 

Since the team has not been announced yet, I think he is available. 
BCB President Farooq Ahmed later said this about Shakib's availability in the Afghanistan series, 'As a former cricketer, I thought that a boy who played cricket for 17 years, he is a brand ambassador, has done a lot for Bangladesh, so I thought it would be good if he (retires from the country) did it. But you have to look at other things as well. Combining those things, he could not come at the last minute, the board had nothing to do about it. It is a completely legal matter and the law enforcement agencies are involved in it. So it was a matter between Shakib and the law enforcement agencies. The board was not part of it. If he came, we would try to provide him security as much as the board could. Since he has not come, there is no point in talking about it anymore.' 

Read more

30 October 2024 
Farooq to go to Chittagong to talk to Nazmul about the captaincy 
The board president also mentioned Shakib's political identity, 'Shakib is not just a player now. He has an identity that he was an MP in the previous government and there are some sentiments (about him). Overall, the government's perspective and the Cricket Board's perspective are not the same.' 

BCB President Farooq Ahmed 
BCB President Farooq AhmedProthom Alo 
Shakib, who announced his retirement from Test and T20 cricket, wanted to play ODI cricket for a few more days. He also wanted to say goodbye to 50-over international cricket by playing the ICC Champions Trophy to be held in Pakistan in February next year. But for that, Shakib had to prepare by playing the upcoming two bilateral series. Bangladesh will travel to the United Arab Emirates on November 4 to play a three-match ODI series against Afghanistan. The West Indies tour is in December. 

Regarding whether Shakib will be available for the Afghanistan series, Farooq Ahmed said, "Since the team has not yet announced (the announcement), I think he is available."

Headline_English: Three more cases of kidnapping, murder and attempted murder filed against Sheikh Hasina
Content_Enlish:
Another case has been filed against ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina for the kidnapping of a man named Syed Hasan Mahmud five years ago. She filed this case at the capital's Shahjahanpur police station. Apart from this, information has been received that two more cases have been filed against Sheikh Hasina on charges of shooting and attempted murder during the student-public movement. The cases have been filed at the Shahbagh court in the capital and the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) court in Dhaka. 

The Awami League government led by Sheikh Hasina fell on August 5 in a student-public uprising. Ten days later, on August 15, the first case was filed against her in a Dhaka court. Since then, at least 236 cases have been filed against Sheikh Hasina across the country. Of these, murder charges have been filed in 199 cases. 

Kidnapping case 
A case was filed against Sheikh Hasina and 24 others on Wednesday for the kidnapping and threatening of a man named Syed Hasan Mahmud five years ago. The case alleges that in 2019, Jatiya Party leader Mashiur Rahman Ranga made objectionable remarks about Nur Hossain, one of the martyrs of the 1990 mass uprising, in a speech. He filed a case in a Dhaka court regarding this. After that, Awami League leaders including Mashiur Rahman Ranga started torturing him. Later, in November 2019, he was attacked at his house in Moghbazar. Later, he left the area and started living in Banasree. At that time, he was a candidate for the post of commissioner in ward number 35. Then, on January 10, 2020, he was abducted in a microbus from under the Khilgaon flyover. Later, he was threatened with being put in the crossfire. He was physically tortured. Later, the kidnappers left him in Malibagh. Apart from Sheikh Hasina, former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, former Roads, Communications and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader, former Law Minister Anisul Haque, former Member of Parliament Mashiur Rahman Ranga, former Information Minister Hasan Mahmud, former Industries Minister Dilip Barua, former Minister Tarana Halim, former Inspector General of Police Benazir Ahmed, and former DMP Commissioner Shafiqul Islam have been named as accused in the case. 

Shot in the stomach in Uttara 
A case has been filed against Sheikh Hasina and 101 others for allegedly shooting and attempting to kill a man named Md. Mohsin in the capital's Uttara area. Mohsin's father-in-law Abudus Salam filed the case at the CMM Court in Dhaka on Wednesday. The case states that Mohsin was shot in the stomach on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway under Uttara Purba Police Station around 12:30 pm on August 4. Apart from Sheikh Hasina, Obaidul Quader, former MPs Khasru Chowdhury and Habib Hasan, and former mayor of Dhaka North City Corporation Atiqul Islam have been named as accused in the case. 

Shooting death 
A murder case has been filed against Sheikh Hasina and 64 others for the murder of a man named Riazul Talukder on Topkhana Road in the capital. On October 26, Riazul's former acquaintance Billal Hossain filed the case at Shahbagh Police Station in the capital. The case claims that Riazul was shot on Topkhana Road during a student-public movement on August 4. Later, he was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and declared dead by the doctors on duty in the evening. 

Apart from Sheikh Hasina, former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader, former Dhaka South City Corporation Mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, former State Minister Junaid Ahmed Palak, former State Minister for Information Mohammad A Arafat, and former Minister Dipu Moni have been named as accused in the case.

Headline_English: The legal advisor will handle the administrative and financial responsibilities of the speaker.
Content_Enlish:
In the absence of the Speaker of the National Assembly, his administrative and financial responsibilities will be carried out by Interim Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Advisor Professor Asif Nazrul. 

The draft of the 'National Assembly Secretariat (Interim Special Provisions) Ordinance-2024' was approved in the meeting of the Advisory Council on Thursday. This issue is there. If the President issues the ordinance, the Legal Advisor will perform this duty. 

The meeting of the Advisory Council was presided over by Chief Advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus at the office of the Chief Advisor in Tejgaon. After the meeting, the decisions of the meeting were announced from the Chief Advisor's press wing. Apart from this, this issue was also raised by the Chief Advisor's Press Secretary Shafiqul Alam at a press conference organized at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital in the evening. 

The draft of the 'National Assembly Secretariat (Interim Special Provisions) Ordinance-2024' was approved in the meeting of the Advisory Council. The draft states that for the interim period, all administrative and financial powers of the Parliament Secretariat such as creation and abolition of posts, determination and reduction-increase of the number of officers and employees, preparation of the annual budget, promotion to the third grade and above, all matters related to amendment of the appointment rules, and all other matters (except for the responsibilities related to parliamentary work as per Article 74 of the Constitution) have been entrusted to the Parliamentary Affairs Advisor (Asif Nazrul). The draft proposes to give other financial and administrative powers to the Secretary of the Parliament Secretariat. 

The draft law also proposes to form an interim Parliament Secretariat Commission with the Parliamentary Affairs Advisor as the chairman. It is to be noted that according to the existing law of the National Parliament Secretariat, some of the responsibilities of the National Parliament Secretariat such as creation and abolition of posts, determination and reduction-increase of the number of officers and employees, preparation of the annual budget, etc. are performed by the Speaker in consultation with the Parliament Secretariat Commission. 

The reason for the initiative of this ordinance is that the President dissolved the 12th National Parliament after the then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina left the country on August 5 in the face of the mass uprising of students and the public. Later, the Speaker of the 12th National Parliament, Shirin Sharmin Chowdhury, also resigned. In the absence of the Speaker, problems are arising in the daily, administrative and financial work of the Parliament Secretariat, including other matters. Incidentally, according to the law, the Speaker of the Parliament is the administrative head of the Parliament Secretariat. 

According to BSS, in response to a question from journalists, Press Secretary Shafiqul Alam said that the government does not see the movement being carried out by the workers of the ready-made garment sector as a conspiracy. After the mass uprising in the country, many factory owners have fled, as a result of which those factories are not able to pay salaries. There is a movement there. There were movements in some such factories before. He mentioned that the government does not see this movement as an attempt to create any kind of instability. 

Shafiqul Alam said that at the moment, 99 percent of the factories in the ready-made garment sector are operational.

Headline_English: Gambhir feels batsmen have forgotten how to bat in Tests because of T20s
Content_Enlish:
Batsmen have forgotten defensive cricket in Tests due to T20 cricket. India coach Gautam Gambhir said this at a press conference today ahead of the third and final Test against New Zealand. 

The third Test of the India-New Zealand series will begin tomorrow at Wankhede. New Zealand is leading the three-match series 2-0. 

This is the first time New Zealand has won a Test series on Indian soil. India's star-studded batting has suffered in the first two Tests. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli could not fight to fight for the team's needs. India was all out for 46 runs in the first Test in Bangalore. Gambhir feels that the defensive mentality that is needed to survive at the crease for a long time in Test cricket has been affected by the aggressive batting of T20s. 

Gautam Gambhir and Rohit Sharma inspect the Wankhede pitch a day before the start of the Mumbai Test 
Gautam Gambhir and Rohit Sharma inspect the Wankhede pitch a day before the start of the Mumbai Test AFP 
The Indian coach said, 'Defense is the foundation of batting in Test cricket. It is linked to playing on flat wickets in T20s. Other teams are also suffering from this problem. Because, the more T20s are played, the less everyone will defend.' 

Read more 
Kohli returns to captaincy again 
31 October 2024 
Kohli returns to captaincy again 
India's field is spin-friendly. India also has star spinners like Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja in the team. But New Zealand defeated India in the second Test in Pune with India's 'weapon'. Kiwi spinner Mitchell Santner took 13 wickets in the 113-run win. Analysts have said that the Indian team's batsmen are not capable of playing against the opponent's spin. But Gambhir does not agree with this statement. 

In Gambhir's words, 'I don't think so. Sometimes you have to give credit to the opponent's team. Mitchell Santner was exceptional in the last match. But we will work hard. We will improve further. I don't think our skills against spin have decreased.' 

Read more 
India calls 35 bowlers in the nets to avoid a blunder 
30 October 2024 
India calls 35 bowlers in the nets to avoid a blunder 
India lost the second Test in Pune in three days. This is their first series loss at home in a decade. India lost after winning 18 consecutive series at home. After the series against New Zealand, Rohit Sharma's men will fly to Australia. There they will face the hosts in a five-match Test series. The first Test begins in Perth on November 22. 

Gambhir said his players are determined to ensure that New Zealand does not get a whitewash, saying, "We should feel bad if we lose at home or away. We will improve from this bad feeling. Points are important in the World Test Championship and there is no such thing as a rule-based match in Test cricket now. We should win this Test. We can fly to Australia with a win."

Headline_English: If elections are held quickly, the work of changing the state will also be done quickly: Mirza Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
The state is not functioning in the current structure and needs to be changed, says BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. He says the reforms undertaken by the interim government are time-consuming. Reforms will not be possible without the approval and support of the people. Therefore, the sooner the elections are held, the sooner the work of changing the state will be done. 

Mirza Fakhrul said these words in his speech as the chief negotiator at a discussion meeting organized to mark the 52nd founding anniversary of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD). The meeting was organized by the JSD at the National Press Club in the capital on Thursday afternoon. 

The BNP Secretary General also explained why BNP wants early elections. He said that no one can represent the people except the elected government. Therefore, he believes that if reforms are to be made, the people will be needed. They will have to get them approved in parliament. They will talk, debate, pass and they will have to accept and implement them. Therefore, the sooner the elections are held, the sooner the work of changing the state will be done. 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir further said that attempts are being made to thwart the revolution. Demands have started coming from various quarters. No one has made these demands before, but now they are coming. 

Stating that BNP is a liberal democratic party, not a revolutionary political party, the BNP Secretary General said that the party wants liberal democracy - this is the main point. Therefore, if someone thinks that BNP will become revolutionary overnight, it is not possible. If the democratic system can be implemented properly, a good situation will be created there. 

'Still concerned' 
Stating that there is trust in the interim government, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that everyone respects and respects the interim government's chief advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus. He will be successful. He himself will do everything to protect his reputation. 

Still, expressing concern, the BNP Secretary General said, "When do I get worried, when something goes wrong there (in the interim government)?" He hopes that the advisors in the interim government will not say or do anything that will create confusion in the public mind. 

Recently, Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Advisor AF Hasan Arif said that the five-year term for running the state should be four years instead of the five years specified in the constitution. 

Criticizing the advisor's statement, Mirza Fakhrul said, "This is not what he (Hasan Arif) is supposed to say. The government has formed a commission, that commission will make proposals, the people will accept the proposals. Then it will be decided whether it will be four years or five years." 

'The market situation is not good' 
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said, "The market situation is not very good. The prices of rice, pulses, oil, and salt have increased considerably. Politicians are not talking about this issue." This should also be discussed. Not to embarrass the government. Those who want to loot money through syndicates must be resisted. 

Stating that the people of Bangladesh believe in non-communalism, the BNP Secretary General said, Hindus, Buddhists, and Christians have always been working together since 1971. Recently, it is seen that an attempt is being made to organize and unite the people of a community and launch a big movement. Which is somewhat similar to what India says about the revolution in Bangladesh. He also mentioned that politicians need to be aware of this. 

Mirza Fakhrul alleged that an attempt is being made to belittle the Liberation War. He also warned that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has 'no forgiveness'. 

'The coup has not yet been able to provide relief' 
JSD President ASM Abdur Rab presided over the discussion meeting on the anniversary. He believes that if they want to establish party rule without reforms, there will be another student-public uprising in the country. 

Mahmudur Rahman (Manna), president of Nagorik Oikya, believes that the interim government should discuss with political parties what kind of reforms it wants. The political crisis must be resolved politically. 

Saiful Haque, general secretary of the Revolutionary Workers Party of Bangladesh, said that the uprising has not yet provided relief. He cited the 'fire' in the market, concerns about the safety of life and property, and various types of unstable behavior as the reasons for this. 

Jonayed Saki, chief coordinator of the Mass Solidarity Movement, believes that the fascist power structure still remains. If this structure does not change, democracy will not come to the country in the future. 

Sheikh Rafiqul Islam, convener of the Bhashani Anusari Parishad, and many others spoke at the meeting moderated by JSD Senior Joint General Secretary Kamal Uddin Patwari.

Headline_English: Jamaat Ameer meets with ambassadors of three European countries
Content_Enlish:
The ambassadors of three European countries, Norway, Denmark and Sweden, who are posted in Bangladesh, met with Jamaat-e-Islami Amir Shafiqur Rahman. They met in a breakfast meeting at the residence of Norwegian Ambassador Haakon Arold Gulbrandsen in the capital's Gulshan on Monday morning. 

The meeting was attended by Danish Ambassador Mr. Christian Breks Moller and Swedish Ambassador Nicolas Weeks, as well as Norwegian Deputy Head of Mission Marian Rabe Navelsrud. 

Later, Jamaat-e-Islami issued a press release stating that the meeting, held in a very cordial atmosphere, was excellent and satisfactory. During this time, issues related to Bangladesh's interests were discussed with the ambassadors of Norway, Denmark and Sweden. In particular, democracy and electoral system in Bangladesh figured in the discussion. They have practical experience in this regard as the proportional representation system currently exists in Norway, Denmark and Sweden. In the light of that experience, they presented their suggestions for introducing the proportional representation system in Bangladesh. 

Jamaat-e-Islami said that the ambassadors of Norway, Denmark and Sweden have expressed optimism about the development, progress and continued overall cooperation with Bangladesh. 

The meeting was attended by the party's Nayeb Amir Syed Abdullah Md. Taher and Central Executive Council member Md. Selim Uddin along with the Jamaat Amir.

Headline_English: Leave the luxury of Bangabhaban and find your own path: Hasnat Abdullah to the President
Content_Enlish:
President Md. Hasnat Abdullah, one of the coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, said to President Md. Shahabuddin, "There is still time, leave the luxury of Bangabhaban and find your own way. We do not accept the constitution of the fascist murderer Sheikh Hasina; but you have broken the oath of that constitution. If you think that you will rehabilitate the fascist murderer Sheikh Hasina, then you are thinking wrong. The rehabilitation of the fascist murderer Sheikh Hasina will never happen in this Bengal. However, this murderer Sheikh Hasina must come to Bengal, she will be brought to justice, she will have to hang on the gallows." 

Hasnat Abdullah said these words at a rally at the foot of the Raju statue of Dhaka University on Monday evening. The rally was held after a torchlight procession on the campus initiated by the anti-discrimination student movement demanding a ban on Chhatra League. 

The anti-discrimination student movement held a torchlight procession on the Dhaka University campus on Monday evening demanding the banning of Chhatra League. 
The anti-discrimination student movement held a torchlight procession on the Dhaka University campus on Monday evening demanding the banning of Chhatra League. Photo: Prothom Alo 
Hasnat asked Legal Advisor Asif Nazrul and Home Affairs Advisor Jahangir Alam Chowdhury at the gathering, ‘If students have to stand at Raju Bhaskar after two and a half months to ban and arrest Chhatra League, then what is your job?’ He said, ‘Students are being harassed and tortured by Chhatra League at every level. Asif Sir, I draw your attention. If you cannot bring every leader and worker of Chhatra League under arrest very soon, then you are betraying the blood of the martyrs and the injured. Whether Chhatra League is relevant in post-24 Bangladesh or not, the decision was made on July 15. The future of Chhatra League and Awami League was buried on August 5. No matter how much they conspire across the border in India, the rehabilitation of fascist forces will not happen in Bangladesh. Chhatra League must be banned as soon as possible. They must be brought under the law as soon as possible.’ 

Hasnat Abdullah said to the members of the advisory council and police officers, ‘If you think that your posts are essential, then you are thinking wrong. Sheikh Hasina also considered herself essential. The students and citizens of Bengal have found an alternative. The way the police and administration are behaving uncooperatively, if you think that Chhatra League will join hands with the fascist murderer Sheikh Hasina and that your role is essential, then you are thinking wrong. We will not hesitate to find an alternative for you immediately. If necessary, we will form a National Resistance Force. There is still time, the interim government must be given administrative support.’ 

At this time, Hasnat also criticized some media outlets. He said, ‘The pens that have written in favor of Sheikh Hasina for the last 16 years have been reactivated. The spines that were sold to Sheikh Hasina in exchange for slavery are trying to straighten up again. The media that strengthened the fascist Sheikh Hasina is also rising again. Such media was buried on August 5. Their rehabilitation in Bangladesh is never possible.

Headline_English: Army Chief meets with Canadian officials, emphasizes visa facilitation and defense cooperation
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh and Canada have discussed ways to explore new horizons to strengthen bilateral relations in a multifaceted way. 

Bangladesh has highlighted the importance of visas for serving and former military officers, as well as facilitating student visas for Bangladeshi students. 

The talks have also paved the way for expanding defense cooperation, including training exchanges between military institutions. 

These issues were discussed during Bangladesh Army Chief General Waqar-uz-Zaman's visit to Canada. 

The army chief arrived in the capital Ottawa on Wednesday and was welcomed by Ajit Singh, Director of the Privy Council Office of Canada and Canadian High Commissioner to Bangladesh. 

Both the army chief and the high commissioner discussed visa-related issues for all Bangladeshi citizens. 

During the visit, the Bangladesh Army Chief met with Canada's Vice Chief of Defence Staff Lieutenant General Stephen R. Kelsey and Salma Zahid MP, Vice-Chair of the Canada-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship Group and Member of the Standing Committee on Citizenship and Immigration. 

Canadian Member of Parliament Salma Zahid met with General Waqar-uz-Zaman yesterday morning and discussed matters of mutual interest. 

General Waqar-uz-Zaman highlighted the importance of facilitating and expediting visas for Bangladeshi students, including student visas, for serving and former military officers. He highlighted the priority of the interim government on youth development and sought Canada's assistance in facilitating more student visas, citing the mutual benefits of both countries. 

Salma Zahid acknowledged that there are challenges in this regard due to the existing housing crisis in Canada. 

He encouraged Bangladeshi students to apply to designated institutions in Canada for expedited visa processing. He also reiterated his commitment to find solutions to address the current constraints in the admission of foreign students. 

They also discussed the possibility of joint cooperation in educational exchange programs and signing a memorandum of understanding between Canadian and Bangladeshi universities. 

They also discussed the possibility of cooperation in agriculture and infrastructure development. 

General Waqar-uz-Zaman offered to help Canada address its housing crisis. The army chief also mentioned Bangladesh's readiness to assist Canada's healthcare sector, including by sending service providers. 

In a separate meeting with Lieutenant-General Kelsey, General Waqar-uz-Zaman advocated for easing visa processing for both serving and retired Bangladeshi military personnel. According to sources at the Bangladesh High Commission in Canada, he emphasized a systematic approach to issuing visas and proposed to resolve any issues in individual cases through bilateral consultations without generalization or stereotyping. 

The army chief emphasized on enhancing cooperation through officer exchange at the National Defense College (NDC) and Staff Colleges to strengthen the professional development of the military personnel of both countries. 

Bangladesh High Commissioner to Canada Nahida Sobhan, Brigadier General SM Asadul Haque and Major Mohammad Shoaib Rifat Ami participated in both the meetings.

Headline_English: Imran Khan's wife Bushra Bibi released from prison after 9 months
Content_Enlish:
Bushra Bibi, wife of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, was released from prison on Thursday after nearly nine months. Imran Khan's party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) confirmed this information on social media X.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Islamabad High Court (IHC) granted Bushra Bibi bail in a new case related to the sale of state gifts (Toshakhana). Based on that verdict, a special court today ordered her release.

A corruption court in Islamabad sentenced former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran's wife to 14 years in prison on January 31 in the Toshakhana case. At that time, Imran Khan was also sentenced to the same term in the same case. Bushra Bibi was taken into police custody on the same day.

Later, Bushra Bibi was sent to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. Imran Khan has been detained in the same jail since August 5 last year. He was also sent to jail in the Toshakhana case.

Imran and Bushra were arrested in the Toshakhana case on July 13. On the same day, they were acquitted in the Iddat or un-Islamic marriage case. The next day, the imprisoned Imran Khan was ‘arrested’ again in a dozen cases on May 9.

Several charges were brought against Imran and Bushra for selling state gifts worth Rs 14 crore. Imran Khan received these gifts from leaders of various countries during his tenure as Prime Minister from 2018 to 2022, but sold them without depositing them in the state treasury.

Headline_English: Mangrove forest destruction activities must be stopped immediately
Content_Enlish:
The court has ordered an immediate halt to the destruction of mangrove forests in Sonadia Island and its surrounding areas (Ghativhanga, Tajiakata and Hamidar Dia) in Cox's Bazar's Maheshkhali. It has also ordered the uprooting of illegal shrimp farms there. 

A High Court bench comprising Justice Fatema Najib and Justice Sikder Mahmudur Raji issued the order along with a rule on Wednesday after hearing a writ petition. The order has been issued to the Environment Secretary, the Director General of the Department of Environment and the Chief Conservator of Forests and the defendants. The defendants have been asked to submit a report to the court within 90 days on the implementation of the order. 

A report titled 'Awami League leaders cut trees in endangered Sonadia to cultivate fish' and 'Cut more shrimp farms by cutting down para forests' was published in Prothom Alo. Including these two reports in the media, Supreme Court lawyer Md. Rahim Ullah, former chairman of Maheshkhali Upazila Joynal Abedin, three local journalists and six students, along with 12 residents of Maheshkhali, filed the writ petition on September 5. 

Lawyer Mohammad Shishir Monir, accompanied by lawyer Mohammad Saddam Hossain, heard the writ petition in the court. Deputy Attorney General Nur Muhammad Azmi and Akhtar Hossain Md. Abdul Wahab appeared for the state. 

Later, lawyer Mohammad Shishir Monir told Prothom Alo that the defendants have been ordered to sow mangrove seeds in Sonadia Island and the surrounding areas and take action against the miscreants who destroyed the mangrove forest according to the law. He said that Sonadia Island and the surrounding areas are covered in mangrove forests. In 1999, the government declared Sonadia Island as an ecologically critical area. Recently, reports were published in various national dailies that illegal shrimp farms are being built by destroying mangrove forests on this island and its surrounding areas (Ghativhanga, Tajiakata and Hamidar Dia). The writ petition was filed after the administration took no visible action in this regard.

Headline_English: National Liberation Council demands President's resignation
Content_Enlish:
The National Liberation Council has demanded the resignation of President Md. Shahabuddin. Arguing in support of the demand, they said that President Md. Shahabuddin made two kinds of statements about the resignation of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. 

In a statement sent to the media today, Friday, the National Liberation Council has also called on the interim government to announce the election schedule without taking much time. 

The statement sent by National Liberation Council President Badruddin Umar and Secretary Faizul Hakim said that during the student uprising on August 5, President Md. Shahabuddin had said in his address to the nation on television and in the media that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's resignation had been accepted. But recently, in an interview with Manab Zamin newspaper editor-in-chief Matiur Rahman Chowdhury, the President said that he had heard; but he did not have any documentary evidence of the resignation of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Through this statement of the President, he committed a moral lapse. After that, he cannot continue as President. 

The statement further said that during a mass uprising, the existing law does not apply. At that time, what has emerged as a historical necessity will continue. Historical necessity moves forward ignoring the existing law. 

The National Liberation Council believes that if the interim government takes too long in the name of reform, it will not be acceptable to the people. In this context, the statement said that the interim government should immediately announce the election period, giving priority to returning the people's voting rights and returning power to elected representatives.

Headline_English: 130 Israeli soldiers will no longer go to war in Gaza
Content_Enlish:
Even after Hamas launched an attack on Israel on October 7 last year, reservist Yotam Vilk was not called up for military service. However, he volunteered to fight for Israel. He then spent 230 days with Israeli soldiers in Gaza. The war had a profound impact on his life. But now he does not want to go to war anymore. 

After serving a second stint with Israeli soldiers in Gaza this summer, Yotam is refusing to go there. He says he will not go again if the government calls him. He believes that in some cases military action in Gaza was necessary. But it should have been as a way to find a diplomatic solution that could help the peace effort. He now believes that the massive destruction in Gaza has made life even more difficult for Palestinians and the hostage release have been made more difficult. The Netanyahu government does not want to achieve peace there. 

On October 9, Yotam, along with 130 Israeli irregulars, sent an open letter to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, saying they would no longer work for the government unless an agreement was signed to end the Gaza war and free the 101 hostages held by Hamas. 
The letter added, “For many of us, the line has already been crossed. For others, it is nearing its end. We are writing this letter with a broken heart to resign from this service.” 

Yotam had already crossed the line. But the decision was not easy for him to make. 

The irregular Israeli soldier felt that if he did not withdraw from the war, he would be part of another occupation war in Gaza. No matter how much Netanyahu said, he had doubts about Netanyahu’s intentions in Gaza. Netanyahu’s cabinet and right-wing ministers were talking about building Israeli settlements in Gaza. 

"They have put me in a terrible situation," says Yotam Vilk. "I feel betrayed by my own government." 

Yotam is not alone. Mark Kress, like him, served 66 days on the Lebanese border. Now he thinks he has had enough. He says he has had trouble adjusting since returning home. He suffers from depression.

Headline_English: Mahmudullah to bid farewell to T20s tomorrow
Content_Enlish:
He said goodbye to Test cricket in July 2021. It happened in a very dramatic way in the series against Zimbabwe. This time, there will be no more drama. Mahmudullah is going to officially announce his retirement from T20s tomorrow, Tuesday in Delhi. He will announce that the current series against India is his last T20 series. 

That means that if all goes well, Mahmudullah is going to play the last T20 match of his career on October 12 in Hyderabad. Before that, he will also play in the second T20 against India in Delhi the day after tomorrow. 
Sources say that Mahmudullah had already decided to say goodbye to T20 cricket in the India series. He has finally informed the top brass of the BCB about his decision in this regard. The BCB has also welcomed his decision to leave the field. 

It is learned that the 39-year-old experienced cricketer will announce his retirement from T20s at a press conference tomorrow, ahead of the second T20 in Delhi. Mahmudullah could not be reached on WhatsApp despite attempts to contact him on this matter.
