Mahmudullah made his T20 debut against Kenya in Nairobi in September 2007. Since then, Mahmudullah has played a maximum of 139 T20Is for Bangladesh. He has scored 2395 runs at a strike rate of 117.74, with an average of 23.48. 

He led the Bangladesh team in 43 T20Is between 2018 and 2022, and under his captaincy, the Bangladesh team played in the 2021 Emirates World Cup. As captain, Mahmudullah has won 16 T20Is and lost 26. Although captain Mahmudullah has the same number of wins as Shakib, Shakib has won 16 fewer matches (39) than him.

Headline_English: Durga Puja will be held smoothly this time: Home Affairs Advisor
Content_Enlish:
Home Affairs Advisor Lieutenant General (Retd.) Md. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury said that there is no security risk in Durga Puja this time. He said that the puja will be held without any hindrance this time. 

The Home Affairs Advisor said these things in response to questions from journalists after visiting the Durga Puja pavilion at Ramna Kali Mandir in the capital on Sunday afternoon. Stating that the army, navy and air force have been deployed for the security of Durga Puja, Jahangir Alam Chowdhury said, "This time, you will not face any obstacles anywhere." 

The Home Affairs Advisor said that the interim government has taken various steps to organize Durga Puja smoothly and peacefully. He said that eight-point instructions have been sent by the ministry to each puja pavilion. Those instructions have been sent to the divisional commissioner, deputy inspector general, district commissioner, police superintendent, upazila executive officer, acting police officer and everyone in the administration. I hope you will be able to celebrate this puja without any hindrance. 

Jahangir Alam said that everyone's cooperation is needed to make the puja without any hindrance. Volunteers have been appointed by the puja committee. They will be on duty at the puja mandap 24 hours a day. He hopes that they will not disappear at midnight. 

In response to a question about whether the communal attacks that have taken place in the last 15 years will be judged or not, the Home Advisor said that those involved in the misdeeds will definitely face justice. 

Aparna Roy Das, convener of the autumn Durga Puja celebration council of Sri Sri Ramna Kali Mandir, was present at the time. She is the marginal manpower development secretary of the BNP central committee. 

In response to a question from journalists, Aparna Roy Das said that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has fled to India. She wants to raise the issue of communal riots to the people by inciting them from India. For the last 15 years, Hindus in this country have been insecure.

Headline_English: Another case filed in Khagrachari teacher's beating to death
Content_Enlish:
Another case has been filed in the case of the teacher being beaten to death in Khagrachhari. At least 500 people have been named as accused in it, including 10 students of the institution, said Abdul Baten Mridha, officer-in-charge of Khagrachhari Sadar Police Station. Khagrachhari Sadar Police Station Sub-Inspector Mizanur Rahman filed the case as the plaintiff on Friday. 

The accused in the case are Nimanta Tripura (22), Tunshu Chakma, Sajeeb Chakma (19), Pranoy Chakma (19), Kos Chakma (21), Tintu Chakma (19), Amlan Tripura (20), Icon Chakma (20), Newton Marma (20) and Anil Chakma (19). Among them, Sajeeb, Pranoy and Kos are students of Technical School and College. 

The case file states that a teacher Sohel Rana was beaten up in the principal's room of a technical school and college after accusing a student of rape and was then locked in the bathroom. At that time, 400 to 500 riotous people and students entered the institution and vandalized it and beat up teacher Sohel Rana and left him in the principal's office. When the people and students went to rescue him, they attacked the police with country-made weapons. Five policemen, including the Assistant Superintendent of Police and the OC of Sadar Police Station, were injured in the attack. The case states that a teacher of the institution also incited and incited the students. 

Abdul Baten, OC of Khagrachhari Sadar Police Station, said that a case has been filed against 500 people, including 10 names, and 500 unknown people. Efforts are underway to arrest the accused. Two cases have been filed in this incident before. One of them is for rape and the other is for obstructing government work. 

On October 1, a communal attack took place in Khagrachhari following the beating and murder of teacher Sohel Rana on charges of rape. This led to chases, vandalism, looting and arson in various areas including Mahajanpara and Pankhaiyapara. A four-member investigation committee has been formed into the incident.

Headline_English: City Corporation's power project at Karnaphuli Char cancelled
Content_Enlish:
The proposed project to generate electricity from waste in Char Baklia on the Karnaphuli River in Chittagong has been canceled. Environmental activists have been demanding the cancellation of this project due to fears of biodiversity loss and river pollution. 

The Chittagong City Corporation wanted to build this power plant through a private organization. An application was made to the Land Ministry for allocation of 35 acres of land for this. But the Land Ministry rejected the application. The Chittagong District Administration wrote a letter to the Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) of Boalkhali Upazila on Thursday informing him of the rejection of the proposal and instructing him to take necessary measures. 

The char that rises in the middle of the river, approximately one and a half kilometers upstream from the Shah Amanat Bridge built on the Karnaphuli River in Chittagong, is called Char Baklia. The total area of ​​the char is about 105 acres. The char is listed in the government's Khas Khatian No. 1. An application was made to the Land Ministry in 2023 to provide long-term settlement of Khas land in favor of the Chittagong City Corporation to build a waste treatment plant in this char. When the matter came to light, a six-organizational front, the 'People's Protest Forum for the Protection of Karnaphuli', started a movement demanding the cancellation of the project in March this year. 

Senior Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate of the Chittagong District Administration Md. Rajib Hossain told Prothom Alo that the Ministry of Land has sent a letter informing about the rejection of the project proposal. This is basically the decision of the ministry. The decision was communicated to the concerned parties after monitoring by the district administration. 

The letter from the Ministry of Land to the Chittagong Deputy Commissioner states, 'If a waste treatment plant is established in the Karnaphuli river, there is a possibility of pollution of the river water and there is a risk of serious destruction of the ecological balance including biodiversity. Therefore, the proposal to establish a waste treatment plant on 35 acres of land at Dag No. 544, registered in BS 1, Char Baklia Mouza of Boalkhali Upazila of Chittagong district has been rejected.

Headline_English: Bangabandhu's portrait may be dropped from new paper notes
Content_Enlish:
The interim government will print new banknotes of 20 taka, 100 taka, 500 taka and 1000 taka. These notes are unlikely to have Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's picture. This information has been learned from the Finance Department of the Ministry of Finance. 

Although it is currently being considered not to have Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's picture on these four types of notes, Bangabandhu's picture may be removed from all taka notes in stages. It may take more than a year and a half for the new notes to be released in the market. 

The Finance Department of the Ministry of Finance has requested Bangladesh Bank in a letter on September 29 to submit a detailed design proposal for the new notes. The central bank's Currency and Design Advisory Committee will make the main recommendations on printing the new notes. The committee is chaired by the Deputy Governor-1 of Bangladesh Bank. The committee also includes artists. 

Currently, all paper notes of Bangladesh from 2 taka to 1000 taka have Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's picture. Some notes have his picture on both sides. Metal coins also have his picture. 

The Finance Department's letter has been asked to inform the Finance Department as soon as possible about the design of the new notes in circulation, taking into account the recommendations of the Currency and Design Advisory Committee of Bangladesh Bank. 

On August 3, the Finance Department wrote to Bangladesh Bank regarding the printing method of 20 taka and 100 taka notes. Then, on September 18, the Bangladesh Bank wrote to Finance Secretary Khairuzzaman Majumder, asking whether the content of the previous letter would be correct. In view of this, the Finance Department wrote to Bangladesh Bank informing it of its decision to suspend the decision taken during the last days of the Awami League government. However, even if the new notes come into the market, all the current notes will remain in use. 

After independence, in 1972, for the first time, 1, 5, 10 and 100 taka notes were released in the market. Each of these notes had a picture of Sheikh Mujib. Later, during the different governments, along with the introduction of new notes, the old notes were removed. In 1996, the Awami League came to power and printed 10 and 500 taka notes with Sheikh Mujib's portrait. As per the government's instructions, Bangladesh Bank started the practice of printing Bangabandhu's portrait on all paper notes from then on. 

The country's bank notes or bank currency are notes of 10, 20, 50, 100, 500 and 1000 taka. These are issued by Bangladesh Bank. And 1, 5, 10, 25 and 50 paisa; one taka, two taka and five taka notes and metal coins are the government currency. These are issued by the Finance Department.

Headline_English: How much influence will Iran's regional allies have in a war with Israel?
Content_Enlish:
As the risk of an all-out war between Israel and Iran grows, it is becoming increasingly clear that the United States is supporting its long-time ally Israel in this war. But the question is how much influence Iran’s regional allies will have if the two arch-nemesis countries in the Middle East engage in war. 

Israel launched an indiscriminate attack on Gaza, Palestine, on October 7 last year. Since then, Yemen’s Houthi rebels have been regularly attacking ships associated with Israel in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab el-Mandeb Straits for almost a year, protesting the massacre in Gaza and expressing solidarity with the Palestinians. 

Last week, Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah was killed in an Israeli airstrike in a residential area of ​​the Lebanese capital Beirut. Since then, Israel has been threatened from various parts of the Middle East. 

After the killing of Hassan Nasrallah, Houthi spokesman Yahya Sari threatened Israel in a televised address. He said that Israel would continue its attacks on the besieged Gaza Strip and Lebanon until it stopped its attacks. He also said that the Houthis had carried out drone attacks on Israeli military installations in Tel Aviv and the Israeli port city of Eliya on the Red Sea coast. 

Since Israel killed Hezbollah's longtime leader Hassan Nasrallah, various Shiite armed groups in Iraq and Yemen's Houthi rebels have been carrying out drone and missile attacks on Israel. However, the Israeli military claims that most of the attacks carried out by Iran and its allies have been repelled by their own defenses, as well as with the help of the United States, Jordan and other countries. In addition to these attacks, Israel claims that Iran's missile attack on Tuesday caused minimal damage. 

Lebanon's Hezbollah is considered Iran's most powerful ally 
Lebanese Hezbollah is considered Iran's most powerful ally File photo: AFP 
Israel is trying to downplay the damage caused by Iran's attack, Sina Toussi, a senior fellow at the US-based think tank Center for International Policy, told Al Jazeera. But there is also a positive side to this. By saying that the damage was minimal, it will not bring as much political pressure on Israel and the US to retaliate against Iran. It will also create a situation where there is no need to retaliate on such a large scale. 

Sina Toussi said, "This will make the ceasefire issue important again. If the Biden administration could have stopped it a few months ago, we would not have seen this situation. But we are heading in a direction that will have very terrible consequences. I think neither side wants this war. Iran and its allies are threatening to prevent that from happening. 

Oil will be the big issue 

In such a situation, oil facilities across the region will become the main issue for Iran and its allies, says Middle East expert Sina Tusi. He told Al Jazeera, "If Israel launches a major attack now, the armed groups in Iraq have threatened to retaliate. They said they will also attack oil facilities in the Middle East. And if this disrupts oil exports through the Persian Gulf, it will have an impact on the global oil market, the global economy and Europe." 

Oil facilities have been targeted in the Middle East before. The massive disruption these attacks have caused to the global oil market has also been seen. In September 2019, the Houthi rebels claimed to have carried out drone attacks on two major oil facilities in Saudi Arabia. These facilities belonged to Saudi Aramco, the state-owned oil company of Saudi Arabia. The United States blamed Iran for the attack on the service. 

Another major Iranian power in the Middle East is the various armed Shiite militia groups in Iraq 
Another major Iranian power in the Middle East is the various armed Shiite militia groups in Iraq File photo: Reuters 
The Houthi attack cut oil production by 50 million barrels a day, half of Saudi Aramco's daily oil production or 5 percent of global oil supply. Sina Tusi said, "We saw what the Houthis can do before they reached a ceasefire agreement with Saudi Arabia. We saw the Houthis launch attacks far inside Saudi Arabia before." 

Iraqi armed groups have also threatened Israel and the United States. On Tuesday, these groups threatened to attack US bases if the United States participates in a counterattack against Iran or if Israel uses Iraqi airspace to attack Iran. 

According to Sina Tusi, in addition to Iraq, the US has military bases in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Bahrain. Iran has threatened to use these bases and Iraqi airspace. Tehran has said that these countries will also be considered responsible for attacks against Iran and that their critical infrastructure will also become targets of Iranian attacks. 

How capable are the groups of attacking Israel 

Andreas Craig, an associate professor at the School of Security Studies at King's College London and an analyst of geopolitical risks, said that the armed groups in Iraq do not have the ability to directly attack Israel from a distance. In addition, their arsenal is not as rich as that of Hezbollah and the Houthis. These weapons were created to confront the US-led NATO forces in the Iraq war. According to him, these were mainly used by guerrillas and have been used in unconventional warfare. These weapons will not have much effect in a war with Israel. 

The geopolitical analyst says that Hezbollah, on the other hand, has a global network. They are active in various regions from Saudi Arabia to West Africa. This makes them much more dangerous for Israel. Because they have the ability to attack Israel from different countries. In addition, the missile or drone attacks that are reported from Iraq are carried out by Iranians in Iraq, not by armed groups in Iraq.

Headline_English: History will be rewritten without any bias: Advisor Nahid Islam
Content_Enlish:
The history of Bangladesh will be rewritten in a new way, and there will be a new perspective, said Information and Broadcasting Advisor Nahid Islam. He said this in response to a question while informing reporters of the decision to cancel eight national days at the Secretariat today, Wednesday. 

In response to the question, the Information Advisor said, 'We are not erasing March 7 from history. We are not erasing the importance of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman from history. Which is part of history, history will be rewritten in a new way, there will be a new perspective. But the practice of celebrating it as a day has a politics. The government of mass uprising cannot allow that politics to continue.' 

In response to a question from journalists whether this government considers Bangabandhu the Father of the Nation, Nahid Islam said, 'Of course not.' At that time, in response to a question like 'Every country has a Father of the Nation...We will not have a Father of the Nation', Nahid Islam said, 'Not just one person, but many people have contributed to the history of the struggle of our land. Our history did not just start in 1952, we have a long history of struggle. There is the anti-British struggle, the struggle of the people of this land in 1947, the struggle of 1971, the struggle of 1990, the struggle of 2004. We have Sher-e-Bangla AK Fazlul Haque, Hossain Shaheed Suhrawardy, Abul Hashim, Jogen Mandal, Maulana Bhashani—we have the struggle of many people here. We think that there is not one Father of the Nation, but many Founding Fathers; due to whose contributions this land, this state, we got independence. Therefore, we do not want to limit it to one group, one person.’ 

Nahid Islam said, ‘The versatility of our history, there are various dimensions, which the Awami League has denied for so long. They have always denied the contribution of Maulana Bhashani. Yet he is one of the founders of the Awami League. They did not put him in history. Now it has to be brought to history.’ 

While explaining the reason for canceling the eight national days, the information advisor said, various party days of the Awami League have been imposed as national days. Those and the days that were considered unimportant have been canceled. They are actually completely Awami League and contain a fascist ideology and that ideology and these days were established to practice that ideology. 

Later, if it is felt that more such days need to be canceled or there are some unimportant days, then they can also be canceled, the information advisor said. He said, new days can also be added. For example, Bangladesh got new independence within the July coup, naturally some days will be added here too. 

Regarding the cancellation of the historic March 7 as a national day, Nahid Islam said, ‘March 7 is an important day, an important speech was made that day. But we do not think that it carries enough importance to be a national day. Many things may be part of our history. But the Awami League has actually ruined history. As a result, many things cannot be taken at the moment, such as March 7. 

Advisor Nahid Islam said, "The Awami League has ruined Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. The way he has started worshipping him by making his idol has become part of the fascist ideology (ideology). We cannot keep this fascist tendency in a government, a new Bangladesh, which was formed through a mass uprising." 

Advisor Nahid Islam said, "The Awami League was in power as a fascist party. They were in power by taking away people's voting rights, committing disappearances, murders, and genocide. ... Whoever called him the Father of the Nation, whoever declared the National Day, that will not continue in this new Bangladesh. We want to shape Bangladesh in a new way. As a result, we will have to bring a new perspective on history." 

The information advisor also said, "If you consider everything done by the Awami League to be national! A government without votes has no legitimacy. A lot has been done during that time. All these things need to be restructured and reevaluated.’ 

In response to a question about the cancellation of Constitution Day, Nahid Islam said, the Constitution did not come into effect from that day (November 4). The day the Constitution came into effect was considered important. Therefore, it seems that there is no need to give special importance to November 4 as a day. The information advisor also believes that there is no need for so many national days.

Headline_English: Israel finalizes plan to attack Iran
Content_Enlish:
Israel has finalized plans for a counterattack on the country in response to Iran's missile attack. The US media outlet CNN reported this information on Wednesday, citing a relevant source. However, the source did not give any details. 

CNN contacted the Israeli Ministry of Defense to find out about this. However, the report did not mention anything about what the ministry said. 

The source said that Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have assured the United States that a limited retaliatory attack may be carried out on Iranian military facilities instead of oil and nuclear facilities. 

CNN, citing multiple US sources, also reported that Israel may attack Iran before the US presidential election on November 5. US officials believe that the attack may take place this month. 

Incidentally, Iran launched about 200 missiles at Israel on October 1. Tehran said the attack was in retaliation for the assassination of Lebanese Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah and Ismail Haniyeh, the head of the political wing of the Palestinian resistance group Hamas. 

Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has since warned Iran that it would face consequences for the attack. Last week, Defense Minister Yoav Gallant said that an Israeli attack on Iran would be “fierce, specific and surprising.” 

Meanwhile, Al Jazeera reported that Iran has warned Israel of a “severe and painful” response if it retaliates. In a phone call on Tuesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres that Tehran was ready to give a “severe and painful” response if Israel attacks its country. 

Mayor killed in Lebanon attack 

Amid concerns over Iran's attacks, Israel has stepped up attacks on Gaza and Lebanon in Palestine. Today, Israel attacked the municipal building of the southern Lebanese city of Nabatieh. Five people were killed, including the city's mayor, Ahmed Kahil. Among the dead was the municipality's media officer, Mohammed Salim Bitar. 

Meanwhile, Hezbollah is responding to the Israeli attack by firing rockets. Several rocket attacks have been carried out, especially targeting the northern part of the country. 90 rockets were fired at 9 pm local time on Tuesday. 

The Israeli army said that at least one of the rockets coming from Lebanon hit the ground in the northern Israeli city of Haifa. However, no casualties were reported in the incident. The previous day, 115 rockets were fired from Lebanon into Israel.

Headline_English: 12-party alliance spokesperson urges Jamaat not to create division
Content_Enlish:
The spokesperson of the 12-party alliance, Bangladesh LDP Secretary General Shahadat Hossain, has urged Jamaat-e-Islami not to create any division between the nationalist and Islamic forces. He said, the people consider it undesirable to create misunderstandings and distance between the two major political parties that fought against the dictatorship after the victory on August 5. 

Shahadat Hossain said this in response to a question at a press conference titled ‘The country’s current situation and people’s expectations’ at the National Press Club this Wednesday morning. 

The spokesperson of the 12-party alliance said, ‘42 political parties have held simultaneous movements. Jamaat has never been in simultaneous movements. We want a unity of nationalist and Islamic forces. We who have held movements against the dictatorship, let us remain united. Let there be no division and confusion among us. This is very important for the democratic spirit, to show respect for the blood of the martyrs. 

Shahadat Hossain said, "Our special message to Jamaat is that Jamaat-e-Islami went to the elections with the Awami League in 1986. The people did not accept that. Jamaat went to the elections separately in 1996. This has affected both the BNP and Jamaat parties, and a fascist government has been established in the country. Otherwise, the Awami League could not have come to power in 1996. Jamaat is responsible for this. Our appeal to Jamaat is that we, who have shed blood to bring down the dictatorship, should walk the path together." 

Syed Ehsanul Huda, the coordinator of the 12-party alliance and chairman of the Bangladesh National Party, presented the 14-point proposal of the 12-party alliance at the press conference. Notable among them are the removal of the fascist allies working in the administration, the new fit list for the appointment of district administrators and the cancellation of the appointments of district administrators against whom allegations have been made, and the cancellation of all contractual appointments from the time of fascism. 

Jatiya Party Chairman Mustafa Jamal Haider, the head of the 12-party alliance, delivered a welcome speech at the press conference. He said that the victory achieved at the cost of much blood and sacrifice must be consolidated at any cost and the country must be led forward on the path of prosperity through harmony by strengthening the foundation of democracy through necessary reforms. 

Also present at the press conference were Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Secretary General Golam Mohiuddin Ikram, Bikalpadhara Bangladesh Secretary General Shah Ahmed, Jatiya Ganatantrik Party Vice President Rashed Pradhan, Bangladesh Kalyan Party Chairman Shamsuddin Parvez, Islami Oikya Jote Secretary General Abdul Karim, Islamic Party Secretary General Abul Kashem, Progressive Democratic Party (PNP) Chairman Firoz Md. Liton and Naya Ganatantrik Party President MA Mannan.

Headline_English: Israel wants to launch a 'devastating' attack on Iran
Content_Enlish:
Amid tensions with Iran, US President Joe Biden and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke by phone. At the same time, Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant pledged a “fierce, specific and surprising” attack on Iran. 

Biden and Netanyahu spoke for 30 minutes last Wednesday, the first time the two leaders have spoken publicly since last August. 

The call between the two leaders came at a time when Israel’s conflict with Iran and the Iran-backed Hezbollah group has taken a serious turn. There is also no sign of a ceasefire with the Palestinian resistance group Hamas in Gaza. 

The conversation between Biden and Netanyahu was “candid and very productive,” White House press secretary Karine Jean-Pierre told reporters. But she acknowledged that the two leaders had their differences and expressed their opinions in their own way. 

Iran launched a missile attack on Israel last week. There is anxiety in the Middle East about a possible Israeli attack in response to the attack. Iran launched the attack on the country in response to Israeli military provocations in Lebanon. Although in the end, no one was killed in the Iranian attack on Israel. 

After the phone call between Biden and Netanyahu, Defense Minister Yoav Gallant's office released a video statement. In it, the defense minister commented that Iran's attack on October 1 had failed. 

In the video, Gallant said, "Anyone who attacks us will be hit back and will have to suffer the consequences. Our attack will be deadly, specific and above all, shocking. They will not even understand what happened and how it happened. They will see the result." 

Netanyahu also pledged that arch-enemy Iran will suffer the consequences for the missile attack. On the other hand, Tehran has said that any kind of counterattack will cause massive destruction to the opponent. This has raised fears of a wider war in the oil-producing region, which could also draw the United States into the conflict. 

Biden failed to broker a ceasefire in Gaza. Biden's relationship with Netanyahu is strained over the Gaza war and the conflict with Hezbollah. Netanyahu has said he will continue the military campaign until Israel is safe. 

28 killed in Gaza shelter attack 
Al-Jazeera reported that 28 people were killed and 54 injured in an Israeli attack on a school in the Deir al-Balah area of ​​Gaza yesterday. The school was being used as a shelter. People who lost their homes in the Israeli attack took refuge there. 

Witnesses said that the violence of the attack left the bodies of children and women mutilated. This also made it difficult to identify many of them. If relatives can identify the dead by looking at their clothing or other signs, it may be possible to identify them. 

Meanwhile, the Gaza Health Ministry said yesterday that 55 more people were killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza in the past 24 hours. 166 were injured. With this, 42,065 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since October 7 last year. 97,886 were injured. 

In addition, the Israeli army claimed that two Hezbollah commanders were killed in an airstrike in southern Lebanon yesterday. On the other hand, at least 14 people were killed in Israeli attacks in various areas of Lebanon the previous night. Five health workers are among the dead.

Headline_English: US authorities plan to break up Google, targeting Chrome and Android
Content_Enlish:
US officials said they plan to ask the court to force Google to divest from some businesses, focusing on Google's Chrome browser and Android operating system. The officials said the businesses maintain Google's monopoly on online search and information retrieval. 

In a landmark case, a judge ruled in August that Google had created an illegal monopoly. Google accounts for 90 percent of all Internet searches in the United States. The solution the Justice Department is proposing would fundamentally change the way search is conducted, while also cutting Google's revenue and giving rivals the opportunity to expand their businesses. 

The Justice Department could be asked to end Google's practice of pre-installing its search engine on transactions with Google or making it the default on new devices. Google paid Apple and other device makers $26.3 billion in 2021 to pre-install Google's search engine on smartphones and browsers. 

Having the Google search engine as the default on smartphones and browsers makes it easier for Google to maintain its dominance in the market. Google, however, plans to appeal the court's decision. In a blog post, the company said that the officials' proposals favor "radical changes" and "may go beyond the legal issues at stake in this case." 

Google also said that users use its search engine because of its good quality. Not only that, but it also faces competition from Amazon and other websites. Users can even set another search engine as the default if they want. 

Google's parent company Alphabet is the world's fourth-largest company, with a market capitalization of more than $2 trillion. But it has recently faced intense pressure from competitors and US competition authorities. 

In a separate case, a US judge ruled on Monday that Google must open its app store, 'Play,' to competition. It must ensure that Android-based apps from competing sources are available in the Play Store. Google is also under pressure from the Justice Department to break up its web-based advertising business. 

Google wants to further increase its dominance in the world of artificial intelligence. However, the Justice Department says that Google can force Google to allow competitors to use the indexes, data and models that it uses in its general search and artificial intelligence-based search systems. The Justice Department is also considering ensuring that Google cannot make any agreements that could reduce the ability of competitors. 

However, Google says that the proposals being made about artificial intelligence could stall the sector. According to the company, if the government intervenes in this important sector by dragging out investment, distorting incentives and putting shackles on the feet of new business models, it could create great risks. That would come at a time when investment in this sector needs to be encouraged. 

The US Justice Department is expected to submit a detailed proposal on Google to the court by November 20. Google, on the other hand, will have until December 20 to submit its own proposal on how to address the concerns raised by the Justice Department. 

Facebook parent Meta Platform, Amazon.com and Apple have filed separate lawsuits in the US court, alleging that they are operating a monopoly. The idea of ​​breaking up Google has previously received support from smaller rivals such as Yelp and DuckDuckGo.

Headline_English: Intake Properties aims for safe housing
Content_Enlish:
Despite the rapid progress in the housing sector in Bangladesh, gaining the trust of buyers is still a big challenge for many developer companies. Many companies are constantly being added to the list of victims for failing in these areas - timely handover of flats, quality construction and fulfilling customer promises. 

However, Intech Properties Limited stands in contrast to all this. Since the beginning of the business, the company has been handing over flats and apartments within the specified time as promised. The company's Managing Director, M Fakhrul Islam, is taking Intech Properties forward through visionary leadership, contributing to the prosperity of the country's housing sector. M Fakhrul Islam has been conducting business with confidence and reliability even in the extreme recession of the housing sector. As a young entrepreneur, he is paying special attention to restoring confidence in the housing industry and handing over flats as promised to buyers. His keen leadership and foresight have made Intech Properties one of the top housing companies in the country. 

The company has been conducting its activities continuously since its establishment in 2010. Currently, Intech Properties has successfully completed several residential projects in various important locations in Dhaka. The company gives special importance to timely handover of flats, which has helped in gaining the trust of buyers. Keeping in mind the needs of domestic and expatriate buyers, Intech Properties is operating its projects in developed locations. In addition to various offers at various times, the company is also providing the facility of buying flats in installments. 

During the crisis of confidence in the housing sector, Intech Properties Limited is handing over flats while maintaining quality standards on time. As the project is developed in accordance with the rules of RAJUK, buyers are able to invest safely, which is restoring trust.

Headline_English: Farewell meeting of the Russian Ambassador with the Chief Advisor
Content_Enlish:
Russian Ambassador to Bangladesh Alexander V. Montitsky paid a farewell call on the Chief Advisor to the Interim Government, Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus. 
The meeting was held at the Chief Advisor's office in Tejgaon, Dhaka, on Wednesday. During the meeting, Montitsky recalled the eventful period of his three-year tenure as the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Bangladesh. 

The Ambassador briefed the Chief Advisor about the progress of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant and said that they expect the plant to start generating electricity next year. The project is being implemented mainly with Russian financing and technical or expert assistance. 

The meeting discussed the exploration activities of Russian state-owned company Gazprom in Bangladesh, the export of wheat and fertilizer from Russia, and the repayment of the Rooppur project. 

The Chief Advisor appreciated Russia's assistance in the power and energy sectors and Russia's role in supplying wheat and fertilizer to Bangladesh. He said that the Interim Government will resolve the issue of repayment of the Rooppur project. He welcomed more Russian investment in Bangladesh.

Emphasizing the need for both countries to work together, Dr. Yunus said, “We will work together.” 

Lamia Morshed, Senior Secretary to the Principal Advisor on SDGs, and Md. Abul Hasan Mridha, Director General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, were present during the meeting.

Headline_English: Sedition case against Imran and PTI leaders
Content_Enlish:
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan is being held in large-scale protests across the country demanding his release from prison by his party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). Police have filed sedition and terrorism cases in Lahore and Rawalpindi against PTI founder chairman Imran Khan and senior party leaders over the protests in Islamabad. 

The police FIR names senior PTI leaders Hammad Azhar, Salman Akram Raza, Ghulam Mohiuddin, MPA Shahbaz, Musarrat Jamshed Cheema, Sheikh Imtiaz, Ali Imtiaz, and Sabbir Gujar, besides Imran Khan. 

The FIR states that Imran Khan, who is imprisoned in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail, has been given extraordinary privileges. This allows him to communicate with party leaders and workers. The FIR claims that Imran is inciting party leaders and workers to commit violence against the state from inside the prison. As a result, PTI leaders and activists are doing things like raising anti-state slogans and vandalizing. Police constable Bilal was injured in their beating. Police have arrested 16 PTI leaders and activists from the scene. Action is being taken against them. 

In addition to the sedition case, several other cases have been filed against PTI leaders and activists for protesting in Islamabad in violation of Section 144. 

Apart from Islamabad, separate cases have been filed against PTI leaders and activists in Lahore's Millat Park and Hanjarwal police stations. Out of these, ASI Aqil of the police has filed a case against 20 PTI workers in Hanjarwal. Sub-Inspector Hafiz Imran has filed a case against 10 leaders and activists in Millat Park police station. 

Meanwhile, legal action has been taken against PTI leaders and activists in addition to police arrests. Cases have been filed against 300 PTI leaders and activists in Rawalpindi. The names of senior leaders and activists who participated in the protests in Islamabad have been added to the case. 

The case has been registered at Nesarabad police station under the Anti-Terrorism Act. In addition, charges of conspiracy to commit a crime and provocative speech have also been brought. Police say that Imran Khan and important leaders of Rawalpindi have been named in the FIR for aiding and abetting the crime. The case has been sent to the In-Charge Investigation Department for investigation. 

The FIR filed by Police Sub-Inspector Mehboob Rahman states that the PTI chairman and local leaders are planning to overthrow the government and are implementing their agenda through violent means. 

Imran's two sisters on remand 

The police arrested PTI leaders and activists, along with Imran Khan's two sisters, Aleema Khan and Uzma Khan, on charges of terrorism during the protests in Islamabad on Friday. They were taken to court on Sunday and a 20-day remand was sought. The court granted them a one-day remand. In addition, the court sent nine female PTI workers to Adiala Jail on Monday.

Headline_English: Demand to stop Israeli attacks on Palestine and Lebanon
Content_Enlish:
The Left Democratic Alliance held a procession and rally in Chittagong city demanding an end to Israel's genocide in Palestine and Lebanon. The Left Alliance held this program on Monday afternoon, the first anniversary of Israel's invasion of Gaza, Palestine. 

The rally, chaired by Left Democratic Alliance and BSD (Marxist) District Coordinator Shafi Uddin Kabir, was addressed by CPB District Committee President Ashok Saha, BSD District In-charge Al Qaderi, and BSD District Leader Jasim Uddin. 

The speakers at the rally said that the government of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has destroyed the Gaza Strip by killing 42,000 Palestinians in the last 1 year. They have killed Nasrallah, the head of the Lebanese Hezbollah group fighting for Palestine. Currently, they are carrying out genocide in Lebanon by conducting ground operations and air strikes. Israel is continuously attacking Palestine and Lebanon with the support of the US, showing the thumbs up to world public opinion. The warlord Israel needs to be stopped. 

The speakers said that the United Nations is not able to play an effective role in stopping the war. Israel should be brought to justice in an international tribunal for war crimes. It should be expelled from the United Nations. 

After the rally, a protest march started from the old station and ended at the New Market intersection.

Headline_English: Committee formed to monitor harassment cases against journalists
Content_Enlish:
The government has formed an eight-member committee to monitor harassment cases against journalists working in the media. The committee's job will be to monitor various harassment cases against journalists working in the media and inform the authorities about the cases from time to time. This information was given in a notification by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Monday. 

It is worth noting that many journalists have also been accused in various murder cases after the Awami League government fell on August 5 in the student-public uprising. 

The notification said that it is seen that various harassment cases are being filed against journalists working in the media. In order to monitor these cases, a 'Committee on Monitoring Harassment Cases Against Journalists Working in the Mass Media' has been formed with the participation of officials. 

The committee is chaired by the Additional Secretary (Broadcasting) of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The members are the Chief Information Officer of the Directorate of Information, a representative of the Law and Justice Department (of the rank of District Judge), Director General of the Directorate of Film and Publication (DFP), Managing Director of the Bangladesh Journalists Welfare Trust, Director General of the Bangladesh Press Institute and Secretary of the Bangladesh Press Council. The Joint Secretary (Press) of the ministry will be the member-secretary of the committee.

Headline_English: The US economy will suffer a huge blow if Trump wins
Content_Enlish:
The November US presidential election is important for many reasons. It is not just about the survival of American democracy. It is also about the far-reaching economic implications that will affect the future of the rest of the world. American voters are now faced with the choice of which of two different policy objectives to choose. 

Although the Democratic Party’s nominee, Vice President Kamala Harris, has not yet detailed her economic goals and objectives, it is expected that she will maintain the core principles of President Joe Biden’s existing program. Such as maintaining economic competitiveness, protecting the environment (including reducing greenhouse-gas emissions), lowering the cost of living, maintaining a steady growth trajectory, increasing national economic sovereignty and resilience, and reducing inequality. 

In contrast, Donald Trump has no interest in a more just, strong, and sustainable economy. In return, he has promised to give coal and oil companies a “blank check,” which has delighted billionaires like Elon Musk and Peter Thiel. Trump’s policy could be called a “recipe” for making the US economy weaker, less competitive, and more discriminatory. On the one hand, setting goals for sound economic performance and formulating policies to achieve those goals is necessary; on the other hand, having the ability to handle shocks and seize new opportunities is no less important. 

We already have a rough idea of ​​how Trump and Kamala will handle these issues. Trump handled the Covid-19 pandemic very poorly while in office, and more than a million people died in the United States due to his missteps. Any unprecedented situation requires the best science-based decisions to deal with it. Trump’s lack of that science-based consideration is obvious. 

On the other hand, Kamala Harris shows a leadership that makes her seem thoughtful and pragmatic in finding a balanced solution to trade and the economy. We see in Trump an emotional and self-centered mentality that seems to see chaos as a stepping stone and dismisses scientific expertise. 

Consider Trump’s response to the Chinese threat. Trump has said he is proposing to impose tariffs of 60 percent or more on Chinese imports. After making this proposal, any sensible economist should have told Trump that doing so would dramatically increase the cost of goods in the United States. This would not only increase the cost of goods imported directly from China, but also the cost of many domestic products that use Chinese components. This would put a cost burden on low- and middle-income Americans. This would increase inflation. 

Worse still, Trump has gone so far as to threaten the independence of the Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States. If you think about it from that perspective, it makes sense that if Trump were to win another term, the US economy would be in a state of uncertainty. Investment would be in a state of despair. Growth will be hit and inflation will almost certainly rise. 

While populist rhetorical leaders like Trump don’t worry about the investment deficit, he should worry investors at home and abroad. 

Because the explosion of unproductive spending will dramatically increase inflation, reduce economic performance, and increase inequality. If Trump were to take office and repeal the Inflation Reduction Act signed by the Biden administration, it would not only be bad for the environment, but it would also harm a sector that is crucial to the country’s future. Repealing the law would destabilize the pharmaceutical industry. The provisions that have kept the cost of producing drugs down would then be eliminated. That would hurt the health sector. 

If Trump were to roll back the strong competition policies of the Biden-Harris administration, it would further increase inequality in the United States. That would have repercussions for the rest of the world.

Headline_English: AI chatbot made in Bangladesh to be used in Kuwait
Content_Enlish:
Kuwait Telecommunications Company will use AI chatbot and live chat technology developed by Reev Chat, a subsidiary of Bangladeshi multinational software company Reev Systems. The company, which operates the largest 5G network in Kuwait, recently signed an agreement with Reev Chat to improve the quality of its customer service. Reev Systems announced this information in a press release on Thursday. 

The press release said that the AI ​​chatbot, which is a combination of cutting-edge AI (artificial intelligence) and natural language processing (NLP), can answer customer questions instantly. With the NLP facility of the latest technology, the chatbot can provide solutions separately according to specific incidents or problems. As a result, customers of Kuwait Telecommunications Company will receive faster customer service. 

M Rezaul Hasan, CEO of Reev Systems, said, “We are happy to add our AI chatbot to the customer service of Kuwait Telecommunications Company.” We believe our AI technology will enhance the customer connectivity and service quality of Kuwait Telecommunications Company.

Headline_English: No rehabilitation of fascists until full trial
Content_Enlish:
Fascists will not get the opportunity to be rehabilitated in the country until a full trial is held. The interim government has decided to ensure their trial as criminals against humanity. The government will also discourage fascist parties and alliances from holding public programs. 

Youth and Sports Advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan gave this information at a press briefing after the meeting of the Advisory Council of the interim government on Thursday. 

Chief Advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus presided over the meeting of the Advisory Council at the Chief Advisor's office in Tejgaon in the afternoon. This is the fifth meeting of the current Advisory Council. In this meeting of the Advisory Council, held on the one-month anniversary of the student-people's uprising, it was decided to make Ganabhaban, the official residence of the Prime Minister of Bangladesh, a 'July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum'. 

Later in the evening, Youth and Sports Advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan announced the decision of the advisory council meeting at a news briefing at the Foreign Service Academy on Hare Road in the capital. The Chief Advisor's Press Secretary Shafiqul Alam was present at the time. 

Asif Mahmud said, "We have already seen various programs in different places to rehabilitate the defeated fascist forces. Since we are a government formed on the basis of a mass uprising of students and the public, we believe that there is no opportunity to rehabilitate the fascists until full justice is ensured." 

In response to a question from journalists, Asif Mahmud said, "We have left the question to the people whether the fascist political party or political alliance that established fascism in Bangladesh can do politics until full justice is done. However, in terms of holding public programs, the government is thinking about how it will be implemented. That has not been discussed in detail yet. However, we will definitely discourage it. "Measures have been taken for a full trial, the Law Ministry is working. They will be tried as criminals against humanity," he said. The Law Ministry is looking into the matter of trial. The Law Ministry will soon release an outline on how the trial will be conducted. 

The anti-discrimination student movement has been describing the Awami League as a fascist party. 

Responding to a question at the briefing whether the Awami League will be able to run its activities as a party, Asif Mahmud said that the people of the country will decide on this matter. Since the Awami League has committed a genocide in the country, how they will return or whether they will be allowed to return or not, this will be decided by the people of the country. This is the people's decision. 

'July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum' 
Informing that it was decided to make Ganabhaban the 'July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum' in the meeting of the Advisory Council, Advisor Asif Mahmud said that Ganabhaban will be opened to the public. It will be established as the 'July Uprising Memorial Museum' to preserve the memory of the martyrs of the July Uprising and all the injustices and injustices committed during the past fascist period. 

Activities in this regard will begin soon, said Asif Mahmud, adding that the Ganabhaban will be kept in the condition it is in, the way the people have kept it. A museum will be established inside it. So that the memory of the uprising is preserved. A decision has been taken in this regard in the meeting of the advisory council. He said that this museum will be established based on the experiences of different places. Visible steps will be taken in this regard very soon. The Ministry of Public Works and Foreign Affairs will jointly complete the work.

Headline_English: Restructuring of Election Commission and Anti-Corruption Commission is urgent: BNP leader Zahid Hossain
Content_Enlish:
BNP Standing Committee member AZM Zahid Hossain has demanded the restructuring of the Election Commission (EC) and the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) supported by the Sheikh Hasina government. He said that it is very important to restructure the Election Commission and the Anti-Corruption Commission now. Because, beneficiaries of the previous government have been placed in these two institutions. It is the government's responsibility to weed out these beneficiaries. 

AZM Zahid Hossain said these things at a press conference of the party's relief collection committee at the BNP central office in Nayapaltan in the capital on Wednesday afternoon. 

Alleging that the Election Commission was a 'supplier' of the Sheikh Hasina government, this newly appointed BNP Standing Committee member said, 'You have seen that the one who has contributed the most to strengthening the previous regime (government) of this country is this fake Election Commission. They are a party-slave, supplier commission. Even if that fascist government falls, the Election Commission they formed is still sitting in its place. 

Zahid Hossain further said, "This commission is still sitting shamelessly. I think this Election Commission should come to its senses. To avoid the wrath of the people, it should resign and give this government a chance to form a new Election Commission." 

At the same time, criticizing the Anti-Corruption Commission, Zahid Hossain said, "The commissioners and officials of the ACC who are still sitting are beneficiaries of the previous government. I will tell the interim government that it is very important to restructure the ACC. Because, the then opposition party and the people of the country were tortured by placing relatives of those who fell in the ACC and their beneficiaries. Today, to bring back the money laundered, to bring back the money looted from banks, to expose corruption, a strong Anti-Corruption Commission is needed." 

Zahid Hossain said that people from different levels, including the BNP and its affiliates, are providing relief materials to the affected people according to their ability. As of last night, relief materials and cash worth more than 130 million taka have been distributed to the affected people. 

BNP Relief Collection Committee Convener Zahid Hossain said, "We are not the government. The government is doing its own activities. Along with the government, BNP as a political party is carrying out this relief program under the advice of party chairperson Khaleda Zia and the specific instructions of our acting chairman Tarique Rahman." 

BNP Chairperson's Advisory Council member Abdus Salam, Joint Secretary General and Relief Collection Committee member secretary Abdus Salam Azad, members Mir Sarafat Ali, Taiful Islam were present at the press conference.

Headline_English: US formally accuses Russia of trying to interfere in US election
Content_Enlish:
The United States is going to formally accuse Russia of trying to interfere in the upcoming US presidential election. This information was reported in US media reports on Wednesday. 

According to a CBS report, President Joe Biden's administration may officially make various announcements today regarding the Kremlin's efforts to influence US public opinion in the upcoming presidential election. The media outlet said that several measures against Russia, including criminal charges, may be announced. 

Another US media outlet, CNN, reported that the measures that the Biden administration is going to announce will be based on the Russian state-owned media outlet RT, which was previously known as Russia Today. 

Today, it is reported that US Attorney General Merrick Garland may announce sanctions or other legal action regarding Russia's attempts to interfere in the US election. 

US officials have warned that since Russia's interference in 2016, attempts by various foreign adversaries to interfere in the US election have been increasing. 

Last June, a group of hackers affiliated with the Iranian government accessed the online data of former US President and upcoming Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump's campaign and leaked some internal documents related to it.

Headline_English: Implementation of CEDAW Charter is necessary to eliminate discrimination against women: Social Prevention Committee
Content_Enlish:
The Social Resistance Committee has demanded the full ratification and implementation of the CEDAW Convention to eliminate discrimination against women. This demand was made at a press conference organized by the Social Resistance Committee on the occasion of the International CEDAW Day today, Tuesday. 

A press release said that the press conference titled 'We want the full ratification and implementation of the CEDAW Convention to eliminate discrimination against women' was organized at the Zahur Hossain Chowdhury Auditorium of the National Press Club. We Can Alliance National Coordinator Zinat Ara Haque presented a written statement on behalf of the Social Resistance Committee. 

In response to a question at the press conference, Bangladesh Mahila Parishad President Fawzia Moslem said that the main basis of the CEDAW Convention is to ensure the state's responsibility to establish equality between women and men. Since the Bangladesh government still has reservations on Article 2 of the CEDAW Convention, real equality is not being ensured. In this case, the state's responsibility is essential. It is important to monitor what steps the state is taking to fulfill its responsibility. He further said that the ongoing social movement for the full ratification of the CEDAW Charter to establish equality between women and men must ensure the participation of all. The youth must come forward for this work. The country must be taken forward with the spirit of the Liberation War. 

Present at the press conference were Maleka Banu, General Secretary of Bangladesh Mahila Parishad, Nurun Nahar Begum of ActionAid, Mahbub Akhtar of Nagorik Udyog, Shahida Parveen of Trade Union Center, Shahida Ferdous of Steps Towards Development, Gender Expert Ferdousi Sultana, Samsun Nahar of Mass Literacy Campaign, and others. 

The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women is abbreviated as CEDAW. 

The CEDAW Charter was adopted by the United Nations on December 18, 1979, with the aim of eliminating all forms of discrimination between women and men and establishing equal rights. Various countries signed the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women on 1 March 1980. The Convention came into force on 3 September 1981. The Government of Bangladesh signed and ratified the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women on 24 September 1984. Bangladesh has maintained reservations to Articles 2 and 16 (1) (c) of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women on the elimination of discrimination against women and on equal rights in marriage and divorce.

Headline_English: Two expatriate brothers beaten to death the day after returning home
Content_Enlish:
Two brothers were beaten to death in Fatikchhari, Chittagong. The incident took place at around 8 pm on Tuesday in Fatehpur village of ward number 8 of Jafatnagar union of the upazila. 

The deceased are Alamgir Alam (40) and Muhammad Jahangir Alam (45). They are residents of that area. Both are expatriates from the United Arab Emirates. They came to the country yesterday, Monday. 

It was learned from talking to local public representatives and residents that the elder brother of the deceased, Muhammad Karim, and his wife Nigar Sultana were having a marital dispute. While the wife was in her husband's house, Karim lives in a rented house with his children in the upazila headquarters. At around 8 pm today, Karim went to the house with his four brothers. Later, he injured his wife on the head and body with a ramda. 

When the neighbors came forward to stop the wife from getting injured, Muhammad Karim and his brothers also attacked them. At that time, five to six local residents were injured. The neighbors got angry and chased Karim and his brothers and beat them up. Alamgir Alam and Muhammad Jahangir Alam died on the spot. Local public representatives said that the bodies of the deceased were still lying at the scene at around 9 pm when this report was written. 

From the scene at 9 pm, Jafatnagar Union Parishad (UP) Chairman Zia Uddin told Prothom Alo that Karim had also had a mediation with his wife regarding the family dispute. However, it was not resolved. Meanwhile, Karim took his four brothers and beat his wife when the neighbors stopped him. At that time, a clash broke out between the two parties when the neighbors were attacked. At one stage, two brothers died due to beating by the agitated crowd. 

Zia Uddin also said that the bodies were lying at the scene. However, the injured people have been rescued and sent to Chittagong Medical College Hospital. 

Fatikchhari Police Station Inspector Abu Jafar told Prothom Alo, "I have heard about two deaths and five to six injuries in the exchange of fire between the two sides. Police have been sent to the scene."

Headline_English: BNP seeks explanation from Salahuddin Ahmed
Content_Enlish:
BNP has 'summoned' party standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed and joint secretary general Khairul Kabir Khokon for their controversial actions. In a separate letter, they have been asked to provide an explanation to the central office within 24 hours. BNP central office sources said that Salahuddin Ahmed was given the summons on Monday and Khairul Kabir on Sunday. 

Salahuddin Ahmed, a member of the BNP's highest policy-making body, the Standing Committee, went to his locality Pekua in Cox's Bazar on Wednesday to receive a reception in a car owned by controversial business group S Alam. After the matter was reported in the media, various discussions arose. In view of this, the top leadership of BNP has sought an explanation in this regard. However, Salahuddin Ahmed expressed his regret to the countrymen, calling the incident of riding in the car of the S Alam business group 'inadvertent' and 'unintentional'. He held a press conference at his Gulshan residence this afternoon and highlighted the entire incident.

Meanwhile, Khairul Kabir met another controversial diamond trader and Awami League Central Industry and Commerce Subcommittee member Dilip Kumar Agarwala at a hotel in Gulshan. When the incident came to light, BNP sought an explanation from him. 

Khairul Kabir told Prothom Alo, "I did not hold any secret meeting. I went there to talk to the protocol officer of the BNP Chairperson. There, a relative of mine introduced me to Dolan Agarwala, former president of the Bangladesh Jewellery Association, whom I have never seen before in my life. Bashundhara Group has a dispute with them. Because the Jewellery Association has taken over Bashundhara. They want BNP's cooperation in this regard. They want to meet the Secretary General through me. I have expressed their inability." 

Khairul Kabir claimed that there were many more people there. It will be clear if you look at the hotel's CCTV. 

Salahuddin's apology 

Salahuddin Ahmed believes that there has been some confusion in the public mind over the incident of going to Cox's Bazar for a reception in a car owned by the controversial business group S Alam. He said, "When I went to my district Cox's Bazar after a long 10 years, a reception was organized by my party. There, I used a car, which belonged to a company; the news has been written that it belongs to S Alam Company. I myself did not know which car I was getting into. I was very emotional at that time, I was soaked in the love of my countrymen and I was absorbed in the desire to visit the graves of my parents. At that time, my state of mind was not that I was getting into which car or whose car I was getting into…."

Headline_English: Educational programs will be launched quickly after evaluating students' opinions: DU VC
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka University (DU) Vice-Chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan has said that the university's educational programs will be launched quickly based on consensus by evaluating the thoughts and opinions of the students. To this end, after exchanging views with the students at the hall level, views will also be exchanged with student representatives and concerned parties at the department and institute levels. 

This Monday evening, the Vice-Chancellor said these things during an exchange of views with student representatives of the university's Dr. Muhammad Shahidullah Hall, Kabi Sufia Kamal Hall, Amar Ekushey Hall and Fazlul Haque Muslim Hall. This information was given in a university press release. 

During the exchange of views, Vice-Chancellor Niaz Ahmed Khan said that the university administration is working to ensure discipline in the halls and security on the campus in order to resume the university's educational programs as soon as possible. As a result of the exchange of views with the students, several issues have already come to light, which the administration is considering seriously. A roadmap is being prepared to resume educational activities as soon as possible through ongoing discussions with teachers and students. 

It is worth noting that Vice-Chancellor Niaz Ahmed Khan has been visiting the halls of Dhaka University continuously since August 31 to exchange views with students. 

During this time, students presented proposals and opinions on the overall issues of the hall, including ensuring campus security, mobilizing the internal transportation system, making the campus drug-free and removing uprooted people, increasing the number of seats in the hall and constructing new buildings, ending the public room system, improving the quality of food, high-speed internet and free Wi-Fi connection. 

University Treasurer Professor Mohammad Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, Proctor Saifuddin Ahmed, and the principals and residential teachers of the concerned halls were present at the discussion today.

Headline_English: National Citizens' Committee debuts tomorrow
Content_Enlish:
The National Citizens' Committee is making its debut, embodying the aspirations of the student-public uprising. It has been announced that the committee will make its official debut at the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka tomorrow, Sunday at 4:30 pm. 

A press release sent to the media on Saturday night said that the participation of people from all walks of life in the country under the leadership of the anti-discrimination student movement and the sacrifice of thousands of martyrs and injured people led to the fall of the worst fascist ruler in the history of Bangladesh, Sheikh Hasina. The second phase of the student-public uprising, that is, the goal of a new political settlement, must be achieved by abolishing the fascist system. 

The press release also said, 'In order to implement the new political language and potential of the population that the student-public uprising has presented, Bangladesh must be re-formed. One of our objectives is to reach a new historical understanding through exchanging views with various political parties and socio-cultural initiatives active in the society regarding the formulation of a new democratic constitution through the Constituent Assembly and to organize the people of Bangladesh accordingly. To this end, the National Citizens Committee is going to be formally launched at the Central Shaheed Minar tomorrow at 4:30 pm. Everyone has been invited to participate in this event.' 

When asked about this, Ariful Islam, a member of the Liaison Committee of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement, told Prothom Alo, 'The National Citizens Committee is being formed in continuation of the aspirations and legacy of the mass uprising of the students and the public. After the formation of the central committee, citizen committees will be formed in 64 districts and 12 metropolitan cities of the country and then at the police station level. This committee will work as a pressure group for the necessary reforms of the state to abolish the fascist system.' 

Meanwhile, the divisional and district-level tour of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement is starting tomorrow. During this tour, a coordinating team of the student movement will participate in a meeting with the students and the people who caused the uprising in each district. The meeting will be held in Munshiganj tomorrow as the first district of the Dhaka divisional tour, a press release said today.

Headline_English: Committee to be formed soon for police reform: Home Affairs Advisor
Content_Enlish:
Home Affairs Advisor Lieutenant General (Retd.) Md. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury said that a preliminary committee will be formed soon for police reform. He said that this committee will determine the process, how and who will be included in the police reform. 

The Home Affairs Advisor said this during a meeting with an eight-member delegation led by UNDP Resident Representative in Bangladesh Stefan Liler at the Secretariat on Monday afternoon. During the meeting, the two sides discussed various issues including police reform and flood rehabilitation. 

This information was given in a press release signed by Faisal Hasan, Senior Information Officer of the Home Ministry. It said that the issue of police reform is still in the initial stage. No committee has been formed in this regard yet. However, a preliminary committee will be formed soon for police reform. The preliminary committee will determine the process, how and who will be included in the reform. 

The advisor told the UNDP delegation that the process will be taken forward based on the recommendations and opinions of the preliminary committee and the next course of action will be determined. Their opinions and suggestions will be taken after formal discussions with UNDP and other interested countries. However, only those opinions and suggestions that are relevant to the Bangladeshi context will be considered for further action and implementation. 

UNDP Resident Representative Stefan Liler said that police reform in Bangladesh should be carried out in such a way that the public can gain trust and confidence in the police and there is no criticism. This reform needs to be implemented after consultation with the public, including representatives of civil society. In this regard, the UN is ready to provide necessary technical and financial assistance. 

The UNDP Resident Representative said in the meeting that UNDP is conducting a study on the rehabilitation of flood victims in Bangladesh. He also said that UNDP will spend $ 1 billion for this work.

Headline_English: Bangladesh lost to Bhutan
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh somehow managed to win their first international friendly match against Bhutan on Thursday. Javier Cabrera's team won the match despite not playing very well after Sheikh Morsalin scored a lucky goal in the sixth minute. But Bangladesh lost to Bhutan in the second match today. Bhutan defeated Bangladesh 1-0 in Thimphu with Kinga Wangchuk's goal in the 91st minute of the match. This is Bangladesh's second loss to Bhutan in the two teams' head-to-head matches, the previous one being in Thimphu in 2016. 

Bangladesh suffered their second loss in Bhutan due to haphazard play, lifeless football and a failure to create goal opportunities. Rakib Hossain and Bishwanath Ghosh could not play today due to injuries. None of their replacements were able to match their potential. 

Rakib's absence was felt the most in the attack. Although the defense managed to cope with it fairly well, it could not be done in the end. When Dawa Tshering's free kick flew into the box, no one could clear it. The ball floated in the air and went to Kinga Wangchuk, who was standing in the gap. He easily put the ball into the net. Bhutan created a couple of more scoring opportunities in the match, but Bangladesh's defense was strong and they could not capitalize on those opportunities. But in the end, the defense was responsible for Bhutan's winning goal.
