Headline_English: James-Hassan to sing at 'Concert for New Bangladesh'
Content_Enlish:
For the first time in the UK, two Bangladeshi band stars James and Hassan will sing on the same stage. The two stars will sing at the ‘Concert for New Bangladesh’ to help those affected by the recent floods in Bangladesh. 
About the concert, ION TV CEO Ataullah Farooq told Prothom Alo, ‘This is the first time that Hassan and James will sing on the same stage not only in the UK but also in Europe. We have organized this concert to help those affected by the floods in Bangladesh. This arrangement is in line with George Harrison’s historic “Concert for Bangladesh” at Madison Square Garden in New York City during the Bangladesh Liberation War.’ 

Ataullah Farooq also said, ‘The recent floods have caused extensive damage in many districts of the country. The concert is being held to stand by the people of the country from abroad during this crisis. The funds collected through the concert will be delivered to the flood-affected areas of the country.’

Headline_English: 10 arrested in attempted robbery at Exim Bank remanded
Content_Enlish:
Police have remanded 10 people arrested in connection with the attempted robbery at Exim Bank in the capital's Gulshan-2 area. 

Gulshan Police Station said that the police have remanded 10 people involved in the attack on a three-day remand through a court today, Sunday. 

The arrested accused are Ashraf Rahman (46), Ashequr Rahman (41), Md. Aslam (44), Md. Sohel (35), Md. Ratan Islam (26), Syed Shahid (54), Md. Harun Or Rashid (45), Raihan Sarkar (27), Shariful Islam (30) and Ahmed Hossain (42). 

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Riazul Haque told Prothom Alo on Sunday that some information has been found in the initial investigation. The bank attack was not carried out for political reasons. Whether the incident was an attempted robbery or due to internal conflict is being investigated seriously. 

Police sources said that a group of miscreants entered the Exim Bank (Gulshan-2) branch of the Finance Square multi-storey building in Gulshan-2 area after 1 am on Friday. On receiving the information, the police went to the spot and arrested 10 people. After analyzing the CCTV footage of the building, the police said that the arrested persons entered the Finance Square building with two cars and several motorcycles. At that time, they were wearing masks. Immediately after entering the building, they tied the hands and faces of the security personnel. Then they vandalized the building. Local people came to know about the matter and informed the police and surrounded the building. Later, the police came and arrested them and took them to the police station. 

The bank has filed a case with Gulshan Police Station regarding the vandalism and attack. Gulshan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md. Touhid Ahmed told Prothom Alo that a robbery case has been filed. However, no robbery was committed from the bank. Efforts are being made to find out the details of the incident by interrogating the arrested persons. 

SM Oliuur Hachan, executive officer of the women's branch of Gulshan Exim Bank, the plaintiff in the case, told Prothom Alo that whether it was an internal dispute or they attacked for robbery, the police investigation will reveal.

Headline_English: Delhi has not yet taken a decision on Dhaka's request for Yunus-Modi meeting in New York
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka has proposed a meeting between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Dr. Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government of Bangladesh, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly session in New York later this month. However, New Delhi has not yet taken a decision on the matter. The Indian media Hindustan Times reported this news on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter. 

The people, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told Hindustan Times that the comments made by Dr. Muhammad Yunus in an interview with an Indian media outlet earlier this week make it unlikely that he will meet Narendra Modi. The reason for this, they said, was that the comments made by Dr. Muhammad Yunus in that interview were not well received by New Delhi. 

Dhaka made a formal request for the meeting between Dr. Muhammad Yunus and Narendra Modi earlier this week. They are scheduled to be in New York later this month to attend the UN General Assembly session. Citing sources, Hindustan Times reports that New Delhi has not yet taken any decision on the request made by Dhaka. The subject of the discussion of Modi's possible bilateral meeting in New York is also not yet finalized. 

In the interview given to the Press Trust of India, Dr. Muhammad Yunus criticized the comments made by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Bangladesh while she was in India. In the interview, Dr. Yunus hinted that Bangladesh may seek her (Sheikh Hasina) extradition and said that India should move away from the statement that all parties in Bangladesh except Sheikh Hasina's Awami League are 'Islamist'. 

Dr. Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government, also said in the interview, 'If India wants to keep her (Sheikh Hasina) until Bangladesh returns, then the condition may be that she has to remain silent.' Dr. Muhammad Yunus said, 'She is talking and giving directions while sitting in India. Nobody likes this. This is not good for us or for India.’ 

New Delhi has not yet given any official response to Dr. Muhammad Yunus’s comments. However, sources said that such comments by him (Dr. Muhammad Yunus) were not helpful for good relations between the two countries. 

Sheikh Hasina resigned on August 5 in the face of student and public protests. That day, she left the country for India in a military plane. Sheikh Hasina has been in India since then. The Bangladesh government has already canceled her diplomatic passport. In this situation, various questions are being raised about whether she will be able to stay in India or not and her possible extradition. Demands to bring her back are also growing. 

Regarding the asylum granted to Sheikh Hasina, India has said that Sheikh Hasina is allowed to come to India at a short notice. When asked what New Delhi will do if Bangladesh requests Sheikh Hasina’s extradition, Indian Foreign Ministry officials recently said that this is a speculative question. They refused to answer such speculative questions.

Headline_English: Miraj's idea of ​​avoiding defeat before winning
Content_Enlish:
India scored 12 runs in the first over. Rohit Sharma hit Khaled Ahmed for sixes in the first two balls of the second over. Rohit and Jaiswal took the team's score to 51 with 22 runs in the third over. Mehidy Miraj was surprised to see their T20 cheap batting. He immediately realized that they had come up with a well-planned plan. 

Miraj-Shakib could not thwart the plan of a strong team like India. They scored 285 runs in just 34.4 overs and took a lead of 52 runs. India's goal is to quickly all out Bangladesh on the last day and win. Miraj said at the press conference that they will also try to bat as far as possible. He also mentioned that they will think about their own safety, that is, a draw, before winning. 

Miraj said, "It will take time to win. We only have one day. We have to give them a good target, then take 10 wickets. It is more important to think about our own safety than winning from here. We will try to bat as far as possible tomorrow." If the situation comes like that, we will think about winning. We are thinking about ourselves first.' 

Bangladesh lost 2 wickets for 26 runs in the late afternoon of the fourth day. According to Miraj, to save their backs, they will have to bat for at least two sessions. They will also have to add runs to the scoreboard that India will not be able to score in one session. Spin all-rounder Miraj, who took 4 wickets in the first innings, commented that the matter is challenging. 

He said, 'It is not that we have lost the match. Anything is possible in Test cricket. Since the wicket is good for the batters, we can take chances. We know it will be challenging, but the situation will change if we can bat well for one session.' 

Miraj also commented that India attacked in a planned manner. According to him, from the beginning to the end, they all batted to score runs, 'To be honest, I was surprised, they came with a good plan. We tried to stop them according to our strength. Sometimes in Tests, a different picture is seen. They came out to bat to win.'

Headline_English: China wants to further strengthen ties with Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
China is keen to advance strategic bilateral relations by strengthening trade and economic ties with Bangladesh. China wants to invest in solar panels in Bangladesh. 

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Dr. Muhammad Yunus, Chief Advisor to the Interim Government of Bangladesh, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly session. He expressed this interest there. 

The talks took place at the UN headquarters on Wednesday, local time in New York. 

Quoting the Chief Advisor's Press Secretary Shafiqul Alam, BSS reported that Chinese solar panel manufacturers are interested in setting up factories in Bangladesh in response to Dr. Yunus's call. The Chinese government is taking the matter very seriously. 

Last month, the Chinese ambassador to Dhaka paid a courtesy call on the Chief Advisor, Professor Yunus. There, he urged Chinese solar panel manufacturers to invest in Bangladesh. 

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said that Beijing will encourage businessmen of the two countries to increase cooperation and partnership. He also said that China has sent a team of Red Cross doctors to Dhaka to treat students who were seriously injured during the July-August mass uprising. The Chinese foreign minister said that China will welcome more students from Bangladesh. 

Dr. Yunus thanked China for this sincerity. Chinese solar companies can invest in Bangladesh on a large scale, which will benefit from preferential market access for exports to many rich countries. He added that other Chinese manufacturers, besides solar companies, can relocate their factories to Bangladesh. 

The chief advisor stressed the importance of closer ties with China and called for the beginning of a “new chapter” in relations between the two countries. He also called for increased technical cooperation between businesses in the two countries. 

Dr. Yunus said, “We want to cooperate with Chinese companies. We have many opportunities to work together.” BSS reported.

Headline_English: Kazi Farms donates Tk 1.22 crore to flood victims
Content_Enlish:
Kazi Farms Group has responded to the call of the Interim Government's Chief Advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus to help those affected by the recent floods. To stand by the flood victims, the officers and employees of Kazi Farms, Kazi Media Limited and Kazi Food Industries Limited have donated one day's salary. The amount is 1 crore 21 lakh 88 thousand 838 taka. 

The donation amount was deposited in the Chief Advisor's Relief Fund on Monday. Kazi Farms Director Kazi Zahin Hasan handed over the check of the donation amount to Faruk-e Azam Bir Pratik, Advisor to the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief at the Secretariat. Tanvir Haider Chowdhury, CEO of Kazi Food Industries Limited, was present at the time. 

In addition, Kazi Farms has taken the initiative to help poultry farmers affected by the floods. As part of this, Kazi Farms will provide free chicken chicks to farmers to start their poultry farms affected by the floods. 

Kazi Farms has been producing and supplying various poultry products, including quality eggs and chicks, to improve the quality of protein in the country for a long time. Standing by the flood victims is a part of that.

Headline_English: Pakistani band Jaal's concert in Dhaka postponed
Content_Enlish:
The concert titled ‘Legends of the Decade’ featuring Pakistani band Zal has been postponed. The organizing organization announced this information in a statement. 

The concert was scheduled to be held at the 300-foot Dhaka Arena in the capital on Friday. The Pakistani band Zal is currently in Dhaka to participate in it. The band was supposed to celebrate the 20th anniversary of their popular ‘Adat’ album at the concert. The concert was also scheduled to feature Anthaheen, Vikings and Conclusion.

Assen’s media spokesperson Sharmin Rahman said, ‘This postponement is due to rain. I can assure everyone that the concert will be held in a day or two. It is impossible to organize this event in the rain that is happening today and will continue. Because the entire event is open air. We hope to be able to announce the new date of the concert in the evening press conference. Because the members of Jal have already been in Dhaka for three days. Other bands have also prepared themselves for this concert. So there is no room for delay.

Headline_English: Shigeru Ishiba to be Japan's new Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Former Defense Minister Shigeru Ishiba has been elected leader of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) by lawmakers. He is set to become the country's next prime minister. AP News 

Ishiba (67) defeated Sanae Takaichi, a staunch nationalist and a disciple of former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, to become the party's leader. 

The two topped the first round of nine candidates. Ishiba won the runoff vote today with 215 votes to 194. 

In a short speech, he said, "I want to trust the people. I want to speak the truth with courage and sincerity. I want to keep this country safe and secure so that everyone can live here with a smile again." 

Ishiba was defeated by former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2012.

Headline_English: Bangladesh wants closer ties with Maldives
Content_Enlish:
Principal Advisor Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus met with Maldives President Mohamed Muizzoo on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly session on Friday. During the meeting, he stressed the importance of closer ties with the Maldives. 

During the talks, the two leaders discussed trade, investment, tourism, SAARC activation, climate change research cooperation and ways to expand people-to-people ties. 

The Principal Advisor called for a “closer” relationship with the Maldives, saying the two countries share many things, including the serious impacts of climate change. Referring to the dangers posed by the climate crisis, Professor Yunus said that our entire existence is at stake. 

The Maldivian President praised the role of Bangladeshi workers in the country’s construction and tourism sectors. Mohamed Muizzoo said the two countries can work together in tourism, fisheries and climate change research. He called for expanding trade and economic cooperation between the two countries. 

The Maldivian President said that if our two countries work together, it will be beneficial for the people of both countries. 

The Chief Adviser said that he wants to see the SAARC initiative as a platform for economic cooperation and closer integration of the South Asian region. 
Professor Yunus said, "We will be close. We should not be far apart."

Headline_English: Full speech of the Chief Advisor to the United Nations
Content_Enlish:
The Chief Adviser to the Interim Government, Dr. Muhammad Yunus, addressed the 79th session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) at the UN Headquarters in New York on Friday. He began his speech at 11:24 am local time in New York. The nearly 38-minute-long speech ended at 12:02 pm. During his speech, the audience applauded his speech as he raised various important issues. Khabar BSS 

The full speech is reproduced below- 

Bismillahir Rahmanihir Rahim 

First of all, I would like to congratulate you on being elected as the President of the United Nations General Assembly. I assure you that the Bangladesh delegation will provide you with full support in fulfilling your duties. 

I also express my sincere appreciation to Secretary-General Antonio Guterres for his strong conviction and successful leadership in upholding the mandate of the United Nations and resolving global crises. I particularly appreciate the visionary role of the Secretary-General in organizing the ‘Summit of the Future’. 

I believe that the ‘Pact for the Future’ and the ‘Declaration on Future Generations’ that were unanimously adopted at the conference will be of great help in determining the global development agenda after Agenda 2030. Bangladesh believes that the achievements of this conference will serve as a guide in formulating our common aspirations and cooperation framework for global prosperity. 

I have been able to attend this great parliament of the world community today in the context of the epoch-making changes that have taken place in Bangladesh this July-August. The immense power of our people, especially the youth, has opened the door to a new possibility of radical transformation of our existing state structures and institutions. 

The movement of our students and youth was initially mainly an anti-discrimination movement. Gradually, it took the form of a mass movement. Then the whole world watched in amazement as the people of Bangladesh stood firm on the streets and social media against dictatorship, oppression, discrimination, injustice and corruption. 

Our students, through their unyielding determination and conviction, have liberated us from an authoritarian and undemocratic regime. I believe that the future of our country lies in their collective determination, which will elevate this country to the status of a responsible nation in the world community. 

This mass movement has united all the people of Bangladesh who are deprived of political rights and development. The people of Bangladesh wanted an inclusive partnership in development activities. Our people fought for a fair, inclusive and effective democracy, for which our new generation sacrificed their lives. 

We are overwhelmed by the wisdom, courage and conviction shown by our youth. Despite the bullets, our youth stood firm. Our young women spoke out strongly against the illegal state power. School-going teenagers sacrificed their lives fearlessly. Hundreds of people lost their eyesight forever. Our mothers, daily wage workers and countless people of the city took to the streets shoulder to shoulder with their children. Regardless of the scorching sun, rain and fear of death, they defeated the evil conspiracy of operating the state machinery against the true and just aspirations for a long time. 

As far as we know, in this movement of the people, we have lost more than eight hundred lives at the hands of autocratic forces. 

The Bangladesh state emerged from the people's deep faith in liberalism, pluralism and secularism. The values ​​that our people fought for in 1971, many years later, have been taught to see those values ​​in a new light by 'Generation G'. We saw this in the Language Movement of 1952 when Bengali was established as the mother tongue. 

This ‘Monsoon Uprising’ in Bangladesh will inspire people in different parts of the world to stand up for freedom and justice in the coming days. I therefore appeal to the world community to engage with our new Bangladesh in a new way to make our freedom and democratic aspirations a reality. 

Honorable President, 

To reconstruct the state structure that has become miserable, our youth and the entire people of the country have unanimously entrusted me and my Advisory Council with the great responsibility of running the government. 

After assuming office, we can see with deep astonishment and disappointment how totalitarian corruption has turned an effective democratic system into ruins, how the core institutions of the state have been imprisoned in a vicious cycle of partisanship. How the people's wealth was looted mercilessly, how a special group of vested interests unjustly took over all business and commerce and freely smuggled the country's wealth abroad. In short, how justice, principles and morality disappeared at every level. 

In such a situation, we have been given the responsibility to reconstruct the country and return the desired state system to the people. Our main goal at the moment is to correct the mistakes of the past and build a competitive and strong economy and a just social system. 

In the current changed situation, all political parties are now able to freely express their opinions. Our priority is to ensure the accountability of every person or institution involved in state work and decision-making process. 

We are firmly determined to uphold and protect the fundamental rights of the people. Our goal is that the people of our country will speak freely, assemble without fear, and vote for the person of their choice. We are also committed to preserving the independence of the judiciary and consolidating the freedom of the media, including in the cyber domain. 

We are emphasizing on increasing allocations to the health and education sectors instead of building huge infrastructure so that even the children of one of our farmers or workers can reach the highest heights of society. Our goal is to restore good governance at all levels of the state system. 

Our government is determined to uphold the international, regional and bilateral agreements to which Bangladesh is a party. Bangladesh will continue to actively participate and contribute to multilateral world structures, including the United Nations. Bangladesh is eager to maintain friendly relations with all countries of the world on the basis of mutual respect, dignity and protection of interests. 

Honorable President, 

In just seven weeks, our government has taken several important steps. Responding to our request, the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has quickly sent a fact-finding mission to Bangladesh to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the human rights violations committed during the mass movement in Bangladesh and to provide advice on preventing the recurrence of these incidents. I thank him profusely. 

Within two weeks of assuming office, we have acceded to the International Convention on the Prevention of Enforced Disappearances. The necessary domestic laws and regulations for its immediate implementation are currently in the process of being formulated. 

An inquiry commission is currently working to investigate the allegations of enforced disappearances in Bangladesh over the past decade and a half. 

To restore people's trust and confidence and to ensure that the brutal past does not return, we are prioritizing reforms in certain specific sectors. To that end, we have formed an independent commission to reform the existing electoral system, constitution, judiciary, public administration, law and order system. A separate commission is also in the process of forming commissions on several other issues, including a separate commission for reforming newspapers and media. 

In order to create a conducive environment for business and commerce, we have taken initiatives for comprehensive reforms in the banking and financial sectors. We are also determined to ensure that no foreign business or investment is harmed. We are working to ensure that these reforms are sustainable in the long term and to create an environment conducive to free, fair and participatory elections.

I call for the international community to broaden and deepen its support and cooperation with Bangladesh in realizing its ambition to emerge as a just and inclusive democratic society through the achievement of democracy, the rule of law, equality and prosperity.

Headline_English: 40 percent of heart attack victims are young
Content_Enlish:
The number of heart patients in Chittagong is constantly increasing. The concern is that more than 40 percent of the victims are young. A large proportion of heart attack deaths are also young. However, despite the increase in the number of patients in the port city, medical facilities have not increased at the same rate. No specialized hospital has been established for heart patients. In this situation, the only hope is the cardiology department of the government medical center Chittagong Medical College (CMC) Hospital. The condition of this department, which many patients rely on, is also fragile. Despite the pressure of a large number of patients, medical services are being provided with only one cath lab. Doctors have to struggle to manage the pressure of patients. Experts blame diet for the young people suffering from heart disease and death. 

According to the cardiology department of CMC Hospital, a large proportion of the patients admitted to the department daily and those who come for treatment in the outpatient department are young. So far this year, 13,454 patients have been admitted to the department. Of these, more than 40 percent are young. In addition, a portion of those over 40 years of age are admitted to the hospital due to heart disease. The number of patients who died during this period is 1,383. A portion of whom died of heart attacks. This year alone, 9,820 patients have had their ECGs done in the cardiology department. 5,195 have had echo tests. 

The cardiology department of the Chittagong region relies on only one cath lab. This ward, which has a capacity of more than two hundred patients, has more than doubled the number of patients admitted every day. Due to which many are forced to lie on the floor for treatment. Every day, more than two hundred patients come to the outpatient department for treatment. On average, 30 to 40 patients in the ward need angiograms, pacemakers, and heart rings every day. However, it is not possible to provide services to more than 10 patients per day in a single cath lab. Due to this, helpless and poor patients have to wait for a long time. 

According to doctors, patients need to be examined in the cath lab to know the condition of the heart muscle, valves, and arteries, and to understand the blood pressure in the heart. Due to the lack of a cath lab, doctors cannot provide services to many patients who are waiting every day. Although several private hospitals in Chittagong provide heart disease treatment, poor and helpless patients cannot get treatment from there due to the additional cost. 

Associate Professor Dr. Ashish Dey, Head of the Cardiology Department of CHMEC Hospital, said that the rate of heart disease among young people is increasing. A large proportion of deaths due to heart attacks are also young. A few years ago, heart disease patients did not come to the ward at a young age like now. A large number of patients from this region come here. This means that doctors have to constantly struggle to handle the increased patient load. If there was a specialized heart disease hospital, such a situation would not have arisen. 

According to heart disease experts, 17 percent of deaths from various diseases in the country are due to heart disease. Heart attacks and heart disease need immediate treatment. Delay leads to death. Therefore, if there were more medical facilities locally in Chittagong, many lives could have been saved. Apart from this, unhealthy lifestyle, ignorance, smoking are major causes of heart disease. There is no alternative to walking to keep the heart healthy. Increasing healthy food in the daily diet, leading a worry-free life, increasing physical activity and abstaining from smoking can reduce the risk of heart disease. 

On the occasion of World Heart Day today, Sunday, various programs including processions, discussions and meetings have been organized by the cardiology department and various hospitals in Chittagong.

Headline_English: DC's appointment with Rs 3 crore cash check: Investigation committee formed

Headline_English: A statement from Shaheed Minar announcing the government's resignation
