Headline_English: The benefits Netanyahu will receive from the Haniya assassination
Content_Enlish:
The recent assassinations of Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh and top Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukour in Iran and Lebanon could be politically lucrative for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, analysts say. The killings could help restore Netanyahu's political authority, although they could hurt his chances of freeing Israeli hostages, Qatar-based media outlet Al Jazeera reported. 

Follow Google News for the latest news from gnewsdainik Ittefaq 
"Haniyya's assassination is good for Netanyahu's security and political achievements. It's a political truth," Hughes Lovatt, an Israel-Palestine expert at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told Al Jazeera. 

Israel has been rocked by internal protests and divisions. First, months of protests against Netanyahu's government's controversial judicial reforms. The prime minister has come under increasing criticism for not signing a ceasefire agreement with Hamas. 

Last week, right-wing Israeli ministers and members of the Knesset, the parliament, expressed outrage over the arrest of soldiers accused of torturing and raping Palestinian prisoners. 

On July 30, Israel killed Shukur in a missile strike in the Dahiya area of ​​Beirut, Lebanon. Shukur was a top Hezbollah commander. He played a key role in the group's military strategy. Israel claimed the attack was carried out after 12 children were killed in the Golan Heights. Hezbollah has not claimed responsibility. 

Haniyeh was killed hours after Shukur was killed. He was killed in the Iranian capital, Tehran, while attending the inauguration of new President Masoud Pezeshkian. Israel has not claimed responsibility for the attack. But Iran and Hamas have accused Israel. 

A day after Haniyeh's killing, Israel claimed to have killed Hamas' top military commander, Mohammed Deif, in a raid in Gaza on July 13. Deif was the founder of Hamas's military wing, the Qassem Brigades, and had been at the top of Israel's most wanted list for years. 

Israeli political expert Ari Goldberg said the recent killings have helped restore the reputation of Israel's military and political establishment. But many Israelis, especially those demanding the release of hostages, fear that the killings will make it harder for a ceasefire to take hold. 

"These killings could politically sustain Netanyahu," Lovatt said.

Headline_English: Remittances decreased by 7.5 billion taka in one month
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh received a record amount of remittances or expatriate income in June this year due to the increase in the price of the dollar and Eid-ul-Azha. Less than a month later, the opposite picture is visible. Remittances have decreased due to the situation created by the student movement across the country over quota reform. According to the Central Bank, expatriates sent remittances of 1.9 billion US dollars to the country in the just-ended July. This is the lowest in the last 10 months. 

Follow Google News to get the latest news from gnewsdainik Ittefaq 
As per the rules, the remittance information of the previous month is published on the Central Bank's website on the first working day of every month. But on Thursday (August 1), the Central Bank did not publish it. In the afternoon, journalists asked Bangladesh Bank Executive Director and Spokesperson Md. Mejbaul Haque about the remittance information, and he said that the report is not yet complete. The work is ongoing, and will be announced when it is complete. Later, around 5 pm, instead of publishing the report, he briefly shared on WhatsApp how many dollars came in in July. 
The spokesperson said that 1.9 billion 9 million dollars in expatriate income came into the country in July. In July of the previous year, it was $197.3 million. 

According to the central bank, remittances came in July of the first month of the 2023-24 fiscal year (2023), $197.3 million, $1.59 billion in August, $1.33 billion in September, $1.14 billion in October, $1.93 billion in November, $1.99 billion in December, $2.11 billion in January 2024, $2.16 billion in February, $1.99 billion in March, $2.04 billion in April, $2.25 billion in May, and $2.54 billion in June. 

There is a risk that remittances will decrease this month due to various reasons, including the internet shutdown caused by the student movement over quota reform in the country. Many expatriates are campaigning against sending remittances through banking channels in the country in protest of the many casualties caused by the violence in the movement. 

A review of the central bank's data shows that remittances decreased by $632 million in July compared to June this year. The amount in Bangladeshi currency is about 750 million taka. 

After the 'crawling peg' was introduced on May 8 to restore stability in the foreign exchange market, the dollar rate jumped by 7 taka and the intermediate rate was set at 117 taka. As a result, the dollar rate was stable at 117 to 118 taka for more than two months. Now it has started increasing.

Headline_English: Thousands protest in Turkey over Ismail Haniyeh's killing
Content_Enlish:
Thousands of people have protested in Turkey against the assassination of Ismail Haniyeh, the head of the political wing of the Palestinian independence movement Hamas. Thousands of pro-Palestinian protesters took to the streets in Istanbul on Wednesday night (July 31). Reuters reports. 

Follow Google News to get the latest news from gnewsdainik Ittefaq 
Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh was killed in an Israeli strike in the Iranian capital Tehran around 2am on Tuesday. The Iranian regime has threatened harsh revenge for the assassination. The assassination of Haniyeh has raised fears of a new major war in the Middle East. 

Protesters in Istanbul held posters with Haniyeh's picture and banners. The posters read, "Martyr Haniyeh, Jerusalem is ours and your path is our path." 

During the march in Istanbul's Fatih district, protesters waved Turkish and Palestinian flags and chanted slogans including "Murderer Israel, get out of Palestine" and "A thousand salutes from Istanbul for the resistance to Gaza City." 

Israel is widely believed to be involved in the attack on Ismail Haniyeh, but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government has not yet claimed responsibility. The Israeli military said it would not comment on the killing. 

Earlier on Wednesday, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the killing in Tehran, saying the killing of Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh would not break the morale of the Palestinians.

Headline_English: Low-lying areas in Cox's Bazar flooded, millions in distress
Content_Enlish:
Heavy rains are continuing in Cox's Bazar in the middle of Shrawan. Due to the heavy rains and hill floods in the last few days, Matamuhuri, one of the rivers in the district, Eidgaon's Fuleshwari, Bakankhali and Rezukhal, have overflowed their banks. River water is overflowing the dams. In many places, canal and river water is entering the localities. Along with the rain and water coming down the hills, at least two hundred villages in different upazilas are being flooded. 

Public representatives have claimed that several lakhs of people in Cox's Bazar Sadar, Ramu, Teknaf, Kutubdia, Chakaria, Pekua, Ukhia upazilas have been waterlogged. The most waterlogged area is Ukhia upazila. Many areas of the Cox's Bazar-Teknaf-Ukhia highway are submerged under water. 
Thousands of families have suffered as water has entered their homes in the flooded areas. Many homes are facing a food crisis. This has left the householders, including the elderly and children, in extreme distress. But locals said that relief materials had not reached the affected areas till Thursday (August 1) afternoon. 

Ukhia Upazila Parishad Vice Chairman Russell Chowdhury said that due to continuous rain for 3 days, lakhs of people in three unions were waterlogged since Wednesday evening. In addition to the roads, ghats, canals and bilges in the area, water has also entered homes. It is unfortunate that the administration did not have any immediate assistance. Government assistance is negligible compared to the suffering. 

Cox's Bazar Municipality Panel Mayor Helal Uddin Kabir said that the low-lying areas of the municipality have been flooded due to continuous rains from Monday night to Thursday.

Headline_English: Learn karate to stay safe and fit
Content_Enlish:
Karate is a technique of self-defense with bare hands in everyday life. Karate does not mean attacking, but protecting oneself. This technique of self-defense originated in Japan. 
And in the current context of social unrest, it is important for all women to know this technique to repel the enemy's attack at any moment. Through this, teenage to middle-aged women can avoid many unpleasant incidents. In most cases, it is quite risky for women to move independently. 

There are various nuisances including eve-teasing. Therefore, in the future, school and college girls can take karate training, so that they can move with confidence. In addition, karate is very popular as a way for women to stay healthy and physically fit. 

Many people find it boring to go to the gym to exercise in the traditional way. As a result, they do not find much motivation to workout regularly. Therefore, many people are choosing different types of sports to stay fit these days. In fact, there is no boredom in sports. Even if you play the same game every day, no one gets tired mentally. Therefore, the importance of martial arts like judo, karate, etc. can be increased. 

When asked about the importance of karate in physical exercise, physical exercise teacher Md. Mozammel Alam said that karate is not only a strategic means of protection, it is also an excellent exercise to keep the body healthy and fit. In addition, in addition to losing weight, it will strengthen the bone structure and improve blood circulation in the body.

Headline_English: Police-RAB-BGB did not have permission to shoot, will be tried
Content_Enlish:
State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat has said that the police, RAB, and BGB were not allowed to shoot anyone to quell the violence surrounding the quota reform movement. He also said that every incident of casualties during this time will be investigated independently by a judicial commission and those responsible will be brought to justice. 

He said these things at a press conference called on recent issues at the Information Ministry's conference room at the Secretariat on Thursday. 

The state minister said that the law enforcement forces, including the police, RAB, BGB, and others, were not allowed to shoot anyone. However, they had to work to protect the constitution and the law. At this time, we are not denying that some people did not break the law in the field. We will investigate and bring them to justice. Such incidents happen all over the world. The government's responsibility is to investigate and bring to justice those who have broken the law and committed injustice. 

At that time, the state minister said that the government wants to say unequivocally that the law will be applied only to terrorists. Those who are found to be involved in criminal offenses based on specific evidence will be prosecuted and arrested. We have said unequivocally that no ordinary student should be harassed in any way. We have spoken with the police administration, and that all the students who were in the movement, raised slogans, and distributed water should not be harassed in any way, and that no member of their family should be harmed in any way. Because we respect the emotions of all the students and the students involved in the movement. We have full sympathy and support for this. But those who are wreaking havoc by capitalizing on their emotions are not ordinary students. We want to ensure that not a single student who was in the movement with their emotions is harmed in any way, and we will bring the terrorists under the law. 

In the briefing, State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat also said, "The casualties that have occurred in the past few days surrounding the quota movement are very unfortunate and very sad for the government, the country, the people of the country, especially the affected families. On behalf of the government, the Prime Minister himself and I have expressed deep regret many times and condemned each and every casualty. The Prime Minister announced in his address to the nation on July 16 that a judicial inquiry commission would be formed, and it has been formed. Every casualty will be investigated through the independent judicial inquiry commission and the responsible persons will be brought under the law. In this regard, if necessary, we will also take the help of a foreign expert. Here we want to be completely transparent and accountable. 

He said, the Prime Minister met and spoke to many of those who were affected by the casualties, who lost family members, at Ganabhaban. I was also present at that time. Abu Saeed's family members were also there. I also spoke to them separately. I was told, we do not want anything, we want justice. 

The State Minister further said, for every death, for every casualty, today the government and Bangladesh are affected, the people of the country are affected. Maybe some third party is taking advantage of it. But if anyone is affected, initially the affected families who have directly lost their members and then this government and this country. A kind of malicious attempt is being made to spread propaganda and defame Bangladesh today around these deaths and incidents. Just as the victims of these incidents want justice, the government also wants justice. We want to go deep into this and we want to bring every responsible person to justice. Because the government is also affected here. One death was not desirable for the government. Every death and casualty is heavy on our chest. The government is sorry for these deaths and casualty incidents. 

He said, the government was concerned about the safety of the students. The government wanted to ensure their safety. It had to face a complex situation while applying the law against the third party who entered among them and committed terrorist acts. 

Addressing the students who are still protesting, the State Minister for Information said, "Those who are taking their emotions to the streets should be careful. We have already seen abuse by terrorists and third parties. If terrorists take this as an opportunity, and if they create casualties and conflicts, who will take responsibility for it? Students have to play a responsible role here. Because third parties are trying to lead the country into anarchy."

Headline_English: Pakistan government will fall within two months: Imran Khan
Content_Enlish:
Former Prime Minister Imran Khan has said that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N)-led government will be able to stay in power for only two more months. He made this prediction to reporters at a temporary court set up at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, Pakistan on Thursday (August 8). Geo News reported. 

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan said, "The government is currently in a disastrous situation. The rulers are taking wrong steps and are not willing to accept anything. From this, my guess is that this government has only two months left." 

At this time, Imran Khan also raised the issue of his statement on Wednesday, offering a conditional apology for the riots that took place on May 9 last year. He said that the misconception that he had offered an unconditional apology was not correct. According to Imran Khan, he will apologize if evidence is found that PTI leaders and workers were involved in the violent protests that spread across Pakistan after his arrest in a corruption case. 

On May 9, various government properties and military installations were attacked. Imran Khan said that PTI leaders and workers were not involved in the attack, but rather they were protesting peacefully. Despite this, they were labeled as 'terrorists'. He questioned, 'Am I so stupid that I will tell our people to attack the army?' 

In an interaction with journalists, Imran Khan also talked about the Election Commission of Pakistan. He accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raza, saying that the CEC had organized 'rigged elections' in the past and 'stuffed the ballot boxes with fake votes' during by-elections. 

Imran Khan said that he would not accept any interim arrangement under the ruling government. At the same time, he is reluctant to participate in any election under the current CEC.

Headline_English: Bangladesh Bank Governor resigns
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder has resigned. 

He sent his resignation letter to the concerned official of the Ministry of Finance online on Friday (August 9) afternoon. 

Sources said that Abdur Rouf Talukder resigned citing health reasons. 

Earlier, more than a hundred central bank officials protested demanding the governor's resignation. 

The Bangladesh Bank Governor has been absent from his office since Sheikh Hasina's resignation on August 5. Then, in the face of widespread protests since August 7, four deputy governors, the BFIU head and the central bank's banking advisor were forced to resign. The governor resigned today, four days after Sheikh Hasina's resignation. 

Bangladesh Bank Executive Director and Spokesperson Mejbaul Haque did not answer the phone when called to inquire about this.

Headline_English: Narendra Modi wishes Dr. Yunus all the best
Content_Enlish:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Dr. Muhammad Yunus on taking oath as the chief advisor to the interim government of Bangladesh. He said that India hopes that normalcy will return to Bangladesh very soon. 
In a post on social media X at around 10 pm today, Thursday (August 8), Narendra Modi wrote, ‘I congratulate Professor Muhammad Yunus on assuming the new responsibility. We (India) hope that normalcy will return to Bangladesh very soon and that the safety and security of all minority communities, including Hindus, will be ensured.’ 

The Indian Prime Minister also wrote, ‘India is committed to working with Bangladesh to fulfill the common aspirations of the people of both our countries for peace, security and development.’ 

Sheikh Hasina resigned from the post of Prime Minister last Monday in the face of student and public protests. Now, an interim government of 17 advisors has been formed to run the country under the leadership of Dr. Muhammad Yunus. Dr. is the chief advisor to that government. Muhammad Yunus and 13 advisors were sworn in by the President at Bangabhaban tonight. 

Shortly after the advisors to the interim government took the oath, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi wished Dr. Muhammad Yunus well.

Headline_English: 'Kalki' sets new record
Content_Enlish:
Nag Ashwin's film 'Kalki 2898 AD' has created a stir at the box office by crossing the Rs 500 crore mark as the first film of this year. The film was released in cinemas on June 27 this year. The film will be released on OTT this August. Before that, the film set a new record. 
According to the Hindustan Times, 'Kalki' has surpassed Shah Rukh Khan's controversial film 'Jawan', which was released last year, in terms of revenue. 

'Kalki' has earned Rs 760 crore in 40 days from Indian theaters. On the other hand, Atlee's 'Jawan' had earned a little more than Rs 750 crore. 

There were already indications that the film would create a storm at the box office. After its release on June 27, 'Kalki 2898 AD' earned Rs 95 crore at the Indian box office. Out of this, Rs 64.5 crore was earned from the Telugu version. The film earned Rs 24 crore in the Hindi version. 

'Kalki 2898 AD' is directed by Nag Ashwin. The film stars 'Baahubali' fame Prabhas, Deepika Padukone, Amitabh Bachchan, Kamal Haasan, Disha Patani. 

The film also features Mrunal Thakur, Dulquer Salmaan, Vijay Deverakonda, SS Rajamouli, Ram Gopal Varma in guest roles.

Headline_English: Supreme Court suspends judicial proceedings: Chief Justice
Content_Enlish:
The judicial proceedings of the Appellate and High Court divisions of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh have been suspended until further orders. 

The court administration issued a notification stating that Chief Justice Obaidul Hasan made this decision in consultation with the President on Wednesday (August 7). 

The notification said that the Chief Justice of Bangladesh, in consultation with the President, has suspended the sessions (judicial proceedings) of both divisions of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh until further orders.

Headline_English: Indian Visa Centers closed indefinitely
Content_Enlish:
Due to the unstable situation, all Indian Visa Application Centres (IVACS) in the country have been closed until further instructions. 

The Indian Visa Application Centre (IVACS) announced this in a message on its website on Wednesday (August 7). 

It said that due to the unstable situation, all IVACS will remain closed until further instructions. The next application date will be communicated through short message service (SMS) and it is requested to collect the passport on the next working day. 

All Indian Visa Application Centres were closed till Wednesday due to the prevailing situation centered on the quota reform movement.

Headline_English: Decision to form an interim government headed by Dr. Yunus
Content_Enlish:
President Md. Shahabuddin met with the heads of the three services and the coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, and it was decided to form an interim government headed by Nobel laureate Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus. 

13 coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement went to Bangabhaban shortly after 6 pm on Tuesday (August 6) to discuss the current situation in the country and the outline of the interim government with the President. This decision was then made. 

Then at 7:40 pm, the army chief, navy chief and air force chief entered Bangabhaban. This government was formed after the discussions between the 13 coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement and the heads of the three services with the President. 

Sheikh Hasina resigned from the post of Prime Minister and left the country on Monday (August 5) afternoon. Her younger sister Sheikh Rehana also left the country with her. The cabinet was dissolved soon after this. 

After Sheikh Hasina's resignation, Bangladesh Army Chief General Waqar-uz-Zaman addressed the nation. In his speech, he said that the country will be governed by forming an interim government. 

Meanwhile, President Md. Shahabuddin declared the dissolution of the National Parliament on Tuesday. This information was given in a press release sent to the media from Bangabhaban.

Headline_English: Urgent action needed to protect democracy in Bangladesh: UK
Content_Enlish:
The UK believes that urgent action is needed to protect democracy in Bangladesh. A spokesman for the country's Prime Minister Keir Starmer has reacted in this way. 

Sheikh Hasina left the country after resigning from the post of Prime Minister of Bangladesh on Monday. The UK's response came after that. 

The UK Prime Minister's spokesman told reporters in London, "Prime Minister Starmer is deeply saddened by the violence we have seen in Bangladesh in the past few weeks. I hope that urgent action will be taken to protect democracy (in Bangladesh) and to advance the peace process and the security of the people of Bangladesh."

Headline_English: 'Decision to release Khaleda Zia immediately'
Content_Enlish:
President Md. Shahabuddin held a meeting with leaders of various political parties and representatives of civil society in the presence of the chiefs of the three services at Bangabhaban. The meeting discussed the immediate release of Khaleda Zia. 

The meeting was held on Monday (August 5) night. This was announced in a press release signed by Muh. Shiplu Zaman, Deputy Press Secretary of the Public Department of the President's Office. 

The meeting decided that the National Parliament will be dissolved and an interim government will be formed as soon as possible. And the army will take steps to normalize the current anarchic situation. Khaleda Zia will also be released immediately. 
The meeting was attended by BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Mirza Abbas, Jatiya Party leaders GM Quader, Mojibul Haque Chunnu and Anisul Islam, Nagorik Oikya's Mahmudur Rahman Manna, Hefazat Islam's Mamunul Haque, Mufti Monir Qasemi, Mahbubur Rahman, Jamaat-e-Islami's Dr. Shafiqur Rahman and Sheikh Md. Masud, Major General (retd.) Fazle Rabbi, Zaker Party's Shamim Haider, Khelafat Majlis's Jalal Uddin, Gana Sanghati Andolan's Junaid Saki, Gana-Odhikar Parishad advocate Golam Sarwar, Dhaka University professor Dr. Asif Nazrul, Firoz Ahmed, Anti-Discrimination Student Movement Coordinator Abdullah Al Hossain, Arif Talukder, Omar Faruk, Mobashera Karim and Engineer Anisur Rahman. 

The meeting adopted a condolence resolution in memory of those killed in the anti-quota movement and prayed for forgiveness and peace for their departed souls.

Headline_English: Prisoners detained in student protests and false cases will be released: President
Content_Enlish:
President Md. Shahabuddin has said that all prisoners, including those arrested in the anti-discrimination student movement and various false cases, will be released. 

He said this in an address to the nation on Monday (August 5) night. 

The President said that compensation will be provided to the families of the victims of the anti-discrimination student movement and necessary assistance will be provided to the injured for proper treatment. 

A decision has been taken to release BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia, said Md. Shahabuddin. 

He said, I urge political parties to normalize law and order in the country and stop looting and destructive activities. I am instructing the armed forces to take strict steps to protect the lives and property of the people and state assets. 

The President said, I urge everyone to come forward to ensure communal harmony and the security of minorities and to protect government assets. I urge everyone to play an effective role in keeping the country's economy, administration, and industries running.

Headline_English: Army calls for curfew compliance
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh Army has urged the public to comply with the curfew and provide overall cooperation. 

The call was made in a circular signed by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director Sami Ud Daula Chowdhury on Sunday (August 4). 

The circular said that due to the ongoing deterioration of the law and order situation in the country, an indefinite curfew has been imposed from Sunday. This decision has been taken to ensure the safety of people's lives and property and important installations of the state. 

The circular further mentioned that the Bangladesh Army will fulfill its promised duties under the country's constitution and existing laws.

Headline_English: Fakhrul calls for 'March to Dhaka' program to be successful
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has called on the countrymen, including the leaders and activists of the anti-discrimination student movement, the 'March to Dhaka' program, to succeed. At the same time, Mirza Fakhrul also called on the Prime Minister to immediately step down from power in accordance with the demands of the student movement. 

He made this call in a statement on Sunday (August 4) night. 

The BNP Secretary General said, I call on the countrymen, including the leaders and activists, supporters and well-wishers of the BNP and its affiliates, to make the anti-discrimination student movement, the one-stage movement of the student movement, the 'March to Dhaka' program, a success and at the same time to continue the movement struggle in their respective areas. I also call on all political parties to stand by the student movement in its ongoing mass movement. 

He said, on the first day of the non-cooperation movement called by the anti-discrimination student movement demanding the resignation of the genocidal dictatorial government, law enforcement forces and armed terrorists of the Awami League, Chhatra League and Jubo League, who have seized power, opened fire at various places in various districts and upazilas across the country, including the capital Dhaka, on Sunday, killing nearly a hundred students. Thousands more have been seriously injured by bullets. On Saturday, the Awami League announced that on Monday, they planned to gather armed leaders and activists of the Awami League all over the country and unleash them on the pro-democracy students and public. 

Mirza Fakhrul said, Awami League terrorists and law enforcement forces opened fire with deadly firearms at various places in Dhaka, including Dhanmondi, Science Laboratory, Mirpur, Uttara, Topkhana Road. They have turned the entire country into a battlefield today and tried unsuccessfully to suppress the movement by killing, torturing and using force. The government is killing the student crowd by shooting indiscriminately on the pretext of talks. 

He said, as always, on Sunday, Awami terrorists are planning to attack various establishments including BSMMU and plot to blame the protesters. Like Saturday, on Sunday, Awami terrorists are establishing a reign of terror by attacking the homes of BNP and other opposition party leaders in different parts of the country. Demanding the resignation of the government, terrorists vandalized and set fire to the residence of NPP Chairman Dr. Fariduzzaman Farhad in Narail and the residence of BNP, Mymensingh South District Senior Joint Convener Zakir Hossain Bablu in Mymensingh, the BNP office in Jessore, and the CNG station of Dhaka Metropolitan BNP Member Secretary Tanvir Ahmed Robin in various areas. 

Fakhrul said, the government wants to sabotage the victory of the movement by inciting clashes and clashes in a planned manner. 

The people of Bangladesh, who are protesting in the burning Bangladesh, will defeat the government's conspiracy and snatch victory, Insha Allah. And those who killed the students in the ongoing movement, including the non-cooperation movement on Sunday, will definitely be tried on Bangladeshi soil. I pray for the eternal peace of the souls of all those who died and express my deep sorrow and condolences to the bereaved families. Their sacrifice will be written in golden letters in the history of Bangladesh. I also wish a speedy recovery to all the injured.

Headline_English: All garment factories announced to close
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers Association (BGMEA) has announced the closure of all garment factories in the country due to the ongoing student movement. 

This information was given in a press release sent by BGMEA on Sunday (August 4). 

The release signed by BGMEA President SM Mannan Kochi said that considering the emerging situation, all garment factory owners across the country have been requested to remain closed until further notice, keeping in mind the overall safety of workers and employees.

Headline_English: Police officer asks for '5 kg of potatoes' as bribe
Content_Enlish:
A police officer in Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh, India, has asked for 5 kg of potatoes as a bribe. However, the investigation has revealed that he used potatoes as a symbolic word for bribery. 

Follow Google News to get the latest news from gnewsdainik Ittefaq 
An audio recording of this SI named Ram Kripal Singh was leaked. After that, the matter came to light. He asked a farmer for a bribe to settle a case. 

In the viral audio, SI Kripal Singh is heard telling the farmer that he must give him 5 kg of potatoes. Then the farmer said that he could not afford it. Instead, he could give 2 kg of potatoes. The police officer got angry after hearing the farmer's reply. At one point in the conversation, the farmer agreed to give him 3 kg of potatoes. 

Kannauj SP Amit Kumar Anand has ordered the suspension of the sub-inspector posted at the Bhawalpur Chapunna Chowki under Sourikh police station. A departmental investigation into the case has also been suggested.

Headline_English: BNP to write to UN seeking investigation into murder
Content_Enlish:
BNP has decided to write to the United Nations and the chief advisor of the interim government seeking an impartial investigation into the killings that took place during the student-public movement. 
The party's Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir announced this decision at an emergency press conference at the BNP Chairperson's office in Gulshan on Saturday (August 10) night. 

Mirza Fakhrul said, "We have been talking about the brutal massacre that the government carried out with its government forces before the victory in this movement. The United Nations was also most concerned about this issue. We have decided to send a letter to the United Nations for an impartial investigation in this regard." 

He added, "We have also decided to write to the chief advisor of our interim government." 

Mirza Fakhrul said, "Around 50 workers have been imprisoned in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for supporting this movement. We will also write to the government to take initiative for their release." 

He also said, 'We are very concerned about the attacks on minorities. Misleading news is being spread about the current situation in Bangladesh in the media at home and abroad. There is talk of attacks on minority communities and deterioration of law and order situation, which we do not think is correct. Problems are being created in some places, which is a completely political incident.' 

Strongly condemning the attempt to spread news of these incidents involving BNP, Mirza Fakhrul said, 'BNP is not involved in such incidents, no healthy political party or person can be involved. This is a conspiracy through which an attempt is being made to sabotage the new independence achieved by Bangladesh.' 

BNP Standing Committee members Mirza Abbas, Abdul Moin Khan, Vice Chairman Barkat Ullah Bulu, Joynal Abedin, Advisory Council member of the Chairperson Masud Ahmed Talukder, Legal Secretary Kaiser Kamal and Mejbah Uddin were present at the press conference.

Headline_English: Tulip Siddique in new controversy
Content_Enlish:
Tulip Siddique has not been spared from controversy since becoming the UK's city minister in July this year. Recently, an investigation was launched against her regarding property-related income. This time, she has made a new headline for taking advantage of her aunt Sheikh Hasina's aide. 
In a report last Friday, the British media Daily Mail reported that Tulip is currently renting out her own house in a luxurious house worth 2 million pounds owned by her aunt Sheikh Hasina's special friend Abdul Karim. This property is located near the house Tulip Siddique bought herself. 

According to the Daily Mail report, Sheikh Hasina gave this British Bangladeshi named Abdul Karim the special status of CIP. Not only that, she also helped him get the post of Vice Chairman of Shahjalal Islami Bank. Despite having no experience, Karim got such a position in the bank with Hasina's patronage. 

And Tulip has obtained unfair advantages from this person who has the special blessing of Aunt Sheikh Hasina. He also hid the information about the rental of that five-bedroom luxurious house.

Headline_English: Justice Manik apologized to the presenter
Content_Enlish:
Retired Appellate Division Judge AHM Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik has apologized for misbehaving with host Deepti Chowdhury as a 'son of a king' during a talk show on the anti-discrimination movement. He also apologized to the public. 

The former judge apologized in writing to Supreme Court senior lawyer Fauzia Karim Firoz on Monday, who sent the legal notice. 

In response to the notice, former judge Manik wrote that he is a patient of hypertension and diabetes. He was feeling very tired. Due to this, he lost control of himself during the talk show. He apologized to the host for this kind of behavior. 

In this regard, Fauzia Karim Firoz told the media on Monday, 'Former judge Manik has responded to the legal notice. In it, he apologized in writing to host Deepti Chowdhury and the public. He sent me a message on WhatsApp at 5:38 pm on Monday (August 12) and attached a two-page letter written by him. 

Former Justice Manik was sent a legal notice on Sunday to publicly apologize to the nation for his misbehavior with Channel i TV presenter Deepti Chowdhury.

Headline_English: National University Vice-Chancellor resigns
Content_Enlish:
Now, the Vice Chancellor of the National University, Professor Mashiur Rahman, has resigned. He submitted his resignation to the Secretary of the Ministry of Education on Sunday afternoon. 
The matter was confirmed by Mohiuddin Mahi, Public Relations Officer of the National University. 

Professor Dr. Mashiur Rahman said, "I have resigned from the post of Vice Chancellor of the National University and joined Dhaka University." 

This professor from the Department of Sociology of Dhaka University was appointed as the Vice Chancellor of the National University in May 2021. Before that, he served as the Deputy Vice Chancellor of the university. 

It is known that on August 5, Awami League President and former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina resigned and left the country in the face of the uprising of students and the public. Since then, Mashiur Rahman has been absent from the university.

Headline_English: Police uniforms and logos are changing
Content_Enlish:
The decision to change the police uniform and logo has been taken. The decision was taken at a meeting of a delegation of protesting police members with Brigadier General (retired) M Sakhawat Hossain, Advisor to the Home Ministry, on Sunday afternoon. 

Senior Secretary of the Security Services Division of the Home Ministry Mashiur Rahman, Secretary of the Public Security Division Md. Jahangir Hossain, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md. Mainul Islam, Director General of BGB, Director General of the Passport and Immigration Department and various officials of the ministry were present at the meeting. 

The meeting assured that some of the 11-point demands of the police would be fulfilled in a short time. The other demands will be fulfilled in a long term. According to the decision of the meeting, from now on, no attack on the police will be allowed. If there is a complaint against any police member, higher officials should be informed. 

Advisor M Sakhawat Hossain held a meeting with the students before sitting with the police members. After the meeting, Adviser Brigadier General M Sakhawat Hossain said that the morale of the police has been broken due to the incidents of the last few days. He said, "The demands they have put forward are reasonable. Therefore, I have promised that we will accept their demands in the short and long term. We will accept some of the demands now." 

Criticizing the political government, he said, "The police are not at fault, but those who commanded them are more at fault. Many political tasks have been done through them. We will discuss these issues in detail in the cabinet meeting. The police members have promised me that they will work properly from now on. Earlier in the afternoon, I had a meeting with the students. The students told me that they have no conflict with the police. The police will fulfill their duties." 

Says M Sakhawat Hossain, who said that they have reached a consensus on forming an independent commission for police members, "There should be a police commission. The police will be run under that commission. They will not be under any political party. We must ensure that the police are not used politically.’ 

After the meeting, Inspector Zahidul Islam, the coordinator of the protesting police members, and Constable Shoabur Rahman, announced the withdrawal of the police strike. They said, ‘We are announcing the withdrawal of the strike with the assurance that most of the demands we had made to the government will be accepted. We hope that everyone will return to their respective duties in a peaceful manner.’

Headline_English: Rezaul survives fight with tiger in Sundarbans
Content_Enlish:
A fisherman named Rezaul Paik (45) was injured after being attacked by a tiger while cutting wood in the Sundarbans. 

He was attacked by a tiger while cutting firewood in the Sabed Ali canal of the Sundarbans at around 12 noon on Saturday (August 10). Rezaul is the son of the deceased Surat Paik of Paswekhali village in Munshiganj union of Shyamnagar upazila. 

It is learnt that Rezaul went to the Sabed Ali canal of the Sundarbans alone at around 12 noon on Saturday to cut wood. At that time, when the tiger attacked, he hit the tiger in the face with the tusks in his hand. Then the tiger ran away, leaving Rezaul behind. 

Forest Department's Koikhali Station Officer Salj Kumar Dwip confirmed the matter and said that the injured Rezaul is known to be hearing impaired. He is currently undergoing treatment at his home.

Headline_English: Former YouTube CEO Susan Wojcicki dies
Content_Enlish:
Former YouTube CEO Susan Wojcicki has died. She died on Friday (August 9) at the age of 56. 
Susan made space in her garage when the search giant Google was founded. She worked as a long-time executive at Google. 

Wojcicki served as CEO of YouTube for more than a decade, in addition to managing Google's main source of income, the company's 'advertising business'. 

Wojcicki's death was confirmed by her husband Dennis Tropper and Google CEO Sundar Pichai on social media. 

Wojcicki joined Google in 1998. She served as CEO of YouTube from February 2014 to February 2023. Later, Wojcicki resigned, citing "family, health, and personal work" as the reason. 

Tropper and Pichai said in the post that she was battling 'non-small cell' lung cancer. And earlier this year, her son Marco Tropper also died.

In 2014, former YouTube CEO Wojcicki was named one of the 50 most influential people in the world by The Verge. 

Wojcicki has long been considered one of the most powerful women in the company. In 2011, the San Jose-based Mercury News reported that she personally persuaded Google's board of directors to buy YouTube. 

Most importantly, Wojcicki also played a role in building Google's massive advertising business, where she helped the company create AdSense. 

The former Google executive was also instrumental in the 2007 acquisition of advertising company DoubleClick, a deal that is considered crucial in laying the foundation for Google's advertising empire.

Headline_English: Shakib likely to go to Pakistan to play Tests, but not coming to Dhaka
Content_Enlish:
All-rounder Shakib Al Hasan may join the Bangladesh team for the two-match Test series against Pakistan. However, there is no possibility of him returning to Dhaka for now. In that case, he may join the team directly in Pakistan instead of coming to Dhaka, according to Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) sources. 

Bangladesh is scheduled to play the first Test in Rawalpindi from August 21 on the Pakistan tour. After that, the second Test will start in Karachi from August 30. Pakistan has already announced a 17-member team for the series. However, Bangladesh has not yet announced the squad. 

According to BCB sources, the Bangladesh team may be announced on Sunday (August 11). And Shakib Al Hasan's name may be in it. 

According to reliable sources in the Cricket Operations Committee of the Bangladesh Cricket Board, Shakib has spoken to the selection panel. There, there was a discussion about Shakib joining the team directly in Pakistan. 

The country's best all-rounder is currently in Canada to play the Global Twenty20 tournament. 

Earlier, last week, Cricket Operations Committee Manager Shahriar Nafees said that Shakib has a no-objection letter until August 12 to play in this tournament. Shakib also said that he will be contacted about his participation in the Pakistan tour. 

Incidentally, Sheikh Hasina resigned from the post of Prime Minister on August 5 in the face of student protests. Since then, MPs and ministers close to the government have been in hiding. Cricket Board officials who have good relations with the Awami League government have also not been seen. Shakib Al Hasan was an Awami League member of parliament in the recently dissolved parliament. Therefore, the possibility of his returning to the country in the current unstable political situation is very low.

Headline_English: Rajkumar-Shraddha's 'Stree 2' sets new record on first day of release
Content_Enlish:
The horror-comedy film 'Stree' directed by Bollywood director Amar Kaushik was released in 2018. The film was a commercial success at the time. Since then, movie lovers have been waiting for its sequel. So, the makers were somewhat sure that 'Stree 2' would earn well. But after the film was released yesterday on India's Independence Day, everyone was surprised by its unexpected success. The film set a new record on the first day of its release. 

Indian media ABP Anand said that the film 'Stree 2' produced by Dinesh Bijan and starring Rajkummar Rao and Shraddha Kapoor did great on the first day of its release. According to box office data, the film has earned 76.5 crore rupees after its release yesterday. It is known that the budget of this film by Amar Kaushik is around 60 crore rupees. The film has crossed the total budget on the first day of its release. The makers have already started seeing profits. 

'Stree 2' has done business close to Rs 100 crore on the first day at the world box office. Seeing the income so far, the makers are hopeful that 'Stree 2' will cross the century mark this weekend. The film has already set a new record. 

Stree.2 
Rajkummar Rao and Shraddha Kapoor in a scene from the film 'Stree 2'. Image - Collected 

On the first day of its release, 'Stree 2' has surpassed Sunny Deol's 'Gadar 2' and Salman Khan's 'Tiger 3' in terms of earnings. The film has even surpassed Hrithik Roshan's 'Fighter' and Prabhas's 'Kalki 2898 AD' in Hindi. These two films earned Rs 22.5 crore on the first day of their release. 'Stree 2' earned Rs 23.36 crore from advance bookings. 

Meanwhile, apart from 'Stree 2', 'Veda' and 'Khel Khel Mein' have been released on the occasion of India's Independence Day. This action-thriller film starring John Abraham and Sharvari Bagh has been released in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu. 

On the first day of its release, 'Veda' earned Rs 6.52 crore. On the other hand, 'Khel Khel Mein' starring Akshay Kumar and Taapsee Pannu has done business of only Rs 5 crore. 

Apart from Rajkummar Rao and Shraddha Kapoor in the lead roles, 'Stree 2' also stars Pankaj Tripathi, Aparshakti Khurana, Abhishek Banerjee. Akshay Kumar and Varun Dhawan have been seen in guest roles in the film. Apart from this, Tamannaah Bhatia has already created a storm in the item song of the film.

Headline_English: Monkeypox virus detected in Pakistan
Content_Enlish:
Monkeypox virus has been detected in Asia. The health department of Pakistan's northern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province reported this information on Friday (August 16). So far, monkeypox virus has been detected in the bodies of three people in the country. According to the British news agency Reuters. 
The health department said that the virus was found in the bodies of the three people after returning from the United Arab Emirates. 

There have been previous outbreaks of monkeypox in Pakistan, but it has not yet been confirmed which type of virus the infected patients have been infected with this time. 

Salim Khan, Director General of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Health Department, said that monkeypox virus was detected in the bodies of two of the patients, and the samples of the third person have been sent to the National Institute of Health in the capital Islamabad for testing. He said that all three have been kept in quarantine. 

A spokesman for the Pakistani health ministry said that a suspected case of monkeypox has been detected in the country. 

The World Health Organization (WHO) declared a global public health emergency on Wednesday after an outbreak of monkeypox in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The following day, the organization confirmed the monkeypox virus had been detected in a person who had returned from Africa in Sweden.

Headline_English: Shakib Khan buys Dhaka franchise in BPL
Content_Enlish:
The ongoing political unrest in the country has affected all sectors. The sports arena was not left out. After the government fell in the face of student and public protests, the interim government took charge of the country. The country's sports arena, especially cricket, is going through an extreme crisis. New uncertainty has also arisen regarding the Bangladesh Premier League BPL. However, in the meantime, new news has emerged, Remark-Harlan, owned by popular Bengali film hero Shakib Khan, has bought a team in the BPL. 

Since the last edition of the BPL, it was heard that several franchises may withdraw their names from this year's event. At the top of that list was the 4-time champion Comilla Victorians. At the beginning of the 2024 BPL, the team's captain Nafisa Kamal had threatened the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) not to field a team before the start of the season, demanding a share of the income. 

The changes that are going to come in the cricket board in the changing context of the country after the fall of the government are also very visible. Therefore, it is believed that Nafisa Kamal's Comilla Victorians, who threatened not to keep a team in the last season, will not be in the upcoming BPL. 

But even though Comilla is not there, the presence of star owners in the BPL is not decreasing. This company of Shakib Khan, which is associated with the cosmetics business, has bought the franchise of Dhaka. 

Shakib joined this company called 'Remark and Harlan' at the beginning of this year, and the best superstar of domestic films is the managing director and owner of the company. However, Shakib is not the main entrepreneur of this company, Remark-Harlan was formed at the initiative of the country's electronics manufacturer Walton. 

Remark-Harlan has bought the ownership of the Dhaka franchise for the next BPL. A source from the Cricket Board has confirmed the truth of the matter. 

Both parties have already completed the formal process of buying the team, including signing money. In the last BPL, Dhaka was owned by the Newtex Group. The team's name was Great Dhaka at that time. Although the team was owned by Rupa Group in the previous BPL. Under Rupa Group, the team's name was Dhaka Dominators. This time too, the old culture of changing names will continue. This is what the relevant organization has said. 

This year's BPL is likely to start by the end of the year. And the players' draft is expected to be held sometime in September. However, after the change of government, BCB will have to suffer a lot with the new franchises.

Headline_English: Saudi Arabia to build cable car in Hera Cave
Content_Enlish:
Saudi Arabia plans to build a cable car system to make it easier for the general public to access the Hira Cave, where the Holy Quran was revealed. The country aims to launch this service by 2025. 

Visitors will be able to easily reach the Hira Cave through the cable car. This cave is located 4 kilometers away from the Holy Kaaba Sharif and at an altitude of 634 meters. The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) received the first words of the Quran from Allah in this cave. 

The Saudi government is planning to develop the area around the Hira Cave as a cultural center. The construction of the cable car system is part of this larger plan. 

Located on the famous Jabal Al-Nur mountain, Hira Cave is also known as the 'Mountain of Light'. The shape of the mountain is like a camel's hump and it has many steep slopes. 

The Hira Cave can accommodate five people at a time. It is a very important place for Muslims, as the memory of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the history of Islam are deeply intertwined with it. Before the advent of Islam and the revelation of the Quran, the Cave of Hira was not well known.

Headline_English: What kind of country do young people want?
Content_Enlish:
'Ethics should be brought back to education' 
—Nusrat Jahan, Student, National University 
What the future curriculum should be like is now a matter of thought. First of all, attention should be paid to skill development. A student is forced to enroll in different courses to develop skills separately after completing his studies. The curriculum should be made in such a way that they can develop skills during their student life. Textbooks should include subjects that are useful in real life. In higher education, Honors is four years and Masters is one year. This is a very long-term process. After the Honors Masters, the student has to study separately for a job. This long-term Honors Masters should be reduced. Looking at the syllabus of job exams, it seems that the history books have been opened. It is probably the demand of the hour to change this method of taking job exams by memorizing history. To keep pace with the world of the future, technical skills and polished English are required. Along with this, emphasis should be placed on research activities. 


'Corruption in development projects should be stopped' 
—Tasnia Hossain, student, Development Studies, BRAC University 
Although our public universities can play the role of a maternity ward in the movement and struggle, they are not doing well in education and research. We must focus on improving the quality of education to build the future of the country. We must ensure 100% transparent recruitment through merit verification in all government and private jobs, because corruption starts from there when recruitment is done considering 'references'. We want radical changes in government institutions that directly serve the common people. We do not want any more suffering or harassment for hours; bribery should also be completely eliminated. Besides, most of the country's major development projects are centered in the capital Dhaka. This time, decentralization initiatives need to be taken. We have seen examples of various manipulations to increase the cost of any project in the past, we do not want that in the new Bangladesh. This corruption should be stopped forever. 



'Reform in sports is very important' 
—Zahirul Qayum Firoz, young journalist 
In Bangladesh, popularity has alternated between cricket and football. There is no third sport in existence. Cricket and football are also in name only. They are unsuccessful in the international arena. To rebuild the fragile structure, the first thing that is needed is reform and decentralization of the minds of the audience. The days of only talking about two or three sports and their stars are over. We have to keep an eye on and keep informed about all sports. The biggest sporting event in the world is the Olympic Games. This time, five people from Bangladesh were represented, but there was no success. An Olympic medalist plays a big role in the country. Since there are many sports under one umbrella, the scope and potential are vast. Reform is needed here. To carry out the work of reform, decentralization of the audience, and holding players accountable, all boards will have to be reorganized. A long-term plan will have to be taken. 



'Let the free media be the voice of the new Bangladesh' 
—Tasnimul Hasan Uday, former student, Rajshahi University 
To consolidate the democratic system of a country, it is imperative to ensure the freedom of the media and the right to express one's opinion. Currently, Bangladesh's position in the free media index is below all other South Asian countries except Afghanistan. Which is very disappointing for us. I would like the media to have the opportunity to work independently in the future of Bangladesh. Due to the lack of a healthy democratic environment for a long time, the country's media has failed to provide objective and impartial news. As a result, a crisis of public trust in the media has arisen. The younger generation is becoming more dependent on social media for news. There is no alternative to working sincerely with the common people to restore trust in the public.

Headline_English: Dipu Moni used to sell the VC position for 2 crores
Content_Enlish:
Former Social Welfare Minister Dipu Moni is on a 4-day remand in the case of shooting dead grocery store owner Abu Sayed in the capital's Mohammadpur. Police arrested him on Monday (August 19) night from Baridhara in the capital while he was in hiding after the fall of the Awami League government. He has held the responsibilities of the Foreign Affairs, Education and Social Welfare ministries for the past 11 years. He was most discussed when he was the Education Minister.

Despite knowing about Dipu Moni's corruption and irregularities, the secretaries of his ministry did not open their mouths out of fear. Many say that he had a hand in everything from secondary school teachers to the appointment of university VCs. He used to take bribes of 2 crores for the appointment of university vice-chancellors (VCs) and 5 million taka for the appointment of college principals. During his time, this was an 'open secret' in the education sector. 

Those concerned said that Dipu Moni was the minister of three different ministries in three of the four terms of the Awami League government. By abusing his power, Dipu Moni himself and his relatives got involved in corruption. 

While Dipu Moni was the Education Minister, he established a huge kingdom of recruitment business through his brother Titu. The most discussed issue was the appointment of VCs and college principals in government universities. His brother had complete control over every transfer in the education administration. Various posts in the education administration were sold for a minimum of two lakh taka to a maximum of two lakh taka. 

Among government universities, there were more or less financial transactions in the appointment of VCs of all universities except DU, RU, CU, and Jahangirnagar. In the end, a saying spread that 'give 2 crores and become VC'. After that, VCs in the country's public universities indulged in recruitment business. 

An official of the UGC's government universities branch said that there was no precedent of financial transactions in the appointment of VCs of government universities in the history of Bangladesh. But Dipu Moni has set that example. 

According to the new curriculum, although the sale of note guides is banned, these books are being sold in large numbers across the country. A study has shown that 97 percent of students are dependent on notes or guides. Despite opposing note guides in public, Dipu Moni is accused of regularly taking commissions from note-guide sellers. He was assisted in this work by a publishing house owner. The owner of that publishing house lives in Chandpur.

Headline_English: Captain Ashiq receives Sena Gaurab Medal for showing patience
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Army's renowned Captain Ashiq has been awarded the 'Sena Gaurab Padak' (SGP) for his professionalism and patience. 
He was given the award at the office of Army Chief General Waqar-uz-Zaman on Sunday (August 18) afternoon. 

Captain Ashiq was honored at the office of Army Chief General Waqar-uz-Zaman. 

At the time, the Army Chief praised Captain Ashiq for maintaining professionalism even in adverse situations. He was also inspired for the future. 

Incidentally, a video recently went viral on social media. It can be seen that Captain Ashiq handled the situation with great prudence and patience and resolved it.

Headline_English: Cambodia fears government collapse like Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Sen has expressed concern that a movement to overthrow the government could start in Cambodia, inspired by the recent movement in Bangladesh. He said that people can enjoy freedom of expression, but that freedom should not be used to organize large-scale mass protests. Radio Free Asia reports. 

The Cambodian Prime Minister made this statement at a meeting with businessmen in the capital Phnom Penh recently. At that time, he mentioned the recent protests in Bangladesh and the incident of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina resigning and leaving the country as a result. 

Hun Sen said, "I do not want to see such a situation in Cambodia." 

The Cambodian Prime Minister claimed that he wants to prevent instability in his country, especially in the capital Phnom Penh. 

Addressing the guests present, he said, "If legal action is taken against those who try to create instability in Cambodia and press for protests like in Bangladesh, the government will not be accused of being dictatorial." 

Hun Sen became the Prime Minister of Cambodia in August 2023. His father, Hun Sen, previously ruled the country for decades.

Headline_English: Where is Zafar Iqbal, students are looking for him
Content_Enlish:
Where is Professor Dr. Muhammad Zafar Iqbal, the controversial and critical novelist and educationist who opposed the anti-discrimination movement? Has he also left the country or is he hiding in the country, students want to know. 

After former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina resigned and left the country, many influential Awami League members, influential leaders, ministers and state ministers of the newly overthrown government, mayors, councilors, journalists, and teachers have gone into hiding due to fear of arrest. Prominent Awami League figures are not found. However, Zafar Iqbal, an educationist who has been missing since before, has been missing. 

Zafar Iqbal was criticized for taking a stand against students in the midst of the anti-discrimination movement. After August 5, many students were seen posting on social media Facebook asking where Zafar Iqbal was. Many were also seen commenting that he was 'in a hole'. 

In addition, students who were agitating were trolling and making memes about Zafar Iqbal on various Facebook groups and pages. Many people posted pictures of the hole and captioned it as 'Zafar Iqbal's current status'. 

In the comment box of posts related to Zafar Iqbal on Facebook, Zafar Iqbal is seen being called 'broker', 'flatterer' and 'fraudster'. 

One Facebook user wrote, "Has the hole-dweller Zafar Iqbal disappeared into the hole again?" 

Another posted - "Well, where is Zafar Iqbal?" 

One person wanted to know how Zafar Iqbal Sir feels in the newly independent country? 

Many are also seen logically criticizing Zafar Iqbal. 

It is worth noting that in protest of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's statement calling him a Razakar, the quota reform movement at Dhaka University raised the slogan 'Ami ke, tumi ke; Razakar, Razakar'. A note by Zafar Iqbal expressing the students' reaction to such protests went viral on social media. In that note, Zafar Iqbal wrote, ‘Dhaka University is my university, my favorite university. But I don’t think I’ll ever want to go to this university again. When I see the students, I think that they might be the Razakars. And as long as I live, I don’t want to see the face of any Razakars. There is only one life. Why should I see the Razakars again in that life?’ 



After Zafar Iqbal’s comments, there was widespread anger among the protesting students. Professor Dr. Muhammad Zafar Iqbal was declared undesirable for taking a stand against the students’ demands and was banned for life by the protesting students of the Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUBST) in Sylhet. 

After the incident, Zafar Iqbal’s books are not available on the country’s largest online bookstore, Rokamari.com. Many publishers, including Bengal Books, have announced not to sell his books.

Headline_English: Metrorail service resumes after 37 days
Content_Enlish:
After being closed for 37 days, the metro rail is running again on the Uttara-Motijheel route in Dhaka. The metro rail is running as per the regular schedule from Sunday. However, the metro rail will not stop at the affected Kazipara and Mirpur 10 stations of the metro rail and passenger service activities are suspended. 


The office of the advisor to the Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges of the interim government informed on Saturday that the metro rail will start operating as per the new schedule from Sunday. Necessary instructions regarding metro rail travel for passengers can be found on the website and Facebook page of the metro rail operating company Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL). However, due to unavoidable reasons, the metro rail will not stop at Mirpur-10 and Kazipara stations for the time being and passenger service activities will be suspended. 

According to the previous schedule, the first train from Uttara North to Motijheel leaves at 7:10 am and the first train from Motijheel to Uttara leaves at 7:30 am. The last train from Uttara North to Motijheel will depart at 8:33 pm and the last train from Motijheel to Uttara will depart at 9:13 pm. 

However, only MRT/Rapid Pass can be used to travel on the two metro trains departing from Uttara North Metrorail Station at 7:10 am and 7:20 am. And only MRT/Rapid Pass can be used to travel on the metro trains departing from Motijheel Metrorail Station after 9:13 pm. 

DMTCL sources recently revealed that the lines, coaches and signaling system of the metro rail are all fine. Even then, the reason for the non-operation of the metro rail was the strike of the lower-level employees. The metro rail employees went on strike, alleging that senior officials were taking extra benefits. That is why the metro rail was closed even though there was no technical problem. 

Incidentally, miscreants attacked various important state institutions in the capital, taking advantage of the students' movement demanding quota reforms in government jobs. On July 19, they attacked the Kazipara and Mirpur-10 stations of the Metrorail. Earlier, when violence broke out, the Metrorail service was suspended from the afternoon of July 17. 

In this context, on the morning of July 20, the Metrorail operating company, Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMDCL), announced the suspension of Metrorail service until further notice for the need for urgent repairs and in the interest of the safety of people's lives and property.

Headline_English: At least 40 injured in Ansar-student clash, Hasnat Abdullah in hospital
Content_Enlish:
At least 40 people were injured in the chase and clash between Ansar members and students and the public in the capital's Secretariat area. The injured have been rescued and brought to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH). 

Hasnat Abdullah, one of the coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, fell ill at the time. He was taken to the One Stop Emergency Center (OSEC) of Dhaka Medical College Hospital. 

He was brought to the hospital sick around 11pm on Sunday (August 25). Earlier, a clash took place in front of the Secretariat at around 9:20pm. 

Inspector in-charge of the DMCH Police Camp, Bachchu Mia, told reporters, "When one of the coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement fell ill at the Secretariat, he was brought to Dhaka Medical College. He is currently undergoing treatment at the OSEC. He suddenly fell ill while being confined at the Secretariat. He has been put on oxygen at the OSEC of the emergency department. Doctors said he has no major problems." 

Ansar members had been protesting around the secretariat since morning. They were accompanied by night guards from government primary schools. The protest continued at night as well. Some advisors of the interim government, secretaries of various ministries and senior officials were trapped as the Ansar members surrounded the secretariat. Later, when the students tried to resist them at the call of two coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, a clash broke out between the two sides. The army arrived at the scene around 10 pm. 

Several employees of the secretariat said that Ansar members had surrounded the secretariat since morning to press for their demands. After office hours, the protesters closed the gates of the secretariat. At that time, various officials and employees, including the advisor and secretary, were trapped. Media workers were also trapped. Upon receiving news that the Ansar members were blocking the secretariat, the students started gathering at Raju Bhaskar at the call of the two coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement. At around 8:30 pm, coordinators Hasnat Abdullah and Sarjis Alam posted on social media on Facebook. The post reads, “Everyone comes to Raju. The autocratic power wants to return as Ansar. Despite accepting the demands, everyone is being kept in the secretariat.” 

Students clash with Ansars at the secretariat Students clash with Ansars at the secretariat 
Since then, students have been gathering at Raju Sculpture. At this time, many were seen holding sticks. The gathered students started chanting various slogans. At one stage, the students set off towards the secretariat. At this time, Ansar members chased the students. At this time, there were incidents of batons and bricks being thrown between the two sides. At one stage, the Ansar members retreated. 

At this time, the army members fired a few rounds of blank bullets and the police threw a few sound grenades to bring the situation under control. At this time, the army members are stationed at the gate of the secretariat. The Ansar members have dispersed. They have quickly left the secretariat and the surrounding area as they can. 

Meanwhile, after 10:30 pm, Advisor Nahid Islam and Advisor Asif Mahmud came out of the secretariat. They asked the agitated students to remain calm. They also said that action would be taken against the Ansar members who attacked the students at that time.

Headline_English: Big changes coming to the Google Play Store
Content_Enlish:
Big changes are coming to the Google Play Store from September. As a result, thousands of apps may be deleted from the Play Store. Google has taken this decision mainly to ensure the security of Android users and to make the Google Play Store more secure. 

Over the past few years, many users have fallen victim to apps containing malware. As a result, their personal information was stolen. Even a woman fell victim to a crypto app, due to which she lost a lot of money. Such incidents have forced Google to further strengthen the security system of the Play Store. 

Google has decided to make this big change to the Play Store considering the security of Android users. As a result of this decision by Google, the user's personal information will not reach third parties. 

Questions have been raised about the security of the Play Store before. The EPFL of Switzerland and other security agencies have expressed concerns about the security of Android. Many dangerous apps have been removed from the Play Store from time to time. Hackers have stolen and defrauded users' data through the Play Store apps. 

According to Google's new policy, uploading apps through third-party apps from the Play Store will be prohibited. As a result, users will no longer be able to download and install apps from outside the Play Store. 

Google's decision will make users safer. It will reduce the number of apps containing malware as well as reduce the risk of users' personal information being stolen.

Headline_English: Mirza Fakhrul calls for release of election roadmap
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Alamgir has urged the interim government's chief advisor, Nobel laureate Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus, to provide a roadmap for national elections and necessary reforms. 


He made the call at a discussion meeting marking the 9th death anniversary of Kazi Zafar Ahmed at the National Press Club on Saturday (August 24). 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said, "We have high expectations from the interim government. We all think that this government will arrange a fair election within a reasonable time. The chief advisor will present to the people what he wants to do very soon. We hope that he will arrange for the election very soon through a roadmap." 

He further said, “The interim government must hold discussions with political parties to meet the needs of the people as soon as possible. Arrangements must also be made on how to hold an election as soon as possible. Today, a new future has come before us. We must uproot all the garbage and take the country forward in a beautiful way.” 

At the same time, he also called on the interim government to take visible steps considering the interests of the people. 

Stating that the Awami League’s allies are still active, he urged the government and the protesting students to be vigilant to prevent conspiracies. He also instructed BNP leaders and activists to stand by the flood victims.

Headline_English: Garment worker murder case against Shakib Al Hasan
Content_Enlish:
A murder case has been filed against cricketer Shakib Al Hasan at the DMP's Adabor Police Station for ordering the murder of garment worker Rubel. Shakib Al Hasan has been named as the accused in the 28th complaint of the case. 


The address of accused number 28 in the case is Md. Shakib Al Hasan, former member of parliament, father: Mashrur Reza, Sang-Sahapara, Notun Bazar, Post Office: Magura. 

In addition, the remaining accused in the case are former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Obaidul Quader and 156 others. An unknown 400-500 people have been made accused in the case. 

On Thursday (August 22), garment worker Rubel's father Rafiqul Islam filed the case as the plaintiff. DMP's Adabor Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Md. Nazrul Islam confirmed the matter of the case. 

In the case statement, the plaintiff alleged that on August 5, Rubel participated in a protest march on the Ring Road of Adabor. At that time, someone opened fire on the procession with the direct and indirect instructions, instigation, assistance, cooperation and direct support of the accused. Rubel was taken to the hospital with bullet wounds in the chest and stomach and died on August 7 while undergoing treatment.

Headline_English: Ronaldo breaks world record by opening YouTube channel
Content_Enlish:
Cristiano Ronaldo is already quite active on social media. He has accounts on Facebook, X (formerly Twitter) and Instagram. However, he did not have an account on YouTube. Recently, he is opening a YouTube channel named “UR Cristiano”. 

Internet users have been in a frenzy since the channel was opened on Wednesday (August 21). The number of followers on the channel has exceeded 12.5 million in one day. 

Al-Jazeera reported that the number of followers on Cristiano Ronaldo’s channel reached 1 million or 1 million in the first hour. Which is a new world record. No other YouTube channel has surpassed 1 million followers in such a short time. 

Cristiano Ronaldo is considered one of the greatest stars in the world of football. The only one who is equal to him in the fight for excellence is Argentine superstar Lionel Messi. Ronaldo surpassed Messi in the number of followers on the YouTube channel in just 2 hours. 

Messi’s YouTube channel journey began 18 years ago. The number of followers of that channel was 2.16 million on Wednesday night at around 11 pm. And the number of followers of Ronaldo increased to 2.17 million in just 2 hours. 

Ronaldo announced the launch of a YouTube channel under his own name on Wednesday evening (Bangladesh time). He wrote on social media, “The wait is over. Finally my YouTube channel is here! SIUUUSubscribe (Subscribe) and join me on this new journey.”

Headline_English: 2.9 million people affected by floods
Content_Enlish:
The Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief has said that 440,840 families in eight districts of the country have been affected by the ongoing flash floods in the country. 

In a statement on Thursday (August 22), the ministry said that about 2.9 million people in eight districts have been affected by the floods. Two people have died due to drowning in the flood waters. 

The statement, citing weather agencies, said that the trend of heavy rainfall in the northeastern region and its adjacent upstream areas may decrease in the next 24 hours. At this time, the flood situation in Moulvibazar in the northeastern region and the low-lying areas adjacent to the Manu, Khowai, and Dhalai rivers in Habiganj district may initially be stable and may improve later. 

Experts had warned of the threat of floods in advance Experts had warned of the threat of floods in advance 
The Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief said that relief distribution activities are ongoing in the flood-affected districts, and that so far the number of flood-affected districts is eight. They are Feni, Comilla, Chittagong, Khagrachari, Noakhali, Moulvibazar, Habiganj and Brahmanbaria. 50 upazilas of these districts have been flooded. 357 unions have been affected. 

The information report also mentions that one person died in Feni and one in Brahmanbaria in the flood. 

The ministry said that a total of 1,534 shelters have been opened to provide shelter to people trapped in the water or affected by the flood and a total of 75,668 people and 7,459 cattle have been sheltered in the shelters. 

The Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief also said that a total of 444 medical teams are operational to provide medical services to the affected people in 8 districts. And the ministry has so far allocated 18.2 million taka in cash and 13,600 tons of rice for distribution among the flood victims. 

The army and navy are engaged in rescue operations in the flood-hit areas of Feni district, the ministry said. 160 personnel and 40 rescue vehicles from the army have been sent to Feni district. A water treatment plant has also been set up. 71 personnel and eight rescue vehicles from the navy are working.

Headline_English: Cyclone 'Asana' is approaching
Content_Enlish:
The deep depression formed in the Arabian Sea has intensified into Cyclone Asana. The cyclone is said to be moving westwards. 

The India and Pakistan Meteorological Departments gave the information on Friday. Reuters reported. 

The Pakistan Meteorological Department said that Cyclone Asana is currently located 190 km west-northwest of Bhuj region of Gujarat in India and 200 km southeast of Karachi. 

Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast said that Cyclone Asana may hit the western Indian state of Gujarat as well as the coast of Pakistan's southeastern province of Sindh. After that, it may move towards Oman over the northeastern Arabian Sea. 

It is known that due to the impact of this cyclone, rainfall has already started in Gujarat. Vast areas have been submerged in water. There is a possibility of further deterioration of the situation in that area. The district authorities have urged local residents to leave their homes and take shelter in shelters due to the cyclone. 

Indian meteorologists say that cyclones are rare in this region during the monsoon season. Usually, between June and September, low pressures cannot transform into cyclones due to the strong resistance of the southwest monsoon.
