Wang Huning, Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), expressed this conviction in a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. 

Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud gave this information at a press briefing held at the St. Regis Hotel in Beijing on Tuesday (July 9) evening. He also said that earlier in the afternoon, 16 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) were signed between several companies of Bangladesh and China. 

Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud said that in a very cordial atmosphere between Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and the Chairman of the National Committee of the CPPCC, both sides emphasized the importance of increasing communication between the Bangladesh Awami League and the Communist Party of China. The meeting also reached an agreement on mutual visits of party leaders. Wang Huning said that the common goal of both the Communist Party of China and the Awami League is the welfare of the people. 

While highlighting the courtesy call on Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) President Jin Liqun in the parlor room of the Prime Minister's Beijing residence, St. Regis Hotel, on Tuesday morning, Dr. Hasan Mahmud said that the Prime Minister has called on AIIB to invest in suitable sectors including infrastructure development, river dredging, and climate change in Bangladesh. The AIIB President described Bangladesh's development and progress under the leadership of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as unprecedented. 

Friday 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina attended the 'Summit on Trade, Business and Investment Opportunities Between Bangladesh and China' conference at Shangri-La Circle in Beijing on Tuesday afternoon. Dr. Hasan said that about 90 business representatives from Bangladesh and more than 100 businessmen from China attended the conference and 16 MoUs were signed between several companies from Bangladesh and China. At the conference, the Prime Minister invited the Chinese business community to invest in Bangladesh by taking advantage of the world's most liberal investment regime. Sheikh Hasina called for greater investment in infrastructure, ICT, tourism, agro-processing industries, energy sector including renewable energy, climate-resilient smart farming, waste management, green technology and development sectors. 

When the Prime Minister mentioned the plan to establish three special tourism zones and the investment opportunities in the Chinese real estate and hospitality sectors there, the Chinese also showed considerable enthusiasm in this regard. At the conference organized by the Bangladesh Embassy, ​​BIDA, BSEC China World Summit Wing, Chinese Vice Minister of Commerce Mr. Li Fei, Chairman of China Communications Construction Group Company Limited Mr. Wang Tong Zhu, President and CEO of HSBC China Mr. Mark Wang, Senior Vice President of Huawei Mr. Simon Lin expressed their interest. 

In response to a question, the Foreign Minister said that all the programs of the Prime Minister's visit to China remain unchanged. Only instead of the morning of the 11th, the Prime Minister will leave for Dhaka on a special flight of Bangladesh Biman on the night of July 10. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina left for China on a state visit last Monday morning. Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a bilateral meeting with the Prime Minister at the Great Hall of the People. Before that, the Prime Minister will be received at the Great Hall of the People of China on Wednesday morning. After the reception, the Prime Minister will meet with Chinese Premier Li Keqiang and hold bilateral meetings with high-level delegations from both countries. After that, the two sides are expected to sign memorandums of understanding and announce the inauguration of several projects in the presence of the heads of government of both countries.

Headline_English: Tulip Siddique, Britain's first Bangladeshi-origin minister
Content_Enlish:
Tulip Siddique MP, granddaughter of Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, is set to become the first British-Bangladeshi minister in the British cabinet. She will be the Minister for Cities in Sir Keir Starmer's new government. An official announcement from the new British government is yet to be made. 

This information was reported by the American media outlet Bloomberg in a report on Tuesday (July 9). 

The Labour Party won last week's election in the UK. Tulip Siddique won the election for the fourth time in a row. She was working as a shadow minister as a Labour Party MP. This time, the party has appointed her as the Minister for Cities. 

Tulip, 41, has worked in the City of London's financial district since 2021. 

Tulip will replace Bim Afolamir as the Minister for Cities. Bim is a former HSBC banker. He served under the previous Conservative government. 

Tulip first won the Hampstead-Kilburn seat in 2015, marking his first entry into the House of Commons. He then won the same seat in the 2017 and 2019 elections. That year, he was named one of the 1,000 most influential politicians in the UK.

Headline_English: The next program of the anti-quota movement will be announced on Saturday evening.
Content_Enlish:
The anti-quota protesters will announce the next program of their movement on Saturday.

Follow Google News to get the latest news from Daily Ittefaq
One of the organizers of the movement, Abu Bakar Majumder, said that all the coordinators of the movement from campuses across the country will consult using both online and offline platforms and come to a decision on their next steps.

He said that the program will be announced in front of the Central Library of Dhaka University at 6 pm on Saturday.

Earlier, in response to the police attack on students in several places outside Dhaka and demanding justice, Dhaka University students held protest rallies and blocked Shahbagh intersection.

As per the previously announced program, Dhaka University students gathered in front of the Central Library and took out a protest procession and came to Shahbagh intersection and blocked the road unannounced on Friday.

Later, around 4:30 pm, Dhaka College students came to Shahbagh with a procession and joined the Dhaka University students.

There, the protesters raised slogans demanding justice for the police attack on students.

They ended the protest program after Majumdar announced tomorrow's program before leaving Shahbagh at around 6:20 pm.

In 2018, the issue of 56 percent reservation of posts in various quotas in government jobs was canceled. In 2021, the descendants of the freedom fighters filed a writ challenging this decision. Then, on June 5, 2024, the High Court declared the abolition of the 30 percent freedom fighter quota in jobs illegal.

Later, the government applied to the Appellate Division Chamber Court to stay the High Court order. The court ordered a one-month stay on the High Court's verdict on the restoration of the freedom fighter quota system in first and second class government jobs.

Headline_English: Imran Khan's party gets reserved seats in Pakistan's parliament
Content_Enlish:
The Supreme Court of Pakistan has declared that Imran Khan's party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) is eligible for 23 reserved seats in the country's parliament. The announcement was made by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in an order on Friday. 
Follow Google News to get the latest news from Daily Ittefaq 
The National Assembly elections were held in Pakistan on February 8. The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leaders participated as independents as they were banned from participating in party elections. 

Although they won the largest number of seats in parliament, the Election Commission announced that independents would not get a share of the 70 reserved seats. These seats are reserved only for political parties. 

As a result, those seats in parliament were distributed among political parties. Most of these seats were won by the parties of the ruling coalition government in Pakistan. 

While reading out the Supreme Court's order on Friday, Chief Justice Qazi Faiz Isa said, "PTI as a political party is eligible for reserved seats. The order was supported by eight judges of the 13-member bench of the court. Five were against. 

Although the PTI gets 23 reserved seats in parliament, it will not affect the majority of Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif's coalition government. However, it will strengthen the political position of Imran Khan's supporters.

Headline_English: Torch march at JU to protest attacks on quota protesters
Content_Enlish:
Students of Jahangirnagar University (JU) have taken out a torchlight procession to protest attacks on students in several parts of the country in the ongoing movement demanding reform of the quota system in government jobs. 
Follow Google News to get the latest news from Daily Ittefaq 
On Friday (July 12), at 7:30 pm, students took out a torchlight procession under the banner of 'Anti-discrimination Student Movement' from in front of the university's central library. 

The procession passed through the campus's Battola, circled the streets in front of the students' residential halls, and ended at the Central Shaheed Minar. Later, the students held a short rally there. 

During the procession, students chanted 'Why was my brother attacked? They shouted slogans like 'Trial, trial, trial', 'In the Bengal of the Liberation War, there is no place for discrimination', 'Report to all Bengal, bury the quota system', 'Let the quota system be abolished, let the talented be free', 'The tool of the 18th grade, roar once again', 'It has awakened, it has awakened, the student community has awakened', etc. 

The students said at the rally that during our rational movement, the police attacked students in various universities of the country. We strongly condemn and protest this incident. Along with this, those involved in this heinous incident should be identified and brought to justice. 

Alif Mahmud, a student of the English department, said that the movement cannot be suppressed by attacking and filing cases. The movement will continue until our demands are accepted. 

The rally was moderated by Abdur Rashid Jitu, a student of the Bangabandhu Institute of Comparative Literature and Culture, and was addressed by Mahfuz Islam Megh, a student of the Department of Environmental Science, and Arif Sohel and Touhid Siam, students of the Department of International Relations.

Headline_English: Anti-liberation forces have taken over the anti-quota movement: Obaidul Quader
Content_Enlish:
Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader has commented that the spirit of the Liberation War and anti-liberation forces have taken over the students' anti-quota movement. He said that the Appellate Division has issued a four-week stay on the Supreme Court's High Court Division's verdict on quota reservation in government jobs. After this order of the Appellate Division, the High Court Division's verdict is currently ineffective. Even then, there is no logic in the students' movement continuing. The spirit of the great Liberation War and anti-liberation forces have taken over this movement. Follow Google News to get the latest news from Dainik Ittefaq 
He said this in a statement sent to the media on Friday (July 12) evening. 

Obaidul Quader said, against whom will the students protest? The order of the Supreme Court's Appellate Division is in their favor. The fact that the movement is continuing proves that some group or group is instigating this movement to achieve political objectives. If the students continue this movement, the suffering of the general public is increasing. Public suffering is being created. If the people become hostage to this movement, they will lose trust in young students. 

Stating that a certain political group is trying to create conflict between students and the people and gain advantage, he said, "We do not believe that all the students who are soft-hearted want to ignore the directives of the country's highest court. Only those who are politically motivated are trying to show strength by ignoring the directives of the court." 

In the statement, Obaidul Quader said that whenever there is any movement, BNP-Jamaat and their allies use it as a tool and become immersed in the nightmare of coming to power. Now they are trying to rely on the quota movement. Because the people have no trust in them. When they were in power, they turned Bangladesh into a failed state through corruption, looting, terrorism and radicalism. 

Stating that BNP could not succeed in any anti-government movement, he said, "That is why whenever a non-political movement is organized, BNP tries to capitalize on it and do politics." 

Obaidul Quader requested the protesting students to return to their educational institutions and said, "You will not be abused as someone's political tool." The lawyers for the protesters have the opportunity to present further arguments in the final hearing. The country's highest court will settle the matter through the final hearing. The court will take into account the grievances of the protesting students and give a realistic final verdict during the final hearing and the matter will be settled. We urge the protesters to be patient. At the same time, we once again request them to avoid all such programs that may cause suffering to people and return to their respective educational institutions as per the court's instructions.

Headline_English: The Olympics will be held in Saudi Arabia for the first time
Content_Enlish:
Saudi Arabia will host the Olympic Games for the first time in 2025, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced on Friday (July 12). 
Follow Google News to get the latest news from Daily Ittefaq 
IOC President Thomas Bach said in a statement, "We are very fortunate to be working with Saudi Arabia on the Olympic Games. The Olympic Games will benefit greatly from this experience." 

Saudi Arabia's Sports Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki Al Faisal said, "We are a young nation with more than 23 million athletes. Our country has become a global hub for professional sports. This (hosting the Olympics) is a good step for our young athletes, our country and sports fans around the world." 

Last year, Saudi Arabia launched an annual sports world cup. The first edition is currently being held in Riyadh from July 3 to August 25. 

Saudi Arabia currently invests heavily in various sports, including football, boxing and golf. 

The International Olympic Committee has also been trying for years to connect with a younger generation of potential Olympic fans. Hosting the Olympics in Saudi Arabia is one such attempt.

Headline_English: Coronavirus still kills 1,700 people a week
Content_Enlish:
Covid-19 is still killing around 1,700 people a week worldwide. The World Health Organization on Thursday urged vulnerable populations to get vaccinated against the disease. 
Follow Google News to get the latest news from Daily Ittefaq 
World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has warned of a decline in vaccine coverage. 

The UN health agency chief told a news conference that despite the continuing death toll, “data analysis shows that vaccine coverage has declined among health workers and people over 60. These are the two groups most at risk.” 

“The World Health Organization recommends that people in the highest-risk groups receive a Covid-19 vaccine within a year of their last dose.” 

The WHO has reported more than seven million Covid deaths, although the true death toll in the pandemic is believed to be much higher. 
Corona has also shattered economies and crippled health systems. 

Meanwhile, the World Health Organization has urged governments to maintain virus surveillance and sequencing and ensure adequate access to affordable and reliable tests, treatments and vaccines. 

Tedros declared the outbreak an international public health emergency in May 2023, more than three years after the virus was first identified in Wuhan, China, in late 2019.

Headline_English: Trump is unfit to lead: New York Times
Content_Enlish:
The editorial board of the influential newspaper The New York Times has declared Republican Party candidate Donald Trump ‘unfit to lead’ in the upcoming US presidential election. They said that he is dangerous in words and deeds. He puts himself above the country. 
The editorial board of the New York Times said this in an article published on Thursday ahead of the Republican Party National Convention. 

The Republican Party National Convention will be held next week. At this convention, Trump will be officially announced as the party’s candidate for the upcoming US presidential election. 

The New York Times editorial board noted that Trump is going to get the Republican Party’s nomination in the US presidential election for the third time in eight years. 

The board said that a once great political party (the Republican Party) is now working for the interests of one man (Trump). He is a man who is clearly unfit to be president of the United States. His values, whims, ideas and language are in direct opposition to many of the things that have made this country great. 

The council called Trump's nomination a disappointing decision. For more than two decades, a large majority of Americans have said they are dissatisfied with the way the country is being run. The post-pandemic climate of rampant inflation, high interest rates, social divisions and political instability has left many voters even more frustrated. 

The council said the Republican Party once used electoral power to solve such problems. The party's vision for the country was rooted in values ​​such as freedom, sacrifice, personal responsibility and the well-being of all. The council cited George H.W. Bush, John McCain and Mitt Romney as examples. It said the party's understanding of these values ​​was reflected in its long-standing conservative policy agenda. Today, many Republicans are not concerned with Trump's stance on immigration, trade and taxes. But the issue in this election is not about policy differences; it is about something more fundamental. That is, what qualities are most important in a president and commander in chief of the United States. 

The council said Trump has displayed a character that is unbecoming of the president. He has shown a complete disregard for the Constitution, the rule of law, and the American people. He lacks a compelling vision for the future of the country; rather, he is driven by a thirst for political power. That is, the use of government power to advance his own interests, appease his enemies, and exact revenge on those he believes have wronged him. Simply put, he is unfit to lead.

Headline_English: Hasaranga steps down from Sri Lanka captaincy
Content_Enlish:
Hasaranga de Silva has resigned as the captain of the Sri Lankan T20 team. He has sent his resignation letter to Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC). He was appointed captain of the shortened version of the Sri Lankan team in January. 

In a statement, the SLC said that Hasaranga stepped down in the larger interest of Sri Lankan cricket. In his resignation letter, Hasaranga wrote, "As a player, I will always give my best in Sri Lankan cricket and I will always stand by my team and support the leadership." 

The Sri Lankans could not get out of the group stage of the recently concluded T20 World Cup in the United States and the West Indies. Hasaranga had to face criticism for the team's failure. After the World Cup, Sri Lanka's head coach Chris Silverwood and consultant Mahela Jayawardene stepped down from their positions. Former captain Sanath Jayasuriya has recently been appointed as the interim coach. 

With Hasaranga stepping down, Sri Lanka will have to quickly find a new captain for the T20 format. Because the Sri Lankans will play a three-match T20 series against India at home starting July 26 this month. 

Batsman Charith Asalanka is in the running to replace Hasaranga as captain. He previously led the team in two matches in Hasaranga's absence. In these, there was one win and one loss. Hasaranga captained Sri Lanka in 10 T20Is. Under his leadership, the Sri Lankans won 6 and lost 4.

Headline_English: Case filed against students for attack on journalist
Content_Enlish:
A case has been filed against students protesting against the cancellation of quotas in connection with the attack on a journalist in the capital's Shahbagh. The case alleges assault on a journalist with intent to kill, obstruction, causing damage and intimidation. 

Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mostazirur Rahman confirmed that the case was filed at Shahbagh Police Station on Saturday (July 13). 

He said that Syed Asaduzzaman, senior manager of the human resources and administration department of Somoy Television, filed the complaint as the plaintiff. Many unidentified people have been mentioned in the complaint. 

The complaint states that on Thursday (July 11) at around 6:20 pm, the protesters started abusing Somoy Television's senior reporter Toha Khan Tamim (37) and cameraman Sumon Sarkar (36) in foul language. They said, "Take the camera of Somoy TV, you *fuck it." The protesters then started throwing several large bricks at journalists Toha Khan Tamim and Sumon. One of them landed on Tamim's left hand. 

At this time, the protesters tried to snatch the camera and live broadcast device from Sumon's hands and took off Tamim's helmet and hit him hard on the head with the intention of killing him. The statement also mentions that the protesters intimidated them and threatened to kill them in various ways.

Headline_English: Elon Musk donates to group working to elect Trump
Content_Enlish:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk has donated to a 'super political action committee' supporting Donald Trump in the US presidential election. 

Bloomberg reports that it is not clear how much Musk has donated. However, it is believed to be a large amount. 

Former US President Trump, who is officially nominated as the Republican Party's candidate, recently met with Elon Musk and other wealthy donors. 

Elon Musk has donated to candidates in both parties in the US for years. The New York Times previously wrote that Elon Musk's donations have been divided roughly equally between Democrats and Republicans over the years. 

The US presidential election will be held on November 5. Trump has already confirmed the Republican nomination. 

Incumbent US President Joe Biden, who is seeking a second term as president, has received enough delegates to win the Democratic nomination. 

Both the Republican and Democratic parties are expected to choose their presidential candidates at party conventions in late summer.

Headline_English: KP Sharma returns to power in Nepal
Content_Enlish:
A new government has been formed in Nepal after Maoist leader Pushpa Kamal Dahal alias Prachanda lost a confidence vote. Three-time Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli has been appointed as the Prime Minister of this government. 

The Kathmandu Post reported that President Ram Chandra Paudel has appointed him as the Prime Minister for the third time. Oli will also take oath with the new cabinet on Monday. 

He was appointed Prime Minister in the face of political instability and difficult challenges in the country. 

The 'pro-China' Oli is the head of the Communist Party of Nepal (Unified Marxist Leninist). He returned to the Kathmandu chair with the support of the Nepali Congress led by Sher Bahadur Deuba. 

Pushpa Kamal Dahal lost a confidence vote in the House of Representatives on Friday. As a result, the process of forming a new government under Article 76 (2) of the country's constitution has begun. 

President Paudel Oli was appointed by the government under Article 76(2) of the Constitution after receiving the support of 166 lawmakers, including 88 from the Nepali Congress and 78 from the UML. 

72-year-old K P Sharma Oli previously served as the Prime Minister of Nepal from 11 October 2015 to 3 August 2016, from 5 February 2018 to May 2021, and from May 2021 to 13 July 2021.

Headline_English: 5 instructions including ban on outsiders in DU halls
Content_Enlish:
The administration has taken 5 decisions to control the situation arising on campus and ban outsiders from the halls. Instructions have also been given accordingly. 
This decision was taken in a meeting organized with the hall provosts on Monday (July 15) afternoon. This information was given in a notification sent by the university's public relations office. 

The instructions are - students will stay peacefully in their respective halls; the principal and resident teachers will stay in the halls at all times and take necessary measures to ensure the safety of the students; no outsiders will be allowed to stay in the halls; all concerned are being called upon to refrain from any kind of rumors and propaganda; all are being asked to refrain from subversive activities. 

If anyone is involved in subversive activities, strict action will be taken according to the university rules. The meeting called on all concerned to behave responsibly to maintain the peaceful environment of education at the university. 

Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. ASM Maksud Kamal presided over the meeting, and Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Administration) Professor Dr. Muhammad Samad, Pro-Vice Chancellor (Education) Professor Dr. Sitesh Chandra Bachar, Treasurer Professor Momtaz Uddin Ahmed and the principals and wardens of various halls and hostels.

Headline_English: A 4 billion taka pawn has fled to the US.
Content_Enlish:
Jahangir Alam, the controversial businessman who became the owner of 400 crore taka, has fled to the United States. He left for the United States on Sunday night amid discussions and criticism. Jahangir's elder brother Md. Mir Hossain confirmed this information to the media on Monday (July 15) afternoon. He is the president of the Khilpara Union Awami League in Chatkhil Upazila of Noakhali. 

Jahangir has a four-story house in Naharkhil village of Khilpara Union. When I went to that house in the afternoon, I met Mir Hossain on the ground floor. The upper three floors of the house are empty. Jahangir used to live on the second and third floors. No one lives there now. All the floors are locked. 

When asked where Jahangir is now, Mir Hossain told a media outlet, "Jahangir has married twice. The first wife has one child and the second wife has three children. The first wife is in the country, but Jahangir has no contact with her. The second wife lives in the United States with her children. Jahangir went to him on Sunday night. 

Mir Hossain also said, "We knew that he had a very good relationship with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. He used to come and go to her office. Suddenly, I was ashamed and shocked to hear that he had become the owner of Tk 4 billion at the Prime Minister's press conference on Sunday. In the evening, the matter spread in the area. Jahangir was still in the country. Then at night, I heard that he had gone to the United States. However, I have not spoken to him yet. All his personal mobile numbers are switched off. That is why I cannot contact him." 

To confirm this, Jahangir Alam's personal mobile number could not be connected despite multiple attempts. He did not respond to SMS and WhatsApp messages on his mobile. 

Earlier, at a press conference held at Ganabhaban on Sunday afternoon, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina brought up the issue of the financial assets of a former peon in her house while talking about taking action against corruption. The Prime Minister said, "He worked in my house, he was a peon, now he is the owner of Tk 4 billion. He cannot do without a helicopter. It is a fact. How did he make so much money? I found out, I took action later.’ 

Although the Prime Minister did not indicate the identity of the peon, multiple sources in the Prime Minister’s Office said that the peon’s name was Jahangir Alam. A special notification was issued by the Prime Minister’s Office about him before the 12th national election. Everyone was advised to be vigilant and seek the help of law enforcement agencies regarding him. Jahangir served as the Prime Minister’s personal employee for the entire two terms from 2009 to 2018 and for part of the Prime Minister’s third consecutive term. Jahangir also worked as a personal staff at Sudha Sadan, the Prime Minister’s residence, when he was in the opposition party. 

Investigation revealed that although Jahangir was the Prime Minister’s personal employee, he used to introduce himself as the Prime Minister’s Personal Special Assistant. He used this identity to regularly lobby the Secretariat. At the same time, he embezzled money from various leaders of the Awami League by lobbying them. Using the same identity, he also secured the post of Vice President of Noakhali District Awami League. He has created his own political circle in the Noakhali-1 parliamentary constituency. 

A district intelligence source said that Jahangir understood that he could be arrested at any time. Therefore, he planned to leave the country by any means. 

Meanwhile, Bangladesh Bank has ordered the freezing of the bank accounts of Jahangir Alam, his wife Kamrun Nahar and their related organizations. They have also been asked to send all the information including the account opening form within the next five days. On Sunday afternoon, the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) of the central bank sent instructions to all banks in this regard. 

The instructions said that if there are any accounts in the names of the mentioned individuals and the organizations owned by them in the banks/financial institutions, the transactions of those accounts have been suspended for 30 days under Section 23(1)(c) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2012. 

When asked about Jahangir Alam's escape to the United States, Noakhali-1 MP HM Ibrahim said, "I have heard about it. But I don't know if it is true or false."

Headline_English: Foreign woman arrested with 4 kg of cocaine at Chittagong Airport
Content_Enlish:
A foreign woman has been arrested at the Chattogram Shah Amanat International Airport with cocaine-like substances. Airport Security and Intelligence (APBN) members arrested her on Monday (July 15) morning. A 3 kg 900 gram packet of cocaine was recovered from a UPS after searching her bag. 

The woman arrested, named Stalia Shante, is a citizen of the Caribbean island nation of Bahamas. However, her details are not known. The substance seized from her custody has been sent to the Narcotics Control Department for testing to determine whether it is cocaine or not. 

It is learned that Stalia reached Dubai from Brazil on an Emirates flight on July 12. From there, she arrived in Chittagong on a Fly Dubai flight on Saturday. However, her luggage did not arrive that day. Stalia had been staying at the Agrabad Hotel in the city for the past three days. 

Based on a secret tip-off, APBN members followed her. When he went to the airport at around 10:30 am on Monday to collect the luggage that arrived two days later, the security and intelligence team and APBN members detained him. After searching the luggage, cocaine-like substances were recovered. The weight of the items was 3 kg 900 grams. They were kept inside a UPS in the luggage.

Headline_English: Books of Bengal will not sell books written by Zafar Iqbal
Content_Enlish:
Books of Bengal is a platform for buying books in Bangladesh and West Bengal, India. They have about 77 thousand followers on social media. Books of Bengal has announced that it will not sell children's writer and educationist Muhammad Zafar Iqbal's books in the wake of a statement he made about the quota reform movement. 

In a post on Facebook on Tuesday (July 16), Books of Bengal said, 'Like many, we also grew up reading Muhammad Zafar Iqbal's writings. Like many, he instilled an interest in the Liberation War in us. But the kind of statement he made today about the quota movement and Dhaka University is in no way acceptable to us.' 

They also wrote, 'We condemn this statement. As a protest, Books of Bengal Bangladesh will not sell any book by Muhammad Zafar Iqbal from today onwards.' 

Earlier, a part of a two-page letter written by Muhammad Zafar Iqbal went viral on social media. In it, he wrote, 'Dhaka University is my university, my favorite university. But I think I will never want to go to this university again. When I see the students, I think that they might be the 'Razakars'. And as long as I live, I do not want to see the face of any Razakars. There is only one life, why should I see the Razakars again in that life?'

Zafar Iqbal told the media, 'I support the need to reform quotas. However, I do not support disrespecting the Liberation War in the name of the movement.' Muhammad Zafar Iqbal made this statement after being deeply shocked by the 'Razakar' slogans raised by the students at Dhaka University.

Headline_English: All universities announced to be closed
Content_Enlish:
The University Grants Commission (UGC) has directed all public and private universities in the country to remain closed. The UGC issued this directive on Tuesday (July 16) night. 

The UGC notification said that in accordance with the decision of the government's Ministry of Education, all public and private universities in the country and all colleges, including university-affiliated medical, textile, engineering and other colleges, will remain closed until further notice, considering the safety of students. 

At the same time, the notification has instructed students to leave the residential halls for the sake of their safety and stay in safe places. 

Meanwhile, the National University has announced the closure of the National University affiliated colleges in a notification. The notification said that all colleges and institutions affiliated to the National University will remain closed until further notice.

Headline_English: Improving the quality of medical colleges will produce more skilled doctors: Health Minister
Content_Enlish:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr. Samanta Lal Sen said, we need to increase the facilities of our medical colleges. Medical colleges produce our doctors. If the quality of medical colleges increases and if they provide advanced and up-to-date education, we will get more skilled doctors. 
The Health Minister said this as the chief guest at a view-sharing meeting with teachers and students at M Abdur Rahim Medical College in Dinajpur on Sunday (July 14) morning. 

The Health Minister also said that the draft of the Health Protection Act is in the final stage to protect medical professionals and patients. We have already held many meetings in the ministry on this. 
In his speech as a special guest, Secretary of the Health Services Division Md. Jahangir Alam highlighted the importance of doctors completing post-graduate degrees in all existing subjects and talked about the initiative to create super-numerary posts for doctors if necessary. 

M Abdur Rahim Medical College Principal Professor Dr. A. F. M. The meeting, chaired by Nuruullah, was attended by the Whip of the National Parliament, Iqbalur Rahim, Secretary of the Health Services Division of the Ministry of National Health and Family Welfare, Md. Jahangir Alam, Director General of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, Professor Dr. Abul Basar Mohammad Khurshid Alam, and officials of the Health Department and local administration.

Headline_English: Quota movement: Stars for and against
Content_Enlish:
The entire country is in turmoil with the movement of ordinary students under the banner of the 'Anti-Discrimination Student Movement' demanding quota reform in government jobs. Although showbiz stars were initially silent on the issue, many have spoken out after the attack on students on Monday (July 15). 

Several stars from the showbiz arena have posted on social media condemning the attack on students and expressing their stance in favor of quota reform. Some have also posted against the quota reform movement. 

Actress Parimoni shared a bloodied picture of a female student on her verified Facebook page and wrote, 'If you keep your mouth shut about violence against women, you are a hypocrite.' 

Actress Shabnam Bubli wrote in her post, 'Why will students bleed?' 

Actress Runa Khan shared a bloodied picture of a female student on social media. She did not write anything in the post, but she expressed her pain over the attack on students by putting a 'heartbroken' emoji on the picture. 
Actress Sadia Ayman wrote on Facebook, ‘How much more blood will our beloved Bangladesh become independent?’ 

In another post, actor Niloy Alamgir requested the Prime Minister, ‘Honorable Prime Minister, today’s students are the future of tomorrow. They will one day take over the country. So many students cannot make wrong demands. I am also saying as the son of a freedom fighter, please reform the quota. We are grateful to you for the respect and love you have always shown to the freedom fighters of Bangladesh and their families. But the freedom fighters and their families are now a laughing stock to the common people of the country. Even if you want to keep the place of honor of the freedom fighters, accept the quota reform. This plight of the protesting students is unbearable. The entire nation is waiting for your decision.’ 

Content creator Salman Muktadir has promised to stand by the students. Salman Muktadir wrote, ‘Is there any student who has been attacked or is unable to enter the hall? I will take care of you.… If anyone needs a place to stay or needs medical care, I am here.… I am truly devastated, embarrassed.’ 

Former Dhaka University student filmmaker Siam Ahmed has sought a response to the attack on students on the university campus. Posting the blood-stained logo of Dhaka University on his verified Facebook account, he wrote, ‘Why is my campus bloody? Why will the blood of students be shed?’ 

benodon-aditto-3 

Supporting the students’ movement, producer Suman Anwar wrote, ‘Great Dhaka, excited country. Bangladesh will turn around.’ 

Producer Badrul Anam Saud wrote in a Facebook post, ‘One mistake after another. Mistakes on all sides. Logic, thinking, statics – everyone is sitting there forgetting everything. Excitement and power are fighting. Dialogue is sitting there helplessly.’ 

Producer Khizir Hayat Khan wrote, ‘Our future is on the streets across the country today. There are many questions about their slogans, but there is no talk about why this slogan is so. The movement for fair rights does not make anyone a Razakar, rather, freedom comes from their hands. I stood by them.’ 

Producer Rezwan Shahriar Sumit wrote, ‘No matter how much they shout ‘Joy Bangla’ with their chests full of joy, I do not think that today’s Chhatra League of 2024 has any connection with the great liberation war of 1971. Today, they are nothing but unconscious, misguided, money-grubbing locusts. I do not know what ideological politics this locust army has spread without discussing with the protesting students. However, I can say for sure that it has no resemblance to Bangabandhu’s politics or philosophy. When will the entire nation become senseless, misguided, and greedy for money as these locusts multiply? 

benodon-aditto-1 

Chirkut band leader Sharmin Sultana Sumi wrote, “Our university, our generation, future generations; We humbly request you to ensure the safety and prosperity of all with good conscience.” A post has also been posted from Chirkut’s verified Facebook page in support of the students. 

In a Facebook post, producer Ashfaq Nipun called on students to stand by him in this movement for quota reform. Calling Begum Rokeya University student Abu Sayeed, who was shot dead by the police, a martyr, he wrote under his slogan ‘Live with your spine as long as you are alive’, ‘Live with your spine as long as you are alive.’ 

In addition to protesting the attack on students, producer Mishuk Moni questioned the silence of showbiz people on this matter on Facebook. 

Many showbiz stars have once again taken a stand against the quota reform movement. They have condemned the chanting of 'Rajakar' slogans in the procession. 

Writer and director Masum Reza wrote on Facebook, 'You are introducing yourselves as those who were defeated in 1971! How talented you are! What ghost is supplying you with so much talent!’ 

Actor Marjuk Russell posted a picture of the clash and wrote, ‘Both sides are students but education is different.’ 

Actress Shamima Tushti wrote, ‘Those who do not hesitate to call themselves Razakars, and they are the ones who want quotas for government jobs, I wonder what will happen if the country goes to them.’ 

Rawnak Hasan, general secretary of the Actors’ Association, wrote, ‘Quota reform may happen...but looking at the direction in which this movement of thousands of ordinary students has been skillfully channeled, it is clear who the masterminds are.’ 

On the other hand, the Actors’ Association has issued a statement claiming that freedom fighters are being disrespected in the name of the quota reform movement.

Headline_English: Bangladesh lags behind in artificial intelligence readiness
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh ranks 113th out of 174 countries in the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) AI Readiness Index. The index has been created on four pillars - digital infrastructure, human capital and labor market policies, innovation and economic integration, and regulation and policy. India, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Vietnam, and Indonesia are ahead of Bangladesh in this index. And African countries like Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana, and Senegal are also ahead of Bangladesh in this index. Singapore is at the top of the AI ​​readiness index. 

Regarding this index, Professor Dr. B. M. Mainul Hossain, Director of the Institute of Information Technology, University of Dhaka, said, "This is not actually the status of AI use, but an indicator of readiness. This has been done so that countries can decide on their policies and readiness. Here, they have taken into consideration infrastructure, skilled human resources, labor laws. It is clear that we are not very proactive in the direction of the human resources needed for AI." 

The IMF says AI can increase productivity, economic growth and income. It can create employment for many people. However, it can also increase inequality and make many people lose their jobs. 

According to IMF research, AI can put 33 percent of jobs in advanced economies, 24 percent in emerging economies and 18 percent in low-income countries at risk. On the other hand, AI is bringing great potential in increasing the productivity of existing jobs. 

Dr. B. M. Mainul Hossain said that just as there is a risk of job loss, there will also be new employment opportunities. And that will require high skills. 

'More than five hundred organizations are working on AI' 

The use of AI is increasing in various sectors in Bangladesh. Especially the telecommunications sector, mobile banking, marketing. Parag Obaid, CEO of Tech Garlic, an organization working on AI, said that its use has also started in the agricultural sector. He said that there are now more than five hundred organizations in Bangladesh that work on AI and machine learning. However, the number of such people working individually outside the organization is at least 1 million. He said that institutional work on AI has started in Bangladesh since 2008-9. 

Parag Obaid said, "Many corporate houses, including mobile phone companies and mobile banking, are now taking advantage of AI technology. Its use has also started in the agricultural sector of Bangladesh." His organization is providing assistance in the agricultural sector with AI technology for irrigation. 

According to him, AI has potential in all sectors of Bangladesh. Obaid believes that the use of AI can save a lot of damage, especially in the case of natural disasters. 

He said, those who work here are mastering this technology on their own initiative. It changes every day. That is, it is a continuous learning process. It is not possible without skills and great interest. Moreover, bank loans are not available to invest in this sector. 

‘Government sponsorship is needed’ 

Shahrukh Islam, co-founder of Bondstein Technologies, said that now domestic and multinational companies are using AI in marketing. Bangladeshi companies are getting work. However, our mindset has not changed much yet. Earlier, when the use of computers started, many people used to discourage the use of computers for fear of losing their jobs. We still see that Biman Bangladesh has turned off its computers after its website was hacked. In fact, new technology should be welcomed. 

According to him, for this, government sponsorship is needed. The Indian government ordered 100,000 graphic processing units (GPUs) from the world’s largest AI company last April. GPUs are the raw material for AI. And we bring them from the USA or Singapore on our own initiative. It costs us a lot of dollars. If the government sets up an AI center and brings GPUs and rents them to us, then we entrepreneurs will benefit. 

Shahrukh Islam of Bondstein Technologies said, "AI is not a tangible product or object. The banking sector in Bangladesh does not provide loans for the production of this product. They provide loans for hardware. As a result, we do not get loans. We have to raise money in various ways. The government needs to see this." 

Still, he said, seven to eight companies in Bangladesh are now providing AI solutions outside the country. 

How ready is Bangladesh? 

Dr. Senjuti Rahman, Chairman of the Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering Department of Dhaka University, said, "We are actually not ready for AI technology yet. We are still going through Digital Bangladesh. If we are to move into the third era of technology, we will need skilled and trained youth. We do not have that system here, we do not have the institutions. Again, we are not able to retain those who are being created, they are leaving the country. Just as we need to make arrangements to retain them, AI needs to be incorporated into our education at various levels." 

According to him, the government is supporting many startup companies with AI in various ways in our neighboring countries. But we are not doing it here. Funds should be given to young researchers. 

Professor Dr. B. M. Mainul Hossain said, it should be remembered that the skill of creating website designs and the skill of AI are not the same. For Digital Bangladesh, some training should have been given in the short term. But that is not possible here. We have to create technology. That skill will be needed. 

According to him, the risk of artificial intelligence is that it will analyze the information it is prepared with in the same way. Its thinking is not like that of humans. As a result, it is possible to spread rumors or conduct one-sided analysis with it. 

Dr. Senjuti Rahman said, Amazon gave AI the responsibility of selecting CVs for a technical recruitment instead of humans. Then it was found that AI excluded all women's CVs in the beginning. In fact, it gives results the way it is trained. So there are various risks of using AI. Of course, that depends on humans. How we want to use it. It can also be used for harmful purposes. 

Initiatives to create a law 

The Bangladesh government has already taken the initiative to make a law on AI. The draft law is now in the Law Ministry. 

Analysts believe that the law is definitely needed to prevent its misuse. At the same time, infrastructure, skilled human resources, and technical support are much needed for AI. 

State Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Zunaid Ahmed Palak recently inaugurated the government's artificial intelligence-based GPT platform G-Brain at the Bangladesh Computer Council Auditorium in Agargaon. The government's artificial intelligence-based GPT platform was inaugurated with three features: Startup GPT, Constitution GPT, and Budget GPT. He said there that the draft of the Artificial Intelligence Law is coming by September this year.

Headline_English: Gold price hits highest in country's history, increases by 1190 taka per ounce
Content_Enlish:
The price of gold has been increased in the country's market. The price of a bhori (11.664 grams) of the best quality or 22-carat gold has been increased by 1,190 taka to 1,20,081 taka. Which is the highest in the country's history. 
The Bangladesh Jewelers' Association (BAJUS) announced this information in a press release on Sunday (July 14). 

The release said that according to the new price, the price of 22-carat gold per bhori (11.664 grams) will be 1,20,081 taka. In addition, the price of 21-carat bhori has been fixed at 1,14,622 taka, 18-carat bhori at 98,246 taka and traditional gold per bhori at 81,229 taka. The new price will be effective from Monday (July 15). 
Earlier, BAJUS last adjusted the price of gold in the country's market on July 7. At that time, the organization had increased the price of a 22-carat gold bhori by 1,609 taka, setting the price at 1,18,891 taka.

Headline_English: What is happening in the name of the spirit of the Liberation War cannot be accepted: ZI Khan Panna
Content_Enlish:
Senior Supreme Court lawyer and human rights activist ZI Khan Panna said that the activities being carried out in the name of the spirit of the liberation war cannot be accepted. If any freedom fighter touches his chest. At that time, the High Court said that the Appellate Division has settled this matter. 

ZI Khan said, if I had seen that students could move around safely, could go to schools and colleges, then I would not have had any objection. The objection is when block raids are conducted in each area at night, as happened in 1971. 

He said these things today, Monday, during the hearing of the writ petition seeking the immediate release of 6 coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement and instructions not to open fire on the protesters. 

On Monday (July 29), a bench of Justice Mustafa Zaman Islam and Justice SM Masud Hossain Dolan held a hearing on the writ petition. 

ZI Khan Panna said, in 1971, I saw that the Pakistani invaders conducted block raids at night to search for the presence of the Mukti Bahini. Today in 2024, we saw them knocking on doors and searching to see if there were students. If there were students, they would check their mobile phones. Is there any law for this? They are crossing the line. 

Additional Attorney General SM Munir said that he made this statement at Paltan Maidan. In response, ZI Khan Panna said, I came to give a statement at Paltan Maidan. I did not commit Razakargiri. At that time, he addressed the court and said, this is the government's situation. What will happen outside? This is the government's situation inside the court. I don't want to say what they are doing outside. Is what they are doing at night with block raids legal? Not at all. 

Additional Attorney General Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury for the state said, can they confirm that there will be no more attacks on BTV-Metrorail? The accused were freed by attacking Narsingdi prison. What will the law enforcement agencies do then? At that time, the court said, regarding the matter of Narsingdi, a boy died during a procession there. 

Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury said, whatever illegal action they took will be brought under the law. All will be investigated, it is happening. 

Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury also said, we saw on TV these six people sitting in the DB and eating with a spoon. At that time, the lawyers present got excited and kept saying various things. The court said, who told you to do this? Why did you do this? You don't make fun of the nation. Whoever you catch, sit at a dining table. Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury said, none of the relatives of the six people came to the court. A rule cannot be issued on this application. 

Additional Attorney General Sheikh Mohammad Morshed said, we want time, let the Attorney General come. The court said, it will be tomorrow. Then Barristers Anik and Haque asked for a verbal order. 

At that time, Sheikh Mohammad Morshed said, we have to see whether there is any obstruction in the exercise of the legal jurisdiction of the law enforcement agencies. Both sides are being injured. Who said that the other 6 people (coordinators) were detained, where did they say that? The court said, if they were not detained, how could they be kept day after day? 

Sheikh Mohammad Morshed said, did anyone on behalf of the family say that they were detained? If they were arrested, they would have been taken to court within 24 hours. 

Later, the next hearing and order on this matter was fixed for tomorrow, Tuesday. Earlier, Supreme Court lawyers Manzoor-al-Matin and Ainunnahar Siddique filed the writ.

Headline_English: Decision to ban Jamaat-Shibir at 14-party meeting
Content_Enlish:
Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader said that a decision has been taken to ban Jamaat-e-Islami at a 14-party meeting at Ganabhaban. He made this statement after a meeting with top leaders of the 14 parties on Monday (July 29) night. 

Obaidul Quader said that BNP-Jamaat are involved in a conspiracy to make the country ineffective through anarchy. In order to eliminate the evil forces against the country in the national interest, a unanimous decision has been taken at the 14-party meeting to ban Jamaat-e-Islami politics. 

Obaidul Quader also said that the Prime Minister has instructed the Home and Law Ministries to implement the decision. 

In the last meeting of the 14 parties with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on the night of July 19, it was decided to impose curfew in the country and deploy the army in the situation created by the quota reform movement. After 10 days, an emergency meeting of the alliance was called again today. There, it was decided to ban Jamaat-e-Islami. However, the Election Commission had already cancelled Jamaat-e-Islami's registration in view of the war crimes tribunal verdict. 

Multiple sources present at the meeting at Ganabhaban said that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said at the beginning of the meeting that Jamaat-Shibir is behind the recent incidents of sabotage, arson and attacks on police in different districts of the country. She has an intelligence report on this matter. For a month, trained people of Jamaat-Shibir were gathered in Dhaka from different districts of the country. They are the ones who committed these misdeeds. If the spirit of the liberation war is to be upheld, a decision will have to be taken about them. 

The leaders of the partner parties then gave speeches one by one in the meeting. First, Workers' Party President Rashed Khan Menon said that an analysis of the current political situation is needed. The issue of banning Jamaat-Shibir came up during the trial of war criminals. It was not done then. It can be taken into consideration now. 

Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD) President Hasanul Haque Inu directly proposed banning Jamaat-Shibir. He said that now is the time to ban Jamaat-Shibir. He also proposed to ban them and hold processions and rallies on the streets to shape public opinion on the issue. 

Samyabadi Dal General Secretary Dilip Barua said that in addition to banning Jamaat-Shibir, efforts should also be made to promote alternative political forces. 

Jatiya Party (JP) Secretary General Sheikh Shahidul Islam also supported banning Jamaat-Shibir. He also emphasized on directing students towards educational institutions. For this, he said that secondary schools should be opened gradually and examinations should be started. 

Tariqat Federation Chairman Syed Najibul Bashar Maizbhandari mentioned that he had filed a case to cancel Jamaat's registration. He strongly demanded that Jamaat-Shibir be banned. 

Towards the end, Sheikh Hasina asked 14-party coordinator Amir Hossain Amu to conclude the meeting. But he said that the issue was important and that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina should do it.

Headline_English: Six men in plain clothes took away three coordinators: Nahid's sister
Content_Enlish:
Nahid's elder sister, Fatema Tasnim, has alleged that six men in plain clothes took away three coordinators of the quota reform movement, Nahid Islam, Asif Mahmud and Abu Bakar Majumdar. She told the French news agency AFP. 
In a post on the social handle X, AFP reported the three coordinators being taken away from the hospital. The three coordinators were undergoing treatment at the capital's Gonoshasthaya Nagar Hospital. Several hospital officials and employees told AFP that the intelligence police took them away from there in the afternoon. 

Anwara Begum Lucky, a supervisor at Gonoshasthaya Nagar Hospital, said that the hospital authorities did not want to give the three students a discharge certificate. But the police took them away under some kind of pressure. 

Nahid's elder sister, Fatema Tasnim, told AFP that six men from the intelligence agency wearing plain clothes took away the three of them. 

According to hospital sources, Nahid, Asif and Abu Bakar had been undergoing treatment at Gonoshasthaya Nagar Hospital for the past few days. 

The AFP report also said that the three people undergoing treatment were under the surveillance of law enforcement agencies. No one was allowed to meet them since Thursday evening. Nahid Islam and Asif Mahmud had previously alleged that they were taken away and tortured. 

However, none of the senior officials of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police have commented on this. AFP also says that no one has acknowledged that they were taken away on Friday. 

Earlier, Nahid Islam and Asif Mahmud, coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement who were undergoing treatment at the hospital, were kept under strict surveillance. They have also been accused of blocking them in their cabins and cutting off the hospital's Wi-Fi and telephone connections. This was reported in a report by the country's national daily The Daily Star. 

The coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, a platform for students in the quota reform movement, said that they were supposed to announce their new program on Thursday after the end of the four-day ultimatum. Since one of the coordinators, Nahid Islam and Asif Mahmud, is admitted to the hospital, they said that they would announce the program from there. But when they went to the hospital at night, they saw two members of the law enforcement agencies guarding the rooms of Nahid and Asif. 

The coordinators alleged that members of the law enforcement agencies went to the hospital on Thursday and locked Nahid and Asif in their cabins. They also disconnected the hospital's Wi-Fi and telephone connections. Due to this, they could not communicate with each other on time. 

However, that afternoon, Asif told Mahmud's media that they would meet with the coordinators and announce a new program. Later, at around 7:15 pm, Asif called and said that he and Nahid were locked in the hospital and that the law enforcement agencies had cut the hospital's Wi-Fi and telephone lines. Due to this, they could not communicate with the other coordinators. He also said that a press briefing would be held at the hospital between 8 and 9 pm. However, no preparations for the press briefing were seen at the hospital around 8 pm that day. 

The Daily Star report says that that night, three law enforcement officers in plain clothes were seen in front of Nahid's cabin on the seventh floor of the hospital and four in front of Asif's cabin on the third floor. They did not allow the reporter to enter the cabin, introducing themselves as members of the intelligence agency. They also said that there were strict instructions from higher authorities in this regard. 

Later, Abdul Hannan Masud, another coordinator of the student movement against discrimination, told the media, "We went to the hospital for a news briefing. But the law enforcement officers in plain clothes did not allow us to meet Nahid and Asif. We left the hospital later." 

And Nahid Islam said, "Many law enforcement officers are stationed outside the hospital. They are not allowing anyone to enter or exit. I have not been able to get internet connection since afternoon. 

Earlier, on Saturday morning, there were allegations that Nahid Islam was taken away from a house in Sabujbagh in the capital under the guise of law enforcement officers. He was found the next day, Sunday. At that time, he had severe pain and deep wounds on his left thigh and shoulder. On the other hand, Asif Mahmud was allegedly kidnapped on Friday. He was found five days later.

Headline_English: What is happening in Bangladesh is the internal matter of that country: Indian External Affairs Ministry
Content_Enlish:
India has commented that the recent developments in Bangladesh are the internal affairs of that country (Bangladesh). The country hopes that peace will return to Bangladesh very soon. The situation will be normal. 
Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said these things at the weekly briefing of the Indian Ministry of External Affairs on Thursday. 

In last week's briefing, several questions were asked about the quota movement in Bangladesh. It was also said that what is happening in Bangladesh is the internal affair of that country. 

Today, Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked many questions about the student movement in Bangladesh. More than two hundred people have died in the violence surrounding the movement. 

In the briefing, it was asked whether the Indian Prime Minister, Foreign Minister or anyone else spoke to the leaders of Bangladesh during this time. Or whether India has any reports of outside involvement in that movement. It was asked whether anti-India slogans were heard from the mouths of the protesters and whether India is concerned about the opposition of a section of the people of that country. 

Randhir Jaiswal has deliberately avoided answering these questions. He did not comment on the movement or the nature of the movement. He repeatedly said that what is happening in Bangladesh is the internal matter of that country. India's relations with Bangladesh are very strong, warm and friendly. 

Referring to the immense help and cooperation of the Bangladesh government in bringing back Indian students and others living in that country safely during the movement, the spokesperson said that so far more than 6,700 Indians have returned home safely. He said that the Indian High Commission and Assistant High Commission have kept a 24-hour helpline open for their safe return. He said that India is keeping a close eye on the developments in that country. However, what is happening there is entirely their internal matter. India hopes that the situation in Bangladesh will return to normal very soon. 

The spokesperson, however, admitted that the Bangladesh government has protested a recent comment by West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. The protest letter has reached India at the diplomatic level. He commented that the reports in the media regarding this are also correct. 

Randhir Jaiswal said in this regard, in the first list of the seventh schedule of the Indian Constitution, it is said that everything related to foreign affairs is under the control of the central government. Central list. This field is not in the state list or the concurrent list. It is in the central list. Therefore, no state government has any jurisdiction over any matter related to foreign affairs. He said, the state government has nothing to worry about which is not a state matter.

Headline_English: Life with social sites vs. these days without the internet
Content_Enlish:
After the 1980s, and between the 1990s and the first half of the 2000s, the children born between these one and a half decades have less contrast in their upbringing. But as time has progressed, the mindset of the generation has changed very rapidly. Their daily lives, entertainment styles, study patterns, communication with others—everything is changing in the blink of an eye. However, the generation born sometime after the 1990s and sometime before the 2000s has probably witnessed several variations at the same time. Although their childhood was very simple. 

The routine was such that at seven in the morning, everyone would go to school in groups. In the afternoon, after class, the boys would come home and eat a couple of snacks, and go out with tape, tennis balls, and cricket bats. If these were not available, there was football. On the other hand, girls would also play outside, playing Ekkadokka, Kanamachi; Some will fly kites on the roof, or jump into the pond — where a quick swimming competition will be held between two or four people. Then, in the evening, there is a strict rule to return home and sit down to study as usual, otherwise, you may get a couple of blows from your father or mother's cane on your back! Then, after studying, you will get the opportunity to watch TV for a while at night. Sometimes, you have to sit like a crow in a shrine waiting for your favorite program. Popular drama series, movies-serials, shadow plays; Alif-Laila, MacGyver, or Meena cartoons are at the top of the list. If there is no electricity, or if the television antenna is not working, you can just sit and enjoy the story, what's the problem with all the siblings playing Ludo together and making a fuss! 

On the other hand, in the break from school tiffin, go to the library and quickly buy three detective or mystery magazines from Seva Prokashani, and dive into the sports pages when the newspaper comes home; The moments of waiting for the pages of the newspaper or other colorful stories on a weekend were also very joyful. Chacha Chowdhury, Billu-Pinky, Nonte-Fonte, Hada-Bhonda, Batul the Great and even Phantom were my companions! 

This simple and joyful feeling has now changed. Computers, smart devices and the Internet have taken over all the places of many entertainment media. More broadly, Facebook and other social media. It may seem to the naked eye that many daily tasks in life have become much easier, communication has increased; but in reality, the lives of many people are stuck in some kind of complex-compound number. What that number is, I will come to that later. But before that, let me say that the nostalgia that has been talked about so far — that time has come back to many people's lives in a time machine in these few days without the Internet. Think about it, do you see the similarities? 

Let's go back a little. It is not that the Internet has suddenly changed all habits. This change has happened gradually, especially in the last 15 years. For example, in 2008, 2009 or 2010, the internet was new to everyone in the country. The speed was also very slow. Mobile phones were not yet 'smartphones'. Some phones could use Opera Mini, eBody or Nimbaz Messenger on Java-supported operating systems. Skype and Yahoo Messenger were used on computers. Interest in Facebook was also growing at that time, many people used it to communicate with acquaintances and find lost childhood friends. Some used all sorts of strange names - blue sky, white butterfly, red fairy, yellow bird, etc.! In these accounts, even strangers were 'friends'. Buying a 20 megabyte package on the phone for 20 taka would last for several days. A 1 gigabyte package was used on the modem for 300 taka. That too lasted for about a month. There was no artificial intelligence or heavy graphics used in simple apps and websites. YouTube, Twitter, Instagram, TikTok were still very far away! Even unlimited broadband internet connections were not on anyone's mind at that time. 

After that, technology improved quite rapidly. Computer configurations increased, unlimited internet became easily available; 3G, 4G and 5G came. Various applications and websites developed rapidly, testifying to the diverse experiences. In the beginning, only statuses were written on simple Facebook, mostly some pictures of happy moments could be shared with family and friends. Then videos were added. In the next step, some games were played in groups through Messenger. The simple Facebook of that time is now filled with conflict news videos, live advertising of clothing and cosmetics stores, various reels, marketplace ads, other promotional content, links to colorful headlines of digital news from newspapers and magazines, and many true and false games. Everyone has seen this ‘rapid transition’, so there is no need to tell the story of how the digital world became like this. 

However, even though the use of the internet became affordable in a short time, we got involved in that world without much preparation or sufficient awareness. Instead of keeping any discipline there, we did too much. As a result, how do we spend our time now? The morning starts on social media. To be more precise, on Facebook. I see who shared what. As soon as I scroll through the feed, various videos come up. Time passes by watching them. Then I rush to the office, and there too, Facebook, Instagram or TikTok accompany me on the journey. Even during office breaks, my eyes are on the smartphone screen. I return home, and there too, the eyes of two people in the same room are on both sides! Thanks to the internet, so much ‘information’ and ‘content’ are constantly coming to people, which is keeping everyone busy. 

Those who are studying in school and college are now completely device-centric in their entertainment. They spend their time depending on social sites, YouTube content, and various games. The little ones don't want to eat without watching videos on their phones, and the older ones are busy trying to figure out which pictures will get more likes, which videos will go viral, and which topics will increase their 'reach' - to match those numbers! Now, as much as we consume various trending content on Facebook or other sites every day, we are becoming consumed by the complex calculations of the like-share-comment algorithm. If the type of content does not match the demand of artificial intelligence, our numbers also do not match. Due to this, we are suffering from a kind of restlessness, thinking of ourselves as competitors in some invisible race. 

However, the time when the internet was shut down due to the turbulent situation of the last few days brought back the nostalgia of the days gone by. It is true that many important things including various emergency services, online banking, and freelancing were shut down; It is true that we cannot live without the internet anymore. However, as the saying goes, ‘Every cloud has a silver lining’. These days, children have been hanging out together on the rooftops of city houses, playing cricket in parking lots or in the streets; the child who never wants to leave the online game is also forced to open the Sapludu board and sit down. Many people have chosen story books, old comics stored at home, or canvases for drawing as an alternative to digital content to pass the time. Many have also been able to complete the work that has been left behind for a long time due to ‘lack of time’. The whole family watched ‘Zee Cinema’ or Bengali dramas on television together, which is no longer possible with YouTube. Those who had lost the habit of watching TV news have also relied on the scrolls and bulletins of various channels these days. 

In fact, we have changed while changing our lives through the benefits of technology. In this, it has become clear that the internet was absorbing our ‘brains’. It's also a chance to take a break and look back a bit. From now on, it might not be a bad idea to occasionally observe a 'No Internet Day' or 'No Facebook Day'. What do you think?

Headline_English: Messi's message to everyone wishing them a happy New Year
Content_Enlish: The year 2022 is different for Lionel Messi. He has won everything in previous years, except the World Cup. The adorable title was achieved in December last year. 36 years of regret have passed. Messi has not yet returned to the field after winning the World Cup. He is spending time with family and friends in Rosario. From there, the Argentine captain sent a message of love to his fans and family on the last day of the year. In the message given on social media, Messi spoke about his family, friends, and supporters all over the world. Messi began his writing like this, 'I will never forget the year that is ending. The dream that I have always had, that dream has come true this year. This joy would not have been complete if I had not been able to share the joy with such a wonderful family. If I had not been able to share the joy with those friends who have always supported me, who have been by my side whenever I have stumbled.'

Headline_English: Bees can detect cancer germs by smelling them
Content_Enlish:
‘Bees, bees, where are you going, dance, dance, don’t stand still, brother.’ If it is said that bees can detect cancer germs by standing still for a moment, would it be credible? But that is what new research says. Bees have a strong sense of smell. A new study has shown that bees can detect lung cancer germs by sniffing human breath. Some scientists from Michigan State University in the United States have said that bees have been able to detect even the faintest odors on the breath of people with lung cancer in the laboratory. They have also recently published a research paper on the sense of smell of bees in the Journal of Biosensors and Bioelectronics. 

During the research, electrodes were attached to the brains of living bees and observed. Then, the brain signals were recorded by exposing the bees to the scents of various objects around them. In this regard, Debjit Saha, a neuroengineer at Michigan State University, said that different odors stimulate the bee's brain. Bees use a different technique in their neurons to detect odors. As a result, bees can be used as living sensors to initially detect cancer in the future. Currently, various types of odor-sensitive devices, including electronic noses or e-noses, are being developed. Bees' sense of smell is stronger than these devices. No other device can do what bees can do. 

Flora Gougere, a chemical scientist at France's National Research Institute for Sustainable Development, said that various insects communicate with each other through smell. Smell is their language. Scientists have found that dogs can detect COVID-19 by sniffing the smell of human sweat. Many insects also have the ability to detect diseases through smell. A strategy for detecting cancer can be found by using bees' sense of smell. 

By analyzing the electrical signals in the bee's brain, researchers have found that bees can distinguish between human breath in about 93 percent of cases. As a result, the bee's brain can identify the breath of healthy people and people with cancer separately. Bees can not only detect the smell of cancer, but also the presence of various chemicals in the air. And so, scientists hope that in the future, cancer germs can be easily identified through bees.

Headline_English: 15,203 HSC candidates absent on first day, rain causes problems
Content_Enlish:
HSC and equivalent examinations have started across the country, except for Sylhet division, on Sunday. 15,203 candidates were absent on the first day. Of these, 9,970 candidates were from the eight general education boards and the rest from the madrasa and technical education boards. 

Education Minister Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury presented this information at a press conference organized at the International Mother Language Institute in Segunbagicha in the capital this afternoon. Later, detailed information about the absent candidates was also given in writing by the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee. 

This time, the total number of candidates under the other eight general education boards, excluding the Sylhet board, was 9,33,689. Of these, 9,23,719 participated in the examination. Among the absent candidates, 2,601 were in Dhaka Education Board, 1,508 in Rajshahi, 1,156 in Comilla, 1,328 in Jessore, 975 in Chittagong, 727 in Barisal, 1,131 in Dinajpur and 662 in Mymensingh Education Board. 

In addition, there were 1,88,863 candidates in Madrasa and Technical Education Board. Of them, 1,83,630 took the exam. 2,988 candidates in Madrasa Board and 2,245 candidates in Technical Board were absent. 

49 candidates were expelled today for using unfair means in HSC and equivalent exams. In addition, two inspectors were expelled. 

Due to the flood situation, the HSC and equivalent exams of Sylhet division were postponed until July 8. However, the exams that were scheduled to be held from July 9 will go ahead as usual. The dates of the postponed exams will be announced later. 

The Education Minister mentioned that due to rain and waterlogging, candidates will have difficulty reaching the centers in some places, especially in Dhaka and Chittagong. However, the minister said that the secretaries of the centers have been instructed to adjust the timings of the students who reached the centers a little later. 

Referring to the forecast of the Meteorological Department, the Education Minister said that there is a possibility of rain tomorrow, Monday as well. However, there will be no exams tomorrow. The Education Minister said that a decision will be taken regarding the exams tomorrow considering the situation. However, so far, it has been decided to conduct the exams on time. 

The Education Minister said that this exam will be brought forward from next year. He hopes to start this exam in April next year. 

State Minister for Education Shamsun Nahar, Secretary of the Secondary and Higher Education Department Md. Soleman Khan, Director General of the Secondary and Higher Education Department Nehal Ahmed, Chairman of the Dhaka Education Board Tapan Kumar Sarkar were present at the press conference.

Headline_English: Zelensky is making plans to stop the war with Russia
Content_Enlish:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he is developing a ‘coordinated plan’ to end the war with Russia. He made the remarks at a press conference in the capital, Kiev, on Friday. 

Slovenian President Natasa Piers Musar was present at the press conference with Zelensky. At that time, the Ukrainian president said, ‘It is very important for us to put forward a plan to end the war. This plan will have the support of the majority of countries in the world. We are working diplomatically to stop the war.’ 

Despite the talk of stopping the war, there are currently no talks between Ukraine and Russia on this. And recent statements by Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin suggest that the two countries are now the furthest from a possible peace agreement. 

As a condition for a peace agreement, Kiev has repeatedly said that Russia must withdraw its troops from internationally recognized territories of Ukraine. These territories include the Crimean peninsula, which Russia seized in 2014. Only then will Kiev begin peace talks with Moscow. 

Meanwhile, Russian forces have made further progress on the battlefield, President Vladimir Putin has claimed. According to him, Ukrainian troops have left more areas in the east and south of Ukraine in the face of Russia's offensive. Kiev has basically surrendered there. Those areas are currently under the control of Russian forces.
