Headline_English: Winning and losing are part of politics, it's a game of numbers: Modi
Content_Enlish:
Narendra Modi has resigned from the post of Prime Minister of India before taking oath for a third consecutive term. Before resigning, the last meeting of the current cabinet was held at Modi's official residence. In that meeting, Narendra Modi said, winning and losing are part of politics and the game of numbers continues here. We have done very well in the last 10 years and will continue to do so in the future. 
He made these comments after the BJP's worst performance in the last three elections. According to the results of the vote, the BJP-led NDA alliance won 292 seats out of 543 seats, while the BJP alone won 240 seats. 

Addressing the cabinet members, he said, "You, the ruling party, have fulfilled the expectations of the people everywhere and will continue to do so in the future. You all have done a very good job and worked hard." 

After the meeting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi went to the Rashtrapati Bhavan on Wednesday morning and met the Head of State and submitted his and his cabinet members' resignations. President Draupadi accepted his resignation. 

Despite losing the single majority, Narendra Modi is going to become the Prime Minister for the third consecutive time with the victory of the BJP-led NDA alliance. His swearing-in ceremony is likely to take place on Saturday afternoon. 

If Modi takes oath as Prime Minister this time, he will be the third consecutive term Prime Minister of India after Jawaharlal Nehru.

Headline_English: I am proud to join the dream club: Mbappe
Content_Enlish:
Rumors, drama, excitement at every turn! Mbappe's contract with Real was no less thrilling than the action scenes of a thriller movie. It has been going on for the past few years. Finally, the drama of this team has come to an end. The fans left the half alive. Because the French star has been brought into their camp by the Spanish giant Real Madrid. At the same time, this World Cup-winning star feels proud to be part of his dream club. 

The day before yesterday, at 11 pm Bangladesh time, the team Real Madrid, which has won the Champions League for the most times, released a statement on its official website and social media. The moment this statement was published, it went 'viral'. Because with this statement, the long wait of Real fans has ended. Los Blancos' website was about to be closed due to pressure from the fans. That shows how much the fans were waiting for this news. 

The statement released by Real said, 'Real Madrid FC and Kylian Mbappe have reached an agreement. He has completed his contract with Real Madrid for the next five seasons.' Although the club did not disclose how much money the French star has brought into their camp. However, according to international media reports, Kylian Mbappe completed his contract with Real for 180 million euros. 

Earlier, in 2021, Real Madrid offered Mbappe 180 million euros. However, since the star was under contract with PSG at that time, the French club rejected Real's offer. That season, the Spanish giants were willing to spend a total of up to 200 million euros to bring this star to the team. Although that was not possible at that time. However, the French star was always in the eye of Real Madrid President Florentino Perez, known as 'Papa Perez'. After Real Madrid made an official statement, Mbappe shared a post on his social media. 

In that post, he said about his dream club, 'A dream has come true. I am very happy and proud to be part of my dream club. How happy and excited I feel at this moment. It is impossible to explain.' Along with that, the French star said about his dream club and the club's fans, 'I can't wait to see you. Madridistas, thank you for your incredible support. I can't explain to anyone how excited I am at this moment. Hala Madrid.' 



Earlier in 2013, Kylian Mbappe became an ordinary spectator at the Santiago Bernabeu. At that time, this World Cup-winning star was only 13 years old. At that time, Mbappe met his favorite player, former Real Madrid star Cristiano Ronaldo. The French star's favorite player Ronaldo commented on the post in which he expressed his feelings about his favorite club. This is something bigger than a dream. Ronaldo wrote in Mbappe's post, 'It's my turn. I'm looking forward to seeing you play at the Bernabeu.' 

The fans had questions even before this French star signed for Real Madrid. What number jersey will he wear when he arrives at Real Madrid? Because he used to wear the number 7 jersey at PSG and wore the number 10 jersey for the national team. However, Vinicius Junior is wearing the number 7 jersey at Real Madrid and Luka Modric is wearing the number 10 jersey. Since this Croatian star has another season's contract with Real, that's why this French star is not getting the number 10 jersey.

Headline_English: Walk for 15 minutes every day.
Content_Enlish:
Nowadays, in a busy life, it is not possible to give yourself much time. But to stay healthy, it is very important to give yourself some time along with good food and good clothes. Take out at least 15 minutes a day to walk to stay healthy. Do you know how much you will benefit from it? Let's find out: 
Walking is a simple exercise. It improves blood circulation in the body. Walking for 15 minutes a day can reduce the risk of heart disease, even a little. Therefore, there is no alternative to walking regularly to control blood pressure and keep the body active. 
Takes care of the mind 
Walk on a very sad day. You will feel good. Because, walking releases hormones like endorphins, which keep the mind happy. According to the American Psychological Association, regular walking keeps mental problems like depression and anxiety away. 

Keeps the brain active 
Walking regularly also increases brain function. Walking for just 15 minutes can increase memory. It helps reduce the risk of diseases like Alzheimer's. 

Keeps weight under control 
Many people give importance to walking for weight loss. Regular walking is good for health. It also helps in burning calories, so it is easy to lose weight. Also, since regular walking exercises everything from muscles to bones, it strengthens bones. 

Sleep well 
Can't sleep at night? Then walk. Even walking for at least 15 minutes a day will reduce energy in the body. As a result, sleep is comfortable.

Headline_English: 31 more deer carcasses found in Sundarbans
Content_Enlish:
Another 31 dead deer have been recovered from various chars in the Sundarbans affected by Cyclone Remal. Forest guards buried the deer recovered till Saturday (June 1) afternoon. 
Earlier, 96 dead deer and 4 dead pigs were recovered from various chars in the forest from the storm till Wednesday. With this, the forest department has recovered 131 dead wild animals, including 127 dead deer, from the Sundarbans after Cyclone Remal. 

In addition, 18 deer and a python, both alive and injured, have been recovered and released into the forest. 

Khulna region's forest conservator Mihir Kumar Dey said that the Sundarbans have suffered a lot of damage due to the onslaught of Cyclone Remal. Most parts of the Sundarbans have been flooded by tidal and tidal water. All the freshwater ponds have been flooded with salt water. After the storm, 127 dead deer were recovered from various areas of the forest, including Katka, Kachikhali, Karamjal, Pakshirchar, Dimerchar, Shelarchar, and Narikelbaria.

Headline_English: Impact of marital conflict on children's mental health
Content_Enlish:
There can be quarrels in married life. However, children can be negatively affected by this quarrel. Children in the house are attentive. So any negative incident leaves a big impression on their minds. At this time, Dr. Helal Uddin Ahmed, Associate Professor of the Department of Child, Adolescent and Family Psychiatry at the National Institute of Mental Health, is analyzing how children are mentally damaged and what parents can do in this case. Let's listen to his suggestions on this matter. 
Risky behavior is revealed in children 
Parents are exemplary for any child. But when he sees his parents quarreling, he suffers from a kind of insecurity. If the parents' quarrel is prolonged, violent, risky or criminal behavior is revealed in many children. If the parents stop talking to each other, then there can be problems in the child's mental, emotional, behavioral and social interaction. Mental strength starts to decrease 
Children can easily perceive the coldness of their parents. Children can understand the conflict between the parents in the family. A child can feel family unrest from the age of six months. Although he cannot express it. If the situation is like this, his mental foundation is not very strong. 

Disturbance in the child's sleep 
Children's sleep can be disturbed due to quarrels between parents. The early development of the child's brain can be affected in this way. Anxiety and worry can arise. Not only that, there may be problems in his behavior at school. The child may suffer from depression and inattention in studies may be seen. Sometimes, if the child grows up a little, they tend to harm themselves. 

If you are new to marketing If you are new to marketing 
From mental depression to criminal tendency 
A boy who grows up through family strife, after growing up, his tendency to drug addiction, disobedience, and fighting can be more likely. On the other hand, since girls are of a suppressed nature, they feel pressure inside and are restless. Later, they develop various types of mental problems, including fear of the world and depression. 

Teenagers are at higher risk 
The negative impact of family marital strife is greater on teenagers than on children. At this age, the sense of right and wrong is already born. As a result, they often take the initiative to stop their parents' quarrels out of fear. Children who grow up a little want to harm themselves, many become suicidal. They may become disobedient to their parents, giving more priority to their own wishes. But all parents are aware of the impact that family strife has on their children. After a minor quarrel, the parents' agreement gives peace to the child. Children can also learn a good lesson from the fact that parents argue about an issue and resolve it. They can use this lesson in their own lives. 

Children are victims of trauma 
If the problems of marital strife cannot be overcome, the child will continue to be a victim of trauma. In a fight, one of the two people wants to dominate. Sometimes there is a tendency to play the victim role. Meanwhile, the child is afraid and feels helpless. Therefore, before the fight, ask yourself how much you actually gain by winning this fight? Never force the child to take sides in a family dispute. Try to speak patiently instead of going to the path of conflict. You should never get involved in arguments in front of your children. If the situation goes to an extreme level, try to remove the children from there. Before the fight, think about what kind of adverse impact it may have on the people around you. Don't let your child's beautiful childhood become a trauma because of some of your own mistakes.

Headline_English: Awami League's 10-point program to mark its 'Platinum Jubilee'

The path of the Awami League for the past seven and a half decades has been glorious. 

He said that the independent Bangladesh state was established through the great Liberation War under the undisputed leadership of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman along the path of the independence struggle. All the great achievements of the people of this country have been achieved under the leadership of the Awami League. In keeping with the evolution of time, today, the Bangladesh Awami League is the dreamy adventurer of smart Bangladesh, crossing the path of digital Bangladesh. Bangladesh has transformed from a least developed country to a developing country under the able leadership of Sheikh Hasina, the daughter of the successful statesman Bangabandhu, after a long path of success and struggle. 

10-point program on the occasion of Platinum Jubilee

Headline_English: Make concerted efforts to resolve Rohingya crisis: Foreign Minister at UN
Content_Enlish:
Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud has urged the UN agencies and other partners to take coordinated steps for the repatriation of about 1.3 million Rohingyas sheltering in the country to their home country of Myanmar, to resolve the ongoing conflict in the country's Rakhine State, and to develop the Rohingya population. 
The Foreign Minister made this call in four separate meetings with the President of the General Assembly, the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for Myanmar, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, and the heads of six UN development agencies at the UN Headquarters in New York on Friday. 

The matter was informed in a statement by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. 

It was further informed that Dr. Hasan Mahmud told the President of the UN General Assembly, Denis Francis, that when about 1 million fled to Bangladesh in 2017 to escape violence in Myanmar, the people of Cox's Bazar and Chittagong welcomed them with compassion. But gradually the Rohingyas are leaving the camps and are finding employment in different places, and the camps have become a haven for various crimes including human trafficking, drug smuggling, and militancy. As a result, the lives of the locals are miserable. 

In a meeting with UN High Commissioner for Refugees Filippo Grandi, the Foreign Minister said that along with the Rohingya refugees, about 750 members of the Myanmar Border Guard Police and Army have fled to Bangladesh at various times since last February. Most of them have been sent back, while the rest are in the process of being returned. Not only that, there have been casualties due to shelling by conflicting groups in Myanmar on the Bangladesh side. It is imperative to prevent a recurrence of these incidents. 

In a meeting with the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy on Myanmar, former Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop, he said that the ongoing conflict situation in Myanmar is not a new phenomenon and it is inappropriate to allow it to be used as an excuse against the repatriation of Rohingya. 

Earlier, Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud spoke at an event titled 'Crisis, Conflicts and Inter-Agency Collaboration: Nexus Approach' at the UN Headquarters. The heads of six UN agencies - UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS, UN Women and the deputy heads of UNICEF and WFP - participated in the meeting. 

The Foreign Minister highlighted the benefits of nexus or joint efforts of UN agencies, especially in conflict-affected regions of the world. He mentioned the situation in Rakhine and Cox's Bazar and called on all UN agencies, funds and programmes to work in a coordinated manner to resolve the refugee crisis and improve the situation of the Rohingya population. 

Ambassador Muhammad A Muhith, Permanent Representative of Bangladesh to the UN, and other members of the ministry and mission accompanied the Minister in the meetings.

Headline_English: New Hajj rules come into effect, severe punishment for breaking them
Content_Enlish:
Saudi Arabia has implemented new rules for Hajj. These restrictions will be in place for the next 20 people from Sunday (June 2). Severe punishments have been imposed for violating the rules. 

According to a report by the Khaleej Times, any citizen or foreign tourist who goes to perform Hajj without permission will be fined 10,000 Saudi riyals, which is more than 312,000 taka in Bangladeshi currency. 

In addition, anyone who provides transportation facilities to Hajj pilgrims without permission will be jailed for six months and fined 50,000 Saudi riyals, which is more than 1.5 million taka in Bangladeshi currency. 

Saudi Arabia has announced that this time no one will be allowed to perform Hajj without permission. No one will be able to approach Mecca, the holy site, the Haramain train station, security posts, screening centers and temporary checkpoints without permission. 

If expatriates living in Saudi Arabia go to perform Hajj without permission and are detained, they will be sent back to their own countries and will not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia for a specified period. 

In addition, those who transport pilgrims without permission will first be sent to jail. They will be detained there for six months. After that, they will be sent back to their own countries.

Headline_English: Firefighter dies in devastating floods in Germany
Content_Enlish:
Germany is hit by severe flooding. A firefighter died while trying to rescue people in a rubber dinghy in heavy flooding, Deutsche Welle reported. At least one person is missing in southern Germany. 
The flooding has disrupted rail services in several regions. The country's weather service said more rain is expected in the region. 

The firefighter was trying to reach a collapsed house in the Bavarian town of Pfaffenhofen an der Ilm to rescue residents, the report said. The 42-year-old volunteer died. The man's body was recovered on Sunday morning. Local officials said other rescue workers in the rubber dinghy were alive. 

A woman in Schrobenhausen, Bavaria, went missing after her basement flooded. According to media reports, the 43-year-old woman was in the basement when the water level suddenly rose in the area. She has not been found since. The house also collapsed. 

Police and divers were deployed to the scene, but they were unable to reach the lowest level of the house. Authorities decided to evacuate the house and the surrounding area on Sunday morning. 

Germany's weather agency DWD issued a new warning for flood-affected areas on Sunday. The weather office said parts of northern Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg could receive up to 70 liters of rain per square meter by Sunday afternoon. 

A state of emergency has been declared in several parts of Bavaria as the Danube and other rivers rose. 

The latest weather warning says the storm could affect the states of Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, as well as Thuringia. Part of Günzberg flooded by the Danube Rescue workers are evacuating people from Munich and the town of Günzberg in Stuttgart due to the rising waters of the Danube. 

"Several parts of our urban area are flooded. People are being rescued from their homes and apartments by boat and helicopter," Mayor Gerhard Yewernisch wrote in an online post. He urged Günzburg residents to stay home, follow rescuers' instructions and keep roads closed to facilitate rescue efforts. 

After the floods in southern Germany, Bavarian Premier Markus Söder said 40,000 rescuers had been deployed in his state alone. 

The most important thing, he told reporters, was to quickly replace them. The longer rescuers work without rest, the more mistakes they make. Fatigue also increases the risk of death and injury. 

Söder, along with Economy Minister Robert Habeck, visited the affected town of Markt Riessershofen. Söder is seeking support from the federal government in both funding and manpower. 

Local officials said on Sunday that two dams on the Par River, a branch of the Danube, had collapsed near the Bavarian town of Pfaffenhofen an Ilm. 

Residents were advised to leave their one-story homes and stay on the upper floors of buildings. A fire department spokesman said the flooding in the Pfaffenhofen area was unprecedented. 

"We have no choice, we have to give up," he said. Firefighters are still working to save lives, he said. 

Olaf Scholz 'gratitude and respect' for rescuers 

Chancellor Erhard Scholz expressed his condolences over the death of a firefighter in Pfaffenhofen. He thanked rescuers and helpers in a post on social media. The German chancellor also offered his condolences to the firefighter's family. 

German railway operator DB has issued a travel warning for flood-hit areas. Trains have been cancelled across southern Germany due to flooding and landslides. Most trains are running late. 

A spokesman for Deutsche Bahn (DB) said several connections to and from Munich, Stuttgart and Augsburg were affected. Among them were cancellations between Munich and Berlin, Munich and the Swiss metropolis of Zurich, as well as between Stuttgart and Frankfurt.

Headline_English: Remittances in May reached $2.25 billion
Content_Enlish:
In May this year, $2.25 billion in remittances were received, which is 32.35 percent more than the same period last year. According to Bangladesh Bank data, remittances received in the same period last year were $1.7 billion. 
In this context, Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Md. Mejbaul Haque said that as a result of various initiatives taken by Bangladesh Bank, expatriate income increased by 32.35 percent compared to the same month of the previous year. According to the central bank, remittances increased by 10.29 percent in May compared to the previous month of April. 

Those involved in the banking sector say that expatriates usually send extra money to their families and relatives before the two Eids. Eid-ul-Azha is ahead. Remittance flow has increased in view of Eid-ul-Azha. 

According to Bangladesh Bank data, the highest expatriate income was received in May out of the 11 months from July to May of the current fiscal year. However, the second highest remittance came in February. That month, $2.16 billion was received.

Headline_English: Shanto will return to the track any day: Papon
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh's worries in the T20 World Cup are due to the lack of form of the top order batters. Liton Das has not been in rhythm with the bat for a long time. Along with this, Soumya Sarkar and captain Nazmul Hasan Shanto are able to do justice to their names. Which is creating quite a concern. However, BCB President Nazmul Hasan Papon believes that they have the ability to do something good on their day. 
While talking to the media on Sunday (June 2), Papon said, 'Soumya and Liton Das will have to play one day. That day will be important someday. The problem is that we need it now. We can hope that they will regain their courage and form soon.' 
About captain Shanto, the BCB chief also said, 'Shakib is experienced, Mahmudullah Riyad is there. Now come those who came before him. If I am going to talk about them, then of course Soumya, Liton, Shanto. I hope Shanto will come to the runs at any time.'

Headline_English: Canada to provide 5,000 free visas for Gazans
Content_Enlish:
Canada's Interior Minister Mark Miller has announced a major change in visa policy to make it easier for Palestinians to travel to Canada. He said that the number of visas for relatives of Palestinians living in Canada will be increased by five times. Al Jazeera News. 
Ottawa is increasing the number of visas for Gazans to 5,000 under a special program, Miller said. The minister said, "We are deeply concerned about the inhumane conditions in Gaza. Many people there are worried about their loved ones. The Canadian government is considering providing this facility for Gazans under a special policy. 

Noting that the Canadian government is working with the Palestinian government to issue visas to Gazans, he said that it is difficult to implement any measures at the moment because the current situation is not favorable. 

Those who want to leave Gaza and join their families in Canada need an Israeli permit. It is also quite difficult for Gazans to leave the place. The suffering of Gazans has increased since Israel recently took control of the Rafah crossing in Egypt. Israeli forces are detaining them in a kind of Gaza and committing inhuman atrocities on them. 

Keeping this situation in mind, the Canadian Minister of Home Affairs said - although it is not easy for them to leave Gaza now, we will make arrangements to bring those who want to come to their families from there as soon as this situation changes. 

Egypt and Israel are very important for visiting families in Canada. Canada has also announced contact with these two countries.

Headline_English: Elections postponed on St. Martin's Island due to inclement weather
Content_Enlish:
The 3rd phase of the Upazila Parishad election will be held in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar on Wednesday (May 29) at midnight. Although all the arrangements have been made by the Election Commission for this election, due to adverse weather conditions, it will not be held in St. Martin's Union among the 6 unions and one municipality of Teknaf Upazila. 
The matter was confirmed by Chittagong Regional Election Officer, Mohammad Nasir Uddin Patwari. 
He said that due to the rough sea due to adverse weather conditions, the Election Commission has kindly decided to postpone the voting process in St. Martin's Union of Teknaf Upazila, Cox's Bazar, which was to be held on May 29, 2024, until further orders, as per the decision of the Dhaka Election Commission Secretariat. 
According to the mentioned decision, the voting process at Jinjira Government Primary School polling station in St. Martin's Union of Teknaf Upazila has been postponed, he said.

Headline_English: Japan builds world's first wooden satellite
Content_Enlish:
Japanese researchers have built the world's first wooden satellite. The experimental satellite, called Lignosat, is made by scientists at Kyoto University and logging company Sumitomo Forestry in Japan. Each side is just 4 inches, or 10 centimeters. 
The scientists say the satellite will be launched into space next September on a SpaceX rocket from the Kennedy Space Center, bound for the International Space Station (ISS). From there, the satellite will be released from the Japanese ISS Test Module to test its strength and durability. 

The makers hope that when the device re-enters the atmosphere, the wooden material will burn up completely. A retired satellite will find a possible way to avoid the formation of metal particles when it returns to Earth. 

The developers said Tuesday when they announced the satellite's completion that these metal particles could negatively impact the environment and telecommunications. 

"Satellites that are not made of metal should become mainstream," said Takao Doi, an astronaut and special professor at Kyoto University, at a press conference at the university auditorium. 

Professor Takao Doi, head of the Kyoto University research team, told AFP that this problem led them to think about making a satellite out of wood. The artificial satellite they have built will be destroyed when it enters the Earth's atmosphere at the end of its life, but there will be no debris in the air. 

In addition, the developers plan to hand over the satellite, called Lignosat, made of magnolia wood, to the space agency JAXA next week, Doi said. 

"Data from the satellite will be sent to researchers who can check for signs of strain and whether the satellite can withstand large temperature changes."

Headline_English: City Bank approves 25 percent dividend
Content_Enlish:
City Bank, a listed banking sector institution, has approved a 25 percent dividend for its shareholders in 2023. This includes 15 percent cash and 10 percent stock dividends. 
The dividend was approved at the 41st Annual General Meeting (AGM) held virtually on Thursday (May 30). The meeting was presided over by Aziz Al Kaiser, Chairman of the Bank's Board of Directors. 

The meeting was attended by the Bank's Vice Chairman Hossain Khaled, Directors Rubel Aziz, Hossain Mehmud, Syeda Shayrin Aziz, Savera H Mahmud, Rebecca Brosnan, Independent Directors Salim Mahmud and Matiul Islam Nowshad, Managing Director and CEO Masrur Arefin, Company Secretary Md. Kafi Khan, senior officials and a large number of shareholders. 
Praising the bank's consolidated profit after tax of Tk 638 crore in 2023, the bank's Chairman Aziz Al Qaiser said that this 33.5 percent growth in profit from Tk 478 crore in the previous year is a reminder of City Bank's strong financial foundation and good governance. 

He also said that the bank's total current and savings deposits increased to 51 percent of total deposits in December 2023, which was only 36 percent four years ago. 

He mentioned the strong popularity of City Bank's digital banking platform CityTouch and said that customers transacted more than Tk 60,000 crore on CityTouch in 2023, which will cross Tk 1 lakh crore this year. 

At the meeting, the bank's Managing Director and CEO Masrur Arefin presented the overall picture of the organization to the shareholders and answered various questions raised by them.

Headline_English: All tourist centers in Sylhet declared closed
Content_Enlish:
The main tourist centers of Sylhet have been declared closed as the flood situation has taken a terrible shape due to continuous rain and landslides coming down from the upstream. Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) Mobarak Hossain confirmed this information on Thursday (May 30). 
It is learned that Jaintapur, Zakiganj, Kanaighat, Gowainghat and Companiganj upazilas of Sylhet have been submerged in water due to the rainfall of the last few days and landslides coming down from the upstream. 

The Additional Deputy Commissioner said, 'As the water level of the rivers has increased and various areas have been submerged, tourist centers including Sadapathar, Jaflong, Bichanakandi are in a very risky condition. In this situation, there is no environment to visit the tourist spots. Due to this, the main tourist centers of Sylhet have been declared closed.' 

Meanwhile, dry food, rice and cash have been handed over to the upazila administration for distribution in the five flood-affected upazilas of Sylhet. On Thursday afternoon, the Sylhet district administration handed over relief materials for flood victims to the administrations of five upazilas of Sylhet.

Headline_English: Germany sued over arms sales to Israel
Content_Enlish:
Human rights lawyer Alexander Schwarz told German news outlet DW that there is "reasonable reason" to believe that Israel is committing war crimes in Gaza with weapons it has received from Germany. 
The German government is violating international law by sending weapons to Israel, Schwarz told DW's chief political correspondent Nina Hase in an interview on Thursday. 

He is deputy program director of the International Crimes and Accountability Program at the Berlin-based human rights organization 'European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights', or ECCHR. 

The ECCHR is suing the German government in the federal court in Berlin, hoping to stop the arms exports. Schwarz says the weapons Germany has given to Israel include bazooka rocket launchers, ammunition and tank engines. 

The ECCHR has "reasonable grounds to believe that Israel is committing crimes against civilians in Gaza with these weapons. These crimes include war crimes and crimes against humanity, which the chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court recently confirmed," Schwartz told DW. 

Israel denies the accusations of war crimes, saying it is fighting Hamas, which the US, EU and others consider a terrorist organisation. 

Schwartz said his organisation had collected videos, photographs and eyewitness accounts as evidence of possible crimes. "We have collected reports from various organisations, including the UN and Human Rights Watch, which describe many of the incidents," he said. 

The human rights lawyer said Israel has an "inherent right" to self-defence. However, "Israel must respect human rights law, which from our perspective it seems they are not doing," Schwartz said. 

In 2023, Germany sold 326.5 million euros worth of weapons to Israel, second only to the United States. 

According to German law, "weapons" include tanks, bombs and missiles. By this definition, only two percent of the weapons Germany exports to Israel are weapons. These weapons will be the subject of the case filed by the ECtHR in the Berlin court. 

A case is being planned in another court in Frankfurt for the remaining 98 percent of the weapons exported, Schwarz said. He told DW that he had information that Germany had already stopped supplying weapons to Israel. However, Schwarz said that it could start again at any time.

Headline_English: Winning the title 14 times cannot be called luck.
Content_Enlish:
Real Madrid is the most successful team in the UEFA Champions League. Los Blancos have won the title a record 14 times. This time, Carlo Ancelotti's team is in the running to win the 15th title. Real will take on Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League final on Saturday (June 1). 
Real defender Antoni Rudiger is not feeling any pressure before the final. This German defender is even reluctant to consider Real lucky. In an interview with 'El Mundo' before the final, he said, 'If someone wins the title 14 times, then you can't talk about luck. The only thing on people's faces on the streets now is, let's get the 15th trophy. This is Real's DNA. Winning, winning. When I signed for this club, I felt that this club only wants to win. For me, the meaning of life is to keep winning. 

Referring that he has no fear before the final, Rudiger added, "Fear of the final? Fear is only for God. At the end of the day, we are all human beings, and as a human being, there is nothing to fear from another human being. I am a Muslim. A person of strong faith. So, I only fear God, who created everything."

Headline_English: Rohingya camps could become hub for international terrorists: Home Minister
Content_Enlish:
Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan said that there is unrest in the camp due to the delay in the repatriation of Rohingyas, and said that it could become a hub for international terrorists, a hub for weapons. Many things could happen. We are seeing some signs of that happening. We are also seeing the presence of a few people who are fighting in Myanmar and conducting various activities. 
He told reporters after visiting Camp No. 19 of Ukhia Rohingya Refugee Camp in Cox's Bazar and exchanging views with the Armed Police Battalion on Friday (May 31) afternoon. 

Stating that Myanmar is not cooperating in repatriating the Rohingyas, the Home Minister said, "The Rohingyas have been expelled from Myanmar, leaving everything behind. What their future is in this is invisible to them. So we have been saying for a long time to send them back. In this regard, Myanmar has made an agreement promising to work together, but the agreement has not been reached. No work has been done. 

Mentioning that there are various problems within Myanmar, Asaduzzaman Khan said, an agreement has been reached with Myanmar to take back the Rohingyas immediately after 2017. We think that they will take them back. The sooner it happens, the better for us. 

The Home Minister said, the most frightening thing is what we have always been afraid of. No drugs are being manufactured in our country. Drugs are coming from there (Myanmar). Some people in the camp are involved in it. We are trying to identify them. Everyone is working to identify those who are roaming around the camp with weapons and are involved in bloodshed and take legal action. 

At 11 am, the Home Minister exchanged views with the APBN at the Ghonar Para camp, No. 19, Ukhia. Later, at 12:15 pm, he visited the hilly area of ​​the A-7 block of the camp. 

The Home Minister highly praised the Armed Police Battalion and said that they are working day and night to maintain law and order in the camp. They also have to face many difficulties. He said he came to the APBN camp to see all these facilities and inconveniences. 

Inspector General of Police Chowdhury Abdullah Al Mamun, Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner Mohammad Mizanur Rahman, APBN Chief Additional Inspector General Salim Mohammad Jahangir and Additional Inspector General Anwar Hossain, along with senior police and administration officials, were present at the time. 

Earlier, the Home Minister was present as the chief guest at a meeting on law and order in the Rohingya camp at the Hilltop Circuit House in Cox's Bazar town on Thursday night.

Headline_English: Even with five to six times more money, their future is now uncertain.
Content_Enlish:
According to the agreement between the governments of the two countries, the cost per worker is set at 78,990 taka. 
The syndicate agencies have charged 544,000 taka per head. The quota for hiring migrant workers in Malaysia has been met. Last March, the country had announced that no more workers would be hired after May 31. But in the last two months, many more have made preparations to go to Malaysia. On Friday (May 31), thousands of people who want to go to Malaysia are flocking to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport. They have passports and visas. But the agency in charge of recruiting could not provide tickets. 

It is learned that the agencies have charged several times more money than the government has set for these people who want to go to Malaysia as workers. Even after charging six to seven times more money, they are not taking responsibility for them. The government is blaming these agencies. The agencies are also blaming the government. But more than 30,000 people have faced extreme losses. Their future is now uncertain. Many of them sold their land or paid for their trip to Malaysia by taking loans. 

Malaysia opened visas for Bangladeshi workers in August 2022. This process was suspended for four years due to irregularities by the syndicate. According to the agreement between the governments of the two countries, the cost per worker was fixed at 78,990 taka. But a survey says that the cost per worker was 544,000 taka. According to this, the syndicate has earned an additional 1 billion dollars. 

The agencies say that due to the lack of flights from Dhaka to Malaysia, tickets could not be arranged for 31,000 Bangladeshi workers. According to the decision of the Malaysian government, no workers from 15 countries, including Bangladesh, will be allowed to enter the country after Friday (May 31). 

On the last day, Friday, only 1,500 workers were allowed to go to Malaysia. It was decided in advance who would go on which flight and which plane. Apart from this, another 31,701 Bangladeshi workers got the opportunity to go to Malaysia with jobs and got visas, but are in danger of not getting tickets. 

Malaysia is the second largest labor market in Bangladesh. There are about 1.5 million Bangladeshi workers there. Last year, 351,683 workers went there. Till April this year, 44,727 have gone. 

Workers have not received tickets, saying that this crisis has been created due to the government's indifference, Association of Travel Agents of Bangladesh (ATAB) President Abdus Salam Aref told reporters, "50-60 thousand people have to go to Malaysia within a month. Due to the government's indifference, there is no preparation, no discussion. This is the misfortune of our expatriate workers going to Malaysia!" 

Some people waiting at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka to go to Malaysia said that many of them have been waiting for three days. Most of them have not yet received their flight tickets. The recruiting agencies through which they deposited money to go to Malaysia are also no longer answering their phones. 

Many have mortgaged their land and taken loans from banks and individuals to give money to the agencies. They came to the airport even after the agencies told them to. But they are making various excuses to pay for the tickets, some are not even picking up the phone. 

Several other passengers who appeared at the airport said that they have demanded that the government take measures to extend the time to go to Malaysia. They say that they have given five to seven lakh taka to the companies. If they cannot go now, they will be in danger. Some have also expressed doubts about whether the companies will return the money they have given. 

When asked about the rush of passengers going to Malaysia, the airport's executive director, Kamrul Islam, said, "There has been pressure from many passengers going to Malaysia for two days. To handle this additional pressure, additional flights are being arranged in addition to regular flights." 

Why are so many people suffering now despite being informed about the matter so early? State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury, told the media that the list of how many people could not go was requested from the Bangladesh Association of International Recruiting Agencies (BAIRA). But they did not provide it. 

However, placing the blame on the government, Baira Secretary General Ali Haider Chowdhury said that the Malaysian government had long ago said that the sending of people must be completed by May 31. Why was the overall management done at the last minute? 

Shariful Hasan, associate director of BRAC and head of the migration program, said, "What is happening with Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia is corruption. The syndicate is triumphing here. This cannot be a rule. Even though the visa is valid, they will not be able to enter that country. Both countries are responsible here. This has tarnished the image of the country." 

Demanding the formation of an independent investigation commission in this incident, he said, "Here the business syndicate has won, the expatriate workers have lost. Yet the country runs on the money of these expatriate workers. We want the government to form an independent investigation commission in this incident, investigate the real truth, and take necessary measures accordingly." 

It is worth noting that initially, there were 25 recruiting agencies in the cycle of sending workers to Malaysia. Later, a total of 100 private agencies gradually joined it. Later, the government recruiting agency Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL) joined. In the past decade, worker visas have been introduced in Malaysia more than three times. But they have been repeatedly closed due to irregularities by the syndicate.

Headline_English: Easy reading and memorization techniques
Content_Enlish:
This problem of not remembering what you read or forgetting everything you read is more or less common among students. Many people forget it after a few days even if they do not read in the right order. If they do not apply the right strategy, there is a high chance of forgetting what they read. More or less everyone faces this problem when it comes to studying. It is quite difficult to find someone who has not suffered from this. There are some special ways for this. Let's look at the strategies for remembering what you read: 
Try to understand what you are learning with your heart. Many people read without understanding. As a result, there is a possibility of forgetting it in a short time. If you understand, the possibility of remembering increases up to 9 times. And set a goal to maintain this focus. Decide how many pages of the book you will finish in how much time 

Take a break. After reading for 30 minutes without reading for a long time, take a 5-minute break. Also, practice getting enough sleep to increase brain performance. 

Create a summary. Create the main summary of a big chapter so that just by looking at that summary, you can get an idea of ​​the entire chapter. Now write the summary on a small piece of paper and pin it to the corner of the page where the chapter is in the book. Then it will be easier to memorize. You can also write through a concept tree. Draw a tree and draw the points between the leaves of the tree. The tree can be compared to a chapter. If you write a summary under the parts on each page, it will be easier to remember the reading. 

How to measure weightHow to measure weight 
Try to memorize important points. Also, try to bring a big sentence into a keyword, so that the entire line is remembered when you see that keyword. Then, if you can remember that keyword during the exam, you will remember the entire line. 

You need to practice writing and reading. When we write and read, many more areas of our brain are stimulated. The parts of the brain that are involved in writing help convert information into permanent memory. 

The brain mainly works to create memories during sleep. Research has shown that the work or events of the day are converted into memory during sleep. Therefore, if you want to convert any information into memory, you need to get enough sleep along with studying. 

Practice regularly. Keep repeating what you read today once after 30 minutes of reading, once after 1 day, once after 1 week, and again after 1 month. Repeating the same subject repeatedly causes structural changes in the brain's memory-making area, which helps in creating long-term memory.

Headline_English: IPL is over, Kohli's jabs don't end
Content_Enlish:
Despite making a great comeback in the group stage and reaching the playoffs, Virat Kohli's Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB) was eliminated in the Eliminator. Then, after the qualifiers, the IPL final also ended yesterday, with Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) defeating Sunrisers Hyderabad in the final to win the title. 

But in the midst of all this, how did Virat Kohli find himself at the center of all the criticism? Even after the IPL final yesterday, former India batsman Ambati Rayudu took a dig at Kohli. 

Bengaluru has not won the IPL in all these years, and the criticism is likely to continue. It is difficult for Bengaluru, which has repeatedly formed an unbalanced team, to win the title. This time Kohli was in dazzling form in the IPL – he scored 741 runs in 15 innings at an average of 61.75 and also won the 'Orange Cap' award for the highest run-scorer in the IPL. Not only did he not score runs, but amidst criticism over his strike rate, Kohli scored runs at a strike rate of more than 154! 
But what will happen if Kohli gets runs, Bangalore, which is largely toothless in bowling, has been sloppy. Despite somehow passing the group stage, they lost to Rajasthan Royals in the Eliminator. 
Many people have criticized Kohli that day too. Rayudu himself has criticized him. He criticized him again after the final yesterday. 

Although Rayudu did not mention Kohli's name, he criticized him by mentioning the Orange Cap. He told Star Sports, "Congratulations to KKR for standing by the likes of (Sunil) Narine, (Andre) Russell and (Mitchell) Starc, and also doing their part to help the team win. That's what makes a team win the IPL! The Orange Cap won't win you the IPL, but you can win the IPL if you have such players scoring 300 runs each." 

The implication is clear, Kohli won the Orange Cap, but Bangalore couldn't play as a team. 

Earlier, on the day of Bangalore's farewell, Rayudu had taken a dig at Kohli by mentioning 'personal milestones'. That day, he said, "I feel bad for the RCB fans who have been supporting the team for years and years. If only the team management understood the issues, and the team leaders did not give importance to their personal milestones over the interests of the team, then RCB would have won a few titles by now! 

Even that day, everyone understood that Rayudu had taken a dig at Kohli, who had become the highest run-scorer in the IPL even though the team could not do well.

Headline_English: Landslide fears in Khagrachari, 100 shelter centers opened
Content_Enlish:
Rain has started in Khagrachhari since the evening due to the impact of Cyclone Rimal. The administration is issuing alerts to deal with landslides. The municipality and fire service are conducting miking operations in various risky areas of the district to evacuate residents to safe places. The administration has taken all kinds of preparations to deal with the cyclone. 

The district administration has ordered residents living at risk at the foot of the mountain to evacuate safely. 100 shelter centers have already been prepared in 9 upazilas of the district. The leaves of government officials and employees have been canceled to deal with the disaster. 

In this regard, Khagrachhari Municipality Mayor Nirmalendu Chowdhury said, "We are working in the field in coordination with the district administration. Miking operations are being conducted to evacuate residents living at risk at the foot of the mountain safely." 

District Administrator Md. Sahiduzzaman said that all kinds of preparations have been taken to deal with Cyclone Rimal. The leaves of government officials have been canceled, and a control room has been opened. He also said that a meeting of the Disaster Management Committee has been held with the heads of the concerned departments.

Headline_English: Qatar Airways flight suffers severe shaking, 12 injured
Content_Enlish:
A Singapore Airlines flight was hit by air turbulence and made an emergency landing in Bangkok not long after. Meanwhile, another flight has been hit by air turbulence. This time, a Qatar Airways flight has been hit by air turbulence. As of last news, 12 people have been injured. 

The news agency Reuters says that a Qatar Airways flight was flying from Doha, Qatar to Dublin, Ireland on Sunday. It was hit by air turbulence on the way. Confirming this information, the Dublin Airport authority said that there was no major damage. The aircraft landed safely. 

The Dublin Airport authority says that a Boeing 787 Dreamliner flight was hit by air turbulence. After it landed, everyone was evacuated on an emergency basis. The injured were quickly taken to the hospital. 

The Irish media outlet RTE, citing several people on the flight, said that the severe shaking lasted less than 20 seconds. Everyone was being served food and drinks at the time. Several people were injured.

Qatar Airways did not say whether it was actually an air turbulence incident. Instead, it said it was investigating. In a statement, Qatar Airways said a small number of passengers and crew on the flight were injured. However, none were seriously injured. They were given first aid.

Headline_English: Rain all day, waterlogging in the capital
Content_Enlish:
Due to the impact of Cyclone Rimal, it rained throughout the day in the capital Dhaka. It rained in the evening as well. This has caused waterlogging in several areas including Mirpur, Jatrabari, Green Road. As a result, the residents of the capital have to face extreme hardship. The most affected are employees and students. Meanwhile, due to the cyclone, there was a fault in the Metrorail signal. Traffic was stopped for several hours. 

On Monday, continuous rain caused water to accumulate on the main road of the capital's Green Road. Traffic suddenly stopped on the road. Many people had to go to work while getting wet in the rain. School and college students were in extreme distress. Since schools were open and exams were held, they had to go to educational institutions despite the rain. 

Rickshaw and auto-rickshaw drivers were seen taking advantage of the poor weather of the capital. They charged higher fares in the adverse weather. Several people have complained like this. 
Due to the impact of the cyclone, there was a fault in the Metrorail signal. Passengers had to face difficulties as traffic was stopped for several hours. 
The Meteorological Department says that 143 millimeters of rain has fallen in Dhaka in 12 hours. Rain is also forecast for Tuesday. 
Azizur Rahman, director of the Meteorological Department, said, "The maximum wind speed in Khepupara, Patuakhali, was 111 kilometers per hour during the storm. Due to the influence of a deep depression over land, it is raining all over the country, which will continue until Tuesday afternoon." 

Trees have fallen on many roads in the capital due to the storm. As a result, traffic movement is disrupted.

Headline_English: PM seeks US businessmen's cooperation to build 'Smart Bangladesh'
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has sought the cooperation of American businessmen to transform Bangladesh into a ‘developed and smart’ country by 2041. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina made the remarks in her address to a delegation of the US-Bangladesh Business Council at her official residence Ganabhaban this morning. 

She said, ‘I call upon you to be a partner in our journey of a ‘developed, prosperous and smart’ Bangladesh by 2041. We aspire to become a ‘smart nation’ by 2041. We need your support to increase our global competitiveness and expand our export base.’ 

Stating that Bangladesh will transform from a ‘less developed’ to a ‘developing’ country by 2026, the head of government said, ‘They are determined to realize the dream of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib. Their efforts have led Bangladesh towards significant socio-economic growth in the last 15 years. Bangladesh is now recognized globally as a ‘role model of socio-economic development’. This has been possible due to good governance, rule of law and stability, investment in the rural economy, women’s empowerment, and ICT, which has transformed into ‘Digital Bangladesh’. 
Noting that America has been a major economic and development partner for Bangladesh for decades, the Prime Minister said, ‘Both countries have close engagement in many areas, especially in trade and investment. Our shared goal is to achieve mutual benefit and prosperity for our people. This is reflected in our growing bilateral trade and people-to-people interaction.’ 

Sheikh Hasina said, ‘The United States is currently the largest single-country destination for our exports. She is optimistic that this economic engagement will further increase in the coming days. The United States will become a long-term partner in achieving our development goals through trade, investment, and technology transfer, and by creating a smooth and predictable supply chain for mutual benefit. 
“Therefore, I invite you to invest in our many vibrant and high-potential sectors such as renewable energy, shipbuilding, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, light and heavy machinery, chemical fertilizers, ICT, marine resource extraction, and medical devices,” she said. 

Sheikh Hasina expressed hope that the US-Bangladesh Business Council will play an important role in advancing trade and investment cooperation between our two friendly countries. Finally, she urged all US business leaders to seize business opportunities and invest in Bangladesh. 

She also said that her government has established 100 ‘Special Economic Zones’ (SEZs) and 28 high-tech parks in the country. Some of them are operational. Especially in the IT sector, with over one million free-lancing IT professionals, Bangladesh is the right destination for investment in the IT sector. 

The Prime Minister said, “Here, I would like to remind you that Bangladesh has the status of the most liberal investment policy in the region. Rest assured that we are giving top priority to improving our investment climate.” 

After the meeting, the Prime Minister’s speech writer M. Nazrul Islam told reporters in a briefing that the Prime Minister had invited the US business delegation to invest in Bangladesh, adding that after the formation of the government in 1996, she had increased the multifaceted facilities on her personal initiative. The US investors expressed their ambition to invest in Bangladesh. But they mentioned some challenges that are necessary in investing in Bangladesh. 

US-Bangladesh Business Council Chairman Steven Kobos delivered the welcome address and its President Ambassador (Retd) Atul Kesap moved the vote of thanks, BSS reported.

Headline_English: India-Pakistan ticket price 23 lakh taka? Indian administrator scolds ICC
Content_Enlish:
The T20 World Cup is about to begin in a week. The biggest attraction of the World Cup to be held in the United States and the West Indies is the India-Pakistan match. It is natural for the audience to be interested in the match between the two arch-rivals in New York. However, former IPL chairman Lalit Modi has lashed out at the ICC over the ticket prices for the India-Pakistan match. 

No matter where the India-Pakistan match is held in the world, the audience is very interested in this match. As a result, the ticket prices for the match are naturally high. However, this time Lalit Modi has accused the ICC of profiting by selling tickets instead of promoting cricket. 

Former IPL chairman Lalit Modi wrote in a post on social media X-A (formerly Twitter), 'I am surprised that the ICC is selling Diamond Club tickets for the India-Pakistan match for $20,000 (about 23 lakh taka). This year's T20 World Cup is being held in America to promote cricket and entertain the fans. Not to make a profit by selling tickets.’ 

The black market for India-Pakistan match tickets is nothing new, but this time many are accusing the ICC of charging extra money against the ticket price. 

India will play its first match in the T20 World Cup against Ireland on June 5. After that, Rohit Sharma and his team will face Pakistan in their second match.

Headline_English: Israeli attack on Rafah follows ICJ order
Content_Enlish:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ordered Israel to stop its military operations in Rafah, Palestine. Minutes after the order, Israel launched a series of airstrikes on the Shaboura camp in the center of the city of Rafah. The British media outlet BBC reported this information.

On the other hand, in Kajla Linepara in Nachol upazila, Lamia drowned in a pond while playing near her house without anyone noticing. Locals said that some neighbors saw Lamia's body floating and informed the family members. Later, the family members recovered her body. 

Nachol Police Station OC Tarequr Rahman Sarkar said, "After the incident, the police were sent to the spot. After the legal process, the body was handed over to the relatives." 
It is worth noting that in the last one month, 9 children have died due to drowning in rivers and ponds in Chapainawabganj. Those concerned say this is very worrying.

Headline_English: MP Azim's murder: What we know about the events

Anwarul Azim, a member of parliament from Jhenaidah-4 constituency, went missing in Kolkata, India. Police in Dhaka and Kolkata say he was murdered there. But how? What happened to his body? The mystery is not being solved. Let's see what has been revealed about MP Azim's murder so far— 

May 12: Anwarul Azim's family said that he went to India for treatment and the wedding of his friend's daughter. He entered the Indian side through the Darshana check post alone. He did not stay at any hotel. He stayed at Gopal Biswas' house in Mandalpara Lane under Baranagar police station area. 

May 13: Azim spoke to his personal assistant (PS) Abdur Rouf. He left Gopal's house that day, talking about treatment. Gopal claimed that Azim would then go to Delhi. He also refused to call him (Gopal) as he was with a VIP. 

May 16: At 7:46 am, the last call came from MP Azim's phone to PS's number. PS could not pick up the call. When PS called him a minute later, he did not receive it from the other end. Since then, there has been no further contact with Azim. Azim has been missing since then. 

May 18: Gopal Biswas filed a general diary (GD) at Baranagar police station in North 24 Parganas district adjacent to Kolkata. Meanwhile, Jhenaidah Superintendent of Police Azim ul Ahsan said that the family has informed about the absence of MP Azim. On the same day, an extended meeting of the Awami League district committee was held regarding the by-election to Jhenaidah-1 constituency. Although Anwarul Azim was supposed to be present there, he could not be reached on the phone, said District Awami League General Secretary Md. Saidul Karim Mintu. He said that when he contacted the family, he was informed that Azim, who had gone to India, could not be found. He informed the matter to senior party leaders. On the same day, Azim's personal assistant Abdur Rouf said that he too has not been able to reach MP Azim on his phone since May 16. Some people have been sent to India by his family to search for him. 

May 19: Anwarul Azim, MP from Jhenaidah-4 constituency, has been out of contact with his home for 4 days after going to India for treatment. Jhenaidah Superintendent of Police Azim Ul Ahsan said that they are searching. But Azim has not been found yet. 

May 22: 9 am - Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal said that the government does not have updated information on this matter. He said, 'Our NSI, SB, police are all in touch with the law enforcement agencies of India. We hope that with India's help, he will be found soon.' 
The Intelligence Department (DB) of Bangladesh said that it is in constant contact with India's Special Task Force STF in search of MP Azim. STF told DB that Azim's last location was in Muzaffarabad in Uttar Pradesh. Apart from this, his SIM location has been found in several areas. 
DB Additional Commissioner Harun Ur Rashid said, 'We are constantly in touch with the Indian Special Task Force and intelligence agencies. The house where Anwarul Azim stayed in India is being searched. The name of the house is being searched.'

1:30 pm—Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal said that Anwarul Azim, a member of parliament from Jhenaidah-4, was murdered in a planned manner. He said that the Bangladeshi and Indian police are working to find out who committed the murder. At the same time, he also said that three people have been arrested in this incident. He is an officer of the Excise (Customs) Department of West Bengal. Sanjeev Roy rented the flat to an American citizen named Akhtaruzzaman." What is his relationship with the victim or the accused, Kolkata police are still investigating. 

Two people were arrested in Kolkata in this incident. One of them is a cab driver. Deputy Police Commissioner of Bidhan Nagar Police Manab Shringla said, "During interrogation, the cab driver said that the person he picked up in his car on May 13 was dropped off at this apartment complex." 

A GD was filed at the Sinthi police station adjacent to Kolkata in the case of MP Azim's disappearance. A top officer there said that the murder took place inside the flat in Sanjeev Garden. There are blood stains and other evidence there. Three people entered there with the MP on May 13. 

CCTV footage showed that each of the three left the flat separately. One on May 15, another on May 16 and another on May 17. One of the three was also a woman. Two of them were men who returned to Bangladesh. When the Bangladesh Intelligence Department was informed, they arrested and interrogated the two. Based on the information provided by them, the Kolkata Police confirmed the death of Anwarul Azim. 

8:30 PM—Mr. Anwarul Azim's daughter Mumtarin Ferdous Doreen filed a case at the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station in the capital seeking the whereabouts of MP Anwarul Azim. The case was filed in the evening. In the case statement, Doreen said that on May 9 at 8 PM, Azim left his house in NAM Bhaban for his village home in Jhenaidah. On May 11 at 5:45 PM, while talking on a video call, his speech seemed incoherent. After that, when he called several times, his phone was found switched off. 

Doreen wrote, 'On May 13, a message came from my father's Indian SIM number +917063214569 to Wazir's uncle's WhatsApp number, "I am suddenly going to Delhi, I have a VIP with me. There is no need to call me. I will call you later." Apart from this, several other messages came. The kidnappers may have sent those messages using my father's mobile phone.'

10 pm - Various information about MP Anwarul Azim, who went to India for treatment and was killed, continues to emerge. According to the law enforcement agencies of India and Bangladesh, he may have been killed due to a dispute over money from the hundi business and gold smuggling. The investigation by Indian intelligence agencies found the names of three Bangladeshis and one Indian citizen behind the murder. 

The Indian CID said that the apartment was rented from Sanjib Roy by a Bangladeshi American named Akhtaruzzaman Shaheen. He is the younger brother of Kotchandpur Municipality Mayor Selim in Jhenaidah. Azim had business contacts with Selim. It is believed that Shaheen met Azim through that source.

In the meantime, the Detective Branch (DB) has arrested Amanullah and Faisal Sajid. Another person named Mustafa Fakir has been arrested with them. 

The DB said that Azim's body has not been found. The arrested people said that he was killed, dismembered, thrown into the toilet and flushed. They believe that Azim was involved in hundi and gold smuggling. And some conflict over this is the reason for the murder.

May 23: Kolkata Police seizes a car used in Azim's murder. The country's police say that MP Azim rented the Suzuki Swift model car (WB18AA5473) for transportation. Important evidence has been collected from the car. The owner of the car has also been taken into custody by the police. 

At this stage, it can be confirmed that the name of the woman who went to Sanjeev Garden with Azim is Celesta Rahman. At the same time, it can be confirmed that this woman is not Indian, but a citizen of Bangladesh. Celesta's village is in Tangail. However, she is a resident of Old Dhaka in the capital. 

Meanwhile, Kolkata Police announced the arrest of another young man named Juber alias Siam on suspicion of being involved in Azim's murder. He was the one who rented the flat in Sanjeev Garden. Siam is also an American citizen. He was present in the flat in Sanjeev Garden on the day of the incident on May 13. Kolkata Police said that Siam is one of the masterminds in Azim's murder. Siam had arranged accommodation for those who had gone to Kolkata from Bangladesh on April 30 to kill Azim. On the same day, the West Bengal CID reported the seizure of another vehicle used to remove Azim's body. 

Around noon, Dhaka Metropolitan Police Additional Commissioner (Detective) Mohammad Harun Or Rashid said that after killing Anwarul Azim, the bones and flesh were separated. Later, they were removed from the Sanjeev Garden flat in two briefcases. The DB chief also informed about the arrival of a team of Indian police. He said that the murder was planned two months ago in the capital's Gulshan and Bashundhara residential areas. To destroy the body, the separated bones and flesh were mixed with turmeric in different places. Although the murder was initially planned in Bangladesh, it was later decided to implement it in India. 

In this briefing, Harun spoke about a man named Zahid or Jihad, whose identity was later revealed by the Kolkata Police – butcher Jihad, who had been hired to cut up Azim's body. 

That night, a team of Kolkata Police arrived in Dhaka. 

May 24: West Bengal CID said that the killers had hired a butcher named Jihad Hawlader to kill Anwarul Azim. West Bengal State Police said that Jihad Hawlader was a Bangladeshi infiltrator. His home was in Dighlia police station in Khulna district. However, Jihad lived in Mumbai, India. He worked as a butcher in a meat shop there. Two months before the murder, Jihad was brought to Kolkata from Mumbai by the mastermind Akhtaruzzaman. The Kolkata Police claim that Jihad confessed to the murder during the initial interrogation. He was produced before the Barasat court. The court granted him a 12-day remand. 

Meanwhile, Jihad's family in Khulna said that Jihad has been a fugitive in India for about a year and a half and works as a dyer there. Meanwhile, the Indian police say that Jihad has been working as a 'butcher' in India for a long time. 

Jihad's family members said that early last year, the DB police raided his house in a case in Jessore. Since then, Jihad and his elder brother Zahed Howlader have been absconding. A few months later, Jihad called his wife and told her that he was working as a dyer in India. There has been no further contact since then. Jihad has multiple cases against him at the Dighalia police station, including robbery and murder. 

On the same day, the Dhaka Magistrate's Court granted an eight-day remand of three suspects, including Celesta Rahman. Investigators from both countries, including members of the Kolkata Police who came to Dhaka, will question them. 

Meanwhile, along with the Indian police, the country's Ministry of Disaster Management launched an operation to find MP Azim's body. They conducted an operation to recover the body from a canal in Hatishala. However, the body was not found.

Headline_English: Israeli settlements allowed in northern West Bank
Content_Enlish:
Israeli Defense Minister Yov Gallant speaks at a news conference in Tel Aviv. File photo: Reuters 
Israeli Defense Minister Yov Gallant speaks at a news conference in Tel Aviv. File photo: Reuters 
Israeli Defense Minister Yov Gallant on Wednesday lifted a ban on Israelis entering the northern part of the Palestinian West Bank, allowing the resettlement of Israeli settlements that were demolished in 2005, CNN reported. 

The report said Gallant described the move as "historic." Last year, the Israeli parliament repealed a 2005 law on the issue. Now, the law has lifted the ban on Israeli settlements. 

The 2005 law, known as the “Disengagement Law,” banned Israelis from entering four former settlements in the northern West Bank. Gallant’s announcement means Israelis can now enter the four former settlements without military restrictions. 
“Lifting the ban will ensure the security of Jews in the occupied West Bank,” Gallant said in a statement. 

Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank will still require government approval. However, Gallant’s decision could make it easier to build illegal settlements, even though Israeli settlements in the West Bank are illegal under international law. 

Yossi Dagan, head of the Samaria Regional Council, echoed Defense Minister Gallant’s comments, saying it was a “historic moment of righting a historical wrong” and “necessary” for Israel after the October 7 Hamas attack. 

Incidentally, the decision came amid Israel's continued attacks on the Gaza Strip in Palestine. Even after seven months, Israel's attacks on Gaza have not stopped. The clashes are also causing casualties in the West Bank. There is no sign of a compromise or ceasefire. Israeli forces have intensified their attacks on the southern city of Rafah in Gaza. More than 35,000 Palestinians have been killed in the Israeli attack on Gaza for more than seven months. About 80,000 have been injured.

Headline_English: Umpire's decision in favor of Kohli in IPL, huge controversy
Content_Enlish:
The on-field umpire gave it out, but the third umpire gave it not out. That too for an LBW, where the ball hit the bat or not, even the commentators have doubts. 

There is a lot of controversy over the umpire's decision for Virat Kohli's Royal Challengers Bangalore in the Eliminator against Rajasthan Royals in the IPL today. Batsman Dinesh Karthik is the beneficiary of the decision. 

Rajasthan won the toss and sent Bangalore to bat first. Kohli's 33 off 24 balls, Rajat Patidar's 34 off 22 balls and Mahipal Lomrar's 32 off 17 balls helped Bangalore score 172 runs for 8 wickets in 20 overs. In reply, Rajasthan have lost 3 wickets in 11 overs at the time of writing this report. 
Whatever the outcome of the match, there will be controversy over Karthik's decision to avoid LBW. If Bangalore wins, the controversy will be even greater, for sure. 
The incident happened in the 15th over of Bangalore's innings. Avesh Khan dismissed Patidar on the second ball of that over, and the decision on the next ball was controversial! Avesh's inswinger hit Karthik's pads, and an LBW appeal was raised, and the umpire gave him out. Karthik took the review. 

The replay showed that when the ball hit Karthik's feet, the lower part of Karthik's bat was very close to Karthik's extended leg. However, it was not 100% certain whether the ball hit the bat or not. Although a spike was seen at Ultra Edge, there was no way to be 100% certain whether it was because the ball hit the bat or because the lower part of the bat hit the pads. 

In such a case, most third umpires are supposed to accept the umpire's signal, i.e. the decision of out. However, the TV umpire of the match, Anil Chowdhury, went against the decision of the on-field umpire and declared him not out. 

The commentators also said that the third umpire's decision seemed wrong to them. Rajasthan's cricket director, Sri Lankan legend Kumar Sangakkara, was seen talking to the fourth umpire in a very excited manner. 

If Karthik was given out, Bangalore's score would have been 122 for 6. At that time, Karthik, who was on the verge of being out for 0 runs in 1 ball, could not do much, in the end he scored 11 runs in 13 balls. However, in his partnership with Lamrar, Bangalore scored 32 runs in 24 balls.

Headline_English: Conspiracy against Sheikh Hasina still ongoing: Salman F. Rahman

Headline_English: Who will become the president of Iran if Raisi dies?
Content_Enlish:
Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi has been involved in an accident. A helicopter carrying Raisi has crashed. His helicopter crashed on Sunday, the country's state TV channel reported, citing Reuters. It has not been possible to contact the helicopter so far. 
However, there is uncertainty about whether the Iranian president is injured or even alive. If he dies, who will become Iran's president? 

Qatar-based media outlet Al-Jazeera says that the Iranian constitution clearly states this. It states that if the president dies suddenly, the country's vice president will take over. 

Currently, Mohammad Makhbar is in charge of Iran's vice president. If Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi dies, he will take over this responsibility. And this responsibility will be approved by the country's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

In Iran's political system, the country's highest leader is the Supreme Leader, who is currently in the position of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. And Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi is the second in power. 

If the president dies, the first vice president will take over this responsibility. Then elections will be held within 50 days. Meanwhile, several sources in Iran say that President Raisi is expected to become the country's supreme leader after Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. 

Citing a report by Iran's Tasnim news agency, the British media outlet The Telegraph said that Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi was not found there after the accident. However, it could not confirm any of the truth of this news. 

Citing a report by Iran's state TV channel, the Reuters news agency said that the accident occurred when the helicopter was landing. Rescue teams quickly went there after the incident. However, it is not known whether they were able to start the rescue. 

Several Iranian media outlets have reported on the incident, but no official statement has been made. It is also not known whether Ebrahim Raisi was injured in the incident.

The AP news agency says that Ebrahim Raisi went to Iran's East Azerbaijan Province. The accident occurred near an area called Jolfa. This is a border area with neighboring Azerbaijan.

Rescue teams are unable to work properly due to adverse weather conditions. Red Crescent and military members have also joined the rescue. Some local media outlets say that the area is covered in fog. Due to this, the position of the helicopter cannot be understood.
