Headline_English: Principal beats up teacher for coming late to school
Content_Enlish:
A teacher was beaten up by the principal of a pre-secondary school in Segana village, Agra, India, for coming late. The video of the incident has gone viral on social media. According to an NDTV report, the female principal of the institution beat up the teacher, Gunjan Chowdhury, for coming late to school. During this, she was also accused of trying to tear the victim's clothes. In the video, the victim is seen trying to free herself. At this time, they are seen being held by the principal's clothes. Her driver first tried to free them. Then the principal misbehaved with the driver. 

In the video, someone is heard saying, "The incident will be recorded. Madam, you are behaving rudely. Does this suit you?" 

Her colleague claims in the video that the teacher was injured in the incident. 

In the video, the victim is heard saying, "Shameless woman." After that, he accused her of coming late to school. 

During the argument, both of them used obscene language which is in no way befitting their profession. 

During the argument, the victim teacher told the principal, ‘Mar ke dikhade agar dum hai to (Show me if you have the courage). Kya kar lega tu aur tera driver (What will you and your driver do)?’ 

Then the principal said, ‘Kisiki dadagiri nahi chalegi yaha (No one will be allowed to be bullied here)’

Headline_English: Sadiq Khan elected Mayor of London for a record third time
Content_Enlish:
Sadiq Khan has set a record by being elected as the mayor of London for the third consecutive time. He won on the promise of fighting crime and clean air. Labour Party candidate Sadiq Khan won with 43.7 percent of the vote. His rival Susan Hall of the Conservative Party received 32.6 percent of the vote. Sadiq Khan was first elected as the mayor of London from the Labour Party in 2016. He was later elected for a second time in 2021. 

Analysts believe that Sadiq Khan won the election through a fierce campaign against his Conservative Party rival Hall. He was even elected after leaving behind other high-profile Tory candidates, including former London minister Paul Scully. 

Sadiq Khan, of Pakistani origin, is the son of a disadvantaged family. Sadiq Khan is one of eight children of his parents. Sadiq Khan, who came from Pakistan, was a bus driver and his mother worked as a seamstress for a living. 

They lived in a government council flat built for the poor in an area of ​​​​south London.

From a young age, Sadiq Khan never shied away from fighting for his ideals and overcoming all odds to succeed. 

Sadiq Khan's father, Amanullah Khan, and mother, Seherun Khan, came to London from Pakistan in 1970 - shortly before Sadiq Khan was born. 

Sadiq Khan was the fifth of eight children. They had seven brothers and one sister. Their large family had to live in a three-room flat in south-west London, where they lived. 

He attended a local government school and it was there that he became interested in politics at the age of 15 and joined the Labour Party. The headmaster of the school, Ernest Bevin College, was the first Muslim headmaster of a secondary school in the UK. 

Sadiq Khan has been a Muslim since childhood and says he was taught by his parents that ‘if you see something wrong, you have to try to change it.’ 

He was good at school, and was a fan of football, boxing and cricket. He even trained for the Surrey County Cricket Team for a while as a youngster. 

However, he has described how he and his brother were subjected to racist comments on the football field, which made him feel ‘safe’ to watch the game at home. He later became a Liverpool fan. 

He initially studied science – thinking of becoming a dentist. Later, on the advice of a teacher, he went on to study law. The teacher told him, ‘You should always argue.’ 

In 1994, he joined a law firm as a human rights lawyer. That same year, he met and married his wife, Sadia Ahmed. Sadia was also a law student and coincidentally, the daughter of a bus driver. 

They have two daughters – Anisa and Ammara. 

Sadiq Khan worked in local government for 12 years. In 2004, he left his law practice to enter politics full-time. 

In 2005, he was elected MP for Tooting, a constituency in south London. 

His contemporaries in politics across the political spectrum have described him as "very intelligent" and "intelligent" and "often difficult to refute". 

In a 2010 interview with the Guardian, Sadiq Khan said, "I don't want to make any arrogant comments - but there are very few people in the British Muslim community who can make a coherent argument, very few Muslims say, 'I'm British, Muslim and Londoner - I'm proud of that.'"

Headline_English: Rohingya youth hacked to death in Ukhiya camp
Content_Enlish:
A Rohingya youth was hacked to death in a Rohingya camp in Ukhia, Cox's Bazar. The murder took place at around 6 pm on Sunday (May 5) in S 4-5 block of Extension No. 20 of Ukhia. The deceased, Zafar Ahmed (42), is the son of Ranju Mia, a resident of G-9 block of Rohingya camp No. 4 Kutupalong in Ukhia. It is learnt that the deceased Rohingya was an active member of RS. 
With the help of the camp police, Ukhia police recovered Zafar's body and sent it to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital for autopsy. 

Additional police have been deployed inside the entire Rohingya camp since the incident. 14 Armed Police Battalion Commander Md. Iqbal confirmed the incident.

Headline_English: What the Law Minister said about reducing cadet college tuition fees
Content_Enlish:
Cadet College is a specialized educational institution. Here, the salary of students is determined depending on the income of the guardian. Recently, this salary has been increased by up to 30 percent. In this context, Jhenaidah-2 MP Md. Naser Shahriar Zahedi has proposed to reduce the tuition fee of Cadet College students. On Sunday (May 5), during the question and answer session in Parliament, MP Naser Shahriar Zahedi drew the attention of Law Minister Anisul Haque, who is in charge of the Ministry of Defense, to this issue. 

Naser Shahriar Zahedi raised the question and proposed whether any measures will be taken to determine the salary increase at a reasonable level for the benefit of lower middle class and middle class children. He said that tuition fees are increased in cadet colleges in 19 stages. Among these, in the highest stage, in stage 18, if the guardian's income is more than 1 lakh taka, the tuition fee is 20 thousand taka. If it is increased by 30%, it will be 26 thousand taka from 2024. If the guardian's income is 40 thousand taka in the middle stage, then he will have to pay 16 thousand 250 taka for the child, which is 40 percent of his entire income. In this situation, the MP proposed that the government consider re-fixing it to a more tolerable level instead of increasing the tuition fee. 

In response, the Law Minister said that since the cadets in the cadet colleges do not have their own source of income other than tuition fee and according to the decision of the Ministry of Finance, there was initially a proposal to increase the tuition fee in order to increase their own income, but it was not increased. Later, the tuition fee of the new cadres of the seventh class was increased in 20 steps. In the lowest step, the fee was 1000 taka. And in the highest step, it was increased to 28 thousand taka, which was previously 22 thousand taka. 

The Minister said that a plan has been taken to form an endowment fund in each cadet college for the meritorious children of indigent families. Through which indigent meritorious students will enjoy much more benefits than before. It is particularly noteworthy that due to the lack of bulk allocation of housing pension in cadet colleges, the payment of retirement allowance to retired officers and employees of cadet colleges has been stopped from the fiscal year 2022-23. 

After a while, the minister said, I have just learned from the Prime Minister that the government has signed the file for the allocation of the money that was supposed to be given for pension. In this context, I would like to say that if an application is made to the authorities based on the question asked by the member of parliament, they may consider the matter.

Headline_English: The entire country has been turned into a prison: Mirza Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has said that the entire country has been turned into a prison by sending opposition leaders and activists to jail. He said this in a statement sent to the media on Monday (April 29). Mirza Fakhrul issued the statement condemning the rejection of bail and sending to jail of Yubadal President Sultan Salahuddin, BNP National Executive Committee member SM Obaidul Haque, Kurigram District BNP Joint General Secretary Sohel Hosnain and other leaders. 

Mirza Fakhrul said that the Awami ruling class has now become more reckless, authoritarian and oppressive after 'snapping' power through the 'dummy' election on January 7. In order to maintain the illegal state power, the government has brought down the sword of repression on the BNP and its affiliates, democracy-minded opposition parties and people of different views and paths. 

He said, "Currently, the rule of law and good governance have disappeared from the country, so the leaders and activists who participated in the democratic struggle are being deprived of justice. A totalitarian anarchy has spread in the country. The illegal Awami League ruling group is spreading fear and panic everywhere from cities to villages to prolong their misrule." 

The BNP Secretary General said, "I express deep concern over the constant government-backed imprisonment of opposition leaders and activists in false cases, including the issuance of mandatory sentences and denial of bail, across the country, and I strongly urge the immediate withdrawal of the false cases filed against Jubo Dal President Sultan Salauddin Tuku, BNP Executive Committee member SM Obaidul Haque Nasir and the aforementioned leaders and their unconditional release."

Headline_English: Pro-Khalistan slogans raised in front of Trudeau, India summons Canadian ambassador
Content_Enlish:
'Pro-Khalistan' slogans were raised at an event in the presence of Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. India summoned Canada's Deputy High Commissioner on Monday after the incident. India-Canada diplomatic relations have recently hit rock bottom over the Khalistan movement. This has added to the tension. In a statement, India's Ministry of External Affairs said, 'The Government of India has expressed deep concern and strong protest over this incident. Canada is allowing such activities to continue unchecked, which is worrying. It is yet again evidence that separatism, extremism and violence are being given political patronage in Canada.' 
The statement further said, 'Their expressions not only affect India-Canada relations but also encourage an environment of violence and crime in Canada to the detriment of its own citizens.' 

A video released by Canada-based CPAC TV showed that the slogan 'Khalistan Zindabad' was raised even louder after Trudeau took the stage to deliver a speech on the occasion of Khalsa Day. 

Thousands of people gathered in downtown Toronto on Sunday for the city's largest annual rally. 

In his speech, Trudeau accused India of involvement in the killing of Sikh leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar last year. Trudeau also pledged to always protect the rights and freedoms of Sikhs in Canada and to protect the community from hatred and discrimination. 

India has rejected the Canadian government's accusations as "unfounded and motivated." Instead, New Delhi has accused Ottawa of harboring Sikh separatists.

Headline_English: Austria proposes to invest in green energy, set up trade office and hire skilled workers in Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
Austria is interested in investing in green energy, especially wind and energy from waste, in Bangladesh. The country has also proposed to open a trade office in Dhaka. They have also expressed interest in hiring skilled workers from this country. Foreign Minister Alexander Schallenberg made this proposal in a bilateral meeting with Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud in the Austrian capital Vienna on Monday (April 29) morning. In the meeting, the two foreign ministers emphasized the need to increase the travel of trade delegations and the rapid signing of the proposed agreement to avoid double taxation, noting that there is ample opportunity to increase bilateral trade with Bangladesh and Austrian investment. 

Minister Schallenberg agreed to send a trade delegation to Bangladesh soon, open a trade office in Dhaka, and sign a memorandum of understanding on migration and public relations. 

The two foreign ministers agreed to deepen bilateral relations in areas such as economic cooperation, trade and investment, migration and mobility, climate change, waste management and trade facilitation even after Bangladesh's transition to a middle-income country. 

Hasan Mahmud highlighted that Bangladesh's ICT professionals are also capable of contributing to Austrian institutions. 

Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud discussed with Austrian Foreign Minister Schallenberg the situation in Myanmar, the Middle East and the Indo-Pacific, as well as regional development, peace and stability in South Asia and Europe. 

At the time, he called for assistance in the repatriation of the Rohingyas forcibly displaced from Myanmar from Bangladesh to their homeland Myanmar. 

The meeting was also attended by the country's Ambassador and Permanent Representative in Vienna, Asad Alam Siam, and the Foreign Ministry's Western Europe Officer, Kazi Russell Parvez. 

Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud is in Vienna to attend an international conference titled 'Humanity at the Crossroads: Autonomous Weapons Systems and the Challenge of Regulation'.

Headline_English: ADB provides $121 million to Bangladesh for solar power generation
Content_Enlish:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has signed a $121.55 million financing package with Dynamic Sun Energy Private Limited for the construction and operation of a 100-megawatt grid-connected solar photovoltaic power plant in Pabna. The power plant, to be built with foreign financing, is the country’s first private sector utility-scale solar facility, a release said. The financing package includes $46.75 million from ADB, a $28.05 million B-loan syndicate from the Fund—an Amsterdam-based emerging market credit fund that serves as ADB’s lender of record in support of sustainable development goals—and a $46.75 million collateral loan from the Japan International Cooperation Agency. 

“As Asia’s climate bank, ADB welcomes the opportunity to support renewable energy in Bangladesh – where long-term financing for such projects is a challenge,” said Suzanne Gabory, Director General of ADB’s Private Sector Operations Department. 

She added that this partnership is an example of our leading role in mobilizing financing for clean energy facilities and stimulating more investment where it is needed most. 

The solar power plant will generate 193.5 gigawatt-hours of electricity annually and avoid 93,654 tons of carbon dioxide emissions annually. 

PT Managing Director Shakhawat Hossain said, “We are pleased to secure financing for one of the largest private sector solar projects in Bangladesh to date, with the support of international lenders led by ADB.” 

She added that partnering with an internationally acclaimed financial institution like ADB marks a significant step forward in our journey towards sustainable growth and is a recognition of our capabilities. 

DSE, owned by Paramount Textile PLC (PT), one of the largest winter clothing manufacturers in Bangladesh, also operates several power plants.

Headline_English: Far left and far right working together to overthrow government: Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that the extreme left and the extreme right are working together to overthrow the government. She said that politically bankrupt and some so-called intellectuals are constantly gossiping. And the extreme left and the extreme right have united with them. Their main goal is to overthrow the government. She said these things at the meeting of the Awami League's central executive council at Ganabhaban on Tuesday (April 30) evening. 

The Prime Minister said that whenever the Awami League came to power, it has worked to change the fate of the people. The Padma Bridge has already collected a toll of 1500 crore taka. This is proof that Bangladesh can do it. While the world is praising it, some people are criticizing. Whatever anyone says, Bangladesh will move forward with ashes in the face of the enemy. 

She said, now the question is whose ideology, and to what extent has anyone deviated. The extreme left has no ideology, they say the government must be overthrown. What is our crime? However, the people of this country do not accept it if votes are stolen. We have returned the people's right to vote to the people and made them aware. 

1 

The Prime Minister said, during the Corona, we gave vaccines for free. The rich countries of the world did not give them, but Bangladesh did. We did the tests for free, no rich country did either. We have taken steps to save people by spending money like water in both hands. Very few countries have been able to do that. We have achieved success there. 

Highlighting the government's development, Sheikh Hasina said, today the lives of the people of the country have changed. The poverty rate is now seen in the cities, not in the villages. If the Awami League is in power, a developed country can be built by 2041. 

Criticizing BNP, she said, BNP has started criticizing the government because it is not able to loot while in power. BNP is a party that has no brains. They can only give instructions online. People should not forget the misdeeds that BNP committed on October 28. 

Commenting, Sheikh Hasina said, those who are raising questions about the vote do not understand why the countrymen are happy to vote in this election. The Awami League has gained the trust of the people because people believe that the Awami League benefits them. 

2 

Mentioning that the trust of the people is the main strength of the Awami League, the Prime Minister said, today the lives of the people of the country have changed. If the Awami League is in power, a developed country can be built by 2041. The country has earned 1500 crore taka less than a year after the inauguration of the Padma Bridge. This is an achievement. 

The Awami League President said that the United States, without looking at its own face in the mirror, is giving Bangladesh a lesson on human rights. If any political party had raised its hand against an American policeman, what would the police there have done? Didn't the American police commit atrocities on the movement of ordinary people opposing the war a few days ago! This is a violation of human rights. What is the answer to this?

Headline_English: The use of robots as weapons of war is increasing
Content_Enlish:
Many things in science fiction are now reality. This also applies to weapons of war. The use of artificial intelligence-powered weapons is being seen in the Ukraine war. Robots can be friends, entertain, or even help in some tasks. There is also another type of robot, called 'killer robots'. So far, we have seen such robots in Hollywood movies. They destroy everything, kill without emotion. Artificial intelligence professor Toby Walsh said, when you hear killer robots, you think of robots seen in science fiction movies. But the problem is, these are now happening in reality. These are not Terminator robots. These are a type of drone that we can see being used in the Ukraine war. The amount of control of these drones by computers rather than humans is increasing. 

Tanks, soldiers in trenches - we saw this at the beginning of the Russian attack on Ukraine. But later both sides started using artificial intelligence. For example, Bayraktar's drone. Each costs more than 11 million euros.

German defense analyst Professor Dr. Gary Schall said that many of the weapons that Ukraine and Russia have later been AI-enhanced. As a result, there has been a change in warfare. For example, we have seen Russia use AI-enhanced glide bombs. And Ukraine's AI-enhanced weapons include drones. The reason why Ukraine was effective and successful in the first few months of the war was because they understood the situation very well. 

Military conflict means collecting information and understanding its meaning. How quickly it can be done is also important. AI can do that and make decisions. 

Axel Schulte of the Bundeswehr University in Munich said that now that so much has been automated, we have to think carefully about the division of labor between humans and machines. Humans have goals, machines do not. We use these machines, these automated systems, as tools. 

But can drones be humanoid killer robots or Terminators? Axel Schulte said, Terminator? No, that's not possible. We're not that far ahead technically yet. Yes, we see great videos of Boston Dynamics on YouTube. We see that these machines are quite good at controlling their speed. They can do things like dig bombs or something. But that doesn't mean they're dangerous killer robots. 

Global military spending in 2022 exceeded two trillion euros - a record. The United States is at the top with 750 billion euros. But China is also trying to get close. Russia increased its military budget by nine percent in 2022. 

German defense analyst Professor Dr. Gary Schall said, "If you have a force that uses AI, then your strategy will be different from others that don't use AI. It's not just about putting artificial intelligence into the machine. 

Companies that are making robots for peaceful purposes are working on making automated machines. And they get money from the government for that. Such work is being done in about 60 countries.

Headline_English: Kumar Biswajit's son Nibh opens his eyes after 14 months
Content_Enlish:
The condition of singer Kumar Biswajit's son Nibh, who was seriously injured in a road accident, is improving somewhat. Nibh, who was lying in a hospital bed in Canada, has started opening his eyes after almost 14 months. Kumar Biswajit confirmed the matter to the media on Tuesday (April 30) afternoon. Nibh was seriously injured in a road accident in Canada on February 14 last year. He was admitted to St. Michael's Hospital there. He has been undergoing treatment there since then. Kumar Biswajit with his wife Naima Sultana and child Nibh | Regarding his son's latest physical condition, Kumar Biswajit said that his physical condition is improving somewhat. But it is difficult to say when he will fully recover. He still has to stay in the hospital. However, preparations are underway to take him to rehab from the hospital. 

Kumar Biswajit and his wife Naima Sultana look at their son to hear his parents calling out to him. Doctors are not yet able to say when Nibh's voice will come out. They are trying all kinds of medical treatments. 

Nibh Kumar was seriously injured when his private car crashed into a road divider in Toronto, Canada, on February 14 last year. Three other Bangladeshi students lost their lives in the accident.

Headline_English: Comilla University closed indefinitely due to teachers' protest
Content_Enlish:
Comilla University has been closed indefinitely due to the ongoing teachers' agitation. The residential halls will also be closed. This decision was taken at the 92nd emergency syndicate meeting of the university. The matter was learned from the university's syndicate member sources on Tuesday (April 30). Syndicate sources said that the decision to close the university and the halls for an indefinite period has been taken. Later, after discussions, two committees of the university will be formed. One will be on the demands of the teachers and the other will be an investigation committee into the incident that took place on April 28. 

In response to the question why the decision was taken to close the residential halls, the syndicate member said that the vice-chancellor claimed that a lot of weapons are entering the residential halls. Students are being given money. This could lead to different incidents here.

Headline_English: Expatriate medical scientist Dr. Jasim Uddin's discovery of organic compounds to detect cancer
Content_Enlish:
The initial stage of deadly colon cancer is called colonic adenoma. If it is diagnosed and treated in time, it is possible to prevent this deadly disease. The cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) enzyme is found to be overexpressed in cells affected by adenoma. To identify this, Dr. Jasim Uddin, a teacher and medical scientist in the Department of Biochemistry at Vanderbilt University in the United States, has discovered a biological compound. It is known worldwide as florcoxib. After this biochemical compound is introduced into the animal's body, it starts working by binding to the COX-2 enzyme. Currently, Dr. Jasim Uddin is working as the Mary Geddes Stahlman Professor of Cancer Research and Research Associate Professor of Biochemistry. Dr. Jasim Uddin's discovery has been published in the international scientific journal The Cancer Research Journal. The news of this discovery has been highlighted in various international media around the world including Asia, Europe, America. In fact, Dr. Jasim Uddin's florcoxib cancer, the first COX-2-based imaging agent, is being widely used in research around the world, including the United States. 

Until now, white-light colonoscopy has been the only clinical method used to detect colon cancer. But 30 percent of adenomas remain invisible or undiagnosed. They are later diagnosed as colon cancer. As a result, statistics show that about one hundred thousand people die from colon cancer every year in the United States alone. 

Dr. Jasim Uddin's new nanotechnology, which is based on florcoxib, is able to easily detect the COX-2 enzyme in colonic adenomas. In this, he used a US FDA-approved polymer called Chloronic. 

This new discovery, published in 2023 in the international scientific journal The Journal of Biomedical Optics, is the first in the detection of colonic adenomas by fluorescence and has opened a new chapter in medical science. Now his new nanotechnology is waiting to contribute to human welfare.

Headline_English: Simple solution for rough hair
Content_Enlish: Everyone wants to have shiny, healthy hair. But in this scorching heat, the scalp is sweating all the time. To clean the scalp, one has to resort to shampoo. Although it cleans the hair, it becomes rough. It is not possible to cut the hair of the hobby quickly. So what is the solution? There is an easy way to remove the roughness of the hair. This problem can be solved with three simple ingredients at home. Banana, honey and olive oil are more or less available in all of our homes. If you apply a pack made with these three ingredients two or three times a week, you will get the solution to your problem. Let's know how to make this pack: Put a ripe banana in a blender. Mix 1 tablespoon of honey and 1 tablespoon of olive oil with it. Once you mix it well, your hair pack is ready. Before applying this pack, comb your hair well. Make sure that there are no tangles in the hair. Now apply this mixture to the entire hair and keep it for half an hour. However, those whose scalp is very oily, apply this mixture only to the bottom of the hair. By using this pack regularly, you will get the beautiful, shiny hair you desire.

Headline_English: Columbia students refuse to dismantle tents erected in support of Palestinians
Content_Enlish:
Columbia University in New York City has begun expelling students who have been protesting in support of the Palestinians and who have refused to move their tents on campus after a deadline passed. The college had warned protesters that they would face disciplinary action if they did not leave by 2 p.m. Monday, U.S. time. But dozens of students continued to gather at the site despite the deadline. 

“What is happening at Columbia is absolutely disgraceful,” House Speaker Mike Johnson wrote on Twitter. “There is now a campus full of anti-Semitic students and faculty.” 

The Louisiana Republican has once again called on the university’s president, Nemat Shafik, to resign. 

Meanwhile, police have arrested more than a dozen students at another protest at the University of Texas in Austin. 

The anti-Israel movement is the most important in American educational institutions since the Vietnam War and the civil rights movement in the 1960s. The protests against the Vietnam War were widely attended by students, who were arrested, and the peaceful demonstration turned violent. 

The students who protested have said that their protest is peaceful. However, the university administration considers the protests to be a disruption of their activities. The administration is using the police to maintain order on campus. Anger against the arrests of students by the police is spreading across the United States.

Headline_English: Rajshahi's sweet paan gets GI product registration certificate
Content_Enlish:
Sweet betel from Rajshahi region has received a ‘Geographical Identification-GI’ product registration certificate. The Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks under the Ministry of Industries has issued Geographical Indication (AIO) certificates for four new products. On Thursday (April 25), 14 new products have received GI certificates. Earlier, in August 2023, Rajshahi Deputy Commissioner Shamim Ahmed applied for registration of Rajshahi’s betel as a GI product. He applied to the Department of Patents, Industrial Designs and Trademarks (DPDT) of the Ministry of Industries for GI registration of sweet betel, the main cash crop of farmers in Rajshahi region. 

The maximum amount of sweet betel in Rajshahi district is produced in Mohanpur upazila. Apart from this, betel is cultivated in Durgapur, Bagmara, Paba, Charghat and Puthia upazilas of the district. Recently, the total area of ​​betel cultivation in the district has increased to about 3,500 hectares of land. Of these, betel is cultivated on about 1317 hectares of land in Mohanpur Upazila alone. The annual production of betel in Rajshahi is 21,072 metric tons. Its estimated market value is 607 crore 46 lakh 62 thousand 5 hundred taka. 

Although betel is cultivated everywhere in Mohanpur Upazila, the Kesharhat municipal area including Mougachi, Motihar, Dhuroil is notable. To market the betel produced here, betel is sold every day in at least 10 places in the upazila including Mougachi Hat, Ekdiltala Hat, Pakuria Hat, Kesharhat, Mohabbatpur Hat, Bakshimail Hat, Dhuroil Hat. Wholesalers from various districts including Dhaka, Chittagong, Naogaon, Rangpur, Dinajpur, Bogra, Gaibandha, Sherpur, Jamalpur, Chapai and Nawabganj come to buy betel. 

It is worth noting that Deputy Commissioner Shamim Ahmed had applied for GI registration for Natore's raw golla. This has been recognized as the 17th GI product in the country. Apart from this, Bangladesh has received Geographical Identification (GI) certificates for 31 products. 

So far, the GI recognized products of Bangladesh are - Jamdani, Hilsa, Chapainawabganj's Khirsapat mango, Bijoypur's white soil, Dinajpur's Kataribhog, Black cumin, Rangpur's Shatranji, Rajshahi's silk, Dhakai Muslin, Bagda shrimp, Fazli mango, Sherpur's Tulshimala rice, Chapainawabganj's Langra mango, Chapainawabganj's Ashwina mango, Bogra's yogurt, Sylhet's Shitalpati, Natore's Kachagolla, Black Bengal goat, Tangail's Porabari's Chamchom, Comilla's Rasmalai, Kushtia's Sesame Khaja, Tangail's Tanteer saree, Rangpur's Hadibhanga mango, Moulvibazar's Agar Atar, Mymensingh's Muktagachha's Manda, Jessore's Date Jaggery, Narsingdi's Amrit Sagarkala, Mishti Pan of Rajshahi, Rasgolla of Gopalganj and Nakshi Kantha of Jamalpur. 

GI is a geographical indication that is used to indicate the reputation or qualities of a product due to its specific place of origin. Usually, GI includes the name of the place of origin (city, region or country). If the soil, water, climate and culture of a country play the most important role in the production of a product, then it is recognized as a Geographical Indication (GI) of that region or country.

Headline_English: Temperatures are unlikely to drop this month
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has extended the heat wave warning in Bangladesh until Sunday. A meteorologist said that this April is the hottest in the history of Bangladesh since independence. Bangladesh is not getting relief from the intense heat right now. The Meteorological Department issued a notification on Thursday, extending the heat wave warning for another 72 hours. Meanwhile, the latest weather forecast said that an intense heat wave is blowing over Khulna division, Dinajpur, Nilphamari, Rajshahi, Pabna, Faridpur and Gopalganj. In addition, a moderate heat wave is blowing over Mymensingh, Moulvibazar, Rangamati, Chandpur, Noakhali, Feni and Bandarban districts, Barisal division and the remaining districts except Rangpur, Rajshahi and Dhaka. There is a temporary forecast of rain in one or two places in Sylhet division for the next three days. In addition, the Meteorological Department said that the rainfall trend in the northeastern part of Bangladesh may increase after April 27. 

Bangladesh's highest temperature on Wednesday was 41.6 degrees Celsius in Mongla. 

'Hottest April since independence' 

The temperature in Dhaka last week was four to five degrees Celsius higher than the average for the same period in the past 30 years, the AFP news agency reported, citing the Bangladesh Meteorological Department. 

5f117659-5f39-4d32-998b-bb0e05bf3b5a 
Photo: Abdul Gani 

Meteorologist Toriful Newaz Kabir told AFP, 'April is the hottest month in Bangladesh. But this April is going to be the hottest since independence.' 

He said less than normal rainfall was one of the reasons. He said the situation would remain the same for the rest of the month. Due to the excessive heat, there has been an outbreak of diarrhea in the southern city of Patuakhali, said Bhupen Chandra Mandal, a health official there.

Headline_English: Things you can carry with you in summer
Content_Enlish:
Summer means the intensity of the sun. When you see the sun shining outside, you certainly don't want to leave the house. But necessity is no longer an obstacle. Let's find out what those who are leaving the house in this heat need to have with them every day: Water 
In the intense heat, the body sweats excessively. Due to which water deficiency occurs. Keep a water bottle with you to avoid dehydration in this heat. You can also keep food saline. Even sprinkling a little water on a sunburned face after drinking water can provide a lot of relief. Umbrella 
Use an umbrella to avoid heat stroke in the heat. Colored umbrellas are available in the market. According to experts, black umbrellas can absorb the most sun rays. So whenever the sun shines, open an umbrella as a precaution. 
Sunglasses 
Everyone finds it more or less difficult to look into the bright sun. Again, if you can hide your eyes from the sun's rays, the heat will also be felt much less. Sunglasses will also protect your eyes from dust. So use sunglasses for your eyes. 

Sunscreen 
To protect your skin from the sun, you should use sunscreen with SPF. For those whose skin does not burn directly in the sun, you must use sunblock to protect it. 

7 

Tissue or handkerchief 
Tissue or handkerchief is a very useful thing. We have to wipe our skin with a tissue or handkerchief almost all the time. Or we have to wipe the sweat that sticks to the skin. In addition, it is essential to have a tissue or handkerchief as there is a high tendency to sweat in the heat. 

Mist and lip balm 
The face, neck and palms of the hands become sticky due to the sun and sweat. If you feel uncomfortable, spray face mist on the face, neck or palms. This will give you a refreshing feeling. Along with this, it will spread fragrance. Also, dehydration occurs in the body in the heat. Due to this dehydration, lips often crack. So keep a tinted lip balm in your bag. You can also use it as an alternative to lipstick.

Headline_English: 5 agreements signed with Thailand
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who is visiting Bangkok, held a cordial private meeting with her Thai counterpart Sretha Tavisin, held bilateral talks and signed an agreement, three memorandums of understanding and a letter of intent between the two countries. Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud informed this at a press briefing after the meeting at the Government House in the Thai capital on Friday (April 26) afternoon. In the presence of the Prime Ministers of the two countries, an agreement on visa exemption for official passport holders, three memorandums of understanding on mutual cooperation in energy, tourism and customs and a letter of intent to start negotiations on a free trade agreement were signed. 
The country's Finance Minister Abul Hasan Mahmud Ali, Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud, Ambassador to Bangkok Mohammad Abdul Hai and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Thailand Dr. Pranpri Bahiddha Nukara were present at the meeting.

Dr. Hasan said that the meeting between Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and Thai Prime Minister Sreetha Tavisin was held in a very cordial atmosphere. First, they spoke privately, then a bilateral meeting was held between the two countries. The Prime Minister discussed many issues in detail, including the Rohingya issue. 

The two Prime Ministers expressed deep interest in further strengthening, multidimensionalizing and expanding the brotherly and friendly relations between Bangladesh and Thailand, he said. 

The Foreign Minister further said that Bangabandhu's daughter Sheikh Hasina, in addition to describing the development and progress of Bangladesh, called for Thai investment in 100 economic zones and IT villages in Bangladesh. She also said that if Thai businessmen want, they can set up a special economic zone in Bangladesh for them. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has given shelter to about 1.3 million Rohingya people who were expelled from Myanmar in Bangladesh. Dr. Hasan also said that the problems arising for them in Bangladesh were discussed in the meeting. 

2 

The Foreign Minister said that many Rohingya have also taken shelter in Thailand, and many are still coming. Thailand is also burdened by the burden of these fleeing people. Both the Prime Ministers expressed their interest in working together to solve this problem. 

When the Prime Minister arrived at Government House on this day, the Thai Prime Minister was with the state guard of honor given to Sheikh Hasina. Sheikh Hasina attended the state lunch hosted by the Prime Minister of Thailand and spoke at his courtesy. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina arrived in Bangkok on Wednesday at the invitation of the Prime Minister of Thailand. On Thursday, Sheikh Hasina attended the 80th session of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNSCAP) at the United Nations Conference Center in Bangkok. In her speech there, the Prime Minister called for speaking out against all forms of aggression and atrocities and saying 'no' to war. The Prime Minister is scheduled to return home on April 29 after the visit.

Headline_English: Unable to take the exam, the examinee rolls on the street
Content_Enlish:
An examinee who was unable to take part in the 46th BCS preliminary examination in Rajshahi lay down on the road and cried. The incident took place on Friday (April 26) at the Mosque Mission School center in Sahebbazar area of ​​Rajshahi. The victim examinee, Fahad Faisal, said, "Sir, let me take the exam, this is the last exam of my life. Otherwise, I will die, sir! Give me a chance, sir." At one point, while talking about the atrocities, Fahad Faisal, who was dreaming of becoming a BCS cadre, tried to enter the hall by climbing the main gate of the examination center. But the police stopped him and sent him out again. Unable to enter the hall at that time, Fahad Faisal lay down on the road in tears. During this time, he kept saying - I will die, if I cannot take this exam, I will die, sir. I will not live anymore." During this time, he cried loudly on the road in front of the center. He also hit his head on the road, beat his chest and cried. Still, the minds of the people concerned at the examination center were not changed. At the time of the incident, the traffic on that road was stopped. However, despite all the crying, Fahad Faisal could not take the exam. At one stage, the police removed him from there. Then he left there crying. 

It is known that Fahad Faisal, a 46th BCS preliminary examinee. Fahad Faisal's home is in Naogaon district. The reason for his inability to take part in the BCS exam is that the exam was supposed to start at 10 am. The rule was that the examinees had to enter the center half an hour before the start of the exam (at 9:30 am). When Fahad arrived in front of the center, the clock was striking 9:40 am. The main gate of the examination center had already been closed. So he was not allowed to enter the center. Fahad Faisal first requested the police members to let him in. But the police did not agree.

If you want to know, Public Service Commission (PSC) Rajshahi Regional Office Deputy Director Nur Ahmed Masum said, a few days ago, the PSC Chairman held a virtual meeting with all the center secretaries. He instructed that if anyone does not enter the center half an hour before the start of the exam, he should not be allowed to enter. That instruction was implemented during the exam today. That candidate should have come to the center on time. The authorities are not responsible for this. 

On Friday, there were 31,947 candidates from eight districts of the division in 29 centers in Rajshahi metropolis. Of these, 24,118 took the exam. The exam was held smoothly from 10 am to 12 noon. However, one candidate was expelled from the Shah Makhdum College center during the exam. Besides, the exam was held in a peaceful atmosphere in other centers.

Headline_English: 3 children drown in Comilla's Devidwar
Content_Enlish:
Three children drowned in three separate places in Debidwar, Comilla within a span of four hours. The incident took place in Bijlipanjar, Bara Alampur and Gunaighar villages of the municipality on Saturday (April 27). The death of the three children has cast a shadow of grief over the area. 

The three deceased children are Raisa Akhtar (7), daughter of Rang Mistry Aliullah of Bijlipanjar village in Debidwar municipality. Eighteen-month-old Salman, son of Sohrab Hossain Sohag of Bara Alampur village, and Hafsa (5), daughter of Yunus Bhuiyan of Imandi Bhuiyan of Gunaighar village in Gunaighar North Union. Debidwar Upazila Health and Family Welfare Officer Dr. Ali Ehsan confirmed the deaths of the three children. 

Ward No. 7 Councilor Md. Bashir Uddin Molla, a resident of Bijlipanjar village, said that Raisa and some children went to bathe in the pond together. When the other children returned home, Raisa did not return home, so they searched for her, recovered her body from the pond, and brought her to the Upazila Health Complex. The doctor on duty declared her dead. The deceased Hafsa was a student of the first grade of Bijlipanjar Government Primary School.

It is known that an eighteen-month-old child named Salman drowned in a pond in Boro Alampur village of the municipality at around 4:30 pm. Ward Councilor Md. Abul Hossain confirmed Salman's death. He said that the mother of the child Salman returned home after bathing in the pond and found Salman was not at home. Later, when her mother saw Salman's body floating in the pond, the locals came and recovered Salman's body and brought it to the Upazila Health Complex, and the doctor on duty declared him dead. 

In the third incident, a child named Hafsa (5) drowned in a pond at the house of Imandi Bhuiyan in Gunaighar village of Gunaighar Uttar Union of the upazila. Confirming this, UP Chairman Md. Mokbal Hossain Mukul said that Hafsa went missing after going to bathe in the pond with her grandmother around 1 pm. The grandmother and others searched the pond and recovered Hafsa's body from the pond and brought it to the Upazila Health Complex, where the doctor on duty declared her dead. 

Debidwar Police Station OC Md. Nayan Mia said, we have come to know about the deaths of three children in three separate incidents. No one has filed any written complaint in this regard.

Headline_English: Over a hundred trees destroyed in Lawachhara due to Kalbaisakhi
Content_Enlish:
A sudden Kalbaishakhi storm has uprooted nearly a hundred trees in Moulvibazar's Lawachhara National Park. 40 trees have fallen on the railway tracks. Train services to and from Sylhet across the country were suspended for two hours from 5:20 pm. 
A storm hit on Sunday (April 28) at around 4:30 pm. The strong Kalbaishakhi storm caused extensive damage in various places in Srimangal and Kamalganj upazilas. 

It is learnt that the strong Kalbaishakhi storm has uprooted a large number of trees in Lawachhara National Park. Numerous trees have fallen on railway tracks and roads. Apart from this, extensive damage has also been caused in some areas of Madhabpur and Adampur unions in Srimangal and Kamalganj upazilas. Train services to and from Sylhet across the country have been suspended since 5:20 pm due to the fallen trees. The Sylhet-bound Jayantika Express train was stuck at Srimangal station from 5:20 pm and the Dhaka-bound Parabat Express train was stuck at Bhanugach station from 5:40 pm. Train services were restored to normal at 7:40 pm after the fallen trees were removed from the railway track. 

Bhanugach Railway Station Master Kabir Ahmed confirmed the news and said that 40 trees had fallen on the railway track inside Lawachhara Udyan. Train services were restored to normal at 7:40 pm after the trees were removed.

Headline_English: ADB to provide $71 million loan to Bangladesh for flood control
Content_Enlish:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) will provide a loan of US$71 million to Bangladesh to improve flood control, irrigation and water management. This assistance will strengthen the preparedness of rural communities in Gopalganj and Madaripur districts to cope with the impacts of climate change. To this end, a loan agreement was signed between the Economic Relations Division (ERD) and ADB in Dhaka today (April 20). ERD Secretary Md. Shahriar Quader Siddiqui signed the agreement on behalf of Bangladesh and ADB Resident Chief Edmond Ginting signed the agreement on behalf of ADB. 
Edmond Ginting said that this project will reflect ADB’s commitment to helping Bangladesh cope with climate change. As it will lead to significant improvements in flood control and water management, which will mainly help in addressing climate challenges.

Headline_English: BNP is claiming those arrested for terrorist crimes as its workers: Foreign Minister
Content_Enlish: Foreign Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud said that BNP is also claiming those arrested for terrorist crimes as its workers. He said this in response to questions from journalists after the chief guest's speech at the inauguration of the 14th International Women SME Expo organized by the Chittagong Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry at the Polo Ground in Chittagong City on Saturday (April 20) evening. The Foreign Minister said that thousands of people are arrested in Bangladesh every day for theft, robbery, kidnapping and other terrorist activities. The accounts given by BNP leaders Mirza Fakhrul and Rizvi show that those involved in terrorist activities are being arrested every day, and those who are criminals in the police's records are also being claimed as BNP workers. He also said that no political cases are filed against any BNP leader or worker. The cases filed against them are car burning cases, attacks on police and people, and terrorist activities cases. They have been arrested in these cases, and cases are pending in court against them. Asked by reporters whether it was confirmed that those who fled from the Myanmar junta forces would go to Bangladesh the day after tomorrow, Dr. Hasan said, "As discussed with us, they are scheduled to be taken on April 22. However, it will depend on many things. The situation there, how safe it is to transport them, as well as the sea and weather conditions. Dilawara Yusuf MP, Shamima Harun Lubna MP, FBCCI President Mahbubul Alam, Jatiya Mohila Sangstha President Chemon Ara Tayyab, among others, also spoke at the inaugural ceremony. State Minister for Commerce Ahsanul Islam Titu MP spoke as a special guest at the inaugural ceremony chaired by Chittagong Women's Chamber of Commerce and Industry President Monowara Hakim Ali.

Headline_English: Staying in AC day and night in the scorching heat?
Content_Enlish:
The countrymen are tired of the intense heat. In the midst of this, the cool air of the AC is a little relief. However, this relief can be a cause of harm. So you have to be aware of the use of AC. You must enjoy the pleasure of AC. But you have to do it in moderation. In this regard, Dr. Nikita Toshi gives some advice in India's PharmEasy: If you have asthma problems 
It is better for those who have asthma or allergy problems not to run the AC all day. It can also cause breathing problems along with sneezing. If you want, you can reduce the temperature of the room by running the AC a while before going to bed. You can turn off the AC when the room gets cold. Dryness of the skin 
If the AC is on all day, the skin becomes dry and flaky. Sleeping with the AC on often causes eye problems. According to experts, the air conditioner also reduces the amount of moisture in the air along with cooling the room. That is why such problems occur. Body pain 
Sleeping with the AC running all night makes the muscles of the body stiff. Joint pain increases. If you have arthritis, it's best not to stay in AC all day long.

Headline_English: Awami League to hold peace rally on April 26
Content_Enlish:
The Awami League will hold a peace and development rally on Bangabandhu Avenue in the capital on the afternoon of April 26 (Friday). A press release signed by Dhaka Metropolitan South Awami League Office Secretary Md. Riaz Uddin Riaz announced this on Sunday (April 21) evening. The release said that the party's General Secretary Obaidul Quader will be present as the chief guest at the peace and development rally organized by the Dhaka Metropolitan South Awami League on Bangabandhu Avenue at 3 pm on Friday (April 26). The peace and development rally will be presided over by freedom fighter Abu Ahmed Mannafi, President of Dhaka Metropolitan South Awami League. The rally will be moderated by Dhaka Metropolitan South Awami League General Secretary Md. Humayun Kabir. 

Meanwhile, the BNP has announced a rally in Nayapaltan on Friday (April 26). The party leaders, warning the government to leave, say that the people will take to the streets in protest. BNP has planned a large crowd for this rally.

Headline_English: Liberation War-era weapons recovered in Kishoreganj
Content_Enlish:
Police have recovered some abandoned weapons from the Liberation War period in Kishoreganj, Nilphamari. Local people found these weapons while digging the soil for canal renovation on Monday (April 22) afternoon. It is learnt that the soil for the renovation of the Dalia Main Irrigation Canal adjacent to the Bazedumaria Canal market in Sadar Union of the upazila was being excavated. At that time, 1 grenade, 1 three-knot three rifle, 2 mines, 1 motor cell (broken) and 1 rifle magazine came up while digging the soil with an excavator. Local people saw these weapons and informed the police. When the police went to the scene and confirmed the existence of the weapons, a police detachment was deployed there. 
Kishoreganj Police Station OC Palash Chandra Mandal said that the RAB's Bomb Squat Team has been informed to examine the weapons. It is believed that the freedom fighters may have hidden these weapons during the Liberation War.

Headline_English: Coal unloading underway, all sailors will return to the ship
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladeshi-flagged ship MV Abdullah, which was freed from Somali pirates, has docked at Al-Hamriya Port in the United Arab Emirates and is now unloading coal. Once the unloading is complete, 23 sailors will board another chartered ship and set off for the country. However, two of the sailors were scheduled to return home by plane earlier. The remaining 21 sailors had already announced that they would return by ship. However, the two sailors later changed their decision. Officials from the ship's owner, KSRM Group, said that the unloading of 55,000 metric tons of coal on the ship began around 12 am on Monday. 

The ship was captured by pirates on March 12 while en route to the United Arab Emirates from Maputo Port in Mozambique with 55,000 tons of coal. The ship reached the United Arab Emirates on Sunday night, eight days after being freed from Somali pirates on April 14. 

Meherul Karim, CEO of SR Shipping, a subsidiary of KSRM Group, said the ship's 23 sailors have decided to return home on board.

Headline_English: 28 percent of tuberculosis patients are victims of superstition
Content_Enlish: Tuberculosis patients and their families are affected by social stigma in various ways. These stigmas are hindering their efforts to control tuberculosis. Such information has emerged from a study by the Center for Diarrhea Research, Bangladesh (ICDDR, B). It is seen that about 28 percent of tuberculosis patients feel the impact of stigma or prejudice in the first three stages of their treatment and care cycle. This information was given at a seminar organized to release the results of the study titled 'Status of Tuberculosis-Related Stigma in Bangladesh' at the Sasakawa Auditorium of ICDDR, B in Mohakhali on Tuesday (April 23). The seminar, which presented the research report, said that about 22 percent of the family members of a person with tuberculosis face stigma. And 14 percent of tuberculosis patients and 11 percent of their family members also experience stigma at home.

Headline_English: Myanmar rebel group forced to retreat from border
Content_Enlish:
Earlier this month, the Karen National Union (KNU) rebel group in Myanmar overran the commercial town of Myawaddy on the border with Kayin State, ousting the junta military. This time, the group withdrew its fighters from there in the face of a counterattack by the ruling junta troops. Reuters reports. Most of the government troops in the city surrendered in the previous attack by the rebels, while the rest fled. On Saturday, fierce fighting broke out again between the two sides in Myawaddy. About 3,000 civilians fled the city in one day. The rebels launched an attack to drive out government troops trapped on a border bridge connecting Myanmar and Thailand. But additional government troops from outside, supported by a local militia, were able to counterattack and enter the city. 

KNU spokesman Sao Tao Ni said on Wednesday that their fighters had temporarily retreated from the city of Myawaddy after the junta troops returned. 

The spokesman added, “The junta troops have advanced into Myawaddy town. The KNLA troops will destroy them and the troops behind them.” 

The KNLA, or Karen National Liberation Army, is the armed wing of the KNU. The KNLA is one of Myanmar’s oldest rebel forces. 

Thailand said on Wednesday that fighting there had largely stopped and that it hoped to reopen the border crossing; already much damage has been done to cross-border trade. The strategically important city handles more than $1 billion in foreign trade annually, Reuters reported. 

“The situation has improved significantly. However, we are closely monitoring the situation, which could change at any time,” Thai spokesman Nikorndej Balancura said at a briefing.

Headline_English: Hamas chief to visit Türkiye this week: Erdogan
Content_Enlish: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Wednesday that Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh would visit Turkey this week. AFP reports. Erdogan, a fierce critic of Israel, told lawmakers, “The Palestinian leader will be my guest this week.” The two leaders will meet on Saturday at the Dolmabahçe Palace in Istanbul, private television channel NTV reported. Their last meeting was in July 2023. At that time, Ankara invited Haniyeh to the presidential palace, as well as Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas. Erdogan has been one of Israel’s most vocal critics since the war in Gaza began on October 7. According to Israeli figures, 1,170 people have been killed in the attack, most of them civilians. Israel has launched ground and air strikes in Gaza in response. The Health Ministry in Hamas-run Gaza said at least 33,899 people, mostly women and children, were killed in the Israeli offensive. The Turkish leader has developed friendly relations with Haniyeh, who is based in Qatar. Erdogan offered his condolences to Haniyeh for the deaths of his three sons and grandchildren in an Israeli attack on Gaza last week. Erdogan has called Israel a “terrorist state” and accused it of committing genocide in Gaza. He has called Hamas “freedom fighters” or “mujahideen” who are fighting for their land.

Headline_English: Hezbollah drone attack in Israel, 18 injured
Content_Enlish: At least 18 people were injured in a drone attack by the armed group Hezbollah on a community center in Israel, with one of them in critical condition. Hezbollah launched the attack from Lebanon on Wednesday on the village of Arab al-Aramshi on Israel's northern border. Claiming responsibility for the attack, Hezbollah said the attack was in retaliation for the killing of three members, including two commanders, in an Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon just a day earlier. The target was a building used by the Israeli army. The attack used missiles and explosive-laden drones. Video footage circulating on social media showed the explosive-laden drone falling on the community center and exploding. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said several strikes had been carried out in the border settlement. Its media outlets reported that a vehicle was also hit near the affected community center. However, they did not immediately provide any information about the injuries in the attack.

Headline_English: EU to impose new sanctions on Iran
Content_Enlish: The European Union is considering new sanctions on Iran for its attacks on Israel, the regional bloc's top diplomat, Josep Borrell, told reporters. After an emergency meeting of EU foreign ministers on Tuesday, Borrell announced the start of work on the new sanctions. He cited recent remarks by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres that the Middle East has reached the brink of a precipice. "Today, ministers took a strong position. They called on all parties to step back from the brink so as not to fall into the abyss," he said. Borrell warned that a full-scale war could break out in the Middle East if the blows and counter-blows continue. Borrell said that some EU member states have proposed new sanctions on Iran. Several other countries, including Germany and France, have supported the proposal. Some countries have also proposed sanctions against Iran's Revolutionary Guard Force. More discussions will be held on the issue at the next meeting in Luxembourg on Monday.

Headline_English: Dubai Airport returns to normal after 24 hours
Content_Enlish: Dubai International Airport was severely disrupted after unprecedented rains in the United Arab Emirates and neighboring countries. After being closed for 24 hours, its operations are finally returning to normal. BBC News. Heavy rains and thunderstorms hit the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday, flooding roads and important infrastructure, including the country's international airport. The flash floods killed 20 people in Oman and one in the United Arab Emirates. Some domestic flights resumed on Thursday. However, the entire Dubai International Airport is not yet fully operational. The world's second-busiest airport said on Thursday that it had started receiving inbound flights at Terminal 1, which is used by foreign airlines. However, outbound flights are still being delayed. Authorities later announced that check-in for Emirates was open at Terminal 3. But they warned that a large number of passengers were waiting to check in, which could lead to long delays. In a post on social media X early on Thursday, officials urged passengers to go to the airport only after confirming their bookings. “We are going through an incredibly challenging time. I have never seen anything like it in my lifetime,” said Paul Griffiths, head of Dubai Airports. The surrounding roads were closed as people rushed to the airport. On Wednesday, nearly 300 flights were cancelled and hundreds more were delayed. The United Arab Emirates has seen record rainfall in its history. The desert nation received up to 259.5 mm (10.2 inches) of rain on Tuesday.

Headline_English: 4 robbers arrested with country-made weapons in Madaripur
Content_Enlish: Police have arrested four people with country-made weapons while preparing for a robbery in Rajoir, Madaripur. They were arrested from Sutarkandi area of ​​Rajoir upazila on Tuesday (April 16) night. The arrested are Tohurul Sheikh (31), son of the deceased Titla Sheikh of Baradi village in Barkhada union of Sadar upazila of Kushtia, Kaushik Hira (38), son of Haran Hira of Baraikandi village in Sahapur union of Sadar upazila of Gopalganj, Animesh Gain (31), son of the deceased Kshitish Gain of Kadambari village in Rajoir upazila of Madaripur, and Debashish Mondal (31), son of Sunil Mondal of the same village. Superintendent of Police Md. Masud Alam gave this information at a press conference at the Madaripur Police Superintendent's office on Wednesday afternoon. Mohammad Kamrul Hasan, who was promoted to the post of Police Superintendent from Additional Superintendent of Police, Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Ops) Moniruzzaman Fakir, Additional Superintendent of Police (District Special Branch) Bhaskar Saha, Additional Superintendent of Police (Sadar Circle) Alaul Hasan, Assistant Superintendent of Police Md. Mursalin, OC of Rajoir Police Station Md. Asaduzzaman Howlader, Madaripur Sadar Model Police Station OC AHM Salauddin, Madaripur District Detective Branch OC Anisur Anis and many others. Superintendent of Police Md. Masud Alam said at the press conference that a team of Rajoir Police Station went on a raid in a mango orchard in Sutarkandi based on a secret tip-off that a house was being prepared for robbery. Later, the police arrested 4 people named Debashish Mondal, Animesh Gain, Kaushik Hira and Hajrul Sheikh from there. During their interrogation, two big ramda, a chhoda, a house-breaking hammer, a grill and an iron gate-breaking machine were seized as they were hiding next to them. The arrested people have been committing robberies in different districts of the country for a long time. There are several cases against them, including robbery and kidnapping. Later, a case was filed against them at Rajoir Police Station and they were handed over to the court.

Headline_English: Investment must be increased for the development of art and culture: State Minister for Information and Broadcasting
Content_Enlish:
State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat has said that investment should be increased for the development of art and culture. The State Minister made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the inauguration of the 12th Liberation Docfest Bangladesh, an international documentary festival on liberation and human rights, at the Liberation War Museum auditorium in Agargaon in the capital on Thursday (April 18) afternoon. Indian filmmaker and mentor of the Exposition of Young Film Talent Nilotpol Majumder and Indian national and international award-winning filmmaker Hawbam Pawan Kumar were present as special guests at the event. Liberation War Museum Trustee Asaduzzaman Noor MP and Liberation War Museum Trustee and Festival Director Mofidul Haque also delivered speeches at the event. Liberation War Museum Trustee and Member Secretary Sara Zaker delivered the opening speech at the event. The State Minister for Information and Broadcasting further said that the idea with which Bangladesh gained independence after the Liberation War was to create a non-communal, modern and peaceful society, where there would be no place for extremism and fundamentalism. To create such a society, we need a lot of investment in the field of art and culture. 

He further said that how many foundations are needed to become a developed Bangladesh in 2041. We have already achieved a lot to create these foundations. Our economic development has been a lot in the last fifteen years, we need to develop more. However, we need to increase our investment in the development of art and culture in the next five years. Because if we want to fight against extremism, fundamentalism and evil forces, then there can be no greater weapon than art and culture. We need the development of art, literature and culture now. At the same time, innovative talent is very much needed in the field of art, literature and culture. 

The State Minister further added, the state's job is to financially support and advance the industry so that the talent that is born in the society can develop, and more humanity and humanity can spread through industry. At the end of the day, we want to build a humane world and become global citizens. 

He further said, we want to ensure a healthy industrial development environment in the country. We will try to do this through the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

Headline_English: Iranian embassy in Paris surrounded over suspected explosives
Content_Enlish: French police surrounded the Iranian consulate in Paris on Friday after reports that someone had entered the embassy with explosives. They were also preparing to enter at the mission's request, a security source told AFP. "A witness saw a man entering with a grenade or an explosive belt," the source said. French elite police units were called to the consulate after being asked to investigate. An AFP journalist said the entire area around the consulate in 16 districts of the capital had been cordoned off and a police presence had been increased. Paris transport agency RATP on X said two metro lines had been closed. The lines passed near the consulate.

Headline_English: BNP is now a lost traveler, the address of militancy: Obaidul Quader
Content_Enlish:

Headline_English: 60 percent voter turnout in first phase of Lok Sabha elections in India
Content_Enlish:
The Lok Sabha elections in neighboring India began today (Friday). The first phase of the seven-phase election has begun. This election is being called a milestone for the BJP and a fight for survival for the opposition. The first phase of voting was held in 102 seats in 21 states and union territories. The voter turnout was about 60 percent. The voter turnout was 59.7 percent till 5 pm Indian time. The voter turnout was 63.2 percent in Tamil Nadu, 50.3 percent in Rajasthan, 57.5 percent in Uttar Pradesh and 63.3 percent in Madhya Pradesh. Along with the general elections, for the state elections, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh recorded 67.5 and 64.7 percent votes respectively. 
The first phase of voting took place in 39 seats in Tamil Nadu, 12 in Rajasthan, 8 in Uttar Pradesh, 6 in Madhya Pradesh, 5 in Uttarakhand, 2 in Arunachal Pradesh, 2 in Meghalaya, 1 in Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 1 in Mizoram, 1 in Nagaland, 1 in Puducherry, 1 in Sikkim and 1 in Lakshadweep. Besides, five seats each in Assam and Maharashtra, four in Bihar, three in West Bengal, two in Manipur and one each in Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir and Chhattisgarh are included in the first phase. 
Four states—Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh—will also hold fresh assembly elections along with the Lok Sabha elections. Of these, Arunachal Pradesh (60 seats) and Sikkim (32) are at the top.

Headline_English: Is your outfit in a bad state due to sweat?
Content_Enlish:
The temperature is increasing at a rapid pace. Everyone is more or less in pain. However, life is going on as before. So the office, court, class do not stop. In the summer, everyone is choosing light-colored loose clothes. But the danger occurs when women wear light makeup. In the summer, everything gets washed away by sweat. So you have to be a little clever in your makeup during this time! 
Before makeup, clean your skin well. Make sure that dirt does not accumulate in the pores of the skin. Clean your face and rub ice. When the ice water dries, then start makeup. Then choose a primer that absorbs. If you use this type of primer, the makeup will not wash off easily. In the case of eye makeup, use waterproof eyeliner. Eye makeup melts the fastest in the summer. So use a good eyeliner to maintain the beauty of your eyes. And if you want to wear kajal, then apply eyeshadow over the kajal.

Headline_English: Tourists flock to Cox's Bazar, no place for moles on the beach
Content_Enlish:
This year's Eid-ul-Fitr is associated with the New Year, along with a weekly holiday. As a result, the country is trapped in a six-day holiday. Although the employees are happy due to the continuous closure, the tourism related people of Cox's Bazar are disappointed. Because, the first two days of the six-day holiday have been empty of tourists. However, since the day of Eid, the influx of tourists has decreased in Cox's Bazar tourist centers. Moreover, today, Friday (April 12), despite the heat, a large number of tourists have flocked to the Cox's Bazar sea beach. There is no place for sesame seeds there. Tourism related businessmen expect this trend to continue tomorrow as well. Meanwhile, the authorities of the star hotel Ocean Paradise Limited in the tourism zone are organizing a three-day Baisakhi fair on the occasion of the first Baisakhi. Various stalls of the Baisakhi fair are being set up in the parking area, Nagardola, and lobby. The hotel and its surroundings have been decorated in Baisakhi decorations. There are various events including cultural programs by the water song artist group for entertainment. Abul Kashem Sikder, president of the Cox's Bazar Hotel-Guest House Owners' Association, said, "This year, the heat has been intense since the middle of Ramadan. As a result, Cox's Bazar was empty of tourists compared to other Ramadans. Moreover, there was no much noise in the first two days of the Eid holiday. As a result, there was a standstill in hotels, motels, restaurants and tourist-dependent businesses. But since Eid, the number of people in the tourist area has increased. People are on the beach despite the heat. It seems that this trend will continue for two more days." Rashedul Islam Dalim, general secretary of the Cox's Bazar Restaurant Owners' Association, said, "After Ramadan, the city's residential and dining rooms are cleaned and sanitized to welcome tourists. Small traders and hawkers also make preparations. Everyone's prior preparations were worth mentioning, hoping for a noisy environment along the beach, which had been in a quiet and quiet state for a month and a half. But even though the previous hopes were not fulfilled, a significant number of tourists came to Cox's Bazar sea beach on Friday. 
Tour Operators Association of Cox's Bazar (TUAC) President Tofail Ahmed said, "There are more than 500 hotels, motels, guest houses and resorts in Cox's Bazar that can accommodate about 150,000 tourists. 80-90 percent of the rooms were booked for April 12-13 before the end of Ramadan. Despite the continuous closure, I expect there to be a little more pressure on these two days. However, it is expected that the tourist presence will be fair on Pahela Baishakh as well. In total, several lakh tourists may come in these three days."

Headline_English: Sadarghat accident: 5 people including launch master remanded for three days
Content_Enlish:
A court has granted three-day remand to five people arrested in connection with the death of five passengers, including three from the same family, after a rope snapped off a launch named MV Tashrif-4 in the capital's Sadarghat. On Friday (April 12), Judge Arifa Chowdhury Himel granted three-day remand when the Dhaka Chief Judicial Magistrate applied for a 10-day remand. The lawyers for the accused also applied for bail. The five people taken on remand are - Farhan-6 launch master Abdur Rouf Howlader (54), second master Selim Howlader (54), manager Faruk Khan (70) and Tasrif-4 launch master Mizanur Rahman (48) and second master Moniruzzaman (28). Two launches named MV Tashrif-4 and MV Pubali-1 were tied to pontoon number 11 in Sadarghat in the afternoon of Eid. Shortly before 3 pm, another launch named Farhan tried to enter the pontoon between these two launches. At that time, the rope of MV Tashrif was torn and hit five passengers waiting to board the launch on the pontoon. They fell into the pontoon and were seriously injured. Later, when they were taken to the hospital, the doctors declared them dead. 

Among the deceased were three people from a family. They are - Md. Belal (30), his wife Mukta (24) and their 4-year-old daughter Maisha from Mathbaria, Pirojpur. Belal worked in a garment factory in Gazipur. He lived there with his wife and daughter. He was returning to his village home for Eid holidays. The other two deceased are Rabiul (19) from Thakurgaon and Ripon Hawlader (38) from Patuakhali.

Headline_English: New travel guidelines for 3 upazilas of Bandarban
Content_Enlish:
During the joint forces' anti-terror operation in three upazilas of Bandarban (Ruma, Thanchi and Rowangchhari), any kind of travel to tourist centers in those areas has been discouraged. Deputy Commissioner Shah Mojahid Uddin told reporters on Friday (April 12) afternoon. The joint forces are conducting this operation against the armed organization KNF in Bandarban in connection with bank robberies, weapons and money looting. The Deputy Commissioner said that tourists have been discouraged from traveling to all tourist spots in the areas of the district where the joint forces' anti-terror operation is ongoing or will continue. Meanwhile, the Ruma Upazila administration has also issued instructions in this regard to tourist guides, transport owners and hotel-motel owners' associations. 

It said that during the joint forces' operation, any kind of tourist travel to tourist areas in Ruma Upazila has been discouraged. In addition to discouraging travel, those involved in tourism have been instructed to follow four things. 

Land survey and census have not been conducted in the three hill districts of Rangamati, Khagrachari and Bandarban in 24 years. 

The instructions signed by Ruma Upazila Executive Officer (Acting) Mohammad Didarul Alam are as follows: During the joint force operation, no hotel or motel will be allowed to rent rooms to tourists. No tourist guide will be allowed to take tourists to any tourist center. No jeep will be allowed to take tourists to any tourist center and no tourists will be allowed to be taken to any tourist center by water. 

On April 2 and 3, there were robberies at Sonali and Krishi Banks in Ruma and Thanchi, kidnapping of the bank manager, looting of money and snatching of 14 weapons from the police and Ansar. Although the bank manager was later rescued, the looted weapons and money could not be recovered. Law enforcement agencies have said that the armed organization KNF carried out this terrorist incident. Army, BGB, RAB, police and Ansar members are participating in the operation to arrest the terrorists and recover weapons and money. The army is coordinating the operation.

Headline_English: Ukrainian attack on Russian-controlled city, 16 killed
Content_Enlish:
Ukraine has attacked the Russian-controlled region of Zaporizhia in southern Ukraine. At least 16 people have been killed, a pro-Russian official in the region said on Sunday (April 14). Reuters reports. At least 20 more people were injured in shelling by Ukrainian troops in the town of Tokmak, pro-Russian official Yevgeny Balitsky said. The attack took place on Friday afternoon. Twelve of the injured are in critical condition. 
Earlier, another local pro-Russian official, Vladimir Rogov, said on Telegram that five houses had been partially destroyed in the shelling. Reuters could not independently verify the claims of pro-Russian officials. There was no comment from Ukraine either. Zaporizhia is one of four regions that Russia claims as its territory after an all-out offensive in Ukraine in 2022. However, Russia has not yet taken full control of these areas.

Headline_English: An attack on Salman's house was planned in America
Content_Enlish: One after another, sensational information is coming to light in the incident of firing at Salman Khan's house. It is learnt that the plan of this attack was hatched in faraway America. According to a report by NDTV, this is what the Mumbai Police has come to know after investigating the incident. Not only that, but according to police sources, the plan to attack the megastar's house was hatched for about a month. Meanwhile, the Crime Branch of Mumbai Police has taken over the investigation of the incident. According to police sources, the motorbike on which the miscreants came and opened fire is registered in Panvel, Maharashtra. Salman Khan's farmhouse is also in Panvel. According to sources, the police are collecting information about the owner of the motorbike. The police suspect that it may have been stolen. After firing, the miscreants abandoned the motorbike near Mount Mary Church and fled. Police suspect that they may have gone outside Mumbai city. Based on the statement of the security guards of the actor's house, the Bandra police have registered a case of attempt to murder against unidentified miscreants and started the investigation. This time, the investigation into the incident has been handed over to the Crime Branch of the Mumbai Police. Meanwhile, Anmol Bishnoi, brother of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi, has admitted responsibility for the incident by posting a threat to Salman on social media. The IP address of the Facebook page that took responsibility was found in Canada. It is learnt that the police are investigating whether a VPN was used to make the Facebook post. After the incident, Maharashtra Chief Minister Eknath Shinde spoke to Salman Khan over the phone. Salman has been given Y category police security. He also has a personal gun license. However, after this incident, the Maharashtra Chief Minister has spoken to the police officials about strengthening Salman's security.
