Headline_English: What Argentina coach Scaloni said about Di Maria's death threats
Content_Enlish:
Benfica's Argentine star Angel Di Maria announced last week that he wants to play the last game of his career at his boyhood club Rosario Central. At the same time, he called for peace to be restored in Rosario, which is notorious for drug-related violence. The Argentine World Cup winner has since received death threats. 

Di Maria is currently in the United States with the Argentina team for a friendly match against Costa Rica. He heard the death threat while he was there. It's hard to believe that someone in the family will be killed if Di Maria returns to Rosario. 
Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni 
Argentina coach Lionel ScaloniAFP 
So how is Di Maria feeling now? Asked at a pre-match press conference whether he was fit to play in the friendly against Costa Rica at 8:50 am Bangladesh time tomorrow, Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said Di Maria was fine and would be in the starting XI against Costa Rica. 

Scaloni said, "I spoke to him. He will play tomorrow. He will be in the starting XI. So nothing has changed for this match. He is calm. As far as I can see, he is fine and he knows that he will have all the support we need." 

Scaloni believes that it would be better for Di Maria to keep busy with his love life in such a desperate moment, "The most important thing is that he plays. That will keep him a little bit more stable."

Headline_English: British-Bangladeshi Aki Rahman conquers Everest in 14 dangerous mountain expeditions
Content_Enlish:
Aki Rahman, the first British-Bangladeshi Everest winner, has embarked on a new expedition to climb the world's 14 most dangerous mountains. Through this expedition, he wants to raise a fund of 1.5 million pounds. The money collected from the fund will be spent on the welfare of oppressed and helpless people in various countries, including Gaza, Palestine. 

Aki Rahman will start the mountain expedition from April 15. This long expedition to climb 14 mountains consecutively will end in October next year. If this expedition is successful, he will become the 52nd person in the world to reach the milestone of climbing the 14 highest mountain peaks. 

Aki Rahman is the first British-Bangladeshi to conquer Mount Everest, the world's highest mountain peak, in 2022. He completed this daring expedition in just 21 hours. His expedition was widely discussed in the UK. This time, the UK-based international humanitarian aid organization UK Islamic Mission (UKIM) will assist in this expedition. 

Aki Rahman wants to complete the difficult expedition to climb 14 mountains in four stages. The first phase includes Kanchenjunga, Mount Everest, Lhotse and Makalu. He will climb the peaks of these mountains from April to June this year. The second phase includes Pakistan's Nanga Parbat, Gasbrum One, Gasbrum Two and K2 and China's Broad Peak from June to August. The third phase will include Nepal's Annapurna, China and Nepal's Chu Yu, China's Shishapagma from April to June next year, and Nepal's Manachlu and Dhaulagiri from Nepal in the fourth phase in September-October. 

Aki Rahman wants to complete the difficult expedition of climbing 14 mountains in 4 stages 
Aki Rahman will spend the money collected from the mountain expedition for the welfare of the endangered and helpless people of Gaza, Palestine, the UK's 'Community Wellbeing' project, the 'Children and Orphan' project, as well as the Islamic Mission in Africa, Syria, Morocco, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Afghanistan through UKIM. 

Aki Rahman's home is in Baudharan village in Jagannathpur upazila of Sylhet. He migrated to the UK with his family at the age of one and a half. He spent his childhood in the city of Oldham. 

The father of three children, this mountaineer has previously gained experience in climbing several small and large mountain peaks. In July 2020, he achieved his first success by conquering Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Tanzania. Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest single mountain in the world. After that, he conquered Mont Blanc, the highest mountain in France at 4,810 meters. 

In October 2020, he took on the challenge of conquering in 24 hours and reached the summit of Mount Elbrus (height 5642 meters), the highest mountain in Russia and Europe, in just 8 hours. He also conquered Karbadino-Balkaria, Russia. Then in 2021, he conquered the world's hardest mountain, the Himalayan Amada Blam, located in Nepal, which has a height of 6856 meters.

Headline_English: City Bank's record profit of Tk 638 crore last year
Content_Enlish:
Private sector City Bank made a record profit of Tk 638 crore in 2023. At the end of last year, the bank made this after-tax profit, which is 33.5 percent more than the previous year. City Bank's after-tax profit in 2022 was Tk 478 crore. This information was revealed in the last year's financial report finalized at the bank's board of directors meeting today, Wednesday. 

Due to the record profit, the bank's earnings per share or EPS also increased. City Bank's EPS stood at Tk 5.21 paisa at the end of last year; which was Tk 3.90 paisa in 2022. 

This information was given in a notice sent by the bank today after the board of directors meeting. The notice said that the consolidated annual financial report for 2023 was finalized at the meeting. Based on that report, the bank has declared a 25 percent dividend for investors. Of this, 15 percent is cash and 10 percent is bonus dividend. The dividend announced will be distributed after approval at the bank's annual general meeting (AGM) to be held on May 30. 

In the notice, City Bank said that in 2023, the bank's income from foreign exchange transactions or foreign exchange decreased by 74 percent compared to the previous year due to the dollar crisis. Despite this, the bank made a record profit. The major reasons behind this profit were the bank's decrease in deposit costs, growth in good loans, profit from loans and increase in profit from government treasury bills or bonds. Last year, City Bank made an operating profit of Tk 1,391 crore. In 2022, the operating profit was Tk 1,237 crore. 

City Bank said that two notable aspects of the bank's income are that 26 percent of its total income came from various types of fees and commissions. And 40 percent of the income came from the personal sector, which includes retail, cards and microfinance. 

City Bank said that last year, the bank reserved a total provision of Tk 256 crore against the loans it disbursed.

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia's sentence suspended for six months, will not be able to travel abroad
Content_Enlish:
The government has extended the release period of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia by six months by suspending her sentence on two conditions (not being able to travel abroad and receiving treatment in Dhaka) as before. The Home Ministry has issued a notification in this regard after receiving the opinion of the Law Ministry. 

According to the notification issued on March 21, Khaleda Zia's sentence will be suspended for the next six months from March 25. 

Khaleda Zia, who was convicted in two corruption cases, was imprisoned on February 8, 2018. The former prime minister was imprisoned for more than two years. 

The government suspended the sentence of former prime minister Khaleda Zia, who was convicted in the Zia Orphanage Trust and Zia Charitable Trust corruption cases, on March 25, 2020. After that, the government has been extending her release period by suspending her sentence on six consecutive applications.

Headline_English: Bloody body of young woman found in under-construction building in Rajshahi, 3 arrested including brother-in-law
Content_Enlish:
The bloody body of a young woman named Sandhya Rani (20) was found in a house under construction in Gogram area of ​​Godagari upazila of Rajshahi. On Wednesday morning, local people came to know about the body and informed the police. Later, the police went and surrounded the body. The body remained there until noon. Later, the body was recovered after the police's Criminal Investigation Department (CID) personnel went there. The police have arrested three people, including the stepbrother and sister-in-law of the deceased girl in this incident. 

The deceased Sandhya Rani is the daughter of Harilal of Shisha Banshpir village of Sundarganj upazila of Gaibandha. She lived in the house of her stepbrother Phulbaboo Rabidas alias Babu (22) in Karnahar police station area of ​​Rajshahi. In this incident, the police have arrested Babu, his wife Minti Rani (19) and a young man named Adil Ahmed (19) in this incident. Adil is the son of Awal Hossain of Lalpukur village of Godagari. 

Police said that they went to the house under construction in Gogram area of ​​Godagari around 9 am today after receiving information from locals. The CID team recovered the body from the second floor of the house and collected evidence. The police could not identify the girl till noon. During the search, stab marks were found on the girl's stomach and neck. The CID found a mobile phone in the deceased girl's hand. Later, her identity was identified based on the mobile phone. 

Police sources said that after investigating, the police came to know that Sandhya Rani lived in the house of her stepbrother Phulbaboo in the Karnahar police station area. There was a dispute between them over a matter. They planned to kill Sandhya. In continuation of this, Sandhya was taken to the spot at around 9 pm on Tuesday with the help of Phulbaboo's friend Adil after giving her sleeping pills. Later, she was taken to the second floor of the under-construction building and stabbed to death. Three people were arrested in the afternoon on charges of involvement in the incident. The knife used in the murder was seized from the place shown by the accused Adil. 

The police questioned the accused after arresting them. A police source said that Adil, along with members of the family, worked in a company in Dhaka. Sandhya Rani liked a boy there. The relatives, including the stepbrother, did not take it well. They committed a crime there. Recently, the family arranged for Sandhya Rani to marry someone her stepbrother knew. But Sandhya Rani did not agree to the marriage. She threatened her relatives that if she got married elsewhere, she would tell the police about the incident in Dhaka. Then the relatives got worried and planned to kill her. 

The police source said that the accused bought a cutter from a hardware store in the city's Hargram area and a knife from another store for 65 taka. Later, they rented a battery-powered auto-rickshaw and went to Godagari. Adil is familiar with the Gogram area. On his advice, they brought him to an under-construction building and fed him sleeping pills along with food. Later, the three of them killed him. Police seized the knife used in the murder from a drain three kilometers away from the scene. 

Abdul Matin, officer-in-charge of Godagari Model Police Station, told Prothom Alo that there was a secret crime between them, which the deceased Sandhya wanted to reveal. The murder was committed out of fear that the accused might be harmed if the incident is revealed. They are investigating the matter. He said that the plaintiff in the case could not be found after the incident. They inquired at Sundarganj Police Station and found out that the father of the deceased girl had also fled out of fear. Now the police are preparing to file a case as the plaintiff. The body is kept in the Rajshahi Medical College morgue. 

Rajshahi Additional Superintendent of Police (DSB) and media spokesperson Rafiqul Alam said, "This is a sensational murder. It was completely clueless. The police were able to bring the people involved in the murder to justice in a short time."

Headline_English: Biden overtakes Trump in popularity
Content_Enlish:
US President Joe Biden has received some big good news. Seven months before the country's presidential election, Biden is catching up with rival Donald Trump in several 'battleground' states or swing states. Biden received this good news in a survey conducted by the American research institute Morning Consult and the media Bloomberg News on Tuesday. If various surveys conducted before an election show that neither of the two parties is a clear favorite in a state, then that state is identified as a swing state. Meanwhile, a top leader of the Democratic party said, 'Biden's sudden shock' regarding the news of Biden's lead. 

According to the survey data, Biden was behind Trump in the state of Wisconsin four months ago. He is now ahead by one point there. The two have the same points in Pennsylvania. Last month, Trump was ahead by six points here. The two have the same points in Michigan. 

The fate of the two will be determined by the votes in other states in the US presidential election next November. Among them, Trump was ahead in Arizona, Georgia, Nevada and North Carolina. But among them, Trump is now ahead only in Georgia. 

Biden campaigned in North Carolina on Tuesday. Meanwhile, although he is behind Biden in raising campaign funds, no date has been set for Trump's campaign. 

Meanwhile, Trump appeared in court in New York last Monday. There, he was heard in two cases. One of them is a criminal case, the other is a fraud case. Earlier, in 2016, he was accused of bribing a porn star to silence him on the eve of the presidential election. However, Trump has denied all 34 charges brought against him. The former president argues that the charges against him do not amount to a crime. His trial in that case will begin on April 15. Judge Juan Marchán set this date on Monday, rejecting the defense's request for time. There are four criminal cases against Trump. But this is probably the only case the presumptive Republican nominee will have to appear in court before the November presidential election. 

On the same day, another New York court reduced Trump's bond from $464 million to $175 million at the last minute in a fraud case. He has 10 days to post the bond. 

Trump faces 14 criminal charges related to election insurrection and 40 felony charges for withholding confidential information. Trump has also posted a $92 million bond in rape and defamation cases. 

On Monday, a Biden campaign spokesman described Trump as "weak and desperate" as a person and as a presidential candidate. He said Trump's campaign cannot raise campaign funds. Trump is not interested in campaigning outside his country club. Every time he speaks, he alienates moderate and suburban voters from his dangerous agenda. 

The Biden campaign did not comment on the Bloomberg and Morning Consult polls. 

Trump campaign spokesman Jason Miller said Trump is leading 47 to 43 percent in seven swing states. Repeated polls have shown voters are uncomfortable with Biden's policies on crushing inflation, leaving loopholes in southern border management and destroying industries like electric cars. 

Biden may have been counting on Trump's rival Nikki Haley in the Republican primary. Democrats thought Haley, who has been vocal about her opposition to Trump, would not support Trump. But that hope has been dashed. Voters who had a positive view of Nikki Haley may now lean toward Trump. But Nikki Haley has changed her mind. Nikki, who challenged Trump to the end, has said she will support Trump in the November election. 

The positive side for Biden is the country's improving economic situation. In addition, Biden recently announced his fight with Trump in his State of the Union address. Earlier this month, Biden referred to former US President Donald Trump as a threat to democracy in his speech. Without directly mentioning Trump by name, Biden alleged that Trump and his Republican Party supporters tried to change American history on January 6, 2021. After Biden's victory in the 2020 presidential election, Trump supporters attacked and vandalized the US Capitol building. 

Democratic strategist and political commentator Simon Rosenberg said that the election is now clearly changing and moving towards Biden. Biden has been shown to be ahead in 10 recent national polls. He is now ahead in the Economist poll. Biden has been shown to be moving forward in the Harris poll. Now the Bloomberg and Morning Consult polls have also shown Biden moving forward. Biden's push now seems real. 

More than half of Biden voters surveyed by Bloomberg and Morning Consult said they were confident in preventing Trump from becoming president. Eli Yokley, a US political analyst at Morning Consult, said that negative energy motivates people. During the 2020 election campaign, a negative energy powered Biden's campaign. Those who are supporting Biden today are the ones who expressed that negative energy.

Headline_English: Calls for immediate arms embargo against Israel
Content_Enlish:
A UN expert has said that he believes Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. For this reason, he has called on UN member states to quickly impose arms and other sanctions on Israel. He made these remarks at the UN Human Rights Commission in Geneva on Tuesday. 

Francesca Albanese, the UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights in the Occupied Territories, presented a report titled ‘The Anatomy of a Genocide’ at the UN Human Rights Commission. She said, ‘My responsibility is to report on the worst human conditions and present the findings. I have seen that the threshold of the crime of genocide has been met against the Palestinians as a group in Gaza.’ 

Albanese calls for an arms embargo on Israel, saying, ‘I call on member states to abide by their obligations. This will start with imposing arms and other sanctions on Israel. This is necessary to prevent such incidents from happening again in the future. 

Meanwhile, Israel has rejected Francesca's report. However, countries such as Qatar, Algeria, and Mauritania have supported it. 

At the same time, pressure is increasing on Israel to allow humanitarian aid to enter Gaza quickly. On Tuesday, German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock called on international organizations to provide relief aid to Gaza quickly. US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin said that protecting Palestinian civilians is morally and strategically imperative. 

The UN Security Council passed a resolution on Monday calling for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. Since then, relations between US President Joe Biden and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have reached a low point. 

Israel has been threatening to attack Rafah in Gaza for some time. However, the US has objected to this. A high-level Israeli delegation was scheduled to visit Washington this week to discuss this. However, Netanyahu canceled the trip after the United States abstained from a Security Council vote calling for a ceasefire in Gaza. US Secretary of State Antony Blinken said that an Israeli attack on Rafah City would further complicate the situation. 

The resolution passed by the Security Council called for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. At the same time, it demanded the immediate and unconditional release of hostages held by the Hamas ruling group in Gaza. 

Despite the passage of the ceasefire resolution, Israel did not stop its attacks on Gaza. Israel continued its bombardment of Gaza and Rafah City on Wednesday. The Gaza Health Ministry said yesterday that Israeli forces had killed 76 Palestinians in the past 24 hours. The number of deaths in Israeli attacks since October 7 has reached 32,490. In addition, 74,889 people have been injured.

Headline_English: Ministry's new guidelines to prevent anesthesia-related accidents
Content_Enlish:
In the context of the recent deaths and sudden complications of some patients due to anesthesia, the Health Services Department has issued some instructions. To avoid such complications in the future and to ensure the quality of the drugs used in anesthesia, it has been asked to use halogen in anesthesia. 

These instructions were given in a notification signed by Jasim Uddin Haider, Joint Secretary of the Health Services Department of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on Wednesday. 

The instructions of the Health Services Department include—1. Isoflurane/sevoflurane (anesthetic drugs) should be used instead of halothane (anesthetic drugs) as inhalation anesthetic (anesthetic drugs that are inhaled) in operation theaters in all government and private hospitals across the country. 

2. The total number of halothane/isoflurane/sevoflurane vaporizers in all government and private hospitals across the country and the financial allocation required to replace the existing halothane vaporizers with isoflurane/sevoflurane vaporizers should be estimated. 

3. Necessary measures should be taken to prevent the purchase, sale and use of halogens without the approval of DGDA. 

4. Necessary measures should be taken to ensure that all anesthesiologists (government/private) across the country comply with the instructions regarding the use of isoflurane instead of halothane. 

5. Measures should be taken as per the demand to replace the existing halothane vaporizers with isoflurane vaporizers from all government healthcare institutions. 

6. In the case of purchasing new anesthesia machines, the inclusion of isoflurane/sevoflurane vaporizers should be clearly ensured in the specification.

Headline_English: No ban on peaceful events during Ramadan: Dhaka University
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka University authorities have not imposed any ban on organizing peaceful and positive programs during the holy month of Ramadan. This information was given in a press release sent to the media by the university's public relations office on Thursday. 

The press release said that the attention of the Dhaka University authorities has been drawn to the news published in some newspapers recently about the ban on organizing Ramadan programs at Dhaka University. The reports said that the authorities have imposed a ban on organizing programs related to Ramadan discussions at Dhaka University. This is an untrue, misleading and purposeful report. In the interest of maintaining a fair educational environment and peace and order at the university, a circular was recently issued from the Proctor's Office. The word 'ban' on organizing Ramadan programs is not mentioned anywhere in that circular. 

On March 13, some students of the Law Department were attacked by the Chhatra League while conducting a seminar titled 'Productive Ramadan' at the mosque of Bangabandhu Tower, the residential building for employees on the Dhaka University campus. Two days after the incident, on March 15, Proctor Md. Maksudur Rahman sent a letter to all deans, vice-chancellors, chairmen and directors of the university requesting them not to allow such activities to be conducted 'to protect a fair educational environment and avoid unwanted incidents'. The letter went viral on social media on Wednesday. 

The letter sent to all deans, vice-chancellors, chairmen and directors of the university said that recently, some students of the law department gathered at the university's Bangabandhu Tower building without prior permission to organize a seminar titled 'Productive Ramadan'. As a result, an unwanted incident occurred there and some students of the law faculty were injured. The university authorities have informed the state law enforcement agencies about the matter. 

The letter also said that later, some political organizations and politically known individuals are trying to divert the matter to a different sector in order to destabilize the campus. The university authorities have formed a committee to take necessary measures. The committee is working to investigate and take appropriate action in this regard. In such a situation, it is requested not to allow any such activities to be conducted in order to protect the proper environment of education and avoid unwanted incidents. 

A section of the university's former and current students have strongly criticized this letter on social media Facebook, alleging that a ban has been imposed on organizing Ramadan-related programs on the campus. Reports titled 'Ban on organizing Ramadan programs in DU' have also been published in some media outlets. 

In such a context, a university press release said this afternoon that teachers, students, officers and employees of the university have been organizing Iftar Mahfils at different places on the campus every day. Followers of some political organizations have caused one or two unwanted incidents on the Dhaka University campus during the holy month of Ramadan, as a result of which the prevailing norms of the university have been violated and the proper environment of education has been disrupted.

Headline_English: Russia launches massive attack on Ukrainian power plants
Content_Enlish:
Russia has carried out major attacks on dozens of power plants in Ukraine, leaving more than a million people without power. The attacks took place on Thursday night, the Ukrainian presidential office said. 

The Russian attack left 700,000 residents of the Kharkiv region without power. 200,000 residents each in the southern Odessa region and the southeastern Dnipropetrovsk region are without power. In addition, more than 110,000 residents in the central Poltava region are without power, Deputy Head of the Presidential Administration Oleksiy Kuleba said on Friday. 

Meanwhile, one of the two supply lines to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant was damaged in the Russian attack, Ukrainian Energy Minister Zherman Galushchenko said in a Facebook post. 

The Atomic Energy Agency of Ukraine said the situation was very dangerous and could increase the risk of an emergency at any moment. 

The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant is the largest in Europe. Russian troops seized the power plant after the invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. 

The Russian airstrikes overnight knocked out power in seven regions, AFP news agency reported, citing Ukraine's electricity supplier. Many power plants were damaged in the attack. 

"Dozens of power plants were damaged. Seven regions were hit by a blackout," state-owned Ukrenergo said in a post on Telegram. 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had carried out a major attack on Thursday night using 90 missiles of various types and 60 "Iranian-made" drones. 

Zelensky said the world could see as clearly as possible the targets of the Russian terrorists' attacks - power plants, energy supply lines, hydroelectric dams, ordinary residential buildings, and even electric buses. 

The Ukrainian Interior Ministry said at least two people were killed in the attacks. 14 were injured. Three others are missing. 

After the attack, the Ukrainian president again called on Western countries to supply weapons. He said, “As much as arms aid is delaying the arrival of our country, Russian missiles are not delaying it as much.” 

Zelensky said, “We need air defense systems to protect people, facilities, houses and dams. Our partners know exactly what we need. They can definitely help us. We must save lives from these inhumane people from Moscow.” 

Earlier, Russia also carried out a major attack on the capital Kiev on Wednesday night. The Ukrainian armed forces claimed to have shot down 31 missiles that day. It was also reported that some people were injured by the debris of the downed missiles.

Headline_English: Enrique jokes about whether to rest Mbappe against Barcelona
Content_Enlish:
No official announcement has been made. However, Kylian Mbappe is almost certain to leave PSG at the end of the season. Among them, several European media outlets, including Spanish media outlet Marca, have also brought forward detailed information about Mbappe's contract with Real Madrid. Rumors are that everything has been done except for signing the contract. Even the behavior of PSG and coach Luis Enrique towards Mbappe has changed a lot. 

The French star did not get the opportunity to play 90 minutes in four consecutive matches in Ligue 1. Mbappe, upset by the club's behavior, spoke to coach Enrique. The PSG coach also had to talk to the media about the matter. He said that his team wants to get used to playing without Mbappe with an eye on the future. 

Although Enrique took the risk of not playing Mbappe in the domestic league, he did not go that way in the Champions League. The World Cup-winning star played the full 90 minutes in the second leg of the last sixteen against Real Sociedad. PSG won 2-1 in the last eight with his double. Earlier, a goal came from Mbappe in the first leg, which also won 2-0. 

Now PSG will play against Barcelona in the last eight. Mbappe is PSG's biggest hope in this important match. Although there is an opportunity to take the risk of not playing the forward full-time in the league and getting the team used to it, something like this can be suicidal in the Champions League. PSG coach Enrique is not unaware of that. However, while talking on his Twitch (video live-streaming service) channel, the Spanish coach made a joke about resting Mbappe against Barca. 

PSG coach Luis Enrique 
PSG coach Luis EnriquePSG website 
Former Barcelona coach Enrique recently launched the Jana Foundation, a charity named after his late daughter. Jana died of cancer at the age of 9. After the charity was launched, the PSG coach spoke about it on his Twitch channel. 

A follower jokingly asked, "If I get how many subscribers, will Enrique play Mbappe as a center back against Barca?" Enrique did not avoid the question and answered it quite jokingly. He said, "No subscribers. Donate 4 or 5 million euros to this charity (Jana Foundation), I can also give Kylian (Mbappe) a rest. Send me your receipt." 

Even though he joked on Twitch, Mbappe will be Enrique's trump card against Barca. This is also the last chance for Mbappe to bring PSG the Champions League title before leaving. If Mbappe can win this much-loved title for PSG, the French star will have the opportunity to leave the Parisian club as a hero.

Headline_English: Cannes Film Festival: The first movie to premiere announced
Content_Enlish:
The 77th Cannes Film Festival is knocking on the door. The submission period for this important festival has already ended. Now we wait for the nominations to be announced. Before that, the official site of Cannes announced the premiere of a film yesterday. 

The film 'Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga' is going to premiere at the Cannes Film Festival. It will be screened in the Out of Competition section of the festival on May 15. The film of the 'Mad Max' franchise was directed by George Miller. It stars Anna Taylor-Joy and Chris Hemsworth. The prequel of the film is being released after 9 years. 

A scene during the shooting of the film 'Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga'. Photo: From the official site of the Cannes Festival 
A scene during the shooting of the film 'Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga'. Photo: From the official website of the Cannes Film Festival 
Miller told Variety, “The idea for this prequel goes back over a decade. The film is going to premiere in Cannes, and to be back in Cannes again is an exciting thing. The Cannes premiere of “Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga” is the best place to share the experience of the film with audiences around the world.” 

Miller has served as a judge at the Cannes Film Festival twice before, once as a member and once as jury president. The 77th Cannes Film Festival will run from May 14-25. The deadline for submissions to Cannes was March 15. The names of the films nominated in various categories will be announced on April 11.

Headline_English: Gavaskar is impressed with the way Ruturaj has used Mustafizur Rahman
Content_Enlish:
Chennai Super Kings' new captain Ruturaj Gaekwad has been praised by Indian legend Sunil Gavaskar. Chennai won the opening match of the IPL against Royal Challengers Bangalore by 6 wickets with 8 balls in hand yesterday. Gavaskar was impressed by the way Chennai captain Ruturaj used the bowlers in this match. He especially remembered the way Ruturaj used Bangladesh pacer Mustafizur Rahman. 

Mustafiz's debut for Chennai yesterday was also excellent. His bowling figures are 4–0–29–4. However, if you have not watched the match, it is not possible to understand Mustafiz's devastation well by looking at his bowling figures alone. He took 2 wickets for 4 runs in his first over. Then he took 2 more wickets for 3 runs in his second over. After that, Mustafiz bowled 2 more overs but did not get a wicket. He took these 4 wickets in his first 10 balls. And look at the wickets too—Faf du Plessis, Rajat Patidar, Virat Kohli and Cameron Green. 

Chennai announced Ruturaj as the new captain in place of Mahendra Singh Dhoni the day before the start of the IPL. Ruturaj repaid the trust in his first match as the captain of the franchise team. Listening to Gavaskar's words to TV channel Star Sports, it seems like this, 'The thing that catches his (Ruturaj) eye is the change of bowling. The way he has bowled Mustafizur, the way he has used him; that is extraordinary.' 

Chennai captain Ruturaj Gaekwad 
Chennai captain Ruturaj GaekwadChennai Super Kings 
After winning the toss, Bengaluru batted first and scored 37 runs for no wickets in 4 overs. In the fifth over, Ruturaj brought Mustafiz and removed du Plessis and Patidar. After 6 overs, Ruturaj brought Mustafiz back to bowling.

Headline_English: Meta starts moderating political content on Instagram and Threads
Content_Enlish:
Meta has started a process to limit the display of political content on its Instagram and Threads apps if users are not interested. The company has taken this initiative to prevent the spread of rumors and false information using social media during elections in various countries. Under this new initiative, ‘Limit’ has been automatically selected in the political content control option for several users of Instagram and the Threads app operated by Instagram. 

According to Instagram, if ‘Limit’ is selected in the political content option, no political content will be recommended on Instagram’s Explore, Feed and Reels. However, users will be able to see political content posted by accounts they follow. 
Last month, Instagram head Adam Mosseri said that our goal is to respect users’ opinions about viewing political content. And therefore, Instagram and Threads will not recommend viewing political content if users are not interested. 

It is worth noting that an option called ‘Political Content’ can be seen along with content on various topics when entering the content preferences from the settings of Instagram and Threads. There are two options, Limit and Don't Limit. Users can control the display of political content on their accounts by enabling the Limit option.

Headline_English: BNP leader Aman released on bail
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka Metropolitan North BNP convener Amanullah Aman has been released on bail. He was released from the prison cell of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) in the capital at 9 pm on Sunday. BNP Chairperson's Media Cell member Shairul Kabir Khan confirmed this information to Prothom Alo. 

The Appellate Division granted bail to Amanullah Aman, who was sentenced to 13 years in prison in the case of concealing information about assets and acquiring assets disproportionate to his known income, on March 20. 

The trial court sentenced him to 13 years in prison in that case. The High Court delivered its verdict on May 30 last year on a re-hearing of Amanullah Aman's appeal against that verdict. The verdict upheld the trial court's sentence. Amanullah Aman was ordered to surrender to the relevant court within 15 days of the trial court receiving a copy of the verdict. 

The full verdict of the High Court was published on August 7 last year. Amanullah Aman was sent to prison by a Dhaka special judge's court after his surrender on September 10 last year. He has been in prison for more than six months since then.

Headline_English: Amir wants to come out of retirement and play for Pakistan team
Content_Enlish:
Mohammad Amir retired from international cricket in 2020, accusing the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and its coaching staff of 'mental torture'. It was later learned that Amir decided to retire due to a rift with the then PCB chairman Ramiz Raja and coaches Waqar Younis and Misbah-ul-Haq. 

The star Pakistani fast bowler, however, said that if Ramiz, Waqar, and Misbah leave, he will return. They left long ago. But Amir was not announcing his return. At one time, it seemed that he might never play for the national team again. However, Amir finally made the announcement. The 31-year-old pacer wants to play for Pakistan again. 

Today, while announcing his return to the Pakistan team on social media, Amir wrote, 'I still dream of playing for the national team. Life brings us to a crossroads where sometimes we have to reconsider our decisions.’ 

Amir further wrote that he has already spoken to the board about returning to the team, ‘I have had positive discussions with the PCB. They (board officials) have respectfully explained to me that the team needs me and that I still have the ability to play for Pakistan. After discussions with my family and well-wishers, I have taken the decision and announce that I can be considered for playing in the T20 World Cup. I want to do this for the country (come back from retirement). Because, it comes before personal decisions. Playing in the green jersey and serving the country has always been and will be my biggest desire.’ 

Mohammad Amir emerged like a comet in international cricket. He started putting the best batsmen in the world to a tough test with speed and swing. But at a young age, he was banned from all forms of cricket for five years for being involved in the spot-fixing scandal. He also had to serve such a prison sentence. Amir made a great comeback to international cricket after serving the ban. He played a major role in Pakistan winning the ICC Champions Trophy in 2017. Three years later, he retired, disrespecting the board. 

Amir has played 147 matches for Pakistan in three editions. He has taken 259 wickets. 

The T20 World Cup will start on June 1. Before that, Pakistan will play 9 matches against New Zealand and England in this edition. The New Zealand series will start on April 18 at home. Amir can be seen in the Pakistan team again with that series. 

However, PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi has left the matter of Amir playing for Pakistan again to the selectors. He said, 'The selection committee will decide on the future of Mohammad Amir in Pakistan cricket.' 

Ahead of Amir, left-arm spin all-rounder Imad Wasim announced his retirement and return to the Pakistan team tomorrow.

Headline_English: How to reduce dependency on medical treatment in India
Content_Enlish:
Recently, the Governor of Bangladesh Bank said that every year, an amount of money equivalent to five billion dollars (about 60 thousand crore taka) goes abroad in the name of medical treatment. Such a huge amount of money going abroad every year is a huge pressure on the economy of a country like ours. 

In the new political reality of the country, it is time to think about the issue. In addition, it has become difficult to go to India for medical treatment and some hospitals there have announced that they will not treat Bangladeshi patients. 

About 500,000 people go abroad for medical treatment every year, 80 percent of whom go to India. The vast majority of this huge amount of money is spent illegally, through hundi. 

What can we do in such a situation? 60 percent of the country's healthcare comes from the private sector. Two-thirds of the hospital beds, doctors and health workers are from the private sector. And those who go abroad for medical treatment also rely on private hospitals when they seek medical services within the country. 

Now the question is, do we have the necessary capacity to provide medical services to those who go abroad for treatment? Statistical calculations say that on average, about 1,000 patients go abroad for treatment every day. And the number of beds in the country at the private level is about 100,000. Of this, 20,000 are for the tertiary level. So, it can be said that the number of doctors, health workers, and beds that are available is sufficient to provide medical services to patients going to India. 

Patients go abroad first of all for specialized doctors, tests, and proper diagnosis. Currently, Bangladesh has specialized, skilled, and experienced doctors, who are undoubtedly on par with Indian doctors in terms of quality. Our quality of tests is also world-class. There are several institutions including LabAid, Popular, Ibn Sina, from which doctors in India, Thailand, or Singapore accept the test results. They do not ask for a new test. 

Now let's talk about the disease. People usually go abroad for heart disease, cancer, kidney, neuro, orthopedic treatment. All types of heart disease treatment are now done in Bangladesh. There are several integrated cancer treatment centers in the country; LabAid Cancer Hospital, Ahsania Cancer Hospital are notable among them. 

The technologies available in these hospitals, including tumor boards, specialized tests, chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy, and follow-up, are similar to those in the developed world. Then, the quality of kidney, orthopedic, and neuro-related treatment here is similar to that of Indian hospitals. But it is also true that we are a little behind in organ transplantation. The main reason for this is the negative publicity of our media and regulatory obstacles. 

Coming to the issue of cost. Patients go abroad and get treatment at a cost. Therefore, they can easily afford the cost of healthcare in private hospitals in the country. The cost of good centers in India, such as Max, Fortis, Apollo Hospital, is 2 to 3 times the cost of our private hospitals. Thailand's cost is 6 to 7 times and Singapore's medical cost is about 10 times. In addition, the cost of accompanying people, staying, and going back for follow-up - all of these add up to a lot of expenses. In comparison, the cost of private hospitals in the country is much lower; although since there is no allocation for health in the daily expenses, this expense often becomes a cause for annoyance. 

We need to rethink our doctors, health workers, hospitals, and testing centers. Our mentality needs to change. Doctors should see patients more sincerely, give them more time. The counseling part of the hospital should be increased; along with this, we expect patients to trust the doctors and hospitals in the country. 
Let's come to a much-discussed topic. Some reasons are often mentioned behind the low trust of people in the country's doctors, hospitals, and medical system. There is anger among the general public over the use of doctors, giving patients less time to doctors, unnecessary tests, commissions. After a thousand successful treatments, one unsuccessful or misunderstanding is more widely shared. 

On the other hand, we also have many positive events. From 2020 to 2022, no patient could travel abroad for treatment due to Covid. We provided treatment and that successfully. 

After the change of government, many people could not travel to India for four months from August to December this year due to several complications including visa. We have provided treatment for many complex diseases in these four months. We are still providing treatment. We have not received any news that anyone died without treatment due to not being able to travel to India. 

So we think that now is the time. We need to think anew about our doctors, health workers, hospitals, and testing centers. Our mentality needs to change. Doctors should see patients more sincerely, give them more time. The counseling part of the hospital should be increased; along with this, we also expect patients to trust the doctors and hospitals in the country. 

Another important thing is that we need to have our own funds for treatment. If we save 5 to 6 percent of the monthly expenses for treatment, then we will not have to face any sudden accident or medical problems. Along with this, the media should also be careful in publishing reports on medical incidents. On the other hand, doctors should also improve the quality of service by increasing patient care. Only if this happens simultaneously will people's confidence in our medical services increase. 

I can emphasize one thing, it would not be an exaggeration to say that we are in no way inferior to the Indian medical system. There is no more dependence on the Indian medical system. Let us all love our country together. Let us treat those who come for treatment as our own relatives and build a Bangladesh that is self-reliant in healthcare.

Headline_English: Polythene and plastic are coming from Saint Martin...
Content_Enlish:
I left Dhaka for St. Martin's after carefully checking that there was no plastic or polythene in my travel bag. It took me three hours to cover the distance from Fakirapul to Shanir Akhra by bus. Then, I had to stay on the road for another two hours due to a road accident in Chakaria. 

Anyway, I got off the bus at Dolphin More in Cox's Bazar and took an autorickshaw to Nuniachhara Ghat. By then, arrangements were being made to release the ship. A few people were standing at the entrance checking the tickets of the passengers. A man standing next to me was telling the tourists that polythene bags cannot be taken with them. I thought that the tourists must be carrying polythene or plastic out of a sense of responsibility. But the opposite picture was seen as soon as I sat on the deck of the ship. Almost everyone had plastic water bottles in their hands. I wondered, aren't plastic water bottles plastic? 

The journey from Cox's Bazar to St. Martin's is about six hours. Those who didn't take food with them will have to rely on the food on the ship. Khichuri, popcorn, sandwiches, burgers, coffee and ice cream are available. Some food is served in paper bags, but most of the food is served in plastic packets. Coffee is in one-time cups. 

The number of tourists allowed to visit St. Martin has been reduced to 2,000 in December-January this year. Polythene and plastic have been banned on the island. But drinking water is a big problem for tourists there. I have seen many local residents storing rainwater in large tanks in their yards. As a result, there is no alternative to bottled water for tourists. 

Let's assume that if an average person drinks two liters of water a day, at least two water bottles are being collected. Although many are aware of the environment and plastic pollution, many care little. Starting from the beach, plastic bottles are being thrown everywhere. If this problem of drinking water is not solved, the issue of eco-friendly tourism will remain like a gold mine. 

Plastic soft drink bottles are added to drinking water bottles. If the island is to be made plastic-free, soft drinks in plastic bottles must be stopped. Chips and crackers are sold in temporary shops along the beach. Many people throw abandoned packets on the beach after eating chips and crackers. There is no system to remove or recycle this waste from the island. 

More than two hundred resorts and hotels have been built across St. Martin. Electricity has to be provided for the remaining 22 hours, except for a two-hour break. However, almost the only source of electricity supply on the island is a diesel-powered generator. There is a privately owned solar power project. But the cost of electricity per unit is 50 taka. Is it possible for the islanders to use solar power at such a high cost? Electricity is being generated by burning diesel, poisoning the environment. Is there any way out of this without the supply of low-cost renewable energy? 

During the tourist season, 5 to 10 thousand people used to visit every day. Now it has reduced to 2 thousand. As it has become a lucrative tourist destination, the wealthy have rushed to build hotels and resorts there. They have been built by buying the land of the locals. Most of the land on the island is now under their control. I have also seen new resorts being built. However, the sale of land for building construction is legally prohibited there. Many people have built concrete structures. Government institutions are also not lagging behind in this work. 

There are signboards of ownership by purchase on many of the remaining lands of the coral island. I saw a signboard of 15 bighas of land owned by one person on the way to Chheradwip. If influential people from outside continue to buy the land of a small island, where nothing but rice is cultivated on the sandy soil, then it will definitely become a cause of major conflict with the local residents in the future. If this cannot be stopped, the story of protecting the environment of St. Martin will remain a myth. 

There are thousands of dogs on the island. Their food supply has created a big problem. Due to lack of food, they often eat turtle eggs. It is necessary to scientifically verify how logical and suitable it is for the natural balance to have so many dogs on a small island. It is important to remove unnecessary dogs from the island and rehabilitate them. 

Coconuts are known as zingira for their rows of coconut trees. Thousands of coconut trees all over the island. Yet, not a single coconut is seen on the trees. Each coconut costs 250 to 300 taka on the island. Coconuts come from Teknaf. Islanders believe that coconuts are not growing on the trees because of mobile towers. Botanists say that coconuts are not growing on the trees because of white flies and viruses. Yet coconuts are important for the island's economic viability. 

Except for fish, almost everything has to be brought from Teknaf. The number of people on the island is increasing, but employment opportunities are not increasing. Many people no longer want to go into the risky and difficult fishing profession of their predecessors. The economy is boosted when more tourists come. Again, the opportunity for free tourism is bringing destruction to the coral island. Educational opportunities are limited. Most cannot pass the primary school level. Most of those who can, get stuck in SSC. The incidence of going outside the island to engage in other jobs is also relatively low. Due to the limited tourism, anger and frustration are increasing among everyone. If no comprehensive plan can be made for life and livelihood, tourism and environment, then will the plan to save St. Martin's Island be realized? 

On the day of return, I set off towards the ship through the long iconic bridge of the St. Martin's shipyard. Lines of people are walking towards the ship along the wooden bridge. Almost everyone is carrying plastic bags. Some are carrying dried fish in polythene bags. Some are carrying pickles in polythene bags. All this polythene comes to the island from Teknaf. The environmental advisor has banned the entry of polythene and plastic into St. Martin. But how will the polythene and plastic coming from St. Martin be stopped? What could be more ironic than viewing the issue of environmental protection in isolation!

Headline_English: Central Asia is the new stage for the 'Great Game' between China, Russia, and the US
Content_Enlish:
Some thought that the great power rivalry ended in the 20th century. But the war in Ukraine has reborn from the ruins. 

After the immediate heat of the conflict subsided, Central Asia has become one of the stages of great power competition. 

Observers have long been talking about the strategic importance of the region. In the period of post-war normalization that is being talked about, Central Asia is an important center where tensions are growing between Russia, China and the United States over their interests. 

In this great power conflict, Central Asia is different from all other areas of geopolitical competition. Because two of the three superpowers in the world today (China and Russia) have a large border with the countries of the region. As a result, the stakes here are much higher. 

Central Asia, consisting of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan, finds itself at a critical juncture. 

Historically, Central Asia has been a crossroads of empires. Since its independence from the Soviet Union, it has maintained a delicate balance with neighboring major powers. 

However, the lack of a strong and local mechanism for collective security has created a fragility in the region. The geopolitical vacuum created by the fragmented political and economic landscape here has led to an increasing interest of major powers to fill it. 

The lack of a unified regional identity in Central Asia initially seems like a weakness. But it has also brought both challenges and opportunities in the ongoing competition between great powers. 

The interests of the great powers are divergent. For Russia, Central Asia remains an important center of influence. Central Asia is a buffer zone for Russia against threats from the West. It is an important transit route for Moscow. 

Policymakers in Washington, Beijing, and Moscow must understand this dynamic in Central Asia. They must find ways to engage there in constructive ways. It is important not only for the stability and prosperity of Central Asia, but also for the wider Eurasia. 
As the war in Ukraine strains Moscow’s resources, this “near abroad” has become a source of economic activity and an alternative trade route. 

China sees Central Asia as an essential element of its continental connectivity through its Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Central Asia is a vital resource and strategic location for China’s westward expansion. 

US engagement in Central Asia has historically fluctuated. Counterterrorism, promoting democratic governance, and reducing Chinese and Russian influence have shaped US engagement in the region. 
The interests of the three superpowers in Central Asia are not the same. Conflicts among these interests are inevitable. 

The war in Ukraine and China’s growing economic and political influence have weakened Russia’s position in recent years. 

Although the current discussions at the official level between Russia and China are focused on partnership, in the long term, China’s rise in the region has become a source of discomfort for Moscow. On the other hand, the major concern of the United States is that China and Russia are expanding their authoritarian models in the region and that the democratic space in Central Asia is shrinking. 

Issues such as infrastructure projects, security cooperation and even cultural exchanges have become areas for the superpowers to demonstrate their authority. In this situation, a strong regional framework is needed among the Central Asian countries. In its absence, there is a risk that Central Asia will become a stage for the ‘Great Game’ of the superpowers. 

Opportunities are also emerging from these challenges. ‘C5+1’ is such a platform. It is a diplomatic platform between the five Central Asian countries and the United States. 

Here, a flexible policy has been adopted to allow each country to engage with foreign powers according to its needs and interests. 

Whether Central Asia becomes a mere arena for great power competition, or whether the region’s strategic importance in geopolitical terms can be effectively harnessed, will depend on the success of platforms like the C5+1. 

Policymakers in Washington, Beijing, and Moscow must understand this dynamic in Central Asia. They must find ways to engage there in constructive ways. That is important not only for the stability and prosperity of Central Asia, but also for the greater Eurasia. 

Miras Zhayenbayev, head of the Foreign Policy and International Studies Program at the Maksut Narikbayev Institute for Networking and Development in Astana, Kazakhstan 

Taken from Asia Times, briefly translated from English

Headline_English: Will the minimum age for voters be 17?
Content_Enlish:
Professor Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government of Bangladesh, has proposed at a conference organized by the Forum for Bangladesh Studies that the minimum voting age in Bangladesh should be reduced by one year to 17. 

He is in favor of making young people voters sooner. Because the younger they are, the more interested they are in change. Moreover, their own opinions about their own future should be given national importance. He hopes that the Election Commission will definitely recommend such an age. His proposal stems from the desire for qualitative change in Bangladeshi politics. But the re-determination of the minimum voting age has huge legal and political significance. So, let us first look at the legal aspect of the chief advisor's opinion. 

According to our Child Act, 'All persons up to the age of 18 (eighteen) years shall be considered children.' According to the United Nations, 'Any human being under the age of 18 is a child, unless otherwise provided in national law.' According to our Child Policy-2011, children between the ages of 14 and 18 will be considered adolescents. 

According to the prevailing law of the country, if these children are involved in any specific crime, then there is a provision for investigating and investigating those crimes separately and also conducting trials in the children's court. The transitional period that has to be passed from childhood dependence to becoming a self-reliant adult is called adolescence. 

Including 17-year-old children and adolescents in the voter list means recognizing the ability they have acquired to give valuable opinions on matters of state and public importance. If this ability has been acquired at the age of 17, then we must declare it legal to arrange marriages for 17-year-old adolescents. 

However, according to the currently in force Child Marriage Prohibition Act, marriage before the age of 18, which means taking on family responsibilities, is a punishable offense. Now the question is, will the voting age be revised without amending other existing laws of the country related to the age of 18? 

Now let's turn our attention to the political side. Our national database is being updated every day. Birth and death registration is an annual process. As a result, there is less scope for fraud here. However, it is natural to have an estimate that the newly added 17-year-old voters will not vote for the existing major political parties in the country. 

It is important to ensure that a new crisis does not arise around the issue of lowering the voting age (there is already unrest in the bureaucracy over administrative reforms). Otherwise, the election and reform process may be delayed. The political crisis may intensify. 
If the minimum voting age is reduced by one year from 18 and teenagers are allowed to vote, how many new voters will be able to vote in the next election? We do not have any direct information on this. 

However, we can get an idea from how many candidates take part in the SSC or equivalent exams every year. For example, in 2023, more than 2 million candidates participated in the secondary or equivalent examinations. 

To this, another 300,000 students of Qawmi Madrasas can be added (because, about 15 percent of our total youth are now receiving education in the Qawmi system). 

And if we add to this the students who dropped out at the primary and secondary levels (3 and 34 percent respectively), the number will rise to 3.2 million. That means we can assume that if the minimum voting age is raised to 17, about 3.2 million voters will increase in the next election. We can assume that these voters are again evenly distributed across the country. 

Our total parliamentary seats are 300. If 3.2 million new voters are spread across the country, then the number of teenage voters in each seat will increase by a little more than 10.5 thousand. If the national elections are fair, then these teenage voters can be expected to become one of the most decisive factors in the next election. 

It is important to ensure that a new crisis does not arise over issues such as lowering the voting age (there is already unrest in the bureaucracy over administrative reforms). Otherwise, the elections and reform process may be delayed. The political crisis may intensify.

Headline_English: I want to see the ACC as an independent institution.
Content_Enlish:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) Executive Director Dr. Iftekharuzzaman. He is the head of the Anti-Corruption Reform Commission. The commission's report is scheduled to be submitted to the interim government next week. He spoke to Prothom Alo about what is in the report, what the future Anti-Corruption Commission should be like, etc. Interviewed by Prothom Alo Joint Editor Sohrab Hasan 
Prothom Alo: How much progress has been made in the work of the ACC Reform Commission. You are supposed to submit your report by January 7. 
Iftekharuzzaman: The progress of the work must be satisfactory. The work of preparing the draft is underway. Hopefully, we will be able to submit the report by January 6. 

Prothom Alo: How was your experience while working? How much cooperation have you received from the administration? 
Iftekharuzzaman: We must say that our experience is good. We have identified the areas that need to be identified in terms of combating corruption. The desire to establish a corruption-free society has been created through the uprising of students and the public, that was in our thoughts. The institution that will play a regulatory role in stopping corruption is the ACC. We have discussed the ACC with people from different levels. Many have spoken spontaneously. We have also exchanged views outside Dhaka. Everyone has expressed disappointment with the current structure of the ACC. The ACC has not been able to fulfill the state that people want to see it in. They have been run the way the government wants them to be for so long. 
Prothom Alo: What is the difference between your work and other commissions? 
Iftekharuzzaman: We were very different from other commissions. We did not take secretarial facilities from the government. TIB provided this facility. The things that people have said openly about corruption, they might not have said in the government environment. In that case, I would say that we have been able to maintain some distance from the government. 
Prothom Alo: You have talked to former ACC officials. Have you received any information from inside the institution that you did not know before? 
Iftekharuzzaman: We have discussed with former and current ACC officials. We already had an idea about the ACC based on the work of TIB. But while working on the reform commission, we saw that its internal problems were obvious. The disparity between the ACC's own officials and those who came from the outside bureaucracy is very high. The ACC's own officials wanted to do a lot, but they were not successful due to bureaucracy and political interference. 
Prothom Alo: If you say anything about the ACC's legal weaknesses. 
Iftekharuzzaman: I won't say that there are no legal weaknesses at all. But structural weaknesses are the main ones. Our recommendations will also include the issue of legal weaknesses. For example, the tax law, the money laundering law. The tax law has the opportunity to whiten black money, in which case the ACC cannot question it. We have examined these. We have made the necessary recommendations. 

Prothom Alo: While your work was ongoing, the government formed a new ACC and it was under the old law. Were you consulted on this? 
Iftekharuzzaman: This is a very interesting incident. We have been saying from the beginning that the former ACC was not able to fulfill its duties. But the government did not restructure the ACC at that time. They did not investigate the allegations that the ACC had against the former government ministers and Awami League leaders. After August 5, they suddenly moved. They filed cases against many. They also started withdrawing the cases against BNP leaders. They wanted to show their work. Through this, the ACC proved that they were working as subordinates to the ruling party. On the day we were supposed to have a meeting with the ACC, the office bearers resigned under government pressure. As a result, the meeting did not take place. Everyone said that the ACC's investigations should continue. After the resignations, the formation of a new commission became mandatory. Without a commission, there would be no investigation or inquiry. The commissioners were appointed based on political considerations. The way we thought about appointing commissioners no longer existed. This worried us. We asked the search committee about the process by which they were appointed. They even gave us time to talk. But they could not keep it.
Prothom Alo: That is, there was no meeting. What did you do after that? 
Iftekharuzzaman: We met with the chief advisor and said that the criteria for ACC appointments should be correct. The chief advisor said that the matter is with the cabinet. Even then, he said that he would look into it. Currently, the ACC has a commission of three, including the chairman. We said that the number should be increased. In terms of the scope or depth of work, three commissioners are not enough. We said that the tradition of taking people from the administration to head the commission should be broken. There should be representation from other prestigious professions. We think that the commission that has been formed is interim. Hopefully, a new commission will be formed after receiving our recommendations. If those who are currently there can show their qualifications and skills and stay, then the number of the commission should be increased. 
Prothom Alo: A kind of tone of disappointment is being observed in your speeches and statements at meetings. 
Iftekharuzzaman: I wouldn't exactly say disappointment. There is apprehension. Those who were in power in Bangladesh for the past 53 years did not try to build state institutions. Rather, they destroyed them through partyization and politicization. A possibility was created through the July-August mass uprising. The question is whether we can sustain it or not. The interim government has taken up the task of institutional reform. That is why I am optimistic, but there is a debate about how the reform will be done, before or after the elections. I think a compromise is needed in this regard. 
Prothom Alo: How do ACC or similar institutions work in other countries? 
Iftekharuzzaman: In other countries, these institutions work completely free from political and party influence. They are employed by the government but not controlled. The government has to be accountable to the institution. And they cannot even think of holding the government accountable here. But that has to be done if corruption is to be controlled. 

Prothom Alo: A former chairman of the ACC called the institution a toothless tiger. Have you been able to set teeth? 
Iftekharuzzaman: First of all, we talked about bringing transparency and accountability in the appointment process. We talked about appointing those who can perform their duties free from all kinds of influence, those who have a good image among the people. An institution that was toothless for 20 years will not become toothless overnight. However, the process has to be started. We wanted to do that. In addition, we talked about bringing about changes in the internal management of the ACC. Corruption cannot be tolerated in an institution whose responsibility is to fight corruption. The ACC must be freed from the hands of corrupt people. 
Prothom Alo: The new ACC Chairman Abdul Momen has made his assets public after taking office. Do you think this is positive? 
Iftekharuzzaman: It is positive. We said that the assets of the ACC commissioners should be submitted to the Reform Commission and made public. The Chairman has done that. The other commissioners have not done it yet. I hope they will do it too. Secondly, the account must be updated every year. And we have also said to check whether the asset account is correct or not. The asset statement of every employee from the top to the bottom of the ACC must be published regularly. We want to see the ACC as a completely independent institution. Currently, there is no accountability for the ACC. 
Prothom Alo: A looting economy has been going on in Bangladesh for a long time. How effective can the ACC be while maintaining this? 
Iftekharuzzaman: A looting economy is part of the capitalist system. It exists more or less in all countries of the world; but there is accountability. There is justice. Even in countries where there is no democracy, exemplary trials of corruption are held. Both justice and accountability are absent here. Here, the looting group is controlling the accountability sector. Because there is no accountability here, the country's top defaulter becomes an important person in the state structure. If this theft and looting cannot be stopped, corruption cannot be stopped. Business, politics and bureaucracy - three vicious circles have spread corruption in Bangladesh. It is not possible to control corruption while keeping this nexus intact. That is why we at TIB have been talking about reforming the business sector for a long time. But the government has not taken it into account. One of the main sources of corruption is the business community, they use politicians, bureaucracy and even the media as shields for this purpose. However, not all business people commit corruption. We have a coterie of business people here, they used to control everything. To stop this, we need to strengthen the practice of integrity in the business sector. 
Prothom Alo: Let's assume that your commission made a good recommendation to stop corruption. But what is the guarantee that it will be implemented? 
Iftekharuzzaman: We want to see its implementation. Even if we get an ACC of ideal and international standards, they will not be able to suppress corruption if the bureaucracy, business community and politicians do not practice integrity. To stop corruption, we must remember the ideals with which the Liberation War was fought in 1971, and the objectives with which the student uprising took place in 1924. 

Prothom Alo: In the last four and a half months, the interim government has not been able to play a strong role in any issue. 
Iftekharuzzaman: I am not very surprised. Although the government was established through a movement, I do not see the reflection of the great trust that the people have in them in many areas of the government's work. The work of the advisors has become reactionary, not pre-planned. If the government had presented a policy strategy to the countrymen after taking office on August 8, including a time frame, then it would have been easier to do the job. They did not do that. If they had a policy strategy, they could have decided to complete this work within this time. That is why we see multiple advisors giving different statements on the same issue. 
Prothom Alo: Corruption cases are filed against politicians in Bangladesh. The trial process goes on. Again, with the change of power, we see those cases being withdrawn. How do you view the matter? 
Iftekharuzzaman: There is a culture within the ACC that no action can be taken against those in power. Cases are being withdrawn against those who have come to power or think they will come. This has happened before. It is still happening. We have seen that after August 5, a new wave of extortion and extortion has started. The more politics becomes election-oriented, the more this trend is increasing. Because money will be needed for elections. At the same time, arrest-trading, lawsuit-trading are also going on. 
Prothom Alo: Nomination-trading and money games have been going on in our electoral politics for a long time. Is the Reform Commission putting forward any specific proposal in this regard? 
Iftekharuzzaman: We have tried to say that the ACC cannot control corruption alone. Many institutions are involved in this. If state and non-state institutions are transparent and accountable, then corruption can be brought under control. Political parties are at the top of non-state institutions. If there is no transparency and accountability among those who will be in power or try to come to power among the political parties, corruption cannot be stopped. That is why we have said that political parties also need to be reformed. This is where the question of election financing comes in. In all countries, political parties take donations and contributions from businessmen. But they publicly disclose from whom and how much money they have taken. We have recommended that transparency and accountability be ensured in election spending. Which party has taken donations and contributions and from whom, it should be disclosed. In that case, we think that black money and nomination-trading in elections can be brought under control.

Headline_English: How to defeat discriminatory activities
Content_Enlish:
When the Sheikh Hasina government came to power again for the third time in early 2024, after not holding elections, two reactions emerged in society. On the one hand, individuals and groups associated with government power were excited and even more arrogant at the prospect of gaining permanent power; on the other hand, the fear of further increase in corruption, looting and oppression created a deep depression at all levels of society, which can be called social depression. 

Anger was indeed accumulating behind the depression. There were many reasons for this accumulating anger. Although the Hasina government showed a high rate of GDP growth, the obvious problems of employment, the strain on the economic life of the majority of the people, the constant increase in the price of goods, as well as loan fraud, the looting and smuggling of huge wealth through unusually high expenditure on various development projects, and the increase in inequality have angered the people. Another major reason for the anger is the government's terrible inaction in solving the problems of the people, as well as the arbitrary oppression of the people by the people of the government party.

In the name of various leagues like Chhatra League and Jubo League, there was encroachment, looting, deforestation, and river destruction. Along with this, there was extortion and torture from sidewalk shops to university halls. If someone was disliked, government forces were called in, there were threats against expression of opinion, crossfire, and disappearances. 

The third issue that has further increased anger is the subordinate relationship with India. Border killings are ongoing, water barriers are increasing day by day. Yet, instead of resolving them, they have been treated with contempt and given one benefit after another. Sheikh Hasina visited India twice in June this year. On the second visit, she expanded transit benefits even further. The people did not know anything about these agreements. When various leagues, including the police and BGB, attacked the student movement demanding work, and even started indiscriminate killings, then this accumulated anger exploded, and people from all walks of life took to the streets. 

On June 5 this year, the court reinstated the old quota system in its verdict based on a case regarding quota reform. In response to this, the quota movement started again after 2018. This movement gradually expanded in June. From July 1, a strike called by students in all educational institutions began, at which time teachers in all public universities also went on strike for their professional demands. 

This strike was called by the Teachers' Association Federation and all teachers' associations, who have always been known for their unquestioning loyalty to the government. After coming to power for the third time through fraud and coercion, the government's tendency to belittle the demands of the people had increased a lot. 

Instead of discussing the demands of either teachers or students, the government was using humor, jokes, and insults. This was most evident on the night of July 14, with the violence against students, wholesale attacks, and indiscriminate killings from July 16. It was difficult for people to accept so much, so there was a public explosion. 

The way the ‘Droha Yatra’ organized by 37 cultural organizations and the University Teachers’ Network created a mass movement on August 2, the way people flocked to the Shaheed Minar on August 3, and the way the outline of the Teachers’ Network’s interim government for the democratic transformation of the post-Hasina state received public support on August 4, made it clear that the Hasina government no longer has any relevance. Even after thousands of people were killed and more than 20,000 injured, that mass explosion did not stop, but rather brought down the government in an irresistible mass uprising, and Sheikh Hasina fled with her entourage. 

The people of Bangladesh liberated this country through the 1971 Liberation War with incredible courage and a sea of ​​blood. The desire was created for a non-discriminatory, non-communal democratic state. But instead, a political system of concentration of wealth, military-civilian dictatorship, looting, and injustice was created. 

Sheikh Mujibur Rahman came to power in 1972 with the highest popularity in history. But it was his hand that laid the foundation for dictatorship in the constitution, and within three years Bangladesh emerged as a one-party, almost feudal state. In 1975, Sheikh Mujib and his family were killed and military rule came. Then, under the hands of the military rulers, BNP and Jatiya Party were born one after another. Awami League and these parties came to power at different times, and Jamaat also became a partner in power as their ally. 

Despite repeated disappointments over the decades, public resistance did not stop. Among these, people have resisted, been beaten, and given their lives for numerous issues, including the movement against military-civilian dictatorship, the mass uprising against Ershad, the movement to try war criminals, the movement for the caretaker government, the movement for the rights of workers and students, the movement for autonomy in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, the movement against rape and sexual harassment, the movement for democracy, the movement to protect the Phulbari-Sundarbans-river-forest-land and the cancellation of agreements against national interests, the movement against corruption and looting, the movement for safe roads. In the continuity of these, people from all walks of life have created the mass uprising of 2024. 

The successes of this extraordinary uprising of the students and the people are mainly three: 1. The fall of the corrupt and tyrannical, powerful Hasina government. 2. The liberation of people from daily torture and threats in various fields, including universities. An end to state disappearances and extrajudicial killings. 3. Discussions and debates are rife in various corners of Bangladesh through numerous initiatives. It seems that everyone has something to say, worries about the future of the country, and has different opinions. 

In this mass uprising, as before, the youth have remained at the forefront of the movement. However, although various left-right parties played a role in this movement, there was no direct political party leadership.
