Secondly, students, teachers, guardians, and women played an active and sensitive role in this movement. Thirdly, digital technology played an important role, through which news reached the people quickly, videos of atrocities and resistance were distributed to gather people, and the protesters remained connected. 

Fourthly, in this movement, numerous centers have been formed due to the lack of a clear position of the central leadership. Spontaneous participation and decentralization of leadership are its special features. This is reflected on the walls. The desire for a discrimination-free Bangladesh expressed in the crude hand-written drawings is extraordinary. There, the dream of an equal Bangladesh has emerged by eliminating all religious, ethnic, and gender discrimination. However, the dream of the interim government formed three days after the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government and that of her and her fellow student leaders has not yet been realized in their words and actions. In fact, it is being proven time and again that they had no preparation or vision for such a major change. 

The opposite of expectations has also been seen in the last few months. The vast majority of those killed and seriously injured in the mass uprising are children or workers from poor or lower-middle class families. The state is supposed to take responsibility for the treatment of the families of the killed and the injured. This is still in a chaotic state. 

Many people from minorities due to religious and ethnic identity are still spending their days and nights in fear of insecurity. Many works of art, including temples, shrines, and mosques, have been damaged. Many factories have been shut down, leaving thousands of workers unemployed, and many workers are still having to take to the streets to demand their arrears of wages. Extortion has started again. The prices of goods are still high. Air pollution in Dhaka city is still the worst in the world. 

The environmentally destructive and life-threatening projects and agreements against national interests of the Hasina era are still ongoing. Traffic jams, accidents or structural killings continue. On the other hand, the movements of discriminatory politics are gradually increasing. The tendency to dismiss the tradition of struggle of the people of this township by belittling or denying the 1971 Liberation War and glorifying communal ideology is becoming increasingly visible. 

Coercion, tagging, mob violence and misogynistic activities are being seen at various levels. The trend of neo-liberal economics under the authority of the World Bank, IMF, ADB, which paved the way for occupation, plunder and corruption, is also being continued. Needless to say, these things will have to change if the aspirations of the mass uprising are to be fulfilled. 

However, the government has formed reform commissions on various issues. Those commissions are working in detail to prepare their reports. The White Paper Committee has already submitted its report, which contains detailed information on the irregularities, corruption, looting and wealth laundering of the previous government. 

To establish a Bangladesh free of discrimination for all, a political system with specific policies and programs to eliminate class, gender, caste and religious discrimination will be needed. To implement the pro-people change that 2024 has opened up, discriminatory activities must be defeated in 2025. And the philosophy and politics of establishing a Bangladesh free from discrimination, oppression and domination must be strengthened.

Headline_English: Whose war is the Russia-Ukraine war really?
Content_Enlish:
The most talked about event in the world after Covid is the Russia-Ukraine war. The war that is changing the geopolitical and economic equation. To put it bluntly, the high inflation in Bangladesh today is due to this Russia-Ukraine war. Due to this war, the price of oil increases and as a result, inflation increases all over the world. During the crisis, the value of the dollar increases as a medium of exchange. Due to these two reasons, the inflation index goes up, which is still going up. 

But why and in what context is this war? Badrul Alam Khan, a former teacher at Rajshahi and Chittagong Universities, has written an excellent book on this subject in Bengali. There are no books on geopolitics in the country in Bengali, although our intellectual community and the people as a whole are also becoming interested in these subjects. I believe that this book will be able to meet that need to a large extent. 

To summarize the book, Flapp's words can be quoted: The book The Russia-Ukraine War: The Battle of Truth and Lies describes how the overwhelming insistence of the United States to satisfy its geostrategic interests and the jealousy of Russia over becoming a powerful opponent are turning Ukraine into ruins. 

The collapse of the Soviet Union, the far-reaching plan to corner Russia in world politics, and the provocation of the expansionist policy of the aggressive alliance called NATO on that occasion make this war inevitable. This book can be called an impeccable and unbiased account of Ukraine's desire to emerge as an independent country, the background of Ukraine's historical ethnic unity with Russia, and the US's attempt to drag Ukraine into the Western political circle. 

It is obvious to the naked eye that Russia is fulfilling its geopolitical ambitions by attacking its neighboring country, Ukraine. But the author Badrul Arab, by quoting events from different periods of history, shows that the matter is not so simple and one-sided. Rather, the Western powers, led by the United States, have forced Russia to go to this war. Needless to say, a small country like Ukraine cannot continuously provoke a superpower like Russia into war like this without the help and assistance of the West. 

That is why the author rightly says that he has his own doubts about the relevance of the title of the book, ‘Russia-Ukraine War’. His own comment: ‘The title would have been more appropriate in my opinion if it could have been called ‘Russia-NATO’ or ‘Russia-US War’. I can mention at least two reasons behind this idea. First, this war would never have started if the United States and NATO had not incited Ukraine against Russia. Second, Ukraine received full support in this war from the military organizations called the United States and NATO. Ukraine has become so dependent on America that the United States controls its economy, politics, military equipment supply, military training, strategic advice, and even important decisions such as ending or continuing the war. As a result, the war is actually between NATO and Russia, and in that sense Russia and the United States.’ 

This view is not the author’s alone; the author says that renowned scholars of international relations such as John Mercimer, Chris Hodge, and Jeffrey Sachs also hold this view. 

The author says that Moscow went to war with three main objectives in mind. They are to free Ukraine from the US-European sphere of influence, to protect the human rights of Russian-speaking citizens in Ukraine, and to force Ukraine to follow a neutral policy. In his opinion, Russia has been able to fulfill these three objectives, not completely, but partially. Russia has not been able to remove Ukraine from the European-American sphere of influence, but rather the question of Ukraine’s economy and security depends on the European Union and NATO. The western part of the country is angry and hostile towards Russia. That feeling has been intensified by the war. Russia is no longer acceptable to them. 

The possibility of regaining the historical relationship that Moscow has been claiming with Ukraine is now zero. Kiev has not yet given up hope of becoming a member of NATO. Even if not in NATO, it will definitely join the European Union after the war. As a result, its ties with Europe will be even stronger. On the other hand, Russia has occupied the Russian-speaking regions of Ukraine such as Donetsk, Donbas, Luhansk, Zaporizhia and, it can be said, their assimilation into the Russian state is almost complete. The division that existed in the ethnic identity of Ukraine before the war has now widened to such an extent that the eastern part of Ukraine will never return to the political structure of Ukraine. The same claim can be made in the context of Crimea. The possibility of its return to Ukraine is also zero. 

On the other hand, I do not think that Russia can claim itself as a country in Europe anymore. Its relationship with Europe has reached a point where it is almost an enemy-to-enemy relationship. This hostility does not seem to be possible to eliminate in the near future. On the other hand, if even some of the US's pre-election cuts to NATO are implemented, Europe will also increase its military spending. Then a different reality will be created. From that perspective, Russia has partially failed to fulfill its first objective. 

What Russia has managed to do is that, by moving away from Europe, it is becoming more involved with China and the Global South, which includes India, the Islamic world, Africa and Latin America. In particular, its trade and military relations with China have improved, although once they were in the same ideological camp, their relations had gone to a snake-like stage. This war has united them. China has money, Russia has weapons and vast natural resources. The combination of these two has given rise to the BRICS. With Russia's mediation, the border tensions between China and India have eased to a great extent; they have even withdrawn their troops from the disputed area. 

The reality is that in order to stimulate Russian nationalism, it was necessary to develop a special identity for the citizens. That identity is neither European nor Asian, but a mixture of the two; what Russian President Vladimir Putin has called Eurasian. The Global South is interested in building a new system favorable to them instead of the existing world order. But it is also true that the region is plagued by various divisions, there are religious, ethnic and regime differences. As a result, it will not be easy for Russia to strengthen its position under that complex system. The United States will also constantly try to create divisions there, if possible, to build a united front against Russia. 

Russian President Vladimir Putin said that the Western world has betrayed Russia after the collapse of the Soviet Union. Russia has tried to normalize relations many times, but the West has not listened to it. In an interview with American journalist Tucker Carlson in February this year, Putin also said that Russia is no longer a communist country, but the hatred of the West is not over. The latest thing they did was to expand NATO to the eastern part of Europe. This incident is like driving the final nail in the coffin. Along with this, Putin also criticized the leaders of the time for not being able to show wisdom when the Soviet Union collapsed. 

After the start of the Russia-Ukraine war, many initially thought that the country's economy would collapse due to the sanctions imposed by the West on Russia. In reality, that did not happen. Compared to many Western countries, the Russian economy is in a better position now; although its impact in other countries is lasting. 

In the last two years, dedollarization has accelerated around the world. Not only Russia or anti-Western countries, but also many countries known to be close to the United States have started to hold foreign exchange reserves or stocks in other currencies instead of dollars. Trade in other currencies is also increasing. At the end of the third quarter of 2023 (July-October), the dollar's share in global reserve currencies fell to 59.2 percent, down from 70 percent in 2000. 

Meanwhile, international trade in the Chinese yuan and the Russian ruble is increasing. China has almost made arrangements to buy oil in its own currency, the yuan, from Saudi Arabia. In fact, the US sanctions on Russia and the aggressive increase in policy interest rates by the US central bank, the Federal Reserve, to prevent global inflation have led to an increase in the dollar exchange rate. This has led to a severe dollar crisis in many countries, including Bangladesh. Many countries are forced to start trading in other currencies instead of the dollar. The BRICS also want to trade in a common currency or the currencies of their member countries instead of the dollar. Dedollarization has already begun, and it has gained momentum due to the war. 

The book has a total of eight chapters. Starting from a detailed account of how the US brought the country under its control by causing the Orange Revolution, to a description of the blueprint for expanding US influence. There is a list of US crimes: ‘John ​​Pilger is a renowned Australian journalist. His countless writings and documentaries help highlight the various criminal aspects of US foreign policy. He claims, citing evidence, that so far the US has succeeded in overthrowing governments in at least 50 countries or has been involved in overthrow conspiracies, although most of the victim countries were democratic. So far, the US has interfered in the elections of 30 countries. It has carried out airstrikes in at least 30 countries, killing helpless innocent people who are unable to defend themselves. The US was directly involved in conspiracies to assassinate the leaders of 50 countries. America’s name is also associated with attempts to suppress or thwart the freedom movements of 20 countries (Bangladesh is included in this list) (Pilger, John, 2022). This long list of crimes highlights the horrific picture of US diplomacy. There is enough evidence to prosecute every president who was or is involved in that history for the crime of genocide. 

Author Badrul Alam says that in geopolitics, there is a concept of sphere of influence, that is, expanding one's influence around the country. The work that the United States started 200 years ago. But after the collapse of the Soviet Union, the United States threw that concept in the trash. They did it to weaken Russia, so that its sole authority would be established. The author says that the United States has no forgiveness for these crimes.

Headline_English: The decline of the center-right in Europe has led to the rise of the far-right.
Content_Enlish:
What was once called the ‘centre-right’ has seen its final decline this year. It has never had a coherent political philosophy. It has generally been a mix of giving priority to the needs of big business interests and supporting so-called traditional values. Above all, it has called for a buffer zone to prevent the further rise of the far right. 

But this plan has not materialised. British politician Nigel Farage claims that his populist right-wing Reform Party now has more members than the Tories. If true, it would be the first time in British history that a right-wing party has outnumbered the Conservative Party. Nearly two decades ago, then-Tory leader David Cameron dismissed Farage as ‘crazy, eccentric and a secret racist’. But today Cameron’s party has fallen by comparison. 

What is behind this change? For more than a decade, Tory economic policies have led to a stagnant standard of living in the UK. The government infrastructure is in ruins. The Tories, unwilling to solve their own problems, have used divisive issues to divert public attention. They have created scapegoats to shift blame. Former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher’s Thatcherism proposed selling off public housing and increasing privatisation. While this brought some short-term benefits, it also cost them dearly in the long term. But it did appease voters. Today, there is no such alternative. Instead, the Tories are being forced to emulate a form of politics that they once considered too extreme or too vulgar. 

David Cameron played a key role in making immigration a toxic issue in British politics. He was a key architect of Brexit. Saida Warsi, former chair of the Tory Party. She expressed concern about the views of Cameron’s close ally Michael Gove on British Muslims. Jack Goldsmith’s vile Islamophobic campaign for the London mayorship took place during Cameron’s term. Cameron also paid no less attention to right-wing extremist Liz Truss. 

The landmark Brexit saw the Tories break down the remaining walls of rational resistance by resorting to populism. Theresa May’s infamous 2016 speech was a nod to Boris Johnson’s appeasement of right-wing extremists. Liz Truss has joined the ranks of American right-wing orators since her fall as prime minister. But it’s not just Britain that’s been doing this. Consider the Trumpian takeover of the Republican Party. This was made possible by the party’s own institutional leadership promoting conspiracy theories and Islamophobia. Liz Cheney, who in 2009 was involved in spreading conspiracy theories about Barack Obama’s birth certificate, is now seen as a ‘moderate’. 

The same trend is evident across Europe. Austria’s People’s Party formed its first coalition with the right-wing Freedom Party in 2000. After 24 years, the more extreme Freedom Party came first in the elections. And the People’s Party has moved further to the right. In Hungary, the ruling Fidesz party has transformed from center-right to pre-fascist. In Italy, the so-called center-right is a junior partner in a right-wing-led government. In Germany, the Christian Democrats have moved to the right, and the country’s far-right is growing. 

Some parts of the old media have helped bring this to a point. In particular, those led by Rupert Murdoch. They have waged a relentless campaign of hatred against minorities—Muslims, immigrants, refugees, and transgender people. Today, Elon Musk is using his Platform X (formerly Twitter) as a weapon to spread right-wing extremism. This is not to express any nostalgia for the old center-right politics. Since the 1980s, they have gradually encouraged “self-sustaining” economies and military intervention. Democratic ideals are no longer popular. The previous consensus on the extreme right has collapsed. 

On both sides of the Atlantic, open hatred, misinformation, and the portrayal of opponents as dangerous enemies of the nation have become commonplace in politics and the media. Where will it end? There is no clear answer. Because the limits of the mainstream right are no longer controlled. The sad truth is that the Western world will probably not be able to escape this ideology without seeing the consequences. A terrible reckoning awaits.

Headline_English: How expatriates can be involved in preventing propaganda
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh is now at a crucial juncture in the international context. It is crucial to send a strong message to migrants and expatriate Bangladeshis that their economic contribution is not limited to sending remittances; rather, it is essential for the country's social and political stability. Mohammad Jalal Uddin Sikder writes on how to engage expatriates in countering propaganda 
Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus, currently the chief advisor to the interim government of Bangladesh, in his first address to the nation, mentioned the important contribution of Bangladesh's migrant workers and diaspora community. He said that expatriates have played a role not only in economic development but also in various historical movements of the country. He also called on them to strengthen the country's economy by sending remittances through more legitimate channels. However, in the current context, the fight against false information and fake news has become a major challenge. 

Certain groups in India are spreading false propaganda against Bangladesh, which is damaging the stability and image of the country. In this situation, it is very important to create a strong connection with the expatriate and migrant Bangladeshis. Bangladesh is now at a time when its expatriate and migrant workers can play an important role in the security and development of the country, not only for remittances; but also through information dissemination and international lobbying. 

It should not be forgotten that Bangladeshi expatriates, including Dr. Yunus, played an important role in the liberation war in 1971 by raising funds, international lobbying and shaping global public opinion. In the past, we have seen that many countries have taken the help of the expatriate community to overcome their crises. 

How other countries have received help from the expatriate community 
We can learn from the experiences of different countries how effective the cooperation of the expatriate community can be for any country. For example, the Philippines can be mentioned. The Philippines has built a strong economic structure with the help of the expatriate community. Expatriate Filipinos have not only sent remittances; but have played a strong role in protecting the image of their country on international platforms. The Philippine government maintains regular contact with its expatriates and ensures insurance, training and social security for them. 

■ Dr. Bangladeshi expatriates, including Yunus, played a significant role in the 1971 liberation war by raising funds, lobbying internationally, and shaping global public opinion. ■ Expatriates and migrant workers can play an important role in the security and development of the country, not only through remittances; but also through information dissemination and international lobbying. 
South Korea has set an example for development through the diaspora. South Korea completed its economic reconstruction in the post-war period through remittances from the diaspora community and international lobbying. Diaspora Koreans have played a significant role in investing and providing technical assistance to their country. 

Lebanon has been in the midst of a prolonged political crisis. During this time, their diaspora community has stood by the country by providing financial assistance and information dissemination. The Lebanese government has created a centralized platform to integrate the diaspora community, which has made significant contributions to the economy and diplomacy. 

These examples show us how close contact and coordination with the diaspora community can be a powerful asset for a country. It is also time for Bangladesh to re-energize its relationship with its diaspora and migrant communities. 

Why the involvement of the interim government is important 
Communication with the diaspora and migrant Bangladeshis should not be limited to a formal relationship. By talking to them directly and listening to their problems, they should feel that they are part of the strength of the country. If Dr. Yunus speaks to the diaspora through a live online session, it will have a profound impact on them. They will feel that the government is listening to them and giving importance to their opinions. This will create a sense of empowerment among them and motivate them to work for their country. 

Similarly, the government’s direct connection with the diaspora and migrant Bangladeshis as well as internal migrant workers is very important. Internal migrant workers are one of the pillars of the country’s economy. They contribute to the garment sector, construction industry, agriculture and various service sectors. The contribution of these workers to the overall development of the country is immense; but their problems are often ignored. 

Well-organized strategy to connect with the diaspora 
The Bangladesh government needs to adopt a well-organized strategy in this regard. First, the government needs to establish direct contact with the diaspora. The Bangladeshi diaspora, especially those living in the United States, Canada and Western countries, can play an important role in global diplomacy and information dissemination. 

The number of Bangladeshis living in these countries is significant and many of them are in important positions in the educational, economic and social fields. If the government can build a close relationship with these diasporas, then it is possible to create a strong international lobby for Bangladesh through them. This goal can be achieved through regular communication with them, exchange of information and active participation of the Bangladeshi embassy. 

Secondly, many of the diaspora want to express their opinions to the media or play an active role in social media. Bangladeshi embassies can provide training and financial support to these diasporas so that they are able to disseminate truth and counter false information. A special platform can be created for expatriates, where they can involve themselves in fact-checking and dissemination. This will create an environment of unity among the expatriates and they will work as a united force to protect the country. 

However, training expatriates alone is not enough. The government needs to ensure that embassies play an active role. Embassies need to work closely with the expatriates in addition to diplomatic relations. This will not only empower the expatriates; it will also make embassies more effective in protecting the image of the country. 

In many cases, expatriate workers fall into the trap of false information and hatred. Joint efforts by the government and embassies are very important to free them from this trap. An important part of these initiatives is regular communication and training with expatriates through the use of information technology. 

Thirdly, many of the migrant workers are illiterate or semi-literate and do not have the ability to verify information. Training programs in simple language should be introduced for them, so that they know how to avoid false propaganda. Embassies can create a centralized information repository using social media, where expatriates can be aware of false information and confusion. At the same time, embassies can organize regular discussions and workshops to build trust among the expatriate community. 

Fourth, Bangladeshi embassies can collaborate with embassies or expatriate communities of other countries. Bangladeshi embassies should take the initiative to directly communicate with the expatriate community in India and Indian expatriates. Although the historical, geographical and cultural connections between India and Bangladesh are deep, attempts are currently being made to create confusion between the two countries through false information and propaganda. 

To counter this confusion, it is important to inform the Indian expatriate community about the truth. Bangladeshi embassies can invite Indian expatriates and organize direct discussions. Through this discussion, the nature of false information being spread about Bangladesh and its motives can be explained. 

Fifth, Bangladeshi embassies can play an effective role not only in disseminating information; but also in countering fake news and confusion. An information dissemination structure can be created in coordination with embassies and diaspora communities of other countries. The voice of Bangladeshi diaspora needs to be strengthened at the international level. 

It is necessary to build an international communication network, where Bangladeshi diaspora can disseminate true information not only to their own communities but also to diaspora communities in other countries. In this way, it is possible to create a strategic force through diaspora, which will play an important role in countering false propaganda against Bangladesh. 

Seventh, connecting with Bangladeshi diaspora youth and students can be another important initiative. Even though they live abroad, their roots are connected to Bangladesh. A platform should be created for them, where they can use their talents and skills for the country. If the diaspora youth feel their responsibility towards the country, it will not only contribute to their personal development; but will also play a positive role in the development of the country. 

Hundi: Financing false propaganda and illegal activities 
Hundi is not only a big threat to the country's economy, it is also being used to spread false propaganda and confusion against Bangladesh. Every year, 
10-12 billion US dollars are transferred out of the country through hundi. This money is not only flowing out of the legitimate economy of the country; it is also being used to finance illegal drugs, human trafficking, gold smuggling and disinformation in India and Myanmar. 

In particular, the money flowing into India and Myanmar through hundi is being used directly to finance the spread of fake news and misinformation. This money is acting as a powerful tool behind false information and tarnishing the image of Bangladesh. Those who work hard for the country and earn foreign exchange are unaware that the money they earn is being used for illegal purposes through hundi. 

A clear message needs to be given to migrant workers and expatriate Bangladeshis that if they send their earned money through legal channels, it will be used to maintain the country's development and social stability. However, if they send money through hundi, it is being used for immoral purposes, which is in conflict with their religious beliefs and their responsibility to the country. 

The government and Bangladeshi embassies need to launch a large-scale awareness program on this issue. They should be informed that stopping sending money through Hundi and sending remittances through legal channels will help in the country’s economic development and maintaining Bangladesh’s rightful position in the international arena. 

Final words 
Bangladesh is now at a crucial juncture. It is very important to send a strong message to the migrant and expatriate Bangladeshis that their economic contribution is not limited to sending remittances only; rather, it is also essential for the social and political stability of the country. In such a situation, the government’s relationship with the migrant and expatriate Bangladeshis is not only the demand of the hour, it is a national necessity. This will help ensure the overall development and stability of Bangladesh; their contribution will help in building a strong and stable Bangladesh for the future generations of the country.

Headline_English: Who will eliminate discrimination in government salaries?
Content_Enlish:
No article has received such a response before. It can truly be compared to an earthquake. Some of it comes from misunderstanding. And some of it comes from the brutal reality of life. 

The title of our column was, ‘They (government officials and employees) get dearness allowance, others will stand in line for TCB trucks?’ 

Many people have considered it as an opposition to dearness allowance for government officials and employees. In fact, we have not opposed anyone’s dearness allowance. We have said that at least 7 million people will benefit from dearness allowance. The government should also think about the huge population outside of this. 

A reader wrote, ‘I joined as an assistant teacher in a primary school in 2023. In total, my salary is 18,340 taka. How will a family of seven including parents survive for a whole month with this money?’ Teachers have different salary structures in all countries of the world. They are paid higher salaries and allowances. But in our country, teachers are paid less. From primary to higher levels.

Another wrote, ‘Do you have any idea how much salary an officer in grades 11-20 gets? Do you know what percentage of employees get a car or car loan? Do you have the mentality to feel what kind of inhuman life those who work honestly and do not earn illegally are living?’ 

Our question is also, why would this happen? Why can’t a government or private sector employee run a family with their salary? The problem is not the expensive allowance. It is the government’s discriminatory approach. The government makes the people above happy by giving more and more opportunities, while the people below cannot live well despite working day and night. 

A reader mentioned the salary gap between government and private banks and wrote, ‘I got a total salary of around 25 thousand in grade 10 from working as an officer in a government bank. My colleagues in private banks now get a salary of around 60 thousand. I have sinned by being misled by the lure of government jobs.’ 

One person said in a tone of helplessness, ‘It has become very difficult for lower-ranking government employees to survive in society. Every family is burdened with debt. It is not possible to treat old parents. At least speak up for the small and honest employees. Except for grades 1-5, the lower-ranking employees are living a very miserable life.’ 

A fourth person commented, ‘The daily wage of a daily wage laborer is at least 700-800 taka! Those who drive rickshaws and vans also earn at least more than 800 taka a day! Recently, the wages of garment workers have been increased! The minimum wage has been set at 12,000 taka! The increase will be 9 percent per year.’ 

Another wrote, ‘You only talked about government officials who take bribes, but there are many autonomous government positions; ordinary employees, they have no opportunities, they cannot survive on a small salary. The rent of MPO-affiliated institutions is 1000 taka, medical allowance is 500 taka, total salary is 9 thousand taka, and there are no other allowances, how will they manage their family on 9 thousand?' 

We also think that teachers and employees of MPO-affiliated institutions are the most deprived. We definitely want an end to this deprivation. There should be no such class distinction in education as government-private or MPO-affiliated and non-MPO-affiliated.

One person said in a tone of helplessness, 'It has become very difficult for lower-ranking government employees to survive in society. Every family is burdened with debt. It is not possible to treat elderly parents. At least speak up for the younger and honest employees. Except for grades 1-5, the lower employees are living a very miserable life.' 

An employee wrote with great confidence, 'Not all employees are corrupt. Is it possible to run a family of six members on 15 thousand taka? We will work with a stone tied to our stomachs, brother?’ 

Of course, no employee in the government or private sector will work with a stone tied to their stomachs. Everyone will work with dignity. The government will also ensure that they get their basic needs, i.e. food, clothing, housing, education and healthcare. 

The clear statement in response to the government employees is: I did not oppose giving dearness allowance to government officials and employees anywhere in my writing. I wrote, ‘The interim government has decided to give dearness allowance to all government officials and employees. What will happen to people outside the government?’ 

The main point of the writing was that the government has decided to give dearness allowance to government officials and employees, they will definitely benefit from this. But the government should also think about the large population outside it. It is true that many high-ranking officials in the private sector receive higher salaries and allowances than those in the government sector. Their house rent and other facilities are also higher. But it is also not true that many private sector employees and workers do not have a guarantee of minimum wages and allowances. There is no appointment letter. There is no gratuity, no provident fund. The owners lay off workers whenever they want, and lay off factories whenever they want. 

Most readers have talked about the difference between the first grade and the 20th grade in the government salary structure. We also think that this difference should be reduced and brought to a reasonable level. In the latest salary structure formed in 2015, the highest salary was 78 thousand taka and the lowest was 8 thousand 250 taka. Why should there be so much inequality? In addition to the salary of the higher-level officials, there are many facilities and benefits. But the employees in the lower ranks do not have them. That is, those who work harder, their salaries and allowances are lower. This situation should end. 

The Declaration of Independence talks about equality, human dignity and social justice. That will be ensured only when a person can meet his needs by working as much as he can. 

I completely agree with the emotions and feelings of the government officials and employees who have expressed their anger. I said that the government should also do something for those outside the government sector. The owners have agreed to increase the wages of the workers in the ready-made garment industry. This will also benefit the workers, employees and officials of that sector. But the government cannot ignore the large population outside it. 

And we must also remember that dearness allowance does not always work to prevent inflation. For example, suppose the government gave dearness allowance at the rate of 20 percent. And the prices of daily necessities also increased by 20 percent. As a result, the actual salary will not increase by a single taka. 

There are many types of discrimination in our country. Political discrimination. Social discrimination. Cultural discrimination. But the most terrible thing is economic discrimination. The government is not willing to give a 'hand' here for some mysterious reason. 

Past governments have nurtured discrimination. They have given oil to the head. We do not believe that the interim government formed through the anti-discrimination movement will do the same. The journey against discrimination should begin by eliminating the mountain-like inequality between the top and bottom. In that case, it is hoped that the wage gap between the top and bottom workers in both the government and private sectors will be reduced, if not completely eliminated.

Headline_English: The more data, the better AI?
Content_Enlish:
A week ago, Ilya Satskever, former co-founder of OpenAI, gave an interesting talk at the NeuroIPS conference in Vancouver, Canada. For so long, we have thought that the more data, the more computing power, the better the AI. This has become self-evident to us when working with artificial intelligence. But a big problem is coming. Which can completely change our traditional thinking about artificial intelligence. 

The processing power of computers is increasing day by day, but data is not increasing. There is only one internet in the world. Ilya referred to it as the ‘fossil fuel of AI’ and said that one day this fuel will also run out. Maybe we will have to find new ways, where AI can learn a lot even with very little data. He made an interesting comparison. 

There is a relationship between the body weight of animals and the weight of their brains. Especially in mammals, the relationship between the body weight and their brain weight is proportional. For example, the body weight of a small mouse and the weight of its brain, the body weight of a cat and the weight of its brain, the body weight of a dog and the weight of its brain, there is a certain ratio between them. The larger the body, the larger the brain also becomes at a certain rate. 

But in the case of humans, this relationship is different. In the case of hominids (human species), this ratio is different. Their brain weight increases much faster than their body weight. Ilya Satskever showed the graph of this ratio at that conference for an important reason. 

What he means is that there are examples in nature where the scaling (growth rate) of the same thing can suddenly change. For example, the brain development of hominids has taken a different path from that of other animals. This difference is very significant. This means that the brain of hominids has grown much faster than that of other mammals compared to the body. This shows us that different scaling is possible in nature too. 

Just as it is possible to break old rules and walk in new paths, it is possible to find new possibilities. Just as nature broke its own rules to evolve the human brain, we too may find new paths in AI. We just have to find those possibilities and dare to walk down new paths. 
This is what Ilya Satskever is trying to say in AI. For so long, we have thought that the more data, the more computing power, the better AI. Now, perhaps, this is the axiomatic path. It is a straight line like that of ordinary mammals, very much predicted. But perhaps we have now come to a crossroads where this rule no longer applies. Perhaps we need to find new paths, where AI can learn a lot with very little data, just as hominids evolved in their own way. 

Nature is showing us that big changes are possible, but they may be beyond the path we are taking. We just have to find those new paths. Maybe that is where the next ‘big leap’ in AI lies. This is not just a scientific fact, it gives us a path of hope.

Just as it is possible to break old rules and walk in new directions, it is possible to find new possibilities. Just as nature broke its own rules to evolve the human brain, we too may find new paths in AI. We just have to find those possibilities and dare to walk in new directions.

Headline_English: Is it even possible to make the potato market bearable?
Content_Enlish:
Potatoes are a well-known vegetable worldwide. It is difficult to find a person who does not like French fries. People in Bangladesh use potatoes in various ways as a vegetable. Potatoes are an essential ingredient in fish and meat. Potatoes are used in almost all types of vegetables. Alubhora, fried dried chilies with Bengali panta is a traditional favorite food. Without this, it is not like Poyala Boishakh is welcomed. Even if there is nothing else, the poor common people of the village have breakfast with alubhora and raw chilies from the trees planted in the yard. 

In November, the price of that potato exceeded 100 taka. New potatoes have appeared in the market. It is not correct that the price is high because the demand for new potatoes is high. This is mainly due to the low supply of new potatoes at the beginning of the season. 

It is not because potatoes are new, but in the last few years, potatoes have become a topic of discussion only because of its high price. Before the new potatoes are available, the price of old potatoes also increases. The explanation is that the price is high due to the increase in the cost of cold storage. The price of potatoes is high because of syndication in the potato market. The supply of potatoes is low compared to the demand. The price is high because people eat more food made from potatoes instead of rice. The price of potatoes is high because the alternative use of potatoes has increased. The price is high because potatoes are exported. The price of potatoes is high because potatoes are made into purple because of heavy rain. The price of potatoes is high because of power outages because potatoes are spoiled. The supply of other vegetables is low, so the price of potatoes is high. The production of other vegetables has been disrupted by sudden rains or floods, so the price of potatoes is high. It is almost impossible to list and finish the many other reasons for the increase in prices that I am hearing. 

So is there no chance that the potato market will stabilize in any way? This cannot be the case. The matter can be seen like this. In reality, the amount of satisfaction that can be obtained by consuming or eating or drinking any product cannot be measured in any way. But economists have been able to measure the satisfaction of consuming products on the basis of a number of assumed conditions. It is necessary to try and see if something like that can be done in the case of controlling the potato market. 

As a graduate of agricultural economics, I believe that by discussing with a few farmer brothers and getting the right information, we will be able to find out how much money the farmer brothers spend per kg or bigha on potato production. It is not difficult to find out how much profit the farmer brothers want per kg. Now, if we can estimate the total cost of those who will buy and store potatoes and how much profit they want per kg, we can estimate the profit share of the wholesalers and retailers. Now, it comes to calculating how much money the retailers will sell for. 

For the convenience of calculation, if we assume that after calculating all the costs of a potato farmer, it was found that the production cost per kg is 20 to 22 taka (in 2019, the production cost of 1 kg of potatoes at the farmer level was 10.56 taka and their selling price was 13.88 taka). They expect a profit of at least 2 to 3 taka per kg. Then the selling price of the farmer brothers will be 22 to 25 taka.

If those who buy potatoes and store them in cold storage calculate all their expenses, they expect their cost per kg to be 4 to 5 taka and their own profit of 3 taka per kg, then it can be seen that the conservator's selling price will be 29 to 33 taka per kg. The retailer's purchase price can be a maximum of 35 to 38 taka by adding the wholesaler's commission along with transportation costs. The retailer will expect a profit of 3 to 4 taka per kg. Then, according to the estimated calculation, the retail price of potatoes can be a maximum of 38 to 42 taka. 

This calculation can be done through small-scale research and it is also possible to do the calculation through the government's agricultural marketing officers. Based on the results of the research, if the relevant government department monitors the market and conducts campaigns, it will be revealed who is hindering it. However, if the demand for potatoes in the market is very high, then naturally the market will be unstable. In that case, it is very important to have accurate information about the demand and supply of potatoes in the market. The government must also do that work regularly. If the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics and the Department of Agricultural Extension verify and compare the data and publish updated information year by year, it will be possible to get a proper idea about the potato market. 

It is possible to increase or decrease production by estimating the increased demand year by year. If there is an agricultural commodity pricing commission at the national level, they can conduct small studies and give advice on increasing production, pricing, importing if necessary and other urgent matters. 

Agricultural marketing officers can also work closely in this regard. There may be differences in prices by district and division. If production is disrupted due to natural disasters, it is not a very difficult task to determine prices taking that into account. In fact, difficult problems arise when plans are made in an unplanned manner and a solution is sought based on that. In these cases, it is very important to stand on a foundation and face the situation patiently. If that cannot be done, it is not possible to be successful again and again. 

According to BBS sources, the total production of potatoes, including indigenous and foreign varieties, was 1.431 million metric tons in 2022-23 (BBS, 2023). And the demand is 8.5-9 million metric tons. The total potato storage capacity in 365 cold storages in 43 districts across the country is about 3 million metric tons. Even though the production is high, about 10-15 percent of potatoes have to be kept for seeds (according to the 2020 BARC study, 10.06 million metric tons of potatoes were supposed to be kept for seeds). 

In addition, potatoes are currently exported to about 11 countries in the world. According to the Ministry of Agriculture, a target of 1.8 million metric tons of exports has been set for 2024, which is slightly higher than the previous trend. Considering the storage for seeds, alternative uses of potatoes and the amount of exports, it is safe to say that the supply of potatoes is not in excess of the demand. 

In addition, if potatoes are not stored properly, there will be a tendency for shortages, which is why it will be difficult to keep the potato market stable. In this reality, the strategy of controlling the market by fixing the price of potatoes does not seem right; rather, it is more reasonable to focus on increasing potato production and the decision to import potatoes to increase supply in the short term seems more effective. The excuse that the government gives that there is a rampant syndication in the agricultural market without any specific information makes the market more unstable. Because it discourages honest traders. If any unscrupulous group disrupts supply unnecessarily by syndicating, the government will take care of it by conducting a campaign and take exemplary punishment against them, it is the government's responsibility. 

It is important to focus on increasing production for strategic reasons. If potato farmers are provided with good and high-yielding seeds at affordable prices on time, subsidized fertilizers, pesticides and irrigation, provided with training on advanced technology and arranged for proper marketing of the produced potatoes, the production volume will increase and the possibility of getting them at a lower price will increase. 

Since potato production, like Boro rice, occurs during a less risky period, if production costs can be reduced, farmers will come forward to produce potatoes. If the crop is not disrupted by natural disasters, it will not be difficult to supply potatoes as per demand throughout the year. If the supply of potatoes in the market is increased in this way, it will be possible to keep the prices at a tolerable level. 

Research is very important to solve the problem. In 2019, a study was conducted on daily commodities such as rice, potatoes and onions in a short period of time at the initiative of the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council and its results were presented. There, an attempt was made to find out the reasons for the price increase and it was also recommended that some government institutions could work to resolve them. In fact, research needs to be continued every year. Because the production of agricultural products is highly variable. Since potato production takes a long time and is in high quantity, it is not easy to manage it. However, if the government takes appropriate initiatives, it is possible to find solutions to these in stages. 

No calculation will be effective unless everyone wants to serve the society or the people of the country with human values. However, it is true that as long as we cannot enter a developed and stable economy, there will be inequality. Through the establishment of the rule of law, a just social system will be developed and people will think about the interests of others before their own interests, this is expected. Many countries in the world have developed continuously in this way. Our country can also do it. The day is not far away when we will also enter a developed economy. And then, of course, inflation will be at the desired level and the market will be stable overall.

Headline_English: How Gen Z is changing politics
Content_Enlish:
We live in a world where celebrity is everywhere. The former and future president of the United States spent more than a decade as a reality TV star. Just a few days ago, Taylor Swift wrapped up the biggest and most profitable pop music tour in world history. Big entertainment is still star-driven. Just ask anyone who is going to see ``Wicked'' or ``Gladiator 2'' this holiday season and you will find proof of this. And then there are all the little dramas involving interesting and famous people. We are all buzzing about them. 

Now I am going to make an argument that may seem strange to you. Because it is the complete opposite of what I have said. We are moving away from this traditional era of mass celebrity. Not just moving away, we are moving towards a new and uncertain era. Even those who were worshipped blindly a few years ago are now being treated with a new kind of hostility in this new world. 

A large part of this new world is made up of the youngest generation of adults, the so-called Generation G and the millennials under 40. Generation G is perhaps the most misunderstood generation. They are coming of age at a time when the old one-sided culture is crumbling. Many of them are young. They are not supposed to know about the dominance of cable television, the golden age of stars from Julia Roberts to Brad Pitt, or the fanatical devotion that once surrounded tech moguls like Steve Jobs. 

In the past five years, the mainstream media has said many different things about Generation G. They may be overly liberal, overly discriminatory, or far-right, poisoned by the influence of the Internet. They don’t read books, they are addicted to a few podcasts. 

The big battle of the next decade will not be between left and right. It will be between those who openly hate existing institutions and those who want to establish a new order. This devotion to Manjione is not really for Manjione. It is a sign of where we are going. This anger will not stop. 
The reality is more complicated. Because every generation is more complex than the previous one. Some Gen G and young millennials are a little harder to generalize about. Because they live in a time when culture is on the verge of collapse. These millions of teenagers or young adults no longer enjoy a TV show or drama that airs at a certain time. They no longer get their political ideas from a talk show. 

The days of one-sided broadcasting like television are over. Television can no longer influence elections. Hollywood can no longer maintain its dominance as the center of culture. 

There is no longer a central culture. At least it is rapidly weakening. Many have gained fame using new platforms like TikTok. A recent trend has gone viral. TikTok users have been called upon to deliberately ignore celebrities and influencers, in order to prove that TikTokers are no less powerful than celebrities. As a result, the number of likes on the videos of celebrities with huge social media followings has dropped alarmingly. 

Of course, these celebrities are so rich that they have not suffered any financial loss. However, this trend was unthinkable even five years ago. There is no doubt that celebrities have become wary. 

Author Mo Diggs calls this trend ‘personality annoyance’. Especially in the internet world, ordinary people are fed up with the rich and famous. And politically, people are suspicious of leaders or those who tell them what to do. They no longer take their words at face value like they used to. 

This has been seen in this year’s US elections. Taylor Swift and Beyoncé are extremely popular. But despite their enthusiastic support, they could not significantly bring young voters to Kamala Harris. Left-leaning Gen G voters were particularly angry at celebrities who did not publicly oppose Israel in the Gaza conflict. This distrust of elites is growing. 

Into this void has stepped the ultimate “anti-influencer,” Luigi Mangione, 26. Mangione, accused of murdering United Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson, has now garnered a massive online following, unprecedented in recent history. The murder of a CEO who made $1.2 million in 2023 is a political allegation. But it is not tied to any party. 

When right-wing pundits like Ben Shapiro or Matt Walsh condemned the killing, their comment sections filled with anger against the American healthcare industry and support for the murder. 

Liberals who condemned Thompson’s killing are not in a good position either. The media and political establishment agree that the public’s fascination with Mangione is not good. But the public’s sentiment online is different. Video game character Luigi is widely sold on Amazon. Some have even bought candles with Mangione’s image on them. 

The message is clear: if there is to be a new idol, it will not be a singer, dancer or actor. At least that’s what the younger generation thinks. Their anger at the establishment is growing. Telling them to stop making Luigi memes will not help. Trump, who claims to be a great changemaker, will not be immune to this trend even as president. 

The big fight of the next decade will not be between left and right. It will be between those who openly hate the existing institutions and those who want to establish a new order. This devotion to Mangione is not for Mangione. Rather, it is an indication of where we are headed. This anger won't stop.

Headline_English: The invisible battle that rages in politics
Content_Enlish:
Nowadays, there is a thing called prank. It is also called practical joke. In Bengali, it can be called making fun. In the age of Facebook, no one is left to recognize this prank. There is a difference between a prank and a mere verbal joke—there is something here. The purpose of a prank is to fool someone, to make them uncomfortable—and to have fun by doing so. 

The boundaries of a prank are not very small. In 2017, an e-mail prankster fooled US Homeland Security Advisor Tom Bowser. He emailed a Bowser with the name of Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, and convinced him to have dinner that afternoon. The matter was not light. Kushner was then a special adviser to the US president. Bowser even agreed to the invitation and gave his personal e-mail address in response to that email. The prankster made a subtle joke about the US invasion of Iraq in an email—‘I promise, our arrangements will not be worse than the food we ate in Iraq.’ 

Politics revolves around what can be seen and what can be said. Why did a large number of women who were present in the struggle during the mass uprising disappear? Why do workers die in front of our eyes during the march demanding wages but remain invisible? What can be seen is actually seen because it is wanted to be shown. If we get stuck in it, no real change will come. 
In 2016, two teenagers, aged 16 and 17, caused a commotion at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art by pranking them. A large exhibition was going on there. The two teenagers left a pair of glasses on the floor in an empty space on the wall inside the museum. Soon, a crowd gathered around the glasses. Speculation began about which artist these glasses were installation art by. Arguments arose about the meaning of this art. Many people began to praise it very much. A teenager took a picture of these and tweeted. It was retweeted more than fifty thousand times. 

Among those who cheated were great art critics, artists, professors, and intellectuals. How could this happen? This is something to think about. So we do not decide for ourselves what we will see, what we will understand by seeing it. Society decides what we will see, and what we will not see. 

In an art gallery, they hang it in a frame on the wall and tell us that it is a work of art. You have to enjoy it. If the same thing is lying on the sidewalk, it is no longer art, and I will not care. That is why no one can imagine that someone could leave glasses left on the floor of the Museum of Modern Art as a joke. Arguments about the art of those glasses begin. 

This is not only true about things. We usually do not decide when, how, and what we will say. Some party decides, sets the rules. 

This is the idea of ​​a French philosopher named Jacques Rancière. He believes that there is a mutual relationship between power, politics and art in society. Whatever is tangible, where it is located is important. It depends on this who will see, hear, say and who will remain silent. The more powerful the one in the power structure, the more he decides who will be visible. If there is a slight scratch on someone, there will be a commotion; on the other hand, even if someone dies in a row, they will only become a number, they will remain invisible. 

There is a system in society. That system decides who will be seen, who will not be seen. It decides who is right and who is wrong. Since the post-independence period in Bangladesh, how many groups of people have become visible. And how many people have remained invisible. The groups at the center of power have made themselves visible. Their efforts for this visibility are endless. 

This struggle between seeing and not seeing goes on in politics. The movement to eliminate discrimination through the quota reform movement, the safe road movement and the mass uprisings—an attempt to make visible what was kept invisible. These movements challenged the existing power structure and demanded a new distribution of the visible and the invisible. 

Politics revolves around what can be seen and what can be said. Why did a large number of women who were present in the struggle during the mass uprisings disappear? Why do the deaths of workers in the wage demand marches happen before our eyes but remain invisible? What is visible is actually visible because it is wanted to be shown. If we are stuck in this, no real change will come.

Headline_English: What Trump's foreign policy could be like
Content_Enlish:
Predictions are always difficult. And it is even more difficult with Donald Trump. Because he talks randomly. He changes positions repeatedly. And he thinks that acting erratically is a good bargaining strategy. However, his election campaign statements, the identity of his appointees and his first term activities can give some idea. 

If we discuss what Trump's approach will be regarding China, what will we see? We can see that the Trump administration has chosen Marco Rubio as Secretary of State and Michael Waltz as National Security Advisor. Both of them consider China to be a major threat and both are in favor of taking a tough stance against China. Trump himself has said in the campaign that he will impose new tariffs on imports from allies and higher tariffs on Chinese products. 

Trump's statements indicate that he wants to follow the old trend of US foreign policy. In his first inaugural address, he said, “From now on, America’s interests will come first… We will not force anyone to be like us; rather, we will set an example for all.” This approach does not suggest isolationism; but it also does not lead to a policy of increasing mutual relations. 
Trump has already announced tariffs on imports from Mexico, Canada, and China. So some tariffs will certainly increase. But it is not yet clear how much the tariff rate will increase, how long the tariff will remain in place, and what products the tariff will affect. 

Domestic politics and Trump’s will will play a role behind this. His Treasury Secretary-designate Scott Besant said, “In many cases, Trump creates tensions and uses strategies to reduce them. My goal for his administration will be to protect international trade.” It is not clear what Trump will do if US trading partners impose retaliatory tariffs. If this trade war escalates into tariffs and higher commodity prices, inflation could rise in the US. This would increase public anger. 

Trump, who claims to be a skilled negotiator, may want to make some compromises. For example, he could make a deal with Chinese President Xi Jinping in which the US would reduce support for Taiwan. In return, he would sign a trade deal that he would present as his success. Some US allies in Asia are worried about such a situation. 

Read more 
How Trump's trade policy could affect Bangladesh 
November 25, 2024 
How Trump's trade policy could affect Bangladesh 
Analysis of Trump's campaign and previous term suggests that he will place less emphasis on international agreements and alliances. He wants to withdraw from the Paris climate agreement and increase oil and gas production and exports. Although renewable energy prices are falling in the US, his policies could leave these industries behind in the competition.

In the Middle East, Trump has always supported Israel. He negotiated the Abraham Accords, which normalized relations between four Arab countries and Israel, and he has always been proud of it. 

The Biden administration wanted Saudi Arabia to recognize Israel; but Saudi Arabia stipulated that Israel must take steps towards the establishment of a Palestinian state; but Israel’s right-wing government opposes a two-state solution. After the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, the Israeli public has also lost interest in the two-state solution. Trump may want to build on his previous successes in the region; but it is difficult to see how he will do so. 

On Europe and NATO, Trump has said that he will end the war in Ukraine “in one day.” But in reality, that is not possible. It is still uncertain how he will bring about a ceasefire. It may be that Trump will reduce aid to Ukraine and lead it to a situation where Ukraine is forced to accept Russia’s conditions. 

He could also move towards a solution called the ‘Korean solution’. In this solution, the current border of the battlefield would be turned into a demilitarized zone, where UN or European peacekeepers would be stationed. 

Trump’s statements suggest that he wants to follow the old trend of US foreign policy. In his first inaugural address, he said, ‘From now on, America’s interests will come first… We will not force anyone to be like us; rather, we will set an example for everyone.’ This approach does not suggest isolation from others; but it does not go towards a policy of increasing mutual relations either.

Headline_English: How are the insecure poor people of Bangladesh doing?
Content_Enlish:
The poor people of Bangladesh have been forced to reduce their food intake due to the current food price inflation. Not only that, they are also being forced to reduce the protein content of fish, meat, eggs, milk, etc. and fill their stomachs with only rice or flour-based carbohydrates. The poorest may not be able to eat even a little rice to fill their stomachs. 

This reality came to light recently at a discussion meeting on the living conditions of industrial workers, inflation and physical health at a hotel in the capital. The speaker at this seminar was the current DG of BIDS, Binayak Sen. The discussion meeting was presided over by Syed Mainul Hossain, Emeritus Professor of Concordia University, Canada. 

The meeting presented data from a survey conducted by BIDS on 3,887 households in 64 villages in 64 districts from October to December 2023-24. These data prove the truth of the above statement. 

Poverty is increasing 
Thanks to the recently published white paper, we also learned that there are currently about 20 million people in Bangladesh who will be forced to fall below the poverty line if they cannot work or earn for two days. The number of people below the poverty line in our country had already increased by 40 percent during the Corona period. Later, the previous government claimed that it had decreased to 18 percent after Corona. But now, due to the increase in food prices, the fixed or earned real income of urban workers and low-income people in villages has decreased. With the money they receive, it has become difficult to feed their children. 

Especially for urban workers, housing costs, transportation costs, fuel costs, etc. have increased so much that it is not possible for them to procure the necessary 3,000 calories of nutritious food with the meager amount left in their hands. 

If we take into account the 20 million people who have become newly poor, it would not be an exaggeration to say that our national poverty rate has reached 40 percent again. Policymakers are not bothered about this at all. That is why there is intense anger in the minds of the people. 

According to the BIDS survey, the prices of a total of 11 types of food items have increased by 15 percent to 20 percent in the same period of 2023 compared to the October-December quarter of 2022. Although the official figures still claim that the inflation rate is 10-12 percent. 

Recently, the Chief Advisor has mentioned inflation as the number one problem. Yet the current government has been unable to control prices. As a result, there is a shortage of imports, extortion, the dominance of middlemen and syndicates, and an increase in production costs. 

Now many educated lower classes are joining them. Their new Bengali name is ‘insecure proletariat’ or ‘insecure floating workers’. The combined force of the proletariat in the productive formal sector of Bangladesh and the ‘insecure precarious workers’ in the informal sector has now become a vast majority. In one sense, none of them are free from the threat of poverty in one way or another. 
What was needed to be done in ‘stagflation’ 
The trade advisor has already left, admitting his failure and handing over the responsibility to someone else. Instead of touching the real issue, the current government is trying to control inflation by increasing interest rates and contracting demand and credit as per the advice of the IMF. But although this is more effective for developed countries, it is not being effective in this country. Since the country is still in recession, if demand and credit are controlled and reduced, the recession will deepen. 

If banks cannot provide working capital to the productive sectors in an appropriate amount, then production, employment and supply will be disrupted. This will further increase prices. As a result, in our country, recession, unemployment, inflation and poverty will increase at the same time. Economists have named this complex situation – stagflation. To reduce deflation, supply must be increased at the same time, supply costs must be reduced, waste and spoilage must be reduced and the supply channel must be made competitive. 

A new cooperative structure of direct relations between consumers and producers must be developed. Our policymakers are unable to pay attention to these alternative policies due to their philosophical narrowness and Western dependence. They are not even willing to move on this path. They consider the free market path as the ideal path, or they are mostly looking at the so-called ‘humanitarian capitalists’ or ‘social entrepreneurs’ as Professor Yunus called them. But due to class nature, there is no response there. 

In addition, the burden of inherited loot is becoming more complex. No money has been recovered from them in reality. Rather, they have quickly packed up and moved abroad. That is why their institutions and banks are now closing down and going bankrupt. In order to save the banks without looking at the past, the central bank governor has gone back on his previous promise and injected 22,000 crore taka into the economy. But if a large part of this money had been spent there and instead given to the productive sector, better results might have been achieved. 

This strategy of bailing out the large private sector by printing money or taking money from the people's tax money is American. This strategy was adopted during the financial crisis of the capitalist world in 2008. It is now going to return to our country again. 

Declining urban poverty and what to do 
According to BIDS, the minimum monthly living expenses for a family of four of a worker engaged in the production sector are 22,979 taka. The researcher also says that the workers try to earn this amount of money by eating less and working more. But even then, about one-fifth (20 percent) of the workers engaged in the production sector cannot earn this amount of money. The laid-off workers are in the worst condition. They are forced to work as auto or rickshaw van, street vendors, coolies, construction workers or return to the village to work in the informal sector, such as agriculture. Their numbers are currently the majority. About 80-85 percent of the entire labor group. Their income is very low in most cases. The lowest is 100 taka per day. The highest is 500 taka per day. 

Meanwhile, a High Court verdict suddenly imposed the sword of unemployment on autorickshaw workers without making alternative arrangements. However, due to a huge movement led by the Left, that verdict was withdrawn again. However, the final verdict and what the government's policymakers will do in this regard will be known on December 25. These 6 million autorickshaw drivers, along with 25 million working poor people, are facing a threat. 

Not only the civilized bourgeoisie, but also the ancient slave owners and aristocratic landlords did not hesitate to give whatever was needed to reproduce the labor force. Because, these people are the source of labor power for them like a goose that lays golden eggs. 

If they are not kept alive and put to work, they will not be able to continue their surplus income and luxury like profit, interest, etc. But the greedy-looters dependent on the bourgeoisie in underdeveloped countries want to kill the goose and seize all the eggs at once. That is why the workers in the formal and informal sectors here are victims of a special kind of ruthless exploitation. Here they cannot even continue their minimum income. There is no guarantee of work. Therefore, they are now not called 'proletariat' but have been given a new name 'precarious' even in developed countries. 

Now many educated lower classes are coming and joining them. Their new Bengali name is 'insecure proletarian' or 'uncertain floating worker'. The combined force of the working class of Bangladesh's productive formal sector and the 'insecure precarious workers' of the informal sector has now become the overwhelming majority. In one sense, none of them is free from the threat of poverty in one way or another. 

If we redefine poverty alleviation in the light of the 1972 constitution by permanently and collectively integrating food, clothing, education, medical care, entertainment and job security, then about 60-70 percent of these people are facing more or less poor or vulnerable conditions. It is time for the workers of the formal and informal sectors to stand together as the vanguard against this inequality and discrimination.

Headline_English: What will be Trump's policy towards the Taliban government in Afghanistan?
Content_Enlish:
Since Donald Trump's re-election, there has been much discussion about what his new administration's Afghanistan policy might look like. Many believe that Trump will take a tough stance on the Taliban. However, an analysis of his previous actions and related statements suggests that he will not make significant changes to the pragmatic and non-interventionist foreign policy he followed in his first term. 

During his first term, Trump adopted a policy of not worrying about foreign countries for a long time. In particular, he made his position clear by opposing a prolonged US presence in Afghanistan. 

Trump was the architect of the 2020 Doha Agreement, which paved the way for the withdrawal of US forces from Afghanistan and ultimately ensured the return of the Taliban to power. 

The Doha Agreement was a major twist in the US Afghanistan strategy. Dissatisfied with the progress of US South Asia policy, Trump saw a lack of responsibility among his military advisors. He wanted to prove to voters that he was capable of ending America's longest and most expensive war. He began direct talks with the Taliban after traditional strategies to end the war failed. 

After his re-election, Trump is likely to maintain his business-like foreign policy. He will prioritize pragmatic agreements rather than costly conflicts or military interventions in Afghanistan and elsewhere. 

The Taliban also believe that a Trump administration could be beneficial for their future. 

For example, Abdul Qahar Balkhi, a spokesman for the Afghan Foreign Ministry, said in a post on Xe (formerly Twitter) in November, “We hope that the future Trump administration will take practical steps in relations between the two countries and open a new chapter in the relationship between the two nations.” 

The Taliban’s optimism about future relations stems largely from their positive experience during the first term of the Trump administration. 

The Taliban know that the first Trump administration, by directly engaging the Taliban, began the process of withdrawing US troops from Afghanistan and paving the way for their return to Kabul. 

But the Taliban also know that even if Trump is interested in establishing a realistic relationship with the Taliban, he will not give them full freedom to run the country or provide everything they need without conditions. 

If the Taliban fails to fulfill their promises in the Doha agreement, Trump will likely reduce US aid to Afghanistan or provide it with certain conditions. He is in favor of reducing foreign aid due to the ‘America First’ policy. If necessary, he will not hesitate to impose tough sanctions on the Taliban. 

Currently, under the Taliban, humanitarian aid of about $40 million per week plays a vital role for the Afghan people. If this aid is reduced, the Afghan economy will weaken further and there will be a major impact on the lives of the people. Improvements in education, health and food security will also decrease. Global attention on Afghanistan has decreased since Trump’s term ended. Afghanistan is no longer a top priority for Washington due to the withdrawal of US troops and the conflicts in Ukraine and Palestine. That’s why Trump, in his new term, may think that Afghanistan is now a problem that he has already solved. 

But if Trump cuts aid or imposes sanctions on the Taliban, Afghanistan’s economy could collapse. This would increase instability in the country, create a new migration crisis, and increase the activity of extremist groups. 

Trump’s anti-interventionist policy may be popular with a segment of the American public wary of getting involved in foreign conflicts. But Trump’s policy could create a weaker and poorer Afghanistan in the future, creating long-term security challenges. 

Such a situation would also have dire consequences for the Afghan people. It would further exacerbate the country’s economic woes. The health system could collapse. The country could be plunged into new conflict and become further isolated from the rest of the world. 

This would affect not only the Afghan people, but also the entire international community. 

In short, if Trump is to succeed in his Afghanistan policy in a second term, he will need to find a balance between pragmatic isolationism and the responsibility of global leadership. Otherwise, trying to end one conflict could create a new and more complex conflict.

Headline_English: A dangerous imperialist era is about to begin.
Content_Enlish:
The first quarter of the 21st century is coming to an end. At the same time, competition between countries around the world has reached a turning point. The world order we see today was rebuilt in the first half of the 20th century. From the ruins of two world wars. The Cold War era that emerged from that global conflict was the beginning of American hegemony. 

Today we live in an era in which American influence is declining. A multi-faceted global order is emerging. 

Some of the effects of this change have been clearly evident in the past 12 months. Donald Trump’s protectionism is one aspect of this change. New industrial powers often implement protectionist policies, as the United States did in the first half of the 20th century and Britain before 1840. When industrial powers are in a dominant position in the market, they usually do not rely on protectionist policies.
