The more the state presses, the more popular Imran is becoming 
On the other hand, the biggest problem of the government is the problem of its 'reputation'. However, this is no longer 2014, although it was still the Muslim League (N) government. Nawaz Sharif was the Prime Minister. 

Imran Khan sat on a sit-in strike at D Chowk for 126 days. Finally, the trouble ended through a judicial commission. After all, what is the reason that no obstacles were placed on the sit-in strike at that time? Is it because the support of the real powerful people was with Imran Khan at that time? Or is it because of the May 9 incident? 

It has been 17 months. The cases are not moving forward. The cases are still being politicized. However, action has been taken against many officers within the army itself. Former ISI chief General Faiz Hamid is also being investigated. Punitive action is imminent. 

In such a situation, it seems that Imran and PTI's protest is more against the real powerful than the current government. However, according to newspaper reports, the powerful are not ready for any kind of negotiation. 

South Asian democracy and politics have a history of killing or silencing popular leaders. For these reasons, people's sympathy is more for the family than the party. At a time when the circle around PTI leaders and workers is being narrowed, Imran Khan is expecting a reaction like February 8 from his supporters with the 'final call'. If that fails, the role of wives and sisters may increase. When the people of the party are sold out, what is Imran Khan's option other than relying on the family? 
A few things are very important in any protest movement. Organization, unity, ideology, emotions, strategy, assessing the strength of one's opponent, taking supporters and workers to the streets in large numbers, the role of the party's legal wing in legal action in the event of arrest, showing flexibility in negotiations and evaluating the success or failure of negotiations. 

The call for protests has been given at a time when the clear policy of the state and government is to arrest and suppress 'protests' by all means and to keep Islamabad away from any kind of agitators. 

If a sit-in is held on the roads and highways now, it will not be easy in this cold and smoky weather. The situation is not conducive now, like the sit-in strike of 2014. Excessive use of force by the government or law enforcement agencies can make matters worse. If Tehreek-e-Insaf fails to show extraordinary strength, it will become even more difficult for it in the future. 

In such a situation, Imran's 'political isolation' can harm him. It would have been better if this 'call' had been announced by the alliance. The alliance was formed for this purpose. If Jamaat-e-Ulema-e-Islam and Jamaat-e-Islami were involved in this protest, then this protest could not have been called a ‘single effort’. 

Imran may be expecting his voters and supporters to come out on the same path as on February 8. Imran Khan has not closed the door to ‘negotiations’ with the real powers that be. But the problem is that no one is coming from the other side to open the door. 

However, many PTI leaders feel that it would have been better to make the announcement after full preparation. However, those who favor the ‘kill or die’ slogan are worried that the spies in the party will leak the plan, and there is no way to know when. Many important leaders seem to agree with this second view. For these reasons, Imran Khan seems to have started relying more on his wife Bushra and sister Aleema politically. 

Many have criticized Imran’s political strategy. Imran, who has always criticized the family system in politics, is now moving in that direction himself. The results of the final call on November 24 will show how right Imran Khan's critics are. If Imran Khan gets a long sentence, the role of Bibi Bushra or sister Aleema will be important. Just like Begum Nusrat Bhutto in 1978 or Begum Kulsoom Nawaz during General Musharraf's rule. Believe it or not, there seems to be a family tradition in PTI. 

South Asian democracies and politics have a history of killing or silencing popular leaders. For these reasons, people have more sympathy for the family than the party. At a time when the circle around PTI leaders and workers is being narrowed, Imran Khan is expecting a February 8-like reaction from his supporters with the 'final call'. If that fails, the role of his wife and sister may increase. When the people of the party are sold out, what is Imran Khan's option but to rely on the family?

Headline_English: China's overproduction will increase tensions in the world
Content_Enlish:
Donald Trump's threat to raise tariffs may soon be the headlines in international news. But China's overcapacity is also a major long-term challenge to the global economy and trade system. Developed and emerging countries have recently imposed tariffs on Chinese imports. In response, China has taken various measures and provided incentives to the macro economy. As a result, it is becoming increasingly clear where China's overcapacity problem will lead in the coming years. It is understood that this crisis will have a major impact on global geopolitics. 

On October 29, a month after the United States imposed tariffs on Chinese overcapacity, Europe also imposed tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles (EVs). While these measures have been widely publicized, China's complaint to the World Trade Organization (where China protested Turkey's EV tariffs) has remained largely ignored. The case highlights China's failures. This suggests that China has so far failed to discourage emerging markets from following the path of advanced economies, despite its efforts to discourage them. 

Meanwhile, the global economy is changing as China's overseas production increases, and China's role in the global economy is changing. 

China's recent stimulus plans show that the government acknowledges the country's weak domestic demand but is not trying to restore the balance of the economy. As a result, the US-China trade war may escalate again. Because Trump has announced in advance that he will impose a 60 percent import tariff on Chinese goods. The impact of China's excess production will be greater on other major economies. 

The European Union (EU) may be the most affected by this. Because Europe's trade dispute with China is escalating. The tariffs that the EU has imposed on Chinese electric vehicles can be called 'just the beginning'. Although there are disagreements among member states on these tariffs, more major steps may be seen in the future. 

Under pressure from developed countries, Chinese exporters are now sending their products to developing countries. Because in 2023, more than 50 percent of China's exports went to these countries. China's exports will increase further in the future. As a result, China's trade deficit with major countries will increase. These countries are benefiting from cheap Chinese goods and investment. But they are unable to enter the Chinese market. This is making it difficult for their own industries to develop. 

Trump has promised to impose new import tariffs on China and impose 10 to 20 percent tariffs on imports from other countries. As a result, China's exports will go more to emerging markets and the European Union. This will increase the dependence of the global trading system on China. 

The United States and the European Union have raised the problem of China's excess production capacity. They have started to address this problem of Chinese industry through tariffs and international relations. The hope is that Chinese companies have reduced their expansion plans. Because domestic demand is low and it has become difficult to export excess products. 

But the problem needs stronger trade sanctions and new policies. The pace of action by the G7 suggests that more action will be taken in the future. Imports from China will be subject to increased scrutiny on safety, environmental and labor issues. 

China has increased foreign investment. This has been welcomed by its trading partners. But there are doubts about how effective the plan will be.

Headline_English: What will be the final outcome of the Awami League?
Content_Enlish:
What will be the ultimate fate of the fallen autocratic party Awami League? This question arose when Sheikh Hasina fled to India with all her forces after the student-public revolution on August 5. Even though everyone in the Awami League fled, they left behind a history of brutal massacres of a bloody mass revolution. 

The Awami League is responsible for the genocide in this revolution. The Awami ruling class mercilessly shot and killed the revolutionary students and public. The Awami League as a party cannot avoid responsibility for this genocide in any way. Due to the genocide and brutal repression, the question naturally arises whether the Awami League will be able to return to politics or not. Even if it returns, will it be able to return in its own name? 

After the fall of Baksal in 1975, the Awami League returned in its own name in 1979 during the reign of Ziaur Rahman. Even then, there were allegations of indiscriminate killing and torture of civilians by the Awami League and the Baksal Rakshi Bahini. The same allegations are still against the Awami League. 

Sheikh Hasina's Awami League is a continuation of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's misrule. Therefore, questions have been raised about the right of Awami League to engage in politics. When various parties are criticizing and discussing these issues, the chief advisor has put the responsibility of rehabilitating Awami League in politics on the shoulders of BNP. 

Recently, in an interview given to the Indian media, he said, 'BNP wants elections with the participation of all parties. BNP is a big party. We have accepted their demand.' However, BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has rejected this. He said, 'We did not say that we want to bring anyone to the elections.' Although the chief advisor spoke about BNP, in September the Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami also made it clear that they do not want Awami League to be banned. 

Meanwhile, government advisor Asif Mahmud said that when the Awami League was talked about being banned, political parties tried to obstruct it through speeches. In this case, he mentioned the Nazi Party of Germany and said that this party was banned in 1945. It is still banned. He thinks that the Awami League should also face a similar fate. 

In light of the situation, it seems that the government wants to keep the path open to banning the Awami League. But the political parties do not exactly agree with this. The students are in favor of banning it. However, the demand to ban the Awami League should have been raised by the political parties. Because, they have been the ones who have suffered the most in the long decade and a half. In this case, the opposite has happened. 

The government probably wanted to move towards banning the Awami League. Because, the International Tribunal had prepared a draft to take peaceful measures against the political party if it was involved in crimes against humanity. Legal Advisor Professor Asif Nazrul had said that this provision was being added by amending the Tribunal's ordinance. Later, this clause was not added in the amendment. Rather, the government pushed the ball towards the political parties. 

If the aforementioned clause had been added, the Awami League could have been found guilty of crimes against humanity according to the ordinance. The tribunal has enough material and evidence to convict the Awami League. In addition, Chief Advisor Dr. Yunus said that the massacres during the July Revolution will be tried. For this, the assistance of the international court will be sought. He also said in his address to the nation that he has spoken at various places. 

When the government came to power in 1996, it established the mafia system of Haji Selim, Haji Maqbul, Hazari, Shamim Osman. This time too, people are talking about rehabilitating the Awami League with people with a clear image. But by nature, the party embraces fascist ideology. It is not possible for them to be democratic. Therefore, there is no alternative but to put the Awami League on trial as a political institution. 
Dr. Yunus said that not only the massacres during the July Revolution, but also the disappearances and extrajudicial killings of the last 15 years will be tried. However, not only this law, but also according to Section 6 of the 1978 Political Party Ordinance, the government can ban the Awami League through the court if it wants. No matter how much the Awami League people are raving or the political parties take a stand against the ban, the Awami League's reach may shrink if the students want to ban the Awami League. There is pressure on the government from the students on this issue. 

When this is the position of the government and the students, why are the political parties not talking directly about banning the Awami League? Have the BNP-Jamaat forgotten the atrocities and tortures they have faced in the last 15 years? Have the political parties forgotten so quickly the fact that millions of their leaders and activists were accused in cases, fled the country as refugees, were disappeared, and were killed without trial? 

In addition, BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia has been kept in jail for years in false cases. The Awami League has not given her the opportunity to go abroad for treatment. It has pushed her to death without treatment. It has deported BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman. 

But keeping these brutal tortures in mind, perhaps BNP-Jamaat are saying that no party should be banned to build a liberal tolerant political culture. They have moved away from the American emperor Hammurabi's policy of a tooth for a tooth, an eye for an eye. They are seeking justice for the individual instead of the party. These two parties are probably trying to push away the politics of violence and disputes and start a new era of politics. Maybe this is their political strategy or generosity. But we need to think about whether this strategy is realistic and timely.

How should we view Awami League's declaration of 'another war'? 
It is true that after August 5, a large number of violent incidents have been avoided. The credit for this should be given to BNP and other parties. But people want to see not only Awami League leaders and workers, but also Awami League as a party on trial. No one is talking about revenge here. Talking about justice. There is no tolerant politics by giving concessions without trying the criminals. Therefore, the people of the country cannot accept the liberal attitude of the political parties towards the Awami League. In the July Revolution, individuals and groups collectively committed crimes against humanity. The Awami League as an organization will have to face justice for this collective crime. If political parties cannot understand the public's attitude, they will lose their place in the political arena. 

Recent history shows that the fascist parties involved in the genocide were not able to return to politics. Not only in Germany or Italy, but also in African and Latin American countries, authoritarian regimes were established at different times. Most of them had to face justice later. 

Accordingly, the Awami League is not supposed to be able to return to politics. If everything goes on as usual and what Dr. Yunus is saying is implemented, most of the party's leaders, many bureaucrats and police officers who served during the Awami League period will be found guilty of genocide. Headline_English: To what extent is disability being taken into account in education policy?
Content_Enlish:
What teaching methods and strategies can be taken into account for students with disabilities, it needs to be included in teacher training. Even how the student or the student's classmates will behave towards the student with disabilities, should be included in the training. Tariq Manjur has written about why disability should be taken into account in the education policy and education system

Disability has never been seriously considered in the education policy and education system of Bangladesh. There is no guidance in the teacher's manual on how a disabled student should take lessons and how to express it in an alternative way. It was recommended to take all types of disabilities into account in the new curriculum in the name of integrated education, and some proposals were also made in this regard. But they are not sufficient, and not even very clear.

The 2010 Education Policy also did not make any proposals on the education method or evaluation process for children with disabilities; there was not even a definition of disability. It was only said that disability-friendly arrangements will be ensured in schools for using toilets and facilitating mobility. In reality, it has not been possible to ensure even this minimum right for them.

Broadly speaking, every person has some kind of disability. For example, some people cannot mix with others or feel uncomfortable speaking. On the other hand, children from ethnic minorities experience a crisis in linguistic communication after being admitted to school. However, in our country, students with disabilities are mainly understood as students with visual impairment, hearing impairment, physical impairment and intellectual disability. Measures need to be taken according to the type and degree of each disability.

A student who cannot hear cannot understand the general teaching of the school by listening to it. The sign language suitable for him is unknown even to the school teachers. Again, a student who cannot see cannot express it in writing. However, such a student also has to write answers in a notebook and get marks. In board exams, there is an opportunity to appoint dictation writers for students who are visually impaired or unable to write. But in reality, proper evaluation of the student is not possible in this way.

The National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) printed Braille books for the first time in 2017 for visually impaired students. Earlier, some Braille books were provided through the Department of Social Services. In addition, the NCTB website has multimedia talking books for each class. These books can be read by ear or by sight. But teachers are not seen using these books in class activities. Apart from that, teachers do not take any kind of disability into account when writing on the board or explaining reading.

What can be the teaching methods and strategies considering disabled students, it is necessary to include it in teacher training. Even how the behavior of the disabled student or the student's classmates will be towards the disabled student, it is also necessary to include it in the training. Not only will the facilities for taking lessons and publishing be increased, but even in the evaluation of such students, the opportunity to use alternative media according to their disabilities should be provided. It is important to remember that it is not possible to establish a society without discrimination by keeping any student outside the society.

Teachers do not really have an idea of ​​how to integrate disabled students into general education. They do not receive training in this regard. Even the teacher assistants do not have any idea about this. As a result, even if there is a disabled student in the classroom, the teacher ends up teaching in his own way. However, if he shows the main part by writing it down along with speaking, or if he also tells it orally along with writing and drawing, the class activities can be more enjoyable for all the students. He can give students the opportunity to cooperate with each other in learning, expressing, and even evaluating.

Textbooks written in Braille also have problems. These books may provide models of cell structures or atoms. But for ease of understanding, descriptions of the pictures are not provided. As a result, the concept of the pictures remains unclear to the student. The book needs to have detailed descriptions of these pictures or finger-friendly pictures. Mathematics books written in Braille are also difficult to understand due to mathematical symbols and other complications. It is not easy for visually impaired students to read and understand them. Information technology books do not teach the use of keyboards in computer education in a way that is suitable for the visually impaired. If this were done, ordinary students would also get additional benefits in using computers.

Educational stipends are given to disabled students every month. But the amount is not worth mentioning at all. Apart from this, a very limited number of students have come under the scope of this stipend. Service activities for the disabled are mainly conducted under the control of the Department of Social Services of the Ministry of Social Welfare. If the education plan of such students is taken under the Ministry of Education, it may be possible to include more disabled students in the education program.

There are eight government schools for speech and hearing impaired students and five for visually impaired students across the country. In these schools, only certain types of disabled people get the opportunity to study and receive vocational training. But these schools conflict with the inclusive concept of society. Because, all children belong to society and have to live their lives from birth to death as part of society. Therefore, all types of students, including disabled people, should be given the opportunity to study together in ordinary schools. Through this, everyone will learn to cooperate with each other and learn to live together in society.

Recently, the Bangladesh Computer Council is going to launch an online 'Braille Converter'. As a result, it will be possible for visually impaired students to convert any text into Braille and read it. In addition, there is software to make Bengali writing audible and to convert spoken words into writing. Sign language has also been standardized by the government initiative. It is hoped that new facilities will be added for students who are physically unable to write or walk, or who are intellectually disabled.

It is necessary to include in teacher training what teaching methods and techniques can be taken into account for disabled students. Even how his or the student's classmates will behave towards disabled students, should also be included in the training. Not only will the facilities for taking lessons and publishing them increase, but such students should also be given the opportunity to use alternative media according to their disabilities in the evaluation process. It is important to remember that it is not possible to establish a society without discrimination by leaving any student outside the society.

Headline_English: Why is Rampal power plant not being shut down?
Content_Enlish:
The interim government has decided to cancel unprofitable and unimportant projects taken for political reasons by the previous government. A list of 35 such projects has been prepared, which will be canceled, funding suspended or cost cut. The total cost of these projects is more than one lakh crore taka. 

Of the 35 projects that are going to be canceled or suspended, some are in the middle of work, some have just started work, some have not yet started work and some projects are at the approval stage. The government has said that the projects taken during the previous government are being canceled considering three aspects. These are - one. To what extent has the project been taken for the needs of the people. two. What will be the benefit from the project. three. Whether the project is harmful to the environment or not. (Prothom Alo, November 10, 2024). 

I welcome this decision by the interim government to cancel unnecessary, unprofitable and environmentally harmful projects. At the same time, I think that the three considerations on which projects under construction or planned are being canceled should also be applied to projects that have already started. 

Planning and Education Advisor Wahiduddin Mahmud's words are important in this regard. In a meeting with officials of the Planning Ministry on August 19, he said, "It is not necessary to keep the project if it is running. If the remaining money is spent, it will be profitable or a loss. This is economic rationality. If there is a loss, it is better to drop it. 

In this regard, if a project is unnecessary, if it is proven to be harmful from an environmental perspective, it is necessary to cancel it even after it is built. Because, the longer the harmful project continues to operate, the greater the damage will be. Rampal Power Plant is one such project, which is unnecessary on the one hand, and on the other hand, the economic and environmental impact of the harmful impact it will have on the Sundarbans is immeasurable. 

Rampal Power Plant is not essential to meet the country's electricity demand. In the country, about 40 percent of the production capacity of the power plants is idled and capacity charges are paid. Apart from that, the power plant is often partially or completely shut down due to technical faults and coal shortages. The National Committee for the Protection of Oil, Gas, Mineral Resources, Power and Ports, as well as many others, including Syeda Rizwana Hasan, the current government's environment, forest and climate change advisor, have said that the construction of the Rampal power plant is unnecessary, damaging the Sundarbans. 

She and her organization, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA), have opposed the construction of the Rampal power plant since 2012. She questioned why a polluting coal-based project like Rampal is needed even when the country has overcapacity in electricity. (Daily Star Online Bangla, July 6, 2021) 

Therefore, the environmental advisor clearly understands how harmful the Rampal power plant is to the Sundarbans. Now it is necessary to take steps to quickly shut down the power plant to protect the Sundarbans. It has already started to have a detrimental effect on the Sundarbans. Citing a report by the government organization Center for Environment and Geographic Information Services (CEGIS), news has been published that the wastewater from the power plant is being discharged into the Maidara and Pashur rivers of the Sundarbans without any treatment. 

According to this report by CEGIS, completed from February to April 2024, coal is being transported without being properly covered. The construction of coal storage sheds, coal stack yards and ash silos has not been completed as planned. As a result, the environment of the Sundarbans is being polluted and the amount of mercury, nitrates and phosphates in the river water has increased more than before. (New Age, November 2, 2024; Daily Star, November 10, 2024) 

This CEGIS, however, conducted an environmental survey of the Rampal power plant and ruled that the power plant was environmentally friendly. As a result, there are questions about how much the real picture of the pollution of the power plant will emerge in this organization's report. Even then, what has emerged in the report is quite worrying. 

Apart from the fallen dictatorship and its allies, the Rampal power plant was opposed by all political, social and cultural circles of the country at that time, including the National Committee for the Protection of Oil, Gas, Mineral Resources and Power and Ports, the National Committee for the Protection of the Sundarbans, various environmental organizations and many domestic and foreign independent experts. The then main opposition party BNP and the 20-party alliance also demanded the cancellation of the Rampal power plant. BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia gave a press conference in August 2016 and presented a picture of the negative impact of the Rampal power plant on the environment, economy and above all the Sundarbans. (BBC Bangla, 24 August 2016) 

The United Nations organization UNESCO also urged the government to withdraw from the construction of the Rampal power plant, which is harmful to the Sundarbans. But the government, desperate to protect India's strategic interests in exchange for support in power, built the Rampal power plant in an authoritarian manner, ignoring all public opinion. In this regard, Syeda Rizwana Hasan once said, ‘The Rampal power plant has no acceptance among the people, it has been imposed by force.’ (Prothom Alo, July 10, 2020) 

There is a kind of consensus within the country that the Rampal power plant is harmful to the Sundarbans. Like the previous government, the current government has no responsibility to look after India’s interests. Therefore, before further damage is done to the Sundarbans, the interim government should take the initiative to close the Rampal power plant and initiate the necessary legal process for it.

Headline_English: What needs to be done to develop artificial intelligence
Content_Enlish:
A large part of my day is spent using artificial intelligence (AI). 

That's why I don't want to be a ginger merchant and get news about ships, but now I have to because of the eco-system. 

The monthly subscription for these AI systems is quite expensive. A significant portion of the total global electricity consumption is spent on various data centers, where the use of AI-supported systems is increasing. 

As this use is increasing, it is becoming difficult to generate sufficient electricity through 'conventional' and 'traditional' methods. 

Now, experts believe that conventional electricity generation methods are not enough to meet this 'increased demand'. As a result, tech giants like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft are leaning towards purchasing modern and safe nuclear reactors. Shopping is going on in the nuclear market. 

I think that this step will create an opportunity to generate additional electricity, which can be sold to other data centers, in addition to meeting their own electricity needs. 

Research suggests that companies like Google could create a new business model by selling excess electricity generated from nuclear reactors. 

The shift towards modern nuclear power could have a positive impact on the environment, given the safety issues with traditional reactors. 

Although nuclear waste is a concern, it emits less carbon than electricity generated from fossil fuels. Modern technology has also made nuclear waste management safer and more efficient. 

Current nuclear reactors are built to much higher safety standards. Significant advances in nuclear technology have been made in the past few decades, making this energy source much safer than before, according to a document from the World Nuclear Association. 

Modern reactors have automated safety systems, improved core designs and ‘extended’ accident resistance. 

In addition, strict regulatory policies and regular ‘inspections’ further ensure the safety of these power plants. 

Although modern nuclear reactors are much safer, their installation and operation are complex and expensive. 

In addition, raising public awareness and achieving social acceptance are also major challenges. Close cooperation between government, industry and researchers is needed to address these challenges. 

Experts believe that this relationship between AI and safe power generation will deepen in the future. Advanced nuclear technologies, such as small modular reactors (SMRs) and fusion reactors, are creating the possibility of safer and more efficient power generation in the future. 

This increased use of artificial intelligence and the trend of tech giants towards advanced and safe nuclear power to meet the ‘huge’ amount of electricity required for it is a significant change. 

This move is not only to meet their own electricity needs, but also to usher in a new era in the overall energy sector. 

‘AI is the new oil’, or ‘AI is the new electricity’. In that sense, this AI is synonymous with our new energy as well as AI for energy.

Headline_English: How will the Democrats turn around now?
Content_Enlish:
As the shock of Donald Trump’s victory slowly becomes a reality, analysts and politicians are pondering the implications of this shock. They are wondering how far the United States’ influence on global politics will extend in the future. Understanding how a divisive and “unqualified” candidate like Trump won again has become crucial for Democrats. 

Because the question is starting to arise: Have Democrats gone too far left and lost the support of the majority of middle-class Americans? Or has the moderate neoliberalism pursued by Democratic presidents since Bill Clinton failed, and this failure has created a demand for change among Americans? 

In my opinion, the answer is clear: 40 years of neoliberalism have given the United States unprecedented inequality, stagnation in the middle income level (worse at the bottom), and a decline in average life expectancy (especially through an increase in “deaths due to depression”). 

Before the election, the Biden administration appeared to be in a strong position, especially compared to other G7 countries. But that wasn’t enough to win over voters. Americans have not forgotten that the Democrats (under Clinton) had liberalized the financial sector. When workers and homeowners who lost their jobs in the Great Recession paid the price, the Democrats (under Barack Obama) helped bail out the banks. However, that did not change the fate of the people much. 

The only real difference between the Democrats and the Republicans is that only the Democrats claimed to feel the pain of the people who were affected. But in the end, Americans sadly voted for Donald Trump. 

Trump’s first term and his 2024 re-election campaign have made it clear that he has no intention of implementing policies that ordinary Americans need. Trump is essentially in favor of tax breaks for the wealthy and large corporations. He also wants to repeal Obamacare (the Affordable Care Act) and impose high tariffs on imported goods. This tariff would essentially impose an additional tax on American consumers and businesses. 

In addition, this tax system could encourage corruption. Because this system would give special benefits to the wealthy who poured money into Trump's election campaign. Other countries could also impose tariffs in response to Trump's increased import taxes. This would hurt American jobs. Overall, Trump's policies would be more effective in benefiting the rich and powerful than ordinary people. 

Trump would run up huge budget deficits. This would lead to higher interest rates and reduce investment in America's future. If Trump and Republican members of Congress repeal the Inflation Reduction Act (which includes a provision to lower the price of prescription drugs) and Obamacare, the cost of healthcare for Americans would increase even more. This is worse than neoliberalism. Because neoliberalism at least talked about competitive and undistorted markets. On the other hand, ‘Trumponomics’ is a misguided capitalism, run by the powerful and for the powerful. Money is paramount. 

Americans have lost faith in their institutions. They have lost the belief that government works for the people. This is the result of the last 45 years of Republican (and neoliberal Democratic) campaigns. To illustrate this situation, one can quote Ronald Reagan’s famous quote, ‘The nine most dangerous words in the English language are: I’m from the government and I’m here to help.’ 

Cultural clashes or ‘culture wars’ played a significant role in Trump’s victory. His campaign successfully spread the idea that Democrats are over-emphasizing gender, race and other social issues while most Americans are struggling to survive. Many voters believe that Trump will reverse, if not slow, the long-standing social class divide. They support him in the belief that he will protect the traditional American social order. 

Like other nationalists, Trump blames America’s problems on external factors such as illegal immigration or “unfair” trade. While it is true that these issues have not been handled well; Trump’s proposed solutions will ultimately be harmful to the US economy and the world. 

It is not clear how much Trump voters understand this. But it seems that most of them have been drawn to Trump’s political drama. They wanted to send a message of their dissatisfaction, and they delivered that message by voting for Trump. 

There is a clear message for Democrats in this. That is, Democrats must abandon their old policies and adopt the kind of people-friendly policies of the era of Franklin D. Roosevelt and Lyndon B. Johnson. They need to envision a society where 
everyone is given education and opportunity. Where businesspeople compete to create better products instead of exploiting people. 

We need to understand that we have moved beyond the industrial age and are now entering an economy where services, knowledge, innovation, and public service are more important. The new economy means new rules and a new role for government—Democrats need to understand this truth.

Headline_English: China has bet on the wrong horse
Content_Enlish:
China's rapid economic growth over the past three decades, coupled with its growing military might, has transformed the country from a regional power to a global power. 

The 2023 annual report of the US Department of Defense acknowledged that China is the only rival to the US that has the ability to reshape the international order. China has solidified its status as a great power. 

At the heart of China's national rejuvenation strategy is the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). It is an initiative to expand global connectivity and trade to ensure China's sustainable growth and development. The strategy is consistent with China's concept of Military-Civil Integration (MCF). The idea is that military capabilities will grow in parallel with economic development. 

The BRI project consists of six economic corridors. The main corridor among these is the Bangladesh-China-India-Myanmar (BCIM) corridor, which later became known as the China-Myanmar Economic Corridor (CMEC). The CMEC corridor extends from China's Yenan province to the deep sea port of Chakpyu in Myanmar. Through this, China has gained direct access to the Bay of Bengal. 

The corridor has rescued China from the 'Malacca dilemma'. This corridor is important for ensuring China's energy supply and natural resource logistics. It is very important for China's economic stability. The CMEC corridor is also important for China's 'String of Pearls' strategy. Because the core of the String of Pearls strategy is to create a network around the Indian Ocean. This strategy is also consistent with China's 'Two Oceans' (Pacific and Indian Ocean) strategy. 

In this context, no matter who is in power in Myanmar, it is essential for China to keep the country under China's influence. However, recent events suggest that China has bet on the wrong horse in Myanmar. 

Historically, China has maintained its influence in Myanmar by supporting ethnic insurgent groups in the border areas along with the country’s military. 

There is the question of the government’s legitimacy, but the biggest issue is that the junta government’s economic policies have made it difficult for the people to survive. In 60 years, the Myanmar military has become a source of disrespect even to the country’s majority ethnic Bamar. 
For decades, ethnic armed groups have been fighting the Myanmar military and the Burmese army for autonomy. China brokered a ceasefire agreement between the two sides to ensure that their business environment in Myanmar remained stable and investment was protected. 

After the military coup in Myanmar in 2021, China initially refrained from openly supporting the Myanmar junta government. However, as the Spring Revolution in Myanmar gained momentum and the battlefield changed, China's position began to change. 

The start of the joint operation of Myanmar's ethnic armed groups (Operation 1027) led to a shift in the balance of power there. The Myanmar army lost a large part of the territory in northern Shan State to the rebels. 

Similarly, the Arakan Army (AA) in Rakhine State took control of a large area. They occupied the area around the strategically important Chakpyu port. In Kachin State, the Kachin Independence Army also achieved unprecedented success. 

In this reality, China changed its position and began to openly support the Myanmar junta government. China's change in position on the Myanmar issue began with the visit of the country's Foreign Minister Wang Yi to Naypyidaw in August of this year. We saw its final form in November with the visit of Myanmar's military junta Min Aung Hlaing to China. This was his first visit since the coup. 

China has also put pressure on the armed groups of the Taung National Liberation Army (TNLA) and the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) in their border provinces. It has closed the border and hindered their trade. China has demanded that these rebels avoid contact with Myanmar's exiled National Unity Government and its armed group, the People's Democratic Forces. 

China has also allowed the recruitment of private security forces such as the mercenary group Bhagnana Group to protect their investments. 

Supporting the Myanmar junta government will ultimately be counterproductive for Myanmar. The fall of Myanmar's military government is inevitable, it is only a matter of time. Many ethnic armed groups in regions that do not share a border with China, such as the Arakan Army, the Karen National Union, the Karenni Nationalities Force and the Chin group, are outside China's direct influence. 

In addition, armed groups in the border areas, the TNLA and the MNDAA, are also continuing to fight the military despite the ceasefire agreement. 

In addition, these groups believe that true autonomy and security under the Myanmar junta government is impossible. They believe that only a federal democratic Myanmar can guarantee that. 

According to unconfirmed sources, the ethnic armed groups and the national unity government have reached a consensus on this issue. Due to geopolitical sensitivities, they are not making a formal announcement on this issue right now. 

The Myanmar junta government is now widely unpopular among the people of the country. 

There is the question of the government's legitimacy, but the biggest issue is that the junta government's economic policies have made it difficult for the people to survive. In 60 years, the Myanmar army has become a source of disrespect even to the country's majority Bamar ethnic group. 

In contrast, the national unity government has taken a realistic approach towards China. They have promised to protect Chinese investment. For this reason, they have given a 10-point ‘Position on China’. 

The tough stance that the US Donald Trump administration will take on China can benefit China by increasing its allies internationally. The legitimacy of Myanmar’s national unity government is much higher than that of the junta government. As a result, if China allies with the national unity government, it will greatly enhance their global image and reputation.

Headline_English: What will Trump's Iran and Gaza policy be like?
Content_Enlish:
Donald Trump’s victory was no surprise to the people of the Middle East. The governments of the region had already prepared themselves, assuming that Trump would win. They had completed all preparations to work with Trump a month before his inauguration. 

However, the situation in the Middle East during Trump’s first term is completely different from the situation in the Middle East today. 

The biggest changes during this period have been in Iran and Gaza. 

Let’s start with Iran. Trump canceled the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA, also known as the Iran Deal) that was agreed to limit Iran’s nuclear program during his first term. At that time, the Iranian president was the moderate Hassan Rouhani. 

He was replaced in 2021 by the ultra-conservative Ebrahim Raisi. But now a relatively moderate leader has come to the presidency of Iran. He is Masoud Pezeshkian. 

Before Pezeshkian took office, Iran took the initiative to improve relations with its Arab neighbors. In March 2023, Iran and its main regional rival, Saudi Arabia, restored diplomatic relations. This unexpected and highly significant agreement is part of an ongoing Chinese initiative aimed at reducing tensions and promoting stability in the region. 

Another change is that Iran’s relations with China and Russia have deepened (and they have improved their relations with each other). Trump was always hostile towards China and Iran during his first term; although he had a kind of “bromance” with Russian President Vladimir Putin. 

But while Trump has shown a willingness to coordinate directly with Putin to end the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, he will have to adjust to the dynamics of the new relationship this time. 

However, reducing hostilities in the Middle East will not be easy. On October 7, 2023, Israel launched an operation in Gaza in retaliation for a Hamas attack. The attack has so far caused many civilian deaths, displacements, and suffering. 

The US and France have managed to broker a ceasefire in Lebanon, and Israel’s campaign against Hezbollah is likely to end before Trump is sworn in. 

However, it is difficult to say at this point whether a peace deal in Lebanon will make it easier or harder to reach a similar deal in Gaza. Trump’s position on many issues is unclear. 

US President Joe Biden is relatively easy to understand. He and his Secretary of State, Antony Blinken, share a certain degree of Zionist ideological leanings. That is why the Biden administration has called on Israel to stop its campaign and threatened to cut off aid to Israel if the situation for civilians in Gaza does not improve; while at the same time, it has continued to justify Israel’s actions and supply it with weapons. 

Even after the ceasefire in Lebanon, the Biden administration is reportedly planning to sell Israel $680 million in weapons. 

Trump has also shown a similar tendency to prioritize Israel’s interests. During his first administration, he broke with decades of policy by moving the US embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem; recognized Israeli sovereignty over the occupied Golan Heights; and cut funding to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA), the main program that helps Palestinian refugees. 

Trump also initiated the Arab-Israeli “normalization process.” Through this, Israel signed the so-called Abraham Accords with the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan in 2020-21. 

Trump plans to include a large number of pro-Israel figures in his new administration. However, given Trump’s lack of specific ideological commitments to the Gaza war, his goal is clear. That is, to make a deal. But it is understood that any deal will likely be detrimental to the Palestinians. This is not only because of the pro-Israeli stance of the US administration, but also because the agreements brokered by outsiders usually prioritize the existing balance of power; and this clearly favors Israel. 

The Palestinians do not receive much support from Arab countries either. Of course, Saudi Arabia has declared that it will not establish diplomatic relations with Israel unless an independent Palestinian state is established within the 1967 borders. But the Abraham Accords, which are proposed to normalize relations between Israel and Arab countries, have not yet collapsed, despite pressure. 

According to Israeli journalist Barak Ravid, Trump may be harboring resentment towards Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Because Netanyahu hastily congratulated Biden after Trump lost the 2020 election. This angered Trump. It is not at all impossible for Trump to hold that resentment, having repeatedly promised to target enemies. 
But if Trump makes a new deal, it may not be very good for Israel either. According to Israeli journalist Barak Ravid, Trump may be harboring resentment towards Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Because Netanyahu hastily congratulated Biden after Trump lost the 2020 election. This angered Trump. It is not impossible for Trump, who has repeatedly promised to target enemies, to hold that resentment. 

The most likely scenario is that the current war ends and the situation returns to the state that existed before October 7. However, due to Trump’s instability and pro-Israeli stance, many in the region are worried that Trump may allow Israel to occupy parts of the West Bank or approve Jewish settlements in Gaza. 

Trump has tried to make a pro-Israel deal before. In January 2020, he released his Middle East peace plan. He called that deal “the best deal of the century.” But in the end, that deal failed completely. 

The problem is that the Palestinians will react harshly whenever they see that a two-state solution is no longer possible. So even if Trump makes a deal to return to the status quo before October 7, that deal won't last long.

Headline_English: Have the students been able to return to their desks?
Content_Enlish:
Two major incidents of violence took place in educational institutions in two consecutive weeks. On November 20, students of Dhaka College and City College clashed in the Science Lab area of ​​the capital. Within three days, on November 24, the government Shaheed Suhrawardy College was attacked and in response, Dr. Mahbubur Rahman Molla College was attacked the next day. At least 60-70 people were injured in these clashes and attacks. Property worth crores of taka was damaged. 

The way one student attacked another student with a stick and rod is unbearable to watch. It is also unacceptable considering their age. In the reality of the July uprising, the police are making mistakes in determining tactics in many cases. Students are also unable to control themselves in many cases. Classes and exams have started in colleges and universities. But looking at the overall situation, it does not seem that students have been able to return to their desks at all. 

Neither of the two incidents was such that the conflict could have escalated this far. The incident that took place in the Science Lab area on the 20th began the day before. That incident was trivial. Some students of Dhaka College got into a fight with City College students over boarding a bus. If there had been tolerance among the students, the fight might not have happened. As a result, some students of City College vandalized two buses of Dhaka College the next day. Later, students of Dhaka College also joined forces and attacked City College. There were clashes between the two sides in stages. 

And the incident on the 24th began on November 18 with the death of a student at the National Medical College in Dhaka. The student who died of dengue was Dr. Mahbubur Rahman Molla College. Alleging that he died due to wrong treatment, students of that college and some other colleges surrounded the National Medical College and protested on the 20th. Later, the hospital authorities formed an investigation committee into the death. If proper investigation had been taken, the incident could have ended here. But that afternoon, students from nearby colleges, including Suhrawardy, taking the side of the hospital, beat up some students from Mahbubur Rahman Molla College. As a result, there were widespread vandalism and looting in both the hospital and the college on the 24th and 25th. 

Now the question is, why are the students becoming so intolerant? Who can guarantee that there will be no more violence or attacks on educational institutions in the future? In this situation, it is necessary to understand what the role of educational institutions, teachers and students will be. If educational institutions are unstable, it can have an impact on the overall education sector. Even the reform work of the state can be hampered. We have to decide what to do in this regard by keeping the students in trust. 

Educational institutions have been unstable for six to seven months due to the anti-discrimination student movement and the fall of the government. The chain of relations between teachers and students has been broken in many cases. So far, students have not been able to come out of the trend of demanding demands. Teachers have not been able to fully trust them or make them focus on class and exams. Students themselves consider themselves opponents in some cases. There is also a dilemma among the concerned people about the way to resolve the mismanagement that has been going on in the education sector from the institutional level to the state level for a long time. 

The most important thing is that the students have not been able to come out of the mental stress. The consequences of the major incidents that they have witnessed were not comfortable for them. In 2018, they took to the streets demanding safe roads. That logical demand was stopped through state terrorism. Then in 2020, they were confined to their homes for more than a year and a half due to the attack of the Covid pandemic. As a result, no steps were taken to make up for the deficit in their studies. And this July-August experience is truly horrific! A direct encounter with bullets and blood! 

These incidents have definitely caused mental damage. But no institutional or state initiative has been taken to remedy it. To be honest, the need for mental care has not been taken into consideration at all. Some universities, including Dhaka University, have arranged counseling. However, it is very limited. Most students have remained outside this program. 

Judging by the role of students in the last few months, it seems that they are not satisfied with the existing state and system of education. They are also concerned about the educational environment in schools, colleges and universities in the country. They believe that education reform is an important part of state reform. Therefore, before going to the study table, they want a change in the existing education system. They also understand that there is no immediate solution to this. But at least they want an assurance of reform. 

The Dhaka University administration has reduced the problem by taking quick measures in some cases. For example, the student politics that has ruined the educational environment in the university due to the tail-end student politics has been banned. It has been possible to establish discipline in the residential halls by quickly solving the problem of allocating rooms and enrolling students. Considering the capacity and situation, various departments have started class and examination step by step. Apart from this, each department has held discussions with students in its own way to improve student-teacher relations and resolve the institutional crisis. Central instructions have been given for the same purpose, so that each department forms a committee with teachers, student advisors and students separately. 

No student is in favor of violence. If the law and order situation in the country improves, students themselves will want to stay away from conflicts, if justice is guaranteed, they will not want to take the law into their own hands. But first of all, these students need to be brought into confidence. The teachers of the institution must come forward in this regard. Students should be listened to, problems should be seen as problems and work together to solve them.

Headline_English: What will happen in Syria now that dictator Bashar has fallen?
Content_Enlish:
The word ‘historic’ is appropriate here. Because the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime has come. What has happened after more than 50 years of brutal dictatorship and 13 years of civil war and endless suffering is a turning point. 

The Syrian people, at least the majority of them, are celebrating today. Let them enjoy this moment. This celebration is theirs. This celebration is reminiscent of the jubilation that followed the fall of Saddam Hussein in Iraq and Muammar Gaddafi in Libya. But these memories are a warning and a threat to us. 

The warning is that if the sudden collapse of Assad’s authoritarian structure turns into uncontrollable chaos, this joy of the people could very soon turn to tears. And the threat is that the political and military vacuum that has now been created in Syria could be taken over by vested interests who are more interested in power and revenge than justice and reconciliation. 

Revenge is a ‘food’ in Syria that is served hot and hot, and it is now back on the ‘menu’. 

The campaign to overthrow Assad began in 2011 with a popular uprising in Daraa, southwest Syria. In that context, the successful advance of the militant group Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), which established a base in the northwest of Idlib, and the fall of the capital Damascus with the support of the people have closed a chapter. In that sense, it can be called a people’s revolution. 

However, no one can yet say what the future of Syria will be under HTS leader Abu Muhammad al-Jolani. 

Once a militant and most wanted terrorist linked to al-Qaeda, Jolani has now established himself as a national liberation hero. But the HTS he leads in Idlib has a record of human rights abuses and dictatorship. 

As Jolani’s forces advance south, many Syrians have flocked to the HTS banner. But other groups (with different goals and objectives) are also trying to capitalize on the crisis. These include a coalition of Kurdish-led nationalist militias in the northeast; the US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces; Turkish-backed rebel groups (collectively known as the Syrian National Army) and opposition groups in the south. While they share the STS’ hatred of Assad, they disagree on many other issues. 

Before the war, Syria was multi-ethnic, multi-religious, tolerant and secular. Can that old Syria be rebuilt now? Is Jolani fit to lead the country? Or will someone else be able to prevent this chaos and division? No one has the answers yet. 

The US, Britain and European countries are equally surprised by the situation in Syria. It is a major intelligence failure. But the West has a long record of failure in the Syrian war. They have largely looked on silently as the events here, such as terrorism, war crimes and the use of chemical weapons, have been witnessed. The West is still a silent spectator. 
Assad’s prime minister, Mohammad Ghazi Jalali, has declared that he will not flee like Assad. Instead, he wants to stay in his place and work with the rebels. His words are brave. Let’s hope he can stick to his word. 

The challenges ahead are truly daunting. More than 300,000 people have died in the civil war. Some say the number could be double that. 

Nearly 100,000 people have disappeared or disappeared since 2011. Where are they? The grim reckoning will now begin. Almost half the population, or 12 million people, have been displaced. Thousands have been detained without trial. They have been tortured. 

Now the detention camps are emptying. A wave of physically and mentally wounded and vengeful people is returning to a shattered society. Millions of refugees in Turkey and Jordan may try to return home together. The threat of humanitarian and security catastrophe lies ahead. 

Foreign intervention has been a key part of the country’s crisis since the start of the Syrian war. Assad’s fall is a major defeat for his main backers, Russia and Iran. 

In 2015, when then-US President Barack Obama prioritized the fight against terrorism over supporting pro-democracy forces in Syria, Vladimir Putin entered Syria. The Russian air force and Iran’s Revolutionary Guards helped keep Assad in power. In return, Putin gained military bases and strategic advantages. Now all of this is at stake. 

The fall of Syria is another major blow to Iran. Israel has weakened Hezbollah since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023. And Hezbollah was a major supporter of Assad. This has further jeopardized Iran's position. 

It is reported that the Iranian embassy in Damascus was attacked, and its diplomats fled. But Russia and Iran will not give up easily. They will try to shape the new situation in their own way. And this may not be good for the Syrian people. 

The same can be said for Israel. In its campaign against Hamas and Iranian-backed groups, Israel has repeatedly bombed sites in Syria, including Damascus, that it claims are targets of Iran and Hezbollah. 
Tehran believes that Israel had a hand in Assad's downfall. Now Israel is worried about a collapsed state on its border. They are worried about who is getting hold of Assad's chemical weapons and how much of a threat Islamist militants pose. 

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan may have given the HTS the green light to launch an attack after they rejected Assad's proposal to create a buffer zone. He is concerned about the Kurdish 'threat'. So he may send more troops to the border. 

But did Erdogan want to overthrow Assad's regime and create chaos in all of Syria? Perhaps he can explain how this change could work in Turkey's interests.

No help can be expected from Arab countries either. A year ago, Assad returned from the Arab League conference, having cleared his international reputation. Many, including Saudi King Mohammed bin Salman, welcomed him to the Arab League.

Headline_English: Playgrounds are essential for health and well-being.
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh. Dhaka has developed into a populous city by combining modernity with tradition. Dhaka is particularly important as the political, economic and cultural center of the country. But due to the development and rapid urbanization of the city, the lack of playgrounds has become a significant problem. Playgrounds are not only places for sports and entertainment; they play an important role in maintaining physical and mental health, building social relationships and preserving cultural heritage. The reasons why we need playgrounds are, 

1. Health and well-being: The role of sports in maintaining physical health is immense. Regular physical activity such as sports protects people from diseases such as heart disease, diabetes and obesity. The lack of playgrounds for children in Dhaka is causing them physical health problems. Children become housebound if they do not get the opportunity to play in the field, which has a negative impact on their physical and mental development. Various studies have shown that regular sports play a helpful role in the physical health and development of children. Problems such as physical illness, mental stress and anxiety are increasing among children due to the lack of playgrounds. 

2. Social relations: The state of social relations in this busy Dhaka is deplorable. Playgrounds are not just for playing but also for building social relationships. Playing with friends, participating in local tournaments and socializing with the community builds bridges between young people. Lack of playgrounds is increasing loneliness and social isolation among the younger generation, which can create instability in society. Playgrounds are also important in establishing social justice and equality. People from different backgrounds come together on the playground and they build friendships with each other, which increases the unity of the society. 

3. Importance of Mental Health: Mental well-being is very important for physical well-being. Sports are very important from a psychological perspective. Sports reduce stress, increase confidence and improve problem-solving skills. In the current situation of Dhaka, the stress level of youth is increasing. Various social, economic and political challenges are putting pressure on them. If adequate playgrounds are not provided for them, it can have a detrimental effect on mental health. Sports, especially team-based sports, create a sense of cooperation and harmony among people, which is essential for mental well-being. 

4. Development of Sports Talent: There are many potential athletes in Dhaka city, who are unable to develop their talents due to lack of proper opportunities. Due to lack of playgrounds, there is no opportunity for competitive play, which is preventing the development of future sports stars. It is very important to produce talented players in the country's sports field. It is necessary to produce more players to participate in sports competitions at the international level, and for this, the importance of the field is immense. 

5. Culture and Tradition: Sports are not just physical activities; they are a part of our culture. Various local tournaments and festivals held in playgrounds represent the unity and culture of the society. The development of this culture is also being hampered due to the lack of adequate playgrounds in Dhaka. Local sports events and traditions help in instilling cultural values ​​among the youth. There is a danger of losing this tradition and culture due to lack of playgrounds. 

6. Infrastructure Development: The infrastructure development of Dhaka is limited only to the construction of buildings and roads. However, the construction of playgrounds is also very important for the balanced development of the city. Creating playgrounds in every residential area and neighborhood will increase the quality of citizen life. In addition, if the fields are developed using modern technology, they can be more effective. Adequate infrastructure and well-equipped playgrounds will support the development of the city. 

Analysts and policymakers need to think about what solutions and initiatives to take in this situation. The government and local administration should take effective initiatives to address the shortage of playgrounds in Dhaka city. It is important to allocate funds for the construction of playgrounds as part of urban planning and ensure public participation. If private organizations also cooperate in the construction of playgrounds through sponsorship, it can be a coordinated initiative. The importance of sports should be given to the local community by increasing awareness. The importance of playgrounds needs to be highlighted to everyone to ensure the balanced development of the city and the well-being of the young generation.

Headline_English: People are looking for relief, how can they find it?
Content_Enlish:
The kind of chaos that usually occurs after a mass uprising is no exception in Bangladesh. The problem is that if this situation continues for a long time, the frustration among the people will continue to grow. The first and foremost duty of any government after coming to power is to provide relief to the people. People should feel that this government is their government. 

Let's start with commodity prices. In the recent past, one of the driving forces behind all the mass uprisings in the world has been the rise in commodity prices. Along with the lack of good governance. The Arab Spring began with the suicide of Tunisian vegetable seller Muhammad Bouazizi. Basically, fed up with police torture, he set himself on fire; the picture of his burning body was published in the world media. The fire broke out instantly. The gunpowder was ready, so his suicide ignited the fire. 

High inflation, lack of employment, mismanagement and corruption formed the basis of our July-August mass uprising. People's anger was especially extreme towards the law enforcement agencies; it was towards everyone involved in the government, from public administration to everyone. As a result, it didn't take long for the fire to spread like wildfire. 

The point is, people want relief. If this were the case, who would be in the government or what their political intentions are, it doesn't matter that much. The main reason why Sheikh Hasina managed to get by despite holding one-sided elections in 2014 and 2018 was economic and social stability. At that time, Bangladesh had high growth, there was corruption, and inflation was around 6 percent. The most important thing is that there was a kind of stability in the macroeconomics. It was possible to do a lot more by using that stability, which didn't happen. Despite the political divisions, there was a kind of stability in society. 

The stability of the macroeconomics began to be destroyed during Covid; then, when the Russia-Ukraine war broke out in 2022, the situation deteriorated seriously. Along with this, news of an increase in bank defaults and major corruption began to be published in various ways. People started hearing about incredible corruption and looting. These government-sponsored corruption and looting incidents angered people. At that time, a kind of uncertainty was created among people. Many people even asked journalists whether it would be safe to keep money in banks. Lack of good governance, lack of democracy, lack of justice, the government's repressive behavior and stubborn attitude, the behavior of the police like party cadres, and the arbitrariness of the government party people - all these created the background for the mass uprising in July-August. 

But the first problem is that the high inflation that has been talked about so much for so long is still ongoing. There is no sign of liberation from that tradition. Bangladesh Bank has taken a strict stance in principle. But in a country like Bangladesh, it is not possible to reduce inflation through monetary policy or the central bank's actions alone. For that, a coordinated effort is needed. 

It is known that floods in August and then heavy rains will damage crops, but were there any special preparations for that? Has any initiative been taken to further open up imports by determining in advance when there may be a supply shortage in the market? Even domestic poultry traders do not want the government to allow eggs to be imported. They have the same lame argument in their mouths, that if the domestic industry is imported, it will harm the domestic industry; the plight of the people cannot melt their hearts. 

They take this position even after the price of eggs has risen to 180 taka per dozen. The government has of course allowed imports. But when it comes to our necks, we are making decisions. We cannot take action in advance. The price of eggs has indeed come down in three to four days; but the suffering of these few days will remain in the minds of people; especially low-income people. The price of fish and meat is already high, and the price of vegetables is also high during heavy rains—in this reality, their precious jewel was eggs. But the price of those eggs rising to 180 taka per dozen is like a kick in the stomach for them. 

Everything in the country had become vestigial in the hands of a handful of groups. The fact that the egg import ban is still in place means that those groups still exist. It is not that they will suddenly vanish into thin air. But the question is how much capacity does the current interim government have to change this system? 

This is the state of the market. Every day, some party or group is protesting and struggling with various demands in the capital. They are even entering the secretariat. The main problem is that due to these protests and struggles, the suffering of the people has reached its peak. There is no order left on the roads. Traffic jams have reached an extreme level. In this situation, a sense of annoyance is being created among the people. The suffering on the roads has reached an extreme level. There was suffering before, but there was a kind of order among the irregularities, which broke down after August 5. The work of bringing order there is not being done as quickly as it should have been. 

Another issue is the violence of autorickshaws. Autorickshaws are now plying on almost all the roads of the capital. These autorickshaws seem to be increasing every day. It seems that Dhaka city is like an autorickshaw city; What this situation reveals is the high unemployment. Young people from villages are coming to the city without getting work or hoping for a good income and are driving autorickshaws. For so long, Dhaka was known as a city of rickshaws, now it may be the city of autorickshaws. 

Extortion in transportation is going on as before. As a result, just as before, a kilometer of road was rented for 10 taka or in some cases 20 taka, it is still happening. However, we know that there is no police violence on the roads. What has happened is that extortionists from one group have been replaced by extortionists from another group. If we cannot overcome these, people will not be able to feel the positive impact of the interim government. 

The 23-year dictatorship of President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali ended in 27 days in the Tunisian uprising. Then, in just 18 days of movement in Tahrir Square in Cairo, Egypt, the dictator of three decades, Hosni Mubarak, left power. It took 36 days to bid farewell to our 15-year fascist ruler. But the people of Tunisia and Egypt could not reap the fruits of the popular uprising. That is why it is very important to determine what to do after the uprising. 

The reality is that there is no such initiative that can bring relief and stability to the lives of the people. Instability was the main reason behind the failure of the Arab Spring. We must be careful about this. 

In addition, if political-economic good governance is not achieved, the anti-people administrative structure will remain intact. As this will increase the frustration among the people, the fallen ruling class can use this opportunity to conspire to create chaos.

Headline_English: Will the US's attitude towards Bangladesh change if Trump wins?
Content_Enlish:
Will the US election results have any impact on Bangladesh? The question arises because Bangladesh is currently running a special type of government. This special government needed Western support in the immediate aftermath of the coup. The interim government not only got it, but achieved it quite well. But whether it will have any impact after the US election is being analyzed at many levels. 

Finally, an X message from former president and Republican candidate Donald Trump suddenly fueled the discussion. In which he claimed that there is anarchy going on in Bangladesh now. A claim that the Awami League has been making for several months. Trump also claimed that there is oppression of minority communities in Bangladesh. Which is basically a claim of India, which sincerely dislikes this government in Bangladesh. Although the Indian and its media made the claim in a very loud tone, it did not attract global attention in the end. But after Trump's comments, an opportunity has been created to start a new discussion. 

Trump also dragged India into his X message. He said that India and its Prime Minister Narendra Modi are his good friends. This is also enough to cause major concerns for the future of Bangladesh. 

Earlier, Modi had raised the issue of persecution of minorities in Bangladesh in a phone call with current President Joe Biden. Modi also revealed it in his X message. However, Modi did not receive a positive response from the United States in this regard. Which actually disappointed him quite a bit. But there, Trump himself is confirming Modi's words. There is also talk about whether this is a new political polarization in the future of US-India relations on the Bangladesh issue. 

It is true that the words Trump said just six days before the US election were meant to attract the country's Hindu voters. Clearly, surveys say that this election will be a close one. Hindu voters are considered the second largest immigrant voting bloc in the United States after Mexicans. About 2.6 million voters are registered among the 5.2 million Hindu population living in the United States. Although they usually vote for Democrats, this survey says that Kamala Harris, despite being the first Indian-origin presidential candidate herself, is losing popularity among Hindu voters. A survey conducted by the Carnegie Endowment for International Foundation says that while Biden got 61 percent of the Hindu vote in the 2020 election, Kamala will get 4 percent less votes this time. 

The Democratic leaders have a long-standing relationship with Dr. Muhammad Yunus's government. Former President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary Clinton have personal relationships. The three top Democratic leaders who have the most influence on current President Joe Biden are Clinton, Hillary, and Barack Obama. So it is natural that Clinton and Hillary will play a role in ensuring all kinds of support for the Dr. Yunus administration. 
Therefore, it can be said that Trump made a trick to attract Hindu voters before the election. He may not be in this position after the election. The allegation of minority oppression in Bangladesh arose right after the fall of the government. There is a lot of mystery about Trump talking about it almost 3 months later. Many concerned say that Trump's statement was drafted by the USA Hindu Federation. They are the ones who told Trump about it. In exchange for a promise to vote for him in the next election. 

However, it should be remembered that Trump's election transition team is led by former President John F. Kennedy's nephew Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and former Congresswoman Tulsi Gabbard, who has switched from the Democratic party to support Trump this time, and is known as a right-wing Hindu extremist.
