Behind it was the determination of Bangabandhu's daughter Sheikh Hasina and the dream of a developed and prosperous Bangladesh. Today's Bangabandhu Tunnel is the staircase of that dream. 

Fulfillment of promises 

In the 2008 national election, Bangabandhu's daughter promised various developments around Chittagong. She understood very well that the development of the entire country would not be possible by leaving Chittagong behind. Later, Sheikh Hasina's government, with continuous forgiveness, took forward the construction of the Bangabandhu Tunnel step by step among various projects in Chittagong. Although it was not easy for the Prime Minister to cross this path. Despite repeatedly stumbling in various conspiracies, she moved forward with steel and determination. Then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina inaugurated this tunnel on October 28, 2023. 

About the beginning 

Immediately after the formation of the government in 2009, the daughter of the Father of the Nation took the initiative to build the Bangabandhu Tunnel. The bridge authority conducted a feasibility study for this. The project was approved at the meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on November 12, 2015. Earlier, a memorandum of understanding was signed between the Bangladesh government and the Chinese government. In June 2015, an agreement was signed with the Chinese contractor China Construction Communication Company Limited to implement the project for the construction of the tunnel. On October 14, 2016, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and Chinese President Xi Jinping jointly laid the foundation stone of the Bangabandhu Tunnel. Construction work officially began on February 24, 2019. On that day, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina inaugurated the boring of the northern tube (from Patenga to Anwara) of the tunnel. Its work was completed on August 2, 2020. Then, the boring of the second tube (from Anwara to Patenga) began on December 12, 2020. It was inaugurated by Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader. The excavation was completed on October 7, 2021. On October 28, 2023, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina inaugurated the Bangabandhu Tunnel. 

Tunnel at a glance 

The total length of the Bangabandhu Tunnel is 9.39 kilometers. The length of the main tunnel is 3.315 km. The length of the approach road is 5.35 km. It is a two-lane dual tunnel. It has an entrance near Chittagong Airport and Seaport, and a Navy College on the downstream side of the Karnaphuli River. Its exit is near the fertilizer factory at the Anwara end. (Source: Statement by Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader and website of the Bridges Department) 

Cost 

The construction of the Bangabandhu Tunnel began in February 2019. Although it was scheduled to be inaugurated in November 2020, the completion of the project was delayed several times, including the Covid-19 pandemic. The cost also increased. Initially, what was slightly less than 8,500 crore, increased to 10,689 crore 71 lakh taka. In October 2015, during the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to Dhaka, a loan agreement was signed for the construction of the Karnaphuli Tunnel. According to the agreement, China's Exim Bank provided 5,913 crore taka as a 20-year loan at two percent interest. The rest of the financing was provided by the Bangladesh government. 

Maintenance 

The Bangladesh Bridge Authority has signed a 5-year agreement with China Communications Construction Company for the maintenance of the Bangabandhu Tunnel. 

Firefighting system 

There is a state-of-the-art fire system inside the tunnel. There is a control room for monitoring the entire tunnel. From there, what is happening inside the tunnel will be monitored. If a fire occurs inside the tunnel, it can be controlled from the control room. 

Security 

More than 100 CCTV cameras have been installed in the tunnel for security. The speed of vehicles moving in the tunnel will not exceed 60 kilometers per hour initially. The tunnel cannot be crossed on foot. Similarly, motorcycles and three-wheeled vehicles will not be allowed to move through the tunnel. Vehicles heavier than the specified weight will not be allowed to pass through this tunnel. For this, a weighing scale has been built at the entrance of the tunnel. If the vehicle exceeds the measurement, it is not allowed to pass. 

Service Area 

There is a special part called 'Service Area' within the tunnel project. There are 30 bungalows, a VIP bungalow, motel mess, health center, field, tennis court, convention center, museum, swimming pool, mosque, helipad. 

Toll 

The main and only source of income for the tunnel is the vehicle toll. The bridge authority has set 12 vehicle classes and toll rates for crossing the tunnel. Of these, the toll for private cars is 200 taka, microbuses 250 taka. The toll for buses with 31 or less seats is 300 taka. The toll for buses with more than that is 400 taka. The toll for three-axle buses is 500 taka. The toll for trucks up to five tons is 400 taka. The toll for trucks from five to eight tons is 500 taka, and the toll for trucks from eight to 11 tons is 600 taka. On the other hand, the toll for three-axle trucks/trailers has been set at 800 taka. The toll for four-axle trucks/trailers has been set at 1,000 taka. If there are more than four axles, an additional toll of 200 taka will have to be paid per axle. The tunnel was opened to traffic on October 29. After this, a toll of 4.45 crore taka was collected from the tunnel in a month. On the other hand, the maintenance cost of the tunnel in the first month was 71 crore 4.2 lakh taka. 

Benefits of the tunnel 

Due to the Bangabandhu Tunnel, vehicles in Dhaka have reduced the distance towards Chittagong by about 15 kilometers due to the use of the Outer Ring Road-Patenga-Karnaphuli Tunnel, which was built on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway via Faujdarhat-Patenga and the Bandar Toll Road. In addition, the distance towards Cox's Bazar has been reduced by about 30 kilometers as the Karnaphuli Tunnel connects directly to Cox's Bazar Sadar via CUFL Ghat-Chatri Chaumuhani-Baanshkhali-Pekwar Magnama in Anwara Upazila. The government has built this tunnel with the aim of developing 'One City to Town' on the model of Shanghai, China. Industrialists and businessmen said that the economic activities of the Chittagong region have increased significantly due to the Bangabandhu Tunnel. Its impact on the overall economy of the country. It has created a bridge between the tourist city of Cox's Bazar and the hilly district of Bandarban, in addition to southern Chittagong, with other regions of the country. This has also affected the country's gross domestic product (GDP). 

Chittagong Chamber of Commerce sources said that businessmen have taken the initiative to build at least 100 industrial factories including garments, shipbuilding, edible oil, fish processing, steel, cement on the south bank of Karnaphuli using this tunnel. Several of these companies have also started production. At least 15 domestic and foreign companies have taken the initiative to invest in the China Economic Zone. Work on 4 new factories has also started in the Korean EPZ. Saad Musa Industrial Park is under construction half a kilometer from the tunnel. 

Roads and Highways Department (SOHD) sources say that 6.3 million vehicles will ply through the Karnaphuli Tunnel in the first year itself. The connecting roads will have to handle this pressure. Although the Shikalbaha-Anowara Road does not directly connect any divisional headquarters, it is gaining special importance considering its economic importance. It will be connected to Chittagong Port through a national highway, a regional road and the Karnaphuli Tunnel. In addition, the Dhaka-Chittagong-Cox's Bazar highway connects Matarbari Power Hub, Maheshkhali Deep Sea Port and Teknaf Land Port. The road that will go to Cox's Bazar through the Karnaphuli Tunnel will eventually extend to Kunming City in China through Myanmar. A power hub is being established in Chittagong under the master plan. 

Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Industrial City is being built on 33,805 acres of land in Mirsarai, about 10 kilometers from the Dhaka-Chittagong highway and 65 kilometers from the port city. It is being connected to the tunnel through a marine drive along the coast. The marine drive will later connect to the Matarbari Deep Sea Port. Investors say that this will save time and money as well as accelerate industrialization in the area. 

A BEPZA report last October revealed that an agreement has been signed to lease 5,271.47 acres of land to 152 companies in the Mirsarai Economic Zone. Of these, 26 companies have invested $1.67 billion in setting up factories on 410 acres of land. 52,238 people have already been employed. The total investment of 152 companies registered through lease agreements is $18.5 billion and employment will be provided to 775,228 people. 

It is expected that 539 plots will be allocated in this zone by 2030 and production will begin. This will increase the total investment several times. There will be direct employment for more than 1.5 million people. 

In addition, 38 factories of the Korean EPZ on 2,500 acres of land south of Karnaphuli will benefit from this tunnel. Now the Korean EPZ exports products worth $1.5 to $2 billion every year. 

The China Industrial Zone is next to the Korean EPZ. Although it was inaugurated on 753 acres of land in Anwara in 2016, land development work is underway. According to BEPZA, 371 factories are being set up in this zone, which can create employment for 50,000 people along with an investment of $18 billion. 

Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the Father of the Nation, dreamed of a golden Bengal free from hunger and poverty. His daughter, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, dreams of a developed and prosperous Bangladesh based on that dream. She is not limited to just dreams, Sheikh Hasina is moving forward with the determination to build a developed and prosperous country by 2041 through the development of various aspects of infrastructure, including information technology, through digital and smart Bangladesh. Bangabandhu Tolen is one of the fruits of his dream; which is changing the economy of the entire southeastern region, including Chittagong, with its touch.

Headline_English: Decision on Khaleda Zia's release application today
Content_Enlish:
A decision will be made on Tuesday (March 19) on the permanent release of BNP Chairperson Begum Khaleda Zia and her application for treatment abroad. This information was confirmed by Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Anisul Haque. 

On Monday (March 18), Anisul Haque said that in the letter, they are still seeking Khaleda Zia's permanent release. The decision will be made by Tuesday (March 19), InshaAllah. 

Earlier, on March 6, her younger brother Shamim Iskandar applied to the Home Ministry for Khaleda Zia's permanent release. Along with the application, permission was sought to take her abroad for treatment. It was sent to the Law Ministry to get an opinion on that application. 

The suspension period of Khaleda Zia's sentence has been extended eight times on two conditions. The condition was that she would receive treatment from her home in Dhaka and that she would not be able to travel outside the country during this time. 

The last time Khaleda Zia's sentence was suspended and her release period was extended for six months from September 24 last year. That period will end on March 24. If extended this time, Khaleda Zia's release period will be extended for the ninth time.

Regarding this, Khaleda Zia is suffering from various physical complications including arthritis, diabetes, kidney, liver, lung and eye problems. She has to be taken to the hospital sometimes when her illness worsens. She was also taken to Evercare Hospital on the night of March 13. She returned home the next day. 

Former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, who was convicted in two cases, was initially imprisoned. Khaleda Zia's sentence is being suspended by the government's executive order and she is being allowed to stay at home.

Headline_English: Nearly 3,500 Bangladeshis legalized in Greece in 2023
Content_Enlish:
3,405 Bangladeshi nationals have become the latest to become legal citizens. They applied for legalization at the beginning of last year. They were working illegally before that. They were granted legalization on December 31 last year based on their application. This information was reported by Info Immigration. 
This was done on the basis of the Athens-Dhaka Memorandum of Understanding. 
According to Info Immigration, as a condition, the applicant is required to submit a Bangladeshi passport valid for at least two years, proof of residence in Greece before February 9, 2022, and proof of job security if regularized. 
The rule is that irregular migrants must first register at the Bangladeshi Embassy in Athens and then apply on the Greek government's online platform. 
According to information provided by the Greek authorities, a total of 10,337 irregular Bangladeshis have applied for regularization in 2023 under the Memorandum of Understanding. 
Among those who pre-registered last year, 113 irregular Bangladeshis have applied for legalization as of February 15, 2024. 
In addition, out of the total applications, 5,910 applications are under consideration.

Headline_English: Google will update 5 billion devices
Content_Enlish:
Google is bringing new security features to the Chrome browser for 5 billion desktop and iOS devices to prevent online security and privacy breaches. The features will help identify and block phishing attacks (fraudulently obtaining personal information). Forbes News. 

Google claims that the browser will be able to identify and block 25 percent of phishing attacks with the new update. On March 14, Google Chrome and Safe Browsing Product Managers released a statistic. The report said that cybercriminals can usually steal personal and financial data using flawed sites in less than 10 minutes. 

This short time creates a huge opportunity for criminals. Hackers can steal personal information within this time. Therefore, Google has announced an update to the Chrome browser's security features. With this update, the company will stop hackers from taking advantage of even small vulnerabilities. 

Explaining more about the feature, Google says that Chrome's Safe Browsing feature lists the addresses and files of potentially risky sites. This list was updated every 30 minutes to 1 hour. During this time, three malicious sites could enter and exit the browser before Google knew it. 

To keep up with the increasing speed of hackers, Google is bringing a real-time safe privacy-preserving URL browsing feature to Chrome users on desktop or iOS. In addition, the company is also bringing a new password protection feature to the Chrome app on iOS for safe browsing. 

According to Google, the Chrome browser is active on 5 billion devices. 1 billion addresses and files on these devices will be covered by Google's Safe Browsing feature every day and will warn users by sending 3 million notifications in real time. 

The tech giant says, 'If we suspect a site is a risk to you or your device, you will be immediately notified to be careful.'

Headline_English: CU 'D' Unit admission test results released, pass rate 35.60 percent
Content_Enlish:
The results of the combined 'D' unit admission test for the 2023-24 academic year of Chittagong University (CU) have been published. The pass rate is 35.60 percent. 

The results were published on the university's website and official Facebook page at around 9 pm on Tuesday (March 19).

Headline_English: Hasaranga banned from Bangladesh-Sri Lanka Test
Content_Enlish:
Sri Lankan cricketer Wanindu Hasaranga has been banned from the Test series against Bangladesh by the International Cricket Council (ICC). Hasaranga breached Article 2.8 of the ICC Code of Conduct by misbehaving with an umpire in the final ODI against Bangladesh on Monday (March 18). For this, he was also fined 50 percent of his match fee. He was also given three demerit points. This ban was imposed on Hasaranga after he received 8 demerit points in the last two years. 

Cricket's highest governing body, the ICC, said that if a cricketer receives 8 demerit points in 2 years, then it is considered as 4 demerit points under Article 7.6. As a result, the cricketer was banned for 2 Tests, 4 ODIs and 4 T20 matches. This law has also been enforced in the case of Wanindu Hasaranga. 

Read more: Pakistani cricketer smokes cigarette in dressing room after taking five wickets 

On the other hand, Hasaranga played a game of wits by behaving badly with the umpire. This is what cricket analysts think. Because according to the ICC rules, the cricketer who gets 8 demerit points will be banned in the format that comes first. The T20 World Cup will be held in June this year. Sri Lanka does not have any ODI or T20 matches before that. In that case, Hasaranga, who is under this ban, could have been banned for four matches of the T20 World Cup. As such, Hasaranga has deliberately stepped into the trap of another ban to escape one ban, it is believed.

Headline_English: How much of your privacy does Google keep?
Content_Enlish:
The world is at your fingertips with just one click. Google is an unprecedented creation of technology. It has the answer to any question. It seems that all the information in the world is hidden inside it. If you search, you can easily find a simple solution to any question. 

However, no matter how much personal information you get on Google, you will be a fool if you know how much personal information Google keeps about you. Unknowingly, you are giving Google a lot of your personal information. Let's find out exactly how much information your favorite search site keeps about you. 

Google collects all the data you have searched till date. This site presents the advertisements you need in front of you by analyzing that information. Even if you delete your search history, Google collects your entire life's search list. 

Google can also read your mental state with the help of your search history. Apart from this, this site also keeps track of what songs you have listened to on YouTube and what kind of songs you like. 

This site also keeps a close eye on your clothes and lifestyle. This site also remembers what kind of clothes you have bought online. Google keeps track of the number of pages you spend on throughout the day, every hour and minute. It also keeps track of where you've been and when.

Headline_English: How to make Iftar-Special Haleem
Content_Enlish:
The holy month of Ramadan is going on. After fasting all day, everyone wants new dishes for Iftar. Many people do not want to cook at home because they think it is a hassle. For them, an easy recipe is Iftar-Special Haleem. It also takes less time to cook. Check out the recipe below- 

Ingredients 

Boneless khasi or beef, gram dal, moong dal, lentil dal, biuli dal, dalia, kamini atap rice. Also, ginger-garlic paste, sour curd, saffron and salt, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili, black pepper, garam masala. All the spices should be powdered. 

Method 

Wash all types of dal, dalia and rice well and soak them in water for two hours. On the other hand, marinate the meat with all the spices and keep it in the fridge. After a while, boil the marinated meat a little. Boil the dal-rice mixture well with a little ginger garlic paste, salt, turmeric powder. 

Add ginger-garlic paste, a little salt, dry chili powder, garam masala powder and a little turmeric powder. Mix the meat pieces well and put them in the pressure cooker for four whistles. Now open the lid of the cooker and boil for another 15-20 minutes. 

Heat oil in a large pot and fry the chopped onion well and add the ginger-garlic paste. 

Now add the boiled meat to the pot. Grind the meat well with all the powdered spices. In the meantime, add sour curd and stir for another 10-15 minutes. 

When the meat is mixed with the spices and curd, pour the boiled rice, dal, and dal mixture. Now add ghee and mix well. 

Boil everything slowly on low heat. When it releases a nice aroma, sprinkle saffron water on top. Haleem is ready. Now sprinkle lemon, coriander leaves, and mint leaves on top and serve hot.

Headline_English: Finland tops the list of happiest countries, what is Bangladesh's position?
Content_Enlish:
A list of the happiest countries in the world has been published under the auspices of the United Nations. Finland has maintained its top position for the seventh consecutive time in this list, published on Wednesday (March 20). Bangladesh is ranked 129th in this list. Afghanistan is at the bottom of the list. 

This survey includes 143 countries. Bangladesh has slipped 11 places since last year. Bangladesh's current position is 129th from 118th position. 

In this list, published on Wednesday (March 20) on the occasion of World Happiness Day, Denmark is in second place after Finland, Iceland is in third place, and Sweden is in fourth place. Israel comes in fifth place. 

The Netherlands, Norway, Luxembourg, Switzerland and Australia are in sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth places on the list, respectively. Among the South Asian countries, Nepal is in 93rd place, Pakistan is 108th, Myanmar is 118th, India is 126th, Sri Lanka is 128th and Afghanistan is in 143rd place. 

For the first time in more than a decade, the United States and Germany, one of the world's richest and most prosperous countries, did not make the top 20 list of the happiest countries.

Headline_English: Prime Minister's initiatives for women's empowerment
Content_Enlish:
Begum Rokeya, who is known as the pioneer of women's awakening and the first Bengali feminist essayist, novelist, literary figure and social reformer, worked for the education and empowerment of women. In addition to providing education to distressed women, she tried to empower them economically by training them in small and medium industries. And as a worthy successor to the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has been working tirelessly for women. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said at various times that half of the country's population is women. Real development is never possible without keeping women out of development. 

She is a role model in the world in women's empowerment. Earlier, the women of the country were confined to their homes. Bangabandhu took the initiative to move women forward. Later, with the help of Bangabandhu's daughter Sheikh Hasina, the women of the country are moving ahead of men in many fields. 

Bangabandhu's daughter Sheikh Hasina's government is implementing extensive programs to establish the proper status of women, including economic, social, administrative and political empowerment, expansion of women's education, establishment of women's rights, and prevention of all types of violence. 

Bangabandhu for the overall development of women: 
In 1972, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's direct instructions were observed to ensure the overall development and empowerment of women for the purpose of women's development. In 1972, Bangabandhu reserved a 10 percent quota for women's development in government jobs. Bangabandhu awarded the title of Birangana to women who lost their dignity due to Pakistani soldiers during the Liberation War. Under the instructions of the Father of the Nation, the government established rehabilitation centers for the Biranganas in 1972. The Women's Rehabilitation Board was formed and measures were taken for their family and social rehabilitation. In a speech to the women's organization, she said, "From today, write Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in place of the name of the father of the raped girl." And write the address Dhanmondi 32.'' 

Bangamata in women's empowerment: 
Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's wife Bangamata Sheikh Fazilatun Nesa Mujib's contribution to women's empowerment is immense. Bangamata Sheikh Fazilatun Nesa Mujib, a great woman who will always be remembered in the history of independent Bengal, relentlessly stood by Bangabandhu with immense patriotism, sacrifice and courage and inspired him. She has constantly stood by to empower and respect women. 

Prime Minister's initiatives in women's empowerment: 
We see Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's unique contribution in the economic, political, social and environmental conditions of women at every level of society, decision-making, education, work, medical care, security, etc., or in creating a strong position for women in all these areas. 
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has worked to implement women's empowerment. She came to power in 2009 and formulated the National Women's Development Policy 2011. She was the first to elect a woman as the Speaker of the National Parliament. Sheikh Hasina was the first to give responsibility to a woman as the first Home Minister and Foreign Minister in her cabinet. The Deputy Leader of the Parliament also became a woman. The Prime Minister has ensured the provision of women being elected by creating the post of Vice Chairman in the Upazila Parishad and by participating in the election of three women members in the Union Parishad. 

Women in Bangladesh are now not only judges, district administrators, and police superintendents, but are also performing their duties at the policy-making level and in the administration of the state with skill. All this has been possible only because of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, the daughter of Bangabandhu. 

In addition, women in Bangladesh are leaving marks of success in all challenging professions including education, medicine, science and technology and diplomatic skills, sports, mountaineering, and working in NASA. In Bangladesh, there are now female officials working in important government secretaries or equivalent positions, including the Ministry of Finance, which was not the case before. Sheikh Hasina's government has also appointed a High Court judge, the first female Vice-Chancellor of a university, and the first female Major General of the army. 

Prime Minister's speech at the 15th BRICS Summit on Women: 
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina addressed the heads of state and government who were in Johannesburg for the 15th BRICS Summit. At that time, she drew the attention of the Global South leaders to 5 important issues needed to develop women and girls as agents of change. In her first proposal, the Prime Minister said, "We need to mitigate the adverse effects of the ongoing food, energy and financial crises to ensure the nutrition, health and security of our women and girls." 

Secondly, she called for efforts to keep the country's girls in school, protect them from cybercrime and reduce their growing digital divide. Many girls face these problems. 

Sheikh Hasina's third proposal calls for increasing opportunities for gainful employment, decent work, wage equality and financial inclusion for women. 

In her fourth and fifth proposals, the Prime Minister suggested creating a level playing field for women for an active and sustainable political career, as well as taking measures to protect and survive women due to the impact of climate change. 

More initiatives: 
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has taken various initiatives at different times to empower women in Bangladesh's development progress. One of the steps is Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's ten special initiatives. These ten initiatives have opened up ten horizons for women's empowerment. 

After being formed in 2014, the government led by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has prioritized poverty and hunger eradication, housing, education, medical care and social security in order to ensure the fundamental rights of all people in the country. A total of ten special initiatives have been taken for the overall progress of society and the state. Which are known as Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's ten special initiatives. These 10 special initiatives are said to have indirectly paved the way for women to become self-reliant. 

The initiatives are- 1. One House One Farm (currently Palli Sanchay Bank) 2. Ashrayan Project 3. Digital Bangladesh 4. Education Support Program 5. Women Empowerment 6. Electricity in every home 7. Community Clinic and Mental Health 8. Social Security Program 9. Investment Development 10. Environmental Protection. 

1, One House One Farm (Currently Palli Sanchay Bank): At the beginning of the My House My Farm project, it was made mandatory for every Gram Unnayan Samity to have at least 40 women members out of 60 members. As a result, 60 percent of those who have become successful through this association using their own resources are women. And if Palli Sanchay Bank now has 6 million members, then 4 million of them are women members. There is a hidden goal of making rural housewives financially self-reliant through this project. Which has been possible because of Bangabandhu's daughter Sheikh Hasina. 

2, Ashrayan Project: Another successful step to ensure women's empowerment is the Ashrayan Project. To ensure women's empowerment, the Ashrayan project provides land and house ownership rights in the joint names of husband and wife of landless, homeless, distressed and uprooted families. In this case, special priority is given to the disabled, families affected by river erosion, freedom fighters, third gender (hijra), elderly, widows and widowers. So that the resettled families do not face any complications related to ownership in the future, the land ownership rights are transferred on-site along with the registered document/acknowledgement, name registration and entry by the upazila administration. 

3, Digital Bangladesh: Digital Bangladesh has played an important role in women's empowerment. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's unpaid ICT advisor Sajeeb Ahmed Wazed (Joy). Bangladesh is moving forward in ICT with the help of Sajeeb Ahmed Wazed Joy, the Prime Minister's worthy son. The project was adopted as the Women's Empowerment Project (Phase 2) through Information and Communication Technology to build a Digital Bangladesh. The National Women's Organization has been implementing this program since April 2017 under the initiative of the Ministry of Women and Child Affairs. The goal of this project is to empower women through access to information technology for disadvantaged rural women and provision of information technology-based services. Under this project, one information center has been established in each of the 492 upazilas of Bangladesh. In each information center, 1 information service officer and 2 information service assistants are engaged in providing information services. They are known as 'Tatha Aapa' in the project area. 

4, Education Assistance Program: The path to women's economic empowerment has been paved through the Education Assistance Program. In this regard, the contribution of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is immense. The Prime Minister has aimed to ensure that no one is deprived of educational opportunities due to lack of money. The Education Assistance Trust was formed under the Education Assistance Program to ensure education for poor and talented students who are deprived of educational opportunities due to lack of money. This program was taken with the aim of preventing the dropout rate of poor and meritorious students from class 6 to graduation (pass) and equivalent by providing stipends, preventing child marriage and ensuring the quality of education. As a result, the rate of female education has increased in the last decade and the dropout rate has decreased. 

5, Women's empowerment: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has worked to ensure the empowerment of women everywhere. To create opportunities for women's participation everywhere and eliminate discrimination against women, the ''National Women's Development Policy 2011'' was formulated, the ''Women Rehabilitation Board'' and ''National Women's Organization'' were established to empower women and create opportunities for women's education. ''Joyita Foundation'' was established in 2011 to develop women entrepreneurs with the aim of sustainable economic empowerment of women. So that small and medium women entrepreneurs can run their business activities without any risk. To solve the housing problem of working women and women entrepreneurs, the construction of women's hostels in divisional cities, the adoption of women entrepreneur development projects and the creation of self-employment opportunities are reflections of the visionary development thinking. The enactment of the "Prevention of Violence against Women Act 2015" and the inclusion of the mother's name in the passport have also consolidated the position of women in society. 

6, Electricity in every home: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has delivered electricity to every home. Electricity is one of the driving forces for achieving national growth, poverty alleviation and the socio-economic development of the country. When the socio-economic conditions improve, the opportunities for women to be involved in economic activities in society naturally increase. Therefore, although the picture of women's empowerment is not directly visible in the electricity activities in every home, this initiative is indirectly playing an important role in the path of women's empowerment. In addition to ensuring almost 100% electricity supply across the country, significant progress has been made in the lives of women. With electricity facilities in remote areas, women's safety has increased. As a result, they are able to spend more time outside and are involved in economic and social activities. In addition, a vast market has been created for buying and selling products of women entrepreneurs online. 

7, Community Clinics and Mental Health: Women's health has always been a neglected issue in the socio-economic mindset of Bangladesh. After Bangabandhu, his worthy daughter Sheikh Hasina has worked for the development of women's health. For a woman who makes a vital effort to protect the health of everyone in her family, the thought of going to the doctor was almost impossible, let alone minor health problems, even if she was sick and confined to her home. The initiative of the community clinic, which was taken with the aim of providing healthcare to the doorsteps of the rural poor, is contributing to the health protection of women in both direct and indirect ways. As the rate of healthcare use by the general public has increased through community clinics, it has also become easier for rural women to access healthcare. As a result, the average life expectancy of women has increased and the good health of children has been ensured. 

8, Social Security Programs: The Sheikh Hasina government has taken 123 social safety net programs for the neglected, disabled, and destitute people of the society. এসব কর্মসূচির মধ্যে রয়েছে বিধবা নারীদের জন্য ভাতা প্রদান, স্বামী পরিত্যক্তা নারীদের ভাতা প্রদান ইত্যাদি। এছাড়াও মহিলাদের আত্মকর্মসংস্থানের জন্য ক্ষুদ্রঋণ কার্যক্রমের আওতায় প্রতি অর্থবছরে ১৫০০ জন দুস্থ, অসহায়, মহিলাদের ১.৫০ কোটি টাকা ঋণ বিতরণ করছে।

৯, বিনিয়োগ বিকাশ: ঘরে ঘরে বিদ্যুৎ একসময় স্বপ্ন হলেও এখন সেই স্বপ্ন বাস্তবে ধরা দিয়েছে প্রধানমন্ত্রীর হাত ধরে। বিনিয়োগ বিকাশের অন্যতম পূর্বশর্ত হলো বিদ্যুৎ। আর সেই ঘরে ঘরে বিদ্যুৎ পৌঁছে দিয়েছেন প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনা বর্তমান সরকারের সময়ে বিদ্যুৎ উৎপাদন বৃদ্ধি, যোগাযোগ খাতের উন্নয়ন, পদ্মা সেতু নির্মাণ, মহাসড়কের উন্নয়ন, আধুনিক সমুদ্র বন্দর স্থাপন ইত্যাদি কারণে বাংলাদেশে বিদেশি বিনিয়োগ বৃদ্ধি পেয়েছে। পাশাপাশি স্থানীয় উদ্যোক্তারাও বিনিয়োগে আগ্রহী হচ্ছেন। নারীদের জন্য সহজ শর্তে ঋণ, প্রশিক্ষণ, দক্ষতা উন্নয়ন ইত্যাদি ব্যবস্থা গৃহিত হওয়ায় বৃহৎ ও ক্ষুদ্র বিনিয়োগে এগিয়ে এসেছেন নারীরা। সহজ শর্তে ঋণ পাওয়ায় নারীরা এখন ক্ষুদ্র ও কুটির শিল্পের পাশাপাশি বৃহৎ শিল্পে বিনিয়োগ করছেন। একদিকে যখন কিছু নারী রান্না, সেলাই, সাজসজ্জার বিষয়ে বিনিয়োগ করছেন। অন্যদিকে নারীরা প্রশিক্ষণ, প্রকাশনা ইত্যাদি ব্যবসায় বিনিয়োগ করছেন। এতকিছু সম্ভব হচ্ছে বঙ্গবন্ধু কন্যা শেখ হাসিনার জন্য। 

১০, পরিবেশ সুরক্ষা: পরিবেশ ও জীববৈচিত্র্য সংরক্ষণ, পরিবেশ দূষণ নিয়ন্ত্রণ, জলবায়ু পরিবর্তনের ঝুঁকি মোকাবেলা, গবেষণা, উদ্ভিজ্জ জরিপ এবং বনজ সম্পদ উন্নয়নের মাধ্যমে টেকসই পরিবেশ ও বন নিশ্চিতকরণ এ উদ্যোগের লক্ষ্য। পরিবেশগত বিপর্যয় সমগ্র মানবগোষ্ঠীর ওপর বিরূপ প্রভাব ফেলে। বিশেষত নারী, গর্ভবর্তী মা, গর্ভস্থ শিশু ও শিশু-কিশোররা শারীরিক ও মানবিক বিপর্যয়ের সম্মুখীন হয়। দেশের সার্বিক পরিবেশ সুরক্ষিত হলে এই নারী ও শিশুরা এই বিপর্যয় থেকে রক্ষা পাবে। নারীর ক্ষমতায়নে এ ক্ষেত্রে কাজ করে যাচ্ছেন বঙ্গবন্ধু কন্যা প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনা।

নারীর ক্ষমতায়ন বাস্তবায়নে আরও বিশেষ নানা পদক্ষেপ নিচ্ছেন শেখ হাসিনা। নারীর ক্ষমতায়নের স্বপ্নদ্রষ্টা হিসেবে প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনা ২০৩০ সালের মধ্যে আইসিটিতে নারীর অংশগ্রহণ ৩০ শতাংশ এবং ২০৪১ সালের মধ্যে ৫০ শতাংশে উন্নীত করার লক্ষ্যমাত্রা প্রণয়ন করেছে।

Headline_English: Pakistan government will not last more than 4-5 months: Imran Khan

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan said this after the hearing of the corruption case against Imran Khan at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi on Thursday. 

The World Cup-winning cricketer said that he did not join the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) cabinet because the government would not last long. 

Imran Khan claimed that the corruption case against him was baseless. 

Imran Khan, who was praised for criticizing various unfair steps taken by America during his time as Prime Minister, said that the decision in the case against him has already been taken. The legal processes that are being completed now are just formalities. 

‘The current situation has exposed the entire system. Everything is being manipulated. "The Election Commission, the caretaker government and the establishment are all involved in this," added the PTI founder.

Headline_English: Facebook down: Elon Musk mocks
Content_Enlish:
Meta's popular social media platform Facebook was down for over an hour. The social media platform was down from 9:30 pm to 10:30 pm Bangladesh time on Tuesday (March 5). This caused panic among users worldwide. Many were worried about their IDs and important information. An uproar began around the world. 

In this situation, Meta's Communications Director Andy Stone posted a post on X to reassure users. He wrote, "We are aware of the problems people are facing using our service. We are working on it." 

After some time, X owner Elon Musk took a screenshot of his post and made a sarcastic post, criticizing Meta. In the picture posted by Musk, Facebook, Instagram and Threads are seen with their hands on their heads. And X is seen in a cheerful mood. 

Meanwhile, the British media outlet Daily Mail reported in a report that problems have arisen on Facebook and Instagram all over the world. No one is able to access Facebook and Instagram anywhere in the world. Both the websites and apps of these two platforms have become inoperable. 

The graph of Down Detector shows that till 9:20 pm, 315,817 Facebook users have complained that they are facing problems using Facebook. Then till 9:32 pm, 541,573 users have reported their problems. They also want to know – what happened to the social media? Why can't I log in? When will it be fixed?

Headline_English: Election results were predetermined: GM Quader
Content_Enlish:
Jatiya Party Chairman and Opposition Leader GM Quader raised the public's doubts and mistrust in Parliament about the various irregularities, inconsistencies and results of the 12th national election process. 

He said that there were three types of elections in the 12th parliamentary elections. In some places, only two to three votes were cast per hour. In others, completely fair elections were held. In others, elections were held under the influence of muscle power. The results of the elections were predetermined and the sheets were made. 

GM Quader made this allegation during the discussion on the motion of thanks on the President's address and the closing speech of the first session of the 12th National Parliament on Tuesday. Earlier, the Parliament meeting began under the chairmanship of Speaker Dr. Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury. Then, after the speeches of the Leader of the Parliament and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, the motion of thanks on the President's address was passed by voice vote. 

Participating in the discussion on the motion of thanks, GM Quader said, "I think there were three types of elections. In some areas, all the elections were fair. There was no disturbance. There was generally an uncontested election. There was no strong candidate. There was goodwill from the government. It was 100% fair. However, the attendance was low. Another was free style. There was free use of muscle power and money. Through that, polling stations were occupied. Most of the time, the government party and the rebel candidates were independent candidates or our candidates…. There was another thing that many of our leaders and activists complained about. 

He said, “The election was a predetermined result anyway and the sheet was made.” When the government party members protested this statement, GM Quader laughed and said, “This cannot be.” 

When GM Quader made these statements regarding the election, the government party and independent members protested his statement with a lot of noise and uproar. At one point in the members’ uproar, Speaker Dr. Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury said, “Honorable members, let him speak.” Earlier, the opposition chip whip could be heard saying, “Listen. Be patient.” 

Amidst the uproar, a member of the government party could be heard saying, Jamaat, BNP, Tarique Rahman are giving speeches today…. In the face of the uproar from Awami League and independent members, GM Quader sometimes laughed and sometimes changed the subject and continued his speech by referring to someone else. 

Citing examples of voter turnout in national elections in different countries of the world, GM Quader said, “If all parties come to the elections and vote without any obstacles, even 15 percent of the votes would be acceptable. If all major parties, including Awami League and BNP, participate in the elections, 90-95 percent of the votes would be cast at this time,” he said. He said, “It is difficult to hold participatory elections if a party from Awami League or BNP does not come. People do not come to vote.” 

Stating that he had calculated whether a 42 percent voter turnout in the elections was possible, GM Quader said that in the context in which it was, there should have been an 8-hour queue in front of all polling stations to cast 42 percent votes. But that was not the case. At that time, members of parliament started making noise. 

GM Quader said, “Many have said that there were no more than three or four votes per hour. I am not talking about me. I am talking about my ideas.’ He said, if 42 percent is shown, how did the remaining ballots come, in whose favor? 

GM Quader said, the 12th National Parliament election can be considered legal according to the constitution and existing laws. According to the law, it was legal. No one declared it illegal. But the majority of people think that it was not a good election, they do not think that it reflected public opinion correctly. 

He said, I think that the laws and regulations were violated extensively in this election. Those who avoided watching have often helped in the violations. 

The opposition leader said, the President said that the people's democracy has won the election. As far as I know, most of the people in the country do not agree with this. Only the government and the government party, Awami League, have won this election. After this election, doubts have arisen whether all other parties that have a connection with the people, except Awami League, will be able to survive with their own principles and ideals. He fears that normal politics is now heading towards an uncertain future. 

GM Quader said that the President said that the parties boycotting the elections were able to carry out their political programs independently. They do not agree with this statement. Because they were imprisoned with cases and evicted from their homes with hulia. They were not allowed to stand on the streets. They had to flee to the paddy fields, forests and jungles. There was no environment for them to be able to carry out their programs independently. 

He said that the constitution and law can legitimize any type of election. But it cannot always guarantee that it will be accepted as a correct or good election in all cases. In the sixth election, 21 percent of the votes were cast on February 15. If all parties do not come to the election, the vote does not become spontaneous. It was very acceptable that 75 to 82 percent of the votes were cast in the seventh, eighth and ninth parliamentary elections. 

Stating that the topic of corruption was not mentioned in the President's speech, GM Quader said that the country is flooded with corruption. This has been going on for quite some time. No work can be done without corruption. This is the curse of every society. Suffering due to corruption continues to increase. It hinders social development. The government does not usually admit corruption. 

At this time, GM Quader, citing Transparency International's corruption index, said that Bangladesh has been the champion in corruption five times in a row since 2001. The first time was when the Awami League was in power. At that time, the government and most independent MPs said that BNP was in power. At that time, GM Quader said that it happened four times during the BNP's tenure. Stating that Bangladesh was ranked 13th in corruption when the Awami League came to power in 2009, GM Quader said that we are currently ranked 10th. This means that the corruption position has now gone down. This is the Transparency International report. 

At that time, the government and independent MPs claimed that the report was fake. GM Quader said that we did not see clear guidelines on corruption in the President's speech. At that time, a member of parliament from the side said, "Excellence President." At that time, GM Quader said, "Of course, Excellency President." 

GM Quader also claimed that if there was an organization of TIB regarding loan defaulters, Bangladesh would have gone to number 2-1 in the world in terms of loan defaulters. He questioned the discrepancy between Bangladesh and IMF's accounts regarding defaulted loans. 

GM Quader said, why is there a difference between the IMF and our accounts? The strange thing about banks is that they are cleverly hiding their defaulted loans under the carpet instead of collecting them. People's money. Not their own money. They are taking our money. They are giving it to whoever they want. Then they show that they have this money. GM Quader claimed that there have been allegations that Bangladesh Bank is encouraging this. 

Terming the murder of journalist couple Sagar-Runi as an example of injustice, GM Quader said that the statements of government officials on this issue may encourage delaying the investigation. He advised to be careful in this regard. 

Regarding the increase in commodity prices, GM Quader said that a certain number of people are importing. It is natural for a syndicate to be formed in this. He alleged that these businessmen are directly or indirectly involved in the government's policymaking. He also believes that the government is hostage in their hands because the government has no alternative.

Headline_English: What Meta said about the Facebook-Instagram outage
Content_Enlish:
Facebook, Messenger and Instagram have been restored after being down for about an hour around the world. Many people reported that Facebook was logged out and logged out simultaneously from different parts of the country at around 9:15 pm on Tuesday (March 5). Facebook was then restored at 10:23 pm. 

According to Downdetector, a website that monitors website activity, more than 583,000 users faced various problems, including Facebook logouts, from the start of the problem on Tuesday (February 5) until 9:30 pm Bangladesh time. More than 84,000 users faced the same problem with Instagram. 

However, there was no problem using the popular communication application WhatsApp owned by Meta and the short message writing website Threads. 

British media outlet Daily Mail reported in a report that problems have arisen with Facebook and Instagram all over the world. No one is able to access Facebook and Instagram anywhere in the world. Both the websites and apps of these two media have become ineffective. 

At 10:45 pm Bangladesh time, Meta spokesperson Andy Stone said in a social media post, "We are aware that people are having trouble using our services. We are working on the issue." 

After Facebook, Messenger, and Instagram returned at 10:30 pm, Andy Stone said in another post at 11:19 pm, "Today a technical issue caused problems for users accessing our services. We have resolved the issue as quickly as possible for everyone who had problems. We apologize for any problems that may have occurred." 

Earlier, on Tuesday (March 5), many people reported that Facebook was simultaneously logged out and logged out from different parts of Bangladesh at around 9:15 pm. Time News reporters from the United States said that the Facebook IDs of users there were also suddenly logged out. They can no longer be logged in. 

Meanwhile, SP Md. Nazmul Islam of the DMP's Cyber ​​Crime Unit said that there is nothing to panic about not being able to access Facebook. Their server is not accessible due to a fault. 

After discussions with Facebook's Bangladesh and Singapore authorities, SP Nazmul gave a video message on Tuesday night. There he said, Facebook's activities are currently being disrupted. In the meantime, we have spoken to the Bangladesh authorities and the Facebook authorities in Singapore about this matter. They said that they are working to resolve the problem. The problem will be resolved soon.

Headline_English: 54 percent of men and 46 percent of women use social media
Content_Enlish:
Currently, about 4 billion people around the world use social media. It is believed that by 2027, this number will increase to 5 billion! As a continent, people in the Asian region are ahead in using social media. It is believed that everyone will become addicted to this media someday. 
About 2941.01 million people are active on social media in this region. This information is from Tech.net. A survey by Tech.net shows that women are using social media almost as much as men. 
About 59 percent of people in the world use social media; 54 percent men and 46 percent women. In terms of numbers, men are 2.64 billion and women are 2.25 billion. Men are also ahead in using the most used social media site, Facebook. TikTok usage is increasing day by day. 56.6 percent men and 43.4 percent women use Facebook. Women are ahead in using Snapchat. 53.8 percent women use this social media. Instagram is also being used at the same rate. However, celebrities use it more. 
In Bangladesh, men are also ahead in using social media. About 67.4 percent of men are active on social media. On the other hand, 32.6 percent of women are active on social media. Not only in Bangladesh, but in South Asia, men are much ahead of women in using social media. About 73 percent of men use social media in this region. 
It is known that nine out of every 10 internet users use social media. In addition, people spend at least two hours more on social media every day on average. That is, 10 billion hours are spent on social media every day in the world.

Headline_English: 179 BGPs flee to Bangladesh again
Content_Enlish:
Members of the Border Guard Police (BGP) of Myanmar, who were defeated in the ongoing conflict with the Arakan Army in Rakhine, are fleeing to Bangladesh again. 

A total of 179 BGP members have taken refuge in Bangladesh through the Naikyangchhari border in Bandarban since Monday (March 11) morning. 

Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) Public Relations Officer Md. Shariful Islam confirmed the matter. He said that 179 members of the Myanmar Border Guard Police have taken refuge in Bangladesh through the border area under the responsibility of Jamchhari BOP under 11 BGB in Naikyangchhari, Bandarban. 

Meanwhile, Saber Ahmed, a member of Jamchhari Ward No. 8 of Naikyangchhari Sadar Union, was shot in the afternoon while going to see the fleeing BGP members. 

Locals said that an eager crowd gathered in the Jamchhari area near the border to see the fleeing BGP members on Monday afternoon. At that time, a bullet fired from the Myanmar side hit member Saber Ahmed in the right side of the waist. 

Chairman of Naikshongchhari Sadar Union Nurul Absar Imon and Deputy Commissioner of Bandarban Shah Mojahid Uddin also confirmed that Saber Ahmed was shot. They said that the injured local public representative has been sent to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital for better treatment. 

Earlier, in February, 330 members of the Myanmar junta-backed army, police and border guard force took refuge in Bangladesh in the face of an attack by the joint armed forces of the Arakan Army and independence-seeking ethnic groups. Later, on February 15, they were sent back to Myanmar by ship from the Inani Navy Jetty in Ukhia, Cox's Bazar.

Headline_English: Fasting methods for diabetic patients
Content_Enlish:
Diabetes is a serious condition in the body when our body cannot produce insulin on its own or cannot use the insulin produced efficiently (effectively). As a result, the level of sugar or glucose in the blood is higher than normal. Insulin controls the entry of sugar into the cells of the human body. People suffering from this disease have to take medicine at regular intervals. In such a case, Muslim believers face problems during fasting. Questions arise in their minds about how to take medicine or what to do. 

Many Muslims think that fasting cannot be observed if they have diabetes. This is not correct. Fasting can be performed by keeping diabetes under control. However, some rules must be followed for this. To maintain good health, high blood pressure, cholesterol, weight must be monitored in all aspects. Any complications of the kidney, heart, nerves and blood vessels must also be managed. Many people do not fast because of heartburn, hunger, trembling, etc. There is no evidence that gastric ulcers will occur if they are on an empty stomach. 

* Risks of fasting for diabetics 

There is a risk assessment scale that can be used to score and grade the risks. The risks are graded as mild, moderate, high or very high. In our country, mild risk, high risk and very high risk are graded. Very high risk-Type 1 diabetes, gestational diabetes. Similarly, the elderly who cannot walk, do not understand, unstable heart disease, stroke, or have recently had a heart attack or stroke are at high risk. Patients who are unaware of hypoglycemia and have recently had severe hypoglycemia, all of them are very high-risk patients. Grade-4 or worse chronic kidney disease, dialysis patients, kidney transplant patients, their risk is also very high. Kidney disease is graded using EGFR. EGFR up to 60 is grade-2. Up to 30 is grade 3. Below thirty is grade 4. Below 15 is grade 5 chronic kidney disease. The reality is that many of them fast and are well. However, fasting is not safe for them. Patients who do not even have mild risks do not fast, whether due to lack of understanding or on purpose. The doctor's responsibility is to inform the patient of the risks and the depth of the risks. 

* Who is it difficult to fast for? 

Fasting involves fasting for a long time from dawn to dusk. In other times of the year, eating dinner from 8-10 pm to breakfast from 8-10 am means fasting for about 12 hours. Therefore, the fasting period is almost the same during Ramadan or other times. The things that we do during the day can only be done at night during Ramadan. Many people do not fast due to heart disease and kidney disease. Some are afraid, some do not dare. In fact, the difference between fasting is that it is day instead of night and night instead of day, that's it! Fasting food with risks, exercise during fasting, blood tests (monitoring), complications, especially hypoglycemia, and its treatment should be learned before fasting. 

* Blood test 

Fasting blood sugar test does not break the fast. Everyone who is able to take blood from the fingertip (SMBG) should learn. It may be necessary to test at least three times. As a precaution, hypoglycemia should be checked at 4 or 5 pm. If blood glucose is 5, you should be careful. You should test again within an hour. If it is less than 4, you should break the fast. The more risk you have, the more tests you need. It is good to keep a test chart. If HbA1C is good before starting the fast, and if it is under control without any medication, you can do without testing. 

▶ Test once: If you are on medication, you should do it once in the second half of the day. 

▶ Test twice: If you are an insulin patient, you should test at night and at least once a day if you take two doses of medication. 

▶ Test three times: If you suspect hypoglycemia, you should test again immediately. It can also be done regularly. Every day for the first three days. Then every three days. One day every other day for the last week. 

* Exercise 

Physical labor while fasting is undoubtedly difficult. Those in their fifties will have to change their work schedule. The last work can be done at night. Exercise should be done before Tarawih prayers. In terms of exercise, cardio, i.e. walking, cycling, treadmill (which increase the heart rate), can all be done, but it is better to do it for twenty minutes instead of forty-five minutes. Muscle strengthening or bodybuilding is beneficial, because it reduces dehydration. Stretching or yoga can be done. Exercise can also be done before Iftar. Because it is easy to take action if dehydration occurs. The same situation is from after Tarawih to before Sehri. The plan to skip exercise for a month of fasting is not right. Again, the plan to walk forty-five minutes during fasting is not allowed. Exercise can be done five days a week instead of seven days or the rest period can be increased. The purpose of exercise during fasting is to maintain fitness, maintain habits, and maintain the functioning of the body's hormones. 

* Severe complications of diabetes during fasting 

1. Hypoglycemia 2. Hyperglycemia. 3. Diabetic ketoacidosis 4. Dehydration 5. Thrombosis. 

* Hypoglycemia 

When blood glucose drops too low, it is called hypoglycemia. All diabetic patients, especially those who have to use medication, must have a proper understanding of hypoglycemia. The symptoms are that first you will feel hungry. Then you will shake, sweat. Then you will faint. In this case, you should eat sweets (glucose/sugar or drinks/food made from them) without seeing a doctor. 
Causes of hypoglycemia during fasting: 

▶ Not being able to properly combine medication and physical exertion with fasting. 

▶ Not eating in moderation during Sehri and Iftar. 

▶ Working excessively without making a choice. 

▶ Not being able to adjust the tablet or injection dose to match the time of Sehri and Iftar.

▶ Kidney / liver weakness. 

Treatment and remedy for hypoglycemia: Glucose or sugar should be eaten or taken. This is the only treatment in our country. If it is mild or moderate, the patient can treat it himself. The test should be repeated 15 minutes after eating glucose. If the symptoms go away, complex carbohydrates such as rice, bread, fruits, etc. should be eaten. Milk or protein should not be eaten. If it is severe or if you become unconscious and cannot be fed glucose or sweets, you should go to the emergency department of the hospital. 

* Hyperglycemia 

Hyperglycemia or excessive or dangerous increase in blood glucose levels (> 16.7 mmol or 300 mg. G.) in diabetic patients is a major problem. If you skip or forget to take medicine or injection or take less and eat more, the sugar increases. There are two problems of hyperglycemia. 

1. Diabetic ketoacidosis 

2. Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS) 
Both conditions require hospitalization and treatment under close observation. 

* Diabetes Ketoacidosis 

Read more: How to identify good dates 

It is more common in Ramadan. In the fasting state, insulin decreases in the body and glucose increases. Ketone bodies are formed and eventually ketoacidosis occurs. In most cases, this is due to not taking insulin or reducing it too much due to fear of hypoglycemia. Those who have high glucose before fasting (8.3 to 16.7 mmol), have weak kidneys, and have other complications of diabetes (high/very high risk patients) are more likely to have ketoacidosis and HHS. 

* Dehydration and thrombosis 

Drinking less water is the real cause. Excessive labor, excessive heat, humid weather, and high blood sugar can all cause dehydration during fasting. Excessive dehydration increases blood clotting factors and hinders the process of keeping blood fluid. As a result, blood clots form in the blood vessels. Fasting should be broken due to dehydration. Drink moderate water during fasting and avoid caffeinated drinks. 

* Ways to prevent severe complications of fasting 

▶ One to three months before the start of fasting, one should get an idea about diabetes and its complications. Understand the situation and take necessary preventive measures. 

▶ If you have not done so before, you should get a proper understanding of hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia. 

▶ You should learn about regular blood tests (SMBG) and monitoring yourself. You should test your blood once at night, conveniently, within two hours after sehri and two hours before iftar, and if you have symptoms of hypoglycemia. 

▶ Drinking water and eating three dates during iftar will increase your sugar level. Drinking water in moderation, drinking non-sweet drinks, eating betel leaves, and cucumbers will not cause dehydration. 

▶ If possible, try to control blood glucose with a single dose of glimepiride/gliclazide, analog basal, or analog basal-bolus at iftar.

Content_Enlish:

Headline_English: Petition seeking Khaleda Zia's release and access to medical treatment abroad
Content_Enlish:
An application has been made to the Home Ministry to extend the release period of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia and provide her with the opportunity to undergo treatment abroad under the government's executive order. Khaleda Zia's younger brother Shamim Iskandar filed this application on March 6. 

It is learnt that the Home Ministry will send the application to the Law Ministry for scrutiny of the matter. Khaleda Zia's doctor AZM Zahid Hossain confirmed the matter.

Headline_English: Long traffic jam on Dhaka-Tangail highway
Content_Enlish:

Since the early hours of Wednesday (March 6), traffic jams have been created on about 17 kilometers of the Dhaka-Tangail-Bangabandhu Bridge Highway from Bangabandhu Bridge East to Rasulpur in Kalihati. 

It has been seen on the ground that there is traffic pressure on both lanes of the highway from Elenga to Bangabandhu Bridge East Toll Plaza. However, there is not much traffic on the Dhaka-bound lane from Elenga. Due to the traffic jam, North Bengal-bound and Dhaka-bound vehicles are moving through the bridge roundabout using the Bhuiyanpur-Tarakandi-Bangabandhu Setupur regional road from Elenga. 

Drivers said that traffic jams have been created on this road since mid-morning. They have to suffer due to this. However, today the pressure of transport on the road is more. 

In-charge of the Elenga Highway Police Outpost on the highway, Mir Md. Sajedur Rahman said that the pressure of transport on the highway is more and along with the slow speed of transport on the two-lane road from Elenga to Setupur, truck drivers fall asleep. This has created a traffic jam on the road, even with the vehicles behind. District police members are working alongside the highway police to resolve the traffic jam. However, the traffic jam will be resolved as the day progresses.

Headline_English: 5 foods that can make you sleepy
Content_Enlish:
Insomnia is caused by physical problems like heart disease, nerve weakness, obesity. To solve this, it is important to change the diet. 

According to nutritionists, nutrients like magnesium, calcium, zinc and vitamin B help in bringing sleep. When these elements are lacking in the body, sleep problems start. Insomnia problems also start due to the lack of tryptophan, serotonin and melatonin and other sleep disorders occur. Let's find out the foods that are recommended to be included in the daily diet- 

Hot milk: To overcome the problem of insomnia, you can drink a glass of hot milk every night before going to bed. The amino acids called tryptophan and serotonin in the brain help in bringing sleep. 

Walnuts: Eating walnuts regularly also helps in getting good sleep. Walnuts are a good source of melatonin. Walnuts provide alpha-linoleic acid and omega-3 fatty acids in the body, which help in increasing the secretion of serotonin. 

Pumpkin seeds: If you feel a little hungry, you can eat pumpkin seeds fried in a dry pan. You can also mix these seeds with cornflakes or oats. These seeds are a good source of tryptophan. 

Banana: You will also benefit from including bananas in your daily diet. The vitamin B6, tryptophan, magnesium, and potassium present in it help in bringing sleep. 

Chia seeds: You can keep chia seeds soaked in water in your diet regularly. It also contains tryptophan, which helps in bringing sleep.

Headline_English: Indiscriminate shooting at Palestinians lining up for aid, 104 killed
Content_Enlish:
The Israeli military has carried out a brutal attack on thousands of people standing in line at an aid distribution point in the Gaza Strip, Palestine. At least 104 Palestinians were killed in indiscriminate shooting by Israeli soldiers at the aid center on Thursday. In addition, more than 700 Palestinians were injured. 

This information was reported by the French news agency AFP on Thursday, citing the Palestinian Health Ministry. It said that several Israeli sources also confirmed that soldiers opened fire on a crowd of people waiting for aid. However, they said that the soldiers opened fire on the Palestinians present at the aid center in northern Gaza early on Thursday, believing that they had “created a threat.” 

The Palestinian Health Ministry in the Gaza Strip has strongly condemned the attack by Israeli forces, calling it a “genocide.” The ministry said that at least 104 Palestinians were killed and 760 others were injured in the shooting by Israeli soldiers. 

A local witness told AFP that thousands of people were rushing to the aid trucks at the Nabulsi roundabout in western Gaza City, desperate for food, when the violence broke out. 

The witness, who did not want to be named, said: “The aid trucks came very close to some army tanks. At that time, thousands of people rushed towards the trucks. They attacked the trucks. Israeli soldiers opened fire on the crowd as the people got too close to the tanks.” 

The Israeli army initially said of the incident: “As soon as the aid trucks entered the northern Gaza Strip, Gaza residents surrounded the trucks and looted the relief supplies they were delivering. Dozens of Gazans were injured in the stampede and stampede. The incident is being reviewed.” 

An Israeli source later told AFP, speaking on condition of anonymity, that people had come close to Israeli forces in a way that posed a threat to the soldiers. The threat was later countered by firing live ammunition.

Headline_English: Awami League leader dies in Bailey Road fire
Content_Enlish:
Advocate Ataur Rahman Shamim (65), vice-president of the Kulaura Upazila Awami League of Moulvibazar, was killed in a horrific fire incident in a multi-storey building on Bailey Road in the capital Dhaka. 

Supreme Court lawyer Advocate Shamim contested the 2008 National Assembly elections from the Moulvibazar-2 (Kulaura) constituency with the boat symbol. He was the former office secretary of the US Awami League. His village home is in Sreepur village in Brahmanbazar Union of Kulaura Upazila. 

Read more... Government will provide treatment to those injured in the Bailey Road fire: Health Minister 

Nurul Alam, who was with Advocate Shamim, said that some time before the accident, the two of them went to Kacchi Bhai restaurant from Hotel Capital to have coffee. Just 5 minutes after taking up residence in that restaurant, they heard some noises including black smoke from below the restaurant. Then Ataur Rahman Shamim peeked and saw smoke. Then they first tried to go down, but seeing nothing in the black smoke, they continued to climb up the stairs. 

At that time, Nurul Alam could not see Ataur Rahman Shamim in the crowd. Although he escaped through the helipad, Advocate Shamim died of burns. 

Read more...Fire on Bailey Road: Death toll rises to 46 

Meanwhile, Awami League Central Organizing Secretary Shafiul Alam Chowdhury Nadel MP expressed deep shock and condolences to the bereaved family members after Kulaura Upazila Awami League Vice President Advocate Ataur Rahman Shamim was killed in the fire. 

The fire broke out around 9:15 pm on Thursday. 13 units took part in extinguishing the fire. At least 46 people, including women, were killed. At least 30 people were injured. 70 people were rescued from the building by 12:30 am. In this incident, 38 bodies have been handed over to the families. The Fire Service has formed a 5-member investigation committee.

Headline_English: Using YouTube's PIP mode is even easier
Content_Enlish:
Video streaming platform YouTube is constantly coming up with new features. So that billions of users around the world can use the platform more safely. One of the most popular features of the platform is Picture in Picture mode (PIP). Which could only be used by YouTube Premium subscribers. However, this time YouTube has given good news to Picture in Picture mode users. 

With this feature, the video continues to play in a small window (mini video player) even after exiting the app. As a result, it is possible to watch YouTube while using other apps. Users outside the United States have to purchase a YouTube subscription to use this feature. However, various posts on the social media Reddit have now announced that this feature will be made available to all countries. 

Various videos of this feature are featured on Reddit. In the video, it can be seen that a YouTube mini player is running on top of another app. The feature has been found especially on the devices of users in Europe. Therefore, many people think that this feature will be brought to other regions of the world soon.

However, many technology analysts say that it is not clear whether Google will bring this feature to users without a subscription outside the United States. Because it may be brought experimentally for some users in Europe. In addition, this feature may also be brought by mistake due to an error. 

YouTube said on the X (former Twitter) account that such claims about the feature are not correct. Users outside the United States can only use this feature if they purchase a premium subscription. 

In 2021, YouTube brought PIP mode to iOS premium subscribers worldwide. Later, it was brought to Android users. 

In Bangladesh, YouTube Premium subscription costs 239 taka per month. However, it can be used for one month free YouTube Premium. YouTube Premium does not show ads.

Headline_English: Masters opportunities in the US without IELTS
Content_Enlish:
The Global Studies Center at the University of Pittsburgh in Pennsylvania, USA, is offering a Master's degree without IELTS. The organization will also provide a fellowship. The formal name of this fellowship is the 'HJ Heinz Fellowship'. 

This is a one-year to two-year fellowship, which begins in August and ends in June. The selected student for this fellowship will be given 20,200 US dollars. Which is about 22 lakh 20 thousand taka in Bangladeshi currency. This fellowship is given to talented students from developing countries. 

Applicants for the fellowship must be admitted to a Master's program (at the beginning of the academic year in which they want the Heinz Fellowship). The subject of the Master's will be any one of Public Health, Law, Public and International Affairs, Education or Nursing. The applicant must have completed an undergraduate degree from a university. In addition, they must be proficient in speaking, reading and writing English. Preference will be given to applicants who are in the early or mid-career stage of their career. This fellowship is offered to individuals who are currently working or involved in the policy domain. This fellowship is not offered for basic academic research, academic sabbaticals or medical research. 

This fellowship must be mentioned at the time of application for Masters. However, the application period may vary for different subjects, the student should check with his/her own subject. The names of those selected for the fellowship will be published in May.

Headline_English: Fire breaks out at Gausul Azam Market in the capital, 2 units under control

Headline_English: Palak announces grants for 5,000 women entrepreneurs
Content_Enlish:
State Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology, Zunaid Ahmed Palak, has announced a grant of 50,000 taka to 5,000 women entrepreneurs in the country. He said that this will be launched in this fiscal year as startup seed money for women entrepreneurs to start their businesses in 64 districts and 500 upazilas of the country through Women and E-Commerce. In the past few days, 2,000 women entrepreneurs have been given a grant of 50,000 taka each from the Idea Project under the ICT Department. 

The State Minister made this announcement in his speech as the chief guest at the inauguration of the 'We Colorful Fest 2024' organized by the Women and E-Commerce Trust We, an organization of domestic women entrepreneurs, in Purbachal of the capital today. 

The State Minister said that e-commerce is expanding through the businesses of women entrepreneurs. The ICT Department is training women entrepreneurs to enhance their skills. They are playing an important role in the economic development of the country. All this has been possible due to the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. 

He said that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has established Bangladesh as a shining example or role model of women empowerment, establishment of women rights and gender equality in the world. She is the pioneer of women empowerment and job creation. Through her relentless hard work and far-sighted thinking, sensitivity and everything, women in Bangladesh have visibly come forward in every field. Like the rest of the world, Bangladesh is also going through the golden age of information technology. 

Mentioning that low-cost high-speed internet has been extended to the union, the State Minister said that currently the number of internet users in the country is more than 130 million. Due to the availability of high-speed internet facilities, the country's entrepreneurs are able to expand their products and businesses. More than 2000 services have been digitized so that the common people can get the services they need at a convenient time, place and through. More than 18,000 entrepreneurs are working in more than 9,000 digital centers across the country to deliver services to the doorsteps of the people. Where about 50 percent are women entrepreneurs. As a result, on the one hand, the inequality between men and women, on the other hand, the inequality between rich and poor, and the inequality between rural and urban areas have been eliminated, he said. 

He said that the Prime Minister has taken and implemented various programs for women's empowerment to create financial self-sufficiency and capacity. 10,500 women entrepreneurs have been created in 21 districts through the She Power Project. More than 25,000 smart women entrepreneurs will be created in the remaining 43 districts through the Her Power Project. 

The program was attended by James Gardiner, Foreign Service Officer for Economics, Science and Technology at the US Embassy in Dhaka, GSM Zafarullah, MD of Bangladesh Hi-Tech Park Authority, Shomi Kaiser, President of e-CAB, Nasima Akhter Nisha, Founder of Women and E-Commerce Forum, and many others.

Headline_English: Kartik-Vidya together in the movie 'Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3', when will it be released?
