Agrani Bank is also not exempt from this. Defaulted loans have increased from 12 percent to 16-17 percent. As a result, a capital shortage has been seen. But we have already taken initiatives to reduce defaulted loans. If the economy strengthens this year, these problems will decrease. 

Agrani Bank has also financed projects. We are a major partner in financing the Padma Bridge. We have also financed large industries. We have also received awards from Bangladesh Bank for financing small and medium enterprises. We have also provided additional facilities in financing agriculture. 

We are not lagging behind in terms of digital services. Currently, online services are available in 975 branches of Agrani Bank. There are no major fraud cases like Hallmark, Bismillah, and Anontex in Agrani Bank. We want to maintain this continuity. 



Question: As you were saying, Agrani Bank is a big partner in the Padma Bridge. If you were talking about experience. 
Dr. Zayed Bakht: We were ahead in terms of exports and earning expatriate income. That is why we had enough foreign currency. Regarding this Padma Bridge, our initial understanding with Bangladesh Bank was that we would give foreign currency. And Bangladesh Bank would give us back. But we did not have to take back a single dollar. We did not want it, there was no need to ask for it. 

Question: The government announced incentives to overcome the Corona pandemic. What was the role of Agrani Bank in distributing incentives? 
Dr. Zayed Bakht: As per the government's instructions, we have distributed incentives in all areas - large industries, small and medium industries. So far, the recovery has been satisfactory. In some cases, they have been renewed according to the rules of Bangladesh Bank. If they renew, they no longer get that subsidy. Since the businessmen are in a cash flow crisis, if we pressure them to withdraw money now, they will fall into a crisis. So if they want to renew, we are doing that. If they renew, they will get a breathing space, the money will be returned. 

Question: People had high confidence in private banks. After some incidents, it is seen that people's confidence in government banks is returning. Why is this happening? 

Dr. Zayed Bakht: Even after raising the interest rate to 6-9 percent, every private bank made a profit. Because they increased the interest rate on loans and reduced the interest rate on deposits. Then the depositors saw that there is no loss in keeping money in government banks. The quality of service of all government banks is also good now. As a result, customers' confidence has returned to government banks. Like private banks, government banks are now able to provide all kinds of services. Government banks play a big role in exports and remittances. Online services have been introduced. 

To restore discipline in the banking sector, defaulted loans must be reduced. I think defaulted loans did not increase in a day. The solution will not be in a day. The ongoing cases of defaulted loans must be settled quickly. Due to the long-running case, loans are not being collected. The defaulted loans of lakhs and crores of taka were reduced due to the opportunity of regularizing the loans with a one-time 2 percent down payment. 

Question: The elections are over, the new cabinet has taken charge. What kind of steps need to be taken to reform the financial sector? 
Dr. Zayed Bakht: The exchange rate must be adjusted to the market rate. Bangladesh Bank must take contractionary steps. If the government deals more firmly with the issue of money laundering, then when capital laundering decreases, there will be relief in the external sector. The mega projects that the government has to implement to increase investment must be implemented efficiently. The new ministers will take them forward efficiently. Because if these are implemented, the private sector will also turn around. If Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's bold leadership is carried forward as it was before, the economy will turn around.

Headline_English: I will not back down from accusations that Israel is committing genocide: Netanyahu
Content_Enlish:
Israel will not back down, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said, despite accusations that Israel is committing genocide against the Palestinians. 

Netanyahu made these remarks on Saturday, the 100th day of the attack on Gaza. He announced that the war against Hamas will continue until Israel achieves victory in the Gaza Strip. 

These facts have emerged in a report by Voice of Bengal. It says that so far, more than 1,200 people in Israel and more than 24,000 in the Gaza Strip have been killed in the ongoing conflict. This is more than 1 percent of the total population of Gaza. 

Netanyahu said, 'No one can stop us, The Hague, no evil force, no one.' By evil force, he referred to Hamas, the Iranian-backed Hezbollah forces and the Houthi rebels. 

The Israeli prime minister made these remarks after a two-day hearing at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague, Netherlands. South Africa has filed a case against Israel in the court, accusing it of genocide. Israel has rejected the allegations, calling them insulting and hypocritical.

Headline_English: How to use Google Maps without internet
Content_Enlish:
Many people take the help of Google Maps when going to an unfamiliar place. However, if there is no internet connection on the phone, Google Maps cannot be used. However, Google Maps has a feature that allows this app to be used without an internet connection. 

Let's find out how to use Google Maps without the internet- 
1. To use the offline feature of Google Maps, you first need to download a map of that area. 

2. To download the map, first launch Google Maps and click on the name of the area for which you want to download the map. 

3. Once the map is downloaded, you can view and use it offline. 

4. To use the map offline, first launch Google Maps. Select the place you want to see. You can view that map even if you do not have an internet connection. 

5. Now search for the map of the place you want to see. Now click on Instructions. See public transport lines and stations. 

6. However, the offline map may not have the latest information. The traffic information feature may not work due to lack of internet. 

7. The biggest advantage of Google Maps offline feature is that there are many places where internet does not work. This map will work in all those places. As a result, there will be no problem in going to that specific place.

Headline_English: Tamim wanted Miraz to replace himself as captain
Content_Enlish:
Although Tamim Iqbal, the country's best opener, was appointed as the captain of Fortune Barisal in the upcoming BPL, Tamim wanted me. This was what Tiger all-rounder Mehedi Hasan Miraj told the media. 

Earlier, the franchise's coach Mizanur Rahman Babul had told the media that Tamim Iqbal would be the captain of the team. 

But yesterday (January 16), all-rounder Mehedi Hasan Miraj came to the cricket board. Miraj spoke to the media personnel on his way back at their request. 

At that time, Miraj said, I don't know anything about this (captaincy). Everything will be as per the owner's decision. However, Tamim bhai told me, 'It's better if you do it'. But even then, it is the owner's decision. 

It is worth noting that all three of the five Pandavas will play for Fortune Barisal in this BPL season. Apart from Tamim Iqbal, Mushfiqur Rahim and Mahmudullah, Miraz is also in the squad. The list of possible players to join them in the team includes devastating Australian batsman Glenn Maxwell and South African hard hitter David Miller.

Headline_English: Unregistered mobile network disconnection process to begin soon
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) has announced that the network disconnection process for unregistered mobile phones will be started soon. 

In a notification on Sunday, the government agency has humbly requested the public to check the validity of mobile handsets before purchasing them. 

Director of the Commission's Spectrum Department Dr. Md. Sohel Rana said that all unregistered handsets will be shut down after this comes into effect, but all handsets before this comes into effect will continue to operate as before, they will not be shut down. 

How to check the validity 
Before buying a mobile handset, the validity of the handset can be checked by sending the 15-digit IMEI number (for example KYD 123456789012345) to 16002 from the message option.

Headline_English: Using harmful tonics in dragons to gain weight
Content_Enlish:
Dragon fruit is a very well-known name today. Since dragon fruit cultivation is more profitable than other crops, dragon fruit cultivation is increasing in the country at an increasing rate every year. But a class of unscrupulous farmers are using India's unapproved Dr. Don's Dragon Tonic on dragon fruit in the hope of making more profit. This increases the weight of the fruit. Production is increasing. But the fruit is becoming tasteless. As a result, it has created an adverse effect on the market. 

Dr. Moktar Hossain, Professor of the Department of Horticulture at Bangladesh Agricultural University and Director of the Germplasm Center, said that the weight of naturally produced dragon fruit ranges from 250 to a maximum of 300 grams. And the weight of dragon fruit produced using tonic ranges from 300 grams to 900 grams. The color of this dragon fruit is not uniform. The color of the fruit is then a mixture of purple or red with green. One side or at least one third is green. Because if it is kept on the tree until it is completely uniform in color, it rots. 

Professor Moktar Hossain said that the fruits produced using tonic do not get enough time to develop various nutrients. The produced dragon fruit will be tasty to drink. There will be no sweetness at all. Any artificially produced product has health risks. 

The Department of Agricultural Extension says that large-sized dragons are not unsafe in any way. The use of gibberellic acid or tonic that is being used as plant growth regulators is scientific. It is possible to enlarge the size of dragon fruit by spraying gibberellic acid on the fruits. But it will not change the appearance of the fruit. The taste will also remain intact. 

On the other hand, Dr. MM Dawn's discovery that the use of "dragon tonic" increases the size of the fruit a lot is true, but the use of this tonic causes many problems. Dragon fruit grows but the fruit remains half-ripe and half-raw and it takes a long time to ripen. And if this is used continuously for a long time, the number of flowers and fruits on the tree will decrease, and later the size of the fruit will become smaller. 

Thousands of farmers and agricultural workers are engaged in dragon fruit cultivation. With the way various unscrupulous dragon farmers have started using tonics, it is only a matter of time before dragon cultivation collapses.

Headline_English: Protests over teacher's dismissal at BRAC University
Content_Enlish:
Students of BRAC University are protesting to demand the cancellation of the dismissal order of BRAC University teacher Asif Mahtab and his reinstatement in his post. 

They started forming a human chain in front of BRAC University in Merul Badda from Tuesday morning (January 23). At one stage, the protesters locked the university gate. 

BRAC University teacher Asif Mahtab was dismissed from his job for tearing the pages of the book while speaking about the transgender story 'Sharif to Sharifa' included in the seventh grade textbook. He described the incident as discriminatory behavior. 

On Monday (January 22), the BRAC University Public Relations Office issued a statement in this regard. It said that Asif Mahtab had worked as a part-time teacher at BRAC University. Currently, BRAC University does not have any contract with him. BRAC University is committed to maintaining the confidentiality of its employees and their contracts. BRAC University, in addition to encouraging cooperative, inclusive and cordial behavior among all on campus, respects the freedom of expression of its teachers and students. 

On Friday (January 19), Asif Mahtab tore two pages of a seventh grade textbook at a seminar titled ‘New Textbooks in the Current Curriculum: Reality and Future’ organized by the National Teachers Forum at the Institute of Diploma Engineers in Kakrail, Kakrail, Dhaka. 

Asif alleged that students were being brainwashed by inserting transgender stories in the book. At that time, he asked the seminar participants to buy the book from the market for 80 taka. Later, the teacher tore out the two pages related to the transgender story from the book and asked them to return it to the store. 

After this incident, on Sunday (January 21) at around 12:45 am, Mahtab wrote on his Facebook account, “Today I took a regular class at BRAC.” I just got a call telling me not to go to the university to take any more classes. I don't know why they suddenly made this decision. They didn't give me any reason.

Headline_English: Illegal or unregistered mobile phones may be shut down in July
Content_Enlish:
Illegal or unregistered mobile phones may be banned in July, said State Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Junaid Ahmed Palak. 

And those who have bought unregistered mobile phones will have the opportunity to register, the State Minister also said. 

The State Minister made these remarks to reporters after a courtesy call on European Union (EU) Ambassador Charles Hootley at his office at the Secretariat on Tuesday (January 23) afternoon. 

When asked when illegal or unregistered mobile phones will be banned, Palak said, "We expect that it will take us five months. To develop the technology, test it and make it operational. We do not want to impose any policy suddenly, so that there is no instability. 

For this reason, we have been saying from the beginning that no one should bring a phone illegally. No one should buy a phone illegally, so that they do not suffer later." That is why we are giving a reasonable time that we will develop the technology in the next three months, then test it in two months. We expect to make it operational by July. So that everyone is alert during this time and avoid this illegal path and buy the right way. 

When asked what will happen to the phones of those who have bought unregistered phones, Palak said that those who have bought them will have the opportunity to register. That is why there is a delay in registering new phones and transferring the name of second-hand phones. 

When asked how many such phones there could be in the unregistered and gray market, Palak said, I have not yet received this number. I first asked how many registered phones there are, then I asked how many user numbers there are, then I can tell you what this number is. 

We are getting phones at a much lower price in the gray market, domestic assembling companies are charging higher prices despite taking advantage of tax opportunities, regarding this, Palak said, our 17 assembling plants told me the issues, but after that I came to know and started working.

The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) is trying very sincerely to ensure that unregistered phones do not enter the gray market, do not enter illegally, and do not enter through smuggling. We are trying to protect our local industry by making the best use of technology and working to maintain law and order. 

Will the price of foam produced in our country come down, he said, yes. It will come down. When we can protect it, we can create pressure to add 50 percent value instead of 30 percent. Only then will the backward linkage industry develop. Just as we have seen in Korea, Vietnam, and Thailand, a manufacturing ecosystem will develop in Bangladesh as well.

Headline_English: Woman sets record by standing for 3 hours in freezing cold snow
Content_Enlish:
Due to the cold, many people are taking baths every day or two. Meanwhile, a woman in Poland has set a record for 3 hours in the cold ice. She was immersed in a large box filled with ice cubes for 3 hours. Her name is Katarzyna Jakubowska. 

This information has been revealed by Guinness World Records. 

48-year-old Katarzyna has set a Guinness World Record among women by passing the final test of her ability to tolerate cold. She was in the box filled with ice for 3 hours, 6 minutes and 45 seconds. 

The first record holder among men was Wim Hof, known as the 'Iceman'. He was in the box for 1 hour and 53 minutes. The current record holder is Krzysztof Gajewski of Poland. He was in the ice for 3 hours, 11 minutes and 27 seconds. 

Katarzyna is a professional designer. She took this step to test her endurance and encourage other women to participate in this challenge. 

Katarzyna said, "I believe that as women we have a lot of strength. I want to show people that if we want to, we can do it." 

Before attempting this record, Katarzyna underwent a series of health tests. Because she wanted to make sure that this cold would not adversely affect her health. She trained three times for this challenge.

Headline_English: Severe cold wave in Dinajpur; lowest temperature of the season today
Content_Enlish:
Northern district Dinajpur is gripped by a severe cold wave. The mercury has dropped to five degrees. At the same time, the season's lowest temperature record is going on. The sun is not visible, due to which the level of suffering in public life is now at its peak. 

Due to the cold wind, the intensity of winter is being felt more than necessary. Dense fog has been observed for many days. The fog is pouring like rain. Vehicles are driving on the highway with headlights on even during the day. Low-income working people are the most affected by this cold. Many are ignoring the cold in search of work. Common people are trying to beat the cold by burning straw. 

According to the information from the regional meteorological office in Dinajpur, the lowest temperature recorded in this district on Sunday was 5.5 degrees Celsius. This is the lowest temperature of the current season.

Headline_English: Golpata harvesting begins in Sundarbans today
Content_Enlish:
Golpata is one of the most profitable trees in the Sundarbans, the world's largest single mangrove forest. Every year, at least 450 bawalis earn a living by cutting and selling the leaves of the golpata tree. However, the golpata has to be collected according to the time set by the forest department. This time, fishermen will start collecting golpata from the morning of January 28. It will continue until March 31. 

The bawalis will go to the Sundarbans on Sunday (January 28) morning with permission (pass-permit) from the forest department. They have already made all kinds of preparations for collecting golpata. 

Mozammel Hawlader, a bawali resident of Dakshin Char, Mongla, who has earned a living by collecting golpata for 13 years, said, "I have prepared a boat, bus, rope and sharp axes to go and cut golpata. I will go to the Sundarbans on Sunday with permission from the forest department. 

Siddiqur Rahman, a Bawali from Matherpar area of ​​Sharankhola, said, "Every year, boats have to be repaired before harvesting Golpata. Golpata is no longer available as before. Good prices are not available either. As the price of everything has increased, it is difficult to run a family. Even then, I go to harvest Golpata every year to sustain my profession. 

In addition, the boats for harvesting Golpata are made in a special way. Due to this, when the Golpata harvesting season is over, the boat has to be abandoned. And due to abandonment, extra money is spent on repairs every year, he said. 

According to forest department sources, boats with a capacity of 500 maunds will be able to harvest Golpata from the Sundarbans. Golpata is used in the roofs of houses in the Sundarbans. However, recently, Golpata roofs are also given to some resorts and bungalows for decoration. During the season, 60 taka is being collected as revenue excluding VAT for every quintal of Golpata harvested. 

As the demand for Golpata decreases day by day, the number of Golpata collectors has decreased compared to before. Earlier, Golpata was collected in 150 to 200 boats every year. Currently, the forest department claims that it has come down to less than a hundred. 

Kazi Muhammad Nurul Karim, Divisional Forest Officer of the Sundarbans East Forest Department, said that in 2023, 441 fishermen in 89 boats collected 16,000 quintals of Golpata. This year, Golpata collection will start from tomorrow. The number of fishermen and boats cannot be specified before the collection of the pass.

Headline_English: The Day of Judgment and the Signs Before It
Content_Enlish:
As the age of the world increases, we are facing the Day of Judgment. The question is - what is the Day of Judgment? 

Allah says in the Holy Quran, "The Day of Judgment will certainly come, there is no doubt about it, but most people do not believe in this infallible truth." (Surah Al-Momen, verse 59). When the event of the Day of Judgment occurs, no one will deny its occurrence. (Surah Al-Waqi'ah, verses 1-2). 

The condition of that day is described in the Quran, when the earth will shake with a great earthquake, the mountains will be completely crushed, then it will become scattered dust. (Surah Al-Waqi'ah verses 4, 5, 6). So we know what the condition of the earth will be on the Day of Judgment. So what should we do before that Day comes? Allah says in the Holy Quran, "O mankind, respond to the call of your Lord before that Day comes, and remember that Day when there will be no one to repel it from Allah." There will be no refuge for you on that Day, nor will you be able to deny it on that Day. (Surah Ash-Shura, verse 47). 

What are the signs of the Hour or how will we know that the Hour is near? The sign of the Hour is the continuous increase in tribulations. Tribulation is continuous problems, the loss of faith, the disappearance of affection and compassion among people, the increase in bloodshed or violence, the spread of falsehood, the decline of Islamic knowledge, the spread of music, the loss of trust, the increase in giving false witness, the increase in the tendency to take interest, the increase in bribery, the severing of ties of kinship, so that people will not even know how many types of problems or tribulations they are facing. The Messenger (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, then it will be so difficult to be patient or steadfast in faith that it will be as difficult as holding a burning coal in your hand. The Messenger (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) also said, before the Hour, knowledge will decrease and ignorance will spread. (Bukhari). Narrated Abu Hurairah (RA): The Hour will not come until the Euphrates gives up its golden mountain. People will fight over it and ninety-nine of them will die in a hundred. Each of them will think that perhaps he will be saved. (Muslim, 7008). 

Heavy rains, floods, droughts, severe cold, heat waves, frequent earthquakes and various natural disasters will occur in large numbers, causing the fields to become barren. People will become so wealthy that no one will be found to take Zakat. Islam will be attacked from all sides like a pack of wolves pouncing on its prey. 

What will happen when the Hour comes? Allah says in the Holy Quran, When the earth shakes with its tremors. When it gives up its burden. (Surah Zilzal, verses 1-2). 10 signs before the Hour. 1) Smoke, 2) The appearance of the Dajjal 3) Dabbatul Ard (creatures of the earth) 4) Sunrise from the west 5) The coming of Jesus (peace be upon him) 6) The coming of Gog and Magog 7) Landslides in the east 8) Landslides in the west 9) Landslides in the Arabian land 10) Only the disbelievers will deny the Hour. 

Allah says, And the disbelievers say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will certainly come to you." (Surah Saba, verse 3). No one will have the power to prevent the Hour. Allah also says, "Rather, it will come to them suddenly and will take them by surprise. So they will not be able to prevent it, nor will they be given respite." (Surah Al-Anbiya, verse 40). 

Therefore, every believer should consider every moment of life as the last moment before the Day of Judgment and refrain from the above-mentioned actions. No exchange will be accepted on the Day of Judgment. Allah says, “Fear the Day when no one will avail another in any way, nor will any exchange be taken.” (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 123) 

May Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, protect the Muslim nation from all the signs and horrors of the Day of Judgment. May He grant them the ability to live their lives on faith and good deeds.

Headline_English: What Iran said about the attack on US forces in the Middle East
Content_Enlish:
Iran's ambassador to the United Nations, Amir Seyed Iravani, said on Tuesday that Iran was not involved in any action or attack against the US military. 

In a briefing with reporters on Monday, US National Security Adviser Jack Sullivan said that Washington has every reason to believe that Iran is involved in attacks on US interests in the Middle East. 

Recently, three ships in the Red Sea were targeted by drones and missiles. The US claimed that three drones were shot down by a US warship patrolling there in the attack and attempted attack. 

Last Sunday, local time, the US military claimed that these drones and missiles were launched by the Houthi rebel armed group in Yemen. 

The Pentagon says that the US warship USS Kearney assisted the ships that were attacked. The military forces of 10 countries, including the US, are attached to the warship. The Pentagon claims that these drones and missiles were launched from Houthi-controlled areas in Yemen. Missiles hit two of the three ships.

Headline_English: Why do bats hang upside down?
Content_Enlish:
Birds can fly. At night, they sleep sitting on tree branches. Bats can also fly. But they do not sleep sitting or lying on tree branches like other birds or animals. 

They hang upside down. Day or night—whenever bats rest, they do not sit upright, but hang upside down from trees. But why? 

The first answer is that bats can fly, so it is convenient for them to hang upside down. 

But birds also fly, why don't they hang upside down? 

Bats are not birds, they are animals. 

Bats do not have the same advantages that birds have. Bats are actually the only mammals that can fly. Mammals are not supposed to be able to fly—that's what science says. One reason for this is the physical structure of mammals. 

With the mass per square inch of their body, they cannot actually fly in the sky. Birds can, because their mass (in common parlance, weight) is much less than their body size. Bats were also supposed to have trouble flying, but they didn't, because of a long evolutionary process. Bats have overcome the physical obstacles to flying through evolution. 

In the case of birds, the comparative weight is low, as is the structure of their wings. 

The type of flying depends on how much weight the wings can carry, how much support they provide to the body in the air. The weight and structure of the wings of a bird are such that they can easily fly in the sky by leaning on their feet. In this case, the bird has to use Newton's third law. This law says that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. When a bird flies while sitting on a branch, it first pushes the branch with its foot. As the bird's foot pushes the branch, the branch also returns an equal force to the bird's foot. With the help of that force, the bird moves forward. While moving forward, the bird is supposed to fall down due to the attraction of the earth's gravity. But to prevent that, the bird spreads its wings. The wings act like a parachute. Then the bird flaps its wings and starts flying. This is called airlift. Similarly, insects like wasps, bees, wasps, termites or grasshoppers also fly. 

The structure of the legs of bats is not like that of birds or insects. As I said earlier, bats have a heavy body like other mammals. With this heavy body, it is not possible for them to fly while standing on the ground or a branch. But if a bat is released from the top of a building. It will be able to fly. Before falling from above, it will be able to prepare its wings for flight and will be able to fly comfortably. 

That means that bats cannot fly from a standing position due to physical limitations. But bats also need to stand. For this reason, they hang upside down on the branches of trees. When they need to fly, they release their hind legs from the branch and start falling from the tree towards the ground. However, before landing, bats can flap their wings and start flying. 

Bats have become skilled at this through a long process of evolution. So, after leaving the branch, they do not have to fall very far. They almost immediately prepare their wings and start flying. 

Since there is no opportunity to fly by pushing off the ground or a branch, and there is no need to stand or sit, bats' legs are not suitable for standing or sitting. That is why bats cannot sit on their feet after leaving the ground, nor can they fly. Then the poor thing has nothing to do but flap their wings on the ground. So, hanging is the advantage for bats. 

Since bats' legs are backwards, there is no way to hang straight without hanging upside down. This is how bats have adapted themselves for millions of years. This is how they can sleep and rest.

Headline_English: US suspends V-22 Osprey aircraft operations
Content_Enlish:
The US military has announced that it is suspending operations of its V-22 Osprey aircraft following a crash off the coast of Japan that killed soldiers. 

The US Air Force Special Operations Command said in a statement on Wednesday evening that it had ordered the suspension of operations of the Air Force's V-22 Osprey aircraft "to minimize risk while the investigation continues" into last week's crash. 

Eight US Air Force personnel were killed in the crash last week. The cause of the crash is still unknown, but preliminary investigations suggest that mechanical failure may have caused the crash. 

The V-22 Osprey aircraft is a joint venture between US aircraft manufacturer Boeing and helicopter manufacturer Bell. Its design combines the characteristics of both an aircraft and a helicopter. The V-22 Osprey aircraft can take off and land vertically like a helicopter. 

However, after a series of accidents this year, questions have been raised about the reliability of the aircraft.

Headline_English: Why the Supreme Court returned Imran Khan's appeal
Content_Enlish:
The Supreme Court of Pakistan has rejected the appeal filed by former Prime Minister Imran Khan seeking to quash his three-year sentence in the case of selling state gifts (Toshakhana). Imran Khan filed this appeal through lawyer Sardar Latif Khosa on Saturday. 

The Supreme Court office said that the appeal was sent back as incomplete. 

Earlier, on December 11, Imran had filed a similar appeal in the Islamabad High Court. The High Court dismissed this appeal. Imran Khan then approached the Supreme Court. 

Imran Khan was convicted of selling gifts received while in public office. On August 5, the District and Sessions Judge Court of Islamabad sentenced him to three years in prison. Imran was disqualified from elections for five years due to his conviction and imprisonment. 

Voting for the National Assembly elections in Pakistan will be held on February 8. As part of his bid to contest the election, Imran Khan, the founder of Pakistan's opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, first approached the Islamabad High Court and then the Supreme Court against the verdict. 

Imran Khan lost the prime ministership in April last year after losing a no-confidence vote in the country's parliament. Since then, more than a hundred cases have been filed against him. Imran is currently in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi after being arrested in several other cases, including corruption. 

Imran Khan and his party claim that these cases were deliberately filed against him as part of a conspiracy by the ruling government and the army so that he could not contest the upcoming national elections.

Headline_English: Victory Day celebrated with various events in Jhenaidah
Content_Enlish:
The great Victory Day was celebrated in Jhenaidah through various programs. On this occasion, the program was started by firing 31 cannons at the Sadar Police Station premises at sunrise on Saturday. 

In the morning, a colorful victory rally was taken out from the district Awami League party office premises. In addition, a rally was taken out under the leadership of Advocate Salma Yasmin, General Secretary of the District Jubo Mohila League. The rally went through various streets of the city and ended at Prerna Ekattor Square. 

At 7 am, wreaths were placed at the Independence Memorial. On behalf of the state, first the Deputy Commissioner SM Rafiqul Islam, then Superintendent of Police Azim-ul-Ahsan, District Council Chairman Dr. M Harun Or Rashid, District Awami League, Muktijoddha Sangsad, Jhenaidah Press Club, Television Journalist Forum, government offices, private, voluntary organizations and political organizations. Later, tributes were paid to the statue of the Father of the Nation. In addition, parades, receptions for brave freedom fighters, discussions and cultural programs have been organized on the great Victory Day.

Headline_English: China has built 37 nuclear reactors in 10 years
Content_Enlish:
China is spending a lot of money to develop wind and solar power to close coal power plants and reduce oil and gas imports. In addition, China's biggest goal is nuclear power. The United Nations' International Atomic Energy Agency reported that China has built 37 new nuclear reactors in the last decade. Now the number of nuclear reactors in the country has reached 55. Whereas the United States has built only two new nuclear reactors in the last 10 years. It has the world's largest number of 92 reactors. India currently has 22 nuclear plants. Of these, only two were built in the last 10 years. China is preparing to build eight new nuclear reactors every year. China's nuclear regulatory agency has said that we can install 8-10 new reactors every year. Many countries around the world have started opposing nuclear reactors due to safety reasons. China's State Council (Cabinet) has approved the construction of 10 nuclear reactors in 2022. Currently, 22 nuclear reactors are under construction in China, which is more than any other country in the world. 

It is very easy to build reactors in China due to cheap loans and easy licenses. It is not easy to build new reactors in Western countries. Although in China, state-owned companies build nuclear reactors. Apart from cheap loans, there is no barrier to granting land licenses in China. The government provides subsidies (tariff feed-in tariffs) to companies supplying electricity generated from nuclear plants. The International Energy Agency says that due to these reasons, the price of nuclear power has come down to about 6,500 taka per megawatt hour. Whereas in America it is 10,000 and in the European Union it is about 18,000 taka.

Headline_English: Oil field discovered in Sylhet
Content_Enlish:
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Nasrul Hamid said that oil has been found in well number 10 of the Sylhet Gas Field. 

He gave this information at a press conference at the Secretariat on Sunday afternoon. 

The State Minister said, "We have confirmed the presence of fuel oil along with three gas layers in well number 10 of the Sylhet Gas Field. There is a possibility of getting 500 to 600 barrels of oil there per day." 

Energy and Mineral Resources Department Secretary Nurul Amin and Petrobangla Chairman Janendra Nath Sarkar were also present at the press conference. 

State Minister Nasrul Hamid said that the entire oil reserves will be known after 4 to 5 months. It is expected that the reserves here will be permanent. 

He said that drilling was completed at a depth of 2576 meters in well number 10 of Sylhet. Gas was found in 4 layers in this well. The lower layer is tested at 2540-2550 meters and a flow of 25 million cubic feet of gas is found and the flowing pressure is 3250 psi. The reserve is 43-100 billion cubic feet. Another good gas layer is found at 2460-2475 meters, where it is expected to find 25-30 million cubic feet of gas if tested here. The presence of gas is found at 2290-2310 meters. Another zone is found at a depth of 1397-1445 meters where the presence of oil was found by testing on December 8, which initially has an API gravity of 29.7 degrees. The flow of oil is found at 35 barrels of oil per hour at self-pressure. Once the test is completed, the oil reserves will be known. If produced simultaneously at depths of 2540 and 2460 meters, it will sustain for about 8-10 years and its value as an average weighted value is about 8500 crore taka. If produced at a rate of 20 million cubic feet, it will sustain for more than 15 years.

Headline_English: Soumya's importance has increased in Shakib's absence!
Content_Enlish:
Soumya Sarkar has been included in the three-match ODI and T20I series against New Zealand. Shakib Al Hasan is not playing in this series again. Captain Nazmul Hossain Shanto believes that Soumya's importance has increased in the absence of this all-rounder. 

Earlier, the chief selector had mentioned New Zealand's previous performance in explaining his inclusion. This time, Shanto is talking about the importance of pace bowling all-rounder Soumya in Shakib's absence. 

He said, 'I don't want to talk about any individual cricketer. Everyone is important. But Soumya's responsibility is important. Along with batting, his bowling is also very important. Since Shakib Bhai is not here, (Soumya's) batting and bowling are also important. I think the team management has included him in the team with this in mind. He has experience along with that.'

Headline_English: International Migrants Day today
Content_Enlish:
Today is International Migrants Day. Every year, December 18 is celebrated as 'International Migrants Day' to ensure the dignity and rights of migrants and their families worldwide. 

The United Nations General Assembly decided to celebrate the day globally on December 4, 2000. The origin of this day was mainly around the issues related to the large-scale migration and the interests of large numbers of migrants scattered in different parts of the world. 
In 1990, the United Nations adopted the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families. 
Many countries, government organizations or ministries, including various non-governmental organizations and organizations, celebrate the day with due dignity. Among these, discussions, road meetings, processions, cultural programs, and human chains are notable.

Headline_English: I didn't realize they would beat Sri Lanka like this: Shoaib Akhtar
Content_Enlish:
Former Pakistan fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar had advised India to be careful about the tough challenge against Sri Lanka in the Asia Cup final. However, the way the Sri Lankan team collapsed in front of India in the final has shocked the entire cricket world. Shoaib Akhtar may have felt a little embarrassed after seeing Sri Lanka's defeat. He may not have thought that India would win by playing like this. 

Former Pakistani speedster Shoaib praised the Indian cricket team on his YouTube channel, saying, "How wonderfully India won this tournament! After the previous match (defeat against Bangladesh), it seemed that India might be considered an underdog. But that was not the case. Hats off to India. India, you won brilliantly. Siraj, you won the match. You also did a good job of giving the prize money to the field staff. They deserve it. But you also bowled exceptionally well. Along with that, Hardik Pandya also bowled very well. He also took wickets. 

Shoaib believes that India's aggressive performance is a 'threat' for the rest of the teams before the World Cup, 'I think India will go to the World Cup with a good win (against Sri Lanka) and full of confidence. They have three ODIs against Australia before the World Cup. If they can win that, India will be a very strong team as a unit in batting, bowling and fielding. I think they are a cause for concern not only for Pakistan but for many other countries. The way they have beaten Sri Lanka, the way their bowling unit has performed, is great.' 

Praising Rohit Sharma's leadership, Shoaib said, 'Rohit Sharma's captaincy is going well. Earlier, he seemed very confused. Now his captaincy is understandable. Their management is also very good. The captain and the management are taking good decisions together. Bringing Kuldeep was a turning point. It was important for India to beat Sri Lanka. But I didn't know that they would beat Sri Lanka in such a way that the match would be over in 5-10 overs! From here on, India will play in the World Cup as the most dangerous team.'

Headline_English: 320 garment factories closed in eight months
Content_Enlish:
More than 300 garment factories have closed in the first eight months of this year. At the same time, purchase orders have decreased by 20 percent. Global demand for clothing has decreased due to inflation due to the Russia-Ukraine war. And these small and large garment factories have closed due to banking complications. However, 114 new garment factories have been opened at the same time. These factories have employed 12,500 workers. 

Exporters said that in addition to the depreciation of the rupee and falling global demand, these factories producing clothing for the foreign market have closed due to some other problems. Inflation has reached record levels in Europe and America. As a result, buyers there have reduced spending on consumer goods. This has reduced demand for ready-made garments. Due to this, brands and buyer organizations have reduced export orders. In the context of rising gas and electricity prices and increasing production costs, BGMEA President Faruk Hasan has written a letter seeking cooperation from foreign buyers and brands. In the letter, he has requested to relax the condition of purchasing fabrics and other accessories from specific foreign companies as a condition for garment purchase orders. 

According to the Industrial Police, 320 garment factories in the Industrial Police area have been closed from January to mid-August this year. Of the closed garment factories, 60 are members of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), 16 are members of the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA), 9 are members of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMEA) and five are members of the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority. Most of the remaining 223 are cottage industry enterprises (non-RMG). About 45 thousand workers used to work in the closed garment factories. 16 thousand 943 workers worked in the 60 factories that were members of the BGMEA. 16 thousand 173 workers were employed in non-RMG factories. However, the good news is that 114 new factories have been opened during this period. There have been new employment opportunities for 12,500 workers. About 10,000 workers were re-hired in 60 factories to open the factories. Of these, 38 are in the ready-made garment sector and 22 are in the textile sector. At the same time, 114 new garment factories have been opened. These factories have employed 12,500 workers. When asked about this, Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association President Faruk Hasan told Bangladesh Pratidin that the purchase orders from January to October 15 of this year have decreased by 20 percent compared to the same period of the previous year. It is very difficult, we are going through challenges from all sides. Maintaining export income for these 3 months is not easy for us; rather, it is very difficult. He further said that factories are closing down one by one or two. However, all factories are working much less than their capacity. At the moment, there are orders, not that there are none at all. 

BKMEA Executive President Mohammad Hatem said that many small factories could not survive due to the sky-high exchange rate difference between the taka and the dollar. Citing information from Bangladesh Bank, he said that more than 14 percent of garment factories were in default. He also said that about 100 members of BKMEA did not renew their membership this year. Last year, this number was around 800. They are not doing business now. Ready-made garment exporters believe that the next six months will be challenging for the country's garment industry as purchase orders from international buyers have decreased due to the impact of inflation. Meanwhile, garment imports from the United States from Bangladesh have decreased by 21.77 percent from January to August of this year. According to data published by the Office of Textiles and Apparel (OTEXA) under the US Department of Commerce, the United States imported garments worth $5.18 billion from Bangladesh in the first eight months of 2023. Bangladesh is the third largest garment supplier to the United States. According to OTEXA data, the United States' overall garment imports from the world from January to August of 2023 decreased by 22.77 percent to $53.45 billion. This amount was $69.21 billion in the same period in 2022. Bangladesh's top garment export market, the United States, saw its exports fall 5.51 percent to $8.51 billion from $9.01 billion in fiscal year 2021-22. About 85 percent of garment exports go to the European Union and the United States.

Headline_English: Metrorail's revenue till June last year was Tk 182.8 crore: Bridges Minister
Content_Enlish:
The total revenue from the metro rail since its launch till June last year has been 182.86514 taka, said Road Transport and Bridges Minister and Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader. 

He gave this information in a written reply to a question from Awami League member M. Abdul Latif in the session of the National Assembly on Monday. Speaker Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury presided over the session. 

Obaidul Quader said that the Prime Minister inaugurated the section from Uttara North to Agargaon on December 28, 2022 and the section from Agargaon to Motijheel on November 4, 2023. Now, the metro rail from Uttara North to Motijheel is operating regularly from 7:10 am to 8:40 pm every day except Fridays, according to the scheduled schedule. According to the final accounts of the 2022-23 financial year audited by the audit firm, the total income till June this year is 18,28,06,514 (eighteen crores eighty-two lakhs six thousand five hundred and fourteen) taka. 

He said, following the Prime Minister's directives, the construction work for extending MRT Line-6 ​​from Motijheel to Kamalapur by 1.16 kilometers is in full swing. So far, the overall progress of the work is 25 percent. Plans have been made to launch this part in June next year.

Headline_English: 48 BGB platoons deployed to secure garment factories
Content_Enlish:
The third round of blockade is underway across the country on the call of BNP and like-minded parties. Meanwhile, the garment workers' movement is also underway. In such a situation, 48 platoon members of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in Dhaka and surrounding districts to strengthen the security of factories. A sufficient number of BGB are also deployed across the country to control the law and order situation. 

On Wednesday morning, BGB Public Relations Officer Md. Shariful Islam confirmed the matter. 

He said that 48 platoons of BGB have been deployed in Dhaka and surrounding districts to strengthen the security of garment factories. In addition, a sufficient number of BGB are deployed across the country to control the law and order situation. 

Earlier, the minimum wage of garment workers was set at 12,500 taka. State Minister for Labor and Employment Monnujan Sufian made this announcement at the Secretariat on Tuesday afternoon. On the other hand, labor leaders have rejected the announced wage. 

Meanwhile, garment workers have protested in various areas including Konabari and Jarun of Gazipur City Corporation. They were also seen committing vandalism and arson during this time.

Headline_English: Four messages from the US to the three parties
Content_Enlish:
US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Donald Lu has written to the country's three main political parties, Awami League, BNP and Jatiya Party. The letter mainly contains four messages from the US to the three parties. The letter mentions free, fair and violence-free elections and unconditional dialogue in Bangladesh. US Ambassador Peter Haas met with Jatiya Party leaders yesterday and handed over a copy of the letter. At that time, it was informed that the same letter would be given to the three political parties. Some time later, a message from the US embassy conveyed four messages of the US position. According to diplomatic sources, all four messages of the US position were given in the letter. Yesterday, US Embassy spokesperson Stephen Ebeli said in a message that Ambassador Haas requested a meeting with senior leaders of the three main political parties to present the US position on the upcoming elections. The statement highlighted four statements as the US position. The US position is as follows: 1. The US wants free and fair elections in a peaceful manner and calls on all parties to refrain from violence and exercise restraint. 2. The US does not favor any political party over another. 3. The United States calls on all parties to engage in dialogue without any conditions. 4. We will continue to apply the 3-C visa policy equally to those who are obstructing the democratic election process. Peter Haas went to the political office of the Jatiya Party Chairman in Banani at 3 pm yesterday. He handed over a letter written by Donald Lu to Jatiya Party Chairman GM Quader. Jatiya Party Chairman GM Quader was accompanied by Jatiya Party Secretary General Md. Mujibul Haque Chunnu, Co-Chairman Kazi Firoz Rashid, and Chairman's Advisor Masrur Maula in the meeting with the US Ambassador. Later, in a media briefing, Md. Mujibul Haque Chunnu said that the US Ambassador had brought a letter written by their Assistant Secretary of State for Central and South Asian Affairs Donald Lu. He handed over the letter to our party chairman. Peter Haas said that the same letter is being given to all three parties - Awami League, BNP, and Jatiya Party. Chunnu said, the main point of this letter is that the United States wants to see free, fair and participatory elections in Bangladesh. When asked what was discussed, he told reporters that a lot was discussed in the meeting, but they were unofficial. I do not want to talk about those issues. The United States is our development partner. We have a $6 billion export trade with them. As well-wishers, they want a good election in Bangladesh. They want all parties to participate in the elections. There should be a fair environment during the voting. When asked whether the Jatiya Party has given any message to US Ambassador Peter Haas, Mujibul Haque Chunnu said, how the elections will be held, how to make them fair and impartial, is purely an internal matter of our country. Why should we tell the US ambassador what kind of environment we want for the elections or whether the Jatiya Party will participate in the elections or not? We are asking the Election Commission to organize fair elections, and we are requesting the government for their cooperation. 

Rizvi said about receiving the letter: BNP has received a letter from Donald Lu, Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs of the United States. BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi Ahmed confirmed to reporters that he had received the letter. However, it was not stated when, how, and where he received the letter.

Headline_English: Work begins in Sundarbans to protect endangered freshwater crocodile
Content_Enlish:
After the saltwater crocodile, the Forest Department has officially taken the lead in breeding the freshwater crocodile (marsh crocodile), which is on the endangered list of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). For this, three freshwater crocodiles of the extinct species, rescued from the rivers of Faridpur, Pabna and Narail, have been brought to the Karamjal Wildlife Breeding Center in the Chandpai Range of the East Sundarbans Division of Bagerhat. 

Of these three crocodiles, one is male and two are female. Among them, one of the 14-year-old female crocodiles is an adult. Of the other two juvenile crocodiles, the male crocodile is 12 years old, and the other female crocodile is 10 years old. Since the male freshwater crocodiles are not adults, it will not be possible to hatch babies from eggs through breeding next season. The Forest Department hopes that by utilizing the experience of breeding saltwater crocodiles for almost two decades, it will be possible to hatch freshwater crocodiles from eggs at the Karamjal Wildlife Breeding Center in the Sundarbans by 2025. 

Officer-in-charge of the Karamjal Wildlife Breeding Center in the Sundarbans and crocodile expert Howlader M Azad Kabir said that since the country's first official wildlife breeding center was established in Karamjal in the Sundarbans in 2000, saltwater crocodiles, deer and the extinct species of Batargur Baska turtle have been born and raised through breeding and released into rivers and forests. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) included the freshwater crocodile (marsh crocodile) in Bangladesh in 2000 as there are no freshwater crocodiles. Since then, freshwater crocodiles have not been seen in any river or stream in the country. On October 17 this year, a 90 kg, 7 feet 6 inches long freshwater (marsh crocodile) male crocodile was first caught in Bhubaneshwar, a tributary of the Padma river in Aliabad of Faridpur Sadar. Four days later, on October 21, a 80 kg, 7 feet 4 inches long freshwater female crocodile was caught in Udaypur of Sujanagar upazila of Pabna. The last 80 kg, 6 feet 5 inches long freshwater female crocodile was caught on October 28 from Maigram Beel near the Madhumotir river in Logagra upazila of Narail. On November 9, the Wildlife Management and Nature Conservation Department sent these three freshwater crocodiles to the Karamjal Wildlife Breeding Center in the Sundarbans for conservation and breeding. In Karamjal, saltwater crocodiles and extinct species of Batargur Baska turtles have been kept in three separate pans (crocodile sheds) as all three ponds have salty water for breeding and living. These three crocodiles, who are used to eating fish from open water bodies, have not eaten meat so far. They are eating only fish. The three crocodiles are adapting to the environment in the fresh water shed of the Karamjal Wildlife Breeding Center. After digging a new pond for the three crocodiles or raising the banks of an old pond to prevent saltwater from entering, the three freshwater crocodiles will be released from the pan into the pond. Even if a female crocodile is an adult, it will not be possible to hatch babies from eggs through breeding until only the male crocodile is an adult. This crocodile expert said that in 2025, it will be possible to hatch babies from eggs through breeding freshwater crocodiles at the Karamjal Wildlife Breeding Center in the Sundarbans.

Headline_English: James Webb Space Telescope reveals Milky Way galaxy in the universe
Content_Enlish:
An international research team led by University of California, Riverside (UCR) astronomer Alexander de la Vega, using the James Webb Space Telescope, has identified the most distant barred spiral galaxy similar to the Milky Way. 

The galaxy, named Sears-2112, challenges previous ideas about galaxy evolution. It suggests that spiral galaxies may exhibit structure and order much earlier in the history of the universe than previously thought. 

In the study, published in the journal Nature, scientists from the Centro de Astrobiologia in Spain shed light on Sears-2112. 

Traditionally, barred spiral galaxies like the Milky Way were thought to have formed after the universe reached half its current age of about 13.8 billion years.

Headline_English: Can Brazil play in the 2026 World Cup?
Content_Enlish:
Brazilian footballers seem to be disappointed with the word disappointment. There are doubts whether the five-time World Cup winners will be able to make it through the qualifiers this time. 

Brazil is in dire straits after losing three consecutive matches in the upcoming 2026 World Cup qualifiers. The Seleção have only managed to score 1 point in the last three matches. They lost to Argentina 1-0 at home. 

Argentina is at the top of the South American World Cup qualifiers with 15 points in 6 matches. Uruguay is second with 13 points in the same matches, Colombia is third with 12 points, Venezuela is fourth with 9 points and Ecuador is fifth with 8 points. 

Meanwhile, the Seleção is sixth in the points table with 7 points after losing 3 of 6 matches. In the World Cup qualifiers, ten teams will play a total of 18 matches on a home and away basis. After that, the top six teams will have the opportunity to play directly in the 2026 World Cup. 

Brazil is currently sixth in the points table. If they do not finish in the top six after all the matches, the five-time world champions will not be able to participate directly in the 2026 World Cup. 

If Brazil finishes seventh in the qualifiers, the Selecao will have to participate in the FIFA play-off tournament. And if they do not finish in the top seven, Neymar-Vinicius could have to suffer the same fate as Italy.

Headline_English: Women in Iran could face 10 years in prison if they don't follow dress code
Content_Enlish:
The Iranian government is getting stricter on women's clothing. Lawmakers passed a bill on Wednesday. 

According to the bill, women can be sentenced to up to 10 years in prison for violating the dress code. NDTV reported this, citing AFP. 

According to the report, lawmakers today approved a bill supporting the culture of hijab and chastity. The bill will be on trial for three years. However, the approval of Iran's Guardian Council is required for the bill to be implemented. 

Iran already has a strict stance on women's clothing. Women are punished for any change in their clothing. 

Protests broke out last year after the death of 22-year-old Kurdish woman Masa Amini in police custody over the hijab issue. Hundreds of people, including members of the security forces, were killed in the protests. Officials have arrested thousands of protesters, calling it a foreign-instigated "riot". 

According to the draft bill, if an Iranian woman does not wear a headscarf (hijab) or appropriate clothing at the instigation of a foreign, hostile government, media or organization, she could be imprisoned for five to 10 years. A political revolution took place in Iran in 1979, which is known as the Islamic Revolution. Since then, the hijab law has been enacted in the country. According to that law, women have to cover their hair and wear long and loose clothes. Many Iranian women have been reprimanded, fined and arrested for violating the law. 

NDTV reported that in recent months, Iranian authorities have been making a concerted effort to punish women who fail to comply with the dress code. Police patrols have also been increased. Even surveillance has been increased in businesses to ensure that clothing is sold according to the rules.

Headline_English: Bangladesh team leaves the country this afternoon to play in the World Cup
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has announced Bangladesh's World Cup squad, leaving out dashing opener Tamim Iqbal. The country's best opener did not make it to the 15-member squad due to injury. 

The Bangladesh Cricket Board announced the name of the World Cup squad on its Facebook fanpage last night as the last team for the ICC World Cup 2023. The World Cup jerseys were unveiled in a unique way in a video message and the names of the teams were announced one by one. The 15 cricketers who got a chance in the World Cup squad displayed their jerseys and expressed their opinions. Captain Shakib Al Hasan was the first to display his jersey, followed by Mahmudullah Riyad. 

The Bangladesh team will leave for India today, Wednesday. The Tigers will leave for Guwahati, India, from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 4 pm. Upon reaching India, the Tigers will play two warm-up matches. From there, the Bangladesh team will leave for Dharamsala. The Tigers' first match against Afghanistan will be on October 7.

Headline_English: Facebook must abide by Bangladesh's laws and regulations: Mustafa Jabbar
Content_Enlish:
Posts and Telecommunications Minister Mustafa Jabbar has said that Facebook must abide by the laws, rules and regulations of Bangladesh. It cannot be used as a tool for anyone's misdeeds. Facebook authorities must give utmost importance to this issue. The undesirable situation created by its misuse, including the dissemination of false information and spreading rumors, is a big challenge for individuals, society, the state and Facebook. 

The minister urged Facebook authorities to take initiatives to prevent anyone from opening a Facebook account using a fake identity. 

Facebook's Director for Central and South Asia Sharim Aziz and Head of Public Policy for Bangladesh Affairs Rezan Sarwar met in a meeting at the minister's office at Dak Bhaban in Dhaka on Monday. The minister made this call during the meeting. 

The minister said that the Telecommunication Regulatory Commission will provide all possible assistance to Facebook in verifying the correct identity of a person for a Facebook account. 

Referring to Bangladesh as a big market for Facebook, the minister said, "Our girls can also become entrepreneurs and be empowered by using the opportunity to buy and sell products on social media. But for that, we cannot let the country, state and people become insecure." In continuation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Digital Bangladesh program, high-speed digital connectivity has been reached at the doorsteps of people across the country, including remote areas of the country. 

Mustafa Jabbar called for stopping rumors, propaganda, militancy, communalism, sedition, pornography, gambling and content against the socio-cultural values ​​of Bangladesh in addition to complying with laws and regulations. 

Highlighting the cordial relationship between the two in the last five and a half years following the first meeting with the Facebook authorities in 2018, the minister said, "We want Facebook to remove all the content we report." 

He said, "In addition to creating social chaos by using fake Facebook IDs, many people are being cheated by a class of fraudsters." If you can open an account with a real ID, it is possible to easily overcome the existing challenges. 

The Facebook delegation has agreed in principle to solve the existing problems. The team said that it is possible to remove content related to rumors and propaganda through international fact checking. 

The team acknowledges that the policies, laws of other countries and the situation in Bangladesh are very different. Therefore, Facebook is cautious about harmful content. In any regulation, people's personal safety must be taken into account. The government has also repeatedly said to be aware of risky content in Facebook's policy. Facebook has also taken measures in that light. It will take necessary measures in the future as well.

Headline_English: 2 people sentenced to life imprisonment, 5 others to life imprisonment in Narayanganj murder case
Content_Enlish:
The court sentenced two people to life imprisonment and a fine of Tk 50,000 and five months' suspended imprisonment in a murder case filed at Fatullah Police Station in Narayanganj. Five others were also sentenced to life imprisonment and a fine of Tk 50,000 and six months' suspended imprisonment in default. 

Those sentenced to life imprisonment are Saleha Begum, wife of Idris Chakidar of Dakshin Shiarchar area of ​​Fatullah, and Monir Hossain, son of Billal Munshi of Kotwaler Bagh area. Their Saleha Begum was present in the court and Monir Hossain was absconding. 

Those sentenced to life imprisonment are Md. Kajal Mia, son of Helal Uddin of Kotwaler Bagh area of ​​Fatullah, Md. Jewel, son of the late Abed Ali of Lal Kha area, Md. Nurul Islam, son of Abdul Salam, Majedul Islam Manju of Abdul Salam of Barguna district and Liton, son of the deceased Abul Kashem of Jessore district. 
The verdict was announced in the court of Additional Sessions Judge Umme Saraban Tahura of the First Court of Narayanganj on Monday afternoon. 
Assistant Public Prosecutor Advocate Shipra Modak said that on the night of April 21, 2011, Kabir Hossain (35), a tenant of Anis Mia in Shiachar area of ​​Fatullah, went missing from his house. The next morning, his body was recovered from a pond next to the house. His wife Taslima Akhter filed a case with Fatullah Police Station as the plaintiff in the incident. The court announced the verdict based on the confessional statements of three people and the testimony of 11 witnesses after the long trial of the case.

Headline_English: 17 people die of dengue in 24 hours, 3,084 hospitalized
Content_Enlish:
In the last 24 hours, 17 more people have died of dengue fever in the country. With this, 839 people have died of dengue this year so far. At the same time, 3,084 more people have been admitted to hospitals due to dengue. 

This information was given in a press release sent by the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services on Monday. 

The release said that among the new dengue patients, 894 people have been admitted to various hospitals in Dhaka and 2,190 have been admitted to various hospitals outside Dhaka. 

Currently, a total of 10,032 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in various government and private hospitals in the country. Currently, 3,861 people are admitted to government and private hospitals in Dhaka and 6,171 dengue patients are admitted to various hospitals of other departments. 

This year, 1,70,768 patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country for treatment due to dengue. Of these, 74,127 have been in Dhaka and 96,641 have been treated outside Dhaka. 

Of the infected, 159,897 have recovered from the hospital and returned home. 69,692 in Dhaka and 90,205 outside Dhaka have recovered and returned home.

Headline_English: Finland is the happiest country in the world, Bangladesh is 118th
Content_Enlish:
Today is March 20, World Happiness Day. Every year on the eve of this day, the United Nations publishes a list of the happiest countries. This time too, the World Happiness Report 2023 has been published. 

Finland is at the top of the list for the sixth consecutive time out of 137 countries. Bangladesh is ranked 118th out of 137 countries. Bangladesh was ranked 94th in the 2022 report. 

And this time, war-torn country Afghanistan is at the bottom of the list of happy countries. The country was at the bottom of the list last year as well. 

Top 10 happiest countries 

Finland is first in the list of happiest countries, Denmark is second, Iceland is third, Israel is fourth, Netherlands is fifth, Sweden is sixth, Norway is seventh, Switzerland is eighth, Luxembourg is ninth and New Zealand is tenth. 

South Asian and other countries 

Among the South Asian countries, Nepal is ranked 78th, Pakistan is 108th, Sri Lanka is 112th, India is 126th and Bangladesh is 118th. 
On the other hand, Afghanistan is at the bottom of the list of happy countries this time. Afghanistan was at the bottom of the list last year as well. 

Canada is 13th in the list, the United States 15th and the United Kingdom 19th. And war-torn Ukraine is at 92nd position. Russia is at 70th position. 

How the list of happy countries is made 

To list happy countries, a number from zero to 10 is measured based on people's own assessment of happiness, as well as economic and social conditions. In addition, the personal sense of well-being of the people of each country, personal freedom, GDP and level of corruption are considered.

Headline_English: Awami League wants victory, BNP is also preparing
Content_Enlish:
All five parliamentary constituencies in Jamalpur are currently occupied by the ruling Awami League. Although some from other political parties have been elected separately a few times since independence, Awami League candidates have been elected in most of the five constituencies. Potential Awami League candidates are roaming the field in the hope of nomination to maintain this winning streak. 

Although BNP candidates have said they will not participate in the elections except under a non-partisan caretaker government, they are also preparing for the elections. And the Jatiya Party is in the field in the hope of vacating the seat as a partner in the Awami League-led alliance. 

Jamalpur-1 (Dewanganj-Bakshiganj): Current MP Abul Kalam Azad is in the field as a strong candidate of the Awami League in this constituency. He has been elected as a member of parliament five times from here. After being elected as a member of parliament in the December 29, 2008 election, he served as the Minister of Information and Cultural Affairs. Apart from Abul Kalam Azad, former president of Bakshiganj Upazila Awami League Nur Mohammad is roaming the field to get the party nomination in this constituency. He is campaigning in every ward and union of the area. Barrister Samir Sattar, son of former Commerce Minister MA Sattar, Supreme Court lawyer and president of Dhaka Chamber of Commerce, is in the field as a young candidate to get the nomination of the Awami League. He is campaigning in various ways, including mass communication in the area, distributing relief to the affected and distressed people due to natural disasters. Apart from this, former Additional IGP Md. Mokhlesur Rahman is in the field as an Awami League nomination aspirant. Dewanganj Upazila BNP convener and former MP M Rashiduzzaman Millat is active in the field as a BNP nomination aspirant. Women's party leader Sahida Akhter Rita is also in the field as a strong candidate. Apart from this, Barrister Shahadat Bin Zaman Shobon, advisor to the BNP Chairperson and son of former IGP Abdul Qayyum and Rashiduzzaman Millat, is also a nomination aspirant. Former president of Jamalpur District Jatiya Party and Commerce Minister MA Sattar, and freedom fighter Engineer Sirajul Haque, advisor to party chairman GM Quader, are also seeking nomination from Jatiya Party. Bakshiganj Upazila President of Islami Andolon Maulana Abdul Majid is in the field as the party's sole candidate. 

Jamalpur-2 (Islampur): The strong candidate of Awami League in this constituency is Islampur Upazila Awami League President, current MP and State Minister for Religion Alhaj Faridul Haque Khan Dulal. He has been elected MP from this constituency for three consecutive terms and is vying for party nomination for the fourth time. Apart from this, Awami League's nomination in this constituency is Mehzabin Khaled, daughter of Liberation War Sector Commander Major General (Retd.) Khaled Mosharraf, former MP for reserved women's seat Mehzabin Khaled, former President of Airport Thana Awami League Shahjahan Ali Mandal and current MP for reserved women's seat Begum Husne Ara. Former BNP MP Sultan Mahmud Babu of this constituency was once a vocal figure in the area. Despite that, Islampur Upazila BNP President Sultan Mahmud Babu is a strong candidate for BNP here. Apart from him, District BNP Science and Technology Affairs Secretary Nabi Newaz Khan, former Upazila Chairman, and Upazila BNP former Vice President Monowar Hossain BSC are party nomination aspirants in this constituency. Jatiya Party's nomination aspirants are Presidium member and Jamalpur District and Islampur Upazila Convener Mustafa Al Mahmud. 

Jamalpur-3 (Melandoh-Madarganj): Mirza Azam, the party's central organizing secretary and former state minister, is in the field as the sole candidate of Awami League. He has been elected as a member of parliament for six consecutive times in this constituency since 1991 and has served as the state minister of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute. He has received the title of the embodiment of Jamalpur's development for his extensive development activities in the district headquarters apart from his constituency. In Jamalpur, Sheikh Hasina Medical College, Economic Zone, Cultural Village, Sheikh Fazilatun Nesa Mujib Science and Technology University, Sheikh Fazilatun Nesa Mujib Private University, Textile College, Sheikh Russell Textile Institute, Rural Development Board, flyover, and several bypass road construction projects have been passed by ECNEC. Most of these projects are now visible. Here, Melanda Upazila BNP President Mostafizur Rahman Babul is in the field as the sole candidate of BNP. Babul, known as the leader of the anti-dictatorship movement of the 1990s, is quite popular with Trinamool leaders and activists. He regularly maintains contact with party leaders and activists and participates in meetings and gatherings. 

Jamalpur-4 (Sarishabari): The discussed MP from this constituency is former State Minister Dr. Murad Hasan. Although there has been a lot of discussion and criticism due to some of his activities and statements, he recently apologized in writing to the party president. He is again a party nomination aspirant. Apart from this, Awami League nomination aspirants in this constituency are former vice president of Sarishabari Upazila Awami League and former president of Tejgaon Thana Awami League Principal Abdur Rashid, Sarishabari Upazila Awami League president Chanowar Hossain Badsha, former vice president of Sarishabari Upazila Awami League and water affairs secretary of Swechchhasebak League Engineer Mahbubur Rahman Helal. 

Jamalpur district and upazila BNP president Faridul Kabir Talukder Shamim is in the field as the sole candidate of BNP in this constituency. He is the nephew of former BNP Secretary General late Barrister Abdus Salam Talukder. Former MPs Mamunur Rashid Joarder and Mokhlesur Rahman are the nomination aspirants of Jatiya Party.
