Headline_English: Finance Minister claims inflation and prices of daily necessities are tolerable
Content_Enlish:
The prices of daily necessities including rice, sugar, oil, and onions are on the rise. People from different walks of life are feeling uneasy about this. Meanwhile, Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal claims that inflation and prices of daily necessities are tolerable in the country. 

At a virtual press conference on LDCs on Saturday morning, he said that people's capabilities have also increased. At the same time, the Finance Minister also said that there is no fear of a decline in exports even after transitioning to a developing country. 

Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal said that prices are still at a tolerable level. In addition, people's purchasing power has also increased. According to the Bureau of Statistics, inflation increased in November compared to October. Currently, inflation is 5.98 percent. The Finance Minister is also satisfied with this. 

Responding to a question about the rising prices of daily necessities, the minister said, 'Inflation is present all over the world. We do not have it here. But even if the prices of goods increase, it is increasing less; it is at a tolerable level. If you compare it with any other country, you will see that Bangladesh is in a good position in terms of inflation. We have had an inflation rate of 5 to 5.5 percent for the last 15 years. No other country in the world can be found like this, it is an extraordinary country. 

He said, "Our capacity has increased, the skills of the people of this country have increased, productivity has increased. Our neighboring countries see that we are occupying their position. We take the challenges well, we are flexible in overcoming them. We want to use the challenges as opportunities. We have been successful in this in the past. We will use it extensively in the future as well. Our export trade is close to 45 billion dollars. We will go to 60 billion. Our exports will not decrease, nothing will decrease. We will not have to stumble and we will not be affected." 

The minister also said that the government is working to ensure that no crisis arises after transitioning to a developing country. He claims that increasing production will not have any impact on exports. 

Bangladesh will be added to the list of developing countries on November 23, 2026.

Headline_English: 4 more deaths on the first day of the year, 370 identified
Content_Enlish:
The deadly coronavirus pandemic has claimed 4 lives in the country in the last 24 hours. The total death toll has reached 28,076. During this period, 370 new Covid patients have been identified. 

The number of Covid patients identified has been increasing continuously for the past few days. In the last two days, the number of identified cases has crossed 500. 

On Thursday, 7 people died of Covid in the country. Of them, 4 are men and 3 are women. This is the highest number in more than a month. Earlier, the Directorate General of Health Services had reported the death of 9 people on November 25. 

On Friday, the Directorate General of Health Services said in a notification that 370 people have been identified as Covid-19 in 852 labs in 24 hours out of 15,214 samples tested. With this, the total number of corona infected people has reached 1,585,909. 

Meanwhile, 203 more people have recovered in the last 24 hours. With this, a total of 1,549,304 people have recovered. The detection rate considering the tests is 2.43 percent. 

The number of patients identified yesterday is the highest in 11 weeks. The last time more patients were infected was on October 13. 511 patients were identified that day. 

Since then, the number of daily identified patients has been below five hundred. On Wednesday, the daily identification reached close to five hundred, and a day later it exceeded five hundred. 

Before that, the last news of 382 Covid patients was reported on December 23. On December 11, the country reported the first case of infection with the new type of coronavirus, Omicron. 

Earlier, the first corona infection occurred in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. Within a few months, the virus spread around the world. The first infection of the coronavirus in Bangladesh was detected on March 8 last year. 

Due to the spread of the Delta variant, the number of patients has been increasing steadily since June this year. On July 28, the highest number of corona cases was detected in a single day, 16,023. 

The situation took a terrible turn in July-August this year. On August 5 and August 10, 264 deaths were reported, which is the highest number in a single day during the epidemic. 

At that time, the Delta variant of the coronavirus was spreading at a rate of 1,000 new deaths every five days. As the number of infections began to decline from September, the death toll also began to fall. 

New infections and deaths are increasing in Europe and America at the beginning of winter, and the new type of coronavirus, Omicron, identified in South Africa, is spreading rapidly in various countries. However, the situation in Bangladesh is still under control.

Headline_English: 12 killed in stampede at temple in Jammu and Kashmir
Content_Enlish:
At least 12 people have died in a stampede at the Vaishno Devi temple in Indian-controlled Jammu and Kashmir. At least 14 people were seriously injured in the incident. The incident took place on Friday night local time. 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi tweeted his condolences to the families of the victims. The Prime Minister's Office has announced a grant of Rs 2 lakh to each family of the deceased. Rs 50,000 will be given to the injured. 

According to an NDTV report, the incident took place at the Vaishno Devi temple in Katra. It is believed that the death toll may rise. The injured have been rescued and admitted to the local Narayani Hospital. Meanwhile, additional police have been deployed in the area around the temple after the incident. 

Jammu and Kashmir Police DG Dilbag Singh said that at least 12 people died in a stampede on the premises of the Vaishno Devi temple. Many were injured. He also said that initial investigation has revealed that the incident took place at 2:45 am. 

The police official said that there was an argument between two groups of visitors. When the two groups rushed towards each other, a stampede occurred. 

Every year from December 31 to January 1, extra people gather at this Vaishno Devi temple in Jammu and Kashmir. From Katra, one has to walk about 14-15 kilometers on a hilly path. Many people ride horses on that path. Almost the entire hilly path is a wide road. However, the path inside the temple is quite narrow.

Headline_English: Trade fair begins, ICT is the product of the year
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina inaugurated the 26th Dhaka International Trade Fair by declaring the country's ICT sector products as the product of the year. She inaugurated the fair through video conference from Ganabhaban on Saturday morning. 

This year, the month-long Dhaka International Trade Fair has been organized for the first time at the Bangabandhu Bangladesh-China Friendship Exhibition Center in Purbachal, a new town on the outskirts of the capital. 

This year, the Prime Minister declared ICT products and services as the Product of the Year 2022 to encourage exports according to the export policy at the fair. 

While inaugurating the fair, the Prime Minister said that although there were some problems at the new venue of the trade fair for the first time, businessmen have benefited. 

The Prime Minister said that after the country's independence, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman contributed to creating entrepreneurs to expand business in the country. During his time, the country achieved the highest growth. But after 1975, the country's progress stopped. 

After coming to power in 1996, the Awami League government emphasized socio-economic development. All private sectors were opened up to increase production in the country. Arrangements were made for duty-free import of various products. 

Preparations were made at that time to build Digital Bangladesh. Emphasis was placed on the use of various digital devices including computers. In addition to increasing production in industrial and trade, emphasis was placed on exports. Importance was also given to creating Bangladesh's own market in the world. 

Later, regarding Corona, the Prime Minister said that despite facing problems due to Corona like many countries in the world, Bangladesh's overall exports have increased. During this time, various facilities have been extended to businessmen. Bank loans have also been subsidized along with incentives. 

The Ministry of Commerce, Export Promotion Bureau and other supporting organizations are organizing this fair with the aim of increasing the country's export products and diversifying the market. 

The Dhaka International Trade Fair has been organized since 1995 under the joint initiative of the Ministry of Commerce and the Export Promotion Bureau with the aim of promoting, expanding, marketing and supporting the production of domestic products. 

This is the first time that this fair is being held in a permanent complex. Earlier, the trade fair was held in Agargaon. 

All stalls have been allocated in two halls of the air-conditioned exhibition center with an area of ​​14,366 square meters with state-of-the-art facilities. Pavilions, mini pavilions and food stalls have been constructed outside the fair complex (front and back). 

Bangabandhu Pavilion has been constructed as a special attraction of the fair. A total of 23 pavilions, 27 mini pavilions, 162 stalls and 15 food stalls of different categories have been allocated to various domestic and foreign organizations. 

This time, the products exhibited at the fair include local textiles, machineries, carpets, cosmetics and beauty aids, electrical and electronics, furniture, jute and jute products, household goods, leather and leather products including shoes, sports goods, sanitaryware, toys, stationery, crockery, plastics, melamine polymers, herbal and toiletries, imitation jewelry, processed food, handicraft products, home decor, etc. 

The fair will start from 10 am every day and will continue till 9 pm (till 10 pm on weekends). The entry fee for the fair is 40 taka for adults, 20 taka for children. 

For the convenience of visitors to the fair, 30 BRTC buses and other passenger buses will ply daily from Kuril Flyover. The fare is 40 taka per person. You will have to get off at Kanchan Bridge. From there, you will have to pay 10 taka for a rickshaw to go to the fair premises.

Headline_English: Remittance incentives increased in the new year
Content_Enlish:
The government has announced an increase in remittance incentives at the beginning of the New Year. From now on, expatriates will get a 2.5 percent incentive instead of 2 percent if they send remittances through legal channels. This will be effective from today. 

If someone sends 100 taka from abroad, they will get 102 taka earlier, but now expatriates will get 102 taka and 50 paisa. 

The Finance Ministry announced this information in a press release on Saturday. 

It said that the increase in remittance incentives is the Prime Minister's New Year's gift for expatriate Bangladeshi workers. 

The Finance Ministry says that the increase in government incentives for remittances is the Prime Minister's New Year's gift for expatriate Bangladeshi workers. 

The Finance Ministry's press release said, "Considering the importance of remittances sent by expatriates in improving the overall standard of living of the people, increasing foreign exchange reserves, preventing money laundering, creating employment and encouraging the repatriation of hard-earned foreign income of Bangladeshi workers working abroad to the country through legal means, it has been decided to increase the existing rate of 2 percent incentive/cash assistance provided by the government against remittances to 2.5%. This increased rate will be effective from January 1 of the current 2021-22 fiscal year. 

Earlier, the government announced a 2 percent incentive on remittances to encourage sending money through legal channels in the 2019-20 fiscal year. 

This decision has been taken to improve the standard of living of the people, increase foreign exchange reserves, prevent money laundering, and bring the foreign income of expatriates to the country through legal means."

Headline_English: Lionel Messi tests positive for coronavirus
Content_Enlish:
The new type of coronavirus, Omicron, has started spreading panic across the world. And it has started hitting footballers hard. Lionel Messi's name appeared on this list today. Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) has announced that four of its footballers, including Messi, have tested positive for Covid-19. 

PSG said that apart from Messi, who went to Argentina for the Christmas holiday, the club's Juan Bernat, Sergio Rico and Nathan Bitumajala have been infected with Corona. 

In addition to the four footballers, another support staff member of the PSG team has been infected with Corona. His name has not been announced yet. They were infected with Corona on Saturday night. But at that time, PSG did not name anyone. On Sunday, it was learned that the Argentine star footballer had been infected with Corona. 

Messi left his childhood club Barcelona and joined PSG this season. Meanwhile, PSG has a game in the French Cup tomorrow. They are scheduled to play against third division team Vannes. It is not yet known whether that match will take place. 

PSG has said that there is no reason to worry about the physical condition of the four footballers, including Messi, despite being infected with Corona. They are all in isolation.

Headline_English: 2,500 flights canceled in the United States in one day
Content_Enlish:
More than 2,500 flights have been canceled in the United States in a single day. This is the highest number of flight cancellations in the country during the Christmas season. 

These flights have been canceled due to the prevention of infection with the new type of Corona Omicron and inclement weather, including snowfall. 

About 4,500 flights were canceled worldwide on Saturday due to the imposition of the Omicron ban. Of these, 2,500 flights were canceled in the United States alone. Several airports in the central United States have been covered in snow due to heavy snowfall. 

As a result, more than a thousand flights were canceled from several airports, including Chicago-O'Hare and Midway Airport. 

Starting from December 24, at least 12,000 flights in the country were canceled in one week.

Headline_English: Exports hit record $4.91 billion in December
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh sets new record in exports amid pandemic. In December of the outgoing year, traders exported goods worth $4.91 billion. This is the country's highest export in a single month. And this time too, the ready-made garment sector has led the way. Analysts urge retaining buyers of Bangladeshi products and attracting new investments to continue this trend of exports. 

Bangladesh exported goods worth only $350 million in the year after independence. Of this, 90 percent came from the export of jute and jute products. In the past 50 years, there have been positive changes in the country's economy as well as exports. As a result, the export sector has now occupied an important part of the country's overall economy. 

According to the data released by the Export Promotion Bureau-EPB on Sunday, a record $4.91 billion worth of goods was exported in December amid the Corona adversity. At 86 taka per dollar, this amounts to 42,140 crore taka in local currency. This is the highest export in a single month in the country's history. 

The ready-made garment sector has played a major role in the growth of export earnings as always. Ready-made garments worth $4.04 billion or Tk 34,744 crore were exported in December, which is 52.57 percent more than the same period of the previous year. That is, 80.57 percent of the total export revenue came from this sector. 

Demand for Bangladeshi products is increasing due to various crises including the Corona lockdown in different countries of the world. Therefore, analysts believe that exports of other sectors along with garments have increased. However, they are urging more foreign investment to maintain export growth. 

According to EPB data, in addition to ready-made garments, exports of agricultural processed products, leather and leather products, frozen food, home textiles, engineering products and handicrafts also increased in July-December. However, jute and jute products are still lagging behind.

Headline_English: Directorate General of Health prepared to control Omicron
Content_Enlish:
The Health Department has said that there is a risk of Omicron spreading, but there are preparations in advance to control it. The country has sufficient vaccines, so the Health Department has urged everyone to get vaccinated. 

The Health Department has also said that those who are now found as corona patients are infected with the Delta variant. However, genome sequencing is being done only if any of the infected people are suspected of being infected with Omicron. 

The Omicron variant of corona was first detected in the country on December 11. After that, it was found in the bodies of several others. In total, the number of Omicron infected people in the country has increased by 10 so far. 

The number of Omicron infected people in neighboring India is already increasing by leaps and bounds. The rate of corona infection in the country has increased by 70 percent in the past week. However, community transmission of Omicron has not yet started in the country. 

Additional Director General of the Health Department, Meerjadi Sabrina Flora, said that so far 10 people in the country have been infected with Omicron, and those who are being infected now can be assumed to be the Delta variant. If there is any doubt, genome sequencing is being done. 

In such a situation, the Directorate General of Health is urging everyone except those who have been vaccinated not to go to any public gathering. The Directorate General of Health also claims that measures have already been taken to ensure that medical services are not disrupted in the event of Omicron transmission. The rate of transmission of Omicron is high and can spread quickly. However, the government is alert and measures are being taken, he said. 

The center for taking the booster dose cannot be changed, but if the residence or workplace changes, the booster dose can be taken from any center in a different district.

Headline_English: PM asks Chhatra League to free itself from greed
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has instructed the Chhatra League to stay away from terrorism, militancy and corruption without going astray due to greed. In a discussion on the anniversary of the Chhatra League on Wednesday, she warned the leaders and activists that no one should take a wrong step due to greed. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina virtually joined the main program of the Chhatra League at the Bangladesh Krishibid Institution auditorium in Khamarbari in the capital through video conference from Ganabhaban. 

At that time, the Prime Minister said, I tell the Chhatra League to develop yourselves as ideal workers. Be careful not to slip due to any greed. Strengthen yourselves and move forward on the path of honesty. Strengthen the organization and work in the spirit of the Liberation War with the ideals of the Father of the Nation. And that is how leadership will be developed. 

Stating that the Chhatra League must prepare itself for the 4th Industrial Revolution, the Prime Minister said, "Today we are a developing country, we have to move forward by facing that challenge." The 4th Industrial Revolution will come, in this era of technology, human skills will also change, and our Chhatra League leaders and activists will have to prepare themselves from now on. So that we can utilize the steps we have taken to develop skilled manpower in this era of the 4th Industrial Revolution. We can move forward in time. 

She said, we must take care that no one comes to power in the future and delays the development of the country. 

Referring to the Padma Bridge, the Prime Minister said, this one decision to build the Padma Bridge with our own money has changed the image of Bangladesh in the world. Now everyone respects Bangladesh and does not look at it with pity. 

Sheikh Hasina said, all the leaders of our associate organizations, including the Chhatra League and the Awami League, must be vigilant in this regard, so that no hyena group can come and play tricks on the fate of the people of this country again. No one can be allowed to play tricks on the fate of the people of this country. 

Reminding the Chhatra League that great sacrifice is needed for great achievements, he said, "So, every leader and activist of our Chhatra League should remember that none of them should be confused. Not to be involved in terrorism and militancy. Not to be involved in corruption. We should keep ourselves above all this and pay special attention to ensuring that the country can move forward on the path of peace and development." 

The Prime Minister has not yet found the answer to the question of why everyone stopped after the assassination of Bangabandhu and his family. However, he expressed hope that one day that mystery will be revealed. 

Bangladesh Chhatra League was born on January 4, 1948, in the assembly room of Fazlul Haque Hall of Dhaka University under the direction of Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman with the aim of achieving the freedom of Bengal and Bengalis. 

Chhatra League President Al Rahiyan Khan Joy presided over the program. In addition, Awami League Presidium Member Abdur Rahman MP spoke. Former presidents and general secretaries of Chhatra League were present on stage. The organization's general secretary Lekhak Bhattacharya conducted the program. 

At the program, the Prime Minister reprimanded many Chhatra League leaders and activists for not wearing masks.

Headline_English: A record 2.1 million people were identified in a single day worldwide
Content_Enlish:
Once again, the number of new corona patients detected in a single day has been recorded in the world. 21 lakh 53 thousand new patients were detected in 24 hours on Tuesday. The total number of infected people so far is 29 crore 54 lakh. 7 thousand 230 people have died in the last 24 hours. With this, the total death toll from corona in the world has exceeded 5.4 lakh 73 thousand. 

A new record has also been detected in the United States in 24 hours. 5 lakh 39 thousand new patients have been detected in a single day, along with 1 thousand 800 deaths. 

For the first time since May, more than 10 thousand cases have been found in New York in a single day. Anthony Fauci, the top infectious disease expert in the United States, said that the Omicron infection in the country has not yet reached its peak. 

For the first time since the start of the epidemic, the daily detection in the UK has exceeded 2 lakh. More than 2 lakh 18 thousand corona were detected in the country on Tuesday. Doctors said that 15 percent of the new infected people in the UK are infected for the second time. 

In addition, records have been detected in Italy and France. A record 1 lakh 70 thousand were detected in Italy in a single day. Fears of collapse of the health system in Rome. More than 271,000 corona cases have been identified in France. The Macron government has announced strict measures against those who have not been vaccinated. 

On the other hand, China has completely locked down another city after three corona patients were identified. Omicron infections have increased sharply in Japan's Okinawa prefecture. 

Educational institutions have been closed indefinitely in Ontario, Canada, due to the spread of Omicron. Authorities have imposed a curfew in Delhi, India, from 10 pm every Friday to 5 am on Monday to prevent infection. 

Meanwhile, French scientists have found another new type amid concerns about Omicron. French researchers have named this type of corona IHU or IHU. 

Researchers claim that this new type of virus has mutated at least 46 times. Therefore, they believe that current vaccines may not be very effective in the fight against IHU. The scientific name of IHU is B/One/Six/Four/Zero/Two. So far, 12 French citizens have been infected with IHU.

Headline_English: 10 missing in Narayanganj trawler sinking
Content_Enlish:
Ten people are missing after a passenger trawler capsized in the Dhaleshwari River in Dharmaganj, Fatulla, Narayanganj Sadar Upazila after being hit by a Dhaka-bound passenger launch, MV Farhan-6. The accident occurred at 9 am on Wednesday in the Dhaleshwari River, Dharmaganj, Gudaraghat. Upon receiving the news, a diving team of the Fire Service went to the scene and started rescue work. 

Quoting locals, Deputy Director of Narayanganj Fire Service Abdullah Arefin said that there was dense fog in the river this morning. At that time, the trawler sank with 40 to 50 passengers after being hit by a Dhaka-bound launch from Barisal. 

At that time, locals rescued at least 30 people, including a child, from the middle of the river in another trawler. However, relatives claim that 10 people are missing. 

Abdullah Arefin also said that three diving teams of Dhaka and Narayanganj Fire Service are involved in the rescue work. No bodies had been found as of 1 pm today.

Headline_English: Conspiracies are underway at home and abroad to stop development
Content_Enlish:
Describing her government's development activities, she said that 2022 will be a milestone year. 

The Prime Minister said that the Padma Bridge will be inaugurated in June this year, the Karnaphuli Tunnel in October and the Metrorail by the end of the year. 

The Prime Minister said that after overcoming many conspiracies and obstacles, we are going to complete the construction of the Padma Bridge with our own funds. This bridge will directly connect the southern part of the country with the capital and other regions. 

She said that we have planned to launch the Metrorail from Uttara to Agargaon by the end of this year. Train traffic has started on a trial basis in this section. 

In addition, three-fourths of the tunnel construction work under the Karnaphuli River in the port city of Chittagong has been completed. In her speech, the Prime Minister expressed hope that this first tunnel in the country can be inaugurated next October. 

Sheikh Hasina also called for preparations to face the challenges of the fourth industrial revolution, highlighting the picture of extensive development in the electricity and internet sectors, starting from basic needs. The Prime Minister also warned that conspiracies are being hatched at home and abroad to stop the ongoing development journey. 

Highlighting the success, he said, "As a people's government, I believe it is our responsibility and duty to improve the quality of life of the people. You will evaluate what we have done for you in the last 13 years. However, I can firmly say that we have been able to successfully implement the promises we made." 

Highlighting the government's strict stance against corruption, he said, "No matter which party or how powerful the corrupt are, they are not being and will not be given any concessions. The Anti-Corruption Commission is fulfilling its duties independently. However, social awareness needs to be created to eradicate this disease. 

We have prevented the rise of militants with a strong hand. Bangladesh is a country of communal harmony. People of all religions and castes have been living here with mutual tolerance and will continue to do so in the future." 

In addition, the Head of Government urged people to follow health rules to avoid the new type of Corona, Amicron. The Prime Minister said that a mass vaccination program has been undertaken to bring one crore people under the vaccination program per month.

The Prime Minister said that after the Internet revolution, the world is now entering the era of the fourth industrial revolution of digital technology. Therefore, the Prime Minister emphasized on educating the young generation in technical education to build skilled human resources suitable for the fourth industrial revolution. 

He said that Bangladesh has entered the era of 5G network as the ninth country in the world and the number of internet users has increased to 110 million during the Corona period, which has created employment opportunities for about 600,000 youth of the country through freelancing. In addition, the Prime Minister expressed hope that the poverty rate will be further reduced after the implementation of the Eighth Five-Year Plan. 

Stating that Bangladesh is now self-sufficient in food production, the Prime Minister said that the current production of grain food grains has stood at 45.5 million metric tons. Bangladesh has risen to fourth place in the world in the production of rice, vegetables and onions. This revolution in the agricultural sector has been achieved through continuous policy support and incentives. 

Sheikh Hasina also highlighted the government's initiatives to facilitate road, rail and air connectivity, stating that paved roads have been constructed in almost all villages of the country. 

She said that the Awami League government was the first to integrate rural development into the mainstream of development. 

After the Bangladesh Awami League won the general election held on December 30, 2018 with an absolute majority, Sheikh Hasina took oath as the Prime Minister for the fourth time (three consecutive times) on January 7, 2019.

Headline_English: 7-day quarantine mandatory for foreign returnees in India
Content_Enlish:
The central government has made quarantine mandatory for passengers coming to India from abroad. Even if they show a negative corona test report at the airport, they will not be 'released' before 7 days. 

This information was given in the new instructions of the Union Health Ministry on Friday. 

It has been said that anyone coming to India from any country will have to stay in quarantine at home for 7 days. 

The new rules will come into effect from next Tuesday, the Health Ministry's instructions said. This step is due to the increase in Omicron infections worldwide. 

As before, the instructions have made it mandatory for all air passengers coming from countries on the 'high-risk' list for Omicron to submit samples for RT-PCR testing at the airport. 

Incidentally, according to the current guidelines of the Union Health Ministry, passengers coming from 'high-risk' countries in terms of Omicron infection are sent to quarantine even if their reports come back negative. But passengers coming by air from non-risk countries are allowed to travel without restrictions if their reports come back negative.

Headline_English: Five passport office brokers arrested in Faridpur
Content_Enlish:
Five members of a passport office broker gang have been arrested in a raid by the district detective police in Faridpur. 

During this, 5 books of illegal passport transactions, a challan book for depositing money, two monitors, and 250,000 taka in cash were seized from the arrested. 

The arrested are Nadim Hasan, Tariqur Rahman, Rabbi Mollah, Al Amin Sheikh and Mozammel Hossain Shimul. 

Additional Superintendent of Police Jamal Pasha gave this information at a press conference at the office of the District Superintendent of Police. 

Police said that for a long time this gang had been illegally working at the passport office by taking extra money from people. In addition, the arrested people used to hold the customers hostage and torture them if they did not get the money as per their demands. 

Additional Superintendent of Police of Faridpur district Jamal Pasha said that after receiving a complaint from a person named Julhas Sikder of Nagarkandar police station, we conducted the raid after the initial investigation found the truth in the matter. Later, they were arrested. They will be sent to jail through the court today, Friday. 

He said, Julhas Sikder has filed a case with Faridpur Kotwali Police Station as the plaintiff in this incident, and their arrest has been shown in that case.

Headline_English: Online admission application for XI begins
Content_Enlish:
Online admission applications for students who have passed this year's SSC and equivalent exams have started from today. This process will continue till January 15. Students will be admitted based on the results of the SSC or equivalent exams. Classes will start from March 2. 

The policy for admission to class XI has been published on the website of the Secondary and Higher Education Department of the Ministry of Education. This information has been given in that policy. 

The policy states that all educational institutions will have to apply for admission to class XI in the 2021-22 academic year only online. Admission applications can be made through this website (http://xiclassadmissiongovbd.com/). Online applications will be accepted from January 8 to 15. 

Those who will apply for re-examination will also have to apply for admission within this period. Applications for students whose re-examination results have changed will be accepted from January 22 to 23. 

The time for changing the order of preference will be given from the date of application to January 24. And the results of the students selected in the first phase will be published on January 29. Students will have to confirm their selection between January 30 and February 6. If they do not confirm their selection, they will have to apply again with a fee. 

The second phase of applications will be taken on February 7 and 8. The results of the first migration and the results of the second phase of applications will be published on February 10. From February 11 to 12, the selection of the students selected in the second phase will be confirmed. If the selection is not confirmed within this period, the application will be canceled. 

On February 13, the results of the second migration and the results of the third phase of applications will be published according to the order of preference on February 15. The selection of the students selected in the third phase will have to be confirmed on February 16 and 17. 

If the selection is not confirmed within this period, the application will be canceled. Students will be admitted between February 19 and 24. And from March 2, the eleventh class classes will start in the colleges. 

In the case of online application, you can apply for admission to a minimum of 5 and a maximum of 10 colleges or equivalent institutions by giving your preference. A student will apply to all the colleges, and his/her position in only one college will be determined based on the marks obtained. 

This time, 20 lakh 96 thousand 546 students have passed the SSC examination. There are about 2.5 lakh seats available for admission in colleges. So there will be no shortage of seats. The education board has urged students to apply based on the marks they have obtained.

Headline_English: Transportable stadium built for Qatar World Cup
Content_Enlish:
A transportable stadium has been built for the Qatar Football World Cup. Which can be set up anywhere in the world after the World Cup. Authorities claim that this is the first such stadium in the world. 40,000 spectators will be able to sit in the gallery of this stadium and enjoy the match at the same time. 

The name of this stadium for the Qatar Football World Cup in 2022 is Nine Seven Four. It is named after Qatar's international phone code 974. 

In addition, 974 shipping containers were needed to set up the stadium. Spanish architect Mark Fenwick designed it using unused shipping containers. 

Mark Fenwick, the designer of Qatar's Stadium Nine Seven Four Stadium, said, "We have decorated the entire field with shipping containers. Each container has been shaped into a separate structure. Such as toilets or special places for cameramen, etc. 

It is said that this is the first transportable stadium. Which can be set up anywhere in the world. 

He also said, I think after the World Cup, this stadium will not be needed in Qatar anymore. So I have designed a different type of field, which can be used again after the World Cup. I wanted the field to be divided into several parts and transportable. 

This special stadium has a capacity of 40 thousand spectators. Qatari authorities have said that if any less developed country wants to use this stadium after the World Cup, they will be given it. The stadium's functionality has already been tested.

Headline_English: Online trap, Destiny's Shuvo embezzled Tk 410 crore
Content_Enlish:
A former Destiny official named Shuvo Chowdhury has opened an online MLM business and embezzled Tk 4.1 billion, the CID said. He sold about 410,000 shares at Tk 1,000 in 7 months. Although his associate was arrested posing as a customer, the CID could not catch him. 

Habibur Rahman sells electronic products in Paltan. Last August, he learned that if he invested in a company called Social Mission Share, it would double in 100 days. He lost Tk 3 lakh due to this temptation. Later, he filed a case in the name of the company. 

During the investigation, the CID found an online MLM business in the name of Social Mission Share. The company's MD Shuvo Chowdhury and Saidur Rahman came to meet him in a car, posing as a customer. 

However, Shuvo fled after sensing the presence of the CID. At that time, his associate Saidur was arrested. Torture equipment was also found in the car. 

After questioning Saidur, the CID said that Shuvo Chowdhury is a former Destiny official. And he started this business 7 months ago. Targeting low-income people. There is no office, he would pick up interested people in his car and talk to them. 

Shuvo would sell a share of Social Mission for 1,000 taka. He would offer the temptation of doubling the profit from foreign investments in 100 days. Detectives say that by selling 410,000 shares in this way, he earned 410 crore taka. 

Additional DIG of CID Imam Hossain said that they are conducting a drive to arrest Shuvo. He also advised not to fall for such temptation.

Headline_English: Four new judges in the Appellate Division
Content_Enlish:
Four new judges were appointed to the Appellate Division. Chief Justice Hasan Faiz Siddiqui administered the oath to three of them at the Supreme Court Auditorium at 10:30 am on Sunday. 

A notification in this regard signed by Md. Golam Sarwar, Secretary (in-charge) of the Law and Justice Division of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, was issued today on the orders of the President. 

The judges appointed to the Appellate Division are Justice Borhan Uddin, Justice M. Enayetur Rahim, Justice FRM Nazmul Ahasan and Justice Krishna Debnath. 

Three of them took the oath. Chief Justice Hasan Faiz Siddiqui administered the oath to them at the Supreme Court Auditorium at 10:30 am on Sunday. Justice Borhan Uddin, Justice M. Enayetur Rahim and Justice Krishna Debnath took the oath. 

However, Justice FRM Nazmul Ahasan will take the oath later as he is ill. 

The oath-taking ceremony was conducted by Supreme Court Registrar General Md. Ali Akbar. At that time, the judges of the Appellate and High Court Divisions of the Supreme Court were present. 

According to Article 95 (1) of the Constitution, the President appointed them from the High Court Division to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in consultation with the Chief Justice. With this, the number of judges of the Appellate Division is 8. 

It is said there that the President has appointed them to the Appellate Division by virtue of the powers conferred on them by the Constitution. Their appointment will be effective from the date of their oath-taking.

Headline_English: US blocks WHO proposal
Content_Enlish:
The United States, the largest donor to the World Health Organization, has blocked a proposal to make the organization more independent and stronger. This has called into question the Biden administration's long-term commitment to support the organization. Reuters reported this information in a special report on Saturday. 

The proposal by the World Health Organization Working Group was about sustainable financing. It proposed increasing the mandatory annual contribution of each member of the organization. The document was published online on January 4. 

The coronavirus pandemic has clearly shown the limitations of the WHO in dealing with major crises. The organization had planned to introduce comprehensive reforms to increase its capacity to deal with such crises in the future. 

To that end, the World Health Organization Working Committee made four proposals to strengthen the organization through sustainable financing. It also proposed increasing the annual funding of member countries to $ 200 billion by 2028. 

Although the countries of Europe, South Asia and Africa agreed to the proposal, the United States opposed it. Four European officials present at the discussions confirmed the US's blocking. 

They said the US administration has doubts about the WHO's ability to deal with future threats. Rather than increasing WHO's powers, the US is pushing for the creation of a separate fund that would finance the prevention and control of emergency health crises, they said. 

On the other hand, supporters of the proposal say that the WHO is forced to prioritize donors because it is overly dependent on voluntary donations from member states and charities such as the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. As a result, the organization has little power to criticize members if they make mistakes.

Headline_English: Business summit in Dhaka to increase foreign investment
Content_Enlish:
The International Business Summit Biz-Net-2022 was held in Dhaka on the prospects of foreign investment in business, trade and industry in the post-Covid world. RRM Steel and ZI Foundation jointly organized this summit with the aim of transforming the country's potential into reality through improving international relations. 

The theme of this year's business summit, organized at the prestigious Banani Club in Dhaka on Thursday, was - Global connectivity for global development. 

The summit, with the participation of renowned businessmen, industrialists and business policy makers from the UK, Gibraltar and Bangladesh, emphasized on accelerating the country's progress towards the developed world through the development of mutual relations. 

The evening summit was attended by renowned businessmen, industrialists, heads of multinational companies, business entrepreneurs, academicians and business policy makers, and representatives of local and international media. 

The panel discussion included Bijoy Daryanani, Minister for Business, Tourism, Transport and Ports of the Government of Gibraltar; Tom Hunt, Member of the House of Commons (Ipswich); Samantha Cohen, Chief Executive of the Commonwealth Enterprise and Investment Council (CWEIC); Paul Bristow, Member of the House of Commons (Petersburg); and Zillur Hussain MBE, Entrepreneur and Chairman of Z Group and ZI Foundation. 

In the discussion, Bijoy Daryanani, Minister for Business, Tourism, Transport and Ports of the Government of Gibraltar, mentioned the immense potential of Bangladesh and said that the Government of Gibraltar is interested in contributing to the better use of trade, industry, exports and skilled human resources through the development of international relations with Bangladesh. 

In the welcome speech from Bangladesh, Dr. Suman Chowdhury said, Bangladesh is a fertile field for production, trade and export of various products as well as a potential country for foreign investment. The number of our exportable products in Europe is increasing day by day. I am hopeful that the Government of Gibraltar will sincerely stand by us in increasing the volume of exports to the countries included in the European Union by resolving the problems and realizing the potential of new economic relations after Brexit. I urge you, let us work together to face the economic challenges of the post-Covid world and give a beautiful and prosperous world. 

Manwar Hossain, Chairman of Anwar Group of Industries and President of Bangladesh Steel Manufacturers Association, and Dr. RRM Group Chairman and Vice-President of Bangladesh Steel Manufacturers Association participated as the main negotiators in the discussion on the investment potential in the country's industrial sector, export and trade. Sumon Chowdhury, Partex Group Managing Director and Banani Club President Rubel Aziz, Well Group of Industries Chairman and CEO Syed Nurul Islam, Nagad Mobile Banking Service Provider CEO Rahel Ahmed, and Ranks FC Properties Limited CEO Tanvir Shahriar Rimon. 

The International Business Summit ended with the optimism that Bangladesh will stand by each other in positive and promising initiatives for the welfare of the country, soil, and people through the development of trilateral relations.

Headline_English: Offices to operate with half staff from tomorrow
Content_Enlish:
Various government, semi-government and autonomous institutions are preparing to operate offices with half the manpower in accordance with the government's instructions to prevent the spread of Corona. Officials have said that the instructions will be fully effective in all institutions, including the Secretariat, from tomorrow. 

On a visit to various offices, including the Secretariat, from Monday morning, it was seen that most institutions still have full manpower. 

They said that since the notification was issued yesterday afternoon, many of the officials and employees are not aware of it. Moreover, the schedule for operating offices with half the manpower was not ready, as a result, everyone is still working in the office today. After the preparations, the government's instructions will be fully followed from tomorrow. 

Meanwhile, in a notification issued by the Supreme Court in the morning, all judicial courts will be operated with half the manpower until February 6. 

In addition, Bangladesh Bank has issued a notification ordering all banking activities to be conducted with half the manpower today. The letter signed by Bangladesh Bank General Manager Md. Anwarul Islam said that banking activities will have to be conducted with half the officers and employees in rotation (rostering) following the health rules. However, during this time, other officers and employees will stay at their workplaces and complete their official activities virtually. However, the instructions state that the relevant institutions will be able to decide at their own discretion as needed to continue essential banking services. 

In addition, the letter also instructs customers coming to the bank to wear masks and follow other health rules properly. Earlier, in another instruction sent by Bangladesh Bank yesterday, officers and employees working in banks were instructed to obtain vaccination certificates. 

Meanwhile, due to the rapid increase in the spread of coronavirus, the government has already declared all schools and colleges in the country closed until February 6. On January 21, the Cabinet Division issued a notification instructing universities to take the same measures. 

It states that no gathering of more than 100 people will be allowed in any social, political, religious or state event. Those who join in these cases must show a vaccination certificate or a PCR Covid test report done within 24 hours. 

Officers and employees in government, private offices and industrial factories will have to obtain vaccination certificates. The authorities concerned must confirm the matter. 

Earlier, the government issued 11-point restrictions to prevent the spread of Omicron, which it announced would be implemented from January 13. It banned buses and trains from running with half the passengers, as well as social, political and religious gatherings in open spaces. It also made it mandatory to have a Covid vaccination certificate when eating at restaurants, and it prohibited students over 12 years of age from attending educational institutions without a vaccination certificate.

Headline_English: EC formation bill to be tabled in Parliament on Wednesday
Content_Enlish:
The Election Commission Formation Act may be tabled in parliament for passage on Wednesday. The chairman of the parliamentary committee in this regard, Shahiduzzaman Sarkar, said that no major changes have been made in it. 

It is being recommended to add two conditions to the qualification and disqualification for the appointment of CEC and Election Commissioner. 

The Election Commissioner and Election Commissioner Appointment Bill-2022 was examined and the report was finalized at the meeting of the parliamentary standing committee held at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban on Monday. 

Taking these into consideration, Law Minister Anisul Haque said that this law will be passed in the current session. 

After the bill was tabled in the Jatiya Sangsad on Sunday, it was sent to the parliamentary committee to examine it and submit a report within seven days. The qualification clause of the CEC and Commissioners in the bill tabled in parliament stated that to become a CEC and Commissioner, he must have at least 20 years of work experience in an important government, judicial, semi-government or private position. The Parliamentary Standing Committee has recommended some amendments to this section to include 'autonomous and other professions' along with government, judicial, semi-government or private posts. 

And in terms of disqualification, Section 6 (d) states that a person convicted of a criminal offense involving moral turpitude and sentenced to at least two years in prison cannot become a CEC or commissioner. 

The meeting, chaired by Parliamentary Standing Committee Chairman Shahiduzzaman Sarkar, was attended by committee members Law Minister Anisul Haque, Mostafizur Rahman, Shamsul Haque, Abdul Majid Khan, Shamim Haider Patwary, Gloria Jharna Sarkar, Rumin Farhana and Selim Altaf. 

The term of the current EC led by KM Nurul Huda ends on February 14. The President will have to form a new commission before then. In this case, there is only three weeks to pass the law, publish the gazette and form the EC. 

The Constitution of Bangladesh states that the President has the authority to appoint commissioners to the constitutional body EC. And it will be under a law. Since there is no such law so far, controversy has started every time the EC is formed. 

To avoid this, in 2012, when appointing a new commission, the then President Md. Zillur Rahman created a mediating forum called the Search Committee, which was also controversial. 

In this method, the President, after discussing with the political parties, formed a search committee with a few prominent citizens led by a judge. That search committee prepared a list of names of those eligible to be the CEC and Election Commissioner. From that list, he appointed a CEC and not more than five commissioners. 

Then President Md. Abdul Hamid followed the same method in 2017. This time too, he was moving forward with the same method. But almost all of the 25 parties that participated in the dialogue insisted on enacting a law as a permanent solution to the formation of the EC. The leaders of the parties said that the President also agreed to this during the discussion. 

However, seven parties, including the BNP, did not participate in the dialogue.

Headline_English: Zafar Iqbal breaks students' hunger strike
Content_Enlish:
Students of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, who were protesting demanding the resignation of the VC, broke their hunger strike at the request of Professor Dr. Zafar Iqbal. 

They officially announced the break of the hunger strike on Wednesday morning. 

Earlier, Dr. Zafar Iqbal and his wife Yasmin Haque reached the university campus around 4 pm on Tuesday. Later, he spoke to the students. At one point, the students agreed to break the hunger strike. Later, Zafar Iqbal and his wife broke the hunger strike by making the students drink water. 
At this time, Zafar Iqbal said, "Listen, don't you realize what you have done? 34 vice chancellors of Bangladesh have said that they will resign if the vice chancellor here resigns. I am very fond of watching this. There are such vice chancellors in our country whose ideals are so high that they will resign themselves after seeing others. Although I think this passion will not be satisfied. 

I just want to say that what you have done is incomparable." The movement you have created, every young child of Bangladesh is with you. This popular writer said. 

At that time, he told the students, 'I was asked to write an article for a memorial book on the birth centenary of Bangabandhu. For that article, I was given an honorarium of 10,000 taka by the Prime Minister's Office. I have brought this honorarium money. I am giving the money to the fund of this movement. You keep it. Now, if you can, let them arrest me. At that time, he expressed his anger that the issue of stopping medical services for the protesting students was extremely inhumane. 

He also said, many big people have contacted me. They have promised me. That is why I have come here. 

23 students of Shabiprabir have been on a hunger strike for 7 consecutive days demanding the resignation of the vice-chancellor. Later, 5 more students joined them on Sunday. Several of them are under treatment in the hospital after falling ill. 

Meanwhile, the CID conducted raids in various places in Dhaka on Monday and Tuesday in connection with the case of funding the movement and posting statuses on Facebook. Later that night, they were handed over to Sylhet Jalalbad Police Station. The detainees are Habibur Rahman Khan, Reza Nur Muin, AFM Nazmul Shakib, AKM Maruf Hossain and Faisal Ahmed. They are being questioned, the police said. 

On the night of January 13, students of the university's Begum Sirajunnesa Chowdhury Student Hall staged a protest alleging misconduct with students. As a result, at least fifty people on the campus, including students, were injured in police baton charges, tear gas, rubber bullets and sound grenades. In that incident, the police filed a case against 200 to 300 unidentified students on the charge of 'shooting and assault with intent to kill'. 

In addition, the authorities declared the university closed and ordered the students to leave the hall. But ignoring that order, the students started a protest demanding the resignation of Vice-Chancellor Farid Uddin Ahmed. At one point, on January 19 at 3 pm, they went on a hunger strike. They announced that they would continue their hunger strike until the vice-chancellor resigned.

Headline_English: Nearly 7.5 lakh people in the country have received booster doses
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that 741,265 people have been given corona booster doses so far in the country. She said this in response to a written question during the 16th session of the 11th National Parliament on Wednesday. 

At the time, she also said that after the corona outbreak started around the world, the government has prioritized the issue of providing free vaccination as an effective measure to prevent infection. In addition, even before the corona vaccine was discovered and permission was obtained to use it, the government took all initiatives to procure and administer the vaccine. 

The Prime Minister said that under the nationwide vaccination program, 891,63,978 people have been given the first dose and 570,20,834 people have been given the second dose, making a total of 146,184,812 doses of Covid-19 vaccine. 

She also told the parliament that considering the Covid-19 pandemic situation in the country like the rest of the world, the Bangladesh government also decided to provide booster doses under the ongoing Covid-19 vaccination program. 

He also said that as per the recommendations of the National Immunization Technical Advisory Group, Bangladesh (NITAG, B) and with the approval of the National Committee on the Implementation of the Coronavirus Vaccine Distribution Program, booster doses have been started nationwide from December 28, 2021.

Headline_English: Teenager dies after being hit by bus: Two drivers arrested
Content_Enlish:
RAB has arrested two bus drivers in connection with the death of a teenager Rakibul who was crushed to death during a collision between two buses in the capital's Moghbazar. They were arrested from Paltan in the capital and Srinagar in Munshiganj on Tuesday. 

A 14-year-old teenager Rakibul was killed when two buses ran over him in the capital's Moghbazar around 5 pm on Thursday, January 20. It is said that Rakibul used to work as a bus driver. 

A passerby who brought Rakib to the hospital said that the teenager Rakib was seriously injured after falling between an Ajmeri Paribahan bus and another bus at the Moghbazar intersection. He was rescued in a seriously injured condition and taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared Rakib dead at 5:30 pm. The driver fled that day, but both buses were seized. 

RAB's Legal and Media Wing Assistant Director ASP ANM Imran Khan said that the drivers of two buses have been arrested in the controversial Ajmeri Glory Paribahan bus race that killed a teenager. 

The arrested persons are Md. Monir Hossain and Imran Hossain. This information was given by the organization's Legal and Media Wing Director Khandaker Al Moin at a press conference at the capital's Media Center at noon. 

He said that the assistant of the driver of one of the two vehicles was driving the killer vehicle. The other driver was addicted to drugs. Such accidents occurred due to driving a contract vehicle. RAB also said that the accused admitted responsibility during the initial interrogation.

Headline_English: The Election Commission Act is a unique milestone
Content_Enlish:
Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader has said that the Election Commission Act will be considered a unique milestone in the history of Bangladesh to ensure the voting rights of the masses. 

He made this comment during a briefing at his residence on Friday morning. 

The minister also commented that Bangladesh will take a step forward in institutionalizing democracy through the enactment of the Election Commission Formation Act. 

Stating that the government is committed to ensuring democracy and the voting rights of the people in light of the constitution, Obaidul Quader said that everything that has been done to form a strong Election Commission in Bangladesh and strengthen the Election Commission has been achieved under the leadership of the Awami League. 

He said that all kinds of steps have been taken during the Awami League regime to make the Election Commission independent, impartial and strong like other democratic countries in the world. 

At the same time, he said that the BNP Secretary General's non-compliance with the law on the appointment of commissioners has made ill-intentioned statements. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that lies and fabrications are being spread to make this law controversial and questionable, and added that BNP has no faith in the country's laws and constitution.

Headline_English: Chicken prices fall, but vegetable prices rise
Content_Enlish:
A week ago, the price of edible oil in the capital's market increased by 5 taka. This time, shopkeepers are selling all types of oil, including soybean and palm, at new prices in bottles. Meanwhile, the price of vegetables has increased slightly, and the price of chicken and onion has decreased. 

There is no relief in the uncontrolled edible oil market. Although it was said in a meeting with the government that the price will not be increased before February 6, oil is being sold at higher prices. 

Bottled soybean oil has increased by 5 taka, and it has to be bought at 165 to 168 taka per liter. The price of open soybean and palm oil has also increased. Marketing companies have also printed new prices on the bottles. Meanwhile, buyers are reacting angrily to the successive price increases. 

However, the price of chicken has decreased slightly in the past week. The price of broiler and golden chicken has decreased by 10 taka or more per kg. Broiler chicken is being sold at 165 taka and golden chicken at 270 taka per kg. However, the price is slightly higher despite the increased supply of winter vegetables in the market. 

Potatoes are being sold in the market for 20 taka per kg. The price of onions has also decreased. Local onions are being bought for 30 taka per kg.

Headline_English: Chittagong phase of BPL begins
Content_Enlish:
The Chittagong phase of the BPL starts today. In the opening match, the host Chittagong Challengers will play against Khulna Tigers. The goal of both team captains Mushfiqur and Miraj is to win at the Sagarika wicket. 

T20 is returning to Chittagong after a long time. It is difficult to find out when the last T20 match was held at the Sagarika Stadium. The last T20 match of the BPL was held at this stadium on December 24, 2019. After that, the BPL is returning to the port city after two full years. 

Although the field is hot, the excitement is decreasing due to the lack of spectators in the gallery. Statistics say that there will be a run festival at the Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium. The game starts at 1:30 pm. 

Meanwhile, Soumya has returned after winning the Corona. The Dhaka phase did not go well for Khulna without him. They won one of their two matches with Dhaka. Khulna won against Dhaka after chasing 183 runs. The match they lost was against this Chittagong. And that was by 25 runs in a high-scoring match. They want to learn from the mistakes of that match and defeat the hosts. 

On the other hand, Miraj's team Chittagong Challengers will play four consecutive matches at home. They will want to use the advantage to the fullest. That is why Khulna Tigers are taking the Chittagong phase as very important. 

And in tonight's match at Sagarika Stadium, it will be a fair of stars. Dhaka and Sylhet will face each other. Where the fight for survival is between three superstars. Tamim-Mahmudullah-Mashrafi's team has only one win in four matches. They hope for good things at the new venue by forming a combination. 

Although the opponent Sylhet could not do anything extraordinary, the spin attack has been intimidating. Saikat, Apu, Sanjamul, Gazi - four people have become difficult for the opponent to handle. However, unlike Dhaka, there will be no spin attack in Chittagong. Dhaka's hope lies where Sylhet's thoughts lie. Sylhet had all-out Dhaka for 100 runs in the first match of the two teams. They had to play 17 overs to win. 

Meanwhile, the BPL, which has moved from Dhaka to Chittagong, is adding the ADRS technology as an alternative to DRS from today. The BPL authorities have brought ADRS after facing a lot of controversy due to the absence of DRS in the Dhaka phase. In this alternative to DRS, mats, splits, screens, super slow motion replays and smart microphone audio will be used instead of ball tracking. 

Statistics If the batsmen run rampant on the Chittagong wicket, the bowlers will have a tough time. That is why the toss is becoming very important. In the last season, the captains won the toss 10 times out of 12 matches and took the field. 

Fortune Barisal team cricketer Nurul Hasan Sohan said that although the fans have regrets, the cricketers' regrets are fading. The BPL has moved from the mysterious wicket of Mirpur to a batting paradise. Proof of this can be found in the last 2019-20 season. More than 150 runs were scored in 9 overs. The highest score of 460 runs in a single match in the history of BPL was scored at this venue. 

Afghanistan will again come to Bangladesh to play ODIs and T20Is in February this year. Bangladesh played T20Is against this team at this ground twenty-seven months ago. At that time, the stars have a great opportunity to adapt to the Sagarika wicket and conditions.

Headline_English: Counting underway after FDC artists' association votes
Content_Enlish:
The counting of votes is underway after the voting in the 17th election of the Bangladesh Film Artists Association. This year, Kanchan-Nipun Parishad and Misha-Zayed Parishad are fighting. 

Voting in the election of the Film Artists Association began at the Bangladesh Film Development Corporation (BFDC) from Friday morning. The fight is going on between Kanchan-Nipun and Misha-Zayed Parishad. The biennial election of the Artists Association for the 2022-24 term is going on under tight security. 

Voting in the 17th election of the Film Artists Association at the capital's FDC started from 9 am to 4 pm. A visit to the FDC showed that there is tight security at the entrance of the FDC. Everyone is being allowed to enter the election premises by showing their cards. 

The security department said that 300 police were deployed at the FDC today for the occasion of voting. In the meantime, he told the media personnel present that Ilias Kanchan was the first to cast his own vote at 9:16 am. Another presidential candidate, actor Misha Sawdagar, also said that he cast his vote after a while. 

Ilias Kanchan, a popular film actor and president of the Safe Road Movement, is contesting the post of president from the Kanchan-Nipun panel. Film actress Nipun is the candidate for the post of general secretary from this panel. On the other hand, Khalchari actor Misha Sawdagar is the candidate for the post of president from the Misha-Zayed panel. Film actor Zayed Khan is the candidate for the post of general secretary in this panel. Both panels have said that they are 100% optimistic about the victory of the 21-member committee in this election. 

44 film artists, including two independent candidates, are contesting in this election. A total of 428 voters are in the election. 

This time, Pirzada Harun is serving as the election commissioner. The two members of the commission are Zahid Hossain and Bazlur Rashid Chowdhury. Sohanur Rahman Sohan has been made the chairman of the appeal board. And Mohammad Hossain Jemi and Mohammad Hossain have been made members of the appeal board. 

Meanwhile, the election of the Television Actors' Association has also begun. The voting for the Artists' Association is underway at the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy. The number of voters for the Artists' Association is 752. 

This time, no panel has been formed for the Artists' Association. 48 artists are contesting for 21 posts in the election. All are voting independently. This time, Ahsan Habib Nasim and Shahadat Hossain Nipu are contesting for the post of president. 

Anisur Rahman Milon, Iqbal Babu, Tania Ahmed, Dilu Majumder and Selim Mahbub are the vice-presidents. Nazneen Hasan Chumki, Shamima Tushti and Jamil Hossain are the general secretaries. Saju Khadem, Tushar Mahmud and Zulfikar Chanchal are the organizing secretaries. In addition, Urmila Srabanti Kar, Pran Roy, Mukul Siraj and many others are contesting for other posts. This time, the number of voters for the Artists' Association is more than 600.

Headline_English: Afghan cricket team to arrive in Bangladesh on February 12
Content_Enlish:
The Afghanistan cricket team is coming to Bangladesh on February 12 to play three ODIs and two T20Is. After a 5-day camp in Sylhet, the ODI series with the Tigers will be held in Chittagong and the T20I in Dhaka. The series against the Afghans is part of the ICC ODI Super League. 

The Tigers, currently in second place with 80 points, will go a long way towards the 2023 World Cup if they win the series 3-0. Therefore, the BCB does not want to take any risks. The Mirpur wicket often speaks for the opponent as a boomerang. Therefore, the cautious BCB wants to organize the ODI series in Chittagong. 

BCB Chief Executive Nizamuddin Chowdhury said, "Afghanistan has requested us that they want to hold a conditioning camp. We have planned to organize this conditioning camp in Sylhet." 

Meanwhile, he also said that the BCB is working to have DRS. In addition, the BCB wants to finalize the appointment of a pace bowling coach before the series. 

There is not even a week's break after the BPL. The board is busy with various issues related to the Afghanistan series. Meanwhile, the ICC has made DRS mandatory in international T20s. 

Afghanistan canceled its tour of Zimbabwe in December due to the DRS controversy. The BCB has not yet been able to incorporate this technology in the BPL. Although it is heard that there will be no DRS in the upcoming series, the CEO is optimistic. 

Meanwhile, the BCB has assured to fill the vacant post of bowling coach before the Afghanistan series. The shortlist will be announced in a few days. 

Although this series is also going to be held without any spectators on the field. However, the condition is that the Corona situation must improve. In this case, the board will look at the government's instructions. During the Corona period, the Bangladesh team played all the series in empty galleries. 

The only exception was the home series against Pakistan. However, the country is now in disarray due to the new variant of Corona, Omicron. Therefore, no spectators will be seen in the galleries in the Afghan series either. 

Earlier, Bangladesh's tour of Ireland was postponed in 2020 due to the Corona virus. Which was supposed to be held in May this year. However, the two boards came to an agreement and canceled the three-match ODI series.

Headline_English: A swift crackdown will be launched against rice hoarders.
Content_Enlish:
Food Minister Sadhan Chandra Majumdar has warned that a campaign will soon be launched against illegal rice hoarders across the country. He said this in response to a question from journalists after the Safe Food Day program in the capital this morning. 

Despite good production and record stockpiling, there is no relief in the rice market. Rice is being sold at higher prices than before. Low-income people are suffering the most. 

In the market, fine rice is being sold at 62 to 70 taka per kg, depending on the quality. Coarse rice is being sold at 50 taka per kg. According to TCB, which is about 7 percent more than the same period last year. In such a situation, low-income people are the most in trouble. 

Food Minister Sadhan Chandra Majumdar claims that there is no rice crisis in the country. He admitted the rise in rice prices. A campaign will be launched across the country within a few days to control the market. Imports will also be made if necessary. And this time, fine rice will be imported. 

After the Safe Food Day program, he further said that in addition to monitoring rice production, OMS rice is being distributed through 1,767 dealers across the country.

Headline_English: Suu Kyi's followers no longer object to Rohingya genocide trial
Content_Enlish:
Myanmar's shadow government no longer objects to the jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) to hear the Rohingya genocide case, the NGU, made up of lawmakers and administrative staff from the ousted Myanmar government, said in a statement on Tuesday. 

Aung San Suu Kyi's government had initially objected to the ICJ's jurisdiction to hear the case before the military seized power in Myanmar. 

The news agency Reuters reported that many see the challenge to the ICJ's jurisdiction in the case filed by Gambia alleging indiscriminate genocide of the Rohingya in Myanmar as an attempt to delay the trial. 

However, it is not yet clear whether the NGU's statement will have any impact on the ICJ's legal process. 

In a statement on Tuesday, marking the first anniversary of the military coup, Myanmar's anti-junta shadow government said that the ICJ needs to recognize the atrocities committed by the army against the Rohingya. This will pave the way for the cessation of the atrocities that the junta government is currently committing. 

In November 2019, the African country Gambia filed a case with the ICJ against Myanmar, accusing it of committing genocide against the Rohingya in Rakhine. The UN's highest court is located in The Hague, Netherlands. 

Gambia submitted a 500-page memorial to the ICJ in support of the case. At the same time, the country added an additional 5,000 pages of supplementary documents in support of the accusation. These memorials and documents highlight how the then Myanmar government was responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya. 

However, Suu Kyi denied the accusation of genocide by the military in Rakhine at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands in 2019. 

But after last year's military coup, Suu Kyi was detained by the Myanmar junta government. Suu Kyi is on trial in several cases. After the coup, a shadow government was formed in Myanmar to advance the process of restoring democracy. Suu Kyi herself is also in this government.

Headline_English: The oldest fish is Methuselah
Content_Enlish:
The oldest known lungfish in the world is in the United States. This rare species of fish has been named 'Methuselah'. The fish was brought from Australia to the San Francisco Museum of Art in California, USA, in 1938. It is the oldest fish kept in aquariums in the world. 

The 90-year-old fish is in an aquarium in California. Recently, the California Academy of Sciences has become interested in the fish. With the help of Australian researchers, they are trying to determine the actual age of the fish. 

According to US media, the fish is 90 years old. It is 4 feet long and weighs more than 18 kg. The specialty of the fish is that it has both lungs and gills, which are known as 'lungfish'. 

This huge lungfish was brought to the California Aquarium 84 years ago. Although lungfish usually live an average of 25 years, this fish has survived for 90 years. The Methuselah fish is an Australian freshwater fish. Currently, the number of this type of lungfish is gradually decreasing. 

It is said in the Bible that a man named Methuselah lived to be 956 years old. The fish was named 'Methuselah' after him for his longevity. 

Alan Jan, a biologist at the California Academy of Sciences, said that Methuselah is the oldest fish for no reason. Until 2017, the oldest record was held by another fish. At that time, a fish named Granddad was in the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago. But it died at the age of 95 that year. After that, Methuselah basically took over the place of the oldest fish. 

He also said that Methuselah was brought to this aquarium in California from Australia in 1938. He was not very small at that time. Judging by his height in the picture at that time, it is estimated that he was 5/6 years old at that time. 

The scientist believes that it is a female fish. But its gender has never been tested. Taking blood from the fish's body is risky. However, now the California Academy of Sciences is planning to send its samples to scientists in Australia to determine the sex of the fish. 

This fish in California eats a lot. Methuselah eats everything, including blueberries, grapes, fish, shrimp and earthworms. Since the lungfish has lungs and gills, it was previously thought that amphibian species evolved through this fish. 

Methuselah is an important fish in terms of biodiversity. Because the lungfish species in Australia is under threat of extinction. The California Academy has two more fish of this species. One of them is called 'Medium', the other is called 'Small'. Both of these fish are younger than Methuselah. Methuselah has different characteristics than these two fish. Because this fish can rub its belly in a special way.

Headline_English: Expatriate income has started to increase again
Content_Enlish:
Expatriate income has started increasing again. They sent $1.7044 billion home in January. This income is the highest in the last four months. 

This information has been revealed from the updated report on remittances of Bangladesh Bank. 

Those concerned say that the increase in the price of the dollar and the 2.5 percent incentive have mainly led to the increase in sending money through legal channels. However, overall, remittances have been less in the current fiscal year so far compared to the last fiscal year. 

According to the central bank, remittances have reached $1,944 billion in the seven months of the current fiscal year. In the same period of the last fiscal year, $1,490 billion came. Accordingly, remittances have come in at a lower rate of $2.96 billion in the seven months of the current fiscal year.

Headline_English: Pfizer-BioNTech is bringing vaccines to children under 5 years of age
Content_Enlish:
Pfizer and BioNTech are bringing the corona vaccine for children aged 6 months to 5 years. The US Food and Drug Administration-FDA will apply for emergency use of the vaccine on Tuesday. 

If approved, the corona vaccine for children under 5 years of age will be available by the end of this month. The vaccine will be a two-dose vaccine. The FDA has called on Pfizer to submit an application to analyze its data. Earlier, a review of Pfizer's data showed that one-tenth of the adult dose is safe for children. However, last year, Pfizer claimed that two doses were less effective for children aged 2 to 5 years. 

However, Reuters says that Pfizer-BioNTech and FDA authorities were contacted for comment, but there was no immediate response. 

Meanwhile, the number of corona infected people in the world exceeded 380 million with 2.872 million new cases. 11,000 people died in a day. This brings the global death toll to 5.7 million. 

The highest number of 416,000 corona patients in the world in a single day was identified in France. The number of infected people in the country is about 20 million. The second highest number of 264,000 patients in a single day was found in the United States. More than 2,500 people have died. In India, 158,000 new patients were identified in a single day. 1,728 people have died. The highest number of 125,000 patients in a single day since the start of the epidemic was identified in Russia. And with 183,000 new patients, the number of infected people in Germany has exceeded 10 million.
