Headline_English: 24 eminent personalities to receive Ekushey Padak
Content_Enlish:
This year, 24 distinguished individuals will receive the Ekushey Padak in recognition of their unique contributions to the national field. Their names were announced by the Ministry of Cultural Affairs this morning. 

The government has decided to award the Ekushey Padak to 24 distinguished citizens of the country for their significant contributions to various fields at the national level. The Ministry of Cultural Affairs announced this information in a press release today. 

Mustafa MA Matin (posthumously) and Mirza Tofazzal Hossain (posthumously) will receive this year's Ekushey Padak in the language movement. 

Jinnat Barkatullah will receive it in dance in art. Nazrul Islam Babu (posthumously), Iqbal Ahmed and Mahmudur Rahman Benu in music. 

Khaled Mahmud Khan (posthumously), Afzal Hossain and Masum Aziz will receive it in acting. 

The heroic freedom fighter Principal Md. Matiur Rahman, Syed Moazzem Ali (posthumous), QABM Rahman and Amjad Ali Khandaker. 

MA Malek will receive the Ekushey Padak in journalism this time. 

Professor Gautam Buddha Das in education. 

SM Abraham Lincoln and Sangharaj Gyanashree Mahather in social service. 

Md. Anwar Hossain will receive it in science and technology. 

Poet Kamal Chowdhury and Jharna Das Purkayastha have been nominated for the Ekushey Padak in language and literature. 

Md. Abdus Sattar Mandal will receive the Ekushey Padak in research, Md. Enamul Haque as a team leader. Also, Shahnaz Sultana and Jannatul Ferdous as a team. 

The country's second highest private honor is the 'Ekushey Padak'. 

Since 1976, the Bangladesh government has been giving this award in February every year in memory of the martyrs of the great language movement in recognition of their special contributions in various national fields. Each awardee is given a gold medal, a one-time cash prize, and a certificate of honor.

Headline_English: Facebook's user base declines for first time in 18 years
Content_Enlish:
The number of active users of the social media platform Facebook has decreased. This is the first time in its eighteen-year history that the number of users has decreased. 

Facebook's parent company Meta has reported that the number of daily users was 1.929 billion in the last three months of 2021. The number of users was 1.93 billion in the previous three months. 

Meanwhile, Meta has also warned about Facebook's revenue. The company said that their revenue on the digital platform has decreased compared to competitors TikTok and YouTube. 

One of the reasons for this is that various companies have also reduced the amount of advertising. After that, the price of Meta's shares also decreased in New York. Its value is about 200 billion US dollars. After such an announcement from Meta, the share prices of Twitter, Snapchat and Pinterest also decreased. 

Meta's CEO Mark Zuckerberg said that as Facebook's business decreased, users, especially young users, have started using the platforms of competing companies by reducing their use of Facebook. 

The world's largest advertising company is Google. After that, Meta's advertising company is in the same position. The company said that Apple's operating system has changed. Due to this, Facebook's advertising has decreased. As a result, companies are not able to reach their customers according to their goals by advertising on Facebook and Instagram. 

Dave Wehner, Chief Financial Officer of Meta, said that these changes will affect the company's revenue this year. Its financial value could be $ 10 billion.

Headline_English: Voting in 138 UP constituencies in the seventh phase
Content_Enlish:
Voting is scheduled for a total of 138 Union Parishads in the seventh phase. The election equipment has already reached the centers. The Election Commission has completed all preparations for the election. In this phase, voting will be conducted through EVMs in 9 and ballots in 129 unions. Voting will be held from 8 am to 4 pm without any break. 

Although the 6th phase of UP elections was completed peacefully, incidents of violence occurred in all the previous phases. Therefore, there is a fear of violence regarding the seventh phase elections. 

In such a situation, the Election Commission has completed preparations for the seventh phase of elections. Election equipment started reaching the centers from Sunday morning. However, the ballot papers will be delivered on Monday morning. The Election Commission has taken all kinds of measures to ensure voting in a festive atmosphere. 

In addition to magistrates, Ansar, BGB, RAB, and police will be deployed at the polling centers to ensure security in the elections. 

According to EC sources, there are a total of 24 lakh 51 thousand 782 voters in this election. Of these, 12,57,586 are male voters, 1,194,229 are female voters and 3 are transgender voters. These voters will vote in 7,085 polling stations in 1,350 centers. 

In the seventh phase of the election, 576 are contesting for the post of chairman, 1,236 for the reserved post and 4,062 for the general post. Of these, 11 have been elected as chairman without a vote. 

All preparations for the 7th phase of voting have been completed. 71 candidates have been elected unopposed in the 7th phase. Of these, 11 are for the post of chairman, 13 for the reserved female member post and 47 for the general member post. 

Earlier, six phases of voting have already been completed in the ongoing UP elections. 369 union parishad elections were held in the first phase on June 21 and September 20, and 833 in the second phase on November 11. 

In addition, voting was held in 1,000 UPs in the third phase on November 28, 836 UPs in the fourth phase on December 26, 708 UPs in the fifth phase on January 5, and 218 UPs in the sixth phase on January 31. Voting will be held in 138 UPs in the seventh and final phase on February 7.

Headline_English: President, Prime Minister mourn Lata Mangeshkar's death
Content_Enlish:
President Md. Abdul Hamid and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina have expressed deep grief over the death of the eminent musician of the subcontinent, Lata Mangeshkar. 

The President prayed for the eternal peace of the departed soul of the late Lata Mangeshkar and expressed deep condolences to her bereaved family. 

In her condolence message, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that the death of this queen of music has created a huge void in the music scene of the subcontinent. Lata Mangeshkar will forever live in the hearts of the people of this subcontinent through her work. 

Lata Mangeshkar died at 8:12 am on Sunday. She breathed her last at Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai. 

A two-day state mourning has been declared in India on her death. Indian President Ram Nath Kovind and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have also expressed their condolences. 

Lata, the daughter of Marathi theatre pioneer Pandit Dinanath Mangeshkar, was born in 1929. After Dinanath's untimely death in 1942, when she took over the family of 5 siblings, she was a 13-year-old girl. 

Lata has given us some unforgettable masterpieces. Romantic, religious or patriotic. All the songs had a different sweetness in her voice. From the common listener to Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, those melodies moved to tears. 

She has sung seven and a half thousand songs in 36 languages, including Bengali. Prem Aye Aa Nirob, Ashadh Shravan Mane Na To Man, O Palash O Shimul, Akash Pradeep Jwel, she will remain immortal in Bengali hearts with songs like

Headline_English: PM orders to make manpower export transparent
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has ordered to make the process of manpower export transparent to prevent harassment of the common people. She gave this order in a cabinet meeting. Meanwhile, the cabinet has approved the Forest Industries Development Corporation Act, keeping the provision of permission from the Environment Ministry even for cutting trees in one's own house. 

The Prime Minister joined the cabinet meeting held at the Secretariat on Monday via video conference from Ganabhaban. Later, Cabinet Secretary Khandaker Anwarul Islam briefed journalists about the meeting. 

At this time, the Cabinet Secretary said that the Prime Minister has ordered to make this process transparent to stop cheating the poor people in manpower export. She also ordered to inform everyone about this process. In addition, Sheikh Hasina has ordered to arrange loans easily through the Expatriate Welfare Bank so that expatriate workers do not have to sell their houses in the clutches of brokers. 

She also said that the Prime Minister has specifically instructed to make the people who will go abroad very precise and transparent and to publicize it widely on television, radio and media. People should be told that these are the authorities and this amount of money will be required. And if money is needed, then they should take a loan through the Expatriate Welfare Bank. 

Khandaker Anwarul Islam also said that workers who are going abroad should keep in touch with the Expatriate Welfare Ministry or their directorate. They should not pay any extra money. Many people make payments without knowing it, so the cabinet has advised the Expatriate Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry. 

In addition, regarding the new law on forest conservation, the cabinet secretary said that the cabinet has approved the draft of the Bangladesh Forestry Development Corporation Act, 2022, with provisions for the conservation of all forest areas in the country. It states that permission from the Ministry of Environment must be obtained even for cutting large trees planted in private ownership. All trees planted through social forestry will also come under this. 

Meanwhile, the implementation rate of decisions taken in the cabinet meeting in 2021 has decreased by 19.1 percent compared to 2020. This information has been revealed in the fourth quarterly report of 2021 on the cabinet meeting.

Headline_English: Greece to hire 20,000 workers without cost
Content_Enlish:
Greece will take 20,000 workers in 5 years without immigration costs. The country has signed a 5-year agreement with Bangladesh. The European country will also provide legalization and work opportunities to 15,000 Bangladeshis living there illegally. This agreement was signed between the two countries at the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare this morning. 

Greece is one of the oldest civilizations in the world, with a population of more than 10 million. The economy here is mainly based on the service and tourism sectors. 

Only 3 percent of the country's national economy comes from the agricultural sector. Therefore, Greece has signed an agreement with Bangladesh to take workers in this sector with the aim of expanding agriculture. A related labor agreement was signed between the Greek Minister of Immigration and the Minister of Expatriates' Welfare on Wednesday morning at the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare. 

According to the newly signed agreement, Greece will take 4,000 skilled workers every year at zero immigration costs. In addition, 15,000 Bangladeshis residing in that country will also be given employment opportunities after screening. 

Meanwhile, the technical committees of the two countries will determine the process by which the workers will go. However, the ministry has stated that it will give importance to the training and skills of the workers. 

Greece's Minister of Migration and Refugees, Panagiotis Mitarachi, said that the country wants to send a message that there is an opportunity to go to Greece for work not illegally, but legally. 
Bangladesh signed the first agreement with Greece on the labor market issue among European countries. However, this process will begin after the country's parliament passes a law on illegal immigrants in April.

Headline_English: Tigers batting coach Ashwell resigns
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh national team batting coach Ashwell Prince has resigned. BCB Cricket Operations Chairman Jalal Yunus confirmed the matter. 

Jamie Siddons has recently become the BCB's batting consultant. He is supposed to work with the Tigers in the Afghanistan series. BCB wanted to use Prince in a different way with Siddons' arrival. The Proteas coach did not agree to that plan, the BCB Cricket Operations Chairman said. 

Earlier, a report by South African website Independent Online (IOL) revealed the resignation of Ashwell Prince. IOL reports that Prince resigned due to the desire to give more time to his family. 

BCB CEO Nizam Uddin Chowdhury told the media, we received his resignation email a while ago. The board will now take a further decision on him through discussions. 

Prior to this, Ashwell Prince joined the Bangladesh team as the batting coach in July last year. His contract with BCB was until the T20 World Cup to be held in Australia in October-November. The coach has played 66 Tests, 52 ODIs and 1 T20I for South Africa. 

Prince was scheduled to return to Dhaka on February 18 after a vacation in South Africa. He was also scheduled to work for the Bangladesh team in the Afghanistan series. Bangladesh team head coach Russell Domingo is also scheduled to return to Dhaka on February 18 or 19. 

However, even though Ashwell Prince has left, Domingo will remain as the head coach, BCB CEO Nizam Uddin Chowdhury said.

Headline_English: Nasir and Tamima's trial begins
Content_Enlish:
Charges have been framed against cricketers Nasir and Tamima in a case of illegal marriage through forgery. Through this, the formal trial against them has begun. Nasir's mother-in-law Sumi Akhter has been discharged from the case. 

Additional Judge of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court Tofazzal Hossain issued this order on Wednesday afternoon. 

Later, the court fixed March 10 as the date to take testimony in the case. On October 31 last year, Nasir, Tamima and Tamima's mother Sumi surrendered to the court and applied for bail. Later, the court granted their bail. They are currently on bail. 

Nasir and Tamima got married on February 14, 2019. But Tamima's previous husband Rakib Hasan alleged that she married cricketer Nasir despite not being separated. He later filed a case on February 24, 2021.

Headline_English: 9/11 victims to receive half of Afghanistan's seized money
Content_Enlish:
The United States has decided to return the seized reserve money to Afghan citizens who are facing extreme humanitarian crises, including food shortages. However, only half of the seized $7 billion will go to the Afghan people. Washington has announced that the remaining half will be given to the families of the victims of the 9/11 attacks. 

Afghanistan is going through a terrible humanitarian crisis. Eight million people are in a severe food crisis. Most of them are not guaranteed one meal a day. Analysts say that Afghanistan will collapse if international aid is not received quickly. 

The country was in a financial crisis even before the Taliban came to power. 75 percent of Afghanistan's expenses came from foreign aid. When the Taliban took power after the withdrawal of US troops, aid stopped and suffering reached its peak. And the US government seized Afghanistan's $7 billion reserve that was deposited with the United States. 

Meanwhile, many Afghan private businesses have closed due to lack of money. Millions of people are on the streets due to lack of work. Many have also died from lack of food. 

The United States has decided to return the money to the Afghan people in response to demands from the Taliban and various international organizations. However, the US government will not return the entire $7 billion seized. 

Washington has announced that half of the total amount will be given to the families affected by the 9/11 attacks. President Joe Biden seized the money in an executive order on Friday. Meanwhile, questions have been raised about why their money will be seized since no Afghan nationals were involved in the 9/11 attacks. 

The White House said that a case is underway in a US court regarding the seized Afghan money. The victims of the 9/11 attacks filed the case demanding the money. For this reason, more than $3.5 billion will be kept in the United States. 

The released money will not be given to the Taliban government, the BBC reported. The US government will work to deliver the $3.5 billion fund to the Afghan people. 

The World Food Program has said that the current situation in Afghanistan cannot be described in just dire words. About 5 million children and pregnant women in the country are on the verge of malnutrition. It is difficult for them to get even one meal a day. 

Nature is also angry with the country, which has been devastated by decades of war. The worst winter in recorded history has joined the financial crisis. There is no fuel to survive the severe cold. This seven-year-old girl is burning clothes to keep her house warm. 

Afghanistan was in a financial crisis even before the Taliban came to power. 75 percent of the country's expenses came from foreign aid. After the Taliban seized power, the suffering reached its peak when that aid stopped.

Headline_English: Book fair starts tomorrow
Content_Enlish:
The Amar Ekushey Book Fair, a gathering of writers, readers and publishers, is starting tomorrow. State Minister for Culture KM Khalid has said that the book fair will be conducted in accordance with health regulations to prevent Corona. No one will be able to enter the book fair without a mask. 

Since it started late this year, the book fair may continue even after February. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will inaugurate the Amar Ekushey Book Fair virtually at 3 pm on Tuesday. The organizer, Bangla Academy, has already completed all preparations for the fair. 

This time, 534 publishing houses are participating in the fair. There will be 776 stalls and 35 pavilions in a total area of ​​7.5 lakh square feet, including the Bangla Academy premises and Suhrawardy Udyan. 

State Minister for Culture KM Khalid said at a press conference at Bangla Academy on Monday about the organization of the fair that the book fair will be conducted in accordance with the Corona health regulations. 

Stating that it is mandatory for those coming to the fair to wear masks, he said that since it started late, this year's fair may continue even after February. 

Bangla Academy Director General Kabi Muhammad Nurul Huda said that this year's fair carries special significance in commemorating the 70th anniversary of the language movement and the 50th anniversary of the book fair. 

The book fair will run from 2 pm to 9 pm every day. On Fridays and Saturdays, the fair will start at 11 am. 

In addition, the fair will start at 8 am on February 21. 

It is worth noting that Chittaranjan Saha, owner of Muktadhara Publishing, started selling books by spreading tarps at the gate of Bangla Academy on the occasion of Language Day on February 22, 1972. Later, many others joined him in 1977. 

Then in 1978, the then Director General of Bangla Academy, Ashraf Siddiqui, associated Bangla Academy with this book fair. The following year, the Bangladesh Booksellers and Publishers Association joined the fair. 

In 1983, when Manjure Maula was the Director General of Bangla Academy, preparations were made to organize this fair under the name 'Amar Ekushey Book Fair', but it could not be done. The following year, in 1984, the 'Amar Ekushey Book Fair' was launched on the premises of Bangla Academy.

Headline_English: Team announced against Afghanistan with three new faces
Content_Enlish:
The BCB has announced a 15-member squad for the ODI series against Afghanistan with Ebadat, Nasum Ahmed and Mahmudul Joy in the squad for the first time. 

The 15-member squad was announced on Monday, February 14. 

Mahmudul Hasan Joy has been called up for the first time in the team. Mithun, Sohan, Shamim and Mosaddek have been dropped from the team. 

The Afghanistan cricket team has already arrived in Bangladesh to play the limited-overs series. The three ODIs will be played at the Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium in Chittagong between February 23 and 28. The ODIs will start at 11 am Bangladesh time. The Bangladesh-Afghanistan ODI series is part of the World Cup Super League. 

After that, Afghanistan will play two T20Is on March 3 and 5 at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur, Dhaka. These matches will start at 3 pm. 

ODI squad: Tamim Iqbal (captain), Liton Das, Nazmul Hossain Shanto, Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan, Mahmudullah, Afif Hossain, Mehedi Hasan Miraj, Mostafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, Shariful Islam, Ebadat Hossain, Nasum Ahmed, Yasir Ali, Mahmudul Hasan Joy.

Tour companions: Qais Ahmed, Salim Safi 

Bangladesh has come to Afghanistan to play a bilateral series for the third time. They last played a Test in 2019, which Bangladesh lost. Before that, Afghanistan came to Bangladesh to play a 3-match ODI series in 2016.

Headline_English: Volatile fuel oil prices in the world market
Content_Enlish:
The ongoing Russia-Ukraine tension, the third wave of Corona and increased demand have caused the global fuel market to be unstable. As a result, the price of crude oil rose to $95 per barrel on Monday, which is the highest in 7 years. Meanwhile, the Ukraine issue may disrupt the exports of major oil producer Russia. As a result, analysts fear that the price of fuel oil will exceed $100 per barrel. 

In 2020, the demand for fuel oil fell sharply in the world due to lockdowns and various restrictions. On April 20 of that year, the highest price drop in history occurred. The price of crude oil fell below $18. 

As vaccinations started in each country, the demand for fuel increased again from 2021. However, due to various uncertainties of Corona and the decision of the OPEC alliance not to increase production, the price of oil exceeded $84 in November last year. 

This time, the Russia-Ukraine crisis has been added to the list of ups and downs in the global fuel market. Fuel oil prices rose to a 7-year high on Monday due to fears of a Russian attack on Ukraine.

During this period, the price of Brent crude rose by 1.2 percent to $95.56 per barrel. At the same time, the price of oil in the United States rose by 1.5 percent to $94.38. 

According to analysts, US and European sanctions may be strengthened due to the fear of Russia's attack on Ukraine. Since Russia is one of the largest oil producers, supply may be disrupted. As a result, there is a risk that oil prices will exceed $100. 

In addition, although the OPEC alliance was supposed to increase production by 400,000 barrels per day until March, it has not been able to do so. The International Energy Agency has called on major producers in the Middle East to come forward to keep supply normal. 

In the past week, the price of Brent crude has increased by about 5 percent and in the United States by about 6 percent. And in the space of a year, Brent crude is being sold at a price of 56 percent more per barrel in the world market and has increased by about 62 percent in the United States.

Headline_English: Best Film: Gore-World Beauty, Best Artist: Siam-Dipanvitha

Headline_English: Russia is withdrawing troops from the Ukrainian border
Content_Enlish:
Tensions have been high for weeks over the deployment of more than 100,000 Russian troops on the Ukrainian border. Some Russian troops stationed on the Ukrainian border are returning to their bases after completing exercises, the Russian Defense Ministry said on Tuesday. 

A Russian Defense Ministry spokesman said in a video statement on Tuesday that some troops are returning to their bases after completing exercises near the Ukrainian border. 

Video released by the Russian Defense Ministry showed tanks and armored vehicles being loaded onto open railway wagons. 

The announcement of the withdrawal of troops from Russia came on a day when German Chancellor Olaf Soltz returned to Moscow after a visit to Kiev to continue diplomatic efforts to avoid war. 

The Russian move has raised hopes that it will help ease tensions between Moscow and the West over Ukraine. Meanwhile, the news of the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian border immediately gave a positive reaction on stock markets. 

According to Reuters, after several weeks of lows, Russian stocks and the Russian ruble suddenly rose sharply today. The prices of Russian and Ukrainian government bonds also rose significantly. 

However, Ukraine is still skeptical about Russia's actions. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba said that they will only be able to say whether tensions will ease after they see with their own eyes that Russia is really moving troops. 

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba was quoted as saying by the Ukrainian Interfax news agency, "We are hearing different statements from the Russian Federation at different times. So we have decided to believe only what we see with our own eyes." 

Like Ukraine, NATO countries are also skeptical about Russia's move. 

According to BBC sources, NATO officials and diplomats are trying to understand whether Russia is really taking steps to reduce tensions or if this is another tactic by Moscow. 

Sergei Radchenko, a professor at the Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies, said Russia has always said it is not threatening anyone and that its troops are simply taking part in exercises. Professor Radchenko believes this is a new tactic by President Putin. 

He likens the tactic to "cooking a pot of thick soup" where Putin "will turn the heat up and down as time and convenience dictates to maintain the tension."

Headline_English: The reason for the escalation of Russia's attack on Ukraine
Content_Enlish:
Russia now has about 130,000 troops and heavy weapons deployed on Ukraine's borders. The Americans have been saying for the past few days that Russian troops could attack Ukraine at any moment. 

The future of the entire European security structure depends on what happens with Ukraine now. 

How much is the risk of a Russian attack? 

Russia has repeatedly said that it has no plans for a military operation in Ukraine. Sergei Naryshkin, the head of Russia's foreign intelligence service, has expressed his anger and said that 'dangerous lies' are being spread from the capitals of America and Western countries. 

But no one can ignore the current risk given the history of Russia's attack on Ukraine and the annexation of Crimea in 2014. The NATO Secretary General has said that the risk of a Russian attack is 'not imaginary, it is very real.' America has repeatedly said that a Russian attack on Ukraine could begin at any moment. 

About a dozen Western countries have advised their citizens to leave Ukraine immediately. 

President Biden's top military adviser, J. Mark Milley, has warned that the scale of Russia's planned attack would result in massive casualties and the consequences of urban warfare would be devastating. Ukraine's president, however, has urged Western countries not to give in to "panic." 

France believes that President Putin's main goal is to gain leverage in negotiations with NATO over Russia's security. 

President Putin has threatened to take appropriate "military-technical" measures if Western countries do not, in his words, stop their aggressive activities. 

How big is the Russian troop buildup? 

Russia has deployed about 100,000 troops on the Ukrainian border. In addition, 30,000 Russian troops are taking part in joint exercises in neighboring Belarus. 

Russia's deputy foreign minister recently compared the situation in Ukraine to the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis. The deployment of Russian missiles in communist Cuba created an extreme risk of nuclear war between the United States and the then Soviet Union. 

Why Russia threatens Ukraine 

Russia has long been trying to prevent Ukraine from joining Western institutions like the European Union and NATO. At the heart of Russia's security demands is that Ukraine should never be included in the NATO military alliance. 

Ukraine borders both the European Union and Russia, but as part of the former Soviet Union, Ukraine has historical social and cultural ties with Russia. The Russian language is widely spoken in the country. 

When the pro-Russian president was ousted in Ukraine in 2014, Russia sent troops to occupy southern Ukraine's Crimea region. At the same time, ethnic Russian rebels, with Russian support, took control of a large area in eastern Ukraine. 

Since then, the Ukrainian army has been fighting the rebels intermittently. In which more than 14,000 people have died.

What Russia Wants from NATO 

Russia says it is time to make a final decision on its relationship with NATO. "We need to make sure that Ukraine never becomes a member of NATO," said Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov. 

President Putin has said that if Ukraine becomes a member of NATO, the military alliance will try to take control of Crimea. He recently added, "Suppose Ukraine becomes a member of NATO and starts a war to take Crimea. Would we then go to war with NATO? Has anyone ever thought about that? I don't think so. 

Russia says that NATO is supplying Ukraine with too many weapons and that the United States is stirring up tensions to stop Russia's progress. President Putin said, "Russia has no room to move, do they think we will sit still?" 

Russia wants NATO to return to its pre-1997 borders. They are demanding that NATO's expansion and military activities in Eastern Europe be halted. That means withdrawing NATO troops from Poland and the three former Soviet republics of Lithuania, Estonia and Latvia, and removing NATO missiles from countries like Poland and Romania. 

President Putin said that in 1990, Western countries promised that NATO would "not move an inch further east," but that they did not keep that promise. 

That promise was supposedly made to Mikhail Gorbachev before the collapse of the Soviet Union. However, the promise was made to NATO in the context of East Germany, and Mr. Gorbachev himself later said that he had discussed NATO expansion with him at the time. The Americans have not spoken. 

What does Russia want from Ukraine? 

Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 on the basis of historical claims. Ukraine was part of the Soviet Union. Putin believes that the breakup of the Soviet Union in 1991 also meant that the historical Russian mainland was lost. 

In one of his articles last year, Mr. Putin said that Russians and Ukrainians are 'one and the same people', but that the current leadership of Ukraine is pursuing an 'anti-Russian project'. 

Russia is also angry and frustrated that the international understanding reached in 2015 on eastern Ukraine, called the Minsk Agreement, is not being respected. 

Is it possible to stop Russia? 

President Putin has spoken several times with US President Biden, and French President Macron said that during a long meeting with him, Mr. Putin assured him that he would not start a war. 

The White House says that in addition to sending troops to Ukraine, Russia has also received other weapons There are, such as cyber attacks and paramilitary tactics. 

When 70 Ukrainian government websites were shut down in January, Russia was blamed, although Russia said it was not behind it. 

The US has accused Russia of planning to launch a military operation by creating a video of a fabricated plot in which Ukrainian troops attacked inside Russia for the first time. Russia has said that these are American fantasies. 

Russia recently gave 700,000 Russian passports to rebel-held areas of eastern Ukraine in order to take action under the pretext of protecting its citizens. 

However, NATO has made it clear that it will not accept Russia's demand that no one be admitted to the alliance in the future. "We will not allow anyone to close the door to NATO's open door policy," said US Deputy Secretary of State Wendy Sherman. 

However, Ukraine's ambassador to Britain, Vadym Pyrishtyko, told the BBC that the way Ukraine is being threatened and blackmailed is making NATO more likely to avoid war. They are willing to be “flexible” on the issue of membership. 

Russia is also trying to prevent Sweden and Finland, which are not yet members of NATO, from joining, although the two countries have said they will not go along with Moscow. 

How much will the West help Ukraine? 

The United States and NATO countries have said they will not send troops to Ukraine to fight Russia. But they have also pledged various kinds of help. The Pentagon says 8,500 troops are being kept ready and an additional 3,000 are being sent to Germany, Romania and Poland. 

However, in return, the West has two main weapons: sanctions on Russia and the sending of weapons and military advisers to Ukraine. 

Poland has offered to provide surveillance drones, mortar bombs and anti-aircraft systems. The United States, Canada, Britain, the Czech Republic and the Baltic states have pledged weapons, training, advice and equipment. 

However, President Biden has said that such sanctions will be lifted if war breaks out. will be given that "Russia has never seen before." 

What could be the scope of the sanctions? 

The most damaging thing would be to cut off Russia's banking sector from the international payment system run by the American company SWIFT. But perhaps that system will only be considered if there is no other way, because taking that path could also cause major damage to the European and US economies. 

Another threat is that the US will not allow the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which Russia has built to supply gas to Germany, to be built under the sea. President Biden has also threatened that he will consider imposing personal sanctions on President Putin. 

Britain has warned that 'people close to the Kremlin will have no place to escape.' 

What will an agreement look like? 

Any agreement would have to include overall security as well as the fight against rebel-held areas of Ukraine. 

A fragile ceasefire is in place in eastern Ukraine, but talks to implement the Minsk peace deal, which was reached in 2014 and 2015 between Ukraine, Russia, France and Germany, have so far failed to materialize. 

Ukraine is unhappy with the terms of the deal. They believe it gives too many concessions to Russia and the rebels. But President Putin has told Ukrainian leaders, "You have to accept it whether you like it or not." 

Russia and the United States have held several rounds of talks in recent weeks, sometimes by telephone and sometimes by video link. 

The leak of some written proposals sent to Russia by NATO and the United States has given some indication of what the West is thinking about in terms of alleviating Russia's security concerns. 

The United States has offered to talk to Russia about reducing its deployment of short- and medium-range missiles. . It has also offered to start talks on a new treaty on intercontinental ballistic missiles. 

Washington has also said that it will guarantee that no long-range missiles will be deployed in Poland and Romania if Russia agrees not to host two missile bases. 

However, there has been no promise to Russia to stop NATO expansion in Eastern Europe or to never include Ukraine in the alliance.

Headline_English: High Court seeks government's plan to reduce air pollution
Content_Enlish:
The High Court has issued a rule asking why the government's failure to prevent air pollution should not be declared illegal. At the same time, the rule also asked why the most polluted areas should not be identified and a specific action plan should not be adopted to prevent pollution. 

A bench of Justice Farah Mahbub and Justice SM Moniruzzaman gave the order. 

The order said that the public should be informed about the existence of air pollution monitoring centers, based on the level of different areas, so that they can take necessary personal protection. 

The High Court has also ordered a specific action plan to be given on when the use of block bricks will start to prevent environmental pollution. 

The Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association filed the writ seeking necessary instructions to prevent air pollution. 

Lawyer Syeda Rizwana Hasan heard the writ in the court. Deputy Attorney General Samarendra Nath Biswas was present at the hearing for the state. 

During the hearing, the court said that everyone should work for the people so that everyone has a responsibility. The High Court commented that it is important for those concerned to have a sense of responsibility to create awareness to create a habitable environment for future generations. 

The High Court has ordered the installation of continuous air monitoring stations used to monitor air quality at appropriate places to prevent pollution and the introduction of an alert system to protect the public from dangerous and unhealthy air. 

It has also been ordered to develop an alternative method of burning bricks and implement an action plan. 

The defendants have been asked to submit a report to the court within four months on the implementation of the directive. 

The court has set a date for the next order on June 26.

Headline_English: Thousands of ATMs closed, Ukraine hit by cyberattack
Content_Enlish:
Ukraine has been hit by the largest cyber attack. This attack has halted internet services and shut down government operations. Thousands of ATMs have been rendered inoperable due to the disconnection of the main server with the bank. Ukraine is blaming Russia for this cyber attack. 

Tensions have been rising over the Ukraine issue for the past few days. The people of Ukraine are also worried about the war. Fearing that an attack could occur at any moment, Ukrainians are desperately trying to organize public life as much as possible. 

As a result, long lines are seen in front of ATM booths to withdraw money. But suddenly everything is at a standstill. There is internet on mobile but nothing can be done with it. Even the official website of the country's defense department is at a standstill. Connection to the main servers of several banks was cut off. 

A report in the Indian newspaper Anandabazar said that the country has faced the largest cyber attack in its history. Initially, it is believed that Putin's country, Russia, is behind the hack. 

The Ukrainian defense department said that their website has also been attacked. As a result, no one can access their website in any way. 

This type of cyber attack is called Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS). It is known that Russia has carried out cyber attacks on Ukraine several times before. But this time the scope of the cyber attack is more extensive. 

Meanwhile, a spokesman for the Russian Defense Ministry said that the armies of the southern and western provinces are returning to their respective bases after the relevant exercises have ended. 

The Russian Defense Minister has released a video, which shows that their forces are preparing to leave the Ukrainian border. 

However, the Putin government has not given an estimate of how many units of the forces are moving. It is believed that the tension of the war has decreased somewhat in this incident. But such cyber attacks in Ukraine could once again raise the temperature of tensions.

Headline_English: DU admission test to include unit 3 this time
Content_Enlish:
In the face of discussion and criticism, it has been decided to keep the 'Gha' unit under the Faculty of Social Sciences in the admission test for the 2021-22 academic year of Dhaka University. This decision taken at the meeting of the Deans' Committee of DU on Wednesday is being called a 'preliminary decision'. 

According to the decision of the committee, from the 2022-23 academic year, the faculties of Arts, Social Sciences and Law of the university can take the admission test together. 

After the meeting, the university's Associate Vice-Chancellor (Education) ASM Maksud Kamal told the media, 'Many of the students who are interested in admission this time have already prepared for the Gha unit. Taking into account their preparation, the concerns of their parents and the demands of the teachers of the Faculty of Social Sciences, it has been decided in the meeting of the Deans' Committee that the Gha unit examination will continue this year (2021-22 academic year). 

However, this is a preliminary decision. Later, it will be discussed in the university's General Admission Committee, Academic Council and other relevant forums. He also said that it will be finalized only after that. 

Maqsud Kamal also said, 'The G unit exam is being held in the upcoming 2021-22 academic year. From now on, the faculties of arts, social sciences and law will take the exam together. It has also been decided in the Deans' Committee meeting that how students will get the opportunity to change departments, it has also been said to coordinate through student-friendly decisions without restricting any option. This is the decision of the Deans' Committee.' 

For admission to Dhaka University, the exam was being taken in 'K' unit for science students, 'Kh' unit for humanities, 'C' unit for commerce, 'G' unit for department change, and 'F' unit for fine arts. 

For changing departments of higher secondary, students who passed from science, arts and business education branches could apply for 'G' unit if they fulfilled the qualifications in their respective units. Science students would get the opportunity to get admitted to various departments of arts and business education by taking the exam in this unit. HSC pass students in arts and business education would get the same opportunity. 

On February 7, the university suddenly announced in a notification that for the first year undergraduate (honors) admission in the 2021-22 academic year, the admission test will be conducted in four units - A, B, C, and C. That is, there will be no D unit.

Headline_English: Comilla wins title for the third time
Content_Enlish:
Comilla Victorians won the title by defeating Fortune Barisal by 1 run in the final match of the Bangladesh Premier League. With this, Comilla won the BPL title for the third time. Earlier, Comilla had also won the title in 2015 and 2018. 

In the match, Comilla batted first. They scored 151 runs for the loss of 9 wickets after playing the full 20 overs. In reply, Barisal scored 150 runs for the loss of 8 wickets after playing 20 overs. Batting for a target of 152 runs, Barisal's innings was stopped for 150 runs. 

Barisal opener Munim Shahriar returned to the dressing room for a score of zero after hitting a target of 152 runs. Saikat Ali, who came out for one down, played an innings of 58 runs. 

Then, the match fell under pressure when Nurul Hasan Sohan and Dwayne Bravo were dismissed consecutively in the 16th and 17th overs. In the 19th over, Shanto was out lbw for 12 runs off Mustafiz's delivery, and the match was out of Barisal's hands. 

However, the great batsman Chris Gayle paid close attention to the game. Gayle returned to the dressing room with 33 runs off 31 balls. Then Shakib was out for 7 runs off 7 balls. 

As a result, Barisal's batters could not handle the pressure towards the end. Shakib's innings was stopped at 150 runs. 

Earlier, Comilla won the toss and elected to bat first. Liton Das and Sunil Narine, who scored the fastest fifty, had an opening partnership of 40 runs. 

Captain Shakib Al Hasan brought Liton back and gave Barisal a breakthrough. Sunil Narine's stormy innings of 57 runs off 23 balls with five sixes and five fours was stopped by Mehedi Rana. 

Mahmudul Hasan Joy was run out due to a misunderstanding. Mujib's victim was Faf du Plessis. Bravo dismissed Imrul Kayes for 12 runs. Mujib's second victim was Ariful, who scored a duck. In the end, Comilla were reduced to 151 for 9 with Moeen Ali's 38 and Abu Haider Rony's 19 runs.

Headline_English: Onion prices surge
Content_Enlish:
Unrestrained onion prices in the capital's markets. A week later, the price has increased by about 15 taka per kg. Vendors say the price has increased due to low supply in the market. The prices of oil, flour and broiler chicken have also increased. 

Since the start of Corona, the instability in the daily commodities market has not abated. Consumers are worried about the rise in commodity prices. 

On Friday, an unusual increase in onion prices was seen in the capital's markets. The price of domestic onions has increased by about 15 taka per kg in the past week. The price of imported onions has also increased. 

Although domestic onions were sold at 35 taka per kg last week, today they are being sold at 48 to 50 taka in most markets in the capital. 

Vendors say that due to rain, farmers have harvested their crops before the specified time, which has created a temporary crisis. 

CAB, an organization working with consumers, says that unless the market is regularly monitored and onion production is increased, there will be no permanent solution to the problem. 

The prices of edible oil, flour and chicken have also increased in the market. Packaged flour is being sold at 42 taka per kg, up by 2 taka. Broiler chicken has increased by 10 taka per kg. 

The price of oil has increased by 5 taka per liter. Soybean oil is being sold at 165 taka, sellers said. 

Although there has been no new increase, rice is being sold at the same high price as before. Vegetables are being sold at high prices despite good supply. 

Meanwhile, buyers say that the supply of winter supplies in the market is normal, but the prices are high. Sellers said that the prices have increased due to reduced supply as well as increased transportation costs.

Headline_English: The nation remembers the language martyrs with humble respect
Content_Enlish:
With deep respect, due dignity and full solemnity, the nation observed the 'Great Martyrs' Day and International Mother Language Day' in the first hour of the immortal Ekushey February by remembering the language martyrs. 

There is no fear of sabotage on Ekushey February. However, the Director General of RAB has announced several levels of security across the country, including the Central Shaheed Minar. Dhaka University authorities say that due to Corona, 2 people at the individual level and a maximum of 5 people from organizations will be able to pay their respects together. 

On this day in 1952, the highway was stained with the blood of Bengalis, mainly due to the demand for Bengali as the state language. The recognition of Bengali came at the price of that blood and independence was achieved on its steps. 

Ekushey February is not only a day of sacrifice for the establishment of language rights, but also a memorial written in blood of the movement to protect the nationhood, uniqueness and cultural independence of Bengalis. This unforgettable day in the history of Bengalis was celebrated all over the world yesterday as International Mother Language Day. 

However, like last time, everyone will have to follow several instructions during the Corona period to pay their respects. Dhaka University authorities say that in addition to security checks, masks and vaccination certificates may also be verified. In addition, group travel to the altar has been prohibited to prevent infection. 

Meanwhile, CCTV camera surveillance has been installed on various roads for security on February 21. Although there is no threat of sabotage across the country, RAB has stated that maximum security preparations have been made. In addition to intelligence surveillance, there will be separate monitoring online to control cybercrime. 

The RAB Director General said that special attention will be paid to ensure that women and children do not suffer any kind of harassment in the crowd while paying their respects.

Headline_English: Queen Elizabeth II of Britain infected with Corona
Content_Enlish:
Britain's Queen Elizabeth II has tested positive for coronavirus. Buckingham Palace confirmed the news in a statement on Sunday. It said the queen has mild symptoms. 

A special medical board has already been formed for the queen. Although she is now doing well, the royal family is a little concerned about her, as the queen is now 96 and her condition has not been going well for the past few months. 

However, she hopes to continue her duties in Windsor on a limited basis next week. Queen Elizabeth II is following all the instructions, including the necessary treatment. 

The 95-year-old queen had contact with her eldest son, the Prince of Wales. He was diagnosed with coronavirus last week. The queen received her first dose of the coronavirus vaccine on January 9, 2021. 

No effort has been made to prevent Queen Elizabeth II from contracting Covid in the last two years. A separate team of experts was also formed to protect the queen from coronavirus. 

Queen Elizabeth has not been seen in public in the last two years due to Corona. But even then, Corona attacked the royal family. Prince Philip was infected with Corona. However, Corona could not touch Queen Elizabeth II yet.

Headline_English: Russia is planning a major war in Europe
Content_Enlish:
British Prime Minister Boris Johnson has accused Russia of planning the biggest war in Europe since 1945. He made this comment in an interview with the BBC. 

Johnson said that various Russian activities prove that Moscow is moving forward with big plans. He also commented that the lives of countless people in Ukraine are under threat because of Russia. 

Earlier, the British Prime Minister also spoke at the Munich Security Conference. There, Johnson again warned that the United Kingdom would impose the previously mentioned tough sanctions against Russia if it attacks Ukraine. 

Johnson said that the evidence they have shows that Russia is planning the biggest war in Europe since 1945. 

“All signs indicate that the implementation of the plan has already begun,” he said in an interview with the BBC. 

Johnson said that intelligence believes that Russia wants to launch an attack in a way that will surround the Ukrainian capital, Kiev. 

“Everyone needs to understand that this will only cost human lives,” he said.

The British Prime Minister spoke to the BBC from Munich, where world leaders are gathering for an annual security summit. 

Western officials have warned in recent weeks that Russia could invade Ukraine at any moment, but Moscow says it has no plans to attack its neighbour. 

It has also said troops stationed on the Ukrainian border are taking part in military exercises in the area. 

Recent US government estimates suggest there are between 169,000 and 190,000 Russian fighters near the Ukrainian border. This figure includes pro-Russian separatists in eastern Ukraine.

Headline_English: No threat of sabotage on February 21: RAB
Content_Enlish:
There is no threat of sabotage around the International Mother Language Day on February 21. However, RAB Director General Chowdhury Abdullah Al Mamun said that there will be several levels of security arrangements across the country, including the Central Shaheed Minar. He made these remarks at a briefing at the Central Shaheed Minar on Sunday morning. 

He said that intelligence surveillance, plainclothes patrols and various other surveillance methods have been being carried out across the country since the 18th to ensure security on February 21. 

In addition, searches are being conducted at various places including residential hotels as part of extra precautions. Several teams including a bomb disposal unit, dog squad and medical team will be ready at the Central Shaheed Minar tomorrow. 

RAB Director General Abdullah Al Mamun said that to ensure security in the Central Shaheed Minar area, the RAB patrol team will have 36 pickups (VVIP escorts) and 20 motorcycles, a control room, 50 CCTV cameras and an LED panel. In addition, 2 observation posts, 2 bomb and dog sweeping teams will be kept to ensure security in the area. 230 detectives and 24 special forces will also be in the area. 

The RAB Director General also said that 1,222 RAB members will be in 323 patrol teams inside Dhaka to ensure security on the day. 1,604 RAB members will be in 377 patrol teams outside Dhaka. In total, 2,826 RAB members will be deployed in 700 patrol teams across the country. 

Special vigilance will be maintained to ensure that women and children do not suffer any kind of harassment while paying their respects. 

In addition, a separate RAB team is also monitoring online to control cybercrime. 

Meanwhile, Dhaka University authorities say that due to Corona, 2 people at the individual level and a maximum of 5 people from organizations will be able to pay their respects together. 

The Central Shaheed Minar is ready, almost all the work, starting from beautification, is complete. There will be a beautiful display of fine arts students. 

However, everyone will have to follow several guidelines during the Corona period to pay their respects. Dhaka University authorities say that in addition to security checks, masks and vaccination certificates may also be verified. In addition, groups have been banned from visiting the altar to prevent infection.

Headline_English: Russia will pay a heavy price if it attacks Ukraine
Content_Enlish:
US Vice President Kamala Harris has warned that Russia will pay a huge economic price if it attacks Ukraine. She made this warning at the Munich Security Conference in Germany on Saturday. And British Prime Minister Boris Johnson said that Russia is planning a major war in Europe after 1945. 

Meanwhile, a state of emergency has been declared in the Russian region bordering Ukraine. 

Tensions are rising between Russia and the United States over Ukraine. In such a situation, Western leaders have been warning Russia to prevent an attack on Ukraine. 

US Vice President Kamala Harris said that if it attacks, Washington will take unprecedented economic action against Moscow along with its allies. 

Kamala Harris also said that Europe's security is under direct threat in Ukraine. Any country has the right to decide on its border security. It must be remembered that no country's borders should be changed by force. We are ready for economic action - which will be a quick and unified decision. Russian financial institutions and key industries will be targeted. 

UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson said there is still a chance to avoid unnecessary bloodshed. The threat of Russian occupation in Ukraine will have an impact on the entire world, including Asia. That is why I am calling on Western countries to unite against Russia. 

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Kamala Harris during the Munich Security Conference. He said that Ukraine believes in establishing peace through diplomatic means instead of responding to provocations. 

The German Chancellor commented that it would be a wrong decision for Russia to attack Ukraine. He said that there is no justification for deploying more than 100,000 troops on the border. 

The Ukrainian army claims that the separatists have violated the ceasefire 19 times since the beginning of the day. At the same time, they claim that Ukrainian soldiers have been killed by shells fired by them. 

On the other hand, Russia has started nuclear missile exercises under the supervision of Russian President Vladimir Putin. Joint military exercises are underway at a training center in Belarus. Russian warplanes, helicopters and tanks are deployed there. 

Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to meet French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday to try to ease tensions in Ukraine.

Headline_English: Two injured in Houthi missile attack in Saudi Arabia, including Bangladeshi
Content_Enlish:
Two people, including a Bangladeshi, were injured in a missile attack by Yemeni Houthi rebels in southern Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition said the missile hit the Ahad al-Masarihah industrial area in the southern Jazan region of the country on Sunday. 

The Saudi Gazette reported that a Bangladeshi and a Sudanese national were injured in the attack. Several workshops and civilian vehicles were also damaged in the missile attack. However, the details of the injured were not available. 

In this regard, Mohammad Nazmul Haque, Consul General of the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah, said, “From the information we have received so far, two people have been injured, one of them is a Bangladeshi. Their injuries are not serious. We are trying to collect more information about the injured Bangladeshi.” 

A statement from the Saudi-led coalition described the attack as “malicious and cruel” and said it would deal with it “firmly.” 

They said this was the third time that a foreign national was injured in a Houthi missile attack on the Ahad al-Masariha industrial area. 

Earlier yesterday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had destroyed two drones sent from Yemen. 

The force has been fighting the Houthi group in Yemen since 2015. Last Monday, the Houthis carried out an unprecedented attack on Abu Dhabi, another member of the coalition, the United Arab Emirates. Two expatriate Indians and a Pakistani citizen were killed in the attack. 

In addition, the Houthis have been trying to launch missiles and send drones to target various cities in Saudi Arabia.

Headline_English: Taliban's first meeting with the West begins
Content_Enlish:
The Taliban's three-day meeting with representatives of Western governments and Afghan civil society has begun in Norway. The Taliban leaders are holding their first formal meeting with the West since coming to power five months ago. Afghan Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttahida is representing the Taliban at the meeting, which began in the capital Oslo on Sunday. 

The Taliban seized power in Afghanistan on August 15 last year after the withdrawal of US troops. As a result, when Western countries stopped financial assistance, the Afghan economy collapsed, causing a terrible humanitarian disaster. 

The three-day meeting began in the Norwegian capital Oslo. The Taliban held talks with representatives of the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, France, Germany, Italy and Norway on Sunday to resolve the crisis. 

Before the meeting, the Taliban said that they want to end the war and return to a peaceful environment. 

The BBC report says that the Taliban will request the return of Afghan money held in US banks to overcome the economic crisis. The United Nations says 95 percent of Afghanistan's population is suffering from food shortages. 

Afghan Foreign Ministry official Shafiullah Azam said, "We are requesting them to return Afghan resources and stop punishing ordinary citizens for political unrest. It is time for international resources to come forward, because ordinary Afghans are living in great difficulty due to hunger and severe winters." 

They will also meet with women's rights and human rights activists of Afghan origin. Various issues including addressing the humanitarian and economic crisis, security, human rights, and women's education may be discussed at the meeting. 

Norway's Foreign Minister said in a statement that although the meeting was held, it does not recognize or legitimize the Taliban government. Although many countries maintain good relations with the Taliban government, none has yet recognized them. 

Meanwhile, protests and demonstrations have taken place in several European cities over the Taliban's meeting with Western countries. Earlier, after coming to power, representatives of the Taliban government visited Russia, China, Pakistan, Iran, Qatar, and Turkmenistan. 

Meanwhile, Turkey has launched a relief operation across the country to provide humanitarian aid to the people of Afghanistan. The operation is being carried out by order of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the country's state gazette said. 

The Turkish president gave this instruction in accordance with Article 23 of Turkey's Disaster Management Law 5902. Turkey's Disaster and Emergency Management Agency (AFAD) has been given the responsibility of coordinating the relief operation.

Headline_English: Cold wave in the northern region, winter intensity will increase
Content_Enlish:
The intensity of cold has increased across the country. A mild cold wave is blowing in the northern region. The Tentulia Meteorological Observatory recorded the lowest temperature in the district at 9 am as 8.3 degrees Celsius. This is the lowest temperature recorded in Tentulia upazila of Panchagarh this season. 

The temperature has decreased in Panchagarh for the last two days and the intensity of cold has increased. Since evening, thick fog has been covering the surroundings. Meanwhile, although the temperature has increased in Nilphamari and Meherpur, the cold has not decreased. However, there has been drizzle in Jessore. 

Meanwhile, the Meteorological Office has predicted drizzle in one or two places in Dhaka, Barisal and Khulna. This situation may continue for a few more days. 

During this time, the weather in other parts of the country will remain dry. However, light to moderate fog may fall in some places in the country from midnight to morning. The intensity of cold may increase towards the end of the month. During this time, a moderate cold wave may blow in the northwestern part of the country. 

According to the Tentulia Meteorological Office, the minimum temperature of 8.3 degrees Celsius was recorded in Tentulia on December 24 and 26, as of today, Saturday. The mild cold wave passed, and the minimum temperature was recorded on Thursday at 10.1 degrees Celsius and on Friday at 11.2 degrees Celsius. However, the temperature has dropped again today, Saturday. 

The sky in Tentulia has started to clear since Friday evening. The cold wind from the north started increasing late at night. Along with this, the amount of fog decreased. The mercury started to drop. 

The cold is being felt more due to the foggy weather. Low-income working people are suffering due to the increasing cold. Vehicles are moving on the roads with headlights on. The number of cold-related patients in hospitals has increased. Meanwhile, farmers are worried about the seedbeds of Boro.

Headline_English: 9 zebras die in 20 days at Gazipur Safari Park
Content_Enlish:
Nine zebras born inside the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Safari Park in Gazipur have died. In addition, a tiger died a few days ago. The park authorities are unable to confirm how so many animals died at once. 

However, on Tuesday, experts including the Forest Department and zoologist, and veterinary surgeon and former director of Dhaka Chiriakhana Dr. ABM Shahidullah participated in the meeting to inspect and investigate the matter. 

According to safari park sources, nine zebras have died in the park's core safari in the last 20 days. The park authorities are investigating whether the zebras were killed out of hostility, or died of food poisoning or some other disease. However, they are not yet able to say the cause of death. After the autopsy of the bodies, samples have been sent to various laboratories to find out the exact cause of the mysterious death. 

Project Director of Bangabandhu Safari Park, Jahidul Kabir, told reporters that the matter has been monitored since the incident. The autopsy report and samples of each dead body have been sent to various laboratories for testing. They have been sent to several institutions including Bangladesh Agricultural University, IEDCR. Some reports have come, but nothing has come yet. An emergency board meeting has been called on Tuesday. The reports will be presented there. Later, expert doctors will make a decision. 

Assistant Conservator of Forests in charge of the park, Md. Tabibur Rahman, said that the bodies had to be autopsied in the presence of the District Animal Resources Officer. Later, samples were collected and sent to the laboratory. Finally, the zebras were buried. Initially, the corona test came negative. However, there is a slight difference between the corona test of humans and the corona test of animals. He said that the final results of the corona test of animals will be delayed a little.

Headline_English: 29 Bangladeshi sailors detained along with ship in Ukraine
Content_Enlish:
Amidst Russia's aggression in Ukraine, 29 sailors from Bangladesh Shipping Corporation-BSC's ship 'Banglar Samriddhi' are stranded at the country's Olbia seaport. The ship is unable to leave due to lack of port clearance and mines planted in the sea. 'Banglar Samriddhi' reached the Ukrainian port before the Russian attack began. 

The sailors are spending every moment in extreme fear. In this situation, the stranded sailors have appealed to the government, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the BSC to rescue them. 

One of the stranded sailors, Omar Faruk Tuhin, has outlined their situation in a message he sent to his friend. Tuhin said that they are unable to go anywhere from the port because the Russian soldiers have planted mines in the sea. Bombs are exploding all around. They are in danger of losing their lives due to bombs or missiles at any time. At least five ships around them have already been destroyed in missile attacks. The sailor said that there is 10 to 15 days of food on the ship. 

Like him, 29 Bangladeshi sailors are living a life of being stranded on the ship. There is no way to move the ship forward, because mines have been planted in the sea. 

On February 22, the BSC ship arrived in Olivia, Ukraine, to load goods from the Turkish port of Eregli. Then the Russian aggression began. In this situation, it was ordered to leave the port without loading goods and reach international waters. However, the ship was stranded due to lack of clearance. 

Piyush Dutta, Executive Director of BSC, confirmed to Samakal that the ship and the sailors are stranded in Ukraine. He said that they are in constant contact with the captain of the ship. Where they are is somewhat of a safe zone. However, talks are underway with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs about what can be done in this situation. 

Although it is said that there is sufficient food and fuel reserves, it is not clear what plans are being taken to rescue the sailors, according to officials. BSC officials said the ship, which joined the BSC fleet in 2018, is covered by insurance.

Headline_English: Discussions to bring back stranded Bangladeshis
Content_Enlish:
The government has started discussions with the IOM to bring back Bangladeshis stranded in Ukraine and on the Ukrainian border. However, it is not possible to bring anyone back to the country in the next 3 to 4 days. 

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shahriar Alam told reporters at his office on Monday. 

Arrangements are being made to bring back citizens of each country to their respective countries to rescue them from the war situation in Ukraine. The Bangladesh government has started discussions with the IOM to bring back Bangladeshis stranded in Ukraine and on the Ukrainian border. 

In this regard, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shahriar Alam said that about 500 Bangladeshis have already left Ukraine through the borders of Poland, Romania and Moldova. 

Of these, 45 are in charge of the Bangladesh Embassy. The rest have made arrangements for accommodation at their own expense. 

Of those who were able to leave Ukraine, only about 60 want to return home now. The rest said that they will monitor the situation from a European country for the time being. 

Apart from this, at least 700 Bangladeshis still remain in Ukraine. The State Minister advised them to head towards the border after ensuring their safety and disaster-fighting capabilities. 

On February 15, the Bangladesh Embassy in Poland advised expatriate Bangladeshis living in Ukraine to leave Ukraine immediately. 

Bangladesh Ambassador to Poland Sultana Laila Hossain told BBC Bangla that there are an estimated one to one and a half thousand Bangladeshis in Ukraine and they are in a state of anxiety, Laila Hossain said.

Headline_English: Belarus agrees to deploy Russian nuclear weapons on Ukraine border
Content_Enlish:
Belarus has agreed to deploy Russian nuclear weapons on the Ukrainian border during the Kiev-Moscow meeting. The country made this decision during the Kiev-Moscow meeting on Monday. 

Meanwhile, Russia has also taken control of a nuclear power plant after occupying two cities in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine. The country's Defense Ministry confirmed the matter on Monday. 

Meanwhile, more than 500,000 people have fled Ukraine amid the Russian invasion, says the UN refugee agency UNHCR. 

Russia has occupied the cities of Berdyansk and Enerhodar in the southwestern Zaporizhzhia province of Ukraine. Although Russian forces took control of a nuclear power plant in the province, they did not destroy it. However, Ukraine has completely denied this. 

Amidst the Moscow-Kiev talks, Russia launched a rocket attack on Kharkiv in eastern Ukraine, Ukraine claims. The country also said that many casualties have occurred. 

Meanwhile, the Ukrainian president said that convicted criminals with combat experience will be released from prison. 

The country's President Volodymyr Zelensky said that this decision was made in the interests of protecting Ukraine in the fight against Russia. Such a decision is not easy from a moral point of view. However, it will be useful for defense. I say to the Russian soldiers, lay down your weapons to save your lives. Leave our country. 

Russia has announced the closure of airspace with 36 countries, including the UK, Italy, Germany, Spain, Canada. This decision was made by the Putin government after the European Union banned Russian-owned aircraft from airspace. At a meeting with top government officials, Vladimir Putin criticized the West. 

Vladimir Putin said, I have invited you to talk about economic and financial issues. I spoke with the Prime Minister about the sanctions imposed by the West. As I said before, they are an empire of lies. 

In response to the West's actions, the Russian president ordered the nuclear deterrent force to be on alert on Sunday. Belarus then allowed Russian nuclear and weapons deployment on the Ukrainian border.

Headline_English: Jail murder case accused Khairuzzaman arrested in Malaysia
Content_Enlish:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shahriar Alam said that Major Mohammad Khairuzzaman, an accused in the prison murder case and former High Commissioner who was acquitted during the BNP regime, has been arrested in Malaysia. 

He confirmed this information on Thursday afternoon. Major Mohammad Khairuzzaman was an accused in the prison murder case. However, he was acquitted from the case during the BNP regime. 

State Minister Shahriar Alam said that the Malaysian Home Ministry has informed in writing about the arrest of Major Mohammad Khairuzzaman. Currently, the process of bringing Mohammad Khairuzzaman back is underway. Mohammad Khairuzzaman was appointed High Commissioner to Malaysia in 2007 during the caretaker government. 

After the Awami League came to power in 2009, he was asked to return to Dhaka. Considering it risky to return to the country, Mohammad Khairuzzaman obtained a UN refugee card from Kuala Lumpur and remained there. 

Khairuzzaman, who had been living as a refugee in Malaysia for more than a decade, is accused of being involved in the 1975 prison murders. 

On November 3, 1975, four national leaders, Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmed, M Mansur Ali and AHM Kamruzzaman, close associates of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and leaders of the first government of independent Bengal, were killed in the Dhaka Central Jail. 

Retired Major Khairuzzaman was an accused in the prison murder case, but he was later acquitted. 

When his name appeared in the charge sheet of the prison murder case after the Awami League came to power in 1996, Khairuzzaman, who was then the acting ambassador to the Philippines, was summoned to the country. He was arrested on September 24 that year and given compulsory retirement. 

Later, when the BNP-Jamaat returned to power in 2001, Khairuzzaman was released on bail. On May 4, 2003, he was appointed as the Director General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. 

The following year, a court acquitted him of the prison murder case. In 2007, during the caretaker government, he was appointed High Commissioner to Malaysia.
