Headline_English: PM stresses importance of regional cooperation to ensure food security
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has emphasized on agricultural research and education and transfer and exchange of high technology to ensure food security in the countries of the Asia-Pacific region. 

She said. ‘Cooperation in agricultural research and education should be increased among the countries of the region to ensure food security.’ 

The Prime Minister made this recommendation in the first of the three recommendations she presented at the opening ceremony of the 36th Regional Conference of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) for the Asia-Pacific region. 

In her second point, she said that technologies like biotechnology, nanotechnology, and robotics should be strengthened among the FAW member countries of the region through transfer and exchange of high technology in the agricultural sector. 

In her final point, she added: ‘Since modern agriculture requires huge investments, a special fund can be formed to finance and support the agricultural sector.’ 

Bangladesh is organizing a regional virtual hybrid event for the first time. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina joined it virtually from her residence. 

Stating that the COVID-19 pandemic has affected the agriculture sector like other sectors, Sheikh Hasina said that in the initial phase of the pandemic in 2020, the supply chain between both producers and consumers was disrupted. 

However, our timely and effective measures have helped the sector recover quickly. We have taken special measures, including mechanization, to ensure that food production and supply of agricultural inputs are not disrupted, she said. 

Sheikh Hasina said that the pandemic has also taught us how vulnerable people were in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic and how humanity can work together to address such challenges. 

She said, “Food security is of course the most important issue for people. About 305.7 million people in South Asia still suffer from hunger. If we all try sincerely, we can easily arrange food for them. 

FAO Director-General Qi Dongyu and Fisheries and Livestock Minister SM Rezaul Karim spoke at the conference, chaired by Agriculture Minister Dr. Muhammad Abdur Razzak.

Headline_English: The rise in commodity prices is due to the syndicate.
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has said that the daily necessities market is not under control because of the syndicate of ruling party leaders. He made this comment at a rally organized in front of the National Press Club on Tuesday afternoon to protest the rise in commodity prices and demand the sale of adequate commodities at fair prices. 

At the same time, Mirza Fakhrul also claimed that there is a silent famine in the country. Urging the countrymen to join these programs, Mirza Fakhrul said, "We are going to involve the countrymen by taking these programs at the field level." 

The BNP Secretary General said, "In fact, the prices of daily necessities, including rice, pulses, oil, water, electricity and gas, are increasing uncontrollably. Due to this, the people of Bangladesh are being affected financially. Their real income has decreased a lot. People have moved from the middle class to the lower class, which most people cannot say - this is the reality." 

The workers gathered for the rally in small processions since morning. The main rally started at 10 am. BNP central leaders and activists joined it. 

During the rally, traffic was disrupted in the Press Club area. Additional police personnel were deployed to avoid any untoward situation. Earlier, BNP announced an 11-day program on February 26. This program will end with a protest rally by the Weavers' Party on March 15.

Headline_English: BCB officials angry with Shakib
Content_Enlish:
Team Director Khaled Mahmud Sujon is embarrassed about Shakib's unwillingness to go to South Africa tour. Cricket Operations Chairman Jalal Yunus has said that if Shakib is unwilling to play Tests, he may be dropped from the central contract of the red ball. 

Shakib Al Hasan has once again sparked discussion by expressing his unwillingness to go to South Africa tour. BCB President Nazmul Hasan Papon is angry with the spin-all-rounder's comments. The BCB President said that the thought of not going to South Africa after the team was announced has put the team management in danger. 

Meanwhile, Sujon urges the Tiger all-rounder to tell the board directly if he does not want to play. The team and management are in trouble due to Shakib's unwillingness to play in South Africa. Embarrassed Team Director, embarrassed BCB. Sujon vented his anger in the media, hinting at the BCB's tough stance. 

BCB Cricket Operations Chairman Jalal Yunus said that Shakib and Tamim informed the BCB at the beginning of the year about which format they are interested in playing. Even then, the situation has become complicated because they took leave without thinking about the team. That is why questions are being raised about whether Shakib will remain in the red ball contract. 

Shakib wants to rest to overcome physical and mental fatigue. Although the Tiger poster boy is quite active in the advertisement shooting in Dubai. Shakib's attention is now elsewhere, leaving aside the team for which he plays so famous. 

Khaled Mahmud said, 'Since Shakib has been given 2 days, it is better not to say it. Let Shakib come, let's talk. I hope Shakib will go. There is actually a difference between Shakib going and not going. 

The Shakib problem will be solved only after he returns to his country. The Tiger all-rounder will have to be informed of the decision within the allotted time. 

The Tigers will leave the country in three days for the South Africa tour. We will have to wait for 2 days to know whether the team will go without Shakib or will have to wait for him until the end. 

Earlier, on Sunday night, before leaving for Dubai for personal reasons, Shakib faced the airport media and said that he had informed the Cricket Board about his thoughts. The board has asked him to think for another two days. 

At this time, Shakib told the media that he is suffering from depression due to continuous cricket and biobubble. Shakib Al Hasan does not consider his physical and mental condition suitable for playing international cricket. In this situation, the experienced all-rounder of Bangladesh feels that it would not be right to go on a tour of South Africa. 

Before the end of the Afghanistan tour, the BCB announced the ODI and Test teams for the South Africa tour. Shakib Al Hasan is in both formats. Although there were rumors about Shakib's absence from the South Africa tour even before the team was announced.

Headline_English: JSS-Mag Bahini firing in Bandarban, 4 killed
Content_Enlish:
Four people were killed in a shootout between JSS and Magbahini in Paindu Union of Ruma, Bandarban. Bandarban District Police Superintendent Jerin Akhter confirmed this information on Sunday morning. 

Bandarban District Police Superintendent Jerin Akhter said that locals found the bodies in the deep forest on the border of Rowangchhari and Ruma on Sunday morning. After seeing the bodies, they quickly informed the police from there. 

Then, based on information provided by the locals, a team of district police recovered the bodies. 

However, even after recovering the bodies, the police could not immediately identify the deceased. 

Meanwhile, the district police superintendent said that the clash between JSS and Magbahini took place in a remote forest. 

Police sources said that the incident took place near Mangbaitang Para of Tarasha Union of Rowangchhari. 

Police superintendent Jerin Akhter told reporters that the murders happening here should be viewed separately and not in the context of general law and order issues. Incidents in the mountains cannot be compared with incidents in the plains. The style is different here. 

He said that there are several organizations active here. They have problems among themselves. This is not the problem of the common people. This is the problem of the organizations. This is also being manifested.

Headline_English: 28 sailors arrive safely in Romania
Content_Enlish:
28 sailors of the ship 'Banglar Samriddhi' have been safely brought to Romania. Bangladesh's Ambassador to Romania Md. Daud Ali confirmed this information. He said that the sailors will now be sent back to their country. 

For now, arrangements have been made for their accommodation in a hotel in the Romanian capital, Bucharest, the ambassador said. He said, "They will stay here after reaching Bucharest. Later, arrangements will be made to send them home by flight. Before that, we will talk to the sailors. 

"They have come a long way, they need rest. We will confirm their return home after talking to them." 

Last Wednesday, the MV Banglar Samriddhi was hit by a shell while anchored near the Olbia Port Jetty in Ukraine. The ship's third engineer, Hadisur Rahman, was killed in the attack. 

The ship was then declared abandoned and the sailors were taken off the ship with the help of local Bangladeshis. Later, they entered Romania via neighboring Moldova. 

Earlier, about 12 hours after departing from Ukraine, 28 sailors safely reached the Moldovan border. Later, they left for Romania. They arrived safely in Romania this morning.

Headline_English: Government is blocking the procession because it is a mass dispersal: Nur
Content_Enlish:
Gana Odhikar Parishad member secretary Nurul Haque Nur has said that the police's obstruction of Friday's procession protesting the price hike of daily necessities is a manifestation of the government's alienation from the people. He made this comment at a press conference in the capital's Paltan this morning. At the conference, Nurul Haque Nur demanded proper justice for the attackers. 

Earlier, Gana Odhikar Parishad took out a procession from the National Press Club on Friday afternoon to protest the price hike. When the procession reached Shahbagh, it turned towards Matsya Bhaban in the face of police obstruction. Later, clashes broke out in front of the Engineers Institute. 

Nurul Haque Nur, member secretary of the organization, alleged that the police had obstructed a peaceful procession in front of the Central Shaheed Minar. 

Later, the leaders and activists of Gana Odhikar Parishad reached Kakrail intersection via the Press Club and took up position. They blocked the road for an hour. 

Regarding the procession, Gana Odhikar Parishad convener Dr. Reza Kibria said, "We demand a reduction in the prices of daily necessities including rice, pulses, and oil." 

Meanwhile, the People's Rights Council has announced to stay on the streets to protect the rights of the people. 

At a press conference on Saturday, protesting against the police's obstruction of Friday's procession protesting the price hike of daily necessities, Nur said that during the procession, the police of Ramna Zone and plainclothes people attacked the leaders and activists of the People's Rights Council indiscriminately. 

In addition, the leaders and activists of the ruling party obstructed the program. More than a hundred leaders and activists of the People's Rights Council were injured. 

At the press conference, Nur also threatened to surround the relevant ministries if the prices of daily necessities were not brought under control.

Headline_English: Bangladesh did not vote against Russia for strategic reasons
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh abstained from voting against Russia in the resolution at the UN General Assembly for strategic reasons, said Information Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud. He said this at a press conference at Dewan Bazar in Chittagong in the afternoon. 

Responding to BNP's criticism, Dr. Hasan Mahmud said that Bangladesh wants friendship with everyone. At the same time, the Information Minister condemned Russia's military operation in Ukraine. 

Last Wednesday, an emergency session of the UN General Assembly called in protest against the start of Russia's military operation in Ukraine passed a resolution to stop the Russian attack with the support of a majority of countries. Bangladesh abstained from voting on this resolution. 

Out of 193 member countries, 141 countries voted in favor of the resolution in the General Assembly's resolution to stop the attack and withdraw Russian troops from the international border of Ukraine. 35 countries, including Bangladesh, India, China, and Pakistan, abstained from voting. Five countries, including Russia, voted against the resolution. 

Among the South Asian countries, Nepal voted in favor of the resolution. Four countries known as Moscow's allies, Belarus, North Korea, Eritrea and Syria, voted against the General Assembly resolution, standing in favor of Russia. 

Moscow's long-time allies Cuba and Nicaragua abstained from voting with China. Venezuela could not vote due to non-payment of dues. 

Regarding the resolution to stop the Russian attack, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said, "Today's resolution of the General Assembly reflects a truth. That is, the world wants an end to the terrible humanitarian suffering in Ukraine. I will do everything in my power to immediately stop the hostilities and contribute to urgent peace talks." 

Addressing a press conference at Chittagong's Dewan Bazar, Information Minister Dr. Hasan Mahmud said, "People's purchasing power has also increased compared to before. Per capita income has increased four and a half times in the last 13 years."

Headline_English: Russia takes over Europe's largest nuclear power plant
Content_Enlish:
The Russian army has taken over the Zaporozhye nuclear power plant in Ukraine, the largest in Europe. Russia launched an attack on the power plant on Thursday to take control of it. Ukrainian officials from the region gave this information. 

Earlier, the power plant caught fire due to gunfire from both sides. Later, fire service workers brought the fire under control on Friday morning. This power plant is the largest nuclear power plant in Europe. 

"People involved in the supervision of this power plant are monitoring the situation," the news agency Reuters reported, citing a statement given by local authorities on social media. 

Officials said that the condition of the power generation units is constantly being monitored. 

Earlier, the power plant caught fire when Russian soldiers bombed it. The fire was later extinguished. The US media outlet CNN reported, citing local officials, that the radiation at the nuclear power plant is at normal levels. 

The Zaporozhye nuclear power plant was built between 1984 and 1995. It took 11 years to build. 

The power plant's six reactors generate 5,700 megawatts of electricity, enough to power about four million homes. 

The Zaporozhye nuclear power plant, which normally generates about a fifth of Ukraine's electricity, is located 550 kilometers southeast of the capital, Kiev. 

The news of the fire at Ukraine's Zaporozhye nuclear power plant sent shockwaves across Asian stock markets, with Tokyo and Hong Kong stocks falling the most. 

Japan's Nikkei stock index fell 2.5 percent and Hong Kong's index fell 2.6 percent. Asian crude oil prices also rose above $112 a barrel. 

The fire at Ukraine's Zaporozhye nuclear power plant, Europe's largest, was caused by Russian airstrikes. A Ukrainian emergency services official said they were initially denied entry. 

They were later able to enter and extinguish the fire. The news of the fire being extinguished restored confidence in many investors in Asian stock markets.

Headline_English: Russia is launching cluster bombs in Ukraine: NATO
Content_Enlish:
The largest nuclear power plant in Europe, Zaporizhia, is now under Russian control. This has once again shaken the United States and the Western world. In the meantime, the foreign ministers of NATO countries are holding an emergency meeting in Brussels. At the meeting, the NATO chief accused Russia of using cluster bombs in Ukraine. 

Although the pace is slow, Russian forces are taking control of important cities and settlements, including the capital of Ukraine, Kiev. Russia attacked the Zaporizhia nuclear power plant, the largest in Europe in the country after Chernobyl, on Thursday. 

The power plant caught fire during the gunfire between the two sides. The Russian army took control of the power plant soon after the fire service workers brought the fire under control. 

After various discussions and criticisms over the incident, the foreign ministers of NATO countries are holding an emergency meeting in Brussels. 

Russia is carrying out a pre-planned invasion of Ukraine without provocation. Considering the situation, NATO has launched a Rapid Response Task Force with speed, unity and determination. Every ally is standing by Ukraine, strengthening NATO. 

Condemning the Russian attack on the Zaporizhzhya nuclear power plant, British Prime Minister Boris Johnson said that the security of the whole of Europe is at risk due to this reckless act. 

US President Joe Biden has also called for an end to military activity in the power plant area. 

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has accused Russia of deliberately attacking the nuclear power plant. He called it nuclear terrorism. 

He also said that Russia has knowingly targeted Europe's largest nuclear power plant. They are playing a destructive game. He mentioned that this one power plant can cause 6 times more horror than Chernobyl. 

On the other hand, the International Atomic Energy Agency has said that the radiation level at the power plant is normal.

Headline_English: Tigres are ready to compete in the World Cup for the first time
Content_Enlish:
The Women's ODI World Cup is about to start in a day. This will be the third time this tournament will be held in New Zealand. Bangladesh is participating on the world stage for the first time. In the meantime, the Tigresses have completed their preparations in the difficult conditions of New Zealand. 

The countdown to the Women's World Cup is coming to an end. A four-six battle between eight teams, thirty-one matches in thirty days. This global women's cricket tournament will be held in New Zealand in a day. The 12th edition is special for Bangladesh. Bangladesh is playing in the ODI World Cup for the first time. 

All the matches of the World Cup will be held at six venues in New Zealand. The hosts New Zealand will face the West Indies in the opening match. 

According to the rules of the round-robin league, each team will have to play a total of seven matches. The new Bangladesh will have to give a tough test against the unknown England, Australia and New Zealand. 

Although India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are familiar opponents, the team of Niger Sultana will have to face a tough fight. 

Bangladesh women face the challenge of adapting to the tough conditions of New Zealand. Their mistakes have been verified by playing warm-up matches. 

The Tigresses are confident of showing their best performance to make their debut memorable. 

Like the boys, Australia has also won the women's fifty-over cricket. The six-time champion team. England has celebrated the title four times. No other team has tasted the title. 

Bangladesh has now joined the subcontinental teams. Will Australia or England celebrate the title again or will the Women's World Cup get a new champion; wait until the final on April 3.

Headline_English: If World War III breaks out, it will be nuclear.
Content_Enlish:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said that if World War III breaks out, it will involve the use of nuclear weapons and will cause widespread destruction. 

According to the BBC, Russian news agency RIA quoted Lavrov as saying that if nuclear weapons fall into the hands of Ukraine, it would pose a real threat to Russia. 

The Russian Foreign Minister has previously expressed fears that Ukraine, with the support of Western powers, will try to acquire nuclear weapons. 

Lavrov made the remarks in a video address to the UN Human Rights Council and the UN Conference on Disarmament on Tuesday, according to a BBC report. 

However, the Russian Foreign Minister could not provide any evidence to support this allegation. 

Meanwhile, the Russian Defense Ministry announced that it had captured and established full control over the Ukrainian city of Kherson. However, it is not yet fully certain whether Russian troops have been able to establish full authority. The governor of the Kherson region said that Russian troops have surrounded the area. 

At least 21 people have been killed in a Russian bomb attack on Ukraine's second city, Kharkiv. 

The Moscow Stock Exchange was closed for the third day in a row. The country's currency, the ruble, has plummeted due to various Western sanctions on Russia. The stock exchange was closed to prevent the fall. 

The price of fuel oil has now risen to $ 113 per barrel, the highest in seven years. 

Russian customers are unable to order Nike products through websites and apps. In response to the attack on Ukraine, the world-famous US company Nike has stopped selling its products in Russia. 

US President Joe Biden has announced that American skies are closed to Russian aircraft. In his State of the Union address, Biden said that history has shown that dictators will create more chaos if they do not pay for their aggressive behavior. 

Belarus has announced that it will double the number of troops on its border. The Belarusian government is very close to Russian President Putin. British Defense Minister Ben Wallace said it would be very difficult for Russia to occupy Ukraine.

Headline_English: Orders to demolish illegal brick kilns in 5 districts
Content_Enlish:
The High Court has ordered the demolition of all illegal brick kilns in Dhaka and four surrounding districts. A bench of Justice Ashfaqul Islam and Justice Md. Iqbal Kabir has ordered the demolition of these illegal brick kilns within 15 days of receiving the order. 

The court said, "The Department of Environment and the district administrations of Dhaka, Narayanganj, Munshiganj, Manikganj, Gazipur will implement this order." At the same time, the Director General of the Department of Environment and the Deputy Commissioners of the five districts have been asked to submit a report to the court immediately on the implementation of this order. 

The court has set April 5 as the date for the next order. Senior lawyer Manzil Morshed heard the petition in the court on Tuesday. Lawyer Amatul Karim heard the hearing for the Department of Environment. Deputy Attorney General Kazi Mainul Hasan and Assistant Attorney General Nasim Islam were present at the hearing for the state. 

Meanwhile, the Department of Environment has expressed its unwillingness to completely destroy them, even though it has carried out the eviction process. 

They highlighted various shortcomings, including a manpower shortage. However, the court said in the hearing that the department's officials must come out of the mentality of avoiding responsibility without looking at the environment. 

The supplementary application was filed on January 30 by the human rights and environmental organization Human Rights and Peace for Bangladesh (HRPB), attaching media reports about the highest pollution levels in Dhaka and the operation of illegal brick kilns. 

After hearing the application, the same bench of the High Court on February 1 ordered the submission of a list of illegal brick kilns in the five districts. Earlier, the deputy commissioners of these five districts submitted a list of more than 300 illegal brick kilns to the court.

Headline_English: Russia's central bank doubles interest rates
Content_Enlish:
The ruble has fallen to a record low after Western and European Union sanctions were imposed on Russia over its military operation in Ukraine. Russia has doubled its interest rates amid the ruble's decline and economic instability. The country's central bank has increased the interest rate from 9.5 percent to 20 percent this time. 

Analysts said the ruble's price has fallen after several sanctions, including the international payment system SWIFT banning major Russian banks and preventing the Russian central bank from using its foreign reserves. 

The Central Bank of Russia has taken this step to prevent the impact of the ruble's depreciation on commodity prices. 

Investors have now made more safe investments to avoid losses. In addition to bonds, investments in international currencies such as the US dollar and the Chinese yen have increased. Investments in the ruble have decreased. 

Meanwhile, many Russian citizens have been seen crowding in front of ATM booths to withdraw money, fearing that their accounts may be closed. 

British banking group HSBC, France's Societe Generale and South Korean lenders have stopped dealing with various Russian parties. Mastercard has also said it will block several Russian financial institutions from its payment network. 

Russia's stock market index fell 33 percent on Thursday after Putin declared war. The Russian currency, the ruble, fell to a record low against the dollar. 

Forbes said the top five Russian billionaires - Alekperov, Mikhelson, Mordashov, Potanin and Kerimov - suffered the most losses.

Headline_English: Storm of condemnation on social media against Russian aggression
Content_Enlish:
A storm of condemnation has erupted across social media against the Russian invasion of Ukraine. War victims are expressing their plight on Facebook and Instagram, among other platforms. Many Russian citizens have also stood by the war victims and refugees. They have also condemned President Vladimir Putin. 

The Russian invasion of Ukraine began on February 24 with the announcement of a military operation. After that, sanctions and condemnation were imposed on Russia by various alliances, including superpowers. However, they have also expressed their own reactions on social media. 

Ukrainian citizens are portraying the horrors of the Russian army in the country through various videos. Not only that, many Russian citizens are condemning this aggression in their country and posting on social media. 

Even the name of Ilyazveta Peskova, the daughter of Russian President Vladimir Putin's press secretary Dmitry Peskov, has appeared on the list of those condemning. Where she posted on Instagram, 'No to war'. However, the post was deleted from her profile within a few moments. 

Not only that, another Russian singer Alla Pugacheva, her comedian husband Max Galkin also posted on Instagram with the same title. This list includes the country's renowned fashion designers, influencers and journalists. Each of them has expressed their support for Ukraine from their own positions. 

In addition to popular stars, social media stars have also stood by Ukraine, condemning Russia's aggression. Their own video messages or videos of Russia's destruction in Ukraine are being posted on TikTok. 

Instead of one country spreading hatred towards another, both countries are sharing their message of spiritual harmony with the world. 

An intense war is going on in Ukraine. Ukraine's power is unequal compared to Russia's military. Therefore, ordinary people are standing by the military. They are helping the soldiers in the war from their own positions as much as they can. 

Ukraine has entered the list of war-torn countries in Europe. In the meantime, millions of people have been displaced in the country. According to the UN, 500,000 people have taken refuge in neighboring countries. 

In this situation, ordinary citizens are coming forward to help the fighting soldiers. People who have taken refuge in bunkers and basements are also trying to help as much as possible. 

Residents who have taken refuge in a library in the city of Lviv are making camouflage nets for soldiers from old clothes. This camouflage net is used to distract the enemy on the battlefield. 

Volunteers are making 20 nets every day. They are singing the Ukrainian national anthem. A crowd of people has gathered at the library. Everyone is bringing cloth in bags to make nets. Their goal is to help the soldiers. Most of the volunteers are between 18 and 30 years old.

Headline_English: Loss of hundreds of crores of taka while earning 5.3 lakh taka
Content_Enlish:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has faced a loss of hundreds of crores of taka while earning only 5.3 lakh taka. Important items including seats, movie sets, food galleys and others were broken while transporting cargo on passenger planes during the Corona pandemic. The State Minister for Aviation says that action will be taken if anyone is found to be negligent in these inspections. 

Due to the restrictions imposed by various countries during the Corona pandemic, passenger transport on Biman has almost stopped. Due to the demand for global goods transport, Biman Bangladesh Airlines has started transporting cargo on passenger planes to reduce losses. Although cargo transport increased by 24 percent, the income increased by only 5.3 lakh taka more than the previous year. 

State-of-the-art aircraft like Boeing 777-300 ER and B-737 have been damaged while carrying cargo in the passenger cabin. Seat handles have been bent under the pressure of heavy cargo, monitors in front of the seats, toilets, food galleys and many other important items have been damaged. It is estimated that a loss of about 100 crore taka has been caused. 

The State Minister said that action will be taken if anyone in charge of aviation supervision finds evidence of irregularities. 

According to international law, to transport cargo on a passenger plane, half the weight of a person's baggage must be placed in the empty space between the front and back seats. However, the plane has transported cargo as it pleases, ignoring these rules.

Headline_English: Russia threatens attack on Kiev, warns city residents
Content_Enlish:
The Russian Defense Ministry has warned residents of the city that Russian troops are preparing to attack various targets in the Ukrainian capital, Kiev. 

In a statement on Tuesday afternoon, Russian officials said the strikes would target Ukraine's "technology center and main psy-op center." 

Civilians near these military installations have been asked to evacuate immediately. 

The Russian statement said, "We urge Ukrainian citizens who are involved in inciting nationalists and other residents of Kiev living near these installations to evacuate." 

Russian officials say the strikes are aimed at stopping propaganda against Russia. 

Earlier, Russia's Foreign Minister Dmitry Kuleba claimed that Russia had launched a missile attack on Ukraine's second largest city, Kharkiv. He made the claim by posting a video on Twitter. There are fears of casualties. This information was reported in a report by the British media outlet BBC. 

The attack took place on Tuesday morning in the city's heart, Freedom Square. Government offices there are believed to have been the target of the attack. 

Dmytro Kuleba tweeted a video of the missile attack in Kharkiv, saying, "Barbaric Russian missiles hit Freedom Square and government offices in the heart of Kharkiv." 

Videos circulating on Ukrainian social media show a missile hitting the front of the regional administration building. The powerful explosion blew out windows and cars in nearby buildings. 

Video footage also shows burnt-out cars and rubble in the city center. The attack took place at around 8 a.m. local time. No casualties have been reported so far. The BBC has verified the authenticity of the video. 

Kharkiv, Ukraine's second largest city, is home to 1.6 million people. The city has been the scene of days of clashes and airstrikes between Ukrainian and Russian troops. 

On Tuesday, Kharkiv regional governor Oleh Sinyhubov alleged that Russian forces were firing Grad missiles at residential areas. These are truck-mounted missile systems that can fire multiple rounds at once. 

Meanwhile, Jack Watling, a researcher on land warfare and military science at the Royal United Services Institute, said that Russia has increased its military presence inside Ukraine from 40 to about 75 percent. 

The Russian invasion of Ukraine has been ongoing for six days. Earlier satellite images showed a large military convoy moving towards the Ukrainian capital, Kiev. They are accompanied by weapons, military vehicles, tanks and helicopters. 

In addition, new images released by the space technology company Maxar show Russian troops and attack helicopters within 20 miles of the Ukrainian border in southern Belarus.

Headline_English: Fears of a disaster in the supply of edible oil
Content_Enlish:
Wholesale traders are fearing a major disaster in the supply system of edible oil in the market before Ramadan. Unable to increase prices according to demand, mill owners have drastically reduced supply. Oil sales have also stopped in many shops in neighborhoods. 

Moulvibazar in Old Dhaka is the supply center of daily necessities in the capital. Entrepreneurs here say that they have never seen such a crisis in their 48-year business history. In addition to abnormal prices, there is also a widespread supply crisis. They complain that oil is not available even at the price set by the government. 

Employees complain that soybean oil is not available at the price set by the government. They have had to pay fines in government agencies' raids even after buying at a high price and selling at a small profit. Therefore, the owner has given notices not to sell oil in shops. 

Retailers are also in both crises. Owners have stopped selling soybean oil in many shops in the Gabtola area of ​​​​Moghbazar. And those who are selling it claim that the demand for oil has decreased significantly due to the price increase. 

The Ministry of Commerce has rejected the demand for another round of increase in the price of soybean oil. Mill owners say that selling at a loss is not a business-friendly decision. However, they do not see the possibility of a major crisis. 

In addition to strengthening market surveillance to control the situation, consumers have demanded an increase in oil sales through TCB. 

Earlier, traders had proposed to the ministry to increase the price of soybean oil again. Traders claim that the price of oil has increased in the international market, so it should be increased in the domestic market as well. 

In view of this, Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi said that even if traders propose to increase the price of soybean oil, the government will not respond. 

He also said that the price of edible oil will not be increased before Ramadan. During the last round of price increase, traders were told that the price would not increase again before Ramadan. Despite this, traders have proposed to increase the price. The minister said that traders will have to tolerate the increase in price. 

The last time the price of bottled soybean oil was increased by 8 taka per liter on February 6, bringing the price of bottled soybean oil to 168 taka per liter. Less than 20 days later, oil traders tried to increase the price again. They also announced that the price hike would be effective from March 1. 

However, the permission of the Ministry of Commerce would be required to increase the price. And after this statement by the Minister of Commerce, it was effectively rejected.

Headline_English: Low pressure signal number 1 at sea
Content_Enlish:
The Meteorological Department has asked the country's seaports to display distant warning signal number 1 as the low pressure formed in the Bay of Bengal and the adjacent South Andaman Sea has intensified into a depression. 

Regarding the depression formed in the Indian Ocean, the Indian Meteorological Office says that this cyclonic circulation may further intensify into a deep depression and may take the form of a cyclone on Monday. If it takes the form of a cyclone, then it will be named Ashini. This is the name given by Sri Lanka. 

If the Indian Meteorological Office's forecast is correct, the storm may move towards the Myanmar coast via the Andaman Islands. In that case, Bangladeshi meteorologist Omar Farooq does not see the possibility of it having a major impact on Bangladesh. 

At 6 am on Sunday, the depression was located 1,380 km south of Chittagong Seaport, 1,295 km south of Cox's Bazar Seaport, 1,440 km south-southeast of Mongla Seaport and 1,375 km south-southeast of Payra Seaport. 

Later, it may intensify further and move north-northeast, the special weather bulletin said. 

Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, Mongla and Payra seaports have been asked to display distant warning signal number 1. Along with this, fishing boats and trawlers in the north Bay of Bengal have been advised to navigate carefully near the coast and not to venture into the deep sea. 

Meanwhile, the heat wave that became unbearable at the beginning of Chaitra after winter may continue for another two to three days, according to the weather forecast. Today, the maximum temperature in Rajshahi is 38.4 degrees.

Headline_English: Bank deposits have decreased by 51 percent
Content_Enlish:
Although the economy has recovered from the coronavirus outbreak, the amount of deposits in the banking sector is decreasing. In the first seven months of the fiscal year, the growth of deposits has decreased by Tk 54,000 crore, or more than 51 percent. The central bank claims that deposits have decreased due to increased investment and consumption spending. 

However, analysts say that deposits are decreasing due to the failure to return stimulus money on time, remittances and lower interest rates. 

The country's economy has started to overcome the burden of the coronavirus pandemic. This is increasing the demand for loans in the private sector. However, the problem has become a crisis of funds in banks. 

According to Bangladesh Bank, several banks were provided with liquidity support and special repo support worth Tk 6.5 billion in five working days from February 23 to March 2. 

According to the calculation, before the coronavirus, the annual growth of deposits in February 2020 was 12.82 percent. That growth increased and reached a maximum of 14.5 percent by May 2021. Since then, deposit growth has been declining. Import growth has fallen by 51.5 percent in the first seven months of the current fiscal year through January. 

The central bank claims that people are now investing their savings. Again, the demand for cash has increased due to rising consumer spending due to rising commodity prices. 

Regarding the decline in bank deposits, experts say that regular loans as well as stimulus money have not been returned on time under the pretext of Corona. In addition, deposit growth has slowed down significantly due to the fall in remittances and interest rates. Meanwhile, private sector lending, which has been stagnant for a long time, has regained momentum. Annual loan growth through January was more than 11 percent. Analysts emphasize increasing the investment capacity of banks to continue this trend.

Headline_English: 90% of Ukrainians at risk of extreme poverty
Content_Enlish:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has warned that 90 percent of Ukraine's population will be pushed into extreme poverty if the ongoing Russian invasion continues. 
The agency said on Wednesday that Ukraine will lose two decades of economic capacity if the ongoing war drags on for another year. 

In that case, nine out of ten people in the country will face extreme economic crisis. The UNDP is currently working with the Kiev government to resolve the financial crisis. In addition to initially ensuring financial assistance to internally displaced people, emphasis is being placed on ensuring that civilians do not leave the country to meet their basic needs. 

Since the Russian invasion began on February 24, Ukraine has destroyed $100 billion worth of infrastructure. 50 percent of the country's businesses have completely closed. The World Bank recently approved $200 million in financial assistance to Ukraine. 

Meanwhile, the country's government has taken an innovative initiative to accommodate those who are willing to leave the country due to the Russian military operation in Ukraine. If a British citizen shelters people from Ukraine, they will receive 350 pounds a month. This initiative by the Homes for Ukraine project has received a huge response. About 44,000 Britons applied in the first five hours of the registration opening. About 2.8 million people have left the country since the Russian military operation in Ukraine began on February 24. 

As neighboring countries including Poland and Romania opened their borders, refugees are taking shelter there with minimal resources. However, the UK has been strict about Ukrainians from the beginning. British Border Agency officials have made it clear that entry is prohibited without a visa. Boris Johnson's government has also faced criticism for this. 

Now the UK government has launched a new project to shelter Ukrainians. Under this, British citizens can sponsor Ukrainian individuals or families for at least 6 months of visas. The government will provide 350 pounds a month if they arrange for refugees to live in their own homes. And for this, Ukrainians are not obliged to provide food or any other expenses. 

Registration for those interested in joining the project has begun online. About 44,000 Britons registered in the first 5 hours of the online site being open. Refugees coming to the UK under the project will also receive other government benefits, including national health care. 

Local authorities in various areas of the UK will also receive an allocation of 10,500 pounds per person for refugees. Outside of this project, Ukrainians will also be given shelter in the UK, said the country's Housing Minister Michael Gove.

Headline_English: Iraq interested in importing seasonal vegetables including mangoes from Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
Iraq is interested in importing various seasonal vegetables including mangoes and potatoes from Bangladesh, said Agriculture Minister Dr. Md. Abdur Razzak. In a meeting with the Agriculture Minister at the Secretariat on Wednesday afternoon, Iraqi Ambassador to Dhaka Abdul Salam Saddam Mohisen expressed this interest. 

At the time, the Agriculture Minister said that Iraq is one of the friendly countries of Bangladesh. During the Liberation War, they were one of the most recognized countries of Bangladesh. Although the economic situation was bad due to the war, it is now getting better, he said. 

He also said that an agreement will be signed between the two countries very soon to start the process of exporting fruits and vegetables. Almost half of the vegetables exported from Bangladesh to the world are destined for Middle Eastern countries. 

Earlier, various types of vegetables were exported from Bangladesh. Of these, the most exported are gourd, pumpkin, potol, brinjal, dhandas, potatoes, papaya, chichinga, kankrol, green chili, barbati, beans, tomatoes and various types of vegetables. 

There are many expatriate Bangladeshis all over the world. Of these, about 50 percent are in the Middle Eastern countries. These vegetables will be imported from this country mainly targeting them. 

Meanwhile, in another meeting, the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) expressed its interest in supporting the establishment of an accredited agricultural lab under the Ministry of Agriculture in Purbachal. They said that Bangladesh will receive 240 crore taka until 2025.

Headline_English: Zelenskyy again calls for no-fly zone
Content_Enlish:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has once again called on the West to enforce a no-fly zone over Ukraine. In a virtual speech to the US Congress on Wednesday, he compared Russia's activities to the terrorist attacks on Pearl Harbor and 9/11. During this time, he asked the United States not only for sanctions, but also for more effective and tough measures to stop the Russian aggression in Ukraine. 

Zelensky has been asking the West for a no-fly zone since the start of the Russian aggression in Ukraine. In his speech to the US Congress, he also said that the call to close the airspace over Ukraine in the face of Russian airstrikes is asking too much. 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that NATO members have so far refused to impose a no-fly zone over Ukraine. This is escalating the conflict. If Ukraine's airspace cannot be closed, we will need defense systems and fighter jets to prevent airstrikes. 

The Russian invasion of Ukraine has been going on for three weeks. At the beginning, the United States announced $350 million in weapons and humanitarian aid. In the meantime, Washington has also imposed several sanctions against Russia. However, it is not enough to stop Moscow, believes Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. 

In a virtual speech to the US Congress, he compared Russian activities to the terrorist attacks on Pearl Harbor and 9/11. He wants effective assistance. 

Volodymyr Zelensky also said that life has no meaning if you cannot prevent death. I would like to say to President Biden that you are the leader of a great country. But that is not enough. You have to be a world leader. And being a world leader means taking a stand for peace. 

Zelensky said that he and his country, Ukraine, are grateful to the United States. He called on the United States to do more, including sanctions against Russia. 

He said that all American companies must leave the Russian market, because it is flooded with our blood. 

Earlier, in a video message, the Ukrainian president called the Russian invasion of Ukraine an act of terrorism and demanded that it be tried by an international tribunal.

Headline_English: Bangladesh beat Pakistan to win first World Cup
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh won the Women's ODI World Cup by defeating Pakistan by 9 runs. Batting at a target of 235 runs set by Bangladesh, Pakistan's innings ended at 225 runs. 

Pakistan got off to a flying start with a 91-run partnership between openers Nahida Khan and Sidra Amin. However, Bangladesh turned things around with the bowling of Rumana and Fahima. Pakistan's 9 wickets fell quickly. 

Pakistan opener Sidra Amin scored a century but could not lead the team to victory. Fahima took 3 wickets and Rumana took 2 wickets for Bangladesh. 

Earlier, Bangladesh got off to a good start after losing the toss and opted to bat. Shamima and Supta's opening partnership scored 37 runs. Then captain Jyoti made a brilliant 96-run partnership with Farzana. 

Farzana scored her second consecutive fifty in the tournament. Bangladesh finally scored 234 runs for the loss of 7 wickets. This is the highest total for the Tigresses in ODI cricket against Pakistan.
Short Scores: 

Bangladesh: 234/7 in 50 overs (Shamima 17, Sharmin 44, Farzana 71, Nigar 46, Rumana 16, Ritu 11, Fahima 0, Salma 11*, Nahida 2*; Fatima Sana 10-0-54-1, Diana 5-1-32-0, Nida 10-0-45-1, Nashra 10-0-41-3, Ghulam Fatima 7-0-30-0, Omaima 8-1-31-1). 

Pakistan: 225/9 in 50 overs (Nahida 43, Sidra Amin 104, Bismah 31, Omaima 10, Alia 0, Fatima Sana 0, Sidra Nawaz 1, Diana 12, Nashra 9*, Ghulam Fatima 5*; Jahanara 4-0-20-1, Trishna 4-0-19-0, Salma 9-0-29-1, Nahida 9-0-48-0, Rumana 7-0-29-2, Ritu Moni 9-0-42-0, Fahima 8-0-38-3). 

Result: Bangladesh won by 9 runs. Fahima Khatun was named Player of the Match.

Headline_English: The quality of Napa syrup is correct, the drug administration said after testing.
Content_Enlish:
The Drug Administration Department has tested several samples of Napa syrup and found the quality to be correct. However, the authorities believe that the cause of the death of the two children will be known after the viscera report and investigation. 
Director General of the Department, Major General Mohammad Yusuf, said this at a press conference in the capital's Mohakhali on Monday afternoon. 

He said that 8 samples have been collected from the accused shop and tested. Nothing harmful was found in them. In addition, samples have been brought from 3 factories manufacturing paracetamol and tested. Nothing harmful was found in them either. Therefore, the Director General of the Drug Administration does not see anything to panic about Napa syrup. 

He also said that a total of 82,000 bottles of the medicine were manufactured and marketed in the accused batch. In addition, 3,400 bottles of the medicine from that batch were sold in Brahmanbaria alone. However, no complaints have been received from anywhere. 
On March 10, two children died after consuming the medicine in Durgapur, Ashuganj upazila of Brahmanbaria. The families allege that they consumed Napa syrup. 
Taking cognizance of the complaint, the Drug Administration Department took action. Samples of Napa syrup were collected from the shop. Batch number 32113121 was identified... There were 82,000 bottles in this batch. Apart from this batch, the Drug Administration tested samples from two more batches in the lab. Nothing harmful was found in any of them. 
It is learnt that the accused pharmacy is not licensed. The Drug Administration says that the police have seized the bottle of medicine from which two children died. Tests are underway to find out whether there was anything harmful in it. The cause of the child's death will be known once the viscera report is received.
