Headline_English: There is no Chinese missile maintenance facility in Bangladesh, nor will there be in the future.
Content_Enlish:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shahriar Alam clarified that there is no Chinese missile maintenance facility in Bangladesh. He said, there has never been and there is no opportunity to set up such a factory in the future. 

The State Minister also said that a letter will be sent to Japan's Nikkei media to ask on what information this news was published. 

He said these things while talking to reporters at his office on Monday afternoon. 

Japanese media outlet Nikkei Asia recently published a news item stating that China is building a missile maintenance facility in Bangladesh. 

Similar news was also reported by some Indian media outlets. At a function on Sunday, the Chinese ambassador to Dhaka said that he was also not aware of this. 

The State Minister for Foreign Affairs commented that some media outlets at home and abroad have published news about this, which is completely untrue. India's concern about this is also not correct. 

The State Minister also said that the country is providing assistance in maintaining the military weapons purchased from China in 2011. However, there is no need to build a separate facility for this. 

At that time, regarding the Saudi Foreign Minister's visit to Dhaka, the State Minister said that his visit will have an impact on the labor market.

Headline_English: The country will not run on the prescription of foreign organizations
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that the government is working not on the advice of any international organization, but according to the welfare of the people of the country. 

She said this while virtually joining the program organized on the occasion of declaring 'Joy Bangla' as the national slogan on Monday evening. 

The Prime Minister said that by declaring 'Joy Bangla', which is the root of all the achievements of the country, her government wanted to convey this message to the whole world that Bengalis will not bow their heads but will continue with their heads held high. 

The Prime Minister said, 'This Joy Bangla slogan has become everyone's today and through this slogan we want to reach the people of the world - we are a victorious nation, we have achieved victory, we do not walk with our heads bowed, we will not walk with our heads bowed, Bengalis will walk with their heads held high in the world court. 

Sheikh Hasina mentioned one of her strengths, her only younger sister Sheikh Rehana, who survived the tragic events of '75, and both of us are happier today. Because this slogan of Joy Bangla has helped the people of this country to take the country forward on the path of victory by sacrificing their lives. The slogan with which the people of this country have written in blood - I want to bring victory. Bangladesh will be victorious. Today, that Joy Bangla is the slogan of all of us, the people of this country, the victorious nation, the Bengali nation, our heads held high. 

He expressed his gratitude to everyone for holding this slogan and said that today has proven that no sacrifice goes in vain. Salman Fazlur Rahman, Advisor to the Prime Minister on Private Industry and Investment, and BAB Chairman Md. Nazrul Islam Majumdar spoke at the event. 

The Prime Minister unveiled the cover of a book titled 'Muktidata Sheikh Mujib' at the event. 

Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman ended his historic speech delivered at the Race Course Ground (present Suhrawardy Udyan) on March 7, 1971, by uttering 'Joy Bangla'. Since then, it has become the slogan of the lives of millions of freedom fighters and freedom-seekers. 'Joy Bangla' became the inspiration for unarmed Bengalis to take up arms and shed fresh blood to snatch victory against the Pakistani army. 

Bangabandhu's daughter and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that Bangabandhu took the slogan 'Joy Bangla' from the poetry of Kazi Nazrul Islam. 

Following a writ petition, the High Court ruled on March 10, 2020 to adopt the slogan 'Joy Bangla' as the national slogan of Bangladesh. The decision to make 'Joy Bangla' the national slogan was taken in a cabinet meeting on February 20, 2022, and on March 2, 2022, the Cabinet Division issued a notification declaring 'Joy Bangla' the national slogan. The Prime Minister said that the slogan 'Joy Bangla' was once banned in Bangladesh, which is very sad. 

However, yes, we, the Awami League, and those who have upheld the ideals of Bangabandhu, who believe in the spirit of the independence and liberation war of this country, and the freedom fighters, have upheld it. There have been obstacles, many times we have had to hear a lot of criticism. But even then, we were able to uphold this truth, and today it has received national recognition. 

She said, the slogan Joy Bangla is the slogan of our liberation struggle. The slogan Joy Bangla is the slogan of the liberation war. The slogan Joy Bangla is the slogan of self-sacrifice. The slogan Joy Bangla is the slogan of our achievements. Through the slogan through which we achieved victory. 

The Prime Minister said, Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman dedicated his entire life to the people of Bangladesh. The people who were suffering from hunger and poverty. 

He said that just before the Father of the Nation gave the 6-point demand, he ordered the Chhatra League to take this Jaya Bangla slogan to the field. Its underlying meaning was one thing - to awaken the spirit of independence among the people through struggle and through this slogan, we achieved victory in our independence struggle and liberation war. Every step of which was taken by the Father of the Nation was very well planned.

Headline_English: What you can include in your child's diet to increase their height
Content_Enlish:
All parents worry a lot if their child's height does not grow properly. Genetic factors are not the only reason for not growing tall. Even if there is a deficiency in nutrition, the child's height does not want to grow properly. 

You have to keep an eye on your child's diet. Include protein, carbohydrates, fats and vitamins in the right proportion in your child's daily diet. Prevent your child from eating 'junk food'. 

Nuts, which are rich in vitamins and minerals, are helpful in increasing height. They contain healthy fats and fiber, which also strengthen children's bones. 

Milk contains a lot of calcium, which plays an important role in strengthening bones. Milk is also a good source of protein. Protein also helps in cell growth. Therefore, milk is helpful in increasing the height of children. Apart from milk, paneer, curd, cheese can also be fed. 

What you can include in your diet to increase height 

Peanuts 

Peanuts contain a lot of vitamins, minerals, fiber, lutein and protein, which help in the normal growth of the body and help in increasing height. From fried rice to mung beans, add peas to your cooking whenever you get the opportunity. 

Turnips 

Turnips will help in increasing your child's height. Turnips contain vitamins, minerals, fiber, protein and fat. These ingredients are helpful in increasing height. 

Cabbage 

This vegetable contains a lot of vitamins, minerals, iron, protein and fiber. Which not only increases height but also prevents cancer. Cabbage can be used in all types of cooking from Chinese to Bengali. 

Broccoli 

Broccoli contains vitamin C, fiber, iron, antioxidants which help in increasing height. So if you want to increase height, you should include broccoli in your diet. You can add this vegetable to your child's tiffin as chow mein or in sandwiches or soup.

Soybeans 

Soybeans contain a lot of protein, which helps in the formation of body cells and bones. So, be sure to include soybeans in your children's diet. 

Chicken and eggs 

Eating chicken, which is rich in protein and various nutrients, strengthens children's bones and muscles. Which helps in increasing their height significantly. Eating eggs also increases children's height. The yolk of an egg contains healthy fats, which are very beneficial for the physical and mental development of children. 

Green vegetables 

Vegetables like fenugreek, spinach, and cabbage are rich in vitamin C, vitamin K, calcium, iron, and magnesium. All these ingredients help in increasing children's height. 

Oats 

Oats contain vitamins B, E, potassium, and zinc. It is good for children's brain development. It contains a lot of fiber, which keeps children's digestive system healthy. In addition, the protein present in it helps in increasing children's height. 

Almonds 

Rich in vitamins and minerals, almonds help in increasing height. They contain healthy fats, fiber, manganese, magnesium and vitamin E, which also strengthens children's bones.

Headline_English: Government to provide policy and infrastructure support for investment in Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that she is ready to ensure policy and infrastructure support so that investors can choose Bangladesh as the best destination in the world. She made this call at a ceremony held on Thursday to mark the signing of a memorandum of understanding to establish a joint business council between the United Arab Emirates and Bangladesh. 

Bangladesh is one of the few countries in the world that has maintained the pace of economic growth despite the pandemic. Bangladesh has now emerged as a development wonder in the world. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina made these remarks while joining the event at the Dubai Exhibition Center, jointly organized by businessmen from Bangladesh and the United Arab Emirates, via video conference from Abu Dhabi. 

Highlighting the advantages of geographical location, she said that Bangladesh's economic zones and hi-tech parks in particular are ready for new initiatives. 

The Prime Minister also mentioned that Bangladesh's huge domestic market and the markets surrounding this region are still untapped. 

Later, the FBCCI and the UAE Chambers and Commerce signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a joint business council between the two countries. 

It was signed by FBCCI President Jasim Uddin and UAE Chamber of Commerce and Industry Chairman Abdullah Mohammed Al Mazrouei. 

Earlier, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina emphasized on agricultural research and education and transfer and exchange of high technology to ensure food security in the Asia-Pacific region. She said. “Cooperation in agricultural research and education should be increased among the countries of the region to ensure food security.” 

The Prime Minister made this recommendation in the first of three recommendations he presented at the opening ceremony of the 36th Regional Conference of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) for Asia-Pacific. 

He said in his second point that technologies such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and robotics in the agricultural sector should be strengthened among the FAW member states of the region through the transfer and exchange of high technology. 

In his final point, he added: ‘Since modern agriculture requires huge investments, a special fund can be formed to finance and support the agricultural sector.’

Headline_English: 18,000 volunteers join Kiev's army
Content_Enlish:
Residents of the Ukrainian capital Kiev are determined to defend their city. As Russian forces push deeper into Kiev, the resolve of Ukrainian citizens seems to be growing stronger. The blue-and-yellow national flag is visible everywhere. In the capital Kiev alone, 18,000 volunteers have joined the army in the fight to defend their city. 

Just two weeks ago, residents of the Ukrainian capital Kiev were living a normal life. Street shops were bustling, schools were bustling with students. People were busy at their desks. 

Everything changed with the Russian invasion. The capital's parks have become military vehicle parking lots. Shopping areas lined with boutiques, cafes and fancy restaurants have been transformed into sandbags and concrete blocks. 

Literally fighting for their lives, Kiev's civilians have become volunteer soldiers. In a short time, they are building a defense ring with military skill and protecting their beloved city. So many applications have been received to join as volunteer soldiers that the Territorial Defense Force has been forced to send many back. 

A local said, I have only one son. He is my everything. You have to understand that if you have your own child, protecting him is the main task. Every parent must protect their children. But we are here together, risking our lives because this is our decision. We had no other way to protect the Motherland, we must protect our Motherland first. 

But those who could not join the army are also helping in other ways. Some are making cocktails, some are making various equipment for the barricades. In addition, no citizen refrains from distributing food, hot drinks and cigarettes to the soldiers. In this joint effort, they are raising money for the military to distract the Russian forces from different parts of the city. They have built barricades on the streets. 

In any war, the defense of the city center is the strongest. But experienced soldiers are stationed at checkpoints outside Kiev. Volunteer soldiers are stationed in the city center with tanks and heavy weapons. 

Meanwhile, US defense officials have said that Russian troops have reached within 3 miles of the country's capital Kiev despite strong Ukrainian resistance. On the other hand, Ukrainian President Zelensky has once again called for direct talks with the Russian president. His aide said that Ukraine is ready to hold talks at any time. 

Earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky once again called for a no-fly zone with NATO after the Russian attack on a children's hospital in Mariupol. 

Meanwhile, the BBC reported information about Russian attacks on several important cities in Ukraine. Among them is the city of Lutsk, which borders Poland. 

The BBC reported, citing a close aide to Zelensky, that heavy explosions were reported in at least three cities. In this regard, the Red Cross said that the supply of food and water in the besieged city of Mariupol has decreased. 

Ukraine's Interior Ministry said more than 400,000 civilians have been evacuated so far. Facebook and Twitter have temporarily changed their rules to allow people to protest against the Russian invasion.

Headline_English: College student dies after taking bath in Cox's Bazar
Content_Enlish:
A college student died after going into the sea in Cox's Bazar. He died while bathing at Kalatali Point on the beach in the morning. His body was found by lifeguards at 11 am on Friday. 

Shahed Hossain, who died while bathing in the sea, is a first-year humanities student at Bappi Ramu Government Degree College. He is the son of Shamshul Alam, a resident of Teschipul village in Ramu upazila. 

Shahed Hossain's friend Mohammad Musa, who went missing while bathing at the same place, has been rescued in a critical condition. Mohammad Musa, who was rescued in an injured condition, is being treated in the emergency department at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital. 

Saifullah Sifat, manager of the private Sea-Safety Lifeguard, which is engaged in the rescue of tourists, said that Shahed Hossain and six friends went into the sea north of Kalatali Beach for bathing at around 9:15 am. The tide had started to ebb at that time, but the sea was calm. 

The six friends were floating towards the deep sea with a tire tube. Suddenly, a large wave knocked six people out of the tire tube. Lifeguards conducted a rescue operation in the sea and rescued five people, but Shahed Hossain was missing. His body was found an hour later at around 11 am.

Headline_English: Dhaka-Toronto direct flight to be launched
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Biman's Dhaka-Toronto direct flight will be launched on March 26, said State Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism Mahbub Ali. He made this announcement at the award distribution ceremony of the Biman Half Marathon competition at Hatirjheel in the capital this morning. 

The State Minister said that Biman Bangladesh Airlines has already made great progress in launching the Dhaka-Toronto flight. It is hoped that the flight will be launched within the specified time. He also said that work is being done to launch Biman flights to other destinations. 

1,862 domestic and foreign competitors participated in the half marathon. The winners were awarded tickets for Dhaka-London, Dhaka-Bangkok and Dhaka-Kathmandu flights. 

Earlier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines started the process of operating flights from Dhaka to New York, USA, in 2020 after a long 14-year closure. This initiative to launch the flight has been postponed several times due to Corona. 

Finally, the stalled process has started again. As part of that process, a three-member US delegation came to Dhaka to inspect the security arrangements at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka. 

Although large-scale Boeings and fourth-generation aircraft with the latest technology have been added to Bangladesh Airlines' fleet in the last ten years, complaints about the company's service quality have not decreased. Biman's new routes have not increased. 

Meanwhile, the chaos of fares and ticket shortages on flights to the Middle East have broken all previous records in January-February. Despite various steps being taken, expatriate passengers have not yet benefited.

Headline_English: Mobile operators prepare to launch 5G
Content_Enlish:
In addition to ensuring 4G networks in different parts of the country, various preparations are underway among private mobile operator companies to join the 5G network. However, they are emphasizing on infrastructure development and creating guidelines before the spectrum auction. At the same time, they say that the quality of service will also increase in the spectrum auction at a low price. The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications announced that at least 100 MHz of spectrum will be allocated to operator companies. 

A few months ago, the country entered the 5G era with Teletalk. In view of the 100 MHz application, the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) allocated 60 MHz of spectrum in favor of Teletalk. 

Meanwhile, the spectrum auction is scheduled for March 31 for the three operators Robi, Grameenphone and Banglalink. However, the operators announced various preparations to enter the 5G network before the auction. 

Robi's Chief Corporate and Regulatory Officer Shahedul Alam said that 100 MHz of spectrum is needed to ensure quality 5G services in the country. 

He also mentioned that special consideration is needed in determining the price of spectrum to obtain the necessary spectrum. 

At the same time, operators believe that infrastructure development and guidelines need to be created before the spectrum auction. 

In this context, BTRC said that the initial price of spectrum will be determined a week before the auction. The institutions themselves increase the price of spectrum in the auction. 

Stating that the price of spectrum is not skyrocketing, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Mustafa Jabbar said that at least 100 MHz spectrum will be allocated to institutions. At the same time, there will be guidelines. 

To ensure 5G services, the government has undertaken a project to develop optical fiber to provide 300 Gbps internet speed at the district level and 100 Gbps at the upazila level. This project will cost 1,590 million taka. The period is until 2025.

Headline_English: Pakistan should apologize for the 1971 genocide
Content_Enlish:
Foreign Minister AK Abdul Momen has said that Pakistan should apologize for the torture and genocide in 1971 and punish the guilty. He said this at a program organized at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital on Saturday morning to mark Independence Day. 

The Foreign Minister also said that Pakistan should be ashamed for not apologizing yet. 

Later, regarding the Ukraine issue, he said that Bangladesh is in favor of peace. Bangladesh wants an end to the war and the residents of Ukraine to receive humanitarian assistance. That is why the UN has voted in favor of the resolution of the humanitarian crisis in Ukraine on the issue of human rights. 

However, the Foreign Minister said that there is no reason for Russia to be angry about voting in favor of Ukraine. 

He said that even if there is some pressure as a result of voting, it is possible to handle it.

Headline_English: Bangladesh ahead of India and Pakistan in 51 years of independence
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh is on the cusp of prosperity after 50 years of independence. In 51 years, this delta, which has been dubbed the bottomless basket, has surpassed India and Pakistan in economic and social sectors such as per capita income, life expectancy, health and education. Women are being empowered, dependence on foreign aid has decreased. However, challenges remain in areas such as inequality and good governance. 

Bangladesh was born through a bloody struggle to break the shackles of Pakistan. The then US Secretary of State Henry Kissinger called the war-torn country a bottomless basket. Bangladesh is today a role model of development, disregarding his boastful statement. In the last 15 years of continuous progress, the income of a Bangladeshi is higher than that of a Pakistani or an Indian. 

Bangladesh surpassed India in per capita GDP for the first time in 2020. Bangladesh's per capita income is $2,591, India's $1,947 and Pakistan's $1,666. 

It surpassed Pakistan in per capita income in the 2017-18 fiscal year. According to BBS, Bangladesh's per capita income increased by $2,591 in the last fiscal year. While according to IMF-World Bank and Reuters, India's per capita income is $1,947 and Pakistan's is $1,666. 

Bangladesh is also ahead in average life expectancy. Bangladesh's average life expectancy is 72.6 years, India's is 67.7 years and Pakistan's is 67.3 years. 

The average life expectancy is benefiting from various socio-economic sectors including health and education. According to UNDP's 2020 Human Development Report, the average life expectancy of the country's people is now above 72 years. And in India and Pakistan, it is below 68 years. 

The success in social indicators is also higher than that of the two neighboring countries. 36 percent of the labor force in Bangladesh is women. On the other hand, it is 20.5 percent in India and 22 percent in Pakistan. 

Bangladesh is also in a better position than India and Pakistan in reducing neonatal and infant mortality rates. The infant mortality rate in India is 4, in Pakistan 7, but in the country it is 3 percent. 

Bangladeshi girls are also in education. About 40 percent of women over the age of 25 have completed secondary school. On the other hand, the rate is 27 percent in India and Pakistan. 

One of the places for women's empowerment is the National Parliament. In Bangladesh, about 21 percent of the members of parliament are women. In India and Pakistan, it is 13 and 20 percent. 

In 1971, war-torn Bangladesh was one of the poorest countries in South Asia. After that, the per capita income increased from 94 to 278 dollars in just 3 and a half years due to various initiatives taken by Bangabandhu. GDP growth was 9 percent. 

Although the next three decades did not show much momentum in GDP growth and per capita income, a new level has been achieved in the continuous development of the last one century. By increasing production capacity, Bangladesh is now self-sufficient in food. On March 15, the United Nations officially announced that it has achieved the qualification for transition to a developing country. 

According to the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), Bangladesh's per capita income has increased by 2,591 dollars in the 51 years of independence. And the country's gross national product has increased by 416 billion dollars. 

Besides, even after the Corona pandemic, the country's GDP growth is 6.94 percent. The country of the bottomless basket is now showing the courage to lead the digital world. 

Economists say that Bangladesh has made great progress in the socio-economic sector in the fifty-one years of independence. However, if there was no corruption, this achievement would have been many times greater. Therefore, the challenge now is to eliminate corruption and eliminate the disparity between the rich and the poor. 

In international turmoil like the Corona pandemic and the Ukraine-Russia war, when even developed countries are struggling to cope with the situation, Bangladesh has maintained economic progress by overcoming various obstacles. The government has set a target of 7.2 percent GDP growth in the budget for the 2021-22 fiscal year.

Headline_English: Bangladesh votes in favor of Ukraine at the UN
Content_Enlish:
A resolution has been passed at the United Nations calling for urgent action to resolve the humanitarian crisis in Ukraine. 140 member states, including Bangladesh, voted in favor of the resolution at an emergency session of the United Nations on Thursday. 

After the resolution was passed, US Ambassador Linda Thomas-Greenfield called it a stunning success. 

The vote was held at the UN headquarters in New York during an emergency session of the Council. 

Russia, Belarus, North Korea, Eritrea and Syria voted against this vote. In addition, 32 countries, including China, Pakistan and India, abstained. 

However, Russia is not obligated to comply with this resolution. 

Earlier, on March 2, the General Assembly passed a resolution to stop the attack on Ukraine. At that time, 141 countries voted in favor of the resolution. Bangladesh abstained from voting at that time. 

This time, the resolution emphasizes humanitarian assistance activities. It calls for an immediate end to violence, protection of civilians and respect for international humanitarian law. The previous resolution blamed Russia.

Headline_English: Suffering continues on the fifth day of the ban on online train ticket sales
Content_Enlish:
Passengers are suffering even on the fifth day of the suspension of online and computer-printed train ticket sales. There was a huge crowd of ticket seekers in Dhaka's Kamalapur since morning. Passengers complain that they could not get tickets even after standing in line for hours. 

The station manager said that computer-printed tickets will be given at the counter from the evening. And the situation will return to normal when online sales start from 8 am tomorrow. 

Since online ticket sales are suspended, passengers are now having to physically go to the counter to buy train tickets. This has increased the suffering of passengers. Many people are standing in line for hours in front of the counter at the station but are not getting tickets. Passengers have been suffering since online ticket sales have been suspended since March 20. 

On the spot, a huge crowd was seen in front of the counter for tickets at the capital's Kamalapur railway station. Passengers are having to return disappointed after not getting tickets even after waiting for a long time. Many are forced to buy tickets without a seat on the train. And many are running to the bus terminal without getting train tickets. 

In such a situation, the railway authorities have announced in a public notice that online ticket sales will resume from 8 am on Saturday. Train tickets will have to be purchased by logging into the e-ticket.railway.gov.bd portal. 

On March 14, Railway Minister Md. Nurul Islam Sujan announced the decision to stop online train ticket sales from March 21 to 25 at a press conference. He said that the organization responsible for online train ticket sales, 'Sahaj', has taken five days to create an internal setup. The organization will sell tickets online from March 26. 

Computer Network System-CNS has been selling train tickets online since 2007. After the contract with the organization ended, 'Sahaj Limited' was given the responsibility of selling tickets in a new tender. Online ticket sales were closed from March 21 to fix their server.

Headline_English: Turning off the lights, remembering the terrible night
Content_Enlish:
The entire country turned off its lights to commemorate the horrific massacre of March 25, 1971. On Friday (March 25), Bangladesh observed a 'blackout' program by turning off its lights from 9 pm to 9:01 pm. In memory of those killed in the 1971 genocide, darkness fell for one minute across the country at 9 pm. 

Various organizations held this program to highlight the horror of that dark night to the new generation by lighting candles before and after the symbolic blackout. On this day in 1971, the Pakistani occupying forces carried out the most barbaric massacre in history on unarmed Bengalis. Although the day is observed as National Genocide Day, it has not received international recognition even after 51 years of independence. 

After receiving the direction of independence in Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's speech on March 7, 1971, the seeds of rebellion began to sprout among the freedom-loving people. On the other hand, the Pakistani army prepared for a terrible massacre.

On the night of March 25, the Pakistani army attacked the unarmed people of this country in order to permanently silence the Bengali liberation movement. In that operation called Operation Searchlight, genocide began in various areas including Dhaka University, Rajarbagh Police Lines, Ramna Kali Mandir. At least 7,000 Bengalis were killed that night in Dhaka alone. 

One of the eyewitnesses of that night was Arun Chandra Roy. He lived in Jagannath Hall. When he remembers that massacre by the Pakistani army, he still shudders. 

Madhusudan Dey ran the Madhur Canteen of Dhaka University. His son Arun Kumar Dey said that on that night, starting from vandalizing the canteen, four members of his family, including his parents, were brutally killed. 

The first resistance against the Pakistani invaders was formed at Rajarbagh Police Lines. Despite fighting bravely, more than a hundred policemen were martyred that night. 

However, even after 51 years of independence, the brutal genocide has not received international recognition. On March 11, 2017, the government declared March 25 as National Genocide Day by passing a resolution in Parliament.

Headline_English: Two people including war criminal Khaleq Mondal sentenced to death
Content_Enlish:
The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced former MP Abdul Khalek Mondal, the Ameer of Satkhira District Jamaat, and Khan Rokonuzzaman to death in a 1971 crimes against humanity case. 

The three-judge tribunal, including Justice Shahinur Islam, delivered the verdict on Thursday morning. 

Earlier, the tribunal had set today as the date for the verdict to be announced on Monday. A case was filed against Abdul Khalek and nine others in Satkhira in 2009 on charges of crimes against humanity. Six charges were brought against the accused, including murder, rape, kidnapping, and torture. In 2018, the tribunal framed charges against them and ordered the trial to begin. There were a total of four accused in the case. Two of the accused in the case, Abdullah Hal Baki and Zahirul Islam Tekka Khan, died during the trial. 

Of the two accused, Abdul Khalek Mondal was present in the court during the verdict. However, Rokonuzzaman has been absconding since the beginning of the case. In 1971, Khalek Mondal was the organizer of the Rajkar Bahini in Satkhira, and Roknuzzaman was a member of that force. 

The war crimes they committed in various areas of Satkhira with the help of the Pakistani army while standing against the independence of Bangladesh have come to light in the trial of this case. 

The prosecution had accused the two accused of involvement in a total of six incidents of crimes against humanity. The tribunal said in its verdict that all of them had been proven beyond doubt. 

A case was filed on July 2, 2009 against nine people, including former Jamaat MP Abdul Khalek Mondal, in the Satkhira Sadar constituency, on charges of slaughtering and bayoneting five people during the Liberation War. 

In the early hours of June 16, 2015, police arrested Jamaat leader Khalek Mondal during a meeting at the Khalilnagar Mahila Madrasa in Satkhira Sadar Upazila.

Headline_English: Italy, Portugal to play separate matches in World Cup qualifiers
Content_Enlish:
Italy and Portugal are playing separate matches tonight in a mission to keep their dreams alive in the World Cup qualifiers. Italy's opponent in today's match is Macedonia, and Portugal will play against Turkey. Both matches will start at 1:45 am Bangladesh time.

Before this match, Ronaldo gave a message of not giving up. The Portuguese star said, full attention in the 2022 World Cup. Representing Portugal is always an honor. The road is not easy. We have respect for our opponents. They also have the same goal. But unitedly, we will fight to take Portugal to its rightful place. Let's fight. 

Meanwhile, Italy made a great comeback after forgetting the nightmare of not being able to play in the 2018 World Cup. They also won the Euro title by setting a new record of victories. However, they now have to play the play-offs in the World Cup qualifiers. They will have to win the next two matches to secure a ticket to the Qatar World Cup. 

Their opponent in the first match tonight is Macedonia. Italy, the last Euro 2021 champions, are in danger of missing out on a second World Cup. If Macedonia gets past the hurdle, they could be disappointed by Portugal or Turkey.

Headline_English: Five foods will reduce the risk of heat stroke in summer

Almost everyone experiences this kind of experience in the scorching heat. During this time, if there is a lack of water in the body, the risk of heat stroke also increases. 

If you ignore these symptoms, you may suffer the consequences. If you continue like this regularly, you may lose consciousness, palpitations, low blood pressure problems and even face dangers like heat stroke. 

According to experts, all these problems start due to the lack of water in the body. The water that is constantly lost through various physiological processes like breathing, sweating, and urination is replenished through food and drinks. When the supply of this water in the body decreases, the problem of dehydration begins. 

Moreover, sweating in the heat causes a deficiency of sodium and potassium in the body, which can also cause dangers. In this case, if you can keep several things in your diet, the water deficiency in the body will be satisfied, the body will stay cool, and the sodium and potassium levels in the body will also be maintained. 

Foods that you can keep in your daily list to keep your body healthy in summer 

Coconut water 

Coconut water is one of the ways to escape from the heat. It keeps the stomach cool, along with several nutritional properties. Coconut water maintains the balance of sodium and potassium in the body. Drinking coconut water on a summer day keeps the body healthy. 

Raw mango 

This fruit helps to remove toxins from the body. It is very beneficial in maintaining the balance of body temperature. Eating this fruit on a summer day reduces the risk of heat stroke. 

You can eat raw mango with salt during this time. Apart from that, raw mango sorbet or raw mango chutney also helps to keep the body cool. 

Gourd 

Gourd is also very useful in keeping the body cool. However, the benefits of raw gourd juice are much greater than cooked gourd. Drink gourd juice with a little salt and lemon juice at any time of the day. This drink keeps the body cool and replenishes the water deficiency in the body. 

Sprouted moong dal 

When we get hungry in the middle of work in the office, we eat heavy food. As a result, the water deficiency in the body can increase. If you get hungry in the afternoon on a hot day, you can make a salad of sprouted moong dal and eat it. It has low calories. So the body temperature does not increase. The stomach remains cool, and the sodium and potassium levels in the body are also maintained. 

Curd 

Dak Yogurt 

Dak Yogurt must be included in the diet during summer. Be it with rice or fruit or just sour yogurt. However, if you make yogurt ghee or lasci and eat it, water will also enter the body. As a result, digestion will also be better, and the body's water requirement will also be met.

Headline_English: Recommendation to increase gas price by Tk 105 for two stoves

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission-BERC's evaluation committee has proposed to increase the price of natural gas in the residential sector by Tk 105 for two stoves. 

If this recommendation is implemented, the monthly gas bill for households will increase from Tk 925 to Tk 990 for one stove and from Tk 975 to Tk 105 for two stoves. 

The proposal was made on Wednesday morning at the Biam Foundation Auditorium in the capital's Eskaton while participating in the third day of the hearing. 

Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited participated in the public hearing. In the past two days, the company proposed to increase the price of gas by 117 percent at all levels, including residential, among four companies. 

At the time, Titas Managing Director Harunur Rashid Molla said that Titas Gas is in losses because it is not possible to prevent gas theft. He also admitted that 5 to 10 percent of the company's corrupt officials are involved in this. 

In view of this, the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has called for a four-day public hearing. Titas is holding a hearing on the proposal from 10 am today on the third day of the hearing. 

However, the CAB has proposed to keep the original proposal unchanged since the price will further decrease if it is properly evaluated based on the law. 

Meanwhile, the general civil society says that illegal connections are being made based on communication with Titas, that if Titas' irregularities and corruption stop, the gas price will not increase, and that the evaluation committee is working in a syndicate with Titas. 

BERC, Titas Gas officials and invited guests were present at the hearing.

Headline_English: University student dies after falling from building
Content_Enlish:
A student of Daffodil University has died after falling from a four-storey building in the capital's Shukrabad. The incident took place early Wednesday. The deceased student has been identified as Akash Roy (24). 

He graduated from the Computer Science Department of Daffodil International University in Dhaka. He used to hang out with friends in a house behind New Model College in Shukrabad. Akash's village home is in Chatra village in Pirganj upazila of Rangpur, and his father's name is Ratan Roy. The entire family lives in the village. 

Friends of the deceased said that Akash had been suffering from mental depression for a long time. They believe that Akash committed suicide by jumping from the roof of the building. 

In the morning, the security guard said that Akash had fallen from the building. Among those who took Akash to the hospital was his friend Pankaj Adhikari. The five of them used to hang out on the third floor of the four-storey building in Shukrabad. 

Pankaj said that Akash was seen lying "in a bloody state" under the building in the morning. And Akash's phone was found on the roof of the house. Later, when he was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, the doctor declared him dead. 

Dhaka Medical College Police Station Inspector Bachchu Mia said, "Initially, it is believed that Akash committed suicide. However, Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station has been informed to investigate whether there is any other reason behind Akash's death or how Akash died."

Headline_English: How beneficial is bay leaf for diabetics?
Content_Enlish:
The presence of bay leaves in Bengali cuisine to enhance the taste and aroma is ancient. In addition, although bay leaves are used to enhance the taste, bay leaves are also very useful in reducing diabetes. It has many medicinal properties. 

According to experts, bay leaves contain various beneficial elements like copper, selenium, iron, zinc, magnesium, potassium and calcium. There are also several vitamins. Therefore, even if you have diabetes, bay leaves are not harmful but rather have more hope of benefit. See what properties the well-known spice has— 

1. Diabetes control: Bay leaves can help control diabetes. Research says that eating one to three grams of bay leaves daily can reduce diabetes. According to experts, polyphenol-like ingredients are found in bay leaves. Which can help in controlling diabetes. 

2. Boosting immunity: Bay leaves contain vitamin A, vitamin B6 and vitamin C. These vitamins help in increasing immunity. Many people recommend drinking tea made with bay leaves when your nose is blocked due to a cold. 

3. To keep your mind healthy: The smell of bay leaves increases the level of hormones that create a feeling of pleasure in the human body. In addition, a recent study on rats has shown that 5 minutes of exposure to bay leaf smoke every day increases memory power. However, experts say that more detailed research is needed on this subject. 

4. To heal wounds: Bay leaves have anti-inflammatory properties. This anti-inflammatory property is useful in healing wounds, and tests on various animals have also found the same results. 

5. To protect kidney health: A 2008 study showed that bay leaves can be useful in preventing kidney stones. It controls the amount of an enzyme called 'urease'. If the amount of this enzyme increases excessively, the risk of kidney stones increases. 

The study showed that taking 1 to 3 grams of bay leaves for 30 consecutive days reduces the amount of glucose and cholesterol in the blood. The ingredients in bay leaves significantly control insulin levels. Bay leaves also have many other properties.

Headline_English: The deep depression may develop into a cyclone.
Content_Enlish:
The depression formed in the Bay of Bengal has further intensified and has developed into a deep depression, just before a cyclone. The depression, which is currently located in the North Andaman Sea and the southeastern Bay of Bengal, has moved north-northeastwards and intensified, turning into a deep depression in the same area. 

The Meteorological Office said that at 6 am on Tuesday, it was 750 kilometers south of Cox's Bazar seaport. Due to this deep depression, the sea is moderately rough. Remote warning signal number 1 has been issued at all seaports in the country. If the depression turns into a cyclone, then its name will be Ashani, which is the name given by Sri Lanka. 

Meanwhile, fishing trawlers in the North Bay of Bengal have been asked to operate with caution. In addition, the country is feeling hot due to the effect of this deep depression. The highest temperature in the country was recorded in Rangamati on Monday at 36.5 degrees Celsius. 

The maximum sustained wind speed within 48 km of the deep depression is 50 km/h, increasing to 60 km/h in gusts or squalls. The sea is moderately rough near the deep depression. 

However, according to the Meteorological Department, there is no danger of the impact of cyclone "Ashni" on Bangladesh. It may weaken considerably while at sea and cross the Myanmar coast.

Headline_English: Bangladesh tops the world in air pollution
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh has the highest air pollution in the world. And the capital Dhaka is in second place in the list of the most polluted cities. The Indian capital Delhi is at the top. This information was revealed in a report released on Tuesday by IQ Air, a Swiss company working on air pollution and air purification technology. 

The report was prepared by monitoring the air quality of 6,475 cities in 117 countries and regions of the world. 

The report said that last year, not a single country could meet the expected air quality targets of the World Health Organization. The air quality in Central and South Asia is the worst in the world. 

It has been reported that 46 of the 50 most polluted cities are located in this region. The report was prepared based on the air pollution levels in 6,475 cities last year. 

The study says that India's overall pollution level has worsened in 2021 and New Delhi has once again been named the world's most polluted capital. Bangladesh has been recognized as the most polluted country in 2021 as in the previous year. 

On the other hand, Chad is in second place as the study takes data from African countries for the first time. Bangladesh is ranked in the top 10 countries in the world for air pollution, followed by Chad, Pakistan, Tajikistan, India, Oman, Kyrgyzstan, Bahrain, Iraq and Nepal. 

China has fallen to 22nd place in the PM 2.5 ranking in 2021 after waging a virtual war on pollution since 2014. The country was ranked 14th the previous year. IQAir says that PM 2.5 levels in China fell to 32.6 micrograms in 2021, an improvement from 2020. 

Hotan, in the northwestern province of Xinjiang, was the most polluted city in China, with an average PM 2.5 level of more than 100 micrograms, largely due to dust storms. 

However, the Chinese city of Hotan has slipped to third place in the list of the most polluted cities in the world, surpassing Bhiwadi and Ghaziabad in India.

Headline_English: PM orders production of edible oil by reducing imports
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has directed to reduce the import of edible oil and increase its production domestically. For this, she has said that emphasis should be placed on the production of oilseeds including soybean and mustard. The Prime Minister gave these instructions at the meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Tuesday, March 22. ECNEC Chairperson Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina presided over the meeting by joining virtually from Ganabhaban. 

12 projects were approved at the meeting at a cost of about 16 thousand crore taka. 

Later, Planning Minister MA Mannan gave all this information at the NEC conference room in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar. State Minister for Planning Dr. Shamsul Alam and secretaries of various ministries were present at the time. 

The Prime Minister said that if necessary, more research should be done on oilseed production. For this, farmers should be encouraged. 

The Prime Minister gave instructions at the ECNEC meeting to reduce the import of edible oil and increase the production of various oilseeds including soybean, sunflower and almonds domestically. 

The Planning Minister said that from now on, whenever a new bridge is built anywhere in Bangladesh, arrangements should be made for boats to pass under it. In addition, ECNEC Chairperson Sheikh Hasina has said that the capacity of the railway factories in Saidpur and Pahartali should be increased. She also ordered that 40 to 50 percent of the railway's manpower be recruited from the family quota. 

The Minister also said that 12 projects have been approved in the ECNEC meeting. The total cost of implementing the projects will be 15,744 crore 56 lakh taka. 

Of this, 11,674 crore 83 lakh taka will be spent from government funds, 4,685.3 lakh taka from foreign loans and 1,200 crore taka from the organization's own funds, the Planning Minister also said.

Headline_English: BCB President impressed by Shakib's sense of responsibility towards the team
Content_Enlish:
Shakib's decision to return after playing the series-deciding match against South Africa despite concerns about the health of his mother and children has set an example. BCB President Nazmul Hasan Papon is impressed with Shakib's sense of responsibility towards the national team. 

He told the media on Tuesday, "After the first ODI match, he (Shakib) had said that a medical emergency might come to the family. We said no problem. The family first. Later, he said that he would come to play the second ODI." 

Shakib's return to the country was finalized after playing the second ODI. The BCB had announced his return to the country. The plane ticket was also finalized. But Shakib changed his mind after a while and decided to stay. 

Papon said, "He called again tomorrow and said that he will come after playing the last match. We always have the green signal for him (Shakib) to return. What he is doing for the team is his sacrifice. 

Bangladesh won the first ODI of the series against the Proteas in Centurion. They lost the second ODI in Johannesburg by a big margin. Shakib and Tamim will face Temba Bavuma in the series-deciding match on Wednesday in Centurion. Shakib will return home after playing that match, even if he is in the Test series team. 

Nazmul Hasan Papon wants the batters to perform well to win the series against South Africa. Meanwhile, the board president said that if any IPL team wants Taskin after the South Africa tour, he will be given a break. 

Shakib Al Hasan had left the BCB in an uncomfortable position before the South Africa tour by asking for rest, questions were raised about his responsibility in the national team, everyone praised Shakib in a couple of weeks. Despite concerns about the illness of the mother and children, the decision to return after playing the series-deciding match has set an example. 
Taskin, who was called up for the IPL, has given priority to the national team. The board is also happy with the two, the president has also clarified his position on the issue of Taskin playing in the IPL. 

BCB's plan for this year's South Africa tour is eye-catching. The Tigers have got the power hitting coach they need, the combination of Domingo-Donald has increased their courage. And the team performance has given the Proteas a taste of their first win at the Dera. This time, it's their turn to fulfill their dream of winning the series, the board president is hopeful. 

BCB to organize Mujib Borsho concert on March 29. In the presence of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, the event will be called Cricket Celebrates Mujib Hundred. Oscar winner AR Rahman will spread charm at the Mirpur Home of Cricket.

Headline_English: 40th BCS results published, cadre 1963
Content_Enlish:
The Public Service Commission (PSC) has released the final results of the 40th BCS examination. This time, the PSC has recommended 1,963 people for appointment in various cadres against a total of 2,219 vacant posts. The results were released on the PSC website around 3 pm on Wednesday. 

This time, 245 people are in the administration cadre, 12 in the Ansar cadre, 45 in the audit and accounts cadre, 17 in the cooperative cadre, 72 in the customs and excise cadre, 3 in the food cadre, 25 in the foreign affairs cadre, 17 in the information cadre, 72 in the police cadre, 6 in the postal cadre, 1 in the railway transport and commercial cadre, 59 in the tax cadre, 275 in the agricultural cadre, 1 in the cooperative cadre, 26 in the fisheries cadre, 5 in the food (assistant defense engineer/equivalent post) cadre, 112 in the health cadre, 12 in the information (assistant radio engineer) cadre, 155 in the livestock cadre, 6 in the public works cadre, 5 in the railway engineering cadre, 3 in the roads and highways cadre, 12 in the statistics cadre, 717 in the general education (for government general colleges) cadre, It has been recommended to appoint 3 people in the Education (for Government Teacher Training College) cadre. 

It also said that it was not possible to recommend anyone for 256 posts due to the lack of qualified candidates in the technical/professional cadre. 

This BCS examination has been repeatedly disrupted due to the Corona pandemic. The PSC has also had to rush to conduct the viva examination. Due to the increase in the outbreak of Corona, it had to be postponed many times and restarted. In total, this BCS has been delayed due to Corona. 

On January 27 last year, the Bangladesh Public Service Commission (PSC) published the results of the 40th BCS written examination. 10,964 people passed it. 

In August 2018, the PSC published the notification for the 40th BCS. 4 lakh 12 thousand 532 candidates applied for the preliminary examination of the 40th BCS. Out of these, 3 lakh 27 thousand candidates took the examination. Out of them, 20 thousand 277 passed the preliminary examination.

Headline_English: Smith slaps presenter on Oscars stage
Content_Enlish:
Actor Will Smith, who won the Best Actor award this time, slapped host Chris Rock on stage at the Oscars, the most prestigious award in the film industry. This sudden incident caught everyone's attention at the 94th Academy Awards held at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles. 

During the ceremony, Chris Rock made a joke about Will Smith's wife, Jada Pinkett Smith, on stage when he was presenting an Oscar for another category. 

According to international media, Reuters, stand-up comedian Chris Rock made fun of several nominees at the ceremony. At one point, he started joking about Smith's wife, Pinkett Smith, losing her hair. Rock said, "Jada, I love you. I can't wait to see GI Gen 2." 

Will Smith couldn't take Chris Rock's joke. He was then seen on stage slapping Rock on the cheek. Rock regained his composure and said, "Oh, wow! Wow! Will Smith slapped me and drove the ghost away. Dude, that was a GI Jane joke." 

Rock was actually referring to the 1997 GI Jane movie, in which Demi Moore shaved her head. 

There's a lot of drama on the Oscar stage, and a lot of it is planned. Everyone thought that Smith's slap on Rock was something like that. But Smith's reaction later made it clear that the slap wasn't drama. 

Later, Smith apologized to the Academy Awards authorities and his colleagues when he came to accept the Best Actor award. However, he didn't mention Chris Rock's name at the time. 

Will Smith's wife Pinkett Smith first opened up about her hair loss in a Facebook discussion in 2018. She said, "My hair is falling out. It really freaked me out when it first started." 

The Girls Trip star said that she thought she might have alopecia after a handful of hair came out in the shower one day. "I was like, 'Oh my God, I'm going bald! That's why I cut my hair. And then I always cut my hair." 

And that's probably why Smith couldn't stand Rock's joke about his wife's illness. So this year's Oscars will be remembered for the rest of his life - the one where Will Smith punched Chris Rock. 

There have been a few viral incidents at the Oscars before. Another such incident happened in 2017, when the name of the best picture was reversed.

Headline_English: Canada returns to World Cup after 36 years of drought
Content_Enlish:
The 1986 Mexico World Cup was Canada's first and only World Cup. More than three decades have passed since then. Finally, after a long wait, Canadian football returned to the world stage with a 4-0 win over Jamaica in Toronto in the qualifying round. They became the first team in the CONCACAF region to secure a place in the 2022 Qatar World Cup. 

After the match, various cities in Canada turned into cities of celebration. Toronto's BMO Stadium, packed with 30,000 spectators, was filled with slogans and songs from the audience. 

Canada took the lead in the first half with goals from Larin and Buchanan. Two more goals in the second half gave the team a big win. Canada could have gone on to win this match against Jamaica if it had just been a draw. But the excited team played an aggressive game of football in front of their home crowd and won the match 4-0. After that, the entire team and the stadium erupted in celebration. 

Canada has secured the World Cup first with one match remaining, beating Mexico and the United States, the established powers of the CONCACAF region and regular faces of the World Cup. They have 28 points from 13 matches. 

Meanwhile, the United States is on the verge of qualifying for the World Cup from the same region after defeating Panama 5-1. Christian Pulisic scored a hat-trick to lead the Americans. 

Meanwhile, Senegal and Egypt will fight in a do-or-die match in the African qualifiers. Salah's team is ahead with a 1-0 win in the first leg at home. A few days ago, Senegal won the Africa Cup of Nations for the first time by defeating Egypt. This time, the Pharaohs are desperate to take revenge by defeating the Teranga Lions. 

Before the last match against Bolivia in the qualifiers, midfielder Fred claimed that Brazil is one of the favorites to win the World Cup. Argentina coach Scaloni talked about the team's future with the last match of the qualifiers against Ecuador ahead. 

The European reckoning is also in full swing. Portugal will face giant killer North Macedonia in the play-off final. Cristiano Ronaldo has no chance to take the team that knocked out Italy lightly. 

20 teams have qualified for the 32-team Qatar World Cup so far. Canada is the latest surprise inclusion. 29 teams are still fighting for the remaining 12 spots.

Headline_English: Bangladeshi journalist and engineer missing in Libya
Content_Enlish:
Bangladeshi journalist Zahidur Rahman and engineer Saiful Islam have been missing in Libya for the past six days, their families said. A Libyan driver, Mohammad Khaled, is also reported missing with them. The Bangladesh Embassy in Libya said efforts are underway to find them. 

Zahidur Rahman's wife Taslima Rahman said that Zahidur Rahman, a resident of Savar area of ​​Dhaka, is a special correspondent for NTV. Zahidur went to Libya on March 21. We last spoke to him on March 23 at noon. Since then, his phone has been switched off. We did not understand the matter at first. After 24 hours, many people started telling us that they could not contact him online or by phone. That's when I got worried. 

Their family has not been in touch with their husband for 5/6 days, but they have learned from the family of the Libyan driver who was with them that good news about them may come soon. It is believed that they were kidnapped from the war-torn Libyan capital, Tripoli. 

The Bangladesh Embassy in Libya says that they are being investigated to determine whether they were abducted by government forces or a militia group. 

Zahidur's wife Taslima Rahman also said that Zahid went to London on a Turkish Airlines flight on March 3 on a family visa. From there, he visited Ireland and Scotland and reached Libya on March 21. The next day, on March 22, he posted a status on his Facebook from Tripoli, saying that entering the civil war-torn country was quite a challenge. Before going to London, he collected a visa from Dhaka under special arrangements. 

However, several reports by Zahidur Rahman from London have been broadcast on NTV. After going to Libya, he met expatriate Bangladeshi engineer Saiful there.

Headline_English: Can Trump's 20-point plan stop Israel's 'yellow' plan to occupy Gaza?
Content_Enlish:
Although the 20-point peace proposal of US President Donald Trump has not brought permanent peace to the Palestinian Gaza Strip, the two-year-long Israeli massacre ended in October. Although the residents of Gaza are still losing their lives in attacks by Israeli forces despite this ‘unilateral’ ceasefire, the head of the Israeli military has clearly stated that the so-called ‘Yellow Line’ drawn by Israel dividing Gaza in two is a blueprint for occupying the besieged territory. 
Despite Israel’s various tricks, President Trump is trying to move forward with the second phase of his 20-point peace proposal. The two important points of the second phase are the complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza and the deployment of an international ‘temporary’ force there, and the disarmament of Hamas. But Israel is not willing to withdraw its troops, and Hamas is only willing to lay down its arms once a Palestinian state is established. 
All in all, the future of Gaza is still uncertain. With Israel's continued ceasefire violations and Hamas's pledge to continue its resistance against its plan to occupy Gaza—both of which will keep everyone's eyes on how long the conflict that ended this year will last, everyone will be watching in the new year.
'Global Sumud Flotilla'
The Israeli massacre in Gaza began on October 7, 2023. On that day, Hamas and other pro-independence organizations in Gaza launched an unprecedented attack into southern Israel. Capitalizing on this attack, Israel launched an indiscriminate attack on Gaza on the same day. This massacre continued for two years, with a few days' break for prisoner exchanges. The Israeli army's 'scorched earth policy' turned the besieged valley into a wasteland. Famine descended on Gaza due to the all-out blockade. Children began to die from lack of milk.
The Global Sea Flotilla set sail for Gaza by sea to break Israel's inhumane blockade. The first flotilla set sail from Barcelona, ​​Spain, on August 31. More ships from Tunisia and Sicily, Italy, joined the flotilla from September 13 to 15. More ships from the Greek island of Cyrus later joined the flotilla with relief supplies. The ships carried a symbolic but significant amount of humanitarian cargo, including food, medical supplies and other essential items for the people of Gaza.
A woman walks with a child through rubble in Khan Younis, Gaza
A woman walks with a child through rubble in Khan Younis, GazaFile photo: Reuters
The flotilla initially consisted of more than 50 ships and hundreds of international volunteers, activists and lawmakers representing at least 44 countries. The flotilla also included Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg and Bangladeshi photographer Shahidul Alam. The activists in the flotilla faced adverse weather conditions at sea. In addition, there were suspected drone attacks near Malta and Crete. Some of the ships were damaged and forced to retreat. When the flotilla reached the eastern Mediterranean, there were 44 ships in the flotilla.
But Israel did not allow any of the ships of the flotilla to dock in Gaza. Israeli forces took control of all the ships in the flotilla. They were taken to Israeli seaports. More than five hundred activists were detained. However, they were later sent back to their respective countries.
‘Operation Gideon’s Chariot’
In mid-May of this year, the Israeli army announced the launch of a new military operation in Gaza called ‘Operation Gideon’s Chariot’. The Israeli forces launched this attack primarily targeting Gaza City. To avoid this operation, Hamas offered a two-month ceasefire in exchange for the release of Israeli prisoners. This attempt at a ceasefire collapsed when Israel did not respond.
The remaining houses and structures in Gaza City were demolished through this new operation. The almost defunct hospitals there and their doctors and staff were not spared from this operation. In addition, the Israeli forces used unmanned armored vehicles filled with explosives to demolish houses.
The number of people killed in Gaza due to Israel's continued attacks has exceeded 71,000. About 170,200 Palestinians have been injured. A UN-backed commission and various international organizations have described the massacre carried out by Israel in Gaza as "ethnic cleansing".
Trump's 20-point and 'unilateral' ceasefire
In late September, the White House released a plan to end the war in Gaza. At that time, it was said that if both sides accepted the 20-point proposal of the plan, the war would stop immediately. According to the proposal, all living and dead hostages held in Gaza would be returned within 72 hours and Palestinian prisoners held in Israel would be released.
According to the proposal, a Palestinian technocratic government would take responsibility for governing Gaza in the new system. Hamas would have no role in it. The independence-seeking organization would lay down its arms. Israel would also not occupy Gaza or annex it. The proposal also called for the formation of an international stabilization force (International Stabilization Force or ISF) for the Gaza Strip. In continuation of this, a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel came into effect on October 10. According to the agreement, Hamas handed over all prisoners, both living and dead.
According to the ceasefire agreement, 600 trucks carrying aid were allowed to enter Gaza every day. But according to the United Nations and various non-governmental organizations, currently only 100 to 300 trucks carrying aid are able to enter Gaza every day. Israel is not allowing even the necessary tents to enter Gaza. Even violating the terms of the agreement, Israel has not allowed the Rafah crossing on the Egyptian border to open. Although the ceasefire came into effect in October, Israel's attacks on Gaza have not stopped. Since the ceasefire came into effect, Israel has attacked Gaza about 800 times, killing at least 411 Palestinians. Among them, Raed Saad, a senior commander of Hamas' military wing, the Qassam Brigades, was killed in an Israeli attack on Gaza City on December 13. In addition, according to the ceasefire agreement, 600 trucks carrying aid were allowed to enter Gaza every day. But according to the United Nations and various non-governmental organizations, currently only 100 to 300 trucks carrying aid are able to enter Gaza every day. Israel is not allowing even the necessary tents to enter Gaza. Even violating the terms of the agreement, Israel has not allowed the Rafah crossing on the Egyptian border to open. As a result, the entry of aid into Gaza is being severely disrupted. And at the end of the year, a natural disaster occurred as a nightmare. Heavy rains and bitter cold disrupted the lives of Gaza residents who took shelter in tents.
The ‘yellow’ plan for the occupation of Gaza
In the first phase of the ceasefire agreement, Israel withdrew its troops along a specific border in the valley. That border is called the ‘Yellow Line’. A draft map shows that by drawing the yellow line, about 58 percent of the area of ​​Gaza has been placed under Israeli control. Palestinians are being shot and killed by drone strikes as soon as they approach the yellow line. On December 6, Israeli forces killed seven Palestinians. A 70-year-old woman and her son were among the dead.
An Israeli drone chased and attacked two of them in Gaza City. The Israeli army claims that three people were killed in separate attacks. The three had crossed the “Yellow Line.”
The Yellow Line will be the “new border” between Gaza and Israel, Israel’s military chief, Yal Zamir, has announced. He made the remarks during a recent meeting with Israeli troops deployed in Gaza.
Palestinian homes are being demolished in the West Bank
Palestinian homes are being demolished in the West BankFile photo: Reuters
The failure to withdraw Israeli forces from the Yellow Line means that more than half of Gaza will remain under Israeli control. This includes much of Gaza’s farmland and the Rafah border crossing with Egypt. Yal Zamir said, “The Yellow Line will be (Israel’s) new border. It will serve as our front line of defense. "Our operations will continue along this line. Large parts of Gaza are under Israeli control. We will not move from this defensive line." So far, the Israeli government has not promised to completely withdraw its troops from Gaza. It has said it will maintain a buffer zone "unless there is a renewed threat of terrorism." According to experts, these loopholes in the terms would allow Israel to remain in Gaza indefinitely.

Headline_English: Tarique Rahman's return and the politics of exiled leaders
Content_Enlish:
History never follows a straight line. State crises, repression by those in power, ideological clashes—through all these, history chooses its leadership. In many cases, that leadership is born in the ordeal of exile. 

Exile is therefore not just a geographical separation; it is a battle against time. It is a period of sharpening one's faith and a long pursuit of mental and political preparation for return. 

Bangladesh stands at a juncture today, when the politics of exile has become newly relevant. In this context, Tarique Rahman's long exile and preparation for return are not just a contemporary political event; they are linked to that familiar trend of world history. 

Exile: Not a defeat, but a time of preparation 

In the history of the 20th century, some of the leaders who reached the pinnacle of state power began or completed their political careers through exile. In this context, one can recall the long political struggles of Yasser Arafat in Palestine or Benazir Bhutto in Pakistan. Although Nelson Mandela was not in direct exile, his long imprisonment was an internal exile for him. 

Former Prime Minister of Pakistan Benazir Bhutto 
Former Prime Minister of Pakistan Benazir Bhutto File Photo: AFP 
Benazir Bhutto was forced to leave Pakistan under pressure from the military regime. From exile, she built international public opinion in favor of democracy and returned to power—although her life was ultimately a victim of political violence. 

These examples show that exile does not exhaust leadership; on the contrary, in the right cases, it deepens leadership. 

Tarique Rahman: Politics forged through exile 

Tarique Rahman's 17-year exile can also be placed within this historical trend. During this time, he was not only away from the country—not from politics; Rather, distance has given him the opportunity to understand the reality of the country in a new way. The suppression of state power, the emptiness of opposition politics, the one-sidedness of the administration—he has examined everything since his exile. 

Tarique Rahman at a discussion organized by the UK BNP. He was only away from the country—not from politics 
Tareque Rahman at a discussion organized by the UK BNP. He was only away from the country—not from politics File photo 
Tareque Rahman has understood the moral crisis of state power, the importance of organization and structure. He has realized that the aspirations of a nation can be captured even from a distance. Therefore, his political struggle is not just a story of personal adversities. The political lessons he has learned through lawsuits, torture and exile can be found in the institutional form of the BNP's announced 31-point program. It is a state philosophy—where democracy, rule of law, accountability and social justice are intertwined. 

Politics of Return: A Moral Moment Greater Than Power 

In history, the return of political leadership is never a mere geographical event. Return after exile means not just returning home—it is facing history. Entering into a new dialogue with the public mind. 

Tarique Rahman was speaking at various events in the country virtually from London 
Tareque Rahman was speaking at various events in the country virtually from London File photo 
The politics of return is therefore deeper than the politics of power. Power can be seized through strategy; but return occurs with trust and faith. The returns that are memorable in world history are not because of any victory procession; rather, they are memorable because they changed the mental structure of the nation. 

Bangladesh stands at the exact point today where the politics of return has become meaningful anew. The unilateral seizure of state power for a long time, the suppression of opposition voices, the decline of institutions—all of these have led to the state losing its way.

In this reality, Tarique Rahman's return is not just a political event. It is a response to a void. This void is not just of leadership; it is a void of balance and tolerance. The politics that Tarique Rahman has learned through his long exile is the politics of understanding this void. Because exile does not teach people to rush; it teaches people to wait. Moderation, patience and foresight are born through waiting. 

Tarique Rahman's return is therefore not in the pursuit of power, but in the pursuit of responsibility. There is no easy path of triumph before him. There is the difficult responsibility of rebuilding the state. 

The question of return and reconciliation 

History says that leaders who return from exile walk one of two paths. Some choose the politics of revenge and become transient in history. Others choose the politics of reconciliation and become the lasting shaper of the state. 

Nelson Mandela 
Nelson Mandela File Photo: AFP 
Nelson Mandela is the most shining example. He could have taken revenge if he wanted after 27 years of imprisonment. But he chose reconciliation. That decision saved South Africa from civil war. 

This question is also the most important for Bangladesh today, which way will politics go after Tarique Rahman's return? His political statements, organizational decisions and 31-point program during his long exile indicate that he wants to speak in the language of institutional reconstruction, not revenge. 

The re-establishment of democracy, reform of the electoral system, administrative accountability, all these make the politics of return future-oriented. Finally, one truth must be remembered - return is not the end. It is actually the beginning of the most difficult chapter. While in exile, the leader becomes a symbol; after returning, he has to prove himself in reality. This test is now ahead. 

Tarique Rahman's return to the country is a question standing at the door of history - will the politics of exile give him the courage to reimagine Bangladesh through his return? 

The answer to this question has not yet been written. But history says that a return that happens in the demands of time is never meaningless. 

Zubair Babu: Producer and broadcaster and close associate of Tarique Rahman.

Headline_English: Vijay Book Fair starts from December 10
Content_Enlish: The 'Bijoy Book Fair 2025' is being organized by the Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers Association (BAPUS) on December 10 at the Bangla Academy grounds. The fair will continue until December 22. About 200 publishing houses in the country will participate in the fair. BAPUS held a press conference at the Al Mahmud Writers' Corner of the Bangla Academy on Thursday morning and informed about the organization of the book fair. The organizers said that special importance has been given to the fair since December is the month of Victory. The event is not just a fair to sell books; rather, it is going to be an initiative to increase book reading. The Bijoy Book Fair 2025 will be inaugurated at 4 pm on December 10. The Bijoy Book Fair will be open from 2 pm to 8 pm every day. On holidays, the fair will start at 11 am and will continue until 9 pm. About the fair, Kausar Ahmed, Deputy Manager of Prothoma Prakashan, said, 'Our goal is to ensure that everyone, from children to adults, is interested in reading books.' The Book Publishers and Sellers Association (BAPUS) also announced plans for various international events, including the Southeast Asia Book Fair. The fair organizers said that embassies of 15 countries have been invited to organize the Bijoy Book Fair 2025. Abul Bashar Firoz Sheikh, chief coordinator of the Bijoy Book Fair National Committee and director of the Central Executive Committee of BAPU, said, "Just as the Amar Ekushey Book Fair is a universal festival, we want to gift another festival to the nation called Bijoy Book Fair. We plan to hold book fairs in 64 districts of the country." Sabah Khaled, publisher of Renaissance Publications, said, "Next year, we are going to organize book fairs in schools, colleges and universities. We want readers of all classes to be able to participate in the book fair." The Bijoy Book Fair will feature storytelling competitions, puppet shows, magic shows, bioscopes and many more for children. In addition, cultural programs will be organized daily from December 11 to 22.

Headline_English: Barcelona president outlines three hopes for the new year
Content_Enlish:
Barcelona had a great year in 2025. Camp Nou is bathed in success. Coach Hansi Flick has added La Liga, Copa del Rey and Spanish Super Cup trophies to the club's showcase. For now, Barca also reigns supreme in the La Liga points table; the Catalans are at the top, 4 points ahead of arch-rivals Real Madrid. Will this journey of success continue in 2026? Barcelona president Joan Laporta has expressed his three wishes for the new year. His 'wish list' has emerged in an interview with Spanish media outlet 'Sport'.
First wish: Let the tide of success continue
Current La Liga champions Barcelona
Current La Liga champions BarcelonaReuters
Hansi Flick and his disciples are keeping their feet on the ground despite achieving success one after another. The main goal now is to further strengthen their position as the best team in Spain. Laporta's first wish is therefore straightforward - that this streak of success continues. He says, 'My prayer for the new year is that we play great football this season and win more trophies. May Barca fans all over the world be smiling.'

Second wish: A celebration of democracy
Barcelona president Joan Laporta
Barcelona president Joan LaportaX
2026 is important for Barcelona for one reason off the pitch. This year is the club's presidential election. Laporta did not clarify whether he will run again. His wish is for the election to be transparent and joyful. In Laporta's words, 'I want this Barcelona election to become a celebration of democracy. That the club's members participate in this electoral process in large numbers.'

Third wish: Peace and good health
There is a battle on the pitch, but Laporta is more generous in his sense of humanity. His last wish is for the whole world. He wished for peace, solidarity and good health for everyone. This football organizer dreams of a beautiful world.
