Headline_English: Young woman gang-raped for 2 hours in moving van in New Delhi
Content_Enlish:
A 28-year-old woman was gang-raped for more than two hours in a moving van in Faridabad, the capital of India, New Delhi. Later, at midnight, the miscreants threw her out of the moving vehicle and fled. 
The incident took place last Monday night. The married woman was waiting for a vehicle to go home at night. Then a van stopped in front of her. The two youths in the van picked her up, promising to take her home. 

However, the van did not go towards the house but started moving towards Gurgaon Road. 
It is alleged that the woman was kept inside the van for about two and a half hours. The accused continuously gang-raped her. Even though she tried to stop them, they did not listen. Instead, they threatened her. 

Later, at around 3 am on Monday, the woman was thrown out of the moving van on the road near Raja Chowk in SGM Nagar. As a result, her face was severely injured and she started bleeding profusely. 

The injured woman tried to call her sister. Later, when her sister called back, she narrated the entire incident. Family members quickly reached the spot and admitted her to the hospital in critical condition. The injury was so severe that she had to get 10-12 stitches on her face. 

The woman's condition is currently stable. However, she is in a state of severe mental anguish. Her formal statement has not been recorded yet. 

The victim's sister told the police station that the woman had called her at around 8:30 pm the day before the incident. At that time, she said that she was going to her friend's house due to a fight with her mother. She would return home in three hours. 

The woman is married and has three children. She lives separately from her husband due to a family dispute.

Headline_English: The Yemen incident showed how much Saudi Arabia and the Emirates distrust each other.
Content_Enlish:
The United Arab Emirates has withdrawn its troops from Yemen after a Saudi-led coalition airstrike. The move was seen as a way to ease tensions between the two Gulf oil-rich countries, but the incident has highlighted long-standing disagreements and a lack of trust between the two oil-rich Gulf states. 
The Saudi-led coalition carried out airstrikes on Yemen's southern port of Mukalla early Tuesday. The UAE immediately ordered its troops to leave Yemen. 
The UAE said it was surprised by the airstrikes. It soon announced that it was withdrawing its troops from Yemen for their safety. 
The crisis between Saudi Arabia and the UAE began in early December. Tensions rose when UAE-backed separatists suddenly advanced in southern Yemen. The incident has exposed the differences between the two Gulf states over issues ranging from oil quotas to geopolitical influence. A Gulf source familiar with Saudi Arabia’s plans told Reuters that the tension was sparked by a misunderstanding over a meeting in Washington in November between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and US President Donald Trump. The source added that high-level talks and phone calls between Saudi Arabia and the UAE have been ongoing since December, but have yet to yield any tangible results. 

Saudi Arabia’s bombing of UAE-backed separatist groups in Yemen 
A renewed escalation of tensions between Saudi Arabia and the UAE would be unsettling for the economically prosperous Gulf region, which wants to portray itself as a stable area in a volatile Middle East. 

The disagreements between the two countries could make it difficult to reach a consensus on oil production. Both countries are preparing for a virtual meeting with other OPEC+ members on Sunday. 

“The relationship between the two countries has never been easy,” said Neil Quilliam, an associate fellow at the think tank Chatham House. “But the current tensions seem to be the most intense in years.” 

STC advance 

The UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council (STC), which suddenly began advancing in early December, has already captured large parts of Yemen, including the strategically important province of Hazmau. 

The STC once fought alongside the Saudi-backed and internationally recognized Yemeni government against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, who control the capital Sanaa and the populous northwest. 

Any renewed escalation between Saudi Arabia and the UAE would be unsettling for the financially prosperous Gulf region, which is seeking to portray itself as a stable base in a volatile Middle East. 
The STC has advanced southwards, approaching the Saudi-Yemeni border, an area that many Saudis consider their homeland and has cultural and historical significance to them. 

The attacks also put Saudi Arabia and the UAE on opposite sides of Yemen's long-running civil war, which began in 2014. 

Both Saudi Arabia and the UAE have publicly said they are talking to various Yemeni factions to bring the situation under control. However, the Saudi-led coalition has carried out two airstrikes in the province in recent days. 

Supporters of the UAE-backed separatist group Southern Transitional Council (STC) wave the STC flag at a rally in Yemen. 30 December 2025 
Supporters of the UAE-backed separatist group Southern Transitional Council (STC) wave the STC flag at a rally in Yemen. December 30, 2025Photo: Reuters 
The Saudi-led coalition has asked the STC to withdraw from the occupied areas. However, the STC has rejected this. It has said that it will continue operations to maintain security in Hazramaut and the eastern Mahra province. 

Both Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have publicly said that they are talking to various Yemeni groups to bring the situation under control. However, the Saudi-led coalition has carried out two air strikes in Yemen in the past few days. 
In a statement about the attack on Mukalla, the UAE authorities said that they have tried to reduce tensions since the STC began advancing. They claim that they have nothing to do with attacks on Saudi security forces or border operations. 

Differences over Sudan 

Quilliam said, "Both countries try to play down the conflict in their relationship. They argue that there is competition between states. But last year, the competition has suddenly increased a lot and it is evident in many places.’ 

Both countries try to downplay the conflict in their relationship. They argue that competition between states is natural. But last year, the competition has suddenly increased a lot and it is evident in many places. 
Neil Quilliam, Associate Fellow at Chatham House 
One such area of ​​competition and disagreement between the two countries is Sudan. The country has been in a civil war since April 2023 and is in the midst of the world’s largest humanitarian crisis. Despite diplomatic initiatives by the Quad coalition of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, the United States and the Emirates, the conflict in Sudan continues to escalate. 

Sudan is a sensitive issue for the UAE. UN experts and members of the US Congress have accused the UAE of supporting Sudan’s paramilitary RSF, which is fighting the Sudanese army. 

However, the UAE denies supporting any side. 
Trump and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman discussed Sudan at a meeting in Washington in November. A Gulf source said the UAE leaders were angry about the meeting because they were misinformed about the meeting. They were told that the Saudi crown prince had not only called for more sanctions against the RSF but also called for direct sanctions against the UAE for supporting the group. 

The source said the misunderstanding had fueled tensions in Yemen. The UAE’s foreign ministry did not directly confirm or deny the incident. It cited a statement on Friday that said the UAE welcomed Saudi Arabia’s efforts to maintain security and stability in Yemen. It also said the UAE was committed to supporting the country’s stability. 

Past instability 

Anwar Gargash, the UAE president’s diplomatic adviser, said in a post on social media on Saturday that dialogue and a political solution were essential to preserve friendship and alliances. He did not mention Yemen or Saudi Arabia directly. 

Reuters sought a comment from the White House on the matter. There was no immediate response. 

The Gulf region has witnessed instability in the past. In 2017, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Oman and Egypt imposed an economic blockade on Qatar, accusing it of supporting terrorism. Qatar denies the accusations. 

The current tensions do not seem to be a repeat of the Qatar crisis. 

“We have 100 percent disagreement on Yemen and those differences have increased with the current tensions,” said Abdulkhaleq Abdullah, a UAE-based expert. "Allies have arguments too...but they resolve their differences and strengthen areas of common interest."

Headline_English: Does Trump want to control who will be the head of state and government in which country in the world?
Content_Enlish:
Most heads of state in the world generally follow the diplomatic etiquette of not interfering in the internal politics or elections of other countries. Although there has been a lot of controversy about the political game of the United States behind the scenes for decades, Donald Trump is a leader who does not resort to such tricks or tricks. For Trump, transforming the Republican Party into a personal ideology means politics as a powerful tool to exert influence. And he is not limiting this effort to his own country. 

Setting another example of breaking with tradition as president, Trump is now openly supporting his preferred candidates. He is even trying to bend the political and judicial systems of the countries concerned in their favor. 

The fact that Trump's support is not just verbal is evidenced by the White House's new national security strategy. The document mentions implicit support for overthrowing the leaders of allied countries and bringing hard-right populist leaders to power. 

In his second term, Trump has emerged as the head of a global nationalist movement. He is also trying to shape the politics of countries across the Atlantic, including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Honduras, South Korea, Venezuela, and South Africa. 

Trump is mainly interested in changing the fate of leaders who believe in populist nationalism like him, who praise him, or who are embroiled in legal battles like him. 

On Monday, Trump again hinted at interfering in Israeli politics. He is quite popular in the country and has extensive political influence there ahead of next year's general elections. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is currently on trial on bribery and fraud charges. 

Trump told reporters that the apology he requested for Netanyahu is "in the works." He also claimed that he had spoken to Israeli President Isaac Herzog about the matter. In Trump's words, he (Netanyahu, who is accused of war crimes) is a wartime prime minister and a hero. Why shouldn't he be pardoned? 

However, Herzog's office quickly denied Trump's claim in a statement. They said that no such conversation took place between the two presidents and that any decision would be made in accordance with the legal process. 

If Netanyahu can be protected from criminal prosecution, it will not only ease his personal worries but also help him overcome the electoral hurdle. In return, Netanyahu will be personally indebted to Trump. 

This equation becomes clear from the way Trump praised him in response to Netanyahu's praise last Monday at his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida. 

Netanyahu said to Trump, "Thank you for your support. This comes from the bottom of my heart.’ At the same time, the belligerent Israeli prime minister announced that Trump is the first foreigner to receive Israel’s highest honor, the ‘Israel Prize’. This award has been introduced for the first time in the ‘peace’ category especially for Trump. 

US President Donald Trump welcomed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after he arrived to attend a meeting at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort in Palm Beach, Florida, USA. 29 December 2025 
US President Donald Trump welcomed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after he arrived to attend a meeting at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort in Palm Beach, Florida, USA. 29 December 2025Photo: Reuters 
Netanyahu is quite adept at the tricks of pleasing Trump. Earlier, during a visit, he proposed his name for Trump’s much-coveted ‘Nobel Peace Prize’. 

Although Trump's close associates are rumored to be somewhat annoyed with Netanyahu over Israel's delay in the second phase of the Gaza ceasefire. However, Trump's public support will serve as an invaluable political shield for Netanyahu. 
According to Trump, if there had been another prime minister in Netanyahu's place, Israel would probably have ceased to exist today. It took a special person like him to pull Israel out of this dire situation. In just a few sentences, Trump wrote Netanyahu's next election manifesto. 

Diplomatic etiquette 

Historically, US presidents have hesitated to openly interfere in the internal politics of foreign countries. First of all, it is a kind of 'diplomatic etiquette'. No president would want another country to come and help his political rival and avenge that violation of etiquette. 

It is a fundamental principle of democracy that voters decide who will be their leader. (Although Donald Trump’s refusal to accept defeat in 2020 shows how much he believes in this policy.) 

There are also negative effects of endorsing a particular leader. This can create anti-American sentiment in the country concerned or initially worsen US relations with a new leader when he comes to power. 

However, Donald Trump’s administration rarely refrains from trying to influence foreign policy to advance its own interests. 

For example, last week, Nasri Asfura, the candidate of the conservative National Party of Honduras, was declared the winner of the presidential election. Trump had warned in advance that the consequences would be “very dire” if Asfura did not win after a long vote count. 

The defeated center-right candidate, Salvador Nasrallah, claims that Trump’s interference was the main reason for his defeat. This includes Trump’s pardon of a former Honduran president who was serving 45 years in a US prison for drug trafficking. 

Trump has repeatedly used US power to shape Western Hemisphere politics in his own image. Trump imposed a 50 percent tariff on Brazilian goods as his friend and former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was put on trial for attempted coup. 

The incident shows that Trump is using import tariffs not only as a trade tool; but also as a foreign policy “weapon.” 

Currently, Trump is deploying a large fleet to pressure Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro to oust him. Although the official excuse for this is to stop the drug trade. Maduro’s departure may be good for millions of poverty-stricken Venezuelans. 

However, according to analysts, Trump’s real goal is to install a government in Caracas that follows his ideology and expand his power. 

Trump also has a close eye on the presidential elections in Colombia next year. Over the Christmas break, he warned President Gustavo Petro to be “careful.” Petro told CNN, however, that Trump’s pressure on Venezuela was not to restore democracy; it was to control oil. 

Trump is also exerting his economic influence in Argentine politics. He wants to ensure that his friend and “Maga Hero” President Javier Miquel remains in power as a condition of the country’s $20 billion economic aid package. 

From South Africa to South Korea 

Donald Trump’s political moves are not limited to the Western Hemisphere. When South African President Cyril Ramaphosa visited him in the Oval Office last May, Trump tried to embarrass him at home by showing him a controversial video. 

The video claimed that white people in South Africa were being massacred, which added fuel to the flames of racial tensions in the country. 

Similarly, in August, as South Korean President Lee Jae-myung prepared for talks in the Oval Office, Trump posted a provocative message on social media. He accused South Korea of ​​being unstable by accusing it of raiding churches. 

Although Lee Jae-myung cleverly defused the situation by gifting Trump two “Maga” cowboy hats and a personal golf putter, the incident was a warning sign. It is proof that Trump can go to any length to mentally overwhelm other leaders. 

Attacking European stability 

The Trump administration now seems determined to destabilize the moderate and center-left governments in Europe. The new US national security strategy argues that European culture is in danger of losing its very existence due to Muslim immigration. 

This strategy supports the growing influence of so-called “patriotic parties” (far right) in Europe. The goal of US policy is now to build a “resistance” against the current trend in European countries. 

Leaders in France, Germany and the UK see Trump-backed far-right parties, such as France’s National Rally, Germany’s AfD and the UK’s Reform UK, as major threats to the fabric of liberal democracy. 

No one could have imagined that the US, which had been the guarantor of Europe’s freedoms for 80 years, would now pose a direct threat to their political stability.

Headline_English: Will Saudi Arabia ever get nuclear weapons? Why are they so desperate?
Content_Enlish:
Is Saudi Arabia trying to build nuclear weapons? This question has been coming up repeatedly since the signing of the Strategic Mutual Defense Agreement (SMDA) with Pakistan last September. 
Analysts believe that the agreement has created a connection between Riyadh's economic power and Islamabad's nuclear capabilities. This means that Riyadh will provide financial assistance to Islamabad in various ways as a result of the agreement. In return, Islamabad will stand by Riyadh with the necessary nuclear cooperation. 
This is not the first time that Saudi Arabia has tried to build nuclear weapons or launch a program. Earlier, the country also wanted to launch a nuclear program with the help of China and Russia. But it was not successful. Analysts believe that the result of the agreement with Pakistan is fulfilling Saudi Arabia's desires. 
Under the new agreement, Pakistan's nuclear capabilities (weapons and technology assistance) may be given to Saudi Arabia 
Khawaja Asif, Pakistan's Defense Minister 
The question of why Saudi Arabia is suddenly so desperate to build nuclear weapons is coming up. There are believed to be several reasons behind this. 

Economic reasons 
Saudi Arabia is the world's largest oil exporter. The country's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman wants to reduce carbon emissions. At the same time, he wants to store crude oil for export in the future. For this, the country is looking at nuclear power plants. 
According to data from the US Energy Information Administration last year, 68 percent of Saudi Arabia's electricity comes from gas-based power plants. The remaining 32 percent of electricity comes from oil-based power plants. The country has the highest demand for electricity in June every year. At this time, 1.4 million barrels of crude oil are used to generate electricity daily. 
Pakistani Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman embrace after signing the agreement. In the Saudi capital Riyadh, September 17, 2025 
Pakistani Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman embrace after signing the agreement. Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, September 17, 2025 Photo: Reuters 
Saudi Arabia has long expressed interest in acquiring nuclear technology for civilian use to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels. This was also indicated in the statement of the country's Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud in January. He said that they are ready to enrich and sell uranium, the main component of the nuclear program. 

Building a nuclear power plant can reduce the use of fossil fuels in power generation to some extent. In addition, a lot of electricity is consumed in the country's desalination of brackish water and air conditioning. Alternative fuels can be obtained from nuclear power plants. 

Saudi-Pakistan historical relations are being forged 
The SMDA agreement was signed between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan as a continuation of long-standing security and defense cooperation. It started with the 'Treaty of Friendship' signed in 1951. That agreement laid the foundation for decades of strategic, political, military and economic cooperation between the two countries. 

Later, in 1982, another agreement was signed between the two countries. The new strategic mutual defense treaty formalized a decades-old and strong defense partnership. 
68 percent of Saudi Arabia's electricity comes from gas-fired power plants. The remaining 32 percent comes from oil-fired power plants. 
Both countries have positive views on Saudi-Pakistan relations. Saudi Arabia is the leader of the Islamic world. It is also a major economic power. Saudi Arabia is Islamabad's largest foreign investor. 

Pakistani armed forces have been deployed to Saudi Arabia several times in recent years. They have trained Saudi troops in the Gulf region and in Pakistan. 

Pakistan is relatively weak economically among Asian countries. But it is the only Muslim-majority country in the world that has nuclear weapons. 
Pakistan has one of the largest armies in the world. The army has more than 600,000 members. The agreement will ensure that Pakistan will provide security assistance to Saudi Arabia. A small number of Pakistani troops have been stationed in Saudi Arabia for a long time. The new agreement signals a greater level of involvement. 

The Shaheen-3 long-range ballistic missile is displayed during a military parade in Islamabad to mark Pakistan's National Day. March 25, 2021 
The Shaheen-3 long-range ballistic missile is displayed during a military parade in Islamabad to mark Pakistan's National Day. March 25, 2021 Photo: AFP 
According to Abdul Aziz Sager, chairman of the Saudi Arabia-based Gulf Research Center, it is not yet time to make a decision on the nuclear issue in the agreement. However, one should not rely solely on US security. Because it also has its limitations. This has become clear from recent events. 

According to the agreement, if one country is attacked, Riyadh and Islamabad will see it as an 'aggression' against both countries. 

Deterring Iran and Israel 

The United States has been cooperating in ensuring the security of Saudi Arabia for a long time. There is no reason to think that their position is being shaken by the agreement with Pakistan regarding Saudi Arabia’s nuclear program. 

Washington is still Saudi Arabia’s main arms supplier. The relationship between Riyadh and Washington on defense cooperation is very strong. From joint initiatives to training in the defense sector, it is difficult for Saudi Arabia to find an alternative to the United States. 

However, due to some recent shortcomings in the security promised by the United States in the Gulf countries, an alternative defense partner for Saudi Arabia has become urgent. 

From Saudi Arabia’s perspective, the country, which lags behind nuclear-armed Israel in strategic and conventional capabilities, is trying to fill the gap through this agreement. 
Hassan Al Hassan, Senior Fellow, International Institute for Strategic Studies 
Despite the US defense system, Qatar could not be prevented from two attacks. Last June, Iran fought a 12-day war with Israel. At that time, Iran launched a missile attack on a US base in Qatar. However, there was no damage. 

Three months later, Israel attacked a building in an elite area of ​​​​Doha, the capital of Qatar. It houses embassies, shopping malls and educational institutions. At least five Hamas members and a Qatari security official were killed. 

Read more 
Saudi Arabia-Pakistan deal could change the nuclear security calculus in the Middle East 
20 September 2025 
Pakistan Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman embrace after signing a defense agreement. In the Saudi capital, Riyadh, 17 September 2025 

An emergency meeting of Arab and Islamic countries was called after the attack in Doha. The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries - Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates - attended the meeting. They also announced that they would activate a joint defense system. 

These events have heightened security concerns in the Gulf states and undermined their confidence in the US security apparatus. As the Gulf states seek to enhance their security, countries such as Pakistan, Egypt and Turkey are naturally emerging as their partners. 

Israel has stepped up its military activity across the Middle East since the start of its indiscriminate attack on Gaza in 2023. Saudi Arabia views such an attitude as a threat, as US President Donald Trump has expressed unwavering support for the country’s actions. 

Smoke is seen rising in the sky after the Israeli attack in Doha. An Israeli military official said their airstrikes targeted senior Hamas leaders. September 9, 2025 
Smoke is seen rising in the sky after the Israeli attack in Doha. An Israeli military official said their airstrikes targeted senior Hamas leaders. September 9, 2025Photo: AFP 
In addition, Saudi Arabia has long said that if its arch-enemy Iran develops nuclear weapons, they will follow the same path. However, it is clear that Saudi Arabia has given this warning to increase pressure on Tehran. 

Hassan al-Hassan, a senior fellow for Middle East policy at the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) in London, said that from Saudi Arabia's perspective, the country, which lags behind nuclear-armed Israel in strategic and conventional capabilities, is trying to fill a gap through this agreement. 

Read more 
How Saudi Arabia is warning Trump 
September 28, 2025 
How Saudi Arabia is warning Trump 
Keeping the Houthis in check in Yemen 

The issue of stable security in the Gulf region is also important for Saudi Arabia. The Iran-backed Houthis came to power in Yemen in 2015. Saudi Arabia has since begun to doubt how long the United States' ability to provide regional security will last. Saudi Arabia's suspicions were somewhat justified by various events that occurred between 2019 and 2022. During this time, the Houthis announced the development of drones and long-range missiles that could hit Saudi Arabia. As a result, they also became a threat to Saudi security. 

In the meantime, in 2019, an attack was carried out on the oil facilities of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, Saudi Aramco. It is said that Iran carried out the attack. But the Houthis accepted responsibility for the attack. It is believed that they made this decision to cover up Tehran's role. After that incident, Saudi Arabia's confidence in the security system provided by the United States decreased. 

According to the agreement, if either country was attacked, Riyadh and Islamabad would view it as an 'aggression' against both countries. 
In 2015, Saudi Arabia invited Pakistan to join the Arab coalition formed to fight the Houthis. But Islamabad did not agree to join the coalition at that time. Ten years later, in September, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan strengthened their naval cooperation. The emphasis was on training and defense coordination. 

The multi-dimensional threat from the Houthis is still active. For this reason, the Saudi mutual defense agreement with Islamabad can also be used to repel pro-Iranian attacks in a wide area from the Gulf region to the Red Sea.

Headline_English: Mamdani takes oath as New York mayor in abandoned subway station
Content_Enlish:
As thousands of New Yorkers gather in Times Square to welcome 2026, newly elected Mayor Zohran Mamdani has announced that he will be sworn in at midnight on December 31 at an abandoned subway station built during America's Gilded Age. The 34-year-old Zohran plans to be sworn in on New Year's Eve at the abandoned station beneath New York City Hall. The station is currently used as a loop for the local 5 train. Mamdani said the unusual location symbolizes the "beginning of a new era." In a statement, Zohran Mamdani said the structure is a monument to a city that once dared to be beautiful and build something big that would change the lives of working people. The event is designed to ensure that ambitions don't become a memory of the past or trapped under the tunnels of City Hall. Those who will serve New Yorkers from the building above (City Hall) will aim to bring back that spirit. 

Zohran added that he is blessed to have the opportunity to lead millions of New Yorkers in this era of new opportunities and is honored to carry forward this great tradition of the city. 

This station is one of the first 28 stations opened in New York in 1904. It was later closed during modernization in 1945. It was recognized as a New York 'Landmark' in 1979 and a National Historic Site in 2004. 

The new Mayor Zohran Mamdani will be sworn in by New York Attorney General Letitia James. Then, at noon local time on Wednesday, local time, there will be another ceremony on the steps of City Hall. There, Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders will administer the oath. A large celebration (block party) will be held on Broadway. 

Attorney General Letitia James said that choosing a subway station was the right choice. Because the train system is a “great equalizer” for New Yorkers. 

“Zohran is our next mayor,” the attorney general said. “Because he understands that no matter what subway line we use, all New Yorkers living next to each other have the right to a city where they can live well.” 

Among the former mayors, only progressive Democrat Bill de Blasio has confirmed that he will attend Zohran Mamdani’s swearing-in ceremony. Michael Bloomberg or Rudy Giuliani have not yet announced anything. Outgoing Mayor Eric Adams has also kept his presence vague. 

Mira Nair and Zohran Mamdani 
Mira Nair and Zohran MamdaniReuters 
Adams said at a news conference on Monday that he wanted to speak with Mamdani to make sure his presence would not cause any “disruption.” Adams indirectly criticized Zohran Mamdani's supporters, saying, "This is a very important and historic day. Unfortunately, he has some supporters who like to protest everything. If he wants, I'll go." 

In response, Zohran Mamdani said that the former mayor is definitely welcome. 

Even before Zohran was sworn in, billionaire Elon Musk criticized his choice of fire department chief. When he appointed Linnea Boncino, a veteran female EMS (emergency medical services) officer (56), as the chief of the Fire Department (FDNY), Musk questioned her lack of experience. 

In response, Mamdani wrote on X (formerly Twitter), "Experience definitely matters. That's why I hired someone who has spent over 30 years in EMS. Remember, EMS personnel handle 70 percent of the calls that come to the fire department. 

Last week, Mayor Eric Adams appointed Mark Guerra, a 37-year veteran, as interim fire chief. 

In this regard, Zohraan said that no other incident can dim Linian's ability. The current mayor has full authority to make decisions until the end of this year.

Headline_English: What 90 percent of the world's travelers haven't seen, you can see by visiting one of these 10 places
Content_Enlish:
When tourists go out, they usually think of conventional places like Paris, Bali or New York. But there are some places in the world where the atmosphere of animals and nature is more powerful than people. The experience of these places will take you to a world that is unprecedented. The places are rich in biodiversity, culture and history. This is our arrangement with a brief introduction to 10 such places. If you go to any of these places, you will see so much that 90 percent of the world's tourists have not seen. 

1. Faroe Islands, Denmark 
View of the port of Torshavn in the Faroe Islands 
View of the port of Torshavn in the Faroe Islands File photo: Reuters 
Sitting quietly in the North Atlantic, the Faroe Islands. This group of 18 volcanic islands between Iceland and Norway has more sheep than tourists every year. The landscape here is so enchanting, you will feel like you have been to an alien planet. 

The waterfalls falling directly into the sea, or the colorful beaked sea ‘puffin’ birds wandering around create a magic for the eyes. Each village here has a population of less than 20 people. You can embrace true solitude by looking at the infinity of the Atlantic from the local Kallur Lighthouse. Traveling to these islands is a bit difficult. 

2 
Svalbard, Norway 
Some scientists are heading towards Kongsfjord in the Arctic region by snowmobile in Svalbard, Norway, April 10, 2023 
Some scientists are heading towards Kongsfjord in the Arctic region by snowmobile in Svalbard, Norway, April 10, 2023 Photo: Reuters 
There are more animals like comets and foxes than people on this Arctic archipelago. It is mandatory to have a rifle in your hand when leaving the island's settlements. 

The sun does not set for four months in summer, and the sun does not rise for four months in winter. The settlements are isolated from one another. Yet 2,500 people live here. This northernmost icy region in the world is truly unique. 

3 
Socotra Island, Yemen 
The dragon blood trees of Yemen's Socotra Island are like upside-down umbrellas 
The dragon blood trees of Yemen's Socotra Island are like upside-down umbrellas File photo: AFP 
Isolated from the Arabian Peninsula for millions of years, this island's ecosystem is very unique. The plants and animals here have little in common with those of other regions of the world. 

The dragon blood trees are like upside-down umbrellas, the desert roses seem to be melting. Arriving here means going to a different world with almost deserted beaches, countless caves and the Socotra people.

4 
Bhutan 
Bhutan, known as the daughter of the Himalayas, has a strange rule for tourists—you have to pay a $250 fee to enter the country, which is one of the largest sources of their national income. The country has sparked a new discussion about per capita happiness. 

Walking the streets of Thimphu, Bhutan, you will feel like you have returned to ancient times. Monks in dark red robes use smartphones. However, there are special laws to protect traditional structures from destruction. Looking at the society here, it seems that they have collectively decided—modernity will come not on the terms imposed by the world, but in their own way. 

5 
Easter Island, Chile 
The mystery of the famous Moai sculptures made of stone on Easter Island has not yet been fully revealed 
The mystery of the famous Moai sculptures made of stone on Easter Island has not yet been fully revealed File photo: Reuters 
Many of us may know about the famous Moai sculptures made of stone. But knowing about Easter Island and going there is a completely different matter. This small volcanic island in the heart of the Pacific Ocean is one of the most isolated settlements in the world. The nearest settlement is about 1,200 miles away. 

To get here from Santiago, Chile, you have to take a five-hour flight. The whole time over the sea. Beyond the Moai sculptures, there is a wonderful Polynesian culture. There are also some ancient craters in the volcano, where you can walk down. The night sky here is so clear that the Magellanic Clouds near the Milky Way Galaxy can be seen with the naked eye. 

6 
Madagascar 
The baobab trees of Madagascar look like they've been buried upside down, August 30, 2019 
The baobab trees of Madagascar look like they've been buried upside down, August 30, 2019Photo: Reuters 
For those who have had an idea of ​​Madagascar from watching animated movies, the country on the east coast of Africa is actually much stranger. About 90 percent of the country's animals and plants are found nowhere else on earth. The baobab trees look like they've been buried upside down. 

The call of a lemur (a type of monkey) is like the sound of a car alarm. There is a stone forest—where you feel like the soles of your shoes are being cut off when you walk. There are also settlements where the residents have never seen a foreigner in their lives. 

7 
Papua New Guinea 
The Pacific country of Papua New Guinea has poor road connectivity 
The Pacific country of Papua New Guinea has poor road connectivity File photo: Reuters 
More than 800 languages ​​- this one feature is enough for a country to be culturally diverse. Papua New Guinea is one such country. The country still has many small populations who have just begun to get acquainted with the outside world. The various festivals, costumes, and facial expressions of these populations show ancient traditions. 

The road connectivity of this Pacific country is poor. To reach many regions, you have to use small planes, which land on grass runways cut in dense jungle. However, the country has a 100% adventurous spirit. 

8 
Greenland 
The world's largest island, Greenland, has a population smaller than many of the world's smallest cities. 80 percent of the island is covered in ice. Traveling from one city to another requires planes, boats, or helicopters. 

Despite these harsh conditions, this island is one of the most stunning and unique places in the world. Many people visit the island to see the Northern Lights dance in the northern sky. Here, in the summer, the sun rotates in a way that never sets. 

9 
Traveling on the Trans-Siberian Railway 
A train runs on the Trans-Siberian Railway. Taiga District, about 90 kilometers southwest of the city of Krasnoyarsk in Siberia, Russia, July 2, 2012 
A train runs on the Trans-Siberian Railway. Taiga district, about 90 kilometers southwest of the city of Krasnoyarsk in Siberia, Russia, July 2, 2012 Photo: Reuters 
Traveling on the Trans-Siberian Railway is very famous. The length of this railway line, which starts from Moscow and extends to Vladivostok, is about 9 thousand kilometers. Along the way, you can see major cities, forests, lakes and jungles of Siberia. It is the longest single railway journey in the world. 

It takes seven to 14 days to cross eight time zones by rail. Along this route, you can see the world's deepest freshwater lake, 'Lake Baikal'. It is said that this rail journey changes people's perspectives. 

10 
Turkmenistan 
Turkmenistan is known as the strangest and most diverse country in Central Asia. The country's former president, Saparmurat Niyazov, renamed the month after his mother. He banned gold teeth and created a gold sculpture of himself, which can turn to face the sun.

Headline_English: For what purpose is Israel recognizing Somaliland, and how much risk does it pose to the Arab world?
Content_Enlish:
Israel has become the first and only member state of the United Nations to officially recognize the breakaway Somaliland Republic, which broke away from Somalia. This may not have come as a surprise to seasoned observers of the region. Israel stirred controversy on Friday (December 26) by recognizing Somaliland as an independent and sovereign country. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Gideon Sarr signed a joint declaration of recognition with Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi. 

Israel’s military presence in Somaliland would effectively turn the region into a “mine of explosives” 
Diya-eddine Said Bamakhrama, Djibouti’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia 
Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991. Three decades later, no country in the world has recognized it. Therefore, the region has always been in a state of diplomatic uncertainty. It was somewhat alleviated by Israel's recognition. 

Abdullahi described Israel's recognition as a 'historic moment'. Israel did not recognize the region that broke away from Somalia out of simple considerations. Rather, careful calculations and risky geopolitical equations worked behind the curtain of recognition. 

Despite not recognizing it, some countries such as the United Kingdom, Ethiopia, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) maintain relations with Somaliland. These countries have liaison offices in the capital, Hargeisa. 

Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi 
Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi File photo: AFP 
By recognizing it, Israel broke decades of international restraint over Somaliland. The country did this knowingly. With this move, Israel has presented itself as the main beneficiary of a self-proclaimed country that has long been demanding its place in the international arena. 

Djibouti’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Dia-Eddine Said Bamakhrama, spoke to Arab News about the recognition of Somaliland by the Zionist state of Israel. According to him, this move could cause profound disaster. 

In Bamakhrama’s words, “A unilateral declaration of independence is not just a legal step or an isolated political event. Rather, it has profound structural effects. Such effects include increasing internal divisions and rivalries among citizens of the same nation, eroding the social and political structure of the state, and opening the door to protracted conflict.” 

Critics believe that Israel has long been lobbying for further division in the region under various guises. 

Many Arab countries see Israel’s recognition of Somaliland as a continuation of a strategy. Israel's strategy is to encourage border separatist movements to weaken strong centralized Arab and Muslim states. 
Many Arab countries believe that recognizing Somaliland is part of a continuation of an old Israeli strategy. Israel's strategy is to encourage border separatist movements to weaken strong centralized Arab and Muslim states. 

The recognition of Somaliland is seen not from a humanitarian perspective, but as a way to undermine efforts at national reconciliation within the framework of Somalia's federal government. 

Djibouti's Ambassador Bamakhrama said that the international community has always taken a position against such steps. Because they have historically prioritized regional stability over the dangers of separatist tendencies and their terrible costs. 

Somaliland is located in a very important geopolitical location 
Somaliland is located in a very important geopolitical location Graphics: AFP 
By recognizing Somaliland, Israel has violated international precedent. Through this, the country has used ‘recognition’ as a tool to break regional unity—such allegations have been made from various quarters. 

Israel has previously supported various non-state forces or separatist groups. They have used this support as an excuse to protect minority groups at risk. For example, the Druze of the Levant (the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, including Syria) and the Maronite community of Lebanon. 

Israel's 'periphery doctrine' has served two purposes at the same time. On the one hand, it has created regional allies for Israel. On the other hand, it has recognized the concept of self-rule for ethnic or religious communities. It also supports the legitimacy of Israel as a Jewish state. 

My country will join the Abraham Accords as a step towards regional and global peace 
Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, President, Somaliland Republic 
However, a clearly different policy is being applied in the case of Somaliland. There is no logic in protecting religious minorities here. Because Somaliland is predominantly a Muslim majority region. The logic here is geopolitical. 

Israel wants to deepen its strategic position in the Middle East and the surrounding region. Because the country is historically isolated in the region. Netanyahu sees the recognition of Somaliland as being in line with the 'spirit of the Abraham Accords'. This means that Israel's main goal is not the population of the self-proclaimed country in the Horn of Africa, but its own security, sea control and intelligence gathering. 

Somaliland citizens celebrate Israel's recognition with their national flag in their hands. In the capital Hargeisa, December 26, 2025 
Somaliland citizens celebrate Israel's recognition with their national flag in their hands. In the capital Hargeisa, December 26, 2025 Photo: AFP 
Israel's first major achievement by recognizing Somaliland is expanding its influence in the diplomatic sphere. Israel claims that Somalia's non-joining the Abraham Accords was acting as an artificial obstacle. Now that has been removed. 

Israel claims that Somaliland, a country of about six million people with independently functioning democratic institutions, was very interested in joining the Abraham Accords. 

Somaliland President Abdullahi said his country would join the Abraham Accords as a “step towards regional and global peace.” However, this peace did not come by chance, but through full exchange, that is, formal recognition. 

Israel can now make various arguments by bringing up the “Somaliland model.” The country may say that many more Arab and Muslim countries are willing to normalize relations with Israel if specific political and territorial interests are met. 

By recognizing Somaliland, Israel’s second major achievement is the possibility of establishing military bases in the Horn of Africa. Somaliland’s strategic location in the Gulf of Aden and the Baba al-Mandab Strait are strategically important. It is quite suitable for monitoring the sea route. 
This argument by Israel has challenged the united position of the Arab League and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The long-standing position of various Arab and Muslim organizations is that relations with Israel cannot be normalized without ending the Palestinian conflict. But now it has become even more fragile. 

Israel's second major achievement by recognizing Somaliland is the possibility of establishing military bases in the Horn of Africa. Somaliland's strategic location in the Gulf of Aden and the Bab al-Mandab Strait is strategically important. It is well suited for monitoring sea routes. 

A man holds a poster of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a protest against Israel's recognition of Somaliland as an independent country. In the Somali capital Mogadishu, December 26, 2025 
A man holds a poster of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a protest against Israel's recognition of Somaliland as an independent country. Mogadishu, Somalia, December 26, 2025 Photo: Reuters 
Israel's presence in Somaliland will increasingly increase the risk. Because Yemen is on a small sea that flows past the region. A large part of Yemen's territory is controlled by the Houthis. The Houthis are an armed group that seeks the "destruction of Israel." 

Israel may claim that its military or intelligence presence in Somaliland will increase maritime security to counter the threat of Houthi attacks. But other countries in the region do not think so. They believe that it could increase tensions. 

Djibouti's ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Bamakhrama, warned that Israel's military presence in Somaliland would effectively turn the region into a "mine of explosives." 

The diplomat said, “If Israel can move forward with its plan to build a military base in the geopolitically sensitive area...it would be a strategic victory for Tel Aviv against the Red Sea countries of Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Yemen, Sudan and Djibouti.” 

The Djiboutian ambassador added that the Red Sea is an important international waterway. Any change in its geopolitical balance would have dire consequences for the region.

Headline_English: Tatiana Schlossberg, 35-year-old granddaughter of John F. Kennedy, dies
Content_Enlish:
Tatiana Schlossberg, granddaughter of the 35th President of the United States, John F. Kennedy, died on Tuesday. She was 35. In an article written last November, Tatiana Schlossberg said she was suffering from a rare form of leukemia. 

Tatiana Schlossberg's family confirmed the news of her death. In a post on the social media account of the John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum, the family wrote, "Our beloved Tatiana passed away this morning. She will forever be in our hearts." 

Tatiana Schlossberg was a journalist who covered climate change and the environment. She is the second child of former US diplomat Caroline Kennedy and designer and artist Edwin Schlossberg. Caroline Kennedy is the daughter of the late US President John F. Kennedy. 

In an article published in The New Yorker last November, Tatiana wrote that she had been diagnosed with a rare genetic mutation, acute myeloid leukemia (AML), a type of cancer of the blood and bone marrow. 

In that article, she also criticized her cousin, U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr., for his skepticism about vaccines and his decision to cut funding for cancer research.

Headline_English: Netanyahu government announces boycott of Israeli newspaper Haaretz
Content_Enlish:
For the first time since the establishment of the state of Israel, the government has announced a boycott of the country's influential newspaper 'Haaretz'. The move was taken on the grounds that the media outlet is supporting the 'enemy' in the Gaza war. 
According to the Israeli army-run radio station 'Galei Jahal', the government has decided to sever ties with Haaretz in both advertising and editorial matters. All ministries, government advertising agencies and state-funded companies have been ordered to cease all contact with the newspaper. 

Iran-Israel conflict changes the Middle East's calculations 

The radio station reported that the boycott was implemented based on a government decision taken in November 2024. As part of this decision, the official accounts of the Israeli army's media offices have also been ordered to sever ties with Haaretz. 

An Israeli government statement said that Haaretz had published editorials during the Gaza war that “undermine the legitimacy of the State of Israel in the international community and its right to self-defense.” 

All ministries, state-run advertising agencies and state-funded companies have been ordered to cease all contact with the newspaper. 

The statement added that “the government will not accept a situation where the publisher of a recognized Israeli newspaper would call for sanctions against the country and support the enemies of the state in the midst of a war.” On this basis, all relations with the newspaper have been severed and it has been announced that it will not issue any official statements.

According to the Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth, the move comes about a month after the country's parliament, the Knesset, passed a bill imposing new restrictions on freedom of expression.
