The Hebrew-language daily reported that the bill, titled "Media Reform," was introduced by Communications Minister Shlomo Karhi. The bill passed the Knesset in a preliminary vote. 

The new law would reduce the powers of Israel's Attorney General Gali Baharov-Miara and further increase the powers of the Rabbinical Court (religious court). However, the Attorney General has opposed the bill, warning that it would pose a serious risk to the image of a free press in Israel.

Headline_English: The Iran-Israel conflict has changed the Middle East's calculus
Content_Enlish:
International diplomats no longer see June 2025 as an ordinary month. In the middle of this month (June 13), Iran and Israel launched a direct, open, and full-scale military strike on each other's territory for the first time. The conflict that had been hidden in the shadows, through proxies, or behind a veil of 'denial' suddenly turned into an open war. In this conflict that lasted only 12 days, no country was occupied, no government was toppled. But the conflict has raised questions about the concept of security in the Middle East and the morality of preemptive strikes. In addition to raising the prospect of nuclear war, the conflict has shaken the regional balance of power in a way that will be felt for many years to come. This is what analysts believe. 
Iran-Israel relations had been unusually tense for several months before the conflict began. The long shadow of the Gaza war still hung over the region. Israel’s regular exchange of fire with Hezbollah on the Lebanese border, Israeli airstrikes on Iranian-backed targets in Syria—all of this was a kind of controlled unrest. Within hours of the Israeli attack, it became clear that Iran would not remain silent. First came the political commentary. Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s office said that the attack “will not go unanswered.” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also said that Iran would exercise its right to self-defense. 
Israel’s political leadership was openly saying that it would no longer allow Iran’s nuclear program to cross a “red line.” Tehran was also insisting that its program was peaceful and that it was ready to respond to any aggression. 

At the same time, the reality inside Iran was full of contradictions. On the one hand, the country was plagued by economic pressure, a water crisis, inflation, and social discontent. On the other hand, the state’s rhetoric against foreign threats was repeatedly focused on ‘deterrence’ and ‘national dignity’. In the midst of this dual reality, the country was heading towards an inevitable conflict. 

Early morning of June 13. Many cities in Iran were still silent. Suddenly, there was a sound in the sky—the buzz of drones, followed by explosions one after another. Within minutes, it became clear that this was not an isolated attack; it was a coordinated, planned strike. 

Israel called their invasion ‘Operation Rising Lion’. The target was Iran’s most sensitive facilities—the Natanz and Fordow nuclear facilities, military bases, laboratories, and the residences of some top military officials. The strike was swift, precise, and terrifying. 

Israel’s so-called rationale was clear: it was preemptive ‘self-defense’. They claimed that Iran had reached the brink of developing nuclear weapons. They carried out the attack to prevent the threat. 

But this claim was immediately questioned. The assessment of international nuclear watchdogs and the United States’ own intelligence analysis said that Iran had not yet reached the stage of developing weapons. Naturally, the question arose: could the fear of the future justify the attack? 

International law recognizes that any country has the right to self-defense. But that right is limited and proven. A preemptive strike cannot be launched without an immediate threat. 
Tehran’s response: not silence, but revenge 
Within hours of the Israeli attack, it became clear that Iran would not remain silent. First came the political commentary. Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s office said that the attack “will not go unanswered.” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also said that Iran would exercise its right to self-defense. 

Then came the real response. Missiles and drones rushed toward Israel. Warning sirens sounded in Tel Aviv, Haifa and surrounding areas. People began running for shelters. The counterattack killed 28 people in Israel. Oil refineries, power plants and parts of military infrastructure were damaged. 

A building in Israel damaged by an Iranian missile attack. Central Israel, June 15, 2025 
A building in Israel damaged by an Iranian missile attack. Central Israel, June 15, 2025 Photo: Reuters 
It was a clear message from Iran - they will take the hit, but not one-sided. A 12-day conflict began; what many analysts call a "controlled war". Neither side used all its strength, but tensions were at their peak every day. 

At least 974 people were killed in Iran. Among them were some of the top members of the military, scientists and civilians. The Israeli attack increased pressure on Iranian cities, overcrowded hospitals, and disrupted electricity and fuel supplies. 

The impact of the attack on Israel was also unexpectedly large. Many inside the country admit that the damage done in 12 days was greater than the total damage caused by the conflict with Hamas or Hezbollah in the past two years. 

The conflict shows that in this era of long-range missiles and drones, geographical distance and security are no guarantees. 

Read more 
How Israel secretly invaded Iran 
June 27, 2025 
How Israel secretly invaded Iran 
Iran's nuclear program and initial damage 
The main target of the Israeli attack was Iran's nuclear facilities. The infrastructure hit at the Natanz and Fordow facilities included integrated laboratories, uranium enrichment units and research centers. Initial assessments of the attack indicate that Iran's nuclear program was immediately damaged, but not completely halted. 

However, scientists have commented that such attacks have motivated Iranian researchers to take steps to prevent destructive attacks and strengthen security. International experts say Iran's nuclear program is now more secretive and secure, and is being reorganized to match its missile capabilities. 
As the conflict began, Israeli media insisted that it had destroyed Iran's "core heartland." But military analysts say the reality is different. While the Israeli airstrikes were effective, they were not completely destructive. Iran's underground facilities and nuclear personnel were largely spared. 

As a result, while Israel has achieved military success, the political and strategic gains have been limited. The Israeli leadership has also realized that while a direct attack may have short-term effects, it has given Iran the opportunity to retaliate in the long term. 

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin NetanyahuPhoto: AFP 
Meanwhile, the United States has been involved diplomatically and militarily since the beginning of the Iran-Israel conflict. The White House had declared that it supported Israel’s “right to self-defense.” But in the second week of June, the United States directly participated in the conflict. 

However, the US move hardened Iran’s diplomatic stance. Tehran’s supreme leader said, “We have no choice but to defend our territorial sovereignty. However, we are not interested in a direct conflict with the United States.” 
Israel had repeatedly deceived the United States by developing nuclear weapons itself. 
Regional powers’ attention 
The conflict was not limited to Iran-Israel or the United States. All the important regional powers—Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, and Qatar—were keeping a close eye on the crisis. 

The Saudi cabinet statement said, “Our main goal is to maintain peace and stability in the Middle East. But each regional power will maintain its own security system.” 

This stance made it possible to prevent the spread of the conflict. No regional power directly participated in the conflict. But political pressure, threats and diplomatic mediation were in full swing. 

US President Donald Trump 
US President Donald Trump File Photo: Reuters 
Scientists have commented that the Israeli attack has inspired Iranian researchers to take steps to prevent destructive attacks and strengthen security systems. Various international experts say that Iran's nuclear program has now become more secretive and secure and is being reorganized in line with its missile capabilities. 
International law and pre-emptive strike debate 
The world's attention was then on international law. Is Israel's policy of 'pre-emptive strike' legal? The United Nations, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and various human rights organizations were involved in the debate on this question. 

Legal analysts explain that international law recognizes that any country has the right to self-defense. But that right is limited and proven. Pre-emptive strikes cannot be carried out without an immediate threat. 

Many countries in the world have criticized both sides in this situation. Countries such as the European Union and Nigeria, in particular, have said that preemptive strikes have disrupted international peace and stability. 

The debate is not only legal but also moral. How much of a potential threat is acceptable as a US-Israeli argument, and how much is a strategic aggression, has become an unresolved question. 

Humanitarian and long-term impact of the conflict 
Although the Iran-Israel conflict lasted only 12 days, its humanitarian toll was terrible. Of the 974 people killed in Iran, 230 were children. Many were injured. Hospitals were severely strained. There were widespread problems with electricity and water supplies. 

The number of people killed in Israel was relatively low—28. But the panic, psychological stress, and infrastructural damage were enormous. Oil refineries, power plants, and transportation networks were partially destroyed. 

Behind such numbers, daily life in both countries was disrupted. Businesses and schools were closed. International aid and humanitarian relief efforts were also limited. 

In the long term, the conflict between the arch-enemies Iran and Israel has ended, but peace has not returned to the Middle East. The conflict has not only caused destruction, but also increased distance and hostility between the two countries, challenging the regional balance of power and complicating questions of international law and morality. 

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei 
Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali KhameneiFile Photo: Reuters 
Experts say Iran will now focus heavily on rebuilding its nuclear program. It will take more covert and powerful security measures aimed at Israel and the United States. 

Regional powers will also reassess their strategies. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates—all will be prepared to deal with the potential spread and diplomatic fallout of the war.

Headline_English: Waiting for the election last year
Content_Enlish:
After the coup, the main discussion since the beginning of 2025 was when the elections would be held? The election date was announced in the very last month of the year. The first half of the year was spent on the implementation of the July Charter and reforms. Finally, the decision to implement the reforms in accordance with the July Charter was made through a referendum. The election date has also been fixed. Another big topic of discussion was when will BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman return to the country? Putting an end to all speculation, he also returned on December 25. However, everything in politics was overshadowed by the departure of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia at the end of the year. Her passing ended a glorious chapter of a housewife turning politician. The public was curious about the political destiny of the young people who led the mass uprising at the beginning of the year. This question was answered with the formation of the National Citizens Party (NCP) last February. When the country began its journey towards elections with the announcement of the schedule on December 11, disaster struck the very next day. Sharif Osman Hadi, a potential independent candidate for Dhaka-8 constituency and convener of the Inqilab Mancha, was shot dead by miscreants. He died on December 18 while undergoing treatment in Singapore. This sparked a wave of anger among his supporters. The movement to arrest and prosecute the murderers continues. 
Politics in 2025 was not limited to the negotiating table. Political parties held various programs, including rallies on the streets, demanding elections and reforms. They also tried to show their strength through these programs. In particular, some Islamist parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami and Islami Andolan Bangladesh, went beyond the BNP circle and held large gatherings in Dhaka. Through this, they signaled that they were reorganizing themselves ahead of the next elections. 
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her government's Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, who were ousted in a mass uprising, were sentenced to death by the International Crimes Tribunal on November 17 for crimes against humanity. The Awami League lost its opportunity to participate in the elections as its activities were banned. The party tried to hold separate rallies at various times, and there have also been allegations of creating panic by exploding cocktails and bombs. All in all, 2025 was a turning point for Bangladeshi politics. Tiredness of old politics, the possibility of new politics, fear of violence and the desire for reform - everything has come together. However, the announcement of the upcoming February 12 elections is the most talked about event. Because the future political trajectory and stability in the country depend on this election. Professor Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government, shows who signed the July Charter from which party. The July Charter signing ceremony was held at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka on October 17. 
Professor Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government, shows who signed the July Charter from which party. The signing ceremony of the July Charter was held at the South Plaza of the National Parliament Building in Dhaka on October 17. File Photo: Prothom Alo 
Consensus Document July Charter, Referendum, Reforms took a big place in the country's politics after the fall of Sheikh Hasina in the July Uprising. The pressure to break the old authoritarian trend and create a new style of politics and state governance increased. The interim government also emphasized reforms. 
On February 15, 2025, the government formed the National Consensus Commission, whose goal was to formulate a consensus-based document, which would be called the July Charter, through dialogue with political parties on reforms in various sectors. Several reform commissions had been formed earlier. The work of these commissions was to prepare proposals for necessary reforms in important sectors of the state, including the electoral system, constitutional framework, administration, judiciary and law and order system. There was a need to coordinate the recommendations of various commissions at one place. In this context, the National Consensus Commission was formed. 

The commission prepared reform proposals after a series of meetings with 30 political parties after about eight months. On October 17, the July National Charter was signed by Professor Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government, and leaders of various political parties. However, there was disagreement among the political parties on the process of implementing these recommendations. The responsibility of making a decision rests with the interim government. On November 13, the government announced that a referendum would be held on the implementation of the reforms, and that it would be held on the day of the national elections. 

Although not all parties were satisfied, the July Charter showed that, along with conflict, the politics of negotiation have not yet completely disappeared. This was a moment in 2025 when politics temporarily cooled down and sat at the negotiating table. 

Leaders of the new party at the launch of the Jatiya Nagorik Party on February 28 at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital 
Leaders of the new party at the launch of the Jatiya Nagorik Party on February 28 at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital File photo: Prothom Alo 
NCP announces new politics 

The Jatiya Nagorik Party (NCP) formed in February was one of the most discussed new political events of 2025. The faces of the youth and civic movement that led the July mass uprising directly emerged on the political stage. The new party made its debut on Manik Mia Avenue in the presence of leaders of various political parties. 

They gave voice to public dissatisfaction with the old parties by demanding a new settlement. Some saw it as a ray of hope, some saw it as an experimental political initiative. 

Throughout the year, the NCP was in the news in various ways. However, there were also rumors of various disagreements within it. The party fell into an internal crisis centered on the upcoming national elections. Many announced their departure due to their alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami. Among them were several important women leaders. The NCP, under the Shapla Kali symbol, was in crisis before it went to participate in the upcoming elections for the first time. After the February 12 elections, it will be understood how much the youth party was able to make a mark on the minds of the people. 

Inqilab Manch held a blockade program at Shahbagh in the capital on December 29, demanding the arrest and trial of the killers of Shaheed Sharif Osman bin Hadi. 
Inqilab Manch held a blockade program at Shahbagh in the capital on December 29, demanding the arrest and trial of the killers of Shaheed Sharif Osman bin Hadi. File Photo: Prothom Alo 
Osman Hadi's murder, heat in politics 

Sharif Osman Hadi was campaigning by announcing that he would be an independent candidate in Dhaka-8 constituency. On December 12, two miscreants riding a motorcycle opened fire on Hadi in the capital's Bijoynagar (Paltan) area. The bullet hit Hadi in the head. Emergency surgery was performed at Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Later, he was transferred to Evercare Hospital, where his condition gradually became critical. On December 15, Osman Hadi was taken to Singapore for advanced treatment. He died on December 18. 

Later, the police said that Faisal Karim Masud, riding a motorcycle, opened fire to kill Osman Hadi. He is the leader of the banned Chhatra League. His associate Alamgir Sheikh was driving the motorcycle. Both of them have fled to India. 

Osman Hadi has been a hot topic of discussion throughout the year since the July coup, with his movement to ban the Awami League and his anti-India statements. When the news of Osman Hadi's death spread, protests spread in various parts of the country, including Dhaka. Among them were attacks, vandalism and arson at the offices of Prothom Alo and the Daily Star. On December 19, lakhs of people attended the funeral of martyr Osman Hadi at Manik Mia Avenue. 

The leaders of the Inquilab Manch announced that the movement will not stop until the killers are arrested. The leaders and activists of the Inquilab Manch have started a sit-in program by blocking Shahbagh in the capital since last Friday. Now the Inquilab Manch is holding an all-out blockade program in divisional cities across the country. 

BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman at the public reception stage after returning to the country on December 25 
BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman at the public reception stage after returning to the country on December 25 File Photo: Prothom Alo 
Tareq Rahman's sensational return 

Although directly involved in politics two decades ago, Tarique Rahman's role in BNP was as an aide to his mother Khaleda Zia. When the previous Awami League government sent Khaleda Zia to prison in a corruption case in 2018, Tarique Rahman took charge of running the party from abroad. He left prison on September 11, 2008, during the caretaker government of the 1-11 era, and went to the UK with his family. After his mother went to prison, Tarique Rahman took over the party as the acting chairman. After that, he led BNP and like-minded parties from abroad in every fight and struggle. 

BNP supporters had been hoping for Tarique Rahman's return since the Awami League was ousted from power in the coup. But no clear announcement was coming. In the end of last November, when Tarique Rahman said that his decision to return to the country was not under his sole control; then various rumors started spreading. 

However, putting an end to all the rumors, Tarique Rahman returned to Dhaka from London on December 25. His return to the country was a grand affair, soaked in the love of a huge number of people. He was welcomed at a huge rally. After 17 years of exile, his presence created new enthusiasm and hope among BNP supporters. BNP is going to participate in the next national parliamentary elections under Tarique's leadership. On the day of his return, he was presented as a possible future Prime Minister of Bangladesh in the domestic and foreign media. 

Tarique Rahman's return is being seen as a clear signal in Bangladeshi politics. Even the long exile could not erode his political influence; on the contrary, his return is providing new resources to BNP's enthusiasm. In addition to strengthening the party's internal organization, a new equation is being created in the political field with the next elections in mind. 

Thousands of supporters mourn the death of three-time Prime Minister and BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia at the end of the year 
Thousands of supporters mourn the death of three-time Prime Minister and BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia at the end of the year File photo: Prothom Alo 
Khaleda Zia's death 

Former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, who was released from prison after the July uprising, became a symbol of national unity. She was given a seat of honor by all parties and opinions. After being imprisoned during the Awami League regime, her illness worsened. Even after her release, she had to go to the hospital occasionally. When her illness worsened, she was admitted to Evercare Hospital on November 23. When her condition became critical, a plan was made to take her abroad, and an air ambulance was arranged. But as she could not afford to travel, she continued her treatment in the country. However, all efforts failed and Khaleda Zia said goodbye forever on December 30. 

Khaleda Zia's illness was not only political news but also became a national emotion. The government sought prayers for her recovery. After her death, the entire country was in mourning. The government declared three days of state mourning and one day of general holiday. 

Despite her sudden entry into politics after the death of her husband Ziaur Rahman, Khaleda Zia has made her later life colorful with a path of struggle. Analysts say that although Ziaur Rahman formed the BNP party, its mass base was created through Khaleda Zia. Khaleda Zia took oath as the country's first female prime minister in the 1991 elections with the title of uncompromising leader. After that, she took over as the head of the government again in 2001. 

In 2007, Khaleda Zia had to go to prison during the military-backed caretaker government. Then, after the Awami League came to power, different levels of torture came down on Khaleda Zia. First, she was evicted from her husband's house on Mainul Road in the cantonment, which was associated with her memory. Then her political activities were curtailed by blocking her house and office, and finally she was sentenced in a corruption case and sent to prison. 

However, Khaleda Zia faced these situations with determination. In the past year, everyone in charge of running the state had looked to her as a symbol of unity. As a result, just as the BNP is calling her death the end of an era, the political arena is seeing a huge void, especially in these uncertain times.

Headline_English: They were walking to remember their love for the leader, their contributions to the country, and to witness history.
Content_Enlish:
It was 12:40 p.m. on the clock. When I started walking from Karwan Bazar in the capital towards Manik Mia Avenue, I was accompanied by thousands of people. Everyone had the same destination—Manik Mia Avenue; the funeral venue of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia. Thousands of people from different areas of the capital were walking forward to attend Khaleda Zia's funeral. People from outside Dhaka were also joining this queue. People from all walks of life, regardless of party affiliation, were running to bid the former prime minister a final farewell. 

As I moved forward along Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, the presence of people increased. People on both sides of the main road, people on the footover bridge, people on the roofs of various buildings along the road—Dhaka city seemed to be turning into a city of mourning. No one was shouting slogans, no one was giving instructions, yet everyone was going in the same direction. A silent order, which is born only from mourning. 

The National Parliament Building area became crowded on the occasion of Khaleda Zia's funeral. This Wednesday afternoon 
The National Parliament Building area became crowded on the occasion of Khaleda Zia's funeral. This Wednesday afternoon Photo: Prothom Alo 
Not all of the thousands of people running towards the funeral venue were BNP leaders and activists. There were also ordinary professionals among them. Some of them were walking five kilometers, some seven kilometers. While walking, I spoke to Amirul Islam, a private sector employee. He started walking from Shahbagh area. Amirul said, 'I am not into politics. But a leader has endured so much torture in her life for the people of the country. I will walk a few kilometers to attend her funeral, what is the difficulty in that?' 

The more I move towards Manik Mia Avenue, the denser the crowd becomes. As I reach the Farmgate intersection, I have to slow down my walking speed. People and people in front. Some in groups, some alone. Many have hats on their heads. Some have Bangladesh flags in their hands—everyone's goal is to move forward. 

Adnan, an eighth-grade student, came to attend the funeral holding his elder brother's hand. They tried to push forward through the crowd, but they failed. Adnan told Prothom Alo, "I really wanted to stand at the front and attend the funeral. But I don't think I can go." Not only Adnan, but almost everyone was trying to move forward towards Manik Mia Avenue. However, most of them were failing. At that time, BNP activist Riazul Islam from Nilphamari was trying to move forward. He also failed. He lost his companion in the crowd. Despite repeated attempts to reach him on the phone, he could not reach him. Riazul told Prothom Alo, "I left last night and reached Dhaka around 11 pm. I am walking from Karwan Bazar to bid farewell to the leader for the last time." 

Lakhs of people attended Khaleda Zia's funeral. Today, Wednesday afternoon 

Lakhs of people attended Khaleda Zia's funeral. Today, Wednesday afternoon photo: Prothom Alo 
At one stage, unable to move forward, people started sitting in queues on both sides of the main road. Some spread out mats they had brought in advance, while others spread out newspaper pages and sat on the main road. In the meantime, it was time for Zuhr prayers, and many people were scattered on the road and offered prayers. 

At one stage, the crowd spread beyond the road and spread to Farmgate, where the elevated expressway descends. Unable to find space on the road, a large number of people got on the elevated expressway. At that time, I spoke to Ferdous Navid, a student of North South University. He told Prothom Alo, "I went to Gulshan in the morning to see Khaleda Madam. From there, I left for Manik Mia Avenue. However, I got stuck at the descent part of the expressway." 

People also stood in queues at Karwan Bazar in the capital to attend Khaleda Zia's funeral. This Wednesday afternoon, people stood in queues at the capital's Karwan Bazar to attend Khaleda Zia's funeral. This Wednesday afternoon, photo: Prothom Alo 
From a distance, Khaleda Zia's voice was heard on the microphone, 'I have no address outside the country, this is my address. This country, the soil and people of this country are my everything. So I will not go outside the country.' Khaleda Zia was a housewife. BNP founder and then President Ziaur Rahman was killed by some deviant members of the army on May 30, 1981. BNP fell into the abyss due to a conspiracy by the leadership. In such a situation, Khaleda Zia joined the BNP on January 3, 1982. First, she became the party's senior vice chairman, then acting chairman and finally chairperson. She was under forty at the time. 

After joining politics in 1982, Khaleda Zia joined the movement against dictator Ershad in 1983. A 7-party unity alliance was formed under her leadership. She became known as an 'uncompromising leader' in the 9-year anti-dictatorship movement. After the mass movement of the 1990s, the BNP came to power in the 1991 parliamentary elections with unprecedented public support. Khaleda Zia became the first female prime minister in the country's history. She later became prime minister twice more. 

The funeral site turned into a sea of ​​people. Today, Wednesday afternoon, Manik Mia Avenue in the capital 

The funeral site turned into a sea of ​​people. Today, Wednesday afternoon, Manik Mia Avenue in the capitalPhoto: Prothom Alo 
A stream of people formed in the funeral site area to pay their last respects to the former prime minister. Despite many efforts, it was not possible to move further than Tejgaon College in Farmgate. Many people were turning back because they could not find a place. A terrible situation began due to the impact of that wave. Some were trying to move forward, some were coming back. Two old men lost their way in the intense crowd. In that situation, one of them said that they were both residents of the Kanthalbagan area. They were once colleagues in government service, and are now both retired. They had come to witness history by attending Khaleda Zia's funeral. However, they were in a bit of a bind due to the huge crowd. 

When they started to turn back towards Karwan Bazar after pushing through the crowd, an unforgettable scene came to their eyes. Thousands of people were standing in a queue on the road. They were waiting for the instructions to start the funeral broadcast on the microphone. 

Many broke down in tears after attending Khaleda Zia's funeral 

Many broke down in tears after attending Khaleda Zia's funeral Photo: Prothom Alo 
Khaleda Zia's political life is about 43 years. After coming to politics from a housewife, she gradually became a strong, courageous leader. She kept the BNP united in times of trouble. 

Looking back, it seemed that this gathering was not just for a party leader, but also an expression of love from people of all classes and professions for a former leader of the country.

Headline_English: Fascist Hasina will never be freed from responsibility for this death: Nazrul Islam Khan
Content_Enlish:
BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia's death will never be acquitted by fascist Sheikh Hasina, said Nazrul Islam Khan, a member of the party's standing committee. He said that Khaleda Zia never bowed her head before any evil force at home or abroad. Those who sent her (Khaleda Zia) to jail, those who made her homeless, could not eat cooked food, they were forced to flee. Nazrul Islam Khan said this before Khaleda Zia's funeral at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital on Wednesday afternoon. 
BNP Standing Committee Member Nazrul Islam Khan said that the leader fell seriously ill due to lack of proper treatment while being imprisoned in a dark prison for more than two years from February 8, 2018, as a victim of fascist Hasina's personal vendetta in a false case. The entire country is witness, she entered the prison on foot. But she came out of the solitary prison with extreme illness. According to doctors at home and abroad, her illness has worsened due to not being given the opportunity to go abroad for treatment for four years under house arrest. As a result, this invincible leader finally had to give in to death. Therefore, fascist Hasina will never be free from the responsibility of this death. Nazrul Islam Khan spoke before Khaleda Zia's funeral at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital. December 31 
Nazrul Islam Khan spoke before Khaleda Zia's funeral at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital. December 31 Photo: BNP Media Cell 
Nazrul Islam Khan mentioned that Khaleda Zia's personal popularity, organizational ability and inflexibility in the interests of the country made her political opponents fail to confront her politically and started considering her as a personal enemy. He said, the leader was imprisoned during the dictatorship of Sheikh Hasina, the dictatorship of Hussain Muhammad Ershad, and even during the so-called 1/11 government. Fascist Hasina simply ousted the leader from her martyred husband's memorial house to exact revenge and sentenced her to 17 years in prison on false charges. Yet, she did not compromise with the hegemonic politics; she did not compromise on the issue of freedom of expression or the right to vote. As a result, she became an eternal inspiration for the fight against the fascist regime. 

Crowds of people at Khaleda Zia's funeral 
Pictures of crowds at Khaleda Zia's funeral: Prothom Alo 
Nazrul Islam Khan said, 'Today, the leader is free from all charges and is in front of us at the funeral today, soaked in the respect and love of millions of people. On the other hand, those who sent her to jail, those who made her homeless, could not eat the cooked food, were forced to flee. A death warrant is hanging over their heads. Ershad had to serve a long prison sentence, and key figures in the 1/11 government were also forced to flee the country. 

Nazrul Islam Khan also mentioned that Khaleda Zia accepted the membership of the BNP on January 3, 1982, in order to keep the morale of the party and party leaders intact. He said that this marked the beginning of Khaleda Zia's tireless journey in political life. Gradually, despite being the wife of the party's founder and upholding the party's constitution, she assumed the responsibilities of the party's vice chairperson, acting chairperson, and then elected chairperson in the party council. Out of her 43-year political career, she led BNP, one of the country's major political parties, as the top leader for 41 years, organizing and strengthening the party. 

At the end of the year, countless supporters mourn the death of three-time Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Khaleda Zia. 
At the end of the year, countless supporters mourn the death of three-time Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Khaleda Zia. File photo: Prothom Alo 
Nazrul Islam Khan said that after fighting continuously against the dictator Ershad for 9 years, she brought BNP back to power through free, fair and impartial elections in 1991. She was given the status of an 'uncompromising national leader' by the nation. The ever-uncompromising national leader never bowed her head in front of any evil force at home or abroad to protect the interests of the country and its people. No temptation, conspiracy or threat could force her to choose the path of compromise until the end of her life. She has always stood by the people of the country. 

Stating that Khaleda Zia used to say, 'We have friends abroad, but no god', Nazrul Islam Khan said that she has taken one groundbreaking program after another for the welfare of the people. Her success in achieving development and prosperity made Bangladesh known to the world as an 'Emerging Tiger'. 

Nazrul Islam Khan, who was elected Prime Minister three times, said that she had contested as many seats as a person can in every national election. She had contested five seats in the elections and only three in 2008 and won all the seats. With the genuine support of the people and by a huge margin, the shame of defeat in the elections has failed to touch her repeatedly. Such an example of popularity is rare not only in Bangladesh but also in the world. She was the first woman Prime Minister of Bangladesh and the second woman Prime Minister in the Muslim world. 

Nazrul Islam Khan said that she fought to re-establish democracy out of love for democracy. Because she took the initiative to implement democracy after receiving the responsibility, democracy-loving people at home and abroad honored her as the 'Mother of Democracy'. Her programs for development and prosperity were numerous. The stipend system for the promotion of women's education and the 'Food for Education' program and the establishment of separate ministries for the welfare of freedom fighters and expatriates were among her works. 

Khaleda Zia took oath as Prime Minister for the third time after winning the election in 2001. 
Khaleda Zia took oath as Prime Minister for the third time after winning the election in 2001. 
Nazrul Islam Khan said that during the Great Liberation War, Begum Khaleda Zia, along with her two sons, spent time in captivity at the hands of the Pakistani forces from July 2, 1971 until victory was achieved. Her husband declared independence and served as a sector and force commander in the Liberation War. As a result, Khaleda Zia was captured by the Pakistanis along with her two sons. The contribution of this family in the Great Liberation War is a unique example. 

Nazrul Islam Khan said that Khaleda Zia is leaving with the respect, love and prayers of the entire countrymen, regardless of party affiliation. She left behind an example of a noble woman, a struggling politician, and a patriotic statesman with a unique career; which will be an example to follow for future generations of political leaders and activists. 

Nazrul Islam Khan said, "National leader Khaleda Zia used to say, "I have no address outside the country. Bangladesh is my address. This country, its soil and people are my everything." She breathed her last on the soil of this country. Today, she will lie down next to her martyred husband on the soil of this country forever. Insha Allah, we will move forward under the leadership of Mr. Tarique Rahman. Like the national leader, with the goal of the welfare of the people on the path of democracy, peace, development and prosperity. May Allah Almighty help us.’ 

Khaleda Zia’s funeral was attended by Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus, BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman and others 
Khaleda Zia’s funeral was attended by Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus, BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman and others Photo: BNP Facebook page 
BNP Standing Committee Member Nazrul Islam Khan thanked the Chief Advisor, members of the Advisory Council, political leaders, and officials including the chiefs of the three services for their presence. He also thanked the armed forces, BGB, police, and RAB, as well as everyone involved in law and order.

Headline_English: Hannan Masud's father files nomination for seat, becomes BSP's candidate
Content_Enlish:
In the 13th National Parliament Election, the nomination of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) candidate and the party's senior joint chief coordinator Abdul Hannan Masud has been submitted by his father Amirul Islam Md. Abdul Malek. He has submitted his nomination papers for the Bangladesh Supreme Party (BSP), which has suddenly come into discussion before the 12th election in 2024. The symbol of this party is Ektaara. 

Amirul Islam submitted his nomination papers at the office of the District Returning Officer last Monday. On the same day, his son Hannan Masud submitted his nomination papers as the NCP's party candidate for the Noakhali-6 (Hatia) constituency. Earlier, last Sunday, the announcement of the electoral agreement between the NCP, LDP and AB Party with the eight-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami was made. Although there was talk that Jamaat-e-Islami would support Hannan Masud in this seat as part of the alliance, Jamaat candidate Shah Mohammad Mahfzul Haque has also submitted his nomination. Hannan's father has also become a candidate. All in all, this has created curiosity among voters. 

In July 2023, BSP suddenly came into discussion as a political party. That month, the Election Commission announced its decision to register the party. Then, on July 22, the party held its first rally on the streets. At this rally, the party's chairman, Shahzada Syed Saifuddin Ahmed Maizbhandari, said, "The caretaker government system is contradictory to the country's constitution and is insulting to politicians." In addition, the party was accused of showing family property as a party office. Despite this, the party received registration in August of that year. There were allegations that the Awami League had been involved with the party since it received registration. In September that year, the Awami League government's Liberation War Affairs Minister AKM Mozammel Haque, Information and Broadcasting Minister Hasan Mahmud and five other MPs spoke at the party's rally. The party also participated in the 12th parliamentary elections in 2024. However, the party chairman lost his deposit. 

The party has become active again on the occasion of the upcoming elections. On August 30 this year, the 'Greater Sunni Alliance' was launched, consisting of 3 registered political parties with Sunni ideology. The BSP is in this alliance. The other two are Bangladesh Islamic Front and Islamic Front Bangladesh. Islamic speaker Gias Uddin Taheri recently said that candidates will be fielded from this alliance in all 300 seats. He is the central organizing secretary of the Sufi organization Bangladesh Ahle Sunnat Wal Jamaat. 

NCP leader Hannan Masud admitted to submitting his father's nomination papers. He claimed that his father was a 'dummy candidate'. He told Prothom Alo on Wednesday afternoon that he had initially been nominated. There are more such dummy candidates. They will withdraw when they withdraw.’ 

Hannan Masud’s father Amirul Islam Md. Abdul Malek’s mobile phone was called several times to get his statement on this issue, but he did not pick up. Later, Supreme Party Chairman Syed Saifuddin Maizbhandari told Prothom Alo that Hannan Masud’s father has been a follower of their party for a long time. There are many followers of their party in Hatia. That is why he has been nominated by the party. 

Others in this seat 

According to the District Returning Officer’s office, in Noakhali-6 constituency, apart from his son Abdul Hannan Masud, his father Amirul Islam Md. Abdul Malek, 12 more people have become candidates. They are Bangladesh Nationalist Party BNP’s Md. Mahbuber Rahman, Independent (BNP rebel) Tanvir Uddin (former general secretary of Upazila BNP), Jatiya Party's ATM Nabi Ullah, Independent (BNP rebel) Mohammad Fazlul Azim (former member of parliament and former president of Upazila BNP), Independent Shamima Azim (wife of Fazlul Azim), Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD)'s Mohammad Abdul Motaleb, Gana Odhikar Parishad's Mohammad Azahar Uddin, Jamaat-e-Islami's Shah Mohammad Mahfuzul Haque, Jatiya Party's Nasim Uddin Md. Bayezid, Islami Andolan Bangladesh's Md. Nurul Islam Sharif, Liberal Democratic Party's Mohammad Abul Hossain, Independent Muhammad Nurul Amin. 

When asked, Returning Officer and District Administrator Muhammad Shafiqul Islam told Prothom Alo, 'There is no legal obstacle to two candidates from the same family being candidates. In that case, there is no scope for cancelling the nomination papers of any candidate without a specific reason in the selection process. 

It is worth noting that 88 candidates have collected nomination papers for the six parliamentary constituencies of Noakhali. Of these, 62 candidates have submitted them. The nomination paper selection process will continue from December 30 to January 4. The last date for withdrawal of candidacy is January 20. Symbols will be allotted on January 21. The formal campaign will start from January 22 and will continue till 7:30 am on February 10. The administration is on the highest alert to make the election peaceful, fair and acceptable.

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia: 1946-2025
Content_Enlish:
1946 
Born on August 15 in Jalpaiguri. Khaleda Zia is the third of three daughters and two sons of Iskander Majumder and Begum Taiba Majumder. 
1951 
Started her school life at a mission school called St. Joseph Convent in Dinajpur. 
1960 
Married to the then army captain Ziaur Rahman on August 5. 
1965 
Born on November 20, her first child, Tarique Rahman. Arafat Rahman was born on August 12, 1970. 
1971 
When the Liberation War began, Khaleda Zia went into hiding with her two children. She was in Chittagong. At one point, she was forced to come to Dhaka. On July 2, Pakistani soldiers captured Khaleda Zia along with her two sons from a house in Siddheshari, Dhaka. She was imprisoned in Dhaka Cantonment until December 15 of that year. 
Khaleda Zia with her husband, President Ziaur Rahman, in 1979. Khaleda Zia entered politics after the death of Ziaur Rahman in 1981. She was the Chairperson of the BNP until her death. 
Khaleda Zia with her husband President Ziaur Rahman in 1979. Khaleda Zia entered politics after the death of Ziaur Rahman in 1981. She was the Chairperson of the BNP until her death. Photo: Md. Lutfar Rahman Binu, from the book 'Gontantrar Sangram' 
1981 
The then President Ziaur Rahman was assassinated by some deviant army officers on May 30. Khaleda Zia lost her husband. 
1982 
Khaleda Zia accepted the BNP party membership in January at the request of leaders and activists. 
1984 
She was elected the Acting Chairperson of the BNP in April and the Chairperson unopposed in August. 
Khaleda Zia with her son Tarique Rahman at the BNP office in 1987. Tarique Rahman is now the Acting Chairman of the BNP. 
Khaleda Zia with her son Tarique Rahman at the BNP office in 1987. Tarique Rahman is now the acting chairman of the BNP. Photo: Md. Lutfar Rahman Binu, from the book 'Gontantrer Sangram' 
1987 
Khaleda Zia became the leader of the anti-Ershad movement on the streets. She started a one-phase movement of 'Ershad Hatao'. 
Before the parliamentary elections in 1991, Khaleda Zia traveled all over the country to campaign. 
Before the parliamentary elections in 1991, Khaleda Zia traveled all over the country to campaign. Photo: Md. Lutfar Rahman Binu, from the book 'Gontantrer Sangram' 
1991 
Khaleda Zia contested five seats in the fifth national parliamentary election and won all of them. BNP won 140 seats and formed a government with Jamaat-e-Islami (18 seats). Khaleda Zia became the country's first female prime minister. 
1996 
In the one-sided election of the sixth National Parliament (February 15), BNP won 278 seats. Khaleda Zia became the Prime Minister again. That government lasted 12 days. 
In 2001, Khaleda Zia took oath as the Prime Minister for the third time after winning the election. 
In 2001, Khaleda Zia took oath as the Prime Minister for the third time after winning the election. Photo: Md. Lutfar Rahman Binu, from the book ‘Ganatantrar Sangram’ 
2001 
In the eighth National Parliament election, the BNP-led four-party unity coalition won by winning 216 seats. BNP won 193 seats. Khaleda Zia became the Prime Minister for the third time. 
2007 
Khaleda Zia was arrested on September 3 during the caretaker government on charges of corruption. Her two children were also arrested. BNP called the charges against them baseless. 
2008 
Khaleda Zia was released on September 11 on the orders of the High Court. The caretaker government wanted to send her abroad, but she refused. On December 29 of that year, a four-party unity coalition led by Khaleda Zia participated in the ninth parliamentary elections. It won 32 seats. 
2010 
On November 13, the then Awami League government evicted Khaleda Zia from her Dhaka Cantonment house. She had been living in that house for 28 years. 
2014 
The 18-party alliance led by Khaleda Zia boycotted the unilateral and scandalous 10th parliamentary elections on January 5. 
2015 
On January 24, Khaleda Zia lost her youngest son Arafat Rahman. He died of a heart attack while in Malaysia. 
2018 
During the Awami League government (February 8), Khaleda Zia was sentenced to five years in prison in the Zia Orphanage Trust case (later acquitted). She was sent to prison. BNP participated in the 11th parliamentary elections held on December 30. However, the BNP won 7 seats in the election known as the 'night vote'. 
2020 
On March 25, the government's executive order suspended Khaleda Zia's sentence. She returned home from the hospital. However, her political activities were banned. 
2024 
The Awami League government was ousted from power on August 5 in the July mass uprising. Khaleda Zia was released on August 6 by executive order. 
2025 
On January 7, Khaleda Zia went to the UK for treatment and returned on May 6. 
On January 15, she was acquitted in the Zia Orphanage Trust case. 
On November 23, she was admitted to Evercare Hospital in the capital while ill. 
On December 25, Khaleda Zia's eldest son and acting chairman of the BNP, Tarique Rahman, returned to the country from the UK after 17 years. 
On December 30, Khaleda Zia died while undergoing treatment. A glorious political life came to an end.

Headline_English: Chittagong University admission test begins on January 2, various instructions for students
Content_Enlish:
The first year undergraduate (honors) admission test for the 2025-26 academic year at Chittagong University will start from next Friday (January 2, 2026). The admission test will start with the 'A' unit exam. Some instructions have been given for the information of the candidates and concerned persons who wish to participate in the admission test. These are— 

1. Candidates must confirm their respective seats by 10:30 am. Candidates will be able to enter the examination center after showing the admit card. No candidate will be allowed to enter the examination hall after 11:00 am. 

2. As per the instructions on the admit card, candidates can log in to the admission website and know the location of their respective seats 48 hours before the admission test of the concerned unit/sub-unit. Before viewing the seat plan, the admit card must be downloaded. 

3. Each candidate must bring a downloaded copy of the admit card and the original registration card of the Higher Secondary/equivalent examination or the original copy of the 'A' level Statement of Entry (if applicable) on the day of the admission test.

4. Candidates will be able to use a general-purpose calculator (without Memory Option/SIM) of Fx-100 or below in the examination hall. It is completely prohibited for candidates to carry mobile phones, smartwatches, Bluetooth and any other devices that can be communicated with in the examination hall. However, it is completely prohibited for candidates to carry and use calculators in the examination hall for B Unit and B1, B2 and D1 sub-unit admission exams. 

5. Admission candidates, their guardians and all concerned are requested not to be misled by any kind of propaganda on social media including Facebook. 

6. Guardians accompanying the candidates are requested to carry their national identity cards or their own identity cards (if any) with them at all times for the safety of the candidates.
