Admission exam in three divisions— 
Admission exam will be held in Chittagong, Dhaka and Rajshahi on the same date and time. However, the exam for B1, B2 and D1 sub-units will be held only on the Chittagong University campus. Applicants will have to select the center they want to take the exam at while applying. 

This year, the university will conduct the exam against 4,305 seats. Out of this, 3,786 are general seats and the remaining 519 are allocated for quota. Last year, there were 4,684 seats. Out of this, 4,111 are general seats and the remaining seats are allocated for quota. This year, 54 seats are being allocated for the pet quota. 

Exam schedule— 
The admission exam will start on January 2 with the exam for ‘A’ unit. Apart from this, the exam for ‘D’ unit will be held on January 3, ‘C’ unit on January 9 and ‘B’ unit on January 10. On the other hand, the exams for ‘D-1’, ‘B-1’ and ‘B-2’ sub-units will be held on January 5, January 7 and January 8. 

Distribution of exams – 
The admission test for all units will be of a total of 120 marks. Out of this, 100 marks will be in the multiple-choice admission test and the remaining 20 marks will be added from the GPA of SSC and HSC. Zero decimal 25 marks will be deducted for each wrong answer. The minimum pass mark in the exam for all units except ‘D-1’ sub-unit will be 40. The minimum pass mark in the ‘D-1’ sub-unit exam will be 35. 

In the admission test for ‘A’ unit, 25 marks will be in English, 25 marks each in Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology (students will have to answer any three subjects). In the admission test for ‘B’ unit, 30 marks will be in Bengali or optional English, 30 marks in English, and 40 marks in general knowledge. To pass, a minimum of 7 marks in Bengali, 6 marks in English and 13 marks in general knowledge will be obtained separately. 

In the admission test for ‘B-1’ sub-unit, there will be 25 marks in Bengali or optional English, 25 marks in English, and 50 marks in general knowledge. Apart from this, a minimum of 5 marks in Bengali, 6 marks in English, and 17 marks in general knowledge will be obtained separately. In ‘B-2’ unit, there will be 60 marks in Bengali or optional English, 20 marks in English, Arabic, Islamic Studies, Buddhist Studies, and Pali, and general knowledge (any two subjects must be answered). Apart from this, a minimum of 5 marks in Bengali, 5 marks in English, Arabic and Islamic Studies, Buddhist Studies, and Pali, and 9 marks in general knowledge will be obtained separately. 

In ‘C’ unit, there will be 40 marks in English, 30 marks in analytical skills, and 30 marks in problem solving. Apart from this, 13 marks in English, 10 marks in analytical skills, and problem solving will be obtained separately. In ‘D’ unit, there will be 30 marks in Bengali or optional English, 30 marks in English, 20 marks in analytical skills, and 20 marks in general knowledge, mathematics, or economics. In the 'D-1' sub-unit, there will be 30 marks in Bengali or optional English, 30 marks in English, 25 marks in general knowledge, and 15 marks in principles of games and sports.

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia's death: Classes, exams in educational institutions closed today due to government holiday
Content_Enlish:
Classes and examinations will be closed in all educational institutions in the country today (December 31, 2025) due to the announcement of a government holiday. The government has issued a notification in this regard on Tuesday, declaring a one-day government holiday by executive order on the death of former Prime Minister and BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia. The notification of the Ministry of Public Administration on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) said, "In accordance with the 37th serial number of the Ministry of Public Administration's Allocation of Business Among the Different Ministries and Divisions (Schedule One of the Rules of Business, 1996) Revised Up to April 2017, the government has declared a one-day government holiday by executive order on Wednesday, December 31, in the death of former Prime Minister and BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia. All government, semi-government, autonomous, semi-autonomous and private offices will be closed during the holiday. 
Dhaka University announces 3-day mourning 
Dhaka University has announced three days of mourning from Tuesday to Thursday to show respect and dignity to Khaleda Zia. All classes and examinations of the university will be suspended for these three days. The Dhaka University flag has been kept at half-mast as part of the mourning period. 

New date for postponed examination for the recruitment of assistant teachers announced 
Classes and examinations closed at Jahangirnagar University 
Expressing deep grief over the death of Khaleda Zia, the Jahangirnagar University administration announced the closure of all administrative activities, classes and examinations on Tuesday. 

Chittagong University closes educational activities 
Chittagong University will observe three days of mourning from December 31, 2025 to January 2, 2026 for the death of Khaleda Zia. As announced by the government, all educational and administrative activities of Chittagong University will be closed under the general holiday today, Wednesday. 

Junior Scholarship Exam for Wednesday postponed, new date announced 
Junior Scholarship Exam postponed 
Wednesday's Junior Scholarship Exam has been postponed. At the same time, the date of the postponed exam has also been announced. The exam will be held on January 5, 2026.

Headline_English: Two 'terrorist' groups exchange fire at Rohingya refugee camp, killing young man
Content_Enlish:
A gunfight broke out between two 'terrorist' groups at the Jadimora (Camp-26) Rohingya refugee camp in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar. A young man named Nur Kamal was shot dead during the incident. The gunfight took place in the I block of the refugee camp early Saturday morning. 
The deceased Nur Kamal is the son of Abul Kalam, a resident of C block of the refugee camp. He was rescued from the scene in an injured condition and taken to a private medical center in the refugee camp, where doctors declared him dead. 

There has been panic in the refugee camp since the shooting incident. In this situation, law enforcement agencies have strengthened security. About 36,000 Rohingya live in the refugee camp. 

Teknaf Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md. Saiful Islam said that a gunfight broke out between two terrorist groups over control of the refugee camp. A terrorist named Nur Kamal died in the shooting. There are 11 cases against him at Teknaf Police Station on various charges including murder, kidnapping, robbery, and drugs. 

OC Md. Saiful Islam further said that the body has been recovered and sent to the Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy. Law enforcement agencies are conducting operations in the refugee camp to catch the terrorists. The situation in the refugee camp is normal. 

Mohammad Kausar Sikder, captain of the 16th Armed Police Battalion (APBN), which is in charge of security in the refugee camp, said, "The slain Nur Kamal is a recognized terrorist. Nur Kamal, who formed a force in his own name, was committing various crimes in the Rohingya refugee camp and surrounding areas." 

Quoting local people, captain Kausar Sikder said that there had been a long-standing dispute between Nur Kamal and the Khaleeq group over dominance in the refugee camp. There have been incidents of shooting and clashes between them. Nur Kamal was killed by bullets and sharp weapons during this time.

Headline_English: Young man beaten to death on suspicion of theft in Kurigram
Content_Enlish:
According to police and local sources, the young man was suspected of having come to the Farajipara area late on Friday night to steal. At that time, local people caught him. Later, an agitated crowd beat him up and he died on the spot. On Saturday morning, after receiving information, the police went to the spot and recovered the body. The police have detained three people for questioning in this incident. They are currently in the custody of Kurigram Sadar Police Station. 

OC Jahangir Alam told Prothom Alo this afternoon that the name and identity of the deceased young man has not yet been identified. The body has been photographed and sent to various police stations. It is believed that the deceased may be a resident of the neighboring Nageshwari Upazila. The body is being brought to the police station and legal action will be taken after investigating the matter, he added.

Headline_English: First bone marrow transplant in Bogra claims success
Content_Enlish:
The TMSS Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplant Center in Bogra, outside Dhaka, has claimed the first successful bone marrow transplant. This information was given at a press conference at Hotel Mom Inn in Bogra on Friday afternoon. 

Earlier, the TMSS Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplant Center was officially inaugurated on the evening of December 24. Just two weeks after the inauguration, TMSS founder and executive director Hosne Ara Begum announced the successful bone marrow transplant. 

According to TMSS Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplant Center sources, 60-year-old Md. Mizanur Rahman from Bhandabari area of ​​Rangpur was admitted there immediately after the official inauguration. His disease was diagnosed on February 12, 2024. In December of the same year, he was admitted to a private hospital in the capital. After tests in August last year, the doctors decided to do a stem cell transplant for him. In that sequence, his bone marrow transplant was successfully performed at the TMSS Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplant Center. It was completed under the supervision of the head of the center, Professor Abu Zafar Mohammad Saleh. 

Patient Mizanur Rahman said, "I wanted to give up on treatment at one point, thinking about the suffering and expense. After admission to TMSS, the doctors successfully performed a bone marrow transplant. I am dreaming of living healthy again." 

TMSS Deputy Executive Director Md. Matiur Rahman, TMSS Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplant Center Chief Consultant Abu Zafar Mohammad Saleh, and TMSS Medical College Principal Zakir Hossain, along with other concerned persons, were present at the press conference. 

Matiur Rahman said, for the first time, a bone marrow transplant was successfully performed in North Bengal outside Dhaka. This is not only an achievement of the TMSS Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplant Center; but also a historical milestone in healthcare in the northern region. Through this success, they want to convey the message of improved and quality healthcare to the people of the northern region. 

As a result of this success, patients in North Bengal and surrounding areas will be able to receive bone marrow transplants and modern medical services easily and at a relatively low cost, said Abu Jafar Mohammad Saleh. According to him, this will reduce dependence on capital-based treatment.

Headline_English: Clashes block highway in Madaripur for three hours, 50 grenades explode
Content_Enlish:
People from two sides have clashed over the issue of dominance in Madaripur, blocking the highway. The clash continued uninterruptedly from 3 pm to 6 pm on Tuesday at Mustafapur roundabout in Sadar upazila. During this time, fifty cocktails were exploded, creating panic in the entire area. At least 10 people from both sides were injured in this. 

At least six shops and four houses of both sides were vandalized and looted in the clash. Due to the clash, traffic on the Madaripur-Chandpur-Shariatpur regional highway and Dhaka-Barisal highway was closed for about two hours. This caused severe traffic jams, causing suffering to ordinary passengers and drivers. 

It was learned from talking to the police and local people that Habib Hawlader, Idris Hawlader, members of the local Union Parishad (UP) of Mustafapur roundabout area, had been in a dispute with Shamchu Sardar alias Kopa Shamchu for a long time over the dominance of Shamchu Sardar alias Kopa Shamchu. Shamchu Sardar was recently arrested by RAB in an explosives case. He was out on bail and allegedly beat up a teenager from the Howlader clan this morning. Due to this, the two sides got into a clash with local weapons in the afternoon. Fifty cocktails were exploded, creating panic in the entire area. At least six shops and four houses of both sides were vandalized and looted. 

Upon receiving the information, when law enforcement officers tried to bring the situation under control, several cocktails were thrown at them. Later, local BNP leaders and Krishak Dal member secretary Ahiduzzaman reached the spot and calmed the situation. Traffic on the highway started to return to normal from 6 pm. 

10 people injured in the clash have been admitted to various hospitals including Madaripur 250-bed District Hospital. Among them, one named Hanif Sardar (26) has been admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in critical condition and Zubair Howlader has been admitted to Madaripur 250-bed District Hospital.

Two highways in Madaripur were blocked and clashes continued for three hours without interruption. Tuesday afternoon in the Mustafapur area of ​​Sadar Upazila 
Two highways in Madaripur were blocked and clashes continued for three hours without interruption. Tuesday afternoon in the Mustafapur area of ​​Sadar Upazila Photo: Prothom Alo 
When we went to Mustafapur area around 5 pm, we saw the house of Hawladar to the east of the Mustafapur roundabout. That house was being attacked. After a while, the people of Hawladar's house gathered and launched a counterattack on the house of Sardar to the northeast next to the Mustafapur bus stand. People from both sides were seen carrying spears, spears, clubs, saraki, katra, and ramda. 

When asked, UP member Habib Hawladar said, "Shamchu Sardar nurtures terrorists in the area. This is the battlefield today because of him. He himself makes bombs and deals in drugs. Even the police are afraid to catch him. He has 12 cases against him, including murder, drugs, and robbery. He was recently arrested by RAB. Shamchu kept threatening us even after he was released on bail. Today, when Shamsu attacked our people with his terrorist force, our people repelled it. 

Denying the allegations, Shamchu Sardar told Prothom Alo, "People from the Hawladar clan attacked us. I told the police about the matter. They were retaliated against when the police did not take action." 

Fariha Rafiq Bhavna, Additional Superintendent of Police (Sadar Circle) of Madaripur, told Prothom Alo, "I came to the spot after receiving news of a clash between the two groups of Hawladar and Sardar in Mustafapur. We have police, RAB, DB, and army with us. We have tried our best to bring the situation under control. Considering the safety of vehicles and passengers on the highway, the traffic police has controlled the speed of vehicles. Buses are plying on the Dhaka-Barisal highway intermittently. Although traffic was stopped on the Madaripur-Chandpur-Shariatpur road, everything returned to normal after 6 pm. 

Abul Kalam Azad, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Madaripur Sadar Model Police Station, told Prothom Alo that when the police tried to control both sides, they threw hand grenades at the police. None of them were following the law. The police showed utmost patience and asked them to remain calm. Legal action will be taken against those who practiced domestic weapons in this incident, those who attacked and vandalized.

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia's funeral tomorrow at 2pm, at the South Plaza of Parliament Building: Mirza Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
The funeral prayer of BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia will be held at 2 pm tomorrow at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban and Manik Mia Avenue. After the funeral prayer, she will be buried next to her husband, former President Ziaur Rahman, said the party's Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. 

He gave this information at a briefing after the emergency standing committee meeting at the Chairperson's political office in Gulshan around 2:45 pm today. The meeting of the standing committee began at around 12:30 pm. The standing committee members participated at the time. Earlier, a two-hour standing committee meeting was held at the Gulshan office under the leadership of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman. 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that the khatib of the National Mosque Baitul Mukarram will lead the funeral prayer for Khaleda Zia. The entire funeral prayer program will be conducted by BNP Standing Committee member Nazrul Islam Khan. Everyone will participate in the funeral prayer in a very orderly manner. Will attend his funeral. 

Announcing a seven-day mourning period, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said, "The government has declared a mourning period and a general holiday. We thank the government. In addition, the BNP has declared a seven-day mourning period. We will wear black badges for these seven days. At the same time, black flags will be flown in every party office. Quran recitation and prayers will be offered in every office. I seek everyone's cooperation for this."

Headline_English: The probable date of the JOCSU elections is January 6.
Content_Enlish:
Jagannath University Central Student Union (JCSU) and Hall Parliament elections-2025 may be held on January 6. Members expressed their opinions on the matter in a special emergency syndicate meeting today, Tuesday afternoon. Vice-Chancellor Md. Rezaul Karim gave this information after the meeting. It will be officially announced when the decision is finalized. 
The university authorities decided to postpone the JCSU elections due to the death of former Prime Minister and BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia. This decision was taken in an emergency syndicate meeting this morning. On the morning of the voting day, such a decision caused strong dissatisfaction among the general students. 
As a result, the university administration met again in the syndicate meeting to determine the new date of the elections and the next steps. Voting was supposed to start at 8:30 am today as per the previously announced schedule. Students came to the center in groups from the morning to take part in this election for the first time after two decades of the university's establishment. 

When the news of Khaleda Zia's death spread, the university administration called an emergency syndicate meeting. Considering the tragic situation in the meeting, it was decided to postpone the elections. As soon as this news spread, general students started protesting on the campus. In the face of the students' anger and protests, the administration has not yet officially issued a notification of the postponement. 

Confirming the postponement of the elections, Jagannath University Vice Chancellor Md. Rezaul Karim said after the syndicate meeting, "We do not want election celebrations at this time of mourning. That is why the JOCSU and Hall Parliament elections are being postponed." He said that such a decision was taken because it was not possible to maintain the atmosphere of the elections in an atmosphere of mourning.

Headline_English: Everest to be charged a non-refundable fee of $4,000 per climber
Content_Enlish:
The 'deposit system' for climbers to keep the world's highest mountain Mount Everest clean is no more. The Nepalese government has called it a 'failure' after the rule was in effect for 11 years, but it has not reduced the amount of garbage on the mountain. This information was confirmed by Nepal's tourism ministry on Tuesday. 

According to the old rule, Everest climbers had to deposit a deposit of $4,000 (about 470,000 taka). The condition was that the money would be returned if at least 8 kg of waste was brought down on the way back. But the country is withdrawing from this initiative after the problem of about 50 tons of garbage on the mountain has not been solved even after a decade. 

Himal Gautam, director of Nepal's tourism department, told the BBC that the rule has now become just an administrative burden. Most climbers have received their deposits back, but the garbage at the camps on the mountain has not decreased. 

Tshering Sherpa, head of the Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee, said that climbers usually bring garbage down from the lower camps. But abandoned tents, cans and plastic food packets remain in the remote upper camps. Apart from this, experts see lack of surveillance as one of the reasons for this failure. 

Instead of the deposit system, Nepal is planning to charge a ‘non-refundable cleaning fee’ from each climber from now on. A permanent fund will be formed with this money. From that fund, a checkpoint will be set up at Camp-2 and special ‘mountain rangers’ will be appointed. They will supervise garbage management at the upper camps around the clock. 

Tourism Ministry officials said that a fee of $4,000 may be collected from each climber. It will be implemented after the law is passed in parliament. 

The Sherpa community has welcomed the decision. According to them, no one has ever had to pay a fine under the deposit system, which has called into question the effectiveness of the rule. Now, the money collected through the new fee will be used directly for cleaning Everest. 

Every year, about 400 climbers and a large number of their companions go on Everest expeditions. Due to the extreme cold, even human excrement does not decompose on the upper part of the mountain, which has become a major threat to the Himalayan environment. Nepal's tourism ministry hopes that a new five-year action plan will help clean Everest.

Headline_English: Saudi Arabia bombs UAE-backed separatist group in Yemen
Content_Enlish:
Saudi Arabia bombed the Yemeni port city of Mukalla on Tuesday. Saudi Arabia claims that the attack was carried out in response to a shipment of weapons sent from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to separatist forces. 

The UAE did not immediately comment on the attack. 

The attack has renewed tensions between Saudi Arabia and the UAE-backed separatist group, the Southern Transitional Council (STC), and has strained ties between Riyadh and Abu Dhabi. 

The two countries have been supporting opposing sides in Yemen's decade-long war against Iran-backed Houthi rebels. 

A military statement carried by Saudi Arabia's state news agency (SPA) said the airstrikes were carried out after ships from the UAE port of Fujairah arrived in Mukalla. 

The statement added, “The ships had their tracking devices turned off. They were unloading a large amount of weapons and military vehicles for the STC forces. As these weapons pose a major threat to stability and peace, the Saudi coalition air force carried out a limited airstrike targeting the weapons and vehicles on Tuesday morning.” 

It was not immediately known whether anyone was injured in the attack or whether any country other than Saudi Arabia was involved. However, the Saudi military said it carried out the attack under cover of night to ensure no civilian casualties. 

The United Arab Emirates has not yet commented on the attack. However, the Transitional Council’s television channel (AIC) confirmed the attack. It did not provide any details. 

Analysts believe that the attack targeted a ship named ‘Greenland’. According to information, the ship was in Fujairah, UAE, on December 22 and arrived in Mukalla last Sunday. The identity of the second ship could not be confirmed. 

Yemeni expert Mohammed al-Basha, citing a video on social media, said that new armored vehicles were seen moving in Mukalla after the ship arrived. After this incident, both sides will cautiously increase tensions. The supply of weapons to the separatists from the United Arab Emirates may now be somewhat disrupted. Because Saudi Arabia controls Yemen's airspace. 

Drone footage broadcast on Saudi state television showed several armored vehicles heading towards a specific area in the city of Mukalla. 

The city of Mukalla is located in Yemen's Hadramaut province, which was recently captured by the separatist council. The city of Aden has been used as a center of anti-Houthi forces since the Houthi rebels seized the capital Sanaa in 2014. 

Earlier, Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes on Friday to warn the separatists. Saudi Arabia wants them to retreat from Hadramaut and Mahra provinces. The separatists are now using the flag of South Yemen and are demanding the creation of a separate state, just as Yemen was two separate countries from 1967 to 1990. 

The separatist movement has strained long-standing friendly relations between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, which are members of OPEC and are rivals for trade and regional dominance.

Headline_English: Both pilots killed in mid-air collision between two helicopters in the United States
Content_Enlish:
Two helicopters collided in mid-air in the US city of Hammonton, New Jersey, on Sunday, killing both pilots. 

Hammonton police have identified the pilots as Kenneth L. Kirsch, 65, and Michael Greenberg, 71, both from New Jersey, CBS News reported. 

The US Federal Aviation Administration said there were only two pilots on board the helicopters. It added that a federal investigation would be launched to determine the cause of the collision. 

Hammonton is located on the Atlantic City Expressway, about 35 miles (56 km) southeast of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. 

Police said on Sunday that one of the helicopters caught fire after it hit the ground. Emergency services extinguished the fire. 

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigates civil aviation accidents in the United States. 

According to the agency, the collision occurred between an Enstorm 280C helicopter and an Enstorm F-28A helicopter. The incident occurred at around 4:25 p.m. Greenwich Mean Time (GMT). Both helicopters are light aircraft. They typically carry three or fewer people. 

In January, a military helicopter collided with a passenger plane in Washington, D.C., killing 67 people. 

According to the U.S. Civil Aviation Authority, the average number of fatal helicopter accidents has declined over the past three years.

Headline_English: Agreement with Jamaat, NCP's identity crisis solved?
Content_Enlish:
An important part of the July mass uprising, those who have formed a political party called NCP; now they will hold elections in agreement with Jamaat. Not all the youth have accepted it. Many say that NCP has now lost the purity of their politics.

Protests have arisen from within the NCP itself. The protesters have protested angrily in a letter, citing Jamaat's anti-independence role. In the letter, they said, 'Jamaat-e-Islami's political history, especially its anti-independence role during the great liberation war of 1971, its collaboration in genocide and its position on various crimes committed at that time, is fundamentally at odds with the democratic spirit of Bangladesh and the values ​​of our party.' 

A familiar face of the July movement, Dr. Tasneem Zara, Senior Joint Member Secretary of NCP, has announced to sever ties with NCP. NCP joint convener Tajnubha Jabin resigned from the NCP and said about the agreement with Jamaat, "I can't even digest this thing and die." Former information advisor Mahfuz Alam, who was considered a supporter of the NCP, has also spoken against the agreement.

Will the calculations of the Jamaat-NCP agreement really match?

Many have been disappointed by the NCP's formation of an alliance with Jamaat for an agreement; but is anyone surprised? After the formation of the NCP, the party leaders have spoken loudly on all the issues, Jamaat has also echoed them. Similarly, it can be said that the NCP has also tuned in to the way Jamaat has spoken. The demands of the two parties on various issues of the July Charter were very similar, although Jamaat got more. Because, the history has been changed in the July declaration, which has clarified Jamaat's role in 1971.

Both parties had a consensus from the beginning on outlawing the Awami League by issuing government rules, and both parties have repeatedly spoken out against ‘Indian hegemony’. The NCP was supposed to join the eight-party right-wing alliance formed under the leadership of Jamaat in November 2025; but in the end, they did not join. At that time, a section of the NCP was trying to form an alliance with the BNP. In the end, that alliance did not happen. Considering the reality, the compromise alliance of the NCP with Jamaat is not very unexpected. However, what will be of great interest to everyone is how much these young people can balance the religion-based politics of the alliance.

If the NCP had elected alone, even if they did not get seats, they would have become a contender in the future as a moderate party. The new identity of the NCP in this election will help the BNP consolidate moderate voters. Besides, if the BNP comes to power, they will have to face one opposition party instead of two. This is a distinct advantage for any government party.

What is the identity crisis of the NCP?

After the success of the July mass uprising, a large section of students and youth stayed away from politics. Many of those who remained vocal have made themselves controversial at various times and in various ways. They have blockaded Shahbagh on one issue after another, put pressure on the owners to lay off journalists, talked unbridled about the army, put pressure on them by keeping their representatives in the government, all of these have made the NCP controversial in various ways, which has also created an identity crisis for them.

At one stage, it seemed that they had degraded the liberation war of Bangladesh compared to the 1947 and July mass uprisings. This trend had intensified their identity crisis. It was also reflected in the speeches of the leaders. Sometimes the NCP leaders spoke with pressure and shouting, sometimes with religious politics, and sometimes they came to the gathering of civil servants and spoke like civil servants. Their politics created some confusion among the people. By forming an alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami, the NCP has created a pro-Jamaat identity for itself. However, NCP leaders have said that there is no ideological unity. This is an electoral compromise.

The reality is that there are now two political alliances in the country; the right wing includes Jamaat, Khilafat, NCP, etc. In another alliance, some moderates have gathered under the leadership of BNP, who cannot be called a party, but rather personalities.

Tarique Rahman has made the influence and support of BNP more visible by coming to the country, which will have a huge impact on the elections.

The clean image that Jamaat had planned for so long has slowly started to break down. The true nature of that civility, which capitalized on the civility of the youth, has led to Jamaat winning the DUCSU-JACSU-RAKSU elections alone, has now been revealed. Within two months, the 'slip of tongue' of some Shibir leaders and harassment of teachers have created fear in the public mind. There have also been incidents of amputation of hands and feet outside the university. It is believed that these will have a negative impact on Jamaat's electoral fortunes.

By bringing the NCP, the youth party of the July Movement, into an alliance, Jamaat will be able to create a new 'statement' for them.

The NCP has gradually become limited to the Dhaka-based activities of a few top leaders. Their organization has become known mainly through the acquaintance of a few student leaders of the July Movement. But they have not been able to expand their organizational scope. As a result, discussions about the elections have become fairly limited to the two big parties. In this situation, doubts have arisen in the party's high echelons about whether even the known leaders of the NCP can win any seat by contesting under the party banner. They hope that they will do better if they form an alliance with Jamaat.

If there is a national election, national politics will no longer be on the streets; rather, it will be more important in parliament. In this situation, if the NCP can win even a few seats in parliament by joining hands with Jamaat, they will be able to maintain their position in national politics.

The biggest fear for the NCP is whether the party can maintain its existence. As soon as the process of electoral reconciliation with Jamaat began, there was a huge reaction in the party. Some have left the party. Many of those who did not leave are feeling very uncomfortable.

The NCP will also have to carry some of the negative perception that exists about Jamaat in Bangladeshi politics. Many political analysts believe that this is a risky decision for the NCP.

Many say that BNP will have more headaches. Because, if a new party joins any alliance, the alliance's votes will definitely increase. However, there is a difference of opinion that if the NCP joins, there will not be much change in the number of votes for Jamaat. If the NCP had elected alone, even if they did not get seats, they would have become a contender in the future as a moderate party. The new identity of the NCP in this election will help BNP consolidate moderate voters. Besides, if BNP comes to power, they will have to face one opposition party instead of two. This is a distinct advantage for any government party.

There is a great optimism in breaking and forming political alliances. The enthusiasm of the parties in elections and systematic politics is increasing. It is expected that after the elections, Parliament will become the center of politics.

Headline_English: What to do if asthma worsens during pregnancy
Content_Enlish:
Why Asthma May Increase During Pregnancy 
Pregnancy brings about various hormonal and physical changes in the body. Hormonal changes (especially progesterone and estrogen) can increase the sensitivity of the airways. The enlarged uterus puts pressure on the lungs. Nasal congestion, reflux (gastric) and infections can contribute to asthma. 

Many people stop taking asthma medications or take them irregularly, thinking that they are harmful to the unborn baby. This is also a major reason why studies have shown that one-third of women's asthma increases during pregnancy, one-third decreases and the remaining one-third remains the same. 

What are the risks for mother and baby 
If asthma is not controlled, it can harm not only the mother but also the baby. In the case of the mother, there is a risk of severe shortness of breath, repeated hospitalizations and pre-eclampsia (a serious complication of pregnancy). In the case of a fetus, there may be problems such as low birth weight, premature birth, and lack of oxygen in the womb.

Are asthma medications safe during pregnancy 
There are many misconceptions among us. Asthma is a chronic disease and its treatment cannot be stopped suddenly. Those who already have asthma and have to take regular inhalers or various medications, it is better to consult a doctor regularly after having a child. Using inhalers and all other necessary asthma medications as per the doctor's advice is largely safe for the baby.

What to do if asthma worsens 
Regular doctor follow-up. 

Avoiding asthma triggers (dust, smoke, cold, allergens). 

Using the inhaler correctly. 

Contact the hospital without delay if breathing difficulties increase. 

Completely avoiding smoking and secondhand smoke. 

There is nothing to fear about having a child with asthma. But not having asthma under control is problematic. This can lead to various complications. However, with awareness, regular treatment and the use of the right medication, both the mother and the child can remain healthy.

Headline_English: Why nighttime lights are a silent risk of heart disease
Content_Enlish:
Many of us sleep with the lights on at night, the TV on, or our phones in our hands. All of this seems normal in modern life. But recent research suggests that these harmless habits can create a greater risk of heart disease in the future. 

Those who were exposed to more light at night had an increased risk of— 
• Coronary heart disease 
• Stroke 
• Irregular heartbeat 
• Heart attack 
• Heart failure 
The most important thing is that this risk remained even after taking into account smoking, high blood pressure, diabetes, or sleep duration. 

Many people feel tired when they wake up in the morning 
Many people feel tired when they wake up in the morning Photo: Pexels 
Light and the body's biological clock 
We have a natural biological clock inside our body, which determines— 
• When to sleep 
• When to wake up 
• Blood pressure, heart rate and hormone fluctuations 
Light at night disrupts the rhythm of this clock. In particular, light reduces the sleep hormone melatonin. Melatonin plays an important role not only in sleep, but also in protecting the cardiovascular system and blood vessels. 

Read more 
Why do I wake up in the middle of the night even if I go to bed on time? 
10 September 2025 
Why do I wake up in the middle of the night even if I go to bed on time? 

As a result, the habit of staying in the light of the night for a long time— 
• Can increase blood pressure 
• Increases inflammation in the body 
• Creates additional stress on the heart 

Risk is higher in urban life 
Studies have shown that those who live in brightly lit areas of the city may have a 35-50 percent higher risk of heart disease. Street lights, billboards, car headlights shining through windows—all make the urban night as bright as day.
