How to protect yourself 
Don't sleep with the TV or mobile phone on 
Don't sleep with the TV or mobile phone onImage: Prothom Alo 
We can control this risk to a large extent. 
Keep the room as dark as possible while sleeping. 
Don't sleep with the TV or mobile phone on. 
Use light red or warm light if necessary. 
Stay in the dark for at least 30 minutes after using your cell phone. 
Use thick curtains or blackout curtains on windows. 
Night light not only disrupts sleep, it can silently cause long-term damage to the heart. It is not possible to completely avoid light in modern life, but being aware can greatly reduce the risk.

Headline_English: Electricity will be generated using aircraft supersonic jet engine technology
Content_Enlish:
With the rapid spread of artificial intelligence or AI technology, the power demand of data centers is also increasing. Supersonic jet engines can play an important role in meeting this demand in the future. This is the idea put forward by US-based aircraft manufacturer Boom Supersonic. In the meantime, the company has started manufacturing a special type of turbine called 'Superpower' using the technology of supersonic jet engines. 
Boom Supersonic said that the new turbine is basically based on the technology of the 'Symphony' engine for supersonic aircraft, where some changes have been made as needed. The technology of generating electricity from aircraft engines is not entirely new. Various engine manufacturers have been supplying such turbines to industries and power generation sectors for a long time. However, as the spread of AI technology has created new pressures on data center power management in recent times, interest in jet engine-based solutions is increasing. 

“Our supersonic engine technology offers the advantages of faster power delivery, higher power, and more reliable operation than conventional power turbines,” said Blake Scholl, CEO of Boom Supersonic. These features could be a viable solution for large-scale AI data centers. 

Boom Supersonic is currently developing a commercial supersonic aircraft, the Overture. The company plans to begin passenger service on the aircraft within the next five years. As a result, the project to build superpower turbines to meet the power needs of data centers is seen as a key strategic initiative for Boom Supersonic.

Headline_English: Shaheed Hadi murder: Case filed against accused Faisal under Arms Act at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station
Content_Enlish:
Another case under the Arms Act has been filed against Faisal Karim Masud, the main accused in the murder of Inqilab Manch convener Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi, at the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station in the capital. The case was filed on December 23. 
Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station Mohammad Monirul Islam gave this information in response to a question from Prothom Alo on Monday. He said that a case has been filed against Faisal under the Arms Act. The investigation into the case is underway. 

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Additional Commissioner S.S. Nazrul Islam said at a press conference on Sunday that the main accused in the murder of Hadi, Faisal, and his accomplice Alamgir Sheikh, have fled to India. Eleven people have been arrested in the murder case so far. During the investigation, two foreign pistols, 52 bullets, a motorcycle and fake number plates used in the murder of Hadi, and checks worth Tk 218 crore against 53 bank accounts were recovered. 
Inqilab Manch convener Sharif Osman bin Hadi was a potential candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency. On December 12, miscreants shot Hadi in the Purana Paltan area of ​​the capital shortly after Friday prayers. They later fled on a motorcycle. Hadi died while undergoing treatment in Singapore on December 18.

Headline_English: Former Awami League leader files nomination for Dinajpur-3 constituency
Content_Enlish:
Rabiul Islam has submitted his nomination papers from a political party called 'Janatar Dal' to participate in the 13th National Parliament election in Dinajpur-3 (Sadar Upazila) constituency. He was elected as the Upazila Vice Chairman in the by-election in 2020 as an Awami League candidate. 
On the last day of submitting nomination papers, Monday, Riazul Islam, a resident of the municipal town, submitted the nomination papers on his behalf to the Dinajpur Deputy Commissioner and District Returning Officer. Rabiul Islam is a resident of the Cheradangi area of ​​South Faridpur, Dinajpur Sadar Upazila. He was a member of the Auliapur Union Awami League. 
No response was received even after contacting the mobile phone of Rabiul Islam mentioned in the nomination papers. However, Riazul Islam, who submitted the nomination papers, said on the mobile phone, 'Rabiul Bhai is known to me. He sent me the election papers a few days ago and asked me to submit them. I submitted them today.' After that, he did not want to elaborate further. When asked about Rabiul Islam, he said, "I don't know where he is."

Headline_English: Rumin Farhana, while filing her nomination papers, said, "This vote will be against injustice."
Content_Enlish:
Rumin Farhana, a former MP from the reserved seat and BNP's International Affairs Assistant Secretary, has filed her nomination as an independent candidate for the Brahmanbaria-2 (Sarail-Ashuganj and part of Bijoynagar) constituency.
Rumin Farhana herself appeared before Sarail Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) and Assistant Returning Officer Md. Abubakar Sarkar on Monday afternoon and submitted her nomination.
Responding to questions from journalists after submitting her nomination, Rumin Farhana said, "Allah's plan is beyond human understanding. In this plan of Allah, my father won an independent election against the tide of Awami League in 1973. What a strange plan of the Almighty! In 2026, I have to fight independently against the tide of paddy sheaves. God's plan and the process of its implementation are beyond human understanding.'

Then, in a short speech to the supporters, Rumin Farhana said, 'The mark you want is mine, what mark do you want?' In response, the followers said, 'Duck', 'Duck'.

Referring to Sarail-Ashuganj upazila as two neglected upazilas of Bangladesh, Rumin Farhana raised the question, 'Why is the situation in Sarail-Ashuganj bad even after 55 years of independence? Why has no member of parliament brought about a change in this bad situation? Why have the people of Sarail-Ashuganj not understood their fair share?'

Referring to the BNP, Rumin Farhana said, 'This time is coming for change. This vote will be against injustice. This vote will be against oppression. This vote will be in favor of the woman who was in the field for 17 years. This vote will be held when you were devastated by the lawsuits and attacks, then this vote will be held in favor of the person who spoke for you in parliament and outside parliament.’

Earlier, Ali Hossain, former organizing secretary of the Upazila Jubo Dal, collected the nomination papers from the Sarail UNO on behalf of Rumin Farhana on Wednesday. Today, when Rumin Farhana submitted her nomination papers, former vice president of the Upazila BNP Hossain Mia, former general secretary of the Upazila Chhatra Dal Usman Khan, and president of the Upazila Sramik Dal Ayub Hossain, along with several hundred followers, were with her.

Shahbazpur Union BNP office secretary Mosharraf Hossain was the proposer of Rumin Farhana’s nomination papers, while publicity secretary Jonayed Khan was the seconder.

Rumin Farhana arrived at the upazila headquarters around 2 pm today. At that time, hundreds of her followers, leaders and workers arrived at the Sarail upazila headquarters on motorcycles and other vehicles.

The seat, known as the base of the rice sheaf, has been ceded to the ally Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh through a compromise with BNP. Maulana Junaid Al Habib, vice-president of the party's central committee, has been nominated for this seat.

Brahmanbaria-2 seat currently consists of Chandura and Budhanti unions of Sarail, Ashuganj and Bijoynagar upazilas. Rumin Farhana's ancestral home is in Budhanti union. She is currently a resident of Shahbazpur union of Sarail upazila.

The total number of voters in the seat is 4 lakh 99 thousand 448.

Headline_English: DB gets responsibility for investigating the attack and arson case at Prothom Alo office
Content_Enlish:
It has been decided to give the responsibility of investigating the case filed in the terrorist attack, vandalism, looting and arson incident at the Prothom Alo office to the Intelligence Department (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP). 
On Monday, DMP Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Md. Ibne Mizan confirmed the truth of this information and told Prothom Alo that yesterday, Sunday, the DMP authorities decided to give the responsibility of investigating the case to the DB. 
When contacted today, DB Tejgaon Division Acting Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Rakib Khan told Prothom Alo that he has learned that the DB Tejgaon Division has been given the responsibility of investigating the case. However, they have not yet received the case documents. The attack, vandalism, looting and arson occurred at the Prothom Alo office on the night of December 18. The case was filed at Tejgaon Police Station on the night of December 21. An unknown number of 400 to 500 people have been accused in the case. The case was filed under various sections of the Penal Code, including the Anti-Terrorism Act, Special Powers Act, and Cyber ​​Security Act. The case alleges illegal entry into the office by creating a riot, looting, causing damage, arson with the intention of murder, intimidation, and destroying evidence of a crime. In addition, arson and vandalism to stop the publication of Prothom Alo and obstruct office work, giving instructions for online criminal activities, and sabotage are also alleged. The value of the looted assets alone is mentioned in the case statement. The statement also says that the total initial damage is Tk 320 million. There is CCTV camera footage of the attack and video footage from various media outlets. 
Officials involved in the investigation of the case said that 25 people have been arrested so far in the case of attack, arson, and looting at the Prothom Alo office. And 10 people have been arrested in the attack and arson incident at The Daily Star. 35 people arrested in the cases of these two organizations are now in jail.

Headline_English: Jahangirnagar student sentenced to prison for using ChatGPT during admission test
Content_Enlish:
A mobile court has sentenced a student to seven days in prison for allegedly cheating in the admission test for the first year of the Bachelor (Honours) A Unit (Faculty of Mathematics and Physics) of Jahangirnagar University for the academic year 2025-26. At the same time, the answer sheet of the student's A Unit exam, as well as the answer sheet of the D Unit of the Biology Faculty held earlier, along with his roll number, have been canceled. The imprisoned student, Md. Mahmudullah Hasan, is a resident of Dimla Upazila of Nilphamari district. Savar Executive Magistrate (AC-Land) Abdullah Al Amin conducted a mobile court and sentenced the detained student after the A Unit admission test at the university on Monday afternoon. According to sources from the university's proctorial team, the student was caught red-handed by the inspector in charge of the room while taking a picture of the question paper on his mobile phone and using ChatGPT (Artificial Intelligence) to find out the answer. He was then handed over to the proctorial team. The accused student was taken to the proctor's office. There, the student confessed to Proctor AKM Rashidul Alam that he had cheated in today's exam and the previous admission test of the D unit of the Biology faculty. At that time, evidence of the matter was also found in his phone's Google history. 

Then, a mobile court was set up in the meeting room of the proctor's office under the direction of Savar Upazila Assistant Commissioner (Land) Abdullah Al Amin. There, the accused student was sentenced to seven days in prison, his answer sheet and roll number were canceled. 

In this regard, the university's proctor AKM Rashidul Alam said that the executive magistrate has tried the incident. The answer sheet of the student's DRA unit will be canceled and he has been sentenced to imprisonment.

Headline_English: US-Israeli relations: What will Trump and Netanyahu discuss in Florida?
Content_Enlish:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is visiting the United States. There, he will meet with US President Donald Trump. The meeting is taking place at a time when the situation in the Middle East is reaching an extreme point, with Israeli attacks on Palestine, Lebanon and Syria and rising tensions surrounding Iran. 
Netanyahu will meet with President Trump at the Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida on Monday. The talks are taking place as Washington is increasing pressure to complete the first phase of the ceasefire in Gaza. 
Despite accusations of Israel violating the ceasefire in Gaza almost daily, the US is continuing to try to implement its 20-point so-called 'peace plan' in the Palestinian territories. 
Israel is intensifying its attacks on the occupied West Bank, Lebanon and Syria. At the same time, Israeli officials have indicated that another war with Iran may occur. 

Al Jazeera has analyzed how Netanyahu's visit to the US could go.

What will Netanyahu discuss with Trump in the meeting? Al Jazeera has tried to find answers to various questions such as what is the state of US-Israeli relations. 

The Israeli prime minister arrived in the United States on Sunday. However, this meeting will not take place at the White House. Instead, Netanyahu will meet with Trump in Florida, where the US president is vacationing. 
The two leaders are scheduled to meet today, Monday. 

This is Netanyahu's first meeting with Trump 
This is Netanyahu's fifth visit to the United States in the last 10 months. Trump has welcomed Netanyahu to the United States more times than any other world leader. 

Netanyahu became the first foreign leader to visit the White House in February after Trump became president for the second time. He then visited the United States in April and July. Most recently, he met with Trump in Washington, DC, after the UN General Assembly in New York last September. 

Netanyahu's meeting with Trump will not take place at the White House. Netanyahu will travel to Florida, where the US president is vacationing, to meet with Trump. 

The two leaders are scheduled to meet on Monday. 
During his first term, Trump has increasingly pushed US policy in favor of Israel's conservative government. He moved the US embassy to Jerusalem, recognized Israeli sovereignty over the Syrian-occupied Golan Heights and cut off funding to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA). 

Since returning to the White House this year, Trump has tended to publicly disagree with Netanyahu. However, his administration has expressed strong support for Israel. For example, the US backed Israel's renewed offensive in the Gaza Strip in March after a brief ceasefire. 

Last June, Trump joined Israel in its attack on Iran, which dismayed some of his supporters. 

While Washington seeks to strengthen economic cooperation in the Middle East, Israel is trying to establish “total dominance” across the region, including among the US Gulf allies. 
(Sina Tusi, senior fellow at the Center for International Policy) 
At the same time, Trump is pressuring Israel to ensure the protection of the current ceasefire in Gaza. Trump opposed the Israeli attack on Doha last September. Despite Israeli skepticism, he quickly lifted sanctions on Syria. 

The relationship between Trump and Netanyahu has been through ups and downs. Netanyahu congratulated Joe Biden immediately after his victory in the 2020 US presidential election. Trump was upset because he falsely claimed that the election was rigged. 

"I haven't spoken to him (Netanyahu) since then," Trump told Axios in 2021. 

The two leaders have rekindled their relationship since Trump was elected to a second term in 2024. He has taken a tough stance on Palestinian rights activists in the United States. 

In November, Trump formally asked Israeli President Isaac Herzog to pardon Netanyahu, who has been accused of corruption in his own country. 

But Trump and Netanyahu are not entirely on the same page. They have differences on issues such as the situation in Gaza and Syria and US partnerships with Turkey and the Gulf states. 

Netanyahu is likely to praise Trump and show a warm relationship with him during his visit to the United States. Through this, he will advance his agenda and show political rivals in Israel that he still has Washington's support. 

Netanyahu's relationship with the United States after 2023 
US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 
US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin NetanyahuPhoto: Reuters File Photo 
On October 7, 2023, the Palestinian independence armed organization Hamas attacked southern Israel. In response, Israel began attacking Gaza that day. 

After Israel's indiscriminate attack on Gaza began, Netanyahu sought unfettered diplomatic and military assistance from the United States. 

At that time, Joe Biden was the US president. 11 days after the attack on Gaza began, he visited Israel and announced that supporting Israel was essential for US national security. 

The way Biden hugged Netanyahu sincerely at Tel Aviv airport indicated that the United States would support Israel. However, at that time, Israel was waging a terrible destruction in Gaza. The United States has provided Israel with more than $21 billion in military aid in the past two years. It has vetoed several anti-Israel resolutions in the United Nations Security Council. 

Netanyahu wants to show the United States that Israel is working to advance American interests as well as its own. In a speech to the US Congress last year, he claimed that Israel is indirectly fighting Iran through Gaza and Lebanon. 
Netanyahu told US lawmakers, “We are not only defending ourselves, we are also protecting you.” 

During the war, numerous reports said that Biden and Trump were unhappy or expressed anger with Netanyahu. However, US arms and political support for Israel has continued. Netanyahu has always expressed gratitude to US presidents. Even when tensions are high, it does not waver. 

The relationship between Trump and Netanyahu has gone through ups and downs. Netanyahu congratulated Joe Biden on his victory in the 2020 US presidential election, which angered Trump. He had falsely claimed that the election was rigged. 

US position on Gaza ceasefire 
Last week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the Trump administration's top priority was to complete the first phase of the Gaza ceasefire and move from a mere cessation of hostilities to a long-term phase of governance, stability and reconstruction. 
Israel has been routinely violating the Gaza ceasefire. At least six Palestinians were killed in a recent attack on a wedding party. 

Trump, who has called for peace in the Middle East for the first time in 3,000 years, has focused more on pushing forward the ceasefire than on Israel's day-to-day activities. 

US Secretary of State Rubio has also indicated that there may be some flexibility in disarming Hamas under the deal. He said the focus would be on ensuring that the group does not pose a threat to Israel, rather than on removing weapons from individual fighters. 

Israel’s priorities appear to be different, however. Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday that the country was seeking to establish new illegal settlements in Gaza. He later retracted the comments. But he insisted that Israel would maintain a permanent military presence in the area, which contradicts Trump’s plan. 
In such a situation, Gaza is expected to be a key topic of discussion between Netanyahu and Trump. 

Is a deal possible with Syria 
Last year, Trump virtually embraced Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa. He lifted US sanctions on the country and began cooperating with his government’s security forces. But Israel is pursuing its own agenda in Syria. 

Within hours of the fall of former President Bashar al-Assad's government, Israel began expanding its occupation of Syria beyond the Golan Heights. 
Although the new Syrian authorities have said from the outset that they do not seek conflict with Israel, Israeli forces have carried out airstrikes on Syrian state and military institutions. 

Israeli forces have also been conducting operations in southern Syria, abducting and disappearing locals. 

Trump criticized Israel after an Israeli airstrike killed 13 Syrian civilians last month. 

Trump said, "It is very important that Israel and Syria maintain a strong and genuine dialogue. Nothing should be done that would hinder the development of Syria as a prosperous state." 

Syria and Israel were in talks to sign a security agreement earlier this year. But the talks collapsed when Israeli leaders insisted on keeping control of territory captured after the fall of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. 

Netanyahu is expected to push for a renewed Syria-Israel deal during his visit to the US. 

Why Iran is in the headlines again 
Netanyahu’s visit comes at a time when there have been growing concerns in Israel about Iran’s rebuilding of its missile capabilities, following a 12-day standoff between the two countries in June. 

Last week, NBC News reported that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu would brief US President Trump on plans for further strikes on Iran. 

The pro-Israel wing of the Trump camp is already vocal about Iran’s missile programme. 

US Senator Lindsey Graham visited Israel this month and described Iranian missiles as a “real threat” to Israel. 
In an interview with The Jerusalem Post, Graham said, “The main purpose of this trip is to highlight the threat of ballistic missiles to Israel.” 

During the Iran-Israel conflict in June, Trump authorized a US strike on Iranian nuclear facilities. 

Despite no evidence that Iran was using its nuclear program to build weapons, the fear of a possible Iranian nuclear bomb was cited as the main reason for the US involvement in the conflict. 

Sina Toussi, a senior fellow at the Center for International Policy, said it would be difficult for Netanyahu to convince Trump to support a war against Iran. 

President Trump has presented himself as a peacemaker and has prioritized a potential conflict in Venezuela. 
According to Toussi, further pressure on Iran could backfire on Netanyahu. 

But Toussi also said that there is no way to predict what Trump will do. Because, he has pro-Israeli people like Rubio around him. 

What is the current state of US-Israel relations? 
Despite growing opposition from both the left and right in the US political arena, Trump's support for Israel is still unwavering. 

This month, the US Congress passed a military spending bill. It calls for $600 million in military aid for Israel. 

The Trump administration is also avoiding verbal criticism of Israel's aggressive behavior in the region, including violations of the ceasefire in Gaza or the expansion of illegal settlements in the West Bank. 

On December 16, the White House hosted a ceremony to celebrate the Jewish holiday of Hanukkah. At that time, Trump expressed regret over the growing skepticism in Congress about unconditional support for Israel. He compared this attitude to anti-Semitism. 

ট্রাম্প বলেন, ‘আপনি যদি ১০, ১২ বা ১৫ বছর আগে ফিরে তাকান, তাহলে দেখতে পাবেন ওয়াশিংটনে সবচেয়ে শক্তিশালী লবি ছিল ইহুদি লবি। আর তা হলো ইসরায়েল। এখন আর তা নেই।’

ট্রাম্প আরও বলেন, ‘আপনাদের খুব সতর্ক থাকতে হবে। বিশেষ করে কংগ্রেসে এমন একটা মনোভাব তৈরি হচ্ছে, যা ইহুদিবিদ্বেষী।’

তবে বিশ্লেষকদের মতে, যুক্তরাষ্ট্র ও ইসরায়েলের কৌশলগত অগ্রাধিকারের মধ্যে দূরত্ব বাড়ছে।

সেন্টার ফর ইন্টারন্যাশনাল পলিসির জ্যেষ্ঠ ফেলো সিনা টুসির মতে, ওয়াশিংটন যখন মধ্যপ্রাচ্যে অর্থনৈতিক সহযোগিতা জোরদার করতে চাইছে, তখন ইসরায়েল অঞ্চলজুড়ে ‘পূর্ণ আধিপত্য’ প্রতিষ্ঠার চেষ্টা করছে। এর মধ্যে যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের উপসাগরীয় মিত্ররাও রয়েছে।

টুসি আরও বলেন, ইসরায়েল যে আপসহীন অবস্থান ও কৌশলগত লক্ষ্য অনুসরণ করছে, তা একসময় যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের মূল স্বার্থের সঙ্গে সাংঘর্ষিক হতে পারে।


যুক্তরাষ্ট্র-ইসরায়েল জোটের ভবিষ্যৎ কী
ওয়াশিংটন ডিসির ইনডিপেনডেন্স অ্যাভিনিউ ধরে গাড়ি চালালে কংগ্রেস সদস্যদের দপ্তরের জানালায় অনেক সময় মার্কিন পতাকার চেয়ে বেশি ইসরায়েলি পতাকা চোখে পড়বে।

জনমত বদলাতে শুরু করলেও কংগ্রেস ও হোয়াইট হাউসে ইসরায়েলের প্রতি সমর্থন এখনো বিপুল। রিপাবলিকান শিবিরে ইসরায়েল নিয়ে সমালোচনা বাড়লেও যাঁরা ইসরায়েলের বিরোধিতা করছেন, তাঁদের কোণঠাসা করে দেওয়া হচ্ছে। মার্জোরি টেইলর গ্রিন কংগ্রেস ছাড়ছেন। বিশ্লেষক টাকার কার্লসন নিয়মিত হামলা ও ইহুদিবিদ্বেষের অভিযোগের মুখে পড়ছেন। আর কংগ্রেস সদস্য টম ম্যাসি ট্রাম্প-সমর্থিত এক প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বীর চ্যালেঞ্জের মুখে রয়েছেন।

ট্রাম্পের ঘনিষ্ঠ মহল কট্টর ইসরায়েলপন্থীদের দিয়ে ভরা। যাঁদের মধ্যে আছেন—পররাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী মার্কো রুবিও, ধনকুবের দাতা মিরিয়াম অ্যাডেলসন এবং রেডিও উপস্থাপক মার্ক লেভিন।

তবে জনসমর্থন কমে যাওয়ায়, বিশেষ করে তরুণদের মধ্যে জনসমর্থন কমে যাওয়ায় দীর্ঘ মেয়াদে মার্কিন রাজনীতিতে ইসরায়েলকে হয়তো কঠিন বাস্তবতার মুখোমুখি হতে হবে।

কংগ্রেসে ডেমোক্র্যাট সদস্যদের মধ্যে যাঁরা ইসরায়েলের কট্টর সমর্থক, তাঁদের কেউ কেউ এখন প্রাইমারি নির্বাচনে ফিলিস্তিনি অধিকারের পক্ষ সোচ্চার থাকা প্রগতিশীল প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বীদের চ্যালেঞ্জের মুখে পড়েছেন।

সবচেয়ে প্রভাবশালী ইসরায়েলপন্থী লবিং সংগঠন আমেরিকান ইসরায়েল পাবলিক অ্যাফেয়ার্স কমিটি (এআইপিএসি) ডেমোক্র্যাটদের কাছে ক্রমেই একটি ‘বিষাক্ত’ ব্র্যান্ডে পরিণত হচ্ছে।

ডানপন্থী শিবিরেও ইসরায়েলের প্রতি সমর্থনের ঐকমত্যে ফাটল আরও স্পষ্ট হচ্ছে।
ট্রাম্প প্রশাসন যেখানে ফিলিস্তিনি অধিকারের পক্ষে সোচ্চার থাকা মানুষদের দমন করতে জায়নবাদের বিরোধিতাকে ইহুদিবিদ্বেষ হিসেবে আইনি রূপ দেওয়ার চেষ্টা করছে, সেখানে ভাইস প্রেসিডেন্ট জেডি ভ্যান্স এ বিষয়ে তুলনামূলক সংযত অবস্থান নিয়েছেন।

সম্প্রতি আনহার্ড ওয়েবসাইটকে দেওয়া সাক্ষাকারে ভ্যান্স বলেন, ‘আসলে যা ঘটছে, তা হলো মার্কিন পররাষ্ট্রনীতির একটি দীর্ঘদিনের ঐকমত্যের বিরুদ্ধে শক্ত প্রতিক্রিয়া। আমি মনে করি, আমাদের এই নিয়ে আলোচনা করা উচিত, সেটিকে চেপে রাখার চেষ্টা করা নয়। অধিকাংশ মার্কিন নাগরিক ইহুদিবিদ্বেষী নন। তাঁরা কখনোই হবেন না। আমাদের উচিত আসল বিতর্কে মনোযোগ দেওয়া।’

সব মিলিয়ে বলা যায়, প্রবণতা বদলাচ্ছে। তবে আপাতত ইসরায়েলের প্রতি যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের অঙ্গীকার দৃঢ়ই রয়েছে।

Headline_English: Junta-backed party set to win first round of Myanmar elections
Content_Enlish:
Voting in the first phase of the general election held under the junta government in Myanmar has ended. Based on preliminary information, the country's military-backed influential political party, the Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP), is on track for a big victory in this phase, party sources have claimed. 

The junta government seized power in 2021 by overthrowing the government of Aung San Suu Kyi in a bloody coup. Four years after seizing power, the junta government has organized month-long elections in phases. 
No excitement, just panic in the 'farce' vote in Myanmar 
However, this election has been subject to intense debate and criticism in the international community since the beginning. According to pro-democracy monitoring organizations, this vote is just a ploy to further strengthen military rule instead of restoring civilian rule in Myanmar. 
“According to various reports from around the country, the USDP is winning most of the seats,” a senior USDP official told AFP in Naypyidaw, speaking on condition of anonymity. 

The country’s Union Election Commission has yet to officially announce the results. The next two rounds of voting are scheduled for January 11 and 25. 

Myanmar’s first round of voting complete, young voter turnout low 
In the last election of 2020, Aung San Suu Kyi’s National League for Democracy (NLD) won by a landslide; but the military annulled the results and seized power, alleging fraud. Suu Kyi’s popular party is now banned. Suu Kyi is currently serving a prison sentence. 

Western diplomats, including the UN human rights chief, have questioned the transparency of the election. They say the vote was rigged by a crackdown on the opposition and by allowing only military allies to run. 

Voting is underway in Myanmar's first election since the ouster of Suu Kyi 
However, junta leader Min Aung Hlaing has claimed that the election will be free and fair. "We guarantee a free and fair election. It is being held under the supervision of the military. So we will not let our honor be tarnished," he told reporters after casting his vote in Naypyidaw on Sunday. 

Voting took place in 102 of the 330 townships in civil war-torn Myanmar in the first round yesterday. However, the junta government has already admitted that voting is not possible in about a fifth of the country's lower house seats due to the conflict.

Headline_English: Agree with 90 percent of Trump's 20-point peace plan: Zelensky
Content_Enlish:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that 90 percent of US President Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan to end the Russia-Ukraine war has been agreed upon.
Zelensky made the remarks at a joint press conference with Trump at his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, US, on Sunday local time. Earlier, the two leaders met on the war in Ukraine. Trump said it was an honor to host the Ukrainian delegation visiting the United States. He called the members of the Ukrainian delegation "strong people." Is the Russia-Ukraine war going to end in 2026?

At that time, Zelensky thanked Trump for a "great" meeting.

Zelensky said that they discussed all aspects of the peace framework at the meeting. There was agreement on 90 percent of the 20-point peace plan. On the other hand, there was 100 percent agreement on the US security guarantees given to Ukraine.

Zelensky called this security guarantee an important milestone for “achieving lasting peace.” He said that Ukraine and European allies will continue to work on this issue. They will meet “in the next few weeks” to finalize all the issues discussed.

Whether the war in Ukraine will end or not will be understood in a few weeks: Trump
Zelensky said that President Trump will organize a meeting with these parties in Washington next January.

Asked whether a trilateral meeting between Russia, the United States and Ukraine could take place, Trump said that it would be possible “at the right time.”

At the press conference, Trump said that whether the Russia-Ukraine war will end or not will be understood in a few weeks.

Zelensky in the meeting with Trump 
Trump also hinted at a meeting with European leaders in Washington for a peace agreement to end this war.

Trump stated that Ukraine and the United States are “very close” to an agreement to end the war. "If everything goes well, it will be done in a few weeks. If it goes badly, it could take a long time," he said.

Headline_English: Protests in various Syrian cities, 3 killed
Content_Enlish:
At least three people were killed in protests by the Alawite community in western Syria on Sunday, local health authorities said. The protests were sparked by a bomb attack on an Alawite mosque in Homs province last Friday that killed eight people. 
Thousands of people took to the streets in several provinces on Syria's western coast and in central Syria on Sunday to take part in the protests. Ghazal Ghazal, the spiritual leader of the Alawites, who are members of the community that ousted President Bashar al-Assad in December last year, called the protests on Saturday to protest the bombing. 

The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, a war monitor, said security forces opened fire in the Alawite-dominated Latakia province to disperse the protesters, killing two. 

Later, Syria's state news agency SANA quoted the Latakia health department as saying that three people were killed and 60 wounded in "attacks by remnants of the former regime" on security forces and civilians during protests in the city. 

AFP correspondents in Latakia and the coastal city of Jableh reported clashes between protesters and supporters of Syria's new Islamist government. Security forces intervened to disperse both sides, firing blank shots into the air. 

"Our security forces and protesters were targeted by direct fire from unknown locations," said Brigadier General Abdul Aziz al-Ahmad, the head of internal security in Latakia, according to the Syrian Interior Ministry. Civilians and security forces were injured. 

An AFP correspondent said government forces were later deployed to disperse pro-government supporters. 

According to the Syrian Observatory, violence has also broken out in Homs province, where several people were injured. 

Violence against religious minorities 
A Sunni extremist group called "Saray Ansar al-Sunna" claimed responsibility for an attack on a mosque belonging to the Alawite community on Friday. Violence against Alawites and other religious minorities has increased since the fall of Bashar al-Assad. 

In March, a massacre was carried out in Syria's Alawite-dominated coastal region. An investigation report by the country's National Commission said that at least 1,426 Alawites were killed in the March massacre. However, the Syrian Observatory claims that more than 1,700 people lost their lives in the massacre. The government claims that the conflict was triggered by an attack on security forces. 

A protester holds a placard with a picture of Ghazal Ghazal, the spiritual leader of the Alawite community. In Latakia, Syria, December 28, 2025 
A protester holds a placard with a picture of Ghazal Ghazal, the spiritual leader of the Alawite community. In Latakia, Syria, December 28, 2025 Photo: Reuters 
Last July, fierce clashes broke out in the southern province of Sweida, which is home to the Druze minority. According to the Syrian Observatory, more than 2,000 people were killed. 
Protests broke out in Homs and other provinces late last month to protest attacks and persecution of Alawites. 

Before the massacre of Alawites in March, members of this community were being arrested on a large scale. They were accused of being supporters of Bashar. 

‘We cannot be marginalized’ 
After the mosque bombing last Friday, Ghazal Ghazal called for protests on Saturday, saying in a video message that the world must be shown that the Alawite community cannot be humiliated or marginalized. 

Ghazal Ghazal, head of the Islamic Alawite Council, said in a video message posted on social media Facebook, ‘We do not want civil war, we want a balance of power between the center and the provinces (political federalism). We do not want your terrorism. We want to determine our own future.’ 

Demonstrators in Latakia displayed placards with Ghazal’s picture. They wrote various slogans on the banners expressing their support for him. They demanded that the authorities reduce centralized power and allow regional autonomy. 

Many of the placards read ‘stop sectarian speech’ and demanded that civilians and former soldiers be paid their salaries. 

“Why this killing? Why this assassination? Why this kidnapping?” asked Numair Ramadan, a 48-year-old businessman who had been protesting in Latakia before the clashes. 
“Assad is gone, we don’t even support Assad… so why this killing?” Numair said, referring to the killings and kidnappings last Friday and earlier. 

The Islamic Alawite Council said in a statement on Sunday that authorities were attacking “unarmed civilians” who had taken to the streets to demand their “legitimate rights.” The statement urged supporters to return home. 
The majority of Syria’s population is Sunni Muslim. While Sunnis are in the majority in Homs, several areas are dominated by Alawites. The Alawites’ faith stems from Shiite Islam. 

There have also been calls for the release of those arrested since Sunday’s protests. On Friday, Syrian state television said 70 prisoners had been released in Latakia because "they were proven not to have committed war crimes." More prisoners would be released if they were found innocent. 

Ahmed al-Sharaa became Syria's interim president after the fall of Bashar al-Assad. His government has promised to protect all communities in Syria. But religious minorities have been unable to trust the new Islamist government's assurances. They are demanding federalism, a balance of power between the central and provincial governments. The central government has so far rejected this.

Headline_English: 2,582 nomination papers have been submitted across the country.
Content_Enlish:
A total of 2,582 nomination papers have been submitted for 300 parliamentary constituencies across the country to contest the 13th National Parliament election. That means an average of more than 8 nomination papers have been submitted for each constituency. The Election Commission (EC) announced this information on Monday night after the deadline for submitting nomination papers for the parliamentary election. However, the EC has not yet given details on how many candidates and how many parties have submitted nomination papers for which constituencies. The referendum on the implementation of the National Charter and the voting for the 13th National Parliament election will be held on February 12. 

The last time to submit nomination papers to be candidates in the parliamentary election was 5 pm today. The nomination papers will be selected from December 30 to January 4. An appeal against the decision of the Returning Officer can be filed with the EC from January 5 to 9. The EC will decide the appeal from January 10 to 18. The last date for withdrawal of nomination papers is January 20. After that, the final number of candidates for the next election will be known. 

Earlier, 2,716 nomination papers were submitted in the last 12th parliamentary election. In the end, 1,969 candidates stood for election. 

The EC said that a total of 3,407 nomination papers were filed by potential candidates to contest the upcoming 13th parliamentary elections. Of these, 2,582 were submitted within the stipulated time. 

The EC divides the country into 10 administrative regions. The EC said that 278 nomination papers were submitted for 33 constituencies in Rangpur region. 260 nomination papers were submitted for 39 constituencies in Rajshahi region. 276 nomination papers were submitted for 36 constituencies in Khulna region, 166 for 21 constituencies in Barisal region, 142 for 15 constituencies in Faridpur region, 444 for 41 parliamentary constituencies in Dhaka region, 311 for 38 constituencies in Mymensingh region, 146 for 19 constituencies in Sylhet region, 365 for 35 constituencies in Comilla region and 194 for 23 constituencies in Chittagong region. 

A political party has to register with the Election Commission to participate in the national elections under a party symbol. Currently, there are 60 political parties registered with the EC. Out of these, the registration of Awami League is suspended. The party is not getting the opportunity to participate in this election. It is not yet confirmed how many candidates from the remaining parties have submitted their nomination papers. 

The 12th parliamentary election of 2024 was controversial due to the boycott of the opposition camp. 28 parties participated in that election, which was known as the 'I-Dummy' election. At that time, there were 44 parties registered with the EC. Before that, all 39 registered parties participated in the 11th parliamentary election of 2018. However, that election was questionable. On the night before the election, there were allegations that ballot boxes were filled with votes in favor of Awami League candidates at various polling stations across the country. That election became known as the 'night vote' in the political arena.

Headline_English: The Ship of Theseus and the NCP's rush to shore
Content_Enlish:
The Greek hero Theseus had a ship. Over time, the wood, nails, and sails of the ship began to deteriorate one by one. Each time the damaged part was replaced with a new part. At one point, it was seen that none of the original parts of the ship were left. Then the question arose, is this ship still Theseus' original ship? This is where the argument began. 

One group says, yes, this is Theseus' ship. Because the changes have happened gradually. The continuity of the ship's use, name, and work has never been broken. Another group says, no, this is no longer Theseus' ship. Because, the original ship was made of everything that has changed, and as a result, the ship is no longer the original ship. 

Let's assume that the name of that ship is the National Citizens Party (NCP). And the hero Theseus is the youth who led the mass uprising of 24. The NCP was formed with the oath of building an inclusive Bangladesh without discrimination. 

The party recently entered into an alliance with the right-wing political party Jamaat-e-Islami in exchange for a compromise of only 30 seats. 

The question arises, is this the same NCP that came to be the leader of moderate politics? Why did they have to clash with the right-wing? And if they find refuge in the right wing, what will happen to their promised politics? 

2. 
After the July mass uprising, the youth dreamed of a new Bangladesh, and the deviation of the political force that was formed by capitalizing on that desire is today indicating a deep crisis. The NCP started its journey with the promise of inclusive and non-discriminatory politics, but its recent strategic decisions have struck at the core of that ideology. Due to this ideological decline and leaning towards the right wing, many of the youth of July today feel extremely betrayed by the party. The leaders and workers associated with the party also feel betrayed. 

The NCP's historical stigmatization of leaning towards Jamaat did not appear suddenly. Signs of this had been visible for a long time. When a political party that started its journey with the agenda of building an inclusive society loses its initial diversity, the bells of its moral decline naturally start ringing. Most of the leaders who were the poster boys of inclusive politics, from Alik Mri to Anik Roy, who were associated with different religions, castes and ideologies, left the party long ago. 

Tasnim Zara and Tajnuva Zabin 
Tasnim Zara and Tajnuva ZabinPhoto: Collected 
Recently, there has been a wave of resignations from the party of leading women leaders. This instability shows that the NCP is no longer able to sustain itself as a safe platform for everyone. The resignation of women leaders like Tasnubha Jabin and Tasneem Zara reveals the extreme instability in the internal environment of the NCP. This deviation of the party's leadership is not just personal, but is part of a deep political strategy. 

Despite the strong objections of the leaders and workers, the NCP has allied with Jamaat-e-Islami. Earlier too, the party's leaders have participated in many anti-Women's Commission and hard-right rallies, despite the objections of their own party's women leaders. This means that the tendency to unite with the right is not recent, the process has been going on for a long time. 

The NCP's alliance with Jamaat-Hefazat has come as a big blow to the youth who wanted a liberal and non-discriminatory society. The Democratic Reforms Alliance has also been hit. 

Read more 
What are the concerns and warnings surrounding the national elections 
01 December 2025 
What are the concerns and warnings surrounding the national elections 
A few days ago, the Democratic Reforms Alliance was formed with the determination to become a 'third force' outside the BNP and Jamaat in the election field. The NCP-led Amar Bangladesh Party and the State Reforms Movement were in that alliance. In just a few days, the NCP reached an agreement with Jamaat without any discussion with its alliance partners. On the one hand, this raised questions about the NCP's political credibility, and on the other hand, it also raised doubts about the NCP's moral convictions. 

The NCP has also shown unprincipledness in its election strategy. After announcing candidates for more than a hundred seats across the country, surrendering to Jamaat in an agreement for only 30 seats is a manifestation of the party's political bankruptcy. 

Earlier, the party also showed its arrogance by nominating Sujan, a rickshaw puller who had become famous for saluting students and the public during the mass uprising, for the Dhaka-8 constituency. After Sujan received the NCP nomination, many of the party's frontline leaders were seen talking loudly about the dreams of the working people. But in the end, Sujan's name did not find a place in the NCP's election candidate list. In this incident, it is natural to think that they could not show moral integrity in using the emotions of the working people only as a political shield. 

3. 
The young people who risked their lives on the streets during the bloody days of the July uprising expected new and transparent politics. But looking at the current course of the NCP, it is clear that the party is no longer a representative of the dreams of the common people, but is just a group obsessed with the game of power sharing. By losing all inclusive faces and taking refuge in the circle of right-wing extremism, the NCP has practically betrayed the youth, who were their main strength. 

The youth of July will not forget this betrayal. Because, the spirit of the movement was not to become a ladder of power for any particular group, but to build a livable society free from discrimination and corruption. 

At the beginning of the article, I compared the NCP to the ship of Theseus. The ship started its journey with people of all religions and castes, promising to reach a safe destination. But for their own narrow interests and greed to see the shore quickly, the sailors have thrown the diverse passengers into the middle of the river one by one. They have also thrown away some guides. It is as if they are taking the ship towards a narrow and dangerous quicksand. The question is no longer limited to the identity of the ship. Rather, the important question is whether this ship, designed with inclusion in mind, will be able to reach any destination at all without its initial guides!

Headline_English: BCB announces new tournament, cricketers call for movement
Content_Enlish:
Eight clubs have boycotted first division cricket in a dispute with the BCB. As promised, the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has announced to organize a new T20 tournament called 'Sonar Bangla Pathway' today with the cricketers of these clubs and the cricketers who did not get a team in the BPL auction. 
In a press release, the BCB said that the matches of the tournament, which will start in the first week of January with 6 to 8 teams, will be held at Bogra and Rajshahi stadiums. The teams will be formed by the national selectors. This initiative is to provide a competitive environment for cricketers who are outside the club cricket and franchise league. The board will also pay the fees of the cricketers playing in the tournament. 

However, the Cricketers' Welfare Association of Bangladesh (CWAB) is not satisfied with this decision of the BCB. They have announced to form a human chain in front of Gate No. 2 of the BCB tomorrow. Even after the BCB announced its decision to organize the tournament, the organization is adamant on its decision, said CWAB President Mohammad Mithun. 

Today, Mohammad Mithun said on Prothom Alo, "Trying to cover fish with leaves is a common practice in Bangladesh. (BCB) is doing something to wash the eyes." He claimed that even if it is a tournament, many cricketers will not get a chance to play in it. Mithun also warned of a strict program for the 'deprived' cricketers, if necessary, "It is starting with a human chain. If we do not find a solution quickly, then there will be a step-by-step (program)." 
Chittagong got nothing but Naeem's initial storm, Rangpur started with a win 
Meanwhile, a source said that former national team captain Tamim Iqbal expressed his anger in a WhatsApp group of cricketers by sending a voice message last night as the BCB had not taken any initiative for the cricketers who could not play in the first division. Leaving aside personal concerns, he requested to think about the cricketers, saying, "Now is a very important time to take a tough action." Speaking to the president of the COAB, he also urged the cricketers to "arrange to do something." 

Tamim Iqbal 
Tamim IqbalTamim's Instagram handle 
43 clubs have announced that they will not participate in the Dhaka leagues, calling the current BCB board of directors 'illegal'. Eight of them have boycotted first division cricket. Despite several attempts by the BCB to negotiate in the past few months, the clubs are adamant about not participating in any tournament under this board.

Headline_English: Research center launched at BRAC University to develop semiconductor industry
Content_Enlish:
The Center of Research Excellence in Semiconductor Technology (CREST) ​​was officially inaugurated at BRAC University on Monday. The inauguration ceremony was organized by the Silicon River Ecosystem, a national framework for integrating biotech, electronics, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics in Bangladesh. The event was attended by representatives from the government, universities, industry, the armed forces and Bangladeshi expatriate experts from around the world. The Bangladesh Semiconductor Industry Association (BSIA) announced this in a press release. 
BRAC University Vice Chancellor Syed Ferhat Anwar delivered the opening speech at the event. He expressed BRAC University’s commitment to developing modern research, building innovation-based human resources and implementing national priorities in science and technology. He expressed hope that BRAC University, as the host institution, will serve as an important academic foundation in Bangladesh’s emerging semiconductor and deep-tech ecosystem. 
Secretary of the Ministry of Science and Technology Md. Anwar Hossain. MA Jabbar, President of BSIA and Managing Director of Neural Semiconductor Limited, delivered the keynote address. He highlighted the importance of domestic capacity development, industry-academia collaboration and building an export-oriented semiconductor industry. It is worth noting that Neural Semiconductor Limited is actively involved as a major industry partner of CREST. 

CREST has been established as a national research center, whose main focus is advanced semiconductor technology, which includes AI-centric chip design, VLSI systems, robotics, materials science, packaging and testing and future hardware platforms. 

Mahbub Rashed, Vice President of GlobalFoundries, delivered a special video message at the event. He highlighted the importance of a comprehensive national vision, strong university-industry linkages and long-term investment in research human resources. According to him, CREST is a timely and strategically sound initiative with the realities of global semiconductor trends and changing supply chains. 

The first CREST Fellowship of the event was announced. Under this fellowship, eight postgraduate and two undergraduate students will get the opportunity to work on nine advanced semiconductor research topics under the supervision of their respective teachers throughout the year. The CREST Fellows are Md. Shajol Al Mamun (Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology—BUET), Akif Hamid (United International University), KM Mehedi Hasan (East West University), Md. Sharif Uddin (University of Asia Pacific), Ishmam Hossain (North South University), Priyanka Das (BRAC University), Junaid Jalil (BUET), Md. Khalid Hossain (BUET), Afsana Anjum Akhi (Dhaka University) and Sheikh Tariful Islam (BUET). 

The winners of the BEAR Summit competition were also honored at the event. Recognizing the innovative thinking and creativity of students and young professionals, BSIA awarded the winners Tk 5,000 each. 

The program said that the development of Bangladesh's National Semiconductor Virtual Hub-BOOST will be led by the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST). In a video message, MIST Commandant Major General Nasim Parvez highlighted MIST's role in structured manpower development, national training infrastructure and implementation-oriented activities. 

The Silicon River Vision and CREST initiatives are the brainchild of Muhammad Mustafa Hussain, Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Purdue University in the United States. He said that Bangladesh has the ability to build influential ideas and implementation, global trust and world-class technology brands. 

The program ended with a vote of thanks by Upma Kabir, Dean of the Faculty of Engineering, University of Dhaka. She recognized the combined efforts of universities, industry, government agencies and expatriate Bangladeshi experts in implementing CREST. At the same time, she highlighted the importance of continuous collaboration, mentorship and institutional commitment to develop the next generation of researchers and innovators. 

A panel discussion was held at the end of the inaugural session. The discussion titled ‘Patent Law and Intellectual Property (IP) Protection: Protecting Innovation in a Knowledge-Based Economy’ was moderated by Professor Md. Golam Samdani Fakir. The panelists included Professor Syed Mahbubur Rahman of BRAC Business School, Director (Industrial Design) of the Department of Patents, Industrial Designs and Trademarks Ashok Kumar Roy, Professor Dilara Afroz Khan of Churchill College, University of Essex, London, and Intellectual Property (IP) Law Expert Taslima Jahan. The speakers recommended formulating a policy on the protection of intellectual property (IP) of innovations in the semiconductor sector through a joint initiative of all stakeholders.

Headline_English: Tasnim Zara collects nearly 3,000 signatures in one day
Content_Enlish:
Tasnim Zara will resign from the National Citizens Party (NCP) and contest the election as an independent candidate from Dhaka-9 constituency. To become a candidate, she needs the signatures of 1 percent of the voters in her constituency. This number is about five thousand. 

To this end, Tasnim Zara has started the signature collection process from Sunday morning. She said that the signatures of about three thousand voters have been collected in one day. 

Tasnim Zara said in a post on her verified Facebook page at around 9:30 pm on Sunday, 'We have been collecting your signatures since the morning. So far, about 3 thousand signatures have been collected. To reach our goal, we need to collect 5,000 signatures. 

Tasnim Zara, mentioning the role of volunteers in collecting signatures, said, “Innovative volunteers like Mahi, Sagarika and Rafi are taking the forms from us and collecting 10-20 signatures in a short time and returning them.” 

Tasnim Zara has collected the signatures of about 3,000 voters in a single day to participate in the elections as an independent candidate from the Dhaka-9 parliamentary constituency. 28 December 2025 
Tasnim Zara has collected the signatures of about 3,000 voters in a single day to participate in the elections as an independent candidate from the Dhaka-9 parliamentary constituency. 28 December 2025Photo: Taken from Tasnim Zara’s Facebook page 
Guidelines have also been given to those interested in participating in this activity for Tasnim Zara. While collecting signatures from voters, it has been said to take the name, address and signature on the first page of the form. However, the columns for serial number and voter number must be left blank. On the second page, the same person's name must be rewritten and the voter ID number must be mentioned. It has been informed that there is a risk of cancellation of the form if the prescribed rules are not followed. 

Booths have been set up at two places in Dhaka-9 constituency for submitting the collected forms. One booth is opposite the National Ideal College adjacent to Taltola Market in Khilgaon and the other is in the Basabo Balur Math area. 

Tasneem Zara announced in a Facebook post on Saturday evening that she will contest the election as an independent candidate from Dhaka-9 constituency after resigning from the Jatiya Nagorik Party (NCP). She took this decision in the context of the NCP's electoral agreement with Jamaat-e-Islami.

Headline_English: Dhaka-Mymensingh road blocked in Uttara demanding arrest of Osman Hadi's killers
Content_Enlish:
People from different walks of life are protesting by blocking the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in front of the BNS Tower in Uttara, demanding the arrest and trial of the killers of Inquilab Mancha convener Shaheed Sharif Osman Bin Hadi. 
Police said that the protest began at 2:40 pm on Sunday by blocking the road in front of the BNS Tower. This stopped traffic on both sides of the road. The protest was going on by blocking the road until the writing of this report at 6:30 pm. 
Uttara Paschim Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Kazi Rafiq Ahmed told Prothom Alo at around 6:40 pm today that the road in front of the BNS Tower has been blocked for four hours. This has created severe traffic jams on both sides of the road. 

Inquilab Mancha announced an all-out blockade in divisional cities across the country from 2 pm on Sunday demanding the arrest and trial of Osman Hadi's killers. The program was announced in a Facebook post by Inqilab Manch at around 1:45 am on Saturday. As part of this, a protest began in front of the Uttara BNS Tower. 

Leaders and activists of Inqilab Manch have been holding a sit-in program in Shahbagh in the capital since last Friday afternoon, demanding the arrest and trial of Osman Hadi's killers. People from different classes and professions have also joined it.

Headline_English: Case filed against 18 people over collision between two launches in Chandpur's Meghna
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) has filed a case against eight named people and 18 others, including 10 unidentified people, in connection with the collision of two launches on the Meghna River in Haimchar, Chandpur. Babu Lal Baidya, Deputy Director (Traffic) of the organization's Chandpur River Port, filed the case at Haimchar Police Station at 11 pm on Saturday. 
The names of those named are Md. Firoz Khan (53), Md. Kamal Hossain (55), Md. Monirul Islam (43), Md. Sultan Khan (45), Md. Mintu (28), Md. Sohel (40), Mohin Hawlader (25) and Md. Moniruzzaman (40). These eight are employees of MV Zakir Samrat-3 and Adventure-9 launches. 

Among the accused, four employees of the Adventure-9 launch, Mintu, Sohel, Mohin Howlader and Moniruzzaman, were arrested and handed over to the court on Sunday afternoon. 

Police reported that 4 people were killed in a collision of two launches in Meghna due to dense fog 
Four passengers were killed in a collision of two launches named Dhaka-bound passenger launch MV Zakir Samrat-3 and Barisal-bound Adventure-9 due to dense fog on Thursday night. Several people were injured. The accident occurred between Haimchar upazila and Harina area of ​​Chandpur. 

Confirming the case in this incident, Haimchar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md. Nazmul Hasan said that the Naval Police will investigate the case filed on behalf of BIWTA Chandpur River Port and conduct further proceedings. 

Naval Police Chandpur Region Assistant Superintendent of Police Imtiaz Ahmed said that the four accused arrested in the Adventure-9 launch were brought to Chandpur Naval Police Station from Jhalokati yesterday. They were handed over to the Chandpur court today. The arrest process for the remaining accused is ongoing.

Headline_English: Mortar shell found in front of junk shop in Jaflong
Content_Enlish:
A mortar shell was found in front of a scrap shop in Jaflong, Gowainghat, Sylhet. Locals saw the mortar shell in front of Bachchu Mia's shop in Jaflong Bazar, East Jaflong Union, Gowainghat around 1 pm today, Sunday. The matter was later reported to the police. 
Upon receiving the information, the police went to the spot and cordoned off the mortar shell to keep it safe. 
Confirming the matter, Officer-in-Charge of Gowainghat Police Station, Sylhet, Md. Moniruzzaman said, it is believed that the mortar shell is from the Liberation War period. After recovering the mortar shell, further action is being taken.

Headline_English: Meghalaya Police and BSF deny reports of two accused fleeing to India
Content_Enlish:
The Indian Border Security Force (BSF) and the Meghalaya Police Headquarters have denied the Bangladesh Police's claim that the two accused in the murder of Inqilab Manch convener Sharif Osman Bin Hadi have fled to India. 

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) said in a press conference on Sunday that the main accused in the Osman Hadi murder case, Faisal Karim Masud, and his associate Alamgir Sheikh have fled to India. The Meghalaya Police have arrested two people named Purti and Sami on charges of assisting them. 

However, a top official of the Meghalaya Police Headquarters has termed the Bangladesh Police's claim as 'untrue' and 'completely false'. The police official said that no formal or informal contact has been made by the Bangladesh Police. None of the accused have been found in the Garo Hills and no arrests have been made. 

The Meghalaya Police said that no intelligence or operational evidence has been found to support the accused crossing the border or the role of the two locals named Purti and Sami. 

The three suspects in the shooting of Sharif Osman Hadi are seen at his public relations office. (From left) Alamgir Sheikh, Rubel and Faisal Karim (wearing black jackets) 
The three suspects in the shooting of Sharif Osman Hadi are seen at his public relations office. (From left) Alamgir Sheikh, Rubel and Faisal Karim (wearing black jackets) Photo: Collected 
The Meghalaya Police Headquarters also said that there was no identification or location of Purthi or Sami or any incident of their arrest. This statement is believed to have been made without verification or coordination with the Indian authorities. 

Supporting the Meghalaya Police statement, Inspector General of BSF (Meghalaya Frontier) O P Upadhyay strongly rejected the Bangladesh Police's claim. He said there was no evidence that these individuals had crossed the international border from the Haluaghat sector into Meghalaya. No such incident had been detected or reported by the BSF. These claims are baseless and misleading. 

Shaheed Sharif Osman bin Hadi was a potential candidate for Dhaka-8 constituency. On December 12, shortly after Friday prayers, Hadi was shot while riding a rickshaw on Calvert Road in Purana Paltan in the capital. After shooting him in the head, the assailants fled on a motorcycle. Osman Hadi was later taken to Singapore for better treatment. He died there on December 18. 

On December 21, his funeral was held at Manik Mia Avenue with the participation of lakhs of people. He was buried next to the tomb of national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, adjacent to the Central Mosque of Dhaka University.

Headline_English: Is the Russia-Ukraine war going to end in 2026?
Content_Enlish:
Ukraine's largest Christmas tree stands in Kiev's Sophia Square. Walking along the cobblestone streets, Vasily, a Ukrainian army officer, confidently says that Russian soldiers are terrified of Ukrainians. "I jumped into their trenches. They are really afraid of us," Vasily tells Al Jazeera. 
However, Vasily believes that the fact that Russian soldiers are afraid does not mean that Ukraine will be able to unilaterally influence the war. Because Russia has a large army, a strong economy and a huge amount of money for war. On the other hand, Ukraine is still lagging behind in terms of manpower and weapons. Vasily says, "When I saw the enemy 800 meters away, I shouted on the radio that I saw a tank, and also told him its location. But from the other side they said, "Wait a minute." Then we realized we had nothing to hit.’ 

According to Volodymyr Fesenko, head of the Kiev-based Penta think tank, Ukraine may have to give up the Kiev-controlled part of the Donetsk region in accordance with the White House’s demands. In exchange, Russia would withdraw its troops from three regions in the east and north. Otherwise, the war could drag on until 2027. 
Vasily made this comment, citing a severe shortage of shells while on the battlefield. Vasily was on the front lines until he lost his left leg in a landmine explosion in 2023. 

Although not on the battlefield, Vasily is still serving in the army. However, he asked Al Jazeera not to reveal his last name in accordance with wartime regulations. 
‘The war cannot be expected to end’. However, a Ukrainian general believes that a ceasefire in the ongoing fighting can be the only realistic achievement. The war will mark five years in February 2026. "With such an aggressive neighbor (Russia), no one can hope for a complete end to the war," former deputy chief of the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces, Ihor Romanenko, told Al Jazeera. "Until we liberate all the territories within the (post-Soviet) 1991 borders of Ukraine, there will be no peace with Russia," Romanenko added. Romanenko believes that if Moscow violates the ceasefire, Kiev will have to stop Russian forces on the battlefield. To do this, Ukraine will have to significantly increase its military strength. 

The former deputy chief of the Ukrainian Armed Forces said that Kiev must build up its army "fairly" without making any concessions, further increase domestic weapons production, prioritize wartime needs in economic decisions and enact stricter military law. 

Romanenko said that this year, the Ukrainian military-industrial complex has managed to provide up to 40 percent of the total needs of the armed forces. The remaining 60 percent is provided by Western allies. According to Romanenko, this assistance must be “fast and effective.” 

Ukrainian soldiers emerge from an underground base with a drone to be used to target Russian troops 
Ukrainian soldiers emerge from an underground base with a drone to be used to target Russian troops Photo: Reuters file photo 
Another analyst said that a golden opportunity to sign a peace treaty could arise in the second half of 2026. If Russia cannot advance on the battlefield and realizes that Kiev is capable of digesting a long-term war, then they (Moscow) may agree to a peace treaty. 

“Everything will depend on the readiness of the Kremlin and Vladimir Putin (Russian President) to give their personal consent,” Volodymyr Fesenko, head of the Kiev-based think tank Penta, told Al Jazeera. 

If Moscow sees a “stalemate” in the war next year, a peace deal could be signed by the end of 2026, Fesenko said. 

Even if Putin agrees, it could take months for both sides to agree on peace proposals, according to Fesenko. 

The expert added that Ukraine may have to give up the Kiev-controlled part of the Donetsk region, as demanded by the White House. In exchange, Russia would withdraw its troops from three regions in the east and north. Otherwise, the war could drag on until 2027. 

Analysts say the second half of 2026 could be a golden opportunity to sign a peace deal. If Russia cannot advance on the battlefield and realizes that Kiev is capable of digesting a long-term war, then they (Moscow) may agree to a peace treaty. 
Whether the war will end or not depends on several factors. 

Kyiv-based analyst Ihar Tishkevich says that in 2026 the very concept of the ‘Western alliance’ will change. Washington will step down from its ‘world policeman’ role and the West’s dominance over the rest of the world will end. 

According to Tishkevich, China is increasing its influence in the world and in Asia. But it is not yet able to fully challenge Washington’s dominance. This change will also weaken international law and affect Ukraine’s position. 

Ihar Tishkevich says that the worst thing for Ukraine would be if the situation were similar to the situation in Finland in 1939. In the Finnish-Soviet War of 1939, Moscow tried to recapture a province. The Soviet army suffered heavy losses. In such a situation, the Nazis of Germany attacked the Soviet Union in 1941. However, Moscow took 1/10 of Finland's territory and forced Helsinki to recognize it. 

Tishkevich mentioned another possible situation. That is the 'Georgian' situation, which was seen during the 2008 Russia-Georgia war. Then Moscow defeated the small Georgian army and recognized the two breakaway regions of South Ossetia and Abkhazia as 'independent'. 

For Ukraine, the creation of a Georgian situation would mean that they would not have control over the occupied territories. However, Kiev would not recognize them as part of Russia. 

In addition to these two possible situations, Tishkevich also believes that a third 'interim' situation could arise. And that is, the war would be suspended and negotiations would continue. 

But according to Nikolai Mitrokhin, a researcher at the University of Bremen in Germany, there is only one way to stop the war. And that is if Ukraine withdraws from the remaining one-fifth of the southeastern Donetsk region or voluntarily withdraws. 

According to Mitrokhin, Ukraine must also accept the loss of control over 90 percent of the Zaporizhzhia region and 15 percent of Dnipropetrovsk. These areas are now under Russian control. 

‘Donetsk was the root of our problem’ 

Nikolai Mitrokhin, a researcher at the University of Bremen in Germany, said that the Western strategy of pressuring Russia with sanctions is ‘weak’. Because many countries are interested in trading with Moscow by avoiding them. This gives the Kremlin enough resources to continue the war for at least another two years. 

In contrast, Ukraine has the capacity to resist, but its “corrupt and cowardly” government is failing to mobilize enough manpower. 

According to Mitrokhin, Ukrainian forces are gradually retreating from several key positions as Western mediators fail to stop Russia. 

“But there is a possibility that Trump and his administration will either force Zelensky to leave Donetsk, or organize a wartime (presidential) election and change power in Ukraine,” Mitrokhin told Al Jazeera. 

Many ordinary Ukrainians are increasingly tired of the war, Russian shelling, power outages and economic recession. 

“Donetsk was the source of all our problems,” Mitrokhin told Al Jazeera. Let Russia take it and spend billions of dollars on reconstruction. 

Tymoshchuk made the remarks in reference to the 2014 pro-Russian uprising in Donetsk and neighboring Luhansk. 

“I want to wake up to the sound of birdsong,” Tymoshchuk said. “Not to the sound of Russian drones and missiles.”

Headline_English: Nine arrested in Italy for allegedly raising money for Palestinian group Hamas
Content_Enlish:
Nine people have been arrested in Italy on charges of raising nearly seven million euros for Hamas. They are accused of raising money for the Palestinian independence movement for more than two years. Italian police said in a statement that the money was raised under the pretext of providing humanitarian aid to ordinary Palestinians. In fact, it was being sent to Hamas under special arrangements. 

Police said that in addition to the nine arrests, they have also seized more than eight million euros in assets as part of the investigation. The suspects raised and supplied money in a way that is suspected of supporting terrorist activities. 
Hamas takes control of Gaza City, fierce battle with armed groups 

The arrests were made in a joint effort by Italy's anti-terrorism and financial irregularities police. 

Police also said that they had analyzed "multiple reports of suspicious financial transactions" with several people suspected of being involved in the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks in Israel. Investigators later uncovered a “complex” fundraising scheme. 

Police said they had arrested nine people and seized more than 8 million euros in assets as part of the investigation. The suspects were suspected of raising and distributing funds in a way that was believed to have helped to finance terrorist activities. 
Italian Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi said the most well-known of the suspects arrested was Mohammed Hannun, who is the president of the Palestinian Association in Italy. 

Hannun had previously called the allegations of funding Hamas “false”.

Headline_English: Zelensky meets with Trump to resolve territorial concessions
Content_Enlish:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is going to the United States to discuss the territorial issue, which is the biggest obstacle in the talks to end the Russia-Ukraine war. He is scheduled to meet with President Donald Trump in Florida on Sunday. This is happening at a time when the peace agreement based on Trump's 20-point peace plan is almost at its final stage. Announcing the meeting with Trump, Zelensky told reporters that many issues can be decided before the start of the new year. An agreement between Washington and Kiev on post-war Ukraine's security guarantees is almost ready. The 20-point peace plan is also 90 percent complete. However, Trump said last Friday that nothing is final without his approval. Zelensky told the US media Axios that the United States has guaranteed a 15-year agreement to guarantee Ukraine's security. He mentioned that there may be an opportunity to extend the term of this agreement. Kiev wants such an agreement that has legal obligations to protect Ukraine from Russian aggression in the future. Because they have not been able to get allies on their side after making several agreements in the past. 
Zelensky told reporters that his meeting with Trump in Florida will be aimed at further "refining" the terms of the draft agreement. A possible agreement on Ukraine's economy will also be raised. Zelensky said that he was not ready to say whether Ukraine would sign an agreement with the United States during this visit. However, he said that Kiev is ready for any agreement. Regarding the cession of Ukrainian territory, Zelensky said that, among other issues, the Donbass and the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant will be discussed.

Headline_English: Will China come to save Venezuela?
Content_Enlish:
As Venezuela and the United States teeter on the brink of war, China has strongly condemned the actions of the United States. In Beijing's view, Washington's recent actions, such as the seizure of Venezuelan oil tankers, attacks on ships accused of drug trafficking, and the naval blockade of the Venezuelan coast, are textbook examples of American unilateralism. Such actions amount to interference in the sovereignty of other countries and are a clear violation of the UN Charter. In a telephone conversation with Venezuelan Foreign Minister Ivan Gil on December 17, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi opposed the "unilateral use of force" by the United States. At the same time, he reiterated China's support for Venezuela's "right to defend its sovereignty and national dignity." Beijing has failed to provide any real assistance to Venezuela beyond its rhetoric. China's caution against falling into a geopolitical trap is very clear. This inaction also highlights the limits of China's influence in Latin America. 
For more than two decades, China has been expanding economic relations with Latin American countries. China is now South America’s top trading partner. Mexico, one of the United States’ closest allies, is also China’s second-largest trading partner. 
The United States has traditionally considered Latin America to be a region of its influence. The United States is naturally suspicious and hostile to China’s growing influence in Latin America. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is an outspoken anti-China figure. He has previously described the Chinese Communist Party as an “evil, genocidal regime.” He has launched diplomatic campaigns against China in various Latin American countries. Rubio has tried to limit relations with China. 

However, the United States has not been able to offer Latin American countries any alternative model of economic cooperation; instead, it has chosen to apply pressure through tariffs. Through this, Washington has essentially maintained its dominance in the struggle for influence. 

However, if the United States overthrows the government in Venezuela, it would reveal the limits of China’s power in Latin America. Such a situation will encourage many Latin American countries to reconsider whether it is a good idea to ally with China so close to an aggressive United States. 
The United States scored a major victory this week in the struggle for influence. Trump-backed conservative Nasri Asfoura won the presidential election in Honduras. During the election campaign, he promised to break diplomatic relations with China and restore formal ties with Taiwan. 

Over the past year, several Latin American countries under the Trump administration have bowed to US pressure, deciding to limit economic ties with China. In February, Panama officially withdrew from China’s Belt and Road Initiative. Then in March, the Hong Kong-based company responsible for operating the Panama Canal announced that it would sell most of its shares to a US company. In December, Mexico announced that it would impose a maximum 50 percent tariff on Chinese goods from January 1. 

The US pressure on Venezuela is not due to its close relationship with China; it is related to the domestic political situation in the United States. Rubio is seeking to fulfill his long-cherished political agenda. The goal is to appease American voters from Venezuela and Cuba. 

Any change in the current regime in Caracas would undoubtedly harm China’s interests. Although China is not dependent on Venezuelan oil (China is not among the top 10 suppliers of Venezuelan crude), the US seizure of a Venezuelan oil tanker undermines China’s energy strategy. 

China is not viewing the escalation of US tensions with Venezuela solely from an economic perspective, but also from a geopolitical perspective. This is important in the larger context of how the US seeks to establish itself as a global power. Given Venezuela’s limited economic value and geopolitical distance, the Chinese government will not spend any resources to defend the Latin American country. 

If the US attacks Venezuela, China will likely use it to promote its multipolar worldview. China will present itself as the guardian of international law and the UN Charter. While China may view the US involvement in a protracted war as a positive development, it is almost certain that China will not come to Venezuela’s aid. 

However, if the US were to overthrow the Venezuelan government, it would expose the limits of China’s power in Latin America. Such a situation would encourage many Latin American countries to reconsider whether it is a good idea to ally with China, so close to an aggressive US. 

Yang Xiaotong is a researcher at the Singapore-based Horizon Insights Center
