Headline_English: Why did Trump attack Nigeria on Christmas?
Content_Enlish:
Despite campaigning on a promise to end US involvement in the “perpetual war”, President Trump has ordered airstrikes on Islamic State-linked bases in Nigeria, accusing the Nigerian government of condoning the persecution of Christians. 

On Christmas Day, Trump said US forces had carried out a “strong and lethal” strike on a forested border area in Sokoto state. The US Africa Command said the strike killed “multiple” IS fighters. The missiles were reportedly fired from a US Navy ship in the Gulf of Guinea. 

Trump and parts of the US Christian right have narrowly portrayed the complex security crisis in Africa’s most populous country as a religious conflict. But successive Nigerian governments have struggled to control a deteriorating security situation that has claimed thousands of lives in recent years. 

Attacks targeting militants in Nigeria 
The plight of Christians in Nigeria has become an issue for the right-wing in the United States; conservative politicians and advocacy groups accuse the Nigerian government of tolerating violence by Islamist militants. 

Conservative activist Charlie Kirk made a powerful statement before his death, highlighting Islamist attacks on churches and religious schools. The statement resonated deeply with Trump supporters, especially evangelical Christians. 

After years of lobbying, the Trump administration designated Nigeria a “country of particular concern” on religious freedom. Trump ordered the Pentagon to prepare military options and threatened “guns-a-blazing” intervention if the killings continued. 

How has Nigeria responded to the attacks? 
Nigeria has welcomed US support for the fight against extremists operating in Sokoto state, but has explicitly separated the attack from the religious emergency claim. 

The State Department said, “Terrorist violence in any form—against Christians, Muslims, or any other community—is an affront to Nigeria’s values ​​and international peace and security.” 

Is there persecution of Christians in Nigeria? 
The violence in Nigeria spans religious lines and has no single cause. Christians and Muslims are roughly equal in the country of about 220 million people; both communities are targeted in jihadist attacks, kidnappings, and criminal violence. The US Commission on International Religious Freedom reported last year that extremist violence in Nigeria has affected “significant numbers of Christians and Muslims” in some states. 

According to the American NGO Aclade (Armed Conflict Location and Event Data), 20,409 people were killed in 11,862 attacks on civilians in Nigeria between January 2020 and September 2025. Of these, 385 attacks and 317 deaths were ‘incidents targeting Christians’, where the victim’s Christian identity was a factor. During the same period, 417 Muslims were killed in 196 attacks. 

The main cause of conflicts between farmers and herders is land and water disputes; however, religious and ethnic differences often fuel these conflicts. Separatist movements and armed criminal gangs, commonly called ‘bandits’, carry out widespread kidnappings and attacks; which affect both Muslim and Christian communities equally. Weak governance, poverty, hunger and unemployment make it much easier for people to be recruited by jihadist groups and organized crime. 

What extremist groups are active in Nigeria? 
Nigeria has been battling a jihadist insurgency since 2009. The conflict has killed at least 40,000 people and displaced nearly two million in the northeast. 

Boko Haram gained international notoriety after the kidnapping of the Chibok schoolgirls; many celebrities, including Michelle Obama, called for their release. 

Boko Haram splinter groups—such as the Islamic State West Africa Province—have since spread to Niger, Chad, and Cameroon, causing widespread chaos and increasing migration within Africa and to Europe. 
The U.S. strikes are believed to have targeted a forest stronghold of an IS affiliate called Lakurawa; the group has roots in neighboring Niger. It has increased its activity in areas along the Nigerian border since a military coup in Niger in 2023. 

What could happen next? 
After the Christmas Day attacks, Trump’s Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth promised “more is coming.” But contrary to the loud declarations, the U.S. military presence in Africa has been reduced in recent years, limiting Washington’s ability to conduct long-term operations. 

Airstrikes alone will do little to address a problem rooted in governance failures and economic crises. Nigeria’s economy is heavily dependent on oil revenues; but price volatility and poor diversification have prevented resources from growing in line with the needs of a rapidly growing population. 

Nigeria’s Defense Minister Christopher Musa has said that military action is only about 30 percent of the total work needed; the remaining 70 percent depends on improving governance and strengthening the state’s presence in remote areas.

Headline_English: Silver is also expensive now, 6 thousand taka per pound
Content_Enlish:
As the price of gold continued to rise, the price of silver was also increasing little by little. However, this time the price of silver has suddenly increased by 933 taka per baht. With this, the price of silver has increased by 6 thousand 65 taka. This is the highest price of silver in the history of the country. 
Not only silver, but also the price of gold is going to set a new record. The reason is that the price of gold is increasing again by 3 thousand 149 taka per baht. With this, the price of a good quality, i.e. 22 carat gold, will increase to about 2 lakh 29 thousand taka. The new price of gold and silver will be effective from tomorrow, Monday. 
Today, Sunday at 9 pm, the Bangladesh Jewelers Association announced the adjustment of gold and silver prices. It claimed that the price of ripe gold in the local market has increased. However, the real reason for the increase in the price of gold is the rise in the price of gold in the global market. 

According to the new price, the price of a 22 carat gold, will increase by 2 lakh 29 thousand 431 taka from tomorrow, Monday. Apart from this, 21 carat gold will be sold at 2 lakh 18 thousand 992 taka, 18 carat gold at 1 lakh 87 thousand 732 taka and traditional gold will be sold at 1 lakh 56 thousand 531 taka.

Accordingly, from tomorrow, 22 carat gold is sold at 3 thousand 149 taka, 21 carat gold at 2 thousand 975 taka, 18 carat gold at 2 thousand 566 taka and traditional gold is sold at 2 thousand 216 taka. 

Although the price of gold has increased continuously, the price of silver has not increased continuously. However, the price of silver has more than doubled this year. Headline_English: Akshay did not agree to three times the remuneration, there is a huge controversy over 'Drishyam 3'
Content_Enlish:
Akshay Khanna is in the news again with 'Dhurandhar'. Since the release of Aditya Dhar's film, Akshay's look and dance have been the talk of social media. When the audience was waiting for the actor's new film, it was revealed that Akshay has been dropped from 'Drishyam 3'! Although there have been rumors about this for a while, now the producer of the film has opened his mouth. 
Producer's complaint 
There have been rumors about Akshay Khanna's exclusion from 'Drishyam 3' for a few days. Bollywood Hungama recently published a report on the matter. Putting an end to the speculation, the film's producer Kumar Mangat Pathak directly complained against Akshay. 

He said that he has been financially affected by Akshay's 'unprofessional behavior' and due to this, legal action is being taken against the actor. At the same time, he confirmed that Jaideep Ahlawat will act in Akshay's place. 
Kumar Mangat Pathak said, 'We had a contract with Akshay Khanna. His remuneration was also finalized after many renegotiations. The producer said that initially he wanted to wear a wig for the character. But director Abhishek Pathak convinced him that this was not realistic. Because, the new installment will start from where the previous installment ended. The sudden appearance of hair would create continuity problems. The producer said that initially Akshay accepted the director's argument. 

The producer alleged that later people around Akshay provoked him to wear a wig again. 'They said that wearing a wig would make him look smarter. Then Akshay raised that demand again. Abhishek was still willing to sit in on the discussion. But suddenly Akshay informed that he no longer wanted to do the film,' said Kumar. 

'Akshay was nothing' 
Kumar Mangat Pathak also said, 'At one time, Akshay Khanna was practically nothing. That was when I made "Section 375" with him in 2019. Even then, many warned us that his behavior was very unprofessional. His presence on the set was poisonous. 

This film gave him a new identity. Then I took him in “Drishyam 2”. After that film, big offers started coming to him. Before that, he was sitting at home for three-four years.' 

Akshaye Khanna in the movie ‘Dhurandhar’. From X 
Akshaye Khanna in the movie ‘Dhurandhar’. From X 
The producer's comment, 'It should be remembered that Ajay Devgn is the face of the “Drishyam” franchise. “Chaaba” Vicky Kaushal’s film, “Dhurandhar is Ranveer Singh’s. If Akshaye Khanna does a film as a solo hero, then that film will not be able to earn even Rs 50 crore in India. If someone thinks that he has become a superstar now, then convince a studio to do a big budget single film. Some actors start thinking of themselves as stars after the success of a multi-starrer film. The same thing happened in Akshay’s case. Success has gone to his head.’ 

Kumar Mangat Pathak claims that Akshay also claims credit for the success of ‘Dhurandhar’. 

‘He told us, “The film is working for me.” But in reality, many things worked together in favor of the film,’ says Kumar. 

The producer said that when the script was narrated to him at Akshay’s farmhouse in Alibaug, he was very excited. ‘He said, “This is a film worth Rs 500 crore. I have never heard such a script in my life.” He hugged the director Abhishek Pathak and the writer. Then the remuneration was fixed, the contract was signed. We gave him an advance, the designer for his clothes was also paid. And just 10 days before the shooting, he left the film.' 

Producer Kumar also said, 'Our "Drishyam" is a big brand. Whether Akshay is there or not, it does not matter to the film. Now, Jaydeep Ahlawat has been taken in his place. By the grace of God, we have got a better actor than Akshay, and most importantly, a better person. I am also the producer of Jaydeep's early career film "Akrosh". 
Legal process begins 
Producer Kumar Mangat Pathak said that a legal notice has been sent against Akshaye Khanna for breach of contract. Speaking to news agency PTI on Saturday, Kumar Mangat Pathak said that Akshaye Khanna suddenly decided not to do the film by sending a text message. After that, they were forced to take legal action

The producer said that Akshaye Khanna was signed for the film last month and was also paid in advance. But his sudden withdrawal has severely disrupted the shooting schedule. 

Kumar Mangat Pathak told PTI, "We have been working on the film for almost two years, and Akshay knew about this whole thing. We had read him the entire script, which he liked. Before signing the contract, there were three rounds of discussions about his remuneration. Only after both parties were satisfied, the contract was signed and the signing amount was given." 

Kumar Mangat Pathak said that Akshaye Khanna was paid three times the amount compared to 'Drishyam 2'. Although he did not reveal the exact amount, he said, "The remuneration he wanted was given." 

The film stars Ajay Devgn, who is once again playing the role of Vijay Salgaonkar. Former police officer Mira Deshmukh is playing Tabu. In the role. 

Akshay's statement on the whole matter was not available. 'Drishyam 3' will be released in theaters on October 2, 2026.

Headline_English: Brigitte Bardot, the actress who took the world by storm, has died
Content_Enlish:
French actress and singer Brigitte Bardot has died. She died today at the age of 91, The Guardian reported. After leaving the film world, she dedicated herself to the animal rights movement, but her political stance became increasingly controversial in later life. Bardot gained international fame with the 1956 film 'And God Created Woman'. The film was written and directed by her then-husband Roger Vadim. For the next two decades, she captured the hearts of thousands of young people as an attractive actress. However, in the early 1970s, she announced her retirement from acting and gradually became active in political and social activities. Her vocal stance on animal rights eventually turned into provocative comments against ethnic minorities and open support for France's far-right party, the Front National. As a result, she was convicted of racist remarks several times.
Early Story
Bardeau was born in Paris in 1934. She grew up in a wealthy, traditional Catholic family. Because of her extraordinary dancing skills, she got the opportunity to study ballet at the prestigious Conservatoire de Paris in Paris.

At the same time, she also started working as a model. At the age of just 15, in 1950, Bardot appeared on the cover of the French magazine L. It was through this modeling work that she received an offer to act in films. She met Roger Vadim at an audition; they married in 1952 after turning 18.

Bardot in the movies
Although she initially played small roles, her importance gradually increased. In 1955, she played opposite Dirk Bogarde in the film ‘Doctor at Sea’, which was widely popular in the UK.

However, Bardot’s career turned around with Vadim’s ‘And God Created Woman’. She became an international star by playing the role of a rebellious teenager. The film was a huge success in France and other countries around the world, and brought Bardot to the forefront of French cinema.

Not only for movie lovers, she quickly became an inspiration for thinkers and artists. Young John Lennon and Paul McCartney told their then-girlfriends to dye their hair blonde in Bardot's style. In 1958, columnist Raymond Cartier wrote a long article in the Paris-Machine magazine—'Le ca Bardot'.

In 1959, philosopher Simone de Beauvoir published her famous essay 'Brigitte Bardot and the Lolita Syndrome'. In it, Bardot was portrayed as the most free-spirited woman in France. In 1969, she was chosen as the first living model for Marianne, the symbol of the French Republic.

One movie after another
In the early 1960s, Bardot starred in a series of important French films—Henri-Georges Clouzot's Oscar-nominated film 'The Truth', Louis Malle's 'Very Private Affair' and Jean-Luc Godard's 'Contempt'. In the second half of the decade, she also ventured into Hollywood. Her notable films at this time included 'Viva Maria!' and the Western film 'Shalako' opposite Sean Connery.

Bardot in song
In addition to films, Bardot was also active in the music world. She recorded songs written by Serge Gainsbourg. At the time, she was having an extramarital affair with Serge. However, when her then-husband Gunter Sachs found out about the matter, Bardot requested that the song not be released for fear of scandal. Later, Serge re-recorded the song with Jane Birkin, which was a huge commercial success.

The pressure of stardom
The pressure of stardom was becoming increasingly unbearable for Bardot. In a 1996 interview with the Guardian, she said, "The frenzy that surrounded me always seemed unreal. I was never quite ready for stardom."

In 1973, at the age of 39, she retired from acting after the film 'The Edifying and Joyful Story of Colino'.

She then focused her attention on the animal protection movement. In 1977, she participated in the anti-seal hunting movement and in 1986 founded the Brigitte Bardot Foundation. She sent letters of protest to world leaders against the killing of dogs in Romania, the killing of dolphins in the Faroe Islands, and the killing of cats in Australia. She also regularly made controversial comments about the slaughter of animals according to religious rites.

In her book 'A Cry in the Silence', published in 2003, Bardot took a stand for right-wing politics. There, she used strong language against homosexuals, the teaching community, and the so-called "Islamization of French society." This also led to her being convicted of incitement to racism. Bardot was married four times—to Roger Vadim (1952–1957), to Jacques Charrier (1959–1962); their only child, Nicolas, was born in 1960, to Gunter Sachs (1966–1969), and to former Le Pen advisor Bernard D'Ormal in 1992. She also had several relationships, including with Jean-Louis Trintignant and Serge.

Headline_English: What to do if your child is hyperactive or fidgety
Content_Enlish:
Children are lively—this is normal. But sometimes it seems like the child's 'on button' is always on! Running around, talking, restlessness—nothing stops from morning to night. Parents ask, is it normal for the child to be so restless, or is it a problem? In fact, restlessness is not always a problem. However, it is important to understand the child's hyperactivity and give him the right direction. 

Common signs of hyperactivity in a child 

Inability to sit still. 

Interrupting others while talking. 

Doing whatever suddenly comes to mind. 

Inability to maintain attention. 

Starting and stopping work and getting busy with other things. 

Excessive running or jumping. 

Difficulty following rules in games. 

Getting angry or frustrated very quickly. 

Why some children are hyperactive 

In most cases, this is the nature of some children. It appears as a natural manifestation of their excess energy. This is normal behavior according to age. However, sometimes hyperactivity can be a sign of ADHD. Whether this behavior has been going on for a long time or not and whether it is causing problems in daily life is important. 

A child may be like this due to genetics. Apart from this, it can be caused by some parts of the brain working differently, excessive screen time, not getting enough sleep, eating too much sugar or processed foods, stress, fear, anxiety, excessive screen use at a very young age. 

What parents should do 

Try to make the child sleep, eat, read, and play at the same time every day. Routine creates security in the child's mind and stabilizes behavior. Do not let him stare at the screen for more than 1 to 2 hours a day. Make him run in open spaces, cycle, play football, swim, etc. Do not say 'finish all the homework'; rather say 'do the first three lines, then take a break'. Praise even small successes. This increases good behavior. Make sure he sleeps 8 to 10 hours every day. Do not give too much sugar or processed foods. Feed plenty of water and fruits and vegetables. Give light meals. Too much noise at home, TV or other people's quarrels increase the child's restlessness. These cannot be done. If the child's behavior creates problems in studies, friendships or family, then seek expert advice. 

Remember, hyperactive children do not mean problems; rather, they are creative, curious, lively and fast learners. Your patience, understanding and love are the strength of his future.

Headline_English: Fake Windows activation domains being used to spread PowerShell-based malware
Content_Enlish:
A malicious PowerShell script has been spread through a fake domain created using the name of Microsoft Activation Scripts (MAS), a popular open source tool used to activate Windows. These scripts are infecting users' computers with a malware called 'Cosmali Loader', according to technology news outlet BleepingComputer. 

According to the report, several MAS users on the social media Reddit reported that a warning popup message suddenly appeared on their computers. The message said that their systems were infected with malware due to a small mistake in writing a command in PowerShell while activating Windows. Users said that instead of the actual domain 'Get dot activated dot win', they mistakenly wrote 'Get dot activate dot win'. The difference in just one letter gives attackers the opportunity to confuse users. It is believed that the malicious script is downloaded from the fake domain and activated on the computer. 

The warning claims that the mistake has led to the introduction of the ‘Cosmali Loader’ malware into the computer. The message also states that the malware’s control panel is not properly secured and unauthorized access there could put the affected computer at risk of being controlled remotely. Users are advised to quickly reinstall Windows to ensure their security. They are also asked to check for unusual PowerShell processes running in Task Manager as evidence of infection. 

Security researcher Russianpanda said that these warnings are related to the open source malware Cosmali Loader. There are previous examples of this malware spreading cryptocurrency mining software and a remote access trojan called Xworm. Earlier, malware analyst Karsten Hahn from the Gdata company also reported similar pop-up warnings. 

However, there was no confirmed information about who exactly sent these warnings to the affected users. BleepingComputer reports that it is believed that a security researcher gained access to the malware's control panel and sent these messages to warn affected users from there. 

MAS is essentially an open source collection of PowerShell scripts, through which Windows and Microsoft Office are activated. It uses hardware ID activation, KMS emulation, and various bypass methods. Although the project is openly maintained on GitHub, Microsoft considers it an unauthorized way to activate products without a valid license. Meanwhile, the maintainers of the MAS project have also warned users about this malware campaign. They have urged them to carefully check each character when writing commands in PowerShell. They also advised them to refrain from running remote code without fully understanding what a script does. They have also said that if necessary, they should test in a sandbox and avoid running code from unknown sources.

Headline_English: Coach Mahbub Ali Zaki dies of heart attack on BPL field
Content_Enlish:
The match will start in twenty minutes at the Sylhet International Stadium. Cricketers of Rajshahi Warriors and Dhaka Capitals were warming up at both ends of the field. They were accompanied by members of the coaching staff. Meanwhile, Dhaka Capitals' assistant coach Mahbub Ali Zaki suddenly collapsed on the field. He was immediately taken to the hospital with CPR. A little later, it was learned that Mahbub Ali is no more! The hospital authorities have confirmed the news of his death to the BCB, said BCB's chief physician Debashish Chowdhury. 

Mahbub Ali was admitted to Al Haramain Hospital in Sylhet. The Dhaka Capitals franchise authorities said that he died of a heart attack. After Mahbub Ali fell ill, a crowd was seen gathering around him on the field. Dhaka Capitals had said in a press release at the time that Mahbub Ali collapsed on the field during practice because he felt unwell. But after being taken to the hospital, he could not be saved. He died at 1 pm. 
Dhaka Capitals won the toss and fielded against Rajshahi. A shadow of mourning descended on the Sylhet International Stadium after news of his death came during the match.

Headline_English: Messi is the best athlete of the first 25 years of the 21st century, who are in the top 10?
Content_Enlish:
By the end of 2025, a quarter of the 21st century is coming to an end. Since the beginning of 2000, the feats of extraordinary athletes have reached such a point that the question of who is the ‘best of the best’ in the first quarter of the new century has become almost inevitable. But how do you decide when each athlete selected has shown dominance in their respective sports in different ways? Should you prioritize team sports or individual sports? Olympic sports or professional leagues? Making a decision is not easy. 

Nevertheless, the French-language Canadian media Le Journal Quebec has taken the risk and ranked the 25 best athletes of the past 25 years. Check out the top 10 of this ranking, which is based on the athletes’ achievements and records, social and cultural influence, generational inspiration and personal brand outside of sports, here. 
Journal Quebec on the top 25 athletes of the first 25 years of the 21st century 
1. Lionel Messi 
Lionel MessiReuters 
There is no other sport that evokes emotions like football around the world. Who is the best of his generation? Without a doubt, Lionel Messi. Some even call him the best of all time. The Argentine superstar has endless achievements—10 La Liga and 4 Champions League titles, eight Ballon d’Ors. 

He is also the top scorer for Argentina and FC Barcelona. His achievements were already legendary, but in 2022, at the age of 34, he added a final exclamation mark by winning the World Cup with Argentina, becoming a major icon of the sport around the world. 

2 
Tom Brady (American Football) 

American football is called the most team-based game, but in terms of personal impact, Tom Brady is unmatched. He won seven Super Bowls in 20 years with the New England Patriots and three years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. No quarterback before him had won more than four. 

His long career, winning his first Super Bowl in 2001 and his last in 2020, has become legendary. He has been the regular season MVP three times and the Super Bowl MVP five times. He holds numerous records, including 251 wins and 649 touchdown passes. 

3 
Michael Phelps (swimming) 
Michael Phelps. 
Michael Phelps. AFP 
Many believe that American swimmer Michael Phelps should be at the top of the list, and it is hard to deny this argument. Between 2004 and 2016, he won 28 Olympic medals, 23 of which were gold. 

Phelps' eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics were the most in a single Olympic Games in any sport. He set seven world records at that Games. At the end of her career, she held 39 world records. While swimming's global impact is not comparable to that of other sports, Phelps has transcended her own game. 

4 
Serena Williams (tennis) 
Serena Williams 
Serena WilliamsAFP 
Her on-court performances can be discussed for hours, but even greater is Serena Williams's enormous impact on women's tennis, sports in general, and the black community. 

The American tennis star has become a cultural icon, her presence in major advertising campaigns has made her a global star. In tennis, she spent 319 weeks at the top of the WTA rankings, winning 73 titles, including 23 singles Grand Slams. 

5 
Usain Bolt (athletics) 
Usain Bolt 
Usain BoltAFP 
There is no doubt that Usain Bolt is the greatest sprinter in history. There have been many great sprinters, and there are still many, but Bolt is the exception. The Jamaican has won eight Olympic gold medals and 11 world championships. 

His 100m world record of 9.58 seconds in 2009 still stands. Eight years after his retirement in 2017, he is still considered the fastest man in the world. He is the only sprinter to win gold in both the 100m and 200m events at three consecutive Olympics. 

6 
LeBron James (basketball) 
LeBron James 
LeBron JamesAFP 
LeBron James or Michael Jordan—who is the greatest of all time? Let's leave that debate to others. However, there is no doubt that LeBron James is ahead of everyone from 2000 to 2025. Individually, he is the highest point scorer in NBA history, has won four MVP awards, and has been on the All-Star team 20 times. 

LeBron has won four NBA Finals as a team, becoming Finals MVP each time. He has played in 10 finals for three different teams—the Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers and Los Angeles Lakers. 

7 
Novak Djokovic (tennis) 
Novak Djokovic 
Novak DjokovicReuters 
In an era dominated by Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal, Serbian star Novak Djokovic has not only proven himself, but also surpassed them in terms of achievements. The 'Joker' is now at the top of the list, having won an incredible 24 Grand Slam titles. 

Djokovic has spent a record 428 weeks at the top of the ATP rankings in his career, finishing the year as the world's best eight times. He has won each Grand Slam at least three times, including the Australian Open 10 times. He also added Olympic gold to his illustrious career with the 2024 Paris Olympics. 

8 
Simon Biles (Gymnastics) 
Simon Biles 
Simon BilesReuters 
Simon Biles is the most successful gymnast in history, having won a total of 41 medals in the international arena. Of these, 30 came at the World Championships and 11 at the Olympics. She became a global star when she won four gold medals at the 2016 Rio Olympics. Her dominance was so strong that five gymnastics tricks are now known by her name. 

Biles was undefeated in the all-around at the US Championships, World Championships and Olympics from 2013 to 2021. She made headlines worldwide when she temporarily withdrew from the 2021 Tokyo Olympics due to mental health issues. She returned to the 2024 Paris Olympics and won four medals. 

9 
Kobe Bryant (Basketball) 
Kobe Bryant 
Kobe BryantReuters 
The late Kobe Bryant, who died in a helicopter crash in 2020, profoundly influenced an entire generation of basketball fans. He won five NBA titles with the Los Angeles Lakers, establishing himself as one of the greatest players in history. 

Bryant was a two-time Finals MVP and 18-time regular-season All-Star. His influence was far-reaching beyond sports—his philosophy, known as the “mamba mentality,” has become a symbol of discipline, dedication and perfection in every aspect of life. 

10 
Cristiano Ronaldo (football) 
Cristiano Ronaldo 
Cristiano RonaldoReuters 
Apart from winning the FIFA World Cup, Cristiano Ronaldo has incredible achievements in all the top competitions in football. The Portuguese star, who has won the Ballon d'Or five times as the best player of the year, has set great records wherever he has played. His career is highlighted by five Champions League, three Premier League and two La Liga titles. 

Ronaldo holds the record for the most goals in the Champions League with 140 and the most goals in international football with 143. He is the only player in the world to have scored more than 100 goals for four different clubs and played more than 1300 matches. His influence is still unwavering with more than a billion followers on social media.

Headline_English: Customers of five banks will be able to withdraw money only after transferring their accounts.
Content_Enlish:
The process of transferring the accounts of customers of the five Islamic banks that are in the process of merging to the newly formed Sammilit Islami Bank is underway. Once the process is completed, depositors of the five banks will be able to withdraw up to two lakh taka from their accounts. Bangladesh Bank said this information in a notification today, Saturday. However, a source in Bangladesh Bank said that work is underway to allow depositors to withdraw money from December 30 or 31. The process of transferring accounts will be completed before then. There are about 6 million account holders in the five banks. For this, 12-13 thousand crore taka will be spent from the Bank Deposit Insurance Fund. 
The five banks that are going to merge are First Security Islami Bank, Social Islami, Union, Global Islami and Exim Bank. These banks are struggling to pay salaries to employees due to liquidity crisis and customers are also facing problems in withdrawing money. Among the five banks, Exim Bank was owned by Nazrul Islam Majumdar, former chairman of the Bangladesh Association of Banks (BAB), an organization of bank entrepreneurs. The remaining four were under the control of Saiful Alam, the head of the S Alam Group in Chittagong and a much-discussed businessman. Both of them were close to the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. They have shares in these banks in both names and anonymously, and are also beneficiaries of loans. Bangladesh Bank has nullified all of their shares. 

The Bangladesh Bank notification said that the process of transferring the bank accounts of the depositors of the five banks under the merger process to the newly formed Sammilit Islami Bank is almost at its final stage. If the work is completed within the next (current) week, the deposits of the bank accounts of the customers of the existing five banks will be automatically transferred to the newly formed Sammilit Islami Bank account. As a result, the depositors will get the opportunity to withdraw up to a maximum of two lakh taka through their existing check books. The remaining deposits (if any) will be protected in their bank account and profit will be paid on those deposits at the prevailing rate. Being a state-owned bank, it is expected that the public will have confidence in this newly formed bank and as a result, the demand for depositors to withdraw money will be reduced to a large extent.

Headline_English: The priorities that the new government must ensure
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh is heading towards a national election in less than two months. Naturally, the country’s talk, discussion and debate revolve around political issues; but when the elections are over and an elected government takes power, the country’s economy will be a key issue for the administration. 

This issue should be the top priority for the new government. Because, leaving aside all other issues, the economy is the most pressing concern for the common man. These include inflation, unemployment, inequality of opportunity, debt, quality of basic social services, economic uncertainty and mob violence. But the list is long. So, naturally, it is expected of the new government that the economy will be their priority. 

At the outset, attention needs to be drawn to three issues. First, the economy will be given priority, and along with the announcement of this commitment, it is also necessary to identify which issues will be prioritized in that commitment. Second, the new government will incorporate the commitments and identified priorities of the interim government into its policies. Third, the ruling party must formulate a medium-term economic framework for Bangladesh immediately after assuming power. 

Read more 
How possible is it to suppress the 'mafia economy' in Bangladesh 
01 September 2025 
How possible is it to suppress the 'mafia economy' in Bangladesh 

In view of the current reality of the Bangladesh economy and the future of this economy, this economic framework needs to give importance to three types of problems—current problems, concentrated problems, and impending problems. Poverty and inequality are at the top of the current problems. According to the World Bank report, much of Bangladesh's achievements in poverty alleviation in the recent past have been lost in recent times. 

From 2010 to 2022—in these 12 years, Bangladesh was able to bring about 34.9 million people of its population above the poverty line; but in the last three years, the poverty rate in Bangladesh has risen again from 18 percent to 21 percent. Today, 36 million people in the country live below the poverty line. 

One of the realities of our economy is inequality and discrimination. According to the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey 2022, the average under-5 mortality rate in the country is 31 per thousand. Although there is a gap between rich and poor families, this rate is usually around 45 to 50 per thousand for the poorest 20 percent of families. 

The list of concentrated problems in Bangladesh is quite long. Jobless growth, huge unemployment, defaulted loans, and significant human deprivation are entrenched in the Bangladesh economy. According to official statements, the number of unemployed people in the country is currently 2.7 million. The unemployment rate among university graduates is 13 percent. The unemployment rate among youth is double the overall unemployment rate in the country. Currently, jobless growth and unemployment are converging as problems in the Bangladesh economy. 
The second ongoing problem is the low quality of basic social services like health and education. There is no doubt that the education and health sectors have expanded quantitatively; but with those advances, there has been no qualitative change in services. In education, knowledge or skill acquisition has not become the main objective of education; rather, certification has become the main objective of education. The main goal of the health sector is to build physical infrastructure, not to provide high-quality services. In both sectors, high-quality services are reserved for the wealthy class, and such inequality acts as a driving force in accelerating inequality in Bangladeshi society. 

The third problem is a slowdown in savings, investment and wealth accumulation. Compared to neighboring countries, the savings rate in Bangladesh is very low. In the past, Bangladesh could not attract sufficient foreign direct investment. Just look at Vietnam to understand our shortcomings in this regard. The tax-to-national income ratio in Bangladesh is only 8 to 9 percent, in Nepal 19 percent and in India 12 percent. Bangladesh has historically relied on indirect taxes like export taxes and that dependence has not yet shifted to direct taxes. 

Read more 
How BNP wants to build the country 
December 22, 2025 
How BNP wants to build the country 
The list of concentrated problems in Bangladesh is quite long. Jobless growth, huge unemployment, non-performing loans, and significant human deprivation are entrenched in the Bangladesh economy. According to the government, the number of unemployed in the country is currently 2.7 million. The unemployment rate among university graduates is 13 percent. The unemployment rate among youth is double the overall unemployment rate in the country. Currently, jobless growth and unemployment are condensing as problems in the Bangladesh economy. 

The country's financial sector is in the midst of a deep crisis. The amount of non-performing loans in Bangladesh has reached the highest level in the country's history, which is currently 6 lakh 59 thousand crore taka. None of the huge money illegally smuggled abroad has been recovered. Financial discipline has not yet returned. 

Non-poverty deprivation is intensifying. About 110 million people do not have access to safe drinking water. Only 41 percent of children under the age of five are not registered, and 59 percent do not have birth certificates. 57 percent of children do not reach grade 10 after completing primary education. Child labor has increased in the last six years. The rate of child marriage has increased. The climate change crisis is also intensifying, which will have a negative impact on economic growth and human development. Inequality and violence against women in Bangladesh are not just an unimaginable reality; they have emerged as a concentrated crisis. 

The upcoming problems of the Bangladesh economy will arise from within and outside the country. After many years of continuous decline and stagnation, the fertility rate of women in Bangladesh has increased in recent times. This increase will have an impact on the country's population growth and urbanization. 

This increase will have an adverse effect on the economy of Bangladesh. For example, Dhaka, with a population of 36.6 million, has already emerged as the world's second largest city. Dhaka's social service infrastructure such as air pollution, sewage, and waste management is gradually becoming fragile. With the loss of open fields, ponds, and water bodies, Dhaka has become a city of bricks and stones. All these will create an imminent crisis in public life. 

The transition from the least developed country queue in the global arena and the imposition of retaliatory import tariffs by the United States may create various problems in the Bangladesh economy in the coming days. The question is, how prepared is Bangladesh for those crises and whether Bangladesh will be able to move forward by overcoming all the crises with a well-thought-out plan. 

The next elected government of Bangladesh will have to keep these crises in mind and incorporate them into its future economic blueprint. If the government moves in the right direction with objective and wise policies and institutional strength, Bangladesh can build an economic path. Where the well-being of all the people of the country can be ensured by ensuring an economic democracy with equality and non-discrimination. If the newly elected government fails in that regard, then it will be a huge missed opportunity; which has happened many times in the history of Bangladesh. 

Dr. Salim Jahan is a former Director of the Human Development Report Office and Poverty Reduction Division of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

Headline_English: Tarique Rahman is contesting from two seats, Partha is leaving Dhaka-17 and going to Bhola
Content_Enlish:
BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman is going to contest from the Dhaka-17 constituency as well as the Bogra-6 parliamentary constituency. Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) chairman Andaliv Rahman Partha is going to contest from Bhola instead of this constituency. 

Out of the 20 constituencies in Dhaka, the three constituencies that BNP has left vacant include the Dhaka-17 constituency, which consists of elite areas like Gulshan-Banani and Baridhara. It was being heard that BJP chairman Andaliv Rahman would contest from this constituency as an alliance partner of BNP. 
According to BNP sources, Tarique Rahman has applied to become a voter of Dhaka-17 constituency today, Saturday, after returning home. Among them, senior BNP leaders have requested him to contest from Dhaka-17 constituency. After learning about the matter, Andaliv Rahman has decided to contest from Bhola-1 constituency out of respect for Tarique Rahman. 

Party sources said that Andaliv Rahman has been offered to join BNP and contest under the paddy sheaf symbol. The source says that Andaliv Rahman did not agree to this proposal. He has said that he will contest from Bhola-1 constituency under his party's symbol. He has already submitted his nomination papers for this constituency (Bhola-1). Earlier, BNP had initially announced Golam Nabi Alamgir as the candidate for this constituency. Now, it is learnt that BNP will not field any candidate against Andaliv in this constituency.

Headline_English: Tasneem Zara is an independent candidate, not from NCP
Content_Enlish:
Tasnim Zara, the senior joint member secretary of the National Citizens Party (NCP), has announced that she will be an independent candidate amid differences in the party over the seat-sharing agreement with Jamaat-e-Islami. 

The NCP had nominated her as a candidate for the upcoming 13th parliamentary election in Dhaka-9 constituency. However, she announced on Saturday that she will not contest for any party but as an independent candidate. 

Tasnim Zara made this announcement in a post on her verified Facebook page around 7 pm today. There, she did not mention anything about the NCP. However, NCP sources said that Tasnim Zara has already submitted her resignation letter to the party's top leadership. 

Doctor Tasnim Zara has been associated with the party since its formation in February this year. The party was formed by the young leaders of the uprising. After taking charge in the party, Tasnim Zara was active in various programs. 
30 NCP leaders write to Nahid Islam objecting to alliance with Jamaat 

The NCP has already announced party candidates for 122 seats to participate in the 13th parliamentary elections to be held on February 12 under the Shapla Kali symbol. Tasneem Zara has been nominated for Dhaka-9 (Khilgaon, Sabujbagh, Mugda) seat. After the news of the NCP's seat agreement with Jamaat in the elections was recently leaked, anger and protests erupted among many of the uprising. 30 leaders of the party also wrote a letter to NCP convener Nahid Islam raising objections. 

Meanwhile, Tasneem Zara wrote on Facebook, announcing that she would become an independent candidate, 'My dream was to go to parliament from the platform of a political party and serve the people of my area and the country. However, due to the practical context, I have decided not to participate in the elections as a candidate of any particular party or alliance. I promised you and the people of the country that I will fight for you and to build a new political culture. Whatever the situation, I am determined to keep my promise. That is why I will participate in this election as an independent candidate from Dhaka-9. 

Tasneem Zara did not mention the NCP in explaining the reason for this decision. She wrote, "When a party is a candidate, that party has a local office, a well-organized workforce. There is an opportunity to talk to the government and administration about security or other objections and concerns. However, since I am not with any party, I will not have any of those. My only hope is you. As your daughter, if you give me affection and support in view of my honesty, dedication and indomitable will to do new politics, then I will get the opportunity to serve you." 

There are differences in the discussion of Jamaat-NCP seat agreement 
There was no immediate reaction from the NCP on Tasneem Zara's decision. However, the party's chief coordinator and head of the election management committee, Nasiruddin Patwari, liked her post. 

At the end of the post, Tasnim Zara talked about ‘two special issues’ in becoming a candidate. As the first issue, she wrote, ‘As per the legal obligation, to stand as an independent candidate in the election, the supporting signatures of 4,693 voters of Dhaka-9 constituency are required in a specific form. I will start collecting these signatures tomorrow (Sunday).’ 

Tasnim Zara has asked for spontaneous help from the people of the constituency, stating that it is almost impossible to collect the signatures of so many people in one day. She urged those who want to help in this work by providing a place to sit or as a volunteer to join the Facebook group tomorrow. 
NCP announces candidates for 125 seats: Who got nominations and where 

Tasnim Zara has already raised 4.7 million taka through crowdfunding to cover the election expenses. As the second issue, she wrote that she will refund the money to those who want to get their money back because she is an independent candidate. She also provided a link to fill out an online form in the post to get her money back for those who had sent her money through bKash. 

Tasnim Zara said that those who had sent money through banks will soon be informed about the refund process. 

Tasnim Zara ended this post addressed to the people of Dhaka-9 constituency with the words, ‘Your daughter, Tasnim Zara.’ 

Tasnim Zara, who completed her MBBS from Dhaka Medical College, did her master’s degree from Oxford University in the UK. She also worked as a junior doctor in the UK’s National Health Service (NHS). 

Tasnim Zara became known in Bangladesh by identifying misinformation and rumors during the Covid pandemic and making health videos on her Facebook page. Her videos were also broadcast on Robi Ten Minutes School.

Headline_English: 30 NCP leaders write to Nahid Islam objecting to alliance with Jamaat
Content_Enlish:
Thirty members of the party's central committee have objected to the possibility of a political alliance or seat deal between the National Citizens Party (NCP) and an 8-party alliance including Jamaat-e-Islami. 

They wrote a letter to party convener Nahid Islam on Saturday expressing deep concern over this important policy issue. The party's joint member secretary Mushfiqur Us Salehin confirmed the letter to Prothom Alo. 

In the letter, the leaders cited the NCP's declared ideology, historical responsibility related to the July mass uprising, and democratic ethics as the basis for their objection. 

The letter states, "For the past one year since the July Uprising, the divisive political activities of Jamaat-e-Islami and its student organization Chhatra Shibir, espionage and sabotage within other parties, attempts to blame the NCP for various misdeeds, lies and propaganda about the Bangladesh Democratic Students' Union (BAGHS) and later on Chhatra Shakti in the student parliament elections, attempts to assassinate the character of the NCP and our student organization's female members through their online force, and above all, the fear of the rise of social fascism centered on religion have become ominous signs for the future of the country." 

The letter further states, "Jamaat-e-Islami's political history, especially their anti-independence role during the great liberation war of 1971, their cooperation in genocide and their position on various crimes committed at that time—are fundamentally at odds with the democratic spirit of Bangladesh and the values ​​of our party." 

The statement given by the 30 members of the party's central committee Letter 
Letter from 30 members of the party's central committee 
The leaders mentioned in the letter that any kind of alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami would weaken the moral standing of the NCP. They also believe that it would have a long-term negative impact on political credibility. 

The leaders said that earlier, the party's convener Nahid Islam and chief coordinator Nasiruddin Patwari had announced several times to hold independent elections by fielding candidates for 300 seats. They have announced 125 candidates after selling about 1500 nomination papers. Now, they feel that entering into any alliance for a few seats is tantamount to cheating the nation. 

In the letter, the NCP leaders also said, 'We have observed with great concern that whenever the news of the possibility of this alliance has come to the fore through the media, a large number of people, including workers and organizers who were supporting us, have immediately started withdrawing their support from our party. If the people who support us are moderate and expect new politics, then in the future we will lose the party's moderate support base.' 

The letter also requested to take a clear stand on not entering into any political alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami, and said that strategy should be determined based on policy positions, policy positions should not be sacrificed for strategic reasons. 

The signatory leaders are Chief Member Secretary Mushfiqur Us Salehin, Central Organizer Arman Hossain, Joint Chief Organizers Emon Syed and Sadia Farzana Sina, Joint Chief Coordinators Khan Md. Mursalin, Md. Saddam Hossain, Abdullah Al Faisal and Nazin Nowroz Shah; Joint Member Secretaries SM Saif Mostafiz, Md. Farhad Alam Bhuiyan and Joint Member Secretary Faridul Haque, Joint Organizer (Northern Region), Senior Joint Member Secretary, National Youth Power Dutee Aranya Chowdhury; Joint Conveners Nusrat Tabassum, Arpita Shyama Dev and Khaled Saifullah; Organizers (Southern Region) Nafiul Islam, Hamza Ibne Mahbub, Nayan Ahmed, Asad Bin Roni, Wahid Ul Zaman and Md. Shawkat Ali; Organizer Rafiqul Islam Aini; Central Members Jawanul Karim, Tariq Adnan Mukh, Md. Imran Hossain, Syeda Neelima Dola, Salauddin Jamil Sourav, Khalid Saifullah Jewel, Tauhid Tanzim and Mahbub A Khoda.

Headline_English: Rashed Khan officially joins BNP
Content_Enlish:
Muhammad Rashed Khan has resigned from his post as the General Secretary of the People's Rights Council and joined the BNP. He joined the BNP at a function held at the BNP Chairperson's Gulshan political office on Saturday afternoon. 

Rashed Khan will get the opportunity to contest from the Jhenaidah-4 constituency with the BNP's party symbol, a sheaf of rice. 
Rashed Khan formally joined the party by presenting flowers to BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. Then Fakhrul announced Rashed Khan's nomination from the BNP. BNP Standing Committee member Salahuddin Ahmed was present at the time. 

Rashed Khan joined the party at a function at the BNP Chairperson's Gulshan political office on Saturday afternoon 
Rashed Khan joined the party at a function at the BNP Chairperson's Gulshan political office on Saturday afternoon Photo: From the Facebook page of BNP Media Cell 
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir called on all leaders and activists of BNP and its affiliated organizations to work together to make Rashed Khan win in Jhenaidah-4 constituency. 
Rashed Khan declared unwanted, BNP faction protests wearing shrouds
