Headline_English: Tarique Rahman completes voter registration and national identity card process
Content_Enlish:
Returning to the country after 17 years, BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman completed the process of getting his name included in the voter list and registering for a national identity card. 

Two days after returning from London, on Saturday morning, after visiting the grave of martyr Osman Hadi in the Dhaka University area, he went to Agargaon surrounded by leaders and activists. There, he completed the necessary work to register as a voter and obtain a national identity card at the Election Training Institute. 

Tarique Rahman left his Gulshan home in the morning amid tight security. However, he did not go in a red-green bus today like the last two days. He rode in a white car (SUV), the car was decorated with flowers. 

Tarique Rahman at the Electoral Training Institute in Agargaon, Dhaka this Saturday afternoon to complete the process of becoming a voter and registering for a national identity card 
Tarique Rahman at the Electoral Training Institute in Agargaon, Dhaka this Saturday afternoon to complete the process of becoming a voter and registering for a national identity card Photo: Tanvir Ahmed 
Tarique Rahman had already announced that he would do the necessary work to become a voter on December 27. The Election Commission had also made preparations accordingly. 

Tarique Rahman went to the Electoral Training Institute building behind the Election Building in Agargaon around 1 pm today. NID-related services are provided to expatriates and important people in a room on the ground floor of the building. 

Tarique Rahman went to that room to take a photo, give ten fingerprints, have his iris scanned, and sign. Election Commission Secretary Akhtar Ahmed was present at the time. 

Earlier in the morning, NID Wing Director General (DG) ASM Humayun Kabir told reporters that when a person becomes a voter, their photo, iris and fingerprints are taken. These are uploaded to the EC database. They are cross-matched with the voters' information in the data center. Then a number is generated. This is done in the software. 

Tarique Rahman visits the grave of Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi This morning in the Dhaka University area, the Election Commission has already finalized the voter list for the upcoming 13th parliamentary election. However, the Voter List Act states that the EC can include the name of any person eligible to be a voter in the voter list at any time. 

Tarique Rahman visits the grave of Osman Hadi, will not go to the hospital as he is not injured 
The first voter list with a photo was prepared in Bangladesh in 2008 during the post-11 caretaker government. Tarique Rahman, the eldest son of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia, was released from prison and left Bangladesh for London on September 11, 2008. He was not included in the voter list as he was abroad. He did not come to the country during the subsequent Awami League rule, nor did he become a voter. 

The interim government formed after the Awami League was ousted in the July coup last year is moving towards the 13th parliamentary election in February. The election schedule has been announced for December 11, and voting will be held on February 12. 

Tarique Rahman will contest the next election as a candidate from the Sadar (Bogra-6) constituency in his ancestral area of ​​Bogra. Local leaders have already collected nomination papers on his behalf.

Headline_English: Why Israel is going to be the first country in the world to recognize Somaliland
Content_Enlish:
Israel is set to formally recognize Somaliland as a state. Israel is the first country in the world to do so. This is seen as a significant diplomatic breakthrough in the geopolitics of the Horn of Africa region. 

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced on Friday that Israel and Somaliland have signed a joint declaration to establish full diplomatic relations. 

Netanyahu also said that the declaration was signed in the spirit of the ‘Abraham Accords’. Israel made the Abraham Accords under the mediation of the United States to establish formal relations with Arab countries. 

The Somali government condemned Israel’s announcement in a statement within hours. The statement said that it was an ‘attack on Somalia’s sovereignty’ and an ‘illegal’ move. The Somali government said that Somaliland is an integral part of their country. 

Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991. However, this territory has not been recognized by any member state of the United Nations for many years. This territory is located in the northwestern corner of the former British-ruled northern Somalia. 
Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991. However, this territory has not been recognized by any member state of the United Nations for many years. This territory is located in the northwestern corner of the former British-ruled northern Somalia. 

Somalia has never accepted Somaliland's declaration of independence. 

Strong criticism, rejection 

In response to Israel becoming the first country to formally recognize Somaliland, Somali Foreign Minister Abdisalam Abdi Ali spoke by telephone with the foreign ministers of Egypt, Turkey and Djibouti. At that time, all three countries reiterated their support for the integrity of Somalia. 

In recent years, the Somaliland government has tried to improve relations with the United Arab Emirates and Taiwan to gain international acceptance. Among them, the United Arab Emirates is a signatory to the Abraham Accords. 
The Egyptian Foreign Ministry said that the initiative to recognize the independence of a region within a sovereign country is a violation of the UN Charter. The three countries also agreed that a 'dangerous precedent' is being set through this. 

Respect for the unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of states is a fundamental pillar in the stability of the international system. It should not be violated in any way, said the Egyptian Foreign Ministry. 

Netanyahu congratulated Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi in a video call. At that time, the country's president was praised for his 'leadership and commitment to peace and stability' and invited him to visit Israel. 

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said that the joint declaration was signed after a year of dialogue between the two governments. Full relations have been established based on the joint decision of the governments and heads of state of the two countries. Under this, both countries will appoint ambassadors and open embassies. 

The president of Somaliland described the signing of the joint declaration as a ‘historic moment’. He said that his country is ready to join the Abraham Accords. 

In a statement yesterday, the African Union rejected ‘any recognition of Somaliland’. Somalia is a member of the African Union. The African Union considers Somaliland an integral part of its member states. 

In the statement, the head of the African Union, Mahmoud Ali Yusuf, said that any attempt to undermine the unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Somalia could set a dangerous precedent with far-reaching implications for peace and stability across the continent. 

The beginning of change 

The first recognition by a country after more than three decades of independence is expected to bring a dramatic change in Somaliland’s fortunes after years of diplomatic isolation. 

The region broke away from Somalia during a brutal civil war that lasted for decades under the authoritarian regime of Siad Barre. During that time, government forces carried out widespread destruction in northern Somalia. 

The region broke away from Somalia during a brutal civil war that lasted for decades under the authoritarian regime of Siad Barre. Siad Barre's forces are alleged to have destroyed the north. While much of Somalia descended into chaos, stability returned to Somaliland in the late 1990s. 

Somaliland has gradually developed a political identity separate from Somalia. It has its own parliament, currency and flag. The capital is Hargeisa. However, parts of Somaliland's eastern region are still disputed. Many communities living in the area do not support Hargeisa's "separatist activities". 

US Position 

In recent years, the Somaliland government has sought to improve relations with the United Arab Emirates and Taiwan to gain international recognition. The UAE is a signatory to the Abraham Accords. 

Senator Ted Cruz, a prominent member of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party, has been vocal in his support for closer ties between Israel and Somaliland. Cruz has repeatedly called on Washington to recognize Somaliland. 

However, there has been no sign yet of the US changing its position on Somaliland.

Headline_English: 'Dhakaiya Shamim', two others arrested in Khulna NCP workers' leader shooting incident
Content_Enlish:
RAB-6 has arrested Shamim Sikder alias DK Shamim alias Dhakaiya Shamim and Mahdin in connection with the shooting of Md. Motaleb Sikder, the divisional convener of the National Citizens Party (NCP) affiliate organization, in Khulna. They were arrested from the Basupara area of ​​Sonadanga police station in the city on Friday night. 

Earlier, a suspect in the same case, Md. Arif, and Tanima Tanvi, joint member secretary of the Khulna district branch of the NCP youth organization, Jatiya Yuba Shakti, were arrested. With this, the number of arrests in the case has reached 4. 

Woman arrested in connection with the shooting of NCP labor leader in Khulna 

This information was given by the force's spokesperson and deputy commander, Major Md. Nazmul Islam, at a press conference at the Khulna RAB-6 headquarters on Saturday afternoon. 

The press conference said that a team of RAB-6 visited the scene immediately after the incident. In addition, various information and CCTV camera footage were collected and analyzed. By reviewing the information and video footage provided by the police and other law enforcement agencies, some people were identified as suspects and intelligence surveillance was strengthened. In continuation of this, suspect Md. Arif was arrested at around 8:30 pm on December 25. He was later handed over to the Detective Branch (DB). 

RAB officer Nazmul Islam said that Shamim Sikder alias Dhakaiya Shamim and Mahdin were arrested from the Basupara area on Friday night. During the initial interrogation, Shamim admitted his involvement in the incident. He told RAB that he himself shot Motaleb Sikder in the head. 

Last Monday, at around 12:15 pm, Motaleb Sikder was shot at the rented house of Tanima Tanbi, joint member secretary of the Khulna district branch of the National Youth Power, in Sonadanga area of ​​Khulna. Locals rescued him in an injured condition and took him to Khulna Medical College Hospital. According to doctors, the bullet had touched his scalp and exited. He is currently out of danger. 

Citing the interrogation of arrested Shamim, Major Nazmul Islam said that drug dealing and anti-social activities were going on in the flat rented by Tanima Tanbi. On the day of the incident, Shamim and four-five associates went there at around 7 am. Earlier, Tanbi, Motaleb Sikder, Arif, Ifti, Tanvir (Tanbi's husband), Imran (Tanbi's friend) and a relative of Ifti were present in the flat. After trying to recover the drugs but not finding anything, Shamim got angry and shot Motaleb Sikder in the head with the weapon he had. However, he survived as the bullet was not fatal. 

RAB said that Shamim Sikder alias Dhakaiya Shamim is one of the top terrorists in the Sonadanga area. He has multiple cases against him, including banditry, special powers act, and drugs. Initial investigation revealed that the murder attempt was carried out due to a dispute over drug dealing and sharing of drug money in the Sonadanga area. 

Meanwhile, the investigation has progressed a lot after the case was handed over to the DB, said Taimur Islam, officer-in-charge of the Khulna Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB). He said that vigorous efforts are being made to recover the weapon used during the incident.

Headline_English: Police say election office set on fire in exchange for 10,000 taka
Content_Enlish:
After the election schedule was announced, the district election office was set on fire in Lakshmipur with the aim of creating panic in the public and thwarting the election, according to the police. One person has been arrested in this incident. 
Police claim that Shyamal Chakraborty, a former Awami League MP from Lakshmipur-3 constituency and personal assistant (APS) of the late Aviation and Tourism Minister AKM Shahjahan Kamal, hired a person named Md. Rubel to set the fire in exchange for 10,000 taka. 
Last Thursday night, the Lakshmipur District Detective Branch (DB) arrested Md. Rubel (41) from his house in the South Majupur area of ​​Ward No. 10 of the municipality. Superintendent of Police Md. Abu Tarek gave this information at a press conference organized at the Lakshmipur Police Superintendent's office on Friday afternoon. 

According to the police, Rubel went to the district election office the day before the incident in the afternoon and inspected the place. On the evening of the incident, Shyamal Chakraborty sent 2,000 taka to his bKash number. Later, Rubel bought a one-liter water bottle from the Jhumur Rahmania Hotel in the city and threw the water away. Then he bought a liter of petrol in the bottle from Belal's shop in front of the stadium and took it home. 
Masked youth climbs the wall and enters, then sets fire to the district election office 
The police superintendent said that on December 12, at around 3:30 am, Rubel, wearing a mask, walked to the district election office along DB Road with a bottle filled with petrol. He climbed the gate and found the window of the storeroom on the north side of the ground floor open, poured petrol there and set it on fire with a match lighter. He later threw the bottle over the boundary wall. 

Police said that while setting fire, he suffered burns under his right ear and some parts of his beard. He then took pictures of the scene of setting fire on his mobile phone and quickly left the scene. Rubel also admitted during interrogation that he burnt the clothes he was wearing when he returned home after realizing that there was a CCTV camera. 

Several items and documents in a room on the ground floor were burnt in the fire incident at the Lakshmipur District Election Office on the night of December 12. Lakshmipur Sadar Upazila Election Officer Md. Faruk Hossain filed a case with Sadar Police Station as the plaintiff in this incident. Unknown persons have been named as accused in the case. 

Police said that the afternoon of the next day, Shyamal Chakraborty sent the remaining 8,000 taka of the agreement to Rubel's bKash number. According to Rubel's confession, the used water bottle was recovered from the low-lying land north of the Election Building. Two bKash numbers used to send the money have also been identified. 

When Shyamal Chakraborty's mobile phone was called to inquire about his statement in this regard, it was found switched off. 

The Superintendent of Police also said that a smartphone was seized from Rubel. A still image taken during the fire was found on the phone. After interrogation and analysis of mobile phone conversations, information about a plan to set fire to the district food warehouse and LGED office was also found. 

Rubel is the elder brother of Azizul Hakim, the general secretary of Sadar Thana Chhatra League. He worked as a driver in the electricity office. He was dismissed from his job three months ago due to his brother's political affiliation, police said.

Headline_English: Two more accused in Dipu Das murder case sent to jail after remand
Content_Enlish:
Two more accused who were on remand in the case of the beating and burning to death of garment worker Dipu Chandra Das in Bhaluka, Mymensingh have been sent to jail. They were sent to jail on Friday afternoon. 

Police said that 18 people have already been arrested in the murder of Dipu Chandra Das. Of the 12 accused who were granted remand for three days, 6 have completed their interrogation. On Thursday, the four accused also gave confessional statements in the court under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code. 

4 accused in the murder of Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh confess in court 

Floor in-charge Alamgir Hossain (38) and quality in-charge Miraj Hossain (46) of the factory named Pioneer Knitwears (BD) Limited were produced in court this afternoon. They did not give confessional statements in the court. As the remand ended, the court ordered the two to be sent to jail. 

Dipu Chandra Das, an employee of Pioneer Knitwears (BD) Limited factory, was arrested and beaten to death on the night of December 18 in Dubaliapara area of ​​Habirbari union of Bhaluka on charges of insulting religion. 

The deceased Dipu Chandra Das's home is in Mokamiakanda village of Banihala union of Tarakanda upazila. His brother Apu Chandra Das filed a case accusing 140 to 150 unidentified people in this incident. After the incident, RAB conducted a drive and arrested seven people and the police arrested five. On December 22, the court granted three-day remand for each of them. 

Mymensingh Additional Superintendent of Police (Administration) Abdullah Al Mamun said that four of the six accused on remand confessed on Thursday. The remaining two were sent to jail through the court today, Friday. 

The police official also said that the six accused arrested last Wednesday night were presented in court on Thursday and a seven-day remand application was filed. The court has set a remand hearing for next Sunday.

Headline_English: Dhaka North BNP removes waste from 300 feet of road after public reception
Content_Enlish:
After the public reception organized to mark the return of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman, Dhaka Metropolitan North BNP has removed the garbage lying on the July 36 Expressway (300 feet road) and surrounding areas, an important road in the eastern part of the capital. 

This Friday morning, the party's leaders and activists took part in the cleaning activity in the area. In addition, some local residents took part in the cleaning activity. Since the morning, members of the Volunteer Party, Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal were seen carrying brooms and garbage collection equipment. 

Dhaka Metropolitan North BNP convener Aminul Haque, who directly participated in the cleaning activity, said that BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman always gives instructions that no matter what program the party takes, it should benefit the people. BNP has taken such initiatives out of social responsibility. He also said that the party's leaders and activists will play a role in protecting the environment and public interest along with political programs. 

Dhaka Metropolitan North BNP leaders said that due to the presence of a large number of people at the public reception, various types of waste including plastic, banners, festoons accumulated on the roads and surrounding areas. The main goal of this program was to ensure normal traffic flow and environmental protection by removing them quickly. 

Some local residents said that the initiative to keep the roads clean after the political program is commendable. It not only facilitates traffic flow, but also reduces public suffering. 

Party sources said that such social and environment-friendly initiatives will be continued after the BNP program in the future.

Headline_English: Bodies of father and son missing after trawler capsizes in Bay of Bengal recovered
Content_Enlish:
The bodies of a father and son who went missing after their fishing trawler sank in the Bay of Bengal have been recovered. Their bodies were recovered from the sunken trawler on Thursday night and Friday morning by local fishermen and relatives. 
The deceased are Md. Shamim Jamaddar (40) and his 11-year-old son Siam of Charganga Bandhghat area of ​​Barabaishdia union in Rangabali upazila of Patuakhali. Earlier, the trawler sank in the Pipeboya area of ​​the Bay of Bengal on Wednesday night. 
Shamim Jomaddar's father Md. Siddiq Jamaddar said that there were a total of 6 fishermen including him in the trawler. Last Wednesday night, the trawler owned by him suffered a hole in the sea due to a storm and strong waves. After the sinking, he and four other fishermen were rescued with the help of others, but his son Shamim and 11-year-old grandson Siam were missing. Their bodies were found in the sunken trawler on Thursday night by local fishermen and relatives. 

Fisherman Shaon Hawlader, who rescued the survivors, said that they had gone to catch Hilsa in the Bay of Bengal with the trawler named MV Siddique from Charganga Bandhghat in Barabaishdia Union of Rangabali Upazila at around 10 am on Sunday. 

Shamim Jamaddar's younger brother Shakib Jamaddar said that his brother's body was found on Thursday night after the accident. They found the body of his nephew Siam at around 9 am on Friday. 

Before the rescue, Kuakata Naval Police Outpost In-charge Police Inspector Bikash Chandra Mandal and Rangabali Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md. Shirajul Islam said that after learning about the missing person, they informed the local Coast Guard and other concerned parties.

Headline_English: US hints at more strikes on ISIS hideouts in Nigeria
Content_Enlish:
The US military has attacked the Islamic State (IS) hideout in Nigeria. The attack was carried out at the request of the Nigerian government. US President Donald Trump and the country's military announced this information on Thursday. The US Secretary of Defense said, hinting at more attacks, "More to come." 
Trump wrote on the social media platform Truth Social, "Today, as Commander in Chief, the United States launched a powerful and deadly attack on ISIS terrorists in northwestern Nigeria. This group, especially innocent Christians, was carrying out a brutal killing spree. This has not been seen for many years - even centuries." 

The US Africa Command said that the attack was carried out in Sokoto state in cooperation with the Nigerian authorities. They claim that several ISIS fighters were killed in the attack. Nigerian Foreign Minister Yusuf Maitama Tugar told the BBC that the joint operation was targeting "terrorists". It was not linked to any particular religion. 

Although the Nigerian foreign minister did not specifically name IS, he said the operation had been planned for "some time". The operation was based on intelligence provided by Nigeria. He did not rule out the possibility of further attacks. The Nigerian minister said it depended on the decisions of the leaderships of the two countries. 

The attack came at a time when Trump warned in late October that Christians in Nigeria were under "an existential threat". He also threatened US military action in the West African country. Trump said at the time that the Nigerian government had failed to curb violence against Christian communities. 

'More to come' 
The Nigerian government says armed groups are targeting both Muslims and Christians. And Washington's claim that Christians are the only victims of persecution does not paint the full picture of the complex security situation. Amid such statements, Nigeria has agreed to join hands with the United States to strengthen its military against armed groups. 

According to the Nigerian Foreign Ministry, air strikes on Thursday accurately hit the hideouts of "terrorists". US officials have also reported attacks on multiple IS camps. A video released by the US Department of Defense, the Pentagon, shows at least one missile being fired from a warship. 

Meanwhile, the Nigerian Foreign Minister did not say specifically whether there will be more attacks, but US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth openly hinted at attacks. Praising the Nigerian government's support for the operation, he wrote on social media, "More to come..." 

Who is ISIS in Nigeria 
IS has ties to at least two of the armed groups in Nigeria. One of their armed groups is a branch of Boko Haram. This part is active in northeastern Nigeria. The other group is the Islamic State Sahel Province. This relatively little-known group is known locally as Lakurawa. They operate in northwestern Nigeria. 

Although there is no confirmation from the Nigerian or US governments, security analysts say that the attack on Thursday is likely against the Lakurawa group. They have increased deadly violence in border states such as Sokoto and Kebbi last year. The group often attacks marginalized communities and armed forces. Five people were also killed in an attack in the northeast on Thursday. 

Meanwhile, not only in Nigeria, the United States has carried out large-scale attacks on various Islamic State targets in Syria last week. The US president had already promised to attack the country. Attacks on US troops in Syria were increasing. Washington suspects that the Islamic State is behind the attack.

Headline_English: Putin hints at land swap to end Russia-Ukraine war
Content_Enlish:
Russian President Vladimir Putin may agree to exchange some of the occupied territory under a possible deal to end the war in Ukraine, the Russian newspaper Kommersant reported. However, Putin is adamant that the entire Donbas region will remain under Russian control in exchange. 

Putin outlined the details of the plan to the country’s top businessmen at a meeting in the Kremlin on the night of December 24, according to Andrei Kolesnikov, Kremlin correspondent for Russia’s leading daily Kommersant. 
The report said Putin assured businessmen that Russia is still ready to accept the concessions made at the ‘Anchorage’ conference. That is, there will be no change in the policy that Donbas will remain Russian. Kolesnikov wrote that Putin did not rule out the possibility of a partial swap or transfer of territory under Russian control in other regions outside Donbas. 

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday that Ukrainian and US delegations had made significant progress in finalizing a 20-point peace plan during talks in Miami last week. However, Zelensky made it clear that there was still no agreement on handing over the remaining Ukrainian-held Donbas to Russia. There is also a dispute over the future of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, currently occupied by Russian troops. 

US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner are continuing talks with Russia, Ukraine and European powers to implement his promise to end the bloodiest conflict in post-World War II Europe. The full details of what was "agreed" at the summit between Putin and Trump in Anchorage, Alaska, last August have not yet been released. 

Russia's claims and current position 
According to Russian calculations, they currently control 90 percent of the Donbas and 75 percent of the Zaporizhia and Kherson regions, in addition to Crimea, which was annexed in 2014. Putin had previously stipulated that Ukraine would have to completely withdraw its troops from Donbas, Kherson and Zaporizhia and abandon its hopes of joining NATO as a condition for a peace agreement. 

Kommersant also reported that Putin discussed Zaporizhia, Europe's largest nuclear facility, during a meeting with businessmen. He said that the issue of operating the power plant under joint management by Russia and the United States is under discussion. In addition, the United States has shown interest in crypto mining or digital currency production at the plant and plans to supply part of the electricity generated from the plant to Ukraine.

Headline_English: Russia's shadow over Europe, the risk of a major war is real again
Content_Enlish:
Defense experts gathered in Whitehall, the capital of the United Kingdom, last month to discuss how prepared the United Kingdom and its allies are for a possible war in the next few years. The experts’ verdict was bleak—the Europeans are not prepared. 

The experts’ conference was organized by the London-based research institute Royal United Services Institute (RUSI). Present were current and former members of the military, government and NATO officials, researchers and defense experts. According to them, Russia is preparing for a possible conflict with Europe. 

The experts at the conference presented only one solution. That is, if war breaks out, Europe must ensure victory. For this, it is necessary to invest more in Europe’s defense. In addition, experts warned that a major change in mentality is needed to deal with the situation. The people of the country must be told that the time for avoiding the threat of war for Europe is over. 

Experts agreed that Russia has already launched a “hybrid war” against the West. They cited as evidence Russian fighter jets and drones entering NATO airspace, GPS jamming in the Baltics, propaganda and sabotage of key infrastructure in various countries. Although Moscow has denied any involvement in these. 

Sam Green, a professor of Russian politics at King's College London, said that these attacks have changed the outlook of many people in Europe. People are scared - especially when the realities are coming to light. Drones are being seen outside airports. And there is a growing sense that it is only a matter of time before one of these drones attacks a passenger plane. 

Concerns over the Baltics 

Moscow has not yet directly attacked any NATO member state in Europe. According to experts, one reason for this is that Russia knows that it cannot defeat NATO with its current capabilities. However, the situation may change in the future. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has said that Russia could be ready to use military force against NATO within five years. 

In early December, Russian President Vladimir Putin said he was ready for war if Europe wanted it. One of the Baltic states in Europe is that an attack on them could come within three years. Researchers at the Belfer Center at Harvard Kennedy School have analyzed that Russia could start a war against NATO in 2027 or 2028. 

NATO has drawn up emergency plans to deal with a possible Russian aggression in the Baltic region. However, experts warn that these plans are not sustainable. “There is a plan. But governments are not taking the necessary steps to implement it,” said RUSI researcher Jack Watling. 

At a conference last month, former head of the UK’s Joint Forces Command, General Richard Barons, said that the UK must strengthen its armed forces and civil defense systems. It must increase investment in healthcare, industry and the economy, so that it can quickly deal with war situations. At the current pace, the country will take about 10 years to prepare for war. But it has only three to five years.

Headline_English: Najib Razak sentenced to 15 years in prison
Content_Enlish:
A Malaysian court has sentenced former Prime Minister Najib Razak to 15 years in prison for embezzling and laundering state funds from the 1MDB scheme. 
The court on Friday found him guilty of abuse of power and money laundering. Judge Colin Lawrence Sequerah said during the verdict that “all sentences imposed on the defendant will run concurrently.” 
Earlier today, the Kuala Lumpur High Court found him guilty in the case. The 72-year-old Najib was charged with four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering. The charges allege that Najib illegally transferred about 2.2 billion Malaysian ringgit (about $539 million) from 1MDB. 

Prosecutors say Najib abused his power as prime minister, finance minister and chairman of the 1MDB advisory board more than a decade ago to divert vast sums of money from Malaysia’s sovereign wealth fund into his personal bank accounts. 

Najib was previously convicted in 2020 of embezzling nearly $9.9 million from 1MDB. He was sentenced to 12 years in prison in that case. His sentence began in 2022. His sentence was later reduced to six years. 

He was convicted in the second of the cases against Najib, which is considered the most significant case against him to date.

Headline_English:
US announces arms sales to Taiwan 
China sanctions 20 US companies including Boeing
Content_Enlish:
China's Foreign Ministry has announced sanctions against 10 individuals and 20 US defense companies over the announcement of arms sales to Taiwan. The sanctions were announced on Friday. Boeing's St. Louis branch is also under the sanctions. 

China's Foreign Ministry said that any assets of the relevant companies and individuals in China will be seized. In addition, domestic companies and individuals will be banned from doing business with them. 

The ministry also said that the listed individuals include the founder of defense company Anduril Industries and nine senior executives of the companies under the sanctions. They have also been banned from entering China. 

Other companies under the sanctions include Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation and L3Harris Maritime Services. 

Last week, the United States announced an $11.1 billion arms sale to Taiwan, which is considered the largest US arms package to date. China announced such measures after this incident. 

A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman said in a statement on Friday that the Taiwan issue is the core of China's core interests and the first line of China-US relations that cannot be crossed. 

The statement said China would respond strongly to any provocative actions that cross the line on Taiwan. The statement also called on the US to stop its "dangerous" efforts to weaponize the island. 

China considers democratically-ruled Taiwan to be part of its territory, a claim Taipei rejects. 

The US is legally obliged to help Taiwan develop its self-defense capabilities. However, the US has tensions with China over such arms sales.

Headline_English: Türkiye, Libya step up investigation into killing of Libyan army chief
Content_Enlish:
Libyan and Turkish officials have stepped up their joint investigation into the crash of a plane near the Turkish capital Ankara that killed eight people, including the Libyan army chief. At the same time, forensic work and preparations are underway to repatriate the bodies. 

The head of Libya's criminal investigation department, Major General Mahmoud Ashour, led a delegation to the office of the chief public prosecutor in Ankara on Thursday. The visit was part of a joint investigation. 

A private plane carrying Libyan army chief Muhammad Ali Ahmed al-Haddad developed an electrical fault shortly after taking off from Ankara's Esenboga airport on Tuesday. 

Turkey's communications chief Burhanettin Duran said the plane requested an emergency landing 16 minutes after takeoff. 

Control room officials instructed the plane to turn back towards Ankara. However, the plane disappeared from radar three minutes after it began to descend. The wreckage of the plane was later found in the village of Kesikkavak in the Haymana region of Ankara. A total of eight people, including the three crew members, were killed in the incident. 

Rescue teams arrived at the scene after the Turkish Interior Ministry launched an emergency operation. Various authorities are investigating the cause of the accident. 

Al Jazeera's Malik Traina, reporting from Misrata, Libya, said preparations are underway to repatriate al-Haddad's body. However, it is not known exactly when this will be done.
