Libyan army chief killed in plane crash near Turkish capital 
24 December 2025 
Libyan army chief killed in plane crash near Turkish capital 
Yesterday, Thursday, Traina said, "This morning we spoke with the Minister of Communications. At that time, it was said that the funeral would be held tomorrow. But now that decision is changing. Now they are getting phone calls from government officials. They are saying that the funeral may be postponed until Saturday. 

Traina also said that the rescue operation is taking a long time due to the severity of the accident. The debris is spread over a wide area and DNA tests are needed. 

Traina said, “There is a lot of pressure to finish this process as quickly as possible. We will see if that is possible.”

Headline_English: Former Malaysian PM Najib Razak found guilty in another corruption case
Content_Enlish:
Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak has been found guilty in another corruption case related to the much-discussed 1MDB scandal. The Kuala Lumpur High Court found him guilty on Friday, the second high-profile case against Najib in the scandal. 

Najib, 72, was charged with four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering. The charges allege that Najib illegally transferred about 2.2 billion Malaysian ringgit (about $539 million) from 1MDB. 

Prosecutors say that more than a decade ago, Najib abused his power as prime minister, finance minister and chairman of 1MDB’s advisory board to divert vast sums of money from Malaysia’s sovereign wealth fund to his personal bank accounts. 

Najib was previously convicted in 2020 of embezzling about $9.9 million from 1MDB. He was sentenced to 12 years in prison in that case. His sentence began in 2022. Later, his sentence was reduced to six years. 

House arrest application rejected, Najib Razak to remain in prison 
He was found guilty in the second case against Najib. This is considered the most important case against him so far. Because it directly involved 1MDB-related companies and a large sum of money. 

The trial has been going on for seven years. In this case, the lawyers presented 76 witnesses, including Najib, to the court. 

Bridget Welsh, an honorary research fellow at the Asia Research Institute Malaysia at the University of Nottingham, said: “This case has been delayed many times and is very complex to understand.” 

Welsh also told Al Jazeera that these financial crimes are multi-layered. And the whole process was long and extensive.

Headline_English: Hindutva extremists attack Christians across India on Christmas, Modi government silent
Content_Enlish:
On the occasion of Christmas celebrations in India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi went to a church in Delhi to offer prayers. However, members of extremist Hindu groups supporting his party and the government have been attacking Christians in various states of the country. They have obstructed religious practices. 

Most of the attacks have been carried out in BJP-ruled states like Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Assam, and Haryana. Surprisingly, the BJP has not protested against such attacks. The central government has not condemned them. No statement has been issued. No action has been taken against anyone. Instead, the Delhi Police has filed an FIR against the leaders of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in Delhi. It is alleged that the leaders of the former ruling party in Delhi have hurt the religious sentiments of Christians. 

The Bajrang Dal has carried out a riot at a Christian missionary school in Nalbari, Assam. This organization and the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) have taken a strong stand against the celebration of Christmas in various states. Bajrang Dal supporters entered St. Mary's English School in Panigaon, Nalbari district of Assam and started a riot. 
The school was decorated for Christmas. A Christmas tree was put up. Everything was set on fire. A shop near the school also destroyed Christmas items. 

Similar incidents took place on December 24 and 25 in various BJP-ruled states of the country. In cities like Jaipur, Vidisha, Bhopal, Guwahati, Bareilly, Indore, besides cities like Aam Aadmi Party-ruled Punjab and Left-ruled Kerala, Vishwa Hindu Parishad and Bajrang Dal attacked shopping malls, schools, shops, and even festive people. 

In Kerala, RSS members went door to door in Puducherry villages in Palakkad district and stopped the singing of carols. Christmas celebrations were cancelled at a hotel run by the state tourism department on the banks of the Ganges in Haridwar, BJP-ruled Uttarakhand. 

A visually impaired woman attending a Christmas celebration at a church in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, was physically assaulted. The woman was allegedly assaulted by local BJP leader Anju Bhargava. The leader alleged that the woman was involved in religious conversions. A group of men and women were also prevented from celebrating Christmas in Delhi's Lajpat Nagar. They were celebrating Christmas wearing red and white Santa Claus hats. 

Last Tuesday, before Christmas, the Catholic Bishops' Conference of India issued a statement expressing concern over the possibility of attacks on Christians. That fear proved true. 

Although no action has been taken against this trend by the BJP or the central government as a party, the Delhi Police has filed an FIR against some Aam Aadmi Party leaders for hurting the sentiments of Christians. 

Aam Aadmi Party had posted a post on X a few days ago. It shows that a person dressed as Santa Claus has come to Delhi and is suffering from pollution. The Delhi Police has filed an FIR against three leaders including Saurabh Bhardwaj on the charge that the post has hurt the religious sentiments of Christians. 

Aam Aadmi Party leaders claim that they have given priority to the issue of Delhi's pollution in this post. There is no question of hurting anyone's religious sentiments. At the behest of the BJP, the Delhi Police has set out to fulfill political vendetta. 

Such attacks on minority Christians across the country on the occasion of Christmas have never been seen in the past.

Headline_English: 'A comedy show': The junta's upcoming elections in the eyes of Myanmar's youth
Content_Enlish:
On the outskirts of Mae Sot, a small Thai town near the Myanmar border, the sound of a tattoo machine can be heard, accompanied by loud punk music. 
“Punk means freedom,” says the heavily tattooed Ying La. “It’s not just music or fashion, it’s a way of life,” he tells Al Jazeera as he sits behind his “punk bar” in Mae Sot, Thailand, tattooing a fellow countryman who has fled Myanmar. 

The desire to live freely was one of the reasons Ying La fled Yangon, Myanmar’s largest city. The 28-year-old now lives a precarious life as an undocumented citizen in Thailand. 

But according to Ying La, it’s much better than being imprisoned by the junta government, which he first protested against and later took up arms against. 

“My biggest fear was that if I was caught, I would be handed over to the Myanmar military,” she said. “We are no longer afraid of death. But being caught by the military is even worse.” 

Ying La, who is in exile in Mae Sot, is like thousands of young people in Myanmar who have fled the country to escape the civil war. Her journey began after the Myanmar military seized power in February 2021, overthrowing the democratic government of Aung San Suu Kyi. 

The coup overturned the results of Myanmar’s 2015 and 2020 elections, which were widely seen as the first fair elections in the country’s history. Suu Kyi’s party won a landslide victory in these elections. 

Thousands of people have lost their lives in the civil war that began in Myanmar as a result of the military coup. Airstrikes in rural areas, landmine explosions, conscription and political repression have created a horrific situation throughout the country. 

“At the beginning of the coup, the junta government ordered that no one should leave their homes or protest for 72 hours,” Ying La recalls. “During that time, my two friends and I protested on the streets with handmade banners.” 

Myanmar citizens living in Japan protest against Myanmar’s upcoming elections. December 14, 2025, Tokyo 
Myanmar citizens living in Japan protest against Myanmar’s upcoming elections. December 14, 2025, Tokyo Photo: Reuters 
Fearing arrest, Ying La fled to the jungle on the Thai border and joined the People’s Defense Force (PDF). However, he was forced to flee again after a bloody clash with the army in February 2022. He secretly entered Thailand. There, he set up this tattoo parlor and bar with the help of his partner. 

About his life in Thailand, Ing La said, “I had no documents because I came illegally. I couldn’t go anywhere, and it was impossible to find work to survive.” 

Because of being undocumented, Ing La constantly has to pay various fees or ‘license’ costs to the Thai authorities and is constantly in fear of being deported. 

‘All our hopes and dreams have been destroyed’ 

The military’s argument for the 2021 coup was that Suu Kyi’s party, the National League for Democracy (NLD), had won the election by rigging it. Now, the military is organizing an election under its own supervision next Sunday (December 28). However, this election is being seen around the world as a ‘farce’, the main goal of which is to legitimize the illegally seized power. 

Independent media outlet Democratic Voice of Burma (DVB) reported that while many parties registered to participate in the election, Aung San Suu Kyi's popular party, the NLD, was banned. The UN special envoy for Myanmar, Tom Andrews, called the election a "fake." He said that fair elections are not possible where political leaders are imprisoned and basic freedoms are lacking. 

Al Jazeera's Tony Cheng reported that artists and musicians are being arrested for criticizing the election. Many, like Ying La, are fleeing the country. 

Rebel groups have said they will not accept the results of the election. Ying La also sees no value in the election.

Headline_English: Kim to build more missiles in New Year
Content_Enlish:
North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has ordered the country to increase and modernize its missiles next year. He has ordered the construction of a new factory to meet the growing demand for missiles. This information was revealed by the country's state media on Friday. 

According to the state news agency Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), Kim visited an ammunition factory with top officials. Kim instructed the factories to meet the needs of the country's missile and artillery forces. 

According to the KCNA report, Kim believes that Pyongyang's overall production capacity needs to be further increased to keep up with the needs of the armed forces. To that end, he ordered the construction of a new ammunition factory. 
The North Korean leader said, "The missile and ammunition production sector is of the utmost importance to strengthen war prevention capabilities." 

In recent years, Pyongyang has significantly increased the number of missile tests. 

According to analysts, the aim is to improve the ability to strike precisely targeted targets, challenge the United States and South Korea, and test the weapons with the possibility of future exports to Russia in mind. 

Read more 
Kim's China visit: Blue and clear liquid, cigarettes, Mercedes cars - what's not on the bulletproof train 
02 September 2025 
Kim's China visit: Blue and clear liquid, cigarettes, Mercedes cars - what's not on the bulletproof train 
The news of his visit to the ammunition factory came a day after state media reported that he had visited the nuclear submarine factory. During the visit to the nuclear submarine factory, Kim pledged to counter the "threat" related to South Korea's submarine construction. 

At the same time, Kim also received information about research on "new secret weapons suitable for underwater navigation".

Headline_English: US airstrikes hit ISIS hideout in Nigeria
Content_Enlish:
The United States has carried out a powerful airstrike on the Islamic State (IS) hideout in northwestern Nigeria. Nigerian and US authorities have confirmed this information. 

The operation was carried out on Thursday night, the main religious festival of Christians, 'Christmas'. 

The US Department of Defense (Pentagon) said, 'The attack was carried out at the request of the Nigerian government. Several IS terrorists were killed in the incident.' 

It was also reported that several IS members were killed in the attack. 

Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth praised the successful operation carried out jointly with the Nigerian government in a post on the social media X (formerly Twitter). 

US President Donald Trump also confirmed the news of the attack. He wrote on his own social media, Truth Social, 'I have already warned these terrorists that if they do not stop killing Christians, they will pay a heavy price. That is exactly what happened tonight (Christmas).’ 

Trump also said, ‘May our military be in the grace of God. Merry Christmas to everyone, including the terrorists who were killed. If the killing of Christians continues, many more such terrorists will be killed in the future.’ 

Meanwhile, the Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement early Friday that the Nigerian authorities are actively engaged in security cooperation with international partners, including the United States, to combat the persistent threat of terrorism and violent extremism. 

Read more 
130 schoolchildren kidnapped in Nigeria rescued 
22 December 2025 
130 schoolchildren kidnapped in Nigeria rescued 
The US Defense Forces’ Africa Command said in a post on X that it carried out the strike in Sokoto state at the request of Nigerian authorities and that ‘multiple ISIS terrorists’ were killed in the incident. 

This is the first strike by US forces in Nigeria under President Trump. Trump had previously criticized the West African country in October and November. He said that Christians there were facing an existential crisis and genocide amid the ongoing armed conflict in Nigeria. 

Read more 
Bomb blast in crowded mosque in Nigeria, killing 5 
December 25, 2025 
Bomb blast in crowded mosque in Nigeria, killing 5 
While this diplomatic stance is welcomed by some, others believe that Trump's stance could inflame religious tensions in the populous African country. Hardline Christians in the United States and Europe have long described the ongoing violent situation in Nigeria as religious persecution. However, the Nigerian government and independent analysts dispute this. 

At least 40,000 people have been killed in the terrorist activities of Boko Haram and ISIS in northeastern Nigeria for a decade and a half. More than 2 million people have been displaced. In addition, looting and kidnappings by armed gangs in the northwestern part of the country in recent years have further complicated the situation.

Headline_English: Zelensky presents US plan to end war, will Putin accept it?
Content_Enlish:
Kiev has made several concessions to the terms of the latest version of a US-led draft plan to end the Russia-Ukraine war. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky unveiled the plan on Tuesday. But whether Moscow will accept the new terms remains a big question mark. 

The 20-point plan agreed between US and Ukrainian representatives is currently under review in Moscow. But analysts say it is unlikely that the Kremlin will budge from its hardline stance that Kiev must completely withdraw its troops from eastern Ukraine. 
Zelensky has admitted that he does not like all the points in the draft document. However, Kiev has successfully eliminated those that would have required the immediate withdrawal of Ukrainian troops from the Donetsk region or recognition of Russian-occupied territory as Russian territory. 

However, Zelensky has indicated that the proposal, if implemented, would pave the way for Kiev to withdraw its troops from some areas. This includes the 20 percent of the Donetsk region currently under Ukrainian control; a “demilitarized zone” will be created there. In addition, the previous condition for withdrawing the application to join NATO has also been removed from the new draft. 

Zelensky outlined the plan in a two-hour briefing with reporters on Tuesday. Zelensky said of the latest version of the plan, “The positions where troops will be deployed in Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhia and Kherson regions until the day of signing the agreement will be recognized as the de facto line of contact or control.” 

Zelensky also said that a working group will be formed to determine the necessary military formations to stop the fighting and outline possible future special economic zones. 

The plan appears to be opening the way to new proposals on issues that Ukraine had previously expressed reluctance to do, such as withdrawing troops and creating demilitarized zones. However, the process has been delayed a bit. 

Explaining the current situation, Zelensky said, “We are in a situation where Russia wants us to withdraw from the Donetsk region, and on the other hand, the United States is trying to find a solution.” He added, “They are basically looking for a demilitarized zone or a free economic zone; that is, a structure that can satisfy both sides.” 

NATO, territory and nuclear power plants 
US President Donald Trump is trying to mediate to end the four-year bloody war that began with a full-scale Russian invasion in 2022. This long war has already killed thousands of people, reduced eastern Ukraine to rubble and forced millions to flee their homes. 

Russian forces are currently in a very advantageous position on the battlefield and are constantly advancing. They are launching missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian cities and power plants almost every night. On Wednesday, the Russian Defense Ministry claimed that they had captured another area in the southern Zaporizhzhia region. 

After annexing Crimea in 2014, Moscow has demanded that four more regions of Ukraine—Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhia—be annexed by 2022. 

Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin has so far shown no sign of compromise. On the contrary, his tough demands for the withdrawal of Ukrainian troops and political concessions are seen by Kiev and its European allies as “surrender.” 

Zelensky has made it clear that a referendum in Ukraine would be needed to implement any plan for such a withdrawal. “If there is a discussion about a free economic zone, we will have to go to a referendum,” he said. 

The new plan proposes that the Zaporizhia nuclear power plant, which is occupied by Russian troops, be operated jointly by the United States, Ukraine, and Russia. However, Zelensky has made it clear that he does not want any Russian supervision of this facility. 

Proposal sent to Putin 
Details of the proposal have been sent to Russian President Vladimir Putin by his special envoy Kirill Dmitriev. However, a Kremlin spokesman said that Moscow is currently preparing its response and will not comment publicly on the matter at this time. 

Opinion poll to end the war 
Most Russians believe that the war in Ukraine will end in 2026. This issue has also been raised in a survey by a Russian government research center. Russia's leading public opinion research agency 'VTsIOM' published the results of its annual survey on Wednesday. The survey, which was conducted on the experiences of the outgoing year and expectations for the coming year, showed that Russians have an 'increasingly positive' attitude towards 2026.

Headline_English: Rashed Khan of Gana Adhikar is joining BNP
Content_Enlish:
General Secretary of Gana Odhikar Parishad Rashed Khan is joining BNP. He will also contest the 13th National Parliament election with the symbol of a sheaf of rice. 

A source close to Gana Odhikar Parishad confirmed this information to Prothom Alo. 

BNP has given up the Jhenaidah-4 seat to Rashed Khan in an attempt to reach a seat agreement with its partners in the simultaneous movement. 
The source close to Gana Odhikar Parishad says that in the current political reality, winning the seat from Gana Odhikar Parishad with the symbol of a truck could be very challenging. There will be many uncertainties in winning the election with the symbol of a truck. Therefore, Rashed wants to contest from Jhenaidah-4 with the symbol of a sheaf of rice to ensure victory. That is why he has decided to join BNP. 

According to the source, many of the partners in the simultaneous movement with BNP who have given up their seats have been asked to vote with the symbol of a sheaf of rice. Therefore, Rashed has decided to contest the election with the symbol of a sheaf of rice. The source also said that the decision on who will be the general secretary of the Gana Odhikar Parishad will be taken in the meeting of the executive council and the higher council. 

Read more 
Rashed Khan declared unwanted, BNP faction protests wearing shrouds 
26 December 2025 
Rashed Khan declared unwanted, BNP faction protests wearing shrouds 
BNP is giving up 28 seats to its partners through compromise. Last Wednesday, BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir officially announced the leaders of the partner parties as candidates for 10 seats at a press conference. On that day, he announced the release of Rashed Khan from the Jhenaidah-4 constituency of the Gana Odhikar Parishad. 

Since then, a section of BNP local leaders and activists have become angry. They demand that Rashed Khan be withdrawn from this seat. They have been demanding that the party nominate either Saiful Islam or Murshida Zaman. 

Meanwhile, a press release from the Gana Odhikar Parishad sent to the media on Friday night said that as per the decision of the party's higher council, General Secretary Rashed Khan has been expelled from the party due to clear evidence of his involvement in activities against party discipline.

Headline_English: Party leaders pay tribute to Tarique Rahman at memorial
Content_Enlish:
As it was not possible to reach the altar of the National Memorial in Savar before sunset as per the rules, the party leaders paid tribute to the martyrs of the great liberation war on behalf of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman in the afternoon. 

BNP leaders paid tribute to the martyrs by paying tribute to the martyrs at the altar of the memorial at 5:06 pm today, Friday. BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman could not reach the memorial till the time of writing this report at 6:25 pm. 

At 5:17 pm, BNP Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy told reporters present at the main gate of the memorial that after visiting the grave of martyred President Ziaur Rahman, he (Tareq Rahman) left for the memorial from there. Since there is a rule to place wreaths, it is before sunset, so we placed wreaths on his behalf at 5:06 pm. He will come after a while.’ 

Present during the tribute were BNP standing committee members Gayeshwar Roy and Abdul Moin Khan, BNP Chairperson’s Advisory Council members Amanullah Aman and Lutfuzzaman Babar, Dhaka District BNP President Khandaker Abu Ashfaq and General Secretary Nipun Roy Chowdhury. Also present were BNP’s nominated candidate for Dhaka-19 (Savar-Ashulia) constituency Dewan Mohammad Salauddin, party candidate for Dhaka-20 (Dhamrai) constituency Tamiz Uddin, Dhaka District Jubo Dal President Yasin Ferdous, among others.

Headline_English: New committee of Islami Chhatra Shibir, led by Nurul Islam-Sibgatullah
Content_Enlish:
A new central committee of Jamaat-e-Islami's student organization, Islami Chhatra Shibir, has been formed. Nurul Islam Saddam has been appointed as the president of this committee formed for 2026. And Sibgatullah has been appointed as the secretary general. 

Today, Friday, the members of the student organization elected a new leadership through voting at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in Agargaon in the capital. The names of the new president and secretary general were announced on the organization's verified Facebook page in the afternoon. 
A post on the student organization's Facebook page said, 'Alhamdulillah, the election of the central president of Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir for the 2026 session and the nomination of the secretary general have been completed. Central president Nurul Islam, secretary general Sibgatullah. May Allah Almighty help you fulfill the great responsibility of the religion.' 

Nurul Islam, who was appointed as the president of the camp, has served as the central secretary general of the organization in the current year (2025). Currently, he is doing a postgraduate diploma in entrepreneurial economics under Dhaka University. Earlier, he completed his bachelor's and master's degrees in economics from Khulna University. He was admitted to Khulna University in the 2014-2015 academic year. 

And Sibgatullah, who was given the responsibility of Secretary General, was the Central Office Secretary of Chhatra Shibir this year. He is currently doing his master's degree in the Department of Development Studies at Dhaka University. Before that, Sibgatullah did his bachelor's and master's degrees from the Institute of Social Welfare and Research of the same university. He was admitted to Dhaka University in the 2013-14 academic year. 

With Sibgatullah's rise to the top leadership of the Shibir, after a long 16 years, a student from the Dhaka University branch committee got a position at this level of the organization. The last time someone from Dhaka University got a place in the top leadership of Shibir was in 2009. At that time, a law student from Dhaka University, Shishir Mohammad Munir, became the Secretary General of Chhatra Shibir. After that, due to various internal reasons of the organization, no one from this university got a place in the top leadership of Shibir.

Headline_English: Tarique Rahman's return brings new hope to politics: Mirza Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman's return to the country after 17 years has brought a message of positive change in Bangladeshi politics, said the party's Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. 

According to Mirza Fakhrul Islam, this return has brought new hope to the country's political arena. 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said this while talking to reporters after paying homage to the tomb of BNP founder and independence proclaimer late President Ziaur Rahman in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital after Jumma prayers today, Friday. 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam said that Tarique Rahman returned to the country yesterday Thursday after a long exile since 2006. His return was royal and unprecedented. The people of the country spontaneously welcomed him and participated in the joy and excitement. The people have got their beloved leader back. 

The BNP Secretary General said that very few leaders in the political history of Bangladesh have been able to receive such spontaneous public support and public reception. As a young and promising leader, Tarique Rahman is seen not only by the people of the country but also by the world media as the future Prime Minister of Bangladesh. 

Stating that ‘good winds have now started blowing in the political sky of Bangladesh’, Mirza Fakhrul Islam further said that Tarique Rahman’s return to the country is not just a personal return; it is the beginning of a new chapter in the country’s politics. Through this, the path to restoring democracy and fulfilling the expectations of the people will be more smooth. 

The BNP Secretary General said that Tarique Rahman, returning to the country after 17 years, will pay homage to his father, martyred President Ziaur Rahman, at the tomb today. At that time, he will lay a wreath and pray for the forgiveness of his soul.

Headline_English: Jamaat wants to build an education system where no one will be unemployed: Shafiqur Rahman
Content_Enlish:
Jamaat-e-Islami wants to build such an education system that no one will be unemployed, said the party's Amir Shafiqur Rahman. In this context, he said, many people are counting numbers and saying that they will provide employment to so many crores, so many lakhs of youth. What will happen to others? They say that they will give allowances to others. But they do not want to see or hear that the youth of the country are taking unemployment allowance from anyone. They want to turn everyone's hands into the hands of craftsmen to build the country. They want to give work to everyone. 

Shafiqur Rahman said this in his speech as the chief guest at the central members' conference of Jamaat's student organization Islami Chhatra Shibir at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital on Friday afternoon. 

Shafiqur Rahman commented that any party can make an electoral agreement with Jamaat if it meets three conditions. According to him, the conditions are - no corruption, no indulgence for the corrupt. Equal justice will be ensured for everyone at all levels of society, no politician will be able to interfere in justice. We must promise to implement all the recommendations of reform. 

Regarding the Chhatra Shibir, the Amir of Jamaat said, this (Shibir) is now not just an ordinary student organization, but in the post-24 revolution period, the student community of Bangladesh has accepted this organization with love. It has given them a mandate. Today, the Chhatra Shibir has to fulfill the responsibility of the guardian of the student community. 

Shafiqur Rahman commented that the pen was taken away from the hands of the students for the last 54 years. In this context, he said, the young students were misled and weapons were handed over to them. Educational institutions had become mini-cantonments. There was no guarantee of the dignity of girls, the lives and careers of students. That black chapter has started to leave. But the black shadow has not yet left the nation. The struggle of the Chhatra Shibir must continue until this black shadow is removed. 

Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar commented at the event that a new possibility has emerged for the country. He said, the nation must be united and taken forward. However, at this very moment, a conspiracy is emerging to stop this progress. Unable to stop the Shibir, or the Islamic masses against hegemony, through terrorism, they now want to mislead the nation and push it back again through lies and propaganda. But the nation will never believe any lie. 

Mia Golam Parwar commented that the opponent has failed to confront Shibir with strong arguments and ideology and has chosen the path of lies and propaganda. He said that the opponent has called Shibir anti-independence, called it blood-curdling, and called it secret. But they could not prove it. The people rejected them (the opponent) in the four public university student council elections. The people have never been misled by their words. 

Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Rafiqul Islam Khan, Central Working Committee member and party candidate for Dhaka-12 constituency Saiful Alam Khan Milon, Islami Andolan Bangladesh Presidium member Ashraf Ali Akon, Bangladesh Labor Party Chairman Mostafizur Rahman Iran, Jatiya Ganatantrik Party (JAGPA) spokesperson Rashed Pradhan, among others, also spoke at the event. 

Khilafat Majlis Secretary General Ahmed Abdul Quader, Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Abdul Halim, Hamidur Rahman Azad, Dhaka Metropolitan North Amir Selim Uddin, Secretary Rezaul Karim, Dhaka Metropolitan South Amir Nurul Islam Bulbul, Secretary Shafiqul Islam Masud and other parliamentary candidates from various constituencies were present at the event. In addition, Jamaat leaders and workers from various levels were present. 

Omar Bin Hadi, elder brother of the late convener of Inqilab Manch Sharif Osman Bin Hadi, was also present at the event.

The event was presided over by Shibir's central president Zahidul Islam. The event was moderated by Shibir's central general secretary Nurul Islam Saddam. Thousands of Shibir members participated in the conference.

Headline_English: Tarique Rahman is going to visit his father's grave, leaders and activists are crowded
Content_Enlish:
BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman left his Gulshan residence for Zia Udyan a little before 3 pm today, Friday. There, he will visit the grave of his father, martyred President Ziaur Rahman. 

This news was announced in a post posted on the verified Facebook page of the BNP Media Cell at 2:58 pm today. Tarique Rahman is going to visit the grave of his father, martyred President Ziaur Rahman 
Tarique Rahman is going to visit the grave of his father, martyred President Ziaur Rahman Photo: Taken from the video on the Facebook page of the BNP Media Cell 
Tarique Rahman is going to visit his father's grave in the same bus decorated in red and green. He went to the public reception venue from the airport in this bus yesterday, Thursday. Like yesterday, today too, Tarique Rahman stood in front of the bus and waved to the leaders and workers. Tarique Rahman's motorcade is moving slowly due to the crowd of leaders and workers. 

Since morning, BNP leaders and activists have gathered in and around Zia Udyan in Dhaka's Sher-e-Bangla Nagar. Some have arrived there with party flags, others with banners and posters. 

BNP leaders and activists have gathered in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar 
After visiting his father's grave, Tarique Rahman will visit the National Memorial in Savar to pay tribute to the martyrs of the great Liberation War. 

Tarique Rahman returned home after 17 years on Thursday. Emotions were seen among BNP leaders and activists surrounding the visit to his father's grave. 

The leaders and activists said that this is not just a formal tribute, but a historic and symbolic moment for the party. 

BNP leaders and activists waiting for Tarique Rahman at Zia Udyan 
BNP leaders and activists waiting for Tarique Rahman at Zia UdyanPhoto: Sajid Hossain 
Security has been tightened in the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar area. Additional members of the law enforcement agencies have been deployed at Zia's tomb and the surrounding roads. 

Checkpoints have been set up at the entrances. Party volunteers are also on duty to maintain order. 

Position of law enforcement agencies at Zia Udyan 
Position of law enforcement agencies at Zia Udyan Photo: Sajid Hossain 
On the ground, it can be seen that the crowd started increasing on the roads adjacent to Zia Udyan before noon. Leaders and activists were instructed to stay at specific places for security reasons. The situation was controlled with the activities of law enforcement agencies and volunteers. 

BNP's media cell said on its verified Facebook page in the morning that Tarique Rahman will visit his father's grave after offering Friday prayers today. Later, he will go to the National Memorial in Savar to pay tribute to the martyrs of the Liberation War. 

Tarique Rahman returned home on Bangladesh Biman's BG-202 flight. He arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 11:43 am yesterday, Thursday, via Sylhet from London. He was accompanied by his wife Dr. Zubaida Rahman and only daughter Jaima Rahman. It doesn't take more than half an hour to go from Dhaka Airport to 300 feet in Purbachal if there is no traffic jam. It took Tarique Rahman three hours to go that way yesterday. Because, there are lines of leaders, activists, and supporters on both sides of the road, a crowd of people. Not only leaders and activists, many have come with the curiosity to catch a glimpse of Tarique Rahman returning to the country after 17 years, or to witness a memorable day of return. The six and a half kilometer path from the airport to the reception stage in Purbachal seems to be crowded.

Headline_English: BNP to carry out cleaning activities in 300 feet area including Airport Road
Content_Enlish:
BNP's cleaning activities will begin this Friday morning to remove waste and garbage created in the July 36 Expressway (300 feet) and Airport Road in Purbachal, including the adjacent areas. 

This was stated in a post posted on BNP's verified Facebook page at 10:30 pm on Thursday. 

BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman returned to the country with his family yesterday after a long 17-year exile. He went from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka to the 300 feet area of ​​Purbachal. The six-and-a-half-kilometer journey from the airport to the reception stage in Purbachal was crowded with people. Later, Tarique Rahman was given a reception in the presence of lakhs of people in the 300 feet area of ​​Purbachal. 

The post on BNP's verified Facebook page said that the activities to remove all waste created in the July 36 Expressway, Airport Road and adjacent areas will begin this morning in an unprecedented public gathering on the occasion of Tarique Rahman's historic homecoming. Dhaka Metropolitan North BNP will do this work voluntarily. 

Tarique Rahman's advisor Mahdi Amin also posted on his verified Facebook page about this. He wrote, BNP's cleaning program will start this morning to remove all the waste and garbage created on July 36 Expressway, Airport Road and adjacent areas in the public interest. 

Mahdi Amin thanked in advance the leaders, activists, supporters and volunteers who will participate in this cleaning program. At the same time, he expressed his sincere gratitude to all those who participated in yesterday's mass movement.

Headline_English: There are differences of opinion in the Jamaat-NCP seat sharing talks
Content_Enlish:
Discussions are underway on the seat sharing agreement between the National Citizens Party (NCP) and Jamaat-e-Islami in the 13th National Parliament elections. Although many in the party agree on the issue, a section also has a different opinion. Whether the NCP will reach an agreement with Jamaat or not will be clear in a day or two. 

Earlier, the issue of the NCP's seat sharing agreement with BNP was discussed. However, in the end, the two sides did not reach an understanding. After that, it is known from several sources that the discussion with Jamaat is progressing positively. 

Although, after the return of BNP's acting chairman Tarique Rahman, the top leaders of the NCP are seeing the possibility of discussing the seat sharing agreement with him again. They are interested in meeting Tarique Rahman and discussing the issue. However, there was no indication from the BNP side in this regard until Thursday. 

Earlier, the issue of the NCP's seat sharing agreement with BNP was discussed. However, in the end, the two sides did not reach an understanding. After that, it is known from several sources that the discussion with Jamaat is progressing positively.

Talking to responsible leaders of the NCP, it is learned that the top leadership of the party is already discussing a seat agreement with senior leaders of Jamaat. NCP has asked for concessions in at least 50 seats. However, this number is considered higher by Jamaat-e-Islami. Although Jamaat has not yet said anything final on this issue. It is known that Jamaat and NCP top leaders will discuss this again in a day or two. 

A section of the NCP supports reaching an agreement with Jamaat. However, another section has strong objections. After the talks on an agreement with Jamaat came to light, there was a reaction within a section of the party. Mir Arshadul Haque, known as the leader of the anti-Jamaat faction, resigned from the NCP yesterday. He was the NCP's joint member secretary and the chief coordinator of the Chittagong Metropolitan Committee. 

Meanwhile, Abdul Quader, a former coordinator of the anti-discrimination student movement and one of the front-line leaders of the July mass uprising, has claimed that the NCP is negotiating with Jamaat-e-Islami for electoral seats. He said that the NCP had asked for 50 seats from Jamaat, and after bargaining, 30 seats were agreed upon. According to this condition, the NCP will not be able to field any candidate in the remaining 270 seats. Referring to these issues, Abdul Quader wrote in a Facebook post yesterday morning that if everything goes well, the alliance could be announced on Friday (today). 

The NCP has asked for concessions in at least 50 seats. However, this number is considered high by Jamaat-e-Islami. Although nothing has been said definitively on this issue from Jamaat yet. It is known that the top leaders of Jamaat and NCP will hold discussions again in a day or two. 
However, none of the top leaders of NCP have agreed to officially say anything about the talks with Jamaat. However, an important leader of the party, on condition of anonymity, told Prothom Alo that many of the potential NCP candidates have visited the field level and held public meetings. Most of them said that if they want to win, they have no alternative but to enter into an alliance or compromise with BNP or Jamaat. Therefore, just as discussions are taking place with Jamaat, they are keeping the path of talks with BNP open. The leader said that there is a possibility that top NCP leaders will meet BNP chief leader Tarique Rahman directly. 

On the other hand, whether there will be a seat agreement between NCP and Jamaat or not; if so, how it will be done, will be clear in a few days, a top NCP leader told this reporter yesterday. 

When asked about this, Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Hamidur Rahman Azad told Prothom Alo last night that discussions with NCP are ongoing. 

A section of the NCP supports entering into a compromise with Jamaat. However, another section has strong objections. After the talks on a compromise with Jamaat came to light, there was a reaction within a section of the party. Mir Arshadul Haque, known as the leader of the anti-Jamaat faction, resigned from the NCP yesterday. 
The tone of the alliance is broken 
Ahead of the 13th parliamentary elections, an alliance was formed on December 7 by the NCP, Amar Bangladesh Party (AB Party) and Bangladesh State Reform Movement - these three parties. This alliance is called the 'Democratic Reform Alliance'. 

When the process of forming this alliance began, it was said that the Democratic Reform Alliance would try to become a third strong alliance outside the BNP and Jamaat. Now the State Reform Movement is angry that the NCP and AB Party are trying to reach an agreement with BNP or Jamaat. 

In this regard, Didar Bhuiyan, Joint General Secretary of the State Reform Movement, told Prothom Alo, 'The Democratic Reform Alliance will become a third strong alliance outside the BNP and Jamaat, this consensus was reached in the discussions of the three parties. But that understanding has already been violated after discussions on both sides (BNP and Jamaat). We will make an official statement in this regard soon.'

Headline_English: We Have a Plan: Tarique Rahman
Content_Enlish:
Dear Bangladesh—He started this way. Returning to the country after spending 17 years in exile in London, UK, BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman said in front of millions of people, ‘We have a plan. We have a plan for the people, for the country.’ 

Tareque Rahman also made it clear that everyone’s cooperation is needed to implement the plan (plan) taken for the people of the country, for the country. In his first speech after stepping foot on the country’s soil, he did not mention the details of that plan. He only said that if that plan (plan) has to be implemented to change the fate of the people of the country, then he will need the cooperation of everyone. 

Although Tarique Rahman said ‘I have a plan’ at the beginning of the speech, he later said ‘We have a plan.’ 
The car carrying Tarique Rahman stopped in front of house number 196 on Gulshan Avenue 
Yesterday, Thursday afternoon, BNP organized a public reception to welcome Tarique Rahman on the 300-foot road in Purbachal, Dhaka. He spoke for about 16 minutes standing on a stage built on the road called July 36 Expressway. Lakhs of leaders and workers from all over the country gathered on the 300-foot road to welcome this top leader of BNP. Before Tarique Rahman's speech, BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and party standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed gave brief speeches. They welcomed Tarique Rahman. 

Addressing the party leaders and workers, Tarique Rahman said, 'Haven't you heard of Martin Luther King? He has a famous dialogue, I Have a Dream. Today, standing on the soil of Bangladesh, I want to say in front of all of you, as a member of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, I want to say in front of you, I have a plan, people of my country, for my country. Today, this plan is in the interest of the people of the country.' 

Tareque Rahman came to the reception stage set up on the July 36 Expressway road in Purbachal to greet the leaders and workers by waving their hands. December 25 
Tarique Rahman came to the reception stage set up on the July 36 Expressway in Purbachal to greet the leaders and workers. December 25 Photo: Sajid Hossain 
Seeking everyone's cooperation in implementing the plan, Tarique Rahman said, "If that plan, that program, that plan has to be implemented for the development of the country, for changing the fate of the people of the country, then everyone's cooperation will be needed. If everyone stands by and cooperates, then 'I Have a Plan' will be able to be implemented." 

Martin Luther King Jr. was a leader of the American civil rights movement, who led the non-violent movement against racism and discrimination. When racism reached its peak in America and oppression against black people continued, he became the voice of the disenfranchised. On August 28, 1963, in a historic speech at a huge rally in Washington, DC, he said 'I Have a Dream' while mentioning his dream of ensuring equal rights for people. His speech deeply moved the consciousness of freedom-loving people around the world. 

After his speech of about 16 minutes, Tarique Rahman stood in front of the stage and waved to the leaders and activists. The program was coming to an end. At that time, he went to the microphone again and said, 'Remember, we have a plan. We have a plan for the people, for the country. Insha Allah, we will implement that plan.' 

So that people can be safe 
Tareque Rahman took the stage yesterday at 3:51 pm. He started his speech at 3:57 pm. Earlier, he left Shahjalal International Airport for the reception venue in Purbachal by bus some time after 12:30 pm. The entire route was crowded with people. Due to this, it took more than three hours to reach the Purbachal stage. 

In his speech, Tarique Rahman spoke several times about maintaining people's safety and peace. Highlighting the expectation that all people of the country, regardless of religion, caste, class, or profession, can be safe, he said, "We have to ensure that no matter what religion we belong to, what class we belong to, what political party we belong to, or whether we are a non-partisan person, we have to maintain peace and order in this country at any cost. We have to abandon any chaos at any cost. We have to ensure that people can be safe at any cost. Be it children, women, men—people of any age, any class, any profession, any religion—this is our desire." 

From Tarique Rahman's Facebook page 
In his speech, Tarique Rahman highlighted important chapters in the history of Bangladesh and said that the country's independence was achieved in 1971 at the cost of the blood of millions of martyrs. He reminded that on November 7, 1975, the country was saved from the hands of the hegemonists through the Sepoy-People's Revolution, and in 1990, the people of this country snatched their democratic rights against the dictatorship. However, the conspiracy did not stop. 

The acting chairman of BNP mentioned that people from all walks of life, including students and the public, participated in the 2024 mass uprising. He said that farmers and workers, housewives, men and women, madrasa students, all people, regardless of party affiliation, defended the independence and sovereignty of this country on August 5, 2024. Members of the young generation sacrificed their lives to protect the independence and sovereignty of the country. 

In this context, Tarique Rahman also said that a few days ago, a brave member of the 2024 movement, Osman Hadi, was killed. Osman Hadi was martyred. Osman Hadi wanted democracy to be established in this country, and for people's democratic and economic rights to return. To repay the debt of blood, the expected Bangladesh must be built. 
Patience is important 
Noting that the spies of various hegemonic powers are now involved in various conspiracies, Tarique Rahman said that in this situation, it is important to be patient and the young generation must take responsibility. The young people will lead the country in the future and build the country on a strong democratic and economic foundation. 

Highlighting the hope of forming an inclusive state, Tarique Rahman said that in this country, there are people from the mountains, there are people from the plains, people of different religions including Muslims, Buddhists, Christians, Hindus live. He said that he wants to build a country where a woman, a man, a child - whoever they are - can safely return home if they leave their homes. 

Tarique Rahman said that half of the country's population is women, more than 40 million members of the young generation, about 50 million children, about 4 million disabled people and several million farmers and laborers. These people have expectations and aspirations from the state. If everyone unites, these expectations can be fulfilled. 

Tarique Rahman said, people want to get back their right to speak, they want to get back their democratic rights. They want fair rights to be ensured according to their merits. He said, in this country, there are people from the hills, there are people from the plains; Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians—people of all religions live. Bangladesh includes everyone. 

Peace and order must be maintained 
Stateing that peace and order in the country must be maintained at any cost, BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman said, one must remain calm in the face of any provocation. One must avoid chaos and deal with it patiently. He further said, one must be patient. One must be patient. 

Regarding the administration of the country based on justice, Tarique Rahman said, "Let us all pledge that, God willing, those of us who will take charge of the country in the future will try our best to administer the country in the light of the justice of the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). 

Before returning to the country, BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman did not say anything about the upcoming national elections in his virtual speeches given at various events, but yesterday he did not say anything about it. 

Tarique Rahman has sought prayers from the countrymen for the recovery of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia. He said that as a child, his heart lies beside his mother's bed in the hospital, but he cannot abandon the people of the country for whom Khaleda Zia has sacrificed her life. 

In the front row of the reception stage were BNP standing committee members Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, Mirza Abbas, Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Abdul Moin Khan, Nazrul Islam Khan, Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Selima Rahman, Iqbal Hasan Mahmud, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, AZM Zahid Hossain, party's senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, among others. The host was BNP joint secretary general Shahid Uddin Chowdhury (Annie). Earlier, BNP publicity secretary Sultan Salahuddin (Tuku) made various announcements and slogans from the stage. 

Apart from this, the leaders of the allied and like-minded parties that held simultaneous movements with the BNP included Saiful Haque, General Secretary of the Revolutionary Workers Party, Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) Chairman Andaliv Rahman Partha, Chief Coordinator of the Mass Solidarity Movement Jonayed Saki, Senior Vice President of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD) Tania Rob, former Secretary General of the LDP Redwan Ahmed who recently joined the BNP, Acting President of the Gono Forum Subrata Chowdhury, former Professor of the Political Science Department of Dhaka University Nurul Amin Bepari, President of the Gano Odhikar Parishad Nurul Haque, Secretary General of the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh Golam Mohiuddin Ikram, Chairman of the NPP Fariduzzaman Farhad, Chairman of the NDM Bobby Hajjaj and General Secretary of the Aam Janata Dal Tarique Rahman.

Headline_English: Family Card: Women's progress on the path to self-reliance
Content_Enlish:
Power in the hands of women means a strong family, a strong Bangladesh. For millions of families in Bangladesh, poverty is not a statistic, it is a daily worry. Will there be rice in the cooking pot today? Will the children's books be bought? If someone suddenly falls ill, where will the medical expenses come from? 

The burden of these questions falls on women the most. The story of Rashida Begum from a village in Jhalakathi tells it all. The family somehow survives on the income of her husband's daily wage. One day, when she was unable to cook anything other than rice and dal, she had to endure her husband's anger, abuse, and insults. Lack of food then not only causes hunger, but also becomes a cause of insult and violence. 

Countless women like Rashida silently reduce their food, put their own needs aside, yet they keep the family strong. However, the sad reality is that for a long time, women have been seen in our social security system only as recipients of assistance, not as decision-makers or economic power. The proposal of the family card is to change this reality. 

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) believes that to eradicate poverty, the state must stand directly by the side of women. Because, when women are strong, the family is strong, and when the family is strong, the state is strong. This truth was expressed long ago by Napoleon Bonaparte. He said, ‘Give me an educated mother, I will give you a prosperous nation.’ 

Tarique Rahman has repeatedly given a modern interpretation of this philosophy in his various public meetings and speeches. He has clearly stated that the cycle of poverty cannot be broken unless not only education, but also food security, savings and economic decision-making power are given to women. It is from this belief that he has put forward the concept of family-based social security and identified the family card as a central tool for women’s empowerment. 

The practical embodiment of this vision is the electronic family card. Which is a modern, dignity-based and women-centric social security initiative. It is an important pillar of the 31-point outline for state repair announced by Tarique Rahman in 2023. Through this program, he not only provides assistance; Rather, it is a long-term political commitment to move women towards self-reliance. 

Under the Family Card, each family will receive food assistance worth 2,000 to 2,500 taka per month. This assistance can be given in the form of cash or specific food items, such as rice, flour, pulses and edible oil. This will ensure a large part of the minimum food needs of a family. If the monthly expenditure on food is reduced, the family will get some relief, and women will be at the center of that relief. 

This program will not be imposed suddenly across the country. To ensure transparency and effectiveness, a pilot project will be launched in each division with one upazila. It will be seen there whether people prefer cash assistance or food assistance; which method is less corrupt, which has less administrative cost. 

This innovative social protection program will be financed within the current revenue and expenditure framework, creating the necessary revenue savings by increasing efficiency in allocation and expenditure management and reducing corruption and waste. At the same time, there are plans to receive technical and financial assistance from development partners such as the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank during the initial implementation and expansion stages. Based on this experience, the program will be expanded step by step, first to 5 million families, and then gradually to the entire country. 

Studies in various countries around the world have proven that the benefits of providing direct assistance to women are not limited to women alone. It reaches children's education, family nutrition, and overall productivity. When women receive assistance, it is not wasted; rather, it is an investment for the future. 

The strongest aspect of the family card is its universal or blanket method. Here, there will be no need to select and list anyone's name. Because, experience shows, where there is selection, there is bias, corruption, and fear of exclusion. The family card is for everyone. In this, no one will have to seek political identity, lobbying, or recommendations to survive. When rights are universal, dignity is also universal. 

This card will be given in the name of an adult female member of the family. This is a policy decision. Because, women are the most practical and responsible managers of family expenses. If they save about two thousand taka per month, they can save that money and start small initiatives themselves—poultry farming, vegetable farming, sewing, home-made food, or small businesses. In other words, the Family Card is not just assistance; it is the seed of self-reliance. 

Bangladesh has seen such bold initiatives before. In 1992-93, the Food for Education program was launched. That initiative combined education with food and brought millions of children, especially girls, back to school. Today, the Family Card is the modern form of that tradition. Back then, girl children were brought forward through education, today, it is an attempt to bring adult women out of poverty through food security and savings. 
Research has proven in various countries around the world that the benefits of providing direct assistance to women are not limited to women alone. It reaches the education of their children, the nutrition of the family, and overall productivity. When women receive assistance, it is not wasted; rather, it is an investment for the future. 

Therefore, the Family Card is not a program of kindness. It is a political and moral position. It says that women are not objects of pity, but partners in development. It says that poverty alleviation is not a donation, but an investment in human capacity. 

In today's difficult economic reality, the Family Card is a realistic, transparent and courageous guide. It empowers women, strengthens families and stabilizes the state. 

The Family Card proposes a new social contract, where women's empowerment will be the foundation of a self-reliant, dignified and just Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Gen Z is once again bringing hope to politics around the world
Content_Enlish:
The last month of 2025 was a dismal one. Headlines of arbitrary shootings, crises and intense polarization filled the media. Yet, amid these dark times, a positive shift is signaling hope for the future. 

In countries across the developing world, young people are now loudly demanding jobs, affordable food and energy, economic opportunity and effective action to combat climate change. From South Asia to Latin America, they are sending a clear message to political leaders: ‘Listen and act, or stand down.’ 

Nepal is a clear example. Last September, the government banned 26 major social media platforms. These platforms were showing information about the lavish lifestyles of politicians’ children. This led to widespread protests against corruption, nepotism and a lack of opportunities for young people. Instead of dealing with the situation, 73-year-old Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli mocked the thousands of teenagers who took to the streets. At least 19 people were killed and hundreds injured in security forces' firing, as protesters set fire to the parliament building and attacked Oli's private residence. He resigned the next day. 

Many believe that the wave of this movement began in Sri Lanka in 2022. At that time, the country was in a terrible economic crisis. A severe fuel and electricity crisis led to a large movement led by young people. They set up camp in front of the office of the then 72-year-old President Gotabaya Rajapaksa. The allegations were that his family, who had been in power for a long time, was involved in corruption and nepotism. At one point, Gotabaya had to flee the country when protesters entered the president's residence. 

Two years later, students in Bangladesh took to the streets demanding job quota reforms. The government then shut down telecommunications and imposed a strict police crackdown. Hundreds of ordinary people were killed in this. But this violence could not suppress the movement; instead, thousands more people joined it. In Dhaka, protesters quickly marched to the office and residence of then-76-year-old Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. She fled to India shortly after. 

Around the same time, a protest led by Zen-Gi against President William Ruto’s proposed tax hike spread in Kenya. Dozens of people were killed, hundreds were injured, and many were arbitrarily detained by security forces. After protesters stormed parliament and set fire to it, Ruto withdrew the tax hike and fired most of his cabinet. Protests resumed in June this year, underscoring the depth of public anger. 

Meanwhile, in Peru, a movement against pension reform gradually spread. People spoke out against economic uncertainty and rampant corruption. The crackdown further heated up the situation. Eventually, President Dina Boluarte, who was under investigation for a bribery scandal, was removed from power. 

In each country, these protests led by Zen-Gi quickly gained widespread support from the general public. Young people have used social media to spread information, organize, and build networks. When governments shut down these platforms, they have organized on encrypted servers and even online gaming platforms. And they have not backed down in the face of state violence; they have intensified their movements. 

This movement is not limited to one generation or one region. It reflects the common concerns of working people in all countries, rich and poor. The 2008 financial crisis, Covid-19, the Ukraine war, and rising immigration pressures have all taken a toll on wages, job security, and people’s purchasing power. As a result, governments in power seem increasingly disconnected from reality. But Gen Z activists don’t want to destroy the political system. They want governments that will create jobs, crack down on corruption, and invest in tackling the climate crisis. These demands are realistic and there are ways to meet them. 
Youth unemployment is one example. A decade ago, Portugal, Ireland, Italy, Greece, and Spain—the so-called PIIGS—were suffering from severe debt crises. Now, all four of their countries have dramatically reduced youth unemployment. In Portugal, unemployment among 15- to 24-year-olds fell from 34.7 percent in 2014 to 18.3 percent in October 2025. In Ireland, it fell from 24.2 percent to 13.4 percent. In Greece, it fell from 52.8 percent to 22.4 percent in 2024. In Spain, the rate fell from 53.2 percent to 26.5 percent over the same period. 

The European Union’s Youth Guarantee program has played a major role in this progress. Under this program, governments promise to provide young people with a job, training, apprenticeship or education within four months of leaving school or becoming unemployed. Not all problems have been solved, but it has shown what can be done with political will. Fighting corruption is, of course, more difficult. The experiences of Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova and Ukraine prove it. Still, progress is possible. This requires skilled and well-paid civil servants, strong oversight and audit systems, and real political accountability. E-governance can also help. Rwanda’s digital public procurement system has reduced the scope for corruption. Georgia’s introduction of a fully electronic tendering system has seen early measurable improvements. 

Transparency is crucial here. When corruption becomes tolerated, it spreads. And when it is exposed, social pressure and reputational risk discourage corruption. Whistleblower protection, easily accessible anti-corruption databases, and a responsible role for the business sector are therefore essential.

Headline_English: Delhi must act responsibly
Content_Enlish:
It is clear from the course of events of the past few days that the tension in Bangladesh-India diplomatic relations has reached a worrying level. Last Tuesday, the High Commissioners of the two countries posted in Dhaka and Delhi were summoned on the same day, which is the first time that this has happened. Apart from this, Bangladesh and India summoned each other's diplomats twice in 12 days to express their protest and concerns on various issues. 

We know the initial stage of the deterioration of Bangladesh-India relations. Unfortunately, the Indian government could not accept the fall of Hasina's mass uprising and dictatorship in Bangladesh. It is clear to the people of Bangladesh that it was because of India's support that the Awami League government was able to maintain dictatorship in this country for a long time. They legitimized all the misdeeds of Sheikh Hasina and the non-voter and one-sided elections. The people of Bangladesh, who were hoping for democracy, ended this dictatorship through a mass uprising in July 2024. By taking a stand against the mass uprising in Bangladesh, India has practically taken a stand against the people of Bangladesh. 

The stability of Bangladesh-India relations is essential for the economic development and security of both countries. For that, India must take into account the reality and political changes in Bangladesh. 
The interim government led by Professor Yunus, who took office through a mass uprising, has taken various initiatives to normalize relations with India as a neighboring country in the past one and a half years, but there has been no positive response from India. Starting from the state level, the Indian media has started an extreme anti-Bangladesh campaign. Just as India has taken many negative steps in the commercial sector, it has also narrowed the normal visa process. 

The most important thing is that Sheikh Hasina, the deposed dictator who took refuge in India and is currently sentenced to death for crimes against humanity, has continued various provocative speeches and activities, but the Indian government has not tried to control it. In addition, people at various levels of the Awami League government and thousands of leaders and activists, who were involved in crimes such as murder, disappearances, murder and corruption while in power, are also making various provocative statements about their position in India. 

The people of Bangladesh have every reason to believe that Indian territory is being used for anti-Bangladesh purposes. It is not that India's diplomatic policymakers are unaware of these issues.

04 December 2024 
India's words and actions should be consistent 
Recently, we have seen that extremist Hindutva organizations in India have intensified their anti-Bangladesh activities. According to Prothom Alo, several Hindutva organizations held protests and rallies in front of the Bangladesh Mission in Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai on Tuesday. 

Earlier, a group of extremists attacked the Bangladesh visa center in Siliguri on Monday. On Saturday night, extremists entered the protected diplomatic area in Delhi and threatened the security of the Bangladesh High Commission. Due to such violent protests, Bangladesh had to suspend visas in Delhi, Agartala and Mumbai. 

These continuous actions of India are increasing the anger of the citizens of Bangladesh, especially the young population, which is resulting in increasing tension and violence in the internal politics of Bangladesh. 

Recently, the main accused in the murder of Inqilab Manch convener Sharif Osman Hadi fled to India, according to those involved in the investigation. The fact that the murderers found refuge in India has angered the people of Bangladesh. The tragic and sad murder of garment worker Dipu Chandra Das on charges of blasphemy in Mymensingh has been used by extreme right-wing groups in India to incite public anger there for their own political interests. 
What needs to be done now to restore 'equality' in Bangladesh-India relations 
We believe that the stability of Bangladesh-India relations is essential for the economic development and security of the two countries. For this, India must take into account the reality and political changes in Bangladesh. We must move away from the old mentality of meddling and influencing the internal politics of Bangladesh or how and when elections should be held, or of keeping a government of our choice in power against the will of the people of this country. 

We hope that India's diplomatic and political policymakers will be respectful of the anger, concerns and aspirations of the people of Bangladesh. Tolerance and responsible behavior can defuse diplomatic tensions.

Headline_English:
Corruption in solar power projects 
The share of renewable energy must be increased
Content_Enlish:
The previous government's wrong policies and impunity in the energy sector were implemented to protect the interests of the ruling class, as Transparency International Bangladesh's (TIB) research report on solar power projects once again makes it clear. Unbridled looting in the energy sector has certainly contributed to Bangladesh's economic stagnation, rising poverty rates, and social discontent. TIB's research reveals that in the last 15 years, six solar power projects have cost an additional Tk 3,000 crore. While an average of Tk 8 crore is required for the production of solar power per megawatt, an average of Tk 13.8 crore has been shown in the six projects. 

The TIB report reveals how a network extending from PDB's IPP department officials to local public representatives was involved in corruption. Even though the project was implemented on government land, the production cost per megawatt was shown as Tk 14 crore. Solar power projects were implemented on agricultural land after changing the category, and the mouza price was also shown to be higher through collusion. On the one hand, there has been financial corruption, and on the other hand, agricultural production has also been damaged. Contracts have been signed for four times more than neighboring countries. International standards have not been followed in the sale of electricity. 
All of this corruption and irregularities have been committed by misusing the Electricity and Energy Rapid Supply Increase (Special Act) Act of 2010. Although the interim government repealed the Energy Sector Immunity Act, it has not been able to take any effective initiative to reform the energy sector. The next elected government must pull the energy sector out of the trap of past wrong policies. 

More than 95 percent of the energy demand in Bangladesh comes from fossil fuels or coal, gas and oil. Our energy master plan is fossil fuel dependent. It is not possible to build a self-sufficient, sustainable, environmentally friendly and affordable energy system by relying only on fossil fuels. It is true that we cannot convert from fossil fuels to renewable energy in one go. But there must be a clear roadmap for energy transition, and the share of renewable energy must be increased step by step. 

As a result, it is time to create a new energy master plan with renewable energy at the center, not in a scattered and isolated manner. It is possible to implement solar power projects on land acquired for canceled coal and LNG-based power plants. We hope that political parties will present their plans for the power sector to the citizens by prioritizing renewable energy in their manifestos.

Headline_English: Why Trump and Putin both want to 'destroy' Europe
Content_Enlish:
There are those who believe that Vladimir Putin’s war on Ukraine is not motivated by fear or imperial ambition, but by contempt for other countries. Russia was once one of the world’s two superpowers; but it has lost that status. Russia knows that it no longer commands the respect of other countries (Barack Obama once dismissed Russia as a mere “regional power”). The war in Ukraine is an attempt to regain that lost respect. 

What is somewhat surprising is that Donald Trump’s stance against Europe is driven by similar motivations. Putin knows that his aggressive vindictiveness will not win the love of the countries whose respect he seeks. But if he cannot win love, he at least wants to instill fear. In a social system where you are looked down upon, you have ample incentive to become a “spoiler.” 

Similarly, Trump wants to dismantle a social system that looks down on him and his worldview. The US president and his officials are respected by dictators and kings (Putin and Xi Jinping); but they know that the leaders of many democratic countries look down on them. 

The US now wants to break up the existing hierarchy of respect and create a world where Trump will receive unconditional loyalty. Europe, with its emphasis on the rule of law and multilateralism, is the most powerful example of what remains—a whole system of dignity and values ​​that the Trump administration wants to destroy. 

Ironically, the world that Trump is trying to destroy was built by the US. After World War II, Washington adopted a new global ambition. Republicans and Democrats alike believed that a world based on American values ​​would be better for America. They declared that democracy and the rule of law would be the criteria by which countries were judged. 

Despite the obvious hypocrisy (the US itself has often behaved illiberally and undemocratically), this was the basis of US “soft power”; The ability to influence the world indirectly through culture and values. Other countries looked to the United States as a role model. 

The greatest creation of the old order was modern Europe. After World War II, the United States helped rebuild the economies of Western Europe, encouraged the success of liberal parties, and, when necessary, quietly undermined forces it considered too far left or right. 

The European Union has its historical roots in a system developed to coordinate US aid distributed through the Marshall Plan. Over time, it grew to create a new governance system for Europe based on the cooperation of nation states, the importance of law, and liberal democracy. After the collapse of Soviet rule in Eastern Europe, the EU expanded to include countries in the South and East, on the condition that they adopt democratic principles. In many ways, the European Union embodied the values ​​of the US-created liberal international system more than the United States. 

Now the Trump administration wants to dismantle the old international system and replace it with a new system based on power and national interests. Their new national security strategy says they want to maintain America’s “unparalleled soft power”; but the way to achieve that is to recognize “America’s inherent greatness and decency.” In the preface to the strategy, Trump proudly writes that “America is finally strong and respected again.” 

The problem is that in reality, this is clearly not true. Countries that still cling to liberal values ​​do not respect Trump’s America at all. America’s soft power and its indirect influence on other democratic countries is gradually shrinking. 

That is why so much energy and anger has been spent on Europe in Trump’s national security strategy. On the one hand, the United States is talking about abandoning its desire to change the world with pomp. On the other hand, it is also talking about wanting to intervene in Europe and transform it. 

“Maga” America wants to support the political parties it supports in Europe—they are the hard right. In contrast to the European cooperation that the United States encouraged after World War II, the Trump administration now seeks to exploit the discontent of the new EU members to create a kind of rift with the liberal democratic values ​​of the European Union; to shape Europe into a confederation of sovereign states that will be intensely nationalistic and culturally bound up with a “white” identity. 

The Trump administration can punish the European Union through sporadic and inappropriate interventions, while at the same time trying to help bring far-right parties to power. 
In this world, Europe will no longer be an obstacle to “MAGA” ideology. But the big challenge facing the Trump administration is that it does not have the capacity or global ambition to make this transformation happen. 

Like Russia, this administration wants respect, but it has little power other than to act as a “spoiler”. It wants to influence Europe, while at the same time reducing its involvement with Europe; it also wants to withdraw from its role as a security guarantor of NATO.

Trump’s strategy paper has attacked the “large military, diplomatic, intelligence and foreign assistance structures” that have long been the basis of US global ambitions and is doing everything it can to undermine them. But without those structures, the US will not be able to rebuild Europe in its own way. 

The Trump administration could certainly punish the EU with sporadic and inappropriate interventions, while also trying to help far-right parties come to power. It is already denying visas to people who have worked as fact-checkers or social media moderators; who have been accused of suppressing right-wing opinion; and threatening the EU for having the “audacity” to regulate services like X. But the example of Brazil is that its efforts to punish officials and support Jair Bolsonaro have failed miserably. It shows that these actions may do more harm than good to their ideological allies. 

The Trump administration wants to gain respect and global soft power—which is why it is chasing Europe. But at the same time, it wants to withdraw, reduce global capabilities, and transform the United States into a regional power like Russia; a power that exerts its power by “grandfathering” its neighbors. These two goals cannot be achieved simultaneously.

Content_Enlish:
Depositors of the five banks that are in the process of merging will soon be able to withdraw up to a maximum of Tk 2 lakh. Bangladesh Bank is providing this facility in view of their demand. However, no specific date or time has been finalized yet regarding when the depositors of these five banks will be able to withdraw money. Meanwhile, a news has recently spread on social media and in some media outlets that depositors of a bank under the merger will be given the opportunity to withdraw money from Monday, December 29. Bangladesh Bank has said that this news is not correct. In a notification today, Friday, the regulatory body has specifically requested all concerned not to be misled by false information. 

The five banks that are going to merge are First Security Islami, Social Islami, Union, Global Islami and Exim Bank. These banks are struggling to pay salaries to employees due to liquidity crisis, and customers are also facing problems in withdrawing money. 

Final approval has already been given to form a new bank named ‘Sammilit Islami Bank PLC’. The bank will acquire the five troubled Islamic banks.
