Headline_English: From civil war to the election field, what lies ahead for the junta in Myanmar?
Content_Enlish:
The head of the junta, Min Aung Hlaing, has been in power in Myanmar for nearly five years. Last week, he urged the public to vote in the elections that begin on December 28 from a military base. He also warned that people should choose candidates who can keep pace with the Tatmadaw, or Myanmar's armed forces. 

Hlaing's statement makes it clear that the junta wants to do through elections what it could not do in the civil war. That is, to make its supported party win in the elections. And through this, to further consolidate its power in the face of an armed rebellion. At the same time, to reduce the dissatisfaction with its power abroad. 

However, analysts and diplomats say that the stability that the junta is trying to bring through elections in this Southeast Asian country, where the civil war is getting worse, is a kind of difficult. And while foreigners are criticizing and looking askance at the election, the chances of getting support from those countries after the victory are very low. 

Myanmar will vote in two phases. December 28 and January 11. On these two days, 220 of the country's 330 urban areas under military control will vote. Richard Horse, a researcher at the research organization Crisis Group, said, "Indirect military rule will not bring any solution to armed rebellion or civil resistance, but rather will keep Myanmar immersed in crisis." 

Myanmar gained independence from British colonial rule in 1948. Since then, military officers have ruled the country for most of the time. Min Aung Hlaing was named among them in February 2021. At that time, the democratic government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in Myanmar was ousted in a military coup, accusing her of election fraud. 

Suu Kyi's party, the National League for Democracy, won the elections in 2015 and 2020. The Myanmar Election Commission has dissolved the party. They will not be able to participate in this election. Other anti-junta parties are also not participating. Six parties are running. Among them, the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP) is more likely to win. 

If the USDP wins, Min Aung Hlaing will remain in a strong position. However, there are some different examples in the past. For example, after the 2010 election, the military installed former General Thein Sein as the head of the civilian government. However, he took various liberal steps on the contrary. This allowed the democratic Suu Kyi to come to power. 

It is also true that the current picture is completely different from that time. Myanmar's unity is fragmented in the civil war. Ye Myo Hein, a researcher at the non-profit Southeast Asia Peace Institute, said that the conflict in the country could spread further due to this election organized by the military. As a result, it will not be possible to bring sustainable political and economic stability.

Headline_English: 2.75 billion installations on the world's 3D map
Content_Enlish:
3D model of Bangladesh's parliament building on a three-dimensional map 
3D model of Bangladesh's parliament building on a three-dimensional map Screenshot 
A group of researchers in Germany has created a three-dimensional (3-D) map of 2.75 billion buildings to provide an opportunity to view images of buildings in different parts of the world online. About eight hundred thousand images taken from satellites in 2019 were used to create the three-dimensional map called the Global Building Atlas. In places where satellite images were unclear, 3D models of the size and volume of the building have been created using artificial intelligence (AI) according to the height of the surrounding buildings. 

Instead of the traditional 2-D map, the size of each building can be seen in a 3-D model on the 3-D map. As a result, buildings from various cities, starting from London to China, have also come alive here. It is possible to see 3D models of buildings at specific addresses in specific countries and cities in the search bar above the 3-D map. 

3D models of various buildings in Dhaka on a three-dimensional map 
3D models of various buildings in Dhaka on a three-dimensional map Screenshot 
According to the map data, Asia has the largest number of buildings in the world, about 1.22 billion. The total number of buildings in Asia is almost half of the total number of buildings in the world. Then there are 540 million in Africa, 400 million in Europe, 290 million in North America and 260 million in South America. There are only 14 million buildings in the Oceania region. 
Not only satisfying curiosity, this three-dimensional map also has scientific importance. 

According to researchers, using the three-dimensional map will make it easier to alleviate poverty, plan urban development and manage disasters. The German Aerospace Center has already started using this map to help disaster-stricken areas. However, due to the large number of people using the three-dimensional map online at the same time, the Global Building Atlas authorities said that initially the entire part of the map could not be seen properly.

Headline_English: BNP leaders and activists rush to the public reception venue on motorcycles, buses, trucks, and pickups.
Content_Enlish:
Leaders and activists from different parts of the country have gathered at the mass reception venue for the return of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman to the country. Yesterday afternoon, in the 300-foot area of ​​Purbachal in the capital. 
Leaders and activists from different parts of the country have gathered at the mass reception venue for the return of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman to the country. Yesterday afternoon, in the 300-foot area of ​​Purbachal in the capital. Photo: Prothom Alo 
Party leaders and activists have been coming to Dhaka for several days to attend the mass reception of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman. A large number of leaders and activists arrived in Dhaka from different districts in buses, trains, launches and other vehicles on Wednesday, the day before the reception. 

Tarique Rahman will be given a mass reception at the 36 July Expressway (300-foot road) in Purbachal in the capital on Thursday. Stage construction and other preparations have been going on there for three days. Leaders and activists have been going there for several days. A large number of leaders and workers gathered there throughout the day and night yesterday. 

There was a huge presence there until 9 pm when this report was written. Many were saying that they would stay there overnight. 

Tarique Rahman will arrive in Bangladesh from the UK around 12 noon today. He is returning home after 17 years. Party leaders and workers say that Tarique Rahman's return before the national elections is very significant for the country and the party. Arrangements have been made to give him a public reception on behalf of the party. 

Salahuddin Ahmed, a member of the party's standing committee and convener of the public reception committee, announced Tarique Rahman's three-day program at a press conference yesterday afternoon at the political office of the BNP Chairperson in the capital's Gulshan. He said that after landing at the airport this afternoon, senior leaders of the party will welcome Tarique Rahman. After that, he will go to the July Expressway reception area. He will thank and express gratitude to the leaders and workers waiting there and address the countrymen. No one else will speak. 

BNP says that Tarique Rahman is returning home on a holiday to avoid public suffering and Purbachal has been chosen as the place for the public reception. 

Preparations at the public reception venue 
It was seen throughout the day yesterday that banners and festoons of different colors have been put up on both sides of the July 36 Expressway on the way from Kuril in the capital to the reception venue, welcoming Tarique Rahman. And a large stage of 48 feet long and 36 feet wide is being built with bamboo and wood on the northern part of the road, facing south, quite a distance from the Kuril intersection. Tarique Rahman will be accompanied by 25 senior BNP leaders on the stage during the public reception. 

Strict security measures have been taken at the public reception venue. A large number of members of the law enforcement agencies were seen there. The law enforcement agencies have set up tents on both sides of the stage. Members of the BNP Chairperson Security Force (CSF) are also working on their own security. 

Microphones have been installed on streetlight poles on both sides of the stage. Electronic screens (LED screens) have been installed a little further from the stage. The main stage and the entire program will be broadcast on them. Medical facilities have also been set up at the mass reception venue in case anyone falls ill. A temporary medical center with six beds has been set up. Drinking water facilities have been set up. 

At around 1 pm yesterday, leaders and activists were seen going there in processions. Some of them were standing in front of the stage and doing Facebook 'live', while others were shouting slogans like 'Mother and Mother are calling, Tarique Rahman is coming', 'Tareque Rahman is coming in the guise of a hero, he will come to Bangladesh this time'. 

North South University Chhatra Dal Vice President Ferdous Navid was found in front of the stage. He told Prothom Alo that in the coming days, under the leadership of Tarique Rahman, they will unite and build a new Bangladesh, where there will be justice, freedom of expression, people's right to vote and people's rule. Everyone is waiting for Tarique Rahman with hope. 

BNP wants to ensure a huge presence of people in Dhaka in groups from districts 
BNP wants to ensure a huge presence of people in Tarique Rahman's public reception. Prothom Alo's own reporters and representatives from different districts said that leaders, activists and supporters have set off for Dhaka in various vehicles including buses, launches, trains, and others surrounding the public reception. 

Leaders from Tarique Rahman's own district Bogra say that in the past three days, leaders and activists have come to Dhaka from there in 700 vehicles. The number is about 50,000. Apart from this, at least 10,000 leaders and activists have come to Dhaka from Bogra by train. 

Local BNP leaders and activists say that about 20,000 leaders and activists from Jhalokati district, about 10,000 leaders and activists from Bagerhat, and about 50,000 leaders and activists from Jessore have come to Dhaka. In this way, a large number of leaders and workers are coming from all districts. 

Special trains 
The Railways has started 10 special trains on 10 routes to facilitate people to attend the program organized on the occasion of Tarique Rahman's return to the country. In view of the BNP's application, the Railways will run these trains today in exchange for fare. 

The BNP had applied to start 11 special trains. Due to engine shortage, 10 trains were finally started. In addition, 17 additional coaches have been added to other trains.

Headline_English: Merry Christmas today, the churches are decorated with colorful decorations
Content_Enlish:
Last-minute preparations are underway in churches for Christmas. Yesterday at the Rosary Queen's Church in Tejgaon 
Last-minute preparations are underway in churches for Christmas. Yesterday at the Rosary Queen's Church in Tejgaon Photo: Sajid Hossain 
The main religious festival of Christians is today, Thursday. This festival is known in Bangladesh as 'Christmas'. Christians all over the world celebrate the 'Christmas Day' festival on December 25 as the birthday of Jesus Christ. 

In Bangladesh, too, the Christian community will celebrate the day with prayers and joyful arrangements according to their religious rules. Usually, cakes are cut in houses to celebrate the birthday of Jesus Christ on this day. In addition, delicious food is cooked at home, Christmas trees are decorated and lights are decorated. Gifts are distributed among children. Churches also have decorations and special Christmas prayers. 

Christians believe that Jesus Christ was born on this day in a stable in the West Bank city of Bethlehem, Palestine. Jesus Christ was born to preach the glory of God and guide mankind to the path of truth and justice. 

Yesterday, Wednesday, it was seen on the ground that the churches of Dhaka were decorated colorfully on the occasion of Christmas. In the afternoon, the colors of the festival were seen at the Holy Rosary Queen's Church in Tejgaon and the Saint Christina Church in Mohammadpur. 

The Christmas prayer will be held twice today at the Holy Rosary Queen's Church in Tejgaon - at 7 am and 9 am. And the prayer will be held at the Saint Christina Church in Mohammadpur at 8 am. Thousands of people will pray at the two churches. 

Talking to the Jesus devotees who came to the church yesterday, it was learned that they will participate in special Christmas prayers and religious music. In this, they will call for peace, love and humanity. Many will silently light candles and remember the ideals of Jesus' life. 

Father Kajal Purification, pastor of St. Christina Church in Mohammadpur, said that this Christmas, we will pray for peace in our hearts and in the world. This prayer is for all Hindus, Muslims and Christians. 

Father Jayant S. Gomes, priest of the Holy Rosary Queen's Church in Tejgaon, said that Jesus has always worked to establish the social and human dignity of the marginalized. Through these, he established justice and equality in the world. Our prayer this time will be that peace be established in Bangladesh in the changing situation. That stability prevails in the country. That democracy be established. 

Messages from the President and Chief Advisor 
On the occasion of Christmas, President Md. Shahabuddin and Chief Advisor Professor Muhammad Yunus gave separate messages. In the message, they extended their warmest greetings and congratulations to the followers of Christianity on their biggest religious festival. 

In his message, the President said, ‘Bangladesh is a country of communal harmony. Here, people of all religions have been freely practicing their respective religions and rituals. On this auspicious day, I call upon everyone to further strengthen this communal harmony and join the journey of building a modern and developed Bangladesh.’ 

In his message, the Chief Advisor said, Jesus Christ was a seeker of truth, an ambassador of humanity’s liberation, and a guide of light. Despite hundreds of obstacles and adversities, he always preached the message of peace, truth, and justice. He gave everyone the initiation of love, service, forgiveness, and greatness. 

The Chief Advisor called upon all Christians to come forward, inspired by the great ideals of patriotism and humanity, to realize the dream of Bangladesh.

Headline_English: BRAC Bank ATM service launched at five Metrorail stations

Senior officials of Metrorail operator DMTCL and BRAC Bank at the signing ceremony of the agreement to launch banking services at five stations of MetrorailPhoto: Courtesy of BRAC Bank 
BRAC Bank has set up ATM booths at five important stations of MRT Line-6 ​​in Dhaka to provide fast and hassle-free banking services to passengers. As a result, the bank's alternate banking channel network has been further expanded. 

The ATMs installed at Pallabi, Mirpur-10, Farmgate, Shahbagh and Bangladesh Secretariat stations of MRT Line-6 ​​are now fully operational. 

Metrorail has opened a new horizon in Dhaka's transportation system. BRAC Bank's digital and easy banking service will provide 24-hour banking facilities to users at these important points. In addition to cash withdrawal, passengers will be able to avail various smart banking facilities including fund transfer, balance inquiry, cardless cash withdrawal, bKash cash-out from these technology-enabled ATMs. 

This initiative has been taken under an agreement signed between Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL), the metro rail operator, and BRAC Bank. 

The agreement was signed by BRAC Bank Deputy Managing Director and Head of Alternative Banking Channels Nazmur Rahim and Dhaka Mass Transit Company Managing Director Faruk Ahmed. 

DMTCL Project Director Brigadier General (Retd.) Md. Abdul Wahab, NDC, P.Eng., Company Secretary (Joint Secretary) Khandaker Ehteshamul Kabir, BRAC Bank Head of Alternate Delivery Channels Imtiaz Ahmed, Regional Head of Distribution Network Naqib Zaman, Head of Government Relations Khandaker Emdadul Haque and Cluster Manager Sabina Sarmin. 

Regarding the launch of ATM services at MRT stations, Nazmur Rahim said, “By adding banking services to the centers of daily commute, we are making financial services faster, smarter and more convenient for the city’s customers. We will expand our ATM services to important points and transport hubs to ensure nationwide banking convenience.” 

BRAC Bank is further expanding its banking services nationwide with a wide alternative banking network of 329 ATMs, 103 CRMs and 68 RCDMs across the country. The bank is committed to making banking services more accessible across the country by strengthening and expanding its network. This initiative is a reflection of that commitment.

Headline_English: Trump administration orders two-month embargo on Venezuelan oil
Content_Enlish:
US military helicopters in Puerto Rico 
US military helicopters in Puerto Rico File Photo: Reuters 
The White House has ordered the US military to consider imposing an "exclusive blockade" on Venezuelan oil for at least two months. A US official told Reuters on condition of anonymity on Wednesday. This means that Washington is currently placing more emphasis on economic pressure than military pressure on Caracas. 

The official said that the path to confronting Venezuela militarily is still open. However, Washington will first apply economic pressure through sanctions to achieve its goals. This effort has already put enormous pressure on Caracas. It is believed that Venezuela will face economic disaster by the end of January if an agreement is not reached with the United States. 

Despite deploying a large number of troops around Venezuela, US President Donald Trump has not yet disclosed his goals for the country. Although he has personally pressured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro to resign. Even last Monday, Trump said that it would be wiser for Maduro to leave power. 

As a reason for this military deployment in the Caribbean Sea, Trump said that a large amount of drugs are entering the United States from Venezuela. US forces have been attacking ships labeled as drug carriers for several months. Various countries have accused this of extrajudicial killings. Trump has also threatened to attack various drug-related infrastructure on Venezuelan territory. 

So far, the US Coast Guard has conducted raids on two Venezuelan oil tankers in the Caribbean Sea. The oil has been seized. Sources told Reuters that the Coast Guard is waiting to seize a third tanker. An attempt was made to seize the ship named 'Bela-1' last Sunday. However, a new raid is now being planned with more military personnel. 

The White House did not respond to Reuters' request for comment on what was meant by the embargo on Venezuelan oil. On Tuesday, Venezuela's ambassador to the United Nations, Samuel Moncada, said, "The threat is not Venezuela, but the United States government."

Headline_English: Fake DB tries to handcuff former Chhatra Dal leader in Mymensingh
Content_Enlish:
In Trishal, Mymensingh, they faced resistance from locals when they tried to pick up a former Chhatra Dal leader under the identity of a fake DB. In Trishal, Bir Rampur area on Wednesday night Photo: Prothom Alo 
Fake Detective Police (DB) tried to pick up a former Chhatra Dal leader in Trishal, Mymensingh by putting him in handcuffs. When the locals gathered at the victim's screams, they fled after seeing the situation as dangerous. Later, the fire service was called and the handcuffs were untied. The incident took place in Bir Rampur area of ​​the upazila at around 10 pm on Wednesday. 

Police and locals said that Rezaul Karim (32), the newly former president of Rampur Union Chhatra Dal in the upazila, was returning home from Gafakuri Bazar at around 10 pm yesterday. As he was going to Bir Rampur area, five people posing as DB police blocked his way. At that time, Rezaul was quickly handcuffed. Two of the five were beating him and taking him to a deserted field. Then Rezaul started shouting when he got suspicious. Later, when the locals gathered, the fake DB police quickly fled. 

Later, the Chhatra Dal leader's elder brother contacted the district DB and Trishal police station and found out that no DB team had come out for the operation. After taking the injured Chhatra Dal leader to Trishal Sadar for treatment, the police station and police tried to untie the handcuffs but failed. Later, the fire service personnel went and cut the handcuffs. The injured Chhatra Dal leader has been admitted to Trishal Upazila Health Complex. 

The Chhatra Dal leader's brother Enamul Karim said, "The news that the DB police have caught my brother, I want to know from them, what is my brother's crime? Why did they catch him? Why are they beating him? Do you have any warrant? Where are the weapons and walkie-talkies?" Then they ran away in a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw.’ 

Injured Rezaul Karim said, ‘We had taken out a procession wearing a shroud on November 28 demanding a change in BNP’s nomination in the Trishal constituency. This attack may have occurred due to that incident.’ 

Trishal Police Station Officer-in-Charge Firoz Hossain said, ‘A former enemy attacked the young man by posing as a fake DB. The group fled before we reached the spot after receiving the information. The injured man is now receiving treatment. When he was rescued, he had a pair of handcuffs on his hand. The handcuffs are very old. They were used by the police earlier. They are now in our custody. We have asked him to file a complaint at the police station. We will take legal action if we receive a complaint.’

Headline_English: AIUB Cyber ​​Gaming Fest 2025 held

Majed-ul-Haq, and Lecturer and Special Assistant SM Abdullah Shafi were present at the inaugural and various events.

The media partners were Daily Sun, The Daily Jugantar and DBC News. Kishore Alo was the magazine partner. 

51 teams participated in the online qualifier phase of the PUBG Mobile competition. From there, 32 teams advanced to the semi-finals and subsequently 16 teams advanced to the campus finals. After emerging from the lower-bracket, the All-Stars team faced NaxR E-Sports in the grand final. In the three-match final, All-Stars finally secured the championship. Headline_English: Ending long speculation, Rokonuddin Babul gets BNP nomination
Content_Enlish:
Pradeep Kumar, Crime Reporter Lalmonirhat: 

Ending long-standing speculation, Rokanuddin Babul has finally received the nomination from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) for the Lalmonirhat-2 (Kaliganj-Aditmari) constituency. On Wednesday (December 24), the party high command decided to declare him as the final candidate for the paddy field. 
Immediately after the nomination was announced, there was great enthusiasm among the leaders and activists of BNP and its affiliates across Kaliganj and Aditmari upazilas. Processions, distribution of sweets and a joyful atmosphere were created in various areas. As the long-standing uncertainty about the candidate has come to an end, relief has returned among the general voters. 
Party sources said that Rokanuddin Babul has been nominated due to his organizational skills, selfless political role, public involvement and wide acceptance at the grassroots level. His popularity and active public relations in the area are considered a big strength for the BNP. 
Local leaders and activists said that Rokanuddin Babul is a politician with a clean image. He has stood by the common people in good times and bad times. They expressed hope that his nomination will make the party more well-organized and the victory of the paddy sheesh in the Lalmonirhat-2 constituency in the upcoming elections will be largely assured. 
Regarding the nomination, Rokanuddin Babul said, 
“I have always respected the party’s decision. I had full confidence in the high command. The party nominated me considering me worthy. Now my main responsibility is to strengthen the hands of the country’s leader Begum Khaleda Zia and the future statesman Tarique Rahman by achieving victory in this constituency and to work for the welfare of the common people. For this, I seek everyone’s cooperation.” 
According to political analysts, Rokanuddin Babul’s nomination has added a new dimension to the electoral equation of the Lalmonirhat-2 constituency. This has further strengthened the expectation of victory among BNP supporters. 
All in all, the election field in Lalmonirhat-2 has started to heat up with the announcement of the paddy sheaf candidate. The general voters are now looking towards the future in the hope of change.

Headline_English: 4 accused in Dipu Chandra Das murder case in Mymensingh

Headline_English: Chittagong Royals: Less worried about bowling, more worried about batting

They are different from other teams 
The ownership of the 6 participating teams has been taken by six organizations. But the day before the opening of the tournament, Triangle Services, which had acquired the rights of Chittagong Royals, has given up ownership.

Shariful Islam is the biggest name in pace bowling. His swing with the new ball can become challenging for the opponent's batsmen. He is also a regular face of the Bangladesh team in T20s. Headline_English: 3 people die after being hit by train while walking on railway tracks in Gazipur
Content_Enlish:
Symbolic image of death after being run over by a train 
Three people died after being run over by a train while walking on the railway line in Kaliganj, Gazipur. The accident occurred on Thursday afternoon in the area adjacent to Arikhola railway station on the Tongi-Bhairab railway line. 

The deceased are Sabiya (24), wife of Mubarak of Dayaltek area of ​​Kaliganj Municipality in Gazipur, Ishaq's daughter Mosa. Anabi (11) of the same village, and Ishaq's mother-in-law Mosa. Kamala Begum (55), wife of the late Nazaruddin of Abdullahpur area of ​​Raipura police station in Narsingdi. Kamala Begum had come to visit her son-in-law's house in Dayaltek area. 

Locals and eyewitnesses said that the Coastal Express train from Dhaka to Noakhali was passing through Arikhola station at around 5 pm. At that time, the three people were walking on the railway line in the area between the Arikhola railway bridge and the road towards Dayaltek. They were crushed under the train as they did not hear the sound of the train coming from behind. They died on the spot. Upon receiving the information, the Kaliganj Police and Railway Police went to the spot and recovered the bodies.

Headline_English: Handicrafts can become a billion-dollar export sector
Content_Enlish:
Guests at a seminar titled 'Bangladeshi Handicrafts: Increasing Export Capability and Global Market Challenges' jointly organized by the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) and BRAC University's Center for Entrepreneurship Development (CED). Today, Wednesday at BRAC University. Photo: Prothom Alo 
The global market for handicrafts is more than one trillion or one lakh crore US dollars. However, only 380 million or 380 million dollars worth of products are exported from Bangladesh in this sector. The global market size of these products is about 32 billion or 320 million dollars. 

This was stated in a seminar titled ‘Bangladeshi Handicrafts: Enhancing Export Capability and Global Market Challenges’ jointly organized by the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) and BRAC University’s Center for Entrepreneurship Development (CED) on Wednesday. It said that handicrafts can become a $1 billion or $1 billion export sector of Bangladesh if bonded warehouse facilities and financing are ensured. 

The handicraft sector mainly exports jute carpet products, metal products, stone and bamboo-rattan products from Bangladesh. 

EPB Vice Chairman Mohammad Hasan Arif was the chief guest at the seminar organized at BRAC University. EPB Director Abu Mokhles Alamgir Hossain presented the keynote address at the seminar chaired by BRAC University’s Associate Vice Chancellor Professor Arshad Mahmud Chowdhury. 

We do not have many good entrepreneurs. Many are able to move forward with good products despite having them. No. Because, there is a lack of communication. It is very important for these organizations to be active online. 
—Belal Hossain, President, Bangladesh Handicraft Manufacturers and Exporters Association (Banglacraft) 
EPB Vice Chairman Mohammad Hasan Arif said, ‘You have to overcome problems to become an entrepreneur. You have to move forward through problems. Earlier, we used to give 20 percent cash incentive for exporting handicraft products. However, after transitioning from LDC, it cannot be given anymore. Therefore, the incentive has been reduced to 6 percent. However, there is more work to be done in terms of coordinating incentives.’ 

Regarding participation in foreign fairs with government assistance, Md. Hasan Arif said, ‘Entrepreneurs from Vietnam, China or India do not go to foreign fairs with government assistance. There is also a question about how useful it is. Therefore, we are bringing foreign buyers to the country and holding sourcing fairs. Again, we are thinking of providing training before going to the fair. And we will create an online platform to maintain communication between entrepreneurs and buyers.’ 

The original article said, Bangladesh currently exports only 1.18 percent of global demand. However, with proper policy support, it is possible to export one billion dollars worth of goods annually from this sector. For that, bonded warehouse facilities and financing must be ensured. 

In the article, Abu Mokhles Alamgir Hossain said that the demand for environmentally friendly products in the world is increasing rapidly. Therefore, the market for handicraft products may exceed 2 trillion dollars by 2032. Therefore, products must be manufactured according to the growing global demand. For this, the use of machinery must be increased to compete with India and China. In addition, emphasis must be placed on modernization in design and increasing skilled manpower. 

Belal Hossain, President of Bangladesh Handicraft Manufacturers and Exporters Association (Banglacraft), said, "We do not have many good entrepreneurs. Many are not able to move forward with good products even after having them. Because, there is a lack of communication. It is very important for these organizations to be active online." 

The President of Banglacraft demanded a 20 percent cash incentive as before for the survival of this sector. 

Low interest Bangladesh Bank's Additional Director Mohammad Mostafizur Rahman said that there is a fund of 30 thousand crore taka for loans. He said, 'Loans are given from this fund at an interest rate of 5 to 7 percent. In the future, we will give responsibility to some banks and financial institutions to provide all types of financing to 10 handicraft clusters within 6 months.' 

Md. Nazim Hasan Sattar, Deputy Managing Director of SME Foundation, spoke about increasing coordination between industrial institutions, researchers and government representatives to advance this industry. He said, 'We want to create new entrepreneurs. We are also trying to find out the needs of foreign buyers.' 

The organization's chief designer Md. Rahat Uddin said that 600,000 people are working in BSCIC's 83 industrial parks. He said, 'We have our own design center. There we provide training on designs. Apart from that, we organize various city fairs.' 

Shahedul Islam Helal, advisor to Bangladesh Jute Exporters Association (BJGEA), said that one has to go to five offices to work with jute. He said that it takes time to get so many permissions. He also proposed organizing an online product fair. 

Other speakers at the seminar included Nusrat Hafiz, Assistant Professor at BRAC Business School, and Afsana Chowdhury, Head of CED at BRAC University.

Headline_English: UTL proposes 10 proposals, including use of OMR machines in vote counting in JOCSU elections
Content_Enlish:
Teachers' organization 'University Teachers Link' (UTL) held a press conference at the teachers' lounge regarding the Jagannath University Central Student Union (JUCSU) and Hall Parliament elections. Photo: Prothom Alo 
The teachers' organization 'University Teachers Link' (UTL) has made 10-point proposals, including the use of Optical Mark Reader (OMR) machines in vote counting, to organize the Jagannath University Central Student Union (JUCSU) and Hall Parliament elections in a fair, impartial and orderly manner. 

At a press conference held at the university's teachers' lounge on Wednesday, the convener of the organization's Jagannath University branch, Md. Abu Layek, presented these proposals and their rationale. 

At the press conference, Md. Abu Layek said that the Jagannath University Central Student Union (JUCSU) and Hall Parliament elections to be held on December 30 are an important chapter in the history of higher education and democratic practice in Bangladesh. There has been great interest among students, media, political parties and the general public around this election.

Md. Abu Layek further said that a fair, impartial and acceptable election will not only ensure the democratic rights of the students, but will also strengthen the image, dignity and trust of the university. 

Md. Abu Layek said that UTL believes that if a fair, technology-based and safe environment is ensured, this election can be established as an ideal model for the future. 

He also expressed hope that it is possible for the current university administration to implement it. 

UTL's 10-point proposals are to take effective measures to prevent fake voters and fake votes, ensure transparency and reliability in the use of OMR machines, publish center-based results quickly, strictly follow and implement the electoral code of conduct, ensure the safety of female students, strengthen overall security on campus, introduce technology-based surveillance systems, ensure equal opportunities and public trust in the election campaign, establish a central control and support center during the election, and maintain order and a peaceful environment after the results are published. 

At the press conference, UTL leaders expressed hope that if the university administration seriously considers these proposals, the JOCSU elections will take the form of an acceptable and exemplary election. 

Among others, Jagannath University branch member secretary Muhammad Asaduzzaman Sadi, central member secretary Professor Mohammad Bilal Hossain and other leaders of the university branch were present at the time.

Headline_English: Hand grenade thrown from flyover in Moghbazar, youth killed
Content_Enlish:
A young man named Siam was killed in a hand bomb explosion in front of the Bangladesh Muktijoddha Sangsad Central Command in the capital's Moghbazar intersection. 

The incident took place under the Moghbazar flyover on Wednesday evening. 

Eyewitnesses said that a bomb was thrown downward from the flyover in the evening. When the bomb exploded, Siam was seriously injured on the spot. He was later seen lying in a bloody state. He died a short time later. 

Relatives of the deceased said that he was an employee of a decoration company. He was staying in the area at the time of the incident. Initially, his identity could not be confirmed, but his relatives later identified him. 

Upon receiving the information, the police quickly reached the spot and surrounded the area. Panic spread in the area immediately after the incident. However, the miscreants quickly fled after throwing the bomb. 

Masud Alam, Deputy Police Commissioner of Ramna Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), said that initially it is believed that the bomb was thrown downward from the flyover. The reason for the bomb blast has not yet been confirmed. The matter is being investigated. 

He also said that work is underway to collect and analyze CCTV footage from the surrounding area to identify those involved in the incident. Detailed information will be provided after the investigation is completed.

A live video broadcast by the BNP media cell shows Tarique Rahman standing in an open area after exiting the airport gate. There, he leaned over and touched the ground.

Tarique Rahman was arrested during the military-backed caretaker government that took power in January 2007 and spent 18 months in prison before being released on September 3, 2008. He left Dhaka for London with his family on September 11, 2008.

The main objective of the conference was to exchange views on recent research and progress in microbiology and related disciplines, strengthen scientific cooperation and provide effective guidance to address contemporary challenges. More than 400 representatives from various domestic and foreign institutions participated in the conference. 

The theme of this year’s conference, “Microbiomes for Sustainable Future”, was timely and helpful in highlighting the importance of microbiology in human development and welfare. The host institution was addressed by Prof. Dr. Shakila Nargis Khan, Chairman, Department of Microbiology, University of Dhaka. 

In his welcome address, Dr. Munirul Alam, President of Bangladesh Society of Microbiologists, highlighted the importance of innovation in microbiology research to address global health and environmental challenges. He also mentioned the long-standing role of BSM in promoting microbiology education and research in Bangladesh. A presentation was also given on the recent activities of BSM. The Secretary of the Conference Organizing Committee and General Secretary of BSM, Prof. Dr. Muhammad Manjurul Karim, delivered a speech. The Bangladesh Society of Microbiologists cordially welcomes the country’s academicians, researchers, professionals and media personnel to participate in this important international scientific conference, which reflects Bangladesh’s growing contribution to global microbiology research.

Headline_English: Myanmar junta using 'atrocities' to force people to vote: UN
Content_Enlish:
The United Nations said Tuesday that Myanmar's junta is using violence and intimidation to force people to vote in upcoming military-controlled elections. Armed groups are also using similar tactics to prevent people from voting, AFP news agency reported from Geneva. 

The UN human rights chief said in a statement that Myanmar's military authorities must stop brutal violence against people in their efforts to force them to vote, as well as arresting people for expressing dissent. Myanmar's junta is set to hold the vote on Sunday. It is promoting the tightly controlled elections as a return to democracy. The vote comes five years after the country's elected government was overthrown and a civil war broke out. 

Former civilian leader and Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi remains in prison and her popular party has been dissolved. International observers have gradually dismissed the month-long vote as a new form of military rule. Falkirk told AFP last month that holding elections in Myanmar under the current circumstances was "unthinkable". He warned on Tuesday that ordinary people were facing threats from both the military authorities and armed opposition groups for participating in the elections. 

The statement noted that many people had been detained for exercising their freedom of expression under the “Election Protection Act”. Many had been given “very harsh sentences”, the statement said. Three young men from Hlainghaya Township in Yangon Region were sentenced to 42 to 49 years in prison for putting up anti-election posters. The UN human rights office said it had received reports from displaced people in various parts of the country, including Mandalay Region, who had been warned that they would be attacked or their homes seized if they did not go to vote. 

Falkar Turk stressed that forcing displaced people to vote in unsafe conditions and against their will was a human rights violation. He added that people were also facing “serious threats” from armed groups opposed to the military government. Among them were nine female teachers who were abducted from Kyaw Kyaw last month. They were on their way to attend a ballot training session. The statement said they were later released with a warning from their perpetrators. 

Falkar Turk said the election was being held in an environment of violence and repression, where there was no environment for people to exercise their right to freedom of expression, association or peaceful assembly.

Headline_English: Court orders investigation into allegations of releasing policeman detained with Yaba
Content_Enlish:
The court has ordered an investigation into the allegation that a policeman from Cox's Bazar was released after being detained with Yaba in Chittagong city. The accused policeman is named Imtiaz Hossain. He is working as a gunman for a judge of the Cox's Bazar District Court. Chittagong Metropolitan Magistrate SM Alauddin Mahmud issued the order on his own initiative on Tuesday. 

Chittagong Metropolitan Magistrate Court Nazir Abul Kalam Azad told Prothom Alo that the judge filed the case on his own initiative after taking into consideration a report published in the media. The Deputy Commissioner of the City Police (South) has been instructed to investigate the incident. The court ordered the report to be submitted by January 12 next year. 

According to court sources, the judge mentioned in the order that on December 8, at around 2:15 am, some police members searched a Dhaka-bound bus in the Shah Amanat Setu (New Bridge) area of ​​the city's Baklia police station, and they have to collect the GD and CC copy of their duty registrar. The CC footage of the incident, whether the police identified Imtiaz Ahmed was detained or searched in the bus, whether the incident of recovering 120,000 Yaba pills from him is true, the names and addresses of the bus driver, supervisor and other relevant persons in the bus that was searched, the role of the police members on duty at the scene, the reason for not filing a case and releasing the accused and the report has been asked to be investigated. 

On the night of December 8, an allegation was made that during a search of a passenger bus coming from Cox's Bazar at the check post in the Notun Bridge area of ​​Baklia police station, at the entrance to the city, police member Imtiaz Hossain was released along with 120,000 Yaba pills. Imtiaz Hossain's mobile phone was called several times to get his statement on the matter, but he did not pick up. In addition, he did not respond even though he was sent a text message. 

It is alleged that after knowing his identity, Baklia Police Station OC Aftab Uddin and Inspector (Investigation) Tanvir Ahmed released Imtiaz Hossain without confiscating the yaba pills through bargaining. Baklia Police Station Sub-Inspector (SI) Al Amin, on-duty ASI Saddam and other police members were present at the scene at that time. The estimated market value of the recovered yaba pills is around 3.5 crore taka, according to the concerned people. 

Baklia Police Station OC Aftab Uddin and Inspector (Investigation) Tanvir Ahmed were called on the mobile phones to get their statement on the matter, but they did not pick up the call even though it rang. 

Cox's Bazar Police Lines RI Inspector Ashraf Ali told Prothom Alo that Imtiaz Hossain joined Cox's Bazar Police Lines on July 13, 2022. Since joining, he has been serving as a gunman for various important people. 

Assistant Commissioner (Media) of the city police Aminur Rashid told Prothom Alo that the matter will be investigated. 

It is worth noting that from November 19 to 27, RAB headquarters transferred more than four hundred officers and employees of RAB-15 Cox's Bazar region. In addition, Cox's Bazar battalion commander Lieutenant Colonel Kamrul Islam has been transferred to RAB headquarters in Dhaka. RAB sources said that they were transferred on charges of being involved in various criminal activities including Yaba.

Headline_English: Myanmar has been under military rule for seven decades.
Content_Enlish:
Myanmar has been ruled by the military for most of its independence. Military rulers have always presented themselves as the only saviors to save this country, divided by various ideologies and groups in Southeast Asia, from collapse. Although Myanmar started its journey towards democracy again a decade ago, it did not last long. 

Myanmar has been embroiled in a civil war for five years under the rule of a military junta. In the meantime, the government has organized national elections in the country from December 28. There is much debate in the country and abroad about how transparent these elections will be or how much they will reflect the opinion of the people. Many see it as a tool to strengthen the power of the junta. 

To learn about the beginning of military rule in Myanmar, we have to go back quite a bit. Myanmar was then known as Burma. Myanmar gained independence from British colonial rule in 1948 after World War II. Aung San led Myanmar's independence struggle. He is the father of the country's imprisoned leader, Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi. 

During World War II, Aung San joined hands with Japan to overthrow the British. However, when the tide of war turned and he went to the Allies, he changed sides again. He developed good relations with London for independence. After independence, Myanmar had a lot of potential. However, the civilian government faced internal divisions and fighting with rebels. 

Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi 
Myanmar leader Aung San Suu KyiFile photo: Reuters 
In such a situation, in 1958, the military was given the responsibility of a caretaker government for two years. Then elections were held. However, in 1962, the military seized power by force. Aung San's one-time comrade-in-arms Ne Win took this step, saying that he would protect the country. After Aung San's assassination, he took command of the armed forces under mysterious circumstances. 

Ne Win said that he would hand over power to elected representatives of the people in due time; but he did not keep his word. He ruled Myanmar for 26 years. He established a nominally socialist one-party state system. This isolated Myanmar from the world. As a result, what was expected happened. The economy collapsed. The junta took the path of suppressing dissent to maintain power. 

Junta leader Min Aung Hlaing 
Junta leader Min Aung Hlaing File Photo: Reuters 
In the wake of this, Ne Win resigned in 1988 in the face of a student-led pro-democracy movement. Then the new leadership of the military staged a coup again. The protesters were suppressed with harsh hands. More than 3,000 people were killed. Many were imprisoned. Then in 1992, General Than Shwe took over the military government. 

Than Shwe retired in 2011. He handed over power to a civilian government. President Thein Sein became the new leader of Myanmar. He released Suu Kyi from prison. Suu Kyi's party won a huge victory in the 2015 election. She won again in 2020. However, the military seized power in 2021, alleging that the election was rigged. 

General Min Aung Hlaing became the head of the junta government. Suu Kyi was imprisoned again. The country was divided. An armed rebellion against the junta began. These rebels do not want the December 28 election to take place. Because they see nothing else than the military rule being strengthened through it. In such a situation, voting is going to begin. Once it is completed, the results could be announced by the end of 2026.

Headline_English: 1.6 million people in Gaza face acute food insecurity
Content_Enlish:
Israel continues to attack and block humanitarian aid amid the ceasefire. Millions of Gazans are still not getting enough food. The planned killing that Israel chose by creating an artificial food crisis is ongoing. In this situation, the World Health Organization has warned about mothers and children in Gaza. More than 100,000 children and 37,000 pregnant women will suffer from acute malnutrition by April. Reuters reported that the warning was given after the publication of the United Nations Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, head of the World Food Program, said that at least 1.6 million people in Gaza will face acute food insecurity by mid-April 2026. 

He warned that progress in combating famine is very fragile. Because the Israeli attack has destroyed extensive infrastructure. Livelihoods and local food production have collapsed. Residents continue to struggle with hunger due to restrictions on humanitarian activities. The WHO chief said in his ex-post, “Only 50 percent of Gaza’s health facilities are currently partially functional.” 

On the other hand, the Gaza Health Ministry said that due to the shortage of emergency and intensive care services, 200,000 patients are being deprived of emergency services, 100,000 patients are being deprived of surgical services and 700 patients are being deprived of intensive care. 

A young mother recounts the horrors of war 
Hadil al-Gherbawi was seven months pregnant when the war broke out in October 2023. The 26-year-old was preparing to give birth. The pregnancy was high-risk. She lived near the Israeli border in eastern Gaza City. Being pregnant made it difficult for her to move quickly. “My family has been displaced 13 times since then and my husband’s house has been destroyed. I was in a residential building in Gaza City at the end of October. Israel bombed nearby. It was like a strong earthquake. I have not forgotten the horror of that night. Later I fled to Al-Shifa Hospital. There I became sick from the smell of corpses. It is unforgettable.’ 

Approval of 19 new settlements in the West Bank 
Israel’s security cabinet has approved the recognition of 19 new settlements in the occupied West Bank. The proposal was made by far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said that Israel’s settlement expansion is increasing tensions. It is threatening the stability of a sovereign Palestinian state. On the other hand, US Senator and close ally of Trump, Lindsey Graham, has warned that military action should be taken against Hamas and Hezbollah if they do not lay down their arms. 

42 Israeli incursions into Syria in 21 days 
There have been 42 Israeli incursions into Syria in 21 days since the beginning of December. These incursions have included arrests. The Anadolu Agency said the repeated incursions into Syria are part of an Israeli strategy aimed at capturing additional territory. The Syrian state news agency SANA reported that an Israeli patrol consisting of two military vehicles entered the northern Quneitra province from Adnaniyah Point on Sunday.

Headline_English: Human chain demanding cancellation of BNP candidate's nomination
Content_Enlish:
Five leaders of the party who were denied nomination and their followers held a human chain and protest program at various points along a 20-kilometer road demanding the cancellation of the nomination of the BNP candidate nominated in Kishoreganj-1 (Sadar-Hosseinpur) constituency. Photo: Prothom Alo 
Five candidates who were denied nomination and their followers held a human chain and protest program at various points along a 20-kilometer road demanding the cancellation of the nomination of the BNP candidate nominated in Kishoreganj-1 (Sadar-Hosseinpur) constituency. 

The program was held simultaneously at various points on the Kishoreganj-Bhairab regional highway from Sadullarchar Bazar to Chauddashat Bazar from Tuesday afternoon to evening. Traffic movement on the Bhairab-Mymensingh regional highway was temporarily disrupted during this program. 

The five candidates who were denied nominations and participated in the program are former MP and former general secretary of the district BNP Masud Hilali, former vice president of the district BNP Rezaul Karim Khan (Chunnu), former vice president of the district BNP Ruhul Hossain, former vice president of the district BNP and former chairman of the Sadar Upazila Parishad Shariful Islam, and president of the Sadar Upazila BNP Khaled Saifullah (Sohel). 

The leaders demanded the immediate cancellation of the nominations, alleging various irregularities and corruption against the nominated candidates. They also warned of stricter programs if their demands were not met. The protesters announced that they would hold a sit-in program on the railway tracks tomorrow. 

BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir announced the names of candidates for 36 more parliamentary constituencies across the country in the second phase of the press conference held at the Chairperson's office in Gulshan on December 4. The name of District BNP General Secretary Mohammad Mazharul Islam was announced there for the Kishoreganj-1 constituency. 

Since Mazharul Islam received the party nomination, the candidates who were denied nomination have been holding press conferences, protest marches, sweeping processions, torchlight processions and protest rallies demanding the cancellation of their nominations. 

In this regard, BNP candidate Mohammad Mazharul Islam said, "I went to the houses of other aspiring leaders after receiving the nomination and sought their cooperation. The party's policymakers nominated me after vetting many of the aspiring candidates. BNP leaders and workers from the two upazilas of the constituency are also with me. Thousands of workers are working day and night in the fields on my behalf under the symbol of a sheaf of rice. At this time, some people are creating chaos by creating suffering for the people. If they can't create suffering on the roads like this, let them go to the center and change their nominations. I will accept it. However, I urge them not to malign the party by creating such unrest."

Headline_English: Reducing the price of fish feed will reduce the price of fish
Content_Enlish:
Guests present at the biennial fisheries conference organized by the Bangladesh Fisheries Research Forum at the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC) auditorium in Farmgate on Tuesday. Photo: Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock.
About 60 percent of fish production in the country comes from farming. But even though production has increased, the price of fish has not decreased accordingly. According to researchers and experts, the price of fish food has not decreased because the price is high. At the same time, if safe methods are not adopted to increase production, new challenges will arise in the future. Therefore, emphasis should be placed on reducing the price of feed or fish food and on safe fish farming.

This opinion was expressed at the 10th biennial fisheries conference organized by the Bangladesh Fisheries Research Forum (BFRF) at the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC) auditorium in the capital on Tuesday. Fisheries and Livestock Advisor Farida Akhtar was present as the chief guest at the conference.

The inaugural session of the conference, organized under the theme ‘Next Generation Fisheries and Aquaculture: Safe Food, Equity and Environment’, was presided over by BFRF President and Professor of Bangladesh Agricultural University Joarder Faruk Ahmed. BFRF General Secretary and Professor of Fisheries Science, Dhaka University Md. Monirul Islam delivered the welcome address.

World Fish Bangladesh Country Representative Faruk-ul Islam presented the keynote address at the conference. In this, he said that a third-party certification system can be introduced to ensure the quality of fish production. This has the potential to increase fish exports to three to five billion dollars. He said that there is import dependence in feed or fish food production, so tariffs can be reduced. Along with this, the use of technology needs to be increased in fish farming like agriculture. He also highlighted the possibility of using drones to supply fish food in the future.

In her speech as the chief guest, Fisheries and Livestock Advisor Farida Akhtar said that although the expansion of agricultural production has increased the supply of fish in the country, it has also created new challenges, including food security. She said that there is no point in increasing fish production if food safety is not ensured. If fish produced in aquaculture is not safe, then it cannot be called fish in the true sense. She also emphasized on giving a global dimension to the movement to protect Hilsa like dolphins.

Highlighting the nutritional value of fish, Farida Akhtar said that fish is not just food to fill the stomach; it is an important source of essential micronutrients and calcium. Fish plays a helpful role in the development of eyes, bones and intellect. Fish-based diet also plays a major role in the intellectual development of Bengalis.

* About 60 percent of fish production in the country comes from farming. * The high price of fish food is one of the reasons why prices have not come down.

Advisor Farida Akhtar also spoke about marine fisheries. He believes that Bangladesh has not yet been able to utilize the full potential of the sea. Currently, only 30 percent of the resources are being utilized. Wooden boats and trawlers are fishing in different ways and some of the technologies used in trawlers are causing concern. He also commented that ‘the trend of using gold technology to catch all the fish at once is not right’.

Speaking as a special guest, ACI Group Advisor FH Ansari said that even though fish production in the country has increased, not everyone is benefiting equally. The results of many researches are not being used at the field level. Some farmers said that only one kilogram of pangasius is being obtained with two kilograms of feed. He also said that sufficient processed food is not being produced from fish yet.

Anuradha Bhadra, Director General of Bangladesh Fisheries Research Institute, said that 41 of the 64 endangered fish varieties in the country have been restored. Although there has been progress in feed production, the price is still high. In addition, research on food safety needs to be increased.

Md., Director General of the Department of Fisheries Abdur Rouf said, maintaining fish farming is also a big challenge now. We have to move towards modernization and technology-based farming systems. The increase in sea temperature and salinity due to climate change is also creating new problems.

FAO Representative in Bangladesh Dia Sano, BFRF Vice President Md. Khaled Kanak and others also spoke at the conference.

In addition, researchers, teachers and businessmen and students of fisheries departments of 20 universities participated in the conference.

Headline_English: One lakh tons of rice being imported from India and Pakistan
Content_Enlish:
A total of one lakh tonnes of rice is being imported from India and Pakistan. Of this, 50,000 tonnes of parboiled rice will be brought from India through an international open tender. And 50,000 tonnes of parboiled rice will be brought directly from Pakistan without a government-to-government (G2G) tender. 

These two proposals were approved at the meeting of the Advisory Council Committee on Government Procurement held at the Secretariat on Tuesday under the chairmanship of Financial Advisor Salehuddin Ahmed. The Financial Advisor informed reporters after the meeting. 

Financial Advisor Salehuddin Ahmed said, 'We have to look at our trade and politics with India separately. The relationship with India is not as bad as it is heard from outside. We definitely want to have good relations with India. We are trying to avoid any bitter relations with a big neighbor like India.' 

At the end of the meeting, it was also informed that the Indian company Pattavi Agro Foods Private Limited has been given the job of supplying parboiled rice. The price is 355.77 US dollars per ton, which is about 217 million 54 lakh taka in Bangladesh. And the supplier of Pakistani rice is Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP). The price of this rice per ton will be 395 US dollars, which is about 241 million 52 lakh taka in Bangladeshi currency. 

In addition to the proposal to purchase rice, five other separate proposals for food products were approved in today's meeting. Soybean oil, lentils and rice bran oil will be purchased for sale through the Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB). 

A total of 37.5 million liters of soybean oil are being imported through direct purchase; that is, without a tender. Of this, 20 million liters of soybean oil of Brazilian origin will be supplied by Nigerian company Viadoc Farms and Exports Limited. The price per liter is 121.32 taka. The total cost of this will be 242 million 64 lakh taka. 

The US company Steward Clobanu Gerhardt has been awarded the contract to supply 12.5 million liters of soybean oil. The cost of importing this soybean oil from Tanzania at a price of 132.69 taka per liter will be 166 million taka. And the Malaysian company C Millennium Trade will supply 5 million liters of soybean oil at a price of 132.08 taka per liter. This will cost 660 million taka. 

Meanwhile, three companies have been awarded the contract to supply a total of 10 million liters of rice bran or kundar oil at a price of 167 million taka through a local open tender. Of these, Gaibandha's Prodhan Well Mills will supply 2.5 million liters, Dhaka's Green Well and Poultry Feed Industries will supply 2.5 million liters, and Majumdar Products will supply 5 million liters of rice bran oil. The price of oil per liter is 167.90 taka. 

Apart from this, Khulna-based Joytun Auto Rice and Dal Mills has been awarded the contract to supply 10,000 tonnes of lentils through a local open tender process. The price of lentils per kg is 72.20 taka.

Headline_English: The price of one gram of gold increased by 9,000 taka in three days
Content_Enlish:
As the price of gold increases in the global market, it is also increasing in the country. For the third consecutive day, it has increased again today, Tuesday. This time, the price of gold has been increased by 4,000 taka per bhori, which will be effective from tomorrow, Wednesday. With this, the price of gold has increased by about 9,000 taka per bhori in three days. Yesterday, Monday and today, Tuesday, they increased by 1,000 taka and 4,000 taka respectively. 

With the price increase for three consecutive days, the price of a good quality, i.e. 22-carat bhori will reach 2 lakh 26 thousand taka. This price is the highest price of gold in the country's history. New records were set in the price of gold on both Monday and Tuesday. 

The Bangladesh Jewelers' Association (BAJUS) has announced a maximum increase in the price of gold by 4,199 taka per bhori on Tuesday night. The new price will be effective across the country tomorrow, Wednesday. The matter was announced in a press release signed by Dewan Aminul Islam Shaheen, Chairman of the Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring of the Jewelers' Association. 

According to the Jewelers' Association, from tomorrow, Wednesday, the price of a 22-carat bhori will increase by 2 lakh 26 thousand 282 taka, which was 2 lakh 22 thousand 83 taka until today. That means the price will increase by 4 thousand 199 taka from tomorrow. 

In addition, the price of 21-carat gold will increase by 2 lakh 16 thousand 17 taka, which is sold today for 2 lakh 11 thousand 993 taka. From tomorrow, the price of 21-carat will increase by 4 thousand 24 taka. On the other hand, the price of 18-carat gold will stand at 1 lakh 85 thousand 166 taka tomorrow. Today, the price was 1 lakh 81 thousand 725 taka. That is, the price will increase by 3 thousand 441 taka per bhor tomorrow. 

Until today, the price of gold in the traditional system was 1 lakh 51 thousand 399 taka per bhor. From tomorrow, the price of gold in the traditional system will increase by 2 thousand 916 taka per bhor. 

Along with gold, the price of silver will also increase. From tomorrow, the price of silver will increase by 175 taka per bhor. Till today, the price of a 22-carat bhori of silver was 4,957 taka. From tomorrow, the price will increase to 5,132 taka.

Headline_English: Jamaat candidate alleges widespread extortion in Dhaka-10 constituency
Content_Enlish:
Jamaat-e-Islami's nominated MP candidate for Dhaka-10 constituency Md. Jasim Uddin during the election campaign. This Tuesday morning in the Kathalbagan areaPhoto: Prothom Alo 
Jamaat-e-Islami's nominated MP candidate Md. Jasim Uddin has alleged that extortion is rampant in Dhaka-10 constituency. He said that no one in the area, from small and big businessmen to landlords, is safe from extortion. 

Jasim Uddin said this while campaigning in the Kathalbagan area of ​​Dhaka-10 constituency today Tuesday. 

This Jamaat candidate said that when someone goes to build a house, they fall into the clutches of extortionists. They are told that they have to take specific rods, bricks or cement from him. Later, they take the money and disappear. The same situation is also true when they go to run a shop. Extortion has now become a chronic problem. 

Md. Jasim Uddin promised to take strict action against extortion, encroachment, terrorism and drugs if elected as a member of parliament. He said that people want to live peacefully, want security and assurance of life. Then they want solutions to other problems. 

Highlighting various problems of Dhaka-10 constituency, Jasim Uddin said that this area gets submerged under water with a little rain. There are also cases of people dying due to electrocution. There is a severe gas shortage. In addition, incidents of robbery and theft are also happening regularly. 

Jasim Uddin also said that if elected, he will take initiatives to rescue Dhanmondi Lake from mismanagement and modernize it. He said that there are thousands of problems here. Good will, initiative and sincere leadership are needed for development. If they have them, the problems can be solved. 

During the election campaign, leaders and activists of Jamaat-e-Islami and Islami Chhatra Shibir were present with Jasim Uddin. They talked to the voters and asked for votes with the symbol of scales.

Headline_English: 3 relatives of patient jailed for beating doctors at Dhaka Medical College
Content_Enlish:
Three people have been sentenced to two months in prison each for attacking doctors at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH). The Special Metropolitan Magistrate Court issued the order on Thursday afternoon. The three were arrested in connection with the attack on doctors on Wednesday night over the death of a patient undergoing treatment. 

The convicted persons are Shakib Hossain, friend of the son of the deceased patient Lucky Begum, stepson Imtiaz Ahmed and relative Shahria Nazim. 

Lucky Begum died while undergoing treatment at ward number 702 of the Medicine Department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital around 10 pm on Wednesday. 

Relatives allege that Lucky died due to negligence of the doctors. They got into a fight with the doctors over this. Doctors allege that the patient's relatives beat them up. Demanding security over the incident, the doctors closed the main gate of the emergency department and suspended services from 1 am to 4:30 am yesterday. Three people, including Lucky's stepson Imtiaz, were arrested in the incident, and doctors returned to medical services at 4:30 am. 

In a press release today, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) said that Lucky Begum's son Rakib claimed that his mother died due to wrong treatment. In light of the incident, Rakib called his friend Shakib and brought him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Shakib called and called some of his other friends to the hospital. Shakib and 20-30 other unidentified people came to the hospital and misbehaved with the doctors and nurses. At one stage, they beat up two intern doctors there. 

The DMP also said that at that time, the hospital authorities brought the situation under control and arrested the three people and handed them over to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital police camp.

Headline_English: No information on whether Hadi's killer was in the country or abroad: Home Affairs Advisor
Content_Enlish:
Home Affairs Advisor Lt. Gen. (retd.) Jahangir Alam Chowdhury has said that if the information about the whereabouts of Osman Hadi's killer was known, he would have been arrested by now. He said that no confirmed information has been received yet on whether the accused is in the country or has fled abroad. 

gnews Follow Google News to get the latest news from Dainik Ittefaq 
Talking to reporters at the Secretariat on Monday (December 22), the Home Affairs Advisor said that significant progress has been made in the investigation into Hadi's murder and law enforcement agencies are making every effort to arrest the main mastermind, Faisal. 

He said that Faisal's parents, wife, brother-in-law and motorcyclist have been arrested. In addition, a gang of brokers involved in the incident has been arrested from the border area. He also said that 6,998 people have been arrested so far in the 'Devil Hunt Phase Two' operation. 

The Home Affairs Advisor also said that more intensive operations have been conducted against terrorists and miscreants under Devil Hunt Phase Two and more arrests have been ordered. 

At that time, he said that gunmen have been provided for the security of the editors of Prothom Alo and Daily Star and the security of their homes has also been strengthened. Many of those who are at risk of security have been provided with protection. He also said that about 20 people have been provided with gunmen at present. 

Stating that Tarique Rahman will also be provided with adequate security when he returns to the country, the Home Affairs Advisor said that the government is ready in this regard.

Headline_English: BNP gets permission to host Tarique Rahman's reception
Content_Enlish:
The party has received permission from the Dhaka Divisional Commissioner to organize a reception ceremony on the occasion of the return of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman to the country on December 25. 

BNP Media Cell member Shairul Kabir Khan confirmed the matter on Sunday (December 21) night.

Headline_English: BNP nominee Jalal Uddin, his wife and children banned from leaving the country
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court 
Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court File Photo 
The court has banned BNP's nominated MP (MP) candidate from Chandpur-2 constituency Jalal Uddin, his wife and three children from traveling abroad as the investigation into allegations of illegal wealth acquisition and money laundering is ongoing. 

Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge Court Vacation Judge Md. Abdullah Al Mamun issued the order on Monday following an application by the ACC. 

The others under the ban are Jalal Uddin's wife Shahnaz Sharmin, their sons Syed Mohammad Rizvi and Syed Mohammad Alvi, and daughter Ayesha Tasmia Tanvi. 

Assistant Director SM Mamunur Rashid applied for the ban on traveling abroad on behalf of the ACC. The matter was confirmed by ACC Assistant Director (Public Relations) Tanjir Ahmed. 

The ACC application states that there are allegations of illegal money earning against Jalal Uddin. He has tried to legitimize this money by bringing it into bank accounts in his own name and the names of his stakeholders. In addition, there are allegations of money laundering by smuggling money abroad. These allegations are currently under investigation. In this situation, it is known from reliable sources that Jalal Uddin and his family can flee the country at any time. Therefore, it is absolutely necessary to stop them from traveling abroad for the sake of a fair investigation into the allegations.

Gold prices fall again, 7,500 per baht 
Gold prices have fallen again in the country's market. After a major decline, the gold market recently recovered somewhat. However, that recovery did not last long. This time, the precious metal has seen a major decline in the space of two days. 

On Friday (February 6), the Bangladesh Jewelers Association (BAJUS) reduced the price of good quality, i.e. 22-carat gold, by 7,640 taka per baht. 

The organization issued a notification adjusting the price of gold again at around 10 am today. After the new adjustment, the price of 22-carat gold in the country's market is now 2,54,450 taka per baht. 

The notification said that the price of pure gold has decreased in the local market. As a result, the new price of gold has been determined considering the overall situation. 

According to the new price list, the price of 22-carat gold per bhori (11.664 grams) in the domestic market is now 254,450 taka. In addition, the price of 21-carat gold per bhori is 242,903 taka, and the price of 18-carat gold per bhori is 288,202 taka. In addition, the price of gold per bhori according to the traditional method will be 170,411 taka. 

Earlier, on the afternoon of February 3, BAJUS last adjusted the price of gold in the domestic market. At that time, the organization had increased the price of a bhori by 10,906 taka and set the price of a bhori of 22-carat gold at 262,090 taka. 

Along with the reduction in the price of gold, the price of silver has also been reduced in the domestic market. The price of a bhori of 22-carat silver has been set at 6,357 taka, down by 175 taka. Besides, the price of 21 carat gold has been fixed at 6,065 taka per bhori, 18 carat gold at 5,190 taka per bhori and traditional silver at 3,907 taka per bhori. 

It is worth noting that the price of gold has been adjusted 25 times in the domestic market this year. Where the price has been increased 16 times; reduced 9 times.

Headline_English: Some candidates are being left out of BNP's initial list
Content_Enlish:
The country's largest political party, BNP, is busy in full swing around the upcoming 13th National Parliament election on February 12. Some are dropping out of the previously announced primary 272 seats to finalize the candidates for 300 seats. In addition, BNP has almost finalized the seats of the movement's partners during the Awami League regime. The official final list of candidates will be announced soon. 

In this regard, BNP National Standing Committee member Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku said that the list of potential candidates has been prepared based on multiple field surveys and organizational opinions. However, there is no scope to consider it final. Changes may occur if necessary and internal conflicts will not be tolerated under any circumstances. Preparations will be made to go to the election in a united manner. Those concerned say that BNP concluded the exchange of views and workshops with party candidates for the primary 272 seats last Saturday. Several new candidates have been called for the purpose of changing the candidates. Of these, the candidacies for four seats in Bagerhat district are almost final. The candidates initially nominated for these seats also participated in the workshop. Two important leaders of the Hindu community are being nominated as candidates for the paddy sheesh in two constituencies of Bagerhat. They are Kapil Krishna Mandal, Secretary General of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad and General Secretary of the Matua Samaj Oikya Jote in the Bagerhat-1 constituency, and Somnath Dey, President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad Bangladesh Branch in the Bagerhat-4 constituency. Apart from this, a formal announcement will be made about the seats of the partners by holding a press conference in two-three days. From the seats where there is an agreement, the BNP party candidate will be withdrawn and the partners will elect under their own symbols. On the other hand, district BNP leader and Supreme Court lawyer Sheikh Mohammad Zakir Hossain is being nominated for the Bagerhat-2 (Sadar and Kachua) constituency. Apart from this, it is known that Aslam Chowdhury is being nominated instead of Kazi Salauddin in the Chittagong-4 constituency. 

It is known that the seats of five top leaders of the three alliances that are partners in the simultaneous movement have been confirmed. They are Mahmudur Rahman Manna (Bogra-2) of Nagorik Oikya, Jonayed Saki (Brahmanbaria-6) of Gana Sanghati Andolon, and Saiful Haque (Dhaka-12) of Biplobi Workers Party. A formal announcement regarding the seats of the partners will be made through a press conference in the next two-three days. BNP party candidates will be withdrawn from the seats where there is an agreement and the partners will elect on their own symbols. Although Bhashani has not given any seats to Janashakti Party and Gano Forum for the time being, they have been assured of evaluation if they come to power. 

The candidacies of those who have been called to the BNP's three-day workshop ahead of the 13th National Parliament elections are considered almost certain. On the contrary, there are indications of a change of candidate in those seats that were not invited. Party sources have said that a surprising reshuffle has been seen in some seats. 

It is believed that the candidates for the seats announced in the workshop who were not called may be changed. Among them are Israt Sultana Elen Bhutto from Jhalakati-2. In addition, Aslam Chowdhury has been called instead of Kazi Salahuddin, the declared candidate for Chittagong-4. Chittagong-6 candidate Gias Uddin Quader Chowdhury and Jessore-6 candidate Kazi Rawnkul Islam, including some others, were not invited. 

In addition, out of the 28 vacant seats, Shahadat Hossain Selim has been called for Lakshmipur-1 and Ashraf Uddin Nizan for Lakshmipur-4. They will also contest the election on paddy straw. The remaining seats have been reserved for some parties and the remaining for allies. Which may be announced in a few days. This information has been learned from relevant sources. 

Sources in the party's national standing committee said that the final decision lies with acting chairman Tarique Rahman. The list may be finalized on Sunday night after consultation with the standing committee. The list will be officially announced today or tomorrow.
