Headline_English: FDC is now a haunted house
Content_Enlish:
The sounds of lights-cameras-action cannot be heard for a long time inside the four walls of FDC. There is no loud presence of stars on the shooting and dubbing floors. There is no flashing of shooting lights. Even greater discomfort is that the construction work of the BFDC complex, which began in 2022, has not been completed even after the scheduled time has passed. There is no possibility of this complex seeing the light of day. For these reasons, the officials and employees of FDC themselves and the filmmakers themselves do not hesitate to call FDC a haunted house now. 

Bangladesh Film Development Corporation (BFDC), known as the den of Dhaka cinema. Although FDC has been working for the development of cinema since its inception in 1957, it has become a business organization at some point. Where associations, organizations, meetings, politics, movements, and gatherings are more practiced than the development of cinema. Those involved in the cinema also complain that no matter who comes to the helm of this institution, none of them can play a proper role in the development of cinema. And that is why the heart of cinema, FDC, has gradually gone into a coma. The autocratic Sheikh Hasina has proven that FDC is just a commercial center. During the Awami regime, the work of a 12-story building called 'BFDC Complex' was passed in the ECNEC meeting in 2018. One of the objectives of which was to make a shining light on money laundering in the name of setting up the project. Despite the objections of senior filmmakers, in 2022, the work of constructing a multi-story complex on 94 katha land was started by demolishing the shooting floors and editing buildings of FDC No. 3, 4, 5. The cost of which is estimated at Tk 323 crore. The project was supposed to be completed in June 2024. However, far from being completed, it is seen that only 40 percent of the work has been completed even after the scheduled time. A project official who does not want to be named says that the work could not be completed on time for various reasons. 

We have taken our time, now we hope that the project will be completed in June 2026. It is learned that although the project period was set for December 2021, the construction work began in 2022. Through the latest amendment, the project period has been fixed for June 2026, and the cost has increased to Tk 365 crore. The implementation monitoring and evaluation department of the Ministry of Planning highlighted in its intensive monitoring report in June 2024 that the progress of this project is not at all satisfactory. FDC, which started its journey to develop and expand the film industry seven decades ago, came to a standstill in 2000 due to various mismanagement and not being able to keep up with the times. The government is looking for ways to keep FDC, which has been in debt of about half a billion taka in a decade, operational through alternative means without giving new grants. FDC has taken about Tk 80 crore in grants and loans from the government between 2016 and 2025. The organization's losses and expenses are increasing year by year; there is no sign of any income improvement in the near future. In the meantime, the loss-making organization has applied to the government for a grant or lump sum allocation of Tk 118 crore in the current 2025-2026 fiscal year, saying it will stand on its own feet. In this situation, the government is looking for ways to make the organization profitable. On September 9 of this year, a meeting of the Ministry of Information discussed alternative use of FDC's land and resources and giving a golden handshake to a section of those working there. Which was later forced to be canceled by the government in the face of the anger of filmmakers. Several officials present at the meeting said that a proposal to dissolve the corporation and run FDC under a public-private partnership system was discussed. In that case, successful entrepreneurs in this sector will be involved. FDC expressed disappointment over such a proposal. The current management of FDC does not want to take responsibility for the 'corruption' of the previous Awami League government. They have highlighted several possibilities to make the organization profitable. FDC Managing Director Masuma Rahman Tani said that no investment has been made in the modernization of FDC in the last 16 years. Many leaders of the past have deliberately pushed FDC back and helped the culture of neighboring countries to gain market share in exchange for the glimmer of light of domestic culture. Due to the inadequacy of modern technology, dilapidated studios, inadequate equipment and lack of renovation, FDC is losing its golden glory of the past day by day. An official of the FDC administration, on condition of anonymity, expressed regret to Bangladesh Pratidin yesterday that in order to restore the pace of work and increase income, the rent of various equipment including cameras and other equipment of various shooting and dubbing floors of FDC and film production work within the organization was reduced last year. But that did not bring any benefit either. Because there is no modern equipment and advanced system of film production here. He cited an example and said that now is the era of more advanced cameras including Alexa. However, in 2017, under the modernization project of FDC, Red Dragon, Red Starlet and Sony F55 cameras from the Mandhata era were brought here. With which it is not possible to make films suitable for the time now. Therefore, the producers are going out and working on renting advanced technology cameras and other equipment from private institutions. At the same time, due to the lack of advanced shooting and dubbing systems, producers are outsourcing. It is learned that currently FDC has eight prehistoric cameras. These are one Red Dragon, two Red Scarlet and five Sony F-55 cameras. Out of these, only three Sony F-55 model cameras are operational now. The rest are broken. 

Yesterday, when I visited FDC, I saw that the shooting of a film called 'Banalata Express' directed by Tanim Noor was going on on the second floor. Apart from this, no other film production work was done there yesterday. Filmmakers say that it is fortunate that even if it is a film, shooting is going on today, because due to lack of work, not even a crow is seen here every day. According to the information provided by the FDC's accounting department, FDC, which started in 1957, contributed the highest revenue to the state treasury in 1999-2000; which amounted to 11 crore 9 lakh 99 thousand taka. However, since then, the amount of revenue has been decreasing. And since 2016, the institution has been receiving subsidies from the government. The organization has lost its former glory due to mismanagement and failure to adapt to the times. In light of reality, it would be an 'injustice' to 'think about alternatives' without helping FDC stand on its own feet, says the current MD of the organization, Masuma Rahman Tani. He said, "I have shown with the statistics of last August that the financial problems will be largely eliminated if only the e-ticketing system is introduced and the shooting spots can be rented at the right price. And if modern equipment and technology are added, it is possible to take FDC to a profitable place again. It would not be right to think about anything else here." He also said that in August of this year, FDC's operating income was increased to 24 lakh 71 thousand 232 taka, which was a mere 12 lakh 27 thousand 370 taka and 65 paisa in August of the previous year. This shows that if we work with sincerity and dedication, it is possible to take FDC to a profitable level soon." MD Tani said, the price has been reduced so that directors can shoot sincerely for less money, and also to improve the financial condition of FDC. We have reduced the rate card price of our service from the lowest 500 to 2-3 thousand taka. We are trying to create a friendly environment by simplifying the rules, so that it is easy for film makers or any production companies. 

Meanwhile, filmmakers also complained that water is falling from the roof of the floor; AC is broken. FDC, located on seven and a half acres of land in Tejgaon, previously had nine shooting floors, ponds, gardens, swimming pools, artificial fountains, landlord houses and various shooting spots. But now the only suitable place for shooting is the open space in front of the administrative building and around the fountain spot. All the other places are in a state of distress. In place of the previous nine shooting floors, there are now 5 (1, 2, 7, 8 and 9). Of these, shooting floor number eight has been rented out to a private TV channel for almost a decade. An official of the production department of FDC, on condition of anonymity, said that the production department includes the camera and light department, sound department, editing department, floor and set department. We last got the equipment in 2016. No new equipment has been brought in for almost nine years, as a result, we are lagging behind in terms of modern technology. The 5.1 sound system software for background music has been broken for many years. The dubbing machine is broken, there were two sound mixing machines; they were broken long ago. There is no 5.1 or 7.1 surround sound system. The machines in the editing department are out of order, editing is done through software, they are backdated. The DCP (Digital Cinema Package) machine is broken. The Christie projector machine is of no use. There is no facility for visual effects work. Digital sound equipment was purchased since 2007, but they were not used due to litigation. They are now useless, not usable. Although there are two Jimmy Jib cranes (40 feet), there is no skilled manpower to operate them. The official expressed regret and said that to buy new equipment, money is needed from the revenue sector. But FDC does not have that capacity. Therefore, the equipment was not purchased. According to the information of the FDC's accounting department, the corporation earned 62,274,557 taka and 21 paisa from the operation and service sector in the 2023-2024 fiscal year. That year, 239,964,763 taka and 80 paisa were spent in various sectors. Of this, 34,34,874 taka was spent on interest on bank loans. In the next year, i.e. 2024-2025 fiscal year, the corporation earned 35,733,775 taka. And the expenditure was 244,868,402 taka and 50 paisa. The remaining money of the deficit has to be brought from the government. According to the FDC's accounts department, in the 10 years from the 2015-16 fiscal year to the 2024-25 fiscal year, FDC received a grant of 318 million taka including salary allowances and gratuity for employees, and during this period it also had to take a loan of 483 million taka. That means that FDC had to take a total of 801.3 million taka including government grants and loans in a decade. The organization's audit report for 2021-22 says that the organization's continuous loss amounted to 1423.2 million taka. At the time of the audit, the organization's liabilities were much higher than its assets of 132.48 million taka. This situation shows that FDC is now in boundless uncertainty. As a result, doubts have arisen about whether it will be able to survive or not. On top of this, filmmakers are seeing a statement by the recently departed information advisor Mahfuz Alam as a final blow to the death, namely, that 'FDC should be turned into a research laboratory instead of a film production company.' People in the film world are dissatisfied with his statement.

Headline_English: NCP-Chhatra Dal clash in Shariatpur, cocktail explosion, eight injured
Content_Enlish:
NCP and Chhatra Dal leaders and activists clash in Chowrangi area of ​​Shariatpur city. Today Monday nightPhoto: Prothom Alo 
A clash occurred between Jatiya Nagorik Party (NCP) and Chhatra Dal leaders and activists in Shariatpur. At least eight people were injured in a cocktail explosion. Leaders and activists of the two parties have leveled charges against each other in this incident. 

According to eyewitnesses and police sources, NCP leaders and activists took out a protest procession on Monday evening to protest the killing of Inqilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Bin Hadi and the shooting of Motaleb Sikder, organizer of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party in Khulna, and to demand justice for the guilty. The procession was passing through Chowrangi area of ​​Shariatpur city. At that time, an argument broke out during the procession over the entry of a Chhatra Dal worker's motorcycle. This led to a clash between the two parties. 

At one stage, brickbats and a chase ensued between the two sides. Three cocktail explosions were set off during this time. At least eight people, including five Chhatra Dal leaders, were injured. Leaders and activists of the two parties are leveling allegations against each other over the clash. 

Officer-in-charge of Palang Model Police Station Shah Alam said, "There was a clash with Chhatra Dal over a motorcycle entering the NCP procession. We rushed to the spot after receiving information and brought the situation under control. Legal action will be taken in view of the complaint in this incident." 

The five injured Chhatra Dal leaders have been admitted to Shariatpur Sadar Hospital. Among them, Naeem Bepari, the president of the Tulasa Union Jubo Dal in Sadar, has been sent to Dhaka for better treatment. 

District Chhatra Dal member secretary Sohel Talukder told Prothom Alo, "One of our Chhatra Dal activists was stopped by NCP leader Sabuj Talukder and his supporters while he was crossing the road. When we reached the spot after receiving the information, NCP leaders and activists launched an ambush on us. Then they organized themselves and attacked us with indigenous weapons, causing panic by exploding cocktails. Six of our leaders were injured in the cocktail attacks. 

Meanwhile, Sabuj Talukder, former joint coordinator of the District Citizens Party (NCP), made a counter-allegation. He told Prothom Alo, "We were taking out a procession demanding justice for Hadi's murder and protesting the shooting of an NCP leader in Khulna. A boy from Chhatra Dal entered our procession on a motorcycle and attacked one of our activists. Later, when we held him, Chhatra Dal member secretary Sohel and his people came and attacked us with domestic weapons.'

Headline_English: How Putin is managing the economic crisis and continuing the war
Content_Enlish:
Russian President Vladimir Putin File Photo: Reuters 
The Russian economy is in crisis. Various problems are emerging, including inflation and budget deficits. Economic growth is declining. The reasons for this are, on the one hand, Western sanctions on Moscow due to the Russia-Ukraine war, and on the other hand, the huge cost of waging war. Even so, it does not seem that Russian President Vladimir Putin will agree to stop the war soon. 

Analysts believe that the country can continue the war for several more years at the current pace, despite Western sanctions on Russia. Maria Snegovaya, a researcher at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said that the blow to the Russian economy is not catastrophic. It is possible for the Kremlin to adapt to it for now. 

Richard Connolly, a researcher at the Royal United Services Institute, said the same. "As long as Russia can extract oil and sell it at a reasonable price, it will have enough money to continue the war," he said. "However, the current state of the Russian economy is not at all comfortable for the country." 

Researcher Snegovaya noted that looking at history, Russia has made unfavorable deals in the face of economic crises. For example, after World War I and the war in Afghanistan. However, Russia has not yet fallen into that level of crisis, he said. This is bad news for Ukraine, and even for US President Donald Trump, who is eager to stop the war.

Headline_English: Three killed, including two teenagers, in motorcycle collision in Tangail
Content_Enlish:
Abir Hossain, Likhon Ahmed and Sabbir Hasan killed in road accident 
Abir Hossain, Likhon Ahmed and Sabbir Hasan killed in road accidentPhoto: Collected 
Three people, including two friends, were killed in a head-on collision between two motorcycles in Sakhipur, Tangail. The accident occurred in the Beltoli area of ​​the Kalmegha-Nalua road of the upazila on Monday evening. 

The deceased teenagers are Likhon Ahmed (15), son of Mohammad Ali of Panaullahpara in Kalidas village of the upazila, Abir Hossain (15), son of Moinuddin of Ballachalapara of the same village, and Sabbir Hasan (20), son of expatriate Abdur Rouf of Fuljhunipara. Likhon and Abir are friends. They are ninth-grade students of Kalidas Kaltan Vidyaniketan. And Sabbir Hasan was preparing to go abroad after passing HSC. 

Eyewitnesses said that Abir Hossain was driving one motorcycle and Sabbir Hasan was driving the other. The deceased Abir and Likhon were on the same motorcycle. 

According to local and eyewitness accounts, two motorcycles collided head-on in the Beltoli area this evening. Five motorcycle riders were seriously injured. The injured were rescued and taken to Sakhipur Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty doctor declared Abir Hossain dead. Later, Likhon Ahmed and Sabbir Hasan died on the way to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. 

Kalidas Kaltan Vidyaniketan headmaster Aminul Islam Badal told Prothom Alo that Likhon and Abir were ninth-grade students of his institution, and the deceased Sabbir was a former student of his institution. Coincidentally, all three live in the same village. 

Sakhipur Police Station Second Officer Sub-Inspector (SI) Mosharraf Hossain Chowdhury told Prothom Alo that two bodies have been brought to the police station. The process of bringing another body from Dhaka to Sakhipur is underway. Necessary legal measures will be taken in this incident.

Headline_English: BGB returns BSF member detained on charges of infiltration at Patgram border
Content_Enlish:
The 51 Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has returned the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) member Ved Prakash, who was detained on charges of infiltration at the Patgram border in Lalmonirhat, through a flag meeting. The flag meeting was held at the battalion commander level in the Tin Bigha Corridor area on Sunday afternoon. 

Earlier, at around 5 am on Sunday, members of the 51 BGB battalion patrol team arrested him when he crossed the border in the Dahagram union area of ​​Patgram and entered about 100 yards inside Bangladesh. The detained BSF member was working at the Arjun Camp of the 174 BSF Battalion in Cooch Behar-West Bengal state of India. 

According to BGB sources, a shotgun, two bullets, a wireless set and a mobile phone were seized from the detained BSF member. After the incident, he was taken into BGB custody and the BSF was immediately called for a flag meeting. 

In the meeting, the commander of the 51 BGB battalion, Lt. Colonel Salim Al Deen and Deputy Commander of 174 BSF Battalion Vijay Prakash Shukla led the Indian side. At least 10 members of the border guard forces of both countries from different levels were present at the time.

December 21, the longest night of the year is going to be this Sunday. On this night, everyone will experience the longest night of the year with the light of the moon. If you want, you can read a book tonight. It is possible to allocate a little more time to watch a movie. If you like to sleep, you can sleep a little longer tonight. Because tonight is a little longer than other nights. 

On the other hand, tomorrow, Monday, will be the shortest day of the year. This will of course happen in the countries of the Northern Hemisphere. However, the opposite situation will be in the Southern Hemisphere. There, the longest day and shortest night will be at the same time. 

Why is December 21 the longest night of the year? 

This longest night is due to the southern ascension of the sun. On December 21, the sun is located on the Tropic of Capricorn. The night is longer because the North Pole is tilted a little away from the sun. Basically, the time of day and night changes with the change of seasons.

Since December, the southern hemisphere of the Earth has been tilted towards the sun, while the northern hemisphere has moved far away. At this time, the sunlight falls weakly in the north. As a result, the sunlight falls so little that the day seems to end very quickly. The nights are long. This is called the Winter Solstice or the southern solstice. At this time, the day is longest in the southern hemisphere and the night is longest in the northern hemisphere.

Headline_English: Order to frame charges against 17 people, including army officer, today
Content_Enlish:
An order is expected to be issued today to frame formal charges against a total of 17 people, including 10 army officers, arrested in a case of crimes against humanity for alleged disappearances and torture in the Task Force for Interrogation (TFI) cell during the long rule of the Awami League.

On Sunday (December 21), a three-member judicial panel led by Justice Md. Golam Mortuza Majumder, Chairman of the International Crimes Tribunal-1, will issue this order. Through this order, a decision will be made on whether or not to start trial against the accused in the case. 

Out of the 17 accused in the case, 10 army officers have already been arrested. They are— Former Additional Director General of RAB Brigadier General Md. Jahangir Alam, Brigadier General Tofail Mostafa Sarwar, Brigadier General Md. Kamrul Hasan, Brigadier General Md. Mahabub Alam, Colonel KM Azad, Colonel Abdullah Al Momen, Colonel Anwar Latif Khan, who is on pre-retirement leave, former director of RAB's intelligence wing Colonel Md. Mashiur Rahman, Lieutenant Colonel Saiful Islam Sumon and Lieutenant Colonel Md. Sarwar Bin Kashem. 

The others absconding in this case, along with ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, are Sheikh Hasina's former defense advisor Major General (retd) Tariq Ahmed Siddique, former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former IGP Benazir Ahmed, former RAB DG M Khurshid Hossain, former RAB Director General Barrister Harun Or Rashid and former RAB Director Lieutenant Colonel (retd) Md. Khairul Islam. 

On December 14, lawyer Hamidul Misbah presented the hearing for the three accused arrested in the case, and lawyer Tabarak Hossain presented the hearing for the seven accused. In addition, state-appointed lawyer M Hasan Imam presented the hearing for three including Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, lawyer Sujad Mia presented the hearing for the three accused, and lawyer Md. Amir Hossain presented the hearing for the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. 

During the hearing, each lawyer presented separate arguments (grounds) and requested the acquittal of their clients. On the other hand, prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim, on behalf of the prosecution, requested the start of the trial by framing formal charges against the accused. After hearing both sides, the International Crimes Tribunal set today as the day to announce the order in this regard. 

Earlier, Chief Prosecutor Mohammad Tajul Islam concluded the hearing on the framing of charges on December 3. In the hearing, he highlighted the horror of the TFI cell and commented that a new Bangladesh has emerged on August 5, 2024, after 16 years of disappearances. It is also mentioned that the fate of the disappeared was determined in two ways. If the fate was good, the victims of the disappearance were shown as arrested and sent to prison. Secondly, after being kept in hiding for seven-eight years, they were left in an unknown place. 

On October 22 of this year, 10 officers who were in military custody were presented before the tribunal. After the hearing, the tribunal-1 ordered them to be shown as arrested and sent to prison. At the same time, the absconding accused were ordered to appear and a notice was published in the newspaper. However, since they did not appear on the scheduled date, the court appointed state defense on their behalf. On October 8, the prosecution filed a formal complaint in the case. Later, the tribunal took the complaint into consideration and issued arrest warrants against 17 people.

Headline_English: How Venezuela went from friend to enemy of the United States
Content_Enlish:
The then Vice President of the United States, Richard Nixon, was attacked by a mob during a visit to Venezuela. The time was May 1958. The people of the Latin American country were very angry because the United States had given asylum to the deposed dictator of Venezuela. However, Nixon was able to complete his tour without any damage. 

Venezuela was on the verge of a transition to democracy at the time. Nixon returned to the United States and blamed the mob for the incident on the Venezuelan communists. Caracas came to Washington's special attention. Since then, the two countries have had warm relations for four decades. However, due to dramatic political changes in Venezuela, that relationship has declined in the last 25 years. 

Brian Fonseca, a professor at Florida International University in the United States, said that Venezuela had a broad understanding with the United States in the late 20th century. Washington's motives behind this relationship were Venezuela's vast oil reserves and its conflict with the then Soviet Union during the Cold War. 

However, in the 1960s, the new Venezuelan government was anti-communist. As a friend, the United States began selling arms to Venezuela. In return, American companies began extracting oil from the country. However, a major blow to US interests in Venezuelan oil came a few years later. At that time, Caracas nationalized its own oil sector. 

Even then, the United States maintained good relations with Venezuela as a member of OPEC. Professor Brian Fonseca said that the United States often ignored Venezuela's political and economic weaknesses due to strategic interests. Washington was not as concerned about the country's corruption or human rights because of its affection for the Venezuelan government. 

After the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, American interest in Latin America waned. Still, Venezuela remained an important oil supplier. But at this time, few people in Washington paid attention to the rise of leftist revolutionary Hugo Chavez. He won the election in December 1998. 

But a failed attempt to overthrow Chavez in 2002 changed everything. He alleged that the administration of then-US President George W. Bush had tried to overthrow him. The White House denied it, but declassified documents in 2004 showed that the US had already known about the plot. 

In 2007, Chavez re-established state control over Venezuela's oil industry. Foreign companies were forced to come under the control of the state-owned oil company. These measures were popular in the country and strengthened Chavez's power. After his death in March 2013, his successor, Nicolas Maduro, continued the same policy. As a result, Venezuela's isolation with the US continued. 

Now, tensions are at their peak under Trump. Trump claims that Venezuela's role in immigration and drug trafficking threatens US national security. He wants Maduro to fall. The US also seems ready to invade Venezuela. Washington made similar preparations 50 years ago when Nixon was overthrown by a mob in Venezuela. What happens this time will only be known in the coming days.

Headline_English: Why extremists can come to safe areas: Foreign Affairs Advisor
Content_Enlish:
Foreign Affairs Advisor Md. Touhid Hossain said, the Bangladesh Mission is located inside the diplomatic area in Delhi, a very safe place, why can Hindu extremists come inside the area? Then they have been allowed to come, such an incident is not expected. 

He made such comments in response to questions from journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday afternoon. 

The Foreign Affairs Advisor said, Delhi has presented the issue as simply as it is; it is not that simple. The Foreign Affairs Advisor said, our mission is located deep inside the diplomatic area. It is not that it is somewhere outside or at the beginning of the diplomatic area. They are saying, a group of 20-25 people. It may be. The number may be more or less. That is not the case. 

Incidentally, on Saturday night, a protest was held in front of the Bangladesh High Commission in the Indian capital Delhi under the banner of the Akhand Hindu Rashtra Sena. That night, they stood in front of Bangladesh House with banners for about 20 minutes and raised various slogans against Bangladesh. At that time, 20 to 25 protesters shouted anti-Bangladesh slogans and threatened Bangladesh High Commissioner to India Riaz Hamidullah. 

Touhid Hossain said, they are saying a group of 20-25 people. A group of Hindu extremist organizations. Why can they come so far? In a sanitized area. That means they have been allowed to come then! Normally they are not supposed to be able to come. Then they left with slogans protesting the killing of Hindu citizens. We know that they said many other things. 

The Foreign Advisor said, I do not have evidence. But we have heard that he has been threatened to be killed. Why would they threaten him by coming there? The High Commissioner's family in Delhi is feeling at risk and is feeling threatened. 

Touhid Hossain said, a Bangladeshi citizen has been brutally murdered. It does not make sense to combine the security of minorities with this. The person who was killed is a citizen of Bangladesh and Bangladesh has taken immediate action in this regard. Several people have already been arrested. But the way it has been presented is unacceptable. We feel that the normal security measures have not been followed properly. However, they have said that they will look into the security of the mission, and we have taken note of that. 

Earlier, in a statement, the Indian Ministry of External Affairs said that around 20 to 25 youths gathered in front of the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi on Saturday (December 20). They came there to protest the killing of Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh, raised slogans and called for ensuring the safety of minority communities in Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Law enforcement will be on the polling station for 5 days
Content_Enlish:
Election Commission (EC) 
Election Commission (EC) Photo: BSS 
Members of various law enforcement agencies will be in the field for five days before and after the election as part of the election-time deployment in the 13th National Parliament Election and Referendum. The law enforcement agencies will be specially deployed for the three days before the election, the day of the election and the day after the election, that is, from February 9 to 13. 

The Election Commission (EC) issued a special circular on law and order last Thursday. This action plan was mentioned there. The National Parliament Election and Referendum will be held on February 12. 

The circular said that the prerequisite for making the election fair, free and festive is to maintain law and order. The concerned forces are working towards this goal. The armed forces are already deployed to support the civilian administration, which will continue during the election. The government has given magisterial powers to the military, which will be in force until February 28. 

The EC circular states that the normal deployment of law enforcement forces is ongoing. Apart from this, the election-time deployment will be three days before the polls. Except for the Ansar and the Village Defense Team, all forces will be deployed for five days during the polls. In the case of the Ansars, this deployment will be for six days (four days before the polls, the day of the polls and the day after the polls). 

The EC circular does not mention how many members of which force will be deployed. The circular states that the Ministry of Home Affairs, as the 'lead' ministry, will formulate a detailed plan, coordinate and supervise the law and order situation during the pre-election and post-election periods. It states that effective measures will be taken to recover illegal weapons and prevent the use of illegal weapons, any activities that disrupt the election and terrorist activities and special operations will be carried out. Special security will be ensured at risky polling stations. CCTV coverage will be ensured at polling stations as per the feasibility. Arrangements will be made to display a 'live feed' of the body-worn camera used in the field at the Election Commission's coordination cell. 

The circular states that a law and order and disinformation monitoring cell will be formed in the Election Commission with representatives from the EC, the relevant ministries and all forces. This cell will work four days before the election, on the day of the election and two days after the election. 

The schedule for the 13th National Parliament Election and Referendum has been announced on December 11. The parliamentary election and referendum will be held on February 12. Earlier, on December 9, the press wing of the chief advisor to the interim government had said that after the schedule is announced, all forces engaged in maintaining law and order in the country, including the armed forces, will work to ensure an electoral environment. About 900,000 members of the armed forces and other forces will be engaged in maintaining law and order in the country, which is the highest ever. A record number of 150,000 police members have already been given electoral training to conduct fair elections. 

EC asks to deploy police in offices of returning officers, assistant returning officers 

The EC wrote to the Home Ministry on Thursday to ensure overall security and safety in the offices of returning officers and assistant returning officers for the 13th National Parliament elections across the country. It has been asked to issue instructions to deploy the required number of police in these offices. 

EC sources said that the Election Commission has sent a letter in this regard to the Senior Secretary of the Home Ministry. 

The letter said that the schedule for the 13th National Parliament elections has been announced on December 11. In the meantime, a notification has been issued for the appointment of returning officers and assistant returning officers in order to conduct the elections in a fair and orderly manner. 

Important election-related documents, election materials, and equipment are stored in the offices of returning officers and assistant returning officers. Considering the law and order situation during the election, it is essential to ensure the security of important documents, election materials, and office employees. The letter has asked for instructions to deploy the necessary number of police forces to provide security at the offices of the Returning Officer and Assistant Returning Officer. 

International observers invited to apply 
International observers and foreign media interested in observing the upcoming national elections and referendums can apply to the Election Commission until January 17. The EC issued a notification in this regard on Thursday. It said that interested international election observers or observation organizations and foreign media should apply in light of the EC's policy for 'International Election Observers and Foreign Media'. These policies and related forms can be found on the EC website (www.ecs.gov.bd). 

Schedule revision 
The EC revised the schedule for the 13th National Parliament elections on Thursday. However, the voting date will remain on February 12. According to EC sources, changes have been made to the time of appeal against the decision of the Returning Officer and the schedule for the disposal of appeals. According to the revised schedule, appeals can be filed from January 5-9. And the appeal will be disposed of from January 10-18. Earlier, the last date for appeal was January 11. And the time for disposal of appeal was January 12-18.

Headline_English: BPL to have a small opening ceremony

BCB had planned to hold a grand opening ceremony of the BPL in Dhaka this time. However, due to security concerns, BCB withdrew from the decision to hold it on December 24. Although not in Dhaka, the BPL opening ceremony will be held on a small scale in Sylhet. 

The opening ceremony of the tournament will be held in Sylhet on December 26, on the first day of the tournament. There will be cultural programs before the start of the match or in between the two matches. It is known that some popular bands may perform there. 

Due to this, some changes have been made to the match schedule of the opening day. According to the previous schedule, the match between Sylhet Titans and Rajshahi Warriors was supposed to start at 2 pm. Now it has been postponed to 3 pm. In addition, a 20-minute break has been kept between the two innings. The second match of the day will be held at 7:45 pm, in which Noakhali Express will face Chittagong Royals. 

The 6-team BPL will be held at three venues in Sylhet, Chittagong and Dhaka. Sylhet from December 26 to January 2, and Chittagong from January 5 to January 12. The Dhaka leg will start on January 15. The eliminator, qualifier and final will also be held in Dhaka. The final will be held on January 23. 

The BCB has announced the ticket prices for the Sylhet leg today. The ticket prices range from Tk 200 to Tk 2,000 depending on the gallery.

Headline_English: Bangladesh's pair of Jumar-Urmi win silver medal
Content_Enlish:
Al Amin Jumar-Urmi Akhtar pair has already made history by reaching the final of an international badminton tournament. However, the pair could not win gold at the Unex-Sunrise Bangladesh International Challenge.
They lost to Malaysian pair Datu Anif Isak and Clarissa Sun in the mixed doubles final on Saturday (December 20).

Although they fought in the first set, they could not win the next set. They won silver in the Bangladesh International Challenge tournament after losing by 27-25 and 21-14 points.

No formalities were held in the final due to the national mourning day following the death of Inqilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi. 

Bangladesh's mixed doubles star pair Jumar-Urmi received a cash prize for reaching the final. Bangladesh Badminton Federation President Habib Ullah Don gave them a total of $1,000 in cash prizes of $500 each. At the same time, he also assured to provide all kinds of facilities, including foreign coaches, for the advanced training of the shuttlers.

After the final, Al Amin Jumar said, "It is a joy that we have been able to reach the final of an international event for the first time, but it is also a bit sad that we could not become champions. They are much ahead of us in terms of training facilities. In that respect, we are somewhat behind. I have played in all three categories, singles, doubles and mixed doubles. I did not feel any fatigue, I played with joy. I could not do it this time, but in the future I will definitely win gold medals for the country."

Urmi Akhter said, "The three months of training we had with the SA Games in mind was very useful. That is why we were able to reach the final of this tournament. We have a lot of differences with them. You can tell by looking at their dresses that they play with big sponsors. We do not have any sponsors like that. We do not have the facilities of long-term training." If we had all the facilities like them, we could have gone much further. 

Along with the mixed doubles, four other event finals were held today. In the men's singles, Meiraba Maisnam defeated Numair Shaik by 21-7 and 21-12 points. In the women's singles, Isika Jaiswal of the United States won the gold medal. Isika defeated India's Tanvi Reddy by 22-20, 21-23 and 21-15 points. In the men's doubles final, the Indian pair of Niranjan and Ruban Kumar defeated Vietnam's Dang Khah and Tran Hong by 21-19 and 21-12 points.

Finally, in the women's doubles final, Patharin and Sarisa Janpeng of Thailand defeated Malaysia's Gan Min and Tan Jing by 21-7, 20-22 and 21-15 points.

Lohagara Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Abdul Jalil told Prothom Alo that the police went to the spot after receiving the information. A drive is being launched to bring those involved under the law.

Headline_English: Bodies of 6 Bangladeshi soldiers killed in Sudan arrive in the country
Content_Enlish:
The bodies of six Bangladeshi peacekeepers killed in an attack by armed groups in the Abyei area of ​​Sudan, Africa, have arrived in the country. Their bodies arrived at the Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka around 11 am on Saturday (December 20). 

Bangladesh Army Chief of General Staff Lieutenant General Mizanur Rahman Shamim received the bodies of the peacekeepers at the airport. After the funeral prayers with due state honors tomorrow, the bodies will be sent to their respective addresses by helicopter. Then the burial ceremony will be completed with due military honors. 

It is worth noting that the attack was carried out on the Kadugoli Logistics Base under the United Nations Peacekeeping Mission (UNISFA) in the Abyei area of ​​Sudan on December 13 (Saturday). The separatist armed group launched a sudden drone attack on the army base between 3:40 pm and 3:50 pm local time. Six Bangladeshi peacekeepers lost their lives on the spot. 

Eight more people were injured in the attack, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. 

The six peacekeepers who were killed were Corporal Md. Masud Rana: ASC (Natore), Private Shamim Reza: Bir (Rajbari), Private Md. Mominul Islam: Bir (Kurigram), Private Shanto Mandal: Bir (Kurigram), Mess Waiter Md. Jahangir Alam (Kishoreganj) and Laundry Worker Md. Sabuj Mia (Gaibandha). 

The eight peacekeepers injured in the attack were transferred to the Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi, Kenya, for advanced treatment as soon as possible. They are - Lieutenant Colonel Khondaker Khalequzzaman, PSC, Ordnance (Kushtia), Sergeant Md. Mostakim Hossain: Bir (Dinajpur), Corporal Afroza Parvin Iti, Signals (Dhaka), Lance Corporal Mohibul Islam: EME (Barguna), Soldier Md. Mejbaul Kabir: Bir (Kurigram), Soldier Md. Umme Hani Akhter: (Eng: Rangpur), Soldier Chumki Akhter, Ordnance (Manikganj) and Soldier Md. Manazir Ahsan: Bir (Noakhali). 

Among the injured, Soldier Md. Mejbaul Kabir underwent successful surgery as his condition was critical and he is under close observation. Besides, the rest are currently out of danger. One of them has already left the hospital after treatment. 

The Bangladesh Army has also strongly condemned the brutal and cowardly terrorist attack in Sudan. In a condolence message, it was said that the sacrifice of the slain peacekeepers will be a shining and glorious symbol of Bangladesh's commitment to establishing world peace. The army has expressed its deep condolences to the bereaved families of the martyrs.

Headline_English: National mourning today
Content_Enlish:
A day of state mourning will be observed today on the death of Inqilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi. On this occasion, the national flag will be flown at half-mast in all government, semi-government, autonomous institutions, educational institutions, government and private buildings in the country and Bangladesh missions abroad. After the news of Osman Hadi's death, the chief advisor to the interim government, Dr. Muhammad Yunus, announced the state mourning. The advisors to the interim government have expressed deep shock and condolences on the death of Osman Hadi. In separate condolence messages yesterday, they prayed for the forgiveness of the departed soul and expressed condolences to his family. Various government departments, political parties, organizations and special individuals have expressed condolences. Home Affairs and Agriculture Advisor Lieutenant General (Retd.) Md. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, in a condolence message, prayed for the forgiveness of the departed soul and expressed condolences to his family members. Information and Broadcasting; Syeda Rizwana Hasan, Advisor on Environment, Forests and Climate Change and Water Resources, said, "Hadi's uncompromising stance against injustice, injustice and oppression was a source of inspiration for democracy-loving people." Land Advisor Ali Imam Majumder said, "His role in contemporary political, social and cultural movements became a source of inspiration." In addition, Fisheries and Livestock Advisor Farida Akhtar, Social Welfare and Women and Children's Affairs Advisor Sharmin S Murshid, and Special Assistant to the Principal Advisor in charge of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Faiz Ahmed Tayyab expressed their condolences. In the condolence message, the Bangladesh Election Commission said, "Hadi was a loyal and fighting young voice of the country. His bravery and patriotism are unforgettable.’ 

In his condolence message, BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said, ‘After the fall of the Awami dictatorial regime, the miscreants have indulged in the evil act of gaining benefits through anarchy. The incident of Sharif Osman Hadi being killed in their brutal attack is a manifestation of that evil act.’ Mahmudur Rahman Manna, President of Nagorik Oikya, said, ‘Hadi was a brave, fearless patriot. His strong voice was showing Bangladesh a new dream. 

In addition, Ameer of Islami Andolan Bangladesh Mufti Syed Muhammad Rezaul Karim, Chairman of Amar Bangladesh Party (AB Party) Mujibur Rahman Manju and General Secretary Asaduzzaman Fuad, President of Dhaka Reporters Unity Abu Saleh Akon and General Secretary Mainul Hasan Sohel, President of the People's Rights Council Nurul Haque Nur, among others, expressed their condolences.

Headline_English: A group wants to systematically push the country towards anarchy: Mirza Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has expressed deep concern over the violence, vandalism and arson incidents across the country following the death of Inquilab Manch convener Sharif Osman bin Hadi. He said that an identified group is systematically trying to push the country towards anarchy. This group is conspiring to destabilize the democratic transition process. 

The party's Secretary General said this at a press conference organized at the BNP Chairperson's political office in Gulshan, the capital, on Friday night. Earlier, an emergency meeting of the BNP standing committee was held there. The meeting began at 8:45 pm and ended around 10 pm. 

The BNP Secretary General said, "Inquilab Manch convener Sharif Osman bin Hadi passed away while undergoing treatment in Singapore on Thursday evening." I strongly condemn this murder and demand immediate arrest and trial of the murderers.’ 

At that time, Mirza Fakhrul said, focusing on this unwanted death, a group of unruly people set fire to the Daily Prothom Alo, the English daily Daily Star and several other institutions late last night. This put the lives of working journalists in serious danger. One of the bravest figures in all democratic movements in the country, including the anti-fascist July Movement, and renowned journalist New Age Editor Nurul Kabir, was attacked. Several other cultural institutions, including Chhayanaut, were attacked. Today, Udichi was also attacked and set on fire. 

The BNP Secretary General also said that yesterday, the Indian Assistant High Commission building was attacked in Khulna. No. 32 in Dhanmondi was again set on fire. The Indira Gandhi Cultural Center was vandalized and set on fire. 32 shops were vandalized in the Uttara area and the house of an Awami League leader was set on fire. 

Mirza Fakhrul said, ‘The most horrific incident was the hanging of a Hindu youth from a tree on charges of blasphemy and setting him on fire. Mohiuddin Chowdhury’s house was set on fire in Chittagong. The offices of Prothom Alo and Daily Star were also vandalized in Rajshahi.’ 

Describing these incidents as ‘disgusting and despicable’, the BNP Secretary General said, ‘These incidents prove that an old identified group is trying to destabilize the country in a planned manner. They want to establish a new version of fascism in the country by destroying our voting rights and democratic rights, which were earned at the cost of a lot of blood.’ 

Mirza Fakhrul also questioned the role of the government at the press conference at this time. He said, ‘These incidents are happening right under the nose of the government. People think that the role of the government is not satisfactory. As a result, the image of the country, as well as the government, is being tarnished both at home and abroad. 

Mirza Fakhrul said, "All political parties in the country have already protested against this murder and have demanded the arrest and trial of the culprits. Even so, we believe that such violent attacks are a deep conspiracy to destabilize the national elections and the democratic transition process." 

Calling on the countrymen, the BNP Secretary General said, "On behalf of the peaceful and democratic countrymen, we want to warn these conspirators - this country, which was won at the cost of so much blood, cannot be allowed to be destroyed." This evil force must be stopped unitedly.’ 

BNP Standing Committee members Mirza Abbas, Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Abdul Moin Khan, Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Salahuddin Ahmed, Selima Rahman, Iqbal Hasan Mahmud (Tuku) and Major (Retd.) Hafiz Uddin Ahmed Bir Bikram were present at the press conference.

Headline_English: Power outage after drone attack on power plant in Sudan
Content_Enlish:
Several major cities in Sudan, including the capital Khartoum and Port Sudan, were plunged into darkness on Thursday after a deadly drone attack on a key power plant in eastern Sudan, the French news agency AFP reported.

Headline_English: Osman Hadi returns home in a coffin
Content_Enlish:
Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi returned home in a coffin with the national flag. Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG-585 carrying his body landed in Dhaka at 5:48 pm today, Friday. The Chief Advisor's Press Wing confirmed the matter in a statement. 

His body was taken from the airport to the cold storage of the National Heart Institute and Hospital. 

A separate statement sent by the Chief Advisor's Press Wing said, "Martyr Osman Hadi's Namaz-e-Janaza will be held at 2:30 pm on Saturday at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. Those interested in participating in his Namaz-e-Janaza are requested not to carry any bags or heavy objects. It also said that flying drones in and around the Parliament Bhaban and its surroundings is completely prohibited during this time." 

Earlier, this Biman flight departed from Singapore's Changi International Airport at 2:30 pm Bangladesh time. 

Sharif Osman Hadi, spokesperson of the Inqilab Manch, died at Singapore General Hospital at 9:45 pm on Thursday. Hadi, who was announced as a potential candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency, fought for life and death for seven days and left for the country never to return. 

Interim government advisor Adilur Rahman Khan, BNP standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar, Jatiya Nagorik Party (NCP) member secretary Akhtar Hossain and others were present at the airport to receive his body. 

The government has declared a state mourning tomorrow, Saturday, for the death of the fighter who fought in the July uprising. Chief Advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus made the announcement in an address to the nation after news of Hadi's death came from Singapore on Thursday night. He said that the state will take responsibility for Osman Hadi's wife and only child. 

Hadi was campaigning to run as a potential independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency. He was shot on Box Culvert Road in Purana Paltan on December 12. Hadi, who was shot in the head, was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital with serious injuries. Later, he was taken to Evercare Hospital. On December 15, Osman Hadi was airlifted to Singapore for better treatment. The Inquilab Manch spokesperson died there.

Headline_English: Five exams postponed due to national mourning, State University convocation postponed
Content_Enlish:
The government has declared a one-day national mourning across the country on Saturday (December 20) following the death of Inqilab Manch convener and July fighter Sharif Osman Hadi. Considering the issues of student travel and safety, a total of five recruitment and academic examinations, including the admission test of Dhaka University, have been postponed. In addition, the scheduled convocation ceremony of the State University of Bangladesh has also been postponed as part of the state mourning.

It is learned that the undergraduate admission test of the 'Science Unit' of Dhaka University for the academic year 2025-26 was postponed on Friday (December 19). The university authorities said that the revised date of the exam will be announced soon. 

In addition, the scheduled recruitment test of the Department of Posts and Telecommunications has also been postponed on Friday. The recruitment test to be held for the posts of Assistant Director and Assistant Secretary of the University Grants Commission (UGC) on the same day was also canceled. The exam was scheduled to be held from 3:30 pm to 4:30 pm in the MCQ format. According to UGC sources, a total of 7,351 candidates were scheduled to appear for the exam against 15 posts. The new dates for these exams will be announced later. 

The recruitment exam for four categories of the National Computer Training and Research Academy (NECTA) in Bogra under the Department of Technical and Madrasa Education has also been postponed. The new dates for these exams will be announced later through a press release and Teletalk SMS. 

Due to the state mourning, the LLB exam scheduled for Friday under the National University has been postponed. The university authorities said that the new schedule for the postponed exam will be announced later. However, the schedule for other exams of the first phase of LLB 2024 will remain unchanged. In addition, the special senate session scheduled for Saturday has been changed and will be held at 10:30 am on Sunday at the Academic Building of the Gazipur campus. 

At the same time, as part of the state mourning, the seventh convocation of the State University of Bangladesh will be held on Sunday instead of Saturday. In addition, several recruitment exams to be held under the Bankers Selection Committee have also been postponed. 

In addition, BNP has postponed two of its previously scheduled political programs. In addition, as part of the state mourning, various cultural and festive events have been canceled or postponed across the country.

Headline_English: Shadow nets infest Dhanmondi, operations suspended
Content_Enlish:
Late on Thursday night, protesters entered the Chhayanot Bhaban, a music academy in Dhanmondi, in the capital, and carried out extensive vandalism. CCTV cameras, doors, windows, and other equipment of the building were damaged. 

Computers and laptops were also vandalized and looted. They set fire to the outside of the building. Later, the army, police, RAB, and fire service arrived and brought the situation under control. 

On-site inspection showed that there were signs of arson on the ground floor of the 6-story building. Mattresses, tablas, chairs, and harmoniums were all in a state of disrepair. All belongings and musical instruments in every room from the second to sixth floors were vandalized. 

An eyewitness said that office documents and student papers were damaged in the vandalism. The president's room, the school, the Ramesh Chandra Memorial Auditorium, the main auditorium, and the toilets were vandalized. 

A harmonium and some books kept in a stack were burned in a room on the third floor. The painting of Sanjida Khatun and national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam was cut off. 

At 3:15 am, the Chhayanaut authorities announced an indefinite suspension of their activities. 

Regarding the attack on Chhayanaut, the organization's president Dr. Sarwar Ali told Samakal that Chhayanaut will give an official response this Friday evening. Chhayanaut will continue its journey with steadfast determination. 

Earlier, after the news of the death of Inqilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi spread, a group of people took a procession from Shahbagh to the Prothom Alo office and started a siege and protest. At one stage, they vandalized and set fire to the office with sticks. 

Then they went to the Daily Star building, attacked it, vandalized it, and set it on fire. When the fire was burning on the lower three floors of the building, the journalists took shelter on the roof to save their lives. The trapped journalists were later rescued using a crane.

Headline_English: Cricketers have lost faith in Snicko
Content_Enlish:
Whatever the meaning of the Ashes, it is not friendship. For both Australia and England, it is a fight for prestige. The Ashes, therefore, does not bring the two teams closer, but pushes them further apart due to the fierce competitive mentality. 
However, in the middle of this Ashes, both teams have joined hands in one place - distrust of the Snickometer. Neither England nor Australia can trust Snicko. Both teams want a way out of the current situation. 

What is the problem with Snicko 
Before understanding what is the problem with Snicko, it is better to keep in mind what it actually is. Snicko is one of the technologies used in the Decision Review System (DRS) in cricket. Specifically, Snicko is edge detection technology using images and sound. Through it, it is seen what the ball or bat has come into contact with at what moment. Since the ball and bat contact determines whether a player is out (caught) or not (LBW), the third umpire tries to connect the two. 

However, it is not easy. Because, along with the picture, the words are also important here. If neither of them works properly, the correct result cannot be obtained. The whole matter can be said to be quite delicate. 

The use of this sneaker has been controversial on the first two days of the ongoing Adelaide Test. Questions have arisen around two decisions regarding Australia's Alex Carey on the first day and England's Jamie Smith on the second day. 

On the first day, Carey 
Coincidentally, England's wicketkeeper-batsman Smith is named in all three incidents. On the first day of the Test on Wednesday, Carey, who was on 72 runs in Australia's first innings, took a catch behind the wicket. England took a review when the umpire did not give out. The sneaker shows that the sneaker does not have a spike when the ball approaches Carey's bat. The spike that is there is two frames before the ball reaches the bat. According to ICC rules, the umpire can take into account the deviation of the spike up to one frame. If it is two frames, the ball is considered not to have hit the bat. 

Carey celebrates after century 
Carey celebrates after century AFP 
The third umpire did not give Carey out. However, at the end of the day's play, Carey said that the ball seemed to have hit his bat. Carey, who scored 106 runs and survived being out, also called himself lucky. Then, Snico founder Warren Barren admitted his failure and said that the Snico operator made a mistake. The sound was not picked up from the stump mic where it was supposed to be picked up, so the Snico result did not come out correctly. 

Smith on the second day 
Usman Khawaja took Smith's catch at slip off Pat Cummins in England's first innings on Thursday. On-field umpire Nitin Menon sought help from TV umpire Chris Gaffney, who gave him a not out. Australia was furious. The sneak peek showed that the ball had hit Smith's helmet and slipped. But the Australians believed it had hit his gloves. After 2 overs, another catch appeal was made against Smith for that Cummins delivery. This time too, umpire Menon sent it to the third umpire for a decision. 

Gaffney saw in the sneak peek that a spike was visible in the frame after the ball had crossed the bat. This time, Smith was furious when the third umpire gave out, and England captain Ben Stokes, who was on non-strike, was also seen expressing his dissatisfaction. 

Solution but not solution 
After the mistake in Carey's out on the first day, the angry England team took the matter to match referee Jeff Crowe. Taking the matter into consideration, Crowe reinstated an England review this morning. Before the start of the day's play, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg told SEN Radio that they were not happy with the effectiveness of the sneaker, "We don't think it's good enough. We have to make sure that it doesn't happen again." 

Throw away the sneaker thing. It's nonsense. 
Former England spinner Graeme Swann 
But within hours of Greenberg's 'mockery', the limits of the sneaker have been repeatedly exposed in the Smith incident. Mitchell Starc immediately expressed his anger on the field after Smith was not given out by Khawaja. The Australian left-arm pacer was then heard saying into the stump mic, "Sneaker needs to be dropped. Very bad technology.’ Referring to Carey’s not out the previous day, he said, ‘(Sniko) made a mistake yesterday, he made a mistake today.’ 

After a while, when Smith was given out after looking at the Snikometer, the English batsman expressed his annoyance. 

Australia-England consensus on Sniko 
After Smith’s dismissal, former English spinner Graeme Swann said on TNT Sports Live, ‘Throw that Sniko thing away. It’s useless.’ Another former England cricketer Alex Hartley also said almost the same thing in the Test Match Special, ‘Sniko needs to be dropped. Smith was sure the ball didn’t hit his bat. Australia appealed loudly. Because everyone knows that Sniko can’t be trusted anymore. That’s why they are appealing for everything, taking reviews when necessary.’ 

The Australians have also expressed their discomfort with Sniko. As former captain Ricky Ponting said, ‘The technology we are using is not as good as the technology used in other countries. The third umpire is sitting there and making decisions based on what the technology is giving him. Sometimes the third umpire is making decisions with confidence. This cannot happen. The technology that is there has to be trustworthy.’ Former Australian umpire Simon Taufel has also indirectly raised questions about the limitations of the snickers. He told Channel Seven, ‘The job of technology is to assist the umpire in his work, not to be an alternative to the umpire. We need to go back 20 years, where there was doubt about technology. The batting team always got an advantage. I want the umpires’ soft signal system to come back.’

Is there an alternative to the snickers? 
There is an alternative to the snickers. Ultra Edge is also used for edge detection. England has not used the Snickometer since 2016. India and South Africa also use Ultra Edge now. However, in Australia and New Zealand, Snicko is more commonly used. 

Both Snicko and Hawkeye's Ultra Edge are approved by the ICC. The broadcaster decides which one to use. Fox Sports has a contract with Cricket Australia to broadcast this year's Ashes. They have hired Snicko for technical assistance. The cost of using Snicko is also lower than Ultra Edge. 

However, given the amount of controversy surrounding Snicko in this year's Ashes, it is doubtful whether Cricket Australia will resort to this technology in the future. When trust is lost, what happens?

A group of youths have taken a stand in front of the Indian Assistant High Commission office in Chittagong to protest the killing of Inquilab Manch convener Sharif Osman Hadi. Around 11 pm tonight. Photo: Collected 
A group of youths identified as students and people have taken a stand in front of the Indian Assistant High Commission office in Chittagong to protest the killing of Inquilab Manch convener Sharif Osman Hadi. They started taking a stand in front of the office in the city's Khulshi area around 11:45 pm today, Thursday. Upon receiving the news, members of the city police took a stand there.

At that time, they raised anti-Awami League and anti-India slogans in protest of Hadi's murder. Later, police members arrived there and removed them. 

One of the protesters, Mohammad Tanvir, said that the leaders and activists of the Awami League, which was banned due to its anti-Awami League and anti-India statements, had conspired to attack Hadi while sitting in India. He was targeted due to his anti-Awami League and anti-India statements. 

Khulshi Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shahin Alam told Prothom Alo that 15-20 Indian people took a stand in front of the Indian Assistant High Commission office. They were removed. There were reports that more people were coming. Police members are there.

Headline_English: DSE gets its first female MD
Content_Enlish:
Nuzhat Anwar has been appointed as the new Managing Director (MD) of the country's main stock market, Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE). The capital market regulator Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) approved her appointment on Thursday. She will be the first female MD in the history of DSE. The DSE said this in a press release. 

DSE said that Nuzhat Anwar has more than two decades of experience in financial markets, banking and development finance. Earlier, she worked at the International Finance Corporation (IFC), an institution of the World Bank Group. Nuzhat Anwar has held several leadership positions in the Africa and South Asia regions at IFC. She served as IFC's country officer in Botswana and Namibia. During that time, she played a key role in establishing IFC's operations in Gaborone and advancing the sustainable investment program. IFC's first investment in Botswana was made under her leadership. 

Nuzhat Anwar has expertise in capital management, treasury and liquidity, transaction services, portfolio optimization and market development and advocacy. Earlier in her career, she served in various senior management positions at Citibank Bangladesh and Standard Chartered Bank Bangladesh for 16 years. Nuzhat holds a Master's degree in Commerce (Finance) from Dhaka University. 

Regarding the appointment of Nuzhat Anwar as Managing Director, DSE Chairman Mominul Islam said, "In the past one year, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) and the Board of Directors have worked to appoint a capable leader for DSE. Nuzhat Anwar has excellent leadership qualities, extensive experience in the financial sector at home and abroad, and a deep interest in the transformation of the country's capital market. We believe that these skills and experiences will help DSE move forward successfully in the coming days. The necessary internal processes will be completed as soon as possible to have Nuzhat Anwar assume the responsibilities," he said.

It is worth noting that in August 2022, the then MD of DSE, Tariq Amin Bhuiyan, resigned. The post of MD of the company remained vacant for about a year after his resignation. Then in August 2023, the then Executive Director of BSEC, ATM Tarikuzzaman, became the MD of DSE. In May 2024, Tarikuzzaman resigned and joined BSEC as Commissioner. Since then, the post of full-time Managing Director of DSE has remained vacant; the work was carried out by an acting person.

Headline_English: Government has seized assets worth Tk 66,146 crore: Finance Ministry
Content_Enlish:
Ministry of FinancePhoto: Prothom Alo 
The Ministry of Finance has said that a total of 66,146 crore taka worth of immovable and movable assets have been attached and seized from various industrial groups so far. Of this, 55,638 crore taka worth of immovable and movable assets are inside the country and 10,508 crore taka worth of immovable and movable assets are abroad. The Ministry of Finance gave this information in a notification today, Wednesday. 

Finance Ministry officials said that attachment means that those who have these assets in their names will no longer be able to sell or transfer them. Similarly, the people concerned will not be able to withdraw the seized money from the bank. 

The 30th meeting of the National Coordination Committee formed to formulate and implement various guidelines and policies to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing was held at the Secretariat today, Wednesday. Finance Advisor Salehuddin Ahmed presided over it. The Ministry of Finance issued the notification in the context of this meeting. 

The meeting decided that some sections of the existing Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2012 will be amended to make the recovery of money and assets laundered abroad more efficient and effective. 

The notification said that all have been instructed to file charge sheets in priority cases as soon as possible and take effective initiatives for the speedy disposal of cases. The meeting discussed the progress of the activities of the joint search and investigation team formed for 11 cases identified as priorities to recover money and assets laundered abroad. 

The Asia Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) will complete the fourth phase of mutual evaluation in the coming 2027-28 period to assess Bangladesh's position in complying with existing international standards on preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. The Financial Advisor gave instructions to take necessary preparations, considering this mutual evaluation as the most important activity in the meeting. 

The meeting was attended by the Chairman of the Anti-Corruption Commission, Principal Secretary of the Office of the Chief Advisor, Governor of Bangladesh Bank, Secretary of Finance, Secretary of the Financial Institutions Division, Chairman of the National Board of Revenue, Secretary of Commerce, Secretary of Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs, Chairman of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission, Secretary of Foreign Affairs (Bilateral), Additional Attorney General, Chief of CID, representatives of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Bangladesh Police and Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit.

Headline_English: Child dies in cylinder explosion while visiting grandparents' house
Content_Enlish:
Maisha Akhter (10), daughter of Md. Mainuddin of Shibpur in Daulatkhan upazila of Bhola. She had come to visit Nana, a gas balloon seller, in Ashulia of Savar with her aunt. The child died when the cylinder of that gas balloon exploded. The incident took place inside the Dhaka Cooperative Society in Kurgaon area of ​​Ashulia on Wednesday afternoon.

Police and the child's relatives said that last Monday, Maisha along with her aunt from Shibpur in Daulatkhan upazila of Bhola district came to visit Nana Mannan, a gas balloon seller, in Savar. Mannan lives as a caretaker in a house inside the Dhaka Cooperative Society in Kurgaon area of ​​Ashulia. He sells gas in a part of the house by filling the balloon with gas wholesale and retail. On Wednesday afternoon, Mannan filled the balloon with gas and left the cylinder there to cool down. When Maisha went near the cylinder, the cylinder exploded and most of Maisha's right hand and the right side of her face were severed and fell on the opposite side of the boundary wall of the house. Upon receiving the information, Ashulia police reached the spot and recovered the body.

The deceased child's aunt Seema Akter said, "I was cooking and Maisha was playing outside. No one was there. My father cooled the gas bottle (cylinder) and went outside. Then there was a noise. After Maisha took her class six exam, she said to me, "Auntie, let's go for a walk." Later, I brought her with me. Now I can't afford to take her with me."

Rubel Hawlader, officer-in-charge of Ashulia police station, said that the body has been recovered and sent to the capital's Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for an autopsy. Further legal action is under process in this regard.

Headline_English: Women are more vulnerable to cyber violence
Content_Enlish:
A discussion on ‘Women and Technology: What to do to end online violence and provide legal protection’ was held at the Azimur Rahman Conference Room of the Daily Star Bhaban in the capital. December 17 Photo: Courtesy of Blast
Violence against women and children online is increasing in line with the increase in internet usage in the country. During the mass uprising last year, 620 complaints of cyber violence against women and children were filed in 8 police stations and police superintendents’ offices in the country in the 5 months from July to December. These complaints were filed in Sonadanga in Khulna, Kotwali in Rangpur, Kotwali and Kaunia in Barisal, Superintendent of Police Office in Gazipur, Fatulla in Narayanganj and Bhanga and Kotwali police stations in Faridpur.

In addition, 56 cases of cyber violence were reported in the media in the 10 months from January to October this year. Of these, 54 victims were women.

This information was shared at a meeting on ‘Women and Technology: What to do to end online violence and provide legal protection’ at the Azimur Rahman Conference Room of the Daily Star Bhaban in the capital on Wednesday. The meeting was organized by the ‘Cyber ​​Support for Women and Children’ (CSWC), a platform of 14 organizations. The convener of this platform is Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST).

Speakers at the meeting said that women victims are not interested in reporting their complaints due to various reasons including fear of loss of dignity in the family and society, and the complicated and time-consuming process of cybercrime cases. Women who were at the forefront of the July coup and participated in politics are becoming victims of cyber violence in greater numbers. At this time, the need for digital rights protection is more than ever.

The speakers emphasized on law reform, effective implementation, training of law enforcement agencies, creating awareness on safe use of the internet, and providing services to the victims without any kind of harassment after the incident.

During the meeting, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police of Women Support and Investigation Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Maqsuda Akhter said that many victimized women do not know where to go for redress if they are victims of cyber violence. Publicity should be increased about the places where they can get help. Victimized women and children go through a lot of mental trauma after the incident, so they need counseling first.

Maqsuda Akhter said that victims will benefit if government and private organizations provide services under a network.

Saeed Ahmed, founder and CEO of the Institute of Informatics and Development (IID), delivered the opening speech at the meeting. He said that women who were at the forefront of the July movement were not only removed later, but there were also incidents of online violence against them. But the government was not seen taking any stand against this. Recently, it was seen that the government has requested Google to remove content critical of the government. However, it should have said that content of online violence should be removed.

Sharmin Khan, legal advisor at the International Center for Not for Profit Law (ICNL), said that while reporting a complaint, the victim should not have to face any uncomfortable situation or harassment. For this, an app can be arranged to report the complaint. So that the victimized women can report the complaint through the app within 24 hours of being a victim of online violence.

Raisul Islam, in-charge of the 109 helpline run by the Department of Women and Child Affairs, said that this helpline receives 6 to 7 thousand calls every day complaining about violence against women and children. The number of calls on cyber violence is now increasing compared to before. 5 thousand 126 quick response teams are being formed across the country to prevent incidents of offline and online violence.

Nova Ahmed, associate professor in the Department of Computer Science at North South University, said that the cause of concern about online violence is that it is spread quickly. Even if these incidents of violence are deleted, the footprint remains somehow or the other.

Nova Ahmed also said that girls should be educated in technology without being afraid of it. Technology is changing so rapidly that it is necessary to keep the law amended repeatedly to keep pace with it. It is necessary to keep technologists involved in this process.

The meeting was moderated by Blast Deputy Director (Victim Assistance and Arbitration) Tapsi Rabeyar and the organization's Senior Research Officer Manisha Biswas presented the keynote address.

Among others, Supreme Court lawyers Priya Ahsan Chowdhury and Hamidul Mejbah, Daily Star Senior Associate Editor Najiba Bashar, Blast Director (Advice and Communication) Mahbuba Akhter, One Stop Crisis Center (OCC) lawyer Fahmida Akhter, and Cyber ​​Teens founder Sadat Rahman spoke at the meeting.
