Headline_English: Bangladesh needs a democratic renaissance, will it happen in the elections?
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh needs a democratic restoration right now. But British journalist James Orr has questioned whether the upcoming parliamentary elections can deliver it. He discussed this issue in an article titled ‘Bangladesh needs a democratic restoration: can elections deliver it’ published on the website of Chatham House, a UK-based international research institute, on Monday. 

The article says that Bangladesh is moving towards the parliamentary elections on February 12. Through this, the country is trying to end decades of ‘revenge politics’ and return to a democratic path. Nobel laureate Dr. Muhammad Yunus has been leading the interim government since the fall of then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August 2024. He has been under pressure to hold general elections before the start of the month of Ramadan in mid-February. 

Three-time Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was ousted from power in the face of weeks of student protests against the Awami League government accused of corruption. Analysts believe that the likely outcome of the February vote could be a return to power for the BNP. The party is led by its acting chairman, Tarique Rahman, who has been living in exile in London for nearly two decades. 

Referendum on July Charter 
The big question is whether the new leadership will be able to implement the promises made by the 25 parties in the July 2025 charter to restructure the country's electoral, constitutional and administrative structures. Public support for approving these reforms will be tested through a referendum in February. Chittig Bajpai, Senior Research Fellow for South Asia at Chatham House's Asia Pacific Program, said that what happened in Bangladesh last August, called the so-called 'rain revolution', has been called the country's second independence. But I think the reality will be more towards continuity than change. Because, in the cycle of violent revenge politics that we have seen in Bangladesh's history, there has been no movement towards genuine national reconciliation. We are only seeing the pendulum swing from one extreme to the other. 

According to the United Nations, at least 1,400 people died in the crackdown on protests last year, the worst violence in Bangladesh since the 1971 war of independence. The then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was forced to flee by helicopter to India just hours before protesters attacked her residence in the capital, Dhaka. In November, a special tribunal in Bangladesh sentenced Sheikh Hasina to death in absentia for crimes against humanity. Hasina is currently in exile under the protection of the Indian government, which is unlikely to extradite her. 

Sheikh Hasina’s sentencing comes months after her party, the Awami League, which has been in power for 15 years, was banned from participating in the next election. Many fear the decision could undermine the legitimacy of the election. Naomi Hossain, a professor at SOAS at the University of London, said the most likely outcome was for the BNP to win and for Jamaat-e-Islami to become the main opposition party. But the BNP is not very popular with the public; people are more likely to vote for them under duress. Those who remember them in the early 2000s know how violent and corrupt the party was. 

Last year, Bangladesh ranked 151st out of 180 countries on Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index. According to experts, before Hasina’s rule, state institutions were effective and separate from the executive branch, but that is no longer the case. 

The cycle of revenge politics 
Now, Bangladesh’s civil service and once-independent institutions that once ensured accountability have become irrelevant. The army, police and media have largely fallen into the hands of the Awami League’s authoritarian mindset. Chitigaze Bajpayee said, “Under Hasina’s government, we saw the repression of the BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami. Now we are seeing the purge of the Awami League. The question is, how do you break this cycle? While the interim government has a lot of positive intentions, there is a gap between their words and reality. The fear is that if the old political dynasty is re-established in power, people will become even more disillusioned. And politics will return to the way it was; Which is somewhat visible in the National Citizens Party (NCP). 

Bangladesh is currently in a vulnerable position economically. Although GDP has increased in the last two decades, the growth rate has slowed since the Corona pandemic. The country's natural resources are limited and all of its energy needs have to be imported. Recently, after reducing trade with India, they have leaned towards new strategic alliances with China, Pakistan and Turkey, which can be quite risky. 

Professor Naomi Hossain said that the legitimacy of Bangladeshi governments mainly depends on economic development. But the new government will have very little financial opportunity to help the poor and rebuild the economy. We do not know whether the BNP will follow the capitalist model of nepotism like the Awami League after winning the election. However, the only restraint on them may be the fear of another mass uprising. Apart from that, it is safe to say that there is nothing else.

Headline_English: Women are more vulnerable to cyber violence
Content_Enlish:
A discussion on 'Women and Technology: What to do to eliminate online violence and provide legal protection' was held at the Azimur Rahman Conference Room of the Daily Star Bhaban in the capital. December 17 Photo: Courtesy of Blast 
Violence against women and children online is increasing in line with the increase in internet usage in the country. During the mass uprising last year, 620 complaints of cyber violence against women and children were filed in 8 police stations and police superintendents' offices in the country in the 5 months from July to December. These complaints were filed in Sonadanga in Khulna, Kotwali in Rangpur, Kotwali and Kaunia in Barisal, Superintendent of Police Office in Gazipur, Fatulla in Narayanganj and Bhanga and Kotwali police stations in Faridpur. 

In addition, 56 cases of cyber violence were reported in the media in the 10 months from January to October this year. Of these, 54 victims were women. 

This information was shared at a meeting on ‘Women and Technology: What to do to end online violence and provide legal protection’ at the Azimur Rahman Conference Room of the Daily Star Bhaban in the capital on Wednesday. The meeting was organized by the ‘Cyber ​​Support for Women and Children’ (CSWC), a platform of 14 organizations. The convener of this platform is Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST). 

Speakers at the meeting said that women victims are not interested in reporting their complaints due to various reasons including fear of loss of dignity in the family and society, and the complicated and time-consuming process of cybercrime cases. Women who were at the forefront of the July coup and participated in politics are becoming victims of cyber violence in large numbers. At this time, the protection of digital rights is more necessary than ever. 

The speakers emphasized on law reform, effective implementation, training of law enforcement agencies, creating awareness on safe use of the internet, and providing services to the victims without any harassment after the incident.

During the meeting, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police of Women Support and Investigation Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Maqsuda Akhtar said that many victimized women do not know where to go for redress if they are victims of cyber violence. Publicity should be increased about the places where they can get help. Victimized women and children go through a lot of mental trauma after the incident, so they need counseling first. 

Maqsuda Akhtar said that victims will benefit if government and private organizations provide services under a network. 

Saeed Ahmed, founder and CEO of the Institute of Informatics and Development (IID), delivered the opening speech at the meeting. He said that women who were at the forefront of the July movement were not only removed later, but there were also incidents of online violence against them. But the government was not seen taking any stand against this. Recently, it was seen that the government has requested Google to remove content critical of the government. However, it should have said that content of online violence should be removed. 

Sharmin Khan, legal advisor at the International Center for Not for Profit Law (ICNL), said that while reporting a complaint, the victim should not have to face any uncomfortable situation or harassment. For this, an app can be arranged to report the complaint. So that the victimized women can report the complaint through the app within 24 hours of being a victim of online violence. 

Raisul Islam, in-charge of the 109 helpline run by the Department of Women and Child Affairs, said that this helpline receives 6 to 7 thousand calls every day complaining about violence against women and children. The number of calls on cyber violence is now increasing compared to before. 5 thousand 126 quick response teams are being formed across the country to prevent incidents of offline and online violence. 

Nova Ahmed, associate professor in the Department of Computer Science at North South University, said that the cause of concern about online violence is that it spreads quickly. Even if these incidents of violence are deleted, the footprint remains somehow or the other. 

Nova Ahmed also said that girls should be educated in technology without being afraid of it. Technology is changing so rapidly that it is necessary to keep the law amended repeatedly to keep pace with it. It is necessary to keep technologists involved in this process. 

The meeting was moderated by Blast Deputy Director (Victim Assistance and Arbitration) Tapsi Rabeya and the organization's Senior Research Officer Manisha Biswas. 

Among others, Supreme Court lawyers Priya Ahsan Chowdhury and Hamidul Mejbah, Daily Star Senior Associate Editor Najiba Bashar, Blast Director (Advice and Communication) Mahbuba Akhter, One Stop Crisis Center (OCC) lawyer Fahmida Akhter, and Cyber ​​Teens founder Sadat Rahman spoke at the meeting.

Headline_English: Tiler stabbed to death in Jatrabari
Content_Enlish:
Symbolic picture of stabbing 
A young man named Md. Faruk (19) was stabbed to death in the Kajla Nayanagar area of ​​Jatrabari in the capital. He was a tiler by profession. The incident took place in front of the Al Falah Mosque in the Nayanagar area at around 5:30 pm on Tuesday. 

After the stabbing, Faruk was rescued and brought to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) by his friend Md. Sajeeb. He said that a group of 8 to 10 people including Kalu, Sharif, Al Amin, and Ghalib from the Nayanagar area stabbed Faruk in the right side of the chest and waist and fled on the road. Later, Faruk was rescued and taken to the emergency department of the Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where the doctor on duty declared him dead. 

Faruk's village home is in Mayrapur village of Bancharampur upazila of Brahmanbaria district. Currently, he lives in a rented house with his family in the Nayanagar area of ​​Jatrabari. His father, Mohammad Alam, works as a night watchman in the Jatrabari area. Faruk was the fourth of five siblings. 

Mohammad Alam, the father of the deceased Faruk, said that his son is a tiler by profession. He did not go to work today, he stayed at home all day. 

Mohammad Alam said, "A friend of his named Alam called him outside in the afternoon. Shortly after he went out, I got the news that he had been stabbed. Later, when I got to the hospital, I heard that he had died. Faruk's friends killed him." 

In this regard, Mohammad Raju, the officer-in-charge of Jatrabari Police Station, told Prothom Alo that there was a fight between 15 to 20 youths in the evening. One of them died of a stab wound. He said, "We are not yet able to find out what caused the fight. The police have inspected the scene. Efforts are underway to arrest those involved.’

Headline_English: Narendra Modi's effigy burned at Dhaka University
Content_Enlish:
A group of students under the banner of 'Students Against Hegemony' burn an effigy of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in front of Madhur Canteen at Dhaka University. December 16 Photo: Prothom Alo
An effigy of the country's Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been burned at Dhaka University in protest against India's calling the Liberation War of Bangladesh a 'historic victory' on Victory Day. A group of students under the banner of 'Students Against Hegemony' held the program in front of Madhur Canteen of the university on Tuesday afternoon.

During the program, the students raised various slogans including 'Butcher Modi's mattress, light a fire together', 'Butcher Modi's two cheeks, beat his shoes to the beat', 'Bangladesh, Bangladesh, long live, long live', 'Delhi not, Dhaka Dhaka', 'Indian aggression, people will stop' and 'On this day, Abrar is remembered'.

One of the organizers, Riyad Jubah, told reporters, “The effigy of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been burned in protest against the naked interference in the Victory Day and tarnishing the day.”

Riyad Jubah also said, “India is also the sponsor of the misrule that has been going on in Bangladesh for the last 17 years.” He added, “This is our protest against India’s hegemony in Bangladesh.”

A sticker with Narendra Modi’s picture was also placed on the ground next to Madhur Canteen as part of the program.

Earlier in the afternoon, a group of university students held a shoe-throwing program at the picture of Ghulam Azam, who was convicted of war crimes, in front of the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (DUCSU) building.

At the beginning of the discussion, a special prayer was offered for the speedy recovery of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia. 

Mirza Fakhrul said that he still remembers a memory of his visit to China in 2002. At that time, Khaleda Zia introduced Tarique Rahman to the Chinese Prime Minister and said, 'He is my son'. At that time, the Chinese Prime Minister held Tarique Rahman's hands and said, 'Carry the flag of your father and mother'. The BNP Secretary General commented that Tarique Rahman is returning home on December 25 with that nationalist flag, the flag of independence and the flag of democracy. 

He said, ‘On that day, we will all wake up. Everyone must unite for democracy, for independence, for sovereignty.’ 

Highlighting concerns about the security of the fighters who participated in the July Movement, Mirza Fakhrul said that many are worried if a new government comes after the interim government. He said, ‘If we are elected by the people’s vote, InshaAllah, the security of the July fighters will be ensured. They will not be allowed to face any risk of insecurity.’ 

Citing the issue of 1971, the BNP Secretary General said that those who opposed independence in 1971 are the ones who want to destroy Bangladesh’s independence and democracy anew today. He said that the upcoming elections will decide whether the country will move forward on a liberal democratic path or go backward. 

Regarding the attack on Sharif Osman Hadi, Mirza Fakhrul said, "We strongly condemn the attack on our friend, colleague and son Hadi. There have been protests across the country. We have called for the immediate arrest of the killers." He claimed that the attacker identified as a terrorist is associated with the Awami League. 

In the discussion held under the chairmanship of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and moderated by Publicity Secretary Sultan Salahuddin Tuku, BNP Standing Committee members Abdul Moin Khan, Nazrul Islam Khan, Salahuddin Ahmed, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, Chairperson's Advisory Council member Abdus Salam, former Dhaka University Vice Chancellor Professor Anwar Ullah Chowdhury, Youth Dal's Nurul Islam Nayan, Swechchhasebak Dal's Rajib Ahsan and other leaders from various levels of the party spoke.

Headline_English: Former Jubo League leader arrested on his way back from buying nomination forms for parliamentary elections
Content_Enlish:
A former Jubo League leader has been arrested on his way home after buying nomination forms for the Magura-1 constituency in the 13th National Parliament election. He was arrested from the Atharokhad area of ​​the Magura-Sreepur regional road on Monday afternoon, police said. 

The arrested person has been identified as Qutubullah Hossain Mia. He is the chairman of the Srikol Union Parishad (UP) of Sreepur upazila and former president of the Upazila Jubo League. 

Talking to Qutubullah Hossain's family members, it was learned that Qutubullah collected nomination forms from the office of the Deputy Commissioner and Returning Officer on Monday afternoon to contest for an independent post in the 13th National Parliament election. The police arrested him on his way back to Sreepur from there. 

Confirming the truth of the incident, Magura Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md. Ashiqur Rahman told Prothom Alo that Qutubullah has been arrested as an accused (name not in the complaint) found during the investigation in a sabotage case that took place at Magura Sadar Police Station during the anti-discrimination student movement. The police had been looking for the man for a long time. 

However, the family of Qutubullah Hossain Mia has claimed that two cases were filed against him after August 5. He was out on bail after surrendering and serving time in prison in that case. His brother, former Upazila Parishad Chairman Shariatullah Hossain Mia, told Prothom Alo that Qutubullah performed his duties as UP Chairman in the Parishad yesterday and Sunday. He was moving around normally from home. He was out on bail in all the cases. Shariatullah believes that Qutubullah may have been arrested for collecting nomination forms. 

After collecting nomination forms from the Deputy Commissioner's office on Monday, Qutubullah Hossain told reporters that he has not held any party post for a long time. He has contested elections independently before. He wants to contest this time as an independent candidate as well. 

Qutubullah Hossain Mia was elected as the Chairman of Srikol UP in the UP elections in December 2021 as an independent candidate. He was elected as the President of Sreepur Upazila Jubo League in Magura in the 1990s. After the committee was dissolved, he never again held a position in the party. He contested as an independent candidate from Magura-1 constituency in the 2014 parliamentary elections and lost. His father, Akbar Hossain Mia, was the commander of the ‘Sripur Bahini’ formed during the Liberation War.

Content_Enlish:
As the price of gold increases in the world market, the price of commodities in the country is also going to increase again. This time, the price of a bhori will increase by about 1500 taka. As a result, the price of a bhori of good quality gold will stand at about 2 lakh 17 thousand taka. The new price will be effective from tomorrow, Tuesday, across the country. 

Bangladesh Jewelers Association (BAJUS) announced the decision to increase the price of gold on Monday night. The matter was announced in a press release signed by Dewan Aminul Islam, Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Association on Review and Determination of Gold Prices. Earlier, the price of gold per bhori increased by 3 thousand 452 taka last Sunday. 

According to the new price, from tomorrow, Tuesday, the price of a bhori of hallmarked 22-carat gold will increase by 2 lakh 17 thousand 67 taka. Today, Monday, it was sold for 2 lakh 15 thousand 597 taka. That means that the bhori has increased by 1 thousand 470 taka in one day. 

Meanwhile, the price of a bhori of hallmarked 21-carat gold will increase by 2 lakh 7 thousand 8211 taka, which was sold for 2 lakh 5 thousand 800 taka today, Monday. In this case, the price has increased by 1,411 taka per baht. Similarly, the price of 18-carat has increased by 1,248 taka per baht. It is sold at 1,76,395 taka today. The price will increase by 1,77,643 taka on Tuesday. 

The price of gold in the traditional system will increase by 1,47,899 taka on Tuesday, which is sold at 1,46,838 taka today. In this case, the price is increasing by 1,061 taka. 

Meanwhile, despite the increase in the price of gold, the price of silver remains unchanged. The price of a 22-carat baht of silver is now 4,572 taka.

Headline_English: Renata's preferred shares listed, trading begins a year after
Content_Enlish:
Renata's preference shares have been listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange's ATB. Renata's Managing Director Syed S. Kaiser Kabir, DSE Chairman Mominul Islam and senior officials of the two organizations were present at the ceremony organized on this occasion. Photo: Courtesy of DSE office in Nikunj, Dhaka today, Monday 
Renata preference or preference shares have been listed on the Alternative Trading Board (ATB) of Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE). The share was officially listed on the ATB today, Monday. A ceremony was organized by DSE on this occasion. 

DSE said that even though these shares are listed on the ATB, there will be no trading of these shares for the next one year. This is because there is a one-year sales ban or login imposed on Renata's preference shares. These six-year preference shares will be fully converted into shares at the end of their term. There will be no conversion of any shares in the first two years. From the third year, 25 percent will be converted into ordinary shares. The conversion price has been set at 475 taka. 

According to company sources, Renata has collected 325 crore taka from about 325 crore preference shares. Out of this, 301 crore taka was collected from Renata's existing ordinary shareholders. The remaining 24 crore taka was collected from institutional and individual investors. Each preference share was sold at a face value of 10 taka. Each lot of these preference shares had 190 shares. According to the rules, since these preference shares have a one-year login, there will be no trading of these shares in the stock market for the next one year. Trading will start after one year, in which case the market price of each preference share will be 1,900 taka. 

According to the DSE, the interest rate of these preference shares has been set at 15 percent. Then from the third year, 25 percent of the shares will be converted into ordinary shares. As a result, at the end of the third year, shareholders will receive interest or profit at a fixed rate against 75 percent of the preference shares they hold. After the remaining 25 percent of the preference shares are converted into ordinary shares, they will have the opportunity to sell them at the market price. 

What the guests said 
A program was organized at the DSE office at the DSE Tower in Nikunj, the capital, on Monday to mark the launch of trading in preference shares of pharmaceutical company Renata. Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) Chairman Mominul Islam, Acting Managing Director or MD Mohammad Asadur Rahman and Renata MD Syed S. Kaiser Kabir were the guests at the program. Kaiser Kabir is also the vice-president of the Bangladesh Pharmaceutical Industry Association. 

At the listing program, Renata MD Syed S. Kaiser Kabir said, "There are some businessmen in the country who take loans and do not repay them. However, most businessmen do not have this mentality. Still, all businessmen get a bad name because of a few businessmen. Apart from this, the number of people who deliberately default on loans is very limited. They can be counted by hand. Yet the matter is a risky reality. When there is a debt burden on my head, my head does not work properly. As a result, many creative thoughts are lost.' 

The industrialist opined that there should be alternatives when it comes to investing in the stock market. He said, it is not always the case that initial public offerings or IPOs have to be held. It is also important to have alternative financial products. The more alternative products there are in the market, the more opportunities there are to diversify the capital structure of the company. 

DSE Chairman Mominul Islam said at the event, 'The main stakeholders of the capital market are listed companies and investors. Unfortunately, we have not yet been able to fully develop the strong and trust-based relationship that the stock exchange needs to have with these two parties. However, we are trying to break the old culture and fulfill the desired goals and responsibilities more smoothly.' 

Syed S. Kaiser Kabir also said at the event, 'In the past, we were debt-free for most of the time. Especially there was no short-term debt, even long-term debt was very limited. There were some years when we did not have a single taka of short-term debt. That is why it was a very uncomfortable and difficult experience for all of us to suddenly be under such a huge debt. In any case, we wanted to get out of this debt burden. If we had issued rights shares, then there would have been a major change in the ownership of the majority shareholder. That is why we considered the option of preference shares. But it took 9 months for preference shares to come to the market. The dividend rate is determined based on the interest rate of treasury bonds, when this dividend rate was determined, the interest rate of treasury bonds was close to 15 percent. However, due to bureaucratic complications, preference shares were delayed in coming to the market. Even though the interest rate of treasury bonds decreased during this time, the dividend rate of our shares did not decrease. As a result, it became a very attractive financial product. Because, such a high rate of return is usually available in very few cases.'

Headline_English: Construction of student hall at Dhaka University to begin in first half of next year: Chinese ambassador
Content_Enlish:
Chinese Ambassador Yao Wen to inspect potential construction site of female students' hall at Dhaka University on Monday afternoon 
Chinese Ambassador Yao Wen to inspect potential construction site of female students' hall at Dhaka University on Monday afternoon Photo: Prothom Alo 
The preliminary design of the Bangladesh-China Friendship Hall project proposed to resolve the housing crisis of female students at Dhaka University (DU) has been presented. The construction work will begin in the first half of next year at an estimated cost of about 244 crore taka with Chinese financial assistance. 

Chinese Ambassador Yao Wen made this statement after inspecting the potential construction site at the university on Monday afternoon. 

After the inspection, Ambassador Yao Wen told reporters that this new residential building for female students will be an important milestone in Bangladesh-China relations. After long discussions and preparations, the project is moving towards implementation. 

Earlier, various aspects of the project were discussed in a view-sharing meeting with the Dhaka University administration. The expert team presented the initial design in a meeting with Treasurer Professor M Jahangir Alam Chowdhury. The meeting was attended by the university's Planning and Development Office, Engineering Department and concerned officials. 

Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan thanked the Chinese government for the project. He said that although the number of female students in the university is relatively high, residential facilities are limited. The construction of this hall will greatly reduce the housing crisis for female students. 

Niaz Ahmed Khan said that the possible name of the hall could be 'China-Bangladesh Friendship Memorial'. However, students' opinions will be taken on this matter.

Headline_English: UN Secretary-General calls Chief Advisor to express condolences
Content_Enlish:
Interim Government Chief Adviser Dr. Muhammad Yunus and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres 
Interim Government Chief Adviser Dr. Muhammad Yunus and UN Secretary-General Antonio GuterresFile Photo: BSS and Reuters 
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called Principal Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus to express his deep condolences and sympathy over the tragic death of six Bangladeshi peacekeepers in a drone attack in Sudan. 

In a phone call held at 7 pm Bangladesh time on Sunday, Guterres said, “I called to express my deepest condolences. I am deeply shocked by this incident.” At the same time, he expressed deep concern and anger over the attack. 

Expressing solidarity with Bangladesh, the UN Secretary-General requested the Principal Adviser to convey his condolences to the bereaved families of the slain peacekeepers. 

At that time, Professor Yunus also expressed deep sorrow over the death of the Bangladeshi peacekeepers. He also requested the UN to take measures to quickly transfer the injured soldiers to better quality hospitals for better treatment and to quickly repatriate the bodies of the deceased. 

Guterres informed the Principal Advisor that the injured peacekeepers were initially treated at a local hospital in Sudan and preparations were being made to transfer the seriously injured to a hospital with better medical facilities. 

Professor Yunus thanked the UN Secretary-General for his attention to the treatment and evacuation of the injured. 

During the phone call, Professor Yunus also recalled the UN Secretary-General's visit to Bangladesh last Ramadan. During this time, the two leaders also discussed the upcoming national elections in Bangladesh. 

The Principal Advisor assured the UN Secretary-General that the interim government is committed to holding free, fair, peaceful and festive elections on February 12. In response, Guterres expressed confidence that the elections in Bangladesh will be held smoothly.

Headline_English: CID collects DNA from 40 bodies in one week
Content_Enlish:
CID collects DNA from 40 bodies in a week 
The work of exhuming the bodies of 114 unidentified martyrs of the July mass uprising is underway under the management of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). In the last one week, 40 bodies have been exhumed. As per the rules, DNA samples of the bodies are being collected and autopsies are being conducted. The DNA samples of the unidentified martyrs will be matched with the relatives of the relatives to identify them. 

Special Police Superintendent of Media Branch of CID Jasim Uddin Khan confirmed this information on Sunday evening. The bodies are being exhumed from the graveyard adjacent to Rayerbazar Memorial in the capital since the morning of December 7. Dhaka District Administration, Bangladesh Police, Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) are cooperating in this work. 

CID says that forensic expert Luis Fondibrider came to Dhaka from Argentina through the United Nations Human Rights Office (OHCHR) and is leading the entire process. Apart from this, doctors from the forensic departments of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, Salimullah Medical College and Mugda Medical College Hospital are also participating in this activity. They have been trained before exhuming the bodies from the graves. 

According to the media wing of the CID, 40 bodies have been exhumed from the graveyard adjacent to the Rayerbazar Martyred Intellectuals Memorial in the last one week. Of these, 2 were exhumed on December 7, 4 on December 8, 6 on December 9, 6 on December 10, 7 on December 11, 7 on December 13 and 8 more on Sunday. 

In this regard, CID Special Police Superintendent Jasim Uddin Khan told Prothom Alo, "This is a very laborious task. The work is being done in full compliance with the international Minnesota protocol. After exhuming the bodies, their DNA samples are being collected, autopsied and reburied. According to the rules, DNA samples and autopsies of these bodies are being performed. This work will continue.’ 

11 relatives of seven martyred families have given DNA samples 
Regarding the collection of samples, Jasim Uddin Khan said, ‘So far, 11 relatives of seven martyred families have given their DNA samples to know their identities. After recovering all the unidentified bodies, their DNA samples will be matched with the samples of relatives to confirm their identities. Our main task now is to confirm their identities.’ 

According to CID information, so far, Sohel Rana (28), who went missing from Jatrabari in July, Rafiqul Islam (50), who went missing from Gopibagh, Md. Asadullah (31), who went missing from Uttara, Mahin Mia (25), who went missing from Mohammadpur, Faisal Sarkar (25), Rafiqul Islam (29), and Ahmed Jilani (30) have given DNA samples. 

The identities of 114 of those who were martyred during the July Uprising were unknown. These unidentified bodies were buried in a mass grave in the graveyard adjacent to the Rayerbazar Intellectuals' Memorial. The bodies were buried in July and August 2024 by Anjuman Mufidul Islam, a voluntary organization that buryes unclaimed bodies. 

According to the organization's calculations, they buried 80 bodies as unclaimed in July and 34 in August at the Rayerbazar graveyard. 

On August 4, Dhaka's Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Mohammad Mostafizur Rahman ordered the exhumation of the bodies following a police application to identify the bodies. The application was filed in court on behalf of the police by Mohammadpur Police Station Sub-Inspector Mahidul Islam.

Jagannath Hall administration removes satirical pictures of Golam Azam, Nizami 
The hall administration has removed the pictures of Jamaat leaders Golam Azam, Matiur Rahman Nizami and Quader Mollah, who were convicted of war crimes, painted on the street of Jagannath Hall. Photo: Samakal

On the occasion of Martyred Intellectuals Day on December 14, the hall administration has removed the pictures of Jamaat leaders Golam Azam, Matiur Rahman Nizami and Quader Mollah, who were convicted of war crimes, painted on the street of Jagannath Hall of Dhaka University. 

As part of the program titled 'Picture Exhibition and Tuli Anchade Droh' organized by the Jagannath Hall Sangsad on the occasion of Martyred Intellectuals' Day, the students drew these hateful portraits on the floor of the hall's road on Saturday night. 

According to the students, the hall administration removed the pictures citing security concerns. However, the hall administration says that the pictures were removed on the orders of the university authorities in the face of students' demands. 

The pictures were drawn on the road adjacent to Rabindra Bhavan and October Smriti Bhaban in the hall last Saturday night, which were removed around 10 am on Sunday. 

Hall Sangsad VP Pallab Barman said, Jagannath Hall was the most damaged in the Liberation War. On December 14, the best sons of the nation were killed in this hall. We organized a program called 'Tuli Anchade Droh' to commemorate that December 14. In that program, the students drew these pictures with the treachery within them. 

He also said that the hall administration has deleted the pictures for our safety. We reject their decision. The hall administration will be held accountable for this act. 

When asked, Jagannath Hall Principal Professor Debashish Pal said that ordinary students had drawn the pictures without the permission of the authorities. They had taken permission to display pictures of the Liberation War. However, as a result of drawing these pictures, the inauguration authorities came to their attention. Maybe the students told the administration. So in the face of the students' demands, the university authorities ordered me to delete them. 

He also said that I do not know who or what complained in the higher echelons of the university. I was ordered, so I deleted them. 

When asked, Proctor Saifuddin Ahmed said, we only asked what these are. We did not give any instructions.

Headline_English: Expenditure audits are becoming mandatory in state-owned companies
Content_Enlish:
The government has taken the initiative to make cost audit mandatory along with financial audit to increase transparency and efficiency in the financial management of state-owned companies. Despite the existence of the gazette, cost audit has not been implemented for a long time. Lack of cost audit is one of the reasons for the continuous losses of most state-owned companies. 

According to sources in the Ministry of Commerce, the financial audit of the company is carried out with priority on whether the accounts are correct. In this case, whether the costs are reasonable or not is not taken into account much. However, how reasonable the production and operating costs of government companies are, where is the waste, or in which sectors the costs are unusually high - these issues need to be reviewed in depth. If 'cost audit' is introduced, it will be possible to identify these weaknesses. 

Recently, an inter-ministerial meeting was held under the chairmanship of Commerce Secretary Mahbubur Rahman to update and amend the gazette regarding the implementation of 'cost audit' in state-owned companies listed on the capital market. According to the Companies Act, the Ministry of Commerce issued a gazette order in December 2001 to have all listed state-owned sugar mills audited by cost and management accountants. In addition, in January 2003, similar gazettes were issued for five companies in the energy and power sector and six in the jute sector. Then, in December 2009, gazettes were issued to conduct 'cost audits' of all state-owned chemical fertilizer factories, 12 pharmaceutical companies, and 42 textile companies. 

Although these gazettes were issued about 16 to 24 years ago, they have not been implemented yet. However, this time, an initiative has been taken to implement 'cost audits' to overcome the structural weaknesses of state-owned institutions if the efficiency of production costs and operating expenses is not verified. This will increase accountability in management by reforming the cost structure of state-owned companies. If the losses of the institutions are reduced, the financial pressure on the government will also be reduced to some extent. 

Commerce Secretary Mahbubur Rahman told Samakal that the opinions of the Finance Department, Financial Institutions Department, Industries Ministry, Dhaka Stock Exchange and Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission will be taken. Based on these opinions, an initiative will be taken to amend the gazette by directing the same type of cost audit for all public limited companies without specifying the name of the company. 

It is known that the number of companies listed in the sectors published in the previous gazette has increased. Again, in many cases, some companies are no longer listed. Therefore, overall importance is given to the issue of amending the gazette. According to the previous gazette, the number of companies in the energy and power sector in terms of cost audit has increased to 52. In addition, the number of companies in the pharmaceutical sector has increased to 34. Sugar mills have increased to 16 and companies in the textile sector have increased to 58. 

At the meeting, a representative of the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Bangladesh (ICMAB) said that cost audit ensures the cost transparency of the company, accountability, operational efficiency, proper use of government subsidies, fair tariff determination and cost-price analysis. Which plays an effective role in preventing waste, inefficiency and corruption and helps the company operate profitably and sustainably.

Headline_English: Policemen play cricket at the police club
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Police Club has made a good start in first division cricket by defeating Old DOHS, which once played in the Premier Cricket League, by 8 wickets. Team cricketer Shahadat Hossain faced the media after the match at the Sher-e-Bangla Stadium in Mirpur today. He gave the surprising information right away. 

Police Club does not mean that everyone who plays for them has to be a policeman. Where do the police have time to play when they are busy with their professional duties? But Shahadat revealed the opposite information. Out of the 18 members of the squad of Bangladesh Police Club, the first division cricket team, 10 serve in the police. To a question, this bowling all-rounder, who took 1 wicket for 12 runs in 3 overs, said, "Eight of our players are civilians, the rest of us 10 are police." 

Shahadat, who works as a Naik in the Industrial Police, said that they run both work and play together. Shahadat has also played cricket in the Chittagong League since childhood. There is no player quota in the police, nor is there any separate allowance for playing. They are players despite being police officers due to their own interest and ability. Shahadat says, 'I do duty as well as play sports. When our camp starts, our sirs release us to play.' Of course, even when playing cricket, professional responsibility comes first for them, 'Our duty comes first. We are dedicated to protecting the country and the general public of the country. Then comes our game.'

Crystal Palace 0-3 Manchester City 

First half of the match against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park. Erling Haaland was only able to touch the ball twice in the opponent's box at this time. But for a striker like Holland, two opportunities to touch the ball are enough to score. 

That was seen in the 41st minute. Manchester City right-back Mateusz Nunes crossed from the right edge into the Crystal box. The target was Holland, who was standing inside the box. City did not sit still, capitalizing on this goal scored against the flow of the game. Pep Guardiola's team scored two more goals in the 69th and 89th minutes after the break. In the 69th minute, the Crystal goalkeeper could not stop Phil Foden's left-footed shot from outside the box after receiving a pass from Ryan Sherki. City took a 2-0 lead. 

In the 88th minute, City's Brazilian winger Savino entered the Crystal box with the ball. Sensing danger, Crystal goalkeeper Henderson was forced to foul him. The referee blew the penalty whistle. Haaland scored his second goal of the match in the 89th minute from a spot kick. The Norwegian star scored 37 goals in 27 matches for City this season and scored 5 more goals. With this 3-0 win, City has 34 points from 16 matches. They are 2 points behind Arsenal, who are at the top with 36 points in the same match.

Headline_English: Private bank officials angry over separate incentive bonus policies in public and private banks
Content_Enlish:
Separate policies for providing incentive bonuses have been issued for government-owned and private sector banks. 

Under the new policy, government banks will be able to give an incentive bonus to employees with the permission of the ministry even if they are at a loss. However, private banks will not be able to give incentive bonuses to employees even if they make a profit with special discounts. This decision has angered officials of private banks. However, since it is a decision of the central bank, they did not agree to comment directly. 

The incentive bonus is usually equal to one month's basic salary. The country's government and private banks give a maximum of seven incentive bonuses. In the past, some banks have a record of giving incentive bonuses of more than Tk 20 million to an official. In view of these incidents, Bangladesh Bank has issued several notifications and imposed stricter rules on the provision of incentive bonuses. 

The Financial Institutions Division of the Ministry of Finance issues the policy for public sector banks. On the other hand, Bangladesh Bank sets the policy for private sector banks. 

The guidelines of the Financial Institutions Department state that the net profit of the bank will be determined by adjusting the provisions for loans and advances from the operating profit and the provisions for depreciation and appreciation of investments and other assets. Then the amount of the bonus will be determined based on various indicators. Bank officials and employees will not receive more than three incentive bonuses. However, even if the bonus is not due, the ministry can consider the demand for a bonus. This guideline will also be effective for the incentive bonus for 2024. 

On the other hand, the recently issued policy of Bangladesh Bank states that no private bank can give incentive bonuses to employees if it does not make a net profit. In addition, bonuses cannot be given even if there is a deficit in capital and safety reserves. Even if any delay facility is given, it cannot be taken into account in the calculation of profit. Even if the central bank takes a delayed discount facility on safety reserves, incentive bonuses cannot be given. Industry stakeholders believe that this will block the incentive bonuses of most banks. 

The policy further states that bonuses can be given only if the net profit determined on the basis of actual income and expenditure is achieved. No incentive bonus can be given from accumulated profit. In addition, there must be visible progress in the collection of classified and written-off loans and real improvement in various banking indicators. 

Several officials of private banks told Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity that despite the large deficits in the security reserves and capital of public banks, they have been given the opportunity to give incentive bonuses. However, many private banks make profits on the condition of adjusting these deficits later. If the new rules come into effect, most private banks will no longer be able to give incentive bonuses. 

Currently, many banks give incentive bonuses the day after the end of the year. Some others give bonuses to employees by showing profits with various discounts. As a result of the new directive, these bonuses will practically stop in private banks. According to people involved in the sector, only a handful of bank employees will receive incentive bonuses.

The father of child Sajid, who died after falling into an abandoned hole in a deep tube well in Tanore, Rajshahi, complained after his son's body was recovered that it was a negligence-induced death. He wants justice. However, he does not want to file a case now. Meanwhile, the person who dug the hole, Kashir Uddin, has been in hiding since the incident. He dug the hole illegally without taking the permission of the Upazila Irrigation Committee. 

Last Wednesday afternoon, child Sajid fell into an abandoned hole in a deep tube well on Kashir Uddin's land in Koelhat Purba Para village of the upazila. After a suffocating operation of about 32 hours by the fire service, Sajid's body was recovered from 50 feet below the ground on Thursday night. Sajid (2) is the son of Rakibul Islam of that village. 

When contacted on Saturday evening, Rakibul Islam said, ‘We have decided not to file a case. Allah has taken all our words and Allah has taken the property of Allah.’ After Sajid’s death, he had accused Kashir Uddin of negligence and sought justice. When reminded, Rakibul said, ‘Okay, brother. The meaning of saying this is so that the whole country should be careful about this. So that no one else makes this mistake. The way my child went, brother, if everyone is aware a little earlier; then, God willing, this loss will not happen. So that ten more people can learn a lesson from me.’ 

When asked if there was any pressure not to file a case, Rakibul said, ‘There is no pressure on me. Because the whole country is on our side. God willing, the police administration is on our side. There is no pressure.’ When asked if Kashir Uddin had said anything, he said, ‘No, brother. He has not come yet. I have not been in touch with him yet. He did not contact me.'

Headline_English: Why a 'new Syria' is dangerous in Israel's eyes
Content_Enlish:
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa speaks on the first anniversary of the fall of Bashar al-Assad. Damascus, Dec 8 (Reuters) 
The fall of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in December 2024 was not just a regime change. Assad's fall marked a major turning point in Middle Eastern geopolitics. 

Syria has gradually moved back from the brink of collapse over the past year, but the country remains fragile. Under President Ahmed al-Sharaa's leadership, Syria is no longer an internationally isolated state. The country is moving towards internal stability, regional reintegration and global recognition. However, major challenges remain. The number of regional powers standing by Syria is limited, and several are trying to destabilize the situation there. Israel is a major obstacle in this. 

Syria has seen major changes in the past year. The political and security situation has improved compared to the brutal end of Assad's rule. Nearly three million Syrians have returned to their homeland, including nearly one million refugees and 1.8 million internally displaced people. This reflects their cautiously growing confidence in the future. 

Read more 
Why Israel is plotting to break up Syria 
07 March 2025 
Why Israel is plotting to break up Syria 
The Assad government’s pragmatic foreign policy has prioritized de-escalation, stabilization, and reconstruction, which has helped to quickly normalize regional and international relations. Domestically, the government has emphasized moving from revolutionary legitimacy to institutional legitimacy. As part of this, a general amnesty has been declared for members of the military who were forced to join the military during Assad’s rule. At the same time, while maintaining central control, rapid institutional reforms have been introduced, including a constitutional declaration and the formation of a new parliament. 

In the area of ​​security, the government has taken steps to establish absolute control over all forces. The infamous Mukhabarat intelligence agency was abolished and replaced by the General Security Service. In addition, the process of building a national army by integrating various rebel groups has been strengthened. 

At the regional level, Syria has successfully re-engaged with the Arab world. In this regard, Qatar and Saudi Arabia have emerged as allies of the new government. In the first year of coming to power, President Shara made several unprecedented foreign trips. Among them, the visit to the United States was historic. He also held high-level meetings with France and Russia. As a result of these diplomatic initiatives, the path to the lifting of Western sanctions was paved and Syria's reintegration into the international arena was further strengthened. 

Read more 
Is Syria presenting a new Islamism 
March 11, 2025 
Is Syria presenting a new Islamism 
Turkey is one of the countries that is playing an important role in building a new and stable Syria. After the fall of the Assad regime, Ankara's relationship with Damascus has developed into a very important partnership. The basis of this relationship is border security, economic development, refugee management and addressing common threats. 

In this context, Turkey has become the most important external force influencing the new Syria. In addition to providing political, economic and security assistance, Turkey has made a significant contribution to preventing the collapse of the Syrian state and maintaining stability by playing a strong role in the lifting of international sanctions. 

Nevertheless, the Syrian leadership faces difficult challenges. The responsibility of rebuilding a country devastated by a long war is enormous. The cost of reconstruction is estimated to reach a trillion dollars, and millions of Syrians are still displaced. As a result, the scale of the humanitarian and economic crisis is very deep. 

Over the past year, Israel has carried out several airstrikes and supported minority groups. The aim is to weaken the new government and leave Syria permanently disabled. Iran's influence has diminished since the fall of the Assad regime, but it may try to exert influence again. 
The situation is also complex on political and social levels. The fall of the Assad regime has left some influential minority groups with long-standing privileges. This has created a group that is trying to undermine the new system under various pretexts. They are trying to regain their lost position by promoting concepts such as democracy, decentralization, and inclusive governance. 

Externally, Israel remains the most determined and dangerous power. Tel Aviv is pursuing a strategy of turning the new Syria into a failed state so that it can maintain regional dominance and perpetuate its occupation of the Golan Heights. 

Over the past year, Israel has carried out several airstrikes and supported minority groups. The aim is to weaken the new government and leave Syria permanently incapacitated. Iran’s influence has diminished since the fall of the Assad regime, but it may try to exert influence again.

Europe has no say in Syria

Europe has no say in Syria 
Looking ahead to 2026, Syria's future will be determined by the tension between internal and external rival forces. Just as there is little chance of any sudden major breakthrough towards complete stability and prosperity, there is also relatively little risk of a return to full-scale civil war. The most realistic scenario is to move forward gradually despite various obstacles. 

The relationship between Damascus and Ankara will remain the cornerstone of Syria's future. However, everyone, from the Syrian people to international observers, must have realistic expectations. The road ahead will be long, difficult and risky. Patience and strong commitment are essential on this journey, as well as vigilance against those forces, both internal and external, who want to prevent Syria from moving towards a new era.

Headline_English: Police release photo of suspect in Osman Hadi shooting, seek information
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has released a photo of a suspect in the shooting of Osman Hadi, an independent candidate for Dhaka-8 constituency and spokesperson of Inqilab Manch. The DMP said that he has been initially identified after analyzing the CCTV footage of the scene. The police have sought cooperation in providing information about the suspect. 

The DMP gave this information in a press release on Saturday morning. A press release sent by Deputy Police Commissioner of the Media and Public Relations Department of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Muhammad Talebur Rahman, said that Osman Hadi, spokesperson of Inqilab Manch, was seriously injured in an attack by motorcycle-riding miscreants in the Bijoynagar Box Culvert area of ​​the capital on Friday. Dhaka Metropolitan Police is conducting a vigorous operation in the capital to arrest the attackers. 

The release said that the person in the photo has been initially identified after analyzing the CCTV footage of the scene. Dhaka Metropolitan Police is desperately searching for him. 

DMP said that if you have any information about the person or find him, you are requested to inform the police immediately through the following mobile number or 999. The identity of the finder will be kept confidential and an appropriate reward will be given. 

The police have asked to provide information to the following numbers: 01320040080 of the Motijheel DC and 01320040132 of the Paltan OC. 

On Friday afternoon, Osman Hadi was shot at on Box Culvert Road in Bijoynagar in the capital. He was first taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and later to Evercare Hospital. Doctors said that his condition is critical. 

According to eyewitness accounts and CCTV footage, Hadi and two others were traveling in a battery-powered rickshaw; then the miscreants on a motorcycle shot him and fled. 

The reason for Hadi's shooting has not yet been confirmed. However, those concerned say, 'The person seen firing in the CCTV footage participated in the election campaign with Hadi since morning.'

Headline_English: Law enforcement officers will be able to enter any place, including polling stations: Home Affairs Advisor
Content_Enlish:
Law enforcement officers will be able to enter any place, including polling stations, at any time to prevent any attempt to disrupt the law and order situation or disrupt the election, Home Affairs Advisor Lieutenant General (Retd.) Md. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury said. 

He made these remarks while briefing reporters after the 19th meeting of the Advisory Council Committee on Law and Order at the conference room of the Home Ministry at the Secretariat on Monday. 

The advisor said that all forces have been instructed to work more actively and in a coordinated manner at the field level to control the law and order situation during the election period. The meeting has been instructed to take such measures to maintain the law and order situation during political programs and campaigns ahead of the election. 

He also called on all concerned, including the general public, to cooperate in ensuring the election environment and to comply with the election code of conduct. 

The Home Affairs Advisor said that if the roads are blocked and public suffering is caused, the law enforcement agencies will take appropriate measures immediately. No concessions will be made in this regard. He said that in order to keep the overall law and order situation in the country normal and under control, instructions have been given to increase intelligence surveillance nationwide and to further strengthen the activities of the law enforcement agencies, to be more active and vigilant, and to coordinate intelligence information and data of all forces. 

Md. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury said that the final charge sheet will be issued soon in the case filed in the murder of Sharif Osman bin Hadi, a frontline fighter of the July uprising. He said that political parties should be careful so that fascist agents or saboteurs disguised as collaborators do not infiltrate different political parties. 

The Home Affairs Advisor said that political parties should also be careful so that saboteurs do not take advantage of mutual accusations of political parties or get away with it. 

The advisor said that 14,569 people have been arrested in the Operation Devil Hunt Phase-2 operation launched on December 13, 2025, till January 4. In addition, 201 firearms, 1541 rounds of bullets, 566 rounds of cartridges, 165 indigenous weapons, grenades, mortar shells, gun powder, fireworks, bomb-making materials, etc. have been recovered in this operation. During this time, a total of 33,804 people, including 19,235 people, have been arrested on the basis of cases and warrants. 

He further said that as part of Devil Hunt Phase-2, the number of check posts and patrols has been increased significantly so that terrorists and miscreants do not get through and the recovery of illegal and looted weapons increases further. 

The meeting advised drivers to drive cautiously in foggy weather and advised the transport owners and workers' associations in this regard. The meeting reiterated the government's firm commitment to maintaining communal harmony. The meeting also discussed in detail the prevention of rumors and propaganda through social media and the avoidance of provocative statements. In addition, the meeting discussed in detail the issues of ensuring security on the Bangladesh-Myanmar border, strict surveillance to curb smuggling, drugs and other crimes, and maintaining peace in the hilly regions.

The EC has written to the police to provide special security to Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin, four election commissioners and the senior secretary of the Election Commission (EC) Secretariat. At the same time, it has been asked to ensure security in the EC's field offices across the country. 

EC sources said that the EC gave this instruction to the police in a separate letter today, Saturday. 

In the letter to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner, it was said that the schedule for the 13th National Parliament election was issued on December 11. There is already police security including a car for the security of the CEC. An additional police security including an additional car has been asked to be provided for the CEC during the election period. 

In addition, police security including a car has been asked to be provided for the residences, office travel and round-the-clock security of the four election commissioners and the EC secretary. 

Another letter to the Inspector General of Police has asked to ensure overall security and safety of the EC field offices across the country. It says that the schedule for the 13th National Parliament election has been issued on December 11. After the schedule was issued, miscreants set fire to the Lakshmipur District Election Office and the Mathbaria Upazila Election Office in Pirojpur. 

In this context, the letter has asked to deploy the required number of police forces in the EC field offices across the country.

Headline_English: Cancer, 36 surgeries—'Bezbaba' to tell the story of returning to singing
Content_Enlish:
As diverse as Sumon's musical career is, his personal story is also eventful 
As diverse as Sumon's musical career is, his personal story is also eventfulMashranga Television 
There are some names in the history of band music in Bangladesh who are memorable not only for their music but also for their life struggles, inflexible mentality and fight against time. Saidus Salehin Khaled Sumon is one such name. To his fans and listeners, he is 'Bezbaba Sumon'. As the lead vocalist and bassist of the band Orthhin, he has been leaving his mark on Bengali band music for more than three decades. 

As diverse as Sumon's musical career is, his personal story is also eventful. He started his journey towards band music before he finished school. He developed a penchant for guitar and bass while studying at Government Laboratory High School. The cultural programs of the school at that time, chats with friends and band music of the cassette era - all of this gradually formed a Sumon. 

From Feelings to Warphase 
Sumon often recalls the incident that turned his life around after the SSC exams. Holding the hand of a friend, he reached James. James was busy at that time, but he asked a new boy to play bass. After listening to him for a few minutes, James decided to join Feelings. Sumon worked as a bassist in the Feelings band from 1990 to 1993. This time introduced him to the professional music world. 

As diverse as Sumon's musical career is, his personal life story is also eventful 
Sumon's musical career is diverse, his personal life story is also eventfulMachranga Television 
After that, he played in In Dhaka, Sweet Venom, Rock Brigade, Jolly Roger, Shabd - and even once in Warphase. When he was studying at the Government Laboratory School, he was fascinated by the way Kamal of Warphase played the bass at a function, and Kamal became his biggest inspiration. 

From ‘Suman and Meaningless’ to ‘Meaningless’ 
In 1997, while he was in Warphase, the solo album ‘Suman and Meaningless’ was released. The album received a great response from the audience at that time. This album laid the foundation for the future ‘Meaningless’ band. In 1999, Suman left Warphase and formed his own band—Meaningless. In a very short time, the band became one of the most influential rock bands of the nineties. Meaningless’s four studio albums, as well as Suman’s solo and double albums, gave a different language to Bengali band music—where the mix of rock, satire, protest, and personal feelings is clear. 

Bezbaba Suman 
Bezbaba SumanPhoto: Prothom Alo 
Illness, accident, and return 
In 2011, Suman’s life came under a big shock. He was diagnosed with stomach cancer. After long treatment, surgery and mental struggle, he eventually defeated the cancer. But the danger did not end there. He was seriously injured in a road accident. He had to undergo one surgery after another all over his body—about 36 surgeries in total. Many times, he thought that he might never return to the music stage. But Suman did not give up. He gradually returned to music, to concerts, and in front of the audience. 

Nineties Story and ‘Bezbaba’ 
Recently, Suman looked back on his musical career on Maasranga Television’s ‘Nineties Music Story’ program. Written by Riyad Shimul and produced by SM Humayun Kabir, the program brought up the days of cassette tapes, the Elephant Road chat, the story of playing the guitar with his teeth, and the interesting history behind the name ‘Bezbaba’. Talking about the nineties, Suman said, ‘After the SSC exams were over, a friend took me to James Bhai. He said to play bass. After playing a little, he said to join the feelings. Then I thought - is this true!' This special episode is going to be aired on Maasranga Television on Saturday, December 13 at 12 midnight. Where viewers will once again see the story, struggle and indomitable return of 'Baez Baba' Suman.

Headline_English: Nobel laureate human rights activist Nargis Mohammadi arrested in Iran
Content_Enlish:
Nargis Mohammadi wins 2023 Nobel Peace Prize Photo: AFP 
Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Nargis Mohammadi has been arrested. She was arrested by Iranian security and police forces on Friday. Nargis's brother Mehdi reported this, the 'Nargis Foundation' reported. 

The Paris-based Nargis Foundation said that Iranian security and police forces arrested Nargis Mohammadi. She was arrested at a memorial service for lawyer Khosro Alikordi. Khosro is a well-known Iranian lawyer. His body was recently recovered from his office. 

The British media outlet The Guardian reported that Nargis's husband, Taghi Rahmani, who lives in Paris, also confirmed his wife's arrest. He wrote in a post on the social media X that Nargis was arrested at a memorial service for Khosro Alikordi in the eastern Iranian city of Mashhad. Another top Iranian human rights activist, Sepideh Bahlian, was also arrested with her.

Nargis Mohammadi won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2023. She spent most of two decades in Tehran's Evin Prison. 

Nargis was sentenced to a total of 31 years for activities against national security and spreading propaganda. Nargis was also vocal about human rights while in prison. Nargis underwent surgery in November 2024. The surgery was to remove a tumor-like lesion from a bone in her lower right leg. Doctors suspected it was cancer. The month after the surgery, authorities suspended her sentence for three weeks. It was then thought that Nargis would have to return to prison soon. However, she did not have to go to prison again.

Headline_English: Another shooting in Nabinagar, Brahmanbaria, youth injured
Content_Enlish:
A young man named Sabbir Hossain alias Jalal was shot by miscreants in Nabinagar upazila of Brahmanbaria. The shooting incident took place at around 6:15 pm on Friday in the field of the landlord's house at Kalibari intersection in the municipality.

The shot Sabbir Hossain (20) is the son of Helal Mia of Shahbazpur village in Shyamgram union of the upazila. Currently, Sabbir lives with his family in the Majhikara area of ​​ward number 5 of Nabinagar municipality. He is an ambulance driver by profession.

Incidentally, on the night of October 24 this year, BNP leader Mofizur Rahman (52) was shot by unknown assailants in Adalatpara of Nabinagar municipality. He was the former joint general secretary of Nabinagar upazila BNP and former convener of the upazila Jubo Dal. He was shot twice in the back and below the waist. Then on November 1, two people were shot dead and two others were injured in a clash between two parties over dominance in Nabinagar upazila.

It was learned from the police and local people that at around 6:15 pm today, a gunfight broke out between two groups of miscreants in the Zamindarbari field in Kalibari area. Panic spread around due to the loud sound of gunfire. Local businessmen in Kalibari area started closing their shops. At that time, Sabbir was shot. Local people rescued him in a serious condition and took him to the emergency department of Nabinagar Upazila Health Complex. He was given primary treatment there and sent to Dhaka for advanced treatment.

Habibur Rahman, the resident medical officer of Nabinagar Upazila Health Complex, told Prothom Alo that Sabbir, who was shot, was brought to the health complex at around 6:30 pm on Friday. He was shot in the left rib on his chest. He was sent to Dhaka for advanced treatment after receiving primary treatment.

Helal Mia, the father of the injured Sabbir, told reporters, "I heard that he went to the Zamindarbari field. I came to the hospital after hearing that my son was shot there. I don't know why my son went there.'

Sabbir Hossain, who was shot, said, 'Recently, there was a fight and argument with the locals over a verbal dispute. I complained to the people of the area about the matter. The people on the other side did not accept arbitration. In that incident, people from the Bashgari area of ​​Mirzachar in Raipura upazila of the neighboring Narsingdi district opened fire this evening. I could not recognize who they were.'

Headline_English: Metrorail reopens after 5-hour shutdown due to workers' strike
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka Metrorail File Photo 
The metro rail was closed for five hours on Friday due to the workers' all-out strike. The workers withdrew from the strike after receiving a promise to fulfill their demands during the talks. The authorities said that the metro rail resumed operations shortly after 8 pm. 

The metro rail from Dhaka's Uttara to Motijheel route started operating from 3 pm on Friday, a holiday. The last train left Motijheel at 9:40 pm. 

A section of the regular officers and employees of the company had announced a all-out strike from 7 am on Friday to protest against the breach of promise in formulating independent service rules. Due to this, the trains did not leave Uttara at 3 pm and Motijheel at 3:20 pm on Friday as scheduled. This put passengers in trouble. Traffic jams were also seen in the capital Dhaka on the day of the strike. 

Prothom Alo's associate editor Al Amin Sajeeb went to the metro rail station at 3:45 pm to go to Karwan Bazar from Sheorapara in the capital. He said, when he went, he saw that the collapsible gate to climb the stairs was locked. Many people were standing waiting to get on the station. Many were also standing on the road. But there were no vehicles accordingly. 

Sajeeb said, after not getting buses, CNG and app-powered motorcycles, he took a rickshaw to Karwan Bazar at a high fare. 

Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL) is responsible for the construction and operation of the metro rail in Dhaka. Sources from the company said that the protesters have been stationed in front of the metro rail head office in Diabari since Friday morning. After discussions with the authorities at one stage, the protesters withdrew from the strike when they were promised to approve the service rules at a special board meeting of DMTCL on December 18. The metro rail started operating at night after that. 

However, the company had announced on Thursday night that the metro rail would run as per the scheduled schedule on Friday. But the protesters did not accept the authorities' announcement. 

According to DMTCL sources, the protesters also took a stand in front of the Metro Rail head office last Thursday to demand their demands. At that time, they raised various slogans to demand their demands. 

At that time, the authorities said that the separate service rules would be taken up for approval in a special board meeting on December 18. In that case, the demands of the protesters are being met. In such a situation, there is no more justification for protesting. Therefore, everyone was asked to perform their duties according to the rules from Friday. Most of the protesters agreed with such an announcement. However, some demanded that the rules be approved by Friday. 

On Thursday night, the protesters issued a notice stating that the service rules had not been approved by December 11 as per their demands. Therefore, the strike will continue for an indefinite period from Friday. No passenger service will be provided during this time. The protesters will take a stand in front of the Metro Rail head office from the morning. 

DMTCL's public relations officer, Jahidul Islam, told Prothom Alo that the strike was withdrawn after the assurance that the service rules would be approved by the board on December 18. However, the issue was resolved on Thursday night. Passengers suffered due to the strike on Friday. The authorities are sorry for this.

Headline_English: Mahfuz, Asif in talks to join NCP, take up posts
Content_Enlish:
It is not yet certain whether Mahfuz Alam and Asif Mahmud Sajib Bhuiyan, who left the posts of advisors to the interim government, will join the NCP. There are rumors that they will join the People's Rights Council and become candidates for the BNP alliance. However, according to political sources, the two former advisors will join the NCP if they get the expected rank. 

Last Wednesday evening, the two young advisors submitted their resignations to Chief Advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus. Mahfuz and Asif formally left the government by attending the meeting of the Advisory Council a few hours before the announcement of the schedule for the 13th parliamentary election yesterday. 

There have been rumors for two days about which party the two student leaders of the 24th mass uprising that toppled Sheikh Hasina will join. NCP senior joint convener Ariful Islam Adeeb told Samakal that they will join the party formed by the student leadership of the uprising. However, they are taking a few days to be free from government duties. Everything will become clear in a few days. 

Nahid Islam, another leader of the coup, left the post of advisor last February and took over the responsibility of the founding convener of the NCP. According to NCP sources, Asif wants to be assured of important organizational responsibilities to join the party. He wants the rank of convener next. Mahfuz, who is reluctant to leave the post of advisor, wants an important position in the party even if he does not want organizational power. As a result, joining the NCP is confirmed. 
Samakal could not get the statements of Mahfuz and Asif. The day before the resignation, on Tuesday night, Gana Adhikar President Nurul Haque Noor and General Secretary Rashed Khan held a meeting at Asif's house in Mantripara on Hair Road. Rashed Khan said that Asif has been invited to join Gana Adhikar. He was previously the leader of the student organization of Gana Adhikar. Discussions are underway. However, no decision has been made. 

A senior leader of BNP's ally party Gana Adhikar told Samakal that it is not possible to bring Asif into the party with the post of president or general secretary. It has been proposed to him that if he joins Gana Adhikar, he will be made the BNP alliance's candidate for the Dhaka-10 constituency. However, Asif did not agree to this. He wanted to go directly to BNP. However, this possibility is now slim as the party is not moving forward with the discussion. As a result, the possibility of Asif joining Gana Adhikar is also slim. 
NCP leaders told Samakal the same information. According to them, Asif, who has experience of serving as an advisor to three government ministries for about 16 months, will start election activities in the Dhaka-10 constituency by now. Mahfuz Alam, who is in charge of the Information and Broadcasting Ministry, is not interested in the election. Earlier, he was involved in intellectual work rather than processions and rallies in student politics. He wants to remain in the same role in the future. 

Government and political sources said that Mahfuz Alam, who is in charge of the Information and Broadcasting Ministry, was not willing to resign. The student leader, known as the 'mastermind' of the July uprising, wanted to remain in the government without holding elections. But he was informed by his chief advisor and the government that he would have to resign to keep the government's neutrality in the election period unquestioned. Yesterday, advisor Syeda Rizwana Hasan said that the two advisors resigned to keep the government's neutrality unquestioned. 

According to multiple sources, even at midnight on Tuesday, Mahfuz Alam expressed his desire to remain in the advisory position until the next government hands over responsibility without resigning. But due to advice from various parties and the fear of being removed from the government, he agreed to resign on Wednesday morning. 
A senior NCP leader told Samakal that Mahfuz was not interested in the elections, not yet. But due to the situation, he will have to contest the elections in the end. He will be a candidate in Lakshmipur-1 constituency. If he joins the party, he will get the NCP's nomination. That is why the candidate for Lakshmipur-1 constituency has not been announced. 
Mahfuz is strongly opposed to the electoral agreement with Jamaat. There was also talk of him joining the BNP and becoming a candidate for the paddy field. But the situation has changed due to his resignation. In this reality, he will also have to come to the NCP in the end. The two advisors may be evaluated and new posts may be created or important posts may be given.

Headline_English: A century-old airport is becoming a $30 billion city
Content_Enlish:
All around are fields. A runway and a building in the middle. The airport was built by the famous aircraft manufacturer 'De Havilland Canada' about a hundred years ago. The airport has been abandoned for a long time. Now a huge city is being built there. It will not cost much. The cost is estimated at 30 billion US dollars. 

The name of the airport is Downsview Airport. It is located northwest of Toronto, Canada. During World War II, warplanes were manufactured there on a large scale. Then, in the early 1990s, another aircraft and spacecraft manufacturer named 'Bombardier' ​​bought the airport. However, they also closed down their business there in 2024. 

Then, in early 2026, the construction of the city will begin at the airport. More than 50,000 people will be able to live in this city on 370 acres of land. There will be green trees and open spaces in the city's 75 acres. In the first phase, 3,000 houses will be built by 2031. After 30 years of construction, this will be one of the largest housing projects in North America. 

The runway will not be damaged during the construction of the city. It will be in the center of the city. This runway will connect seven areas of the city. Each area will have its own educational institutions, libraries, shops and community centers. Drake Goring, head of Northcrest Development, the company responsible for this project, said that this runway will maintain the airport's heritage in the city. 

The infrastructure for storing aircraft at the airport will not be demolished either. Instead, it will be renovated and commercial buildings will be built. Various activities, including film production, will be held there. Grass and trees will be planted on the roofs keeping the environment in mind. According to Drake Goring, if the facilities at the airport can be reused without being demolished, carbon emissions will be reduced and nature will be saved.
