Headline_English: Islamic banks repay Tk 590 crore on third day without borrowing
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has launched the 'Islamic Banks Liquidity Facility (IBLF)' facility for Sharia-based banks from Monday. After the launch of this facility, five Islamic banks in the country borrowed Tk 5,247 crore in the next two days (Tuesday and Wednesday). However, on the third day (Thursday), instead of borrowing new money, those banks repaid Tk 5.90 billion. As a result, the total borrowing amount of Islamic banks on Thursday decreased to Tk 4,657 crore. 

It is learned that under the 'Islamic Banks Liquidity Facility (IBLF)', Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Union Bank, Social Islami Bank, First Security Islami Bank and Global Islami Bank borrowed a total of Tk 5,247 crore from Bangladesh Bank for a short term of 14 days in the first two days. Of this, Tk 3,995 crore was borrowed on Tuesday. And Tk 1,252 crore was borrowed on Wednesday. 

Among these banks, Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited is reported to have borrowed the most money. 

Bangladesh Bank sources said that several Islamic banks are still suffering from liquidity crisis due to deposit withdrawals. 

An official of the treasury department of the Islamic Bank said, “In the last few days, some corporate deposits have been withdrawn from our bank, due to which our liquidity crisis has deteriorated rapidly. On the other hand, many small customers have also made new deposits.” 

The official added on condition of anonymity, “We are now trying our best to provide better service to customers. Our branch networks are performing well.” 

Meanwhile, the MD of a bank said on condition of anonymity, “Even with the support of the central bank, some Islamic banks are looking for long-term loans from general banks to deal with their crisis, especially those with good liquidity, seeking loans for at least three months.” 

However, some relevant sources also claimed that not all Islamic banks are in a liquidity crisis. 

“We have a surplus liquidity of Tk 3,200 crore, which is why we do not need the central bank’s support,” said Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, managing director and chief executive officer of Shahjalal Islami Bank Limited. 

“Also, we have recently given loans of about Tk 2,000 crore to other banks on various short-term terms,” he added. 

Sources said that Sharia-based banks mainly relied on Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited for short-term loans, but the largest Islamic bank’s recent liquidity crisis has put those banks in trouble. 

Before Bangladesh Bank launched this liquidity facility on Monday, Islamic banks were borrowing from each other.

Headline_English: Gold reserves of world's central banks reach highest in 50 years
Content_Enlish:
After accumulating huge amounts of gold in the third quarter of the year, central banks around the world are continuing to increase their purchases in the fourth quarter. According to the World Gold Council (WGC), central banks' gold reserves increased by another 31 tons in October. The amount of gold currently owned by central banks is the highest since 1974. 

The United Arab Emirates' central bank bought the most gold in October. 

Their reserves increased by more than 9 tons. This country has increased its gold reserves by 18 tons this year. Turkey's gold purchases also increased by about 9 tons last October. The Central Bank of Turkey bought the most gold in 2022. 103 tons have been added to their reserves. 

Uzbekistan also bought 9 tons of gold last October, and the country is continuing to increase its reserves. More than 60 percent of the country's total reserves are gold. India, the largest economy in South Asia, is also continuing to increase its gold purchases. The country currently has 781 tons of gold in its reserves. The country is the world's ninth largest gold reserve country. 

The WGC said that in the third quarter of the year (July-September), global gold demand increased by 1,181 tons, which is 28 percent more than in the third quarter of last year. Even in the first nine months of this year, gold demand increased by 18 percent compared to the same period a year ago. Investment by users and central banks played a major role. According to the organization, gold purchases by central banks around the world increased by about 400 tons in the third quarter of the year, which is 300 percent more than in the same period last year. Purchases continued in the fourth quarter as well. 

John Carlos Artigas, global head of research at the WGC, said, 'Global gold consumption has returned to pre-corona levels. This is because jewelry sales have increased at the retail level. In addition, demand for gold bars and coins has also increased due to continued purchases by central banks around the world. ' 

Meanwhile, after a long decline for several months, gold prices have started to rise again in the international market. According to market research firm Trading Economics, the price of gold in the global market rose to $1,797 per ounce on Friday, up 2.41 percent in the past month. 

Analysts say that the dollar strengthened due to the aggressive interest rate hike by the US central bank, the Federal Reserve. But investment in gold is increasing as the possibility of higher interest rates in the future is increasing, which is also pushing up the price.

Headline_English: What can be done to solve the liquidity crisis in the financial sector?
Content_Enlish:
The liquidity crisis has become the most discussed issue in the Bangladesh economy at the moment. Because, this liquidity crisis is one of the problems that the country's banks and financial institutions are currently suffering from. 

Dr. Mizanur Rahman, Commissioner of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC), wrote an opinion column in an English national daily on how this liquidity crisis was created and what can be done to solve it. 

In the opinion column, he wrote that this liquidity crisis is fundamentally economic. 

According to him, weak supervision by regulatory agencies and the widespread deterioration in the credit quality of banks and financial institutions have also played a major role in creating this situation. But policymakers are not acknowledging the issue, which may be an obstacle to macroeconomic management. 

This official of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission expressed concern that this liquidity crisis will not only create risks in terms of economic capacity, but it may also instill fear in the minds of economic agents and increase systemic risks in the financial market as a whole. 

Dr. Mizanur Rahman wrote that Bangladesh Bank has been selling foreign exchange reserves since September 2021 to finance the economy's growing current account deficit. 

He said that Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves were at a record US$48 billion in August 2021. As a result of the sale of reserves to support the overvalued exchange rate, they fell to below US$35 billion in October 2022. This rapid deterioration of the economy is taking place amidst imbalances in the money market and multiple exchange rate depreciation in the foreign exchange market. 

In other words, in an environment of great uncertainty, the central bank has taken only interest rates and exchange rates as targets. Due to this, we are seeing two unstable outcomes. 

First, the liquidity crisis in our financial system is intensifying. Because whenever the central bank sells foreign exchange reserves in the open market, the money supply in the financial sector decreases and liquidity in the money market decreases. Since the exchange rate of the rupee against the US dollar is still considered overvalued, the demand for foreign currency is increasing at an increasing rate. This is calling for further depletion of the central bank’s reserves. This will further exacerbate the liquidity crunch. 

The government has placed excessive emphasis on austerity to control its spending. However, this is not the only source of foreign currency demand. More important drivers include household spending and corporate investment, both of which are deeply dependent on interest rates. With interest rates still in the single digits, the only way to control a large part of import demand is to impose import trade barriers (for example, quotas and tariffs) and other administrative guidelines. In my opinion, this is a self-defeating strategy. In my opinion, it does not work in times of crisis. 

Second, the global supply system collapsed during the coronavirus crisis and the overall price level rose rapidly from July 2021. With the rising prices of energy and other essential commodities (due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine) and the economy reopening after the COVID-19 pandemic, aggregate demand has increased significantly. Now, rising inflation has created an imbalance in the money market for the transaction of equal amounts of goods and services. This means that the supply of real money balances has shrunk rapidly in the last 12 months. 

Dr. Mizanur Rahman said that these two factors are creating a massive liquidity crisis in our financial sector. Behind this, there has been a relationship between the weak role of regulatory agencies and good governance. We are observing that the asset quality of banks and financial institutions has deteriorated over the past few years. The increasing amount of non-performing loans (NPLs) has reduced the operating cash flow of banks and financial institutions. 

So how will Bangladesh Bank solve this liquidity crisis? 

In the opinion piece, Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Dr. Mizanur Rahman also gave some suggestions in this regard.

He writes, first, the central bank needs to inject new liquidity into the financial system. Initially through the repurchase agreement market. If there is a shortage of supply of this class of assets, the central bank can consider buying better quality financial securities (such as bank bonds) next. But it must be at a fair price. One downside risk is that inflation may increase further. However, this can be prioritized in the short term to overcome the growing liquidity crisis. 

Secondly, the decline in the real money balance (the supply of real money) demands rapidly increasing interest rates to balance the money market. Here we are talking about the destabilizing role of fixed interest rates. 

It is worth noting that Bangladesh Bank fixed the lending interest rate at 9 percent at the beginning of 2020, which has accelerated the demand for private sector loans. On the other hand, the current account deficit of $ 18 billion and the massive depletion of foreign exchange reserves have reduced the supply of money. There is a huge imbalance in supply and demand in the money market. If there is a free market, the interest rate will be more than 10 percent. So the policy solution is that if the central bank allows the interest rate in the money market to be freely determined, it will act like a bypass surgery for a person under cardiac arrest. Market-based interest rates will help banks and financial institutions determine the fair price of loans and reduce the demand for credit by the private sector. This will restore the fundamental balance of the money market. 

Dr. Mizanur Rahman said that the money market and the foreign exchange market are deeply interdependent. Market-based interest rates will bring balance to the money market and reduce the credit demand of the entire economy. This in turn will reduce the demand for imports and improve the current account deficit. 

The imbalance in the balance of payments will further improve if the obligations of the private sector corporations to repay their foreign debts are not created in the short term. Private sector corporations that have borrowed from foreign lenders without taking into account exchange rate risk will be forced to restructure their debt repayment terms. But the best way to discipline unscrupulous private sector borrowers is to fix the taka-dollar exchange rate at a fair value. Unscrupulous individuals or institutions cannot be controlled by artificially overvalued currency exchange rates. 

The biggest obstacle to the stability of the current account or balance of payments (BOP) is the multiple exchange rates of overvalued taka. In fact, even if the taka depreciates by 25 percent against the US dollar, there is no reason to claim that the value of the taka is set in a balanced manner. 

IMF BOP (Balance of Payments) assistance will reduce volatility in the foreign exchange market in the short to medium term. I am sure that the government will also seek new long-term loans from bilateral and multilateral development partners. It is worth noting that the overall national external debt is still below 25 percent of GDP. 

But the test for the government as well as the central bank is to restore balance in both the money market and the forex market. The common goal of the government and the central bank should be to stabilize foreign exchange reserves and unify the multiple exchange rates of the taka-dollar. The only way to achieve this is to allow interest rates and the exchange rate to adjust freely until the market reaches equilibrium. Such exchange rates and monetary policy will stabilize foreign exchange reserves and the exchange rate of the taka by changing the supply and demand for foreign exchange.

Headline_English: Remittance flow is increasing
Content_Enlish:
Although remittances have increased slightly, expectations are not being met. The various initiatives taken to increase the flow of expatriate income are not being reflected in much. This picture is seen in the report for December 16 published by Bangladesh Bank. 

Such information emerged from the updated remittance report of Bangladesh Bank on Sunday. 

According to the Bangladesh Bank report, remittances received in the first 16 days of this December were 941 million US dollars. In terms of taka, which is about 10,680 million taka. 

Last November, remittances received 1594.7 million US dollars. Accordingly, this remittance is slightly higher. Remittances received in October were 1525.5 million dollars. Accordingly, although the remittances for November or December 16 are not high, they are somewhat positive. 

Various initiatives have been taken by the government to increase the flow of remittances. To facilitate sending remittances through banking channels, the charge fees of banks or exchange houses were waived. Earlier, the incentive for sending remittances was 2 percent. The latest increase was to 2.5 percent. In addition, the CIP honorarium for remittance senders, the expansion and simplification of the remittance distribution process, as well as providing investment and housing financing facilities for expatriates, encouraging international money transfer operators to establish drawing arrangements with Bangladesh banks under the FinTech system, and the option of asking the source of money to send remittances was discontinued. 

According to the latest report of Bangladesh Bank, a review of bank-based remittances shows that on December 16, more remittances came through private commercial banks. The number of state-owned commercial banks has had an impact on remittances. 

Remittances of 767.8 million US dollars came through commercial banks of private banks. And remittances of 146.4 million US dollars came through state-owned banks. And remittances of 22.5 million US dollars came through one specialized bank and remittances of 4.2 million US dollars came through foreign banks. 

As usual, no remittances came through seven banks in the first half of December. The banks are the state-owned Bangladesh Development Bank Limited (BDBL), Rajshahi Krishi Unnayan Bank, private sector Community Bank, foreign sector Habib Bank, National Bank of Pakistan, Uri Bank and State Bank of India. The banks have always lagged behind in terms of bringing in remittances.

Headline_English: Trading ends amid decline in stock market indices
Content_Enlish:
The second working day of the week, Tuesday, ended with a decline in the capital market indices. On this day, the country's main stock market, Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), saw an increase in trading, while the other market, Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE), saw a decrease. 

Market analysis shows that on Tuesday, the DSE main price index DSEX fell by 9 points to 6,180 points. Among the other two indices, the Shariah Index fell by 1 point and the DSE-30 Index rose by 1 point to 1,352 and 2,191 points respectively. 

Shares and mutual funds worth Tk 269.58 crore were traded on the DSE today. This is an increase of Tk 71 crore compared to the previous working day. The previous day, shares and mutual funds worth Tk 198.8 crore were traded on the DSE. 

Shares and mutual fund units of 313 companies were traded on the DSE on Tuesday. Of these, 17 companies increased in price, 136 decreased and 160 companies' shares and mutual fund unit prices remained unchanged.

The overall index of the other stock market, the Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE), CASPI, fell by 24 points to 18,279 points. Out of the 128 companies that changed hands on the CSE today, the share prices of 10 increased, 42 decreased and the share prices of 76 companies remained unchanged. 

Shares and units worth Tk 22.35 crore were traded on the CSE on Tuesday, which is a decrease of about Tk 2 crore compared to the previous day. The previous day, the CSE traded Tk 24.14 crore.

Headline_English: Bashundhara Group pays off bank loans of farmers who went to jail
Content_Enlish:
After releasing the 12 farmers of Pabna who were jailed for bank loans on bail, Bashundhara Group paid the defaulted loans of 37 farmers, including them, along with interest. 

On Tuesday afternoon, at the auditorium of Daily Kaler Kantho, the editor-in-chief of the newspaper Imdadul Haque Milon handed over the defaulted loan amount to Jharna Prabha Devi, acting manager of the cooperative bank, through a check. 

At the check-giving ceremony, Imdadul Haque Milon said, "I feel very happy because we have been able to stand by our farmers. Bashundhara Group has paid off all the loans of poor farmers. It has worked for the Shuvo Sangha of Kaler Kantho." 

He also said, "I took over as the editor-in-chief at that time. As soon as I opened the newspaper, I saw that 12 farmers of a society called Bharaimari Uttarpara Sabjichashi Samabay Samity Limited in Ishwardi, Pabna district had to go to jail for defaulting on loans. I informed our managing director (Saem Sobhan Anvir, managing director of Bashundhara Group). We want to repay the farmers' loans, we demand that he arrange it. Our Managing Director immediately told us to complete it as soon as possible. Kaler Kantho's Shuvo Sangha has provided us with all possible support in this regard. 

Jharna Prabha Devi, Acting Manager of the Cooperative Bank, said, "We have received 13 lakh 94 thousand 623 taka from the 37 members of the Bharaimari Uttarpara Sabjichashi Samabayo Samity Limited as of December 26, 2022, along with 14 lakh 15 thousand 713 taka including the case costs. We will arrange for the settlement of the farmers' cases as soon as possible." 

Jharna Prabha Devi also said that the loans taken by the farmers in 2016 were supposed to be repaid in a year. But they did not do so for a long time. Later, it was decided in the bank's board meeting to file a case, and a lawyer's notice was given in 2021. We do not know when the warrant was issued. We are sorry for this. And special thanks to the Bashundhara Group. 

It is worth mentioning that on November 25, the police arrested 12 farmers in a case filed against them for not repaying loans taken from a cooperative bank. Later, they were sent to jail through the court. On November 23, the Pabna Senior Judicial Court issued arrest warrants against 37 people, including the 12 arrested farmers. The charges against them are that in 2016, 40 farmers took loans of Tk 10,000 to Tk 30,000 from a cooperative bank and did not repay them.

Headline_English: NBR looking for car, house, bank accounts
Content_Enlish:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) is searching for potential taxpayers from vehicle and house registrations and bank accounts. After the transition from the least developed country Qatar, the target has been set to increase the tax-GDP ratio to 18 million by 2026 and increase the tax-GDP ratio to 12 percent. For this, the NBR is going to launch a secondary database audit system. 

Sources said that in the secondary database-based audit system, information will be exchanged between the NBR and the government service providers. For example, TIN numbers or certificates will have to be submitted for vehicle and house registration and bank account opening. The NBR will get information directly by connecting to the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) system that registers vehicles. Since last year, BRTA has started adding the owner's TIN or tax identification number to the database while paying vehicle tax, fitness and other fees. Similarly, information from flat registration and banks will go to the NBR. In addition, the Revenue Department will collect lists from the relevant institutions and organizations. Bangladesh will be upgraded from a least developed country to a developing country by 2026. The NBR is working on a plan to increase the number of income tax payers to 18 million by that time. For this, information proving the financial capacity of the individual will be relied upon to increase the tax coverage. Technology will be used to increase tax collection. The process of paying taxes will be made easier. According to the law, even if there is no taxable income, all those with a Tax Identification Number (TIN) are supposed to submit income tax returns. A large portion of the country's population does not pay income tax. In recent years, it has been seen that the number of people with Tax Identification Numbers or TINs has increased. But the rate of submitting income tax returns has not increased in line with that. According to the NBR, the number of TIN holders in the country is 8.2 million. By the end of November this year, only 2.2 million TIN holders had filed income tax returns. NBR Chairman Abu Hena Md. Rahmatul Munim said, "I will have information whether tax evasion is taking place anywhere. For this reason, we are introducing a secondary database audit system. We have already integrated with various institutions. We will know who the owner of the car is from secondary data. Whether the owner of that car is under tax or not. Whether the car has been shown in the return or not, how many cars he has, how much is his income? All this information will come to us.' Senior Secretary of the Finance Department Fatima Yasmin said, 'The tax-GDP rate is only 8.5 percent. This is very low. We have to increase our tax to GDP to 12 percent. Otherwise, we will not be able to continue our development activities.' Earlier, providing TIN number was mandatory for receiving bank and other government services. But in this year's national budget, the NBR has made proof of income tax return filing mandatory for receiving 38 types of government services. This year too, the deadline has been extended by one month as the rate of income tax return submission within the stipulated time has not been at the expected level. Although the NBR says that the rate of return submission is higher than last year so far. But the return collection rate has not yet met the government's target for revenue collection from income tax.

Headline_English: 9 purchase proposals approved, including 29 million liters of soybean oil
Content_Enlish:
The Cabinet Committee on Government Procurement has approved a total of nine purchase proposals, including three proposals to purchase 29 million liters of soybean oil. The total cost of this will be 2,405,46,48,000 taka. The proposals were approved in a virtual meeting of the committee held yesterday under the chairmanship of Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal. After the meeting, Additional Secretary of the Cabinet Division, Syed Mahbub Khan, said that the 39th meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Government Procurement has been held. Nine proposals were presented for the approval of the procurement committee. 

Among the proposals, four were from the Ministry of Commerce, one from the Ministry of Agriculture, one from the Ministry of Industries, one from the Information and Communication Technology Department, one from the Road Transport and Highways Department and one from the Local Government Department. The total amount of the nine proposals approved by the procurement committee is 2,405,46,48,667 taka. Of the total financing, the GOB will spend 932 crore 16 lakh 78 thousand 516 and ADB, JICA and domestic bank loans will cost 1 thousand 473 crore 29 lakh 70 thousand 151 taka. 

He said that the committee has approved the proposal to import 30 thousand metric tons of TSP fertilizer from Morocco in the 11th lot under the state-level agreement. The total cost of TSP fertilizer at 480 US dollars per metric ton will be 1 crore 44 lakh US dollars, equivalent to 153 crore 86 lakh 40 thousand taka in Bangladeshi currency. 

The committee has also approved the proposal to import 30 thousand metric tons (10%+) of bulk granular urea fertilizer in the 9th lot from the United Arab Emirates through the state agreement. The total cost of this will be 1 crore 44 lakh US dollars, equivalent to 153 crore 60 lakh 48 thousand taka in Bangladeshi currency. 

In the meeting, the committee approved the purchase proposal for the construction and completion of the primary infrastructure of the 'Sheikh Hasina Institute of Frontier Technology'. The total cost of this will be 424 crore 54 lakh 86 thousand 486 taka. The committee has approved the proposal for the procurement of the works of Lot No. DS-05 of the WP-03 package of the SASEC Dhaka-Sylhet Corridor Road Development Project. It will cost 1 thousand 232 crore 95 lakh 78 thousand 581 taka. 

The committee has approved the variation proposal of the consulting firm for the 'Karnaphuli Water Supply Project (Phase-2)' in the meeting. NIJ Consultants Company Limited was appointed as the consulting firm for 245 crore 99 lakh 78 thousand 374 taka, whose contract period ends on June 30, 2022. Due to the extension of the construction period of the project, the committee has approved the proposal for an additional increase in the cost of 245 crore 52 lakh 4 thousand 601 taka for the variation to extend the period of the consulting firm by seven months until January 31, 2023. 

He said that the committee has approved the proposal to purchase 4.4 million liters (+5%) of soybean oil through direct purchase method locally. Considering the urgent need to sell TCB products at subsidized prices to 10 million families holding TCB family cards, it was decided to purchase edible oil locally through direct purchase method. In that context, TCB will purchase 4.4 million liters of soybean oil from Sena Edible Oil Industries through direct purchase method. This will cost 81.18 million taka. The price of soybean oil per liter will be 184.50 taka. 

The committee approved another proposal to purchase 11 million (+5%) liters of soybean oil through international direct purchase method in the meeting. When bids were invited from Jad Al Rahil International LLC, Oman (Local Agent: Sky Trading) to purchase 11 million liters of soybean oil internationally through direct purchase method with the aim of selling soybean oil at subsidized prices to 10 million families holding TCB family cards, the company responded. The bid proposal was responsive after the examination. After all the bidding processes, the cost of importing 10 million liters of soybean oil at 1.31 US dollars per liter from the bidding company recommended by the PEC through negotiations will be 151 crore 73 lakh 73 thousand taka. The cost of each liter of soybean oil up to the TCB warehouse will be 152.86 taka. 

He said that the committee has approved the proposal to import 5.5 million liters (+5%) of soybean oil locally through direct purchase method. When TCB asked for a bid from a local company, Sun Singh Edible Oil Limited, Dhaka, to purchase 5.5 million liters of soybean oil through direct purchase method, the company submitted a bid. The bid proposal was responsive by TEC. After all the bidding processes, the total cost of purchasing 5.5 million liters of soybean oil from the company recommended by the TEC through negotiations will be 101 crore 47 lakh 50 thousand taka. The price of each liter of soybean oil is 184.50 taka. 

The committee approved a proposal to purchase 8,000 (+5%) metric tons of lentils through an international open tender process. When an international open tender was called for the purchase of 8,000 metric tons of lentils at a subsidized price to sell lentils to 10 million families holding TCB family cards, a bid was submitted. The proposal was responsive after the examination. After all the bid proposal processes, the cost of purchasing 8,000 metric tons of lentils from Arabel Bakliat Habubat Santik AS (Local Agent: BINQ, Dhaka) at a rate of 953 US dollars per metric ton will be 815.768 million taka. The price of lentils per kg is 101.57 taka.

Headline_English: Inflation will start decreasing from October: Planning Minister
Content_Enlish:
Planning Minister MA Mannan has expressed hope that inflation will increase in September as well as in July-August, but will start decreasing from October. 

He expressed this hope at a development dialogue organized by the Development Journalists Forum of Bangladesh (DJFB) at the NEC conference room on Tuesday (September 6) morning. The Planning Minister also believes that it will have an impact on the market if the economy stabilizes. 

Planning Minister MA Mannan said, rice prices have already decreased in the market. We will get a loan from the IMF (International Monetary Fund). I am sure we will get it. So, considering all this, I think we will turn around. Our remittances, our agriculture, our labor, these will not be affected. 

Journalists asked questions about various aspects of the economy in the dialogue. To a question about the price of fuel oil and the dollar crisis, the minister assured that the price of oil will not increase but will decrease. If we get a loan from the IMF and the price of the dollar can be kept stable, the economy will stabilize. 

Admitting that government expenditure has increased, the minister said that unnecessary projects are not being taken up. To reduce corruption in projects, it is necessary to increase surveillance in procurement. 

He also said, "Amidst everything, the government is taking care that growth does not fall below 7 percent. We are trying to reduce corruption in projects. Corruption mainly occurs in procurement. We are strengthening our surveillance there. At the same time, I think it is important to enforce the law."

Headline_English: The success story of domestic company Reverie
Content_Enlish:
In 2011, 7 young engineers founded Reverie Power and Automation Engineering Limited. The seven are three friends from the Electrical Engineering Department of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) Md. Jahangir Al Jilani, Md. Zahid Hossain and Md. Ariful Haque. The other four are Mustajab Hossain, Abdur Rahman, AB Siddique, SM Faisal. 

In just 10 years, this organization is now known as a large team of more than 350 engineers and a renowned engineering firm. The organization has earned 100% trust by solving various problems in the country's power sector and implementing various complex projects. 

When Sheikh Hasina's government came to power in 2009, extensive activities were started to develop the country's power sector. At that time, the country's power generation capacity was 3,300 MW, which is now more than 25,000 MW. During this time, not only power generation has developed, but transmission and distribution have also improved greatly. In addition, many power-dependent factories have been established.

Riveri has made a huge technological contribution to the development of the power sector. In addition to power systems, many complex engineering solutions such as control systems, distributed automation systems, SCADA complexes, grid synchronization, etc. have been provided by only Reveri so far, completely by domestic engineers. And these complex engineering solutions are used in almost every sector, starting from power generation to the consumer level. 

Not only technical solutions, Reveri is manufacturing international standard electrical transformers and switchgear. Transformers manufactured by Reveri are accredited by renowned international labs. As a result, their transformers and switchgears are being supplied to the country and abroad through various domestic and international tenders. 

In this regard, Reveri's Managing Director Md. Jahangir Al Jilani said, "It is possible to manufacture electrical equipment by utilizing the country's manpower, reduce import dependence and increase exports, and prevent the imbalance in foreign exchange income and expenditure. The number of consumers of electrical equipment is increasing all over the world, and this demand will always be there. Along with the RMG sector, this sector can also make a big contribution to our economy. We are determined to meet the domestic demand and export our products to different countries.’ 

Riveri Chairman Md. Zahid Hossain said, ‘Our plan is to take the country forward by extending cooperation to other small and big manufacturers in the country’s power sector while maintaining the quality of the products. We are working towards that goal.’ 

The company’s Vice Chairman Md. Ariful Haque said, ‘Riveri is an organization of young engineers based entirely on local talent. We want to prove that we are not just a country dependent on workers; we will not lag behind anyone in terms of talent.’ 

Using its own skills and talent, Reveri has successfully completed many complex projects at the domestic level, which even a few years ago, no one except foreigners could do. Gopalganj Interim 400/132 KV 650 MVA Substation, Desh Energy 200 MW Power Plant, and many government and private milestone projects have made Reverie's crown shine. 

Director Abdur Rahman said, Reverie's sky-high progress, which has played a huge role in the overall power development of the country, has become a cause for concern for many current domestic brokers and foreign companies. Therefore, Reverie's ongoing and future work plans have to keep the issue of conspiracy in mind. Such conspiracies to stop the country's indomitable progress have happened before, and there may be more; in the meantime, we have to continue moving forward. 

Sociologist Dr. Asif Abed said, these young people could have gone abroad and ensured their own good lives if they wanted, they are working day and night in their institutions, which are contributing to the development of the country. We want such young people who, in addition to dreaming of the country's development, will also work to implement that dream.

Headline_English: Net foreign exchange reserves now at $26 billion: Governor
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank's net foreign exchange reserves are now $26 billion, Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder said. He said, "We show the reserves gross. But the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has asked us to show the net." 

The Bangladesh Bank Governor gave this information at a briefing organized by the Finance Ministry after a meeting with the IMF delegation at the Secretariat on Wednesday. In response to journalists' questions, he said, "Currently, the gross foreign exchange reserves are $34.3 billion. If you subtract $8 billion from this, what remains is the net reserves." 

Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal also said in the briefing that the gross foreign exchange reserves in the country are now a little over $34 billion. After overcoming the crisis, the reserve reserves will reach their previous heights again. 

Stating that Bangladesh is receiving a loan from the IMF, the Finance Minister mentioned that it is necessary to implement the conditions given by the organization for ourselves. The IMF is giving us the loan as we wanted. We are going to get the IMF loan, God willing. 

AHM Mustafa Kamal said, the IMF will approve the loan within the next three months. The loan amount is 4.5 billion dollars. This loan will come in seven installments until 2026. The first installment will come in February next year. The remaining loan will be available in 6 equal installments of 660 million SDR (Special Drawing Rights) every six months until 2026. 

Incidentally, the government had applied for a loan of 4.5 billion dollars from the IMF to deal with the global recession and the domestic situation. In view of this, a delegation of the organization came to Dhaka on October 26. IMF officials exchanged views with various government offices including Bangladesh Bank, NBR, BSEC. A final meeting was held with them at the secretariat today, Wednesday.

Headline_English: Padma Bank donates blankets to Prime Minister's Relief Fund
Content_Enlish:
Padma Bank Limited has donated blankets to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's relief fund for distribution among the cold-stricken and distressed people of the country. Padma Bank Chairman Dr. Chowdhury Nafiz Sarafat handed over the samples of the blankets to the Prime Minister at Ganabhaban today, Thursday. 

Padma Bank Managing Director and CEO Tarek Riaz Khan and Bangladesh Association of Banks (BAB) Chairman and Exim Bank Chairman Md. Nazrul Islam Majumder were present at the time.

Headline_English: Gold price rises by $100 in global market
Content_Enlish:
The price of gold has increased in the international market as inflation in the United States has declined. Last Friday, the price of gold increased by more than $100 in one jump. 

According to market-related organization Trading Economics, the price of gold increased by $1,760 per ounce on that day, which is the highest price in almost three months. 

The previous Friday, November 4, the price of gold was $1,636 per ounce. Accordingly, the price increased by $124 or 5.40 percent in one week. 

Inflation in the United States fell by 7.7 percent in October, which is the lowest increase since last January. This has increased expectations that the US central bank, the Federal Reserve, will not raise interest rates sharply again. The Federal Reserve has recently increased interest rates by 75 basis points. 

With such a price increase in the global market, the price in the domestic market has also increased. Before this increase in the price of gold in the global market, the price of gold fell for about a month. In view of the continuous decline in the price of gold in the global market, the price of gold in the domestic market has also been reduced from October 25. 

On the other hand, along with gold, silver and platinum prices also saw a big rise in the global market last week. In the last one week, the price of silver has increased by 4.14 percent to $21.69 per ounce. The price of platinum has increased by 7.04 percent to $1,028.58. 

Meanwhile, the demand for gold has increased worldwide due to the economic crisis. Even this demand has returned to the level before the Corona pandemic. This information was reported in a recently published research report by the World Gold Council (WGC). 

The organization said that in the third quarter of the year (July-September), the global demand for gold increased by 1,181 tons, which is 28 percent more than the third quarter of last year. Even in the first 9 months of this year, the demand for gold has increased by 18 percent compared to the same period a year ago. Investments by users and central banks have played a major role.

Headline_English: 'No bank will close, there is no need to panic about deposits'
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank spokesperson GM Abul Kalam Azad said, "No bank in the country has been closed since independence. No bank will be closed in the future either. In this case, there is no need for customers to panic about their bank deposits." 

A meeting was held on Sunday (November 13) between Bangladesh Bank Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder and World Bank Vice President for South Asia Martin Reiser. Abul Kalam Azad said this after the meeting. 

He told the customers that if any bank fails to pay deposit money, Bangladesh Bank will take action against them. Customers should call 16236 to report any complaints. We will investigate based on the complaints. 

He said that discussions were held on the ongoing projects of the World Bank in the country. The World Bank has assured cooperation in this regard. In addition, the World Bank has expressed interest in investing in new projects.

Headline_English: Balance in foreign exchange market will come in January-February: Bangladesh Bank
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has expressed hope that the balance between demand and supply in the foreign exchange market will return by January-February. Bangladesh Bank Executive Director and Spokesperson GM Abul Kalam Azad gave this information at a press conference on Monday afternoon. 

He also said, 'We have come to know through newspapers that commercial LC opening has been closed. This is not correct. LC has been opened till November 10 for $1263 million. Last month at this time, it was $1232 million. In October, LC was opened for $4743 million.' 

The Executive Director of Bangladesh Bank also said that Bangladesh Bank has no restrictions on commercial LC opening. Banks are opening letters of credit considering their usable foreign exchange funds subject to their remittance income and expenditure. A lot of information is being received about over-invoicing and under-invoicing during special supervision. So far, no foreign currency loan has defaulted and Bangladesh Bank will not allow it to happen.

Headline_English: Bangladesh faces three crises: World Bank
Content_Enlish:
The Russia-Ukraine war, the impact of the Covid pandemic and the climate crisis have hit Bangladesh hard, like the rest of the world, said Martin Riser, Vice President for the South Asia Region of the World Bank. He said that these challenges have created a dire situation for the global economy. Every country is struggling to cope with it, and Bangladesh is no exception. 

He said this in a press release sent from the World Bank's Dhaka office on Tuesday. 

He had earlier arrived in Dhaka on November 12. He left Dhaka on Tuesday morning after a three-day visit. 

In a press release sent by the World Bank, Riser said that Bangladesh can maintain rapid growth by continuing to invest in aggregate revenue collection and financial sector reforms, human resource development and climate change. We are ready to fully support these efforts in these challenging times. 

He also said that the World Bank is proud to be a part of Bangladesh's extraordinary development journey over the past 50 years. Bangladesh is an example for many other countries in the world. Especially for rapid poverty reduction and sustainable growth. 

During the visit, the Prime Minister met with the Finance Minister, the Governor of Bangladesh Bank, and the Secretary of the Economic Relations Division (ERD). The meeting discussed policy measures to mitigate the recent global shocks and economic sustainability. They also discussed the World Bank's support for Bangladesh's development priorities. She was accompanied by Abdullaye Sek, the new World Bank Country Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan.

Headline_English: NGOs are charging high interest rates from the poor: Bangladesh Bank Governor
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder has said that non-governmental organizations (NGOs) are charging high interest rates from the poorest people in the country. This is morally unacceptable. 

The Bangladesh Bank Governor said these things at the Microcredit Regulatory Authority (MRA) e-service inauguration ceremony on Tuesday. 

Stating that NGOs were created to serve the people, the Governor said that the use of cash in microfinance should be reduced and the profit culture should be removed. But very high charges are being charged from there. We have no option but to reduce interest rates. Reducing the exchange of cash in microfinance will increase transparency.

Headline_English: Dollar value falls, oil prices rise
Content_Enlish:
Oil prices rose by more than $5 a barrel, Reuters reported on Tuesday. 

The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates. The report said that oil prices rose due to the weakening dollar and expectations that the US Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates. 

Brent crude rose $5.11, or 5.1 percent, to $106.27 a barrel. Earlier, oil prices rose 2.1 percent on Friday. 

US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose $5.01, or 5.1 percent, to $102.60. Earlier, WTI prices rose 1.9 percent. 

Two US Federal Reserve officials indicated on Friday that the central bank may raise interest rates by 75 basis points at its meeting on July 26-27.

Headline_English: Severe fuel crisis; Army fires to quell protests
Content_Enlish:
Sri Lanka is facing a severe fuel shortage. In a report on June 19, the British newspaper The Guardian reported that the country's military opened fire to quell protests on Saturday night. The protests began at a gas station. 

Protesters have been accused of throwing stones and damaging army trucks. The protests took place in the Biswamadu area north of Colombo on Saturday night. Four civilians and three soldiers were injured in the incident. 

Motorcycle riders started protesting after running out of petrol. Then clashes broke out with the soldiers. Army spokesman Nilantha Premaratne said that a group of 20 to 30 people were throwing stones. Their attack damaged an army truck. 

Sri Lanka is suffering from its worst economic crisis since independence in 1948. Experts have attributed this to various factors. These are the corruption of the Rajapaksa family, which has been at the center of power in the country for a long time, nepotism, the government's short-sighted decisions, the Corona pandemic, the collapse of the tourism sector, tax cuts, etc.

Headline_English: 9-point instructions to stop harassment in the sale of savings certificates
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has instructed commercial banks not to harass customers when selling savings certificates. At the same time, the central bank has also given 9-point instructions to banks to stop harassment. Recently, the central bank issued a circular in this regard and sent it to the chief executives of commercial banks. 

It has been alleged that banks are harassing customers in various ways while buying savings certificates. Due to unnecessary harassment, customers are not able to buy savings certificates on time. This is discouraging customers from investing in savings certificates. The central bank has issued new instructions to stop this. 

The circular, signed by Director (DMD) Khondaker Siddiqur Rahman, states that the person who wants to buy savings certificates must present the cheque submitted by the buyer for clearing within one working day from the date of receipt of his application by the issuing office. In addition, if the customer applies to buy savings certificates through a debit authority, the relevant instrument must be issued in favor of this customer on the date of debiting the customer's account. 

The intimation should be ensured on the date of payment of the profit and the original or principal amount of the savings certificate sold through the National Savings Scheme Online Management System. Necessary action should be taken within a maximum of three working days from the date of receipt of any application after the purchase of the savings certificate by the customer (such as nominee change, account number change, mobile number change, EFT related problems, etc.). 

The district or bureau savings office under the National Savings Department and the responsible link bank of the National Savings Special Bureau will clear the cheques of the customers of the office or bureau in a timely manner and inform the concerned office. In addition, the cheque presented for clearing for the purpose of purchasing the savings certificate cannot be returned without proper reasons. In addition, the profit and original or principal of the savings certificate sent through Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) instruction in favor of the customer cannot be returned. 

During the sale of the savings certificate, the issuing bank or branch cannot force the customer to open an account in that bank or branch. In addition, for security reasons, the user ID of one person or one branch of the bank cannot be used by another person or another branch. 

The circular also states that the PSD Circular No. 4 of 1/2013 issued by Bangladesh Bank on 28 February 2013 and the instructions issued at different times should be followed on the issue of collection of charges on transactions carried out through Bangladesh Automated Clearing House.

Headline_English: Income tax return mandatory for savings certificates worth more than Tk 5 lakh
Content_Enlish:
Proof of return filing will have to be submitted to buy post office savings and national savings certificates worth more than five lakh taka. Till now, there was a rule to submit TIN. Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard on Monday. 

In the wake of a letter sent by the National Board of Revenue (NBR), Bangladesh Bank has given this instruction to the banks to submit proof of return filing. 

The instruction states that according to the NBR's decision, in case of investing more than five lakh taka in post office savings bank accounts and savings certificates, the investor will have to submit proof of income tax return filing to the concerned issuing office. Till now, there was a rule to submit TIN. As a result of this new instruction, from now on, TIN will not have to be submitted to buy savings certificates. 

In this case, an acknowledgement of receipt of income tax return filing, or a system generator certificate containing the taxpayer's tax identification number, name and fiscal year information for which the return was filed, or a certificate issued by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, must be submitted. In addition, in the case of institutional investment, TIN must be submitted instead of proof of return filing.

Headline_English: All bank branches in flood-hit areas closed
Content_Enlish:
All bank branches in flood-hit areas including Sylhet, Sunamganj, Rangpur and Kurigram will remain closed for the time being. However, emergency banking services will have to be provided from nearby branches. 

Bangladesh Bank has sent instructions to all banks in this regard on Sunday. However, most of the branches in these areas have already been closed due to abnormal water rise. 

The instructions state that sudden floods have occurred in Sylhet, Sunamganj, Rangpur and Kurigram and several other districts due to abnormal rise in river water. All branches or sub-branches of the bank where normal banking activities are not possible due to floods will have to be closed and emergency banking services will be provided to customers from nearby branches. 

It says that after the flood situation improves, arrangements will have to be made to provide banking services to customers from the relevant branches immediately.

Headline_English: Income tax return filing deadline extended by two months
Content_Enlish:
The deadline for filing annual income tax returns for individual taxpayers has been extended by two months. Individual taxpayers can file returns until January 31, 2024. In addition, the deadline for filing returns for company taxpayers is being extended by one and a half months from January 15 to February 28. 

This information was given in a notification signed by Mohidul Islam Chowdhury, Second Secretary of the Board of Revenue, on Wednesday. 

The Income Tax Service Month is underway throughout the current month of November, which will continue until November 30. A total of 1.9 million income tax returns have been filed until November 27. Revenue of Tk 4,200 crore has been collected against these returns. 

According to the latest information, the number of TIN number holders in the country is about 9.4 million. Of these, the number of returns filed in the last fiscal year 2022-23 was 2,299,625. Before that, the number of returns filed in the fiscal year 2021-22 was 2,299,625. Concerned people believe that it will exceed 3 million this year. Two-thirds of the income tax returns have been submitted as of November 27.

Headline_English: Recruitment exams of 10 banks and financial institutions scheduled for December 23 postponed
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has postponed the preliminary examination scheduled for December 23 for the recruitment of officers in 10 state-owned banks and financial institutions. 

This information was given in a notification signed by Rafiqul Islam, Director (Current Duty) of the Bankers Selection Committee, sent from the head office of Bangladesh Bank on Thursday. 

The notification said that the preliminary examination scheduled for December 23 for the recruitment of 2,775 vacant posts of Officer (General) in 10 banks and financial institutions affiliated to the Bankers Selection Committee Secretariat has been postponed due to unavoidable reasons. 

The revised date and time of the examination will be announced in due course, the notification also said. 

The 10 banks and financial institutions include Sonali Bank PLC, Janata Bank PLC, Agrani Bank PLC, Rupali Bank PLC, Bangladesh Development Bank PLC, Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, Probashi Kalyan Bank, Karmasangsthan Bank and Investment Corporation of Bangladesh. 

In the first week of January this year, the Bankers Selection Committee published a notification for the recruitment of 2,775 manpower for the posts of Officer (General) in 10 banks and financial institutions. 

Of these, 1,054 are vacant in Sonali Bank, 302 in Janata Bank, 1,000 in Agrani Bank, 15 in Rupali Bank, 35 in Bangladesh Development Bank, 275 in Bangladesh Krishi Bank, 24 in Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, 19 in Probashi Kalyan Bank, 45 in Karmasangsthan Bank and 9 in Investment Corporation of Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Bangladesh will benefit from agreement with Japan: Commerce Secretary
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh will benefit if the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) is signed between Bangladesh and Japan, Commerce Secretary Tapan Kanti Ghosh said. He said, Japan is the world's third largest economy and it is an important trading partner of Bangladesh. 

It is a potential trade area for expanding trade between the two countries. Apart from goods, there is a possibility of developing Bangladesh's relations with Japan in the service and investment sectors as well. 

He said this in response to a question from journalists at a joint press conference on the occasion of the release of the report of the Joint Study Group to conclude the proposed Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between Bangladesh and Japan held at the conference room of the Ministry of Commerce on Wednesday. Japanese Ambassador Iwama Kiminori also spoke at the press conference. Senior officials of the Ministry of Commerce and a delegation from Japan were also present. 

Responding to a question on whether the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between Bangladesh and Japan will finally be concluded or whether there is a fear of being stuck, the Commerce Secretary said, "I am very happy." Because for the first time, we are going to have any real discussions on signing an Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) with a big country like Japan. Japan is a developed country, a very big economy, we are going to have an Economic Partnership Agreement with them. Earlier, we have discussed EPA with many small economies like Sri Lanka and Bhutan. 

In response to the question of what is the possibility of signing this agreement in the end, Tapan Kanti Ghosh said, the publication of this report does not mean the end. In order to give it a final shape, the two countries announced the conduct of a joint feasibility study and prepared a report after three rounds of meetings, which was published today. 

He said, the Economic Partnership Agreement between the two countries will be signed by December 2025 or January 2026. 

He also said, there have been no formal discussions with Malaysia and Indonesia. Whether we can go into discussions with them in this regard; we have only tried that. Recently, we have discussed with Indonesia. There were also three rounds of meetings with them. But that was a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA). Very limited opportunities. Suppose, we choose some products, which we will make duty-free for them, they will also give us some products like this. There will be no other opportunity here. But the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) with Japan will not be limited to trade only, here there will be investment, government procurement and investment in the service sector. 

He said that in order to face the possible challenges after Bangladesh's LDC graduation, according to the government's 8th Five-Year Plan, the Ministry of Commerce has already taken the initiative to conclude regional trade agreements with various commercially important countries and trade blocs in order to preserve and expand Bangladesh's export market and get duty-free access to various countries. 

Tapan Kanti Ghosh said that during Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's visit to Japan in April this year, a decision was taken to upgrade the bilateral relations between the two countries to Strategic Partnership. In view of this, a memorandum of understanding was signed as a step to increase trade, investment and economic cooperation between the two countries. Later, another agreement was signed during the visit of the Japanese Minister of Commerce to Bangladesh. 

Japanese Ambassador to Bangladesh Iwama Kiminori said that it is difficult to say in advance how much both sides will benefit from this agreement. However, it is not only related to customs, but also to various issues including improving the service sector and investment environment. Both Japan and Bangladesh will benefit from this agreement. The agreement must be signed by 2026. That is why the current situation is a little different. 

Incidentally, both countries identified 17 sectors as Scope and Coverage for the proposed EPA. The report was finalized through the participation and involvement of government, private, academia and business representatives. The full report can be found on the website of the Ministry of Commerce (www.mincom.gov.bd).

Headline_English: 129 crore taka traded on DSE in half an hour
Content_Enlish:
The last working day of the week, Thursday (December 28), saw mixed trading on the country's main stock market, the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), and the other stock market, the Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE). Tk 129 crore was traded on the DSE in half an hour. This information was revealed by DSE and CSE sources. 

Half an hour after the start of trading on Thursday, i.e. at 10:30 am, the DSE's general index, DSEX, rose 5 points to 6,248 points compared to the previous day. The DSE Shariah index fell 1 point and the DSE-30 index rose 3 points to 1,365 and 2,090 points respectively. During this period, shares and mutual fund units worth Tk 129.35 crore were traded. 

Of the companies traded during this time on Thursday, the prices of 83 increased, 55 decreased and 104 shares remained unchanged. 

Earlier, the DSEX index fell 1 point in the first 5 minutes of trading today. At 10:10 am, the index increased by 2 points from its previous position. After that, the index's momentum was seen to be upward. 20 minutes after the start of trading, at 10:20 am, the index increased by 4 points from the previous day and stood at 6,248 points. 

On the other hand, at 10:30 am, half an hour after the start of trading, the CASPI index of the Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE) decreased by 1 point to stand at 18,523 points. After that, the index's momentum was seen to be upward. 

As of 10:30 am, shares and mutual fund units worth 1 crore 46 lakh taka were traded on the CSE. During this time, the prices of 22 companies increased, 14 decreased and the share prices of 13 companies remained unchanged.

Headline_English: BGMEA requests not to make garment industry a political tool
Content_Enlish:
BGMEA has requested not to use the ready-made garment industry as a political tool in the interest of the country and the economy. 

This organization of ready-made garment industry owners says, ‘We believe that Bangladesh is currently maintaining a stable economic growth. To maintain this continuity, a fair production environment needs to be maintained in the ready-made garment industry, which in turn will play a role in socio-economic development. In this situation, we request not to use the ready-made garment industry as a political tool in the interest of the country and the economy.’ 

In a recent press release sent to the media, BGMEA President Faruk Hasan said these things. BGMEA also said, ‘Last October-November, there was a labor strike in some areas centered on the minimum wage discussion. At that time, the factory authorities were forced to close the factories on the basis of no work, no wages. However, considering the humanitarian aspect and for the welfare of our workers, the concerned factory authorities paid the full wages to the workers at the request of BGMEA. After all this, when the industry is stable, we do not want a repeat of unwanted incidents in the name of strike. 

The Sammilit Sramik Parishad (SSP) had called for an indefinite strike in the ready-made garment industry from January 1 to demand a seven-point wage of Tk 25,000 for garment workers. Later, the SSP suspended its program in a press conference. BGMEA President Faruk Hasan said, "I believe that our worker brothers and sisters are aware of the overall situation and will not allow their main source of livelihood to be affected in any way. I request every worker brother and sister not to involve themselves in any kind of incitement or mischief."

Headline_English: Rupayan City Uttara residents' get-together
Content_Enlish:
On a cold winter evening, the residents of Rupayan City Uttara, the country's first premium mega gated community, held a gathering. This colorful gathering was organized for the second time on Saturday (December 30). 

A cottage craft fair and a pitha festival were organized to increase the joy of the fair. In addition, there were various games, fireworks, cultural programs and raffle draws for all ages. 

Rupayan Group Advisor Captain (Retd.) P. J. Ullah, Rupayan City CEO M. Mahbubur Rahman, Rupayan City CBO Gautam Tarafdar and senior officials were present to greet the event. 

Md. Nasim Zaman, Md. Mizanur Rahman Nizam, Md. AKM Al Amin, Md. Anwar Hossain and Md. Ershadul Alam Bhuiyan were present for the overall arrangement on behalf of the residents of Rupayan City Uttara. The event was supported by the Facility Management Department of Rupayan City. 

Captain (Retd.) P. J. Ullah, Advisor, Rupayan Group, said, “Rupayan City is not just a place to live, it is a family. Everyone celebrated together in this gathering and strengthened our family bond.” 

CEO of Rupayan City, Mahbubur Rahman said, “Our goal is to ensure a happy and prosperous life for you. This gathering has given our residents an opportunity to celebrate together. We hope this fair will help increase mutual understanding and cooperation among our residents.” 

Residents said that this gathering at Rupayan City Uttara will be memorable.

Headline_English: Tesla recalls 675,000 vehicles from US and Chinese markets
Content_Enlish:
Tesla has recalled 675,000 vehicles in the United States and China over a problem with the trunk and front hood of two models, raising questions about the safety of the popular electric car. 

Chinese regulators announced the recall of nearly 200,000 vehicles on Friday, just hours after identifying 475,000 Tesla vehicles in the United States. 

According to U.S. and Chinese regulators, the trunk and hood problems increase the risk of accidents. Authorities say that repeatedly opening and closing the Model 3 trunk can damage a cable in the rearview camera. 

According to the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), a defect in the Model S' front hood hinge can cause it to open suddenly, blocking the driver's view. Tesla estimates that the problem affects 1% of Model 3s and 14% of Model Ss in the United States. However, no accidents have occurred so far. Mass recalls are not uncommon in the automobile industry. 

Volkswagen was forced to recall 8.5 million vehicles in 2015 in the so-called Dieselgate scandal, in which the German company admitted that it had illegally modified or tampered with millions of diesel vehicles to cheat emissions tests. 

In recent years, automakers around the world have recalled at least 100 million vehicles due to faulty airbags made by bankrupt Japanese company Takata. The Tesla recall represents a quarter of all vehicles built by Elon Musk’s new company.

Headline_English: Central bank's permission to Padma Bank was in accordance with the rules: Ehsan Khasru
Content_Enlish:
A report that ‘Bangladesh Bank has agreed to hide the loss information from Padma Bank’s financial statements to receive foreign investment’ has recently been published in some news media. In view of this, Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has issued a statement expressing concern about the matter. In a press release on Sunday, the Padma Bank authorities have explained their own position by highlighting the real facts. It has been said that the central bank has allowed foreign investment in Padma Bank in compliance with all laws and international accounting standards. 

Padma Bank’s Managing Director and CEO Ehsan Khasru said, ‘Bangladesh Bank has not given any concessions to Padma Bank to bring in foreign investment. Rather, the central bank has helped Padma Bank to consolidate its financial statements.’ He said, ‘The central bank has smoothed the path for the initiative of the Padma Bank authorities to make Padma Bank better by following the rules and regulations to make the process of bringing in foreign investment easy and simple. The central bank has not given any concessions in this regard. Everything was done with transparency. 

Regarding the TIB's statement on the matter, Ehsan Khasru said, "I am shocked that an international organization has issued a statement calling such a transparent initiative a 'fraudulent benefit'. It is astonishing that an international organization has made such a false and misleading statement based only on media reports without doing any research, proper analysis, and verification. I call this an opaque statement from a transparent organization. TIB cannot give such a bizarre statement in any way." 

The Managing Director of Padma Bank said, "The central bank, as a regulatory body, is supporting Padma Bank, which is not new in Bangladesh. Earlier, Bangladesh Bank had provided similar support to state-owned Sonali, Janata, Agrani and Rupali Banks and ICB Islamic Bank. 

It was said, 'California-based investment bank Delmorgan & Company of the United States has proposed to invest more than 6,000 crore taka, equivalent to 700 million dollars, in Padma Bank. Half of this investment will be in the form of capital. The remaining half will be in the form of bonds or other means. Padma Bank is working in compliance with all rules and regulations, including the permission of Bangladesh Bank, for this investment.' 

Ehsan Khasru further said, 'After carefully reviewing, analyzing and researching the financial statements of Padma Bank for 2020, Delmorgan has agreed to invest in Padma Bank. The bank has a bright future, they will get good profits from this. Delmorgan is making arrangements for investment in this bank based on these judgments and analyses. No kind of opaque information has been given here. No kind of fraud has been resorted to. All the reports in the media and on the basis of which the TIB has made statements are false, untrue and misleading. 

He said, "Padma Bank will officially announce the financial statements for the year 2021 that have just ended. Which are being prepared with transparency and accountability. I do not understand why the question of fraud is coming up here. There has been no fraud of any kind since the new Padma Bank started its operations from the former Farmers Bank; everything has been done with transparency and accountability. It has been done in accordance with the rules, regulations and regulations of the central bank." 

Earlier, when the bank was called 'Farmers Bank', Bangladesh Bank stopped the bank's lending activities in January 2017 due to various irregularities in loan disbursement. Later, when it failed to return the customers' money, there was a change in the ownership and management of the bank. With the government's initiative and the mediation of Bangladesh Bank, Sonali, Agrani, Janata, Rupali and Investment Corporation of Bangladesh (ICB) jointly provided capital of Tk 715 crore. As a result, 66 percent of the bank's total capital is in the hands of government banks. 

Regarding the matter, Ehsan Khosru said, "We have improved the bank a lot in the last four years. We have gained the trust of customers, deposits have increased. We are now disbursing loans. Bangladesh Bank is also happy with our work; they have trusted us. Del Morgan has also analyzed and found that if they invest in this bank, they will get good returns. That is why they are making investment arrangements. Bangladesh Bank is also providing all kinds of support for that investment. Nothing is happening in an opaque way here. Everything is happening with transparency and accountability." 

Regarding TIB's statement, Padma Bank CEO Ehsan Khosru said, "I don't understand how those (TIB) who work with transparency can make such statements with opaque ideas or thoughts."

Headline_English: Qcom-Foster wants to return Tk 590 crore out of Tk 500 crore
Content_Enlish:
Despite being owed more than Tk 500 crore, e-commerce company Qcom and payment gateway company Foster Corporation have given a partial account and said that they will be able to refund Tk 590 crore for the time being. They will pay this amount against a total of 6,721 transactions. In a partial report sent to the Ministry of Commerce yesterday, the two companies announced that they will refund this money to the affected customers. 

The report says that the amount mentioned in the partial list has been calculated against the orders against which Qcom has not delivered the products to the customers but the money paid by the customers is stuck with Foster Corporation Limited. The two companies have asked for more time to give a full account. 

Additional Secretary (IIT) of the Ministry of Commerce AHM Shafiquzzaman said that according to the joint partial report of Qcom and Foster, Tk 590.5 crore can be refunded to the customers for the time being. Bangladesh Bank will take action in this regard soon. He said, "We have asked the two companies for a full account by next Sunday." I hope that the process of recovering the money of the affected e-commerce customers will begin by returning the money that Qcom has blocked to the customers.' Earlier, on December 28, the Ministry of Commerce issued a notice to the two companies to provide an account of the blocked money of the affected customers within two weeks. The time limit for the two companies to provide information in this regard was set by January 10. 

According to sources in the Ministry of Commerce, Foster Payment is the only payment gateway operator of Qcom. Before June 22 this year, about 500 crore taka of customer money was transacted between Qcom and Foster. Of this, 397 crore taka is blocked with Foster. The Ministry of Commerce is seeking information from the two companies to recover this money from Foster and return it to the customers.

Headline_English: Bangladeshi entrepreneurs are exporting furniture machinery
Content_Enlish:
An exceptional Bangladeshi entrepreneur in the woodworking industry, Md. Naimul Hossain Khan. He has been playing a role in the development of this industry for the past two decades. He is working to make the furniture industry technology-based, train those involved in this sector, and take this industry forward. 

The company Wood Tech Solution, founded by him in 1999, helps wooden furniture and door manufacturers solve technical problems. To increase the production capacity of an organization, this front liner of the furniture industry is working on designing factories, creating layout plans for machinery, providing necessary machinery, training skilled manpower, and providing after-sales service. 

The development of the furniture industry in Bangladesh began in 1999. Since then, a foreign NGO started a project to develop the country's furniture industry. They involved Naimul Hossain Khan as a partner. He worked in hundreds of factories for years to provide hands-on education by going to all corners of Bangladesh. Later, he established a company called Wood Tech Solution to provide woodworking technology solutions. 

Wood Tech Solution has already started working on capacity building development of small factories. This work has already started by selecting 100 factories based on the region.

Headline_English: Fears of discontent in 125 garment factories
Content_Enlish:
The government's intelligence agency has sent a report to the Commerce and Labor and Employment Ministries fearing labor unrest in 125 garment factories in Dhaka Metropolitan City, Savar-Ashulia, Tongi-Gazipur, Chittagong, Narayanganj, and Mymensingh regions. It says that the factories are unlikely to pay their salaries and allowances for March this year before Eid. The report recommends taking necessary steps in coordination with the administration, owners, and workers to deal with the situation before any untoward incident. 

BKMEA Executive President Md. Hatem commented that the intelligence agency's fears regarding labor unrest are true. He told Bangladesh Pratidin that there is a crisis in some factories. However, the salaries and allowances of the workers must be paid before Eid. This leader of the knit garment factory owners said that initiatives will be taken to pay the workers' salaries, even if it is necessary to take bank loans. 

Regarding the crisis in the garment factories, Md. Hatem said that the necessary gas has not been supplied to the factories for the past two months. As a result, the production of the factories has decreased. The BKMEA leader also complained that the stimulus package announced by the government every three months due to the Corona pandemic has not been fully paid this time. Although they have written a letter to the Finance Ministry requesting Tk 600 crore to avert the crisis, they are unlikely to receive the money before Eid as the Finance Secretary is abroad, he said. 
According to the intelligence report, Bangladesh's garment industry has been facing uncertainty about exporting products to Western European countries including Russia due to financial sanctions imposed on Russian banks after the start of the Russia-Ukraine war. Many owners have stopped sending products after preparing them as per orders due to uncertainty in financial transactions with Russia. In addition, due to the global coronavirus outbreak, the import crisis of garment fabrics and other equipment has also led to a decrease in purchase orders and cancellations. As a result, the production of small and medium and subcontracted garments has been disrupted, and some garment owners have failed to pay their workers' salaries and allowances on time. 

Other recommendations made in the intelligence report to avoid labor unrest are: paying the salaries and allowances of garment workers by the 10th of each month; exploring new markets outside Russia and Ukraine; identifying small and subcontracted factories and taking initiatives to increase their financial and technical capacity; quickly formulating a policy by the BGMEA, BKMEA and the Ministry of Labor to stop unhealthy competition in obtaining foreign orders; strengthening lobbying for foreign buyers to increase orders and product prices; taking measures according to labor laws instead of suddenly laying off workers and closing factories to stop labor protests and unrest; and increasing monitoring by the BGMEA, BKMEA, government, employers and labor organizations to ensure that workers receive their salaries and allowances correctly and on time, the intelligence report recommends.

Headline_English: Janata Bank sets record net profit of Rs 3 billion
Content_Enlish:
Having overcome almost all the previous crises, all the indicators of Janata Bank are now on the rise. According to banking analysts, if this situation continues, the bank will return to its previous position. 

According to Janata Bank sources, according to the bank's approved final financial statements for 2021, Janata Bank has achieved a net profit of more than Tk 300 crore. This is the first time since the bank's establishment that the bank has achieved this record in net profit. In addition, the bank's operating profit has exceeded Tk 1,000 crore. 

The bank has regained this position in operating profit after 2012. The bank's losses have decreased from 51 branches to 39 branches now. The bank's EPS, which was 0.62 percent in 2020, increased to 12.98 percent in 2021. 

Janata Bank has shown significant improvement in reducing classified loans. Classified loans have decreased by 5.08 percent compared to last year. The bank's total classified loans have now come down from Tk 13,700 crore to Tk 12,300 crore. 

The bank's total deposits have now increased to Tk 1,02,000 crore. In addition, advances, exports, spreads and yield of advances (income from loans) have increased and cost of funds have decreased. There has also been a significant improvement in other indicators of the bank. These issues were approved by the bank's board of directors last Saturday.
