Content_Enlish:
The state-owned Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL) has so far invested $2 billion in infrastructure development and renewable energy projects in Bangladesh. The company's current assets are $1 billion. 

IDCOL Executive Director and CEO Alamgir Morshed gave this information at a function organized at a hotel in the capital on Friday night to mark the company's 25th anniversary. Bashundhara Group Managing Director Sayem Sobhan Anvir was present at the function. 

At that time, Alamgir Morshed said, 25 years ago, a small team started its journey with a paid-up capital of one lakh taka. Currently, the loan portfolio is about one billion dollars and the paid-up capital is Tk 7.38 billion. In addition to electricity, we finance the cement sector. We are playing an important role in meeting the government's goals in the field of fossil fuels. We are also financing solar power. 

At this time, Fatima Yasmin, Chairman of IDCOL and Secretary of the Financial Institutions Division, said that private sector participation is important for sustainable development. IDCOL is implementing projects through private-public partnership. It has gained a good reputation in the international arena for renewable energy in remote areas of the country. 

Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI) President Md. Jasim Uddin, Director of IDCOL Nihad Kabir, Chairman of BSRM Ali Hussain Akbar Ali and others were present at the event.

Headline_English: Bangladesh to pay Russian loan in Chinese currency
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh will repay the loan taken from Russia for the Rooppur nuclear power plant project in Chinese yuan. The United States has imposed sanctions on Russian banks after the attack on Ukraine. In this reality, the two countries have decided to settle bilateral transactions in Chinese yuan instead of US dollars. The US media outlet The Washington Post reported this news. 

The report said that Bangladesh will use yuan in the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) to repay a $12 billion loan from Russia. China launched this system in 2015 to prevent the influence of the US dollar. After the war in Ukraine began, Bangladesh faced complications in repaying the loan taken from Russia for the construction of the Rooppur nuclear power plant. Dhaka will be able to overcome the complications by repaying the loan for this nuclear power plant to Moscow in Chinese currency 'yuan' instead of dollars. Bangladesh has also given the necessary approval for this purpose. 

The decision in this regard was taken at a meeting of Russian officials with the Economic Relations Department on April 13. Earlier, Moscow requested to suspend the payment in March last year when Russia was cut off from the global payment channel-SWIFT due to Western sanctions. Under the new agreement, Bangladesh will settle payments through a Chinese bank. And the Russian side will receive the money through China's CIPS or Cross-Border Interbank Payment System. A limited alternative to SWIFT is the yuan-based transaction-based CIPS. 

Earlier, Moscow proposed currency swaps with Bangladesh in bilateral trade settlement in 2020. However, it backed down after US sanctions. Then, Bangladesh was proposed to join the payment channel created by Russia-System for Transfer of Financial Messages (SPFS). On the other hand, Bangladesh has proposed to Russia to settle trade in yuan since 2018. 

Bangladesh Bank Executive Director and Spokesperson Md. Mejbaul Haque told reporters that the central bank has held several meetings with Russia on the mechanism for making payments as loan repayments have been suspended due to US sanctions.

Headline_English: Sugar prices have increased due to rising prices in the international market: Commerce Minister
Content_Enlish:
Stating that about 99 percent of the country's sugar demand has to be imported, Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi said, 'The price of sugar has increased due to the increase in prices in the international market.' The minister also said that the price of edible oil has increased because the National Board of Revenue (NBR) has not continued the duty exemption since April, and not because of the increase in the international market. 

He said this while answering questions from journalists after the chief guest's speech at the inauguration ceremony of TCB's product sales program among one crore low-income families nationwide, organized at the Siraj Mia Memorial School grounds in Badda, the capital, on Sunday. 

The minister said, 'Soybean oil, pulses and sugar are import-dependent products. The price of sugar has increased in the international market for the past few days. The prices of the products that are imported and sold in the country have to be adjusted with the international market. We try to maintain consistency with the international market. Even then, many unscrupulous traders try to sell at higher prices. We are taking measures for this through market monitoring with the National Consumer Rights Protection Department and other concerned parties. 

Tapan Kanti Ghosh, Senior Secretary of the Ministry of Commerce, was present as a special guest at the event. Among others, TCB Chairman Brigadier General Ariful Hasan and North City Corporation Ward No. 37 Councilor Jahangir Alam were present.

Headline_English: Mohammad Ali joins Padma Bank as advisor
Content_Enlish:
Mohammad Ali, a professional banker with over 38 years of experience, has recently joined Padma Bank as an advisor. 

He has previously worked as an advisor to Premier Bank. Mohammad Ali has earned a reputation as the Managing Director of UCB, Social Islami Bank and Shahjalal Islami Bank. 

Ali started his career as a Probationary Officer of Sonali Bank in 1977. During his successful career, he gained experience working in many other reputed banks like National Bank, National Credit Limited (later emerged as NCC Bank), Standard Bank, Shahjalal Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank and others. 

During his long career, he has made his mark in various senior management positions as a reward for his commendable work in Foreign Exchange, International Division, General Banking Operations, Branch Banking and Financial Administration. Mohammad Ali has worked with distinction as Head of Credit, Head of Treasury, Head of International Division and Head of Human Resources Department.

Headline_English: Financial institutions to remain closed for five days including Eid holiday
Content_Enlish:
The government has declared a general holiday on Tuesday on the occasion of the holy Eid-ul-Azha. The Eid-ul-Azha holidays will be on June 28, 29 and 30 (a total of 4 days). The following day, Saturday (July 1), is a weekly holiday and the same day is a bank holiday. Financial institutions will be closed for five days, including Eid and weekly holidays. 

The Financial Institutions and Markets Department of Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard on Thursday. 

The circular said that since the general holiday has been declared on Tuesday, June 27, all financial institutions operating in Bangladesh will be closed on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday (4 days) on the occasion of the holy Eid-ul-Azha on June 27, 28, 29 and 30. However, since the following day, Saturday (July 1), is a weekly holiday, financial institutions will also be closed on that day. The central bank said that this order has been issued under the powers conferred by Section 18(g) of the Financial Institutions Act, 1993.

Headline_English: 10 banks to merge to form digital bank
Content_Enlish:
To make transactions easier, 10 private sector banks have taken an initiative to establish a digital bank. The proposed bank will be named DG Ten Bank PLC at the initiative of these 10 private sector banks. The institutions have finalized the matter after a meeting. The banks will apply to the central bank in the next few days. City Bank has already informed the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) about the matter. 

It is learned that all the banks involved in this initiative are listed in the capital market. They have decided to invest with the approval of the board of directors. Mutual Trust Bank (MTB) Managing Director Syed Mahbubur Rahman told reporters that MTB has decided to invest in a digital bank. We will inform investors by publishing price sensitive information (PSI). In the information provided to the DSE, The City Bank said that their board of directors has decided to invest Tk 138.8 million in the proposed DG Ten Bank PLC. 

According to the central bank's policy, the paid-up capital of the digital bank will be at least Tk 125 million. If City Bank invests, it will be 11.11 percent of the paid-up capital of Digital Bank. That is, City Bank's share in this bank will be 11.11 percent. Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in June to obtain a digital bank license. The central bank has extended the deadline until August 17 as no response was received even on the last date of application, August 1. At that time, this initiative of 10 banks was known.

Headline_English: 11 guidelines from the central bank to avoid cyber attack risks
Content_Enlish:
The central bank has issued 11 instructions to all banks and financial institutions in the country to avoid the risk of cyber attacks. The central bank sent a letter to the institutions last week informing them of what banks will do to prevent cyber attacks. 

Earlier, a group of hackers threatened to launch a cyber attack in Bangladesh. They mentioned August 15 as the possible date of the attack. In view of the threat, the government's 'Computer Incident Response Team' (BGD e-Gov Cert) has already issued a warning on cyber security. 

A press release by BGD e-Gov Cert on August 7 said that the activities of the state's critical information infrastructure (CII), banks, financial institutions, healthcare services and government and private institutions may be disrupted in a cyber attack. All the institutions concerned are asked to take precautions to prevent small or medium-sized cyber attacks. 

In such a situation, Bangladesh Bank has issued 11 instructions to banks and financial institutions to prevent cyber attacks. Notable among these are - 24 hours, especially outside office hours, the network infrastructure should be monitored and whether anyone is removing information should be kept in mind. Access to various websites should be controlled to reduce cyber attacks to a minimum. 

In addition, various measures should be taken to identify unsafe activities on the network and the latest guidelines of the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) should be followed to strengthen security. CERT gives some suggestions to ensure the infrastructure security of the concerned organization to avoid cyber attacks. They are - installing a firewall to analyze incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic and filtering malicious requests and traffic patterns. 

In addition, keeping important services like DNS, NTP and network middle box secure; verifying user input. Backing up the website; implementing HTTPS on the website with SSL and TLS encryption. BGD e-Gov CERT is asked to use updated technology and report anything suspicious to BGD e-Gov CERT.

Headline_English: Export earnings increased by 9.12 percent in July-August
Content_Enlish:
In the first two months of the current fiscal year 2023-24 (July-August), Bangladesh exported goods worth 9.3761 million US dollars abroad. This is 9.12 percent more than the same period of the previous year. 

The Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) released this updated data on Monday. 

According to EPB data, the export earnings received during the July-August period are higher than the strategic target for the two months. The target set during this period was 9.35 billion dollars. As always, the highest export earnings in the period under discussion came from ready-made garments. During this period, clothing exports were worth 7.9985 million dollars, which is 12.46 percent more than the same period of the previous year. 

In the first two months of this year, clothing exports exceeded the target. The target set during this period was 7.8838 million dollars. 

Net clothing exports during July-August were worth 4.5822 million dollars, which is 17.02 percent more than the same period of the previous year. On the other hand, woven garment exports stood at $3.6163 billion, which is 6.86 percent more than the first 2 months of the previous year. 

While the export revenue of plastic products among the main export products increased during the period under review, the export revenue of other products such as agricultural products and fish, jute and jute products, leather products and home textile products lagged behind that of the previous year. During this period, plastic products worth $35.1 million, agricultural products worth $174.4 million, frozen fish worth $61 million, jute and jute products worth $140 million and home textile products worth $125.1 million were exported. 

Meanwhile, export revenue in August, the second month of this year, stood at $4.7821 billion, which is 3.80 percent more than the same month of the previous year.

Headline_English: NRB CIP has 15 demands from the government
Content_Enlish:
The NRB CIP Association, the top organization of expatriates, has made 15 demands to the government. The organization believes that if the government implements the reasonable demands of the expatriates, the image of the government among the expatriates will increase to a large extent and the remittance flow to Bangladesh will increase to a large extent. 

They presented the demands at a press conference at the Zahur Hossain Chowdhury Auditorium of the National Press Club on Saturday. 

In a written statement at the press conference, CIP Association President Mahtabur Rahman raised the demands. These are— 

1. A helpless expatriate fights for his life, earns money by working hard and sending remittances to the country, keeping the wheels of the country's economy moving. When that remittance fighter dies abroad due to lack of treatment, the expatriates have to go door to door to collect donations and send the body of that helpless expatriate to the country, which is very shameful. Therefore, we have a humble request to the government that the body of that helpless expatriate be sent home at full government expense. 

2. Expatriates who have sacrificed their youth and everything in foreign lands and made an important contribution to the country's economy and returned to Bangladesh at the end of their lives, at that time they are no longer able to work. Expatriate allowance should be introduced for those expatriates who will return to the country after 20 to 30 years. The government has already introduced universal pension insurance. Some changes are needed in the policy. Especially, it is not clarified there. If for some reason the expatriate returns to the country after seven to eight years after the introduction of pension insurance, what will the government have to do in that case. It has been said that the principal amount will be returned. We think that the government needs to take steps to continue the expatriate insurance. A part of the 2.5 percent incentive that is being given by the government when remittances are sent through legal channels can be deposited for the expatriates. 

3. Expatriates consider Bangladesh US dollar bonds, US dollar premium bonds, and wage earners bonds as their sure investment in the country. Investment in bonds has been restricted for the last two years. The opportunity to reinvest at the end of the term has been closed. A few days ago, the interest rate on US dollar bonds was only 3 percent, which is disappointing for expatriates. Many developed countries in the world are now paying 6 percent profit instead of dollars. In this way, no expatriate is showing interest in investing in low-interest bonds. Expatriates are taking their investments back to their own countries. As a result, a dollar crisis is being seen in Bangladesh. On the other hand, no declaration has been made by the government regarding wage earners' bonds so far. Therefore, we think that the government should come forward to sell wage earners' bonds without any limits in order to further increase the government's reserves. Rumors about the dollar crisis should be stopped. By doing so, both the country and the expatriates will benefit. 

4. Expatriates face various problems in building houses in Bangladesh from abroad. Therefore, if upazila-based expatriate villages are allocated for expatriates, environmentally friendly housing will be developed. 
Expatriates should be given priority in purchasing government plots and flats and loans should be allocated to expatriates at low interest rates. 

5. Expatriates are running large-scale industries and trade with good reputation in different countries of the world. Many experienced businessmen are showing interest in investing in Bangladesh. The top organization of expatriates, NRB CIP Association, organizes Global Business Summits in different countries. Those reputable businessmen are repeatedly requesting them to invest in the country. In continuation of that, many businessmen are expressing interest in investing in Bangladesh. Their proposal is that if the government can create a separate economic zone for expatriates through guarantees, then many businessmen will invest in Bangladesh. That will create employment for many people in Bangladesh. 

6. Airfare for expatriates to travel to their workplaces in the country and abroad should be brought down to a bearable level. Travel tax should be withdrawn for expatriate workers who go abroad for work. It is to be noted that those expatriates are not going abroad for travel, they are going abroad for work. In any decision taken by the government regarding expatriates, the NRB CIP Association should be included in the policy-making committee on behalf of expatriates. 

7. A separate quota should be kept for the children of expatriates for admission to Bangladesh schools, colleges, universities and medical colleges. Expatriates should be given the opportunity to get voter ID cards through embassies abroad. Although voter ID cards have been introduced in some countries in the meantime, it is insufficient compared to the demand. Expatriates should be given the opportunity to get voter ID cards in all countries. 

8. The process of getting passports for expatriates to go abroad should be made easier. Harassment in the name of police verification while getting passports should be stopped. Police verification in the name of birth registration should be withdrawn in cases where the children of expatriates are born abroad. The number of schools and colleges should be further increased at government expense for the children of expatriates to study abroad. 

9. Financial assistance should be provided for sending sick expatriate workers back home. In terms of financial assistance from the Bangladesh government, a list should be prepared at the union level and the families of low-income expatriate workers should be brought under the ambit of financial assistance. 

10. Expatriate harassment should be stopped at airports in Bangladesh. Expatriate support desks should be opened in all government ministries to provide services to expatriates. 

11. Expatriate entrepreneurs who are creating employment abroad with workers from Bangladesh should be honored and encouraged in Bangladesh with social status. 

12. In many countries of the world, there are some restrictions on sending additional remittances to Bangladesh. In that case, if money is sent to the country through family members, it should be included in the name of the head of the family and an opportunity should be given to apply for CIP. 

13. Expatriates are facing a lot of harassment while paying income tax, in that case, arrangements should be made to stop the harassment of expatriate taxpayers and pay taxes in a simple process. 

14. Embassies in all countries of the world should be made more dynamic and appropriate measures should be taken by taking the advice of expatriates to prevent hundi. 

15. Representatives of the expatriates should be appointed in the great National Parliament to speak on issues related to the interests of the expatriates. 

The organization's senior vice-president Thateyama Kabir, vice-president Md. Monir Hossain, general secretary Mohammad Yasin Chowdhury, organizing secretary MR Khan Shahin, treasurer Mohammad Ashrafur Rahman and journalist Shyamal Dutta, general secretary of the National Press Club, were present at the press conference.

Headline_English: Remittances received 740 million US dollars in 15 days
Content_Enlish:
In the first 15 days of September, the third month of the current 2023-24 fiscal year, Bangladeshis abroad sent remittances worth 739.98 million US dollars. Of this, 49.332 million US dollars are in daily remittances. 

This information was revealed in the updated report of the Central Bank on Sunday. A review of the data showed that the amount of remittances that came into the country in the 15 days of the current month was 66.4 million US dollars through state-owned banks, 19.88 million US dollars through a specialized bank, 65.71 million US dollars through private banks, and 2.99 million US dollars through foreign banks. 

In the first month of the 2023-24 fiscal year, remittances came in at 197.31 million US dollars in July and 159.94 million US dollars in August. Remittances decreased by 373.7 million US dollars in a month. 

In the outgoing fiscal year 2022-23, the total remittance received was 2,161.7 million US dollars. In the previous fiscal year 2021-2022, the total remittance received was 2,103.17 million US dollars. The highest remittance was received in the fiscal year 2020-21. The amount was 2,477.7 million US dollars.

Headline_English: Pharmaceutical exports increase by 26 percent
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh's demand for medicines in the global market is increasing day by day. From July to September, medicines were exported worth $52.6 million. This is 25.78 percent more than the same period last year. This information has been revealed in the latest updated report of the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB). 

Data analysis shows that medicines were exported worth $52.6 million from July to September. In the same period last year, the export income of this sector was $41.8 million. This year, exports were higher than the strategic export target. Until September, the strategic target was $47.3 million, exports were $52.6 million. That is, exports were higher than the target by 11.21 percent. 

At the end of the recently concluded 2022-23 fiscal year, the country's income from medicine exports was $175.4 million. Keeping in mind the potential, the export target of this sector this year has been set at $210 million. However, the export earnings of this sector fell behind slightly in the previous year, i.e. in the 2021-22 fiscal year. Domestic drug manufacturers could not reach the expected target. At that time, the industry suffered a lot as the import of raw materials decreased due to restrictions on opening LCs. In addition, the cost of drug production was high due to the increase in gas and electricity prices, as well as the increase in the price of raw materials in the global market, which pushed the industry towards a crisis. However, those concerned believe that the crisis is being overcome to some extent. 

Traders say that drug exports have improved somewhat in the last three months. The economies of major exporting countries like Nepal, Sri Lanka and Myanmar are recovering. Therefore, they are gradually increasing purchase orders. As a result, drug exports are increasing. However, they say that export earnings have not yet regained momentum, because buyers in the United States and the European Union are still paying less than the actual price.

Headline_English: JCX Housing Fair begins Thursday
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh's fastest growing real estate company JCX Developments Limited is going to organize a four-day housing fair 'Property Expo'. If you book a flat at the fair, you will get a discount of up to 10 lakh taka. In addition, there will be a 50 percent discount on interior design, complimentary kitchen cabinets and home mover service.

Headline_English: TCB's 5 products to start selling tomorrow
Content_Enlish:
Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB) will start selling rice, pulses, oil, sugar and onions at affordable prices across the country from next Sunday. The products will be sold to one crore low-income families holding family cards nationwide for the month of October. 

Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi will inaugurate the sale of TCB products including rice at affordable prices to one crore family card holders at Dhanmondi Lake, Dingi, Road No. 8/A (in front of the Councilor's Office) at 10 am on that day. 

TCB gave this information in a press release on Saturday. 

The release said that under the initiative of the Prime Minister, under the overall direction of the Ministry of Commerce, the sale of TCB products (edible oil and pulses) at affordable prices is underway among one crore low-income beneficiary card holders. It will start across the country from October 15. Cardholder consumers will be able to buy sugar, oil, rice, pulses, and onions from general designated dealers at subsidized prices. 

This sale activity will be held at the dealers' shops/designated permanent establishments. This activity will be conducted with the overall cooperation of the City Corporation, District-Upazila administrations and according to their designated date and time plan. 

In this phase, cardholder consumers will be able to buy a maximum of 5 kg rice, two liters of soybean oil, two kg of lentils, one kg of sugar, and two kg of onions. 

Soybean oil will be sold at 100 taka per liter, sugar at 70 taka per kg, lentils at 60 taka, rice at 30 taka per kg, and onions at 35 taka per kg.

Headline_English: Bitcoin price hits 2-month high in global market
Content_Enlish:
The cryptocurrency market has started to make waves again. The price of a bitcoin has exceeded $ 30,000. Which is the highest in the last 2 months. 

On Friday (October 20), the price of a bitcoin has risen above $ 30,000. This is the first time since last July that the price of a crypto has risen so much. In total, the price of bitcoin has increased by more than 10 percent last week. According to news agency Reuters. 

The main currency of the digital market is bitcoin. Its price has risen to $ 30,022 on the business day in question. Which is the highest since July 23. The price of the currency has risen by more than 4 percent in just one day. Joseph Edwards, head of research at London crypto firm Enigma Securities, said that there was no immediate news catalyst for the increase in the price of bitcoin. 

Incidentally, the global financial market has been under pressure recently. Investor sentiment has been upset due to the Palestinian-Israeli war.

Headline_English: IMF approves second tranche of loan in December
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh is going to receive the second installment of $681 million of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan worth $4.7 billion in December. 

Bangladesh Bank Executive Director and Spokesperson Mejbaul Haque said this at a press conference after the last meeting of the IMF delegation with Bangladesh Bank on Thursday. 

He said, in the discussion with the IMF delegation, ‘We have reached an agreement on everything, the decision has been made, we are getting the next installment. We have agreed to receive the second installment of the loan. ’ 
Mejbaul Haque said, there were several conditions of the IMF, among which we have taken several initiatives. Some of the initiatives taken in view of the international and domestic situation, we have been successful. Some have not been fulfilled. We have expressed our perspectives. After detailed discussions on the issues, both sides have agreed on several issues. We have also agreed on what initiatives should be taken to do those that could not be done. In view of this, it is expected that the second installment of $681 million of the loan will be approved in the IMF board meeting on December 11. We will get the loan money after that. 

In response to a question, the spokesperson said, the IMF gave us some conditions while approving the loan. Some of these conditions have been met. There are failures in one or two places. The reserves are low. Revenue collection has been low. However, many things have been implemented. The financial stability report of the banks was supposed to be published, and the central bank has published it. Reserves are being calculated according to BPMCIX. In addition, a market-determined exchange rate of the currency has been introduced. New rules for interest rates have been introduced. 

The IMF's condition is that the dollar exchange rate must be left to the market. It has not been completely left so far. In response to a question about whether there has been any discussion on this, he said, we have already come to the single price of the dollar. We will also leave it to the market. But not now. Considering the situation, we will leave the foreign exchange rate to the market. 

The policy that was adopted to reschedule the debt has failed. The spokesperson said that the defaulted loans have not decreased, but have increased, and the only way to recover defaulted loans is to recover the loans. The last process to recover defaulted loans is to resort to the law. We will go that way to reduce defaulted loans. The time for giving loans has been given in the right process. However, the impact of the Corona pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war has had some negative effects on loans, due to which defaulted loans are not being reduced as expected. 

When asked about the success of the Bangladesh Bank reform program after starting it, he said that the country's economic growth has been more than 6 percent. Our economy is better than other countries, this is our achievement. 

The IMF approved a loan proposal of 4.7 billion US dollars to Bangladesh in January this year with specific conditions on several issues. Bangladesh received the first installment of 476.2 million 70 thousand dollars of this loan last February.

Headline_English: Expatriate income reached $1.98 billion in October, highest in four months
Content_Enlish:
Remittance flows increased in October amid dollar crisis. This month, expatriates sent $1.98 billion in remittances, the highest in the last four months. Bankers said the increase in remittance flows was due to the dollar exchange rate and increased incentives for remittances. 

According to the Central Bank, expatriates sent $643 million more in remittances in October than in September, a growth of 48.20 percent compared to the previous month. The amount of remittances in September was $1.33 billion, which was the lowest in the last 41 months. In October 2022, expatriates received $1.59 billion in remittances. 

A senior official of the Central Bank said that expatriates send remittances through the channel where they get the highest rate of remittance (dollar). Earlier, remittances came in less through banking channels because expatriates got the highest rate of dollar in the hundi market. The increase in remittances from 2.5 percent to 5 percent at the end of last month has led to higher remittances. 

It is worth noting that remittances in the first four months of the current fiscal year 2023-24 (July-October) amounted to $6.88 billion. In the same period of the previous fiscal year, it was $7.19 billion. Accordingly, remittances in the four months of the current fiscal year have decreased by 4.36 percent.

Headline_English: Saudi Arabian businessmen interested in investing in Bangladesh
Content_Enlish:
Saudi businessmen are interested in investing in Bangladesh on a large scale. A large delegation led by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud will participate in the Business Summit to be held in Dhaka next March. Saudi Arabia's Ambassador to Dhaka Issa Yusuf Issa Alduhailan said this during an exchange of views with Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi at the Secretariat on Thursday. 

The Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI) is organizing the Business Summit next March. Saudi Ambassador Issa Yusuf Issa Alduhailan said that Bangladesh is a friendly country of Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia attaches great importance to Bangladesh in the development of investment and bilateral trade relations. He said that the Saudi delegation will participate in the Business Summit with interest in investing in Bangladesh. 

Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi said that Saudi Arabia is a long-standing major business and development partner of Bangladesh. Several products including ready-made garments, bakery items, vegetables, juices and jute products are exported to Saudi Arabia. Bangladesh imports various products including petroleum wells, petroleum gas, fertilizers and dates from Saudi Arabia. 

He said that in the last fiscal year 2021-22, Bangladesh exported goods worth 290.64 million US dollars to Saudi Arabia, while at the same time, goods worth 1,693.26 million dollars were imported. The Commerce Minister said that 100 Special Economic Zones are being established in important places in Bangladesh under the initiative of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Saudi businessmen can benefit by investing there in an investment-friendly environment. 

Gambian Foreign Minister Dr. Mamadou Tangara, who is visiting Dhaka, paid a courtesy call on the Commerce Minister at the Secretariat today. During this, various aspects of trade, commerce and investment between the two countries were discussed. A delegation led by Canadian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Lily Nicholas exchanged views in the office of the Commerce Minister's official residence. 

The Canadian High Commissioner proposed to export edible oil Kelowna and Kelowna Biz to Bangladesh at the government level. The Commerce Minister said that this issue will be considered seriously. At that time, Tipu Munshi said that Canada is a big market for Bangladeshi ready-made garments. He called on Canadian investors to invest in Bangladesh.

Headline_English: European Union buys $19.4 billion worth of clothing in 10 months
Content_Enlish:
In the first 10 months of last year, European Union countries imported $19.4 billion worth of clothing from Bangladesh. According to the latest data released by the European statistics agency, Eurostat, between January and October 2022, the European Union imported $86.74 billion worth of clothing from the world, a year-on-year growth of 24.41 percent. 

In January-October 2022, the EU imported $19.40 billion worth of clothing from Bangladesh. Bangladesh is the second largest source of clothing imports for the EU. The EU’s clothing imports from Bangladesh increased by 41.76 percent compared to the same period in 2021. 

China continues to be the largest clothing supplier to the European Union (EU) with a 29.39 percent share. In the first 10 months of 2022, the EU’s imports from China reached $25.49 billion, a year-on-year growth of 22.43 percent. At the same time, imports from Turkey also increased by 12.82 percent year-on-year. The EU’s imports from Turkey stood at $10.12 billion. Imports from India reached USD 4.24 billion, a year-on-year growth of 23.46 percent. 

Among other top suppliers, EU imports from Cambodia, Vietnam, Pakistan, Morocco, Sri Lanka and Indonesia increased by 39.69 percent, 33.05 percent, 28.55 percent, 9.59 percent, 18 percent and 31.76 percent respectively.

Headline_English: GDP growth in the first quarter of the 2024-25 fiscal year is 1.81 percent
Content_Enlish:
On a point-to-point basis, the gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 1.81 percent in the first three months (July-September) of the 2024-25 fiscal year. 

This information was revealed in the updated report of the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) on Monday. 

It said that the quarterly GDP of the first quarter of the 2024-25 fiscal year has been estimated based on the currently available data. According to the estimated estimates, the GDP size in current prices stood at 12,666 billion taka. In the first quarter of the 2023-24 fiscal year, which was 11,703 billion taka. 

And the GDP growth rate in the first quarter of the 2024-25 fiscal year stood at 1.81 percent, which was 6.04 percent in the same period of the last fiscal year. Growth has decreased by 4.23 percent. 

BBS also said that the agricultural sector grew by 1.16 percent in the first quarter of the 2024-25 fiscal year. It was 0.35 percent in the first quarter of the last fiscal year. 

On a point-to-point basis, the service sector grew by 1.54 percent in the first quarter of the 2024-25 fiscal year at constant prices, compared to 5.07 percent in the first quarter of the last fiscal year. 

And the industrial sector grew by 2.13 percent in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, according to BBS.

Headline_English: Trading continues in the capital market as indices rise
Content_Enlish:
The third working day of the week, Tuesday (February 7), is the third working day of the week, with the country's main stock market, Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) and the other stock market, Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE), trading is underway with the indices increasing. This information was revealed by DSE and CSE sources. 

Half an hour after the start of trading on Tuesday, i.e. at 10:30 am, the DSE's general index, DSEX, rose 2 points to 6,283 points from the previous day. The DSE Shariah index increased by 1 point and the DSE-30 index increased by 1 point to 1,369 and 2,230 points respectively. During this period, shares and mutual fund units worth Tk 84.25 crore were traded. 

Of the companies traded during this time on Tuesday, the prices of 55 increased, 91 decreased and 74 shares remained unchanged. 

Earlier, the DSEX index fell by 6 points in the first 5 minutes of trading today. At 10:10 am, the index increased by another 2 points from its previous position. Then the index's momentum was seen to be upward. At 10:20 am, 20 minutes after the start of trading, the index increased by 6 points from the previous day to 6,286 points. 

On the other hand, at 10:30 am, half an hour after the start of trading, the CASPI index of the Chittagong Stock Exchange (CSE) increased by 14 points to 18,549 points. After that, the index's momentum was seen to be upward. 

As of 10:30 am today, shares and mutual fund units worth 3.1 million taka were traded on the CSE. During this time, the prices of 16 companies increased, 8 decreased, and the share prices of 7 companies remained unchanged.

Headline_English: Millions of families in trouble as TCB stops selling rice, market also hit
Content_Enlish:
This month, rice sales have suddenly been removed from the list of products of the Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB) family card. This has increased the price of rice in the market. At the same time, one crore low-income families have been put in extreme trouble. 

This has happened because the Food Department has not supplied rice, said Joint Director (Office Head) Humayun Kabir, the officer-in-charge of the TCB regional office in Dhaka. 

He said, "The Food Department has supplied rice until December. Since rice was not supplied in January, it is not possible to supply rice this month. We have continued to communicate with the Food Department. Supply will resume when rice is available." 

It is learned that the Food Department could not supply rice as the Finance Ministry did not release the budget for the purchase of rice. 

Abdus Salam, Director of the Supply, Distribution and Distribution Division of the Food Department, said, it is a matter of inter-ministerial decision. The instructions are implemented as they come from the ministry. The instructions were not received, so the supply was not made. 

TCB sources said that under the overall directives of the Ministry of Commerce, TCB had been selling TCB products such as rice, lentils, sugar and soybean oil at subsidized prices to one crore low-income beneficiary card-holding families. Since July 2023, TCB had been supplying five kg of rice at a price of Tk 30 per kg against each family card. The Food Department used to supply this rice. 

Meanwhile, TCB's special program Truck Sales has also been closed. Humayun Kabir said that under the government's directives, TCB products were sold in truck sales in Dhaka and Chittagong until December 31. It is now closed. It will be reopened if the government gives instructions. 

A reliable source in the Food Ministry said that the Food Department supplies 50,000 tons of rice to TCB every month. However, there is no money allocated in the budget of the Food Department or the Ministry of Commerce for this allocation. As a result, the Food Department is no longer able to supply rice. Due to uncertainty over the payment of the price of rice, the supply is currently closed. 

Meanwhile, although rice sales are suspended, the sale of edible oil and pulses at affordable prices is ongoing. This month, TCB will start selling three products - sugar, soybean oil and lentils - to one crore beneficiaries. However, due to the introduction of smart cards instead of handwritten cards, at least 3.7 million cardholders will not receive any TCB products in January. 

A TCB press release on Tuesday said that cardholders can buy two liters of edible oil, two kilograms of lentils and one kilogram of sugar in January. 

The source also said that to meet the demand, the Food Ministry has applied to the Finance Ministry for an allocation of Tk 1,534 crore for open market sales and Tk 3,372 crore for rice imports. However, no decision has been made in this regard yet. 

According to TCB, the price of coarse rice in the capital has increased by three to four taka per kg in the last one week. Currently, coarse rice is being sold at Tk 60-62 per kg, which was Tk 54-55 till December 31. 

TCB said that currently, one crore low-income people with family cards are provided with affordable products. Edible oil, pulses, and sugar are regularly provided. In addition, onions and rice are sometimes provided. Chickpeas and dates are added during the month of Ramadan. Until now, family cards were handwritten. The government has now taken the initiative to introduce smart digital cards. 

TCB information officer said that so far, 5.7 million customers have received smart cards. Another six lakh cards are being prepared. These will reach the customers within this month.

Headline_English: Big industry in a quadruple crisis
Content_Enlish:
The country's large industries are suffering from capital shortage, high dollar value, gas and electricity shortage. As a result, production in large industries like rod, cement, ceramic and textile sectors is being disrupted. Due to the closure of large government and private projects, the demand for construction materials, cement and rod, has decreased greatly at the consumer level. As a result, the country's industrial sector is now in a four-pronged crisis. 

According to those concerned, there are more than 3,000 large industries in the country. 68 percent of the total employment is involved in manufacturing industries. In addition, 63 percent of raw materials and 56 percent of electricity and fuel are used by large industries like rod-cement and textile sectors. As a result, the high dollar value and gas and electricity shortage are having a direct negative impact on the production of these industries. On top of this, mill owners are in trouble due to lack of demand in the market. Many are in fear of losing capital. 

Demand and production of rod-cement are down: The demand for rod and cement has decreased significantly in the last quarter of 2024 (September to December) compared to the previous year. Data from these two industries shows that the demand for cement in the market has decreased by about 35 percent; on the other hand, the demand for rod has decreased by 65 to 70 percent. Due to the decrease in demand, manufacturers are now trying to maintain the market by reducing prices. Even that is not working. Abdur Rahim, General Manager of the cement manufacturing company 'Diamond Cement', said, 'The demand for cement is currently very low due to the closure of major government and private construction works. As a result, factory production has also decreased. Usually, the demand for cement is high from January to March. But this time the expected sales are not happening.' 

It is known that the 'peak hour' of the construction industry is considered to be the first three months of the year, January, February and March. In these three months, the bulk of the total demand of the year is sold in rod cement and other materials. But the rod-cement manufacturing companies plan their production keeping this time in mind. Raw materials and other materials are imported. Due to the decline in demand before the start of the construction season, the rate of opening import letters of credit (LC) is now decreasing. Production has also decreased. Those concerned said that in the past years, the prices of rods and cement have been on the rise during these three months from January to March. Last year, rods were sold at between 1 lakh 5 thousand and 1 lakh 7 thousand per ton at this time. But this time the picture is different. This year, rods are being sold at 85 thousand to 90 thousand taka per ton. The same situation is in the case of cement. Currently, cement is being sold at 470 to 500 taka per bag depending on the company. Last year, it was 490 to 530 taka at the same time. The decrease in demand as opposed to production has affected production. In the meantime, the production of almost all rod and cement factories has come down by half. Md. Sarwar Alam, Managing Director of HM Steel and Golden Ispat, said, "Even in the peak season, companies manufacturing construction materials including rods and cement are not getting the expected response in sales. During this time, sales are higher than at other times of the year. The sector has been affected by the closure of large and medium-sized public and private construction projects, which have not started new projects. Hopefully, some are being sold by the end of December. 

Private loan Raw material imports have decreased: The latest report of Bangladesh Bank says that in the first five months of the current 2024-25 fiscal year (July-November), capital equipment imports have decreased by about 26 percent compared to the same period of the last fiscal year. Settlement of letters of credit has decreased by about 22 percent. On the other hand, private sector credit growth has gradually fallen to its lowest level in the last three and a half years. 

According to the latest data from the central bank, private sector credit growth in November last year was 7.66 percent compared to the same period of the previous year; in November 2023, it was 9.90 percent. Those concerned said that due to the decrease in imports, foreign exchange reserves have increased slightly from $20 billion to $22 billion; however, despite the increase in reserves, the dollar crisis in the market has not ended. In addition, the price of the dollar is still high. And the high value of the dollar has created a major crisis in the import of raw materials for the rod-cement industry. SK Masudul Alam Masud, founder chairman of the Bangladesh Auto Re-Rolling and Steel Mills Association, recently told Bangladesh Pratidin, "Even though we pay the LC to the banks in Taka, we have to import raw materials in Dollars. Now the price of the Dollar has risen to 120 to 130 Taka. As a result, the capital of the rod and cement industry has decreased by about 40 percent just because of the increase in the value of the Dollar. He fears that if this crisis in the construction materials industry continues, the country's economy may come to a standstill."

Headline_English: Foreigners in Bangladesh increase spending on credit cards
Content_Enlish:
In the last eight months, foreigners spent the most money on credit cards in Bangladesh in November 2024. Foreigners visiting or living in Bangladesh for work spent Tk 204 crore on credit cards in November. Earlier, foreigners spent the most money on credit cards in Bangladesh in March last year. In that month, foreigners made about Tk 226 crore transactions on credit cards in Bangladesh. 

In November of the just-ended year, Bangladeshi transactions on credit cards at home and abroad decreased. In November, 431 crore was spent on credit cards outside the country, which was Tk 499 crore in October. And in November, transactions within the country were Tk 2,793 crore, which was Tk 2,866 crore in the previous month. Accordingly, transactions within the country decreased by Tk 73 crore or 2.54 percent in a month. In addition, transactions outside the country decreased by 680 million taka or 13.62 percent. Overall, Bangladeshi credit card spending abroad decreased in May due to a decrease in spending, mainly in neighboring India, the United States, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Australia and Ireland. Although Bangladeshi credit card transactions decreased in the United States in November, the country is on the top list of spending. Such information has emerged in the latest report of Bangladesh Bank. 

According to the central bank's report, credit cards are used more in 11 sectors within the country. These sectors include department stores, retail shopping, paying bills for various services, cash withdrawals, medicines and pharmacies, clothing purchases, money transfers, spending in the transportation sector, various business and professional services and paying bills for government services. Among these sectors, except for cash withdrawals, credit card holders spent less in all other sectors in November. 

In November, 1,334 million taka was spent in department stores within the country. In the previous month, October, 1,400 million taka was spent through credit cards in this sector. In addition, in other sectors, 406 crore taka was spent on retail purchases in November, 246 crore taka on paying bills for various services, 196 crore taka on cash withdrawals, 164 crore taka on medicines and pharmacies, 148 crore taka on clothing purchases, 76 crore taka on money transfers, 99 crore taka on transportation, 79 crore taka on various business and professional services, and 43 crore taka on paying bills for government services on credit cards. 

People involved in the sector say that after the political change, many are not getting visas to India. Again, many do not want to go into this instability. Due to this, the use of credit cards by Bangladeshis in India has decreased. In addition, Bangladeshis traveled less in November compared to October in some other countries. Due to this, spending on credit cards has decreased in those countries. On the other hand, their spending on credit cards has increased as Bangladeshis traveled more in November. The report shows that Bangladeshi credit card holders spent 68 crore taka in the United States in November. In the previous month, October, they spent 84 crore taka in the country. In the space of a month, Bangladeshis in the United States have spent less on credit cards by 160 million taka or 19 percent. 

The report was prepared by the Bangladesh Bank Statistics Department based on data from 44 banks and 1 financial institution issuing credit cards in the country. The report is prepared on a monthly basis. The financial sector regulator reports on the use of credit cards by Bangladeshi citizens inside and outside the country and by foreign citizens inside the country. The report also shows that Bangladeshi credit card usage decreased significantly in India and the United Arab Emirates in November. In India, credit card usage decreased by 70 million taka or about 13 percent in November compared to October. In India, Bangladeshis spent 540 million taka on credit cards in October, which decreased to 470 million taka in November. 

At the same time, Bangladeshi credit card usage in the United Arab Emirates decreased by 40 million taka or 20 percent. While Bangladeshis spent 200 million taka on credit cards in the Emirates in October, it decreased by 160 million taka in November. In addition, in Australia, credit card users in this country spent 20 million taka less in November compared to October, and in Ireland, credit card users in this country spent 10 million taka less in November compared to October. The use of credit cards has also decreased in the country, as well as abroad. In October, citizens of this country spent 2,866 crore taka on credit cards within the country, which decreased to 2,793 crore taka in November. Accordingly, the spending on credit cards within the country has decreased by 73 crore taka or 2.54 percent in one month. 

Cashless medium is becoming popular day by day around the world. Bangladesh Bank is planning to make three-fourths of the overall transactions in the country cashless by 2027. As part of this plan, various financial and non-financial banks are using various apps and other electronic media. Cards are undeniable for increasing the standard of living and making it digital. Customers are making record money transactions on Cash Recycling Machines (CRMs) and making more purchases through Point of Sales (POS) than ever before.

Headline_English: Unloading of 27,000 tons of rice from India begins
Content_Enlish:
Another consignment of rice imported from India at the government level has reached Chittagong Port. This consignment contains 26,935 metric tons of rice. 

The unloading of this rice, which arrived on the ship named MV SDR Universe, has started since Sunday evening. Earlier, the ship arrived at the jetty of Chittagong Port last Saturday night. 

Controller of the Food Department's Movement Control and Conservation Office, Gyanpriya Bidurshi Chakma, confirmed the matter. 

Sources concerned said that the ship named MV SDR Universe has brought 26,935 metric tons of rice from an Indian port under an open tender agreement. This is the second consignment of rice imported from India at the government level during the current interim government's tenure. The unloading has started after collecting samples of the rice kept on the ship and conducting physical tests. 

Earlier, on December 25, the ship 'MV Tanis Dream' carrying 24,690 tons of rice arrived at Chittagong Port from an Indian port.

Headline_English: VAT increase on 65 products: Purchasing power will decrease, industry will be under new pressure
Content_Enlish:
Traders are surprised and angry at the decision to increase VAT on 65 products including medicines, powdered milk, biscuits, juice, fruits, soap, sweets, etc. in the middle of the fiscal year under pressure from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). They are unable to accept the decision to increase VAT without any prior discussion with stakeholders. This will reduce the purchasing power of the people and will put new pressure on the industry. 

In the middle of the current 2024-25 fiscal year, the interim government has suddenly taken the initiative to increase revenue by increasing various types of taxes including VAT and supplementary duty. As part of this, VAT may be increased to 15 percent on 65 types of products and services including ready-made garments, sweets, AC restaurants, non-AC hotels. The draft of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025 was given in-principle approval in the meeting of the Advisory Council last Wednesday, subject to the vetting of the Parliamentary Affairs Department. 

VAT is the government's major revenue collection tool. Currently, the number of VAT registered organizations is 525,000. Out of these, an average of 350,000 organizations pay VAT regularly. Apart from this, there are still millions of organizations, and the National Board of Revenue (NBR) has taken few effective initiatives to bring those organizations under the scope of VAT. 
Business leaders say that the business and trade sector suffered a major setback after the political change in the student-public uprising. That loss could not be overcome. 

High inflation is also not being controlled. In such a situation, the decision to increase VAT is a blow to the dead. 15 percent VAT will have to be paid on food bills in restaurants. Until now, VAT was charged at a rate of 5 percent on food bills in AC restaurants. The interim government has taken a policy decision to increase it to 15 percent. 

When asked about its impact, Imran Hasan, Secretary General of the Bangladesh Restaurant Owners Association, said, "Restaurant owners are worried. If VAT is increased three times in one go, it will have a terrible impact on business. Income tax will also increase along with VAT. Those who do business according to all the rules and regulations are always oppressed. In fact, there are attempts to set traders on the path on the advice of the IMF. 

Initiatives have been taken to increase the VAT rate for buying clothes as well as restaurants. Currently, there is 7.5 percent VAT on the bill of ready-made garment outlets. This can be increased to 15 percent. This will also increase the cost of buying clothes. In addition, consumers may also spend more when buying sweets. Because initiatives are being taken to double the VAT rate on buying sweets from 7.5 percent. 

When asked, Azharul Haque Azad, president of the Bangladesh Fashion Entrepreneurs Association (FEAB), an organization of fashion house entrepreneurs, said, "We had to face big losses in July-August. We have not had a chance to overcome that yet. There is no chance to increase the VAT rate if we want to sustain business and trade. In this case, the NBR can emphasize on increasing the scope of VAT. 

Former president of the Bangladesh Sweet Producers Association, Madhav Chandra Ghosh, said, "Before taking such a big decision, it should have talked to the businessmen. Earlier, there was a 15 percent VAT. After reducing it to 7.5 percent, VAT collection increased. Because people feel comfortable when VAT is low." 

Apart from restaurants, clothing, hotels, other sectors that are going to have 15 percent VAT are biscuits, pickles, CR coils, mattresses, transformers, tissue paper, etc. at the production stage. The cost of air travel may also increase. Because initiatives have been taken to increase excise duty. In addition, initiatives have been taken to impose 15 percent VAT when making driving license cards. 

In addition to the initiative to increase VAT, businesses may have to pay turnover tax only if their annual turnover is 3 million to 5 million taka. Currently, tax is paid on turnover between 5 million and 3 crore taka. According to the new proposal, VAT can be levied at a rate of 15 percent on the sale of goods and services if the annual transaction exceeds 50 lakh taka. In addition, initiatives have been taken to increase supplementary duty on liquor bills. 

When asked about this, Dr. Mustafizur Rahman, Special Fellow at the Center for Policy Dialogue (CPD), said, "Increasing VAT in the middle of the fiscal year had to be done under pressure. In a high-inflation market, this will definitely create additional pressure on the consumer and producer levels. Increasing taxes on cigarettes or alcohol is logical." 

He also said, "In addition, some products are used by the upper middle class. But the rest are used by the lower middle class. Here, how to increase the coverage of direct taxes without increasing VAT should have been considered. At the same time, strong steps need to be taken to reduce indirect taxes, which affect people from all walks of life."

Headline_English: Three Ansar al-Islam militants arrested
Content_Enlish:
The Anti-Terrorism Unit (ATU) of the police has arrested three members of the banned militant organization Ansar Al Islam. They are Shiblu alias Rafiqul Islam alias Joddha of Hind, Zahidur Rahman alias Zahid and Shahadat Hossain. 

They were arrested in a raid in Noakhali and Comilla early on Friday. At that time, seven extremist books, five mobile phones and 10 SIM cards were seized from them. 

ATU Superintendent of Police Mohammad Aslam Khan said that Shiblu was arrested from Noakhali based on secret information. Later, the ATU arrested Zahidur and Shahadat from Comilla based on the information he provided. They were spreading militancy and conspiring against the state online. They used social media to spread extremist ideology among the common people, create panic, and plan, train and prepare for sabotage. 

The ATU said that the arrested militants had been regularly communicating with interested parties, including secret meetings, by publishing various extremist content online and inviting them to radicalization. They would hold secret meetings every month under the leadership of Shiblu to decide on the next plan with other members of the organization.

Headline_English: 2 arrested for attempting to murder friend by slitting his throat for money
Content_Enlish:
Two of Jahangir Alam's friends tried to kill a young man named Jahangir Alam (27) by slitting his throat for just 2,000 taka. The incident took place late last Friday night in the Love Road area of ​​Mirpur Model Police Station. The two friends involved in the incident, Sagar (32) and Shahed (35), were arrested that night. 

Jahangir is a driver and a motor mechanic. His friends Sagar and Shahed are also motor mechanics. Sagar used to receive 2,000 taka from Jahangir. The two had an argument over this money. Sagar and Shahed planned to kill Jahangir based on the argument. 

Jahangir's father Abdul Halim has filed a case in this incident. The two accused in the case, Sagar and Shahed, were arrested that night. The knife used in the attempted murder, the motorcycle and the accused's blood-stained clothes were recovered.

Headline_English: Young man confesses to kidnapping 2 Japanese citizens
Content_Enlish:
A young man named Abu Russell Pratyay has given a confessional statement in the court in the case of kidnapping from two Japanese citizens. His statement was recorded in the court of Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mainul Islam on Saturday. Later, he was sent to jail along with another accused Jihadul Islam Mamun. 

The two Japanese citizens were robbed at around 8:30 pm on April 24 while visiting the Rayerbazar slaughterhouse. The robbers took away various items including money, iPhones, credit cards and other items from them using country-made weapons. 

After a case was filed at Mohammadpur Police Station in this incident, the police arrested Russell and Mamun from Sitakunda, Chittagong last Friday. A Japanese citizen's iPhone, 30,000 yen, a portable hotspot and a Bluetooth were recovered from them. 

When the two accused were presented in court on Saturday, Russell agreed to give a confessional statement. The court later recorded his statement and ordered the two accused to be sent to prison.

Headline_English: Aarav also cheated with a 60 kg gold falcon
Content_Enlish:
Aarav Khan alias Rabiul Islam, the accused in the police murder case, used to fool many people in Dubai to get various types of fraud traps. He used to tempt them to get various jobs by claiming to have close relations with many influential people in the country. He also took money from some in the name of lobbying. He even does not own all the money he has been promoting on social media. 

It has been learned from talking to several Bangladeshis living in Dubai that Rabiul has been doing strange things in Dubai for a few days around the inauguration of Aarav Jewelers. He announced on his Facebook that a logo in the shape of a hawk has been made with 60 kg of gold on the occasion of the inauguration of the gold shop, which took two and a half months to make. It cost about 45 crore taka to make it. However, several gold traders in Dubai told Samakal that there is doubt whether the logo that is being talked about as being made of gold is made entirely of gold. They also confirmed after investigating where it was made that it was not entirely made of gold. Aarav did this to go viral on social media. He took the help of an Indian businessman to create the logo. He also said on Facebook Live that he would apply to Guinness World Records for a logo in the shape of a falcon. 

Bangladeshi citizen Nazrul Islam has been doing gold business in Dubai with a good reputation for a long time. He is one of the owners of NRI Jewelers in Dubai. When asked about Aarav, Nazrul Islam told Samakal, "Suddenly one day, we saw that Aarav had brought a 60 kg gold falcon logo. At first, we thought it was something huge. We thought that the person who brought such a big event in the world of gold must have a lot of things. Then the fuss about the gold falcon started. Later, after investigating, I found out that it was not entirely made of gold. Those who made it say that it is not made entirely of gold. It is plated with gold. Everyone in Dubai knows now. Aarav's goal was to go viral.

The expatriate businessman also said that none of those who are doing gold business in Dubai have any idea about Aarav. He has been visiting the gold market for some time. He comes wearing branded shoes and clothes. Suddenly he comes and rents a gold shop. No one in Dubai knew him. Shakib Al Hasan made a stir by posting a video about his shop. 

In addition, Aarav Khan has announced on his own Facebook page that he has bought a flat on the 65th floor of Dubai's Burj Khalifa Tower, whose number is 6510. He also owns 4-5 other flats. He also has a swimming pool, a garden and a large duplex house. Where he occasionally invites Bangladeshis by slaughtering a magical deer. He cultivates Bangladeshi vegetables in the garden. He has several expensive cars. Several residents of the Bangladeshi community in Dubai said that the house that Aarav claims to own is not his at all. The house is owned by a Bangladeshi businessman named Russell. 

At least three expatriates living in Dubai said that another aspect of Aarav's fraud was to discredit influential people. He took money from many people on the pretext of knowing people from various Bangladeshi classes and professions. Aarav could not pay the promised money to the Bangladeshi artists he took to Dubai for the inauguration of the Jewelers. The country's detectives are investigating Bayezid and Maruf, who are close to Aarav. Both of them were in Dubai on the day of the showroom inauguration. It is known that Aarav and his associates have been involved in smuggling gold from the country for a long time. He also has friends in the showbiz world. 

The country's best cricketer Shakib Al Hasan has faced criticism for inaugurating the jewelers owned by Aarav Khan, an accused in the police officer murder case. Aarav is an accused in the murder case of Inspector Mamun Emran Khan of the Special Branch (SB) of the police. On April 11, 2019, the Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) filed a chargesheet against 9 people, including Rabiul, in that case. Apart from the murder case, there are 9 arrest warrants against Rabiul in various crimes including weapons, women's torture, and fraud. Bangladesh Police has already written to the international police organization Interpol to bring him back to the country from the United Arab Emirates (Dubai). Meanwhile, discussions have started in various circles, including law enforcement agencies, about how Rabiul, the accused in the murder case, became wealthy in Dubai. 

At an event yesterday, Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal said that Interpol's cooperation has been sought to catch Aarav Khan. All efforts are being made to bring him back to the country. 

No acquaintance with anyone named Aarav: Former Inspector General of Police Benazir Ahmed said that she does not know anyone named Aarav alias Rabiul alias Hridoy. She does not even have a primary acquaintance with him. The former IGP said this in a Facebook post on Saturday amid discussions about Rabiul Islam, who became a big gold trader in Dubai despite being accused of killing a police officer in Dhaka. He wrote, Respected countrymen, I want to assure you all and completely confirm that I do not know anyone by the name 'Arab alias Rabiul alias Hridoy'. Benazir Ahmed said, I have fought against murderers, terrorists, drug dealers, smugglers, adulterators and criminals throughout my law enforcement career, never friendship. 

Asif Nazrul's question: How did Rabiul Islam become the owner of so much money in Dubai in the four-five years of fleeing the country – this question was raised by Dhaka University Law Professor Asif Nazrul. Speaking at a seminar at the National Press Club yesterday morning, he said that the number of beggars in the country is increasing day by day. And the son of a daily wage earner makes logos with gold. That too in just four-five years! What a lot of money is looted! Is this his money? We hear the name of a former senior police officer. We cannot take his name.

Headline_English: Bilkis, Zerin, and Afrin's terrible web on Facebook
Content_Enlish:
Seven men and three women have set up a honey trap. The ringleader is Bilkis Begum. Businessmen or employees are targeted. They roam the cyber world by opening multiple fake Facebook accounts in the name of women. When they find the target by searching through the Facebook profiles of various people, friend requests are sent. After entering the friend list, conversations start on Messenger. The intimacy increases. After this, a large sum of money is taken away by tricking them into 'the lair' and trapping them. 

Investigation revealed that the ring has been active since 2017. The 10-member ring includes - Bilkis Begum, Aisha Khatun Afrin, Ankhi Bairagi Jerin, Raju Sheikh, Raju Fakir, Kamrul Mia, Hasan Sheikh, Lalon Morol, Bakhtiar Mia and Asad Mia. The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime Unit (CTTC) of the police has arrested eight members of the gang, except Bakhtiar and Asad, in a case filed by Gulshan Police Station. Among them, Jerin has given a confessional statement in the court under Section 164. 

Sources said that the gang has set up a 'hideout' for criminal activities by renting three flats in Uttarkhan in the capital. They work in several stages. The job of the female members is to bring the target person to the hideout by any means. The male members enter the house under fake DB or police identity. They take pictures and videos of the victim naked with a young female member on a mobile phone. After that, the gang demands money by threatening to send the pictures to the wife or relatives or spread them on social media. The demands range from three lakh to one million taka. Fearing for their reputation, the victim pays the money in various ways, including mobile banking. After that, they are released from the hideout. 

The gang is also active outside Dhaka. Last December, they trapped four people in the capital and one in Khulna and embezzled Tk 3 million. 

Mohiuddin works in a private company in Motijheel. In early December, he received a friend request on Facebook from an ID named 'Nusrat Jahan'. He accepted it. He started a conversation with Mohiuddin, introducing himself as a young garment trader. Within a few days, they became close. Nusrat's real name is Ankhi Bairagi Jerin. 

On the afternoon of December 30, Jerin asked Mohiuddin to go to his house in Uttarkhan. As promised, he went to the Uttarkhan railway gate. 

From there, Jerin and Afrin, who introduced themselves as Nusrat, took him to his house from the railway gate. Within a few minutes of entering the house, five men entered there. They started beating him up, accusing him of going there for immoral activities. They stripped him naked and took pictures and videos on their mobile phones. Later, they demanded a large sum of money by threatening to send it to his wife and relatives and spread it on the internet. He was forced to pay the money through mobile banking and was released. 

A week before this incident, a businessman named Rouf Ahmed was called to another house in Uttarkhan and money was extorted from him using the same trick. In this incident, Afrin, a member of the gang, was contacted on Facebook. On December 23, Afrin and another young woman of the gang, Zerin, took the businessman from Gulshan to his house in Uttarkhan. He released the gang by paying Tk 12,33,700. 

Additional Deputy Police Commissioner of CTTC Cyber ​​​​Department Nazmul Islam said that the gang members have been extorting money since 2017 by trapping them in a honey trap. Their fraud started by sending a friend request to the target person's Facebook ID. Efforts are also underway to arrest the two absconding members.

Headline_English: Militants planned simultaneous attacks on Kashimpur jail
Content_Enlish:
Sensational information is emerging after the arrest of two top leaders of the new militant organization Jamaatul Ansar Phil Hindal Sharqia. It is learned that these new militant members had planned to release the extremists by carrying out a simultaneous militant attack on Kashimpur prison. 

On Monday, Masukur Rahman Masud alias Ranbir, the head of the military wing of the new militant organization, and bomb expert Abul Bashar Mridha were arrested in a RAB operation in Cox's Bazar's Rohingya camp. After that, videos of training activities in the mountains were seized from their mobile phones. 

Regarding this video, a high-ranking RAB official told Samakal that these small videos were made three-four months ago. They had planned to 'claim responsibility' by carrying out a major attack and releasing these videos along with weapons. They had planned to release the extremists by carrying out a simultaneous militant attack on Kashimpur prison. Most of the weapons training videos were found on the device of Ranbir, a military trainer of the new militant organization. 30-35 youths were seen in the video. The missing list of homeless youths that was published is also in the military training video. Three of those seen in the video have been arrested. They are Saleh Ahmed, Nizam Uddin and Abul Bashar Mridha. 

At a press conference at the Karwan Bazar Media Center on Tuesday, Commander Khandaker Al Moin, Director of the Legal and Media Branch of RAB, said that the arrested Ranbir was a 'robber' in his early life. While in prison, he came into contact with the top leaders of another militant organization, JMB, and got involved in extremism. His home is in Sylhet. Before 2007, he worked in the postal department. He also robbed various places. Several cases were filed against him on charges of robbery. Ranbir was arrested and imprisoned several times in that case after 2007. After being released on bail, he started working for JMB. 

He mainly looked after the families of JMB members who were in prison. He also maintained contact with imprisoned JMB members. Ranbir met Mosharraf Hossain alias Rakib, the current Shura member and head of the Finance and Media Branch of Jamaatul Ansar, in 2017. He joined Jamaatul Ansar as a founding member through Rakib. 

Commander Moin further said that Ranbir used to conduct invitation and training activities of the organization in the Sylhet region, including the selection of members of the military wing. From the beginning, he had been playing a major role in various policy-making issues of the military wing of the organization. Under the direction of the Amir of the organization, he organized Shura committee meetings in various places in the country, including Paduar Bazar in Comilla. In 2021, Ranbir was also present with the Amir of the organization and other Shura members at the agreement reached with the hill separatist party KNF or Bomb Party regarding the training of Jamaatul Ansar. 

More incidents are being heard of common criminals getting involved in militancy after going to prison. Asked whether prisons have become safe havens for extremist initiation, Commander Moin said, "The matter has been reported to the intelligence agencies and prison authorities. They are working."

Headline_English: Case filed over drum explosion in Moghbazar
Content_Enlish:
A case has been filed in connection with a drum explosion in the Wireless Gate area of ​​Bara Moghbazar in the capital. The police filed the case with Ramna Model Police Station on Tuesday night under the Explosives Act. An unknown accused has been named without mentioning anyone. Ramna Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Abul Hasan told reporters on Wednesday morning. 

The OC said, "The police have filed a case in connection with the explosion in Moghbazar. The case was filed last night with an unknown accused. We are working to uncover the true mystery." 

Earlier, an explosion occurred at Bara Moghbazar's Wireless Crossing around 9:45 am on Tuesday. Several people were injured in the explosion. There are two schools under the six-story building where the explosion occurred. One of them is St. Mary's International School, the other is Ramna Kids Kindergarten School. There is a Metro Department Store next to it. There is a drug store under the school. It is initially believed that the explosion was caused by a drum kept there. The explosion shattered the school's window glass and scattered it in different places. Several people, including an engineer, were injured and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. 

It was seen on the spot that the six-storey building is quite old. There is a school on the first, second and third floors on one side. And there is a pharmacy and a superstore on the ground floor. There is another kindergarten school on the other side of the building. And the remaining floors are girls' hostels. The two schools and the pharmacy were closed after the explosion. 

Following the incident, various police agencies started working there. CTTC and CID collected evidence from the scene. CTTC Chief Asaduzzaman, who arrived at the scene that day, said, "The 'explosive material' was already kept in the exploded plastic drum. The explosion occurred due to carelessness in throwing it away. We are working to find out who placed the explosives or how they got here. 

And DB chief Harun-ur-Rashid said, "Numerous splinters have been recovered from the scene of the drum explosion."

Headline_English: Accused in Turag kidnapping case arrested, abductee rescued
Content_Enlish:
RAB-3 has arrested Md. Rubel Hossain (32), the main accused in a kidnapping case filed at Tentulia Police Station in Panchagarh. He was arrested from Chayani Chara Kamar Para area under Turag Police Station in the capital on Saturday. 

RAB-3 commander Lt. Col. Arif Mohiuddin Ahmed said that Rubel is the main accused in a kidnapping case filed at Tentulia Police Station in Panchagarh. He had kidnapped the victim and demanded a large sum of money as ransom from her family. When the victim's family did not agree to his demand, he threatened to kill the victim and physically and mentally tortured her. 

He said that Rubel was arrested in a drive conducted in Chayani Chara Kamar Para area under Turag Police Station in the capital. The abductee was also rescued. Legal action against Rubel is under process.

Headline_English: Couple used to call home and hold hostages in the name of buying land
Content_Enlish:
Police have arrested a couple on charges of calling a seller or middleman to their house and beating him up and taking him hostage to extort money. They are Abdul Halim and Yasmin Akhter.
