They were arrested late on Thursday night from the Paikpara area of ​​Mirpur in the capital. Police said that Halim and Yasmin had been defrauding various people in the name of buying land for the past two years. When Halim received news that someone was selling land in Dhaka and nearby districts, he would rush to them disguised as a broker. He would tell the seller or middleman that the buyer of the land, Yasmin, lives in Mirpur. The price of the land would be finalized by sitting at her house and discussing it. When the seller or middleman fell into their trap and went to their house, they would be caught, beaten up and ransomed. 

Mirpur Police Station OC Mohammad Mohsin said that Halim had been extorting money from people through fraud for a long time. Yasmin is his second wife. He is also Yasmin's second husband. They got married in 2021. Since then, the couple started cheating in the name of land purchase and sale. 

Police said that Halim's village is in Atkapara of Pakundia police station in Kishoreganj. Yasmin's house is in Lakherraj Kasba of Gournadi police station in Barishal. Among the other two members of the gang, Russell Howlader's village is in Kaunia of Betagi police station in Barguna and Rabiul Awal's village is in Dasadi village of Chandpur district sadar. They also lived in Madhya Paikpara in Mirpur. A few days ago, Halim showed interest in buying land from Billal Hossain of Singair in Manikganj. At that time, Halim said that the main buyer is in Mirpur, Dhaka. He will have to sit with him and complete the formalities. Later, Yasmin called Billal on the phone to a house in Mirpur. When Billal went to that house, Halim, Yasmin and 4-5 other members of their gang stopped him. They took Billal to a room, beat him up, and robbed him of 7,500 taka and his mobile phone. Later, Halim and Yasmin called Billal's house and stole another 35,000 taka through bKash. Billal filed a case with Mirpur Police Station in this incident. In a separate such incident, a person from Savar filed a case against Halim and Yasmin last October.

Headline_English: They cheat with fake identities and fake checks.
Content_Enlish:
Four people have been arrested in Dhaka on charges of fraud. The arrested people used a novel method to steal electronic products worth lakhs of taka and escape. Sometimes they bought a large amount of products from a shop by posing as the chairman of the company, sometimes as a senior official, and sometimes as a contractor. Then they skillfully escaped with those products. They committed such fraud by moving from one district of the country to another. On February 12, they escaped with 25 fans. Later, Mirpur Model Police Station arrested them from different places. 

The five arrested are Fakhruzzaman Tapu Bhuiyan (45), Md. Mobarak Hossain (34), Md. Khokon Mia (43) and Md. Mushfiqur Rahman Munshi (35). 

According to the police, on February 12, the accused bought 25 Konka ceiling fans from a shop called Electro Mart by posing as senior officials of Ibn Sina. Then, when asked for the money for the fans, they gave a check stating that they did not have cash. But when he went to the bank, it was found that the signature on the check did not match the signature of the account holder, and even the name of the account holder did not match. Meanwhile, Fakhruzzaman and his gang took this opportunity to escape with a fan. Later, when he complained to the police station, a team of Mirpur Model Police Station arrested them from Gazipur, Narayanganj. 

Fraud by showing the next place, the next building: 

The main tool of fraud of Fakhruzzaman and his gang was the next place and the next building. They first scouted for any under-construction building. Later, seizing the opportunity, they introduced themselves as the contractor for the construction of that building. Since the cable was needed for the construction of the building, they bought the cable from a nearby shop. Then, saying they did not have cash, they gave them a check. But when he went to the bank, it was found that there was no money in that account! The signature given there was also fake! Meanwhile, Fakhruzzaman and his gang escaped with that cable. In this way, this gang fled with goods worth about 1.25 lakh taka from Gopalganj, about 1 lakh taka from Moulvibazar, about 1 lakh taka from Kishoreganj, 1.25 lakh taka from Sunamganj, and about 75 thousand taka from Mirpur. 

Purchase of goods with fake checks: 

His name is Fakhruzzaman Topu Bhuiyan. But the name on his check is Iqbal Hossain! He opened a bank account with a fake name. After purchasing the goods, he gave the check to that account! But the bank found that the signature on the issued check was also fake! 

Sometimes a contractor, sometimes a chairman: 

Fakhruzzaman is a fraudster. But he is sometimes a contractor, and sometimes the chairman of the company! He cheats by pretending to be a contractor in the name of buying cables for a building under construction. Sometimes he cheats by pretending to be the chairman of the company or a senior official. Finally, he pretended to be a senior official of Ibn Sina Hospital and fled with them, pretending to buy 25 fans. 

Fakhruzzaman cheats by moving from district to district: 

Fakhruzzaman cheats by moving from one district to another. He has a driver in his team. That driver cheats in one district and escapes with a car and goes to another district. So far, information about cheating has been found in Sunamganj, Moulvibazar, Kishoreganj, Narsingdi, Gopalganj. 

From expatriate to fraudster in IPL gambling: 

Fakhruzzaman was an expatriate. He lived in Saudi Arabia. He worked there. His income was also good. But his bad days came in IPL gambling. After losing more than 10 lakh taka in IPL online gambling, he returned to the country. Then he became a fraudster.

Headline_English: Death row convict Muhammad Ali was on the run for 10 years
Content_Enlish:
RAB-3 has arrested Abu Muslim Mohammad Ali (70), a convict sentenced to death for crimes against humanity in Gaibandha during the 1971 Liberation War. He had been on the run for almost 10 years. He was arrested from Demra in the capital on Sunday. His home is in Purba Jhinia village of Sundarganj police station in Gaibandha. 

RAB said that Abu Muslim Mohammad Ali was one of the organizers of the Islami Chhatra Sangha in 1971 and a member of the Sundarganj police station Jamaat-e-Islami. In 1971, he carried out killings, kidnappings, torture and looting in the area under the leadership of Maulana Momtaz Uddin, the Gaibandha district head of the Peace Committee. On October 9, 1971, some Razakars and Pakistani invaders led by Abu Muslim attacked and looted the house of Ganesh Chandra Barman in Malibari village. The house was set on fire. Ganesh Chandra Barman was captured, beaten to death, tied bricks and stones to his body and drowned in the river. 

On that day, Akbar Ali from the same area was taken to the camp and killed. Akbar Ali's son Anisur Rahman filed a case in the Gaibandha court in 2013 against Abu Muslim and others for crimes against humanity. 

The case was transferred to the International Crimes Tribunal in 2014. Abu Muslim went into hiding soon after the case. In 2017, the International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Abu Muslim and five other defendants to death.

Headline_English: Faruk murdered over sharing of robbery money, 3 arrested
Content_Enlish:
Police said that Faruk Hossain was murdered in the capital's Panthapath over the money he had stolen from selling a mobile phone. Three people have been arrested in the incident. Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner HM Azimul Haque gave this information at a press conference organized at the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Media Center on Sunday. 
The arrested persons are Saddam Hossain Sabbir alias Situ Sabbir alias Sagar, Md. Roni and Md. Bijoy. They are involved in the robbery. Police said that a knife used in the murder was recovered from them. 
Deputy Commissioner HM Azimul Haque said that the deceased Faruk lived with his family in a slum adjacent to the Karwan Bazar railway line. He was involved in the robbery gang in addition to driving a van. The deceased Faruk and the arrested Sabbir, Roni and Bijoy were arrested in a robbery case and were in jail. They were released on bail three days before the incident. They started robbing again. They stole 12 mobile phones in two days. They sold them. Faruk had an argument with Sabbir about sharing the money.

Headline_English: 1 arrested in lawyer Bhuvan murder case
Content_Enlish:
Police have arrested a man named Himel in connection with the death of lawyer Bhuban Chandra Shil (55), who was shot dead by terrorists in the capital. 

He was arrested from Old Dhaka in the capital on Monday evening. 

SM Arif Raihan, Assistant Commissioner (AC) of Tejga Zone of Dhaka Metropolitan Police. 

Bhuban Chandra was shot dead by terrorists in Tejgaon Industrial Area on September 18 while returning from his office to the mess in Fakirapul Arambagh. After being under treatment for 8 days, doctors declared Bhuban dead at 10:35 am on Monday.

Headline_English: Mohammadpur's panic is 'I don't care'
Content_Enlish:
After the 'Law Thela', 'Anwar alias Suiter Anwar' and 'Akash' groups, 'I Don't Care' (IDC) has now become a terror in the capital's Mohammadpur area. The head of this terrorist group is Md. Sohel. Their slogan is 'King of IDC Son of Mafia'. Currently, this terrorist group is active in some parts of Bashila, Dhaka Udyan, Chandrima Udyan and Mirpur; who have become a terror to the common people. No one even files a case against them due to fear of attacks. 

It is known that Sohel, Atiyar, Rabiul and Akash of Adabor No. 10 are active members of the IDC group. The members of Anwar's group are Bhagina Naeem, Rafat, Tushar, Yusuf, Tunda Babu, Pagla Nasir and Ahmed. These two groups are also known as 'King of Mohammadpur'. Some of them have been arrested by law enforcement officers. However, the rest are still at large. 

A police source says that these terrorists do not have a specific profession. Some are autorickshaw drivers, some are leguna drivers. They are involved in various crimes. The 'Suiter Anwar Group' came to the fore in the incident of cutting off hands and making TikTok. The group was led by bloodsuckers Johnny and Anwar. Later, due to a dispute, they separated with their followers. On July 24, Anwar Group came to attack Johnny. On that day, Johnny's follower Shakil Exa cut off both wrists of Sentu. Five people have been paralyzed by this group so far, who are undergoing treatment in various hospitals in the capital. Among them, Pashu Alamgir, a follower of Johnny, was attacked by Anwar Group. They severed his wrists and made TikTok. Sentu was the second victim of the attack. Later, Arman Hossain, Ruhul Amin and Sajjad were attacked. 

Many eyewitnesses could not forget the terrifying look of Anwar seen during the attack. According to them, Anwar attacked very quickly and fled the scene. In addition, during the attack, he told his followers - don't kill me, teach me, my name will be remembered. 

Jahangir Hossain, the elder brother of the victim Sentu, said, "People from Anwar's group hacked and injured my brother for hanging out with Johnny. Sentu is currently at home. However, his condition is not good. Meanwhile, the terrorists are threatening me because I am talking." 

Ruhul Amin's wife Nadia Begum said, "On the day of the incident, my husband went to the office with 2 lakh taka from his house. At that time, some people including Anwar surrounded him and took the bag of money. When he stopped him, they hit Ruhul on his left hand. This cut two veins in his hand. When he stepped forward to protect my husband, they hacked a person named Sajjad. Both his hands are now immobile." 

Locals allege that the terrorists, including Anwar, Sohel and Naeem, are roaming openly. The law enforcement agencies are not arresting them. This is increasing the incidents of kidnapping and attacks. Apart from this, panic is spreading among the common people. No one wants to file a case for fear of being attacked if they file a case. 

Meanwhile, RAB and police are giving different information about the terrorists in Mohammad area. RAB says about Anwar, Naeem and Sohel that they crossed the border illegally. While the police say that they are in the country. They have left their village due to the operation. In the meantime, on October 2, Anwar hacked and injured two people named Sajjad and Ruhul Amin in Mohammadpur area. Anwar and Naeem were seen participating in it. Sohel was with them. Their names are in the case of this incident. Recently, 14 people were arrested in the police operation and five people from Akash Group were arrested in the RAB operation, a total of 22 people were arrested. However, Anwar and the heads of IDC Group are out of reach. 

Azizul Haque, Assistant Commissioner (AC) of Tejgaon Mohammadpur Zone, told Samakal that several police teams are working in the field. Anwar has left his village after the police operation. He is in the country. Efforts are underway to arrest him. In addition, additional patrols have been increased in the Mohammadpur area. 

Commander Khandaker Al Moin, Director of the Law and Media Branch of RAB, told Samakal that RAB is conducting a drive to arrest several juvenile gangs and terrorist groups that are active in the Mohammadpur area. The criminals have fled in the face of the drive. RAB detectives are active, and wherever they are found, they are being brought under the law. In addition, it is believed that Anwar, the head of the Anwar Group, has left the country.

Headline_English: 5 militants arrested from a house in Comilla
Content_Enlish:
Police arrested five members of the militant organization Allah Dal from a house in the Dakshin Thakurpara area of ​​Kotwali Police Station in Comilla on Saturday. A press conference was organized at the Anti-Terrorism Unit (ATU) headquarters in Baridhara in the capital on Sunday to provide details. 

Speaking at the press conference, ATU Police Superintendent (Media) Mohammad Chanowar Hossain said that the militants are taking advantage of the fact that the law enforcement agencies are busy with the national elections. They have suddenly become active in dawah activities. They are renting houses under pseudonyms and conducting dawah activities for the organization. However, no information is known about their plans to carry out violence. Apart from this, no information about their affiliation with any political party has been found. 

According to a source, especially followers of Ahle Hadith are becoming members of Allah Dal. Their bases are in Gaibandha, Rangpur, Sylhet, Jamalpur and Comilla. The militants use a different code for each of their houses. The code for that house in Comilla is the coaching center. Members were asked to come to the coaching center. They used to work for the organization while sitting there. 

The five arrested are the Comilla district Amir of Allah Dal, Mashiur Rahman Russell, his associates Abu Sufian, Md. Salahuddin, Md. Alauddin and Julhas Hossain. At that time, some members had escaped from there. Mashiur did his honors-masters in English from Comilla Victoria College. He teaches privately and earns a living. This is part of his dawati work. Salahuddin is a diploma engineer. He runs a ready-made garment shop in Comilla. He mainly looks after the financial side of the organization. Alauddin is a teacher by profession. 
Sufian is a second-year student of Comilla Victoria College. Julhas was invited to this organization two months ago. The police have filed a case against them under the Anti-Terrorism Act at the Kotwali Model Police Station in Comilla. They have been taken on a three-day remand for further investigation.

Headline_English: Kalam did not give up theft despite serving 45 prison terms
Content_Enlish:
Abul Kalam Azad (55) has been imprisoned not once or twice, but at least 45 times. Even after this, he did not reform. He did not give up stealing. He was released on bail and started stealing again. Kalam, an accused in 53 cases, used to steal rickshaws in the beginning. 

After getting acquainted with a motorcycle thief in prison, he got out on bail and stopped stealing rickshaws. He got involved in motorcycle theft. He stole four to five motorcycles every month. However, the 'income' from stealing goes behind the scenes. 

Kalam was arrested by the Wari Division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) police last Tuesday night. After that, he confessed to the theft. 

The DB said that Kalam's home is in the southern Dudhal area of ​​Bakerganj police station in Barisal. He lived in Dhaka and Narayanganj for about three decades. Sometimes he used to drive a rickshaw, sometimes he used to push a wheelbarrow. In 2010, his rickshaw was stolen in the capital's Rampura area. After that, he himself went to steal rickshaws. A year later, he was caught stealing and went to jail. So far, Kalam has been arrested at least 45 times and has been to jail. He has been on police remand 10-12 times in various cases. In one case, Kalam had to spend a maximum of 13 months in jail. After his arrest, his wife borrowed money to get him bail. He stole a bike on bail and paid the loan after receiving the money from the sale. 

In prison, Kalam met Jasim, Rakib, and Rahim, members of a motorcycle theft gang. They stole together after getting out on bail, but later, except for Kalam, others became the ringleaders of the theft gang. They formed a separate gang and stole. Usually, Kalam and Khalek steal motorcycles from the garages of residential buildings. There are a few others in the gang. Kalam went to jail three months ago in a theft case. He was released on bail two months ago. A team from the Wari Division of the DB arrested him and four others from the Jatrabari area on Tuesday in a motorcycle theft case. They were sent to court yesterday.

Headline_English: 4 arrested in Farmgate policeman murder case
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) has arrested four people on charges of involvement in the murder of traffic police constable Moniruzzaman Talukder at the capital's Farmgate. 
The DB Tejgaon division arrested them during separate raids in the capital on Saturday. 

Dhaka DB Tejgaon division Deputy Commissioner Md. Golam Sabur confirmed this information to Samakal on Sunday morning. 

Golam Sabur said that four people have been arrested on charges of killing Moniruzzaman. One has confessed to the murder. Details will be provided later. 

He also said that more of our teams are working in the field to arrest the remaining members of this gang. 

Constable Moniruzzaman was stabbed to death in front of Farmgate Sejan Point early Saturday morning. 

Moniruzzaman returned to Dhaka from his village home yesterday morning after spending the Eid holidays. He got down at Tejgaon railway station by train. Later, he was walking to his workplace. Before that, he was stabbed in front of Sejan Point in Farmgate.

Headline_English: The groom-to-be is accused in a rape case, but it later turns out that it was all a lie.
Content_Enlish:
The marriage was finalized, and the wedding was to be held shortly after - at a time when the woman was attempted to rape by the groom-to-be and his companion. A case was filed on this allegation. However, the investigation revealed that the complainant and the accused did not know each other. Technical analysis also revealed that the three were in different places at the time of the alleged rape attempt. When the woman was asked to contact her with a medical certificate and necessary information, she hid her identity. At one point, it emerged that the opponent had used the woman to frame the two people due to a dispute. 
Among the accused, businessman Md. Shahidulya told Samakal, this is not the first such incident. In the last six years, at least 14 cases have been filed against me on various charges. Out of these, 11 have been proven false during the investigation. The court has ruled that I am innocent and the case has been dismissed. 

The case filed on the charge of attempted rape has been investigated by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI). Investigation officer PBI Dhaka Metropolitan North Inspector Mohammad Jewel Miah said that as per the plaintiff's claim, an attempted rape took place in a house in Shah Ali area of ​​Mirpur in the capital. However, during the investigation, the caretaker of the house, Anil, said that he had been on duty there for about two years. During this time, no woman by that name had been a tenant in the house. And he had not heard of any incident of attempted rape. The owner of the house next door, Md. Jamal, also gave similar information to the police. 

The investigation officer said that when the plaintiff was questioned, he did not give any address to the police, nor did he give any other information including his profession. At one point, he stopped communicating with those involved in the investigation. However, technical investigation showed that the accused Shahidullah was in his business establishment in Tejgaon Industrial Area at the time of the incident. The other accused, Khalilur Rahman Khokon, was in the Pallabi Police Station area. None of them were located in Shah Ali, the place where the incident took place. However, according to the plaintiff's claim, the accused went to his house and tried to rape her by stripping her naked. Then, when people came forward, they ran away.

Investigation-related sources said that the court ordered the PBI to investigate the case filed in the Women and Child Abuse Prevention Tribunal. As per the directions of PBI Chief Additional Inspector General of Police Banaj Kumar Majumdar, Additional Superintendent of Police Farida Yasmin Kanta supervised the investigation of the case. On their advice, the investigation officer tried to find out the reason for filing the false case. It was then learned that one party had a dispute with Shahidulla over land in her village home in Noakhali. On the other hand, some of her colleagues also had a dispute with Khalilur Rahman Khokon, an employee of a government organization. Several cases and complaints have been filed against them in different places in the past due to the dispute. 

Although the mobile phone of the plaintiff in the attempted rape case was called to inquire about this, he did not pick up. 

Shahidulla claimed that he had bought 106 percent of the land from a neighbor in Noakhali. But after paying the money, he found out that 56 percent of it belonged to the neighbor. The remaining 50 percent was actually owned by others. As a result, he suffered financial losses. From then on, his dispute with the land seller began. To avoid returning the remaining money he had taken through fraud, the land seller started filing one case after another against him. Although they were ultimately proven to be false, attempts to harass him continued.

Headline_English: Sister stabbed to death by 'drug-addicted' brother in Jatrabari
Content_Enlish:
A woman named Ayesha Akhter Roni (45) was stabbed to death by her younger brother in Jatrabari in the capital. The incident took place on Monday night. She was taken to the hospital in a serious condition and was declared dead by doctors. 

Relatives say that the accused Robin is a drug addict. He has been absconding since the incident. 

Jatrabari Police Station OC Mofizul Alam told Samakal that after receiving the information, the police went to the scene and hospital. An investigation is underway to find out how the incident happened. Efforts are underway to arrest the absconding Robin. 

Police and relatives of the deceased said that Ayesha lived in the Rasulbag area of ​​Doniya in Jatrabari. Her father's house is nearby. She was stabbed there last night. Later, she died at Dhaka Medical College Hospital around 8:45 pm. The deceased's husband Kamal Hossain is an expatriate in Italy. The couple has two daughters and a son. 

Ayesha's father Mokhlesur Rahman said that Robin has been addicted to drugs for a long time. Yesterday, it was decided to admit her to a drug addiction treatment center. That's why Ayesha came home. There, she had an argument with her brother about treatment. At one point, Robin got angry and stabbed her sister. At that time, when she stepped forward to save her daughter, the boy also stabbed her with a knife. This cut her right palm. 

The deceased's daughter Saifun Nahar Sithi said, "My uncle (Robin) is crazy. He killed my mother." 

Inspector in-charge of DMCH Hospital Police Camp Bachchu Mia said that the woman was brought to the hospital in a bloody state. The doctor declared her dead. The body has been kept at the DMCH morgue for autopsy.

Headline_English: Accused in 25 cases including murder and sabotage arrested
Content_Enlish:
The Anti-Terrorism Unit (ATU) has arrested Sadequl Islam, an accused in 25 cases of murder, extremism and sabotage. He was arrested in a raid at a mess in Rangpur's Pirgachha railway station area on Sunday. 

ATU's Media and Awareness Wing's Superintendent of Police Mohammad Chanoar Hossain gave this information on Monday. He said that he has 25 cases under the Special Powers Act, including murder cases. He is a fugitive accused with arrest warrants in these cases. Sadequl is the son of Nasratpur Maqbul Hossain Munshi of Chirirbandar police station in Dinajpur district. 

He said that there are 25 cases against Sadequl in Chirirbandar police station in Dinajpur. He has been hiding in different parts of the country since 2016 to avoid arrest, said ATU's Superintendent of Police Chanoar Hossain.

Headline_English: Cousin murdered for refusing to marry her
Content_Enlish:
The mystery of the murder of Shyamal Ravidas (18), a schoolboy from Shahpara Khalshi area of ​​Gobindaganj, has been solved. He went missing on the night of September 14, 2020. The next morning, he was found seriously injured and unconscious near his house. Shyamal died in the hospital in the afternoon. He had a love affair with his cousin. When he refused to marry, his aunt and cousin killed him. 

Although a murder case was filed three years ago, the whole matter was shrouded in mystery. The family had no idea why he was killed, who or what was involved in it. The police station could not solve the mystery after a 9-month investigation. Later, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) investigation revealed shocking information. When he refused to marry, his aunt and cousin beat him to death. 

The investigation officer of the case, Gaibandha District PBI SI Ilyas Ali, told Samakal that the mystery of the murder was solved based on the text messages received on the plaintiff's mobile phone. The investigation of the case has already been completed. Chargesheets will be filed in court against the three people involved in the murder soon. 

Read more: Death of a schoolboy injured by miscreants in Gobindaganj 

According to investigation sources, Shyamal lived with his family in the Khalshi area of ​​Shahpara. When he did not return home on the day of his disappearance, his relatives found his mobile phone switched off. Then everyone started looking for him. However, he was not found. The next day, at around 9 am, his relatives found him lying unconscious in the drain next to Aunt Malti Rani's house. There were many signs of injuries all over his body. He was rescued and first taken to the Gobindaganj Upazila Health Complex. On the advice of the doctors there, he was transferred to the Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital in Bogra. Later, at around 2:30 pm, the doctor declared him dead. In this incident, Shyamal's father, village police member Sadafal Ravidas, filed a case against unknown persons at Gobindaganj Police Station. Since the police could not solve the incident, the case was transferred to the PBI. 

The investigation officer said that forensic examination of the deceased's father's mobile phone showed that a person named Idris Ali had contacted him several times. A clue to the murder was found in a text message from him. 
While searching for that person, it was found that he was imprisoned in a rape case. Later, the PBI interrogated him with the permission of the court. It was learned that the widow Malti Rani worked as a cook in a student hostel in Rangpur. There, she developed a love affair with Idris. 

PBI sources said that a love affair had developed between Malti's daughter Sita Rani and her nephew (brother-in-law's son) Shyamal. Malti became angry after learning about their physical relationship four days before the murder. He told his son Sagar Ravidas about the matter. Then Sagar came from Rangpur and beat Shyamal. In that situation, Malti proposed to marry her daughter to Shyamal. Shyamal did not agree. Sagar had beaten him a day before the incident. On the day of the incident, Malti and Sagar were waiting with sticks in the bamboo grove next to the house. At around 7:30 in the evening, Shyamal was on his way home when the mother and son beat him and injured him. When he became lethargic from the beating, they threw Shyamal into the drain, thinking he was dead. The next morning, Malti went to the drain under the pretext of searching and shouted that she had found Shyamal. 

The investigating officer said that Malti and Sagar planned the murder. And Idris helped them by giving them advice. Later, when his relationship with Malti deteriorated, he sent a text message to Shyamal's father informing him about the murder.

Headline_English: Woman's dismembered body found in pharmacy: Three accused remanded for 8 days
Content_Enlish:
The court has granted an 8-day remand to three accused in the case of gang rape and murder of Shahnaz Parveen Jyotsna (35), the wife of an expatriate in Sunamganj, and dismemberment of her body in six pieces. Sunamganj Chief Judicial Magistrate Mohammad Abdur Rahim granted the remand at 2 pm on Sunday. 

The accused are Jitesh Chandra Gop, owner of Obi Medical Hall in Jagannathpur, grocery shopkeeper Anjit Gop, and Asit Gop, owner of Arup Pharmacy. 

Confirming the 8-day remand of the three accused, Sunamganj Court Inspector Md. Badrul Alam Talukder said that after the remand was granted, the CID has taken them into custody. 

Earlier, the three accused were presented in court and the investigating officer of the case, Inspector Liton Dewan of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), applied for a 10-day remand for each of them. After the remand hearing, the court granted 8 days of remand for each accused for questioning. 

It is learned that Shahnaz Parveen had been living in her house in the city with her 2 sons and 1 daughter since 2013. She had been suffering from physical problems for some time. When she told Jitesh Chandra about this problem on February 16, Shahnaz Parveen asked her to go to the pharmacy. Then, Jitesh and the other two accused in the case tricked her into giving her sleeping pills and gang-raped her. Then, when she told everyone about the rape, the accused planned to kill her. After strangling her as planned, Jitesh and his accomplices cut her body into six pieces with a knife. Then, they also planned to disappear the body. 

The next day, the police of Jagannathpur Police Station recovered Shahnaz Parveen's dismembered body from the locked Abi Medical Hall. The deceased's brother Helaluddin filed a murder case with Jagannathpur Police Station as the plaintiff in this incident. 

In light of this, on February 18, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the police conducted a raid in the capital and Sunamganj and arrested three accused involved in Shahnaz's murder.

Headline_English: One online gambling ring laundered 200 million taka
Content_Enlish:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DB) has arrested three people, including two agents, of an international gang involved in online gambling operations. In the past one year, the gang has smuggled Tk 20-30 crore abroad, earned through online gambling. The DB also said that these gambling sites are operated from Russia, Malaysia and India. 

On February 19, the Web Based Crime Investigation Team and Organized Crime Investigation Team of the Cyber ​​and Special Crime Department of the DB arrested them in the Khilkhet area of ​​the capital. 

The arrested are Tariqul Islam alias Babu, Rana Hamid and Suman Mia. A private car, Tk 1.18 lakh in cash, four different models of mobile phones and five SIM cards were seized from them during the arrest. 

A press conference was organized at the DMP Media Center on Minto Road in the capital on Wednesday afternoon to provide details in this regard. 

At the press conference, DB Additional Commissioner AKM Hafiz Akhter said that the arrested three and their absconding accomplice Akhter and about 50/60 others were operating an online gambling (betting) site using electronic devices. With the money they received from the site, they became the owners of a lot of illegal assets, including land and cars, in different parts of the country. They were conducting illegal money transactions (e-transactions) through mobile banking or bank accounts. 

He also said that the arrested are the master agents in Bangladesh of two betting websites named Maja PBU and Betbaz 365. As the master agents of the sites, they buy each PBU (virtual currency) from super agents outside the country for 60 taka. Later, they sell it to local agents for 100 taka and to gamblers for 150 taka. They hire local agents for 8/10 lakh taka, which is paid in PBU currency. 

Stating that they have no legitimate source of income, the DB official said that the agents used to communicate with customers through two fake Facebook accounts named Siam Ahmed and Ali Khan. The arrested persons have no public source of income. However, the initial investigation revealed that transactions worth Tk 15 to 20 crore were made in their seized bank accounts and mobile bank accounts. In addition, information on 13 bank accounts and 23 mobile banking accounts was found. 

The DB said that betting is done on the sites on how many runs will be scored in a specific over or ball or on which team will win a specific match in a ratio of 1:3. If the general users win the targeted runs or their specific team wins, they get three times the betting PBU back. This is how betting/online gambling is conducted. 

A case has been filed against the arrested persons at Ramna Police Station under the Digital Security Act. The DB also said that the accused in this case are being interrogated on a three-day remand.

Headline_English: Sharif Uddin's application to ACC chairman seeking his job back
Content_Enlish:
The controversial and dismissed Deputy Assistant Director of the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Md. Sharif Uddin has submitted an application to the commission chairman seeking his job back. 

On Sunday, the chairman accepted his signed application and sent it to the ACC secretary with instructions to examine it. 

Sharif Uddin, the Deputy Director of the ACC's Patuakhali office, was removed on February 16 without giving him a show cause notice or any opportunity to defend himself on charges of abuse of power and breach of discipline. 

The application was submitted on Sunday after a united protest by ACC officials and employees against his removal. 

In the application submitted to the ACC chairman, Sharif Uddin requested a reconsideration of the order to remove him in accordance with Rule 48 of the Service Rules, considering logical, legal and humanitarian reasons. 

The petition states that while performing his duties as an ACC officer and preventing corruption and related irregularities, Sharif has received death threats from his family members at various times. The order to remove him from service is completely unreasonable and inhuman. He was not given any show cause notice before issuing the order, which is a complete violation of Article 135(2) of the Constitution and fundamental rights. 

The petition submitted to the ACC Chairman states that from October 12, 2014 to February 16 of this year, he has performed his duties in the commission with honesty, trustworthiness, diligence and utmost justice. During this period, he has tried to protect the interests of the country by recommending, filing cases and filing charge sheets in more than seventy important cases with utmost effort and efficiency. 

In the petition, Sharif Uddin cited examples of various cases during his tenure and said that the investigation of those allegations is very important. Several officials concerned in law enforcement agencies and the administration have been found to be involved in those allegations.

Headline_English: 17 ministries, departments not implementing ACC recommendations: ACC Chairman
Content_Enlish:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has made more than a hundred recommendations to 17 ministries and departments to prevent corruption, but they have not been implemented, ACC Chairman Mohammad Moinuddin Abdullah said. 

ACC Chairman Mohammad Moinuddin Abdullah told reporters on Monday that various ministries and departments are not implementing the recommendations as per their expectations. It is their responsibility to implement the recommendations. The Cabinet Division has been informed to determine a method to implement them properly. 

He said that hundreds of recommendations have been sent in the last few years. Recommendations related to corruption prevention will be sent to seven more ministries and departments soon. 

The ACC Chairman held a briefing on Monday, the day after submitting the ACC's annual reports for 2020 and 2021 to the President last Sunday. ACC Commissioner (Investigation) Dr. Md. Mozammel Haque Khan, Commissioner (Investigation) Zahurul Haque and senior officials of the commission were also present during the briefing at the conference room of the ACC head office.

In 2018, the ACC formed 25 institutional teams to prepare recommendations for preventing corruption in various ministries and departments. Those committees have submitted 24 reports containing recommendations on the sources of corruption in 24 ministries and departments and their prevention. Out of these, 17 reports have been submitted in phases. The remaining seven reports will be submitted soon. 

In response to the question of why the ACC is not playing a role in investigating corruption of politicians and influential people in various ministries and departments and bringing them under the law, the ACC Chairman said, "There is no opportunity in the ACC Act for anyone to get away with corruption. Those against whom actionable evidence is found will definitely be brought under the law." 

At this time, the ACC Chairman highlighted the various successes of the ACC in recent times. 

Regarding the success in the judicial courts, he said that out of a total of 3,434 cases, 203 were settled in 2021, of which 119 were decided in favor of the ACC. The conviction rate in the Commission's cases is 60 percent, while the conviction rate in the cases of the defunct bureau is 30 percent. The average conviction rate this year is 58.62 percent. 

In the previous year, 2020, out of a total of 3,382 cases pending in the lower courts of the ACC and the defunct bureau, 176 cases were settled. Of these, 121 were decided in favor of the Commission. According to this calculation, the conviction rate in the Commission's cases is 72 percent and the conviction rate in the cases of the defunct bureau is 48 percent. That is, the average conviction rate is 68.75 percent. 

The Commission's Enforcement Unit has been working in the organizational structure since 2019. Although the number of operations conducted is less compared to previous years due to Covid-2019, 487 enforcement operations were conducted through this unit in 2020 and 245 in 2021. 

Since 2018, the ACC Intelligence Unit has been included in the organizational structure of the Commission. 

By the end of 2021, a total of 665 complaints were received for confidential investigation, out of which 250 were disposed of and 415 complaints are under confidential investigation. After the investigation, 154 complaints were sent for public investigation with the approval of the Commission Chairman based on the recommendations of the intelligence report. 

The Commission's Daily and Recent Cell (Verification and Selection Committee) screened 18,489 complaints in 2020 and accepted 822 complaints for investigation. 2,469 complaints were sent for action with recommendations to various government departments. 

Out of 14,789 complaints in 2021, 533 were accepted for investigation and 2,889 complaints were sent for action with recommendations to various departments.

Headline_English: Main accused in the murder of A-League leader Tipu and student Preeti arrested
Content_Enlish:
The main accused in the murder of Awami League leader Zahidul Islam Tipu and college student Samia Afnan Preeti in Shahjahanpur has been arrested. His name is Md. Masum alias Akash. 

Earlier, the shooter involved in the double murder in Shahjahanpur was identified. After that, multiple teams were deployed to quickly arrest him. Detectives have got an idea about the network of those involved in the process, from planning the sensational murder to its implementation on the ground. 

Masum wanted to leave the country after the killing mission: Police 

After his arrest, Additional Police Commissioner of the Intelligence Division (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Hafiz Akhter told a press conference on Minto Road in the capital on Sunday afternoon that Md. Masum alias Akash, arrested in the murder of Awami League leader Zahidul Islam Tipu and college student Samia Afnan Preeti in Shahjahanpur, wanted to flee the country after the killing mission. Police said that he went to the Joypurhat border to flee the country on Friday, a day after the murder. 

The DB official said, "After the arrest, Masum said during interrogation that he was informed about the killing mission five days before the murder. And three days before, he was informed who was to be killed." 

Masum received weapons and a motorcycle a day before the murder: Police 

Masum was provided with weapons and a motorcycle to kill Awami League leader Tipu last Wednesday. However, when asked who supplied the weapons and who was the mastermind behind the incident, Additional Police Commissioner Hafiz Akhter said that extensive interrogation is still underway in this regard. 

In response to a question about how the accused Masum was identified, the police said that after watching CCTV footage from different places and based on intelligence information, Masum was arrested after being 100% certain. It is also known that there are multiple cases against him. He was depressed in these cases. It is being verified whether someone instigated him to complete the killing mission. Md. Police said Masum alias Akash studied graphic arts and design. His father is a school teacher and Masum is married. 

Main shooter in the net 

Police said that the shooter involved in the double murder in Shahjahanpur was identified earlier. After that, multiple teams were deployed to arrest him quickly. Police claim that they have got an idea about the network that worked from planning to execution of this sensational murder.

Headline_English: Protest against offensive statements about IGP and DMP Commissioner
Content_Enlish:
The Bangladesh Police Service Association has protested against the objectionable statements made by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Dr. Benazir Ahmed and Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mohd. Shafiqul Islam. 

The protest was expressed in a statement signed by Bangladesh Police Service Association President and SB Chief Additional IGP Monirul Islam and General Secretary and DMP Gulshan Division Deputy Commissioner Md. Asaduzzaman on Tuesday. 

The statement said that during the discussion on the great Independence Day, the IGP and DMP Commissioner did not target any individual, group or political party but spoke in the light of the correct history of the emergence of Bangladesh and the Liberation War. Bangladesh Police believes that politicians run the state and will do so. Politicians are treated with respect in a civilized society. Bangladesh Police has also always shown respect and honor to politicians. 

But it is with great sadness that it is being observed that responsible leaders, including the Secretary General of a party, are making objectionable, offensive, misleading and embarrassing statements in various rallies and media against the proud police chief and DMP Commissioner who initiated the first resistance war of the Liberation War in the month of great independence - which is planned, indecent and purposeful. 

The statement further said that such threatening statements about a professional force like the police from the leaders of a party who have been responsible for running the government at various times in the past are unwanted, unexpected and unwelcome. 

The Bangladesh Police Service Association expects them to refrain from making such statements in the future. 

It is worth noting that recently, BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi demanded the withdrawal of the comments of the IGP and DMP Commissioner about party chief Khaleda Zia. 

On Monday afternoon, he said at the party office in Nayapaltan that officials of the republic cannot make such statements about the former Prime Minister like party cadres.

Headline_English: 9 members of a gang that stole mobile phones from mosques and madrasas arrested
Content_Enlish:
Chanowar Hossain said that the members of the gang search online for the location of the funeral. After finding the location of the funeral, they start looking for information about the crowd. Once there, they divide into several groups. Each group has three members. The code name for this work is 'body work'. After the location of the funeral is determined, they go there wearing pajamas, Punjabi and a cap. The gang members cleverly steal mobile phones from the crowd of the funeral and give them to the second member of the group. The second member gives the mobile phone to the third member. Later, that person leaves the funeral venue. 

He said that the person who steals the mobile phone from the pocket is called 'Mahajan'. Apart from the funeral, the gang also does the same thing during the Friday prayers. They call this theft 'Masjid Kam'. The gang's most active group is at Baitul Mukarram Mosque, which is the center of the Friday prayers. 

The official said that the gang member Bahar used to collect stolen mobile phones from the groups. Bahar has a motorcycle driver. According to the information provided by Bahar, he collected mobile phones from the groups. Later, he would send the mobile phones to the arrested Masud. The job of the arrested Masud is to deliver the stolen mobile phones to specific shops. 

During the investigation, the ATU found three shops that were selling stolen mobile phones. Among them - SI Telecom in Bikrampur Plaza in Jurain, owned by arrested Saiful. Faisal Telecom in Setu Market in Jurain, owned by arrested Faisal. In addition, a shop on the fourth floor of Jamuna Future Park, owned by arrested Millat. In these shops, the IMEI numbers of the mobile phones were first changed and then sold.

Headline_English: Young woman gang-raped over job offer, 5 arrested
Content_Enlish:
A young woman has been accused of gang-raping a man on the pretext of offering him a job. The woman filed a written complaint with Dhamrai police station on Monday, and the police arrested five people that night. The arrested people were sent to court on Tuesday for a five-day remand. 

The arrested people are Shahid, Monirul Islam, Razzak, Sohrab Hossain and Bikash from Char Dautia area of ​​Dhamrai. 

The complaint states that Shahid from Char Dautia village of Dhamrai called a young woman from Ashulia police station area, whom he knew, to his house on Sunday afternoon, promising to offer her a job. Leaving her at home, he returned with some friends around 9 pm. The victim was then forcibly raped. The accused fled when the woman fell unconscious. 

Dhamrai police station police inspector (operations) Nirmal Kumar Das said that five people were arrested that night on the charge of gang-raping the woman on the pretext of offering her a job. They were sent to court on Tuesday seeking a 5-day remand after being arrested in a rape case.

Headline_English: Policeman Nazmul Tarek suspended for asking 'why did you ask for a tip'
Content_Enlish:
One person was accused of 'event teasing' and 'attempted to kill' in the GD. 

'Wearing a tip is my freedom' 

A storm of condemnation is raging across the country over the harassment of Dr. Lata Samadda, and protests are underway. Anger is being expressed on social media Facebook. Many men and women have protested the incident by posting pictures of themselves wearing a tip on Facebook. The protesters say, 'Wearing a tip is my freedom.' 

Not only on Facebook, representatives of various parties and organizations and prominent figures are expressing sympathy for Dr. Lata Samadda through meetings and statements. Member of Parliament and actress Suborna Mustafa expressed her anger over the incident in Parliament on Sunday. She said that this is a very despicable incident for the women's community. 

Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council has issued a statement demanding that the police administration and the government identify the police member within 72 hours and take appropriate disciplinary action against him. The 'Shahbagh against oppression' rally has set a 48-hour deadline for the trial of the accused policeman.

Headline_English: Gang of robbers active ahead of Eid, 27 arrested with weapons
Content_Enlish:
The robbery gang has become more reckless ahead of Eid. Almost every day, people in different areas of the capital are falling into the clutches of robbers and losing money and mobile phones. Even murders are happening because they are trying to stop the robbery. 

In this situation, the Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) has arrested 27 members of the robbery gang in a special operation. 

On Friday and earlier on Wednesday, the DB's Ramna and Lalbagh divisions conducted the operation in Hazaribagh, Chawkbazar, Lalbagh, Kamrangirchar and Shahbagh areas of the capital. 

DB Joint Commissioner Mahbub Alam presented detailed information at a press conference at the DMP Media Center on Minto Road in the capital on Saturday. 

He said that as part of the security activities for Ramadan and the upcoming Eid-ul-Fitr, special operations are being conducted in different areas of the capital to prevent robbery, banditry, theft and violence by ignorant and ignorant parties. In the operation, 27 people were arrested while preparing for robbery, robbery and banditry. Those arrested in Wednesday's operation were sent to court. 

Citing initial interrogation, he said that the arrested people targeted a person in a group at the busiest bus stop in Dhaka city. Later, they boarded the bus disguised as passengers, took advantage of the opportunity, skillfully used anesthetics to make the target person unconscious, stole money and valuables and fled. After questioning the accused and searching their records, multiple cases including theft, banditry, preparation for robbery and drugs were found against 20 people. 

Those arrested are Abdur Rahman Shuvo, Yasin Arafat Joy, Babu Mia, Md. Farhad, Hridoy Sarkar, Akash, Johnny Khan, Md. Rokon, Mehedi Hasan alias Imran, Monir Hossain, Md. Jewel, Jahangir Hossain alias Michael, Md. Azim alias Galkata Azim, Md. Shakil alias Laden, Emon, Md. Rajib, Russell, Mintu Mia alias Bidyut, Md. Masud, Tajul Islam Mamun, Md. Sabuj, Md. Jibon, Riazul Islam, Munna Howlader, Shakil Howlader, Md. Ferdous and Abul Kalam Azad. 

Iron rods, axes, daggers, knives, anesthetic tablets and ointments were seized from them during the arrest.

Headline_English: Extortion of 8 thousand crore taka during Eid yatra!
Content_Enlish:
Another 4,000 crore taka will be left in the pockets of passengers as an additional 200 taka per trip. 

Due to the increased fare, low-income people will take risks and travel to the villages in goods-carrying vehicles like buses-trains, trucks-covered vans. They will be forced to travel in unfit vehicles at low fares. As a result, the risk of road accidents and loss of life will increase. Therefore, the Passenger Welfare Association has demanded an end to the anarchy and extortion in fares on an urgent basis. 
The Association's Secretary General Mozammel Haque Chowdhury said that a strong syndicate of transport extortionists has been formed by exploiting the public transport crisis this Eid. Due to the patronage of dishonest members of the law enforcement agencies, the anarchy of extra fares and extortion is not stopping despite the government's efforts. 

The Passenger Welfare Association claims that their observations have shown that rickshaw fares have increased by 20 percent after April 25. It may double from today, Friday, as the influx of people heading to the villages decreases after the start of the Eid holidays. The fares of autorickshaws, Lagunas, and easy bikes may also double. 

Mozammel Haque said that the government determines the fare of buses by taking the salary of the driver and assistant and two Eid allowances. But the owners charge the minimum fare of Tk 50 for buses and minibuses in the capital three days before Eid in the name of Eid allowance. 

Increased fare in the air too: The distance from Dhaka to Barisal by air is 61 aeronautical miles. But the fare is being charged at the same rate as the Dhaka-Bangkok route, which is 1500 aeronautical miles away. The fare of 'US-Bangla' flight on this route has increased from Tk 4,000 to Tk 10,800. The fare of Tk 4,800 on Novoair is now Tk 8,400. 

One and a half times the fare on the waterways too: Earlier, the deck fare on the Dhaka-Barisal waterway was Tk 200. After the price of diesel increased, it increased to Tk 350. The fare is being charged from Tk 450 to Tk 500 for the Eid journey. The fare of a single-bed cabin was Tk 900. It is now 1,200 taka. But it is being charged up to 1,500 taka during Eid. The fare for a double cabin has increased from 1,800 taka to 3,000 taka. 

Additional fare by road: Additional fare is also being charged in buses from Dhaka to 38 districts of North and South Bengal by road. Buses from Naogaon, Joypurhat, Dinajpur, Panchagarh, Kurigram are being charged 300 to 500 taka more. It may increase further from Friday. 

According to the report, the fare of Hanif Paribahan on the Dhaka-Rangpur route was 1,000 taka. Now it is being charged 1,800 taka. The fare of Eagle Paribahan on the same route is being increased from 1,200 taka to 1,800 taka. Passengers are being ripped off by forcing them to buy tickets to distant destinations on the pretext of not having tickets for short-distance routes. Even if a passenger gets off at Keranihat or Lohagara in Chittagong from Dhaka, he has to pay the fare for Kop Bazar, which is 100 kilometers away. If someone wants to go to Rajshahi, they are being forced to buy a ticket to Naogaon. 

Black market in railway tickets: The media has reported that people who did not get a train ticket and bought a 350 taka ticket from a black marketer for 1,500 taka. 

The press conference was attended by Sharifuzzaman Sharif, advisor of the Passenger Welfare Association, and Tohidul Haque Liton, vice president of the organization.

Headline_English: 4 arrested along with mastermind behind teacher recruitment exam question leak
Content_Enlish:
The accused are: Md. Iqbal Hossain, son of Md. Amir Hossain of Ullapara, Sirajganj, the ringleader, Md. Iqbal Hossain, son of Sekender Ali of Kashiani, his associate Ramiz Mridha, son of Md. Nazrul Islam, son of deceased Abdul Mannan Talukder of the same upazila, and Md. Modacher Hossain, son of deceased Golam Mostafa Biswas of Meherpur Sadar upazila. 

At the press conference, Khandaker Al Moin said that recently, some unscrupulous individuals/organized fraudsters have been successfully leaking the question papers of various important competitive exams and using hidden spy wireless kits to conditionally extort crores of taka from job candidates and their guardians by guaranteeing them of passing various government/private recruitment exams. RAB has learned from intelligence sources that the fraudsters have increased their activities in view of the upcoming government primary school assistant teacher recruitment exam to be held on May 20. RAB has increased its intelligence surveillance to bring these gangs under the law. 

He said that in continuation of this, a RAB-2 operation team conducted raids in various areas of the capital and its surroundings at around 1 am last night based on secret information and arrested these four individuals. 

Quoting the interrogation, Khandaker Al Moin said that first they collected information about various government and private recruitment exams. Later, they collected information about the exam venue and exam guards of those recruitment exams. At that time, other members of the gang would find government/private job seekers from different parts of the country and lure them with the guarantee of passing the exam and getting a job in exchange for 10-15 lakh taka. Later, they would provide the recovered devices to the interested candidates and train them on how to use them, initially taking 1/2 lakh taka as a deposit. They would make an agreement to pay the remaining money after getting a job. In this way, they have been extorting crores of taka from various job seekers for the past few years. 

He further said that these devices brought from abroad are basically divided into two parts. One part of the device was inserted into the ears of the examinees and the other part, which had a SIM card for automatic call reception, was hidden in different parts of the body and was used to enter the examination hall in a special way. Later, the examinees would send them pictures of the question papers of the recruitment examination using various social media. The gang would prepare a team of talented students in advance to answer the question papers. The answers to the question papers sent from the examination hall would be found out by a team of talented students and given to the contracted examinees. 

RAB said that the ringleader, Iqbal, got a job as an assistant teacher in a government primary school in 2008. He was teaching in his own area. In the meantime, in 2015, he met a person named Altaf Hossain, a retired government employee of the same area. He basically learned from Altaf about extorting large sums of money by guaranteeing passes in various recruitment examinations. Later, when Altaf died, he started running the gang himself. There is a case against him under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act and several general diaries (GIDs) at Ullapara Police Station. 

Arrested Ramiz is one of the associates of this fraud gang and a fugitive accused in a murder case. While he was on the run to avoid arrest, he met Iqbal in 2020. Iqbal made him a member of this fraud gang because of his experience with various electronic devices. 

And Nazrul joined the Social Services Department as an office assistant-cum-computer operator in 1994. Nazrul and Ramiz knew each other since their houses were next to each other. He used to put people in touch with Iqbal and Ramiz by promising them jobs in different parts of the country. 

Modach retired as a social worker from the Mujibnagar Upazila Social Services Office in Meherpur district of Modach in 2019. He also used to find ordinary job seekers and put them in touch with Iqbal and Ramiz. Legal action is under process against the arrested.

Headline_English: Unscrupulous businessmen are handing over walkie-talkies to criminals
Content_Enlish:
Robbery and robbery incidents often occur under the guise of law enforcement officers. In these cases, criminals carry walkie-talkies and weapons to mislead people. However, no one other than government institutions is supposed to use black walkie-talkies. However, unscrupulous businessmen are handing over these sets to criminal gangs in the interest of more profit. 

A joint team of RAB-3 and BTRC arrested two people involved in this illegal business in different areas of the capital on Sunday night. They are Abdullah Al Sabbir, owner of Olefil Trade Corporation, and his associate Al Mamun. In the operation, 168 walkie-talkies, 35 batteries, 32 chargers, 63 antennas, six mouth speakers and six back clips were recovered from Mohammadpur and Gulistan Stadium Markets in the capital. 
A press conference was organized at the RAB Media Center in Karwan Bazar in the capital on Wednesday to inform about this. In this, RAB-3 commander Lieutenant Colonel Arif Mohiuddin Ahmed said, RAB-3 learned based on intelligence information that some unscrupulous businessmen are selling black walkie-talkies to criminals in violation of the law. But this is a domestic crime. 

Therefore, after the investigation confirmed this, the operation was conducted on Sunday night. Initial interrogation of the arrested persons revealed that they had been illegally selling walkie-talkies to various individuals and organizations for a long time through the website and Facebook page of the company called Olephil Trade Corporation. They could not show the license and technical acceptance certificate or any valid documents of the walkie-talkies and parts recovered from their custody. 

This RAB official said that the frequency of the recovered walkie-talkies is 245-246 MHz. It is possible to communicate up to half a kilometer with them without a repeater. In addition, communication can also be made between multiple floors of a multi-storey building. Their price ranges from 5 to 50 thousand taka depending on the battery charge capacity.

He said that criminals have been using walkie-talkies to commit robberies, snatching and kidnapping by posing as members of fake DB, RAB, DGFI, NSI or law enforcement agencies. 

RAB said that the arrested Abdullah Al Sabbir had been illegally selling walkie-talkies for five years. Al Mamun has been working as his associate for two years. So far, they have sold more than two hundred walkie-talkies illegally.

Headline_English: Two members of fake currency ring arrested in Bangshal, capital
Content_Enlish:
RAB-1 has arrested two members of a counterfeit note making ring from Bangshal in the capital along with counterfeit note making equipment. During this, counterfeit notes worth 2 lakh 9 thousand were recovered from them. 

According to a press release from RAB, on Friday afternoon, RAB arrested Ramzan Hossain Tutul (22) and Abdul Malek (37) of the counterfeit note making ring from a residential hotel called Tulip on Nawabpur Road in Bangshal. 

In addition to counterfeit notes worth 2 lakh taka, 1 CPU, 1 monitor, 1 printer and 3 mobile phones were recovered as counterfeit note making equipment. 

Initial interrogation of the arrested accused revealed that they had been making counterfeit notes and supplying them to the market for a long time. 

RAB said that legal action is under process against them.

Headline_English: They used to make marijuana cakes and chocolates and deliver them to their homes.
Content_Enlish:
On Monday afternoon, DC Md. Asaduzzaman of the Gulshan division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police held a press conference at his office and informed about the arrest of the three. 

He said that the gang learned to make cakes, chocolates and milkshakes with cannabis in the domestic method by watching various videos made by Canadian and African drug dealers on YouTube. They used to make these products with cannabis at Zubair's house on Road No. 14, Sector No. 12, Uttara in the capital. Then they would deliver them through home delivery. 

DC Asaduzzaman told Samakal that during the initial interrogation, the three said that for the past six months they had been making and selling cannabis cakes, chocolates and milkshakes. For this, they have also formed a buyer group. They communicate through the Instagram network. They have got some information about these buyers. 

During the initial interrogation of the police, Zubair said that one kilogram of cannabis chocolate was made with five kilograms of cannabis extract. Children of upper-class families are their buyers.

Headline_English: Gang of 24 teenagers raids Tongi
Content_Enlish:
Sajal's gang members include Ali alias Chhota Ali (20), Shabash (21), accused in the double murder case Jewel, Mizan, Babu, Manik, Batla Shaon (20), Sabbir alias KBD (20), Tushar (22), Rahmat (21), Mohsin (24), Rahim Mollah (32), Lineman Zakir (32) and others from Banmala area. They are known as Sajal's 'second in command'. 

Many people said on condition of anonymity that Sajal raised teenagers living in different slums by giving them money. Sajal appeared with members of the force during land grabbing or any fights through agreements. They are also involved in drug sales. Sajal Sarkar was arrested with Yaba in 2018 and was imprisoned. Recently, Tongi East Police Station arrested two members of Sajal while preparing a robbery. 

Regarding the formation of the teenage gang, Sajal Sarkar told Samakal, 'I do politics. When you go into politics, you have to raise some children. I raise 200-250 children. Senior leaders often remind me to take people with motorcycles to their events. Then I take people. Most of them are school and college students. But they are not involved in any crime.' 

Sajal said, 'I have 10 teenagers close to me. Through them, I control everyone.' He claimed, 'I do politics, maybe someone spoke against me out of enmity.' 

Rajib Chowdhury Bappi and Sajeeb Chowdhury Pappur, two sons of Abdul Malek of Arichpur area, have a teenage gang called 'D Company'. Its members number more than a hundred. Locals said that many from rich and noble families are members of D Company. Starting from selling Yaba, they commit various crimes through contracts. Almost all of them have multiple cases against them in Tongi East and West police stations. On June 7 last year, RAB-1 conducted a raid in different areas of Tongi West police station and arrested 12 people of D Company. Foreign pistols, bullets, chapatis, and ramdas were recovered from them. Bappi, the head of this force, and his brother Pappu were also arrested at that time. 

Two more juvenile gangs were led by Arichpur Gail and Parvez. Earlier, Shukkur Ali and Imran Talukder Bashir led the juvenile gang in the Tongi Bazar area at the same time. Currently, Bashir and Shukkur have two separate gangs. Bashir is led by Shukkur Ali in the Medinapara and Notun Bazar areas, and the gang formed by his grandsons Suman and Humayun in the Dattapara area is more powerful. 

According to information received from various sources, there are four juvenile gangs in the Ershadnagar area. A leader of the Jubo League, two leaders of the Chhatra League, and an associate of theirs have formed these gangs. Locals say that at least 200 juveniles are under their leadership. Most of them live in the Ershadnagar slums. 

Apart from this, there is Mehin's gang in the Bharan area, Asad Sikder in the Morkun Gudaraghat area, Saddam Majumder alias Bajan Saddam in the Gopalpur area, Jewel, accused of murdering two expatriate brothers in the Dattapara area, Jewel Mahmud Parvez, Sagar, Zillur Aman Rifat in the Tongi Bazar area, Din Muhammad Nirob in the Machimpur area, Bhola and Jasim in the Gazibari area, Aminul Karim Rana on Safiuddin College Road, Biplob Mim, Joy, Saikat in the Madhumita Tintala Mosque area and Shahin, Niloy, Dipu and Sajjad in the Dattapara Haqe Mor area. There are cases against each of them at the police station. 

A member of the Sukkur force said that his father died in a road accident when he was six years old. Later, his mother started a family in another place. He had to wander around on the road since childhood. At that time, a man took him to Sukkur. He was 11-12 years old at that time. 

A guardian named Rahat Hossain said, I work in a private job. My family consists of a son, a daughter and a wife. I was doing quite well. Suddenly, my son started mixing with other scoundrels in the neighborhood. At one point, it got out of control. All my dreams are over. 

Gazipur Metropolitan Police Deputy Commissioner (Crime South) Iltutmish told Samakal that 13 cases have been filed against juvenile offenders in the last one month. Most of those involved in juvenile crimes are people who have grown up in slums and floating areas. They are being used. 

Tongi East Police Station OC Md. Jabed Masud told Samakal that juvenile crime has increased during the Corona period. It is not possible to control juvenile crime through law alone. Along with family education, social discipline must be strengthened.

Headline_English: 8 'robbers' arrested in Dhaka bus robbery case
Content_Enlish:
The Detective Branch (DB) has arrested eight 'robbers' involved in the robbery of a doctor and his friend by taking them hostage at gunpoint in a bus in the capital's Uttara. The DB's Tejgaon division conducted the operation in Dhaka and its surrounding areas on Sunday. DB officials gave this information at a press conference on Monday. 

The eight arrested are Naimur Rahman alias Naim, Md. Abu Zafar alias Biplob, Sajib Mia, Zahurul Islam, Md. Alamin, Dilip alias Sohel, Md. Alamin and Shahnewaz Bhuiyan Azad. 

The DB said that four chapatis used in the robbery, four knives with iron butts, five pieces of iron rods of different sizes, three towels used for blindfolding, ten mobile phones of different models, two toy pistols and 9,800,000 taka in cash were recovered from them. 

Earlier, on the night of January 20, the Resident Medical Officer (RMO) of the 250-bed General Hospital in Tangail, Md. Shafiqul Islam and his friend boarded a bus called RKR Paribahan from in front of Abdullahpur petrol pump in Uttara to Tangail. As soon as they boarded the bus, the robbers took them hostage at gunpoint, tied their hands and blindfolded them, took them to the back of the bus, took them in cash worth 115,000 taka, 5,000 taka in their mobile phone, and two bank ATM cards and PINs in their bags, and later stole another 160,000 taka, along with mobile phones and other belongings. The robbers continued to rob passengers in the bus for about 12 hours in Dhaka city and its surrounding areas. 

After their arrest, the eight detectives told the police that the robbers had planned to take the RKR Paribahan to Genda area in Savar under the pretext of renting it. From there, the robbers first took the bus driver and helper hostage, took control of the bus, drove the bus themselves and started roaming around various roads in the metropolitan area, targeting passengers. Later, they held the passengers hostage at gunpoint, tied their hands and faces, robbed them of their cash, mobile phones and valuables, and dropped them off at various secluded places in the morning. 

The interrogation also revealed that this gang had committed similar robberies in various places in Savar, Tangail and Gazipur in Dhaka district. There are multiple cases against them in various police stations across the country. 

The DB said that the robbers initially admitted their involvement in the bus robbery incident.

Headline_English: Man sentenced to death arrested 16 years after killing wife
Content_Enlish:
Ujjal Pramanik of Bogra was in hiding in Gazipur for 16 years after killing his wife for not getting dowry. In the meantime, he remarried. Recently, the court sentenced him to death in a wife murder case. Then he changed his address and moved to a house in Ashulia, Dhaka. However, that did not save him. A team of RAB-3 arrested him from there on Tuesday night. 

A press conference was held at the RAB Media Center in Karwan Bazar in the capital on Wednesday to provide details. At that time, RAB-3 commander Lieutenant Colonel Arif Mohiuddin said that Ujjal married Alo Begum in June 2006. At that time, her father-in-law Akbar Ali Sheikh gave 30 thousand taka as dowry. However, a month after the marriage, he again demanded 50 thousand taka as dowry on the pretext of going abroad. He also said that his mother, brother and sister-in-law had embezzled the dowry money given earlier. An arbitration was held with members of the two families to resolve the matter. At that time, Ujjal's family members were adamant in demanding another 50,000 taka for dowry. When Alo's father refused to pay the dowry, they threatened to divorce him. Since the matter remained unresolved in the arbitration, Ujjal and his family members started torturing Alo physically and mentally. 

Lieutenant Colonel Arif further said that on August 1, 2006, Ujjal's brother-in-law Nazmul Hossain Labu informed the victim Alo's family on his mobile phone that their daughter was seriously ill. Upon receiving the news, the family members went to Alo's in-laws' house and found her body on the floor of the house. In this incident, a case was filed at the Bogra Sadar Police Station against Ujjal, his mother Aleya Bewa, brother Hira Pramanik, sister Lovely Begum and brother-in-law Nazmul Hossain Labu on charges of beating and strangulation for demanding dowry. As the charges were proven, the Bogra Women and Child Repression Prevention Tribunal sentenced Ujjal to death on July 24. The court acquitted the other four as the charges against them were not proven.

RAB said that after the murder, Ujjwal fled the village with his mother Aleya Bewa and came to the Gazipur intersection area and started living a life of anonymity. He took a job as a carpenter at a local furniture shop for a daily wage of 600 taka. Six months after escaping, he married a garment worker named Nasima Khatun. They have two sons, aged 10 and 3. Since escaping, Ujjwal has not contacted any of his relatives. However, a few days ago, he learned through a relative that he had been sentenced to death in a murder case. Then, he went to a rented house in Ashulia with his family. In the meantime, RAB arrested him based on intelligence information.

Headline_English: Fake Nokia Samsung phones with imported parts
Content_Enlish:
To repair old mobile phones, various parts including displays, cameras, motherboards, casings, batteries and so on are required. So, in the name of repair, these low-quality components are imported from China. Then, they are added to make new mobile phones. Phones with Nokia and Samsung logos look exactly like real phones. But since the equipment is fake, it breaks down within two to three months. As a result, buyers are financially affected. At the same time, they are facing serious health and safety risks. 

Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Police (DB) came to know about this information after arresting a gang recently while investigating the production of fake mobile phones. Those concerned say that fake International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers are used in fake phones. This makes it difficult to identify their location. Due to this, criminals use these phones to commit various crimes. Along with this, detectives have identified eight risks of using fake mobile phones. They have also given ways to avoid them. 

Monirul Islam, Additional Deputy Commissioner of the Social Media Crime Investigation Team of the Cyber ​​and Special Crime (North) Department of the DB, told Samakal that the main objective of the fake phone manufacturing ring is to earn more profit through fraud. In this case, the common buyer is the one who suffers the most. They are buying these phones because they are getting them at a slightly lower price. At the same time, there are health risks. 

DB officials said that there are several risks or harmful aspects of using fake mobile phones. They are - data and images on the phone getting lost or security risks, risk of malware attacks, loss of important files due to ransomware virus attacks, phone becoming inoperable due to not updating at the right time, serious health risks, call drops due to network defects, environmental damage due to chemical reactions of low-quality components, and risk of explosion due to low-quality chargers and faulty batteries. 

DB also gave some suggestions for identifying real phones. They are - If you write the 15-digit IMEI number in English and send it to 16002, you will get the information of the real phone. In the case of external verification, it can be seen that the buttons of the fake phone are usually arranged randomly, the writing fronts are relatively small, the display is not bright and clear, the camera image is not good, the network is weak, and the battery has stickers with fake information. Moreover, while the real phone can be used for 2-3 years, the fake phone lasts only 3-4 months. 

DB sources said that Mozammel Hossain, the chief administrative officer of Union Tech Park Limited, the authorized manufacturer and distributor of Nokia in Bangladesh, came to know that fake Nokia sealed phones were being sold in various shops in Motaleb Plaza. After getting the truth of the incident, he filed a case with Shahbagh Police Station. The DB Cyber ​​Police conducted a shadow investigation into the case. At one point, six people were arrested from Hatirpool in the capital on October 9 with a large quantity of fake mobile phones. Their interrogation revealed that ordinary mechanics with a fifth-grade degree assemble various parts to make new phones. 

DB investigators said that criminals work in three stages in making fake phones. First, low-quality mobile phone parts are imported illegally. After that, they sell them to second-stage traders through a class of brokers. In this stage, traders assemble the parts with their own craftsmen and put fake IMEI numbers on them to make fake phones. The logos, stickers and packaging used on fake phones are printed from various presses. Third-stage traders buy these phones at wholesale prices and sell them to ordinary buyers as real phones in the hope of higher profits. 

Union Limited General Manager (Business Operations) Ajmal Hasan said that on the one hand, customers are being cheated through fake and low-quality phones, while on the other hand, the original manufacturing company is being harmed. In terms of exports, various questions are also being asked. The government is losing revenue.

Headline_English: 4 arrested in attack on Justice Manik
Content_Enlish:
Four people have been arrested in connection with the attack on retired Supreme Court judge AHM Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik. Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Additional Commissioner (Crime and Ops) AKM Hafiz Akhter gave this information at a press conference organized at the DMP's media center on Thursday afternoon. 

He said that there was a BNP rally in the capital's Paltan area on Wednesday afternoon. Shamsuddin Chowdhury was attacked from there. A case was filed at Paltan Police Station on Wednesday night in this incident. Four people have been arrested in this case. 

At the press conference, Hafiz Akhter said that the DB is being given the responsibility of investigating the case. He said that all those involved in the attack will be brought under the law. 

Paltan Police Station OC Salahuddin Mia said that the four arrested are current and former leaders of various committees of Chhatra Dal.
