They have understood that by hurting the hearts of 2 billion people, it is impossible to live in peace and happiness on earth. 

Surely you remember that in September 2019, Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan gave a very important speech at the United Nations. In that speech, he uttered the phrase ‘combat Islamophobia’. I did not like this phrase. But I liked his argument, the underlying purpose of this phrase. Three years after Imran Khan’s speech, in 2022, the United Nations declared March 15 as the ‘International Day to Combat Islamophobia’. Why March 15? Because on this day in 2019, an Islamophobic person entered two mosques in the Christchurch area of ​​New Zealand and shot and killed 51 people praying during Friday prayers and injured 40 others. 

From now on, people all over the world will observe March 15 as the 'Combat Islamophobia' Day. Combat Islamophobia does not mean that you should resist, punish, or attack anyone who speaks against Islam. Basically, if I have Islamophobia or Islamophobia inside me, I should wage war against that fear, that terror, and hatred. It is a war of positive thoughts against negative thoughts within myself. 

This day will be successful only when the member states of the United Nations highlight its significance and make their citizens aware. Intellectuals, journalists, and writers of their countries/languages ​​will write about the issue. Human rights activists will be vocal about it. Governments will enact the necessary laws to stop Islamophobia. For example, the US has introduced a bill in the Congress to declare Islam a great religion.

Headline_English: Fall of Dictatorship Day and today's thoughts
Content_Enlish:
On December 4, 1990, the dictator Ershad's government fell against the backdrop of an unprecedented mass uprising by the student masses. On December 6, the Ershad government's 9-year dictatorship ended with the formal transfer of power to Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed. 

However, unfortunately for us, this journey of democracy did not last long. Unable to accept defeat, the Awami League president described the 1991 elections, which were acceptable both at home and abroad, as an election of subtle rigging and announced that the new government would not be allowed to remain in peace for even 24 hours. From the beginning, the Awami League began to oppose the elected government led by the BNP at every level, and also began to make the parliament ineffective. In the meantime, the Awami League, the Jatiya Party and the Jamaat-e-Islami brought forward the demands of a caretaker government. In the Magura by-election held in 1994, they began to boycott the parliament under the leadership of the Awami League on allegations of rigging and at one point resigned from the parliament, creating an extreme deadlock. The country was thrown into a state of disaster through the strike-blockade program. 

In order to maintain constitutional continuity, the BNP held the mid-February 1996 elections in parliament, brought the thirteenth amendment to the constitution, and arranged for the next parliamentary elections under the caretaker government, and dissolved the parliament after a month and a half. Then, in the elections held under the caretaker government in June 1996, the Awami League came to power. The BNP-led 4-party alliance returned to power in the elections held in 2001. 

The history that followed was not auspicious for politics. Due to the increase in the age of judges, the recently retired Chief Justice KM Hasan was supposed to be the chief advisor of the caretaker government. The Awami League was reluctant to accept this and they organized a bloody movement against it. An extreme stalemate was created in politics. President Iaz Uddin Ahmed became the head of the caretaker government, the Election Commission announced the schedule. All parties also submitted their nomination papers. Suddenly, the Awami League and Jatiya Party-led grand alliance withdrew their nomination papers and soon after, the army-backed Fakhruddin Ahmed government was established with the direct intervention of foreigners. He disappeared from politics for two years. The 9th parliamentary elections were held on December 29, 2008. The grand alliance came to power under the leadership of the Awami League. In this election, the direct and indirect role of various forces at home and abroad in favor of a particular party was heard. The late President of India, Pranab Mukherjee, has also mentioned this in his published book. 

Despite various limitations, all the 4 elections held under the caretaker government have been accepted at home and abroad. It is undeniable that no election in Bangladesh under a party government has been accepted. 

The next incident is recent. Before the 2014 elections, the Awami League, using a Supreme Court order in 2011 as an opportunity, brought the 15th Amendment to the Constitution with the strength of its majority in parliament, abolishing the caretaker government system, maintaining the parliament, and introducing the provision for parliamentary elections under the party government. A new political crisis arose in the country. 

The 10th National Parliament elections were held in 2014. In this election without an opposition party, 153 MPs were elected unopposed. Not even five percent of the voters voted in the remaining seats. Although the opposition political parties, including the BNP, boycotted the 2014 elections demanding the return of the caretaker government system and the abolition of the parliament, they participated in the 2018 Eleventh National Parliament elections under the party government, trusting in the promises made by Sheikh Hasina, and had a terrible bitter experience. It proved that under a party government, one cannot safely go to the center and vote for the candidate of one's choice and be elected as an MP. 

The election process has already begun according to the schedule of the 12th parliamentary elections announced. The deadline for submitting nomination papers has passed. No one except the Awami League and its alliance-grand alliance partners is participating in this election. Opposition political parties including BNP are simultaneously holding continuous programs to demand free and fair elections under a non-partisan, impartial government. The people of the country also want elections under a non-partisan, caretaker government system. World public opinion is also in favor of free, fair, acceptable and participatory elections in Bangladesh. The United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, Australia, and Japan have continued to pressure the government to ensure free, fair, peaceful and participatory elections in Bangladesh. The United Nations is also vocal in this regard. Various issues on human rights and democracy are being vigorously discussed. Sanctions against individuals and institutions and the implementation of visa policies are all visible. Given the situation, it seems that in the coming days, the ruling party will continue the one-sided electoral process through murder, arbitrary arrests, missing persons cases, speedy sentencing of opposition party leaders and activists, and the use of force. And as a result, the country's economy, business and commerce will be at extreme risk due to clear allegations of labor rights, democracy and human rights violations. Along with the country's business community, socially and politically conscious, patriotic people are passing the time with anxiety and worry. 

In 90, through the sacrifice of countless martyrs, the students and people of the country brought back democracy. 33 years have passed. The people of the country still have to give blood for their votes, for democracy, for democratic rule, and face cruel torture, oppression and imprisonment. Can the people's eternal desire for democracy be suppressed to the end by continuing repression and coercion? No. Bangladesh will not accept defeat. It will not be defeated.

Headline_English: Political unrest will not end unless BNP changes position
Content_Enlish:
Leading intellectual of Bangladesh, Professor Rehman Sobhan, said in an interview with Channel 24 on December 2, that although there are many political parties in the country, since the two major parties, Awami League and BNP, have absolute dominance, it will not take long for the 'two-party system' to take firm roots in electoral politics in this country. Over time, many small parties will either form an alliance with these two parties or will disappear from the political arena. He expressed disappointment that he 'does not see the light of hope' as the matter is not moving in that direction. Professor Rehman Sobhan was my direct teacher in the Economics Department of Dhaka University. Therefore, despite agreeing with Sir, I feel the need to explain the matter. 

Awami League is the party that led the country's independence struggle and armed liberation war. Since its birth in 1949, the party has led the struggle against the colonial exploitation, deprivation and discrimination of the then Pakistan state that was against the people of East Bengal. After the landslide victory of the United Front on the basis of the 21-point charter of autonomy for East Bengal in 1954, the Awami League became a vocal platform for the rights of the oppressed people of East Bengal (in 1955, East Bengal was renamed East Pakistan by the Pakistani rulers). After the death of Hossain Shaheed Suhrawardy in 1963, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman came to lead the party. In 1966, the struggle for autonomy for East Pakistan based on the six points he wrote gradually turned into a freedom struggle. 

By achieving a landslide victory in the first and only free and fair elections of an independent Pakistan held in 1970, the Awami League obtained the mandate as the sole representative of the people of East Pakistan. But when the military junta government refused to give power to the Awami League despite being the 'majority party' of Pakistan, on 1 March 1971, the six-point freedom struggle was transformed into a one-point freedom struggle without any reservations. On March 7, 1971, Bangabandhu declared at the historic Racecourse Maidan, ‘This time’s struggle is our struggle for freedom, this time’s struggle is our struggle for independence’. On the night of March 25-26, at the cusp of the start of the genocide called ‘Operation Searchlight’, Bangabandhu declared the independence of Bangladesh, on the basis of which the armed liberation war began on March 26, 1971. 

BNP, one of the two main political parties in the country, is reluctant to give due importance to the history described above. BNP still claims that Major Zia declared the independence of Bangladesh on March 26, 1971 from Chittagong Radio. BNP has not abandoned this scholastic coercion of bringing Major Zia’s declaration on March 27 to March 26. A distortion of history is absolutely unforgivable. The original constitution of 1972 stated that the nation-state of Bangladesh was established through a ‘historic struggle for national liberation’. 

In the fifth amendment to the constitution adopted during Zia's tenure in 1979, this very important phrase was changed to say, 'We have established an independent and sovereign Bangladesh through a historic war for national independence.' This is a terrible distortion of history. The phrase 'historic war for independence' refers only to the 9-month war of 1971. But the phrase 'historic struggle for national liberation' includes all the historical movements-struggles-people's uprisings-elections-non-cooperation movements of the past for the purpose of national liberation, including the 9-month liberation war of 1971. 

According to the BNP's intellectuals, the liberation war began because of Ziaur Rahman's declaration of independence. Bangabandhu had no contribution there! BNP claims that the nation was confused because Bangabandhu did not declare the liberation war, from which Zia's declaration showed the way out for the people. This incompetent distortion of history and the attempt to deny Bangabandhu's leadership is not considered acceptable by anyone in the country or abroad except the anti-liberationists, but BNP has not abandoned this distortion of history to this day. BNP still does not observe the aforementioned chapters of the history of the nation's liberation struggle with due respect. As long as BNP does not abandon this distortion of history, the peaceful coexistence of the Awami League and the parties that hold and nurture the spirit of the Liberation War with them will not be possible. 

Everyone should remember that after illegally seizing power on November 7, 1975, Ziaur Rahman established BNP in the cantonment on September 1, 1978 with the aim of prolonging his power. On August 15, 1975, Khandaker Mushtaq and the coup-making murderous military junta brought back the defeated Pakistan to independent Bangladesh, and Samarprabhu Ziaur Rahman, the bearer of the pro-Pakistan politics, gave birth to BNP with the aim of ensuring that the spirit of the Liberation War would never again be politically popular in this country. Therefore, BNP is the Bangladeshi successor of the 'Pakistan Muslim League', which played an anti-liberation role in this country. They will never abandon this role. 

BNP's main political ideology is love for Pakistan and anti-Awami League. BNP is the 'nemesis' of Awami League from its birth. In BNP, the responsibility of buying and selling the country's left-wing and right-wing politicians was assigned to the state's intelligence agencies; mainly the armed forces' intelligence agency, DGFI. The intelligence agencies completed this assignment by providing licenses, permits, bank loans, plots, etc. They also resorted to blackmail if necessary. Before starting this game of creating a political party in the cantonment, Zia also forcibly seized the country's presidential seat in 1977. 

Bangabandhu's March 7 speech has no importance to BNP. His March 26 declaration of independence does not even exist! Will BNP leaders and activists still show this extreme audacity to erase the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu from the pages of history? If they do not want to be thrown into the dustbin of history, BNP must withdraw from this world-famous lie. Even in the 52nd year of Bangladesh's independence, when we see that BNP-Jamaat's love for Pakistan and the distortion of the history of the Liberation War remain unbroken, I am presenting the question to the nation whether these two parties can have the right to do politics at all in independent Bangladesh. 

The question of political parties of any country having the right to do politics by denying the independence struggle and liberation war of that country or distorting the history of independence is irrelevant. In Bangladesh too, a law has already been passed in the parliament - distortion of the history of independence is a punishable crime. But why is the ruling class of the state silent about the fact that BNP continues this incompetent distortion of history even today? 

To do politics legally, BNP must immediately accept the correct history of the independence struggle and liberation war. In this regard, the Awami League should immediately form a high-powered impartial judicial commission and arrange for a consensus on the controversial issues. No group, including the Awami League or BNP, can have the right to belittle anyone's contribution to the freedom struggle and liberation war. 

Since the Awami League's popularity plummeted due to corruption when it came to power, the BNP's popularity surged. It happened again this time. The groups determined to oust the Awami League from Bangladeshi politics are bringing this surge. Although not all of them are anti-liberation, they are anti-Hindu, anti-India and pro-Pakistan. They are even willing to sacrifice their lives to oust Hasina from power. That is why even if Bangladesh surpasses Pakistan in all economic fields under Sheikh Hasina's leadership, the hearts of BNP supporters will not melt. Despite the remarkable progress made economically during the 2009-23 period compared to the 2001-06 term of Sheikh Hasina's Bangladesh BNP-Jamaat, there has been no major collapse in the popularity of BNP. Despite Pakistan currently being on the verge of economic bankruptcy, the love of BNP's Pakistan lovers has not waned!

Headline_English: Mashrafe to Shakib: We will all become MPs
Content_Enlish:
Cricketer Shakib Al Hasan bought nomination papers for three seats for the Awami League. Finally, he got nominated for one seat. Actor Ferdous also got nominated for a seat in Dhaka. As a regular player of the national team, Shakib has focused on becoming a member of parliament or MP. Earlier, cricketer Mashrafe Bin Mortaza became an MP. Many artists and actors including Momtaz Begum became MPs. How positive is the issue of players and artists becoming MPs? 

Let's see Shakib's statistics. He led the Bangladesh team in the recently concluded World Cup and Asia Cup, but could not bring the desired victory. The miserable condition of both the Bangladesh team and the team captain in the World Cup is visible. After this, it was seen that the captain bought a ticket to become an MP. His previous contribution to the game is certainly acceptable. He became the best all-rounder in the world by playing well. That is why he became an advertisement model and took various business ventures. Now he wants to become an MP. But recently, how much has he been able to give to the national team - the question is being asked. 
Who doesn't know that becoming an MP is a big business here! The story behind becoming an MP is increasing wealth. Some people have the credit of building mountains of wealth! Sometimes they are news in the newspapers. When someone wants to exploit this profitable medium with the popularity of their professional place, then there is a danger. Mashrafe became an MP, Shakib will become one. Players will come like this based on their sources. But what is the condition of the cricket team? We had a promising team; many had room for hope. But in the current situation, many are disappointed with this team. The problem is also in the cricket administration. There are many questions about the Bangladesh Cricket Board. Party formation has given rise to degradation there too. If becoming an MP is an occasion for personal achievement, what can we expect from that cricket! Especially if there was a voting festival in that sense in the country; if there was an environment for becoming an MP in real competition, the observation at that time would have been different. 

Leaving aside the cricket arena, the film stars who are seen competing to become MPs are the founders of the Bangladesh Film Development Corporation-FDC. 
If we talk about the ideal goal of becoming an MP, it is to serve the people. Those who do politics declare this – they want to serve the country and the world. For them, the country's development is more important than their own development. As if the root of their power is to ensure the democratic rights of the country and everyone. At least that is what it seems if you look at the constitution and structure of every political party. But in our reality, anyone is bound to be confused. That is why people are surprised to see the tendency of stars to become MPs. That is perhaps why Shakib Al Hasan once posted on his Facebook page – 'I am not joining politics and I don't have any intention to join politics in my life.' That is, I am not joining politics and I have no intention of joining politics in my life. After a decade, however, Shakib is no longer in that position. 

Needless to say, politics is now in the hands of businessmen. In the 11th parliamentary election, 61 percent of the MPs were businessmen. However, in the 1973 parliament, the main profession of the legislators was law and business. Apart from that, business and agriculture were also professions. In the parliament at that time, 31 percent of the legislators were lawyers and 18 percent were businessmen. The percentage of businessmen increased in the elections after 1990. Those concerned know that the number of businessmen is increasing due to the increasing influence of money in politics. There is little room to deny this fact in the case of players, artists or stars. Most of them aim to increase their wealth from what they have. According to the information in the 2018 election affidavit, despite being young and new to politics, the then national cricket team captain Mashrafe Bin Mortaza was at the top of the wealth list among the star candidates. The news that broke last year about his wealth is surprising. However, Mashrafe has denied it. 

Players, artists, actors and stars have many fans; who are fans of the work of the respective star. Most of these fans are of the younger generation. But in the two elections held before this, that is, in the elections of 2014 and 2018, many of the young generation voters could not exercise their desired voting rights. The election manifesto announced for the 12th parliamentary election also remains a source of concern for the youth. 

The way artists, writers, and stars used to speak as representatives of civil society; they would take a stand against injustice when they saw it, now many are not in that position. What is the relationship between this and becoming an MP? Whenever they have a desire to become an MP or expect to get something from politics, then the mentality of compromise comes. This situation is also alarming. When the prices of goods are rising, civil society speaks for the people. If they do not join the ranks of the people, where will the people go? 
Becoming an MP is undoubtedly not bad, but we do not have that environment. Becoming an MP for profitable politics cannot bring good results without keeping your own position right and giving your best in your professional position. Especially in our politics, where money and muscle power are the only reliance, celebrities are incompatible. Is there a situation where we can trust that celebrities will walk the path of change by becoming MPs? Whoever goes to Lanka becomes Ravana.

Headline_English: Warnings about human rights cannot be dismissed
Content_Enlish:
The New York-based international human rights organization Human Rights Watch (HRW) said in a statement on Sunday that the Bangladesh government claims to its diplomatic partners that it is committed to holding free and fair elections. At the same time, the country's state authorities are throwing political opponents of the ruling Awami League into prison. The organization observed that after the violence on October 28, the BNP called for a strike from October 31 to November 2. During and after the program, clashes broke out between the police, opposition parties, and ruling party leaders and supporters. Although all sides are responsible, in some cases the police have used excessive force against protesters. Awami League leaders and activists enjoy impunity for their role in the ongoing violence. But opposition members are subject to widespread, often arbitrary arrests. The organization also noted in the statement that the police have sealed the BNP office as a crime scene, blaming the opposition for "creating chaos." They said that when the government shuts down free expression; If the opposition, critics and human rights activists are systematically rendered ineffective through arbitrary arrests, disappearances, harassment and intimidation, then a free election is impossible. 

First of all, what Human Rights Watch has said about the current political situation in the country, especially how the government is treating the BNP and its allies who are protesting for a fair and free election, has happened and is happening before the eyes of the people of this country. Therefore, there is no room for disagreement with the organization's observations; although I saw the Attorney General say that Human Rights Watch's statement is not correct or something like that. Of course, it is part of the culture of our rulers to call someone's statement biased and dismiss it if it does not go in their favor. Maybe someone else from the government will come up with a similar statement. 

Secondly, why are foreigners involved in what is currently happening here with the 12th National Parliament election; the people of our country also think that the election will not be free and participatory. The government is trying to make the election look participatory. For this reason, various unknown political parties are being included in the election process. In this, many such parties may ultimately participate in the election. But an election cannot be called participatory based on mere numbers. We have seen that many parties also participated in the controversial election of February 15, 1996, in which the Awami League did not participate. That is why the election was not called participatory. The same applies this time too. If the BNP does not participate, this election will not be participatory either - everyone agrees on this. 

Now, in this context, Human Rights Watch has said about what the international community can do, that foreign governments should insist that the Bangladeshi authorities uphold their international obligations to uphold human rights. The organization has also said that Bangladesh's diplomatic partners should make it clear that the government's authoritarian repression will endanger future economic cooperation. These words undoubtedly carry significance. 

It must be remembered that the main international players in our upcoming election are China, India and the United States. Although they are hostile to each other on other issues, China and India share the same opinion on our elections. But the position of the United States is completely different from the position of these two countries. US officials have always said that they want to see a free, fair and participatory election in this country. Why they say less here; they do not say it in other countries – that question is irrelevant here. They and their Western allies want participatory elections here – that is the main thing. We also know that to prove that their expectations are not just on paper, they have already implemented a visa policy on this country. It may be strengthened in the future. 

Although there is no direct relationship between Human Rights Watch and the United States, the West values ​​the reports of such organizations. Based on their observations, the United States, the European Union or such states, especially in terms of providing aid and cooperation to various countries, determine their policies. However, those countries do not approach our National Human Rights Commission or any government agency to learn about the human rights situation in Bangladesh. The results of a survey are out. It is said that the National Human Rights Commission of India is the weakest in the world in terms of credibility; Next to that is our National Human Rights Commission. So our government or any of their supporters may reject the Human Rights Watch statement, but that will not stop the deluge.

Headline_English: Putin is going to win.
Content_Enlish:
Twenty months ago, after Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, many senior Russians believed the war would soon end. In their view, the Russian economy was in shambles and Putin’s government was on the verge of collapse. Today, that view has changed dramatically. 

Business leaders, officials and ordinary people have told me that the economy has stabilized despite Western sanctions; Putin’s rule has also looked more stable than at any time in the past two years. 

Moscow’s restaurants are bustling. “The restaurant market is growing day by day, not just in Moscow but across Russia,” says one top Russian restaurateur. “And the quality of the food is getting better and better. In early 2022, there was definitely a panic in the industry. But it quickly passed,” he says. 

Housing prices are rising and construction is booming. Most global brands left Russia in early 2022, leaving empty stores in malls and on the streets. Now, the CEO of a retail chain tells me, those businessmen’s Russian counterparts have filled the void. Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov recently admitted that Russia’s economy was “on the verge of collapse” in the months following the invasion. But he says the country is well past the worst. 

Before the war, Russian business executives typically stashed their money in the West. They also bought housing and real estate there, which could serve as second homes for their families if needed. But now, as one Russian tycoon told me, that door has closed, and investment is booming at home. They have nowhere else to put their money. Huge building projects are now underway in places from the Altai Mountains in eastern Siberia to Karelia on the Finnish border. Bloomberg reported in September that Russian tycoons have brought at least $50 billion back to the country since the war in Ukraine began. According to those I interviewed, this estimate is very conservative; in reality, it is much higher. 

Russia’s industrial sector is booming. Of course, it is led by the arms industry, some of which are expected to grow by more than 30 percent this year. Moscow is selling oil and gas to foreign buyers. Not just China and India, but also European countries. Most of these buyers buy Russian petroleum products through intermediaries such as Turkey, Azerbaijan or Egypt. The West may have succeeded in severing ties with Russia in most areas, but Moscow’s trade with the rest of the world is growing. 

This is not a repeat of the Cold War isolation of the Soviet Union. Putin’s Russia can get much of its supplies from China. For many Muscovites, perhaps the biggest surprise on the streets is the massive replacement of Western cars with Chinese models. 

The sanctions have left Russian business leaders with no choice but to stay in the country. Even those who wanted to stay in the West and help Ukraine have been punished. Mikhail Fridman, the tycoon and co-founder of Russia’s largest private bank, had been critical of the war for a while; he too was briefly arrested by British authorities and placed under US sanctions. A few weeks ago, Fridman gave up, initially moving from his London home to Tel Aviv. He eventually returned to Moscow. 

Fridman’s return had a symbolic effect on the Russian business elite. It gave them the impression that the West saw them only as enemies. That meant their only way to survive was to cooperate with the Kremlin. Because Putin, like the West, has yet to punish any business leaders; not even those who spoke out against the war. 

But the war in the Middle East has convinced Russian business leaders that Putin is winning. In their view, Western public opinion is turning away from Ukraine. In the meantime, Putin will strengthen his position with the Global South. His claim that the United States is responsible for the Gaza crisis resonates with millions of people around the world. 

Speaking of the ongoing war, the Russian authorities have focused their military buildup on the poorest and most desperate regions of Russia; recruits are being promised an average of 10 times the salary. Putin still has plenty of money in his coffers. That means his cannon fodder is unlikely to run out anytime soon. 

Russia’s elite are well aware that Putin’s regime still has many weaknesses. Russia still cannot produce many of the goods it needs. Getting them from its friends is complicated. One businessman told me that their airline could soon be shut down for lack of spare parts for passenger planes. Yet Putin has no room for doubt that public opinion is changing. Twenty months ago, Russia’s elite were convinced that Putin, long unchallenged, had finally played his trump card and that he would probably pay a heavy price for his miscalculations. Now most of them seem to have changed their minds. The Russian president, they say, has made it clear that he is here to stay. 

Mikhail Zhaiger: Exiled Russian writer; Translated from The Washington Post by Saifur Rahman Tapan

Headline_English: BNP is trapped in a trap.
Content_Enlish:
The Election Commission has announced the schedule for the 12th parliamentary elections. The BNP and its allied parties are continuing the blockade and strike by rejecting the schedule. Two professors have spoken about the new political situation that has emerged in this context. 

The political position that BNP has taken ahead of the 12th parliamentary elections is stubborn, short-sighted and devoid of reality. They are still stuck in their demand for the overthrow of the government and the introduction of a caretaker government. They have not been able to achieve this demand because the people are not with them. For the same reason, I think that the demand will not be implemented in the coming days. 
According to the constitution, the EC or the Election Commission is obliged to hold the 12th parliamentary elections within a specific period. Accordingly, they have already announced the election schedule. The EC has already taken several initiatives to hold a dialogue with the BNP; in addition to directly inviting them, they have also sent letters to the BNP for this purpose. They have also tried to communicate with the BNP indirectly. But the BNP has remained steadfast in its position. That is, it has reached a point of no return. 

A state cannot be held hostage to the tyranny of any one party. The state, government and people have to follow a constitutional course. Otherwise, the state will face a major crisis. 
When BNP saw that their one-point demand was not being met due to lack of public support, they should have withdrawn from it as a sign of responsibility. Instead, they reverted to violence like in 2013-14 and 2015 and got stuck in a trap or encirclement. 

Now that they are announcing various programs from secret places, which they have no initiative to implement. They are a kind of apolitical process, even whimsicality. Through this, muscle-based politics is being practiced. They have not learned any lessons from the failure of the politics of burning and killing people in 2013, 2014 and 2015. That is why they are still giving the same kind of strikes and blockades. But nothing will be done; in the meantime, the suffering of the people will increase. The working class, the hard-working people will suffer. Of course, if this class of people suffer, BNP will not do anything. They want a 'golden deer' in return for anything. This is worse than apolitical politics. 

Anyway, the election schedule has been announced; many political parties will participate in it. When the election campaign begins, the involvement of the people will increase. The whole country will enter an election atmosphere. And if the BNP does not come to the elections, it will be separated from the people. This means that BNP will have to remain out of power for many more years. 
Now there is talk of dialogue again. Especially after America sent a letter to the Awami League-BNP and the Jatiya Party in this regard, there is talk of dialogue. But when the government party repeatedly talked about unconditional dialogue, did America take the initiative to take BNP to the dialogue? Or has BNP still said - yes, we want to sit in an 'unconditional dialogue' following America's advice? They did not say that. That means, BNP is not heeding the advice of friendly countries. Now, it is to be seen whether BNP will implement the visa policy against BNP as promised if BNP tries to disrupt the ongoing elections through violence? 

I would like to say another thing about dialogue. That is, politics is a game. All the players in the field want to be in a favorable position. Why would the government party leave the favorable position it is in now? And after the announcement of the schedule, the current government has no role in the dialogue; the government party can be. Now, whatever can be accommodated for BNP under the schedule can be done. There is another opportunity for BNP. They did not ask for the resignation of the President; they can go there. According to the constitution, the importance of the President increases during elections. Because, then his executive power increases. BNP can go there and speak its mind. However, there will be no benefit in talking about one point there. They want to get out of what we have done after meeting the President or telling him in writing. These things can be done in the interest of our participation in the elections. 

The United States is threatening to put various pressures on the government after the elections. I don't think they are right. Because democracy, human rights, etc. are not a matter of policy for America. If that were the case, they would not have supported the Israeli genocide in Gaza. Many countries in the world, where there is not even a trace of democracy; are at the top of America's priority list. After the nuclear bomb test explosion in 1998, the then US administration imposed sanctions on Pakistan. But later, after the Taliban government came to power in Afghanistan, America gave Pakistan weapons, money, everything. America's foreign policy is based entirely on its national interests. As a result, it will be seen that it has strengthened its commercial activities with our government formed through elections. America makes friends with only the government that can deliver; Awami League has that power. And America has talked about participatory elections; it has not talked about the participation of all parties. 

In my opinion, BNP can now say that we are participating in the elections as part of the movement as the last test of whether the elections under the party government are fair and free. But there is substance in this. Because, making this election fair and free is a national demand; the vote must reflect the public opinion. If that is not the case, those concerned will have to pay compensation.

Headline_English: Unilateral elections are not the solution
Content_Enlish:
According to the announced schedule, the parliamentary elections are going to be held on January 7, 2024. Elections are an essential part of the democratic system. In the parliamentary system, the government is formed through parliamentary elections; the position of the opposition party in parliament is also determined. The government is run through mutual cooperation between the government party and the opposition party. Therefore, a strong opposition party is an essential condition of the parliamentary system. A parliament without an effective opposition party is barren and immobile. The proof of this is the 10th and 11th parliaments. 

In the 10th parliament, one of the main rivals for power, BNP, was outside the parliament. The Jatiya Party was both in the government and the opposition. Jatiya Party Chairman Hussain Muhammad Ershad was the Prime Minister's special envoy. And Jatiya Party Co-Chairman Raushan Ershad was the leader of the opposition party in parliament. Jokes used to say, a home-grown opposition party. 

In the 2018 Abhinav elections, BNP came in third place in parliament. The grand alliance partner Jatiya Party gained the status of an opposition party. Due to the opposition's unlimited loyalty to the ruling party, one-party dominance has been established inside and outside the parliament. Therefore, it can be said that if the election is held in 2024 with the BNP out, it will be just a repeat of the parliaments formed in 2014 and 2018. 
Not only BNP; most of the 44 registered parties, including the left and Islamic parties, have announced to boycott this election. It seems that the nation is on the verge of another one-sided election like 2014. However, if a dramatic incident occurs, it will be a different story. 

It is possible to predict what kind of election will be held without the BNP, the left and the major Islamic parties. Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader often says that there will be a game. Everyone understands that the game that will be played if the opposition parties, including BNP, are not in the voting field is a game of Bhanumati. The referees will also vote. The signs of this have already started. Several OCs have already asked for votes under the boat symbol. However, not everyone is like this. Most will not ask for votes openly. They will make their preferred candidate win the vote. The role of the police in the BNP rally on October 28, the lock-up of the Nayapaltan office, and the arrest of thousands of leaders and activists across the country, including Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, have raised questions about the image of the police. 

The Lok Sabha elections in India will be held close to our elections. The difference between the two legislative elections in the two countries is that there is no dispute between political parties about participating in the elections in India. Even if the elections are held under a party government, all parties will participate; Congress or Naxalites will not withdraw from the elections. Because they know that even if there is conflict and rigging at some centers during the elections, it will not change the public opinion and the victory of the opposition party or alliance candidates will not be snatched away. 

In India, a custom and culture of changing governments has developed in elections held under party governments, which we are far from. Our experience shows that elections under party governments are not free and fair; governments never change. In the past, there was no change in the government in any election held under the supervision of Awami League, BNP, or Jatiya Party. If the elections are held under the same management this time too, the same incident will not be an exception. 

The leaders of the ruling party gave examples of various countries, including India. They said that elections are held under party governments in those countries. But they did not say that the police and administration would run independently like in India; they would not have party affiliations. If the police administration were neutral like in India and Western democratic countries, and the Election Commission were not subservient, there would be no objection to elections under party governments in our country. Even then, in 2018, the opposition parties including BNP went to the elections under party governments. An even worse example was set in that election. 

Like India, we also have election laws and regulations. During elections, the police administration is entrusted to the Election Commission. But the Election Commission cannot control them even if it wants to. Rather, the Election Commission itself becomes a puppet in the hands of the government and administration. Because those in power; the administration becomes subservient to them, the police become truncheons. Their ‘job’ is to fulfill the dreams of the government party. That is why the demand for a caretaker government was raised in 1990 and accordingly the elections were held in 1991. In 1996, the provision of a caretaker government was introduced in the face of the demands of the Awami League and its allies. Although it has been abolished, the caretaker government issue has not lost its relevance. Most parties are demanding this and have announced a boycott of elections under a party government. 

Needless to say, I am not one of these agitating parties, I am not a member of any party. I also want a non-partisan government management to uphold civil rights. I was with the caretaker demand in 1990. When the movement for a non-partisan caretaker government was led by Sheikh Hasina in 1996, I still expressed my unwavering support. When the provision of the caretaker government was abolished through the 15th Amendment, I still protested. I still want a neutral government management out of conscience. 

The right to vote was earned at the cost of many sacrifices. Voting rights are the fruit of a long struggle led by Sher-e-Bangla Abul Kashem Fazlul Haque, Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani, Hossain Shaheed Suhrawardy, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, Tajuddin Ahmed and others. Through voting, the participation of the common people in governing the country is established, which cannot be jeopardized by petty political interests. 
Our demands and reality are different. Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader said that there is no more opportunity for dialogue. This means that there is no compromise between the government and the opposition; once again, controversial elections are being prepared. 

It cannot be expected that an effective parliament will be established through another one-sided election. In a word, the government's transparency and accountability space will become narrower. On the other hand, political instability will increase, which can give rise to a multi-dimensional crisis. 
A black shadow will fall on the image of Bangladesh. The distance with Western countries, including the United States, may increase, which may have a negative impact on our export trade, including garments. 

The most important thing is that the country's economic crisis is gradually intensifying. Remittance flows have decreased. Inflation has surpassed past records. The value of the rupee against the dollar has decreased. Foreign exchange reserves are decreasing day by day. The dollar crisis is disrupting essential imports. National unity is needed in the face of this crisis. The dividing line of the nation will widen further in a one-sided election. 
Finally, I would like to say that there is still time for dialogue. If necessary, there is also an opportunity to change the schedule. The overall well-being of the country is expected - no more one-sided elections; no, no farce.

Headline_English: Netanyahu is a burden for Biden
Content_Enlish:
The devastating, deeply painful and unending humanitarian suffering that Israel inflicted on Gaza in response to Hamas’s October 7 attack will leave a lasting mark on all who witnessed it. It has sparked widespread global protests, causing irreparable damage to Israel’s main ally, US President Joe Biden, and the Western-led rules-based order. 

The perception that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is not listening to the US has grown since the Hamas attack. Some 1,200 Israelis, mostly civilians, were killed in the Hamas attack. He has refused to accept any kind of ceasefire until Hamas is defeated and Israeli hostages are released. Even at the risk of being isolated, Israel last week rejected a UN Security Council proposal for a humanitarian ceasefire. Neither the US nor the UK vetoed the proposal, as they had done before. Recent statements by both countries have been critical of Israel. The reasons for this are clear. Joe Biden is under increasing pressure to intervene forcefully in Israel. But he said last week that a ceasefire was “not realistic.” He warned that Hamas was planning more atrocities. He did not, however, question the Palestinian casualty figures as he had previously; he also acknowledged that the Israeli bombing was “indiscriminate.” 

Biden’s stance is clearly at odds with domestic and international public opinion in the United States. A new poll shows that 68 percent of Americans support a ceasefire. And 40 percent say Biden should play the role of “neutral savior” rather than Israel’s protector. Democratic voters in particular are unhappy with Biden’s stance. Another poll found that 56 percent believe the Israeli military has overreacted, up from 21 percent a month ago. Notably, nearly half of young (under 45) voters in the US and nearly half of non-white voters believe Israel is “overreaching.” They live in key 2024 election seats, where Biden is already doing poorly. He is also losing support from Arab and Muslim swing states; he is facing rebellions in some places. None of this is helping his re-election. 

Like Biden, the European Union is under increasing pressure to push for a two-state solution to the Palestinian issue. It is now being touted as the panacea, even though many previous talks have failed. The EU’s foreign policy chief, Josep Borrell, told Israelis that “one atrocity does not justify another.” Although the support behind that is not strong. 

There are concerns about the way Gaza has overshadowed Ukraine’s fight against Russia. Joe Biden’s situation here is not good either. Commentator Fintan O’Toole says Biden’s argument that the wars in Gaza and Ukraine are similar struggles against lawlessness and barbarity has damaged “both his own moral standing and international solidarity in Ukraine.” In his words, “the attempt to give Israel and Ukraine the same moral basis is evidence of hypocrisy.” He says the US is vocal about war crimes in Ukraine but silent about Gaza. 
The world’s view of two similar wars is that Biden and the West are clearly losing in Gaza. The anger that is being felt in the Arab world and beyond is bound to have long-term, adverse geopolitical consequences. The very Gulf states that it encouraged to establish friendly relations with Israel are now criticizing the US. Postcolonial African states have followed a similar path. As discussed here last week, both China and Russia are actively exploiting alleged Western hypocrisy. 

Biden, who is bound by US policy since October 7 and his personal history, is bound to visit Israel. He has visited Tel Aviv and has shown great sympathy for Israel. But he has overstated his sentiments. Netanyahu, however, is a follower of the unprincipled far-right nationalist Donald Trump; he is no friend of Biden. 
Netanyahu often talks about a “long war.” But this war is the best excuse to keep Netanyahu in power and out of jail. 

As long as Netanyahu remains in power in Israel, Biden and Western leaders will face a wall of resistance in Jerusalem, which will prolong the suffering in Gaza; Western credibility will be damaged in every country, and the war will continue. 
The collective message to Joe Biden is: There can be no peace while Netanyahu rules.

Headline_English: Meeting with Xi a boon for Biden
Content_Enlish:
US President Joe Biden is expected to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping in San Francisco on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Their meeting is of great significance. The two leaders have not met since the G20 summit in Bali, Indonesia, last year, due to a lack of consensus between them on ongoing global conflicts, especially the war in Ukraine. 

At that G20 meeting, the two leaders discussed China's position on Taiwan (the US is concerned about China's military actions on the self-governing island), Russia's invasion of Ukraine (the US wants China to put pressure on Russia to end the war), and US-China trade relations (where there is a lot of gravel). These issues are expected to be on the agenda again. 

US-China relations are unlikely to be a decisive factor in the 2024 US presidential election; but it will be an issue then. According to a Pew Research survey, about 83% of Americans have a negative view of China's role in the world and its actions regarding the fate of Taiwan. Chinese attitudes toward the United States are now much softer than before. According to a survey conducted in October, 48% of Chinese consider the United States an enemy, compared to 74% last year. 

Biden's expectations for China 

Biden is unlikely to make a significant change in his position on China. Biden's goal is to curb China's economic growth and limit China's diplomatic influence in the interests of maintaining US geopolitical dominance. The Atlantic Council, a research organization, believes that Biden will gain support from the American public if he maintains an open dialogue with China. A recent survey says that only 13% of Americans want a confrontational approach against China. 

Biden needs a small push ahead of next year's election. Despite creating record jobs and lowering inflation to 3.7%, he is slightly behind Trump in recent surveys. Uncertainty about who might be in the White House in 2025 will affect Chinese expectations for the meeting. China is unlikely to sign a long-term deal with the United States until after the 2024 election. 

Some commentators believe that resuming high-level military dialogue between the two countries will be a key issue for both leaders. Such dialogue could help to defuse potential military crises, especially in contested areas such as the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait, where China claims sovereignty. The Biden administration wants to see greater stability in US-China relations and ensure that any military misunderstandings between the two countries are avoided. 

Perhaps intentionally, neither side has made their expectations clear about the summit. There have already been several meetings between Chinese and US officials in the run-up to the summit. US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen is scheduled to meet with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng before the Biden-Xi meeting. 

China is also currently seeking solutions to its economic crisis. This could open up some room for compromise between the two sides. China’s foreign trade is shrinking. So China will want to talk about improving its trade relations with the US. 

The Trump Factor 

With just 12 months to go before the US presidential election, Biden is unlikely to show weakness towards China. His likely Republican rival, former President Donald Trump, has been increasingly defiant over China’s economic challenges to the US; he has imposed a series of tariffs on Chinese imports since 2018. 

In January 2020, Trump signed a “historic trade deal” with China, in which China pledged to buy $200 billion worth of US goods by the end of 2021. But China ultimately failed to deliver. According to one report, China has bought only 58% of the promised amount, which is less than before the deal. 

Republicans on the House of Representatives Committee on China have written to Biden demanding that he take a stronger stance to “protect American interests and values.” The letter also asks Biden to press Xi for the release of Hong Kong pro-democracy leader Jimmy Lai and others detained by Chinese authorities. 

The prospect of Trump returning to the White House is widely seen as making diplomats around the world reluctant to commit to a long-term partnership with the United States. Trump has said he will “build America by taxing China,” which would surely reignite the US trade war with China. 

All in all, Biden is negotiating with China in a domestic minefield. If he takes a “hard” stance, he risks alienating voters; if he is too soft, he will face harsh criticism from Republicans. If Biden can navigate this juncture well, he will reap the benefits in the next election. He can claim that he is the right person to lead the United States.

Headline_English: Gaza War vs. Arab-Israeli Relations
Content_Enlish:
Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) told Fox News in his first interview in English in the last week of September, “The world cannot see another Hiroshima. If 100,000 people die; that means you are at war with the rest of the world.” Gaza, now the target of genocide, is that “another Hiroshima.” 

Israel has been waging an offensive in Gaza for more than a month. As a result, more than 40,000 people have been killed in the densely populated valley. US-backed Israeli forces have dropped more than 25,000 tons of explosives on Gaza since October 7, which is equivalent to two nuclear bombs. The Geneva-based NGO Euro-Med said in a press release on November 2, “The explosives dropped on Gaza are more destructive than the bombs dropped on Hiroshima.” It is worth noting that the interview with Mohammed bin Salman on Fox News was broadcast just two weeks before the October 7 Palestinian resistance “Al-Aqsa Flood” operation. Interestingly, the target of the crown prince’s statement was not Israel; it was Iran. He was responding to a question about the dangers of Iran’s nuclear bomb program. 

Now it is clear – Israel already has peace treaties with not only Saudi Arabia, but also five other Arab states: Egypt, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Morocco. Despite public pressure against Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza, they are not even talking about revising these treaties. However, the report said that when Bahrain suspended economic relations with Israel and withdrew its ambassador from Tel Aviv, some lawmakers also called for the normalization agreement to be canceled. 

Arab countries that have signed “peace agreements” with the occupying power, Israel, have long touted the agreement as a means to their citizens’ security, prosperity, and regional stability. Mohammed bin Salman himself has made that point. He told Fox News that a potential Saudi-Israeli agreement brokered by the Biden administration would be a historic milestone. It would be the biggest achievement since the end of the Cold War in 1991. 

US President Joe Biden, a defender of Israel, believes that one of the goals of Hamas’ attacks was to disrupt normalization talks between Saudi Arabia and Israel. US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, in his assessment, directly stated that one of the goals behind Hamas’ attacks was to hinder efforts to bring Saudi Arabia and Israel closer together. 
Although no official Saudi position has been made public by Mohammed bin Salman or his Foreign Ministry, Reuters and AFP reported on October 13, citing “reliable sources” and a “Saudi government source,” that Saudi Arabia has decided to suspend normalization talks and has been in contact with US officials to that end. 

Israel appears to be somewhat concerned by this implicit threat. Saudi Arabia has initially called for an end to attacks and protection of civilians, but has consistently condemned the targeting of civilians. However, despite Israel’s direct massacre in Gaza, Saudi Arabia is using cautionary words to appease Washington. Since Saudi Arabia has not yet signed a normalization agreement with Israel, it has no diplomatic obligations with Tel Aviv. But surprisingly, there is a clear reluctance within Saudi Arabia to use its political power and oil influence to push for a ceasefire in Gaza. The proof of this is that Saudi Arabia has delayed the announcement of the ‘urgent’ Arab summit scheduled for Riyadh on November 11 until October 30. This may indicate that Saudi Arabia is further along the path of normalization with Israel than we know. 

It is also clear that the Arab countries do not want to back down from the progress made in the normalization agreement with Israel. This is not a peace agreement to end the war; they are making an agreement with Israel covering various issues such as diplomacy, military cooperation, security, finance and trade. 

After the events of October 7, the issue of normalization of relations depends on the Israeli alliance. The Arabs, like the Americans and the Israelis, consider the incident in Gaza a threat to Israel. Their goal is to eliminate this threat by exhausting the resistance in Gaza. If their bet on Tel Aviv succeeds, they can set aside the complex Palestinian issue and pave the way for a new regional order. 

As Gaza burns, the US-Israeli alliance and the Arab normalization countries are contemplating regional realignment. But the question and major obstacle in their path is whether Israel can win. Because it will not be so easy for Israel to defeat potential resistance forces in Gaza and West Asia.

Headline_English: A separate Palestinian state is the real solution
Content_Enlish:
The war in Gaza has been dividing the world for more than a month. The intensity of emotions has only deepened the divisions. The two narratives, Palestinian and Israeli, have pitted protesters, the media, religions, people, and the region against each other. In the process, the clarity we needed about basic human values ​​and what we could share has become a kind of moral confusion. 

Let’s start with some basic facts. It’s true – the vast majority of the victims of the current situation in Israel, Gaza, and the West Bank are civilians. Israel suffered enormous losses in the Hamas attack on October 7. The deaths of more than 1,000 Israelis, including women and children, have left them deeply traumatized. But since then, Israel has continued its relentless assault on Gaza. More than 11,000 Palestinians have already lost their lives in its indiscriminate bombing. Thousands of children lie in the rubble of Gaza. They are destroying homes, schools, and hospitals. How can such atrocities and genocide be accepted in the name of universal humanity? 

This human misery and global tension call upon us to adhere to the minimum values ​​of humanity; at least before the situation reaches a catastrophic point for everyone. All world leaders should face this ugly reality. Only by understanding this reality can we turn the world away from the dangerous direction it is heading. Our responsibility will not end with humanitarian intervention or ending this brutal war, but it is also important to recognize that the direction the situation is heading is not a path to victory for anyone; especially not in terms of moral clarity. 

I cannot help but believe that the aspirations of Palestinians and Israelis are not different. They are not monsters; they are unwilling to see suffering and death. Palestinians, like Israelis, have the right to live in dignity, security and respect in an independent, sovereign and functioning state. Yet for almost 20 years, Israel has been unilaterally obstructing the peace process. They have shown their thumbs down to the Oslo Accords. Yet this agreement promises a two-state solution of peace and security for both sides. In violation of that and in violation of international law, Palestinian land is being gradually swallowed up. In this way, Palestine has been divided into several isolated enclaves. Israel has tripled the size of its ‘settlements’ on Palestinian land. The residents of Jerusalem have been evicted from their homes. Not only have Muslim and Christian holy sites been attacked; those praying there have also been harassed. Now 2.3 million Palestinians in Gaza are under siege; 60 percent of them are displaced. 

The homes of families in Gaza are being bombed. The people of Gaza are being subjected to wholesale punishment. They have no place to take refuge. Hospitals, schools, and even UN facilities are no longer safe there. However, it must be remembered that no matter how many leaflets or text messages they are told to do so; Gazans will not abandon their homes, they will not abandon them. They know that leaving means losing not only hope and dignity; it also means losing the opportunity to return to their homeland. They have seen their relatives and ancestors struggle in seven decades of war. 

Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza 18 years ago was not for a two-state solution; it created a permanent division. Denying a part of Palestine is, in a way, denying the state of Palestine itself. An Israeli leadership that is unwilling to embrace a path of peace based on a two-state solution will not be able to provide its citizens with the security they need. 

While Palestinians live in a sea of ​​misery and extreme injustice, Israelis cannot continue to live their normal lives with security measures alone. Without a political solution, the promise of a peaceful future remains elusive for both Israelis and Palestinians. 

Is there a realistic alternative to a two-state solution? Just as Israel will have to struggle to accommodate conflicting nationalities in a one-state system, a stateless solution will deny the rights and dignity of the Palestinians. If this situation continues, the future will be even worse. Where we will see war, hatred and killing. Harmful political programs and ideologies teach us to use religion for our own interests. The crisis of extremism, revenge and oppression that will be created will affect not only the region but the entire world even more badly. And a two-state solution will be a turning point for the entire world. It will bring peace, security and prosperity to the region. Therefore, separate states for Palestine and Israel should be prioritized in international efforts. 

The solution will depend on what responsible leaders do. Although the task is not easy, it is urgent. No one can win in the massacre that is going on in Gaza. No one will win unless the Palestinians are assured of their rightful state. This alone will be a true victory for both Palestinians and Israelis in the pursuit of peace. Above all, it will be a victory for humanity in general.

Headline_English: The war that brought humanity to justice
Content_Enlish:
On October 7, the 50th anniversary of the Yom Kippur War, Hamas launched a massive attack on Israel. Thousands of people died in the attack, most of them civilians; more than two hundred were kidnapped. This unexpected attack brought devastation to Israel. The Indian National Congress firmly believes that violence has no place in a civilized world. Therefore, the very next day, the Congress unequivocally condemned the Hamas attack. 

Tragically, the Israeli forces immediately launched an indiscriminate attack on Gaza and its surrounding areas. In almost three weeks, thousands of Palestinian civilians have lost their lives in the Israeli operation. Among them are a large number of innocent children and women. Israel is taking revenge with all its state power on a population that is completely helpless. The weapons of one of the most militarily powerful countries in the world are targeting children, women and men who have no hand in the Hamas attack. Instead, they have been suffering discrimination and misery for decades.

Israel’s indiscriminate attacks have devastated Gaza. Entire families have lost their lives and entire neighborhoods have been reduced to rubble. Medical care is inadequate to deal with the huge humanitarian crisis that has arisen there. Cutting off water, food, and electricity is nothing less than a collective punishment for the Palestinian people. The relief and aid that is being provided to the besieged Gaza Strip from the outside world is minimal compared to what is needed. The situation in Gaza is not only inhumane, but also illegal under international law. Very few Gazans are able to escape the violence. Gazans are densely packed into a small area. They have no other way out. And now, the conflict is spreading even to the occupied West Bank. 

There is no sign of a cessation of the attacks. Israeli officials have spoken of destroying and depopulating large areas of Gaza. The Israeli defense minister has described the Palestinians as “human animals.” This derogatory language is hurtful and comes from descendants of those who themselves were victims of the Holocaust or mass murder. 

Humanity is at stake. As we collectively grieve over the attacks on Israel; so too are we now shocked by Israel’s indiscriminate killings and brutal attacks in Gaza. How many more lives will it take before our collective conscience awakens? The Israeli government’s attempt to equate Palestinians with Hamas’s attacks is a grave mistake. It is attacking the ordinary people of Gaza indiscriminately, determined to destroy Hamas. Given the long history of Palestinian suffering, how can an entire population be held responsible for the actions of a few individuals? 

The complex problems facing the Palestinians are rooted in a crisis created by imperialists under the direction of external forces. It can only be resolved through dialogue. It must be reiterated that these dialogues must address the Palestinians’ demands. Although their right to an independent and sovereign state has been denied for decades; on the other hand, Israel's security has been ensured. Peace cannot come without justice. The way Israel has blockaded the people of Gaza for more than a decade and a half, they are like 'open prisons'. More than two million people there live in densely populated cities and refugee camps. Israeli settlers in Jerusalem and the West Bank, with the help of the Israeli state, continue to evict Palestinians from their land. Their behavior seems to be trying to sabotage the plan for a two-state solution. Peace will come only when the work of making the two-state solution a reality begins again under the leadership of powerful states. 

The Indian National Congress believes that both Palestinians and Israelis have the right to live in peace. We value our friendship with Israel. This does not mean that we will forget the painful memories of the forced displacement of the Palestinians from the land they have owned for centuries and the years of deprivation of their right to live with dignity and respect. 

The world must take action in the current situation. It is very unfortunate that when the influential countries should be doing their utmost to stop the war, they are strongly supporting one side. The most vocal need to stop the military attacks and the powerful countries should step up. Otherwise, this cycle of war will continue and it will make it difficult for the people of the region to live in peace in the long term.

Headline_English: US and Israel hint at opening a second front in Lebanon
Content_Enlish:
The headquarters of the US Central Command or CENTCOM is located in Doha. On Sunday night, CENTCOM announced that the Ohio nuclear submarine is coming to its ‘area of ​​operation’. The announcement is worsening the situation in Palestine-Israel. News of the use of submarines is usually very rare. However, CENTCOM did not provide any additional information. The photo they provided, it seems that it is located near the Suez Canal in Egypt. Interestingly, CENTCOM also provided a separate photo of the nuclear-powered B-1 bombers stationed in the Middle East. 
The presence of both of them together is worth noting. There are already two aircraft carriers and hundreds of modern warships deployed in the eastern Mediterranean and the Red Sea. That is why ‘different equations are also coming to the fore’. US Secretary of State Antony Blinken gave surprising descriptions about Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran during his visit to Israel on Friday. 

Blinken traveled to Palestine from Jordan. During the visit, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told him that the Palestinian Authority is only ready to take full responsibility for the Gaza Strip as part of a “broader political solution” that would include the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and Gaza. Moreover, that security and peace would only come when the “state of Palestine” is liberated and recognizes East Jerusalem as its capital. The meeting lasted less than an hour and ended without public comment. 

The relationship between Iran and Saudi Arabia, brokered by Beijing, has certainly given a different dimension to the regional security equation. There, regional countries are prioritizing solving their own problems without outside interference. Most importantly, the old atmosphere of division and xenophobia created by the United States among them is 
no more. 

The death toll in the Israeli offensive in Gaza has surpassed 10,000. The death is certainly a great loss to the Muslim world. Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei said, "All evidence and indications show that the United States has a direct hand in this war." Khamenei also said that as the war continues, the direct role of the United States will become more apparent. The Fars News Agency, which is known to be close to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, also says that Khamenei met with Hamas' political bureau chief Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran. There, Khamenei told the Hamas leader that supporting resistance groups like Hamas is Iran's "permanent policy." Tehran no longer sees any problem in recognizing Iran's brotherly relations with these resistance groups. This is indicative of a major change. They have been forced to confront the United States and Israel together due to their use of force. In addition, Washington's diplomacy has also failed to isolate Iran. 

No power in the world can stop Israel now. Because both its stability and defense are inextricably linked to this war and the United States is its protector. That is why Israel wants to escalate the war for the sake of survival. Their goal is to spread this fire in Lebanon and Syria and fight shoulder to shoulder with the Americans. 

The US nuclear submarine is stationed east of the Suez Canal. This is an attempt to intimidate Iran so that it cannot intervene. Especially when Israel is moving towards opening a second front in Lebanon with the support of the US. The Israeli administration has already announced the evacuation of people from settlements up to five kilometers from the Lebanese border. That means that an indefinite war is about to begin in the Middle East. It is not known how the 80-year-old American president will deal with the situation when the call for jihad is starting at this moment.

Headline_English: The random equation of politics
Content_Enlish:
After October 28, 2023, the possible equation of politics has become chaotic. BNP's top leadership is being arrested continuously, programs are being announced in favor of BNP from unknown places. On the one hand, the Election Commission is preparing for the elections, on the other hand, it is also talking about dialogue. The ruling Awami League is confidently rejecting the possibility of all kinds of dialogue and is exercising its power in the name of a peaceful rally. 

The statements of the government and opposition BNP about what happened in the capital on October 28 are contradictory. However, whatever the statements, a few simple questions must be asked. Why was such a huge rally not allowed to be held peacefully that day? When sporadic clashes started at one end of the road, why did the police chase the huge rally at the other end? Did the police play a proper role in maintaining order that day? What can be found in the pre- and post-analysis of the policeman who was brutally killed? Why would the terrorist killers brutally kill the policeman before the start of the rally? Who are the murderers of the BNP worker who was killed? Why was Jamaat able to hold a rally without any prior permission that day? 

The results of BNP's failure to hold a rally show that on October 28, the police arrested BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on charges of inciting violence. For the past one and a half years, we have seen that Mirza Fakhrul was leading BNP to hold one political program after another in a non-violent and peaceful manner across the country and heading towards the final program centered on the capital. Why would he suddenly want to incite attacks on the residence of the Chief Justice, hospitals and journalists on the day of his party's rally? Would he be unable to even deliver the speech himself? 

Since the rally failed, BNP had to resort to seemingly violent programs like a strike and blockade. Almost everyone in the main leadership was arrested. Bus communication with the capital from all over the country is suspended on the day of the strike and blockade. In the meantime, buses are burning sporadically. Private cars are running less in Dhaka. The prices of daily necessities are increasing due to transportation problems. What is happening? In general, it can be said that the days of arson and arson are back again! In this situation, the basic question must be asked – are the police only for the government party? The government party's peace rally can be held without any hindrance; Jamaat's rally can be held, but why not BNP's? The United Nations Human Rights Council has issued a statement urging the police to follow the basic principles of law in the use of force. The organization's statement also mentioned the possibility that supporters of the government party were among those involved in the attack on the Chief Justice's residence. From what is reported in the media that day, it is understood that crimes were committed that day at several places including the Chief Justice's residence, Fakira Pool, and the Police Hospital. However, identifying only the BNP central office as a 'crime scene' and bringing it under protection without bringing any other place under protection certainly calls into question the investigation. 

2. 
We do not want to leave anyone outside the scope of suspicion. When a house catches fire, the beneficiaries of the neighborhood come with potatoes in their hands and start burning it. Even in the situation of the country's upcoming national elections, there is certainly no shortage of people who want to eat potatoes with burnt potatoes. Just as it is difficult to measure whether those people are from the government party or the opposition, it is not difficult to understand that many may want to take advantage of the instability. However, those in charge should keep a watchful eye on those who cannot arrange for potatoes to be burnt in the house fire. The way the police are starting to take action as soon as they see the processions and rallies of the opposition party; this is in no way acceptable. The protesters will protest, and the responsibility of the state police is to create opportunities for their protest without any hindrance. When the natural path of protest is blocked, it takes an unusual path. This certainly cannot be expected in a democratic society. There are also allegations that the police are working together with the leaders and activists of the student and youth organizations of the ruling party to suppress the opposition. If this idea that all political parties are on the same level before the police is not effective, it is not possible to create an environment for free elections at all. 

3. 
The Election Commission, one of the biggest partners in organizing free elections, has been regularly engaging in contradictory activities. There has been news that the EC will meet the President, more news has come – they have invited 44 registered political parties for dialogue. Although the EC said, there will be no more talks with political parties. When the negative position of the government party on the issue of dialogue is clear, when the BNP is not willing to have dialogue without the caretaker government; then this initiative of the Election Commission creates curiosity. With whom does the Election Commission want to have a dialogue in BNP? All the main leaders including the BNP Secretary General are in jail or in hiding – is the EC aware of this? Will they ask the government – ​​why is the main leadership of a party that has at least 30 percent of the votes in jail before the elections? Without finding an answer to this question, the EC’s dialogue with 44 registered political parties raises humorous questions. There is no leader who can announce a decision on behalf of BNP, avoiding arrest, in public, who or what will have a dialogue there? The answer to this question may be – there are 43 more registered parties. They will have a dialogue. They will have the election.

Will any political party be registered before the elections? What does the law say? When asked, the concerned legal expert said with a smile, even if there is no law, a law can be made. People always make laws when necessary. 

4. 
I could not agree with the legal expert. People make laws when necessary, but necessity is relative. The complications and ongoing violence over elections are certainly not new in the country.
