The conference was inaugurated by District Awami League President and former MP, freedom fighter Md. Abdul Malek, moderated by Upazila Awami League General Secretary Chowdhury Golam Mostafa. Food Minister, freedom fighter MP Sadhan Chandra Majumder spoke as the main speaker. Central Awami League Health and Population Affairs Secretary Rokeya Sultana, Naogaon-6 (Atrai-Raninagar) MP Anwar Hossain, Naogaon-5 (Sadar) MP Nizamuddin Jalil, and district and upazila Awami League leaders and activists also spoke.

Headline_English: AL wins 28, BNP wins 1
Content_Enlish:
Elections were held in 31 municipalities today amid clashes, fears and various allegations. Out of these, Awami League won 28. 

Elections were held in 29 municipalities as per the fifth phase manifesto. And the postponed elections of Damudya in Shariatpur and Syedpur in Nilphamari were also held today. One person died in election clashes in Syedpur today. 

Elections were held in 31 municipalities using electronic voting machines (EVMs). Out of 31, Awami League candidates won in 28. Independent (Awami League rebel) candidates won in two. They are Rezaul Karim Raja Choyal in Damudya in Shariatpur and Ershadul Haque in Haragache in Rangpur. BNP candidate Rezaul Karim Badsha won in Bogra municipality by a huge margin. He received 82,217 votes under the paddy sheaf symbol. His closest rival, independent candidate (Awami League rebel) Abdul Mannan Akand, received 56,090 votes. 

Out of the 28 municipalities won by the Awami League, Shibchar in Madaripur, Mirsarai in Chittagong and Raozan were declared winners in advance as there were no rivals in Raozan Municipality. All the councilors were also elected unopposed in Raozan Municipality. 

Awami League winners 
The Awami League candidates who won in the municipalities are Mohammad Rezaul Karim in Bariyarhat in Chittagong, Shahjahan Sikder in Rangunia, Mohammad Chanowar Hossain in Jamalpur Sadar, Mirza Golam Kibria in Madarganj and Abdul Quader Sheikh in Islampur. 

Ekramul Haque won in Charghat of Rajshahi, Tofazzal Hossain in Durgapur, Awlad Hossain in Matlab of Chandpur, Haji Abdul Latif in Sharashti. 

Mohammad Moniruzzaman became the mayor of Bhola Municipality and Md. Morshed in Char Fashion. Ashraful Alam won in Kaliganj of Jhenaidah and Abdur Rashid Khan in Maheshpur. 

Rafiqul Islam won in Keshabpur of Jessore, Khalid Hossain Yad in Madaripur Sadar and Raipur Gias Uddin Ruvel Bhat in Laxmipur. 

Abdur Rashid Khan won in Nachol of Chapainawabganj, Ataur Rahman in Habiganj Sadar, Abu Naeem Md. Bashar in Singair of Manikganj, and Iftekhar Hossain in Bhairab of Kishoreganj won. 

Nair Kabir in Brahmanbaria Sadar, Mostafizur Rahman alias Mostaq in Joypurhat, Rafiq Uddin Bhuiyan in Nandail of Mymensingh, SM Robin Hossain in Kaliganj of Gazipur, and Rafika Akhter Jahan Baby in Syedpur of Nilphamari were elected. 

Huge margin 
The vote margin was huge in most of the 28 municipalities where Awami League candidates won. In Rangunia Municipality of Chittagong, Awami League mayoral candidate and current mayor Shahjahan Sikder was elected mayor privately by getting 14,804 votes. His rival BNP candidate Helal Uddin Shah received a total of 221 votes. In Char Fashion Municipality of Bhola, Awami League candidate Md. Morshed won by getting 14,918 votes. His closest rival, BNP's Humayun Kabir (Kabir Sikder), received 746 votes. 

In Naidah's Maheshpur Municipality, Abdur Rashid Khan of the boat symbol got 13,598 votes, while Amirul Islam Khan of the paddy sheaf got 1,055 votes. 

Voting in four centers in Narsingdi 
Voting was held today in four centers that were suspended due to allegations of irregularities including ballot snatching in the fourth phase of the Narsingdi Municipality elections. Based on the results of the votes in those four centers, Awami League candidate Amjad Hossain Bachchu has been declared elected in that municipality. He got 21,768 votes. His nearest rival, independent candidate SM Qayyum, got 19,564 votes.

Headline_English: I can't imagine anyone denying Zia's contribution to the Liberation War: Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said, "We cannot even imagine that anyone would deny Ziaur Rahman's contribution to the Liberation War." Mirza Fakhrul said that the decision to revoke the state title of former President, BNP founder and Sector Commander of the Liberation War Ziaur Rahman is insulting to the independence, liberation war and freedom fighters of Bangladesh. 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir gave this reaction to Prothom Alo from Singapore on Wednesday. Mirza Fakhrul went to Singapore on January 30 for better treatment. 

The BNP Secretary General said, "Ziaur Rahman not only declared independence, he was a sector commander. Later, he was recognized as a very popular president by the people of Bangladesh. We cannot even imagine that anyone will deny his contribution.’ 

The BNP leader said that the BNP will give a formal response to the decision taken by the National Freedom Fighters Council (JAMUKA) to revoke the state title of Ziaur Rahman Bir Uttam. He said that a protest program will also be held. 
Mirza Fakhrul also said, ‘I have serious doubts whether those who have decided to revoke the state title of Ziaur Rahman believe in the Liberation War of Bangladesh.’ 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam said that the entire country will reject such a decision with contempt and will be vocal in protesting against it.

Headline_English: Case filed against 120 BNP members including Rizvi
Content_Enlish:
Police have filed a case against BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi and 120 leaders and activists of the party's organs and affiliates. The case was filed on Wednesday night on charges of attacking police and lighting torches during a protest march protesting the decision to revoke the state title of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman. The case has named 29 people. The rest are listed as unknown. 

Apart from Rizvi, the accused include Dhaka Metropolitan South BNP President Habib-un-Nabi Khan, central executive member Nipun Roy Chowdhury, central youth party president Saiful Islam and general secretary Sultan Salahuddin, central volunteer party general secretary Abdul Quader Bhuiyan, central Chhatra Dal president Fazlur Rahman and general secretary Iqbal Hossain, youth party Dhaka Metropolitan South vice-president Sharif Hossain, and Dhaka University Chhatra Dal president Mehedi Hasan Talukder and general secretary Abul Bashar, among others. 

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ramna Division Sajjadur Rahman told Prothom Alo on Thursday that leaders and activists of BNP and its affiliates took out a torch procession on Wednesday evening. The procession attacked the police and set fire to the road with torches. They snatched an accused from the police. They had a big plan to sabotage. 

The police official also said that Sharif Hossain, vice-president of the Dhaka Metropolitan South Youth Party, was arrested from the procession on Wednesday evening. Based on the information he provided that night, a case was filed against these BNP leaders and activists on charges of sabotage and assault on the police. The arrested Sharif Hossain was sent to jail through the court yesterday. 

The decision to revoke Ziaur Rahman's state title was taken at the 72nd meeting of the National Freedom Fighters Council (JAMUKA) last Tuesday. In protest, the leaders and activists of BNP and its affiliates took out a protest and torch procession in front of Aziz Supermarket in Shahbagh the next evening. The police stopped the procession. Eyewitnesses said that a chase with the police took place at that time. At that time, tires were burned and arson was set on fire on the road in front of Aziz Supermarket.

Headline_English: AL candidate accepts postponement of Kalkini election, others angry
Content_Enlish:
Independent mayoral candidate Mashiur Rahman alias Sabuj and councilor candidates have expressed their anger over the postponement of the Kalkini Municipality election in Madaripur. However, Awami League mayoral candidate SM Hanif has accepted the decision of the Election Commission. 

When the news of the postponed Kalkini Municipality election spread on Thursday night, general voters immediately gave mixed reactions. They say that there was no reason to postpone the election at the last minute after so much drama. General voters are blaming the weak role of the police administration. 

However, District Election and Returning Officer Md. Moniruzzaman said, 'The election has been postponed due to unavoidable reasons. No reason was mentioned in the notification for the postponement of the election. The reason for the postponement may be known next Sunday.' 

Meanwhile, independent mayoral candidate Mashiur Rahman said at his residence around 10 pm on Thursday, in response to the postponement of the election, 'The election has been postponed. Because there is no election atmosphere. As a candidate, we have been put under pressure. But the election atmosphere has not been spoiled yet. I asked the returning officer why the election was postponed? He said they don't know.' 

Expressing his anger at local MP Abdus Sobhan Golap, Mashiur Rahman said, 'Nouka will not be able to win, the MP candidate will not be able to win - this is the main reason for the postponement of the election. There is no other reason. Whether I live or die, on the day this election is held, I will also become a candidate after getting the news. If I do not become a candidate, then we, the people of this region, will collectively and unitedly field a candidate. Whoever the candidate is. But we will not let the MP candidate win.' 
Awami League mayoral candidate SM Hanif protested the independent mayoral candidate's statement. He held a press conference at his residence in Bhurghata area around 11 pm yesterday and said, 'An independent candidate said that the MP candidate, the Nouka candidate will lose; the election has been postponed due to that fear. I don't know where he got these crazy and bizarre things from. 

SM Hanif compared the incident of the police taking away independent candidate Mashiur Rahman to a drama and said, "A few days ago, an independent candidate made a drama. The general public knows these things. There was doubt whether they would have had a security deposit if they had won the election. Now they are talking crazy for fear of losing the election. Independent candidates are trying to fish in murky waters." 

Meanwhile, after the election was postponed, some councilor candidates have protested and held rallies. Asaduzzaman Talukder alias Lavu, a councilor candidate for ward number 9 of the municipality, said, "Senior leaders of the ruling party have interfered in this election to give additional benefits to their own party's candidate. As a result, our election expenses will increase. Who will take responsibility for this? We protest against the postponement of the elections without any reason.’ 

Awami League’s rebel mayoral candidate Sohel Rana said at a press conference at his residence, ‘There were only two days left for the elections. The Election Commission has announced the postponement of the elections citing lack of a fair environment for conducting the elections. I strongly condemn and protest their decision.’ 

According to sources at the District Election Office, a notification signed by Senior Assistant Secretary of the Election Management and Coordination-1 Branch Mohammad Morshed Alam directed the postponement of the Kalkini Municipality elections to be held on February 14. The total number of voters in Kalkini Municipality is 33,400. The number of female voters is 16,700 and the male voters are 17,300. The preparations were underway to hold this Kalkini Municipality election through EVMs in the fourth phase. 

On February 6, independent mayoral candidate Mashiur Rahman Sabuj was campaigning. At around 4 pm, Madaripur Police Superintendent Mohammad Mahbub Hasan called Sabuj’s mobile phone. Immediately, Kalkini Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Nasir Uddin arrived there in a car. From there, Sabuj was taken away in a police car. Sabuj disappeared soon after. In protest, Sabuj's supporters surrounded the Kalkini police station. To disperse them, supporters of Awami League candidate SM Hanif attacked the protest procession with domestic weapons. Later, the two sides got involved in a clash. Fifty people were injured. 

Independent mayoral candidate Mashiur Rahman alias Sabuj returned home 11 hours after his disappearance. Then the issue of Kalkini municipality elections came up for discussion.

Headline_English: 18 arrested, 8 police members injured from BNP rally
Content_Enlish:
Police have detained 18 people from a Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) rally at the National Press Club. BNP leaders and activists hurled bricks and stones during the police baton charge. Police say at least eight of their members were injured in the incident. The officer-in-charge (OC) of Shahbagh Police Station in the capital, Mohammad Mamun Or Rashid, gave this information. 

According to sources at the BNP Nayapaltan office, they will hold a press conference in the afternoon. The arrest and injury of their leaders and activists will be discussed there. 

OC Mamun Or Rashid told Prothom Alo that when BNP activists initially attacked and attacked the police, the police went into 'action'. Later, the police dispersed them. He said that he himself was injured in the leg in the incident. He could not be reached even after calling several times to find out which hospital he was receiving treatment from. No information was available about the OC's treatment even after contacting Shahbagh Police Station Duty Officer Sub-Inspector Abul Momen. 

BNP organized a protest rally in front of the National Press Club at 10 am to protest the decision to cancel the title of 'Bir Uttam' of former President and BNP founder Ziaur Rahman. Later, at around 12:15 pm, police baton-charge and chase took place at the rally. The rally was dispersed after the baton-charge. The Dhaka Metropolitan North and South BNP organized this pre-announced protest in front of the National Press Club in the capital. 
BNP Standing Committee member Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain was present as the chief guest at the rally. BNP central and metropolitan leaders spoke at the rally. Before the rally, the sidewalk shops in the Press Club and its surrounding areas were closed. 
The rally was attended by Chairperson's Advisor Aman Ullah Aman, BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Dhaka Metropolitan South BNP President Habib-un-Nabi Khan, Jubo Dal President Saiful Alam, General Secretary Sultan Salahuddin, and Swechchhasebak Dal General Secretary Abdul Quader Bhuiyan.

Headline_English: Police attack was pre-planned: Rizvi
Content_Enlish:
BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi has blamed the police for the attack on the party rally in front of the National Press Club. He alleged that the police attack on the peaceful rally was pre-planned. The police's behavior was reckless and like that of terrorist cadres. 

The party's Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir made this allegation at a press conference at the BNP central office in Nayapaltan on Saturday afternoon. 

Rizvi claimed, '119 leaders and activists, including BNP Vice Chairman AZM Zahid Hossain, were injured in the police baton-charge. Many of them had their arms and legs broken due to baton-charge, and they have been admitted to various hospitals in the capital in serious injuries. Police have arrested 21 people from there. 

It was informed at the press conference that Jubo Dal Central Vice President Zakir Siddiqui, Swechchhasebak Dal Central Joint General Secretary Sarwar Bhuiyan, Private University Branch Joint General Secretary Obaidullah Naeem, Joint General Secretary Zakir Hossain, Dhaka Metropolitan South Swechchhasebak Dal leader Zahir Majhi, Anwar Hossain, Swechchhasebak Dal Dhaka Metropolitan North's Ebadul Bepari, Nadim Hossain, Hiron, Md. Aziz, Md. Rubel, Iran, Sumon, Rahad, Sajib, Alamin, Joy, Md. Rafiq and more than 21 leaders and activists were arrested by the police. 

Ruhul Kabir Rizvi alleged that the police had been inciting and behaving violently from the beginning of the rally without any reason. Unable to hide various speculations about the government's misdeeds at home and abroad, the government has introduced a reckless 'danda-tantra' as per its usual practice. 

Rizvi strongly condemned the police attack on the peaceful program and demanded the unconditional release of the arrested leaders and activists.

Headline_English: BNP is trying to get involved in a conflict by falling on its own: Quader
Content_Enlish:
Awami League General Secretary and Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader said that BNP has now positioned the people and the police as its opponents. BNP is also making a false attempt to get involved in a conflict. 

He said these things while addressing the Tarash Upazila Awami League conference in Sirajganj district as the chief guest this Sunday morning. Obaidul Quader joined the conference through video conference from his official residence in the capital Dhaka. 

The Awami League General Secretary said that the people are now understanding the sixteenth degree of BNP's apolitical politics. They have positioned the people and the police as their opponents. BNP is also making a false attempt to get involved in a conflict. 

Stating that the Awami League never conspires; rather, it has been the victim of repeated conspiracies, Obaidul Quader said that in a democratic system, the government will change only through votes. Elections will be held according to the constitution when the time comes. Sheikh Hasina has the courage to accept the verdict given by the people. 

The Awami League General Secretary said that when the country is moving towards development, an evil group has started conspiring. After continuous failures in the movement and elections, they have now opened their pockets of conspiracies at home and abroad. 

Stating that there is no such movement issue in the country now, he said that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's people-oriented politics has put BNP in a movement issue-crisis. 

The Awami League General Secretary said that in the districts, upazilas, thanas, unions and wards where the committees have expired, committees will have to be formed through conferences as per the instructions of the center. 

Stating that committees cannot be formed with one's own people to strengthen one's position, Obaidul Quader said that if the party is to be strengthened, the sacrificed workers must be brought forward. 

Tarash Upazila Awami League President Abdul Haque presided over the conference, while Awami League Organizing Secretary SM Kamal Hossain, Health Affairs Secretary Rokeya Sultana, District Awami League Acting President Hossain Ali Hasan, Acting General Secretary Abdus Samad, MP Tanvir Shakil Joy, MP Abdul Aziz, former MP Bir Muktijoddha Amjad Hossain and others delivered speeches. 

The conference was conducted by Tarash Upazila Awami League General Secretary Sanjit Karmakar.

Headline_English: If you touch the title of Zia, your hand will burn in fire: Gayeshwar
Content_Enlish:
BNP Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy has said that if you touch the title of late President Ziaur Rahman, your hand will blister. He said, "I want to make it clear that if you touch the title of Ziaur Rahman, your hand will blister, it will turn into ashes like burning in a fire." 

Gayeshwar Roy said this at a rally at the party's central office in Nayapaltan on Monday to protest the decision to cancel the 'Bir Uttam' title of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman. The event was organized by the Dhaka district committee of BNP. 

Terming the Awami League government as the puppet of the neighboring country, Gayeshwar said, "I said 7-8 years ago, 'This government is not by the people, not for the people, not of the people. This government is by the India, for the India, of the India." So, regarding what is happening today, even though India has not officially accepted Bangladesh as a part of it, they are exploiting this country mentally. 

At the event, the party's senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said, "You will attack in front of the press club, attack in front of the party office, do not give us space. In this vast Bangladesh, from March 25 to December 16, 1971, the Pakistanis also did not give us space. The freedom fighters, wearing lungis and carrying Sten guns, resisted them from rice fields, wheat fields, and canals. We also have rice fields, we also have canals, canals, and rivers. We will confront them from those fortresses." 

BNP Dhaka District President Dewan Md. Joint Secretaries General Syed Moazzem Hossain and Habib-un-Nabi Khan, Publicity Secretary Shahid Uddin Chowdhury, central leaders Abdus Salam Azad, Nipun Roy Chowdhury, General Secretary Khandaker Abu Ashfaq, General Secretary of the Women's Party Sultana Ahmed, among others, also spoke at the protest rally chaired by Salahuddin.

Headline_English: Quader Mirza calls for strike in Companiganj demanding withdrawal of DC-SP
Content_Enlish:
Abdul Quader Mirza, younger brother of Bridges Minister and Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader, has been besieging the Companiganj police station in Noakhali for more than 12 hours and is observing a sit-in strike. In addition, a hartal has been going on in the upazila since Wednesday morning on his call. He started the police station siege program from 8:30 pm on Tuesday demanding the withdrawal of the Deputy Commissioner (DC), Superintendent of Police (SP), Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Companiganj police station and the officer-in-charge-investigation and the arrest of Charkankara Union Awami League leader Fakhrul Islam alias Sabuj. The hartal has started since morning. 

As of 9:30 am today, Quader Mirza was at the gate of the police station with several hundred leaders and activists. All the shops in the upazila are closed due to the hartal. No vehicles are able to enter Companiganj. 

According to local sources, yesterday evening, Abdul Quader Mirza, Mayor of Basurhat Municipality in Companiganj, held a press conference at Basurhat Rupali Chattar in protest against the attack and conspiracy to kill him in Feni's Daganbhuiyan and Chittagong. In it, he accused Feni MP Nizam Uddin Hazari, Noakhali MP Ekramul Karim Chowdhury, as well as the chairmen of Daganbhuiyan and Sonagazi Upazila Parishads. 

Sources said that during this press conference, Charkankara Union Awami League leader Fakhrul Islam alias Sabuj held a rally against Abdul Quader Mirza in Tekerbazar of the upazila. Stating that Quader Mirza had taken Companiganj hostage, he raised various allegations. After the rally, a protest procession was held there. On hearing the news of the rally, a group of Quader Mirza's supporters went to Tekerbazar. There, scuffles and chases took place between the two parties. At one stage, the police went to the police station and arrested Fakhrul Islam. At that time, supporters snatched Fakhrul from the police. In protest of this incident, Quader Mirza took a position in front of the police station with several hundred leaders and activists at around 8:30 pm. In his speech there, he demanded the withdrawal of Noakhali DC Mohammad Khorshed Alam Khan, SP Alamgir Hossain, Companiganj OC Mir Jahedul Haque and OC (Investigation) Rabiul Haque. He also demanded action against MPs Nizam Uddin Hazari and Ekramul Karim Chowdhury. 

Eyewitnesses said that the number of leaders and activists decreased slightly last night, but started increasing this morning. 

Companiganj Police Station OC Mir Jahedul Haque confirmed the truth of this news.

Headline_English: Quader demands making Bangla an official language of the United Nations
Content_Enlish:
Awami League General Secretary and Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader has demanded that Bengali be included as an official language of the United Nations in addition to ensuring the use of Bengali in higher education and high courts. 
He told reporters after laying wreaths at the Central Shaheed Minar on behalf of the Bangladesh Awami League in the first hour of Sunday, on the occasion of the Great Martyrs' Day and International Mother Language Day. 

Obaidul Quader said, 'Today, Bengali is the sixth language in the world in terms of population. However, the United Nations has not yet recognized Bengali as an official language. We are making that demand today from the Ekushey stage.' 

Awami League General Secretary said, 'Even after so many years of independence, our victory could not be consolidated because our main enemy is communalism. The branches of communalism still remain in Bangladesh. So let this Ekushey be a conviction that we want to uproot the poisonous tree of communalism. 

Calling on the people of the country to unite, Quader said, "We are determined to uproot the roots of communal evil forces to build a liberal, non-communal, democratic and prosperous Bangladesh as dreamed of by the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman." 

Awami League Presidium members Matia Chowdhury and Col. (Retd.) Faruk Khan, Joint General Secretary and Information Minister Hasan Mahmud, Cultural Secretary Asim Kumar Ukil, Office Secretary Biplob Barua, and Deputy Office Secretary Sayem Khan were present at the time.

Headline_English: Hearing on framing charges against Khaleda Zia in coal mining corruption case on March 22
Content_Enlish:
The court has fixed March 22 for the hearing of the charge sheet against BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia and other accused in the Barapukuria coal mine corruption case in Dinajpur. 

The hearing of the charge sheet in the case was scheduled for Monday. However, Khaleda Zia could not appear in court due to illness. For this, her lawyer requested time. Judge Nazrul Islam of Dhaka-2 Special Judge's Court granted the application and fixed the new date. 

Khaleda Zia's lawyer Zia Uddin Zia confirmed this matter. 

The case was filed at Shahbagh Police Station on February 26, 2008, on charges of irregularities in the appointment of contractors for the extraction, management and maintenance of the Barapukuria mine and causing damage and embezzlement of Tk 158.71 crore to the state. The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed a charge sheet against 16 accused on October 5 of the same year. 

Apart from Khaleda Zia, the other accused in the case are former Finance Minister M Saifur Rahman (deceased), former Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan (deceased), former Industries Minister Matiur Rahman Nizami (executed in a war crimes case), former Social Welfare Minister Ali Ahsan Md. Mujahid (executed in a war crimes case), Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, MK Anwar (deceased), M Shamsul Islam (deceased), Altaf Hossain Chowdhury, Aminul Haque, AKM Mosharraf Hossain, former Acting Secretary of the Energy Ministry Nazrul Islam, former Chairman of Petrobangla S R Osmani, former Director Moinul Ahsan, former Managing Director of Barapukuria Coal Mining Company Md. Sirajul Islam and Chairman of Hosaf Group, the local agent of the company that got the mining job, Moazzem Hossain.

Headline_English: Government is destroying all the achievements of the country due to greed: Musharraf
Content_Enlish:
BNP Standing Committee member Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain said that this government is destroying all the achievements of the country out of greed just to stay in power. 

Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain said this at a virtual discussion meeting of BNP on the occasion of the great Martyrs' Day and International Mother Language Day on Monday afternoon. 

The BNP leader said, "On the eve of 50 years of the country's independence, I am forced to say with pain that the spirit of Ekushey, the desire of the Liberation War, and the expectation of independence have been shattered today. Who has shattered it? Those in government today have killed democracy in this way just to stay in power by force. They have destroyed the country's judicial system, are destroying all the institutions of the country by partyization, and are leading Bangladesh towards a failed state." 

Stating that this government is doing everything to keep the opposition party in check, Khandaker Mosharraf said that there are over one lakh cases against BNP leaders and activists, and over 3.5 million accused. BNP leaders and activists are victims of disappearances, murders and extrajudicial killings. 

Khaleda Zia has been sentenced to prison in a fabricated case. 

Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain commented that the government is very weak. He said, ‘There is no reason to think that BNP is weak. If BNP is weak, then why did you steal votes on the night of the 29th (the night before the parliamentary elections on December 30)? Because you are afraid of BNP, you are afraid of the people.’ 

Khandaker Mosharraf called on the people to build a strong unity for the movement to overcome this situation. 

The country is independent on paper and pen, but we are subordinate 
Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy said, ‘The best achievement of the past century is the right to our language, and the best achievement was gaining independence. Behind the idea of ​​independence was a democratic system, we have not yet been able to establish that democratic state system. Living in a non-democratic state is not much different from being a citizen of a subjugated country. The country is independent on paper, but we are subjugated.’ 

History cannot be written by force 
Standing committee member Abdul Moin Khan said, ‘We all know who carried out the language movement. Today, we hear new names, they played a great role in the Ekushey Language Movement. I do not want to mention their names. I will just say this, history cannot be written by force.’ 

Standing committee members Iqbal Hasan Mahmud and Selima Rahman also spoke at the discussion meeting chaired by party standing committee member Nazrul Islam Khan and conducted by publicity secretary Shahid Uddin Chowdhury.

Headline_English: No matter how great a leader he is, no one will be able to overcome him: Quader
Content_Enlish:
Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader has made it clear that the party will not take the burden of defaming a few people. He said that the Awami League is going to take strict organizational measures against those who tarnish the party's image. 

Obaidul Quader said this at an extended meeting of the Dhaka Metropolitan South Awami League organized at a hotel in the capital on Wednesday. He joined the meeting through video conference from his official residence. 

The ruling party's general secretary said that if someone is involved in activities against the party's discipline, no one, no matter how big the leader, will get away with it. Everyone is under surveillance, who, where, when and what they are doing, organizational measures will be taken against them in the next central executive committee meeting. 

Stating that the party's discipline must be followed if you form a party, the Awami League general secretary said that you must remember that no one is indispensable in the party at any level except Sheikh Hasina. 

Obaidul Quader told the leaders of the Dhaka Metropolitan Awami League that pocket committees will not be tolerated to make your position heavy. Committees should be formed from the grassroots to the police station in stages through the conference. 

Stating that a sinister group is continuing its evil efforts to overthrow the government with the help of an international evil group and install a puppet government to achieve their goals, the Awami League General Secretary said that everyone should remain united against this evil effort. He said that the defectors should be evaluated. They are the ones who will be with the party in difficult times, the spring cuckoos will not be found. 

Stating that Sheikh Hasina must remain in power to continue the trend of development and achievements of Bangladesh, Obaidul Quader said that everyone should remain united for that. Awami League is a family, and those who create a rift in the unity of this family will not be forgiven in any way, he also made it clear. 

If there is any statement or disagreement on the internal affairs of the party, it should be discussed in the party forum, and if it is not resolved, it should be submitted in writing to the president's political office. 

Obaidul Quader once again said that any committee of the party at the district, upazila, or police station level cannot be abolished without the permission of the center. 

Joint General Secretary of the Awami League Dipu Moni, Organizing Secretary Mirza Azam, General Secretary of the South Awami League Humayun Kabir, among others, spoke at the extended meeting chaired by Abu Ahmed Mannafi, President of the Dhaka Metropolitan South Awami League.

Headline_English: Attorney General removed from AL subcommittee
Content_Enlish:
A change has been made to a member position of the Bangladesh Awami League's Information and Research Subcommittee amid controversy. Supreme Court lawyer Mansurul Haque Chowdhury has been brought into the subcommittee instead of Attorney General AM Amin Uddin. It has been reported that this change has been made so that there is no controversy among people about the post of Attorney General. 

This was confirmed in a press release sent by Awami League's Information and Research Subcommittee Member Secretary Selim Mahmud on Tuesday. It said that AM Amin Uddin was included not as Attorney General, but as a senior lawyer of the Supreme Court and a jurist. According to the Awami League constitution, there is a provision to have some expert members in the party's divisional subcommittees. Such expert members may or may not be primary members of the party. There is no violation of the law and customary practice in this. 

Selim Mahmud said, "Many people have been involved in an attempt to make the Bangladesh Awami League subcommittee controversial by misinterpreting this issue. They are also completely misinterpreting the constitution and the law and making fabricated statements about the Attorney General's post, which is completely undesirable."

Headline_English: BNP wants to hold nationwide rallies in March
Content_Enlish:
BNP wants to hold meetings across the country during the month of independence. For this, BNP met Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed on Wednesday to seek permission to hold the program and security for the event. 

According to a press release from the Police Headquarters, BNP wants to hold nationwide programs in March under the banner of 'National Committee for Celebrating the Golden Jubilee of Independence'. 

According to the release, Inspector General of Police Benazir Ahmed advised the members of the BNP delegation to seek permission from the relevant local authorities in and outside Dhaka separately for each program and venue. In addition, even if approval is received, the IGP requested that they hold 'indoor programs' considering the Corona situation and follow proper hygiene rules. 

The BNP delegation included Md. Abdus Salam, member of the advisory council to the party's chairperson, Bijon Kanti Sarkar, and BNP National Executive Committee Publicity Secretary Shahid Uddin Chowdhury and Liberation War Affairs Secretary Colonel (retd) Zainul Abedin.

Headline_English: DU expels 7 students' union leaders including president, secretary
Content_Enlish:
The central committee of Bangladesh Chhatra Union has expelled seven leaders including central vice president Sampa Das, Dhaka University branch president Sakhawat Fahad, and general secretary Ragib Naeem for six months on charges of disorder and factional activities in the organization. In addition, the committees of Dhaka Metropolitan and private university branches of the Chhatra Union have been dissolved and new committees have been formed. 

Central Chhatra Union Office Secretary Mahir Shahriar Reza gave this information in a press release sent to the media on Thursday afternoon. 

The release further said that central Chhatra Union vice president Sampa Das, Dhaka University branch president Sakhawat Fahad, general secretary Ragib Naeem and assistant general secretary Meghmallar Basu, Dhaka Metropolitan branch president Tasin Mallik, general secretary Billal Hossain and organizing secretary Sadat Mahmud have been expelled for 6 months under Article 56 (a) of the constitution for their activities against the discipline and ethics of the organization. Dhaka University branch vice president Mahir Shahriar Reza has been appointed as acting president and assistant general secretary Shimul Kumbhakar as acting general secretary. 

The student union's notification further said that the organization's central vice president Nazir Amin Chowdhury, vice president Joy Roy, assistant general secretary Mikha Piregu (also president of Jahangirnagar University branch), assistant general secretary Tamjid Haider, members Saddam Hossain and Rathindranath Bappi have been warned for being involved in unorganized activities and appropriate organizational action will be taken if they are involved in such activities in the future. 

In addition, in the fourth executive meeting of the student union, the Dhaka Metropolitan and Private University Branch Student Union Committees were dissolved in accordance with Section 56 (c) of the constitution for violating Section 48 (a) of the organization's constitution and new committees were formed. A 21-member convening committee has been formed in the Dhaka Metropolitan Branch and a 15-member convening committee has been formed in the Private University Branch. 

The notification also stated that the National Council meeting of the Chhatra Union will be held on March 12. 
When asked, the central president of the Chhatra Union, Faiz Ullah, told Prothom Alo that the seven leaders were expelled from the organization mainly for creating chaos in the organization and factional activities. 

Meanwhile, Ragib Naeem, general secretary of the expelled Dhaka University branch, said that this decision of the central committee is not final. It is a matter of approval in various forums of the organization. They do not want to say anything about this outside the organizational forum right now. 

The current central committee of the Chhatra Union was formed through the 40th national conference on November 22 last year, with Faiz Ullah as the president and Deepak Shil as the general secretary. Since then, a section of the organization has been holding various programs separately due to disagreements over the conference process and disputes over leadership. It is in this context that the central Chhatra Union announced this decision to expel the seven leaders of that section.

Headline_English: Hefazat leaders demand arrest of 'Shahin Huzur'
Content_Enlish:
The leaders of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh have demanded the arrest of a person identified as 'Shahin Huzur' in connection with the attack on Maulana Jasim Uddin, Assistant Secretary General of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh. According to them, arresting this person will reveal the identity of the attackers. But the police are not playing any role in arresting him.

In a written statement, the Hefazat leaders said that they have been able to identify the person named Shahin. Shahin's permanent address is in Lalmonirhat. He works as a teacher in the literature department at Ashraful Ulum Boro Katara Madrasa. He changed his name from Shahin to Mushahid at the madrasa. He and his family lived in a rented house in Lalbagh. Two days after the attack, he took leave and left the madrasa on February 11. After that, he did not return to the madrasa. The Hefazat leaders have learned that after the attack, Shahin took refuge in his friend's house at Lalbagh Kella intersection. The police raided the house where Shahin lived in Lalbagh and did not find any members of his family.

Maulana Mamunul Haque, Secretary of Hefazat-e-Islam Dhaka Metropolitan and Central Joint Secretary General, read out a written statement at the press conference. The written statement said that Maulana Jasim Uddin was stabbed on February 9. After that, the police arrested a young man named Masum Ahmed Imran on February 12 after watching the CCTV footage. After the arrest, Masum told the police that he carried out the attack in exchange for money from a person named Shahin Huzur. Later, when Masum was sent to court on February 14, the police mentioned Shahin Huzur's name as the person who ordered the attack in the document. But even after 20 days of the incident, the police have not been able to arrest Shahin. Jasim Uddin is suffering from insecurity. Mamunul Haque alleged that they do not see the effective role of the police in arresting Shahin.

Headline_English: Two more cases against Mamunul Haque
Content_Enlish:
Two more cases have been filed against imprisoned Hefazat-e-Islam leader Mamunul Haque. In these cases, the charges of beating with intent to kill and burning a motorcycle in the Baitul Mukarram Mosque area on April 26, centered on Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Bangladesh, have been filed. The number of cases filed against Mamunul Haque in Dhaka and Narayanganj in this regard has reached 20. 

On Sunday, two people named Abab Ahmed Rajabi and Md. Rumam Sheikh filed two cases at the Paltan Police Station in the capital. Hefazat's Central Joint Secretary General Mamunul has been made the main accused in both cases. In addition, the organization's Joint Secretaries General Maulana Lokman Hakim, Maulana Junaid Al Habib and Nasir Uddin Monir have also been made accused. 

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Bangladesh for two days last month to participate in the birth centenary of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and the golden jubilee of independence. Leaders and activists of several religious organizations protested against his visit. On March 26, after Friday prayers, leaders and activists of the ruling Awami League and its various affiliates clashed with the police and religious leaders and activists in the Baitul Mukarram Mosque area. 

About 70 people from both sides were injured. On April 5, Dhaka Metropolitan Jubo League (South) Deputy Office Secretary Khandaker Arif Uz Zaman filed the first case with Paltan Police Station, making Mamunul Haque the main accused in the incident. 

Abab Ahmed Rajabi and Rumam Sheikh, who filed the case this time, identified themselves to Prothom Alo as doing business in Old Dhaka. 

The statements in the two cases are very similar. The statement in the case filed by Abab Ahmed Rizvi states that on the orders of Mamunul Haque, Hefazat Joint Secretary General Lokman Hakim suddenly hit him on the head with an iron pipe in his hand. He moved away to save his life. Then the blow hit his leg and injured him. He fell to the ground due to the impact. In this situation, Joint Secretary General Junaid Al Habib and Nasir Uddin Monir hit him in various parts of his body with bamboo sticks in his hands, injuring him. 

Rumam Sheikh, the plaintiff in the other case, told Prothom Alo that he had gone to the mosque to pray that day. After the prayers, he was severely beaten and the motorcycle parked at the south gate of Baitul Mukarram was burned. 
Zahidul Islam, Assistant Commissioner of Motijheel Region of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, told Prothom Alo that a decision will be made later on whether the Paltan Police Station or the Intelligence Department will investigate the two cases. 

Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis leader Mamunul Haque was in discussions at various times after the Hefazat-e-Islam rally and violence at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel on May 5, 2013. During this time, he took charge as the General Secretary of Hefazat-e-Islam's Dhaka Metropolitan Branch. A few months ago, he opposed the installation of a statue of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. Then last month, he also opposed Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Bangladesh. On March 26, at least 17 people died in violence in Hathazari and Brahmanbaria of Chittagong following clashes at Baitul Mukarram. 

As the news of this incident spread, Mamunul Haque was surrounded along with a woman at a resort in Sonargaon upazila of Narayanganj on April 3. At one stage, Hefazat activists attacked the resort and freed him. Then, on April 18, the police arrested him from a madrasa in Mohammadpur. The next day, the detective police got him on a seven-day remand.

Headline_English: I will hold a press conference in Dhaka and reveal everything: Quader Mirza
Content_Enlish:
Warning Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader, his younger brother Abdul Quader Mirza said that he will go to Dhaka and hold a press conference and reveal everything. He said these things on Facebook Live of his follower Swapan Mahmud from his office in Basurhat Municipality at 10 pm on Tuesday. He is the mayor of Basurhat Municipality in Companiganj, Noakhali. 

Quader Mirza said, "I am saying it clearly today, stop the repression and oppression here. Obaidul Quader, stop this. This is your manipulation. I will hold a press conference in Dhaka in the next few days and reveal all your information. I have all the information about your wife. We have highlighted your wife's misdeeds. You cannot save your wife. She is still an accused in the ACC case. You are keeping it under wraps." 

Addressing his elder brother Obaidul Quader, Quader Mirza said, "Most of the officials of your ministry have homes in America and Singapore today. I have all this information. You can't shut up.' He complained, 'Today my leaders and workers are being arrested here. There is no police operation going on here. The police are conducting a terrorist operation here. I don't do gun politics. Those who do gun politics have their opponents. If they use guns here and empty the chest of a mother, who will take responsibility for it?' 

Addressing Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader, Quader Mirza said, 'The people are vocal. They know everything. They have silenced journalists by giving them money and threatening them, and they won't be able to stop them. They won't let me hold a press conference in Dhaka. I know how to hold a press conference. They won't be able to stop my press conference.'

Headline_English: Khaleda Zia's treatment will continue in the hospital
Content_Enlish:
BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia, who is infected with coronavirus (COVID-19), will be treated in the hospital for the time being. However, it is not certain how long she will have to stay in the hospital. A decision will be made on when she will return home after some more tests and observations. 

AZM Zahid Hossain, one of the members of her personal medical team, told reporters at a press conference held at the BNP Chairperson's Gulshan office at around 8 pm on Wednesday. 

Earlier, Khaleda Zia was admitted to Evercare Hospital in the capital on Tuesday night. After being admitted, several tests, including a CT scan, were conducted until last night. AZM Zahid Hossain told Prothom Alo on Wednesday afternoon that no major complications were found in the tests conducted after admission. 

At the press conference, Zahid Hossain said that the 7-member medical board of Evercare Hospital and a 10-member medical team, including 3 more members of the personal medical team, have recommended some more tests after observing the tests that have been conducted so far. Those tests will be held today, Wednesday and tomorrow, Thursday. Then the next decision will be taken after observing the tests. 
When asked by reporters when Khaleda Zia will return home, the doctor said, the board members will observe again after the tests are completed. There is a possibility of returning home after the observation. 
When asked whether the body has been affected by Corona, Zahid Hossain said, "I found a minimal infection in the lungs after the CT scan on April 15. Yesterday's (last Tuesday night) test did not find any infection. Apart from that, there are no symptoms of Corona anymore." 

Noting that it is difficult to take her to the hospital every day, this doctor of Khaleda Zia said, considering all aspects, she has been temporarily admitted to Evercare Hospital as per the advice of the doctors. Some tests take 24 hours. Some tests require two days of preparation. Khaleda Zia has not had regular health check-ups due to Corona in the last one and a half years. These tests are being done now.

Headline_English: GD alleges Quader Mirza threatened SI over phone
Content_Enlish:
It has been alleged that Abdul Quader Mirza, the younger brother of Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader, has threatened to check a sub-inspector (SI) working at Noakhali's Companiganj police station on his mobile phone. The name of that SI is Riyadul Hasan. It is alleged that Quader Mirza called his follower Md. Hamid's mobile phone around 9 pm last Tuesday and threatened him. 

Although the threat was made two days ago, the matter came to light today on Thursday. When asked about it on his mobile phone, SI Riyadul Hasan refused to say anything. Later, when asked about the same matter from District Superintendent of Police (SP) Md. Alamgir Hossain, he told Prothom Alo, "He threatens so many people, he talks so much nonsense to the OC. This is not a new issue. There are many such incidents there. A GD has been filed. 

According to a police source at Kompaniganj Police Station, at around 9 pm on Tuesday, the Bridge Minister's younger brother, Basurhat Municipality Mayor Abdul Quader Mirza, called SI Riyadul's mobile phone from his follower Hamid's mobile phone. After Riyadul received the call, Hamid handed the phone to the mayor. The mayor took the phone and said, "I am the mayor. Hey, where is your house?" Riyadul then said, "What will you do with my house?" The mayor then got excited and named some of his followers and complained why they were arrested. 

Sources said that at one point, Mayor Quader Mirza said, "Hey (this son) where did you come from? You are such a big fool! You will threaten my people, you are in danger. I will see to it, where will I give it to you?' Then the mayor himself hung up the phone. The source said that after the mayor hung up the phone, SI Riyadul informed the higher officials about the matter and filed a general diary (GD) in this regard. 

Several members of the police station told Prothom Alo that the bitter experience they had in the past few months since coming to work in Companiganj was unlike any other workplace before. They had never heard so many obscene words from any leader calling the names of police members like this. It has now become difficult to work here with dignity. 

Although Quader Mirza's mobile phone was called several times around 12:30 pm today, Thursday, to inquire about his statement regarding the allegation of threatening the police station SI, he did not pick up the phone. Therefore, his statement on this matter could not be known. However, in most of the speeches given by Quader Mirza on Facebook Live in the last few months, there is evidence of various objectionable words calling the names of police station members and officers, and the district police superintendent.

Headline_English: Hefazat leader Harun Izahar 'helper' of Hathazari violence: RAB
Content_Enlish:
RAB is claiming that Mufti Harun Izahar, the education and culture secretary of the defunct Hefazat Islam committee, was an 'accomplice' in the violence in Hathazari, Chittagong. After arresting him from the Lalkhan Bazar Jamiatul Uloom Al Islamia Madrasa in the city on Wednesday night, RAB said on Thursday afternoon that Harun Izahar will be made an accused in all the cases related to Hathazari. He is the accomplice in this incident. 

Although central leaders of Hefazat-e-Islam have been arrested across the country, this is the first time a central leader of the organization has been arrested in Chittagong. The police have so far arrested 40 leaders and activists in cases filed at Hathazari and Patiya police stations. 

After his arrest last night, RAB took Harun to the Patenga RAB-7 office in the city for questioning. This Thursday afternoon, RAB-7 Chittagong commander Lt. Colonel Mashiur Rahman Jewel told Prothom Alo, "Harun Izahar was the instigator of the vandalism and arson of the Hathazari police station building, land office, and postal bungalow. RAB has been keeping him under surveillance since the incident. Later, information was received that he was involved in the interrogation after being detained. Therefore, he will be taken to court in the afternoon to be arrested in the case filed at Hathazari police station. Since the cases are being investigated by the police station and police, they will appeal to the court." 

However, Harun Izahar's lawyer Abdus Sattar claimed that Harun Hathazari was not involved in the incident. He lives in Lalkhan Bazar in the city. He is being implicated in the false case to harass him politically. 
Mufti Harun Izahar is the son of Mufti Izaharul Islam, chairman of a faction of the Islamic Unity Alliance. 

On March 26, after Friday prayers, protesters clashed with police and government party leaders and activists in the Baitul Mukarram Mosque area of ​​Dhaka over a program opposing Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Bangladesh. Violence broke out in Hathazari and Patiya following the incident. Seven separate cases were filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act against 4,300 people for attacking Patiya and Hathazari police stations, vandalizing land offices, and arson. Later, on April 22, Hathazari police filed three separate cases against Hefazat leaders and activists. In two of these cases, Amir Junaid Babunagri of the defunct committee was accused. In three cases, 3,000 people were accused. Out of these, 148 names were mentioned. 

Harun Izahar was also arrested in the explosives case in 2013. He was later released on bail. His father Mufti Izahar is also an accused in that case. It is pending trial.

Headline_English: Rowshan Ershad in hospital
Content_Enlish:
Opposition leader in the National Assembly, Rawshan Ershad, has been admitted to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Dhaka after he suddenly fell ill. 

Family sources said he was admitted at around 9pm on Thursday. 

The family said he was fasting. Due to the intense heat on Thursday, Rawshan Ershad became dehydrated and had gas in his stomach. 

In this condition, he was taken to the hospital. When he was tested for coronavirus there, the results came back negative. 

Rawshan Ershad's son and Rangpur-3 MP Rahgir Al Mahi (Saad Ershad) told Prothom Alo, "My mother is fine now."

Headline_English: Government is doing business with Corona: Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has alleged that the government is not accountable to anyone. The government has no relationship with the people. That is why the government is doing business with the coronavirus today. 

Mirza Fakhrul made this allegation at a program organized at the BNP Chairperson's political office in Gulshan, the capital, at around 11:30 am today, Friday. The program was organized by the BNP Acting Chairman to distribute Eid greetings to the families of 'disappeared, murdered, and tortured'. 

At the program, Mirza Fakhrul alleged that the government has allowed a company to bring vaccines just to benefit a company and commit corruption. 

The BNP Secretary General said, 'A year and a half ago, we said that vaccines should not be brought from one source. But the government wanted to bring vaccines from one source for its own interests.' 

Mirza Fakhrul said that they said that sources from China and Russia should be looked at as alternatives. The government did not do that then. After so many days, the government is making agreements with China and Russia again. 

Addressing the government, the BNP Secretary General said, the government is drinking muddy water. The country must be protected from them. We must get rid of them. 

Addressing the members of the families of the ‘disappeared, murdered and persecuted’, Mirza Fakhrul said, ‘Every year such events make us emotional. We do not have the power to compensate for the loss you have suffered. It is not even possible.’ 

Addressing the members of the affected families, Mirza Fakhrul said, ‘Every year when we appear before you like this, we feel guilty. Because, so far, we have not been able to change the situation.’ 

Mirza Fakhrul said, ‘For the purpose for which we are agitating, doing politics, these sons of ours have disappeared from us. The goal is the same, we want a democratic social system. We want to establish our rights.’ 

The BNP Secretary General alleged that the Awami League government has taken away our rights by using the power of the state machinery. He said, they want to remove this power and establish a truly people's government. That is why there is so much sacrifice, so much pain, so much anguish. 

The BNP Secretary General said, 'A terrible fascist power has destroyed all our achievements, destroyed the love of the people for the people, and shattered our dreams.' 

Mirza Fakhrul also said that a government that is in power by force has to adopt strategies to survive. They have no relationship with the people. Since they are isolated from the people, they have to commit torture, torture, persecution, murder, and disappearances. 

The BNP Secretary General warned that the government will have to answer for the disappearances and murders. He said that the Awami League will have to answer for this. Those who have disappeared and disappeared must answer to their families. They must answer to the entire nation. 

BNP leaders Iqbal Hasan Mahmud and Mohammad Shahjahan spoke at the event. The program was hosted by former central leader of Chhatra Dal Nazmul Hasan. Families who attended the program today were given money wrapped in envelopes with flowers as Eid gifts.

Headline_English: Japa leaders meet Modi
Content_Enlish:
Leaders of the main opposition party in parliament, Jatiya Party (JP), are going to meet the visiting Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 

The meeting with the Indian Prime Minister has been scheduled for 1 pm today, Friday, at Hotel Sonargaon in the capital, the party has informed. 

Mamun Hasan, private secretary to Opposition Leader in Parliament Rowshan Ershad, told reporters that a four-member delegation of Jatiya Party will participate in the courtesy call with Narendra Modi. The delegation includes Opposition Leader in Parliament Rowshan Ershad, Deputy Leader of the Opposition and Jatiya Party Chairman GM Quader, party Secretary General Ziauddin Ahmed Bablu, and Co-Chairman ABM Ruhul Amin Howlader. 

Ruhul Amin Howlader told reporters that they will discuss issues of bilateral interest, including the common river share, Teesta water sharing agreement and trade discrimination, with Narendra Modi. 
This afternoon, Foreign Minister AK Abdul Momen will meet the Indian Prime Minister at Hotel Sonargaon. 

Narendra Modi arrived in Dhaka on a two-day visit this morning to attend the birth anniversary and golden jubilee celebrations of Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. He is visiting Bangladesh at the invitation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. 

After arriving in Dhaka on a special flight in the morning, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina welcomed him at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport. The Indian Prime Minister was given a red carpet reception at the airport. A guard of honor was given. After the airport formalities, Modi went to pay his respects at the National Memorial. 

Modi will attend the 'Mujib Chirantan' program at the National Parade Square as the guest of honor in the afternoon. After this program, he will go to the Bangabandhu International Conference Center in the capital. There, he will inaugurate the Bangabandhu-Bapu Digital Exhibition with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. After that, Modi will attend a dinner hosted in his honor by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. 

Tomorrow, Saturday, Modi will visit Jashoreshwari Kali Mandir in Satkhira and pay homage to Bangabandhu at Tungipara in Gopalganj. He will also exchange views with the Matua community in Orakandi in Gopalganj. Narendra Modi will return to Dhaka in the afternoon and participate in a bilateral meeting. Before leaving Dhaka today, he will pay a courtesy call on President Md. Abdul Hamid. 
This is Modi's first foreign visit after the start of the Corona pandemic. This is his second visit to Dhaka as Prime Minister. Modi had previously visited Dhaka in June 2015.

Headline_English: 30 people remanded for two days in Motijheel clash
Content_Enlish:
The court has allowed the questioning of 30 people arrested in a case related to protests and clashes in Motijheel area in protest against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Bangladesh. 

Dhaka's Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court Judge Yasmin Ara passed the order on Friday on the police's request. 

Earlier, the police had presented 31 people arrested in a case filed by Motijheel Police Station to the court and requested to take them on remand for 10 days. After hearing both sides, the court allowed the questioning of 30 people on remand for two days each. However, since one of them is a juvenile, the remand application is scheduled to be heard in the children's court within the next five working days. 

The accused who were granted remand are Zahid, Yunus, Nazmul Hasan, Nahidul Tarek, Limon Fakir, Salauddin, Naeem, Ripon, Abdur Rouf, Asaduzzaman, Mushtaq Ahmed, Mizanur Rahman, Sohel Mridha, Azim Hossain, Azharul Islam, Ruhul Islam, Abdullah Al Mamun, Sohel Ahmed, Khairul Kabir, Farid Islam, Sabuj Hossain, Golam Tanvir, Hemayet, Mehedi Hasan, Ismail Hossain, Rezaul Karim, Muntazul Islam, Kazi Mahmud Bin Monir, Mahmudul Hasan and Ruhul Amin. 

They are all leaders and activists of the Student and Youth Council, an organization of former Dhaka University VP Nurul Haque. 

Earlier, the police filed a case in connection with the Motijheel clash. Paltan Police Station Sub-Inspector (SI) Mintu Kumar filed another case in connection with the clash. In that case, 51 people were named and many unidentified people were named as accused. 

On Thursday afternoon, leaders and activists of the Chhatra and Jubo Odhikar Parishad blocked a road in the capital's Motijheel area and staged a protest rally. During this, they exchanged fire with the police. The police said that a total of 33 people were detained from the scene. Rafiqul Islam, known as the 'child speaker', was later released.

Headline_English: Roads occupied by AL, Hefazat did not enter the field
Content_Enlish:
The strike called by Hefazat was occupied by the leaders and workers of the ruling party throughout the day on Sunday, from the capital's airport to Uttara, Tongi, Board Bazar and Chandana Chowrasta areas in Gazipur. In some places, the leaders and workers occupied the roads and held huge processions, in some places, motorcycle exercises, and in some places, they held rallies. Anti-hartal slogans and speeches were given from these rallies. There was no activity by Hefazat in support of the strike in this area yesterday. 

People of the Chhatra League, Jubo League, Swechchhasebak League and other government-backed parties have been stationed at various parts of the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway since the morning to prevent the strike. Around 11 am, Dhaka-18 MP Habib Hasan and his associate leaders and workers held an anti-hartal rally in front of the Rajuk Commercial Market in Uttara, adjacent to the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway. During this time, various anti-hartal speeches were given from the rally. At the same time, Gazipur Metropolitan Jubo League leader Md. Billal Hossain Mollah was occupying the road and marching in the Tongi College Gate area of ​​Gazipur. The leaders and activists, led by Tongi College branch Chhatra League General Secretary Rezaul Karim, conducted a motorcycle exercise. 

Dhaka-18 MP Habib Hasan said, "We have held a rally to protest the heinous incidents that Hefazat-e-Islam is causing across the country. We want peace and order in the country." And Gazipur Metropolitan Awami League General Secretary Jahangir Alam said, "Our people have been on the road all day so that no one can create any kind of unpleasant situation or harm anyone's life and property." 

Meanwhile, Hefazat-e-Islam was supposed to be in various parts of Gazipur, including Abdullahpur, Uttara in the capital, and the airport, since morning as part of the hartal observance program. Zahir Ibne Muslim, the publicity secretary of Hefazat's Greater Uttara Zone, said, "Since the morning, the Awami League people were in a violent position with sticks, so there was no way for us to take to the field. Because, we wanted to observe a peaceful strike. We don't want any chaos."

Headline_English: BNP holds protest rally in front of National Press Club
Content_Enlish:
BNP is holding a protest rally in front of the National Press Club in the capital over allegations of 'killing people' and 'police attacks' on Independence Day. 

BNP has been holding this program in front of the National Press Club since Monday morning. Leaders and activists of the metropolitan BNP and its various affiliates are participating in this program. 

BNP held a protest program in divisional cities including Dhaka on March 29 and in district cities on March 30 in the wake of casualties in clashes last Friday over protests against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit. As part of that program, BNP is holding a protest rally in front of the National Press Club today. Dhaka Metropolitan North and South BNP are organizing this program. 

The leaders and activists participating in the program are staying on the road. Due to this, traffic is being disrupted on the road in front of the National Press Club. Police have been deployed in and around the National Press Club to avoid any untoward incident. 

Party leaders said that BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir will be present as the chief guest in the program. 

Present at the program till the time of writing this report at 11 am were BNP Chairperson's Advisor Aman Ullah Aman, BNP Central Committee Information and Research Secretary Azizul Bari Helar, Organizing Secretary Emran Saleh Prince, Dhaka Metropolitan North BNP Senior Vice President Bazlul Basit, General Secretary Abdul Alim, Metropolitan South General Secretary Abul Basar, Swechchhasebak Dal Acting President Mostafizur Rahman, Chhatra Dal President Fazlur Rahman, General Secretary Iqbal Hossain and others. 

BNP leaders said at the rally that 17 people have been killed so far. Killing people and police attacks on the Independence Day of an independent country are in no way desirable. Independence has been tarnished through this incident on Independence Day. BNP wants a fair investigation and trial of this incident. Otherwise, BNP will strictly resist this injustice under the leadership of Khaleda Zia and Tarique Rahman.

Headline_English: Chittagong BNP convener Shahadat arrested
Content_Enlish:
After a clash between BNP leaders and activists in Chittagong, the party's metropolitan committee convener Dr. Shahadat Hossain has been arrested. The police arrested the BNP leader from his private institution's treatment center in the city's Pravartak area on Monday evening. 

Confirming the matter, City Police Commissioner Saleh Mohammad Tanvir told Prothom Alo on mobile phone that there is a criminal case against Shahadat Hossain on charges of extortion and threats. In addition, he is also involved in the attack on the police, arson and vandalism on Monday afternoon. For this, he has been arrested. 

After the arrest, Shahadat was taken to Kotwali Police Station. Dr. Shahadat contested as the BNP mayoral candidate in the Chittagong City Corporation elections held last January and was defeated. Later, he filed a case in court, accusing Election Commissioner and current Mayor M Rezaul Karim Chowdhury. 

Former office secretary of the city BNP, Idris Ali, has claimed that the extortion case against Shahadat is 'conspiratorial'. He told Prothom Alo, 'It is not credible that someone who treats and helps people without money will extort money. It is all a conspiracy by the police. The police are doing everything to suppress the movement.' 

Earlier in the afternoon, when the city BNP took out a protest procession as part of the central program, clashes broke out with the police. In this, six police members, including the OC of the Kotwali Police Station, and 21 people, including BNP leaders and activists, were injured. The police arrested 15 people, including the president of the city women's party. The road in front of the BNP party office in Nasimon Bhaban was closed for an hour during the clash.

Headline_English: Attempt to create anarchy is part of BNP's plan: Information Minister
Content_Enlish:
Awami League Joint General Secretary and Information and Broadcasting Minister Hasan Mahmud said, ‘The statement of the BNP Secretary General proves that the attempt to create anarchy is part of their larger plan.’ 

The Minister said this in response to questions from journalists at the beginning of an exchange of views with leaders of the Dhaka Journalists Union at the meeting room of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at the Secretariat on Monday afternoon. General Secretary Sajjad Alam Khan, Organizing Secretary Jihadur Rahman and others participated in the exchange of views led by Dhaka Journalists Union President Quddus Afrad. 

The Information Minister said, ‘After the end of the hartal on Sunday, 9 buses and trucks were set on fire in Narayanganj. Walls were erected on the road. BNP and some of their so-called intellectuals, whom I am ashamed to call intellectuals, have also issued statements. Earlier, the attack on the people and government property on the golden jubilee of independence is tantamount to an attack on our independence and sovereignty, which BNP-Jamaat has supported. At the same time, when Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said today in tune that they will call a movement to overthrow the government, then all these anarchy has happened under their advice and patronage, this is proven. 

Regarding the attack on journalists, the minister said, "Any attack on a journalist while performing their professional duties is sad, unintended, unacceptable and condemnable. 

Because if any incident occurs, journalists will fulfill their responsibility to publish it in the media and inform the people, this is normal. In this case, I will request all political parties, all sides so that no journalist is harassed while performing their professional duties, no journalist is attacked.

Headline_English: UP elections may be postponed, decision on Thursday
Content_Enlish:
The Union Parishad elections may be postponed as the rate of coronavirus infection in the country is increasing again. However, the scheduled voting will be held tomorrow, Wednesday, in Jessore Sadar and Kalkini Municipality of Madaripur. In addition, scheduled voting will be held in one ward each in Thakurgaon Sadar and Shibganj Municipality of Chapainawabganj. Earlier, voting in these municipalities was postponed. 

A meeting of the Election Commissioners on Monday came to an opinion regarding the postponement of the elections. However, the final decision will be known on April 1 after the commission meeting. 

Election Commission sources say that in yesterday's meeting, it was decided to hold the scheduled voting until March 31. 

Voting is scheduled to begin in 323 Union Parishads (UPs) in the country in the first phase from April 11. Voting is scheduled to be completed in several phases in about 4,500 Union Parishads. 

The highest number of corona patients detected in the country in 24 hours was recorded on Sunday. 5,181 patients were infected with coronavirus from 8 am that day to 8 am on Monday. The Election Commissioners held a meeting the next day, Monday. 

From March 22 to June 2016, more than 4,000 UP elections were held in six phases on party symbols (for the post of chairman). The Local Government (Union Parishad) Act stipulates that elections should be held within 180 days of the completion of five years from the date of any general election for the formation of the council. Accordingly, the voting was supposed to start from March. But due to the delay in updating the final electoral roll, the election date was fixed in April.

Headline_English: Chhatra League leader resigns after Facebook post supporting Hefazat
Content_Enlish:
The ward Chhatra League leader of Zakiganj Municipality in Sylhet has resigned by posting a status on Facebook expressing support for the Hefazat-e-Islam movement. The resigned Chhatra League leader was the president of Ward No. 5 of Zakiganj Municipality. Last Saturday, around 10 pm, he wrote a resignation letter to the Zakiganj Municipality Chhatra League in a post on his Facebook ID named 'Hafiz Majed'. 

Hafiz Majed wrote in his Facebook status, 'I have resigned from the post of the president of Ward No. 5 Chhatra League for inviting Modi to the country and for strongly condemning and protesting the oppression of Muslims. A party that does not know how to respect Islam, which considers sculptures as halal, and invites attackers of Muslims to come to the country; no Muslim can be in that party. Therefore, I cannot be in that party either. I have boycotted Chhatra League from today.' 

The status given by Hafiz Majed has been shared 30 times till 4 pm today, Tuesday. It received 135 comments and 263 likes. 

Although the mobile number used by Zakiganj Municipality Chhatra League President Nurul Amin was repeatedly called regarding his resignation via Facebook post, it was found to be disconnected. 

In this regard, Municipality Chhatra League General Secretary Tanjim Shahriar told Prothom Alo that in 2019, committees were formed in the wards of the municipality for the three posts of president, general secretary and organizing secretary. At that time, Hafiz Majed was given the responsibility of president of ward number 5. Hafiz Majed's father was the general secretary of the ward Awami League. He was given the responsibility after thorough vetting to prevent infiltrators in the party. After his father died, he went to Saudi Arabia early last year to take care of the family. According to the organization's constitution, he was not supposed to hold any responsibility in the party since then. 

Tanjim Shahriar said that if Hafiz Majed thinks that he is in charge even though he is outside the country, then that would be foolish. Shahriar commented that he might have given such a status to go viral on social media without being in the organization.

Headline_English: Arrest warrants issued for 4 BNP leaders including Minu and Dulu in sedition case
Content_Enlish:
Arrest warrants have been issued against BNP leaders Mizanur Rahman Minu and Ruhul Quddus Talukder Dulu and four other leaders in a sedition case on Wednesday afternoon. Rajshahi Metropolitan Magistrate Court Judge Saiful Islam issued the order. 

Public Prosecutor (PP) of the court and Rajshahi Metropolitan Awami League Legal Secretary Musabbirul Islam confirmed this information to Prothom Alo. He filed the case in the same court as the plaintiff on March 16. 

BNP Chairperson's Advisor and former Mayor of Rajshahi City Corporation Mizanur Rahman Minu, party Organizing Secretary Ruhul Quddus Talukder Dulu, former Mayor of Rajshahi and Rajshahi Metropolitan BNP President Mohammad Mosaddek Hossain Bulbul and General Secretary Shafiqul Haque Milon have been named as accused in the case. 

The case application states that BNP held a divisional rally in Rajshahi on March 2. The rally was held under the chairmanship of Metropolitan BNP President Mosaddek Hossain and moderated by General Secretary Shafiqul Haque. The four BNP leaders made seditious remarks at the rally. They threatened to overthrow the Sheikh Hasina-led government. The Awami League had given Mizanur Rahman Minu a 72-hour deadline to apologize to the nation. After 72 hours, he sent a statement to the media and said, "I express my regret to those who were hurt and shocked by my statement." But when he did not apologize, the Awami League decided to file a case. 

If the case is filed, Judge Saiful Islam ordered the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Rajpara Police Station in Rajshahi City to collect information and data on the case by March 31 and submit a report to the court. The OC submitted the report to the court this afternoon. After this, this order was given.

Headline_English: Awal is in custody, Mamunul met him and informed him
Content_Enlish:
Mamunul Haque, the central joint secretary general of Hefazat, met with the organization's Nayeb Ameer Abdul Awal in Narayanganj. He then said that Abdul Awal has changed his decision to resign and will remain with Hefazat as before. 

Angry over the violence during the strike, Abdul Awal had announced to resign from all posts in Hefazat-e-Islam. In addition to being the central Nayeb Ameer, he is also the Ameer of Hefazat's Narayanganj District Committee. 

Amidst heated discussions over Abdul Awal's announcement, four central leaders of Hefazat, including Mamunul Haque, arrived in Narayanganj on Wednesday. They held an hour-long meeting with Abdul Awal at the Railway Jame Mosque in the DIT area of ​​Narayanganj city in the afternoon. 

Then, Mamunul Haque came in front of the journalists and said, "Abdul Awal will continue to serve as the Nayeb-e-Amir of Hefazat-e-Islam and the president of Narayanganj as before. At the same time, he will lead from the field as before. He has withdrawn the announcement of his resignation. He said that he will carry out the programs we have in the coming days in unity." 
Abdul Awal did not come in front of the journalists at that time. When he called his mobile phone, his servant Mahadi Hasan picked it up and said, "Awal Sahib is not there. The decision taken by the central leaders is his decision." 

Regarding Awal, Mamunul said, "There was some misunderstanding between Huzoor (Awal) due to pride and arrogance, which was resolved at our request and through discussions." 

Regarding the violence during the strike, Mamunul said, "Hefazat-e-Islam is not involved in any anarchy or violence. Hefazat leaders and activists took up positions on the highway. There was no vandalism or arson at their positions. We are protesting the violence that took place. 

In response to the question about the beating of journalists, Mamunul said, Hefazat cannot be involved. There could have been a misunderstanding somewhere. Because, Hefazat-e-Islam respects media workers. However, there could have been a misunderstanding with Hefazat-e-Islam's field leaders and activists, or there could have been a mistake in movement. But no responsible leader of Hefazat beat up journalists. 

In response to another question, Mamunul said, Hefazat-e-Islam did not commit violence. The violence that took place in Brahmanbaria is because the relatives and villagers of those who died there may be 'sentimental'. But why would Hefazat-e-Islam take responsibility for it? Regarding the case, he said, Hefazat did not commit violence. Since the case has been filed, the police will investigate and take action.
