Also present at the time were Central Hefazat-e-Islam Joint Secretary General and Dhaka Metropolitan Committee President Jonayed Al Habib, Joint Secretary General Fazlur Karim, Finance Secretary Monir Hossain Qasemi. District Committee General Secretary Mufti Bashir Ullah, Metropolitan Hefazat-e-Islam President Ferdawsur Rahman and leaders and activists of the organization. 

In the hartal called last Sunday, in Narayanganj, in addition to two people being shot, more than fifty people, including police and journalists, were injured in the clashes between police and Hefazat. 18 vehicles were set on fire. Two media vehicles, more than a hundred vehicles including an ambulance were vandalized. From the morning of that day to 12 midnight, an area of ​​about three kilometers from the signboard of the Dhaka-Chittagong highway to Shimrail was impassable. The next day, Abdul Awal announced his resignation from the party in his Shab-e-Barat speech.

Headline_English: The country has become full of corruption: Mirza Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that the entire country is now full of corruption and the Awami League government has created it. He alleged that the way the entire country is being consumed today to establish an individual, a family and a party, it was consumed in the same way from 1972 to 1975. 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam said these things in a virtual discussion on Friday afternoon highlighting the current economic situation of the country. 

The discussion titled 'Martyred President Ziaur Rahman and Free Market Economy in the Development of the Private Sector' was organized by the BNP's Golden Jubilee Celebration Committee. 

The BNP Secretary General said, 'Today, this government has destroyed the banking sector, it has destroyed the stock market. Money laundering has reached such a level that now the government itself is saying that it needs to be controlled, the ACC is trying. Unfortunately for us, a few days ago, I saw that the former chairman of the ACC was also accused of corruption. 

Mirza Fakhrul Islam alleged that the government wants to create a myth as a middle-income, development role model country among the South Asian countries. But the real situation is that now about six crore people in the country are below the poverty line. Today, due to the impact of Corona, another two crore people have become poor again. On the other hand, some people are becoming the owners of thousands of crores of taka through loot and corruption. 

In this context, the BNP Secretary General said that in 1975 too, they had turned this country into a dump through well-planned loot. 

Highlighting the economic reforms of the late President Ziaur Rahman, the BNP Secretary General said that as a modern man, he wanted to build a modern Bangladesh. He said, "Today, we must follow the path of Ziaur Rahman and first organize our party, unite all democratic forces with the people and snatch democracy, and free the mother of democracy, Begum Khaleda Zia." 

BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman was the chief guest at the virtual discussion meeting. Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, a member of the party's standing committee and former commerce minister, presented the main article at the meeting. Under the chairmanship of Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain and moderated by member secretary Abdus Salam, the discussion was also attended by party standing committee members Zamir Uddin Sarkar, Mirza Abbas, Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Abdul Moin Khan, Nazrul Islam Khan, Selima Rahman, Iqbal Hasan Mahmud, Vice Chairman Abdul Awal Mintu, economist Mahbub Ullah, former vice-chancellor of Jahangirnagar University Khandaker Mostahidur Rahman, among others.

Headline_English: Lockdown is not a solution: GM Quader
Content_Enlish:
Jatiya Party (JP) Chairman GM Quader has urged the government to further strengthen the mass vaccination program for COVID-19. He made this call in a statement on Friday. In the statement, GM Quader demanded the government to build field hospitals for COVID-19 treatment in infection-prone areas. 

The JP Chairman said, "In the reality of our country, the lockdown will not be successful. The lockdown is going on, but it is not possible to keep people indoors. Research surveys say that the standard of living of 25 million people has fallen below the poverty line again in one year due to COVID-19. 

And another 30 million people are already living below the poverty line. Most of the poor people do not have food at home, do not have money to buy medicine and baby food in their pockets. It is not possible to keep such people indoors." 

Describing the government's aid for COVID-19 as insufficient, GM Quader claimed that a large part of the aid is not reaching the real poor. He said that according to the government's estimates, about 15,000 people are newly infected with COVID-19 every day, and more than 200 are dying. That is why mass vaccination should be strengthened and the normal life of the common people should be restored. Only then will there be relief in the lives of the people.

Headline_English: AL's two-party program, Section 144 in Amtali
Content_Enlish:
The upazila administration has imposed Section 144 in Amtoli municipality of Barguna. The order will be in force from 9 am to 12 midnight today, Wednesday. On Tuesday afternoon, Amtoli Upazila Executive Officer (UNO) Md. Asaduzzaman ordered the imposition of Section 144. The administration has taken this decision to avoid an unpleasant situation surrounding the programs of the two factions of the local Awami League. 

According to local Awami League sources, a case has been filed at Amtoli Police Station against 15 leaders and activists of the Awami League, Chhatra League and Swechchhasebak League in connection with the attempted murder of Abul Kalam Azad, a Jubo League activist of Amtoli and nephew of Amtoli Municipality Mayor Matiar Rahman. People from the mayor's party organized a human chain and protest rally at the Amtoli Upazila Parishad premises today, demanding justice for the people involved. 

Meanwhile, another part of the Upazila Awami League organized a human chain and protest rally at the same place on behalf of the accused, seeking exemption from the case. The administration has imposed Section 144 to avoid any untoward situation due to the programs of two factions of the Awami League at the same place. 

Amtoli Municipality Jubo League President Md. Arif-ul-Hasan Arif said that their program has been suspended due to the administration's imposition of Section 144. The program will be announced later. 

Amtoli Upazila Awami League Acting General Secretary Municipal Mayor Matiar Rahman said that necessary measures will be taken after discussing with the upazila administration. 

Amtoli UNO Md. Asaduzzaman confirmed the news of the imposition of Section 144. He said that all types of gatherings and miking will be prohibited while Section 144 is in force. 

On the night of May 21, miscreants hacked Abul Kalam Azad, the nephew of the mayor and Amtoli Upazila Awami League Acting General Secretary Matiar Rahman, and injured him by cutting the veins in his hands and feet in the Khuria Kheyaghat area of ​​Amtoli Upazila. The next day, the injured person filed a case of extortion and attempted murder at Amtoli Police Station against 15 people, including Municipal Awami League General Secretary GM Musa and Upazila Jubo League President GM Osmani Hasan.

Headline_English: Sundarbans is expanding, tiger numbers are also increasing: Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that the Sundarbans are expanding. The number of tigers has also increased. The Prime Minister gave this information in response to a question from Begum Sultana Nadira, a reserved seat member, in the Question and Answer session of the National Parliament today, Wednesday. The question and answer session was tabled at the beginning of the meeting chaired by Speaker Shirin Sharmin Chowdhury. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that according to the 2015 tiger census through camera trapping, the number of tigers in the Sundarbans was 106. In the 2018 census, its number was found to be 114. The amount of carbon storage in the Sundarbans has increased from 106 million tons in 2009 to 139 million tons in 2019. 

The leader of the parliament said that the current government is always sincere and determined to protect the Sundarbans and its biodiversity. No matter what steps are taken for the development of the country, importance is given to ensuring that the Sundarbans and its biodiversity are not damaged in any way. The government has taken initiatives to create artificial mangroves to increase the size of the Sundarbans. Steps have been taken to expand it in the entire coastal region. At the same time, various measures have been taken to protect the trees and wild animals of the Sundarbans, including smart patrolling, to curb forest crime. 

The Prime Minister said that 334 species of plants, 165 species of algae, 13 species of orchids and 375 species of wild animals are now found in the Sundarbans, a haven of biodiversity. Among the wild animals, there are 42 species of mammals, 35 species of reptiles, 8 species of amphibians, 315 species of birds, 210 species of fish, 24 species of shrimp, and 14 species of crabs. The Head of Government also announced steps to increase the number of forest workers by making them up-to-date to protect the plants and wild animals of the Sundarbans. 

Noting that the wildlife sanctuary area was expanded in 2017, the Prime Minister said that currently about 53 percent of the Sundarbans is included in the sanctuary. 

Independent media is important for development 
In response to a question from ruling party MP Shahiduzzaman Sarkar, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that the constitution has given importance to the freedom of the media, including free flow of information, in all matters other than sensitive matters such as defense and defense. The current government firmly believes in the freedom of the media as the fourth pillar of the state after the executive branch, the legislative branch and the judiciary. The importance of independent media and public-oriented journalism is immense in the development of the country. 

Highlighting the various steps taken by the government for the media and journalists, Parliament Leader Sheikh Hasina said that the government has upheld freedom of expression in society by providing all kinds of support to the country's media. She said that currently the number of newspapers published in the country is 3,222. In addition, permission has been given to 45 televisions, 27 FM radios and 31 community radio channels in the private sector. The launch of Bangabandhu Satellite-1 has strengthened the media arena. TV channels in the country are now conducting broadcasting activities using Bangabandhu Satellite-1 at a much lower cost.

Headline_English: Zafrullah stopped for talking about BNP and Tarique
Content_Enlish:
A leader of the Chhatra Dal central committee interrupted Zafrullah Chowdhury, the founding trustee of Gonoshasthaya Kendra, for talking about BNP and Tarique Rahman. At that time, the leader gave a veiled threat to Zafrullah, saying that they would not take responsibility for him if any incident happened in the future. 

The incident took place at a discussion meeting at the Tafazzal Hossain Manik Mia Hall at the National Press Club in the capital on Saturday afternoon. The meeting titled 'Expectations and Achievements in Education: Education Budget 2021-22 during the Corona Period' was organized by the Education Reform Initiative (ERI). 

Ohi comes from London 

Zafrullah Chowdhury was the chief guest at that meeting. At one stage of his speech, he criticized the BNP leadership. Zafrullah said, 'BNP does not have the desire to come to power. To come to power, there must be desire and interest. Immediately, it has to plan what changes to bring. Discussions are needed on those.' He said, 'Today, BNP is being run by Ohi. And that Ohi comes from London. "We are noticing that recently we are not finding people to stand in the elections. So I think that if we want to bring down the authoritarian government, everyone has to unite. That change has to come from within the BNP."

Headline_English: Bangabandhu Sainik League protests against published news
Content_Enlish:
Bangabandhu Sainik League has protested against a part of the news titled ‘73 Bhuinfor Organizations Using Awami League’s Name’ published by Prothom Alo online on July 26. 

The protest letter signed by the organization’s acting president MP Shirin Ahmed and general secretary Harun Or Rashid stated that the inclusion of Bangabandhu Sainik League’s name in the news published is completely fabricated, purposeful and fabricated. They said that the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Trust had no objection to the use of Bangabandhu’s name with the organization in 2000. 

The protest letter said, ‘We also support the objective of the report by acknowledging the fact that during the long-term power of the Awami League, many opportunistic individuals are tarnishing the image of the party by forming unethical organizations in various ways. However, the justice that is established by punishing 10 criminals becomes unjust if an innocent person is included in it. Bangabandhu Sainik League was established in 1995 by the war-wounded freedom fighter Md. Bazlur Rahman.’ 

The protest letter also states that after the death of the organization’s founding president, some groups were trying to create chaos in the name of the organization by claiming to be their president/general secretary for personal gain. This was later resolved. 

The organization claimed that Awami League General Secretary and Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader had said that after the Bangabandhu Sainik League conference, the organization may be recognized as an associate or fraternal organization of the Awami League. In the meantime, the organization’s first national conference preparation committee has been formed with Shirin Ahmed as the convener and Harun Or Rashid as the member secretary. Although the conference was supposed to be held this July, it was not held due to government constraints due to the Corona pandemic. 

The protest letter states, "Bangabandhu Sainik League guarantees that if the organization named after Bangabandhu is not run according to his ideals, we will submit its no-objection certificate and request the dissolution of the organization. Bangabandhu's name and his ideals are more valuable than thousands of such organizations."

Headline_English: BNP is trying to break people's morale by spreading confusion during COVID-19: Quader
Content_Enlish:
Invisible Power Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader has called on everyone, including BNP, to play a responsible role, regardless of party affiliation, to save the people of the country in this critical moment of the Corona pandemic. 

The Road Transport and Bridges Minister made this call at a regular press conference on contemporary issues held at his official residence on Monday morning. Obaidul Quader said, "Instead of providing courage during the crisis, BNP is trying to break the morale of the people by spreading confusion. I urge them to come out of the circle of criticism and criticism and stand by the people. Corona virus does not recognize party affiliation." 

In response to the statement of BNP leaders that "the government believes in the policy of 'let's go it alone'," the Awami League General Secretary said that since the beginning of the crisis, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has repeatedly called for cooperation from everyone, regardless of party affiliation. The Prime Minister is implementing various decisions to combat Corona based on the recommendations of the expert committee. 

The Road Transport Minister commented that BNP has been giving 'lip service' by keeping itself in isolation since the beginning of Corona. He said that Sheikh Hasina's government and Awami League have been by the side of the people since the beginning of the crisis and will continue to be. 

The Bridge Minister said that in line with the high level of infection, BNP's propaganda is also going on at a high level. Their pity for the helpless people is limited to speeches and statements. 

Asking questions to BNP leaders, the Awami League General Secretary said, 'BNP once said a strict lockdown. Again, it said that people are harassed during the lockdown. Now, it is saying that curfew is not the solution. I want to ask the BNP leaders what the government is saying is the solution in curfew?' 

Obaidul Quader said, if people are not saved, for whom will we do politics? However, instead of saving people, BNP leaders are practicing criticism of the government and finding the smell of corruption as politics during this crisis. 

The Bridge Minister said that Sheikh Hasina's government is working for public welfare. It is taking strict measures if irregularities are seen anywhere. Saving the people is politics now. 

The Awami League General Secretary said that in this Corona pandemic, not only Bangladesh, but also in countries around the world where the infection has taken a terrible form, work is being done with the opinions of experts. Experts do not belong to any party. However, BNP wants a committee to be formed with them. There is no tradition of party committees anywhere in the world.

Headline_English: Vaccine crisis over: Deputy Education Minister
Content_Enlish:
Deputy Minister of Education Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury hopes that most of the country's people will be vaccinated within the next six months to a year. He said that the vaccine crisis in the country has been overcome due to the successful diplomatic efforts of Prime Minister Bangabandhu's daughter Sheikh Hasina. 

This Wednesday afternoon, at a community center in Pathantuli, the city, on behalf of Pathantuli Ward No. 23 Councilor Md. Jabed, the Deputy Minister of Education said these things while speaking as the chief guest at a program to distribute relief materials to 700 unemployed people. 

Mohibul Hasan also said, 'The lockdown has been relaxed considering Eid-ul-Azha. If you do not follow the health rules because the lockdown has been relaxed, then we will not be able to deal with Corona with the sole efforts of the Honorable Prime Minister. 

If we and you are not aware and do not follow the proper health rules, then it is not possible to control Corona in any way.' 

Councilor Md. Jabed presided over the program, and the guests included Chandan Dhar, Information and Research Secretary of the City Awami League, Arshedul Alam, member of the Science and Technology Subcommittee of the Bangladesh Awami League, Dost Mohammad, member of the City Awami League, Ibrahim, former General Secretary of Ward No. 23 Awami League, Mohammad Mohsin, Officer-in-Charge of Doublemooring Police Station, Idris Kazemi, Vice President of the Ward Awami League, Mohammad Hasan, General Secretary of the City Chhatra League Zakaria Dastagir, among others.

Headline_English: Helena Jahangir loses AL post
Content_Enlish:
Businesswoman Helena Jahangir has lost her membership in the Awami League subcommittee. She has been removed from the party's women's affairs subcommittee. 

An official press release was issued on Sunday, dismissing Helena Jahangir from the membership of the Awami League's women's affairs subcommittee. The release was given by the subcommittee's member secretary and Awami League's women's affairs secretary Meher Afroz. 

The release said that Helena Jahangir was a member of the Awami League's women's affairs subcommittee. But since her recent activities, which were publicized on social media, were outside the organization's policy, she has been dismissed from the membership of the Awami League's women's affairs subcommittee. 

Before issuing the press release today, Meher Afroz told Prothom Alo on Saturday night that Helena Jahangir is unable to work in coordination with the subcommittee. Some of her activities are embarrassing the organization. Therefore, a policy decision has been made to dismiss her from the subcommittee membership. It will be officially announced soon. 

Helena Jahangir, founder and CEO of Joyjatra Television, became a member of the Awami League's Women's Affairs Central Subcommittee on January 17. Before that, she became a member of the Comilla North District Awami League Advisory Council in December 2020. When Abdul Matin Khasru died, she collected party forms for nomination for that seat. However, she did not get the nomination. 

Comilla North District Awami League President Md. Ruhul Amin told Prothom Alo that they have also decided to remove Helena Jahangir from the advisory council post. Action was taken from the office in this regard last month. 

Awami League party sources said that many people within the party were raising questions about Helena Jahangir's politics. Her pictures were published with top leaders of each party from time to time. Even then, some leaders criticized her for being made a member of the subcommittee. The same source said that several central leaders and ministers recommended that Helena Jahangir be included in the subcommittee. That is why she was made a member despite not having any visible activity in Awami League politics. 

Helena Jahangir recently created discussion and criticism by posting a picture on Facebook announcing that she would be made a leader. Under the banner of an organization called Bangladesh Awami Charkijibi League, it was announced that presidents and general secretaries would be appointed in the district, upazila and foreign branches of the organization, which went viral on the social media Facebook. Helena Jahangir was allegedly named as the central president of this organization and Mahbub Monir as the general secretary.

Headline_English: Sajeeb Wazed has created a stir among the youth: State Minister for Information
Content_Enlish:
State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Md. Murad Hasan said that Sajeeb Wazed Joy is fully supporting the Honorable Prime Minister in establishing the Golden Bangla dream of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu through building a digital Bangladesh. He has created a stir among the youth to build a prosperous Bangladesh of the future using technology as a path. 

The State Minister said, ‘Joy’s leadership has initiated positive changes in our politics, as well as instilled great enthusiasm and enthusiasm among the people for Bangladesh in the future.’ 

Murad Hasan said this in a virtual discussion meeting organized by the Bangabandhu Cultural Alliance on the occasion of the 51st birthday of Sajeeb Wazed Joy, grandson of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and ICT Advisor to the Prime Minister, on Tuesday afternoon. This information was given in a press release sent by the Ministry of Information. 

Murad Hasan said that Sajeeb Wazed Joy has the ferocity like Bangabandhu. There is the vitality of hardworking and youth. His joining politics is auspicious for the country. He will lead the future Bangladesh. 

Deputy Minister for Water Resources Enamul Haque, Awami League leader Balram Poddar, actress Tarin, among others, spoke at the event, chaired by the organization's president, artist Rafiqul Islam.

Headline_English: Prime Minister seeks everyone's cooperation in combating COVID-19
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina expressed concern over the increase in corona infections and deaths and sought everyone's cooperation in combating the spread of the disease. 
The Prime Minister also called on the concerned quarters to give importance to enriching the country's export sector by developing agro-processing industries in 100 special economic zones of the country. She said, "We will be able to deal with this situation (corona). God willing, we have that belief. We want everyone's cooperation in this regard." 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said this in her speech as the chief guest at the 'Bangabandhu National Agriculture Award 1424' presentation ceremony this Sunday morning. She joined the ceremony organized by the Ministry of Agriculture at the Osmani Memorial Auditorium in the capital from Ganabhaban via video conference. 
The Prime Minister said, "Once again, since people are being infected with corona in large numbers and the number of deaths has increased, everyone should be a little careful. Keep yourself and your family safe. My request is to keep yourself and others safe by following the health rules.’ 

Noting that the government is establishing 100 special economic zones across the country, the Prime Minister said, ‘In these 100 economic zones, we want to give importance to the agricultural or food processing industry. Because if we can continue production during this Corona period, we will be able to meet our own needs as well as help others. And we will also be able to increase our products in terms of exports.’ 

Fish and Livestock Minister SM Rezaul Karim spoke as a special guest at the event chaired by Agriculture Minister Abdur Razzak. 
Senior Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture Md. Mesbahul Islam delivered the welcome speech and read out the citations of the award winners. In addition, Maya Rani Baul spoke on behalf of the award winners, expressing her feelings. 
Agriculture Minister Abdur Razzak presented ‘Bangabandhu Krishi Puraskar 1424’ on behalf of the Prime Minister. Which includes 5 gold medals, 9 silver medals and 18 bronze medals. The awards were presented to 32 individuals and organizations in recognition of their special contributions to the agricultural sector. 

A video documentary on the activities of the Ministry of Agriculture was shown at the event and the Prime Minister unveiled the covers of two commemorative books titled 'Bani Chir Sabuj' and 'Chiranjib' based on the words of Bangabandhu. 

The Prime Minister said that just as our farmer brothers and sisters deserve credit for the unprecedented development of the agricultural sector, so do our agricultural scientists and extension workers. 

The Prime Minister said that although Bangladesh has been moving forward on the path of development under the leadership of her government, at present, Corona has brought a stagnation not only in the country but also globally, where Bangladesh, being a densely populated country, is also at risk. 
Referring to the various steps taken by her government to alleviate the suffering of the common people, the Prime Minister said that to ensure food security during the Corona period, the supply of rice and flour through OMS activities and daily necessities through TCB is continuing at 727 places across the country. 

Sheikh Hasina said that her government has provided incentives worth Tk 1,28,441 crore under 23 packages during the COVID-19 pandemic, which is why her government has been able to maintain national growth even though it could not reach the desired target in dealing with this pandemic. 
Referring to the various assistance provided by the government to the people of the entire country during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Prime Minister said that over 50 million people have received our assistance.

Headline_English: Parimoni has the right to get bail: Zafrullah
Content_Enlish:
Gonoshasthaya Kendra founder Dr. Zafrullah Chowdhury said that Parimoni has the right to get bail. He is being told that he will get liquor at his house. But liquor is allowed to be imported. He urged Parimoni to be granted bail. 
He said these things at a discussion meeting on the occasion of the 28th founding anniversary of Gono Forum at the National Press Club in the capital on Sunday. 

Addressing the Prime Minister, Zafrullah said, ‘You have been in power for a long time. Now it is time to form a national government. You step down and form a national government. Make Dr. Kamal Hossain its head. Otherwise, there will be no fair politics.’ 

Zafrullah expressed regret at not seeing the leaders of the opposition wing of Gono Forum, Mustafa Mohsin Montu, Subrata Chowdhury and Abu Sayyid, at the discussion meeting. He said, Dr. Kamal Hossain is a very big and generous person. 

Everyone should be forgiven and sit together. Forgiveness and magnanimity were the great qualities of Bangabandhu. Dr. Addressing Kamal Hossain, he said, "Forget everyone's faults and mistakes. Call them and sit down. Without them, there will be no greater unity."

Headline_English: Many have died due to vaccine mismanagement: Manna
Content_Enlish:
The government has failed to deal with Corona. Mahmudur Rahman Manna, convener of Nagorik Oikya, has commented that many people have died due to the failure in the vaccination management. He said, they (the government) will not be able to save people's lives, they will not be able to save lives. Instead, they can jail people, torture them, arbitrarily disappear and kill them. 

Mahmudur Rahman Manna said this today at a protest rally of the Dhaka Union of Journalists. The leaders said this at a journalist rally demanding the release of former president of the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists (BFUJ) Ruhul Amin Gazi. BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi Ahmed, Daily Nayadiganta Editor Alamgir Mohiuddin, and leaders of DUJ, BFUJ and Sub-Editor Council were present at the event. 

Mahmudur Rahman Manna said, those who can keep journalist leader Ruhul Amin Gazi under false charges for so long will also fall. Professor Asif Nazrul gave a Facebook status. He did not name anyone. Why did he attack them? 

BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said to the Prime Minister, "Proof of historical truth is not needed. Did you fight the Liberation War or not? Did your family fight the Liberation War or not, that is now a matter of proof. Whether you were truly in favor of the Liberation War or wanted to become the Prime Minister of a greater Pakistan, that is now the main topic....They are insulting those who are truly freedom fighters, they (Awami League) are running a festival of corruption and looting." 

Rizvi said that the government is creating one issue after another to hide looting and corruption and is running various types of propaganda. There are also plans to ban political parties of the opposition. 

Stating that 42 journalists, including Sagar and Runi, were killed during the current government's tenure, journalist leaders said that no trial is being held for the murder of journalists. 
Alamgir Mohiuddin, editor of the Daily Nayadiganta, said that journalists are being silenced through various black laws, attacks and cases. 

Quader Gani Chowdhury, president of the BNP-backed Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ), said that in a country where there is no democracy, there is no freedom of the press. Control over the media has reached a level where we are constantly facing obstacles in publishing the truth. 

M Abdullah said, "Abdus Shahid's untimely death is very painful for us. His death is an irreparable loss for us. The journalistic community will never forget his contribution." Drawing a picture of the hostile environment for free journalism in Bangladesh, he said that the Digital Security Act and the recent cases under the Official Secrets Act and defamation cases against journalists have created an atmosphere of fear. 

Poet Abdul Hai Sikder said that writers and journalists are in an extreme crisis today regarding freedom of speech in the country. Now we have to speak thoughtfully even when we speak. Due to the situation, not only the media, but also ordinary citizens think twice about what they say or write. 

Whether something goes against the government or against the influential people, this has now become a matter of great doubt. 

Former DUJ President Elahi Newaz Khan Saju, DUJ General Secretary Md. Shahidul Islam, former DUJ General Secretary Sardar Farid Ahmed and many others also spoke at the event.

Headline_English: Return missing persons to their families: Fakhrul to government
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that the government is responsible for the helplessness of the disappeared families, so the government must take this responsibility. 
Mirza Fakhrul said these things at a human chain organized in front of the National Press Club on Monday, on the occasion of the International Day for the Prevention of Disappearances, at the initiative of the BNP Human Rights Cell. 

Fakhrul said, ‘The government says that disappearances do not happen here. So where did those who cannot be found go? They must be found and returned to their families. This must be done by the government. Otherwise, you will be tried in the people's court.’ 

Some of the members of the disappeared families took part in the human chain holding pictures of their fathers, some of their brothers, some of their children, and some of their husbands. 
Mirza Fakhrul said, ‘Who will take responsibility for the helplessness of these families? There are many here, they have not been found for 9-10 years. Our former organizing secretary Ilyas Ali, Dhaka commissioner Chowdhury Alam and more than 500 of our leaders and workers have been missing for 7-8-9 years. Ilyas Ali's daughter has grown up now, she still stands at the door waiting for her father to return. Father does not return.' 

The BNP Secretary General said, 'We have created such a country, such a state, where my children will disappear, no one will find their whereabouts. Law enforcement officers will take them away, the government will not give any answer. We cannot hold back our tears. The pain of helplessness is eating away at us. I want to declare my solidarity with you and say, we can do nothing more, we just want to stand by you and shout that give back my brother, my father, my husband. We want freedom from here.’ 

Fakhrul said, ‘This fascist Awami League government is illegally and illegally destroying the entire nation just to stay in power. It has destroyed our constitution, pushed democratic rights towards destruction. It has destroyed the economy, and has partisanized the entire administration. For that, we should all unite and defeat this government politically and establish a truly people's government. A government that will work to bring out the missing children and families of these helpless children.’ 

The human chain, chaired by BNP Human Rights Secretary Advocate Asaduzzaman, included the party's Organizing Secretary Syed Emran Saleh Prince, the daughter of the missing Md. Sohel, Saba, Md. Kausar's daughter Meem, Selim Reza's sister Rehana Akhtar Munni, Sajedul Islam Sumon's sister Afroza Islam Akhti, and Khaled Hossain's daughter Shammi Akhtar Nipa spoke.

Headline_English: It is only for your own benefit if you let them speak, Zafrullah tells the Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Gonoshasthaya Kendra Trustee Dr. Zafrullah Chowdhury has demanded the withdrawal of all cases against journalists. He said, "If you let them speak, you will benefit." 

Zafrullah Chowdhury said this as the chief guest at a discussion titled 'Role of Journalists in Protecting Freedom of Expression' organized at the National Press Club on Tuesday afternoon. The Bangladesh Mofusal Journalists Foundation organized this discussion meeting on the occasion of its seventh founding anniversary. 
Zafrullah Chowdhury said, "When democracy is attacked, we have to speak up. Journalists will speak up. But now journalists have been blindfolded." 

Recently, there was a clash between BNP and police at Dhaka's Chandrima Udyan. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina later commented that Ziaur Rahman's body was not there. Regarding this, Zafrullah said, "We are doing politics with the grave. We have gone crazy. 

You (Awami League) are slandering BNP's politics.... They promoted Ziaur Rahman for declaring independence on behalf of Bangabandhu. They did not reprimand him. Aren't we inspired by Zia's speech? I appeal, don't disrespect Bangabandhu. Let Zia also remain (in the grave) like him.' 

Zafrullah Chowdhury also said, 'We will love Bangabandhu. Ziaur Rahman must be respected for his good work....Prime Minister, you save history.' Apart from this, the Gonoshasthaya Kendra trustee also spoke about the Taliban rule in Afghanistan. He said, 'We who fought the liberation war have the responsibility to bring Afghanistan on a good path.' 

Commenting that BNP leader Khaleda Zia is still practically in jail, Zafrullah said, it is possible to make BNP stand with Khaleda Zia. She should be granted bail. 

To the Prime Minister, Gonoshasthaya Kendra trustee Zafrullah said, you should contribute to world politics. You have done a good job by bringing the Rohingyas, you have also created problems. Solve it. 

Mahmudur Rahman Manna, convener of Nagorik Oikya, spoke as a special guest at the event. He said, "I don't think it is necessary to explain how fair freedom of expression is. We have no privacy. There is no point in protesting now. We have seen everything being destroyed. We suffered, but we did not protest then." He said, the government cannot bring a vaccine (for coronavirus). But it misleads people by showing pictures of the metro rail and the Padma Bridge. Referring to the current political party running the country, he said, "It understands itself, but does not understand the people. That is why we have to struggle to achieve rights. Life has no meaning without struggle." 

As the main discussant, M. Abdullah, President of the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists, said, "Human rights are being curtailed in this country. In other countries, animal rights are being discussed. But here we have to struggle to speak for the people. 

Shawkat Mahmud, convener of the Bangladesh Sammilit Peshajibi Parishad, Nurul Amin Rokon, Secretary General of the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists, and many others were also present at the event.

Headline_English: There is no precedent of Zia firing on Pakistani forces: Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that there is no such precedent for Ziaur Rahman to have opened fire on the Pakistani army in the Liberation War. 

Regarding Ziaur Rahman's role in the Liberation War, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said, 'Khaled Musharraf was injured and Zia was made a sector commander. But there is no such precedent for him to have opened fire on the Pakistani army. No one can show such a precedent.' 

Head of Government Sheikh Hasina made these remarks in her speech as the chief guest at a discussion meeting on the occasion of the National Mourning Day on Tuesday morning, the last day of the mourning month of August. She participated in the main program at the Bangladesh Krishibid Institution Auditorium (KIB) in Khamarbari, Khamarbari, in the capital through video conference from Ganabhaban. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina again accused military ruler Ziaur Rahman of being the mastermind behind the assassination of the Father of the Nation and the founder of the politics of assassination, coup and conspiracy in this country. He said, "After 1975, those who illegally violated the constitution and seized power through murder, coup, and conspiracy, even in their own party there were dishonest, hypocritical, Mir Jafar, Khandaker Mushtaq Gong, and their strength was Ziaur Rahman." 

The Prime Minister referred to the self-confessed murderers of the Father of the Nation, Faruk-Rashid, who proudly gave a voluntary interview to the BBC, and said, "They admitted in the interview that Colonel Faruk-Rashid gave to the BBC. Not only that, but their statement has also appeared in many newspapers and magazines that Ziaur Rahman was always with these murderers. This Ziaur Rahman was the main source of power and he was the one who committed the dishonesty." However, it was the Father of the Nation who promoted Zia from a major to a major general, said the Prime Minister. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that the conspiracy of the anti-liberation forces, with the support of foreign powers opposing the Liberation War, to hinder the development and progress of the country is still ongoing. She has urged the nation to be vigilant in this regard. 

Sheikh Hasina said, ‘The war criminals, the defeated forces and the August 15 murderers, the children of those who were hanged, the friends and descendants of the war criminals are still plotting and conspiring against Bangladesh.’ She said, ‘Some of the international powers that opposed our great Liberation War are supporting them. Therefore, the nation must be vigilant in this regard.’ 

The Prime Minister said, ‘The killings that took place in Bangladesh on August 15 and then the grenade attack on August 21, the many attacks on my life, the attack on Kamal (Sheikh Kamal) in 1974. An attempt was made to shoot him too, when they saw that he had survived, false slander was spread in his name. That is, the defeated power was always active in this regard.’ 

At the beginning of the program, a minute’s silence was observed in memory of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu, Bangamata Fazilatunnesa Mujib and the martyrs of August 15. Chhatra League President Al Nahian Khan presided over the discussion meeting, and the organization’s General Secretary Lekhak Bhattacharya moderated the discussion. At the program, the Prime Minister unveiled the covers of Chhatra League’s annual publications Janmabhoomi and Joy Bangla Magazine (second edition). 

The Prime Minister said, ‘There are some people in our country who are always trampling on the feet of those in power. This group of flatterers has always played tricks on the fate of their own country and their own people. They have always destroyed our country by plotting. That is why when the Pakistani occupying forces started the genocide in 1971, the local brokers and the accomplices of the Pakistani forces never wanted Bangladesh to be independent. And then when Bangladesh achieved victory and the Pakistani invaders were defeated, they carried out the August 15 massacre to avenge that defeat. 

Sheikh Hasina said that Ziaur Rahman had led talented students astray by giving them weapons, drugs and money. His wife Khaleda Zia had also threatened that her Chhatra Dal was enough to confront the Awami League when she came to power. She too had given them weapons. 

The Prime Minister directed the Chhatra League to focus on the work of the country and the people in addition to studies and sincerely thanked every leader and worker of the Chhatra League for extending a helping hand to the people of the country during the coronavirus pandemic.

Headline_English: Election situation cannot be changed without political compromise: Mahbub Talukder
Content_Enlish:
Election Commissioner Mahbub Talukder said that the current situation regarding the elections cannot be changed without a political compromise. 

Mahbub Talukder said this at a press briefing at his office at the Election Building on Wednesday. 

The Election Commissioner said that the participation of many parties in the elections is absolutely necessary for a multi-party democracy. It is inevitable to analyze the reasons for the uncontested elections and take measures in this regard. Voters' aversion to elections is also a bad sign for democracy. He said that the election process and election management are involved in all these things. The way out of this situation does not depend entirely on the Election Commission. This situation cannot be changed without a political compromise. 

Mahbub Talukder said, "The silence of everyone concerned, including the media, on the 'International Day of Democracy' on September 15 has disappointed me. The question may arise in the mind, are we expressing reluctance to join the journey of democracy?’ 

Mahbub Talukder said, ‘I served as the Acting Chief Election Commissioner for 6 days from September 17 to September 22. Some journalists wanted to know my successes and failures in the 160 Union Parishad elections and 9 Municipal elections held during that time. It is not possible to suddenly change the electoral management in such a short period of time. Even then, some things remain. Three people lost their lives in the elections. It is very painful. I have always said that elections are not bigger than life. Yet, violence could not be prevented in the bone-to-bone fight in the Union Parishad elections. Whatever the incident or accident may be in the elections, the responsibility falls on the Election Commission. However, measures have been taken to prevent the recurrence of all the election accidents, i.e., chaos, illegal sealing of ballots, threats to opponents, etc., in the local government elections. 

In a news briefing, the Election Commissioner said, "During my duty, the law enforcement agencies were specially warned to discharge their duties legally in the local government elections. Those responsible for the loss of lives have been arrested based on evidence in all the places where there has been an incident of loss of life. Those who practiced with weapons and sticks have also been arrested after watching the video footage. Many more will be brought under the law after further investigation. No one has been spared and will not be spared in preventing violence. A warning has even been sent to a member of parliament for violating the election code of conduct." 

Mahbub Talukder said, "The vote turnout in this year's Union Parishad elections was fairly good, 69.34 percent. But the uncontested elections and the inauguration of 43 candidates for the post of chairman in the Union Parishad without electing them have spoiled this election. On the other hand, in nine municipalities, three candidates were elected mayors unopposed. Since the election is a selection among many, can being elected unopposed be considered an election?

Headline_English: BNP will not rush into the movement
Content_Enlish:
Important leaders of the BNP at the central and field levels believe that the two-phase six-day meeting has received a good response after a long time. 
They say that a message has been sent to the field level about why this meeting was organized and what the BNP leaders are thinking about the upcoming parliamentary elections. 

However, it has been learned from talking to responsible BNP leaders that no matter what the opinions are from the series of meetings, the policymakers have no plans to rush into any movement right now. Because the elections are still two and a half years away. The party is not yet organizationally ready for the movement. On the other hand, the process of restructuring BNP and its affiliates may take another year to complete. The main center of the movement, Dhaka, has just formed a convening committee. Apart from this, the top leadership also has to take into consideration what will happen if the movement is not successful and where the party's position will stand. 

The leaders gave their opinions on the release of the chairperson, restoration of democracy and the political situation. The policy-making council will review and give directions on future actions.
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, Secretary General, BNP 
Party sources said that BNP is going to prepare a political action plan ahead of the 2023 parliamentary elections. A draft outline has been prepared for this purpose. In order to finalize it, a six-day series of meetings was organized to take the opinions of leaders at various levels of the party's central executive committee. The aim is to increase the participation of leaders and activists in future movement programs and strengthen party unity and solidarity. In that regard, the party's policymakers consider the achievements of this meeting positive. 

In this regard, BNP Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy told Prothom Alo, 'We took opinions for whatever program we adopt in the future. Many times, issues arose, programs were imposed; through this, that too was resolved.' 

Gayeswar Roy's observation about the six-day meeting is that there is no fundamental difference in the opinions of the leaders except for some strategic aspects. Everyone agrees that the release of party chief Khaleda Zia and the release of democracy are tied to the same formula. And the leader's release is a prerequisite for fair and impartial elections. 

According to BNP central office sources, the six-day meeting, which began on September 14 in two phases of three days each, lasted for about 35 hours. 281 leaders spoke in the closed-door meeting. The leaders expressed their opinions on various issues including the next parliamentary elections, the release of the party chairperson, the party and the alliance's failures and weaknesses. 

Sources present at the meeting said that everyone agreed on one thing in the series of meetings that no election can be taken under the current Awami League government. There is no other alternative to an all-out movement for impartial elections. Although the party's policymakers have not taken any decision on whether to participate in the next parliamentary elections or not. Again, the position of the relationship with alliance partners Jamaat-e-Islami and Jatiya Oikyafront has not yet been determined. 

However, Nazrul Islam (Manju), BNP's Khulna Divisional Organizing Secretary and Khulna Metropolitan BNP President, considers the six-day meeting to be 'very positive'. He told Prothom Alo on Friday, "This is the first time in the last three years that BNP has sat down with its field-level leaders and is going to take a decision on what the party's politics will be in the future. This is very important. I think that BNP will come up with an effective and constructive idea by correcting the mistakes." 

The first phase was held from September 14 to 16, and the second phase from September 21 to 23 for six consecutive days. Out of the 584 members of the party's central executive committee, including members of the BNP Chairperson's Advisory Council, 525 were invited to these meetings. Of these, 457 attended the meeting. 281 spoke. The meeting was virtually presided over by the party's acting chairman Tarique Rahman. 

Party sources said that those who did not attend these meetings of the BNP executive committee, which were called after a long time, are being given show-cause notices by the party. It is known that 68 of the invited leaders were absent. 

BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir told Prothom Alo that the meeting has received a good response from the party and a positive situation has been created among the leaders and activists. He said that in the meeting, the leaders mainly gave their opinions and suggestions on the release of the BNP Chairperson, restoration of democracy and the prevailing political situation. Now, the policy-making council will review the issues and give directions on the future course of action. 

BNP sources said that the future political course of action will be determined after reviewing the opinions of the six-day meeting. Before that, BNP policymakers will sit with professionals and other political parties on the issue of restoring democracy, elections, voting rights and good governance. 

Political analyst and Dhaka University professor Asif Nazrul believes that BNP has not yet been able to build greater unity. Now if they can convince all the opposition parties that they are capable of providing good governance if they come to power, then they can build a greater unity and achieve success in the movement. However, the problem is that the BNP leader is in her residence under special arrangements. Awami League will use this as a trick. Besides, they will try to suppress the power that the current government has gained by establishing control over the state machinery. This is a big challenge for the BNP.

Headline_English: 'They are the ones who financially established Jamaat-BNP in Lakshmipur'
Content_Enlish:
‘They are the ones who financially established Jamaat-BNP in Lakshmipur! Everyone knows about their kinship with Jamaat. Why did Salah Uddin Tipu get naked without provocation?’ Syed Nurul Azim posted this on social media Facebook targeting Lakshmipur Sadar Upazila Parishad Chairman and District Jubo League President Salah Uddin. Nurul Azim is Lakshmipur District Jubo League leader and former General Secretary of District Chhatra League. 

Nurul Azim and several leaders and activists of Jubo League were waiting to greet the central leaders on the occasion of the extended meeting of Lakshmipur District Jubo League last Tuesday. At that time, an ambush attack occurred on them. 10 leaders and activists of Jubo League, including Nurul Azim, were injured in the attack. It was alleged that the attack was carried out by his followers led by District Jubo League President and Sadar Upazila Parishad Chairman AKM Salah Uddin. However, Salah Uddin denied the allegation after the incident. Salah Uddin is the son of Lakshmipur Municipality Mayor and former District Awami League General Secretary Abu Taher. 

Nurul Azim, who was beaten up on Tuesday, posted this status on Facebook on Saturday five days later. His status titled 'What wrong did I do? Why am I being attacked?' has created quite a discussion among local politicians. Many local leaders say that this is the first post by any leader against Taher's family in public. 

Nurul Azim was previously close to Taher's family. Mayor Taher's eldest son AHM Biplob was sentenced to death in the murder case of Lakshmipur District BNP Organizing Secretary and lawyer Nurul Islam. His sentence was later commuted. Nurul Azim also served time in prison in that case. He was known as Biplob's associate. Recently, when Nurul declared himself a possible candidate for the district Jubo League's general secretary, he had a dispute with Taher's family. 

Despite repeated attempts to contact Salahuddin regarding Nurul Azim's Facebook status, his statement could not be obtained. 

When asked, Nurul Azim told Prothom Alo on his mobile phone, "The central leaders have been informed about the attack. They have assured to look into the incident. No case has been filed for this. Besides, what will happen if we file a case against that family? I have given the status on Facebook to inform the new generation about the real incident."

Headline_English: "Fakhrul Saheb, you don't pay attention, you haven't read the New York Times."
Content_Enlish:
In response to BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir's statement that the Prime Minister's US visit has no achievements, Obaidul Quader said, "Fakhrul Saheb, you are not aware, you have not read the New York Times. Every speech of the Prime Minister, including the speech at the UN General Assembly, has been praised by world leaders." 

He said that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has asked to eliminate discrimination in the corona vaccine. She has asked to ensure vaccines for everyone. Fakhrul Saheb, haven't you heard this, have you seen the New York Times? It has been said that when talking about eliminating poverty, look at Bangladesh, look at Sheikh Hasina's development. 

Awami League General Secretary and Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader said this as the chief guest at a discussion meeting organized on the occasion of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's birthday today, Sunday. The discussion meeting was organized by the party's Relief and Social Welfare Sub-Committee at the Awami League central office. 

Obaidul Quader said, "The countries we know and love have done nothing for us to send the Rohingyas back," Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said bravely in her speech. Bangladesh has risen one step higher in the role of Prime Minister at the United Nations. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has risen even higher. And you, BNP, have fallen one step lower. 

Obaidul Quader says that if BNP wants to create chaos in the country by resorting to violence, we will give a crushing answer to the people. He said, "The BNP's series of meetings is a conspiracy. If there is that evil intention of inciting and burning again, then Awami League is ready to give a crushing answer to the people." 

The Awami League General Secretary said, the BNP's series of meetings is part of a conspiracy. It seems that there is that evil intention again. So remember, if they want to create chaos in the country by resorting to violence, if they want to disrupt Sheikh Hasina's development, then we are ready to give a crushing answer to the people. 

The Awami League General Secretary said, Sheikh Hasina stood in the procession of death and sang the song of life, and stood on the ruins and raised the flag of creation. Because she returned to the country, the trial of Bangabandhu's murder was held, and the war criminals were tried. 

In the discussion meeting chaired by Awami League Presidium Member Matia Chowdhury, Presidium Member Abdur Rahman, Joint General Secretaries Mahbub ul Alam Hanif and AFM Bahauddin Nasim, Organizing Secretary BM Mozammel Haque, among others, spoke. The discussion meeting was conducted by Awami League Relief and Social Welfare Sub-Committee Member Secretary and Relief and Social Welfare Secretary Sajit Roy Naddi.

Headline_English: Sheikh Hasina's history of struggle must be spread: Speaker
Content_Enlish:
Speaker Shirin Sharmin Chowdhury said that the history of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's life of struggle should be spread among the younger generation. 

The Speaker said these things today, Sunday, while speaking as the chief guest at the inauguration of an exhibition titled 'Bangladesh: An Era of Development' on the occasion of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's 75th birthday. 

The Canadian University of Bangladesh organized the exhibition at a hotel in Banani in the capital. This was informed in a press release. 

The Speaker said that in 1984, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, standing in front of the National Parliament, said that this parliament is the parliament of the people. Deep faith in democracy and the support of the masses is the main driving force of the Prime Minister's politics. Starting from her birth in Tungipara as a child, her educational life, marital life, family life, entry into politics, being the President of Bangladesh Awami League, serving as the Prime Minister for four terms, many research findings have been highlighted in the exhibition organized by the Canadian University of Bangladesh, which is very commendable. 

The Speaker said that after the brutal assassination of the Father of the Nation in 1975, an attempt was made to divert the history of this country and destroy the spirit of independence. The Prime Minister's return to his homeland on May 17, 1981, bearing the pain of losing his relatives, contained a message of Bangladesh's turnaround. Since then, a new dimension was added to politics, which is a new turning point in the history of Bangladesh. The people of Bengal stood by him, from which his path began. From there, the movement to establish democracy, the movement to establish the right to rice and voting, the struggle to end dictatorship, the struggle to establish human rights according to the constitution are truly amazing. 

Shirin Sharmin Chowdhury said, 'Under the leadership of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh is a wonder of development for the whole world. The construction of the Padma Bridge with its own funding has amazed the world. She has established Bangladesh as a nation strong in self-power in the eyes of the world. The independent and sovereign Bangladesh that we got under the leadership of the Father of the Nation, Sheikh Hasina, his worthy daughter, has taken the country from the ranks of a least developed country to the ranks of a developing country.' He said that Sheikh Hasina, like her father, deeply loves the people of this country, and the Prime Minister is working tirelessly to realize the unfulfilled dream of Bangabandhu to bring smiles to the faces of the suffering people. Under her able leadership, a hunger-poverty-free, developed digital Bangladesh, as dreamed by Bangabandhu, will be established. 

The program was presided over by Chowdhury Nafiz Sarafat, founder and chairman of the Canadian University of Bangladesh, and Zahid Ahsan Russell, State Minister for Youth and Sports, spoke as a special guest. 

Canadian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Benoit Prefontaine was the guest of honor at the program, and Mohammad A. Arafat, Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Canadian University of Bangladesh, delivered the opening speech. Dignitaries, officials and employees of the university, and media personnel were present.

Headline_English: Voting in 848 UPs in the second phase will be held on November 11
Content_Enlish:
In the second phase, the country's 848 Union Parishads (UPs) will go to polls on November 11. After the election schedule was finalized in the Election Commission meeting on Wednesday, Commission Secretary Md. Humayun Kabir Khandaker announced the election schedule. 
According to the announced schedule, the last date for submitting nomination papers to the returning officer for the posts of chairman, general member and reserved women member is October 17. The selection of nomination papers will be on October 20 and the last date for withdrawal is October 26. The voting will be held on November 11. 

This morning, the Commission meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner KM Nurul Huda finalized the dates for the Sirajganj-6 constituency by-election and the 10 municipal elections of the seventh phase. The elections will be held on November 2. 

Later, the EC Secretary briefed reporters at the Election Bhaban. EC Additional Secretary Ashok Kumar Debnath, NID Wing DG AKM Humayun Kabir, EC Joint Secretaries Farhad Ahmed Khan and SM Asaduzzaman were present. 

According to the announced schedule, the last date for submitting nomination papers to the returning officer in Sirajganj is October 10. The last date for selecting nomination papers is October 11 and the last date for withdrawal is October 17. Voting will be held on November 2. 

And the last date for submitting nomination papers in 10 municipalities is October 8. The last date for selecting nomination papers is October 11 and the last date for withdrawal is October 17. Voting will be held on November 2. 

Voting will be held on EVMs in Sirajganj, 10 municipalities and 20 UPs. Voting will be held on ballot papers in the rest. 

Although the chairman post will be held on the party symbol, the UP will be held on the independent symbol for the membership post.

Headline_English: Sayeed Khokon gave sensational information about August 21: Rizvi
Content_Enlish:
BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said that Saeed Khokon, son of former Dhaka Mayor Mohammad Hanif, has given a sensational information about the August 21 grenade attack. Before the incident, he (Saeed Khokon) had informed the then opposition leader at her house that an attack could happen on August 21. But why she did not take the matter into account is a big question. 
Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said this in response to a question from journalists at the Dhaka Journalists Union (Ekan) office on Saturday afternoon. 

Rizvi said, 'We have already heard a lot about August 21. But yesterday (Friday), Saeed Khokon, son of former Dhaka Mayor Mohammad Hanif, who was also a mayor, gave a sensational information that his father told him about the August 21 grenade attack, that an attack could happen, an incident could happen. You go and inform the leader. Accordingly, Sayeed Khokon told the leader, you have to be careful. Because there may be an attack at your home or on the way to work.’ 

This BNP leader said, ‘Yesterday we came to know that today’s Prime Minister, even after informing the then opposition leader about such information, after hearing everything, she was not very alert or serious about it. Instead of being serious, she said, you can’t do politics if you are so afraid.’ 

Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said, ‘The leader did not take the matter into any consideration, did not care. It is a big question for us that why she did not take the matter into consideration.’ 

Referring to the August 21 grenade attack case, Rizvi said, the previous government of 1-11, which was the fruit of this government’s movement regarding this attack case, could not, did not, put the name of our party’s current acting chairman in the charge sheet. They also investigated, the CID investigated. After the current government came to power, they appointed an investigation officer and investigated the man who made the poster for the Awami League election and included Tarique Rahman's name. 

The BNP leader said, "It is clear that this is completely planned and purposeful. In other words, it seems that it was planned to create a blame game, which is further proven by the incident that happened and what Khokon said yesterday. He said, "Those who are involved in these incidents, who have committed this hellish incident or such a terrorist incident, we strongly condemn it and have condemned it in the past. We never support such bloody violent incidents." 

Rizvi believes that the purpose of involving BNP in the August 21 grenade attack case is to eliminate the nationalist force. According to him, it was arranged and planned. 

Referring to the incident of locking the office of Dhaka University teacher Asif Nazrul, the BNP senior joint secretary general said, the situation is descending into a dark anarchy day by day. Dhaka University teacher Asif Nazrul is known to all for his independent voice. His office is being locked and vandalized just for expressing his views freely. A terrible reign of hooliganism has been created.

Headline_English: Voting for the by-election of Sylhet-3 constituency will be held on September 4.
Content_Enlish:
The by-election for Sylhet-3 constituency will be held on September 4. The decision was made at the Election Commission meeting today, Monday. After the meeting, Election Commission Secretary Humayun Kabir Khondoker told reporters. 

Although it has been decided to hold voting in the postponed parliamentary constituency, no decision has been finalized regarding the local government elections, including the Union Parishad (UP). 

The by-election for Sylhet-3 constituency was scheduled to be held on July 28. The voting was postponed a day before the election by a court order. 

The EC Secretary also said that the Sylhet-3 by-election must be held by September 7. For this, the EC has rescheduled the date of the September 4 by-election. 

In June last year, 204 UP elections were held in the first phase. Due to Corona, the elections of 167 UPs were postponed in the first phase. 

The EC Secretary said that it has been decided to hold other pending elections including Narayanganj City Corporation, Municipality, UP, District Council by December, along with these UPs. This issue will be discussed in the Commission meeting in the first week of September.

Headline_English: 'This is their domestic dispute, Awami administration versus Awami League'
Content_Enlish:
BNP National Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy has said that the politics of the administration has become stronger than the politics of the field of the Awami League. He said this while speaking as the chief guest at a discussion meeting on the occasion of the 41st founding anniversary of the Bangladesh Nationalist Volunteer Party at the National Press Club on Monday. 
Gayeshwar Chandra Roy said, "We don't need to talk so much about the Barisal issue. This is their domestic turmoil. I won't say it's the administration, Awami administration versus Awami League. This is a domestic matter. We have no lessons to learn from this. Awami League politics in the administration is now stronger than the politics of the field of the Awami League. If there is any atonement to be made for this, they will do it, the bureaucrats will not." 

Addressing the senior leaders of the Awami League, Gayeshwar Chandra Roy said, "The Awami League is busy day and night with the organization, it is necessary. However, to show how much strength you have achieved as an organization, come to the streets and hold programs. This will provide hope and courage among the workers. If you stay at home once, you will not get used to leaving your house. 

Gayeshwar Chandra said, the government does not grant bail to the death row convicts but Khaleda Zia. Under which law is the government not granting bail to Khaleda Zia? The people want to know. Instead of dying of COVID-19 at home, we should write our names in the pages of history by protesting on the streets. Khaleda Zia must be freed for the liberation of democracy. The court cannot grant the liberation of democracy. 
BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi spoke as a special guest under the chairmanship of Bangladesh Nationalist Volunteer Party Acting President Mostafizur Rahman. 

At the meeting, Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said, “We are surprised to see the conflict between the Awami League and the administration. The officials of this administration are stronger than the Awami League today. The administration officials are saying, “We gave guns not to keep bullets in our pockets.” The government is responsible for this outcome. There is no room for sympathy. Today, there is no one in their party to tell the truth. You are being attacked, and you are not speaking out. This situation cannot continue.' 

Regarding the country's corona, this leader said, 'Awami League is doing politics of confusion about corona. The Health Minister is saying like a fool that the corona situation is normal. The news is coming, there is no medical equipment in hospitals. People are dying every day. The government is completely failing to deal with corona.' 

The meeting was moderated by the organization's central general secretary Abdul Qadir Bhuiyan. Leaders and activists of BNP and its affiliated organizations participated in the meeting.

Headline_English: Ivy Rahman was declared dead soon after Khaleda Zia came to see him: Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that Awami League leader Ivy Rahman, who was injured in a grenade attack on August 21, was declared dead after then Prime Minister Khaleda Zia visited her at the CMH. 

Ivy Rahman, former Awami League women's affairs secretary and wife of late President Zillur Rahman, was seriously injured in a grenade attack on an Awami League anti-terrorism rally on Bangabandhu Avenue on August 21, 2004. She died three days later while undergoing treatment at the Combined Military Hospital in Dhaka. Today is the 17th death anniversary of Ivy Rahman. 

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina made these remarks while speaking at the Executive Committee meeting of the National Economic Council in the morning, a BSS report said. The Prime Minister participated in the ECNEC meeting held at the NEC Conference Center in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar through video conference from Ganabhaban. 

Sheikh Hasina said, "Today, I am thinking more about my aunt Ivy." Another surprising incident that you may not know is that when he was taken to CMH, we don't know exactly when and at what moment he died. His children were with him. At that time, the then Prime Minister Khaleda Zia said that she would go to see him, so she locked his children who were near the bed in a room. Nazmul Hasan Papon, sister Tania, and Maina were all locked in a room for about three to four hours, after which Khaleda Zia went to see Ivy Rahman. And when Khaleda Zia returned to see him, he was declared dead immediately. Many people don't know this, I have told you how great atrocities they can do!' 

Recalling the horrific incident of the grenade attack, he said, not only the attempted murder, but also the actions they took with the bodies after the murder are beyond words. They did not want to give the bodies of many people after death. They did not give the bodies to their relatives. 

The Prime Minister said that since the party supporters and those who were alive went to Dhaka Medical College to help and after their efforts all night, they handed over the bodies one by one. They did not even want to give the body. If they could, they would have disappeared the body—this was the situation. 

Stating that the injured in the attack have been standing by their side with their benefits and disadvantages, including treatment at home and abroad, Sheikh Hasina said, many of them are no more today, they have died. Many are crippled and living a miserable life. 

The Head of Government said, ‘We have provided assistance to the injured from the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust and from the funds that came from a separate account opened at that time, we have provided financial assistance to everyone undergoing treatment and we are still providing it. On behalf of the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust, we are providing assistance to those injured who need treatment. We are providing food, I am still providing all kinds of assistance to their children for their education, marriage, etc. Those who were in very bad condition, their financial assistance is still continuing.’ 

The Prime Minister sought the prayers of the countrymen for all, including Ivy Rahman, who was killed in the grenade attack on August 21. 

On August 21, 2004, more than a dozen grenades were hurled at the Awami League’s anti-terrorism rally on Bangabandhu Avenue with the aim of killing Awami League President and then Opposition Leader Sheikh Hasina. Sheikh Hasina narrowly escaped death in the attack, but her hearing was damaged. 22 Awami League leaders and workers, including Ivy Rahman, were killed and at least 500 leaders and workers, passersby and journalists were injured.

Headline_English: Those who call Khaleda a freedom fighter should be sent to a mental institution: Justice Shamsuddin
Content_Enlish:
Retired Supreme Court Justice HM Shamsuddin Chowdhury has said that the nation is being misled by calling BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia a freedom fighter. He has called for those who make such statements to be sent to the mental hospital. 

Participating in a human chain in Dhaka on Friday, Justice HM Shamsuddin Chowdhury called BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir a 'son of a king'. He said, 'Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has discovered whether Khaleda Zia is a freedom fighter. Such lunatics, such lunatics, who are misleading the nation by saying such crazy things, should be sent directly to the mental hospital. Otherwise, the nation will be misled.' 

In recent speeches at several events, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has called Khaleda Zia the country's first female freedom fighter and her eldest son Tarique Rahman a child freedom fighter. Awami League leaders have criticized his statement. 

In response, Mirza Fakhrul said at a meeting in Thakurgaon on Thursday, 'When martyred President Ziaur Rahman declared independence in 1971, Khaleda Zia was at the Cantonment (military base) with her two young sons Tarique Rahman and Arafat Rahman. At that time, the soldiers of the 8th Bengal came and said, "The Pakistani soldiers are asking us to surrender our weapons. Should we surrender our weapons or not?" She said that day, "You will not surrender any weapons without the orders of your commander Major Zia." This war started from that day.' 

However, rejecting this statement of the BNP Secretary General, HM Shamsuddin Chowdhury, advisor to the Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee of 1971, said, 'Making Khaleda Zia a freedom fighter means making Rao Farman Ali and Niazi freedom fighters. Those who are doing this ridiculous, this madness, have no place in this society.’ 

Justice Shamsuddin Chowdhury spoke at a human chain organized in the area demanding the removal of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman’s grave from Chandrima Udyan. The human chain was organized by relatives of army and air force members who were executed for mutiny during the regime of then President Ziaur Rahman in the October 2, 1977 incident of hijacking a Japanese plane in Dhaka. 

Speaking at the human chain, Shamsuddin Chowdhury said, ‘Today we have gathered here in support of those who lost their husbands, fathers and brothers. In those days of 1977, the murderer Ziaur Rahman killed hundreds of freedom fighters in the name of a farce of justice. The trial of the freedom fighters who were murdered by the murderer Zia after the hijacking of the Japanese Airlines plane was not a trial in any sense of the law.’ 

The former Supreme Court judge said that none of the legal requirements were followed. They were not given any opportunity to defend themselves. Even the hanging was carried out first. The verdict was given later. What is more sad is that the bodies of those who were hanged were either floated in the river or burned without being handed over to their relatives. This is the work of Zia, who was a more ruthless person than Genghis Khan, Timur Long, and Nadir Shah in history. But Zia killed those who were barricading the road after the declaration of Bangladesh’s independence. That is why Zia is also a ‘war criminal’. 

Demanding a posthumous trial of Ziaur Rahman, Shamsuddin Chowdhury said, "We all demand that a law be made for Zia's posthumous trial. There is no obstacle in our constitution to make such a law. Not only Zia, but all those who carried out such illegal killings should be tried by making a law. Our Law Minister has said that a strong investigation committee should be formed in this regard. An investigation commission should be formed without delay and a law should be made for posthumous trial." 

Describing Zia as a "murderer and war criminal," Shamsuddin Chowdhury said, "A murderer, a war criminal's symbolic grave cannot be near this parliament. We know that the body of the murderer Zia is not here. They have arranged a symbolic grave. It must be demolished and this must be done immediately." 

Sergeant Abul Bashar Khan's daughter Bilkis Chowdhury said in the human chain, "My father was brutally murdered. Even today I don't know where my father's grave is. The murderer Zia unjustly killed my father. We want to know where my father's grave is. I was four years old at the time. I have seen my mother cry all my life. My mother is still crying. But this murder has not been tried.' 

Former Army Chief Lieutenant General (Retd.) Harun-ur-Rashid said, in the Japanese plane hijacking incident, some soldiers and officers were arrested and killed in the name of rebellion. They were killed without trial. The few trials that were held were farce. It also happened that the trial gave a verdict to hang him. But the death sentence has already been implemented. All those standing here today have lost relatives. They have come here to seek justice for the murder of their relatives. It is urgent that this genocide be tried immediately. 

Corporal Mubarak Ali's daughter Mumtaz Begum said, when her father was hanged, he was only six months old. There are no words to describe how difficult it was for him to grow up after that. His mother got married elsewhere. At that time, he couldn't even eat rice to his full stomach.

Headline_English: Does BNP want the right to burn cars and people's property?
Content_Enlish:
Information and Broadcasting Minister and Awami League Joint General Secretary Hasan Mahmud has questioned whether the BNP wants the right to burn cars and people's property freely.
