Hasan Mahmud said this in response to questions from journalists after the opening ceremony of the full-length film 'Dampara', which is based on the heroic story of the then police superintendent of Chittagong, Shamsul Haque, who was martyred during the Liberation War. 

The Information Minister said, 'BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been criticizing the government once in the morning, once in the afternoon, and sometimes in the evening. Their leaders are going around the country holding protests against the government. What more do they want than political freedom? Do they want the right to burn cars and people's property freely? They want to block people by calling hartals day after day, which they did in 2013, 14 and 15, which the people rejected. 

Chittagong Metropolitan Police Commissioner Saleh Mohammad Tanvir presided over the program at the multipurpose hall of Dampara Police Lines in Chittagong. Under the direction of Deputy Police Commissioner Bijoy Basak, DIG of Chittagong Range Anwar Hossain, hero of the film 'Dampara' Ferdous Khan, heroine Ashna Habib Bhabna, dialogue writer of the film Anon Zaman, director Shuddhman Chaitan, Shaheed Shamsul Haque's wife Mahmuda Haque Chowdhury and others spoke as special guests. 

At that time, in response to a question from journalists, Hasan Mahmud said, 'If the BNP wants Khaleda Zia's release on the streets, then why did they appeal to the government to send her abroad. They should avoid this hypocrisy. Despite being accused in the case of burning cars and ordering people to throw bombs while holding them hostage, the kind of political freedom they are enjoying, and the political vendetta against the government and the Awami League, there is a question as to whether they could have done so much in any other country.’ 

The Information and Broadcasting Minister further said that Khaleda Zia is a convicted convict. The Prime Minister has shown great kindness by suspending her sentence and keeping her free and she is taking medical care as she should, i.e. under the supervision of her family and party. She is not taking medical care under the government. So if there is any damage to Khaleda Zia’s health now, the BNP and her family doctors and those who are providing her with healthcare will be responsible for it. 

Earlier, at the Maharat program, Hasan Mahmud said that the Dampara place is a historical place. In 1930, the Chittagong Armory was here. Masterda Surya Sen looted this armory with his revolutionary army and kept the Chittagong region free from the British Empire for 11 days. But not everyone knows that history. 

Hasan Mahmud further said that there is a contrast between the events of 1930 in Dampara and the events of 1971. That contrast is that in 1930, weapons had to be looted from here. By looting weapons, the revolutionaries rebelled against the British and were able to keep the Chittagong region independent for 11 days. On the other hand, there was no looting in 1971. Rather, the keeper of the armory, Superintendent of Police Shamsul Haque, distributed the weapons to the brave freedom fighters.

Headline_English: AL loses 3 out of 6 UPs in Kaunia
Content_Enlish:
In the six Union Parishad (UP) elections in Kaunia Upazila of Rangpur, boat candidates have been defeated in three of the six Union Parishad (UP) elections. Out of the remaining three, Awami League rebel candidates have won in two. An independent BNP candidate has won in one. Upazila Election Officer Sumiyara Parveen announced the results on Sunday night. 

According to the Upazila Election Office and local sources, the winning Awami League candidates in the three UPs are Ansar Ali in Balapara Union, Ashraful Islam in Sarai Union and Abdul Hannan in Shahidbag Union. The two winning Awami League rebel candidates are Rashedul Islam in Tepamadhupur Union and Abdul Majid in Kursha Union. In addition, BNP independent candidate Raju Ahmed has won in Haragach Union. 

After winning, Rashedul Islam, the expelled general secretary of Tepamadhupur Union Awami League, said, "They elected me because the people of the area love me." I am grateful to the people for this.’ 

The Kaunia Upazila Election Officer said, the UP election was completed peacefully yesterday. No untoward incident took place anywhere.

Headline_English: MP Harun alleges that people from the boat occupied the center and entered the booth secretly
Content_Enlish:
BNP MP from Chapainawabganj-3 (Sadar) constituency Harunur Rashid has alleged irregularities in the Chapainawabganj municipality election. He said that people are being brought in from outside to occupy the center and keep people in the secret rooms of the booths and vote on boats. It is a joke in the name of voting. 

The MP made these allegations at a press conference at his residence in Pathanpara Mohalla of Chapainawabganj city at 11 am today, Tuesday. Voting for this municipality election began this morning. 

Harunur Rashid said, 'I have called the Home Minister, Chief Election Commissioner, Rajshahi DIG of Police and Superintendent of Police at least 10 times since morning regarding the irregularities in the vote. But they did not pick up the phone. I complained to the returning officer. But the situation has not improved. The police have not taken even the minimum measures.' 

The MP also said, 'There will be no elections in Bangladesh under this government in the future. It is not possible to implement this election. I think the government is leading the country towards a civil war environment through these local elections. 

Independent candidate (BNP) Nazrul Islam, Sadar Upazila Parishad Chairman Tasiqul Islam and others also spoke at the press conference. 

Allegations of agents being thrown out 
Voting in the Chapainawabganj Municipality election began at 8 am today. There were four candidates for the post of mayor. Among them, Awami League candidate Moklesur Rahman, the party's rebel candidate Samiul Haque and BNP leader Nazrul Islam are contesting as independents. 

Awami League rebel candidate Samiul Haque told Prothom Alo on his mobile phone at around 11:15 am, 'I have visited 20 centers since morning, including Alinagar High School, Nawabganj High School, Nayagola High School, Vocational Training Institute, Haluabandha Government Primary School, Ajaipur Government Primary School. Our agents have been thrown out of all the centers. Voting is being done by occupying the center and standing in a secret room at the boat mark. 

Around 10 am, a person was seen standing in front of a room at the Namoshankarbati High School center in the secret room for voting. At that time, a police officer on duty stopped him when he tried to take a picture. Presiding Officer Shahidul Islam said that no one is supposed to be in the secret room. He took this reporter to another polling station. There too, a young man was seen in the secret room from near the door. Introducing himself as Sohel Rana, he said that he was showing the voting process. He did not give any answer as to who sent him here. 

When asked about the young man, Presiding Officer Shahidul Islam did not comment. 

Earlier, at 7 am, about fifty young men were seen leaving the city's Nawabganj Government College. They were seen boarding a bus owned by Grameen Travels, owned by Boat candidate Mokhlesur Rahman. At this time, we spoke to two people named Abdul Awal and Abdul Halim. Introducing himself as a Chhatra League leader, Abdul Halim said, "We have come from Nachol. We spent the night in the hostel of Nawabganj Government College. Now we will go to different centers by bus." 

In this regard, around 1:30 pm, Boat candidate Mokhlesur Rahman said, "My people did not occupy any polling station. There is no evidence of voting from secret rooms. This is propaganda by the opposition." 

Regarding the allegations of voting with the Boat symbol from secret rooms, Returning Officer Motawakkil Rahman said, "I have received complaints of influencing voters from outside five polling stations. But I have not received any complaints that people are voting from secret rooms. I have informed the police and RAB about the allegations of influencing voters outside the polling stations. They have taken action."

Headline_English: Elections are the same across the country, why are they different in Bhangra? This is the question on my mind.
Content_Enlish:
In the 15 Union Parishad (UP) elections in Bhanga and Charbhadrasan upazilas of Faridpur, Awami League candidates have won one. Out of the remaining 14, two BNP-backed candidates and the other 12 candidates supported by local independent MP Mujibur Rahman Chowdhury alias Nixon Chowdhury have won. Prothom Alo spoke to Faridpur District Awami League President Subal Chandra Saha about the defeat of the ruling party's candidates. 

Question: Prothom Alo: What is the reason for the defeat of Awami League candidates? 

Subal Chandra Saha: Awami League rebels and BNP independent candidates have won in Bhanga and Charbhadrasan. We had nothing to do with the BNP candidates. There is no Awami League party MP in Faridpur-4 (Bhanga, Charbhadrasan and Sadarpur) constituency. This has become a problem for us. In addition, many leaders of our party and allied organizations have openly and secretly opposed our candidate. We will inform the center about everything. In Charbhadrasan, Md. Despite being elected as the General Secretary of the Kawsar Upazila Awami League and the Chairman of the Upazila Parishad as the Awami League nominated candidate, he opposed the party candidate. The center has recommended that he be permanently expelled from the party. The candidates have lost by a large margin due to the opposition of Awami League leaders and workers. 

Question: Prothom Alo: After the defeat of the Awami League candidates, it is being said from various quarters that party presidium member Kazi Zafar Ullah has given the nomination in sole power. Candidates were not selected systematically, many ineligible people were given party nominations... 

Subal Chandra Saha: The party candidate selection was done systematically. Candidates were selected after scrutiny and selection by holding extended meetings in Bhanga and Charbhadrasan upazilas. The Upazila President-General Secretary verified and sent them to us. We signed and sent them to the center after scrutiny. We have not heard anything objectionable about them before. 

Question: Prothom Alo: Awami League candidates lost in opposition to Faridpur-4 MP Nixon Chowdhury—the defeated and local Awami League leaders are saying this. What is your statement on this? 
Subal Chandra Saha: I do not want to comment directly on this. However, Awami League supporters and BNP supporters came together to defeat Awami League candidates. A force worked in a planned manner so that the boat candidate could not win in any way. If there had been a fair election, we would have undoubtedly won. Our party candidates, leaders, workers and supporters were cornered due to the activities of some quarters. 

Question: Prothom Alo: What was the election environment like? Were there any irregularities in the election? 
Subal Chandra Saha: Awami League Presidium member Kazi Jafar Ullah or Awami League candidates did not lose in the Bhanga-Charbhadrasan elections, they were defeated. The way rebels lost all over the country in the UP elections, it did not happen in Bhanga. The whole country had one type of election, why was it different in Bhanga—this is the question in my mind. If the election had been conducted properly, if the party leaders had been more active, we would not have had such a disastrous result. Our leaders and workers could not work smoothly in the election field. 

Question: Prothom Alo: The election field was not smooth—on what basis are you saying this? 
Subal Chandra Saha: I think the administration should have done more. It needed to be more active. We have tried a lot to make the administration active. In the Gazirat election, there was a delay in counting the votes and announcing the results. I have informed the DC, SP and Kazi Zafar Ullah about the matter. 

Question: Prothom Alo: Bhanga is known as an Awami League base. Won't Awami League politics in that area become difficult in the coming days due to such election results? 
Subal Chandra Saha: We have to organize our party well. We have to sort it like a comb. Action must be taken against those who worked against the party. National elections are ahead. Therefore, we have to proceed with great caution. At the same time, we have to remove those who have created confusion in their minds from that path. We are optimistic that we will be victorious in the coming days.

Headline_English: Jamalpur UP election candidate dismissed from party for being 'rebel'
Content_Enlish:
Saiful Islam Khan has been suspended from the Jubo League for being a 'rebel' candidate of the Awami League for the post of chairman in the Kendua Union Parishad (UP) elections in Jamalpur Sadar Upazila. This information was given in a press release signed by the acting president of the district Jubo League Md. Ershad Hossain and acting general secretary Rashedul Islam on Thursday afternoon. 

Saiful Islam Khan was the general secretary of the Jamalpur Sadar Upazila Jubo League. He participated in the election as a rebel candidate for the post of chairman in Kendua Union. 

Party sources said that both Saiful Islam Khan and Sheikh Mahbubur Rahman were seeking party nomination for the post of chairman in Kendua UP. However, in the end, the party nominated Sheikh Mahbubur Rahman. Later, Saiful Islam Khan announced that he would participate in the election as a rebel candidate. He has been temporarily suspended from the Jubo League, accusing him of violating party discipline. 

However, Saiful Islam Khan told Prothom Alo, 'I have not received any letter to suspend me from the party. I did not break party discipline. I am not a rebel candidate. I participated in the election as an independent candidate to protect the love of the people. I did not go against the boat. I participated in the election against an intruder.' He claimed that all the people of that union are with him. 

When asked about this, the acting president of the district Jubo League, Md. Ershad Hossain, told Prothom Alo that Saiful Islam Khan has been temporarily relieved from the post of general secretary of Sadar Upazila Jubo League due to participating in the UP election against the boat symbol by breaking party discipline. He will receive the discharge letter soon.

Headline_English: Expelled at night, asked for votes the next day on a boat
Content_Enlish:
A 'rebel' candidate in Raiganj, Sirajganj has gone in favor of the boat. And in Shibganj, Bogra, there have been four incidents of violence surrounding the election. 
Even on the last day of withdrawal of nomination papers, Ajmal Hossain of Chandaikona, Raiganj, Sirajganj, had decided to participate in the election as an independent candidate (rebel of the Awami League). The symbol was also allotted the next day. When he was expelled from the party that night on charges of violating party discipline, he changed his decision to contest the election and announced that he would work for the boat candidate. 

Ajmal Hossain was the vice-president of Chandaikona Union Awami League. He was expelled last Wednesday night. Ajmal Hossain appeared at the Chandaikona Union Awami League office around 11 am on Thursday. At that time, he announced the withdrawal of his candidacy and said that he would work for the boat in support of the Awami League's nominated candidate. Awami League candidate Abdul Hannan Khan, former organizing secretary of the upazila Awami League Shafiqul Islam Talukder and others were present at the time. 

* 11 election offices were vandalized in Bihar and Majhihatta unions of Shibganj. * 10 people were injured in a clash between Awami League and JPA supporters in Kichak union. 
In this regard, Upazila Awami League General Secretary Abul Kalam Azad said that a decision will be taken later on the withdrawal of his (Ajmal) candidacy. 

Violence surrounding the election: Meanwhile, four separate incidents of violence have already occurred in four unions of Shibganj upazila of Bogra around the election. Election offices have been attacked and vandalized. A case has been filed against the supporters of the boat candidate in these incidents. 

On Wednesday night, the rival candidates alleged that the workers and supporters of the boat candidate were attacked in Bihar and Majhihatta unions and at least 11 election offices were vandalized. After the allocation of symbols in Bihar UP, boat supporters attacked the election office and workers and supporters of 'rebel' candidate Matiur Rahman. The attack took place in the Biharbandar area of ​​the union at around 8 pm. The attack was alleged to have vandalized the election office as well as eight motorcycles. Later on Wednesday night, Matiur Rahman filed a case with Shibganj Police Station accusing 14 boat workers. The current chairman of the boat candidate in this union is Mohidul Islam. 

On October 13, workers of the Awami League candidate clashed with the workers of the rebel candidate. Then the party's candidate Mohidul Islam filed a case with Shibganj Police Station alleging attack and attempted murder during the election procession. 

Meanwhile, in Majhihatta union of the upazila, workers of two candidates supported by Awami League and BNP joined hands to attack and vandalize 10 election offices of an independent candidate. These incidents took place in different areas of the union at around 8 pm on Wednesday. Supporters of independent candidate Eskender Ali (autorickshaw) held a protest rally at Majhihatta Bazar that night in protest of the attack. 

Regarding the allegations, Boat candidate Abdul Gafur said on his mobile phone that autorickshaw workers had instigated an attack on the Boat office in the Bharanhar and Bhanjira areas of the union. His workers also attacked in return. 

On October 26, 10 people were injured in a clash between supporters of Boat candidate ABM Nazmul Qadir Shahjahan Chowdhury and Jatiya Party (JPA) Jamirul Islam in Sonarpara of Kichak Union. The two candidates filed counter-complaints at the police station in this incident. In addition, violence also broke out between supporters of the two rival candidates in Khayrapukur Bazar of Pirab Union on Wednesday. Later, the police went to control the situation.

Headline_English: Attack on independent and rebel candidate's house in Madaripur, 15 injured including woman
Content_Enlish:
There have been allegations of attacks and vandalism at the houses of independent candidate Hafizur Rahman in Alinagar Union of Kalkini Upazila of Madaripur and rebel Awami League candidate Sirajul Haque in Shikarmangal Union. These attacks took place on Thursday night. At least 15 people, including relatives of the two candidates, were injured in the attack. 

Local sources have learned that Awami League nominated candidate Shahid Parvez held an election discussion meeting in front of the Alinagar Union Parishad at around 8:30 pm yesterday. Meanwhile, the current chairman and independent candidate in this election, Hafizur Rahman, was heading towards his house in his personal car passing the UP building. 

10 motorcycles in front of the house of independent candidate Hafizur in Alinagar Union Parishad elections in Kalkini Upazila were vandalized 
10 motorcycles in front of the house of independent candidate Hafizur in Alinagar Union Parishad elections in Kalkini Upazila were vandalized Photo: Prothom Alo 
Hafizur Rahman alleged that Shahid Parvez's workers and supporters got excited after seeing him. Later, they carried out a surprise attack on his (Hafizur) house and the house of his brother Soharab Hossain by practicing with local weapons. 

The attackers threw bricks and caused extensive vandalism to the doors and windows of the house, Hafizur's 1 personal car and 10 motorcycles in front of his house. At that time, eight people, including his relatives and workers, were injured when they tried to stop the attackers. Meanwhile, a team of Kalkini Police Station and RAB-8 visited the scene at around 9:30 pm after receiving information about the attack and vandalism. 

The attackers also vandalized Hafizur's personal car 
The attackers also vandalized Hafizur's personal car Photo: Prothom Alo 
Hafizur Rahman told Prothom Alo that he had already informed the administration in writing about such attacks and vandalism. But they also did not take any action. Such attacks and vandalism by setting up an election camp for a boat candidate right in front of his house is a shameful incident. He claimed that the boat candidate and his people were attacking him and pressuring him to withdraw from the election. 

When asked about the allegations, Shahid Parvez said, "My election camp is in front of the Union Parishad. First, the people of the independent candidate attacked my camp to evict it. Later, to escape the attack, they vandalized their own houses, cars and motorcycles and are blaming us." 

Attack on rebel candidate's house in Shikarmangal 

Meanwhile, it has been alleged that Awami League candidate Sirajul Alam Mridha, his two sons and supporters attacked the house of rebel Awami League candidate Sirajul Haque in Shikarmangal Union at around 6:30 pm yesterday. 

According to local sources, Sirajul Alam Mridha organized an election road meeting at Bahadurpur Government Primary School grounds in North Charfat yesterday evening. The house of 'rebel' candidate Sirajul Haque is just 100 meters south of the meeting venue. 

Sirajul Haque said that Sirajul Alam Mridha, his two sons and several hundred workers and supporters took part in the attack on his house. His elder brother, freedom fighter Harun Or Rashid, sister Murshida Begum, younger brother Monir Mal and seven other family members were injured in the attack. Later, local people rescued the injured and admitted them to the Kalkini Upazila Health Complex. 

Sirajul Haque complained to Prothom Alo, saying, "I filed a written complaint with the Returning Officer last Tuesday regarding the threat to me and the campaigning of the Awami League candidate in violation of the election code of conduct. But to no avail. On the contrary, they entered my house and started a riot. Sirajul Alam will do whatever he wants just because he got a boat! What kind of behavior is this!" 

Denying the accusation of attacking the rebel candidate's house, Sirajul Alam Mridha told Prothom Alo that none of his leaders and workers attacked the rebel candidate's house. Those who are making these allegations are saying this to take advantage of the election. 

In this regard, Kalkini Police Station Officer-in-Charge Istiak Ashfaq said, "The police took quick action after the two incidents. Both parties here are Awami League workers and supporters. Both parties affected by the attack have been asked to file a complaint with the police station. No one has filed a written complaint till 10 am today, Friday. If they file a complaint, a case will be filed."

Headline_English: Awami League's demand for fair elections 'Ram name in the face of ghosts': Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has described the ruling Awami League's demand for fair elections as 'Ram's name in the mouth of a ghost'. He made this comment while quoting a statement by Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader as the chief guest at a human chain organized by the Volunteer Party in front of the National Press Club on Friday. The human chain was organized by the Volunteer Party to protest the rise in commodity prices. 

Mirza Fakhrul said that the Awami League General Secretary said yesterday, 'Our Prime Minister wants a fair election to be held in the country. He wants to see free and fair elections. He (the Prime Minister) also wants to see that everyone can vote.' This is Ram's name in the mouth of a ghost. 

Mirza Fakhrul also commented that the Awami League has destroyed the entire electoral system. He said, they have destroyed three elections. They have destroyed the entire electoral system. Now such a situation has arisen that the MP from Shariatpur has said, ‘I will decide who will be the chairman and who will be the member.’ 

Fakhrul further said, ‘The democracy we fought for in 1971 has been completely thrown into the Bay of Bengal. They have now established a one-party state. No one will be able to remain in the field due to the violence of their leaders and leaders.’ 

Says that the Awami League cannot tolerate dissent, the BNP Secretary General said, ‘They cannot tolerate criticism. They have no tolerance.’ 

The Awami League is systematically destroying communal harmony. We recently held a meeting in front of the party office in protest against this. When the boys were returning after the meeting, the police attacked them from behind and beat them with sticks. They even filed a case against the leaders and workers. Why are they so afraid? Because they have no ground under their feet. The day the people take to the streets, they will not find a way to escape. 

To the police and administration, Mirza Fakhrul said, "You should not torture the people like this for an extremely corrupt, extremely oppressive, anti-state party. This government has taken a stand against the state and the people. The Awami League government is filling its own pockets by cutting into the pockets of the people. Thousands of people are getting poorer and poorer." 

To the leaders, activists and youth of the Swechchhasebak Dal, Mirza Fakhrul said, "I will call on you to organize now. We must build a strong movement against this government with the people. Through national unity, we can unite all political parties and opinions to overthrow this government and establish a people's government. We definitely want elections. However, the elections must be held under a neutral government. Only then will we go to the elections, not otherwise." 

Regarding the rise in commodity prices, Mirza Fakhrul said, "The prices of any item in the daily necessities market are not under the control of the common man. The common man cannot eat well now. Who eats? Awami League people. You will notice that the prices of goods are increasing at a rapid pace. There is a syndicate here. They increase the prices as they wish. At the same time, the leaders and cadres of Awami League are collecting tolls and extortions. Tolls are being collected from the vegetables that are coming from North Bengal or East Bengal on the road. Now such a situation has arisen that the people of the country are holding their breath.' 

Dhaka Metropolitan North BNP convener Amanullah Aman said at the human chain event, 'Awami League leaders and workers are vandalizing puja mandap in various places. They are creating chaos in various places. Cases are being filed and arrests are being made to blame that chaos on BNP. I want to tell the Awami League government to immediately withdraw the false cases. It cannot be pushed aside by the people. This time the people will decide who will come to power.' 

Swechchhasebak Dal acting president Mostafizur Rahman presided over the human chain event. The program was moderated by Abdul Qadir Bhuiyan, general secretary of the Volunteer Party. BNP standing committee member Iqbal Hasan Mahmud, member secretary Aminul Islam, executive committee member Nazim Uddin and organizing secretary of the Volunteer Party Yasin Ali also spoke at the human chain program. 

Unveiling of the book written by Taimur Alam 
Before the human chain program, the cover of the book 'Jatisattar Antarale Tiksha Nishwa' written by BNP leader Taimur Alam Khandaker was unveiled at the National Press Club. BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was the chief guest at the program. BNP standing committee member Iqbal Hasan Mahmud presided over the book unveiling program. 

At the program, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said, 'Currently, an abnormally distorted situation prevails in Bangladesh. Awami League has turned Bangladesh into a crippled and disabled state. It has destroyed all the achievements of the country. It has destroyed our parliament. It has destroyed the judiciary. It has completely partisanized the administration. It is trying to partisanize by controlling the media. This is the character of the Awami League.

Headline_English: Clashes between Chhatra League members in Chame, 2 arrested
Content_Enlish:
Police have arrested two people in connection with a fight between two factions of the Chhatra League at Chittagong Medical College (CMC). They were arrested from the college campus on Saturday night. They are Raktim De (21) and Enamul Hossain alias Simanto (21). Both are second-year MBBS students at CMC. Raktim De 11 and Enamul Hossain are accused number 15 in the complaint. 

The case was filed yesterday morning over the beating of a student named Mahadi J Aqib on the campus. Aqib is currently undergoing treatment at the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of CMC Hospital. Aqib's brother Taufiqur Rahman filed the case as the plaintiff in the incident. 

Panchlaish Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Sadequr Rahman told Prothom Alo that two accused in the complaint have been arrested in the beating of Aqib. They are medical students. 

Meanwhile, additional police have been deployed on the campus since the incident. A faction of the Chhatra League has called for a protest rally on the campus at 11 am today, Sunday, in protest of the beating of Aqib. 

Campus sources said that the fight broke out between the followers of Deputy Minister of Education Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury and former mayor of Chittagong City Corporation AJM Nasir Uddin last Friday night and yesterday Saturday over the issue of dominance. Chittagong University is also heated up by the conflict between the followers of these two leaders. 

Three people were injured in the clash between the two parties at Chittagong Medical College. They are Mahfuzul Haque, Naimul Islam and Mahadi J Aqib. They are undergoing treatment at Chittagong Medical College Hospital. Mahadi J Aqib is a follower of Mohibul Hasan, while the other two are known on campus as Nasir supporters. All three injured are second-year students. 

Hospital sources said that Mahadi's head was fractured. He underwent emergency surgery. He has been kept in the hospital's intensive care unit (ICU). Mahfuzul Quader, assistant professor of the hospital's neurosurgery department, said, "Mahadi J. Aqib underwent surgery. There are injuries to the skull and brain. Nothing can be said right now." 

College sources said that after a long closure due to Corona, physical education classes resumed in the college on September 13. Tensions arose between the two sides within the first two days. However, no clashes occurred at that time. 

Eyewitnesses said that the latest incident began at 11:30 pm on Friday in the main hostel of the college. At night, second-year student Mahfuzul Haque was going to his room after eating in the dining room. At that time, some of the opponents made harsh comments targeting him. At that time, there was an argument between the two sides. At one stage, the followers of AJM Nasir Uddin beat up Chhatra League activists Mahfuzul Haque and Naimul Islam by the followers of Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury. As a result, tension spread on the campus. Two rooms of Mohibul Hasan's followers and one of the opponents' followers were vandalized at night. Later, the college authorities calmed down the two sides by convincing them. After that, the college principal held a meeting in his office yesterday with five representatives from each side. During the meeting, at around 10 am, the opponents caught and beat up Mahadi J Aqib, a Chhatra League activist who was a follower of Mohibul Hasan, on the street in front of the campus. After that, the situation became even more heated. The two sides took positions on the campus and started shouting slogans. There were intermittent clashes between the two sides until noon. At one stage, the followers of Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury took positions in front of the principal's room. The principal was practically blocked at this time. The police arrived and removed them at around 12:30 pm. 

When asked, Panchlaish Police Station Inspector Sadequr Rahman (Investigation) told Prothom Alo that there was a problem in the hostel at night. As a result of that incident, one of the other parties was beaten up on the sidewalk in front of the college yesterday. Additional police personnel have been deployed on the campus to control the situation. 

College closure announced 
The college was closed indefinitely at the academic council meeting around 1:30 pm following a fight between two groups of Chhatra League. College principal Shahena Akhter told Prothom Alo that as per the decision of the academic council meeting, the college has been closed indefinitely. Students have been ordered to leave the hall by Saturday. In addition, a committee headed by Professor Matiur Rahman has been formed to investigate the incident. The committee will submit a report within seven days. 

The college's notification said, 'All ongoing postgraduate professional examinations of the university have been suspended for the time being. General students will not be able to stay on the college and hospital campus unnecessarily until the college opens. The campus has been entrusted to the police administration until further notice. The police can search the room of any student if necessary.' 

Students from far away were in trouble due to the sudden closure announcement. Even then, students were seen leaving the dormitory as instructed. 58th batch student KM Tanvir will go to Dhaka. He said, he has to leave the hall by evening. Suddenly he is struggling to get train or car tickets. Students from far away are in the same situation like him. 

Case at police station 
A student named Taufiqur Rahman, known as a follower of Mohibul Hasan, has filed a case at Panchlaish police station over the fight. The complaint states that on Friday night, Saad Md. Ghalib and some others had an argument with Aqib in the hostel. Following this incident, they hit Aqib with rods, sticks and knives near the main gate of the campus on Saturday. 

Repeated clashes 
Campus sources said that earlier on March 2 this year, two parties fought in the college hostel. Then the hostel was closed. Earlier on August 13 last year, these two parties got into a clash in the hostel. The next day, the college authorities banned meetings and gatherings on the campus until further notice. The day after the March 2 fight this year, a ban was imposed on meetings and gatherings again. But it did not work. 

When asked about this, Principal Sahena Akhter said, "We stopped meetings and gatherings so that the campus would remain calm. After that, there were no meetings and gatherings. The last fight between the two parties was over a trivial incident in the hostel." 

Chittagong University also heated up due to the two parties 
According to campus sources, the Chittagong University campus is also heated up due to the dispute between the leaders and activists of Chhatra League, followers of two Awami League leaders. In the last two months, there have been five clashes between the two parties on the campus. The last time from October 14 to 17, the university branch of Chhatra League, Choose Friends with Care and Sixty Nine, were involved in clashes in phases. 

Former mayor of Sixty Nine, AJM Nasir and the leaders and activists of Choose Friends with Care are known on campus as followers of Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury.

Campus sources said that the leaders and activists of these two parties are clashing over dominance, occupying the hall room and leadership conflict. 

When asked about this, former mayor and Chittagong City Awami League General Secretary AJM Nasir Uddin refused to comment. And Deputy Minister of Education Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury could not be reached as he was ill. 

In this regard, East Delta University Vice Chancellor Professor Sikandar Khan said that if the influence of the leaders' factions falls on the students, then it is harmful for education. After being closed for a long time due to Covid, students have suffered irreparable losses. Now the college has been closed again due to the fight between student organizations. This is not desirable. Leaders should control their followers.

Headline_English: Allegations of counter-attacks against AL and rebel candidate's workers in Natore
Content_Enlish:
In the Nagar Union Parishad (UP) elections in Natore's Baraigram Upazila, allegations of attack and vandalism were received against the workers and supporters of the Awami League and the rebel chairman candidate on Saturday night. Police have been deployed at the scene. 

Talking to the Baraigram Police Station and local people, it was learned that the current chairman Nilufar Yasmin is contesting the elections as the Awami League candidate in the Nagar Union with the boat symbol. Samsuzzoha of the same party is contesting as her rebel with the horse symbol. There has been a dispute between the workers and supporters of both sides since the nomination was announced. 

The office of the rebel candidate of the Awami League was vandalized in the Nagar Union of Natore's Baraigram Upazila 
The office of the rebel candidate of the Awami League was vandalized in the Nagar Union of Natore's Baraigram Upazila Photo: Collected 
Last night at around 9:30 pm, Samsuzzoha inaugurated his election office in Dhanaidah Bazar of the union. Samsujoha's workers alleged that 20 to 30 workers and supporters of Nilufar Yasmin attacked the office shortly after they left the office after the inauguration. The attackers broke the chairs and tables of the office and tore down posters. However, Nilufar Yasmin's supporters alleged that shortly after the incident, Samsujoha's workers and supporters attacked and vandalized the houses of former Union Awami League president Abdul Quader Mandal and worker Md. Sumon. 

According to Samsujoha, the chairman candidate of the horse symbol, 'The boat candidate had threatened me in advance that he would not let me open an office in Dhanaidah Bazar. As a result, his workers vandalized the office immediately after I inaugurated the office. I have reported the incident to the police. The opponent has started a false campaign against me to avoid responsibility.' 

According to Nauk candidate Nilufar Yasmin, 'I was campaigning in the city with former president Abdul Quader and workers. The police were also there. Abdul Quader's house was attacked on this occasion. My workers did not break the horse office. They broke it themselves and are blaming me.' 

Nazrul Islam, the officer-in-charge (OC) of Baraigram police station, said that police were sent to the spot after receiving information about the vandalism. Legal action will be taken if a formal complaint is received. The situation in the area is currently calm. 
Elections will be held here on November 11.

Headline_English: Law will not move at Ziaur Rahman's pace: Law Minister
Content_Enlish:
Regarding the BNP's movement demanding that ailing BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia be sent abroad for better treatment, Law Minister Anisul Haque said, "The law will go at the speed of the law. The law will not go at the speed of Ziaur Rahman." 

The Law Minister said these things at a program in his constituency Akhaura today, Friday. The Law Minister's Public Relations Officer Md. Rezaul Karim sent the video of the minister's program to journalists. 

The Law Minister said, "They (BNP) said they will go on a movement, one point, one demand, but humanity cannot be earned through a movement. And the law will go at the speed of the law. The law will not go at the speed of Ziaur Rahman. 

Anisul Haque said, "If you make them stand, they want to move, if you make them move, they want to lie down, and if you make them lie down, they want to sleep. Now the situation is like this, what else? Now how many should be allowed to go abroad?" Clearly, this is a class that has been dragged out and understands that if an application is disposed of under a law, there is no opportunity to reconsider that disposed application. That is why the Law Ministry has rejected her (Khaleda Zia) application to go abroad twice.’ 

The Law Minister also said, ‘You have seen and heard that 15 lawyers have met me on her (Khaleda Zia) behalf to go abroad. The law I am talking about, the law that I rejected, is correct. Even then, I have taken some time to see if there is any precedent anywhere.’ 

Khaleda Zia has been undergoing treatment at Evercare Hospital in the capital since November 13. Her family and BNP have been demanding better treatment abroad for her. 

An application was made by her family seeking permission to send Khaleda Zia abroad for better treatment. The application was sent from the Home Ministry to the Law Ministry. However, Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan said that the Law Ministry has not informed or given any indication about the next steps to be taken by the Home Ministry in this regard. He told reporters at the Secretariat yesterday that the Law Minister will examine the matter and decide on the next steps.

Headline_English: Prime Minister has set the highest example of human rights for Khaleda Zia: Quader
Content_Enlish:
Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader said that BNP is trying to destabilize the country by making Khaleda Zia's medical treatment an issue. The party's aim is to fish in troubled waters. Obaidul Quader made this allegation during a briefing at his residence this Friday morning. 

Obaidul Quader said that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has set the highest example of human rights for BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia. 

Criticizing the Prime Minister's speech on the Jubo League's founding anniversary recently, BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that such a speech cannot be expected from the leader of any civilized country. Referring to this, he said, who has set an example of humanity in the politics of this country? And who is practicing indecency and indecency in politics? On August 21, BNP wanted to kill Sheikh Hasina using the state machinery. However, then Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, standing in parliament, said that Sheikh Hasina had carried the grenade in her vanity bag. 

Obaidul Quader said to the BNP Secretary General, was Khaleda Zia's statement the statement of any leader of a civilized country? 

The Awami League General Secretary said, when Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina went to console Begum Zia after the death of her child, they closed the door - can the head of a political party commit such inhuman and rude behavior? Will the BNP Secretary General respond to this? Can the head of a party commit abuse against an invitation to tea at Ganabhaban? Will the BNP Secretary General respond to this? 

Obaidul Quader said, did any convicted or sentenced accused get such an opportunity during the regime of Ziaur Rahman and Khaleda Zia? Or can they show any such example of someone from the opposition getting such an opportunity during their regime?

Headline_English: Three ministers looking into US sanctions: Cabinet Secretary
Content_Enlish:
Three government ministers are looking into the issue of US sanctions against seven former and current RAB officials. They are Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, Law Minister Anisul Haque and Foreign Minister AK Abdul Momen. 

This was stated by Cabinet Secretary Khandaker Anwarul Islam. He said this in response to questions from journalists at a press conference organized after the cabinet meeting to announce the decision of the meeting today, Monday. 

The Cabinet Secretary said that this was not discussed in the cabinet meeting. The matter is being looked into by the Home Minister, Law Minister and Foreign Minister. 

The US has imposed sanctions on seven former and current Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) officials on charges of human rights violations. The US Treasury Department (Revenue Division) and the State Department imposed these sanctions separately on International Human Rights Day last Friday. Former RAB Director General Benazir Ahmed is among the officials who came under the sanctions. She is now the Inspector General of Bangladesh Police (IGP). In addition, the current Director General (DG) of RAB, Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun, is also on the sanctions list. 

The government has reacted strongly after this incident. The US ambassador to Dhaka has been summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and a strong protest has been lodged. In addition, government ministers are also criticizing this. 

Regarding the US sanctions, the ruling party's general secretary and the Minister of Road Transport and Bridges said at a program in Dhaka today that militancy and terrorists who sponsor militancy will be given shelter in this incident.

Headline_English: The spirit of the Liberation War has been destroyed: Mirza Fakhrul
Content_Enlish:
BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said that the current ruling class is continuing to oppress and torture the people of this country in various ways to destroy the spirit of the Liberation War and introduce a one-party regime. He said these things while talking to reporters after paying tribute at the Martyred Intellectuals Memorial in Mirpur on Tuesday morning. 

Fakhrul paid tribute to the martyred intellectuals along with several thousand leaders and activists of BNP and its affiliated organizations. The BNP leader said, "The Pakistani occupying forces have brutally killed countless intellectuals including our doctors, teachers, journalists, engineers. They have killed millions of people in the long 9-month war. They have killed intellectuals with the aim of demoralizing the nation." 

Fakhrul said, "This year, we are about to complete 50 years of independence. But unfortunately, we have not achieved the goal with which we started the war of independence in 1971 - a democratic state.' He also said that the current ruling class is continuing to oppress and torture the people of this country in various ways. They have killed and disappeared countless people. 

The BNP Secretary General said, 'BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia has been detained in a fabricated case for several years. Right now, she is sick and at the crossroads of life and death. We have repeatedly said that the national leader Begum Khaleda Zia should be released and sent abroad for better treatment. But the government has not paid attention to it.' He also said that this anti-people government, the anti-liberation government, not only Begum Khaleda Zia, they do not want to let anyone do politics here. They have started the process of depoliticization in this country. 

Mirza Fakhrul said, "On the one hand, they are imprisoning the leader Begum Khaleda Zia and not giving her medical treatment. On the other hand, they are continuing to torture and abuse all patriotic people. On such a day, we pay deep respect to the martyred intellectuals." He also said that the people will once again awaken to the spirit of the Liberation War. The monstrous authoritarian government will be replaced and a people's government, people's parliament and a free state will be established. 

At that time, BNP Standing Committee Member Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Joint Secretary General Habib-un-Nabi Khan, Dhaka Metropolitan North Convener Amanullah Aman, South Convener Abdus Salam, Party Publicity Secretary Shahid Uddin Chowdhury, along with leaders and activists from various levels of BNP and its affiliated organizations were present.

Headline_English: Bangladesh is not in a position to panic over US sanctions: Professor Imtiaz Ahmed
Content_Enlish:
US sanctions on seven members of the law enforcement agencies and incidents like not inviting them to the Democracy Conference are now hot topics in Bangladesh. Imtiaz Ahmed, a professor in the Department of International Relations at Dhaka University, spoke to Prothom Alo about these incidents and their impact. Partha Shankar Saha spoke to him. 
Question: Prothom Alo: The US Department of State and the Department of Revenue have issued sanctions against seven members of the law enforcement agencies, including the IGP of Bangladesh, the Director General of RAB. Why this ban at this time? RAB was formed long ago. 

Professor Imtiaz Ahmed: There are various processes involved in these sanctions and that is why it may take time. The reason for the sanctions at this time may be that the United States is trying to restore democracy after Joe Biden came to power. He is doing this for several reasons. First of all, the attack on Capitol Hill has turned American democracy into a cartoon around the world. It is not acceptable to deny this. If this had happened in any other country, it would have been labeled a failed state. This is unthinkable for the United States. Another thing that many people are not paying attention to is that Donald Trump has not yet acknowledged Joe Biden. He is saying that he is an illegitimate president. He has the support of about 70 million voters behind him. We are seeing some of the effects of this. Starting from not getting vaccinated in many states of the United States, this is visible in various activities. This situation is not desirable in the United States, the main defender of democracy. 

Question: Prothom Alo: Is the United States doing all this because of the fragile position of democracy within the country? 

Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes, and in addition to this, I want to cover the shameful situation in which the United States was almost forced to leave Afghanistan. Leaving in the dark of night, not knowing the Afghan government—the United States wants to handle these situations. So, the defeat in Afghanistan, the attack on Capitol Hill, issues like Black Lives Matter—all of them will try to save its democracy. And a time has come when China has become a major economic power. After the Vietnam War, the United States was in the same situation with democracy. But the Soviet Union was not an economic power then. And China was not around. But China is now a huge economic power. At this very time, the opposition to China is at the core of this conference on democracy. Along with countries like China and North Korea, Bangladesh has also been included here. It is true, the lobby of Bangladesh is very weak. US policy is controlled by the lobby. What their envoy said here is not the point. 

Question: Prothom Alo: One thing some in the Awami League camp are saying is that the lobby of people close to BNP has played a role behind these sanctions. How logical is this? 

Imtiaz Ahmed: Since I do not have any evidence, as a researcher I cannot say this. If I do not say that, then it is true, there has been a criticism of RAB within Bangladesh for a long time. The country's human rights organizations have criticized the activities of RAB in their various reports. But there is a kind of apparent contradiction between going to the United States and talking about extrajudicial killings in Bangladesh. The number of extrajudicial killings in the United States is much higher than in Bangladesh. My point is, the Bangladesh issue should be resolved in Bangladesh. They happen a lot, so it has to happen in our country, it can never happen. We need to create an environment where not a single extrajudicial killing can happen in our country. But if someone complains to other countries about these incidents in Bangladesh and does not talk about the extrajudicial killings in those countries, that would be unfair. The question should also be asked from what moral position these countries are saying these things. 

Question: Prothom Alo: So is there politics behind all this? 

Imtiaz Ahmed: Of course. So many extrajudicial killings are happening in one country, and they are talking about the problems of another country, it cannot be a political issue. The number of disappearances in the United States is huge. In terms of lobbying, lobbies of different countries have worked better than the lobby of the opposition party in our country. It may be that they may have heard negative things about the situation in Bangladesh. And Bangladesh may not have had a strong lobby against the negative stance of these countries. Apart from that, comparing Bangladesh with North Korea and China is surprising. Not only the United States, but our neighboring country India's human rights record is not very good. If I talk about Kashmir or the killings on the India-Bangladesh border, then those are also extrajudicial killings. I never hear the US talk about the number of people killed on our border. If the US were to talk about these things, it would not pass due to the activities of the Indian lobby. In fact, in the case of Bangladesh, the current ban may be due to our weak lobby. There is no reason to worry about it. A statement by New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern has now gone viral. In an interview, she said, I don't understand US at all. I think so too. I don't think they do everything with understanding. 

Question: Prothom Alo: So don't you think this ban is carrying a negative message for the Bangladesh government? How do you see the way the government has reacted to this incident? 

Imtiaz Ahmed: What our government has done is right. The US government must have also wanted to see Bangladesh's reaction. The Foreign Secretary has summoned the US ambassador. Earlier, Bangladesh had summoned the ambassadors of China and the UK in a similar manner. The reason for this is that the Bangladesh of the 1970s and the Bangladesh of today are not the same. In various cases, we have seen that Bangladesh has changed its body language when talking to other countries. One major reason for this is that there has been a relative development in Bangladesh. Its growth is a matter of interest to many. There is not much criticism about the way the government has handled the pandemic. This time, Bangladesh has clearly told the US ambassador after the sanctions that they are not happy. The US ambassador himself does not know about this. If Bangladesh had not called like this, it could have been assumed that Bangladesh was nervous. But Bangladesh is not in a state of nervousness. 
Let me say another thing, the history of our relations with the US is not colorful. There is talk about their role in 1971. A bigger thing is their role during the famine of 1974. Many will not forget this. Even though there was enough food, they did not provide it. US policymakers used to say at that time that Bangladesh is a basket case. Today, at the time of the 50th golden jubilee of Bangladesh's independence, they have also raised questions about Bangladesh's democracy. 

Question: Prothom Alo: So do you think the recent sanctions will not create any major problems for Bangladesh in its relationship with the US? 

Imtiaz Ahmed: The Chinese ambassador was summoned after his comments on the possible situation if the US, Japan, Australia and India join the 'Quad' alliance. But this did not cause any rift in the relationship between the two countries. We also have multi-level relations with the US. There is trade and commerce, we have relations with the military, and there are many Bangladeshis there. So this sanction will not have any major impact. It will be discussed for a few days. It will be written in the newspapers. Then it will fade away. By summoning the US ambassador, Bangladesh has made it very clear that you can say whatever you want and we will listen, that will not happen. When Bangladesh was called a 'basket case', no one protested. This time it has. 

Question: Prothom Alo: One thing is believed to be that the US does not take our leaning too much towards China well. Does it seem to have some influence behind the current events? 

Imtiaz Ahmed: The main basis of China's relations with Bangladesh is economics. We are not in any military alliance. What can displease the United States is the policy of 'friendship with all, hostility with none'. Those who have friends in this country, even within the party, say that it is better to choose a side instead of being like this. They do not understand that Bangladesh cannot take responsibility for this. They may not even know that this policy was not taken after independence. It was in the election manifesto of the Awami League in 1970 under the leadership of Bangabandhu. Not only that, at that time the manifesto said, 'We cannot be in either SEATO or CENTO.' At that time, the whole world was in the throes of the Cold War. In that context, Bangabandhu was able to say 'friendship with all, hostility with none'. So where is the difficulty in saying this today? 
Bangabandhu returned to India in 1972 and went to India for the first time in February of that year. At the reception given to him there, Bangabandhu said in front of Indira Gandhi that all the countries of South Asia should forget their mutual animosity and work together for development. He wanted an end to the animosity of all the countries of South Asia at that time. In the context of that time, his words were groundbreaking. Because at that time, they were just on the way to recovering from the war. India had contributed a lot in that war. He said this while standing in front of Indira Gandhi. That courage has never been seen in any leader.

Headline_English: "The vote was held at night, are we going to keep doing this for the rest of our lives?"
Content_Enlish:
The current government does not believe in transferring power through impartial elections. The elections will be held in the dark of night—this cannot be allowed to continue. 

Speakers made these remarks at a program organized by the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD) at the National Press Club on Monday. JSD President ASM Abdur Rab presented the national government's proposal to resolve the existing political crisis. 

At the program, ASM Abdur Rab said, "I have realized that this nation needs to be saved. For this, I have initiated discussions with the national government's proposal." According to his proposal, the national government's objective will be to transfer power to elected representatives through elections. Establish an independent election commission. Release political prisoners. Withdraw all cases of disappearance. Ensure the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary. 

Mostafa Mohsin Montu, president of a faction of the Gano Forum, said, "What did we see in the 2018 election? The election was held in the dark of night. The same thing happened in 2014. Will we continue to do this for the rest of our lives? They will get away with it like this, it cannot happen.’ 

Jonayed Saki, the chief coordinator of the mass solidarity movement, said that a division has been created among international powers. Competition has started for their own interests. They will continue their various activities to exert influence on Bangladesh. The people of Bangladesh should not be victims of the conflict between international powers. 

Supporting the proposed national government, former VP of DUCSU Nurul Haque said, ‘This government is going through the weakest period in its 12-year rule. Many in the administration have contacted us and requested that you do something. If you do something, we will step down.’ 

Saiful Haque, General Secretary of the Revolutionary Workers Party of Bangladesh, Professor Abdul Latif, lawyer Hasnat Qayyum, among others, also spoke at the event.

Headline_English: It takes a day to make a law: Workers' Party in President's dialogue
Content_Enlish:
The Workers' Party of Bangladesh has demanded that a law be enacted in this regard as per the instructions of the constitution before the formation of the Election Commission (EC). They said that in the past, the law to introduce a caretaker government was enacted in a single day. Therefore, there is still time to enact a law to form the EC. The Workers' Party has suggested that the bill be raised in the first session of the National Parliament in the new year. 

On Tuesday afternoon, at the invitation of President Md. Abdul Hamid, the Workers' Party, an ally of the ruling Awami League, made these demands and proposals while participating in a dialogue at Bangabhaban. A seven-member delegation led by party president Rashed Khan Menon participated in the dialogue. 

After the dialogue, Rashed Khan Menon came out and spoke to journalists at the gate of Bangabhaban. He said that there are three rounds of dialogue with the President regarding the EC. It is unfortunate that we have to come three times on the same issue. Rashed Khan Menon said that in 2011, they proposed to enact a law to form the EC. They made the same proposal in 2016. The same proposal has been submitted to the President again today. 

Former minister of the Awami League-led government Rashed Khan Menon opined that a law must be made to remove the lack of confidence in the formation of the EC. He said, ‘The President also thinks that the enactment of a law has become mandatory for the formation of the EC.’ 

Stating that ‘there is consensus among all political parties, including the Awami League,’ on the issue of enactment of a law on the formation of the EC, the Workers’ Party president said that the President can take the initiative. He can take the opinions of civil society, media representatives and intellectuals. Apart from this, a draft law was prepared during the tenure of former Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Shamsul Huda. It is possible to enact a law based on that draft. He said that the law introducing the caretaker government in 1996 was prepared overnight. 

It did not take long to bring amendments to the constitution regarding appeals in the trial of war criminals. The session of the National Assembly will be held at the beginning of the year. The President will deliver the inaugural address of the session. At that time, he can give instructions on lifting the law on the formation of the EC. 

Workers' Party leaders held a dialogue with the President at Bangabhaban on Tuesday regarding the formation of the Election Commission 
Workers' Party leaders held a dialogue with the President at Bangabhaban on Tuesday regarding the formation of the Election Commission Photo: PID 
Regarding the law, Rashed Khan Menon said that a constitutional council can be set up in the law to appoint the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other election commissioners. This constitutional council can consist of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, the Speaker, the Chief Justice and the Attorney General. This council will propose names to the President for the appointment of the CEC and other commissioners. 

Rashed Khan Menon said that the President did not say anything about forming a search committee to form the EC during the dialogue. However, from outside, there are also rumors of forming the EC through a search committee. If this happens, the Workers' Party has also proposed the formation of a search committee. In it, they said that the search committee should be formed with constitutional office-bearers. They will propose four names for each post of CEC and other commissioners. This list will be selected by the Parliamentary Advisory Committee and a shortlist will be sent to the President. The President will appoint the CEC and other commissioners. 

The dialogue also discussed the election-time government. When asked about the Workers' Party's opinion on this, Rashed Khan Menon said that it was not the subject of discussion. In response to the question of whether an election-time government is needed or not, he said, "We held elections under a party government. There is no alternative to it in the constitution. If the constitution is to be amended, the consensus of all political parties will be required." 
Some political parties are calling the dialogue a drama. When asked what they think, the Workers' Party president said, "Those who are talking about drama should do something opposite to the drama." 

The Workers' Party delegation also included Anisur Rahman Mallick, Mahmudul Hasan Manik, Nur Ahmed Bakul, Kamrul Ahsan, Ali Ahmed Enamul Haque and Nazrul Islam Haqqani.

Headline_English: BNP will not participate in any meaningless dialogue: Standing Committee decision
Content_Enlish:
In the current political context, BNP considers dialogue on the formation of the Election Commission alone to be a waste of time without the constitutional guarantee of a neutral government and impartial administration. Therefore, they will not participate in any meaningless dialogue. 

BNP informed the media of this decision on Wednesday afternoon regarding the President's dialogue with registered political parties on the formation of the Election Commission. A press release sent to the media said that this decision was taken at the meeting of the Standing Committee, the highest policy-making forum of BNP, held virtually last Monday. 

The BNP Standing Committee believes that before the formation of the last two Election Commissions, the registered political parties participated in the dialogue and gave their opinions at the invitation of the President. BNP also submitted a clear proposal in writing to the President on the process of forming the Election Commission. But all the initiatives failed due to the Awami League party government being in power during the election. The electoral system has been destroyed due to the illegal use of the state machinery, the extreme failure and incompetence of the Election Commission. Voters have almost stopped going to the polling stations to vote. The Election Commission has become a party organization of the Awami League. Two successive election commissions have failed miserably to institutionalize democracy. 

BNP believes that the Election Commission will never be able to independently conduct free, impartial and fair elections while maintaining a party government in the political context of Bangladesh. According to them, by amending the constitution in 2011, abolishing the provision of the caretaker government and enforcing the provision of elections under a party government, the Awami League government has actually blocked all avenues for the development of democracy. The people have lost their right to vote. 

BNP's standing committee believes that no election commission can conduct fair, free and acceptable elections without a neutral and non-partisan government during the election. The President himself has said that he does not have the power to change. That is why the dialogue between political parties with the President will not bring any positive results. BNP will not participate in any meaningless dialogue. 

BNP has alleged that corruption is rampant at the highest levels of the government and huge money is being laundered with the help of corrupt people. In this context, the press release, citing a recently published report by the US-based international organization Global Financial Integrity (GFAI), said that about 440,000 crore taka was laundered from Bangladesh in the six years from 2009 to 2015 (excluding 2014). BNP believes that this calculation does not reflect the overall picture. The overall picture of corruption and money laundering is even more horrific. 

The BNP Standing Committee believes that a state of terror has been created in Bangladesh through the disappearance of leaders and activists of opposition political parties and activists of civil society movements for a decade. The incidents of 'disappearances' by the country's intelligence agencies have recently come to light in the report titled 'Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances' of the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) on disappearances. 

The BNP Standing Committee expressed deep sorrow over the tragic deaths of journalists Riaz Uddin Ahmed and Syed Akram Hossain and the 45 people in the launch fire. They have decided to hold a human chain program in metropolitan and district levels across the country and in front of the National Press Club in Dhaka on December 30 to mark the third anniversary of the 'Nishira voter suppression'. 

The meeting, chaired by the party's acting chairman, was attended by BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, as well as standing committee members Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, Zamir Uddin Sarkar, Mirza Abbas, Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Abdul Moin Khan, Nazrul Islam Khan, Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Selima Rahman and Iqbal Hasan Mahmud.

Headline_English: Australia sealed the series on the morning of the third day
Content_Enlish:
Australia won the Melbourne Test on the morning of the third day and sealed the series with two matches in hand. On the morning of the third day, the English were bowled out for just 68 runs, and the Aussies won by an innings and 14 runs. 

At the end of the second day, England were trailing by 82 runs to avoid an innings defeat. The visitors' innings did not last more than 16 overs with debutant Scott Boland taking 6 wickets at the beginning of the third day. 

Earlier, Australia scored 267 runs in reply to England's 186 runs in the first innings. Joe Root, the only batsman to make a half-century in the first innings for England, fought back in the second innings with a lone innings of 28 runs off 59 balls. Ben Stokes scored the second highest score of 11 runs. In addition, the remaining 9 cricketers of the team could not collect their runs in double figures. Debutant Boland was named the man of the match for taking 7 wickets in both innings.

Headline_English: Bangladesh to face India in semi-final
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh will face India in the semi-finals of the Under-19 Asia Cup on Thursday. The match will start at 11:30 am at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the United Arab Emirates. 

Bangladesh has secured a semi-final spot by becoming the champion of Group B this season. After a big win against Nepal by 154 runs in the first match of Group B, the Bengal youth team defeated Kuwait by a huge margin of 222 runs in the second match. 

The last match against Sri Lanka was cancelled. As a result, the Young Tigers secured a semi-final spot by becoming the group champion by leading on run rate. Meanwhile, India secured a ticket to the semi-finals by becoming the runner-up from Group A.

Headline_English: There is a lot of confusion about whether the female victim of the rape was a tourist or not.
Content_Enlish:
The administration has designated a special place for women in Cox's Bazar. Many are criticizing it. 
But I am in favor of the administration's work. 

We are like this as a nation. Has the administration come from outside our nation? What can they do? 

When the exam was a festival of cheating, we focused on changing the type of question paper instead of focusing on stopping cheating. 
When question-out had almost become a national problem, at that time, without thinking about who was cheating the question paper, we started thinking about how to make question-out difficult by raising objective questions. 

When the trawler sank in the Sundarbans and everything was washed away by oil, before the oil was removed, we kept thinking about how to form an investigation committee. 

So, rather than providing security to tourists in Cox's Bazar, we thought it would be easier to make a separate beach for women. This can also be interpreted in this way, only this part of the beach in Cox's Bazar is safe for women. The rest of Cox's Bazar is not safe. 

From my little knowledge, I know that Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Indonesia are Muslim countries. There are beaches there. Local and foreign tourists go there and roam around as they please (literally as they please). For this, the rate of tourists being oppressed or harassed is below 1%. Those countries also have administration, police and criminals. We have them too. 

I do not know any statistics about our rate of oppression and harassment. 

I think it is better not to know the statistics. The statistics will not be good. 

Off the topic: Is there a lot of fuss about whether the woman who was raped in Cox's Bazar is a tourist? Is there any law that makes the punishment for rape less, if not more, if a tourist is a tourist? 
If anyone knows, please tell me.

Headline_English: Sheikh Russell wins in 22-man penalty shootout
Content_Enlish:
The ongoing Federation Cup has been giving birth to various incidents since the beginning. In its continuation, a strange match was seen yesterday. 4 goals from both teams in the scheduled time of the game. Then 25 goals in 26 shots in the tiebreaker. In total, 29 goals were scored in the match between Sheikh Russell Krira Chakra and Dhaka Abahani in Bashundhara Group Federation Cup football yesterday. 

11 footballers from both teams took penalties. Even then, the game was not over. Sudden death continued. In the end, the scoreline ended with a scoreline of 13-12 goals. Sheikh Russell became the champion of Group B and Dhaka Abahani became the runner-up. With this victory, they became the champion of Group B and advanced to the quarter-finals. 

In this match held at Kamalapur Bir Shreshth Shaheed Sipahi Mostafa Kamal Stadium, Abahani took the lead in the 8th minute through a goal by Dorienton. Sheikh Russell's Rabbi restored parity in the match 12 minutes later. Dorienton gave Abahani the lead again in the 61st minute. Sheikh Russell's Ailton scored in the 84th minute. 

The match ended in a 2-2 draw in the regular time. As the scoreline was tied in the 90-minute match, the match went directly to a tiebreaker according to the bylaws.
