Headline_English: Four benefits of hot water for beauty
Content_Enlish:
Winter is almost here in nature. Many people feel heavy in the morning after taking a bath. The clamor for heaters, geysers, and hot water has started. But do you know that using hot water in the bath makes your skin and hair beautiful. However, in this case, the temperature must be right. 
It is better to keep the temperature of the bath water at 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit. Also, to get the benefits of bathing in hot water, you need to mix some ingredients! Let's find out what to mix in hot water for skin and hair care this winter: 
Some ingredients to mix in hot water to get the benefits of bathing in hot water 

You can mix lavender oil with coconut oil and keep it in a bottle. You can shake it slightly and mix 2-3 drops in hot water every day while bathing. This will reduce the roughness of your skin and hair. 
Before shampooing, you can wash your hair with lukewarm water. Then you can use shampoo and clean your hair with the same water. Finally, after using conditioner, wash your hair with normal water. This process is very beneficial in hair care. 
Wash rose or marigold petals in salt water and soak them in coconut oil. Then, when it cools down, you can strain it and store it. Then, add a few drops of this oil in lukewarm water before taking a bath to keep your skin and hair moisturized even in winter. 
Of course, after taking a bath with warm water, you should use moisturizer, coconut or olive oil while the skin is still wet. This will restore the skin's natural oiliness.

Headline_English: Climate change and the future of children
Content_Enlish:
The impact of climate change in the global context is now a topic of discussion. The negative impact of climate change is increasing due to carbon emissions. The more carbon emissions increase, the more visible the impact of climate change will be. Because carbon emissions are related to temperature increase. There is a relationship between temperature increase and the overall context of life, including sea level rise, melting ice, drought, wildfires, and pollution. Naturally, there is a widespread discussion about increasing dependence on renewable energy to reduce carbon emissions. However, despite so much discussion, considering the overall context, the impact of climate change on children, who are the future leaders, seems to be receiving less attention! In the current context, the impact of climate change on children is now visible. 

Due to the impact of climate change, the desired future of children in affected countries is under threat. The world now has to take planned decisions keeping in mind the needs of climate-exposed and vulnerable children. If climate change and children are taken into consideration, it will be easier for policymakers in developed countries to take quick, technical and realistic decisions. If the delay in reducing carbon emissions continues, not only the current generation but also future generations will face terrible problems. We must work now to ensure a sustainable and improved standard of living for children. Reducing carbon emissions, providing financial and technical assistance to affected countries, expanding renewable energy, and adapting to climate change can solve the climate problem. Children are the victims of negative climate change. 

Climate change is affecting every aspect of life in some way or another. Thousands of families are being forced to change their homes due to various climate disasters including rising sea levels, storms, floods, and droughts. Many families are migrating to cities due to climate change. As a result, children's education and normal life are becoming as chaotic as the climate. Child nutrition, child marriage, trafficking, child labor, etc. are related to climate change. Poor children are dropping out of school and starting work at an early age due to the negative effects of climate change. Thousands of families are becoming destitute due to climate disasters. The income of coastal people is decreasing, they are losing their jobs. As a result, climate change is naturally having a negative impact on the lives of children in coastal towns. Due to the damage to various educational institutions due to climate disasters, floods, and cyclones, children's education is being hampered. Thousands of families in coastal districts (Khulna, Bagerhat, Satkhira, Barguna, Patuakhali) are becoming poorer due to climate problems and migrating to cities or elsewhere. As a result, poor families are failing to think about the future of their children. 

In this era of globalization, we must think about the sustainable future of every child. I believe it is the important responsibility of world leaders to ensure that children in developing, underdeveloped, and poor countries are not affected by climate disasters caused by developed countries. Global disasters and climate problems must be addressed globally. Along with this, sustainable technology and environment must be created to adapt to climate change. Now is the time to take planned initiatives to build a livable world for children and ensure a sustainable future.

Headline_English: Specific action plan needed to protect the environment
Content_Enlish:
The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm, Sweden, from June 5 to 16, 1972, as decided by the United Nations General Assembly, and was the first international conference on the environment. In light of this conference, the day has been celebrated every year since 1974 in different cities with different themes. In continuation of this, Bangladesh was the host country for the day from 1975, 1977 to 1984, and 2010. This year, on the 50th anniversary of the celebration of the day on June 5, World Environment Day was celebrated all over the world with the same motto, 'We only have one Earth'. Let us take this opportunity to review our position on environmental oppression and life-threatening environmental issues in the world in the last 50 years. 

According to the United Nations Environment Programme's 'Food Waste Index-2021', more than 10 million tons of food is wasted in Bangladesh every year. The World Health Organization and UNICEF's 'JMP Report 2021', prepared using water and sanitation data from 230 countries, says that in 2020, the rate of people with sanitation facilities was 54 percent in Bangladesh, 68 percent in Pakistan and 71 percent in India, while 22 percent in Bangladesh, 2 percent in India and 3 percent in Pakistan used improvised toilets. The rate of access to water for domestic purposes was 15 percent in Bangladesh, 44 percent in India and 26 percent in Pakistan. According to UNICEF's CCRI Report 2021, Bangladesh is 15th out of 65 countries at very high risk of being affected by the impacts of climate change in the world. According to the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network Report 2021, Bangladesh, India and Pakistan are ranked 109th, 120th and 129th respectively out of 165 countries in achieving the SDGs. According to the Economist Intelligence Unit Report 2021, Dhaka is ranked 137th out of 140 liveable cities in the world. 

The proportion of other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, including PM 2.5, PM 10, ozone, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrous oxide, etc., is gradually increasing, and the volume of the ozone layer in the atmosphere is shrinking. According to a report published by the World Bank, 28 percent of all deaths in Bangladesh occur every year due to environmental pollution-related diseases. According to the World Health Organization, about 7 million people die worldwide every year due to air pollution. In the article titled 'World Air Quality Report 2021' published by the Switzerland-based IQAir Air Quality Index on March 22, 2022, Bangladesh's name has topped the list of countries with the most polluted air in the world, and Manikganj in Bangladesh was ranked 16th in the world's most polluted air city in 2020. According to FAO, in the last 15 years, about 1.4 percent of the world's forests have been deforested, while in Bangladesh, the rate is 2.6 percent, and 2,600 hectares of forests, including protected forests, are being deforested annually. In the last two decades, more than 3,000 hills have been cut down in Cox's Bazar district, and 8,000 acres of protected forest have been cleared to establish shelters for the Rohingya. The Sundarbans, the most famous protected forest in the world, known as the lungs of Bangladesh, has decreased in size and density. Moreover, Bangladesh has now become a country prone to extreme natural disasters due to the severe impact of environmental pollution. In a report published by the US-based environmental organization Environmental Protection Agency in 2018 on the role of governments in protecting the environment of 180 countries around the world, Bangladesh was ranked second from last. Bangladesh is first in the scale of loss of agricultural land and forests in the world and tenth in plastic pollution according to the 2018 report of the World Economic Forum. In the historic Paris Agreement of 2015, 195 countries decided to keep the average temperature increase of the world within 1.5 degrees Celsius this century, which will require reducing carbon emissions by about 8 percent every year until 2030. But within three years of the agreement, about 56 billion tons of carbon dioxide have been emitted by 2018, and if this continues, the world's temperature will increase by 3.2 degrees Celsius by the end of this century. 

As a result of increasing warming, the ice in the polar regions is melting and turning into water, releasing new microorganisms. The water of all the rivers around Dhaka has long lost its natural qualities. We have heard the news of the tragic death of a whale in the sea after swallowing 1,000 plastic bags. It is surprising to know that 50 percent of the amount of plastic waste generated around the world every day is single-use cups, spoons, dinner plates or polythene. More than 5,000 metric tons of waste are being generated in the capital every day. A report published in a national daily says that 124 tons of plastic waste is generated every day in Dhaka city, of which 86 percent is recycled. The rest, which is not used, is mostly polythene. According to a World Bank report, the annual per capita plastic consumption in urban areas of Bangladesh was three kilograms in 2005. But in 2020, that amount has tripled to 9 kilograms. Again, the acid present in rainwater is threatening food security and destroying green forests.

Headline_English: Possible changes during the 'New Normal'
Content_Enlish:
The coronavirus infection is not only causing a humanitarian and financial disaster, but its other effects cannot be ignored. Although there is so much discussion about the impact of the coronavirus on the world and the financial losses, its potential impact on other areas remains neglected. Due to this crisis, our lives may completely change in many areas in the future. Some internationally renowned companies have discovered a vaccine for the coronavirus. They claim that this vaccine is 93 to 95 percent effective. The discovery of this vaccine is being promoted in such a way that it may seem that once it comes to the market, the deadly virus called Corona will not find a way to spread fear. But is it really so? There is no guarantee that the coronavirus will not be transmitted even after taking this vaccine. So there is nothing to be very excited about the vaccine. But the propaganda experts of international organizations are campaigning in such a way that the corona vaccine is a 'panacea'. There will be no more worries when the vaccine comes to the market. It would not be surprising if there is another motive behind this overly confident campaign. 

Because multinational companies, whenever they get an opportunity, market their products in poor countries and loot money. Excessive propaganda about the Corona vaccine can be such a strategy. Now we have no choice but to wait for this newly invented vaccine. There is no shortage of opportunists who capitalize on human suffering or crisis to gain benefits. They understand the opportunity and act accordingly. No matter how much propaganda is made about the Corona vaccine, it can be said with almost certainty that the world is not getting rid of the Corona infection anytime soon. On the contrary, the Corona infection may spread in a more terrible form in the future. Since we are not getting rid of the Corona infection very soon, we have to think about how to proceed in the new normal or new normal situation. If the impact of Corona continues for a few more years, we have to prepare now for the possible social and behavioral changes worldwide. We have to determine the behavior of the new normal or new normal period. 

The investment rate in the private sector was fluctuating at 22-23 percent of GDP. For a developing and rapidly growing economy like Bangladesh, the investment rate in the private sector was required to be at least 40 to 45 percent. Due to Corona, investment in the private sector has decreased drastically. Imports of raw materials and capital machinery used in industry have decreased drastically. The government has provided loan incentives of Tk 40,000 crore to the industrial sector during the Corona period. They have taken almost all of this loan incentive. But even after that, most of the factory owners have laid off workers from their organizations. The laid-off workers are now forced to live inhuman lives. In the future, factory owners may lean towards technology dependence to reduce production costs. If they become technology dependent, the fear of losing jobs for ordinary workers in factories will increase. There is a risk of a drastic decrease in domestic consumption demand in the future. Because the consumption capacity of the common people is not increasing. In this situation, they will not be able to spend much money even if they want to. If the ability to spend money decreases, it will definitely affect the country's production system. During the Corona period, the country's foreign exchange reserves have crossed 42 billion (4,200 crore) US dollars. We are expressing joy about this. But inflated reserves without investment may not always be good. The main reason behind the inflation of reserves is the abnormal upward trend in remittance flows. Expatriate Bangladeshis have brought their savings abroad to the country at once when they returned home after losing their jobs. In addition, the financial needs of local beneficiaries have also increased due to Corona. As a result, expatriate Bangladeshis have sent more money than before. So far, according to government estimates, more than 300,000 expatriate Bangladeshis have returned home. Have we taken any initiative to re-employ or rehabilitate those who have returned home? Everyone unanimously admits that small and medium enterprise entrepreneurs will play a special role in economic rehabilitation during the Corona period. But even half of the Tk 20,000 crore incentive bank loan allocation that has been made for them has not been distributed yet. Banks are not as enthusiastic about lending to big entrepreneurs as they are about lending to small entrepreneurs. We are more interested in ‘giving oil to the poor’. 

In the future, there is a possibility of a major change in our social behavior and customs. We are used to holding various political and social meetings and processions. This may not be the case in the future. Instead of a direct meeting and procession, there may be online meetings and processions. The methods and customs of celebrating social events such as weddings, wedding receptions, birthdays, etc. may change. The culture of visiting relatives’ houses may also be largely stopped. If Corona continues to spread, then social customs like handshakes and hugs may also stop. 

There are some good sides to all the bad. Corona has caused harm to humans. But it has benefited nature and the living world. Due to Corona, humans are not able to destroy nature and animals indiscriminately as before. Nature has come alive again with this opportunity. Rare animals and birds are also able to breed in a harmless environment. The natural imbalance that we are currently witnessing will no longer exist in the future. Crocodiles in the water, tigers on the land - with this, our nature will once again be newly decorated and flourish. The possibility of nature being damaged due to humans will be greatly reduced. Bengalis are known as a chatty nation. But this chat will be interrupted to some extent. Many of the behaviors that we have been accustomed to for so long will change. However, how positive and how negative this possible change will be remains to be seen. 

Author: Retired banker and economics columnist

Headline_English: How Digital Bangladesh is progressing
Content_Enlish:
The wind of change is blowing, Digital Bangladesh is our first demand - with this supreme slogan in front, Honorable Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced Digital Bangladesh 'Vision 2021' in 2009-10, expressing the hope of transforming Bangladesh into a digital country in terms of fulfilling her potential dream. 
And in its continuation, the country is moving forward. After the announcement of the 'First Challenge Vision 2021' of Digital Bangladesh, Bangladesh has made great progress towards digitalization in 12 years. Today, the once backward country has been able to stand tall in the world court under the skillful leadership of Sheikh Hasina. 

Electricity to 3,000 families in Kaptai after 47 years of independence 

When there was an unlimited power crisis going on across the country and keeping in mind the impossible challenge of meeting the power shortage, some so-called intellectuals with the civil name of society ridiculed this far-reaching thought, dream and declaration of the Honorable Prime Minister. Leaving behind those critical trivialities, overcoming the power shortage and facing the challenge of surplus power generation, Bangladesh has been able to make its place in the list of lower-middle-class countries as a result of transforming the dream of implementing Digital Bangladesh into reality. 

Therefore, the voices of all the beneficiaries of Digital Bangladesh, from remote villages to cities, are resounding today, the Golden Bengal of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's dream and the Digital Bangladesh declared by the Desh Ratna Jananetri Sheikh Hasina, in the course of time, is no longer a dream but has taken shape in reality. 

In light of the announcement made by the government to build an information technology-rich digital Bangladesh, internet services, mobile money transfer, air tickets, e-tendering at the district and union levels, education, health, agriculture, trade, high-speed Bangabandhu Satellite-1, Payra deep sea port, Dhaka Metrorail, Bangabandhu Bridge, Padma Bridge, Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, and hundreds of flyovers have been built in Dhaka and most of the district cities of the country to reduce traffic congestion and accidents. 

The Bangladesh government has taken all groundbreaking steps to make the dream of Digital Bangladesh a reality. Union Digital Centers have been set up in 4,550 union parishads of the country with the intention of delivering government services through the use of technology at the grassroots level of the country. One of the largest national web portals in the world has been created. The number of these portals from the central level to the union level is about 25,000. 

All the upazilas of the country have been brought under the internet. Due to various steps taken in the field of telecommunications, the number of mobile phone subscribers in Bangladesh has increased to 123.7 million and the number of internet subscribers to 44.6 million. E-payment and mobile banking have been introduced to make the service delivery process easier and more transparent. The issue of conducting government procurement processes online has been institutionalized. Commercial operations of 4G technology mobile networks have been started. 

We have to make sincere efforts to deliver the benefits of information technology services and digital Bangladesh to the doorsteps of the people, so the people have to come forward unitedly to accelerate the development of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, only then will it be possible to turn this challenge of the Prime Minister into a reality.

Headline_English: Actor-turned-politician Thalapathy Vijay: He showed off his skills in politics
Content_Enlish:
Popular Tamil film hero Thalapathy Vijay has left his mark on the political arena with unprecedented success. Just two years ago, he created a new sensation in Indian politics by forming a political party and contesting the Tamil Nadu assembly elections. 

His party Tamilaga Vetri Kazhagam (TVK) has now emerged as one of the major political forces in the state. Joseph Vijay Chandrasekhar, who is known to his fans as 'Thalapathy Vijay', has been vocal about protecting public welfare and human rights since he formed TVK in 2024. 

In this election, Vijay's party won 107 seats out of 234 seats. Although they are slightly behind the magic figure of 118 seats required to form a government on their own, Vijay's position as the single largest party is now very well consolidated. 

If Vijay takes oath as the Chief Minister, then after a long 49 years, a film star will directly sit on this top seat in Tamil Nadu. Earlier, in 1977, legendary actor M. G. Ramachandran (MGR) had achieved the same feat. Although big stars like Jayalalithaa later became Chief Ministers, they came to power as the heirs of the party built by MGR. 

Vijay's specialty is that he is on the verge of reaching this milestone by forming a completely new party. His long-term political preparation began in 2009 by bringing his fan clubs under the banner of the 'Vijay Makkal Yakkam' organization. Although it initially worked as a social service, it was able to create a strong network at the grassroots level, which played a big role in this election. 

Vijay has become extremely popular among the younger generation due to his strong criticism of various decisions of the central government, including the Citizenship Amendment Act, and his bold stance on issues of public importance like unemployment and corruption. To prove his dedication to politics, he ended his successful three-decade acting career. 

His decision to leave the colorful world of cinema after acting in nearly 70 films sent a clear message to the voters that politics is not a hobby for him. Earlier, in the 2021 local government elections, his organization's candidates had proved by winning that Vijay's popularity is not limited to the cinema screen only, but is equally effective at the ballot box. 

In the election campaign, Vijay has presented himself as a leader who listens to the people, not just a traditional speaker. Even in the event of an unwanted stampede in 2025, his responsible role and mindset to correct mistakes further increased the voters' confidence in the party's discipline and accountability. Currently, Vijay's rise in the political equation of Tamil Nadu has emerged as a strong alternative to established parties like DMK and AIADMK.

Headline_English: Pakistan's opposition wants to come to power by relying on the military
Content_Enlish:
Pakistan is on the brink of a civil-military conflict. The country's civilian leadership, unable to deal with political opposition, sees the military as the main cause of this conflict. The country's opposition political parties are playing a strong role in creating hatred between the government and the army. 

Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan said that the army has been attacked by the opposition for the first time. It was mentioned in the protest rally that the opposition's attack is not focused on the military, but on the institution, but they are trying to establish a deep conspiracy based on the state. Especially after Chief General Javed Bajwa's three-year term extension, they showed the Khan government as a 'beneficiary'. 

The opposition would be happy if the army dissolved the national parliament and forced it to go for early elections. However, the road will be open for politicians and the army during the mid-term elections. Experts believe that this political instability will last for a few weeks, if not months. If Pakistan's economy is under severe pressure, the country may have a bad relationship with foreign donors. Because every country is already in the grip of Corona. In such difficult times of political instability and economic distress, the army is getting involved in remote-control government. 

The scandals with huge payments to the UK have become a nightmare for the Imran government. When it comes to international agreements and defaulting on any obligation, or blaming the past government and corruption cases, or taking 'any' decision against officials, these things cannot help any incoming government. 

Pakistan observers say, this can only act as a domestic political fuel/influencer. The internal discord of the 11-party Pakistan Democratic Movement (PDM) has been resolved, with Maulana Fazlur Rehman expected to distance himself from the Imran Khan government. PDM convener Maulana Fazlur Rehman had announced that the alliance would not only hold a "long march" against the Imran Khan government on January 20, 2021, but also against Imran 'supporters' and his alliance, but it is also reported that it could take place in Rawalpindi. 

Newly appointed Interior Minister Sheikh Rashid Ahmed on January 2 threatened to take punitive action against anyone "using derogatory language against the Pakistani army and state institutions" within 72 hours. The Pakistani government's response to this was comical. Pakistani media reported that the politician often uses such strong language, but the credibility of how effective this measure will be is very low. 

The PDM has remained united in its resolve during several protest rallies. However, its convener, the JI(F), has split and formed a new party. Perhaps Fazlur Rehman's comments about extending the "Long March" to Rawalpindi are being seen as a reaction to this development. A veteran Islamist politician, Maulana Fazlur Rehman has always been close to the army, but he is becoming as antagonistic as the Jamaat-e-Islami. Media reports indicate that he started the "Long March" in March 2020 with the 'assurance' of the army and in November he started his own party. 

The Islamists, as the agitators were part of the opposition, launched a serious agitation against the Imran Khan government. Najam Sethi, in his editorial in The Friday Times (January 1, 2021), said that PML(N) leader Khawaja Asif and, earlier, Nawaz's brother Shahbaz Sharif were arrested because they both maintained 'moderate' views. "He has portrayed the Imran government as a traitor to the army due to the opposition's attacks on the generals. 

Najm Sethi's advice to the army is to give space to the feelings of the people through more democratic political and economic management. Because the situation in Pakistan is becoming unstable day by day.

Headline_English: 50 years of victory and Bangladesh at the World Assembly
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh's victory on December 16, 1971 has opened up a new horizon of possibilities for us. Bangladesh has come a long way in the 50 years of victory. Bangladesh has achieved enviable success in various fields including poverty alleviation, expansion of education, women's development, and reduction of child and maternal mortality rates. Our beloved homeland is moving forward on the highway of development. The United Nations has recognized Bangladesh as a developing country. Initiatives have been taken to establish 100 economic zones across the country, including the construction of the Bangabandhu Tunnel, the construction of a deep seaport in Maheshkhali, and the Bangabandhu Industrial Park in Mirsarai. Electricity has now reached every home in the country. There has been amazing success in the production of rice, fruits, and fish. Bangladesh has positioned itself as one of the ideal countries in the world for the success of the children's vaccination program. 

Digital Bangladesh has created an example in the world by turning its dream into reality. It has been repeatedly discussed in the world for its unprecedented success in the agricultural sector. Bangladesh has already become a role model for the entire world in the areas of intensive integrated management of natural disasters, use of microfinance and success in poverty alleviation, tree plantation, positive changes in social and economic indicators, etc. According to the 2020 index, Bangladesh is now the 41st largest economy in the world. If the current economic development continues, Bangladesh will be the 25th largest economy in the world by 2035, according to the World League Table 2021 report of the British economic research organization Center for Economics and Business Research. According to the report, if the current trend of development continues, Bangladesh's economic position will be 25th among 196 countries in the world after the next 15 years. 

Bangladesh, which was once neglected, poverty-stricken; which the Western world used to mock as a 'bottomless basket'; as a result of the visionary, efficient, creative and courageous leadership of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh is today a wonder of the world, a role model of development. Bangladesh, which once suffered from identity problems, is now known to the whole world because of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu and his daughter, People's Leader Sheikh Hasina. Bangladesh, which started its journey empty-handed, now sends satellites into space, builds the Padma Bridge with its own money. The country, which started its journey by holding Bangabandhu's hand while standing on the rubble, has overcome many ups and downs and is now a wonder in the eyes of the world under the leadership of his daughter, People's Leader Sheikh Hasina. The dream of Golden Bengal that Bangabandhu showed us; that dream is being realized today under the leadership of his daughter, People's Leader Sheikh Hasina, by transforming the country into Digital Bangladesh, by upgrading it from a least developed country to a developing country, and by turning a food-deficit country into a food-surplus country. On the one hand, he has fought and struggled to establish human rights during his long four-decade political journey; on the other hand, he has taken significant and effective steps to change the fate of the people when he got the opportunity to govern the state and implemented them. 

Bangladesh is now one of the top five fastest growing countries. A centenary plan called ‘Bangladesh Delta Plan-2100’ has been adopted to achieve the desired development by confronting the challenges of climate change. Bangladesh is moving ahead at a fast pace towards the implementation of Vision-2021 and 2041. The people of the enclaves have been freed from the cursed life by implementing the 68-year-old unresolved land boundary agreement with India. 17,851 acres of land in 111 enclaves have been added to the borders of Bangladesh. The establishment of Bangladesh’s sovereignty over the maritime border has opened the door to the potential of the blue economy. About 131,098 square kilometers of sea area have been added to the borders of Bangladesh. 

Bangladesh has entered the era of space science with the launch of Bangabandhu Satellite-1. Despite hundreds of conspiracies, most of the work on the Padma Bridge has been completed with its own funding. The construction of a 2,400 MW nuclear power plant in Rooppur, Pabna is progressing rapidly. Eight coal-based mega projects with a capacity of 10,000 MW are being implemented rapidly in Payra, Rampal, Matarbari and Maheshkhali. Groundbreaking development is being achieved through the construction of four-lane, six-lane and eight-lane national highways, flyovers, metrorail, elevated expressways, marine drives, various important bridges, and the Bangabandhu Tunnel. Initiatives have been taken to install electric bullet trains on the Dhaka-Khulna, Dhaka-Rajshahi, Dhaka-Chittagong-Cox's Bazar routes. Chittagong port has been modernized. Economic activities have increased with the start of operations at Payra seaport in Patuakhali. With more than 90 million internet users, 4G mobile technology, machine-readable passports, online publication of exam results and admission process, introduction of e-tenders, digital service centers at the union level, e-commerce, etc., Digital Bangladesh is no longer a dream, but a reality. 

Bangladesh is now second in the world in garment exports, third in freshwater fish production, third in vegetable production, fourth in rice production, seventh in potato production, ninth in mango production, and 10th in food grain production. The standard of living of the marginalized population has been ensured through social security schemes including old age allowance, widow allowance, shelter project, one house one farm, and distressed allowance. 100 special economic zones have been established to attract industrialization and foreign investment. Closed jute mills and textile mills have been reopened. The government is steadfast in its zero tolerance policy against terrorism and militancy. The international community has highly appreciated the government's activities in suppressing terrorism and militancy. The trial of war criminals has been completed in the International Crimes Tribunal formed by the government. Religious freedom of all communities has been ensured. Bangladesh ranks 50th out of 153 countries in the Gender Gap Index and seventh in women's political empowerment. The construction of 100 special economic zones, more than two dozen high-tech parks and IT villages is progressing across the country. 

Bangladesh's position in the diplomatic field is strong in South Asia. Other countries are following Bangladesh in dealing with the impacts of climate change. Even the global pandemic of the coronavirus could not keep Bangladesh in check. The current government has been able to deal with this undesirable situation efficiently. Bangladesh is first in South Asia and 20th in the world in its ability to deal with corona. Disaster management, dealing with the damage caused by climate change, women's empowerment, provision of social security, controlling Covid-19 with great efficiency and providing vaccines for the people, surpassing many developed countries, etc. are exemplary for the world. In Bangladesh's development journey, the benefits of Digital Bangladesh have spread from cities to villages today. Broadband facilities are being provided to remote villages. Bangladesh has advanced four places in the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) Democracy Index-2020. With a score of 5.99, Bangladesh is ranked 76th out of 165 countries and two regions in the index. Bhutan is ranked 84th, Nepal is ranked 92nd, and Pakistan is ranked 105th in the list. Bangladesh's progress and position today in various indicators including socio-economic and infrastructural development is a role model for different countries of the world. 

Bangladesh was upgraded from low-income to lower-middle-income country by the World Bank on July 1, 2015. Bangladesh came to this list due to continuous improvement in per capita income growth. In March 2018, the United Nations Committee for Development Policy recognized Bangladesh as eligible for graduation from LDC. In February 2021, the committee made a final recommendation for Bangladesh to graduate. The United Nations has deemed Bangladesh worthy of graduating from LDC status based on its improvement in per capita income, education, health and other social indicators, and economic capacity. In 2026, Bangladesh will graduate from LDC status and join the ranks of developing countries like India, China and Malaysia that are not LDCs. In 2020, The Economist published a list of 66 strong economies, where Bangladesh ranked ninth. Bangladesh has captured the attention of the world by achieving many indicators of the Millennium Development Goals or MDGs. Bangladesh was able to reduce the poverty rate by more than the target of reducing it by 2015 in the MDGs. Bangladesh has received various international awards for achieving the MDGs. 

Nobel Prize-winning Indian economist Armatya Sen wrote in his book India: ‘Development and Deprivation’ that no one thought that Bangladesh would move forward on the path of social development so quickly. After independence, many people said that Bangladesh’s future was bleak. Some called it a ‘basket case’ and said that no economic aid should be given to this country. Because, it will not be able to keep up with the population explosion in food production. He further said that Bangladesh is not only doing much better than India in various conventional measures of quality of life, but has also gone far ahead. Bangladesh has surpassed India in many social indicators, such as: average life expectancy, infant mortality rate, vaccination rate, traditional fertility rate and even some measures of school education. The entire world is now considering Bangladesh as a 'role model' of development. Development researchers have awarded today's Bangladesh with various titles including 'role model of development', 'booming bull' of South Asia, a Bangladesh of endless potential. In the 50th year of victory, we see another dignified Bangladesh in the world assembly.

Headline_English: Google threatens to shut down search engine services in Australia
Content_Enlish:
Google has threatened to shut down its search engine services in Australia. The search engine has made such a threat at the start of Australia's initiative to enact legislation on giving profit sharing to the media. If the new law is implemented, Google will also be obliged to pay a profit margin to the country's publishers for news content. 

Not only Google, but also other technology companies including Facebook will come under the scope of this proposed law. According to BBC and AFP. 

A BBC report quoting Google said that if this law is passed, Google and Facebook will have to sit down with Australian news publishers and come to discussions to determine the price of content. 

At a hearing on this matter on Friday, Google Australia Managing Director Mel Silva said that the implementation of such a law would hinder Google's services in Australia. If the draft that is being discussed is passed as law, they will have no choice but to shut down Google search in Australia. 

Regarding Google's threat, the country's Prime Minister Scott Morrison said that his country's lawmakers will not back down from any threat. His government is committed to passing the law in parliament this year. Other Australian lawmakers have also described Google's statement as blackmail and a threat to democracy. 

Google has a monopoly in various countries around the world. Australia is no exception. The Australian government says that Google services have now become as essential as daily necessities. And the company has dominated the service market. They are making a lot of profits and Google should also give a share of the profits to news publishers. 

The Australian government has also explained the reason for the new law. According to their information, advertising in Australian print newspapers has decreased by 75 percent since 2005. As a result, many newspapers have closed down due to lack of funds. Many companies have laid off their employees. 

The managing director of Google Australia said that the law proposed by the Australian government is not compatible with the concept of the Internet and online. If this happens, it will not be possible to continue their services in Australia due to the financial and management risks that will be created.

Headline_English: New policy has come, WhatsApp will be deleted if not followed
Content_Enlish:
WhatsApp is one of the most popular messaging apps in the world. However, they have suddenly changed their privacy policy. All users will have to follow that policy. Otherwise, the messaging app may be deleted. 

On Tuesday, a notification came to the app for users of this messaging app. It said that WhatsApp is changing its privacy policy. Until now, whether it is an update or accepting the privacy policy, the 'Not Now' option was available for everything. That is, someone could accept that policy later. WhatsApp used to work fine. But now that is changing. The 'Not Now' option is not there in the new policy. The time to accept this policy is until February 8. If the policy is not followed within this period, the messaging app will be deactivated. 

What's in this new policy: 

Users are being given a non-exclusive, royalty-free, transferable license worldwide to use, reproduce and display the content they upload, submit, store, send or receive on WhatsApp. In addition, the messaging app will also offer several new services. For example, they will keep any images or messages forwarded by the user safe on their servers. So that they can be used later if needed. Even new facilities will be available in the case of WhatsApp payments.

Headline_English: Trump's YouTube account suspended indefinitely
Content_Enlish:
Former US President Donald Trump's YouTube account has been suspended indefinitely. At the same time, former president's lawyer Rudy Giuliani has been banned from updating information on YouTube. This news has come from various US media. NDTV reports. 

A week ago, social media announced the extension of the ban on various Trump accounts. Trump had millions of followers and subscribers on these channels. A week later, YouTube also announced the ban. These bans have been imposed in protest of the violence by Trump supporters on Capitol Hill on January 6 and Trump's indulgence in it. 

Google-owned YouTube, however, was the last to take action on Trump. Earlier, despite all the major media outlets taking measures, YouTube remained silent. However, they have also been criticized in various ways for this. 

The US newspaper Politico, citing a spokesperson for YouTube, said that Donald Trump's account has been suspended indefinitely due to the recent spread of various types of violence. At the same time, the measures imposed on Trump's lawyer Rudy Giuliani were also mentioned. 

The 76-year-old Trump posted offensive videos on his account about Biden's family scandal and the recent US election. His channel had 60 million subscribers worldwide. YouTube initially did not react to this, but criticism forced it to take action.

Headline_English: Bangabandhu's app 'Banga AR' coming on Wednesday
Content_Enlish:
Mobile apps 'Banga AR' featuring Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman will be inaugurated on Wednesday. 

'Banga AR' will start its journey with a grand inauguration at the Liberation War Museum in the capital. 

Innovative Science, the organization that makes these apps, is organizing a quiz and drawing competition to make the two-day event on March 17 and 18 more interesting and memorable. 

Jawad Khandaker, founder president of Innovative Science, said that by using the app, young people will get the opportunity to learn about Bangabandhu and the history of Bangladesh in depth. These apps will be one of the ways to see Bangabandhu in visualization. If you download the app, go to the specific option and click on any picture of Bangabandhu, a documentary will come up for each picture. 

He said that the documentary will have detailed background sound with visuals of the picture. Such apps have never been made in Bangladesh before. Notice.

Headline_English: The new iPhone is coming with the ability to make calls without a network
Content_Enlish:
Apple's next smartphone is rumored to be able to make calls or send messages without a cellular network. It is known that this facility will be provided by connecting to an artificial satellite or satellite. Bloomberg News. 

According to the report, Apple is planning to bring such a facility to the 'iPhone 13' smartphone to communicate with emergency services outside the coverage of the mobile network. 

Earlier, Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said on Sunday that the new iPhone will be able to connect to satellites. He often informs about various aspects of the company's upcoming products before Apple's announcement. His 'guesses' have proven to be relatively reliable. 

The next iPhone may have a facility called 'Emergency Message Via Satellite'. Through this, messages can be sent to emergency services and emergency contact numbers via satellite in places without a cellular network. These messages will have a fixed character limit and will appear in gray instead of the green icon of SMS or the blue icon of iMessage. If you send such a message to someone designated as an emergency contact, the message will still appear on their phone, even if they have the ‘Do Not Disturb’ mode activated. 

Another potential feature would allow iPhone users to notify emergency services in case of danger. According to a Bloomberg report, the phone will ask what kind of danger it is. It will ask if it is related to a car, boat, plane or fire. The user will also be able to send information such as their location and medical ID if they want. 

The next iPhone will also include the necessary components for satellite calling. However, that feature may not come to the iPhone until next year. That means that the features may not be available as soon as the next iPhone is released.

Headline_English: Facebook launches smart glasses
Content_Enlish:
If you can make phone calls, listen to music, or record videos on your glasses, it's not bad. If you have Facebook's smart glasses instead of conventional glasses, it's possible. Facebook has unveiled a new generation of smart glasses or smart glasses to give users a virtual world experience. 

In addition to the virtual experience of these smart glasses, created in collaboration with Ray-Ban manufacturer Essilorluxtica, you can listen to music, make phone calls, and record videos. Facebook's Ray-Ban Stories smart glasses have three microphones for calling. They have two 5-megapixel cameras, which can record a maximum of 30 seconds of video at a time. You can capture photos and videos by pressing the shutter button from the touch control. 

For safety, there is an LED light in front of the smart glasses. As a result, others will be able to understand if you capture photos or videos on your smart glasses. 

There is a touch panel on the frame of the smart glasses for music playback, calls, and volume control. It can store a maximum of 500 photos and 35 videos. It has a Snapdragon processor, 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz dual-band WiFi connectivity. There is a tapping facility to listen to music or control the volume. 

These smart glasses can be connected to smartphones running at least Android 8 and equipped with Bluetooth version 5. The battery and the glasses can be charged through the port through the case that comes with the smart glasses. 

The smart glasses will be available in black, blue, brown and green frames. The price will be between 26 thousand and 40 thousand taka.

Headline_English: Facebook outage: Telegram users increase by 70 million in 6 hours
Content_Enlish:
Seventy million new users have been added to the messaging service Telegram in just six hours. This is a new record in the history of Telegram. Basically, last Monday, Facebook-owned messaging services WhatsApp and Messenger were down for about six hours due to server complications. At that time, users joined Telegram as an alternative to WhatsApp and Messenger. 

Telegram CEO Pavel Durov confirmed this information to the media. 

Telegram and Signal are currently competing with Facebook's WhatsApp and Messenger on the messaging platform. In January this year, the number of regular users of Telegram exceeded 500 million. The platform's users are gradually increasing. 

Interestingly, Facebook has been linked to the sudden increase in the number of users on Telegram before. Last January, many users started joining Telegram due to WhatsApp's privacy policy. There were fears that this could violate the privacy of users. 

Meanwhile, Telegram is struggling to cope with the pressure as it adds billions of users in just a few hours. As a result, many Telegram users are complaining that they are not getting the desired speed. 

Acknowledging this, Telegram CEO Pavel Durov said that some users in the United States have experienced slow usage of Telegram as hundreds of millions of users try to sign up for Telegram at once.

Headline_English: Demand to build the world's fastest electric aircraft
Content_Enlish:
Rolls-Royce, the British aircraft engine manufacturer, has claimed to have built the world's fastest electric aircraft. The company recently announced this information in a statement. 

According to CNN, the aircraft has set a record for flying at a speed of 387.4 miles per hour (623 kilometers per hour), Rolls-Royce said in a statement. The statement also said that the aircraft named 'Spirit of Innovation' has set three world records so far. 

Rolls-Royce said that on November 16, the aircraft set a record for flying 1.86 miles at a speed of 345.4 miles per hour. It also took just 202 seconds to reach an altitude of 3,000 meters, which is one minute less than its previous record. 

The report says the aircraft flew 9.32 miles at a speed of 300 miles per hour at the UK Home Office's Military Aircraft Test Centre, setting another new record.

Headline_English: NASA rocket launches into space to save the Earth
Content_Enlish:
NASA has sent a rocket into space as an experiment to save the Earth from an asteroid strike. NASA has said that it will push the asteroid heading towards the Earth and change its trajectory. 

This may seem like science fiction. However, this experimental mission called DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) is happening in reality. The rocket of the SpaceX company founded by Elon Musk was launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, USA, at 10:21 am local time on Tuesday. Al Jazeera reports. 

This is the first such mission in the world. The mission aims to push the small 'moon-like' asteroid named Dimorphos, which is 160 meters in diameter, and change its possible trajectory. The Dimorphos satellite revolves around the 762-meter-diameter binary asteroid Didymus. Both Dimorphos and Didymus orbit the Sun. 

The rocket is expected to hit Didymus in the third quarter of 2022, when it will be 11 million kilometers from Earth. This will be the first time the satellite has come this close to Earth. 

“We are really trying to learn how to change the threat,” said NASA chief scientist Thomas Zuberchen, referring to the $330 million mission.

Headline_English: Home-made Nokia G-series smartphones launched in the market
Content_Enlish:
HMD Global Bangladesh has announced the launch of two models of Nokia Mobile's 'G' series, G-10 and G-20, in the Bangladesh market. These two sets are manufactured in a factory in Bangabandhu Hi-Tech City, Kaliakoir, Gazipur, Bangladesh. 'Vibrant Software (Bangladesh) Limited', a joint venture of UK-based company Vibrant Software and Union Group Bangladesh, has set up the first factory to manufacture world-famous Nokia brand smartphones in Bangladesh. The company has brought these two sets of advanced technology to the market to win the hearts of users with mobile phones made in the country. 

The launch of the 'Made in Bangladesh' Nokia phone for Bangladeshi customers was officially announced at a hotel in the capital on Thursday. 

Ravi Kunwar, General Manager (Pan Asia) of HMD Global, said, 'Today is a memorable day for us. Undoubtedly, the past year has been very challenging for us, but this time has given us the opportunity to think and prepare and take the next big step. The launch of the G-series phones is a milestone in our journey. 

The G-series phones are so perfectly coordinated that they act as problem-solving technologies. Both the G-10 and G-20 phones are capable of delivering three days of battery backup, the longest ever in a Nokia smartphone. The Nokia G-20 series is backed by Nokia’s signature ‘Android Promise’, which ensures up to three years of monthly protection and up to two years of operating system updates to keep a user’s data as secure as possible. 

Both models offer the option of unlocking the phone through fingerprint and user face recognition. Both these long-lasting phones feature an attractive 6.5-inch teardrop display. There is a brightness enhancement feature for viewing in bright light. 

The G-20 phone with four rear cameras has ample storage, an attractive 48-megapixel wide-angle back camera with Ojo surround audio to capture memorable moments. 

The Nokia G-10 mobile has a triple rear camera and an artificial intelligence-based shooting mode, through which it is possible to take very good pictures even in low light. So every moment can be saved with complete accuracy. 

The Nokia phone factory has been set up in Block 5 of Hi-Tech City, Gazipur. The factory built with modern technology is spacious and has two floors. The highest quality of the product is ensured through multiple verification systems. To ensure the highest quality product, each phone has to pass both automated and human-operated quality tests. 

Alvi Rana, Director of Union Group, said, 'It is a great honor for us to be a partner of a global brand like Nokia. We have set up the factory in the European style under the guidance of HMD Global. "Consumers will definitely get handsets made in Bangladesh at affordable prices and will help Nokia increase its market share in the smartphone market in the country." 

Initially, the factory will assemble 300 phones per day. The factory has a total of 6 production lines, including 2 packaging and 4 assembly. The factory, which has its own laboratory, is self-contained with all the necessary infrastructure and has about 200 employees. 

Locally manufactured Nokia smartphones will be available at a price 30 percent lower than imported phones. The Nokia G-10 has been priced at Tk 13,499 and the G-20 at Tk 14,999.

Headline_English: Digital hospital to provide free healthcare to trafficking victims
Content_Enlish:
Digital Hospital will provide free healthcare to victims of trafficking. The organization has been providing them with various digital healthcare services and is working on rehabilitation. 

Bangladesh-based innovative digital hospital is working to make quality healthcare accessible and affordable for all. The organization is working in partnership with the Swiss-funded Winrock International-run Aashwa project. 

The three-month health package Swadhin (provided by Digital Hospital) includes free 24/7 doctor calls for up to 150 minutes per month (for both the user and his family) as well as free health cashback of up to one lakh taka as hospital stay coverage, 5000 taka as Covid-19 isolation coverage and 1600 taka as OPD coverage. 

The package also includes up to 35 percent discount on products/services at more than 1,000 hospitals, pharmacies and diagnostic centers across the country. 

In addition, beneficiaries have the opportunity to receive appointment-based consultations with specialist doctors for various health problems, health camps and online training. 

By the end of the project in 2022, Aasha plans to help a large segment of trafficked men and women return to normal lives. This includes providing affordable and quality health services to ensure better health of the beneficiaries. 

Health services will be provided in collaboration with social protection partners such as Caritas, Pragati Sanstha, Center for Women and Children Studies (CWCS), Dhaka Ahsania Mission (DAM) and Rights Jessore. 

Andrew Smith, CCO and co-founder of Digital Hospital, said, “Most trafficked people suffer from mental and physical trauma. They face various problems in social and family life rehabilitation (due to social evils), which is one of the main conditions for a healthy and normal life. Aasha is working to support these women and men with counseling, legal services and economic empowerment. And now, Digital Hospital has joined hands with Aasha to provide essential health services to victims of human trafficking. 

The project is currently operating in five districts with high incidence of human trafficking. The districts are Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, Khulna, Satkhira and Jessore. Press Release

Headline_English: Nagad is working to make digital services universal
Content_Enlish:

The company is playing a role in improving the quality of life of all the people of the country by making digital services universal. 

Nagad's Managing Director (MD) Tanvir A Mishuk expressed his opinion about their goals in an exclusive interview with Samakal on Saturday regarding Nagad's role in implementing the vision related to this on the 'Digital Bangladesh' Day 2021. 

He said, at the speed we are moving, we will have no problem establishing ourselves among the developed world before 2041. 

Tanvir A Mishuk said, making a profitable company is not our main goal in any case. Rather, the main goal is to ensure the touch of digital services in the daily lives of the common people through permanent foundations. 

He said, Nagad introduced e-KYC for the first time in the country. This was the best success in our opinion. Financial inclusion has been made easier by starting the account opening process from any mobile phone by dialing *167# within a few days. 

Talking about the country's MFS market, Tanvir A Mishuk said, "Thinking about the people of the country, we are working with the goal of providing the best service at the lowest cost. We just want the people of the country to come under the ambit of financial inclusion. In the meantime, Nagad has brought more than five crore people into financial inclusion. Now we are focusing on the micro SME level. This category of people is still not involved in formal financial transactions in that way. 

Expressing his determination to build a cashless society, he said, "If we are to move towards a cashless society, the most important thing for us is to give people freedom in financial transactions." He said, "We are thinking of bringing something new through which a person, especially a person at the micro SME level, can easily stay connected to the economy." 

Talking about the future, Tanvir, co-founder of Nagad, said, "We are in a good position in the market. We have been able to break the monopoly of the market." In the past 200 years, the Postal Department could not make a profit, we have made a profit. Regarding the formation of the country's first digital bank, he further said, the establishment of a digital bank will change the picture of the country's financial sector. And although the scope of mobile financial services needs to be increased, there are many requirements for digital banks. 

Regarding Nagad's future steps, Tanvir A Mishuk said, there is still a lot to be done. He wants to establish Nagad as the country's national wallet in the future. He also expressed his strong belief that Nagad will play a significant role in the country's economic transformation and fulfilling the dream of Digital Bangladesh through the use of its modern technology in the future.

Headline_English: Hackers monitoring 50,000 people on Facebook
Content_Enlish:
Hackers used Facebook to monitor about 50,000 people around the world. Spying companies from various countries, including India and Israel, were involved in this work. 

Facebook's parent company Meta released this information on Thursday. AFP reports. 

Meta said that the companies monitored rights activists, dissidents and journalists in about 100 countries. For this, about 150 pages and accounts have been closed on Facebook and Instagram. These pages were mainly used to steal information. Seven companies used these accounts and pages. 

Meta sent a message to increase surveillance on hacking companies through this new step. 

Meta took this step at a time when US lawmakers and President Joe Biden have stepped up action against hacking companies. As part of this step, the United States has imposed sanctions on the Israeli spying software maker NSO Group. Meta has also filed a lawsuit against NSO in court. 

Nathaniel Gleicher, head of Meta's security policy department, said that action is being taken against not only NSO, but also companies that work to create software for eavesdropping. 

However, neither Facebook nor Meta has given any explanation about how these eavesdropping companies were found. 

Among the companies taken action are Israel's Black Cube, India's Beltrox. In addition, Facebook has deleted the accounts of Israeli companies Cobwebs Technologies, Cognite, Bluehawk CI. In addition, the accounts of North Macedonia's Citrix and another Chinese company have also been deleted.

Headline_English: Teletalk's 5G operations face initial setbacks
Content_Enlish:
The 5G trial activities of state-owned mobile phone operator Teletalk have stumbled from the beginning due to an unpleasant incident at the inauguration ceremony. Invited officials of three world-renowned companies were prevented from entering the event held at a hotel in the capital on December 12. It is alleged that several officials of Chinese company Huawei, the main partner of Teletalk's 5G trial activities, obstructed this. In the meantime, another Chinese company ZTE has filed a written complaint of serious misconduct against several Huawei officials in this incident. Due to the incident that day, Teletalk's other partner companies have not yet started 5G trial activities. This information has been revealed by relevant sources. 

Huawei is a private Chinese company and ZTE is a state-owned company. Invited officials of Korean company Samsung were also not allowed to enter the event that day. At the same time, Teletalk's other partner European company Nokia also did not start 5G trial activities due to the discourteous behavior of Huawei officials. Responsible sources said that they are going to organize a separate inauguration ceremony again.

There is a stir in the Posts and Telecommunications Department over the whole issue. Posts and Telecommunications Minister Mustafa Jabbar told Samakal that the issue of misconduct by Huawei officials has been taken very seriously. Appropriate action is being taken in this regard. He said that Huawei is a good organization, the quality of their equipment is good, they also cooperate in various works. Such behavior was not expected from them in any way. 

He also said that initially Teletalk was supposed to launch 5G trial activities in a total of 10 sites. But since Samsung and ZTE did not come, now the trial activities have to be started in six. 

According to sources, Teletalk organized the inauguration ceremony of Teletalk's 5G trial activities at Hotel Radisson on December 12. Huawei was the sponsor of this event. The invitation letter for the event was signed by the Posts and Telecommunications Secretary as the chairman of the company. But at the beginning of the event, Huawei prevented the use of the logo of not only Huawei but also other partner Nokia on the banner of the event. That is why none of the Nokia officials attended the inauguration ceremony. On the evening of December 12, the CEO of ZTE, Huawei's main competitor in the telecommunications sector in Bangladesh, was invited to attend the event. Huawei officials stopped him at the entrance to the second floor of the Radisson Hotel. When the ZTE CEO showed the invitation, a Huawei official snatched it and tore it in front of him. At that time, when a senior Teletalk official asked why he had stopped an invited guest, two Huawei officials got into an argument with him. The Teletalk official and the Huawei official also got into a scuffle. At one point, when an official from the ministry arrived, Huawei officials also prevented him from entering. 

Responsible sources at Teletalk said that although the incident that day did not directly affect the 5G trial activities, Huawei's dispute with other equipment suppliers could create a major crisis in Teletalk's full 5G activities in the future.

Headline_English: Black fungus or mucormycosis
Content_Enlish:
Black fungus disease has nothing to do with coronavirus. Black fungus is a rare fungal disease and corona is a viral disease. If black fungus appears in the body, more than 50 percent of patients are at risk of death if not treated quickly. Therefore, it is important to know and be aware of this terrible disease. 

As soon as the fear of coronavirus subsides, black fungus or mucormycosis has brought a new nuisance. There are various rumors about black fungus on social media. Black fungus is not a new disease in Bangladesh, its infection has been observed in uncontrolled diabetes patients before. Hopefully, today's article will clear up many misconceptions and will be helpful in surviving this rare disease. Black fungus disease has nothing to do with coronavirus. Black fungus is a rare fungal disease and corona is a viral disease. If black fungus appears in the body, more than 50 percent of patients are at risk of death if not treated quickly. Therefore, it is important to know and be aware of this terrible disease. 

How does black fungus spread? 

This disease is not contagious; therefore, it cannot be transmitted directly from one person to another. The only way this type of fungus can infect the body is by touching it. Fungi usually grow in an unclean and damp environment. First, the fungus infects the bones of the face (forehead, nose, eyes, and even teeth). The lungs are affected, and skin problems, eye problems, and even vision loss can occur. In severe cases, it can spread to the brain through the blood, and if not treated quickly, 30-50 percent of patients may die. 

Who is more likely to be affected by black fungus disease 

- Uncontrolled diabetes, diabetic ketoacidosis patients are more likely to be affected by black fungus disease. 

- Black fungus disease is more common in patients with cancer or long-term physical illness who are bedridden. 

- Patients taking immunosuppressants, anticancer treatments, and steroid drugs for a long time are more likely to be affected. 

- Severe COVID patients who are on oxygen or ventilator support are more likely to be infected with black fungus. The use of oxygen cylinders and ventilators in unclean and humid environments is increasing the risk of this disease. 
Symptoms 

- Sores/black spots, swelling or pain on the face, nose, forehead, eyes and teeth. 

- Abnormal black discharge may occur, and even blood may flow from the nose. 

- Difficulty breathing, headache, eye pain, swelling around the eyes, double vision, redness of the eyes, difficulty seeing, difficulty closing and opening the eyes. 

- Difficulty chewing or opening the mouth. 

- Teeth may become loose. Some parts of the gums, nose and mouth may swell and even have holes. 

Ways to avoid black fungus It is very easy to avoid this terrible disease. 

- Keep yourself clean and keep the environment around you clean. 

- Keep diabetes under control. 

- Do not take medicines, especially antibiotics, painkillers and steroids, without a doctor's advice. Avoid steroid medicines unless absolutely necessary, and if necessary, take them for a very short time. 

- Eat healthy food to increase immunity. Exercise regularly. 

- If symptoms appear, seek medical attention as soon as possible. 

What is the relationship with COVID-19? 

COVID-19 is a disease caused by coronavirus. One of the many causes of black fungus infection is COVID-19. Polypharmacy (use of unnecessary medicines, especially antibiotics and steroids) in the treatment of COVID-19, decreased immunity, use of oxygen cylinders and ventilators in unclean and unsanitary environments, causes this fungus to settle and spread quickly, causing black fungus disease. 

We try to overcome diseases without fear. Many diseases can be avoided by keeping ourselves and our families clean, keeping our homes and workplaces clean, eating healthy foods, controlling diabetes, and not taking medications without the advice of a registered doctor.

Headline_English: Things to do to avoid insect infestation during the monsoon
Content_Enlish:
During the rainy season, insect infestation becomes the most annoying thing in wet and humid conditions. These pests not only spoil food and furniture, but also have some impact on human health. At this time, you can follow some things to keep your furniture safe and yourself safe from harmful insects. For example- 

Neem leaves and black cumin: These two ingredients, known as natural pesticides, give very good results. Keep dry neem leaves or black cumin tied to a cloth in kitchen cabinets, cupboards, bookshelves, and various shelves and cabinets in the house. The insects will go away. 

Lavender oil: The aroma of lavender is very useful in preventing insects. Especially, this oil works well in repelling mosquitoes. Take one cup of water in an empty shampoo bottle and mix three spoons of lavender oil in it. Then shake it well and spread it in every corner of the house. 

Mint leaves: First boil a handful of mint leaves in water. Then cool it and spray it in all the places where there are spider webs in the house. You can also spray a mixture of mint oil and water. 

Tea tree oil: Mixing tea tree oil with water and spreading the mixture around the house will reduce the pest infestation. It is even very effective for bedbugs during the monsoon. 

Eucalyptus oil: No insect, even rats, can tolerate the pungent smell emanating from the eucalyptus tree. So, fill an empty shampoo bottle with a cup of water, mix one teaspoon of lemon oil and two teaspoons of eucalyptus oil in it and shake it to make a mixture. Spraying this mixture around the house and in the basin will help you stay away from insects during the monsoon. 

Bleaching powder: Spread bleaching powder and carbolic acid around the house every other day. In addition, to avoid corona infection, keep the floor of the house, the places that come into contact with hands more often, clean by mixing bleaching powder in water. 

Camphor: Using camphor is the easiest and most common way to repel mosquitoes and flies. Soaking a few pieces of camphor in half a cup of water and keeping it in a corner of the house reduces the nuisance of mosquitoes and flies to a great extent. Pour boric powder on the doors and windows to get rid of ants. Also, take a cup of coconut oil, mix camphor powder with it and sprinkle it in different parts of the house. 

Kerosene oil and dustbin with a lid: Mix soap and kerosene oil in hot water and spray it under the bed and in every corner of the house. Insect infestation will be reduced. Using a dustbin with a lid in the kitchen will eliminate the problem of flies. Clean the dustbin regularly after use. 

Phenyl: It is important to clean the floor of the house every day. Using phenyl or antiseptic liquid to wipe the house will greatly reduce the number of insects. 

Savlon and vinegar: Wipe the kitchen with savlon and vinegar. To reduce the nuisance of ants, put boric powder on the windows and doors. Vinegar is rich in acetic acid, the smell of which scares spiders away. For this, first mix 1 cup of white vinegar and 1 cup of water in a spray bottle and spray it all over the house. Spray more often where there is a lot of spider infestation. 

To protect against various insects that come out of the basin and commode during the monsoon, mix savlon in hot water and pour it into the commode, basin and kitchen sink every few days. Make sure that the water of savlon must fall directly into the pipe. Otherwise, the commode or basin may crack. 

However, be careful when using chemicals to repel insects. Some chemicals not only make you uncomfortable but can also be harmful to your health. So try to repel insects naturally during the rainy season.

Headline_English: What kind of food to eat to strengthen bones
Content_Enlish:
Bones are one of the most important parts of the body. If the bones are weak or if there is any problem with the bones, problems also arise in the physical structure. Only increasing the immune system is not enough for good health, besides this, strengthening the bones is also very important. Due to weak bones, fractures or broken bones can often be observed with a minor injury. In addition, various bone diseases like arthritis, osteoporosis can also occur. For this reason, some foods should be added to the diet that can strengthen the bones. For example- 

1. Calcium is considered the most essential nutrient for bones. Calcium strengthens bones, helps in bone maintenance and facilitates other important physical functions including muscle control and blood circulation. However, the body cannot produce calcium on its own. The body absorbs calcium from the foods in the diet. So add calcium-rich foods such as milk and dairy products, broccoli, oatmeal, soy, green vegetables, nuts, figs, etc. to the diet. 

2. Vitamin D helps in building bones and absorbing calcium from food. The best source of vitamin D is sunlight. In addition, foods like mushrooms, egg yolks, fatty fish and soy milk are also one of the sources of vitamin D. 

3. Vitamin C helps in the development of healthy bones. Various types of citrus fruits, such as oranges, grapefruits, lemons, strawberries, broccoli and bell peppers are excellent sources of vitamin C. 

4. Vitamin K is very effective in building strong bones. Vitamin K is very important in increasing bone density. It is very necessary for those who have weak bones. This vitamin helps in preventing bones from breaking easily. Basil leaves, thyme, parsley, lettuce, cabbage and cauliflower are good sources of vitamin K. 

5. Magnesium plays an important role in the structural development of bones and makes bones stronger. Magnesium deficiency is observed in most of the elderly. Dark chocolate, avocado, green vegetables, pumpkin seeds, bananas, are excellent sources of magnesium. 

6. Adequate daily protein intake helps the body absorb calcium and prevent the risk of osteoporosis. Protein helps strengthen bones. Adequate amounts of protein are available in foods such as milk, yogurt, cheese, soybeans, eggs, oats, broccoli, meat, tofu, etc. 

7. Phosphorus is one of the nutrients that helps in calcium absorption. Therefore, to strengthen bones, the presence of phosphorus-rich foods in the diet is very important. Fish, meat, dairy products, avocado, grapes, figs, bananas, etc. are excellent sources of phosphorus.

Headline_English: Which egg is more nutritious - duck or chicken?
Content_Enlish:
Everyone knows about the nutritional value of eggs. Some people like to eat duck eggs, some chicken eggs. Some people do not like duck eggs because they have a slightly fishy smell. Many people have a dislike for chicken eggs. According to experts, both duck and chicken eggs are beneficial for the body. However, there are some differences in nutritional value between these two eggs. For example: 

1. Every 100 grams of duck eggs provide 185 kilocalories of energy. On the other hand, 100 grams of chicken eggs contain 149 kilocalories of energy. Although the amount of carbohydrates and minerals is equal, duck eggs contain more protein. Manganese, copper, potassium, sodium, selenium, phosphorus, calcium and iron are found in both types of eggs. However, all the ingredients are present in duck eggs in higher quantities. Duck eggs also have more nutritional value. In addition, every 100 grams of duck eggs contain 181 kilocalories of nutritional value. On the other hand, chicken eggs have 173 kilocalories of food energy. Duck eggs have 13.7 grams of fat, while chicken eggs have 13.3 grams. 100 grams of duck eggs contain 70 milligrams of calcium, 3 milligrams of iron, and 269 micrograms of vitamin A. On the other hand, chicken eggs contain 60 milligrams of calcium, 2.1 milligrams of iron, and 299 micrograms of vitamin A. 

2. The main difference between duck eggs and chicken eggs is that duck eggs are about 50 percent larger. Duck eggs also look a little different. Duck eggs are good for a long time because ducks usually lay eggs near water, so the outer part of duck eggs is hard. Due to their hardness, the eggs are good for a long time. They do not break easily. 

3. The yolk of duck eggs is larger than that of chicken eggs. It also contains more fat. 

4. Duck eggs have more protein than chicken eggs. Duck eggs contain 13.5 grams of protein per 100 grams, while chicken eggs contain 13.3 grams. Those who are allergic to chicken eggs can eat duck eggs. 

5. Duck eggs are rich in omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins A and D, and iron. 

6. Chicken eggs contain 3.1 grams of saturated fat per 100 grams. On the other hand, duck eggs contain 50 percent more monounsaturated fat than chicken eggs. Duck eggs contain more amino acids than chicken eggs. However, chicken eggs also contain amino acids such as threonine, isoleucine, tryptophan, leucine, methionine, lysine, cystine, tyrosine, valine, serine, glycine, proline, aspartic acid, histidine, alanine, and arginine. 

According to nutritionists, duck eggs are more beneficial than chicken eggs in terms of nutritional value. Because they contain more nutrients than chicken eggs. However, duck eggs contain more cholesterol than chicken eggs. The cholesterol content in every 100 grams of duck eggs is 884 milligrams, while chicken eggs contain only 425 milligrams. Therefore, if someone has heart disease, it is better not to eat duck eggs. In addition, if you follow a high protein diet, you should eat only the white part of duck eggs.
