Headline_English: What to do to relieve ear congestion
Content_Enlish:
Ear congestion often occurs due to sneezing, cold, cough, sore throat, and cold. Many people take ear congestion lightly; but it is not at all. This condition of ear congestion can quickly cause inflammation or infection in the middle ear, that is, the inside of the eardrum. Ear congestion means the ear is closed, not hearing anything. Although the issue is reduced with medication; but this ear problem is not at all mild. The eardrum divides our ear into the outer ear and the middle ear. This disease can cause inflammation on the inside of the eardrum, which is called O.M.E. for short. Middle ear inflammation can manifest itself in various forms. Sometimes there is a small amount of fluid in the middle ear, sometimes pus forms in the middle ear, and again this disease can manifest itself through pus in the middle ear and the eardrum coming out through the ear. 

>> Why does the ear get blocked/blocked? 
Auditory tube that connects the nose to the throat and ears. This tube balances the air pressure between the middle ear and the atmosphere. 

If this tube is blocked/does not work properly for any reason, water can accumulate in the middle ear and cause inflammation. Usually, due to sneezing, cold, cough or cold, the tube that connects the ear to the nose and throat is partially or completely temporarily closed. As a result, communication between the middle ear and the outside environment is disrupted. Bacterial infection or inflammation in the upper part of the respiratory tract can cause your ear problems. Therefore, seek treatment before colds and sinusitis become complicated. Otherwise, the middle ear can become inflamed and swollen and water can accumulate. 

>> Who can have this problem? 

Although this problem is usually more common in school-going children, anyone of any age can be affected. Children who have a habit of snoring can have water accumulate in their middle ear. The significant causes (Risk Factors) of this disease include: 

1. Frequent upper respiratory tract infections (URTI); such as: cold-cough-nasal congestion. 

2. Often allergic rhinitis/allergic rhinitis; 

3. Chronic tonsil infection; 

4. Enlarged lymph nodes called adenoids behind the nose in children; 

5. Curved nasal bones/chronic sinusitis problem; 

6. Viral infection. 

7. In addition, if there is a tumor in the nasopharynx behind the nose. 

>> What are the symptoms/what does the patient feel? 

* If the middle ear becomes inflamed due to fluid accumulation, the ear suddenly becomes blocked with a cold and cough. Many people call it clapping in the ear. 
* Suddenly there is a lot of pain in the ear. 
* There is a buzzing and buzzing sound in the ear (tinnitus). 
* There is reduced hearing in the ear. 
* If the infection is severe, the eardrum may rupture and blood-tinged fluid or pus may flow out of the ear. 

If such a problem occurs, you should consult an ENT doctor before complications arise. You can find out from the doctor what the current condition of the eardrum is, whether the membrane has ruptured or not. 

In such diseases, the doctor usually treats with antihistamines; age-appropriate nose drops; antibiotics if necessary through an ear exam. You can take paracetamol-like medications to reduce pain. And if you like to chew gum, then keep chewing gum in your mouth as advised by the doctor and chew it comfortably. This is a very quick and easy method of relieving ear congestion as part of the treatment. 

If the problem is not resolved after 12 weeks of drug treatment, ENT surgeons perform a small operation to puncture the eardrum and drain the fluid. Which is called myringotomy. So do not neglect such problems. Stay healthy and enjoy life.

Headline_English: Countries that like spicy food besides Bengalis
Content_Enlish:
It goes without saying that Bengalis are foodies. They eat with their mouths watering - be it biryani, pulao, korma or kalia. We have a divine array of delicious spice-based dishes that make your mouth water. 

Bengalis have an emotional connection with spices. We Bengalis are crazy about spices! But others are not far behind. There are people in many countries of the world who like spicy and hot food. 

Thailand 

Thai cuisine is one of the most popular cuisines in the world. Thai food is popular in almost all countries. Star fry, soup, curry - a lot of leaves or herbs and raw chilies are used to prepare such dishes. Among these, red chilies are used more. 

Apart from this, a lot of onions, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, mint leaves are added to the food to make it spicy. A vegetable and dried curry called 'Kaeng Tai Pla' is considered the spiciest dish in Thailand. Apart from this, various red curries of fish, meat or vegetables made with red chili paste are also quite spicy. 

Mexico 

Mexico is home to 140 varieties of chili! No food in this North American country is without chili. Many Mexicans even mix chili with alcohol. This country is the birthplace of the famous jalapeno, poblano, serrano, ancho and the infamous habanero chili. In Mexico, eating and tolerating excessive spicy food is considered a symbol of bravery. Mole, salsa, chiles reino, sopa de camarón, aguachile, chilate de payo, etc. are some of the spiciest dishes in this country. 

Malaysia 

Malay cuisine is a great combination of Chinese and Indian cuisine. A large amount of spices and various spices are used in various cuisines of this country. Otak Otak is said to be the spiciest dish in Malaysia. It is a bit like the Binni rice cake of Bangladesh. Otak Otak is made by mixing minced fish with many types of chili powder and spices and wrapping it in banana leaves. 

Korea 

As a result of globalization, many of us are familiar with Korean food culture today. Anyone can be surprised to see Koreans eating spicy food. They use a type of red chili paste called gachuzang in all their dishes. No Korean food can be imagined without gachuzang paste. 

Africa 

The use of spices and spices can be seen in the cooking of almost all African countries. For example, in Ethiopian cuisine, red chili powder called 'berbere' is added with various spices. Again, in Ghana, Liberia, and Nigeria, a paste called 'shito' is used in cooking, which is made with black pepper, palm oil, and aniseed, which looks almost like pepper. 

Jamaica 

Since most people in Jamaica are of African descent, they have a great affinity with hotness. The most famous jerk chicken here requires a large amount of pepper and spices. It is marinated with it. However, the hottest dish in this country is made with duck meat. Jamaican goat curry requires Scotch bonnet pepper, which is one of the hottest peppers in the world. Its Scoville heat unit (a unit of measuring hotness) is more than one million. 

China 

Apart from rice, fish, and biryani, the most favorite dish of Bengalis is Chinese. And why not? Tell me! Bengalis and Chinese have been living together since the 18th century. So it's only natural that Bengalis have a penchant for Chinese food. Some parts of China love spicy food. If you want to taste the real spice of China, head to the southwest and try dried green chilies and Sichuan peppers. Both of these give a zing that will please even the most hardcore spice lovers!

Sinus is a very common problem. Many people suffer from this problem. Sinus problems can be caused by various types of infections, allergies. This results in problems like headache, facial pain, runny nose and blocked nose.

Headline_English: Are light or dark colored egg yolks healthier?
Content_Enlish:
Eggs are a favorite food for everyone from children to adults. Some egg shells are white, some are reddish. Some are yellow, some are orange. Like the color of the egg, many people are in conflict about which color of yolk is more beneficial for health. 

According to researchers from the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), a 50-gram egg contains 72 calories and 4.75 grams of fat (of which only 1.5 grams is soluble). The amount of these nutrients is almost the same in white and red eggs. Therefore, whether red or white, the nutritional value or nutritional value of both types of eggs is almost the same. 

Most people think that the darker the color of the yolk, the healthier the egg. However, according to USDA researchers, the color of the yolk depends mainly on the chicken's diet. And the color of the egg yolk is orange due to the influence of a chemical called carotenoid. The more a chicken has the opportunity to roam in the open, the darker its eggs will be. In some farms, chickens are given food rich in carotenoids. As a result, the yolks of those chickens turn orange. According to researchers in the United States, the color of the yolk can be darker for two reasons. One is if the chicken has the opportunity to roam in the open and gets nutrition from natural food, and the second is if the chicken is fed a special type of food, its eggs can also be darker. 

Researchers say that the eggs of chickens that find nutritious food naturally contain much more vitamin E, vitamin A and omega-3 fatty acids than any chicken on the farm. And the color is also darker. To make the color of the yolk dark yellow or orange, many farm owners feed their chickens carotenoid-rich foods such as red capsicum. But that does not make much difference in the nutritional value or nutritional value of the yolk.

Headline_English: Replacing lost teeth
Content_Enlish:
There is a proverb among us, 'Bengalis do not give dignity to teeth if they have teeth'. Many people have teeth damaged due to dental caries for various reasons that even if they want to, they cannot save those teeth. Gum diseases such as gingivitis or periodontitis can cause teeth to fall out. In that case, the lost teeth need to be replaced. 

Extreme negligence is seen among many people here too. If a tooth is missing, many people do not give it importance, they think, what a loss it would be if one tooth was missing among many other teeth! But if a tooth is missing, many kinds of problems arise. Such as the neighboring teeth becoming crooked and moving, gaps forming between the teeth after a while, if the missing tooth is missing, the lower tooth or if the lower tooth is missing, the upper tooth falling down, the jaw bone (alveolar ridge) decaying, the vertical height (proportional height of the upper and lower jaws) decreasing, and many other problems arise.

In the past, dentures were used in the dental bonding method, which is known as removable partial dentures. This method was used so that the patient could remove and replace the loose tooth himself. Later, fixed teeth were fixed or permanently lost teeth were replaced with dental crowns (caps) and bridges. However, in this method, the teeth on both sides of the gapped tooth (the front teeth and the back teeth of the gapped tooth) are taken as supports, which are called abutments. These two support teeth have to be root canaled and cut and shortened to install the caps. Many people do not want to have two good teeth root canaled. Although it is not harmful if treated properly. 

The most modern treatment method in these cases is dental implants. Dental implants are a state-of-the-art treatment method, just like other body organ implants. In the dental implant method, there is no need to take the teeth on the sides as supports or abutments. Here, titanium implants are placed as artificial roots in the jawbone in the empty space, performing exactly the same functions as real teeth and looking exactly like real teeth. Dental implants have been popular as a tooth replacement method in developed countries for many years. Dental implants have many advantages.

Headline_English: Coconut water to prevent disease
Content_Enlish:
A glass of delicious coconut water will not only bring a touch of peace to the body and mind, you will be surprised to hear that it has a miraculous quality, which plays an important role in reducing weight and keeping you healthy and refreshed. 

Coconut water contains micronutrients, which boost our immunity and increase our resistance to diseases. Many of us do not know that the plant hormone cytokinin works as an anti-aging, anti-cancer. And the source of this hormone is coconut water. 

Coconut water is an important source of minerals, electrolytes and antioxidants. That is why it is accepted as a safe and healthy drink. If you are suffering from dehydration, then naturally calories will burn slowly, and easily available coconut water will eliminate this dehydration.

According to researchers, vitamin C plays an important role in weight loss.

Headline_English: Foods you can eat to protect your lungs during this time
Content_Enlish:
When the coronavirus enters the body, it attacks the lungs. For this reason, special care needs to be taken to keep the lungs healthy at this time. Because if the lung function decreases, the risk of life increases. 

According to experts, the role of food is important in keeping the lungs healthy. It is especially important for those whose lungs are already weak due to age or respiratory problems to be more careful about this. 

Experts have given special importance to some foods to keep the lungs healthy. According to the information of the 'American Lung Association', those with COPD or asthma-like diseases should eat more healthy fats instead of carbohydrate-like foods. However, experts also say that since carbohydrates are part of a balanced diet, they cannot be completely eliminated. Rather, the type of carbohydrates should be changed. 

Instead of simple carbohydrates, complex carbohydrates should be eaten. Vegetables that have less starch should be eaten more. At this time, the amount of potatoes, beets, pumpkins, carrots, etc. should be increased. In addition, eating flour bread instead of flour, brown rice instead of white rice will not only reduce lung damage, but will also keep weight and diabetes under control. In addition, to keep the lungs healthy, potassium-rich foods such as green vegetables, tomatoes, beets, potatoes, bananas should be eaten regularly. In addition, protein-rich foods such as fish, meat, eggs, milk, yogurt, lentils, chickpeas, etc. are also good for the lungs. 

According to researchers, in addition to eating and drinking according to the rules, eating some special foods increases the immunity of the lungs. For example, 

Onion and garlic: These ingredients reduce the tendency of inflammation, provide strength to fight against infections. In an article published in the 'Journal of Cancer Epidemiology' and 'Biomarkers and Prevention', researchers said that smokers who regularly eat raw garlic have a 40 percent reduced risk of suffering from various lung diseases. 

Ginger: The anti-inflammatory ingredients in it reduce inflammation. Regular consumption of a small amount of ginger root improves lung health. 

Green chili: Regular consumption of green chili improves blood circulation, reduces the risk of infection. 

Turmeric: Curcumin in turmeric reduces inflammation. 

Fruits and vegetables: Apples, guavas, cucumbers, and watermelon are all beneficial for the lungs. The flavonoids and vitamin C in apples and lemons increase lung function. 

Vegetables: Antioxidants and vitamin C in carrots, pumpkins, and bell peppers increase lung function. 

Different types of beans and seeds: Magnesium in different types of beans and seeds plays an effective role in increasing lung function. Vitamin E in flax seeds increases immunity. 

Apart from these, experts have emphasized drinking enough water and regular exercise to keep the lungs healthy.

Headline_English: Things that diabetic patients need to keep in mind while fasting
Content_Enlish:
The month of fasting is going on. During this time, diabetic patients should take more care of themselves, otherwise various physical problems can arise due to the decrease or increase in sugar levels. There are many symptoms of decrease or increase in sugar levels in diabetic patients. When the sugar level of diabetic patients decreases, they experience excessive sweating, chills, hunger, increased heart rate and dizziness. And when the sugar level increases, the patient's lips become dry and they start urinating frequently. Therefore, according to the advice of experts, diabetic patients should eat protein and fiber-rich foods during the fasting month. 

How to make Sehri for diabetic patients: 

Diabetic patients should eat foods that are digested a little late in Sehri. Usually, diabetic patients cannot eat parathas, but they can eat parathas made with less oil in Sehri. Haleem is also included in foods that are digested late. Due to the presence of meat and pulses in Haleem, fiber is available in large quantities, due to which they do not feel hungry for a long time. The stomach remains full. Avoid eating excess oil-spice-fried foods during Sehri. Do not eat custard or any kind of sweet food during Sehri. 

Diabetics should break their fast with dates: 

Diabetics can break their fast with dates. According to research, six grams of carbohydrates are found in a date. In addition, dates also contain minerals, fiber, phosphorus and potassium. Potassium helps in relieving fatigue. Fruit salad can be eaten during Iftar without sugar, cream and milk. A little lemon juice can also be given with fruits. Excessive consumption of oil, salt, red chili powder and sugary foods should be avoided. 

Diabetics can include fruits, vegetables, pulses, curd etc. in their diet during fasting. To eliminate dehydration, drink sugar-free drinks or as much water as possible. The effect of fasting for 14-15 hours has an effect on blood pressure. Therefore, diabetics should be aware of their blood pressure. It is also important to check sugar on time.

Headline_English: How to take care of plants in summer
Content_Enlish:
Not everyone may have their own space or roof, but they have a hobby of gardening. That is why many people these days grow not only flowers but also various types of vegetables on their balconies. However, in summer, the heat of the sun increases a lot, and the soil easily becomes rough. Then the plants need extra care. Things to keep in mind at this time are- 

1. Cut off the dry leaves of the plant regularly. If the tip of a leaf dries up, cut off that part. Because the plant has to put more effort into providing nutrients to that part. This has a detrimental effect on the entire plant. 

2. Take the plants with large leaves, such as rubber trees or fiddle leaf plants, to the basement of the house at this time. Keep them in a place where the sun will enter, but there will be no strong winds. Because the larger the leaves of the plant, the more moisture it needs. Therefore, it is better to keep these plants indoors rather than outside. 

3. You can spray neem oil to protect the plants from insects. 

4. This is the best time to plant brinjal or gourd in pots. Fill the tubs with cocopeat instead of clay. Since this type of soil is very loose, it is easy to grow plants from seeds. Sow the seeds of the plant one inch deep. After this, water them well and cover them with plastic in a separate place. After a week, when you see that they have 4-5 leaves, you should replant the plants in a larger tub. Now, mix fertilizer and other soil with the cocopeat to nourish the plants. After that, take care of them regularly. 

5. At this time, you can also plant mint leaves, Italian basil, and coriander leaves. You don't have to plant them in separate tubs and move them to a larger place later. You can spread the seeds in a large pot at once. 

6. If you want to get vegetables at the right time, you need to plan the garden accordingly. Find out in advance how long it takes for a vegetable to ripen. Plant the seeds accordingly. 

7. You can buy plant seeds online. You can also buy them from a nursery if you want. However, make sure that the seeds are free of insects. Because if there are insects, the tree will not grow from the seed at once, and on the contrary, the insects and spiders can harm other plants.

Headline_English: Things to avoid after waking up
Content_Enlish:
Many people's lives have changed in the Corona situation. Life is different now. If you arrange it in such a way that you get positive energy all day long. If you get up one day if you need to, it's okay, but if you do it one day and another, the physiological issues are completely messed up. So try to wake up at a specific time. Try to wake up early in the morning. Because at this time, the positivity of cosmic energy is very high. 

Many times we unknowingly bring our own danger. However, many things should not be done on an empty stomach at all. Let's take a look at the ones that will be useful if avoided. 

1. Painkillers 

Do not take any painkillers on an empty stomach. Even if you do not have the opportunity to eat a proper meal, you can eat at least two biscuits or dry muri. Taking aspirin, paracetamol or any other anti-inflammatory medicine on an empty stomach is very harmful. It can cause various types of physical problems including gastric bleeding. 

2. Chewing gum 

If you have a habit of chewing gum on an empty stomach, change this habit now. You are unknowingly inviting danger. This produces digestive acid and eating it on an empty stomach greatly increases the chances of gastritis. 

3. Do deep breathing 

After waking up, lie down straight for a while with your arms stretched out, then sit up. After waking up, sit up straight quietly and do deep breathing for a while. 

4. Refrain from drinking strong coffee or tea 

Never drink strong coffee or tea after waking up. This thing deprives your body of nutrients on an empty stomach. Drink a glass of water first on an empty stomach. Do not stay on an empty stomach for a long time after waking up. Especially women of the house start all the work on an empty stomach. Never do this. Eat some nutritious food first and then do your daily work. 

5. Drinking alcohol 

Do not drink alcohol on an empty stomach at all. As a result, the amount of damage to the body increases to a great extent. There is a possibility of rapid infection with kidney, liver, and heart diseases. You may also suffer from acidity and indigestion. 

6. Vitamin C fruits 

Avoid eating vitamin C fruits or fruit juices on an empty stomach. As a result, the stored citric acid creates gas in the stomach. 

7. Workout 

Many people think that exercising on an empty stomach will burn more calories. However, that is completely wrong. On the contrary, it reduces the body's energy and makes it difficult to exercise properly. It is better to exercise after eating enough and taking a break.

Headline_English: E-commerce customers will be refunded after receiving clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Content_Enlish:
The 214 crore taka of e-commerce sector customers stuck in the escrow service will start returning quickly after June 30. This money has been frozen by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the police. A letter has been sent to the Home Ministry to unfreeze it. The money can be distributed only after receiving their clearance. 

On Monday, after the second meeting of the 15-member committee formed by the Cabinet Division on e-commerce, Additional Secretary to the Ministry of Commerce AHM Shafiquzzaman told reporters this information. 

This committee was formed this month to bring e-commerce companies under supervision and monitoring and to protect the rights of consumers who have been cheated due to unethical business practices of e-commerce companies. Shafiquzzaman is the head of this committee. 

Shafiquzzaman said that a letter has been sent to the Home Ministry to return the 214 crore taka of e-commerce sector customers stuck in the escrow service. The money can be distributed only after receiving their clearance. In this case, 1 percent taka may be deducted as service charge. Since the money was paid online, it will be refunded online.

Headline_English: CPD recommends withdrawal of fuel price hike
Content_Enlish:
The private research organization Center for Policy Dialogue (CPD) has recommended withdrawing the increased price of fuel oil and bringing it back to the previous price. Analyzing the comparison with the international market of fuel oil, the organization said that the government's profit is more than its loss in the last seven years. In addition, there is no need to increase the price if the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) withdraws the duty at the sales and supply level. The decision to increase the price of fuel in the recovery process from the impact of Corona will put pressure on the general public. The recovery process of the economy will be delayed. 

CPD presented this recommendation and argument at a press conference on Wednesday. The press conference titled 'How much was the increase in fuel oil price necessary?' was held at the organization's own office in Mohammadpur in the capital. 

CPD Executive Director Dr. Fahmida Khatun highlighted the national and international market situation of fuel oil at the press conference. 

Honorable Fellow of the organization, Professor Mostafizur Rahman, said that from an economic point of view, increasing the price of fuel at a moment is not the right decision. It was not morally correct. It is also a wrong decision politically. CPD Research Director Dr. Khandaker Golam Moazzam, Senior Research Fellow Taufiqul Islam Khan and others also spoke at the press conference.

Headline_English: Service export earnings must be brought into the country within 4 months
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has set a deadline for bringing service export earnings to the country, just like goods. From now on, service export earnings will also have to be brought to the country within a maximum of four months. Accounts in cryptocurrencies or similar currencies cannot be opened for such earnings. 

A circular in this regard has been issued and sent to banks. 

To make it easier for service exporters and freelancers to bring their earnings to the country, the central bank had earlier allowed them to open merchant accounts with international market platforms in October. Apart from this, informal or 'notional' accounts are also allowed to be opened in licensed payment gateways of other countries. Legal earnings received through international market platforms or foreign payment gateways must first be deposited in the 'nostro' account of the bank that transacts foreign currency. After that, there are rules for depositing them into the customer's account. 

The circular states that the obligation to bring export earnings to the country within four months will also apply to service exports. This income will have to be brought through the notional account or merchant account operated abroad by the service exporter. Apart from this, accounts in any other currency, including cryptocurrencies, cannot be opened outside the country. The money received from export earnings cannot be used to make capital investments or portfolio investments abroad, or to purchase fixed or virtual assets. 

The concerned said that in recent times, exports of various IT and freelancing services, including software, have been increasing. At one time, there was no opportunity to bring such income into the country. However, in 2011, for the first time, foreign exchange-transacting banks were allowed to establish relationships with online payment gateway service providers (OPGSPs) abroad to repatriate income from the service sector on a small scale. The policy is being eased in phases.

Headline_English: Dollar remains unyielding despite Bangladesh Bank's increased sales
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank is selling a lot of dollars to meet the demand of banks. Even then, the price is increasing. Banks are now buying dollars from each other at a rate of 85 taka and 80 paisa. At the beginning of this month, it was 85 taka and 70 paisa. Last August, the rate in interbank transactions was below 85 taka. Meanwhile, importers have to buy dollars at 86 taka. And they have to spend 90 taka to buy each dollar in the carb market or open market. 
Stakeholders said that since last August, there has been an increased demand for dollars in the currency market. Due to the massive growth in imports and a decrease in remittances, many banks are struggling to meet the demand with the dollars they have. Remittances increased by 36 percent last fiscal year. However, they have decreased by about 20 percent in the current fiscal year until last October. Due to low supply, one bank is protesting at the central bank because it is unable to buy dollars from another bank to pay import liabilities. 
Bangladesh Bank sold its first 5 million dollars on August 19 after a long time. Then, in the three months up to November 18, it sold 1.822 billion dollars. In contrast, more than 15,600 billion taka has been deposited in Bangladesh Bank from the market, which is currently one of the reasons for the tension in the country's currency market. 
It is known that Bangladesh Bank has increased the sale of dollars to deal with the situation. Of these, 130 million dollars have been sold in the market in the last two weeks. On November 16, 70 million dollars were sold in one day. Even then, compared to the beginning of this month, the interbank rate per dollar has increased by 10 paisa to 85 taka and 80 paisa. Earlier, until August 3, the dollar rate had remained unchanged at 84 taka and 80 paisa for a long time. 
Along with the interbank rate, the cash dollar rate has also increased. Cash dollars are now being sold at up to 90 taka in the open market. After a long period of international travel being closed due to Corona, additional pressure has been created here as well. Banks are now selling cash dollars at 88 to 89 taka. However, many people buy dollars from the open market instead of going to the bank due to the additional hassle, service charges and the lack of opportunity to buy more than the specified limit. 
Former president of the top trade organization FBCCI, Shafiul Islam Mohiuddin MP, told Samakal that the dollar rate is market-based, but it is somewhat regulated. This regulation is imposed mainly because imports are higher than exports. However, nothing regulated in the economy is good. Of course, recently, the rate is being increased tolerably little by little. However, with the way the prices of goods are increasing in the international market, there will be no choice but to increase the dollar rate further in the future. 
A senior official of Bangladesh Bank told Samakal that considering the demand of the economy, there is no choice but to regulate the dollar rate. Because if Bangladesh Bank had not bought it when the demand for dollars decreased last fiscal year, it might have fallen to 70 taka. Then exporters and remittance recipients would have suffered. Similarly, if it had not been sold now and provided support in the market, it might have reached 90 taka that day. This would have increased the price of imported goods and put huge pressure on inflation. That is why balanced price fluctuations are encouraged. He said, due to Corona, there has been a huge demand in the international market after a long time. At this time, a slight increase in the dollar rate is a relief for export trade to survive in international competition. However, imports are higher than exports in Bangladesh. Therefore, attention is being paid to ensure that the increase in the dollar rate does not reach an unbearable level and create massive pressure on inflation. 
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Managing Director of Mutual Trust Bank, told Samakal that imports are increasing at a very high rate. On the other hand, remittances are decreasing. Again, many import liabilities that received one-year deferred benefits due to Corona are now having to be paid. That is why the dollar rate is increasing. He said, the prices of goods in the international market continue to increase. As a result, if the central bank had not supported the banks by selling dollars, the prices would have increased further. In addition, the central bank's supervision is also continuing at this time. 
According to Bangladesh Bank data, 18.72 billion dollars were spent on imports in the three months up to last September. Which is 47.56 percent more than the same period of the previous fiscal year. Despite this increase in imports, exports increased by 22.62 percent to $15.75 billion as of last October. However, as of October, expatriates have sent home an equivalent amount of $7.06 billion. This is 19.97 percent less than the same period of the previous fiscal year. This has put pressure on the balance of foreign transactions. The trade deficit has more than tripled to $6.5 billion in the first three months of the current fiscal year.

Headline_English: No scope to overstate reserves: Bangladesh Bank to IMF
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank is overstating its reserves by considering non-liquid assets - The IMF's observation that Bangladesh Bank is overstating its reserves is incorrect, the Bangladesh Bank said in a recent letter to the organization. The central bank said that foreign exchange reserves have been calculated in the same manner for a long time in accordance with international practice. In this case, there is no scope for overstating the reserves. 

It is learned that the IMF considers the six billion dollars provided to the Export Development Fund (EDF) from foreign exchange reserves and the $640 million given to the Payra Port Authority through Sonali Bank as non-liquid assets. For this reason, the organization questions the inclusion of these assets in the reserve account. The observation was made on the report based on last June. At the end of last June, Bangladesh Bank's reserves were $46.39 billion. 

Bangladesh Bank said that the net and gross of foreign exchange reserves are calculated separately. Loans given to EDF and Payra Port Authority are excluded from the net calculation. And since 1989, the money contributed to the Export Development Fund has been shown as gross reserves. The IMF or any other organization has not questioned this method so far. In addition, the size of the EDF fund has been increased to support the economy like other countries due to Corona. After April last year, two and a half billion dollars have been newly contributed to the EDF. 

An official of Bangladesh Bank told Samakal that reserves have been calculated in this way for a long time following the international system. It is not clear why they suddenly made such an observation. Their observation has been answered. 

He also said that if the financing of EDF and government projects cannot be shown as gross reserves, then the money allocated to the IMF's SDR cannot be shown here either. Therefore, their observation is not correct.

Headline_English: The news published quoting BSEC is not correct: Bangladesh Bank
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has said that some media reports that investment in bonds is being excluded from stock market exposure and that bank investment in the stock market will be calculated at market value are not correct. The central bank gave this information in a press release on Wednesday evening. 

The central bank said that detailed discussions were held with the delegation of the stock market regulator BSEC on other issues related to investment by scheduled banks and financial institutions in the stock market. However, no decision has been made in this regard. 

The press release said that the BSEC delegation was made clear to the delegation about some legal restrictions existing in the Bank Company Act 1991 and the Financial Institutions Act 1993 regarding investment by banks and financial institutions in the stock market. However, after the meeting, the news that was circulated in various media outlets quoting a representative of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission about some decisions being taken in that meeting is not correct. 

The press release further said that the pre-scheduled meeting with BSEC was held at the central bank office under the chairmanship of Bangladesh Bank Deputy Governor AKM Sajedur Rahman Khan. The meeting discussed the resolution of the complications created in the case of scheduled banks and financial institutions due to the formation of the Capital Market Stabilization Fund at the initiative of BSEC and the distribution of cash dividends from the profits of the relevant year despite the existence of accumulated losses. 

In addition, the meeting explained the issues of Section 35(1)(c) and Section 22 of the Bank Companies Act 1991 and Section 10 of the Financial Institutions Act 1993 and stated that it is not legal to transfer unclaimed funds of banks and financial institutions to the Capital Market Stabilization Fund and to pay cash dividends despite the existence of accumulated losses. 

Bangladesh Bank has requested to bring necessary amendments to the BSEC directive in this regard. 

The stock market has been falling for eight consecutive working days from November 21 to Tuesday due to various issues. More than 90 percent of the shares lost their prices. This caused the main price index DSEX to fall by 388 points or 5.5 percent. 

But after the news that the meeting was positive and that Bangladesh Bank had agreed to bring amendments to some of the outstanding issues, the market prices of 293 out of 373 shares and mutual funds traded on the DSE on Wednesday increased, while only 45 decreased and 35 remained unchanged. 

As a result, the main price index DSEX rose by 143.75 points to 6,847 points. However, share turnover decreased by Tk 44 crore to Tk 1,102 crore.

Headline_English: Bangladesh ranks sixth in the world in sending migrants, eighth in receiving remittances
Content_Enlish:
Despite the Corona pandemic, Bangladesh became the sixth largest country in the world in sending migrants and the eighth largest in receiving remittances in 2020. The amount of remittances sent in 2020 increased by about three billion US dollars or about 32 thousand 700 crore taka compared to 2019. The amount of remittances received from abroad in 2019 was about 18 billion US dollars or 1 lakh 56 thousand 600 crore taka. And in 2020, the amount of remittances added to the Bangladesh economy was 21.76 billion US dollars or about 1 lakh 89 thousand 312 crore taka. 

This information was given in the 'World Migration Report 22' of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) published on Thursday. The report also said that there was a 60 percent decrease in air passengers in 2020 compared to 2019. 

The report said that despite global movement controls and travel bans due to the COVID-19 pandemic, internal displacement due to disasters, conflicts and violence has increased dramatically. According to the report, the number of international migrants has increased from 84 million (84 million) worldwide in 1970 to 281 million (281 million) in 2020, which is 3.6 percent of the total world population. So far, most people worldwide (96.4 percent) live in the country where they were born. 

The report says that in 2020, the number of internal displacements due to disasters, conflicts and violence increased to 45 million. In 2019, the number of internal displacements was 31.5 million. The number of passengers by air worldwide has decreased by 60 percent. The number of passengers in 2019 was 4.5 billion, which stood at 1.8 billion in 2020. 

The report, giving information on Bangladesh's migration, says that in 2020, the number of Bangladeshi migrants living worldwide was 7 million 40 thousand. Even though they live outside Bangladesh, the expatriates play an important role in the development of the country. Bangladeshi migrants from different countries of the world sent more than 18 billion US dollars to the country in 2019, of which 73 percent are expatriates The remittances came from workers who work mainly as low-skilled workers in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. And in 2020, $21.76 billion in remittances were added to the Bangladeshi economy. Here too, the number of low-skilled workers from the GCC countries is high. 

Assessing the migration sector in Bangladesh, Fatima Nusrat Ghazzali, Officer-in-Charge of IOM Bangladesh, said in a statement that despite the negative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on remittance flows, remittance flows to Bangladesh increased in 2020, which proves that migration has become an important part of Bangladesh's development. Migrants migrate for better economic, social and security conditions in their destination countries and then help improve the quality of life in their home countries. 

About the report, IOM Director-General Antonio Vitorino said, “This year, while preparing the report, we have noticed a paradox that has not been seen before in human history. That is, billions of people are stranded due to COVID-19. Travel restrictions have reduced travel. But Despite this, millions of people have been displaced, leaving a large number of people homeless. 

The report's editor, Mary McAuliffe, said the 11th edition of the World Migration Report series highlights migration trends through an analysis of the latest data and information on migration and explains new aspects of migration policy.

Headline_English: 25 percent tariff on garment exports to Indonesia takes effect
Content_Enlish:
Indonesia has taken safeguard measures against the import of ready-made garments and clothing accessories from various countries, including Bangladesh. As a result, a 25 percent duty has been imposed on Bangladeshi garments. Until now, the country had duty-free benefits for garment exports. Except for 8 types of hats and ties, all other types of garments are covered by this measure. The decision to take this safeguard measure for three years has been effective from November 12. This information has been reported from the Ministry of Commerce.

Export entrepreneurs believe that there is no reason for Bangladesh to be worried about this move by Indonesia. The country is not on the list of significant markets for Bangladeshi garments. According to the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) and BGMEA, it can be seen that only about 30 million dollars worth of garments go to Indonesia annually. 

Mohammad Hatem, executive president of BKMEA, an organization of ready-made garment manufacturers and exporters of knit category, told Samakal that Indonesia itself is a garment exporting country. That is why very few garments go to the country from Bangladesh. As a result, Bangladesh will not have any problems with this safeguard measure.

It is known that Indonesia has taken this step to protect the local garment industry. Before taking this step, the country's Safe Guard Committee (KPPI) visited Bangladesh. The committee recommended taking steps to impose tariffs to protect the local garment sector. After seeing the infrastructure and capacity of the country's garment sector on the spot, KPPI members said that Indonesia does not have the capacity to compete with the Bangladeshi garment sector. As a result, the free entry of Bangladeshi garments into the Indonesian market can be controlled to some extent through safeguard measures. The same argument has been made in the case of other garment exporting countries.

10 years ago, Turkey similarly took safeguard measures in the interests of the local garment industry. However, as it is one of the largest importers of Bangladeshi garments, exports to the country decreased.

Headline_English: Revenue must be collected without causing hardship to taxpayers: Finance Minister
Content_Enlish:
Revenue should be collected without causing hardship to taxpayers. Revenue collection can be increased by simplifying the rules and regulations for paying taxes and expanding the scope. Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal gave this advice while speaking as the chief guest at a discussion event organized on the occasion of National VAT Day and VAT Week on Friday. 

The National Board of Revenue (NBR) organized the discussion meeting at the auditorium of the Institution of Diploma Engineers in the capital. The meeting, chaired by NBR Chairman Abu Hena Md. Rahmatul Munim, was attended by FBCCI President Md. Jasim Uddin, the president of the apex business organization. 

The Finance Minister said that people want to pay taxes, but are afraid. To remove this fear, an environment must be ensured so that taxes can be paid without any hindrance. For this, laws and forms must be simplified. Then the people will come forward to pay taxes, and revenue collection will also increase. 

He told the revenue officials, 'There is no harm in plucking the feathers of the swan as much as you want, but care must be taken that the duck does not get hurt.' 

FBCCI President Md. Jasim Uddin said that the scope of income tax and VAT needs to be expanded. He proposed to launch another large taxpayer unit in Dhaka and a large taxpayer unit in Chittagong. In addition, in view of the increase in the prices of various raw materials in the international market, he also proposed to provide tax exemptions on the import of those products. 

The FBCCI President said that the strategy of collecting VAT by harassing, issuing demands and notices is not helpful for businessmen. However, strict action must be taken against those who deliberately evade. 

NBR Chairman Abu Hena Md. Rahmatul Munim said that the NBR is under multifaceted pressure. Just as there is pressure to provide revenue to the government and increase the tax-GDP ratio, there is also pressure to provide revenue exemptions to ensure equality in the society. He said that exemptions must be given. However, it must be in a case through which socio-economic development is achieved and the common people benefit. 

At the event, 9 businessmen with the highest VAT payers at the national level were honored. The Finance Minister handed over the honors to representatives of VAT payer organizations. This year, 525 businessmen across the country have been selected as the best VAT payers.

Headline_English: Finance Minister hopes growth will be 7.2 percent this year
Content_Enlish:
Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal has expressed hope that the GDP growth rate will be 7.2 percent in the current fiscal year. He said this in response to questions from reporters after the meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Procurement on Monday. 

The minister said, our growth is good in all sectors. Exports are increasing, imports are also increasing. The economy is dynamic. Therefore, the way the economy is progressing, it is expected that the growth rate will be 7.2 percent by the end of the current fiscal year. 

The GDP growth rate has been estimated at 7.2 percent in the budget for the current fiscal year 2021-22. Mustafa Kamal said, we hope that the specified growth rate will be achieved as per the progress of the economy. 

The International Monetary Fund has said that Bangladesh's GDP growth rate will be 6.6 percent this year. In this regard, the Finance Minister said, the IMF and the World Bank are always conservative. We hope that growth will be achieved according to the budget target. 

The Finance Minister said, remittances have decreased slightly. However, there is no reason to worry. There are two Eids ahead. Then more remittances will come. 

He said, if the trend of remittances continues, we will exceed $25 billion by the end of the year. In response to journalists' questions, the minister said, the country has achieved a lot in 50 years. 

He said, it took 38 years to achieve a GDP of $100 billion. In the remaining 12 years, $41 billion was achieved. The country has made the most progress during this period. This has been possible due to the strong leadership of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. 

He said, our goal is to become an upper-middle income country by 2030 and reach the ranks of the developed world by 2041. The way we are progressing, God willing, we will be able to reach the desired goal. 

In response to a question, the Finance Minister said, road shows are held to showcase Bangladesh in the world. It has nothing to do with the capital market. I think the capital market is in the right place.

Headline_English: World Bank approves $500 million loan for electricity
Content_Enlish:
The World Bank has approved a $500 million loan to modernize and transform Bangladesh's electricity distribution system. The amount in local currency (Tk 86 per dollar) is Tk 4,300 billion. The World Bank's Board of Directors approved the loan in Washington, the organization said in a press release on Wednesday. 

It said that the World Bank's loan under the Power Distribution Modernization Program will help provide improved electricity services to about 40 million people in Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions. The program will construct and modernize more than 31,000 kilometers of distribution lines and 157 substations and related infrastructure. In addition, steps will be taken to increase climate resilience in 25 rural electricity networks. Investments will be made in new and advanced technologies to modernize the power system as a whole. 

Dandan Chen, Acting Country Director of the World Bank in Bangladesh, said that Bangladesh has quadrupled electricity generation in the past decade and more than 99 percent of the country's people are now covered by electricity. But this significant progress in electricity generation has not been matched by improvements in the distribution system. This program will help modernize the distribution system and ensure climate resilience.

Headline_English: Central Bank does not object to appointment of MD in Islamic Finance
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has not given a no-objection to the proposal to appoint Chowdhury Manjur Liaquat as MD of Islamic Finance and Investment. Instead, it has been suggested to appoint a person with a clean image. Manjur Liaquat is currently the MD of another financial institution, Union Capital. 

It is learned that Islamic Finance wrote a letter on September 27 seeking no-objection to the appointment of Chowdhury Manjur Liaquat as MD. After various reviews, Bangladesh Bank said in a letter on Tuesday that Chowdhury Manjur Liaquat could not be given no-objection as MD in the interest of depositors. In light of the central bank's 2015 circular, it has been suggested to appoint a person with a clean image as Managing Director without delay. 

Those concerned said that Union Capital has unpaid interest of Tk 106 crore on loans given to its own subsidiary. And there is a provision deficit of Tk 43 crore 22 lakh. Since it does not have the capacity to save this money at once, the institution has taken 8 and 9 years to save it. As such, 185 million taka is supposed to be saved every year. However, without saving a single taka, the audited annual financial report for 2020 says that unpaid interest adjustments and provisions have been saved in light of the central bank's instructions. 

After the Bangladesh Bank's review found these irregularities, the central bank first issued a notice on October 6 asking why punitive action would not be taken against the institution and its stakeholders. Unable to be satisfied with Union Capital's explanation, restrictions were imposed on loan disbursements of more than one crore taka on November 3. At the same time, an action plan was ordered to be prepared for the return of deposits that had expired.

Headline_English: Stock market on the rise at the end of the year
Content_Enlish:
The stock market is on the rise at the end of the year. After a few days of continuous decline, the share prices and market price indices of most of the companies traded in the country's stock market increased on Monday. The upward trend has continued since the start of trading today, Tuesday. 

At the end of the first three hours of today's trading, at 1 pm, shares and mutual funds of 378 companies were traded on the main stock market Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE). Of these, 289 were trading with increasing prices. 

At this time, 60 shares were trading at a loss and 29 were trading with unchanged prices. 

Since most of the shares were traded at an increase, there was a positive impact on the market price index. The main price index of the DSE, DSEX, was seen to have increased by 62 points to stand at 6731 points. 

Till this time, shares worth 557 crore 66 lakh taka were traded. The pace of trading was higher than in the past few days. 

Market insiders believe that the stock market may remain upward for the remaining two working days of this year. They said that this upward trend may be the result of institutional investors finding new investment opportunities. 

Various brokerage house officials said that about half of the country's banking, insurance and financial institutions have investments in the stock market. Their financial accounting year ends in December. Therefore, almost at the end of every year, these companies sell the shares in their portfolios that have profits and 'realize' the profit. The main reason for this sale is to increase the company's net profit to pay better dividends to shareholders. 

Market insiders also said that share prices tend to fall in November-December almost every year due to the pressure of institutional investors to sell shares. When they start buying shares again after the sale, the share prices also rise again. 

Today's DSE sector-wise trading review shows that most of the shares in all sectors except jute are on the rise. 

However, among the major sectors, the textile sector has seen the highest price increase. At 1 pm, 51 out of 58 companies in the sector were trading at an increase of 3.5 percent. 

In addition, shares in the engineering sector were trading at an increase of 2.5 percent, and shares in the banking sector were trading at an increase of about 1 percent. 

However, the insurance sector still dominates the trading. At the end of the first three hours, shares worth 122 crore taka were traded in 52 companies in this sector, which was 24 percent of the total trading. 

In the sector-wise trading, shares worth 90 crore taka were traded in 14 companies in the miscellaneous sector, which was in the next position. Although Beximco Limited in this sector had a transaction of 30 crore taka.

Headline_English: Ministry of Industries' ADP implementation progress 45 percent
Content_Enlish:
The Ministry of Industries and its subordinate agencies have implemented 46 percent of the projects included in the Annual Development Program (ADP) until November of the current fiscal year. 

This information was given at a meeting to review the implementation progress of the projects included in the Annual Development Program at the conference room of the Ministry of Industries on Thursday. 

Industries Minister Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun and State Minister for Industries Kamal Ahmed Majumder were present at the meeting chaired by Industries Secretary Zakia Sultana. In addition, concerned officials of the Ministry of Industries, heads of various organizations and corporations under the ministry, and various project directors were present. 

It was informed at the meeting that there are a total of 33 projects in the Annual Development Program of the Ministry of Industries for the fiscal year 2021-2022. Of these, 30 are investment projects, 2 are technical assistance projects, and 1 is being implemented with its own financing. In total, the allocation for these projects is Tk 4,660 crore. 

Of this, 1,203 crore taka has been allocated for the GEO sector, 2,817 crore taka for the project support sector and 46 crore taka for the organization's own financing sector. 1,855 crore 35 lakh taka has been spent against the projects till November 2021. 

Speaking as the chief guest at the meeting, Industries Minister Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun said that the progress of the Industries Ministry's ADP implementation till November 2021 is satisfactory; however, more needs to be done. 

Referring to the recent visit to Carew & Company (Bangladesh) Limited in Chuadanga and the inauguration of the sugarcane threshing season for the 2021-2022 season, the Industries Minister said that he has instructed the concerned to invent high-yielding sugarcane varieties to overcome the continuous losses in the sugar industry. 

In addition, the work of modernizing the mills and factories will continue. 

Similarly, he has instructed the heads of organizations and departments to formulate plans to take effective steps to reduce losses in other sectors and implement them. 

The minister ordered the opening of a second unit at Carew & Company and the formulation of a new project to utilize the unused land owned by corporations in Tongi. 

State Minister for Industries Kamal Ahmed Majumder said that the progress of the buffer godown construction project in different districts of the country for fertilizer storage and distribution facilities is going on slowly, the project work must be completed quickly to deliver fertilizer supply to the doorsteps of farmers. Legal action must be taken against syndicates who increase the price of fertilizer in different districts of the country, give less than the weight, and give less than the weight in fertilizer bags. 

He said that the BSCIC land should not be misappropriated and its proper use should be ensured. He called on everyone to fulfill their responsibilities to turn the non-profit organization into a profitable one.

Headline_English: Benefits of remaining debt-free by paying 15 percent
Content_Enlish:
If a borrower pays 15 percent of the amount that is supposed to be paid this year, no one will be in default. Along with the young, the old will also get this benefit. This decision was made in a meeting of the top business organizations, FBCCI, BGMEA, BKMEA, BTMA, and other organizations in Bangladesh on Thursday. 

In the meeting room of Bangladesh Bank, chaired by Governor Fazle Kabir and led by FBCCI President Md. Jasim Uddin, the meeting was attended by business leaders, Deputy Governors Kazi Saidur Rahman, Abu Farah Md. Naser, and other officials at various levels. 

Due to Corona, it was announced that if a borrower pays 25 percent of the amount that is supposed to be paid this year by December 30, no one will be in default. Business organizations sent a letter demanding a further increase in this benefit. However, it was informed from the bankers' meeting held on December 28 that the benefit for everyone will not increase. Only entrepreneurs in the CMSME sector will not be in default if they pay 15 percent. However, after today's meeting, Bangladesh Bank backed down from its previous position. 

In addition, businessmen demanded an increase in the EDF's credit limit and repayment of short-term foreign loans. The central bank will review this issue and decide later.

Headline_English: Despite being far away, the trade fair in Purbachal will be bustling: Commerce Minister
Content_Enlish:
Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi said that although it is a bit far away, the trade fair in Purbachal will be bustling as a new area. Because it is an extension of Dhaka. Already, there is extensive development in this area, including communication systems. 

He said these things at a press conference organized on Friday at the Bangabandhu Bangladesh-China Friendship Exhibition Center (BBCFEC) in Purbachal on the occasion of the inauguration of the 26th Dhaka International Trade Fair. 

This is the first time that the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) is organizing a trade fair in Purbachal with the support of the Ministry of Commerce. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will inaugurate the trade fair virtually on Saturday. 

At the press conference, the Commerce Minister said that this fair will play an important role in achieving the target of $51 billion in export earnings. There is no alternative to increasing trade and commerce if we want to achieve the SDGs by 2030 and reach developed countries by 2041. 

In response to journalists' questions about the poor condition of the road from Kuril Bishwa Road to Purbachal, he said that 90 percent of the road development work has been completed. The remaining work will be completed in a short time. In addition, initiatives will also be taken to arrange accommodation for the participants of the fair in the future. However, since the fair is being organized for the first time at a new location, there may be some minor mistakes. 

Tipu Munshi said that an international trade fair will be held in Purbachal for one month. In the remaining 11 months, various business organizations will be able to organize fairs here to promote their products. He requested the businessmen to organize small fairs here at other times of the year. 

Stating that all kinds of initiatives will be taken to promote and promote the products manufactured in the country, the Commerce Minister said that one of the strategies to increase exports is to develop products and create a market for them. And the main strategy to create this market is to organize trade fairs. By organizing a trade fair at this newly built BBCFEC, a new chapter is going to be added to the development and expansion of the country's trade and commerce. 

When asked how crowded the fair will be outside the main Dhaka, Commerce Secretary Tapan Kanti Ghosh told Samakal, "In addition to Dhaka, people from Narayanganj, Gazipur, Narsingdi will come to the trade fair. There is more open space here, so there will be a large gathering of people." 

However, although the organizing organization has made all the preparations to inaugurate the fair today, construction work on almost all the stalls was underway when we visited the fair premises. 

In this regard, Iftekhar Ahmed Chowdhury, director of the fair organizing committee, told Samakal that the construction work of most of the stalls has been completed. The rest will be completed by today itself. 

This year, Bangladesh Tourism Corporation will operate a cafeteria with 500 seats inside the main building of the fair. There will be two mother and child centers. All kinds of measures, including CCTV, have been taken for the safety of visitors. There will be ATM booths of several banks at the fair. There will be several passenger bus services, including BRTC buses, from Kuril Bishwa Road to the fair grounds at fixed fares for the travel of buyers and visitors.

Headline_English: Price of 12 kg LPG increased to Tk 1,033
Content_Enlish:
LPG prices have increased. The price of LPG at the private level has been fixed at 86 taka 7 paisa per kg, while the price of a 12 kg cylinder has been fixed at 1033 taka. At the same time, the price of autogas is also increasing. The price of autogas has been fixed at 50.56 taka per liter. This will be effective from September 1. 

In August, the price of a 12 kg cylinder at the private level was fixed at 993 taka. Earlier, it was 891 taka in July and 842 taka in June. Meanwhile, per liter of autogas was 48 taka 71 paisa in August, and 44 taka in July. 

Accordingly, the price of a 12 kg LPG cylinder has increased by 40 taka compared to August and the price of autogas has increased by 2.39 taka per liter. 

The Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced this price of LPG at the consumer level in an online press conference on Tuesday. BERC Chairman Abdul Jalil, Commission members Mohammad Abu Faruk, Maqbul-e Elahi, Bazlur Rahman, Kamruzzaman, Secretary Rubina Ferdousi and other senior officials were present at the time. 

The price of a 12 kg cylinder at the government level will remain at Tk 591 as before. Since this price has nothing to do with Saudi CP. Which can be found on the commission's website. 

The commission has re-determined the price of LPG supplied in the reticulated system at the consumer level at Tk 83.77 per kg excluding VAT or Tk 0.1861 per liter. 

The BERC Chairman said that in August, as per Article A of the BERC Act, the Saudi CP prices of propane and butane announced by Saudi Aramco in August were $660 and $655 per metric ton respectively. Accordingly, this price has been determined considering the average Saudi CP of propane and butane at $656.75 per metric ton in August, considering the propane and butane mixture ratio of 35:65. 

The Commission announced the price of LPG for the first time on April 12.

Headline_English: Bangladesh Bank's letter to conduct separate audits on e-commerce companies
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has written to the Ministry of Commerce to conduct separate audits of 10 e-commerce companies. 

The central bank has sent a letter to the Ministry of Commerce on Sunday advising it to appoint an auditor and conduct an audit. 

The 10 companies are Evaly, Dhamaka, E-Orange, Sirajganj Shop, Aladiner Pradeep, Qkum, Boom Boom, Adian Mart, Need.com.bd and Alesha Mart. 

The Ministry of Commerce had sent a letter to Bangladesh Bank on August 24 seeking information on bank transactions and financial information of 9 companies other than E-Valley. In response, the central bank wrote to the Ministry of Commerce. 

Bangladesh Bank spokesperson and executive director Md. Sirajul Islam told Samakal that the Ministry of Commerce had asked Bangladesh Bank to inquire about these companies. Work is underway accordingly. In addition, Bangladesh Bank has been asked to audit those companies through an external audit firm. 

A case was filed against the owners of e-Orange in August for embezzling Tk 1,100 crore for not delivering products or returning the money even after taking advance money. 

Among the accused, e-Orange owner Sonia Mehjabin and her husband Masukur Rahman and Chief Operating Officer (COO) Amanullah Chowdhury have been arrested. 

The other accused, another owner of e-Orange, Bithi Akhter alias Nazneen Nahar, and Chief Technology Officer Kawsar Ahmed, have not been arrested yet. 

Bithi Akhter is the wife of Banani Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Sheikh Sohel Rana, who was temporarily suspended. Sonia Mehjabin is his sister. Sheikh Sohel Rana is also an accused in a separate case. He was arrested in India a few days ago while trying to escape.

Headline_English: Commerce Ministry recommends legal action against Evaly
Content_Enlish:
A committee of the Ministry of Commerce has recommended legal action against Evaly. The decision was made at a meeting of the committee on Tuesday afternoon, said Hafizur Rahman, head of the Digital Commerce Cell of the Ministry of Commerce. The Ministry of Commerce will request the Ministry of Home Affairs to take action as per the committee's recommendation. 

Hafizur Rahman said, "The committee's decision is that Evaly has violated the law. For this, the Ministry of Commerce will not take direct responsibility, but the law enforcement agencies will take necessary action." 

He said, "There is a huge difference between Evaly's liabilities and assets. Where this money went is a big issue. On the other hand, they have cheated the customer by not delivering the product on time. For this, there is an opportunity to take action against them under the Digital Security Act and the Consumer Rights Act. It is hoped that the law enforcement agencies will take necessary action."

Headline_English: Financial institutions will not be able to reschedule loans more than 3 times
Content_Enlish:
Non-bank financial institutions will no longer be able to reschedule any loan more than three times. And if a customer fails to repay the loan even after the third round of rescheduling, he will be considered a natural or wilful defaulter. In addition, only the interest against the rescheduled loan that is recovered can be taken into the income category. 

Bangladesh Bank has made such a strict policy on loan rescheduling for financial institutions on Tuesday. 

At the beginning of the policy, it is said that various financial institutions are repeatedly rescheduling loans without verifying the customer's ability to repay the loan. The real picture of the recovery of these institutions is not reflected due to the rescheduling of the payment schedule and not following the rescheduling process properly. From now on, financial institutions will only be able to reschedule loans classified as adverse (low, doubtful and loss-making). At each stage of regularizing the loan, the central bank will have to take downpayment at the rate determined by the central bank. 

Bangladesh Bank has said that a term loan can be rescheduled for 48 months in the first phase, 36 months in the second phase, and 24 months in the third phase in the case of a substandard loan. And in the case of rescheduling in a doubtful or bad debt classified condition, it can be rescheduled for 36 months in the first phase, 24 months in the second phase, and 18 months in the third phase. Short-term loans can be rescheduled for a maximum of 12 months in the first phase after the due date or payment of the last installment. Financial institutions can do it regularly for 6 months in the second and third phases. 

In the case of downpayment, it has been said that in the first phase of loan rescheduling, a minimum of 15 percent of the overdue installment or 10 percent of the total outstanding amount, whichever is less, must be paid in both term and short-term cases. In the second phase, 30 percent of the overdue installment or 20 percent of the total outstanding amount, whichever is less, must be paid. And in the third phase, 50 percent of the overdue installments or 30 percent of the total outstanding, whichever is less, will have to be paid. The loan regularized in this way can be paid through monthly or quarterly installments. If the unpaid installment of the rescheduled loan is equal to 6 monthly installments or 2 quarterly installments, it will have to be classified as loss-making. 

It also states that every financial institution must have a policy for loan rescheduling approved by the board of directors. It must provide all the conditions that will not be easier than this policy of the central bank. Before rescheduling, the credit committee of the financial institution will highlight the rationale and impact through a written report. To verify the ability of the customer to repay the loan, his cash flow statement, audited balance sheet, income and expenditure and other financial statements will have to be reviewed. A decision on rescheduling must be taken within one month of the deposit of the downpayment of a customer. However, the amount deposited as an installment cannot be shown as a down payment.

Headline_English: ADB forecasts 6.8% growth in the country in the current fiscal year
Content_Enlish:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) expects Bangladesh's gross domestic product (GDP) to grow by 6.8 percent in the current fiscal year 2021-22, which is lower than the government's target. 

This was revealed in the ADB's updated report titled 'Asian Development Outlook (ADO)-2021 Update' released on Wednesday. 

The report said that Bangladesh's economic recovery process is continuing well despite the Corona pandemic. 

Incidentally, the government's target for the current fiscal year is to achieve 7.2 percent growth. In the last fiscal year, 5.47 percent growth was achieved despite the Corona outbreak.

Headline_English: Tk 19 crore missing from Union Bank vault
Content_Enlish:
Tk 19 crore has disappeared from the vault of the Gulshan branch adjacent to the head office of Union Bank, a private sector Islamic Sharia-based bank. Last Monday, the Bangladesh Bank inspection team revealed such information. Now, Bangladesh Bank will inspect the vaults of all the bank's branches. Even after revealing the information about the irregularities, no information was found about taking action against anyone in the branch. After checking with Gulshan Police Station, it was learned that no complaint was filed in this incident. 
It is known that last Monday, a team led by a joint director of Bangladesh Bank's Banking Inspection Division-7 went to inspect the Gulshan branch of Union Bank. They reached the branch before 10 am. As per the usual rules, they inspected the vault at the beginning. Although Tk 31 crore was shown in the branch's vault on paper and in pen, the inspection team found Tk 12 crore there. The branch officials could not immediately respond to this. After that, the branch authorities started various activities to cover up the matter. Instead of taking action against the branch managers, the senior officials of the bank's head office got busy covering up the incident. At one stage, a party in Bangladesh Bank also took a stand in favor of not taking any action in this incident. However, in the end, Bangladesh Bank decided to seek an explanation from the bank. 
The concerned said that the branch manager, second officer and cash in-charge are responsible for reconciling the vault accounts at the end and beginning of each transaction. If there is any discrepancy in the amount of money in the vault, it is the responsibility of these officers to reconcile it. Sometimes, a small discrepancy in the amount of money can occur due to a mistake in the calculation. However, if there is a discrepancy of a huge amount of money, it is a criminal offense. As a result, the responsible officer should be immediately handed over to the police. However, the bank did not file any general diary with the police station in this incident. Bangladesh Bank did not file any complaint in this regard with the police station either. On the contrary, until last Tuesday night, efforts were made to cover up the entire matter. In addition, those who revealed this information during inspections were put under pressure. Generally, such discrepancies are not found in the vault during inspections of any branch. 
Despite repeated telephone and SMS calls to the bank's managing director ABM Mokammel Haque Chowdhury from Tuesday to Wednesday, there was no response. When the bank's deputy managing director (DMD) Hasan Iqbal was called on Tuesday, he told Samakal that he had not heard of any such incident. Another DMD of the bank, Md. Nazrul Islam, said that he had heard of such an incident for the first time from this reporter. 
Union Bank Gulshan branch operations manager Saiful Azam Mahmud told Samakal, "They have no right to do anything outside the banking regulations. No such incident has occurred in the branch. Someone is misleading with wrong information." 
Bangladesh Bank spokesperson and executive director Sirajul Islam told Samakal yesterday that he heard that discrepancies in money were found during an inspection of the vault of Union Bank's Gulshan branch. Now they will be summoned for an explanation. Legal action will be taken if a reasonable explanation is not received.

Headline_English: Show cause notices issued to four e-commerce companies
Content_Enlish:
The Commerce Ministry has issued show cause notices to four e-commerce companies. 

The Commerce Ministry's Digital Commerce Cell has issued notices to companies named Thale, Dalal Plus, Anander Bazar and Allshopper. They will have to respond to the notice by October 17. 

The notice states that recently, it has been reported from various media and mobile media that these companies have created instability in the digital commerce sector by making unusual offers. Due to this, customers are being confused and cheated in online shopping. 

At the same time, customers and merchants have been asked to inform the companies about their liabilities, company assets and future plans.

Headline_English: Commerce Ministry requests withdrawal of duties on sugar, edible oil
Content_Enlish:
The Commerce Ministry has requested the National Board of Revenue (NBR) to reduce the market price of sugar and edible oil. 

A meeting was held at the Commerce Ministry on Monday to keep the stock, supply, import and price situation of essential commodities normal and stable. Commerce Secretary Tapan Kanti Ghosh said this at a briefing after the meeting. 

He said, "There is an advanced tax on sugar, there is also an advanced tax on edible oil. We have written to the NBR to withdraw this tax. Although an application was made to withdraw the tax on onion for the next four months, it was not made for oil and sugar. The NBR will monitor the market situation and take action. Last year, the duty was withdrawn for four months. We hope that the duty will be withdrawn for three months this year." 

Last September, the Commerce Ministry fixed the price of loose sugar at 74 taka per kg and packet sugar at 75 taka. In addition, at the retail level, soybean oil is priced at 129 taka per liter, bottled soybean oil at 153 taka per liter, and 5-liter bottled soybean oil at 728 taka. 

Recently, it was seen that retailers in the capital are not selling soybean oil and sugar at the government-set prices. Vendors are selling loose soybean oil at 140 to 145 taka per liter, bottled soybean oil at 148 to 150 taka per liter, loose sugar at 80 taka and packaged sugar at 85 to 87 taka. Retail sugar is being sold at 78 taka to 80 taka per kg. And packaged white sugar is being sold at 80 taka per kg, red sugar or cane sugar at 90 taka per kg. 

Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi joined the meeting online. In addition, officials from the NBR, TCB, and the Ministry of Commerce and business leaders were present. 

In addition to onions, the meeting discussed the prices of edible oil, sugar, and lentils. 

At the beginning of the meeting, Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Commerce, A. H. M. Shafiquzzaman, presented a comparative picture of the international market prices of these four products and the situation in Bangladesh.

Headline_English: The maximum cost to send money to another bank via the internet is 10 taka.
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has fixed the charges for electronic transactions of customers of one bank to another bank. A maximum of 10 taka can be charged from the customer for transferring internet banking funds from one bank to another bank. A charge of 0.7 percent of the total transaction can be deducted from the merchant in Bangla QR. Out of this, 0.4 percent will have to be paid to the card issuing bank as an interchange fee. For payments of government services through cards issued in Bangladesh, a maximum of 20 taka will be charged from the customer per transaction for payments up to 25 thousand taka. For transactions exceeding 25 thousand taka, the concerned banks will pay the prevailing fee. Bangladesh Bank has issued a circular on Monday and sent this instruction to the banks. 

So far, only charges for cash withdrawal from interbank ATMs, balance inquiry and mini statement were fixed. These have been kept unchanged and the charges for interbank POS, internet banking, Bangla QR and government challan have been fixed. 

Under Bangladesh Bank's National Payment Switch, if a customer of one bank withdraws money using an ATM of another bank, a maximum charge of 15 taka can be charged as at present. The card issuing bank will pay the remaining 5 taka. In addition, a fee of five taka will be charged from the customer for balance inquiry and micro-statement as at present. In addition, a maximum fee of ten taka will be charged from the card issuing bank for transferring funds from ATMs and twenty taka for depositing at ATMs of other banks. 

A maximum charge of twenty taka will be charged from the customer for each transaction for cash withdrawal using point of sales or POS. If a customer of one bank pays a purchase bill at a point of sales of another bank, the business will collect a minimum discount of 1.60 percent of the total transaction from the business.
