Out of this, 1.1 percent will be paid to the card issuing bank as an interchange fee.

Headline_English: It has become easier to bring service export revenue into the country
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh Bank has made it easier for service exporters and freelancers to bring their income to the country. From now on, service exporters will be able to open merchant accounts with international market platforms. They will also have the opportunity to open informal accounts (notional accounts) with licensed payment gateways in other countries. Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard and sent it to banks on Monday. 

The circular states that the income received through international market platforms or foreign payment gateways will first be deposited as 'nostro' of the bank that transacts foreign currency. Then the bank will deposit it in the customer's account that provides the service. In addition to the customer's bank account, the money can also be deposited in the local digital wallet. If the customer wants, he can deposit the applicable portion as ERQ. In all cases, the provisions of paying the necessary taxes must be followed. And it must be ensured that the income is brought to the country within four months of service export. 

It also states that banks will have to comply with certain conditions when bringing money from accounts opened in international market platforms or payment gateways. In particular, the service provider will have to obtain information about the merchant account management with the international market platform and its notional account with the licensed payment service provider abroad. Information about the service activities will be collected and a declaration will be taken. A commitment will be taken from the customer to immediately bring the income received against the service to the country through the international market platform within the specified time or by depositing it in an informal account. 

An official of the central bank said that in 2011, Bangladesh Bank allowed AD banks to establish relationships with overseas OPGSPs for the repatriation of income from the service sector on a small scale. Now the policy has been simplified further.

Headline_English: Buyers' stuck Tk 214 crore to be returned in three months
Content_Enlish:
The 214 crore taka stuck in the e-commerce payment gateway of buyers will be returned in the next three months. Bangladesh Bank will work for this. The decision was made in an emergency meeting held at the Commerce Ministry on Monday afternoon, Commerce Minister Tipu Munshi said. 

The meeting held at the conference room of the Commerce Ministry was attended by Posts and Telecommunications Minister Mustafa Jabbar, Prime Minister's Private Industry and Investment Advisor Salman F Rahman, State Minister for ICT Junaid Ahmed Palak, and FBCCI President Md. Jasimuddin. 

The Commerce Minister said that in today's meeting, it was decided to launch a unique ID for registration, a central log-in tracking system, a complaint management system, and to return the money stuck in the scroll service from July 1. This work will be completed within the next three months. The ICT Division will provide information about the software in this regard within the next two weeks. 

State Minister for ICT Junaid Ahmed Palak said that new laws and authorities are not needed for the e-commerce sector. This sector can be managed through existing laws.

Headline_English: Three more records in the stock market in one day
Content_Enlish:
The country's main stock market, the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), set three records on Monday. The market capitalization and the two main indices reached record highs at the end of trading today. 

Earlier, three records were set in a single day on July 19. 

The main index of the DSE, the DSEX, rose 56 points or about 1 percent to about 6,482 points today. And the DS-30 index, which is composed of 30 companies selected from among the listed companies, rose 16 points to 2,344 points. These two indices were launched on January 27, 2013. Almost eight and a half years after their launch, the two indices have reached their highest levels today. 

In addition, the market capitalization of the DSE rose by Tk 3,466 crore in a single day to Tk 5,37,831 crore. This is the highest market capitalization so far.

Headline_English: Committee to investigate abnormal share prices of 9 companies
Content_Enlish:
The stock market regulator Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) has formed an investigation committee to investigate the reasons for the abnormal increase in the share prices of 9 listed companies. The companies are - Anwar Galvanizing, GBB Power, Emerald Oil, Bangladesh National Insurance, National Feed, Paper Processing and Packaging, Dhaka Dyeing, Fu-Wang Ceramic and Beacon Pharma. 

The prices of these shares have fallen by 3 to 11 times in the last 4 to 11 months. Stock market experts believe that there is a case of manipulation behind the abnormal increase in the prices of these companies. There are strong rumors that the owners of the companies are also involved in this. There are also allegations that the financial reports have been fraudulently inflated to increase the prices. 

The regulatory body BSEC formed a four-member investigation committee headed by Director Sheikh Mahbub Ur Rahman on Tuesday to investigate these issues. The remaining three members of the committee are BSEC Assistant Director Ziaur Rahman, Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) Deputy General Manager Mohammad Shafiqul Islam Bhuiyan and Central Depository Institution CDBL Application Support Department Head Md. Moinul Haque. The committee has been asked to submit its report within the next two months. 

The committee will look into the inconsistencies in the financial reports of these companies, price manipulation, insider trading, illegal share trading and any violation of stock market laws. Among these 9 shares, the share of the paper processing company that returned from the OTC has increased more than 11 times in less than two months. It returned to the main market on June 13 with a market price of 16 taka. But in this short time, the share price has risen to 179 taka 70 paisa. The share was last traded at 155.30 taka on Tuesday. 

After that, the market price of Bangladesh National Insurance has increased the most by almost 7 times. In the last 11 months, the share price has increased from Tk 23 to Tk 158, which is almost seven times. The share price has been declining for the past few days. The last transaction was on Tuesday at Tk 118. 

In the last 5 and a half months, the share price of Emerald Oil has increased 4 times. The highest price of the share has increased from just Tk 9.5 to Tk 38.40. In addition, the market prices of Anwar Galvanizing, GBB Power, National Feed Mills, Dhaka Dyeing, Fu-Wang Ceramic and Beacon Pharma have increased more than three times in the last 4 to 8 months. 

Among them, the market price of Anwar Galvanizing increased from Tk 95 to Tk 339 in four and a half months. The last transaction was on Tuesday at Tk 313. The market price of GBB Power increased from Tk 13.60 to Tk 40 in eight months. The last transaction was at Tk 35.60. 

The market price of National Feed Mills has increased from Tk 14 to Tk 44 in the last four months. It was last traded at Tk 33.10 on Tuesday. 

The market price of Dhaka Dyeing Company shares has increased from Tk 7 to Tk 28.40 in the last four months. It was last traded at Tk 24.40 on Tuesday. 

The market price of Fu-Wang Ceramic Company shares has increased from Tk 9 to Tk 28 in the last four months. It was last traded at Tk 24.90. The market price of Beacon Pharma has increased from Tk 70 to Tk 235 in the last 6 and a half months. The share was last traded at Tk 209.20 on the DSE on Tuesday.

Headline_English: They stole 13 billion taka from another financial institution.
Content_Enlish:
Another financial scam against the controversial PK Halder and his syndicate has been revealed again. Almost 1,300 crore taka of Fast Finance and Investment Limited was embezzled in the name of 20 non-existent organizations without accepting loan applications and without any collateral. The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) investigation has revealed evidence of this terrible corruption. 

ACC sources said that 700 crore taka was withdrawn with a single signature of the former MD of Fast Finance, Russell Shahriar. Although PK Halder did not hold any position in Fast Finance, he pulled out all the stops to embezzle money. Former MD Russell Shahriar was a close associate of PK Halder. Therefore, PK Halder used to attend the meetings of the board of directors of the organization without paying attention to the rules. Loans were passed in the name of the paper organization as per his instructions and advice. 

ACC says that officials of Fast Finance misused their power for dishonest purposes and fraudulently provided fake loans in the names of about 20 paper organizations without accepting any loan applications, verification, and collateral. This is how Tk 1,300 crore was siphoned off. 

ACC's investigation revealed that the huge amount of money was not deposited in the bank accounts of the 20 fake organizations. As planned, all the money went to the respective banks of PK Halder's syndicate members. PK Halder's close associates Ujjwal Kumar Nandi, Siddiqur Rahman, and Jahangir Alam were members of this syndicate. The information received so far shows that the syndicate has embezzled about Tk 7,000 crore from several important financial institutions in the country. ACC sources said that in late 2014, PK Halder's syndicate members bought shares of Fast Finance and took control of the organization. Then, they strategically laid off the old officials and appointed people of their choice.

Headline_English: Reserves increase by $48 billion
Content_Enlish:
The country's foreign exchange reserves have jumped from $46 billion to $48 billion. At the end of the day on Tuesday, the reserves stood at $48.04 billion or $48.04 billion. 

Bangladesh Bank officials said that the sudden increase in reserves was due to the liquidity support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to deal with the impact of Corona. 

They said that Bangladesh has received an allocation of Special Drawing Rights (SDR) equivalent to $1.448 billion from the IMF. On August 2, the IMF decided to allocate $650 billion equivalent to SDR for different countries around the world to deal with the impact of Covid-19 on the economy. Which became effective on Tuesday. Bangladesh also received this assistance. As a result, the country's foreign exchange reserves have increased. Earlier, on June 29, Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves crossed the $46 billion mark. 

The IMF allocates SDR to its member countries as liquidity support. SDR is a unit of five currencies for maintaining reserves in foreign exchange. Currently, these five currencies are recognized by the IMF as reserve currencies. The highest 41.73 percent of the SDR basket is in the US dollar. The euro has 30.93 percent, the Chinese yuan has 10.92 percent, the Japanese yen has 8.33 percent and the pound has 8.09 percent. 

Since the start of the impact of Corona, the supply of foreign exchange has been higher than the demand. Due to which the dollar rate in the interbank currency market has remained unchanged at 84 taka 80 paisa for a long time. However, the dollar rate has been slightly higher this month due to various reasons including increased imports. In the last few days, it has increased by 35 paisa per dollar and reached 85 taka 15 paisa on Tuesday. Due to which Bangladesh Bank sold 50 million dollars last Thursday and another 50 million dollars on Tuesday. In this, the foreign exchange reserve has crossed the 48 billion dollar mark in one leap.

It is known that the amount of reserves at the beginning of the day on Tuesday was 46.58 billion dollars. After some additions and subtractions due to the addition of IMF's SDR allocation, the reserves left 48 billion dollars. With this amount of money, it is possible to meet about 10 months of import liabilities. Generally, if there is enough money to meet 6 months of import liabilities, it is considered strong.

Headline_English: ACC asks for all Evaly documents
Content_Enlish:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has sent a letter to Evaly, seeking all business documents, including customer liabilities. The letter was sent to the MD and CEO of the controversial e-commerce company, Md. Russell, more than a week ago. The letter is signed by Mamunur Rashid Chowdhury, the ACC's assistant director and head of the investigation team investigating Evaly's irregularities and corruption allegations. The documents have been asked to be sent within seven working days of receiving the letter. 
After receiving the letter, Evaly has provided company, business and approval-related documents. These include documents related to the Registrar of Joint Stock, City Corporation and E-Commerce Association of Bangladesh (e-CAB). 
They have asked for time to provide other documents. Another official of the investigation team is Sihab Salam, Deputy Assistant Director of the ACC. 
The list of information sought from Evaly authorities in the ACC's letter includes - all types of licenses for the company to operate its business; Information related to business ownership, how many purchase orders were not delivered against which products were not delivered, how much money was paid against those orders, how the outstanding amount against the buyer's order was paid, by what method - these are the information; their plans to repay the customer's liabilities, their specific plans to deal with the existing business crisis and the account of all liabilities including bank loans (if any). 
In addition, the ACC has also asked to know how many customers Evaly has paid so far since the investigation by the Ministry of Commerce began, how much VAT and tax has been paid since the company's establishment, the company's audit report in different fiscal years, the company's overall cost account, the source of money spent on establishing the company, the amount of discount given to customers on various product offers at different times, the total value of the offers given so far. 
If the activities of this e-commerce company are stopped, the deprived customers will not get their money back. In addition to investigating irregularities and corruption, the ACC has also taken this issue into consideration so that the customers get their money back. Evaly has already stated that its customers across the country are 7 million. 
The ACC is also keeping an eye on the ongoing investigation by the Ministry of Commerce into Evaly. A high-level committee of the ministry is working to investigate the overall activities of the company, including irregularities and corruption. In the meantime, the committee has also taken statements from top officials of Evaly. The ACC will also collect the decision that the ministry will take after the investigation for the sake of a fair investigation. 
If all types of documents are provided as per the ACC's request, they will be verified. After the investigation work in these cases, Evaly's MD and CEO Md. Russell and Shamima Nasrin, the wife of the company's chairman Md. Russell, will be questioned about the allegations. If evidence of irregularities and corruption is found after the entire investigation, legal action will be taken against the top officials involved. 
An investigation report by the Ministry of Commerce said that Evaly's debt to individual and merchant customers is Tk 3.38 billion. The ministry's investigation report mentioned that this amount was embezzled by removing it from their bank accounts. 
Early last year, the ACC began investigating allegations of customer fraud against Evaly. At that time, the investigation into the complaint was progressing slowly. At the end of the same year, the Ministry of Commerce completed the investigation into the allegations against Evaly. The ministry recommended legal action and sent the investigation report to the ACC. Then, the ACC's investigation gained momentum. Later, the ministry sent another investigation report to the ACC on July 7. Some documents related to Evaly's fraud were also sent to the ACC from Bangladesh Bank. 
Evaly registered for e-commerce business on May 14, 2018. It started its formal business in December of the same year. In the beginning, they attracted customers of different classes and professions by offering attractive offers in the sale of various types of products. They started offering to sell one product after another at an unusually low price compared to the market price. This campaign was carried out by providing products to some customers at a huge discount. They also had 200 to 300 percent discount offers. Numerous customers rushed to buy products at low prices. But even after paying the price of the product, they still did not receive their desired products.

Headline_English: Apple Lifestyle Company: Intel's New CEO
Content_Enlish:
Competitors talk about the American technology company Apple. That's why the 'lifestyle' company called Apple a 'lifestyle' company for the first time. The new CEO of chip manufacturer Intel, Pat Gelsinger, has called Apple a 'lifestyle' company. He will take over as Intel's CEO next month. Before that, he gave Apple a 'snitch'.

Citing a local US newspaper called 'The Oregonian', technology website The Verge reported that Gelsinger recently held a meeting with employees. There, he said, 'We have to deliver a better product to the PC ecosystem than any possible product from a lifestyle company in Cupertino.' He basically meant Apple by the Cupertino company. Last November, Apple authorities announced that they would end their long-standing relationship with Intel and use their own processors for Macs. 

Gelsinger said, 'We have to do even better in the future.' 

When Apple announced the creation of its own silicon-based processors, many were surprised. In November, Apple announced the MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, and Mac Mini with the M1 processor. Within a short time, Apple's own processor-based laptops received great praise in the market. The heat fell on Intel. 

Apple, however, did not say that it would completely abandon the use of Intel processors. However, it is easy to understand that their dependence on Intel will decrease in the next few years. 

After taking charge of Intel in February, Gelsinger will have to face great challenges. Not only Apple, but another chip manufacturer AMD will also challenge Intel. Gelsinger previously worked as the CEO of VMware. In addition, he has 30 years of experience working at Intel. Time will tell whether he can take on new challenges in the market or not.

Headline_English: How much life has changed in a year
Content_Enlish:
At the beginning of 2021, people had to stay indoors. Amidst the loose lockdown, people were wearing casual dresses. As a result, people's interest in loose clothes has increased. Even after everything became normal, people's interest in tight jeans has decreased. Celebrities are also often seen in loose jeans now. In 2021, people's attention was on comfortable clothes. Especially in the summer, the use of gabardine increased. The use of loincloths or Punjabis was normal during Eid, Puja or national festivals. However, no heavy work was seen in Punjabis. Various famous brands have also tried to keep the design as simple as possible this time. People tried to keep everything simple in 2021. However, there was a lot of change in hair fashion. At this time, many people started growing their hair. Especially since schools, colleges, and universities were closed, many people grew their hair. In addition, the trend of changing hair color also started. Many people changed their hair color due to the influence of social media like TikTok and Likee. Girls have shown interest in medium-length hair and bleached hair. One such person is Mafrooha Livin from Rampura. She said about changing her hair color, "I am a fan of Korean Bond girls and pop. So I like to dye some parts of my hair pink or green."

The sale of leather shoes has decreased slightly in 2021. People's attention was on sneakers, or lightweight shoes. Especially among boys, the popularity of Burmese sandals has been noticed. However, sneakers and high heels were more popular among women. Addition of masks to fashion

The fashion of masks was popular in 2021. Masks of different colors and designs were seen on sidewalks, shops, online shops and pharmacies. Masks of different prices and designs began to be seen frequently in the fashion world. Many people started using masks for events or to enhance their fashion. Many people developed the habit of wearing masks with clothes.

We spoke to one such mask seller under the Farmgate overbridge. He said that cotton masks and dust-resistant sponge masks are in high demand in the market. Everyone goes to the pharmacy to buy a mask that will provide protection. However, people go to sidewalks or online shops for cotton mask fashion. There are masks of different designs and prints in the market. Many people can now make masks with their own prints. The value of hand-painted dresses

In 2021, the value of hand-painted pictures started to increase. Instead of needles, threads, beads, and lace, the value of hand-painted clothes has started to increase. Hand-painted dresses are especially being sold through various pages on social media.

Since different artists depict different types of work, diversity can also be seen in this type of clothing. Nabila Haque, a student of Jahangirnagar University, said in this regard, 'While I was off campus, I got the idea of ​​hand-painted clothes by looking at others. Since the university is off, I have been able to focus on this work. The value of saree bangles, the front of the waist, and even couple hand-painted dresses has started to increase. Innovation in makeup trends

No matter what the time is, makeup trends will never change. However, preferences may change a little. Due to staying at home in 2021, makeup has changed a lot. Especially the trend of changing eyebrows and eye color. Nude colors have been used more in lipstick. Also, although the use of soap, gel, mascara, etc. has increased, there has been a tendency towards natural and no-makeup looks. In this regard, Sharmin Nishu, a student of a private university, said, "I am not very comfortable wearing heavy makeup in regular life. I feel comfortable wearing a no-makeup look every day in class or regular work."

Ordering products online.

Popularity in online shopping

Various institutions were closed in the beginning of 2021 as well. During this time, trust in online shopping has increased. Especially, the popularity of many online shops, including Daraz, has started to increase. As a result, the quality of service of these shops has also started to increase.

However, some online shops have also made many customers suffer through scamming. The biggest advantage of online shops was 'customization'. Consumers have also been easily attracted to this direction as online shops provide the opportunity to order custom clothes, bags, masks or other products. In this regard, dancer Sanjida Rahman said, since I dance, I often need various costumes. I don't always have much time to go to the market and buy. Then I have to rely on online shopping.

Understanding food ordered online.

Food at home

In 2021, many people have still taken advantage of online food shopping. They have ordered through various restaurant apps including Foodpanda or on the Facebook page of the food shop. In addition, many have been able to buy food at affordable prices due to the various discount opportunities. The demand for food will increase in the coming years as there is a facility to complain even after the food is delivered and the quality is maintained.

The owner of Dhanmondi Cafe Basmati said, "We didn't have to go through much trouble. Usually, we just have to inform the number of orders we have for delivery. This has enabled many food chains to survive in the beginning."

The use of smartwatches has increased.

Benefits of smartwatches, not watches

The demand for smartphones started increasing in 2021 as part of the development of technology. Therefore, along with smartphones, confidence in smartwatches also started increasing. In this regard, a seller at Bashundhara's K R Y Shop said, "Usually, smartwatches will give you the opportunity to customize them. You get the opportunity to change the strap and it can be used in various fields as it has other features attached to it. That is why everyone is leaning towards smartwatches. Moreover, since the price is lower than a good watch, people of all levels can buy smartwatches. There is no shortage of style in it."

There was a high demand for round smartwatches in the market. Even many famous brands were interested in making smartwatches.

A person working on a laptop.

Demand for laptops and phones

The computer and smartwatch market was the most diverse in 2021. Meanwhile, some famous brands such as LG announced to stop making phones. Still, there was no shortage of good phones in the budget. Everyone showed interest in buying a good phone or laptop to ensure online classes and regular communication.

Especially the refurbished computer market was always busy. In this regard, an official of An Noor IT in Mirpur said, "Initially, there was no supply in the market. Still, we had to procure good laptops or computers in various ways and give them to the buyers. As a result, the prices of computer parts have increased in the market now." In addition, the demand for Wi-Fi routers has also started to increase.

Symbolic Internet.

Changes in Internet Facilities

During the Corona period, everyone has leaned towards using Wi-Fi. Especially since the closure of free Facebook, everyone has turned to Wi-Fi to reduce mobile data costs. At this time, the number of games like Ludo, Spades, or Free Fire PUBG has increased. These games were also quite effective in keeping in touch with friends.

Wedding attire.

Changes in wedding arrangements

In early 2021, there were various restrictions on gatherings. However, festivals or wedding arrangements did not stop. Event management businesses mainly survived on wedding arrangements. However, there have been changes in arrangements. In most cases, weddings have been organized on a small scale by families. As a result, the additional costs of arrangements have been reduced.

Everyone has tried to remain normal in terms of attire. Weddings have been organized from community centers to restaurants or party centers. Various normal events before the wedding have been held domestically. Although the wedding arrangements have been completed through pre-wedding photoshoots and post-wedding photoshoots.

However, the deterioration of relationships is also noticeable. The divorce rate has also increased by about seventeen percent during this time.

A couple went on a trip with their children.

Tours have become more popular

Tours were popular during the restrictions in 2021. A tourist named Sanjida Akhter, who visited Cox's Bazar, said, "Since there is an indefinite holiday, we have to make plans in a hurry. Sitting at home increases mental depression. Along with tour spots, hiking and bicycle riding have been seen to be popular.

A young woman on rideshare.

The number of pathao and ride shares has increased

People have had good and bad experiences with ride shares in 2021. With restrictions on bus or rickshaw operations and the subsequent increase in diesel prices, people have turned to ride shares. A passenger in Jhigatola said, "I can reach my destination in a very short time. Although it seems a little more money, it is actually saving time."

A person exercising.

Focus on health awareness

Everyone had extra attention towards health awareness in 2021. In this regard, changes have been observed in diet, running, meditation, and eating habits. Along with the increase in gym membership, there has been an interest in personal exercise. Even stars have regularly shared posts about exercise on social media.

In this regard, documentary filmmaker Lawrence Das Niloy said, since we are going through a difficult time, there is no alternative to health awareness at this time. And exercise is the first step to maintaining the body's stamina and fitness and it is very effective.

Headline_English: Create a new routine in the new year to stay fit
Content_Enlish:
After the Corona disaster, many people have turned their attention to disease-fighting abilities. Life may have returned to a little normalcy. Still, the Corona situation has not completely passed. So special attention should be paid to health care. But how do you think you can focus on your health care next year? At least without going to the gym. 

Keep health apps 
It is possible to develop some good habits by using health apps. These apps play the role of a guide. Since everyone has a smartphone, health apps will play an effective role. In this way, you can develop some good habits. 

Make your home a gym 
If you want, you can organize a gym at home. You can exercise with a few necessary equipment based on expert advice. Who said expensive equipment is the solution to all problems? 

Meditate 
It is possible to protect your mental health through meditation. Especially if you develop the habit of meditating in the park or with people around you in the morning, both social relationships and mental health will improve. 

Walk 
Those who do not like exercise, develop the habit of walking. Developing the habit of walking at different times of the day is good for health.

Headline_English: 5 tips to control high blood pressure
Content_Enlish:
Many people have the problem of sudden increase in blood pressure. It is quite difficult to reduce it when the pressure increases. If it is not very dangerous, you can easily reduce it at home. Blood pressure refers to the pressure of blood on the arterial wall. Its level can decrease further throughout the day. As you get older, the risk of increasing pressure also increases. 

High blood pressure is, of course, a very common thing. An adult's high blood pressure is usually within 130/80. However, women's blood pressure is five levels lower. If your high blood pressure is 180 systolic and 120 diastolic, then you need to seek medical attention quickly. 

The main question is, how can you reduce blood pressure before the condition becomes serious? We have some ways. 

Lose weight 

Focus on losing weight 

Excess weight or fat puts pressure on your veins. So, focus on losing weight while you still have time. 

Exercise regularly 

Keep yourself busy with physical exercise 

You should develop a habit of regular exercise. Especially in the morning, easily keep yourself busy with physical exercise by walking, running or playing sports in the park. 

Reduce salt intake 

health 
Do not eat raw salt at all 

According to a report by the World Health Organization, you should not eat more than five grams of salt per day. Especially do not eat raw salt at all. Use other flavor enhancers instead of salt. 

Eat potassium-rich foods 

Consume potassium-rich foods 

Ensuring a balanced diet will definitely benefit you. However, consume potassium-rich foods. Cow's milk, boiled potatoes, raw tomatoes, and prunes are rich in potassium. 

Refrain from smoking or drinking 

Refrain from smoking 

Do not smoke or drink alcohol. Then you will get relief from high blood pressure.

Headline_English: Healthy foods that increase weight
Content_Enlish:
Eating healthy food is important. To keep your health on tip-top, you have to develop eating habits. However, some healthy foods cause rapid weight gain. Headline_English: 2021 will be a year of possibilities
Content_Enlish:
If Bangladesh can use the experience of the adverse situation of 2020 in 2021, it will be an example for the whole world. Because, Bangladesh is moving forward at a fast pace after overcoming the shock of the pandemic. The rural economy is still strong. Expatriate income is increasing at a fast pace. Export income is increasing. Mega projects are also gaining momentum. The stock market, which was in crisis, has now found life. Banks have enough money for large-scale investment. Various domestic and foreign international organizations are also saying that the Bangladeshi economy is moving forward. The World Bank's recent forecast report has expected the highest growth (1.6 percent) in South Asia. Although this is less than the government target. Despite this, very few countries have been able to maintain positive growth during the Corona period. 

The indicators of the country's economy that are in a good position despite the Corona hit in 2020 are expected to become even stronger in 2021. If there is no need to go into lockdown due to the second phase of Corona, then all economic indicators will be dynamic. Several economic indicators, including expatriate income, are already in a strong position. 

Bangladesh's export earnings hit rock bottom in April as the global economy ground to a halt due to the coronavirus pandemic. In total, only $520 million worth of goods were exported that month. Only $360 million was earned from garment exports. After that, export earnings started increasing in May. They increased much more in June. After that, the positive trend continued in the first three months of the current 2020-21 fiscal year. Due to the lockdown due to Corona and the return of many foreign workers and engineers to the country, the work on major projects like the Padma Bridge, Metrorail and Karnaphuli Tunnel, which were the government's priorities in 2020, could not proceed at the desired speed. However, most of the projects gained momentum towards the end of the year. Everyone expects that the economy will be strengthened through mega projects in the new year. 

The year 2020 has passed and 2021 has come. Leaving behind 2020, the year when thousands of people lost their relatives, lost jobs, lost capital, and the economy was paralyzed, the new year will be a year of possibilities for Bangladesh. Bangladesh will be close to achieving its goal of building a strong reserve of $50 billion by 2030 by 2021. Those concerned say that although it will take time for all people in Bangladesh to get vaccinated, developed countries are getting vaccinated already. As a result, their shopping, travel, and consumption expenses will increase. As a result, our exports and labor market will turn around again in the new year.

Headline_English: Journalists are fearless despite Corona: Information Minister
Content_Enlish:
Bangladesh is moving forward under the leadership of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina even amid the Corona pandemic, and media workers are also working fearlessly, said Information and Broadcasting Minister and Joint General Secretary of the Awami League Dr. Hasan Mahmud. 

He said this while representing Bangladesh at the ministerial-level inaugural discussion at the Leaders Web Summit organized by the Asia-Pacific Institute for Broadcasting Development-AIBD in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, online from his office at the Secretariat on Wednesday (June 2) afternoon. 

Dr. Hasan Mahmud said in his speech that Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries in the world. Despite this, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, the daughter of Bangabandhu, has been able to control the Corona infection in the country under her visionary leadership and has not allowed any crisis in food and work for the people of the country. Not only that, in the last one year, the country's per capita income has surpassed India's to 2,227 US dollars, making Bangladesh the third among the 20 countries with positive GDP growth in the world. 

Highly praising the role of the country's media during the Corona period, the Information and Broadcasting Minister said that the country's mainstream media is playing a huge role in providing people with accurate information about Corona, spreading health awareness messages and preventing rumor mongering, and journalists are working fearlessly. Hundreds of media workers have been infected with Corona, many have also died. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has continued special assistance for all media workers. 

AIBD Director Philomena Nana Pragasam chaired a discussion on the role of the media in providing information on the pandemic, which was attended by Malaysian Minister of Communications and Multimedia Dato Saifuddin Abdullah, Nigerian Minister of Information and Culture Alhaji Lai Mohammed, Philippine Minister of Information Jose Ruperto Martin Andanar, and Cambodian Deputy Minister of Information Dr. Sok Prasith. 

A discussion meeting was held in the ministry's conference room this afternoon to mark the transfer of Secretary Khawaja Mia and the retirement of Additional Secretary Jahanara Parveen.

Headline_English: What is in the 50th budget of Bangladesh?
Content_Enlish:
Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal is going to present the budget for the upcoming fiscal year 2021-22 in the National Parliament on Thursday under the title 'Bangladesh on the path to a strong future by prioritizing life and livelihood'. 

This is the third budget of the government led by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in a row. This is AHM Mustafa Kamal's third budget as Finance Minister. He will begin his budget speech at 3 pm. The Finance Ministry has mentioned that the marginalized population of the country will be given priority in this budget. 

Tajuddin Ahmed announced the first budget after Bangladesh became independent. The size of that budget announced on June 30, 1972 was only 786 crore taka. After a long journey, AHM Mustafa Kamal is bringing the 50th budget of Bangladesh. The size of which stands at 6 lakh 3 thousand 681 crore taka. That is, the size of the country's budget has increased 767 times in the 50 years of independence. So far, a total of 49 budgets have been presented by 12 people. Among them, one is the President, 9 Finance Ministers and two Financial Advisors. The late M Saifur Rahman and Abul Maal Abdul Muhith have presented the most budgets as individuals, 12 each. Among them, Abul Maal Abdul Muhith presented a record 10 consecutive budgets for the Awami League. 

Although the size of the budget increases every year, the development allocation is decreasing. After independence, 55 to 60 percent of the total budget was allocated for the development sector. But in the budgets presented in recent years, less than one-third of the total expenditure is allocated for development programs. That is, a large part of the expenditure is going to sectors like government salaries and allowances, interest payments, and subsidies. 

The size of the budget deficit that is determined could be kept within 5 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) in previous years. But after the start of the Corona outbreak, the budget deficit is now being calculated by keeping it above 6 percent. The budget was announced on the assumption that the deficit would be large since the start of the Corona outbreak last year. 

As always, a press conference is being organized the day after the budget presentation. In accordance with health regulations during this time of Corona, the post-budget press conference for the fiscal year 2021-22 will be held virtually on Friday, June 4 at 3 pm.

Headline_English: Initiatives have been taken to produce vaccines in the country: Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that in addition to procuring the coronavirus vaccine, initiatives have been taken to produce it in the country. Discussions are underway with various countries and manufacturing institutions for technology transfer to this end. 

She said this in response to a question from Begum Monira Sultan, a member of parliament from the reserved women's seat, during the question and answer session in the National Parliament on Wednesday. The question and answer session was tabled in the parliament meeting chaired by Speaker Dr. Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury. 

Earlier, the Prime Minister said that the current government has taken various important steps from the beginning to ensure the health of the people from the corona pandemic. The closure of educational institutions was announced along with the implementation of nationwide and regional lockdowns. In addition, the government has taken various incentive measures to save livelihoods and the economy, including providing relief assistance to the poor. Bangladesh has proven its capability to prevent the spread of the virus by providing protective equipment to frontline warriors in the fight against Corona, including doctors, nurses, health workers, law enforcement agencies, and administration, providing financial incentives, importing testing kits on time, and setting up labs in different parts of the country, making necessary arrangements for Corona testing. 

He said that Bangladesh is one of the countries in the world that was able to start vaccination activities early to prevent Corona infection. The government has taken initiatives from the beginning to get Corona vaccines on time. The steps taken by the government to procure vaccines are- Corona vaccination activities are ongoing with vaccines collected by the government from the Serum Institute of India and received as a gift from the Government of India. As of May 18, a total of 96 lakh 41 thousand 312 doses of vaccine have been administered to various groups of people over 40 and on the front lines in the country. Vaccine procurement activities from India are continuing. 

The Government of India imposed a ban on vaccine exports in April due to the serious deterioration of the Corona situation in India. As a result, the Bangladesh government has taken the initiative to procure vaccines from China and Russia as an alternative source. The purchase of vaccines from China's Sinopharm has already been approved by the Cabinet Committee on Health. In June, July and August; 5 million vaccines will be available from China each month. Five hundred thousand doses of the Covid-19 vaccine have been received as a gift from the Chinese government. The work of providing these vaccines has started on May 25.

Headline_English: Train tickets will be available at the counter from June 8
Content_Enlish:
New rules for selling train tickets will come into effect from Tuesday, June 8. Train tickets will also be available at the counter from today. Currently, tickets are being sold only online. An instruction regarding the sale of tickets at the counter was issued by Bangladesh Railway on Tuesday. 

It said that due to the coronavirus pandemic, new rules have been introduced for issuing tickets for Bangladesh Railway passenger trains. Tickets will be sold at the counter from June 8. 

In this regard, Bangladesh Railway Additional Director General (Operations) Sardar Shahadat Ali said that during the Corona period, according to government instructions, passenger trains will transport 50 percent of passengers. Now tickets are being sold only online. Tickets will be available at the counter as well as online from June 8. 

According to the new instructions, from June 8, 50 percent of Bangladesh Railway intercity train tickets will be issued through online and mobile apps and the remaining tickets will be issued at the railway counter from 8 am in advance. 

Unsold tickets from counters, mobile apps and online quotas will be issued simultaneously, i.e. through any medium, 48 (forty-eight) hours before the start of the journey. Other rules for issuing issued tickets and adhering to hygiene rules will remain unchanged.

Headline_English: A TikTok girl who returned to India recounts horrific accounts of torture
Content_Enlish:
A court has granted five-day remand to four people, including Ashraful Islam Rafi, the mastermind of a trafficking ring arrested in a case filed in India on charges of trafficking women and forcing them into sexual acts. 

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Begum Yasmin Ara issued the remand order on Wednesday (June 2) afternoon. Apart from Rafi, the other accused are Abdur Rahman Sheikh, Ismail Sardar and Mosh. Sahida Begum. 

Investigation officer Mohammad Mohiuddin Faruk presented the accused in the court in the case filed by Hatirjheel Police Station in the capital and applied for 10-day remand for each. After the hearing, the judge granted them five-day remand. 

RAB has arrested Ashraful Mandal alias Boss Rafi, one of the masterminds of an international women trafficking ring, and his associate Madam Sahida, in connection with the recent brutal torture of a Bangladeshi girl in India. 

From Monday (May 31) to Tuesday (June 1) morning, RAB headquarters detectives and RAB-3 arrested four members of a women trafficking ring from Jhenaidah Sadar, Abhaynagar in Jessore and Benapole. RAB said that during initial interrogation, they confessed to being involved in the trafficking ring. 

A TikTok group pool party is organized every week at a five-star hotel in Tongi in the capital. Young women of all ages participate in this pool party. After they show TikTok videos, they are selected for trafficking based on their qualifications. Hundreds of young women have been trafficked from the pool party to various countries in neighboring India and the Middle East by showing the lure of becoming TikTok models. So far, more than five hundred young women have been trafficked to India and the Middle East through this ring.

Headline_English: The postponed 371 Union Parishad elections are scheduled for June 21.
Content_Enlish:
The first phase of elections in 371 union parishads, 11 municipalities and the by-election in Lakshmipur-2 constituency were postponed due to the increase in the coronavirus outbreak in the country. The voting will be held on June 21, said EC Secretary Md. Humayun Kabir Khandaker. 
He made this announcement at a press conference at the Agargaon Election Building in the capital on Wednesday (June 2). Earlier, voting was scheduled for these places on April 11. But due to the increase in the coronavirus infection, the commission postponed all types of elections from April 1. 
In addition, the by-elections for the vacant seats in Sylhet-3, Dhaka-14 and Comilla-5 will be held on July 14, the EC Secretary said. The secretary said that the last date for collection of nomination papers is June 15. The date for selection of nomination papers is June 17. Appeals can be filed between June 18 and 20. The date for disposal of appeals is June 21-22. The last date for withdrawal of candidacy is June 23. Symbol allocation will be on June 24. Voting will be held on July 14.

Headline_English: 720 job seekers opened their eyes
Content_Enlish:
720 job seekers opened their eyes in disappointment. They have been recommended for the government job called 'Sonar Harin'. The Public Service Commission (PSC) has recommended 720 candidates for appointment to first-class non-cadre posts from among those who passed the final results of the 38th BCS but did not get a cadre. 

The recommendation to appoint these candidates was made at a special meeting of the commission on Wednesday based on the merit list of BCS and the appointment rules of the relevant posts. This was announced in a press release of the PSC. 

In a PSC release on Wednesday (June 2), it was said that in accordance with the provisions of the Appointment to Non-Cadre Posts (Special) Rules-2010 and the Revised Rules-2014, the commission has temporarily recommended 780 candidates to non-cadre first-class posts from among the candidates who were not recommended for cadre posts in the 38th BCS examination, based on the merit list obtained in BCS and the appointment rules of the relevant posts. 
The number of candidates who passed the written and oral exams of the 38th BCS but were not recommended for cadre posts due to shortage of posts is 6,173. Out of these, the number of candidates who applied for recommendations for non-cadre posts is 5,032. Earlier, 983 people were recommended for appointment to non-cadre first class posts in two rounds. The PSC has published the results by recommending 780 posts in a total of 39 categories, including 661 in three categories of the Technical and Madrasa Education Department of the Ministry of Education. 
All PSC examination activities temporarily suspended 
The PSC published the final results of the 38th BCS on June 30 last year. It recommended the appointment of 2,204 people from various cadres. The PSC published the notification for the 38th BCS on June 20, 2017. The preliminary examination of the 38th BCS was held on December 29 of that year. About four lakh candidates applied. The PSC published the results of the preliminary examination of the 38th BCS on February 28, 2018. 16,286 people passed it. The BCS written exam began on August 8 last year. In this, 9,862 people were nominated for the oral exam.

Headline_English: Alok Sharma meets the Prime Minister
Content_Enlish:
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina received a courtesy call from Alok Sharma, President of the United Nations-hosted World Climate Conference (COP-26) and British MP. He met the Prime Minister at Ganabhaban on Wednesday morning. 

Later, the Prime Minister's Press Secretary Ihsanul Karim briefed reporters. He said that the meeting discussed various issues including climate change situation, its global adverse effects, adaptation, mitigation and climate fund and the corona pandemic.

During the meeting, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that Bangladesh hopes that the UK will highlight the interests and priorities of countries at risk of climate change in international forums. Regarding the adverse effects of global climate change, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that Bangladesh and other countries at risk of climate change will be severely affected by the adverse effects of climate change. Although the rate of carbon emission in Bangladesh is very low, we are still being severely affected.

Alok Sharma expressed hope that Bangladesh, under the leadership of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, will play an important role in combating the adverse effects of global climate change as the President of the Climate Vulnerable Forum (CVF).

He invited Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to attend the next COP-26 conference to be held in the UK in November. Highlighting the importance of green energy, Alok Sharma said that everyone should move towards green energy. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said that we are moving towards green energy. We have been given 5.8 million solar energy connections. Prime Minister and Awami League President Sheikh Hasina also said that the government and the party have undertaken a massive tree plantation program in Bangladesh. Alok Sharma said that the vaccination program for the coronavirus pandemic is going well in the UK.

Highlighting Bangladesh's steps to combat the corona pandemic, Sheikh Hasina said that despite being a densely populated country, Bangladesh has taken various steps to keep the wheels of the country's economy moving even during this pandemic.

Among others present during the meeting were Ambassador at Large Mohammad Ziauddin, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister Dr. Ahmed Kaikaus, Bangladesh High Commissioner to the UK Saida Muna Tasneem, and UK High Commissioner to Bangladesh Robert Dickson. The UN-hosted World Climate Conference (COP-26) will be held in Scotland in November this year.

In the absence of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, the senior among them will preside over the session.

Condolences were expressed on the deaths of former members of parliament, film actress Sarah Begum Kabori, Meraj Uddin Mollah, Gazi M.M. In this case, a member of parliament will attend the session for three to four working days. It is mandatory for them to have a corona negative certificate to join. As a result, members of parliament will need to undergo multiple sample tests to attend the session.

Headline_English: The suffering of Bangladeshi expatriates going to Saudi Arabia has been reduced.
Content_Enlish:
Saudi expatriates returning to their workplaces in Bangladesh will be able to book hotels in Saudi Arabia through more than 300 local travel agents listed by Saudi Airlines through Saudi Airlines' financial and software channels from Thursday (June 3). 

This eliminates the problem of institutional quarantine for Bangladeshi expatriates traveling from Bangladesh to Saudi Arabia. 

Moreover, since May 20, Saudi Airlines authorities have agreed to reissue tickets free of charge to expatriates who have missed their flights due to hotel bookings. Ticket date changes or re-issues can be done at the Saudi Airlines office at Sonargaon Hotel in Karwan Bazar as well as travel agents. 

Also, from now on, those who purchase Saudi Airlines up-down tickets from Saudi Arabia and return to the country can reconfirm or change their dates at listed travel agents located in Dhaka, Sylhet, Chittagong and other cities. This reduces the need to come to the Saudi Airlines office in Karwan Bazar, Dhaka from remote areas of the country. 

Travel agents have been charged a maximum of two thousand taka for hotel bookings and a maximum of five hundred taka for ticket re-issuance. 

To prevent the spread of the pandemic corona, the Saudi government issued various travel-related instructions on May 17. Which came into effect from May 20. According to them, foreign workers who have not received two doses of corona vaccine in their own country or have not received one dose of vaccine while in Saudi Arabia will have to undergo mandatory institutional quarantine in specific hotels if they want to travel to Saudi Arabia. 

In this, Saudi expatriates who came to the country on vacation were unable to book hotels due to various reasons, including severe financial crisis and institutional quarantine. Since the full amount has to be paid at the time of hotel booking. Since most of the expatriate workers do not have international credit cards, they were unable to book hotels. To solve this problem of expatriates, the Ministry of Expatriate Welfare and Overseas Employment decided to provide financial assistance of 25,000 taka to expatriates, but the expatriates were unable to book hotels. In view of this, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment has formed a Quick Response Team to quickly resolve all the problems of expatriates. 

The team has agreed to resolve this problem after holding regular meetings with Saudi Airlines and ATAB (Association of Travel Agencies Bangladesh).

Headline_English: Budget allocates funds to build 33 new power plants
Content_Enlish:
Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal has presented a proposed budget of Tk 6,368.1 billion for the fiscal year 2021-2022 in the 11th National Parliament. A revenue target of Tk 3,89,000 billion has been set in the budget. Out of this, Tk 27,484 billion has been proposed for the Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Department in the proposed budget. The Finance Minister has proposed this allocation for the construction of 33 more power plants and an LNG terminal in the country. 

Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal announced this information in the draft budget for the fiscal year 2021-22 in the National Parliament on Thursday (June 3) afternoon under the title 'Life and livelihood are the priority, the future of Bangladesh'. 

The Finance Minister announced this allocation in his budget proposal on Thursday afternoon. The proposed allocation is Tk 726 billion more than the outgoing fiscal year. In the fiscal year 2020-21, the allocation for this sector was Tk 26,758 billion. 

The Finance Minister said in his budget speech that tenders for six power plants with a capacity of 650 MW are under process. He said that 33 power plants with a capacity of 15,19 MW are under planning. Due to the government's strict measures, the system loss of electricity has reduced from 14.33 percent to 8.73 percent. 

Mustafa Kamal said that due to the government's far-sighted and timely measures, the country has achieved unprecedented success in the power and energy sectors in the last 12 years. Currently, 5 times more electricity is being generated compared to 2009. The total power generation capacity in the country (including captive and renewable energy) has increased to 25,227 MW. 

In his budget speech, the Finance Minister mentioned that the implementation of the Prime Minister's commitment to 'deliver electricity to every household' has made it possible to bring 99 percent of the country's total population under the power facility. 

He said that to meet the growing electricity demand of Bangladesh, 38 power plants with a capacity of 14,115 MW are under construction and agreements have been signed to build 20 power plants with a capacity of 2,961 MW. Among the mega projects taken up in the power sector, the work on the construction of the Rampal coal-based Maitree Super Thermal Power Plant Project, the Matarbari Ultra Super Critical Power Plant Project and the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant Project is progressing at a fast pace, the Finance Minister said. 

The Finance Minister said that electricity production has started on a commercial basis after the construction of the 1,320 MW Payra Thermal Power Plant. Currently, 722 MW of electricity is being generated from renewable energy. He also believes that through the implementation of the projects, it will be possible to meet the growing demand in the transmission and supply of electricity in the country. 

Highlighting the issue of ensuring energy security, the Finance Minister said in his budget speech that a large part of our total energy demand is met through natural gas. Out of the 27 gas fields discovered in the country, 20 are currently in production. In 2009, natural gas production in Bangladesh was 1,744 million cubic feet, which has now increased to about 2,525 million cubic feet. The remaining part of the total demand for natural gas is being imported as LNG and added to the national grid, said Mustafa Kamal. 

Finance Minister Mustafa Kamal said that two floating LNG terminals with a total capacity of 500 million cubic feet each have been set up in Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar district, with a total capacity of 1,000 million cubic feet. The imported LNG is being converted back into gas through the floating terminals, and an average of 600 to 700 million cubic feet of gas is being added to the national grid daily. Initiatives have been taken to set up a land-based LNG terminal with a daily capacity of 1,000 million cubic feet in Matarbari, Cox's Bazar to increase LNG supply. The Finance Minister also said that the government has taken initiatives to increase fuel oil reserves to increase and consolidate energy security. 

The proposed allocation is Tk 726 crore more than the outgoing fiscal year. In the 2020-21 fiscal year, Tk 26,758 crore was allocated for this sector.

Headline_English: Allocation for sports fields reduced

In order to increase sports opportunities, the construction and development of sports infrastructure including modern stadiums, gymnasiums, swimming pools has been continued across the country, and as part of this, the construction of Sheikh Russell Mini Stadium is underway in the upazilas. In addition, 14 projects for the construction and development of sports infrastructure are underway in the fiscal year 2020-21.

Headline_English: Prices of motorcycles and hybrid cars are falling
Content_Enlish:
In the proposed budget for the upcoming fiscal year 2021-22, duty exemption is being given on the import of motorcycle raw materials and fuel-efficient motorcycle mopeds. In addition, duty on microbus import may be reduced to encourage the use of safe public transport to prevent accidents. As a result, the price of motorcycles and hybrid vehicles may decrease in the market. 

Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal presented the budget for the fiscal year 2021-22 in the National Parliament on Thursday (June 3). 

In the budget proposal for motorcycles, the Finance Minister said, I am proposing to make necessary amendments to the existing notification for the motorcycle manufacturing or assembly industry by including some new raw materials to expand the aftermarket industry. Mopeds are fuel-efficient motorcycles. Since they play an important role in the economic activities of small traders and the public, I am proposing to reduce the duty rate on mopeds to ensure affordable prices. 

Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal said in his budget speech, "I propose to reduce the duty rate on the import of microbuses in order to discourage the use of accident-prone vehicles like Nasimon and Laguna and encourage the use of microbuses as an alternative public transport. I propose to rearrange the duty rate on the import of hybrid vehicles in order to encourage the use of environment-friendly hybrid vehicles." 

In the proposal, he said, "To protect the dumper or tipper assembling industry, I propose to reduce the duty rate on the import of dumpers or tippers in CKD condition." 
Incidentally, mopeds are smaller than motorcycles. Their capacity is within 50 cc.

Headline_English: TIN not required to buy savings certificates up to Tk 2 lakh
Content_Enlish:
Now, there is a requirement to submit a Tax Identification Number (TIN) certificate to buy savings certificates worth more than Tk 50,000. This limit will increase from the next fiscal year. 

From the first day of the 2021-22 fiscal year, a TIN certificate will not be required to buy savings certificates worth more than Tk 2 lakh. That is, TIN will be mandatory to purchase savings certificates worth more than Tk 2 lakh and to open a postal savings account. 

Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal said this in his budget speech for the proposed 2021-22 fiscal year in the National Parliament on Thursday. 
Usually, the government resorts to two sources to meet the budget deficit. Foreign and domestic sources. In the next budget, the dependence on domestic sources is being reduced somewhat and the dependence on foreign sources is being increased. The target for borrowing from the domestic sector this time is Tk 1,13,453 crore. The government will borrow Tk 76,452 crore from banks within the domestic sector. And Tk 32,000 crore will be borrowed from national savings certificates. Tk 5,01 crore will be borrowed from other sectors. 

The budget has set a target of 97,738 crore taka for borrowing from foreign sources. The target for borrowing from foreign sources is also the highest ever. The government had set a target of 20,000 crore taka for borrowing by selling savings certificates in the 2020-21 fiscal year. However, due to the increase in the sale of savings certificates, it was revised to 30,303 crore taka. The government has set a target of further increasing it to 32,000 crore taka in the 2021-22 fiscal year.

Headline_English: House rent must be deposited in the bank
Content_Enlish:

The Finance Minister said, "If any amount of house rent, salary and allowances exceeding Rs 15,000 and any other type of expenditure exceeds Rs 50,000, I am proposing to impose the obligation to pay that amount through mobile financial service or MFS in addition to bank transfer." 

He also said, "If the supply and contractor bills are not taken through banking or mobile financial service (MFS), I am proposing an additional 50 percent deduction of tax at source."

Headline_English: Even if you build a house in the village, you will have to pay taxes.
Content_Enlish:

In addition, TIN has also been made mandatory for the registration of any cooperative society. Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal has imposed this provision in the proposed budget for the upcoming fiscal year 2021-22. 
In addition, if you start a cooperative society with friends or colleagues, you will have to take a TIN even if you register it. As a result, homeowners and cooperative societies will come under the tax net.

Headline_English: Per capita income increased to $2,227, average life expectancy 72.6 years
Content_Enlish:
Per capita income in Bangladesh has increased to 2227 US dollars. In terms of taka, which amounts to 1 lakh 89 thousand taka. And the average life expectancy of people has increased to 72.6 years in 2019-20. Finance Minister AHM Mustafa Kamal gave this information in his budget speech. 

The Finance Minister said that Bangladesh is a changing country. We have passed a golden era in the history of Bangladesh, which after the globally acclaimed Bangabandhu, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has brought Bangladesh to the highest level in history in all areas including economy and development, social policy, culture, law and order, foreign policy. In the last 12 years, the average GDP growth was 6.6 percent, which was more than 7 percent in the 2016-17, 2017-18 and 2018-19 fiscal years and exceeded 8 percent in the 2018-19 fiscal year. Inflation was at a tolerable level. 

He further said, in the fiscal year 2005-06, our per capita income was 543 US dollars, which has now increased to 2,227 US dollars. At that time, the poverty rate was 41.5 percent, currently the poverty rate has decreased to 20.5 percent. The size of the GDP has increased from 4,82,337 crore taka to 28 lakh crore taka. 

The Finance Minister said, in the fiscal year 2005-06, the size of the budget was 61 thousand crore taka, which has increased tenfold in the current fiscal year. The average life expectancy of the people has increased from 59 years in the fiscal year 2005-06 to 72.6 years in 2019-20. The infant mortality rate has decreased from 84 to 28 per thousand and the maternal mortality rate has decreased from 370 to 165 per lakh.

Headline_English: 10 youths arrested in ice trade, all from upper-class families
Content_Enlish:
They are children of wealthy families. Some have returned from abroad with higher education. And now they are involved in the dangerous drug crystal meth or ice business. They also used to consume this deadly drug. After receiving information about this gang, the Narcotics Control Department (DNC) tried for about a month. Finally, from Friday afternoon to Saturday, 10 members of the gang were arrested in a drive in Banani, Uttara, Banasree and Khilgaon areas of the capital. 

The arrested are - Md. Rubayat, Rohit Hossain, Masum Hannan, Aman Ullah, Mohaiminul Islam Ivan, Musa Will Babar, Syeda Anika Zaman alias Arpita Zaman, Laila Afroz Praya, Tanzim Ali Shah and Hasibul Islam. Half a kilogram of ice and five thousand yaba were recovered from them. Eight cases are being filed against them. 

A press conference was organized at the Dhaka Metropolitan (North) office of the Narcotics Control Department in Tejgaon in the capital on Saturday to inform about this. In it, Additional Director General of the department, Fazlur Rahman, said that drug addicts are now leaning more towards ice than Yaba. Ice is 20 times stronger than Yaba. It looks like a palm candy. It is possible to make 500 pieces of Yaba with just one gram of ice. And one lakh Yaba could be made with the half kilogram of ice seized. The guardians of the arrested people, and even many members of the law enforcement agencies, are still not familiar with ice. That is why they found the business of ice more convenient than Yaba. Moreover, it is easy to make Yaba by bringing the raw materials. 

Fazlur Rahman said that according to the initial interrogation, a group of 10-12 people controlled the sale and purchase of ice in Dhaka. One of that group was arrested on August 5. As a result, the work of identifying the rest of the gang has become easier. First, a phone number was found, and the operation was started based on that number. 

The operation to arrest the ice business gang was led by Mehedi Hasan, Assistant Director of the Directorate. He said that Rubayat, Rohit Hossain and Babar were first arrested from Banani. Among them, Rohit studied business management in Malaysia. Like the others, he is also from a wealthy family. His father owns a market. Rubayat's father has a construction materials business. These three regularly consumed and sold drugs in Babar's rented flat in Banani. Later, Masum Hannan was arrested from his house. The family had already filed a GD against him. During the operation, the family members handed him over. The father of arrested Ivan was a big contractor. Ivan used to collect ice from Laila. And Laila used to buy from Anika Zaman. Each of them has seven to eight regular buyers. They used to sell a gram of ice for 10 to 12 thousand taka. 

An official of the Narcotics Control Directorate told Samakal that the person arrested first is one of the few second-tier ice sellers. He has been involved in the ice business for a long time. It is believed that this gang imports ice from Myanmar and supplies it to various parts of the country, including Dhaka. The arrested people said during initial interrogation that to increase the number of ice buyers, they initially supplied it to the target people for free. Later, they became addicted and became regular buyers.

Headline_English: Five members of car theft gang arrested in Narayanganj
Content_Enlish:
RAB-4 has arrested 5 members, including the main coordinator of an organized car hijacking gang, along with firearms, from Fatulla, Narayanganj. 

RAB members have recovered 3 pickups and 1 CNG stolen from them. 

According to a press release from RAB, from the afternoon of August 27 to the night, RAB-4 conducted a raid in the Fatulla area of ​​Narayanganj and arrested the main coordinator of the car hijacking gang, Md. Azim Uddin (38), and his associates Kamrul Hasan (26), Omar Faruk (25). They all live in Noakhali district. 

In addition to the pickup and CNG, RAB recovered 1 pistol, 1 round of bullets, 3 knives, 1 Chinese axe, 6 mobile phones and 12,000 taka in cash. 

RAB said that during the initial interrogation, the arrested persons said that they are members of an organized car hijacking gang. 15-20 people are involved in this organized gang. The main mastermind and coordinator of this gang is the arrested Azim Uddin. This group has been active for the past 5-6 years. This syndicate members have hijacked more than a hundred cars from different areas of the country. So far, this gang is said to be doing business worth more than crores of taka through car hijacking. 

The arrested persons told during interrogation that they used to hijack and steal pickups, CNG in Narayanganj, Savar, Gazipur and surrounding areas along the Dhaka-Chittagong route. 

There are several cases against them in different police stations of Dhaka, Narayanganj, Narsingdi, Comilla and Gazipur. 

RAB said that these syndicate members were previously involved in various crimes. They increased the number of members of this gang by getting acquainted with criminals in jail after being arrested in various cases. The ringleader, Azim, also has a drug case against him.

Headline_English: Nurul, a computer operator, now owns assets worth Tk 460 crore
Content_Enlish:
RAB has arrested Nurul Islam (41), a former contractual computer operator of Teknaf Port, from Mohammadpur in the capital, who had embezzled crores of taka through brokerage. Fake money, foreign currency and drugs were recovered during the operation. 

RAB said that the estimated value of Nurul's illegally acquired assets is Tk 4.6 billion. He has a total of 19 bank accounts in different banks under his name and anonymity. 

Based on a secret tip-off, a joint operation by an intelligence agency and RAB was conducted in the capital's Mohammadpur area on Monday midnight and he was arrested. This information was given in a press release sent by RAB. 

Nurul is the son of Md. Abdul Motaleb of Dhunia West Kanainagar area of ​​Bhola Sadar Upazila. Fake notes worth Tk 3,46,500, 3,80,000 Myanmar currency, 4,400 pieces of Yaba tablets and Tk 2,160 in cash were recovered during the operation. During the initial interrogation, Nurul gave various information about his criminal involvement. 

RAB said that during the initial interrogation, the arrested Nurul said that he took a job as a computer operator at the Teknaf land port in 2001 on a contractual basis at a daily rate of 130 taka. While working at the port, he used his position to learn the techniques of smuggling, customs evasion, illegal goods clearance, brokerage, etc. Then, using his position, he joined various brokerage syndicates at the port. At one point, he created a brokerage syndicate. In 2009, he quit his job and arranged for a trusted person to be appointed as the computer operator. And he retained control of the brokerage syndicate. In this way, Nurul embezzled crores of taka. 

RAB further said that Nurul is one of the main bosses of the Teknaf port-based brokerage syndicate. His syndicate has 10-15 members. Who are divided into several groups and conduct brokerage activities. This syndicate was active in unloading goods, controlling transport serials and also unloading illegal goods on the way. With the help of the syndicate, illegal goods were brought from neighboring countries under the guise of wood, dried fish, pickled plums, fish, etc. The members of the gang controlled the Teknaf port, truck stands, port labor and the arrival and departure of ships. 

He said that the arrested Nurul was in cahoots with identified drug dealers. He also coordinated with the hundi syndicate for the trade of other illegal goods and cleverly manipulated under and over invoices. He created several companies to hide the source of illegal income. Among them are MS Al Nahian Enterprise, MS Miftaul Enterprise, MS Alka Enterprise, Alka Real Estate Limited and MS Kaniz Enterprise. Nurul has 6 houses and 13 plots in Dhaka city. In addition, he has a total of 37 places/plots/garden houses/houses in different places including Savar, Teknaf, St. Martin, Bhola in his name/anonymously. The estimated value of his illegally acquired assets is Tk 460 crore. He has a total of 19 bank accounts in different banks in his name/anonymously. Currently, he was investing in the shipping industry and an amusement park near Dhaka. Legal action is under process against him.

Headline_English: Russell doesn't know when he will refund customers' money: RAB
Content_Enlish:
Mohammad Russell, the managing director of e-commerce company Evaly, does not know when he will be able to refund customers' money. 

Commander Khandaker Al Moin, director of the Rapid Action Battalion's (RAB) legal and media wing, told the media that he told RAB this during initial interrogation after being arrested in a fraud case at the capital's Gulshan police station on Wednesday night. 

At a press conference at the RAB head office on Friday, Khandaker Al Moin said, "Russell was confident that he would gradually involve many foreign companies in Evaly, who would invest in Evaly. He hoped that his customer base would increase. But in the current situation, he himself told us that he was skeptical about when he would be able to pay customers and provide them with products." 

Khandaker Al Moin said that during initial interrogation, Russell told RAB that Evaly's debt was about 1,000 crore taka. He claims that the number of customers is 4.4 million. 

Commander Moin said, "His business strategy was to return their products within seven to 45 days, which he would delay for 6 months to a year. After 6-7 months, he would give some money or products to some of the old customers in part. He would not give them to the new ones. In this way, he increased his liabilities through continuous losses. His company has become a liability capital company." 

RAB officer Moin said, "Russell's aim was to create brand value. Russell wanted people to recognize Evaly as a single company in South Asia. He tried to lure many foreign companies at different times. Many companies were interested in investing. But once they get inside, the amount of debt is so high that it is really difficult to get out of that situation. 

After one after another of the complaints against Evaly, the Ministry of Commerce formed an inter-ministerial committee with representatives from the Bangladesh Competition Commission, the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Information Technology (ICT) Division, Bangladesh Bank, the National Board of Revenue (NBR), and the National Consumer Rights Protection Department. 

When Evaly's debt-to-asset ratio was gradually increasing, the committee set a time of three weeks for them to respond. But Mohammad Russell could not present any evidence to the committee. 

Russell told RAB during initial interrogation that the entire amount spent on Evaly's advertising campaign was spent from the money invested by customers. 

Russell has not been able to pay the salaries of Evaly's officials and employees since last June. Evaly now has 1,300 permanent employees and 500 temporary employees. 

During interrogation, it was revealed that Russell and his wife Shamima Nasrin used to receive a salary of 5 lakh taka as their official position. They used to personally use the Audi and Range Rover bought with Evaly's money. Their company has 25-30 cars. According to ancestral sources, there are several lands in Savar, the financial value of which is 7-8 crore taka. 

Evaly has collected customers in the shortest possible time through 'Cyclone Offer', 'Earthquake Offer', 'Cashback Offer', 'Cash on Delivery', 'Priority Store Offer'. 

In addition to 'Eid Offer', 'Baishakhi Offer', Evaly also announced various packages including 'T-Ten', 'T-Five', 'Tri-Three'. 

Commander Khandaker Al Moin said, 'These tempting offers lured the common people. He lured the common people with huge offers, huge discounts, cashback offers. "Which resulted in him becoming a huge customer in the shortest possible time. His (Russell's) business strategy was to extort huge amounts of money from the manufacturer or customer chain network."

Headline_English: 2 Ansarullah Bangla Team militants arrested
Content_Enlish:
The Anti-Terrorism Unit (ATU) of the police has arrested two active members of the banned militant organization Ansarullah Bangla Team (ABT). The operation was conducted in the Kalibari Mosque area of ​​Chechua Bazar under Muktagachha police station in Mymensingh on Thursday. 

The arrested are Kawsar Ahmed Milan and Zahid Mustafa. Two mobile phones, four SIM cards, soft copies and printed copies of seven extremist books were seized from them. These include books by Al Balag, Titumir Media, Sahm Al Hind Media, Jasimuddin Rahmani and Anwar Al Awlaki. In addition, 34 screenshots of their organization's extremist activities and book sales were seized from Facebook and Messenger. 

Police Superintendent Mohammad Aslam Khan of the ATU's Media and Awareness Branch said that the arrested persons had been using social media to sell extremist books by ABT chief Mufti Jasimuddin Rahmani and other authors online for a long time. They had planned and prepared to conspire against the government and the state, create terror in the public mind and endanger public safety. Among them, Kawsar has been involved in collecting, selling and supplying books promoting ABT ideology from different places in Dhaka for 9 years. And Zahid had been cooperating with him for two years. 

The police superintendent said that they used multiple fake Facebook IDs to sell extremist books to ABT members across the country under the guise of a bookstore in Chechua Bazar.

Headline_English: 3 arrested for fraud on Facebook
Content_Enlish:
