The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Detective Branch Lalbagh Division has arrested three people on charges of embezzling money by promising jobs on social media platform Facebook. 

They were arrested from Kalyanpur in the capital on Friday. 257 check books, 234 debit cards, 8 mobile phones and 11 mobile SIMs of different banks were seized from them. 

The three arrested are Md. Kabir Hossain, Md. Shamsul Kabir and Md. Yasin Ali. 

DB Additional Police Commissioner AKM Hafiz Akhter gave details about this at a press briefing organized at the DMP Media Center on Saturday at 12 noon. 

He said that a case was filed under the Digital Security Act at Kadamtali Police Station on Thursday following a complaint from a victim regarding the embezzlement of money by promising lucrative jobs in Canada through Facebook. The Detective Branch Lalbagh Division arrested the three fraudsters Kabir, Shamsul and Yasin in the case.

Headline_English: Chargesheet filed against Parimoni in drug case
Content_Enlish:
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the police has filed a chargesheet in court accusing actress Porimani in a case under the Narcotics Control Act. 

Additional DIG of CID Imam Hossain informed Samakal about this information. He said that a chargesheet has also been filed against Porimani's associate Ashraful Islam Dipu and their drug supplier Kabir. 

The CID says that all the allegations made against the actress in the drug case have been initially proven. Therefore, a chargesheet will be filed against her and three others. 

RAB arrested Porimani in a raid at her house in Banani on August 4. Her alleged uncle Ashraful Islam alias Dipu was also arrested from there. Empty bottles of foreign liquor, bottles of liquor, Yaba, Ice and LSD were seized from the house. Later, RAB filed a drug case against them at Banani Police Station. On the same day, RAB raided the house of Porimani's close friend and producer Nazrul Islam Raj and arrested him and seized drugs. A case was filed against him at Banani Police Station under the Narcotics and Pornography Act. 

Earlier, on August 1, model Mariam Akhter Mou from Mohammadpur and Faria Mahbub Piyasa from Baridhara were arrested. The police filed a case against them under the Narcotics Control Act. The CID is responsible for investigating these cases. 

Porimani was remanded in three phases in the drug case and questioned by the investigation authorities. When Porimani was presented in court for the remand hearing, she expressed her anger in the court premises and said, 'I have been framed. I am innocent. There was no alcohol in my house. A false case has been filed.' After 26 days, this popular film actress of Dhaka cinema was released on bail from prison on September 1. 

The plaintiff in the case filed against Parimoni at Banani Police Station was RAB-1 officer Mojibar Rahman. 

The statement said that based on secret information, RAB came to know that Parimoni had collected foreign liquor through her associate Ashraful Islam Dipur at a house in Banani and kept it for storage. 19 bottles of foreign liquor were seized from inside a wooden frame in her bedroom. Each bottle of liquor costs Tk 9,000. In addition, four grams of ice and an LSD blot were recovered. Another person named Kabir was also made an accused in the same case. 

Meanwhile, the day after Parimoni's arrest, the force's legal and media wing director Khandaker Al Moin said at a press conference at the RAB headquarters in Uttara that the actress has a mini bar at her house. Although she has a liquor license, it has expired long ago. This gang, including Parimoni and Nazrul Raj, used to earn huge money by organizing DJ parties. Parties were held regularly at Parimoni's house. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DB) initially started investigating the case. Later, the case was transferred to the CID.

Headline_English: 2 members of international financial scam ring arrested
Content_Enlish:
The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) Unit of Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested two members of an international financial scammer ring on charges of embezzling a large amount of foreign currency and illegally transacting. The arrestees are Md. Ziaul Haque and Md. Sajid Hasan Setu. 

A team of the Cyber ​​Crime Investigation Department arrested them from Sirajganj in a special operation on Tuesday. 

According to the Cyber ​​Crime Investigation Department, the arrested are accused of embezzling a large amount of foreign currency and illegally transacting through fraud in a foreign investment consulting firm. The investment consulting firm that is a victim of financial fraud has to provide personal information as part of the account opening process as well as bank account information. The firm temporarily transfers the equivalent of $1 to the bank account linked to the account as part of account verification for each newly registered account. Once the verification process is completed, the money is returned to the account of the institution within 2-3 days. 

The CTTC said that the arrested persons took advantage of the account authentication process of the financial institution. They first purchased social security numbers with fake names and addresses and anonymous foreign bank accounts from domestic and foreign fraudsters through various social media platforms such as 'Perfect Money', 'WebMoney', 'Payoneer' accounts. Using this information purchased online, they created 300-400 fake accounts of the investment advisory firm against each bank account. In this way, if the money was deposited into a specific bank account for verification of 300-400 accounts at once, the ring would transfer the money to another bank account before returning the money to the relevant institution. To complete this process, they mainly used international mobile banking platforms such as GO2Bank, Chime Bank, etc. This fraud ring has initially admitted that it has created numerous fake accounts and embezzled thousands of US dollars through fraud. 

This new type of fraud is called 'New Account Fraud'. The arrested have been sent to court on a 7-day remand in a case filed at Ramna Police Station.

Headline_English: Patient dies after removing oxygen mask: Accused employee arrested
Content_Enlish:
RAB has arrested a hospital employee accused of taking off a patient's oxygen mask after receiving a tip of Tk 50 less. Asaduzzaman Dhalu, an employee of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College (SZMC) Hospital in Bogra, has been arrested from Dhaka. RAB's media director Khandaker Al Moin confirmed this information on Thursday morning. RAB will brief the matter at the RAB Media Center in Karwan Bazar in Dhaka. 

Employee took off oxygen mask after receiving a tip of Tk 50 less, schoolboy dies in SZMC 

Earlier, around 11 pm on Tuesday, the Bogra Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College (SZMC) Hospital formed an investigation committee after criticism began across the city over the death of the patient. After the death of the student named Bikash Chandra at the hospital, his relatives alleged that he 'took off' the patient's oxygen mask after the hospital employee 'gave him a tip of Tk 50 less'. The deceased Bikash Chandra is the son of Bishu Chandra Karmakar of Putimari village in Saghata upazila of Gaibandha and is a class 8 student of a local school. 

Regarding the arrest, RAB Bogra Company Commander Squadron Leader Sohrab Hossain said that he was arrested from Abdullahpur at 4:30 am on Thursday. A murder case was filed with Bogra Sadar Police Station on Wednesday night against Asaduzzaman Dhalu, a temporary employee of the hospital, on charges of killing schoolboy Bikash Chandra, who was undergoing treatment at Shajimech Hospital on Tuesday night. Dr. Abdul Wadud, Deputy Director of Bogra Shajimech Hospital, said that the hospital's ward master Rafiqul Islam filed the case against Dhalu as the plaintiff. 

Bikash, the son of Bishu Chandra Karmakar of Putimari village in Saghata upazila of Gaibandha, was injured in a road accident last Tuesday evening. He was first admitted to the local Upazila Health Complex. Later that night, he was admitted to Bogra Shajimech Hospital. 

The allegation is that at around 11 pm, a temporary employee of the hospital, Asaduzzaman Dhalu, put Bikash on a trolley to take him from the emergency department to the ward. Later, he asked Bikash's relatives for a tip of 200 taka. At that time, Bikash's father gave him 150 taka. But when he was given 50 taka less, he removed the oxygen mask from Bikash's face and left. Bikash died shortly after that. Asaduzzaman Dhalu has been absconding since that incident. 

Bikash's uncle Sachin Chandra Karmakar told Samakal, "After completing the activities of the emergency department of the hospital, the patient Bikash was taken to the third floor with oxygen. An employee named Dulu of the hospital took the patient to the bed on a trolley and demanded a tip of 200 taka. At that time, Bikash's father gave him 150 taka. When he told them that they had no more money, employee Dulu removed the oxygen mask from the patient's face. As a result, Bikash died of suffocation within 5 minutes. At that time, when other patients attacked the employee, Dhulu fled with the help of the Ansars working at the hospital. 

Sachin Chandra Karmakar said that due to family tensions, Bikash was working in a workshop along with his studies. On Tuesday evening, around 7 pm, while returning home on a bicycle, Bikash suffered a serious head injury after being hit by a motorcycle. 

He was admitted to Saghata Upazila Hospital and given primary treatment, and then admitted to Bogra Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital at 10 pm for advanced treatment. 

Shamim, Sub-Inspector (SI) of Shajimech Hospital Police Outpost, said, "There was tension there after the patient's death. On receiving the information, the police went to the third floor and controlled the situation. But the employee fled before the police arrived." 

Shajimech Hospital Deputy Director Dr. Abdul Wadud said, "Dhulu is not a government employee. He used to do duty there occasionally. A committee has been formed to investigate the allegations made against him. "If he is found guilty in the investigation, strict legal action will be taken against him."

Headline_English: Main driver of truck that ran over Notre Dame student Nayeem arrested: RAB
Content_Enlish:
Harun, the driver of a garbage truck of Dhaka South City Corporation, has been arrested in connection with the incident of running over Notre Dame College student Naeem Hasan in front of Gulistan Market in the capital. He was arrested from Jatrabari on Friday, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) said. 

In a RAB release on Friday, it was said that the incident of Notre Dame College student Naeem being run over by a garbage truck in Gulistan area of ​​Dhaka metropolis on Wednesday created a nationwide sensation. In this context, RAB-3, along with other law enforcement agencies, started a shadow investigation and intelligence surveillance. Based on secret information, a team of RAB-3 conducted a special operation early Friday morning and arrested the main driver of the garbage truck, Md. Harun, from Jatrabari area of ​​Dhaka metropolis. His village home is in Fardabad, Bancharampur upazila of Brahmanbaria. 

The cleaner took the job of driving the car for 2.5 lakh taka 

It is said that during the initial interrogation, Harun said that he has been driving this garbage truck regularly since 2020. His assistant Russell drove the car because he was absent on Wednesday. Both Harun and Russell do not have a driving license.

Headline_English: 7 arrested for embezzling Tk 50 crore through lucrative campaign
Content_Enlish:
A gang has recruited a large number of members for an online MLM company by promising that the investment amount will double in just one month. Then they are asked to bring more members. For each new member, they will get 50 taka. And if they can bring 150 members, there is a special prize. They will get an iPhone, a personal car and the opportunity to travel abroad. Many people fall into the trap of such a tempting campaign and invest as much as they can. And the fraudsters have embezzled about 50 crore taka by capitalizing on their trust. 

Based on the complaints of the victims, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the police has finally arrested seven members of this gang. They are - Abul Hossain Pulak, Mahadi Hasan Mallick, Mizanur Rahman alias Bravo Mizan, Mohiuddin Jamil, Saiful Islam Akand, Kavez Ali Sarkar and Shahanur Alam Shahin. The operation was conducted in the Aminbazar area of ​​​​Savar, Dhaka on Saturday. At that time, 9 mobile phones of different brands, 20 SIM cards, check books of multiple bank accounts, ATM cards of multiple banks, 62 thousand taka in cash and business plan documents of various illegal MLL companies were found in their possession. 

A press conference was organized at the CID office in Malibagh in the capital on Sunday to provide details. In this, Additional DIG of CID Dhaka Metro Imam Hossain said that the gang first opened an online group and started promoting their business. They said that members had to deposit 1,850 taka to become members. And if they invested the money, they would get double the amount back after 15 or 30 days. To attract people, they would organize expensive events in different hotels. They would drive expensive cars and wear expensive clothes. Basically, they would try to recruit more members by showing these things. The one who could add 150 new members among the members would be given the status of star member. 

He said that various events were organized in the country and abroad with some star members. A few days ago, they spent a huge amount of money and took more than 500 investors to Cox's Bazar by plane and car. They held a function at a luxury hotel there and lured them into investing more. Numerous pictures and videos of these functions were found on the mobile phones of the arrested. In this way, they collected 5-6 lakh members in four illegal online-based MLM organizations, most of whom are women, through various methods. 

According to the CID, the ringleaders of this ring are Abul Hossain Pulak and Mahadi Hasan Mallick. The two of them used to work at Destiny. From there, they started defrauding online with the idea of ​​multi-level marketing or MLM business. However, they have named this method 'network marketing'. 

The CID does not have the authority to shut down these online platforms. However, they will recommend this to the concerned authorities in this regard. The money was taken from the victims through various mobile banking services. Some of the money was invested, and some of it was used to organize a grand event. It is also known that some of their money was kept in the bank. CID officials are hoping to learn more about the money during the remand interrogation.

Headline_English: Case filed against Tahsan-Mithila-Shabnam Faria in Evaly case
Content_Enlish:
A case has been filed against nine people, including popular stars Tahsan Khan, Rafiat Rashid Mithila and Shabnam Faria, for allegedly aiding and abetting the activities of the controversial e-commerce company Evaly. On December 4, an Evaly customer named Saad Sam Rahman filed the case at the Dhanmondi Police Station in the capital. 

The investigation officer of the case, Sub-Inspector (SI) Md. Rajib Hasan, confirmed the matter to reporters on Thursday night. 

The other accused in the case are Mohammad Russell, the arrested Managing Director (MD) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Evaly, his wife Shamima Nasrin, the company's chairman, Akash, Arif, Taher and Md. Abu Taish Kayes. 

Saad Sam Rahman mentioned in his complaint that customers' money was fraudulently embezzled and aided in this. The amount of embezzled money is three lakh 18 thousand. Which he has not been able to recover yet. 

According to the case report, Tahsan, Mithila and Shabnam Faria were in various positions at Evaly. Saad Sam Rahman invested in them with confidence due to their presence and various promotional talks. The complaint states that the plaintiff in the case was cheated due to these stars. 

In this regard, SI Rajib Hasan said that Evaly's chairman Shamima Nasrin and MD Mohammad Russell have been shown arrested in the case. Information is being collected about the rest. If their involvement is found in the investigation, legal action will be taken. 

It is learned that Tahsan was Evaly's goodwill ambassador. And Mithila was Evaly's goodwill ambassador for Evaly's Face of Evaly Lifestyle. Besides, Shabnam Faria was the chief public relations officer.

Headline_English: Death row convict who spent 22 years in hiding is finally arrested
Content_Enlish:
RAB has arrested Adam Khan alias Rafiq, a 22-year-old fugitive convicted of the murder of widowed mother Nurchan Begum in front of her children in Chunarughat, Habiganj. 

Speaking at a press conference at RAB's media center in Karwana Bazar in the capital on Wednesday afternoon, RAB's Legal and Media Wing Director Khandaker Al Moin said that a RAB-9 operation team arrested Rafiq from the Baipail area of ​​Ashulia, Dhaka on Tuesday night. Rafiq confessed to the murder during initial interrogation. 

On May 31, 1999, over a financial transaction, Adam Khan stabbed victim Nurchan Begum (40) in front of her three-year-old child Tajuddin. Victim Nurchan Begum died on the spot. Later, Nurchan Begum's other son Shafiq filed a murder case as the plaintiff. 

Shafiq's father died seven months before the incident. The case was conducted with the financial support of Shafiq and Tajuddin's uncle and the people of Laka. 

After the investigation in 2002, on July 17, 2002, the court sentenced the accused Adam Khan to death as the maximum punishment based on the evidence. 

After the initial interrogation, Khandaker Al Moin said that 1 year before the murder, the accused Adam Khan borrowed 2,000 taka from the plaintiff in the case, Shafiq, the son of the victim Nurchan Begum. Four months later, Nurchan's husband Abdur Rahman died. 

On May 31, 1999, when Nurchan went to ask for the money back, Adam Khan got into an argument with her. At one stage of the argument, Adam Khan started stabbing her. Nurchan Begum died on the spot. 

Khandaker Moin said that after the murder, Adam Khan fled. First to Sylhet, then to Ashulia in Dhaka. In 2012, Adam Khan created a birth certificate identifying himself as Rafiqul Islam. The address was written as Bypail, Ashulia, Dhaka. Through that fake certificate, he tried to obtain a national identity card, which mentioned Madhabpur, Habiganj as the permanent address. 

He said, ‘To change his appearance, he disguised himself at that time and introduced himself in Ashulia as Rafiq instead of his real name Adam Khan. Later, he created an NID and Smart NID card using a fake name and address through fraud. Then, he gradually established a permanent residence in Ashulia and started working as a mason in disguise. Adam Khan did not go to his village home for 22 years before being arrested.’

Headline_English: Murder on a contract of 2 lakh taka with the dream of becoming a don
Content_Enlish:
Hridoy Hossain is a resident of Mazar Road area of ​​Mirpur in the capital. He is not yet 18 years old. As soon as he reaches adolescence, he is obsessed with the dream of becoming a don in the crime world of that area. To fulfill this terrible dream, he embarks on the path of murder. He kills a teenager from Shahali area, Shahadat Hossain Hasib, for a contract of two lakh taka. 

The deceased Hasib worked at a tailoring company called 'Topten' in Mallick Tower in that area. He was hacked to death on his way home after work last Monday night. The police have released this information after arresting five people, including Hridoy, on suspicion of involvement in the incident. The other three arrested are Saddam Hossain, Humayun Kabir and Mofazzal Hossain Mandal. One is under the age of 16. 

Police officials say that Hasib's house is in Begumganj, Noakhali. He worked as a tailor craftsman at 'Topten', but he left home when the shops closed due to the coronavirus. Six months later, he joined work at the beginning of this month. However, this time he was called in a planned manner to 'punish' him. Due to a dispute over land in the village house, his expatriate cousin Md. Bipul brought him to Dhaka on the plan. 

Police officials held a press conference in the Mirpur area on Friday to reveal the mystery of the murder. At the press conference organized at the office of the Deputy Commissioner of the Mirpur Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Additional Deputy Commissioner AZM Taimur Rahman said that they suspect that Hasib was killed due to a dispute over land. A total of five people were found involved in the murder. Three of them were directly involved in the murder. Hridoy and Saddam admitted their involvement in the murder in their statements given under Section 164 in the court. 

The police official said at the press conference that Hasib's father had a case regarding his uncle's land in the village house. As a result, the previously known Mofazzal was given the responsibility of killing Hasib. As per the plan, Mofazzal again gave the responsibility of hiring a killer to Humayun Kabir. Humayun found the previously known Hridoy group and made a murder contract for two lakh taka. Hridoy also wanted to become a don by causing a big incident. 

Shahali Police Station OC Abul Basar Mohammad Asaduzzaman said that expatriate Md. Bipul once worked at Topten. After he went abroad, his cousin Hasib started working at that organization. The arrested Mofazzal taught the two people how to work. Bipul contacted this Mofazzal due to previous acquaintance. Mofazzal established contact with the Hridoy group through Humayun. 

The OC said that this group was not discussed in the area before. No previous cases were found against them. 

Police said that after the murder, Hridoy was first identified by looking at the CCTV footage around the scene. Later, after analyzing the technical information, his location was found to be Chandpur. Because, he left that area immediately after the incident. Then from there, he changed his location to Bhola and finally to Jhalakathi. He was arrested from there last Thursday. Then, based on the information he gave, four other people were arrested from the Mirpur area.

Headline_English: Taking him to India for talking about Europe and torture him in a torture cell: RAB
Content_Enlish:
The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested three people on charges of smuggling people to India, promising to send them to various countries in Australia and Europe, and then holding them in torture centers for ransom. On Monday night, a team of RAB-4 conducted a drive in the capital's Uttara and Mirpur areas and arrested them. 

The three arrested are Mallick Rezaul Haque alias Selim (62), Bulbul Ahmed Mallick (55) and Niranjan Pal (51). RAB said that fake passports, fake visas, application forms and important documents related to human trafficking were seized from them. 

Officials of the organization gave information about the arrest of the three people at a press conference organized at the RAB Media Center in Karwan Bazar on Tuesday. 

At the press conference, RAB-4 captain Mozammel Haque said that this gang has been involved in human trafficking for several years. Selim is the mastermind of this gang. Bulbul and Niranjan work as his associates. There are at least seven other members in Selim's gang in different parts of the country. Apart from this, information has been found about three people of this gang in India. 

He said that Selim's gang targets people interested in going abroad and lures them with high-paying jobs in Australia and various countries in Europe. Then, they smuggle them to neighboring countries by promising to take them to those developed countries. They deceive them by telling them that it is easy to get visas to those countries from India and take them there and lock them in their torture cells. Then, Selim's Indian associates physically and mentally torture those who want to go abroad and threaten to kill them. They record the torture scenes and later show the videos to family members in the country to collect ransom. 

Mozammel Haque said that the gang took 12 to 15 lakh taka per person for sending them to Australia and Europe, saying that they were first taken to a torture cell in Kolkata. From there, they were taken to a cell in Delhi and ransom was demanded. Efforts are underway to arrest other members of the gang. 

It was informed at the press conference that a person named Jahangir recently escaped from a torture center in India and returned to the country. While investigating the complaint, Selim's gang was identified. Selim and Bulbul demanded 3.4 million taka to send Jahangir to Australia and Jahangir's nephew Akash to the Netherlands by luring them with jobs. After taking 1.4 million taka, they sent Jahangir and his nephew Akash to India in December 2020 on fake visas. Since being trafficked there, these two gang members were detained by Niranjan and his Indian associates. At that time, another 9.5 million taka was collected as ransom from the families by physically and mentally torturing them and threatening them with death. 

RAB officials said that although Jahangir managed to escape, his nephew Akash is still being held by the traffickers in India. Apart from those two, Niranjan Pal smuggled three people named Billal Hossain, Robin Hossain and Shaheen Khan of Nawabganj to India in 2020 on the pretext of sending them to Portugal and Malta from Bangladesh. They endured torture there and returned to the country after paying ransom after six months. 

The three arrested told the RAB that Rajiv Khan, Manik and Robin Singh of Delhi were working as their associates in Kolkata.

Headline_English: Main accused Ashiq arrested in tourist rape case
Content_Enlish:
RAB has arrested Ashiqul Islam Ashiq (29), the main accused in the case of gang rape in Cox's Bazar, from Madaripur. 

RAB's Assistant Director of Law and Media Wing ANM Imran Khan said that after the incident, Ashiq came to Madaripur from Cox's Bazar and hid. He was arrested from there at around 9:30 pm tonight based on intelligence information. 

Based on intelligence information, the list of various crimes committed by Ashiqul Islam Ashiq (29), the main accused in the case of gang rape in Cox's Bazar, has started to emerge. 

The former Ward No. 1 Commissioner of Cox's Bazar Municipality told Samakal that Ashiqul Islam Ashiq of Madhyam Baharchara, Ward No. 11 of the municipality, is a listed terrorist of the police. 

After searching in the Kalatali Cottage Zone of Cox's Bazar city, it was learned that Ashiq became even more dangerous after being released from prison on November 16. On November 24, he took a hotel owner hostage at gunpoint and extorted 60,000 taka. The next day, Ashiq and his accomplices took another cottage owner hostage and looted 100,000 taka. However, a businessman in the cottage zone, who asked not to be named, said that prostitution is carried out in the hotels or cottages where Ashiq looted and robbed. That is why hotel owners do not take refuge in the law. 

Cases against terrorist Ashiq 

Cox's Bazar District Police said that Ashiq entered the world of crime as a teenager. On August 20, 2011, the first case was filed against him at the Cox's Bazar Sadar Police Station under the Fight Act. Ten months later, on July 20, 2012, the same police station filed a case against him for attempted murder. On January 14, 2014, another case was filed under the same section, on September 15 of the same year, one for attempted robbery, one under the Arms Act, and another for attempted murder. 

In March 2015, a case was filed against him under the Prevention of Violence against Women and Children Act. In November of that year, two separate cases were filed under the Arms Act. In the same month, a robbery case was also filed against him. Then, in September 2018, another case was filed under the Robbery Act. In October of that year, a case was filed against this terrorist under the Narcotics Control Act. 

Last June, an attempt to murder case was filed against Ashiq. A robbery case was filed in November. The latest case against him was filed against him on December 23 for raping a housewife. 

Vast terrorist force 

The main accused in the housewife rape case, Ashiq, has 25-30 terrorists in his group. Among them are Mubarak, Fahim, Babu, Mehedi Hasan Babu, Israfil Jaya and a few others from Baharchhara. Cox's Bazar Municipality's reserved women councilor Nasima Akhter said that Ashiq and his friends are the terror of Baharchhara and the surrounding areas. No one opens their mouths for fear of them. They are involved in the yaba business in the city. 

Cox's Bazar Sadar Police Station OC Munirul Gias said that he was arrested on November 7 in a robbery case and sent to jail through the court. However, he was released on bail on November 15. 

Cox's Bazar Police Superintendent Md. Hasanuzzaman said that many terrorists have been arrested and sent to jail. But nothing can be done against them if they are on bail.

Headline_English: Student files lawsuit against Holy Family teacher
Content_Enlish:
A medical student is filing a case against a teacher at the capital's Holy Family Red Crescent Medical College on charges of sexual harassment. Her classmates have already stood by her. 

The victim of sexual harassment said that on Monday evening, she and some of her classmates went to Uttara West Police Station to file a case against Holy Family Red Crescent Medical College's assistant professor Dr. Salauddin Chowdhury. 

But she was turned away without filing a case, citing the fact that the place of the incident was outside the jurisdiction of that police station. Since Holy Family Red Crescent Medical College is under the jurisdiction of Ramna Police Station, the West Police Station advised her to file a case there. 

Regarding not filing a case, Uttara West Police Station OC Shah Md. Aktaruzzaman Ilias told Samakal that the place of the incident is under the jurisdiction of Ramna Police Station. Therefore, if a case has to be filed, it should be filed at Ramna Police Station. 

A final-year student at Holy Family Red Crescent Medical College has alleged that Dr. Salauddin Chowdhury has been making immoral proposals to her in various ways. The teacher has sent him 'obscene' messages on messenger several times. In addition, he has been called to the college and 'threatened' for not agreeing to the 'immoral proposal'. 

On December 22, he filed a general diary (GD) against Dr. Salahuddin at Uttara West Police Station.

Headline_English: Case filed for alleged VAT evasion of Tk 39 crore
Content_Enlish:
The VAT Intelligence Department has filed a case against Mohammad Trading Tiles Marketing Company for allegedly evading VAT of Tk 39 crore in the capital. 

A press release from the VAT Intelligence Department on Monday said that the case was filed after allegations of VAT evasion were proven against this company on Jasimuddin Avenue in Uttara. 

VAT Intelligence officials said that the company purchases tiles and sanitary items of various sizes from RAK Ceramics Bangladesh Limited and Star Ceramic Limited and supplies them to the local market. The company did not properly deposit the applicable revenue against its VAT-eligible services to the government treasury and concealed the correct sales information. 

Later, allegations were made against Mohammad Trading Tiles Marketing Company for evading VAT by storing VAT-related documents in undeclared places and thereby ‘personally benefiting’ themselves. 

In response to specific allegations, a team of VAT detectives conducted a surprise raid on the company's unregistered premises (Northern Village 89, Gausul Azam Avenue Sector #14, Uttara, Dhaka) on October 3. The allegations were confirmed. 

The VAT detectives said that the company's original VAT documents were packed and piled up at the location for destruction.

Headline_English: Mauritius 'rape victim' files case in Dhaka
Content_Enlish:
A Bangladeshi female worker was raped by the owner of the company and some Bangladeshis while working at a garment factory in Mauritius. The woman filed a case with the capital's Rampura police station on Saturday. She filed the case under the Human Trafficking and Women and Child Abuse Prevention Act. 

According to the case source, when the plaintiff went to the African island nation of Mauritius on February 5 last year, she was given work at a garment factory named Fire Mount Tapetile. 

One day, Bangladeshi national Mohammad Shah Alam, who runs the garment factory's canteen, and his sons Furkan, Siddique, and Aslam told the female worker that the owner of Fire Mount had 'liked' her. It would be better to 'be with' the owner. 

In the case report, the victim said that Shah Alam intimidated her if she did not agree to the proposal. One day, he took her to the house of the garment owner Anil Kohli. Anil Kohli raped her. Shah Alam and Anil Kohli sexually abused her for several months, threatening to spread the rape video on social media. 

The case file also states that the victim became pregnant at one point as a result of the rape. Shah Alam and Anil Kohli took her to a hospital in Mauritius and had an abortion. They stipulated that if she returned to the country, the woman's father would be given a job and brought to Mauritius. 

She was sent back to the country on December 28 last year while she was ill. 

The woman alleged that her father had contacted the recruiting agency M/s Golam Rabbi International (License No. 1078) to go abroad. The agency staff told her that he could not go because he was too old. Instead, they offered to send her daughter to Mauritius for a salary of Tk 28,000. 

The victim was sent to Mauritius through the recruiting agency M/s M Akhtar & Sons. 

The victim said that after returning home, she and her father were threatened. She attempted suicide. After the 'torture news' came to the media in Bangladesh and Mauritius, the accused are offering a compromise. She wants them to be brought to justice. 

Shariful Hasan, head of BRAC's migration program, said that the victim described the horrific torture. Sexually abusing someone or forcing them into prostitution under the pretext of a job abroad is a crime included in human trafficking. The governments of Mauritius and Bangladesh should jointly investigate the truth of these allegations and take action.

Headline_English: Ansar al Islam's 'spiritual' leader arrested
Content_Enlish:
A top leader of the banned militant organization Ansar Al Islam has been arrested. His name is Mahmud Hasan Gunbi alias Hasan. 

RAB said that the arrested person is the ‘spiritual leader’ of Ansar Al Islam. He was arrested from the area adjacent to the embankment of Shah Ali Police Station in the capital on Thursday night. 

This information was given in a message sent by RAB’s media wing on Friday. A briefing will be held at RAB’s media center in Karwan Bazar at 4 pm on Friday to provide detailed information on this matter, the elite force said.

Headline_English: Cyber ​​'hijacking' increases 4-fold during pandemic
Content_Enlish:
In the first year of the coronavirus pandemic, ransomware attacks on digital platforms have increased by about 400 percent, or four times, compared to the previous year. During this time, the amount of damage to various organizations affected by the attacks has also doubled, reaching $ 3 trillion to $ 6 trillion. US-based cybersecurity monitoring company 'Expert Insight' has reported this. 
The company has prepared a report by analyzing government and private information related to ransomware attacks from June 2020 to June 30, 2021. Ransomware has been considered the most dangerous malware in the world for almost a decade. Once this malware enters a computer or smart device, it takes its entire operating system hostage. Then the attackers demand a large sum of money to restart the device. For this reason, such attacks are also called 'cyber hijacking'. Experts consider this to be the world's largest business 'cyber attack' today. 
Earlier, about 120 public and private institutions in the United States, including the Washington DC police server, were hit by ransomware attacks. Apart from this, public and private institutions in the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Germany, and France have also been hit by ransomware attacks in waves. According to this year's report by 'Expert Insight', attacks targeting servers of banks and financial institutions in developing countries in Asia have increased. 
On the other hand, a report by 'HackerOne', a popular US-based company for hacking information, said that the rate of hackers providing information on cyber attack risks in one year of the pandemic has increased by 63 percent compared to the previous year. This means that hackers spent 63 percent more time monitoring cybersecurity risks around the world during the pandemic than the previous year. 
This report was also published in July after analyzing data from June 2020 to June 30, 2021. The report says that among all the areas where the risk of cyber attacks has increased, the risk has increased the most due to the creation of 'misconfiguration' or incorrect security management in cybersecurity. Especially, in the rush to create cybersecurity management during the pandemic, the latest information related to hacking tools has not been verified in most cases. 
Increase in ransomware attacks: According to the report by 'Expert Insight', in the first two quarters of the year after the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in early 2020, ransomware attacks increased 485 times compared to the two quarters of the previous year. However, the number of attacks decreased slightly in early 2021. Considering the period from April to June 2020, ransomware attacks increased by 400 percent overall from April to June 2021. This information was obtained from the relevant government agencies in the United States, the report said. However, citing cyber counterterrorism expert Zohar Pinashi, it was said that according to this expert, ransomware attacks increased by about 800 percent in 2021 compared to 2019. 
The report also said that ransomware attackers have so far targeted institutions in economically developed countries. Because, if it is possible to successfully attack institutions in these countries and take over servers or digital systems, it is possible to demand a large amount of money to free them. However, during the pandemic, attacks targeting various institutions in developing countries in Asia, especially financial institutions and bank servers, have increased. 
Another cybersecurity company, 'Blackfog', said in a report that although the number of attacks has increased significantly compared to before, the success rate has increased slightly. Whereas the success rate of attacks was about 8 percent earlier, it has increased by about 11 percent in the last one year. However, in the last one year, attackers have increased the ransom amount for devices in attacks. Previously, ransoms were generally asked for from $5,000 to a maximum of $50,000. But now the amount has reached over $100,000, even a million dollars. 
Recently, a $5 million ransom was demanded after a successful ransomware attack on a server of a financial institution in the United States. The report said that the total loss from ransomware attacks in the five years before 2015 was about $3 trillion. The total loss as of June 2021 is about 6 trillion US dollars. 
The report recommends using genuine or licensed software, plug-ins and add-ons, including the operating system, to protect against ransomware attacks. In addition, it is recommended to store device files on a separate storage system or cloud. 
HackerOne report: According to 'The Hacker Report 2021' published by HackerOne, the amount of cybersecurity or system creation by organizations in different countries around the world during the pandemic has increased by about 310 percent compared to before. But in most cases, properly updated technology has not been used or 'misconfiguration' has been done. At the same time, the system has not been updated regularly. Especially from Asian and Eastern European countries, the picture of cybersecurity weaknesses has emerged more. As a result, many new targets for various malware attacks have been created in the past year.

Headline_English: SSC form filling time increased again
Content_Enlish:
The time for filling the SSC exam form without late fee ended on Saturday. That time has been extended. Now, Dhaka Education Board students will have the opportunity to fill the form without penalty until June 5. And educational institutions have been instructed to submit the fee online by June 6. 

On Sunday, the Dhaka Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board announced the extension of the form filling time. A letter was sent to all school and college heads informing this. At the same time, the Dhaka Board has warned educational institutions not to collect additional fees for filling the form. 

The letter sent by the board said that the time for filling the SSC exam without late fee has been extended until June 5. The last date for submitting the fee online by educational institutions is June 6. There is no opportunity to collect additional fees for filling the SSC exam form as determined by the board. Strict action will be taken if any complaint is received about collecting additional fees for filling the form. 

Earlier, students had the opportunity to fill the SSC form from April 1 to April 7. However, due to ongoing restrictions to prevent upward transmission of Corona, many students were not able to fill out the forms, so they were given the opportunity to fill out the forms. In the second phase, the form filling was carried out from May 22 to May 29. That time was extended again.

Headline_English: DU Teachers' Association requests accommodation in halls for examinees
Content_Enlish:
The University Teachers' Association has requested the Vice Chancellor to take the initiative to conduct physical examinations of various departments of Dhaka University from June 15 in phases (from Masters to first year) in compliance with health regulations. At the same time, the organization has also requested that only examinees stay in the halls during the examinations. 

In a letter written to Vice Chancellor Akhtaruzzaman on Sunday, Teachers' Association President Professor Rahmat Ullah and General Secretary Professor Nizamul Haque Bhuiyan made these requests. 

The Teachers' Association has made a total of seven requests to the Vice Chancellor. The other five requests are to take initiatives to normalize educational activities by quickly contacting the government and ensuring vaccination of all university family members including students; to ensure casual and medical leave of Dhaka University teachers through a legal framework as per the prevailing provisions; to ensure cleanliness and hygiene in the university; to take necessary steps to quickly resolve other administrative issues including the promotion of teachers and to take necessary steps to improve the quality of services at the university medical center and ensure round-the-clock healthcare during the corona period. 

In the letter, the association leaders told the vice-chancellor that the Dhaka University Teachers Association is always ready to provide all-out cooperation in improving the university and the educational environment.

Headline_English: UGC seeks information from private university students for vaccination
Content_Enlish:
The University Grants Commission (UGC) is taking steps to vaccinate students of all private universities in the country to prevent the spread of Corona and avoid health risks. 

To ensure that all students get vaccinated, students' information related to Covid-19 has been sought from the concerned universities. At the same time, teachers, officials and employees under the age of 30 of these universities have also been asked to fill in the prescribed form with the information and send it by July 28. 
Recently, a letter from the UGC was sent to the VCs and registrars of all private universities. The letter said that in view of the decision of the Ministry of Education, it is requested to send the list of all students of the university and all teachers, officials and employees under the age of 30 in a file as per the prescribed form to the Commission's e-mail (private.ugcl@gmail.com) by July 28.

Headline_English: Scholarship opportunities at Abu Dhabi University for undergraduate and postgraduate studies
Content_Enlish:
Abu Dhabi University in the United Arab Emirates will offer scholarships to international students for the 2021 academic year. The scholarships will be awarded for undergraduate and postgraduate programs. Abu Dhabi University was founded by Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed of the United Arab Emirates. Abu Dhabi University is one of the largest private sector universities in the United Arab Emirates. 

Scholarship opportunities 
* Academic Scholarships, 
* Alumni Scholarships, 
* Chairman's Scholarships, 
* Family Tuition Waivers, 
* H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed Scholarships, 
* University Scholarships. 

Eligibility 
International and national students can apply for Abu Dhabi University Scholarships. Applicants must apply for a full-time program. Students from other countries, including Bangladesh, can apply for this scholarship. 

Abu Dhabi University is ranked 701-750th in the QS Global World University Rankings for 2021. Interested students must apply by December 30 of this year. 

Application Procedure 
Click here to view application details.

Headline_English: SSC assignment information to be sent by August 19
Content_Enlish:
The assignment process for this year's SSC examinees is underway. The three-week assignments of the examinees have already been published. The government has sought overall information about this process. It has been asked to send this information to the Department of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHHE) of the Ministry of Education by e-mail by August 19. 

The Directorate of Education has sent a letter to the regional deputy directors with this instruction. In the letter, the regional deputy directors have been asked to know how many students have accepted the assignment, how many have submitted it and how many students have not submitted the assignment. All information about submitting the three-week assignment should be sent to the Monitoring and Evaluation Wing by August 19. 

In the letter sent to the deputy directors, the department says that due to the Corona pandemic, assignments are being conducted in the light of the revised syllabus for the 2021 SSC examinees sent by the National Curriculum and Textbook Board as per the instructions of the Ministry of Education. A notification has been issued on the website from the Secondary Branch of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education on July 18 for three weeks in the first phase. In light of that instruction, it is necessary to monitor whether the assignment activities of the students are being conducted properly at the field level. 

Summary table 
Information regarding the submission of assignments by the 2021 SSC examinees should be sent in the prescribed table according to the assignment grid. The table information should be sent by mentioning the number of government and private secondary schools under its jurisdiction, the total number of students who will participate in the SSC examination in 2021, the number of students who accepted the assignment in the first three weeks, the number of students who submitted the assignment in the first three weeks, and the number of students who did not submit the assignment in the first three weeks. The name of the region, e-mail ID, mobile phone number, total number of districts, and total number of upazilas should be mentioned in it. 

The regional deputy directors have been asked to prepare the information according to the table and send it to the e-mail of the Monitoring and Evaluation Wing of the department (assignment.mew@gmail.com) by August 19. Officials have been asked to follow the instructions in the notification issued by the department and adhere to proper hygiene rules when sending information. 

Due to the inability to start educational activities due to the outbreak of the Corona pandemic, the government has planned to conduct this year's SSC and HSC exams in only three group-based elective subjects instead of all subjects. The short syllabus of these subjects will be completed on the basis of assignments. Out of these, a total of 24 assignments are being given to the candidates in SSC and 30 assignments in HSC. Education Minister Dipu Moni has announced plans to conduct the SSC exams at the end of November and the HSC exams in December if the situation normalizes. However, he also said that there is a plan to evaluate the students through assignments if the exams are not conducted.

Headline_English: Students' 4-point demand for class exams
Content_Enlish:
General students of Dinajpur Haji Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University have formed a human chain with four demands, including conducting semester final exams in accordance with health rules, opening all residential halls, and bringing every student under vaccination. They held an hour-long human chain program on the Dhaka-Dinajpur highway in front of the university's main gate at 12 noon today, Monday. Later, they submitted a memorandum to the university's vice-chancellor. 

Uttam Pal, a 17th batch student of the Department of Statistics, Waheduzzaman, a student of the Faculty of Agriculture, Zulkifal Islam of the Department of Food Processing and Engineering, and Nahid Ahmed of the Department of Sociology, among others, spoke at the human chain. The speakers said that since the beginning of the Corona pandemic, the university administration has assured to open educational institutions and conduct exams in several phases. All institutions are running outside the educational institutions, but the university administration has not taken any initiative. Only nominal online classes are running. Not all students are able to participate in online classes because they are not covered by device and network coverage. 

The students said, "Due to Corona, I have been stuck in a session for one and a half to two years. I cannot even prepare for my studies by sitting at home. The residential halls have been closed there. Many students have to live in the mess, taking risks and facing financial losses." At that time, they demanded that the university administration and the residential halls be immediately vaccinated against Corona and opened in accordance with health rules. Otherwise, the general students warned of a strict movement. 

In this regard, the university's registrar, Professor Fazlul Haque, said that the students have submitted a memorandum. There they have stated their various demands. But the point is that the university administration does not have the authority to go beyond the government's decision. He said, "We know about the loss of students due to Corona. But what else is there to do? However, we have made arrangements to strengthen online classes and bring every student under it."

Headline_English: RUET, CUET and KUET admission tests postponed by two months
Content_Enlish:
Considering the current situation of coronavirus, the undergraduate admission test of engineering cluster of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET) and Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET) has been postponed by two months. The test will be held on August 12 as per the previously announced time instead of June 12. The Joint Admission Test Committee of CUET, KUET and RUET announced this in a notification. 

This information was given through a notification jointly signed by the President of the Joint Admission Committee of CUET, KUET and RUET, Md. Rabiul Alam and Member Secretary Md. Mainul Islam. In addition, this information has been given on the Joint Admission Test website of CUET, KUET and RUET (https://www.admissionckruet.ac.bd). 
Out of the eligible applicants for 3,201 seats, the top 30,000 will be given the opportunity to participate in the test based on the total marks in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and English subjects in the Higher Secondary or equivalent examination. The list of eligible students to participate in the admission test will be published on June 2.

Exam Subject and Distribution 
This year's admission test will have 500 marks in the MCQ system for the general engineering department, i.e., the urban and planning department, i.e., Group 'A'. Along with engineering, a 700-mark MCQ test will be held in the architecture department, Group 'B'. 

The best 30,000 applications will be accepted from all over the country based on the application for the exam. The eligibility for the application is a minimum GPA-4 in 2017 or 2018 secondary or equivalent and a total grade of 20 with GPA-5 in higher mathematics, physics, chemistry and English separately in higher secondary. 
Earlier, on April 20, the joint admission test committee of CUET, KUET and RUET published the admission notice. It was said that the admission test for Group 'A' (Engineering departments and Urban and Regional Planning Department) will be held on June 12 from 10 am to 12:30 pm and for Group 'B' (Engineering departments, Urban and Regional Planning Department and Architecture Department) from 10 am to 1:45 pm. Now, according to the changed date, the admission test for the Engineering cluster will be held on August 12 as per the previously announced time.

Headline_English: Students' unique ID form filling suspended
Content_Enlish:
The process of filling out the Unique ID form and data entry for students has been suspended. Banbase has announced that this process will be suspended until the training of teachers is completed and the schools are reopened. This decision was made at a meeting of the district education officers and regional deputy directors with the IEIMS project officials on Wednesday (May 26) afternoon. An order has already been issued informing about the matter. 

In this regard, the process of filling out the Unique ID form and data entry has been suspended amid the suffering of teachers. The order signed by Project Director Professor Shamsul Alam said that since the training of teachers through the IEIMS project has not been completed and the teaching activities of educational institutions have not started, it has been requested to suspend the process of filling out the information table and data entry for the time being. 

It also said that the process of filling out the information table for issuing Unique ID can be taken up in phases after the teaching activities of educational institutions start. The deadline for filling out the information table will be announced later. 

Many were facing complications in filling out the form and data entry work as the training activities of teachers had not been completed. This was discussed in the meeting on Wednesday. Apart from this, students and guardians suffered due to the issuance of notices regarding the submission of birth certificates on time. They were also at risk of health. Considering the overall situation, Banbase decided to suspend the form filling and data entry.

Headline_English: Socialist Student Front demands 25 percent allocation for education sector
Content_Enlish:
The Samajtantrik Chhatra Front has demanded that 25 percent of the next national budget be allocated to the education sector. The organization made this demand at a human chain program at the National Press Club on Thursday. 

The leaders of the Samajtantrik Chhatra Front, who participated in the human chain, said that the government should announce a waiver of student salaries and fees during the Corona period, provide special incentives for affected teachers, students, officials and employees, and announce a roadmap for opening campuses in accordance with health rules. 

The speakers at the human chain said, "Educational institutions have been closed since March 18 of last year to avoid infection. Due to the closure of educational institutions for almost one and a half years, various complications have arisen in the entire education system. The common people have been economically affected due to the long lockdown without appropriate measures due to Corona. In such a situation, the budget for the current fiscal year will be announced on June 3. This budget can play a special role in protecting students and people related to education. According to the existing rules, 25 percent of the national budget is supposed to be allocated to the education sector. But we have seen that last year, during the Corona period, 15 percent of the total budget was allocated for education, which is much less than the need. 

The leaders and activists of the organization said that the lower-middle-class and middle-class people of the country have been the most affected by Corona. Where it has become difficult to meet family expenses, meeting school-college-university expenses has become a 'sore on the back'. Students who used to pay their own expenses have also fallen into the same trap. 

If all kinds of salaries and fees of students are waived this year, teachers and guardians will be able to stand by them in this crisis. In addition, financial incentives must be announced for teachers-students, officials and employees affected by the Corona period. 

The human chain program was presided over by Masud Rana, President of the Central Committee of the Samajtantrik Chhatra Front. The organization's Publicity and Publication Secretary Rafiquzzaman Farid moderated the human chain, and Finance Secretary Pragati Barman, members Arup Das, Sadequl Islam, and others spoke at the human chain.

Headline_English: Instructions to prepare for opening of educational institutions from June 13
Content_Enlish:
The Ministry of Education has ordered preparations to open educational institutions from June 13. On Thursday (May 27), a notification in this regard was issued by the Administration and Establishment Division of the Secondary and Higher Education Department. 

The ministry's notification said that, subject to the corona infection situation being under control, it is requested to open secondary and higher secondary educational institutions under this department from June 13 and take necessary preparatory measures to conduct educational activities. At the same time, educational institutions will be closed until June 12. During this time, students will stay in their respective homes for the sake of everyone's safety. Online education will also continue. Guardians will ensure that students stay at home. 
On Wednesday afternoon, Education Minister Dipu Moni said in a virtual press conference that the ongoing holidays of educational institutions have been extended until June 12 due to the corona pandemic. Online education activities will continue during this time and teachers, students and guardians will have to follow the health rules. 

Educational institutions in the country have been closed for 14 months due to coronavirus. Due to this, about four crore students from primary to higher education are facing serious problems. Many students are moving up to higher classes with deficiencies due to the closure of classes and examinations. How much has been learned cannot be verified. 

A few days ago, a private study found that 19 percent of primary and 25 percent of secondary students are at risk of not being able to learn or have learning disabilities due to the coronavirus-related closure. In such a situation, educationists are urging a long-term plan to compensate for this loss of education. Many of them have also recommended opening educational institutions in areas where there is no or low infection. 

It is known that earlier the government, in consultation with the National Technical Advisory Committee on Corona, had decided to open schools and colleges from May 23. But recently, due to the increase in coronavirus infections and concerns about the Indian model, the opening of schools and colleges was postponed to May 29, along with the idea of ​​increasing the ongoing restrictions

Headline_English: More than 500 migrants rescued off Italian coast
Content_Enlish:
The country's coast guard has rescued more than 500 migrants from the coast of Italy. This information was reported by BBC Online on Sunday. 

The migrants were rescued from the Italian island of Lampedusa on Saturday, authorities said. The total number of migrants rescued is 539. Among them are women and children. 

According to Italian authorities, the migrants were on a dilapidated fishing boat. They were trying to enter Europe by sea. 

After the rescue, the migrants were brought to the island of Lampedusa. The Italian coast guard and financial crime police vessels assisted in this work. 

Yesterday, the largest number of migrants were rescued from the Italian coast in a single day in recent times. 

Lampedusa Mayor Toto Martello said yesterday's arrival was the largest number of migrants brought to the island in recent rescue operations. 

The Italian island of Lampedusa is one of the destinations for migrants seeking to cross the sea to Europe. 

The island has a shelter for the rescued migrants. The shelter has a capacity of 300 people, but there are five times as many migrants there. 

A doctor from Doctors Without Borders said that some of the migrants rescued yesterday had been subjected to violence. It is believed that they were subjected to violence while waiting for a boat in Libya to reach Europe. 

Italian investigators are investigating what exactly happened to the rescued migrants in Libya.

Headline_English: 30 Saudi-led coalition soldiers killed in Houthi rebel attack
Content_Enlish:
At least 30 soldiers of the Saudi-led coalition were killed and 60 wounded in an attack by Houthi rebels in Yemen. The attack was carried out on the Al-Anad military base on Sunday with drones and missiles. 

Mohammed al-Naqib, a spokesman for the southern Yemeni army, said the attack by the pro-Iranian rebels killed 30 to 40 of their soldiers. At least 60 were wounded. He said the death toll could rise. 

The attack came at a time when peace talks between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis are underway under the mediation of the United Nations and the United States. However, the two sides have not yet reached a compromise agreement. 

Two hospital sources said that several bodies, including 16 wounded people, were brought to the main hospital in Lahj province. However, they were not sure whether any civilians were among the casualties. 

Locals said they heard several heavy explosions in the Al-Anad area. The area is about 70 kilometers from the southern port city of Aden. Several residents in the disputed central city of Taiz also said they heard missiles fired from the eastern city controlled by the Houthi rebels. 

Yemen has been at war since 2014, when Houthi rebels overran the capital Sanaa and ousted the government of Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi. A Saudi-led coalition and the United Arab Emirates intervened in March 2015 to restore Hadi to power. The two sides have been fighting since then. Thousands of people have been killed in the fighting, and the conflict has created the world's largest humanitarian crisis.

Headline_English: North Korea has started up a nuclear reactor: UN
Content_Enlish:
The UN's International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) fears that a closed nuclear reactor in North Korea has been restarted. The reactor is believed to have produced plutonium used to make nuclear weapons. The news agency Reuters reported this information on Monday, citing the IAEA's annual report. 

The IAEA report, published last Friday, said that a reactor is believed to have been restarted at the Yongbyon nuclear complex, about 100 kilometers from the North Korean capital Pyongyang. It has a capacity of five megawatts. There were no signs of any activity in the reactor from December 2018 to early July 2021. However, since then, there have been some indications that the reactor has been restarted. The UN report has mentioned the matter as worrying. 

Earlier this year, the IAEA said that there were indications of plutonium production at the Yongbyon nuclear complex. They say that the reason for this is that cooling water has leaked from the complex. Usually, such water comes out when the reactor is operating. 

To prepare the report, the IAEA had to monitor North Korea. However, the organization could not enter the country. The observation had to be carried out from satellite images. Because, since 2009, the country's government has imposed a ban on the investigation of this UN monitoring organization. 

Since that ban, North Korea has continued its nuclear weapons development activities. It has also exploded nuclear weapons experimentally. North Korea last conducted a nuclear test in 2017. 

Meanwhile, the cause of the headache is not only the Yongbyon reactor. The IAEA says that a uranium enrichment plant is also believed to have been operating in the same nuclear complex for some time. In addition, movement has been observed at a uranium mine and plant in the Pyeongsan area of ​​the country.

Headline_English: Kabul airport under Taliban control
Content_Enlish:
The Taliban have taken control of Kabul airport after US forces left. According to the BBC, new video footage shows Taliban members entering Kabul's Hamid Karzai International Airport. They are checking a hangar at the airport. 

Taliban members entered the airport after the last US plane left Kabul airport. The incident was recorded by the Los Angeles Times correspondent Nabih Bulls. In this video, he said, "We are now with the armed members of the Taliban. A minute ago, it was under the control of US forces. Now the Taliban are taking control of this airport." 

According to another US media outlet, CNN, Taliban members are checking what US forces have left behind after entering Kabul airport. 

Earlier, Marine General Frank McKenzie, head of US Central Command, announced the withdrawal of troops at a press conference at the Pentagon on Monday local time. US troops have been withdrawn from Kabul in the final stages. McKenzie said, "I am here to announce the completion of the withdrawal of troops from Afghanistan. We have not been able to get everyone out of Afghanistan. But I think if we could have stayed another 10 days, we could have gotten everyone out. And that is what we wanted." McKenzie also admitted that many people in Afghanistan are still frustrated. The situation has become very difficult. 

According to the BBC, McKenzie said that the US and its allies have been able to evacuate about 123,000 people from Afghanistan

Headline_English: Ban on sale of liquor and meat in Mathura, India, advice on selling milk
Content_Enlish:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has imposed a complete ban on the sale of liquor and meat in Mathura, India. This information was given in a report published by NDTV Online. 

The ban was announced yesterday, Monday. Adityanath made the announcement at a function in Lucknow. 

The Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister said that the officials concerned have been instructed to formulate a plan for this ban. 

Adityanath suggested that those involved in the liquor and meat business of Mathura can start selling milk to revive the glory of the place. 

Mathura was once known for producing large quantities of animal milk. Now the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister wants to revive that glory. 

Adityanath said that places of religious faith of people have been neglected for a long time. Now they are being revived.

Headline_English: Immigrant emergency workers demand citizenship
Content_Enlish:
The US has demanded US citizenship for the 5 million essential workers who have kept the US urban areas open during this difficult time of the Corona pandemic. Rallies were held in major US cities including New York on July 23 to demand this. 

Thousands of immigrants working in various professions held banners and festoons at the rally demanding their legal right to live in the United States. Local liberal political circles and lawmakers, along with civic organizations, joined these rallies of immigrants. 

The Chinatown area of ​​New York City was covered with banners and festoons of thousands of immigrant workers. From cab drivers to hotel and restaurant workers, workers at various levels of health care institutions, people working in delivery services, workers engaged in the food preparation industry, cleaning workers and others were present at the rally. 

According to the rally in New York, when the Covid-19 infection began in March 2020, the city went into lockdown. People in the essential sectors kept the city open by risking their own safety. Most of the people who risked their lives working in transportation, services, food preparation, and delivery were immigrants. 

Speakers said that by risking their lives, immigrants have once again demonstrated their commitment and commitment to the United States. 

Speaking at the rally in New York, Mourad Awadeh, executive director of the Immigration Coalition, a civic organization, said that immigrants in the United States have fulfilled their responsibilities during the country's most critical time. Many immigrants have risked their lives and the lives of their families to work. Many immigrants have lost their lives working while working. 

Mourad Awadeh said that it is time for undocumented immigrants in the United States to breathe freely. He said that the pandemic has once again proven that immigrants are always important to the United States. 

US President Joe Biden is trying to reverse many of the hostile anti-immigration policies of former President Donald Trump after coming to power. He has promised to build a humane immigration system in the United States. Former President Barack Obama introduced temporary immigration benefits for people who came to the United States with their parents or in some other way as minors. Former President Donald Trump tried to block this immigration program, known as ‘Daka’. After President Joe Biden came to power, he ordered the Daka program to be accepted again. 

Last week, a conservative court in Texas ruled that the Daka program was illegal. Seven hundred thousand immigrants have already applied for this program. Thousands of people affected by the court’s ruling on the Daka program joined the rally on July 23 with banners and festoons. 

The Daka program members at the rally demanded that the political game stop with them and immediately open the path to U.S. citizenship for all undocumented immigrants through a comprehensive immigration program. 

Jose Lopez, co-executive director of the immigrant citizen organizer Make the Road New York, said that many undocumented emergency workers have been waiting to immigrate to the United States for years. He demanded immediate immigration benefits for the more than 5 million frontline workers who have risked their lives for the safety of the public. 

The rally began on July 23 in the city's Chinatown area, but spread to Columbus Circle. US media reported that such rallies were spontaneous in major cities including Philadelphia, Chicago, Washington DC, and Los Angeles. 

At the New York rally, State Senator Jessica Ramos said that the federal government has announced a commitment to building a humane immigration system. She mentioned at the rally that immigrants scattered in New York City have the right to provide services to the public without any worries. 

New York taxi cab drivers also joined the rally by stopping their work. Yellow taxis were also seen hanging posters in solidarity with the rally. 

Instead of going through the long and contentious process of passing immigration reform legislation through Congress, President Joe Biden is trying to make changes to the immigration system through a spending bill. Linking immigration to the country's economy, President Biden has included a separate budget for immigration in his proposed infrastructure bill. 

Immigrant groups believe that the passage of the infrastructure bill could pave the way for permanent immigration for hundreds of thousands of immigrants already living in the United States.

Headline_English: Israeli tycoon's oil tanker attacked, 2 killed
Content_Enlish:
Two sailors were killed in an attack on an oil tanker owned by an Israeli tycoon off the coast of Oman in the Arabian Sea. One of the dead sailors was a British national and the other a Romanian. The tanker was attacked on Thursday night, the British newspaper The Guardian reported. 

The attack took place on the Liberian-flagged oil tanker Mercer Street off the island of Masirah, 185 miles (300 kilometers) northeast of the Omani capital Muscat. 

Israeli officials did not immediately comment on the attack. Tensions between Israel and Iran have reached new heights in recent months. The attack on an Israeli-owned ship comes amid allegations that Iran is behind several previous attacks. 

Israel, on the other hand, is suspected of carrying out several strikes to stop Iran's nuclear program. 

London-based Zodiac Maritime, owned by Israeli billionaire Yael Ofer's Zodiac Group, said in a statement that the Liberian-flagged ship was owned by a Japanese person. The British Ministry of Defence initially gave an incorrect statement about the ownership of the ship. 

Zodiac Maritime called the incident "piracy" but did not elaborate. Shortly afterwards, it reported the death of two sailors in the attack. It did not say whether anyone else was injured. 

In a brief statement, the British military's Maritime Trade Operations said an investigation was underway. It did not elaborate, but said the incident was not linked to piracy. 

Oman declined to comment on the incident.

Headline_English: Attack on UN compound in Afghanistan, 1 killed
Content_Enlish:
An attack on the main UN compound in Afghanistan's western Herat province has killed at least one security guard. However, no UN officials were injured. The United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) has blamed the attack on "anti-government" insurgents. 

Reuters news agency reported, citing UN officials in Afghanistan, that Taliban fighters advanced deep into Herat city on Friday. At that time, Afghan troops clashed with them near the UNAMA regional headquarters. At one stage, the UN facility was attacked with gunfire and rocket-propelled grenades. 

President Joe Biden has announced that all US troops will be withdrawn from Afghanistan by August 31. The Taliban have increased their attacks in Afghanistan since the start of the withdrawal process. They have already taken control of a large part of the country. 

However, it is not yet clear who carried out Friday's attack. The Taliban said the incident may have been a result of gunfire between the two sides. Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said on Twitter that fighting was going on very close to the office. Security guards may have been injured in the "crossfire." The UN office is not under any threat. 

The UN issued a statement after the attack on the office. It said that it is trying to quickly get a full picture of the attack. In addition, it is keeping in touch with the relevant parties. In this regard, Deborah Lyons, the UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for Afghanistan, said, "This attack on the UN is regrettable and we condemn it in the strongest terms." The White House also condemned the attack. 

Many civilians have been killed in the ongoing violence in Afghanistan since the start of the process of withdrawing US and allied troops. UNAMA has warned that if this violence is not stopped, Afghanistan could face the highest number of civilian casualties in a decade. A report by the organization said that 1,659 civilians were killed in Afghanistan in the first half of 2021. 3,254 were injured. This number is much higher than last year.

Headline_English: Myanmar junta committed crimes against humanity: HRW
Content_Enlish:
It is about to be six months since the military coup in Myanmar. Anti-junta protests are underway in the country. On the eve of the six-month anniversary, university students in the country have protested against the junta on the streets. And in recent days, the rights organization Human Rights Watch (HRW) has accused the junta of committing crimes against humanity for killing and torturing its own people in the name of suppressing the protests. 

On Saturday, local time, university students marched on motorcycles on the streets of Mandalay, Myanmar's second largest city. At that time, they raised anti-junta slogans with red and green flags. At that time, the students took a stand against any talks with the junta to hand over power to a civilian government. They demand that the junta government must agree to unconditionally hand over power. 

Meanwhile, the New York-based Human Rights Watch said in a statement on Saturday that the junta has carried out armed repression against people participating in protests against Myanmar's military rule. Torture has been carried out on detained opposition figures. Many have been killed, which is a clear violation of international humanitarian law. 

Brad Adams, the organization's Asia director, said that the Myanmar junta has committed crimes against humanity by repressing, torturing and killing its own people. 

The country has been experiencing protests since the Myanmar military seized power in early February. 
However, the rights organization did not respond to requests for comment on the junta's allegations when it contacted Zaw Min Tun, the junta's spokesman, for comment. 
On February 1, a bloodless military coup took place in Myanmar. Pro-democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi and influential politicians in the country, including the country's leader, were arrested. Multiple cases were filed against them. The results of last November's general election were annulled. Suu Kyi's party, the National League for Democracy (NLD), won a landslide victory in that election. The junta rejected the election results and staged a coup. 
Immediately after the coup, ordinary people in Myanmar took to the streets to protest. Their demands are two- the lifting of military rule and the release of political prisoners including Suu Kyi. The rights organization Assistance Association of Political Prisoners (AAPP) has reported that 939 people have been killed in the country so far due to the junta's repression. Nearly seven thousand people, including artists, teachers, students, politicians, journalists, and doctors, have been detained. 

Myanmar's ousted politicians are continuing their fight to restore democracy by forming a shadow government. Overall, the country is at risk of civil war. In such a situation, Western powers, including the United States, have imposed new sanctions against the junta. However, the regional alliance of Southeast Asian countries, ASEAN, has taken steps to restore peace in Myanmar. The members of the alliance have taken steps to hold peaceful talks between the conflicting parties based on five points.
